examples.translation_ko: 그 말들이 블랑슈 스트루브에게 미친 효과에 나는 놀랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: A calque of Latin locus commūnis, referring to a generally applicable literary passage, itself a calque of Ancient Greek κοινὸς τόπος (koinòs tópos).
definition_en: A widely accepted or conventional idea or practice.

senses.gloss: Ordinary; not having any remarkable characteristics.
senses.example: In the old days, hopping onto the platform from a not-yet-stopped train was a commonplace stunt for daily commuters in a hurry.

examples.text: I couldn’t muster up a single commonplace out of the thousand in my head.
examples.translation_ko: 머릿속에 있던 수천 가지 평범한 말 중에서 하나도 꺼낼 수가 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He looked commonplace.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 평범해 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a genuine enthusiasm for the commonplace.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 평범한 것에 대한 진정한 열정을 가지고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English temperen, tempren, from Old English ġetemprian, temprian, borrowed from Latin temperō (“I divide or proportion duly, I moderate...
definition_en: A person's normal or usual mood.

senses.gloss: A general tendency or orientation towards a certain type of mood, a volatile state; a habitual way of thinking, behaving or reacting.
senses.example: to have a good, bad, or calm temper

senses.gloss: State of mind; mood.
senses.example: She bowed to him, to put him in a good temper.

senses.gloss: A tendency to become angry.
senses.example: to have a hasty temper

examples.text: His temper cracked a little.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 성질이 조금 터져 나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was of uncertain temper.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 변덕스러운 성격이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But he recovered his temper immediately, and looked at me with a smile.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그는 즉시 화를 가라앉히고 미소를 지으며 나를 바라봤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English likely, likly, lykly, likliche, from Old English ġelīclīċ (“suitable”) and Old Norse líkligr (“likely”) (probably independent f...
definition_en: Having a good chance of happening or being true.

senses.gloss: Probable; having a greater-than-even chance of occurring.
senses.example: Rain is likely later this afternoon.

senses.gloss: Reasonably to be expected; apparently destined, probable.
senses.example: Do you think there's likely to be snow?

senses.gloss: Appropriate, suitable; believable; promising, having a good potential.
senses.example: Jones is a likely candidate for management.

examples.text: “Of course I’m not likely to see anybody, but if I do.”
examples.translation_ko: "물론 누굴 만날 일은 없겠지만, 만나게 되면 말이에요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: So he invented just the sort of Jay Gatsby that a seventeen-year-old boy would be likely to invent, and to this conception he was faithful to the end.
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 그는 열일곱 살 소년이 만들어낼 법한 바로 그런 제이 개츠비를 창조했고, 이 개념에 끝까지 충실했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: An appeal to the emotions is little likely to be effectual before luncheon.
examples.translation_ko: 점심 전에는 감정에 호소하는 것이 효과를 거두기 어렵다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Do you think it’s likely that a man will do any good when he starts at your age?
examples.translation_ko: "당신 나이에 시작해서 뭔가 성과를 낼 수 있다고 생각하세요?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English difficult (ca. 1400), a back-formation from difficulte (whence modern difficulty), from Old French difficulté, from Latin diffi...
definition_en: Difficult to do or understand something.

senses.gloss: Hard, not easy, requiring much effort.
senses.example: There is not the strength or courage left me to venture into the wide, strange, difficult world, alone.

senses.gloss: Hard to manage, uncooperative, troublesome.
senses.example: Stop being difficult and eat your broccoli—you know it's good for you.

senses.gloss: Unable or unwilling.
senses.example: “I hope, madam,” said Jones, “my charming Lady Bellaston will be as difficult to believe anything against one who is so sensible of the many obligations she hath conferred upon him.”

examples.text: Her face was sad and lovely with bright things in it, bright eyes and a bright passionate mouth, but there was an excitement in her voice that men who had cared for her found difficult to forget: a singing compulsion, a whispered “Listen,” a promise that she had done gay, exciting things just a while since and that there were gay, exciting things hovering in the next hour.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 얼굴은 슬프면서도 사랑스러웠고, 밝은 눈과 밝고 열정적인 입술 같은 빛나는 것들로 가득했지만, 그녀의 목소리에는 한때 그녀를 사랑했던 남자들이 좀처럼 잊기 어려워하는 흥분이 담겨 있었다. 노래하듯 사람을 끌어당기는 힘, 속삭이는 "들어봐"라는 말, 그리고 조금 전까지 즐겁고 흥미진진한 일들을 해왔으며 다음 시간에도 그런 일들이 기다리고 있다는 약속 같은 것이.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I have never known a more difficult patient.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이보다 더 다루기 힘든 환자를 본 적이 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “It must have been difficult to explain to Robert,” I said.
examples.translation_ko: "로버트에게 설명하기가 힘들었을 텐데요." 내가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English accioun, accion, from Old French aucion, acciun, from Latin āctiō(n) (“act of doing or making”), from āctus + action suffix -iō...
definition_en: A thing done or undertaken to be done.

senses.gloss: The effort of performing or doing something.
Something done, often so as to accomplish a purpose.
A way of motion or functioning.
senses.example: Knead bread with a rocking action.

examples.text: Mr. McKee was asleep on a chair with his fists clenched in his lap, like a photograph of a man of action.
examples.translation_ko: 맥키 씨는 의자에서 잠들어 있었는데, 무릎 위에 주먹을 꽉 쥔 채로 있는 모습이 마치 행동하는 남자의 사진 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Because we do a good action?”
examples.translation_ko: "선행을 베푼다고 해서?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You know, I’m not sure that your husband is quite responsible for his actions.
examples.translation_ko: "있잖아요, 당신 남편이 자신의 행동에 대해 온전히 책임질 수 있는 상태인지 확신이 서지 않아요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English failen, borrowed from Anglo-Norman faillir, from Vulgar Latin *fallire, alteration of Latin fallere (“to deceive, dis...
definition_en: To be unsuccessful or make a mistake.

senses.gloss: To be unsuccessful.
senses.example: Throughout my life, I have always failed.

senses.gloss: Not to achieve a particular stated goal. (Usage note: The direct object of this word is usually an infinitive.)
senses.example: The truck failed to start.

senses.gloss: To neglect.
senses.example: The report fails to take into account all the mitigating factors.

examples.text: For a moment he looked at me as if he failed to understand.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 그는 이해하지 못하겠다는 듯 나를 바라보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She saw something awful in the very simplicity she failed to understand.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 자신이 이해하지 못하는 바로 그 단순함 속에서 끔찍한 무언가를 보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I think your courage failed.
examples.translation_ko: "당신의 용기가 꺾인 것 같습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I want her to know that I shall never fail her.”
examples.translation_ko: 내가 절대 그녀를 저버리지 않을 거라는 걸 알아주었으면 합니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English erly, erlich, earlich, from Old English ǣrlīċ (“early”, adjective), equivalent to ere + -ly.
definition_en: Happening or done before the expected time.

senses.gloss: At a time in advance of the usual or expected event.
senses.example: at eleven, we went for an early lunch; she began reading at an early age; his mother suffered an early death

senses.gloss: Arriving a time before expected; sooner than on time.
senses.example: You're early today! I don't usually see you before nine o'clock.

senses.gloss: After but close to the start of a period of time.
senses.example: The play "Two Gentlemen of Verona" is one of Shakespeare's early works.

examples.text: “I came here earlier, but you weren’t in.”
examples.translation_ko: "일찍 여기 왔었는데, 당신이 없더군요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You don’t think it’s too early?” said the Captain.
examples.translation_ko: "너무 이른 시간이라고 생각하지 않나?" 선장이 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English knokken, from Old English cnocian, ġecnocian, cnucian (“to knock, pound on, beat”), from Proto-West Germanic *knokōn, from Prot...
definition_en: To hit or strike something with a sudden force.

senses.gloss: An abrupt rapping sound, as from an impact of a hard object against wood.
senses.example: It came to me, like a knock on the door / Erasing all that had gone before / Broken wings can be mended / But this love of ours, we've got to defend it

senses.gloss: A sharp impact.
senses.example: He took a knock on the head.

senses.gloss: A criticism.

examples.text: She turned her head as there was a light dignified knocking at the front door.
examples.translation_ko: 현관문에서 가볍고 품위 있는 노크 소리가 나자 그녀가 고개를 돌렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I hardly know where I am when I hear about a thing like this and am completely knocked down and out.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 일에 대해 들으면 제가 어디에 있는지도 모르겠고 완전히 넘어져서 기진맥진해집니다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I knocked.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 문을 두드렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He knocked at a door, but again there was no answer.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 문을 두드렸지만 역시 대답이 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From obvious + -ly.
definition_en: Clearly apparent or evident.

senses.gloss: In an obvious or clearly apparent manner.
senses.example: She was in floods of tears and obviously very upset.

senses.gloss: Used as a filler word, or to introduce information even when not obvious.
senses.example: You weren't to know, but I've spoken to, obviously, Jim about this, and ...

examples.text: “Oh, yes,” said Tom, gruffly polite, but obviously not remembering.
examples.translation_ko: "아, 그래요." 톰이 퉁명스럽게 예의를 차리며 말했지만 분명히 기억하지 못하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The first part of this was obviously untrue, for someone had begun to whistle “The Rosary,” tunelessly, inside.
examples.translation_ko: 이 말의 앞부분은 명백히 거짓이었다. 안에서 누군가 "로사리오"를 음정도 맞지 않게 휘파람으로 불고 있었기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was obviously very ill.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 명백히 매우 아팠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I discovered that in Paris he had been painting just the same stale, obviously picturesque things that he had painted for years in Rome.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 파리에서도 로마에서 수년간 그려왔던 것과 똑같은 진부하고 뻔히 그림 같은 소재들을 그리고 있었다는 사실을 알게 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English corage, from Old French corage (French courage), from Vulgar Latin *corāticum, from Latin cor (“heart”). Distantly related to c...
definition_en: The quality of being brave and strong in the face of danger or adversity.

senses.gloss: The quality of being confident, not afraid or easily intimidated, but without being incautious or inconsiderate.
senses.example: It takes a lot of courage to be successful in business.

senses.gloss: The ability to overcome one's fear, do or live things which one finds frightening.
senses.example: He plucked up the courage to tell her how he felt.

senses.gloss: The ability to maintain one's will or intent despite either the experience of fear, frailty, or frustration; or the occurrence of adversity, difficulty, defeat or reversal. Moral fortitude.
senses.example: I hope you live a life you’re proud of. If you find that you’re not, I hope you have the courage to start all over again.

examples.text: Her frightened eyes told that whatever intentions, whatever courage she had had, were definitely gone.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 겁에 질린 눈은 어떤 의도든, 어떤 용기든 그녀가 가지고 있던 것들이 완전히 사라져버렸음을 말해주었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: However, that was my fault, for he was one of those who used to sneer most bitterly at Gatsby on the courage of Gatsby’s liquor, and I should have known better than to call him.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그건 내 잘못이었다. 그는 개츠비의 술에 힘입어 개츠비를 가장 신랄하게 비웃곤 했던 사람 중 하나였는데, 나는 그에게 전화를 걸지 말았어야 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I think your courage failed.
examples.translation_ko: "당신의 용기가 꺾인 것 같습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You have not the courage of your convictions.
examples.translation_ko: "당신은 자신의 신념을 관철할 용기가 없군요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From embarrass + -ment.
definition_en: A feeling of being ashamed or embarrassed.

senses.gloss: A state of discomfort arising from bashfulness or consciousness of having violated a social rule; humiliation.
A person or thing which is the cause of humiliation to another.
senses.example: Jack, you are an embarrassment to this family.

senses.gloss: A large collection of good or valuable things, especially one that exceeds requirements or causes some sort of hindrance.
senses.example: At one time, I reflected, we'd had an embarrassment of good, qualified squad leader—ready men in the platoon.

examples.text: “I was asleep,” cried Mr. Klipspringer, in a spasm of embarrassment.
examples.translation_ko: "잠들어 있었습니다," 클립스프링거 씨가 당황한 나머지 소리쳤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: After his embarrassment and his unreasoning joy he was consumed with wonder at her presence.
examples.translation_ko: 당황스러움과 이유 없는 기쁨 다음에, 그는 그녀의 존재에 대한 경이로움에 사로잡혔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Stroeve hesitated a moment with embarrassment.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브가 당황한 듯 잠시 머뭇거렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: My eyes, resting on him curiously, caused him no embarrassment.
examples.translation_ko: 호기심 어린 내 시선이 그에게 머물렀지만, 그는 전혀 당황하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French fourniture (“a supply, or the act of furnishing”), from fournir (“to furnish”).
definition_en: Items for furnishing a room or building.

senses.gloss: Large movable item(s), usually in a room, which enhance(s) the room's characteristics, functionally or decoratively.
senses.example: The woman does not even have one stick of furniture moved in yet.

senses.gloss: The harness, trappings etc. of a horse, hawk, or other animal.
senses.example: Horse furniture included a white sheepskin with red ‘wolf's teeth’; blue shabraque with yellow edging and royal cypher; blue valise with yellow edging.

senses.gloss: Fittings, such as handles, of a door, coffin, or other wooden item.

examples.text: She came in with such a proprietary haste, and looked around so possessively at the furniture that I wondered if she lived here.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 마치 주인이라도 되는 듯 성급하게 들어와서는 가구들을 소유자라도 되는 듯 둘러보았기에, 나는 그녀가 여기 사는 것은 아닌지 궁금했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The living-room was crowded to the doors with a set of tapestried furniture entirely too large for it, so that to move about was to stumble continually over scenes of ladies swinging in the gardens of Versailles.
examples.translation_ko: 거실은 문간까지 태피스트리 가구 세트로 빼곡했는데, 그 방에 비해 너무 큰 가구들이어서 돌아다니려면 베르사유 정원에서 그네 타는 귀부인들의 장면 위로 계속 발이 걸렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She let her flat and sold her furniture.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 아파트를 세놓고 가구를 팔았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “It’s lucky the furniture in the flat is in Amy’s name.
examples.translation_ko: "다행히 아파트 가구들은 에이미 명의로 되어 있어.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Feeling or showing sorrow.

senses.gloss: Feeling sorrow; sorrowful, mournful.
senses.example: She gets sad when he's away.

senses.gloss: Appearing sorrowful.
senses.example: The puppy had a sad little face.

senses.gloss: Causing sorrow; lamentable.
senses.example: It's a sad fact that most rapes go unreported.

examples.text: “It makes me sad because I’ve never seen such—such beautiful shirts before.”
examples.translation_ko: "이렇게—이렇게 아름다운 셔츠들을 본 적이 없어서 슬퍼요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He drew me into his office, remarking in a reverent voice that it was a sad time for all of us, and offered me a cigar.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 나를 사무실로 끌어들이며 우리 모두에게 슬픈 시절이라고 경건한 목소리로 말하고는 시가를 권했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Even here is something sad and terrible.
examples.translation_ko: 여기에도 슬프고 무서운 무언가가 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is sad that I can remember nothing of all this scintillation.
examples.translation_ko: 이 모든 번뜩이는 대화를 하나도 기억하지 못한다는 것이 안타깝다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French desconcerter, from des- (“dis-”) + concerter (“to bring into agreement, organize”).
definition_en: Cause someone to feel confused or embarrassed.

senses.gloss: To upset the composure of; to startle.
senses.example: The embrace disconcerted the daughter-in-law somewhat, as the caresses of old gentlemen unshorn and perfumed with tobacco might well do.

senses.gloss: To bring into confusion.
To frustrate, discomfit.
senses.example: The emperor disconcerted the plans of his enemy.

examples.text: And then came that disconcerting ride.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 그 당황스러운 드라이브가 시작되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was disconcerting and rather horrible.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 당황스럽고 다소 끔찍했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It disconcerted me, but I did my best not to show it.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 당황했지만, 그것을 드러내지 않으려고 최선을 다했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From earlier lunching, of uncertain origin.
Possibly related to lunch, q.v. It is unclear which came first. Possibly influenced by nuncheon (“light...
definition_en: A light meal eaten between breakfast and dinner.

senses.gloss: A formal meal served in the middle of the day.
senses.example: Most people thought the food at the luncheon was mediocre.

senses.gloss: A large, cheap, processed sausage served in thin slices.
senses.example: Ian bought the luncheon since it was on special.

senses.gloss: Any midday meal; lunch.
senses.example: Have you had luncheon?

examples.text: “I got dressed before luncheon,” said the child, turning eagerly to Daisy.
examples.translation_ko: "점심 먹기 전에 옷을 입었어요." 아이가 데이지를 향해 열심히 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Of course, I immediately suggested a luncheon in New York—and I thought he’d go mad:
examples.translation_ko: 물론 나는 즉시 뉴욕에서 점심을 함께 하자고 제안했는데—그러자 그가 미쳐버릴 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “She gives luncheon-parties.
examples.translation_ko: "그분은 오찬 파티를 여세요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: After all, it pleases her to ask us to luncheon, and it doesn’t hurt us.
examples.translation_ko: 어쨌든 우리를 점심에 초대하는 게 그분 기쁨이고, 우리에게도 나쁠 것 없잖아요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fode, foode, from Old English fōda (“food”), from Proto-West Germanic *fōdō, from Proto-Germanic *fōdô (“food”), from Proto-Ind...
definition_en: A substance that people or animals eat to sustain life.

senses.gloss: Any solid substance that can be consumed by living organisms, especially by eating, in order to sustain life.

etymology:
From late Middle English absolutly, equivalent to absolute + -ly.
First attested in 1425.
definition_en: Used to emphasize the truth of something.

senses.gloss: In an absolute or unconditional manner; utterly, positively, wholly.
Independently; viewed without relation to other things or factors.
As an intensive: extremely, very, indeed.
senses.example: The most absolutely terrifying creature lifted her head.

examples.text: “Absolutely, old sport.”
examples.translation_ko: "물론이죠, 형씨."

examples.text: “I’m absolutely in training.”
examples.translation_ko: "저는 지금 완전히 훈련 중이거든요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Absolutely unchanged.”
examples.translation_ko: "전혀 변하지 않았어요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Is it absolutely final?”
examples.translation_ko: "완전히 끝난 건가?"

etymology: Adjective and noun from Middle English drye, dryge, drüȝe, from Old English drȳġe (“dry; parched, withered”), from Proto-West Germanic *drūgī, *dra...
definition_en: To become or make something free from moisture.

senses.gloss: Free from or lacking moisture.
senses.example: This towel's dry. Could you wet it and cover the chicken so it doesn't go dry as it cooks?

senses.gloss: Unable to produce a liquid, as water, (petrochemistry) oil, or (agriculture) milk.
senses.example: This well is as dry as that cow.

senses.gloss: Built without or lacking mortar.
senses.example: [A]lready the gate was blocked with a wall of squared stones laid dry, but very thick and very high, across the opening.

examples.text: “Not that day I carried you down from the Punch Bowl to keep your shoes dry?”

examples.text: I found the humidor on an unfamiliar table, with two stale, dry cigarettes inside.
examples.translation_ko: 낯선 탁자 위에서 시가 상자를 찾았는데, 안에는 바싹 마른 담배 두 개비가 들어 있었다.

examples.text: She had dried her eyes and powdered her nose.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 눈물을 닦고 코에 분을 발랐다.

examples.text: Presently she released herself and dried her eyes.

definition_en: A view or judgment formed about something.

senses.gloss: A belief, judgment or perspective that a person has formed, either through objective or subjective reasoning, about a topic, issue, person or thing.
senses.example: I would like to know your opinions on the new filing system.

senses.gloss: The judgment or sentiment which the mind forms of persons or things; estimation.
senses.example: Friendship […] gives a man a peculiar right and claim to the good opinion of his friend.

senses.gloss: Favorable estimation; hence, consideration; reputation; fame; public sentiment or esteem.
senses.example: This gain’d Agricola much opinion; who […] had made ſuch early progreſs into laborious […] enterpriſes.

examples.text: “Look here, old sport,” he broke out surprisingly, “what’s your opinion of me, anyhow?”
examples.translation_ko: "이봐, 형씨," 그가 갑자기 터뜨렸다, "도대체 나에 대해 어떻게 생각하나?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Now, don’t think my opinion on these matters is final,” he seemed to say, “just because I’m stronger and more of a man than you are.”
examples.translation_ko: "자, 이런 문제들에 대한 내 의견이 최종적이라고 생각하지는 마라"고 그가 말하는 것 같았다. "단지 내가 자네보다 더 강하고 더 남자답다고 해서 말이야."

examples.text: He was independent of the opinion of his fellows.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 동료들의 의견에 좌우되지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I am disappointed that I cannot report any extravagances in his opinions on the old masters.
examples.translation_ko: 거장들에 대한 그의 견해에서 별다른 기행을 보고할 수 없다는 것이 실망스럽다.

etymology: From Middle English schadowe, schadewe, schadwe (also schade > shade), from Old English sċeaduwe, sċeadwe, oblique form of sċeadu (“shadow, shade; ...
definition_en: A dark shape or area that is created by something blocking the light.

senses.gloss: A dark image projected onto a surface where light (or other radiation) is blocked by the shade of an object.
senses.example: My shadow lengthened as the sun began to set.

senses.gloss: Relative darkness, especially as caused by the interruption of light; gloom; obscurity.
senses.example: I immediately jumped into shadow as I saw them approach.

senses.gloss: An area protected by an obstacle (likened to an object blocking out sunlight).
senses.example: The mountains block the passage of rain-producing weather systems and cast a "shadow" of dryness behind them.

examples.text: The room, shadowed well with awnings, was dark and cool.
examples.translation_ko: 차양으로 잘 가려진 방은 어둡고 시원했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The shadow of a tree fell abruptly across the dew and ghostly birds began to sing among the blue leaves.
examples.translation_ko: 나무 그림자가 이슬 위로 갑자기 떨어지고 유령 같은 새들이 푸른 잎사귀 사이에서 노래하기 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It throws a shadow of insincerity over their most deeply felt emotions.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 그들의 가장 진실한 감정에까지 위선의 그림자를 드리운다.

senses.gloss: An eating establishment in which diners are served food, usually by waiters at their tables but sometimes (as in a fast food restaurant) at a counter.
senses.example: That Italian restaurant serves some of the best food I've ever had in my life.

definition_en: To make a strong request for something.

senses.gloss: An application to a superior court or judge for a decision or order by an inferior court or judge to be reviewed and overturned.

A person's legal right to apply to court for such a review.

etymology: From Middle English steire, staire, stayre, stayer, steir, steyre, steyer, from Old English stǣġer (“stair, staircase”), from Proto-West Germanic *...
definition_en: A set of steps leading from one floor to another.

definition_en: To regard with contempt or disdain.

senses.gloss: To regard with contempt or scorn.

senses.gloss: To disregard or ignore.

examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그는 자신을 경멸하지 않았고, 일이 그가 상상했던 대로 흘러가지도 않았다.

definition_en: Considered to be cursed or doomed.

senses.gloss: Godforsaken.

senses.gloss: Variant of profane damn, used to express contempt, exasperation, etc. towards someone or something.
senses.example: Their damned lawyers can go to hell.

senses.gloss: Ellipsis of I'll be damned.
senses.example: Damned if I know.

examples.text: But all the rest of that’s a God damned lie.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그 밖의 모든 건 새빨간 거짓말이야.

definition_en: Feeling or showing a strong and unreasonable anger.

senses.gloss: Angry, annoyed.
senses.example: Are you mad at me?

senses.gloss: Used litotically to indicate satisfaction or approval.
senses.example: Wow, you really made this pie from scratch? I'm not mad at it.

examples.translation_ko: "분명 미쳤던 거예요."

examples.text: Such a mad act as that man did should make us all think.

definition_en: A type of beverage made from roasted coffee beans.

senses.gloss: A beverage made by infusing the beans of the coffee plant in hot water.
senses.example: The great use of coffee in France is supposed to have abated the prevalency of the gravel, for where coffee is used as a constant beverage, the gravel and the gout are scarcely known.

senses.gloss: A serving of this beverage.
senses.example: As I sip a coffee at Brasserie Balzar, two well-known intellectuals, one publisher and a Sorbonne professor were discussing Sarkozy's future: "He won't finish his mandate" says one.

senses.gloss: The seeds of the plant used to make coffee, called ‘beans’ due to their shape.

examples.translation_ko: "커피라도 드시겠어요?"

examples.text: “I think we might have our coffee here, don’t you?”

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then we went to a tavern to have coffee and liqueurs.

senses.gloss: To say suddenly and with strong emotion.
senses.example: You never pump your arm when you score, you never exclaim anything, you don’t even smile when you fire a perfect backhand straight down the line.

senses.gloss: The portion of the lower limb of a human that extends from the knee to the ankle.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Wild rumours were circulating about her—how her mother had found her packing her bag one winter night to go to New York and say goodbye to a soldier who was going overseas.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀에 대한 황당한 소문들이 돌고 있었다—어느 겨울밤 어머니가 그녀를 발견했는데, 해외로 떠나는 한 군인에게 작별 인사를 하러 뉴욕에 가려고 가방을 싸고 있었다는 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She had all the graces of the soldier’s wife.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 군인의 아내가 갖춰야 할 모든 품격을 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I remembered my anticipation long ago that she would marry a soldier.
examples.translation_ko: 오래전 그녀가 군인과 결혼할 것이라고 내가 예상했던 것이 떠올랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A particular occurrence or situation.

senses.gloss: An occurrence; something that happens.

senses.gloss: A prearranged social activity (function, etc.)
senses.example: I went to an event in San Francisco last week.

senses.gloss: One of several contests that combine to make up a competition.

examples.text: On the contrary, they were merely casual events in a crowded summer, and, until much later, they absorbed me infinitely less than my personal affairs.
examples.translation_ko: 오히려 그것들은 분주한 여름 속의 우연한 사건들에 불과했고, 훨씬 나중까지도 내 개인적인 일들보다 훨씬 덜 나를 사로잡았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Reading over what I have written so far, I see I have given the impression that the events of three nights several weeks apart were all that absorbed me.
examples.translation_ko: 지금까지 써온 것을 다시 읽어보니, 몇 주 간격으로 벌어진 세 밤의 사건들이 나를 완전히 사로잡았다는 인상을 주었다는 것을 알겠다.

examples.text: She’ll have that at all events.”

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was a little puzzled, but at all events I understood that I might now take my leave.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 약간 당황했지만, 어쨌든 이제 작별 인사를 해도 된다는 것을 알았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English singuler, from Old French, from Latin singulāris (“alone of its kind”), from Latin singulus (“single”).
definition_en: Being the only one of its kind.

senses.gloss: Being only one of a larger population; single, individual.
senses.example: A singular experiment cannot be regarded as scientific proof of the existence of a phenomenon.

senses.gloss: Being the only one of the kind; unique.
senses.example: She has a singular personality.

senses.gloss: Distinguished by superiority: peerless, unmatched, eminent, exceptional, extraordinary.
senses.example: a man of singular gravity or attainments

examples.text: He told me a singular story.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 나에게 기이한 이야기를 들려주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Their life in its own way was an idyl, and it managed to achieve a singular beauty.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 생활은 나름대로 목가적이었고, 독특한 아름다움을 이루어냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A secret or obscure fact or situation.

senses.gloss: Something secret or unexplainable; an unknown.
senses.example: The truth behind the events remains a mystery.

senses.gloss: Someone or something with an obscure or puzzling nature.
senses.example: That man is a mystery.

senses.gloss: An account, story, book, film, or play, often with the theme of crime or murder, with a surprise ending that explains all the strange events that have occurred.

examples.text: “I don’t like mysteries,” I answered, “and I don’t understand why you won’t come out frankly and tell me what you want.
examples.translation_ko: "나는 수수께끼 같은 일을 좋아하지 않습니다." 내가 대답했다. "그리고 왜 당신이 솔직하게 나와서 원하는 바를 말하지 않는지 이해할 수 없어요.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The city seen from the Queensboro Bridge is always the city seen for the first time, in its first wild promise of all the mystery and the beauty in the world.
examples.translation_ko: 퀸즈보로 다리에서 바라본 도시는 언제나 처음 보는 도시였고, 세상의 모든 신비와 아름다움을 약속하는 첫 번째 거친 약속이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her reserve was not without mystery.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 과묵함에는 신비로운 구석이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Ten miles away the island of Murea, like some high fastness of the Holy Grail, guarded its mystery.
examples.translation_ko: 십 마일 떨어진 무레아 섬이 성배의 높은 요새처럼 그 신비를 지키고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To stop or avoid something from happening.

senses.example: I brush my teeth regularly to prevent tooth decay.

senses.gloss: To take preventative measures.
senses.example: I think you must be mad, and she shall not have a glimpse of it while I'm here to prevent!

examples.text: He had seen me several times, and had intended to call on me long before, but a peculiar combination of circumstances had prevented it—signed Jay Gatsby, in a majestic hand.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I had to bite my lip to prevent myself from laughing.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 웃음을 참기 위해 입술을 깨물어야 했다.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: The portion of the past that is known and recorded by this field of study, as opposed to all earlier and unknown times that preceded it (prehistory).

definition_en: Permit or approve something

senses.gloss: To let one have as a suitable share of something.

senses.gloss: To not bar or obstruct.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: A race condition; a bug or problem that occurs when two or more components attempt to use the same resource at the same time.
senses.example: As the name implies, a race condition means that two processes are competing within the same time interval, and the race affects the integrity or correctness of the computing tasks.

examples.text: “I can’t seem to remember, but I think we talked about the Nordic race.

definition_en: Having a quality of being difficult to understand or explain.

senses.gloss: Of unknown origin.

senses.gloss: Having unknown qualities.
senses.example: Our boss is a mysterious man who hardly ever meets with us.

senses.gloss: Difficult to understand.

senses.gloss: A record of a thing or an event stored and available for later use by the organism.

senses.gloss: The part of a computer that stores variable executable code or data (RAM) or unalterable executable code or default data (ROM).

examples.text: “My memory goes back to when first I met him,” he said.

examples.text: I thought if I held my tongue and pretended not to see, everything would come right.

etymology: From Middle English quietely, quyetly, equivalent to quiet + -ly.
definition_en: In a quiet manner.

senses.gloss: In a quiet manner.

examples.text: I even had a short affair with a girl who lived in Jersey City and worked in the accounting department, but her brother began throwing mean looks in my direction, so when she went on her vacation in July I let it blow quietly away.
examples.translation_ko: 저지 시티에 살면서 회계부에서 일하는 한 여자와 짧은 연애를 하기도 했지만, 그녀의 오빠가 나를 못마땅하게 쳐다보기 시작해서, 그녀가 7월에 휴가를 떠났을 때 조용히 끝나도록 내버려두었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She lies on her back quite quietly.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 등을 대고 조용히 누워 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I stood quite quietly, looking at him.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 조용히 서서 그를 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To be indebted or responsible for something.

senses.gloss: To be under an obligation to give something back to someone or to perform some action for someone.
senses.example: We owe it to our children to make our nation a better place to live in the future.

senses.gloss: To have debt; to be in debt.
To have as a cause; used with to.
senses.example: The record owes its success to the outstanding guitar solos.

examples.text: “What do I owe you?”
examples.translation_ko: "얼마를 드리면 됩니까?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “What do I owe you?” demanded Tom harshly.
examples.translation_ko: "얼마를 드리면 됩니까?" 톰이 거칠게 물었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “To what do I owe this honour?”
examples.translation_ko: "무슨 영광스러운 일로 오셨습니까?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You owe me a dinner, you know.”
examples.translation_ko: 자네가 나한테 저녁 한 끼 빚진 거 알지."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From polite + -ly.
definition_en: Used to show respect or courtesy.

senses.gloss: in a polite manner
senses.example: If pressed about a serious accusation like rape, you can politely reply that you can’t answer questions pertaining to such an allegation without legal representation and wish to remain silent.

examples.text: “What?” I inquired politely.
examples.translation_ko: "뭘 하셨는데요?" 나는 정중히 물었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Go on,” Gatsby said politely.
examples.translation_ko: "계속하세요." 개츠비가 정중하게 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When he shook hands with Capitaine Brunot he enquired politely after Madame et les enfants.
examples.translation_ko: 브뤼노 선장과 악수할 때는 정중하게 마담과 아이들 안부를 물었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In a little while she went out, but in a minute returned and, passing our table, very politely asked us to buy her something to drink.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 후 그녀가 나갔다가 곧 돌아와서 우리 테이블을 지나가며 아주 정중하게 술 한 잔 사달라고 부탁했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English honest, honeste (“honourable, appropriate, excellent”), from Old French honeste, from Latin honestus, from honor. For the verb,...
definition_en: Being truthful and sincere.

senses.gloss: Scrupulous with regard to telling the truth; not given to swindling, lying, or fraud; upright.
senses.example: brutally honest

senses.gloss: True, especially as far as is known by the person making the statement; fair; unbiased.
senses.example: an honest account of events

senses.gloss: In good faith; without malice.
senses.example: an honest mistake

examples.text: I thought you were rather an honest, straightforward person.
examples.translation_ko: 전 당신이 꽤 정직하고 솔직한 사람이라고 생각했어요.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Everyone suspects himself of at least one of the cardinal virtues, and this is mine: I am one of the few honest people that I have ever known.
examples.translation_ko: 누구나 자신에게 적어도 하나의 추기경 덕목이 있다고 생각하는데, 내 것은 이것이다. 나는 내가 아는 몇 안 되는 정직한 사람 중 하나다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Sooner or later he would marry some honest soul in Holland, and I felt sure he would be happy.
examples.translation_ko: 조만간 그는 네덜란드의 어떤 선량한 여인과 결혼할 것이고, 분명 행복할 거라고 확신했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was all false, insincere, shoddy; and yet no one was more honest, sincere, and frank than Dirk Stroeve.
examples.translation_ko: 모든 것이 거짓되고 부성실하고 조잡했다. 그런데도 더크 스트루브보다 더 정직하고 성실하고 솔직한 사람은 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English significaunce, from Middle French significance, from Old French significance, from Latin significantia. Doublet of si...
definition_en: The quality of being significant or important.

senses.gloss: The extent to which something matters; importance
senses.example: As a juror your opinion is of great significance for the outcome of the trial.

senses.gloss: Meaning.
senses.example: the significance of a gesture

examples.text: Possibly it had occurred to him that the colossal significance of that light had now vanished forever.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 그 불빛이 지녔던 엄청난 의미가 이제 영원히 사라져버렸다는 생각이 그에게 떠올랐을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Michaelis had seen this too, but it hadn’t occurred to him that there was any special significance in it.
examples.translation_ko: 미카엘리스도 그것을 보았지만, 거기에 특별한 의미가 있다고는 생각하지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They had a significance which was all their own.
examples.translation_ko: 그 색채들만의 고유한 의미가 있었어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They seemed to me ugly, but they suggested without disclosing a secret of momentous significance.
examples.translation_ko: 그림들은 내게 추하게 보였지만, 중대한 의미를 지닌 비밀을 드러내지 않은 채 암시하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English synken, from Old English sincan, from Proto-West Germanic *sinkwan, from Proto-Germanic *sinkwaną, from Proto-Indo-European *se...
definition_en: To go down or fall below the surface of a liquid.

senses.gloss: To descend or submerge (or to cause to do so) into a liquid or similar substance.
senses.example: A stone sinks in water.  The sun gradually sank in the west.

senses.gloss: To (directly or indirectly) cause a vessel to sink, generally by making it no longer watertight.
senses.example: An iceberg sank the Titanic.  British battleships sank the Bismarck.

senses.gloss: To push (something) into something.
senses.example: The joint will hold tighter if you sink a wood screw through both boards.  The dog sank its teeth into the delivery man's leg.

examples.text: The murmur trembled on the verge of coherence, sank down, mounted excitedly, and then ceased altogether.
examples.translation_ko: 그 중얼거림은 무슨 말인지 알아들을 듯 말 듯 떨리다가 가라앉았다가 다시 흥분되게 높아지더니 완전히 멈췄다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A humorous suggestion was made that she sing the notes on her face, whereupon she threw up her hands, sank into a chair, and went off into a deep vinous sleep.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀 얼굴의 음표들을 노래해보라는 우스운 제안이 나오자, 그녀는 두 손을 번쩍 들어올리고는 의자에 주저앉아 깊은 술잠에 빠져들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She sank into a chair, and buried her face in her hands.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 의자에 주저앉아 두 손으로 얼굴을 묻었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Finally I gave him a draught, and he sank into uneasy slumber.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 나는 그에게 수면제를 주었고, 그는 불안한 잠에 빠져들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English excitement, from Old French excitement, equivalent to excite + -ment.
definition_en: A strong feeling of enthusiasm and eagerness.

senses.gloss: The state of being excited (emotionally aroused).
senses.example: to get caught up in the excitement

senses.gloss: Something that excites.

examples.text: Gatsby sprang to his feet, vivid with excitement.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 흥분으로 얼굴을 붉히며 벌떡 일어났다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was the hour of a profound human change, and excitement was generating on the air.
examples.translation_ko: 인간의 깊은 변화가 일어나는 시간이었고, 공기 중에는 흥분이 생겨나고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His flushed face was shining with excitement.
examples.translation_ko: 흥분으로 달아오른 그의 얼굴이 번들거렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is hazardous to play poker with them, but their ingenuity adds a peculiar excitement to the best game in the world.
examples.translation_ko: 그들과 포커를 치는 것은 위험하지만, 그들의 기발함은 세상에서 가장 훌륭한 게임에 독특한 흥미를 더해준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Partially a back-formation from preparation; and partially borrowed from Middle French preparer, from Classical Latin praeparāre (“make ready in ad...
definition_en: Make or become ready for something.

senses.gloss: To make ready for a specific future purpose; to set up; to assemble or equip; to forearm.
senses.example: We prepared the spacecraft for takeoff.

senses.gloss: To make ready for eating or drinking; to cook.
senses.example: We prepared a fish for dinner.

senses.gloss: To make oneself ready; to get ready, make preparation.
senses.example: We prepared for a bumpy ride.

examples.text: But you are prepared for the greatness of Michael Angelo.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 미켈란젤로의 위대함에는 마음의 준비가 되어 있는 법이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I did not know how he would take the remark I had prepared.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 준비해온 말을 그가 어떻게 받아들일지 알 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lawe, laȝe, from Old English lagu (“law”), borrowed from Old Norse lǫg (“law”, literally “things laid down or firmly establishe...
definition_en: A rule or principle made by a government or other authority.

senses.gloss: The body of such rules that pertain to a particular topic.
senses.example: property law

senses.gloss: Common law, as contrasted with equity.
The body of binding rules and regulations, customs, and standards established in a community by its legislative and judicial authorities.
senses.example: The courts interpret the law but should not make it.

examples.text: “Walter could have you up on the betting laws too, but Wolfshiem scared him into shutting his mouth.”
examples.translation_ko: "월터는 도박법으로도 자네를 고발할 수 있었지만, 울프샤임이 겁을 줘서 입을 다물게 했어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Can the law get blood out of a stone?
examples.translation_ko: "법이 돌에서 피를 짜낼 수 있겠는가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You remember my brother-in-law, don’t you?
examples.translation_ko: "제 처남 기억하시죠?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English startlen, stertlen, stertyllen (“to rush, stumble along”), from Old English steartlian (“to kick with the foot, struggle, stumb...
definition_en: Sudden shock or surprise

senses.gloss: To move suddenly, or be excited, on feeling alarm; to start.
senses.example: a horse that startles easily

senses.gloss: To excite by sudden alarm, surprise, or apprehension; to frighten suddenly and not seriously; to alarm; to surprise.
senses.example: The high voice in the night air startled me. Without thinking, I started to run. Then stopped. I spun around, my heart heaving against my chest. And saw a boy. About my age.

senses.gloss: To deter; to cause to deviate.
senses.example: As they turned into Hertford Street they startled a robin from the poet's head on a barren fountain, and he fled away with a cameo note.

examples.text: she asked, startled.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 깜짝 놀라며 물었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Your wife does,” exclaimed Tom, startled.
examples.translation_ko: "당신 아내가?" 톰이 놀라서 소리쳤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was startled.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 깜짝 놀랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She was startled.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 깜짝 놀랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From real + -ise, possibly from French réaliser and Middle French réaliser (“to make real; to convert (something) into assets or cash”). See realize.
definition_en: Understand or become aware of something.

senses.gloss: Non-Oxford British standard spelling of realize.
senses.example: Do you reckon Hissing Sid realises what a shagnasty that Mary is?

examples.text: I realised in myself the same desire as animated him.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그를 움직인 것과 같은 욕망이 내 안에도 있음을 깨달았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She realised that the old life was gone and done with.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 예전 생활이 끝나고 말았다는 것을 깨달았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lenen (“to lean”), from Old English hleonian, hlinian (“to lean, recline, lie down, rest”), from Proto-West Germanic *hlinēn, f...
definition_en: Having a small or moderate amount of body fat.

senses.gloss: To incline, deviate, or bend, from a vertical position; to be in a position thus inclining or deviating.
senses.example: a leaning column

senses.gloss: To incline in opinion or desire; to conform in conduct; often with to, toward, etc.
senses.example: I’m leaning towards voting Conservative in the next election.

senses.gloss: To rest or rely, for support, comfort, to use as a hard surface for writing, etc.
senses.example: The slightest effort made the patient cough. He would stand leaning on a stick and holding a hand to his side, and when the paroxysm had passed it left him shaking.

examples.text: She came back into the studio and leaned against the table.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 작업실로 다시 들어와 탁자에 기대어 섰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Slackening his pace for a moment, he leaned over and spoke.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 속도를 늦춘 그가 몸을 기울이며 말을 걸었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English querele (“altercation, dispute; argument, debate; armed combat; trial by combat; basis for dispute, complaint; claim, legal sui...
definition_en: A quarrel is a noisy argument or disagreement between people.

senses.gloss: A dispute or heated argument (especially one that is verbal).
senses.example: We got into a silly quarrel about what food to order.

senses.gloss: Often preceded by a form of to have: a basis or ground of dispute or objection; a complaint; also, a feeling or situation of ill will and unhappiness caused by this.
senses.example: A few customers in the shop had some quarrels with us, so we called for the manager.

senses.gloss: A propensity to quarrel; quarrelsomeness.
senses.example: If I can faſten but one cup vpon him, / With that which he hath drunke to night already, / Hee'll be as full of quarrell and offence, / As my young miſtris dog:— [...]

examples.text: How stupid of me to quarrel with him.
examples.translation_ko: 그와 다툰 제가 정말 바보였어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Had they quarrelled already, or was his infatuation passed?
examples.translation_ko: 벌써 다툰 것일까, 아니면 그의 열정이 식어버린 것일까?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English angry; see anger.
definition_en: Feeling or showing strong displeasure.

senses.gloss: Displaying or feeling anger.
senses.example: His face became angry.

senses.gloss: Inflamed and painful.
senses.example: The broken glass left two angry cuts across my arm.

senses.gloss: Dark and stormy, menacing.
senses.example: Angry clouds raced across the sky.

examples.text: Angry, and half in love with her, and tremendously sorry, I turned away.
examples.translation_ko: 화가 나고, 그녀를 반쯤 사랑하고, 몹시 미안한 마음으로 나는 돌아섰다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Angry as I was, as we all were, I was tempted to laugh whenever he opened his mouth.
examples.translation_ko: 화가 났지만, 우리 모두가 화가 났지만, 그가 입을 열 때마다 나는 웃음이 터질 뻔했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was not angry with her.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀에게 화를 내지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Strickland, breathing laboriously, kept an angry silence.
examples.translation_ko: 거칠게 숨을 몰아쉬던 스트릭랜드는 화가 난 채로 침묵을 지켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A feeling of sadness or disappointment about something that has happened.

senses.gloss: To feel sorry about (a thing that has or has not happened), afterthink: to wish that a thing had not happened, that something else had happened instead.
senses.example: He regretted his words.

senses.gloss: To feel sorry about (any thing).
senses.example: I regret that I have to do this, but I don't have a choice.

senses.gloss: To miss; to feel the loss or absence of; to mourn.
senses.example: He more than ever regretted his home, and with increased desire longed to see his family.

examples.text: For a moment the last sunshine fell with romantic affection upon her glowing face; her voice compelled me forward breathlessly as I listened—then the glow faded, each light deserting her with lingering regret, like children leaving a pleasant street at dusk.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 동안 마지막 햇살이 낭만적인 애정으로 그녀의 빛나는 얼굴에 내려앉았다. 그녀의 목소리는 내가 숨을 죽이고 듣는 동안 나를 앞으로 이끌었다—그러다 그 빛이 사라지고, 모든 광채가 아쉬운 듯 그녀를 떠났다. 마치 황혼녘 즐거운 거리를 떠나는 아이들처럼.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Have you never regretted it?”
examples.translation_ko: "후회한 적은 없나?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “‘And do you never regret Europe?
examples.translation_ko: "'그럼 유럽이 그립지 않나?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English aprochen, borrowed from Old French aprochier (modern French approcher), from Late Latin appropiāre, a verb based on Latin prope...
definition_en: To come near or draw closer to something.

senses.gloss: To come or go near, in place or time; to move toward; to advance nearer; to draw nigh.
senses.example: It beckoned Scrooge to approach, which he did. When they were within two paces of each other, Marley's Ghost held up its hand, warning him to come no nearer. Scrooge stopped.

senses.gloss: To play an approach shot.
Used intransitively, followed by to: to draw near (to someone or something); to make advances; to approximate or become almost equal.
senses.example: He approaches to the character of the ablest statesman.

examples.text: The thing approached the proportions of a scandal—then died away.
examples.translation_ko: 그 일은 스캔들에 가까운 규모로 번져갔다가 사그라들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was saying some last word to her, but the eagerness in his manner tightened abruptly into formality as several people approached him to say goodbye.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀에게 마지막 말을 건네고 있었지만, 몇몇 사람들이 작별 인사를 하러 다가오자 그의 태도에서 드러나던 간절함이 갑자기 격식을 차린 모습으로 굳어졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: he said, as we approached the end of our silent meal.
examples.translation_ko: 조용한 식사가 거의 끝나갈 무렵 그가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They are easy of approach and affable in conversation.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 접근하기 쉽고 대화에서 상냥하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From constant + -ly. Displaced native Old English singallīċe.
definition_en: Happening or done repeatedly.

senses.gloss: With steadfastness; with resolve; in loyalty, faithfully.
In a constant manner; occurring continuously; persistently.
Recurring regularly.

examples.translation_ko: 그렇다면 그가 그 6월 밤에 열망했던 것은 단순히 별들만이 아니었던 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: You seem to walk with your head among the stars.
examples.translation_ko: 마치 별들 사이로 머리를 들고 걷는 것 같을 거야.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Above was the blue sky, and the stars, and all about the desert of the Pacific Ocean.
examples.translation_ko: 위로는 푸른 하늘과 별들이 있었고, 사방으로는 태평양의 광막한 바다가 펼쳐져 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fixen, borrowed from Old French *fixer (attested only as ficher, fichier; > English fitch), from fix (“fastened; fixed”), from ...
definition_en: To repair or mend something.

senses.gloss: To pierce; now generally replaced by transfix.
(Of a piercing look) to direct at someone.
senses.example: He fixed me with a sickly grin, and said, "I told you it wouldn't work!"

senses.gloss: To focus or determine (oneself, on a concept); to fixate.
senses.example: She's fixed on the idea of becoming a doctor.

examples.text: “Fixed the World’s Series?”
examples.translation_ko: "월드시리즈를 조작했다고?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Daisy went to the mirror and stood with her back to us, fixing her hair.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지는 거울 앞으로 가서 우리에게 등을 돌리고 서서 머리를 만지작거렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His eyes were fixed on the ground.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 시선은 바닥에 고정되어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He kept his eyes fixed on mine till I had finished, and then he turned away.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내가 말을 마칠 때까지 내 눈을 고정시켜 바라보다가, 그제야 시선을 돌렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English huge, from Old French ahuge (“high, lofty, great, large, huge”), from a hoge (“at height”), from a (“at, to”) + hoge (“a hill, ...
definition_en: Extremely large or impressive.

senses.gloss: Very large.
Very strong, powerful, or dedicated.
senses.example: Both of my parents are huge supporters of animal rights.

senses.gloss: Very interesting, significant, or popular.
senses.example: The band's next album is going to be huge.

examples.text: “That huge place there?”
examples.translation_ko: "저 거대한 집 말이야?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: On the last night, with my trunk packed and my car sold to the grocer, I went over and looked at that huge incoherent failure of a house once more.
examples.translation_ko: 마지막 밤, 트렁크를 싸고 차를 식료품점 주인에게 판 후, 나는 그 거대하고 지리멸렬한 실패작 같은 집을 다시 한 번 보러 갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He took my hand in both of his—they were huge—and gave me a hearty look, in which, however, was great shrewdness.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 거대한 두 손으로 내 손을 감싸 쥐고는 진심 어린 눈빛으로 나를 바라보았는데, 그 시선에는 예리한 통찰력이 깃들어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In a little while Tough Bill, accompanied by two huge negroes, came in, and it was easy to see that he was already three parts drunk.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 후 터프 빌이 두 명의 거대한 흑인을 데리고 들어왔는데, 이미 거의 만취 상태라는 것을 쉽게 알 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From bed + room.
definition_en: A room for sleeping.

senses.gloss: A room in a house, apartment, hotel, or other dwelling where a bed is kept for sleeping.
senses.example: Please don't enter my bedroom without knocking.

senses.gloss: The location of sexual activity.
senses.example: "How are things in the bedroom?" asked the marriage therapist.

examples.text: The apartment was on the top floor—a small living-room, a small dining-room, a small bedroom, and a bath.
examples.translation_ko: 아파트는 최상층에 있었다—작은 거실, 작은 식당, 작은 침실, 그리고 욕실이 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His bedroom was the simplest room of all—except where the dresser was garnished with a toilet set of pure dull gold.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 침실은 모든 방 중에서 가장 소박했다. 다만 화장대가 순금으로 된 화장 도구 세트로 장식되어 있는 것만 빼고는.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They had but the studio, a bedroom, and a tiny kitchen.
examples.translation_ko: 그들에게는 화실과 침실, 그리고 작은 부엌뿐이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He went back into the bedroom and threw himself on the bed.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 침실로 돌아가 침대에 몸을 던졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English profound, from Anglo-Norman profound, from Old French profont, from Latin profundus, from pro + fundus (“bottom; foundation”).
definition_en: Having or showing a deep understanding of something.

senses.gloss: Descending far below the surface; opening or reaching to great depth; deep.
senses.example: A gulf profound as that Serbonian bog

senses.gloss: Very deep; very serious
Intellectually deep; entering far into subjects; reaching to the bottom of a matter, or of a branch of learning; thorough
senses.example: a profound investigation

examples.text: It was the hour of a profound human change, and excitement was generating on the air.
examples.translation_ko: 인간의 깊은 변화가 일어나는 시간이었고, 공기 중에는 흥분이 생겨나고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Tom’s getting very profound,” said Daisy, with an expression of unthoughtful sadness.
examples.translation_ko: "톰이 아주 심오해지고 있네요." 데이지가 생각 없는 슬픔의 표정을 지으며 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I could only feel for him a profound compassion.”
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 깊은 연민만을 느낄 수 있었다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It created profound astonishment, and wild rumours were current.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 깊은 충격을 불러일으켰고, 온갖 터무니없는 소문들이 돌았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English kne, from Old English cnēow, from Proto-West Germanic *kneu, from Proto-Germanic *knewą, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵnéw-o-m, a ...
definition_en: The joint between the lower leg and thigh.

senses.gloss: In humans, the joint or the region of the joint in the middle part of the leg between the thigh and the shank.
senses.example: Penny was wearing a miniskirt, so she skinned her exposed knees when she fell.

senses.gloss: In the horse and allied animals, the carpal joint, corresponding to the wrist in humans.
The tarsal joint, uniting the tarsometatarsus and the tibiotarsus (homologous to the human ankle).

examples.text: Her body asserted itself with a restless movement of her knee, and she stood up.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 몸이 무릎을 가만히 두지 못하는 움직임으로 자신을 드러내더니, 일어섰다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Wilson’s eyes fell upon Tom; he started up on his tiptoes and then would have collapsed to his knees had not Tom held him upright.
examples.translation_ko: 윌슨의 시선이 톰에게 떨어졌다. 그는 발끝으로 일어서려 했지만 톰이 붙잡지 않았다면 무릎을 꿇고 주저앉았을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It is worn round the waist and hangs to the knees.
examples.translation_ko: 허리에 둘러 입고 무릎까지 늘어뜨린다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: A sudden pang seized him, and his knees felt so weak that he almost fell.
examples.translation_ko: 갑작스러운 고통이 그를 엄습했고, 무릎에 힘이 빠져 거의 쓰러질 뻔했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English wasshen, waschen, weschen, from Old English wascan, from Proto-West Germanic *waskan, from Proto-Germanic *waskaną, *watskaną (...
definition_en: To clean something with water.

senses.gloss: To clean with water.
senses.example: The car is so dirty, we need to wash it.

senses.gloss: To carry away or erode by the force of water in motion.
senses.example: Don't pour that in the drain; it will wash downstream.

senses.gloss: To be eroded or carried away by the action of water.

examples.text: “Don’t ask me,” said Owl Eyes, washing his hands of the whole matter.
examples.translation_ko: "묻지 마세요." 올빼미 눈이 그 모든 일에서 손을 털며 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Daisy went upstairs to wash her face—too late I thought with humiliation of my towels—while Gatsby and I waited on the lawn.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지가 세수를 하러 위층으로 올라갔는데—너무 늦었지만 나는 수건 생각에 굴욕감을 느꼈다—개츠비와 나는 잔디밭에서 기다렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She washed him.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그를 씻겨주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was dressed in a bedraggled suit of khaki, and his hands would have been all the better for a wash.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 너덜너덜한 카키색 양복을 입고 있었고, 손은 씻었다면 훨씬 나았을 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French fantastique, borrowed from Late Latin phantasticus, borrowed from Ancient Greek φᾰντᾰστῐκός (phăntăstĭkós, “imaginary, ...
definition_en: Extremely good or exciting.

senses.gloss: Wonderful; marvelous; excellent; extraordinarily good or great (used especially as an intensifier).
senses.example: "I had a simply fantastic vacation, and I can't wait to tell you all about it!"

senses.gloss: Existing in or constructed from fantasy; of or relating to fantasy; fanciful.
senses.example: He told fantastic stories of dragons and goblins.

senses.gloss: Not believable; implausible; seemingly only possible in fantasy.

examples.text: West Egg, especially, still figures in my more fantastic dreams.
examples.translation_ko: 특히 웨스트에그는 지금도 내 환상적인 꿈속에 등장한다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The most grotesque and fantastic conceits haunted him in his bed at night.
examples.translation_ko: 가장 기괴하고 환상적인 상념들이 밤마다 침대에서 그를 사로잡았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was strange and fantastic.
examples.translation_ko: 기이하고 환상적이었어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I amused myself by thinking that in his choice of books he showed pleasantly the irreconcilable sides of his fantastic nature.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 책 선택에서 그 환상적인 성격의 화해할 수 없는 양면이 유쾌하게 드러난다고 생각하며 나는 즐거워했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English drivere, dryvere, dryvare, equivalent to drive + -er. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Drieuwer (“driver”), Dutch drijver (“drive...
definition_en: A person who drives a vehicle.

senses.gloss: A person who drives a motorized vehicle such as a car, truck, bus, train, forklift, etc.
senses.example: The driver will make an announcement when the trip is nearing its completion.

senses.gloss: A pilot (person who flies aircraft).
A person who drives livestock: a drover.

translations_zh: 驅趕動物者 /驱赶动物者

examples.text: A bad driver and not even trying!”
examples.translation_ko: 운전도 못하면서 시도조차 안 했다니!"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You’re a rotten driver,” I protested.
examples.translation_ko: "당신은 형편없는 운전자예요." 내가 항의했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Again he made no reply, but the driver of our carriage came to my rescue.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 또다시 대답하지 않았지만, 마차 운전사가 나를 구해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I gave the driver the necessary direction, and in renewed silence we drove on.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 운전사에게 필요한 지시를 내렸고, 다시 침묵 속에서 우리는 계속 달렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English strecchen, from Old English streċċan (“to stretch, hold out, extend, spread out, prostrate”), from Proto-West Germanic *strakkj...
definition_en: To extend or lengthen something to its full extent.

senses.gloss: To lengthen by pulling.
senses.example: I stretched the rubber band until it almost broke.

senses.gloss: To lengthen when pulled.
senses.example: The rubber band stretched almost to the breaking point.

senses.gloss: To pull tight.
senses.example: First, stretch the skin over the frame of the drum.

examples.text: Before me stretched the portentous, menacing road of a new decade.
examples.translation_ko: 내 앞에는 불길하고 위협적인 새로운 십 년의 길이 펼쳐져 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It eluded us then, but that’s no matter—tomorrow we will run faster, stretch out our arms further …
examples.translation_ko: 그때 그것은 우리를 피해갔지만, 그것은 상관없다—내일 우리는 더 빨리 달리고, 팔을 더 멀리 뻗을 것이다…
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He stopped, somewhat dramatically, and stretched out his arm.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 다소 극적으로 멈춰 서서 팔을 뻗었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was the picture of a woman lying on a sofa, with one arm beneath her head and the other along her body; one knee was raised, and the other leg was stretched out.
examples.translation_ko: 소파에 누워 있는 여인의 그림이었는데, 한 팔은 머리 밑에 베고 다른 팔은 몸을 따라 늘어뜨린 채였다. 한쪽 무릎은 세우고 다른 쪽 다리는 쭉 뻗어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English mone, from Old English mōna (“moon”), from Proto-West Germanic *mānō, from Proto-Germanic *mēnô (“moon”), from Proto-Indo-Europ...
definition_en: The natural satellite of the Earth.

senses.gloss: Alternative letter-case form of Moon (“the Earth's only permanent natural satellite”).
senses.example: "I suppose I may have leave to do that!" Yes, she could do that, he said, but there was no road to that place; it lay east of the sun and west of the moon, and she could never find her way there.

examples.text: It had seemed as close as a star to the moon.
examples.translation_ko: 달에게 다가선 별처럼 가깝게 느껴졌었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A silver curve of the moon hovered already in the western sky.
examples.translation_ko: 은빛 초승달이 이미 서쪽 하늘에 떠 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He loved to moon about the harbour talking to the natives.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 항구를 어슬렁거리며 원주민들과 이야기하는 것을 좋아했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is the same emotion which is excited in the human heart by the sight of a lovely woman, the Bay of Naples under the yellow moon, and the Entombment of Titian.
examples.translation_ko: 아름다운 여인의 모습이나, 노란 달빛 아래 펼쳐진 나폴리 만이나, 티치아노의 「그리스도의 매장」을 보고 인간의 마음에서 일어나는 감정과 같은 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English brekefast, brekefaste, equivalent to break + fast (literally, "to end the nightly fast"), likely a variant of Old English fæste...
definition_en: The first meal of the day.

senses.gloss: The first meal of the day, usually eaten in the morning.
senses.example: You should put more protein in her breakfast so she will grow.

senses.gloss: A meal consisting of food normally eaten in the morning, which may typically include eggs, sausages, toast, bacon, etc.
senses.example: We serve breakfast all day.

senses.gloss: The celebratory meal served after a wedding (and occasionally after other solemnities e.g. a funeral).

examples.text: “I enjoyed breakfast, Gatsby.”
examples.translation_ko: "아침 식사 잘 먹었어요, 개츠비."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was nine o’clock when we finished breakfast and went out on the porch.
examples.translation_ko: 아침을 마치고 현관으로 나간 것은 아홉 시였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I’ll get you some breakfast.”
examples.translation_ko: 아침 좀 사줄게."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Come and have breakfast, mate,” he said.
examples.translation_ko: "가서 아침이나 먹자, 친구." 그가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English barre, from Old French barre (“beam, bar, gate, barrier”), from Vulgar Latin *barra, of uncertain origin. Doublet of barre.
definition_en: A bar is a place where people drink and socialize.

senses.gloss: A solid, more or less rigid object of metal or wood with a uniform cross-section smaller than its length.
senses.example: The window was protected by steel bars.

senses.gloss: A solid metal object with uniform (round, square, hexagonal, octagonal or rectangular) cross-section; in the US its smallest dimension is ¹⁄₄ inch or greater, a piece of thinner material being called a strip.
senses.example: Ancient Sparta used iron bars instead of handy coins in more valuable alloy, to physically discourage the use of money.

senses.gloss: A cuboid piece of any solid commodity.
senses.example: bar of chocolate

examples.text: The bar, where we glanced first, was crowded, but Gatsby was not there.
examples.translation_ko: 우리가 먼저 들여다본 바는 붐볐지만, 개츠비는 거기 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: In the main hall a bar with a real brass rail was set up, and stocked with gins and liquors and with cordials so long forgotten that most of his female guests were too young to know one from another.
examples.translation_ko: 메인 홀에는 진짜 황동 난간이 달린 바가 설치되어 있었고, 진과 리큐어, 그리고 너무 오래전에 잊혀진 코디얼들로 가득 채워져 있어서 그의 여성 손님들 대부분은 너무 어려서 하나하나를 구별할 줄도 몰랐다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Behind the bar was seated a woman nursing her baby.
examples.translation_ko: 바 뒤편에는 아기에게 젖을 먹이는 여자가 앉아 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The women scattered to the door and behind the bar.
examples.translation_ko: 여자들은 문 쪽과 바 뒤로 흩어졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English couche, cowche, from Old French couche, from the verb (see below). Doublet of cwtch.
definition_en: An item of furniture, often upholstered, for the comfortable seating of more than one person; a sofa.

senses.gloss: An item of furniture, often upholstered, for the comfortable seating of more than one person; a sofa.
senses.example: […] I want to try to describe my efforts to take psychoanalysis as a method off the couch and into the work of creating and using a political conference table.

senses.gloss: A bed, a resting-place.
senses.example: [H]e and those / Shall bide eternal bedfellows / Where low upon the couch he lies / Whence he never shall arise.

senses.gloss: The den of an otter.
senses.example: A couch was located under the roots of an uprooted tree in a medium dense spruce patch and the second couch was located under a free standing spruce along a regulation channel.

examples.text: Daisy sat back upon the couch.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지는 소파에 등을 기댔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The sister Catherine sat down beside me on the couch.
examples.translation_ko: 누이 캐서린이 소파에서 내 옆에 앉았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English dauncen, from Anglo-Norman dauncer, from Vulgar Latin *dantiāre, of uncertain origin. Displaced Old English sealtian, and parti...
definition_en: A sequence of rhythmic steps or movements usually performed to music, for pleasure or as a form of social interaction.

senses.gloss: A sequence of rhythmic steps or movements usually performed to music, for pleasure or as a form of social interaction.
senses.example: I do a dance when she plays the drums!

senses.gloss: A social gathering where dancing is the main activity.
senses.example: The dance we had in August 2008 is one of the greatest moments of my life!

senses.gloss: The art, profession, and study of dancing.

examples.text: “The dance?”
examples.translation_ko: "댄스 파티?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Daisy and Gatsby danced.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지와 개츠비가 춤을 췄다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English wir, wyr, from Old English wīr (“wire, metal thread, wire-ornament”), from Proto-Germanic *wīraz (“wire”), from Proto-Indo-Euro...
definition_en: Metal formed into a thin, even thread, now usually by being drawn through a hole in a steel die.

senses.gloss: Metal formed into a thin, even thread, now usually by being drawn through a hole in a steel die.
senses.example: Holonyms: cable; wiring harness; wire wool

senses.gloss: A piece of such material; a thread or slender rod of metal, a cable.
A metal conductor that carries electricity.
senses.example: We need to buy a wire that connects to our IPhone.

examples.text: Get my wire?”
examples.translation_ko: 제 전보 받으셨나요?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “There haven’t been any wires.”
examples.translation_ko: "전보는 한 통도 오지 않았어요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology:
Coined between 1350 and 1400 as Middle English personalite, from Middle French [Term?], from Latin persōnālitās.
Morphologically personal + -ity
definition_en: The combination of characteristics or qualities that form an individual's distinctive character.

senses.gloss: A set of non-physical psychological and social qualities that make one person distinct from another.
senses.example: The president has a unique personality.

senses.gloss: Charisma, or qualities that make a person stand out from the crowd.
senses.example: The best contestant shows most personality.

senses.gloss: A set of qualities that make something distinctive or interesting.
senses.example: His writing has a lot of personality.

examples.text: With the influence of the dress her personality had also undergone a change.

examples.text: “But I swore I wouldn’t tell it and here I am tantalizing you.”

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I swear it by God.”
examples.translation_ko: 하나님께 맹세해요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I could swear I’ve lived here before.”
examples.translation_ko: 전에 여기서 살았던 적이 있다고 맹세할 수 있을 정도예요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fressh, from Old English fersċ (“fresh, pure, sweet”), from Proto-West Germanic *frisk (“fresh”), from Proto-Germanic *friskaz ...
definition_en: Having a pleasant and cool quality.

senses.gloss: Newly produced or obtained; recent.
senses.example: He followed the fresh hoofprints to find the deer.

senses.gloss: Not dried, frozen, or spoiled.
senses.example: After taking a beating in the boxing ring, the left side of his face looked like fresh meat.

senses.gloss: Still green and not dried.

examples.text: the freshest and the best, forever.
examples.translation_ko: 가장 싱싱하고 가장 아름다운 부분을, 영원히.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The windows were ajar and gleaming white against the fresh grass outside that seemed to grow a little way into the house.
examples.translation_ko: 창문들은 반쯤 열려 있었고, 밖의 싱싱한 잔디밭에 맞서 하얗게 빛나고 있었는데, 그 잔디는 집 안으로 조금씩 자라 들어오는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Strickland, a boy fresh from school, went into a broker’s office without any feeling of distaste.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 학교를 갓 졸업한 소년으로서 아무런 혐오감도 느끼지 않고 중개업소에 들어갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Dirk was going home to dinner, and I proposed to find a doctor and bring him to see Strickland; but when we got down into the street, fresh after the stuffy attic, the Dutchman begged me to go immediately to his studio.
examples.translation_ko: 디르크는 저녁 식사를 하러 집으로 가려 했고, 나는 의사를 찾아 스트릭랜드를 진찰하게 하자고 제안했다. 하지만 답답한 다락방을 나와 상쾌한 거리로 내려왔을 때, 네덜란드인은 즉시 자신의 작업실로 가자고 간청했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English conneccioun, connexioun, conneccyon, conneccion, from Latin connexionem (nominative connexio (“a conclusion, binding together”)...
definition_en: A link or relationship between people, things, or ideas.

senses.gloss: The act of connecting.
The point at which two or more things are connected.
senses.example: the connection between overeating and obesity

senses.gloss: A feeling of understanding and ease of communication between two or more people.
senses.example: As we were the only people in the room to laugh at the joke, I felt a connection between us.

examples.text: He might think he saw a connection in it—he might think anything.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 거기서 어떤 연관성을 보았다고 생각할지도 모른다—그는 뭐든 생각할 수 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But the connection came through as a man’s voice, very thin and far away.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 연결된 것은 남자 목소리였고, 매우 가늘고 멀리서 들려왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When I come to his connection with Blanche Stroeve
examples.translation_ko: 그와 블랑슈 스트루브의 관계에 이르러서는
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I have tried to put some connection into the various things Captain Nichols told me about Strickland, and I here set them down in the best order I can.
examples.translation_ko: 니콜스 선장이 스트릭랜드에 대해 내게 들려준 여러 이야기들을 어떻게든 연결해보려 했고, 내가 할 수 있는 최선의 순서로 여기에 적어본다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English glowen, from Old English glōwan, from Proto-West Germanic *glōan, from Proto-Germanic *glōaną, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵʰleh₁...
definition_en: Give off light

senses.gloss: To emit light as if heated.
senses.example: The fire was still glowing after ten hours.

senses.gloss: To radiate thermal heat.
senses.example: Iron glows red hot when heated to near its melting point.

senses.gloss: To display intense emotion.
senses.example: The zealots glowed with religious fervor.

examples.text: The grey windows disappeared as the house glowed full of light.
examples.translation_ko: 집 전체가 환하게 밝아지자 회색빛 창문들이 사라졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As if his absence quickened something within her, Daisy leaned forward again, her voice glowing and singing.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 부재가 그녀 안의 무언가를 재촉하기라도 하듯, 데이지는 다시 몸을 앞으로 기울였고, 그녀의 목소리는 빛나며 노래했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He glowed with happy pride.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 행복한 자부심으로 얼굴을 빛냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English baby, babie (“baby”), a diminutive form of babe (“babe, baby”), equivalent to babe + -y/-ie (“endearing and diminutive suffix”)...
definition_en: A very young human being.

senses.gloss: A very young human, particularly from birth to a couple of years old or until walking is fully mastered.
senses.example: In that film, I often hid my head in my hands, unable to watch scenes about dead babies and diving into gruesome lavatories.

senses.gloss: A very young human, even if not yet born.
senses.example: When is your baby due?

senses.gloss: Any very young animal, especially a vertebrate; many species have specific names for their babies, such as kittens for the babies of cats, puppies for the babies of dogs, and chicks for the babies of birds. See :Category:Baby animals for more.

examples.text: Then she added irrelevantly: “You ought to see the baby.”
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 뜬금없이 덧붙였다. "아기를 봐야 하는데."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A pair of stage twins, who turned out to be the girls in yellow, did a baby act in costume, and champagne was served in glasses bigger than finger-bowls.
examples.translation_ko: 무대 쌍둥이 한 쌍이 나타났는데, 알고 보니 노란 옷을 입은 그 소녀들이었고, 의상을 입고 아기 연기를 했으며, 샴페인은 핑거볼보다 큰 잔에 담겨 나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: ‘She cooks my food and looks after her babies.
examples.translation_ko: '음식을 해주고 아이들을 돌본다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Behind the bar was seated a woman nursing her baby.
examples.translation_ko: 바 뒤편에는 아기에게 젖을 먹이는 여자가 앉아 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham
