definition_en: A sight or prospect seen from a particular place.

senses.gloss: The act of seeing or looking at something.
senses.example: He changed seats to get a complete view of the stage.

senses.gloss: The range of vision.
senses.example: If there are any rabbits in this park, they keep carefully out of our view.

senses.gloss: Something to look at, such as scenery.
senses.example: My flat has a view of a junkyard.

examples.text: A new point of view occurred to me.
examples.translation_ko: 새로운 관점이 떠올랐다.

examples.text: He jumped off to give me a better view.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내가 더 잘 볼 수 있도록 차에서 뛰어내렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There is so much in his character which is strange that I feel it would complete the picture if his views were outrageous.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 성격에는 기이한 면이 너무 많아서, 그의 견해까지 터무니없다면 그 인물상이 완성될 것 같은 느낌이 든다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Strickland was not, I should say, a man of great intelligence, and his views on painting were by no means out of the ordinary.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 내가 보기에 대단히 지적인 사람은 아니었고, 회화에 대한 그의 견해도 결코 평범하지 않은 것은 아니었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Back-formation from dawning. (If the noun rather than the verb is primary, the noun could directly continue dawing.) Compare daw (“to dawn”).
definition_en: The first light of day.

senses.gloss: To begin to brighten with daylight.
senses.example: A new day dawns.

senses.gloss: To start to appear or become obvious.
senses.example: I don’t want to be there when the truth dawns on him.

senses.gloss: To begin to give promise; to begin to appear or to expand.
senses.example: Leave the time of war behind and let a time of peace dawn!

examples.text: After that, he stayed there alone with Wilson until dawn.
examples.translation_ko: 그 후 그는 새벽까지 윌슨과 단둘이 그곳에 머물렀다.

examples.text: He was glad a little later when he noticed a change in the room, a blue quickening by the window, and realized that dawn wasn’t far off.
examples.translation_ko: 창가에서 푸른빛이 빨라지는 것을 보고 방 안의 변화를 알아차렸을 때, 새벽이 멀지 않았다는 것을 깨달으며 그는 조금 안도했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They started at dawn, and the boy I sent with them didn’t come back till next day.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 새벽에 출발했고, 내가 함께 보낸 소년은 다음 날이 되어서야 돌아왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The sky had still the pallor of dawn, and there was a ghostly silence on the lagoon.
examples.translation_ko: 하늘은 여전히 새벽의 창백함을 띠고 있었고, 석호에는 유령 같은 정적이 흘렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English disapeeren, equivalent to dis- + appear. Displaced native Old English fordwīnan.
definition_en: To cease to be seen or heard.

senses.gloss: To vanish.
To go missing; to become a missing person.
senses.example: Eighteen years after Jaycee Dugard disappeared in 1991, she was found alive in the summer of 2009.

senses.gloss: To go away; to become lost.
senses.example: A turban and loincloth soaked in blood had been found; also a staff. These properties were known to have belonged to a toddy drawer. He had disappeared.

examples.text: Then for three hours he disappeared from view.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고 나서 세 시간 동안 그는 시야에서 사라졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The grey windows disappeared as the house glowed full of light.
examples.translation_ko: 집 전체가 환하게 밝아지자 회색빛 창문들이 사라졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He would turn up in Papeete every few months and stay a little while; he’d get money out of someone or other and then disappear again.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 몇 달마다 파페에테에 나타나서 잠시 머물곤 했다. 누군가에게서 돈을 얻어내고는 다시 사라지곤 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He and Strickland were assigned to different rooms, and when, thrown out of bed at five in the morning by a stalwart monk, he had made his bed and washed his face, Strickland had already disappeared.
examples.translation_ko: 그와 스트릭랜드는 서로 다른 방에 배정되었고, 새벽 다섯 시에 건장한 수사에게 침대에서 쫓겨나 잠자리를 정리하고 세수를 마쳤을 때, 스트릭랜드는 이미 사라진 후였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bot, boot, boet, boyt (“boat”), from Old English bāt (“boat”), from Proto-West Germanic *bait, from Proto-Germanic *baitaz, *ba...
definition_en: A small vessel for travel on water.

senses.gloss: A craft used for transportation of goods, fishing, racing, recreational cruising, or military use on or in the water, propelled by oars or outboard motor or inboard motor or by wind.
senses.example: Philander went into the next room[…]and came back with a salt mackerel[…]. Next he put the mackerel in a fry-pan, and the shanty began to smell like a Banks boat just in from a v'yage.

senses.gloss: A full house.
A conveyance, utensil, or dish somewhat resembling a boat in shape.
senses.example: a stone boat;   a gravy boat

examples.text: So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 우리는 계속 노를 젓는다, 끊임없이 과거로 밀려나면서도 물살을 거슬러.

examples.text: Slowly the white wings of the boat moved against the blue cool limit of the sky.
examples.translation_ko: 천천히 배의 하얀 돛이 하늘의 푸르고 시원한 경계선을 배경으로 움직였다.

examples.text: They can sail a boat.
examples.translation_ko: 아이들은 배를 몰 수 있습니다.

examples.text: When it was an English boat, they would dodge into the forecastle and get a hearty breakfast from the crew.
examples.translation_ko: 영국 배일 때는 선원실로 몰래 들어가서 선원들로부터 푸짐한 아침을 얻어먹었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: To consider as part of something; to comprehend.
senses.example: The vacation package includes car rental.

senses.gloss: To enclose, confine.
senses.example: I could have here willingly ranged, but these straits wherein I am included will not permit.

examples.text: This included me.
examples.translation_ko: 여기에는 나도 포함되어 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He excused himself with a small bow that included each of us in turn.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 우리 각자를 차례로 포함하는 작은 인사로 양해를 구했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They belonged to all the countries in the world, but this was no bar to good-fellowship; for they felt themselves freemen of a country whose frontiers include them all, the great country of Cockaine.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 세계 각국 출신이었지만, 이것이 우정에 장애가 되지는 않았다. 그들은 모든 나라를 국경 안에 포함하는 위대한 나라, 코케인의 자유민이라고 스스로를 여겼기 때문이다.

definition_en: To rest in a state of reduced consciousness.

senses.gloss: To accommodate in beds.

examples.text: “You’d better come home and get some sleep.”

examples.text: “Get some more ice and mineral water, Myrtle, before everybody goes to sleep.”
examples.translation_ko: "머틀, 모두 잠들기 전에 얼음과 광천수를 더 가져와요."

Coins made from silver or any similar white metal.
senses.example: […] maybe two or three twenties, a dozen tens, and twenty or thirty fins. The rest is all aces and silver.

senses.gloss: Cutlery and other eating utensils, whether silver or made from some other white metal.

examples.text: A silver curve of the moon hovered already in the western sky.
examples.translation_ko: 은빛 초승달이 이미 서쪽 하늘에 떠 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was nothing in it but a small, expensive dog-leash, made of leather and braided silver.
examples.translation_ko: 그 안에는 가죽과 은실로 짠 작고 비싼 개목줄 외에는 아무것도 없었다.

senses.gloss: A vehicle that may be hired for single journeys by members of the public, particularly one with an automated meter to calculate the fare.

[Sobbing uncontrollably] I thought I could make it work between us because you looked a bit like a man.
TAXI!

examples.text: But I’d be glad if you’d order me the taxi.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 택시 좀 불러주시면 고맙겠어요.

examples.translation_ko: 택시가 끙끙거리며 떠나갈 때 개츠비가 잔디밭을 가로질러 내게로 걸어오는 것이 보였다.

etymology: Borrowed from French chauffeur.
definition_en: A person employed to drive a private motor car or a hired car of executive or luxury class (like a limousine).

Super Nintendo, Sega Genesis
When I was dead broke, man, I couldn't picture this
50-inch screen, money-green leather sofa
Got two rides, a limousine with a chauffeur

examples.text: Tell your chauffeur to go far away and spend an hour.”
examples.translation_ko: "운전기사에게 멀리 가서 한 시간 정도 있다가 오라고 해."

examples.text: With scarcely a word said, four of us, the chauffeur, butler, gardener, and I hurried down to the pool.
examples.translation_ko: 거의 말도 없이 우리 넷—운전기사, 집사, 정원사, 그리고 나—이 서둘러 수영장으로 내려갔다.

definition_en: Guidance; help.

senses.gloss: Guidance; help.
A polite approach made to another person, especially of a romantic nature; an amorous advance.
senses.example: [H]e was thus agreeable, and I neither insensible of his Perfections, nor displeased at his Addresses to me […].

senses.gloss: A manner of speaking or writing to another; language, style.
senses.example: a man of pleasing or insinuating address

examples.text: “Left no address?”
examples.translation_ko: "주소는 남기지 않았나요?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: My address is care of B. F.—”
examples.translation_ko: 내 주소는 B. F.—"

definition_en: A flaw or weakness in a system or relationship.

senses.gloss: Culpability; the responsibility for a blameworthy event.
senses.example: No, don't blame yourself. It's my fault that we lost the game.

senses.gloss: A failing of character; less severe than a vice.
senses.example: Despite all her faults, she’s a good person at heart.

senses.gloss: A characteristic, positive or negative or both, which increases one's risk of danger or difficulty.
senses.example: You're still young, that's your fault.

examples.text: That was my fault—Gatsby had been called to the phone, and I’d enjoyed these same people only two weeks before.
examples.translation_ko: 그건 내 잘못이었다—개츠비는 전화를 받으러 갔고, 나는 불과 2주 전에 이 같은 사람들과 즐거운 시간을 보냈던 것이다.

senses.gloss: To provide what is wanted or required for (something).

examples.text: Most of those reports were a nightmare—grotesque, circumstantial, eager, and untrue.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The saddest thing about them was that they were grotesque, and the more pathetic they were, the more you wanted to laugh.

etymology: From Middle English practical, practicale, praktycall, from Medieval Latin practicālis.
definition_en: Having or showing a common-sense approach to problems.

senses.gloss: Relating to, or based on, practice or action rather than theory or hypothesis.
senses.example: Jack didn't get an engineering degree, but has practical knowledge of metalworking.

senses.gloss: Being likely to be effective and applicable to a real situation; able to be put to use.
senses.example: Jack's knowledge has the practical benefit of giving us useful prototype parts.

senses.gloss: Of a person, having skills or knowledge that are practical.
senses.example: All in all, Jack's a very practical chap.

examples.text: After she had obliterated four years with that sentence they could decide upon the more practical measures to be taken.
examples.translation_ko: 그 한마디로 4년의 세월을 지워버린 후에야 그들은 더 현실적인 조치들을 결정할 수 있을 터였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: From the moment I telephoned news of the catastrophe to West Egg village, every surmise about him, and every practical question, was referred to me.

senses.gloss: The end for which something is done, is made or exists.
senses.example: What is the purpose of your visit?

senses.gloss: Function, role.
senses.example: The exceptionally small gate-leg table served the purpose of a tea table admirably.

senses.gloss: meaning for existing or doing something.
senses.example: This place gave him purpose, gave him joy. It was both his life and his lifeline and she was both thrilled and relieved that he'd recovered enough to be able to maintain the place.

examples.translation_ko: "그런 느낌이 어렴풋이 들긴 했습니다, 솔직히 말하면."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “I was vaguely told that something was wrong.”
examples.translation_ko: "뭔가 잘못되었다는 말을 어렴풋이 들었을 뿐입니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Scots bauther, bather (“to bother”). Origin unknown. Perhaps related to Scots pother (“to make a stir or commotion, bustle”), also of...
definition_en: Cause annoyance or disturbance.

senses.gloss: To annoy, to disturb, to irritate; to be troublesome to, to make trouble for.
senses.example: Would it bother you if I smoked?

senses.gloss: Damn; curse.
To feel care or concern; to burden or inconvenience oneself out of concern.
senses.example: I never bother about such trivialities.

examples.text: That’s why I been bothering you about the car.”
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 자동차 때문에 당신을 귀찮게 했던 거고요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As a matter of fact you needn’t bother to ascertain.
examples.translation_ko: 사실 굳이 확인해볼 필요는 없소.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Will you tell me why you bothered about Blanche Stroeve at all?”
examples.translation_ko: "도대체 왜 블랑슈 스트루브에게 관심을 가졌던 거요?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “I don’t suppose Mrs. Strickland wants to be bothered with me just now,” I said.
examples.translation_ko: "지금 스트릭랜드 부인이 저 때문에 번거로워하고 싶지는 않을 것 같은데요." 내가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Derived from Old French divorce, from Latin dīvortium, from dīvertere (“to turn aside”), from dī- (“apart”) + vertere (“to turn”); see verse.
definition_en: The legal dissolution of a marriage.

senses.gloss: The legal dissolution of a marriage.
senses.example: Richard obtained a divorce from his wife some years ago, but hasn't returned to the dating scene.

senses.gloss: A separation of connected things.
senses.example: The Civil War split between Virginia and West Virginia was a divorce based along cultural and economic as well as geographic lines.

senses.gloss: The separation of a bonded pair of animals.

examples.text: I’m as obstinate as he is, and I’ll never divorce him.
examples.translation_ko: 나도 그 사람만큼 고집이 세니까, 절대 이혼해주지 않을 거야.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: At last I was disgusted with him, and I got a divorce.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 나는 그가 역겨워져서 이혼했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cheosen, chesen, from Old English ċēosan (“to choose, seek out, select, elect, decide, test, accept, settle for, approve”), fro...
definition_en: To select or decide on something.

senses.gloss: To pick; to make the choice of; to select.
senses.example: I chose a nice ripe apple from the fruit bowl.

senses.gloss: To elect.
senses.example: He was chosen as president in 1990.

senses.gloss: To decide to act in a certain way.
senses.example: I chose to walk to work today.

examples.text: All my aunts and uncles talked it over as if they were choosing a prep school for me, and finally said, “Why—ye-es,” with very grave, hesitant faces.
examples.translation_ko: 모든 숙모와 숙부들이 마치 내게 맞는 예비학교를 고르듯 상의를 했고, 마침내 매우 진지하고 망설이는 표정으로 "음—그래"라고 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And yet I couldn’t believe that they would choose this occasion for a scene—especially for the rather harrowing scene that Gatsby had outlined in the garden.
examples.translation_ko: 그런데도 나는 그들이 이런 자리를 택해서 한바탕 소동을 벌이리라고는—특히 개츠비가 정원에서 내게 설명했던 그런 참혹한 장면을 연출하리라고는 믿을 수 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “She can do as she chooses,” said Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: "그녀가 원하는 대로 하면 되지." 스트릭랜드가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Let the others go if they choose, but I will not leave thee.
examples.translation_ko: "다른 사람들은 원한다면 떠나도 좋지만, 나는 당신을 떠나지 않겠어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English harm, herm, from Old English hearm, from Proto-West Germanic *harm, from Proto-Germanic *harmaz (“harm; shame; pain”). Cognate ...
definition_en: Damage or injury to someone's health or well-being.

senses.gloss: Physical injury; hurt; damage.
senses.example: No harm came to my possessions.

senses.gloss: Emotional or figurative hurt.
senses.example: Although not physically injured in the car accident, she received some psychological harm.

senses.gloss: Detriment; misfortune.
senses.example: I wish him no harm.

examples.text: “No harm in trying,” he said.
examples.translation_ko: "해봐서 나쁠 건 없죠." 그가 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I’m one of these trusting fellas and I don’t think any harm to nobody, but when I get to know a thing I know it.
examples.translation_ko: "나는 남을 잘 믿는 성격이고 누구에게도 해를 끼치려 하지 않지만, 뭔가를 알게 되면 확실히 아는 편이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “There is no great harm.
examples.translation_ko: "별일 아니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He’ll do us some great harm.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 우리에게 큰 해를 끼칠 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English partener, partiner, alteration (due to Middle English part) of Middle English parcener, from Old French parçonier, parçonneour ...
definition_en: A person with whom one has a business or professional relationship.

senses.gloss: Either of a pair of people or things that belong together.
A member of a business or law partnership.
A spouse or other person with whom one shares a domestic, romantic or sexual bond.

examples.text: “Did he tell his partner he was leaving?”
examples.translation_ko: "동업자에게는 떠난다고 말했나?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I think, even, he hated the inevitable partner in his debauchery.
examples.translation_ko: 심지어 그는 자신의 방탕한 행위에 불가피하게 동반되는 상대방까지도 미워했던 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From in + stead, from Middle English ine (“in”) + stede (“stead”). Related to German statt.
definition_en: Used for contrasting two things.

senses.gloss: In the place of something (usually mentioned earlier); as a substitute or alternative.
senses.example: I was going to go shopping, but I went dancing instead.

examples.text: Instead of taking the shortcut along the Sound we went down to the road and entered by the big postern.
examples.translation_ko: 해협을 따라 지름길로 가는 대신 우리는 큰길로 내려가서 커다란 뒷문으로 들어갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They look out of no face, but, instead, from a pair of enormous yellow spectacles which pass over a nonexistent nose.
examples.translation_ko: 그 눈들은 얼굴에서 내려다보는 것이 아니라, 존재하지 않는 코 위에 걸린 거대한 노란 안경테에서 바라보고 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He used gestures instead of adjectives, and he halted.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 형용사 대신 몸짓을 사용했고, 말을 더듬었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Fred would fly into a passion, and there’d be a quarrel, and things would be worse instead of better.
examples.translation_ko: 프레드는 화를 내며 달려들 테고, 다툼이 벌어져서 상황이 나아지기는커녕 더 악화될 거예요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + expected.
definition_en: Happening or done unexpectedly.

senses.gloss: Not expected, anticipated or foreseen.
senses.example: The windmill presented unexpected difficulties.

examples.text: The answer to this was unexpected.
examples.translation_ko: 이 질문에 대한 답은 예상치 못한 것이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her throat, full of aching, grieving beauty, told only of her unexpected joy.
examples.translation_ko: 아프고 슬픈 아름다움으로 가득한 그녀의 목소리는 오직 예상치 못한 기쁨만을 전했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “It was all so unexpected,” she said.
examples.translation_ko: "모든 게 너무 뜻밖이었어요." 그녀가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The air you breathe is an elixir which prepares you for the unexpected.
examples.translation_ko: 숨 쉬는 공기는 예상치 못한 일들을 준비시켜 주는 영약이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English generally, generalliche, equivalent to general + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is usually or often the case.

senses.gloss: Popularly or widely.
senses.example: It is generally known that the Earth is round.

senses.gloss: As a rule; usually; typically; in most cases.
senses.example: I generally have a walk in the afternoon.

senses.gloss: Without reference to specific details.
senses.example: Generally speaking …

examples.text: There were generally a few rioters around, but they never came into the library, so it was a good place to work.
examples.translation_ko: 대개 몇몇 소란꾼들이 있었지만, 그들은 도서관에는 들어오지 않았기 때문에 일하기에 좋은 장소였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Generally he was one of these worn-out men: when he wasn’t working, he sat on a chair in the doorway and stared at the people and the cars that passed along the road.
examples.translation_ko: 대체로 그는 지쳐버린 사람들 중 하나였다. 일을 하지 않을 때면 출입구의 의자에 앉아서 길을 지나가는 사람들과 자동차들을 멍하니 바라보곤 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It’s generally a gesture to arouse pity or terror in their lover.”
examples.translation_ko: 보통은 연인의 동정이나 공포심을 불러일으키려는 몸짓일 뿐이죠."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Women are constantly trying to commit suicide for love, but generally they take care not to succeed.
examples.translation_ko: 여자들은 사랑 때문에 자살을 시도하는 경우가 많지만, 대개는 성공하지 않도록 조심합니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English brigge, from Old English brycġ (“bridge”), from Proto-Germanic *brugjō, *brugjǭ (“bridge”), from Proto-Indo-European *bʰerw-, *...
definition_en: A structure built to span a physical obstacle.

senses.gloss: A construction spanning a waterway, ravine, or valley from an elevated height, allowing for the passage of vehicles, pedestrians, trains, etc.
senses.example: The rope bridge crosses the river.

senses.gloss: The upper bony ridge of the human nose.
senses.example: Rugby players often break the bridge of their noses.

senses.gloss: A prosthesis replacing one or several adjacent teeth.
senses.example: The dentist pulled out the decayed tooth and put in a bridge.

examples.text: “Anything can happen now that we’ve slid over this bridge,” I thought; “anything at all …”
examples.translation_ko: "이 다리를 건너고 나니 이제 무엇이든 일어날 수 있을 것 같다"고 나는 생각했다. "정말 무엇이든…"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was dark now, and as we dipped under a little bridge I put my arm around Jordan’s golden shoulder and drew her toward me and asked her to dinner.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 어둠이 내렸고, 우리가 작은 다리 아래를 지날 때 나는 조던의 황금빛 어깨에 팔을 두르고 그녀를 내 쪽으로 끌어당기며 저녁 식사를 함께 하자고 청했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He beamed at her, and settled his spectacles on the bridge of his nose.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아내를 보며 환하게 웃으면서 콧등에 안경을 고쳐 올렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: My husband said he went to the club three or four nights a week to play bridge.
examples.translation_ko: 남편이 일주일에 서너 번 클럽에 가서 브리지를 친다고 했거든요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English careles, from Old English carlēas (“careless, reckless, void of care, free from care, free”), equivalent to care + -less. Cogna...
definition_en: Not careful or attentive.

senses.gloss: Not concerned or worried (about).
Not giving sufficient attention or thought, especially concerning the avoidance of harm or mistakes.
senses.example: Jessica was so careless that she put her shorts on backwards.

senses.gloss: Free from care; unworried, without anxiety.
senses.example: Jessica was careless about putting her shorts on properly.

examples.text: “I hate careless people.
examples.translation_ko: "난 부주의한 사람들이 싫어.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was all very careless and confused.
examples.translation_ko: 모든 것이 매우 경솔하고 혼란스러웠다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Why should you think that beauty, which is the most precious thing in the world, lies like a stone on the beach for the careless passer-by to pick up idly?
examples.translation_ko: "세상에서 가장 소중한 것인 아름다움이 해변의 돌멩이처럼 굴러다니면서 무심한 행인이 아무렇게나 주워갈 수 있는 것이라고 왜 생각하는 거요?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I imagine that a pickpocket, proud of his light fingers, must feel a sort of indignation with the careless woman who leaves in a cab a vanity-bag with all her jewels in it.
examples.translation_ko: 손재주가 뛰어난 소매치기라면, 보석을 모두 넣어둔 화장품 가방을 택시에 부주의하게 두고 내리는 여자에게 일종의 분노를 느낄 것이라고 나는 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From apparent + -ly.
definition_en: It seems so from what one knows or has heard.

senses.gloss: Plainly; clearly; manifestly; evidently.
senses.example: If he should scorn me so apparently.

senses.gloss: Seemingly; in appearance.
senses.example: A man may be apparently friendly, yet malicious in heart.

senses.gloss: According to what the speaker has read or heard.
senses.example: Apparently you are quite a good dancer.

examples.text: It was apparently new.
examples.translation_ko: 새 것인 듯했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A pause followed this apparently pointless remark.
examples.translation_ko: 이 별 의미 없어 보이는 말 뒤로 침묵이 흘렀다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was apparently living in an Hôtel.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 어떤 호텔에 살고 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He smoked on in silence, taking no further notice of me, and apparently was absorbed in thought.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 조용히 담배를 계속 피우며 더 이상 나에게 관심을 보이지 않았고, 무언가 생각에 잠긴 듯했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English providen, from Latin prōvidēre (“to foresee, act with foresight”). Doublet of purvey.
definition_en: Supply or give something that is needed.

senses.gloss: To make a living; earn money for necessities.
senses.example: It is difficult to provide for my family working on minimum wage.

senses.gloss: To act to prepare for something.
senses.example: provide against disaster.

senses.gloss: To establish as a previous condition; to stipulate.
senses.example: The contract provides that the work be well done.

examples.text: For a while these reveries provided an outlet for his imagination; they were a satisfactory hint of the unreality of reality, a promise that the rock of the world was founded securely on a fairy’s wing.
examples.translation_ko: 한동안 이런 몽상들은 그의 상상력의 출구가 되어주었다. 그것들은 현실의 비현실성에 대한 만족스러운 암시였고, 세상이라는 바위가 요정의 날개 위에 단단히 세워져 있다는 약속이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was employed in a vague personal capacity—while he remained with Cody he was in turn steward, mate, skipper, secretary, and even jailor, for Dan Cody sober knew what lavish doings Dan Cody drunk might soon be about, and he provided for such contingencies by reposing more and more trust in Gatsby.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 애매한 개인적 자격으로 고용되었다—코디와 함께 있는 동안 그는 번갈아 가며 사환, 항해사, 선장, 비서, 심지어 간수 역할까지 했는데, 술에 취하지 않은 댄 코디는 술에 취한 댄 코디가 곧 어떤 방탕한 짓을 벌일지 알고 있었고, 그런 상황에 대비해 개츠비에게 점점 더 많은 신뢰를 맡겼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I asked for something I knew could not be provided, and in a minute came out into the street.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 구할 수 없다는 것을 알고 있는 물건을 달라고 했고, 잠시 후 거리로 나왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The Cuillère de Soupe and the Asile de Nuit were both closed to them, and their only sustenance was the wedge of bread which the Bouchée de Pain provided.
examples.translation_ko: 퀴예르 드 수프와 아질 드 뉘 모두 그들에게는 문이 닫혀 있었고, 유일한 끼니는 부셰 드 팽에서 주는 빵 한 조각뿐이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The adjective is derived from shab (“(obsolete except UK, dialectal) scaly skin disease; skin disease of sheep; crust forming over wound, scab”) + ...
definition_en: Showing signs of wear and tear.

senses.gloss: Of clothing, a place, etc.: unkempt and worn or otherwise in poor condition due to age or neglect; scruffy.
senses.example: They lived in a tiny apartment, with some old, shabby furniture.

senses.gloss: Of a person: wearing ragged or very worn, and often dirty, clothing.
senses.example: The fellow arrived looking rather shabby after journeying so far.

senses.gloss: Of a person, their behaviour, etc.: despicable, mean; also, not generous; stingy, tight-fisted.
senses.example: shabby treatment

examples.text: Everything was dirty and shabby.
examples.translation_ko: 모든 것이 더럽고 초라했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I could be just as happy in a shabby studio in Chelsea as in this flat.”
examples.translation_ko: 이 아파트에서 사는 것만큼이나 첼시의 허름한 작업실에서도 행복할 수 있을 거예요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English unesy, equivalent to un- + easy. Merged with Middle English unethe, uneathe (“difficult, not easy”). See uneath.
definition_en: Feeling or showing unease or discomfort.

senses.gloss: Not easy; difficult.

examples.text: It made me uneasy, as though the whole evening had been a trick of some sort to exact a contributory emotion from me.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 마치 밤 전체가 내게서 어떤 동조하는 감정을 뽑아내려는 일종의 속임수였던 것처럼 나를 불안하게 만들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But he would be uneasy anyhow until he had given them something, realizing in a vague way that that was all they came for.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그들에게 뭔가를 대접하기 전까지는 어쨌든 불안할 것이었다. 그들이 온 이유가 바로 그것뿐이라는 걸 막연히 깨달았기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It made me uneasy.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 나를 불편하게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Finally I gave him a draught, and he sank into uneasy slumber.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 나는 그에게 수면제를 주었고, 그는 불안한 잠에 빠져들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The verb is from Middle English amen, aimen, eimen (“to guess at, to estimate, to aim”), borrowed from Old French esmer, aesmer, asmer, from Latin ...
definition_en: To direct one's efforts or attention at something.

senses.gloss: The pointing of a weapon, as a gun, a dart, or an arrow, or object, in the line of direction with the object intended to be struck; the line of fire; the direction of anything, such as a spear, a blow, a discourse, a remark, towards a particular point or object, with a view to strike or affect it.
senses.example: to take aim

senses.gloss: The point intended to be hit, or object intended to be attained or affected.
Intention or goal.
senses.example: My number one aim in life is to make money to make my parents, siblings, and kids happy.

examples.text: His soul aimed elsewhither.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 영혼은 다른 곳을 향하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I do not know to what inscrutable Nirvana you aim.

senses.gloss: A period of the year in which a place is most busy or frequented for business, amusement, etc.

definition_en: A problem or difficulty that is hard to bear.

senses.gloss: A heavy load.

senses.gloss: A responsibility, onus.
A cause of worry; that which is grievous, wearisome, or oppressive.

c. 1710-1730, Jonathan Swift, The Dean's Complaint Translated and Answered
Deaf, giddy, helpless, left alone, / To all my friends a burden grown.

definition_en: A group of people born and living at about the same time.

senses.gloss: The act of creating something or bringing something into being; production, creation.
senses.example: The generation of peat, when not completely under water, is confined to moist situations […]

senses.gloss: The act of creating a living creature or organism; procreation.
senses.example: Generation by Copulation (certainly) extendeth not to Plants.

senses.gloss: Race, family; breed.
senses.example: Thy Mothers of my generation: what's she, if I be a Dogge?

examples.text: “You’re very polite, but I belong to another generation,” he announced solemnly.
examples.translation_ko: "정중하긴 하지만, 나는 다른 세대 사람입니다." 그가 엄숙하게 선언했다.

examples.text: It was hard to realize that a man in my own generation was wealthy enough to do that.

etymology: From Middle English sete, from Old English sǣte, possibly from (or simply cognate with) Old Norse sæti (“seat”), both from Proto-Germanic *sētiją (...
definition_en: To sit down.

senses.gloss: A place in which to sit.
senses.example: There are two hundred seats in this classroom.

senses.gloss: The horizontal portion of a chair or other furniture designed for sitting.
senses.example: He sat on the arm of the chair rather than the seat, which always annoyed his mother.

senses.gloss: A piece of furniture made for sitting, such as a chair, stool, or bench; any improvised place for sitting.
senses.example: She pulled the seat from under the table to allow him to sit down.

etymology: From Middle English recoveren, rekeveren, from Anglo-Norman recoverer and Old French recovrer, from Latin recuperāre, alternative form of reciperār...
definition_en: To become healthy or strong again after being ill or injured.

senses.gloss: To get back, to regain (a physical thing; in astronomy and navigation, sight of a thing or a signal).
senses.example: After days of inquiries, he finally recovered his lost wallet.

senses.gloss: to salvage, to extricate, to rescue (a thing or person)
senses.example: They recovered three of the explorers very much alive, then another, wracked with severe hypothermia, who was taken to hospital.

senses.gloss: To replenish to, resume (a good state of mind or body).
senses.example: At the top of the hill I asked to stop for a few minutes to recover my strength.

definition_en: A white liquid produced by mammary glands of female mammals.

senses.gloss: A white liquid produced by the mammary glands of female mammals to nourish their young. From certain animals, especially cows, it is also called dairy milk and is a common food for humans as a beverage or used to produce various dairy products such as butter, cheese, and yogurt.
senses.example: Skyr is a product made of curdled milk.

senses.gloss: A white (or whitish) liquid obtained from a vegetable source such as almonds, coconuts, oats, rice, or soy beans.
senses.example: For environmentally minded consumers, the news is hard to swallow: almond milk is not healthy for the planet and the popular milk substitute is especially hard on bees.

senses.gloss: An individual serving of milk.
senses.example: Table three ordered three milks.

senses.gloss: A girl or an unmarried young woman; maiden.
A female servant or cleaner (short for maidservant).
A virgin, now female but originally one of either gender.

examples.text: The maid came back.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Aren’t they sweet?” said Mrs. Stroeve.

senses.gloss: A day declared free from work by the state or government.
A period of one or more days taken off work for leisure and often travel; often plural.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English dampnen, from Old French damner, from Latin damnāre (“to condemn, inflict loss upon”), from damnum (“loss”).
definition_en: Used to express strong disapproval or annoyance.

senses.gloss: To condemn to hell.
senses.example: The official position is that anyone who does this will be damned for all eternity.

senses.gloss: To condemn; to declare guilty; to doom; to adjudge to punishment.
senses.example: Lack of access to support services can damn children with disabilities and lesser means to lives where they never harness their full range of abilities.

senses.gloss: To put out of favor; to ruin; to label negatively.
senses.example: I’m afraid that if I speak out on this, I’ll be damned as a troublemaker.

examples.text: “Not a damn.”
examples.translation_ko: "조금도."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Damn it all, I wanted her.”
examples.translation_ko: "젠장, 그 여자를 원했으니까."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English reprochen, from Old French reprochier (Modern French reprocher).
definition_en: A feeling of shame or guilt that someone has been criticized for something.

senses.gloss: A mild rebuke, or an implied criticism.
senses.example: My father made no reproach in his letters and only took notice of my science by inquiring into my occupations more particularly than before.

senses.gloss: Disgrace or shame.
An object of scorn.

examples.text: He raised his hand to stop my words, looked at me with unforgettable reproach, and, opening the door cautiously, went back into the other room.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내 말을 막으려고 손을 들어 올리더니 잊을 수 없는 원망의 눈빛으로 나를 바라보고는, 조심스럽게 문을 열고 다른 방으로 돌아갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His family were enormously wealthy—even in college his freedom with money was a matter for reproach—but now he’d left Chicago and come East in a fashion that rather took your breath away: for instance, he’d brought down a string of polo ponies from Lake Forest.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 가문은 엄청나게 부유했다—대학 시절에도 그의 돈 쓰는 방식은 비난거리였다—하지만 이제 그는 시카고를 떠나 동부로 온 방식이 숨이 막힐 정도였다: 예를 들어, 레이크 포레스트에서 폴로 조랑말 한 떼를 끌고 내려온 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He did not reproach her.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀를 비난하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She’ll never make you a single reproach.”
examples.translation_ko: 당신을 단 한 번도 비난하지 않을 겁니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English stoute, from Old French estout (“brave, fierce, proud”) (Modern French dialectal stout (“proud”)), from earlier Old French esto...
definition_en: Having a thick or solid build.

senses.gloss: Large; bulky.
senses.example: Yossarian walked out of the office and down the stairs into the dark, tomblike street, passing in the hall the stout woman with warts and two chins, who was already on her way back in.

senses.gloss: Bold, strong-minded.
senses.example: The lords all stand / To clear their cause, most resolutely stout.

senses.gloss: Proud; haughty.
senses.example: Commonly […] they that be rich are lofty and stout.

examples.text: She was in the middle thirties, and faintly stout, but she carried her flesh sensuously as some women can.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 서른 중반쯤 되어 보였고 약간 살이 쪘지만, 어떤 여자들이 그러하듯 관능적으로 몸을 움직였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Looked at from a distance, however, the hen resolved itself into a bonnet, and the countenance of a stout old lady beamed down into the room.
examples.translation_ko: 그러나 멀리서 보니 그 암탉은 모자로 변했고, 통통한 노부인의 얼굴이 방 안을 향해 환하게 미소 짓고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The doctor was a stout man in shabby clothes, and when he took off his hat I noticed that he was very bald.
examples.translation_ko: 의사는 남루한 옷을 입은 뚱뚱한 남자였는데, 모자를 벗었을 때 나는 그가 매우 대머리라는 것을 알아차렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was a Jew named Abraham, a blond, rather stout young man, shy and very unassuming; but he had remarkable gifts.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아브라함이라는 이름의 유대인으로, 금발에 다소 뚱뚱한 젊은 남자였는데, 수줍음이 많고 매우 겸손했지만 뛰어난 재능을 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English contenten (“to satisfy”), from Latin contentus (“contained; satisfied”), past participle of continēre (“to contain”).
definition_en: Satisfied or pleased with something.

senses.gloss: Satisfied, pleased, contented.

examples.text: They were out in the open at last and Gatsby was content.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 모든 것이 드러났고 개츠비는 만족했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Human sympathy has its limits, and we were content to let all their tragic arguments fade with the city lights behind.
examples.translation_ko: 인간의 동정심에도 한계가 있는 법이고, 우리는 그들의 비극적인 다툼이 뒤편으로 사라져가는 도시의 불빛과 함께 희미해지도록 내버려두는 것으로 만족했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But I must content myself with a few paragraphs.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 나는 몇 단락으로 만족해야겠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The great majority are perfectly content to do the ordinary thing.”
examples.translation_ko: 대다수는 평범한 일을 하는 것으로 완전히 만족하고 있어."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From gradual + -ly.
definition_en: Happening or done at a slow and steady rate.

senses.gloss: In a gradual manner; making slow progress; slowly.
senses.example: The most likely conclusion, the researchers say, is that the Levallois method was not taken to Eurasia by African migrants, but evolved there gradually and independently.

senses.gloss: by degrees
senses.example: Horns, upon the due accession of Moisture, doth gradually become Soft.

examples.text: Daisy took her face in her hands as if feeling its lovely shape, and her eyes moved gradually out into the velvet dusk.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지는 자신의 아름다운 얼굴 형태를 만져보듯 두 손으로 얼굴을 감쌌고, 그녀의 눈은 서서히 벨벳 같은 황혼 속으로 향했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Only gradually did I become aware that the automobiles which turned expectantly into his drive stayed for just a minute and then drove sulkily away.
examples.translation_ko: 기대에 찬 채 그의 진입로로 들어서는 자동차들이 잠깐만 머물다가 시무룩하게 돌아가는 것을 나는 서서히 깨닫게 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I’d send you a certain sum of money, and you could give it him gradually, as he needed it.”
examples.translation_ko: "일정한 금액을 당신에게 보내드릴 테니, 그가 필요할 때마다 조금씩 나누어 주시면 됩니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: With some men it needs a cataclysm, as a stone may be broken to fragments by the fury of a torrent; but with some it comes gradually, as a stone may be worn away by the ceaseless fall of a drop of water.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 사람에게는 격류의 분노로 돌이 산산조각 나듯 격변이 필요하지만, 어떤 사람에게는 물방울이 끊임없이 떨어져 돌이 닳아 없어지듯 점진적으로 찾아온다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English eȝebreu, alteration of Old English ēaganbrū (“eyebrow”), equivalent to eye + brow. The corresponding Old English ēagbrǣw meant ...
definition_en: A hair growth above the eye.

senses.gloss: The hair that grows over the bone ridge above the eye socket.
A dormer, usually of small size, whose roof line over the upright face is typically an arched curve, turning into a reverse curve to meet the horizontal line at either end.
A clump of waste fibres that builds up in a roller machine.

examples.text: Mrs. Wilson rejected the compliment by raising her eyebrow in disdain.
examples.translation_ko: 윌슨 부인은 경멸하듯 눈썹을 치켜올리며 그 칭찬을 일축했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Myrtle raised her eyebrows in despair at the shiftlessness of the lower orders.
examples.translation_ko: 머틀은 하층민들의 게으름에 절망하며 눈썹을 치켜올렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Dr. Coutras raised his eyebrows.
examples.translation_ko: 쿠트라 박사는 눈썹을 치켜올렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The blighter came round this morning—the master, you know; when he saw my drawing he just raised his eyebrows and walked on.”
examples.translation_ko: "그 자식이 오늘 아침에 왔어요. 선생 말이에요. 내 그림을 보더니 그냥 눈썹만 치켜올리고 지나가더군요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From non- (“no, none, lack of”) + sense, from c. 1610. Compare the semantically similar West Frisian ûnsin (“nonsense”), Dutch onzin (“nonsense”), ...
definition_en: Meaningless or absurd talk or behavior.

senses.gloss: Letters or words, in writing or speech, that have no meaning or pattern or seem to have no meaning.
senses.example: After my father had a stroke, every time he tried to talk, it sounded like nonsense.

senses.gloss: An untrue statement.
senses.example: While at the hospital, David kept screaming and yelling nonsense, stating Vladimir Putin bailed him out of jail and is a god.

senses.gloss: That which is silly, illogical and lacks any meaning, reason or value; that which does not make sense.

examples.text: “I don’t care; it’s rotten nonsense.”
examples.translation_ko: "상관없어. 완전히 헛소리야."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Nonsense,” I said, a little embarrassed.
examples.translation_ko: "무슨 소리예요." 나는 약간 당황하며 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English request, from Old French requeste (French requête), from Vulgar Latin *requaesita, from Latin requīsīta, feminine of requīsītus...
definition_en: A polite asking for something to be done.

senses.gloss: To ask for (something).
senses.example: The corporal requested reinforcements.

senses.gloss: To ask (somebody) to do something.
senses.example: She called me into her office and requested me to sit down.

examples.text: That request seemed superfluous when I wrote it.
examples.translation_ko: 그 편지를 쓸 때는 그런 요청이 불필요해 보였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was calling up at Daisy’s request—would I come to lunch at her house tomorrow?
examples.translation_ko: 데이지의 부탁으로 전화를 건 것이었다—내일 그녀 집에서 점심을 함께 하지 않겠느냐는 것이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When I reached London I found waiting for me an urgent request that I should go to Mrs. Strickland’s as soon after dinner as I could.
examples.translation_ko: 런던에 도착했을 때, 저녁 식사 후 가능한 한 빨리 스트릭랜드 부인을 찾아달라는 긴급한 부탁이 나를 기다리고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He chose his moment carefully, and tried to make his request sound casual; but he could not master the trembling of his voice; and he felt himself that into words that he wished to seem jovial and friendly there crept the bitterness of his jealousy.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 신중하게 때를 골라 자신의 부탁이 무심한 듯 들리도록 애썼지만, 떨리는 목소리를 억누를 수 없었다. 그리고 유쾌하고 친근하게 들리기를 바랐던 말에 질투의 쓰라림이 스며드는 것을 스스로 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fade, vad, vade (“faded, pale, withered, weak”), from Middle Dutch vade (“weak, faint, limp”), from Old French fade (“weak, wit...
definition_en: Gradually become less intense or noticeable.

senses.gloss: Weak; insipid; tasteless.
senses.example: His masculine taste gave him a sense of something fade and ludicrous.

examples.text: His voice faded off and Tom glanced impatiently around the garage.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 목소리가 흐려졌고 톰은 초조하게 정비소 안을 둘러보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A dim background started to take shape behind him, but at her next remark it faded away.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 뒤로 희미한 배경이 윤곽을 드러내기 시작했지만, 그녀의 다음 말에 그것은 사라져버렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Mrs. Strickland’s sister was older than she, not unlike her, but more faded; and she had the efficient air, as though she carried the British Empire in her pocket, which the wives of senior officers acquire from the consciousness of belonging to a superior caste.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인의 언니는 그녀보다 나이가 많았고, 그녀와 닮았지만 더 초췌해 보였다. 그리고 마치 대영제국을 주머니에 넣고 다니는 듯한 유능한 분위기를 풍겼는데, 이는 고위 장교의 부인들이 우월한 계급에 속한다는 의식에서 우러나오는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English frown, froun (“a threatening appearance; lowering of the clouds”), from frounen (“to frown”). See below.
definition_en: To lower the corners of one's mouth in a sign of disapproval or unhappiness.

senses.gloss: A wrinkling of the forehead with the eyebrows brought together, typically indicating displeasure, severity, or concentration.
senses.example: He encounters some obstacle in his train of reasoning ... and then a frown passes like a shadow over his brow.

senses.gloss: A downturn of the corners of the mouth, typically expressing sadness.
senses.example: The smile and the frown are both indicated and the operation of a motor driven flasher causes the face to look happy and sad in turn.

senses.gloss: Any facial expression that indicates disapproval or displeasure.

examples.text: He frowned.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 인상을 찌푸렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Why candles?” objected Daisy, frowning.
examples.translation_ko: "왜 촛불이에요?" 데이지가 얼굴을 찌푸리며 반박했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Mrs. Strickland frowned a little.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인이 살짝 눈살을 찌푸렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “I didn’t,” he answered, frowning.
examples.translation_ko: "그런 게 아니었어." 그가 인상을 찌푸리며 대답했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English dismayen, from Anglo-Norman *desmaiier, alteration of Old French esmaier (“to frighten”), probably from Vulgar Latin *exmagare ...
definition_en: A feeling of great disappointment or anxiety.

senses.gloss: To cause to feel apprehension; great sadness, or fear; to deprive of energy
senses.example: What words be these? What fears do you dismay?

senses.gloss: To render lifeless; to subdue; to disquiet.
senses.example: Do not dismay yourself for this.

senses.gloss: To take dismay or fright; to be filled with dismay.
senses.example: Dismay not, princes, at this accident,

examples.text: He looked round the squalid attic in dismay.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 더러운 다락방을 둘러보며 경악했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He looked again at the poor dead thing that had been man, and then he started back in dismay.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 한때 사람이었던 불쌍한 시체를 다시 바라보다가 경악하며 뒤로 물러섰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English pacience, from Old French pacience (modern French patience), from Latin patientia (“suffering; endurance, patience”),...
definition_en: The quality of being patient; tolerance.

senses.gloss: The quality of being patient.
senses.example: Musical perfection requires practice and a lot of patience.

senses.gloss: Any of various card games that can be played by one person. Called solitaire in the US and Canada.

examples.text: “I have no patience with you.
examples.translation_ko: "당신이 참 답답해요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: With infinite patience she prepared to snare me and bind me.
examples.translation_ko: 무한한 인내심으로 그녀는 나를 덫에 걸어 묶어두려 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lappe, from Old English læppa (“skirt or flap of a garment”), from Proto-Germanic *lappô (“cloth; rag”), of uncertain origin, p...
definition_en: The space between the thighs when sitting.

senses.gloss: The loose part of a coat; the lower part of a garment that plays loosely; a skirt; an apron.
An edge; a border; a hem, as of cloth.
The part of the clothing that lies on the knees or thighs when one sits down; that part of the person thus covered.

examples.text: Then she fell over into my lap and I drove on.
examples.translation_ko: 그러자 그녀가 내 무릎 위로 쓰러졌고 나는 계속 운전했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Mr. McKee was asleep on a chair with his fists clenched in his lap, like a photograph of a man of action.
examples.translation_ko: 맥키 씨는 의자에서 잠들어 있었는데, 무릎 위에 주먹을 꽉 쥔 채로 있는 모습이 마치 행동하는 남자의 사진 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her hands lay on her lap motionless, one in the other loosely clasped.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 손은 무릎 위에 움직이지 않은 채 놓여 있었고, 한 손이 다른 손을 느슨하게 감싸고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Mrs. MacAndrew smoothed down the lap of her gown, and gold bangles fell over her wrists.
examples.translation_ko: 맥앤드류 부인은 무릎 위의 드레스를 매만졌고, 금팔찌들이 손목 위로 흘러내렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin convincō (“I refute, prove”), from con- + vincō (“I conquer, vanquish”). Doublet of convict. Displaced native Old English oferr...
definition_en: To persuade someone to believe or do something.

senses.gloss: To make someone believe, or feel sure about something, especially by using logic, argument or evidence.
senses.example: I wouldn't have or do something, unless I'm convinced that it's good.

senses.gloss: To persuade.
To overcome, conquer, vanquish.
senses.example: […]his two Chamberlaines / Will I with Wine, and Waſſell, ſo conuince, / That Memorie, the Warder of the Braine, / Shall be a Fume,[…]

examples.text: “You see I think everything’s terrible anyhow,” she went on in a convinced way.
examples.translation_ko: "있잖아, 난 모든 게 다 끔찍하다고 생각해." 그녀가 확신에 찬 어조로 계속 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For a moment I suspected that he was pulling my leg, but a glance at him convinced me otherwise.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 그가 나를 놀리는 것은 아닌가 의심했지만, 그를 한 번 보니 그렇지 않다는 확신이 들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was convinced he had been drinking, and I smiled.
examples.translation_ko: 술을 마셨다고 확신했고, 나는 미소를 지었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You know, I’m convinced you were mistaken about Charles being alone.
examples.translation_ko: "있잖아요, 찰스가 혼자라고 하신 말씀이 틀렸다고 확신해요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English createn, from Latin creātus, the perfect passive participle of creō, see -ate (verb-forming suffix). In this sense, mostly disp...
definition_en: To make or bring into existence something new.

senses.gloss: To bring into existence out of nothing, without the prior existence of the materials or elements used.
senses.example: In the beginning God created yᵉ heauen and the earth. And the earth was without forme & voyde, and darkenes was vpon the depe, & the Spirit of God moued vpon the waters.

senses.gloss: To make or produce from other (e.g. raw, unrefined or scattered) materials or combinable elements or ideas; to design or invest with a new form, shape, function, etc.
senses.example: Couturiers create exclusive garments for an affluent clientele.

senses.gloss: To bring into existence; (sometimes in particular:)
senses.example: You can create the color orange by mixing yellow and red.

examples.text: He must have looked up at an unfamiliar sky through frightening leaves and shivered as he found what a grotesque thing a rose is and how raw the sunlight was upon the scarcely created grass.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 무서운 나뭇잎 사이로 낯선 하늘을 올려다보았을 것이고, 장미가 얼마나 기괴한 것인지, 겨우 자라난 풀 위의 햇빛이 얼마나 날것인지 깨달으며 몸서리쳤을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It created profound astonishment, and wild rumours were current.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 깊은 충격을 불러일으켰고, 온갖 터무니없는 소문들이 돌았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “And the passion that held Strickland was a passion to create beauty.
examples.translation_ko: "그리고 스트릭랜드를 사로잡은 열정은 아름다움을 창조하려는 열정이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English summe, from Old French summe, from Latin summa (“highest point; sum”), from summus (“highest”).
definition_en: The total or amount of something.

senses.gloss: A quantity obtained by addition or aggregation.
senses.example: The sum of 3 and 4 is 7.

senses.gloss: An arithmetic computation, especially one posed to a student as an exercise (not necessarily limited to addition).
senses.example: We're learning about division, and the sums are tricky.

senses.gloss: A quantity of money.
senses.example: […]With a great ſumme obteined I this freedome.

examples.text: “I got a Jew in, and he gave me a round sum for the lot.
examples.translation_ko: "유대인 하나를 불러서 모든 것을 일괄로 넘겼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I’d send you a certain sum of money, and you could give it him gradually, as he needed it.”
examples.translation_ko: "일정한 금액을 당신에게 보내드릴 테니, 그가 필요할 때마다 조금씩 나누어 주시면 됩니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English eyed, eied, iȝed, y-yȝed, equivalent to eye + -ed.
definition_en: Having or using one's eyes.

senses.gloss: Having eyes.
Having eye-like spots.
senses.example: The back of the beetle was eyed to make it appear to be a snake to a predator.

senses.gloss: Having the specified kind or number of eyes.
senses.example: Three victims in chains—and one of them, the little servant, the sad-eyed angel.

examples.text: After a moment the proprietor emerged from the interior of his establishment and gazed hollow-eyed at the car.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 후 주인이 가게 안쪽에서 나와 움푹 들어간 눈으로 차를 바라보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As Gatsby closed the door of “the Merton College Library” I could have sworn I heard the owl-eyed man break into ghostly laughter.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비가 "머튼 칼리지 도서관"의 문을 닫을 때, 나는 부엉이 눈의 남자가 유령 같은 웃음을 터뜨리는 소리를 들었다고 맹세할 수 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: On the easel was a half-finished picture of a smiling Italian peasant, holding a bunch of grapes over the head of a dark-eyed girl.
examples.translation_ko: 이젤 위에는 미소 짓는 이탈리아 농부가 검은 눈의 소녀 머리 위로 포도송이를 들고 있는 반쯤 완성된 그림이 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The Chink’s Head was a name the beach-combers gave to a wretched inn off the Rue Bouterie, kept by a one-eyed Chinaman, where for six sous you could sleep in a cot and for three on the floor.
examples.translation_ko: 중국인 머리라는 곳은 해변의 부랑자들이 루 부트리 거리 근처의 한심한 여관에 붙인 이름이었는데, 외눈박이 중국인이 운영하는 곳으로 6수를 내면 침대에서, 3수를 내면 바닥에서 잘 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French gratitude, from Medieval Latin grātitūdō (“thankfulness”), from Latin grātus (“thankful”). Displaced native Old English þancung.
definition_en: A feeling of appreciation for something.

senses.gloss: The state of being grateful.

examples.text: “Be ver’ nice,” said Mr. Sloane, without gratitude.
examples.translation_ko: "아주 좋겠군요." 슬론 씨가 고마워하는 기색도 없이 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “She’s much obliged, I’m sure,” said another friend, without gratitude, “but you got her dress all wet when you stuck her head in the pool.”
examples.translation_ko: "고마워하실 거예요." 다른 친구가 감사함 없이 말했다. "하지만 당신이 그녀 머리를 수영장에 처박을 때 드레스를 다 젖게 만들었잖아요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was a man without any conception of gratitude.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 감사라는 개념 자체가 없는 사람이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was an obsession so complete that there was no room in his soul for prudence or gratitude.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 너무나 완전한 강박이어서 그의 영혼에는 신중함이나 감사함이 들어설 여지가 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French impacient (modern French impatient), from Latin impatiēns. By surface analysis, im- + patient.
definition_en: Having or showing a tendency to become annoyed or irritated when waiting for something.

senses.gloss: Restless, short of temper, and intolerant of delays.
senses.example: She dances when she becomes impatient.

senses.gloss: Anxious and eager, especially to begin or have something.
Not to be borne; unendurable.
senses.example:
Dismayed with so defperate deadly wound,
And eke impatient of unwonted payne,
He lowdly bray'd with beastly yelling sownd

examples.text: He was never quite still; there was always a tapping foot somewhere or the impatient opening and closing of a hand.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 결코 완전히 가만히 있지 못했다. 어디선가 항상 발을 두드리거나 손을 조급하게 쥐었다 폈다 하곤 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I shouldn’t have been so impatient.
examples.translation_ko: 그렇게 성급하게 굴지 말았어야 했는데.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Dirk, you make me impatient,” said Mrs. Stroeve.
examples.translation_ko: "더크, 당신은 정말 답답해요." 스트루브 부인이 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French sardonique, from Latin sardonius, from Ancient Greek σαρδόνιος (sardónios), alternative form of σαρδάνιος (sardánios, “bitter or scornf...
definition_en: Expressing contempt or disdain through irony.

senses.gloss: Scornfully mocking or cynical.
senses.example: He distances himself from people with his nasty, sardonic laughter.

senses.gloss: Disdainfully or ironically humorous.

examples.text: I could see his sardonic smile.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그의 냉소적인 미소를 볼 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then he gave the sardonic smile which was usual with him.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 평소와 같은 냉소적인 미소를 지었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English rollen, partly from Old French roller, roler, röeler, röoler, from Medieval Latin rotulāre (“to roll; to revolve”), from Latin ...
definition_en: To move or cause to move with a rotating motion.

senses.gloss: To revolve by turning over and over; to move by turning on a horizontal axis; to impel forward with a revolving motion on a supporting surface.
senses.example: To roll a wheel, a ball, or a barrel.

senses.gloss: To wrap (something) round on itself; to form into a spherical or cylindrical body by causing to turn over and over.
senses.example: To roll a sheet of paper; to roll clay or putty into a ball.

senses.gloss: To bind or involve by winding, as with a bandage; to enwrap; often with up.
senses.example: To roll up the vase in bubble wrap.

examples.text: The dilatory limousine came rolling up the drive.
examples.translation_ko: 느릿느릿한 리무진이 차도를 따라 굴러 올라왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I laughed aloud as the yolks of their eyeballs rolled toward us in haughty rivalry.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 눈동자가 거만한 경쟁심을 담고 우리 쪽으로 굴러오자 나는 큰 소리로 웃었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He rolled up to him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 비틀거리며 그에게 다가갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: And you want to roll yourself in it.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 그 속에서 뒹굴고 싶어져.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English blowen, from Old English blāwan (“to blow, breathe, inflate, sound”), from Proto-West Germanic *blāan, from Proto-Germanic *blē...
definition_en: A sudden gust of wind.

senses.gloss: To produce an air current.
senses.example: Hark how it rains and blows!

senses.gloss: To propel by an air current (or, if under water, a water current), usually with the mouth.
senses.example: Blow the dust off that book and open it up.

senses.gloss: To be propelled by an air current.
senses.example: The leaves blow through the streets in the fall.

examples.text: His own face was covered with blood from a blow on the nose.
examples.translation_ko: 그 자신의 얼굴도 코를 맞아 피투성이가 되어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was just going to make a great hole in the picture, I had my arm all ready for the blow, when suddenly I seemed to see it.”
examples.translation_ko: 막 그림에 큰 구멍을 뚫으려던 참이었다. 팔을 들어 내리칠 준비를 모두 마쳤는데, 갑자기 그것이 보이는 것 같았다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English relacion, relacioun, from Anglo-Norman relacioun and Old French relacion (whence French relation), from Latin relātiō, noun of ...
definition_en: A connection or association between people or things.

senses.gloss: The manner in which two things may be associated.
senses.example: The relation between diet and health is complex.

senses.gloss: A member of one's extended family; a relative.
senses.example: Yes, he's a relation of mine, but only a distant one.

senses.gloss: A relationship; the manner in which and tone with which people or states, etc. interact.
senses.example: the foreign relations of the United States

examples.text: Her grey, sun-strained eyes stared straight ahead, but she had deliberately shifted our relations, and for a moment I thought I loved her.
examples.translation_ko: 햇빛에 지친 그녀의 회색 눈동자가 정면을 응시하고 있었지만, 그녀는 의도적으로 우리 사이의 관계를 바꿔놓았고, 순간 나는 그녀를 사랑한다고 생각했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She had relations there.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀에게는 그곳에 친척이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Our relations were peculiar.
examples.translation_ko: 우리의 관계는 묘했다.

definition_en: To prevent something bad from happening or to keep something safe.

senses.gloss: To help (somebody) to survive, or rescue (somebody or something) from harm.
senses.example: She was saved from drowning by a passer-by.

senses.gloss: To keep (something) safe; to safeguard.
senses.example: Thou hast[…]quitted all to save / A world from utter loss.

senses.gloss: To spare (somebody) from effort, or from something undesirable.
senses.example: I'll save you / That labour, sir. All's now done.

examples.text: * Save $5.00 [crossed out] $3.00 per week
examples.translation_ko: * 일주일에 5달러 [지워짐] 3달러씩 저축하기
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He stretched out his hand desperately as if to snatch only a wisp of air, to save a fragment of the spot that she had made lovely for him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 한 줌의 공기라도 붙잡으려는 듯, 그녀가 자신에게 사랑스럽게 만들어준 그 장소의 한 조각이라도 구하려는 듯 필사적으로 손을 뻗었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Perhaps we can save him.
examples.translation_ko: 어쩌면 그를 살릴 수도 있을 거야.

examples.text: She’s saved several hundred francs.’
examples.translation_ko: 그 애는 몇백 프랑을 모아뒀어요.'
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sharply, scharply, from Old English sċearplīċe (“sharply, smartly”), equivalent to sharp + -ly.
definition_en: Used to describe something that is sharp or cutting.

senses.gloss: So as to terminate in a sharp point or edge.
senses.example: The stick was sharply tapered at one end.

senses.gloss: Rapidly, abruptly.
senses.example: When I touched the snake it recoiled sharply.

senses.gloss: Suddenly and intensely like a gasp, but typically as the result of an emotional reaction.

examples.text: Tom turned to Daisy sharply.
examples.translation_ko: 톰이 데이지를 향해 날카롭게 몸을 돌렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “That’s a great expression of yours, isn’t it?” said Tom sharply.
examples.translation_ko: "그거 자네 특유의 멋진 표현이지 않나?" 톰이 날카롭게 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I asked, rather sharply.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 다소 날카롭게 물었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English propertee, properte, propirte, proprete, borrowed from Anglo-Norman and Old French propreté, proprieté (“propriety, fitness, pr...
definition_en: A thing owned or possessed.

senses.gloss: Something that is owned.
senses.example: Leave those books alone! They are my property.

senses.gloss: A piece of real estate, such as a parcel of land.
senses.example: There is a large house on the property.

senses.gloss: Real estate; the business of selling houses.
senses.example: He works in property as a housing consultant.

examples.text: The none too savoury ramifications by which Ella Kaye, the newspaper woman, played Madame de Maintenon to his weakness and sent him to sea in a yacht, were common property of the turgid journalism in 1902.
examples.translation_ko: 신문 기자인 엘라 케이가 그의 약점에 대해 마담 드 맹트농 역할을 하며 그를 요트에 태워 바다로 내보낸 그리 깨끗하지 못한 복잡한 사연들은 1902년 선정적인 언론계의 공공연한 비밀이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Ata’s property was right away in a fold of the mountain.
examples.translation_ko: 아타의 집은 산 접힌 곳 저 멀리에 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I felt nothing of the peculiar thrill which it is the property of art to give.
examples.translation_ko: 예술이 주는 특별한 전율 같은 것은 전혀 느끼지 못했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English space, from Anglo-Norman space, variant of espace, espas et al., and spaze, variant of espace, from Latin spatium, from Proto-I...
definition_en: A vast and seemingly infinite three-dimensional expanse that contains all matter.

senses.gloss: The Distance between objects.
senses.example: But neere him, thy Angell / Becomes a feare: as being o're-powr'd, therefore / Make ſpace enough betweene you.

senses.gloss: A physical extent across two or three dimensions (sometimes for or to do something).
senses.example: They also wanted a larger garden and more space for home working.

senses.gloss: A physical extent in all directions, seen as an attribute of the universe (now usually considered as a part of space-time), or a mathematical model of this.
senses.example: These are not questions which can be decided by reference to our space intuitions, for our intuitions are confined to Euclidean space, and even there are insufficient, approximative.

examples.text: Their eyes met, and they stared together at each other, alone in space.
examples.translation_ko: 두 사람의 눈이 마주쳤고, 공간 속에서 홀로 남은 채 서로를 응시했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Tom flung open the door, blocked out its space for a moment with his thick body, and hurried into the room.
examples.translation_ko: 톰이 문을 벌컥 열더니 두툼한 몸으로 잠시 그 공간을 가리고는 서둘러 방 안으로 들어왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It gave you an awful sense of the infinity of space and of the endlessness of time.
examples.translation_ko: 무한한 공간과 끝없는 시간에 대한 경외감을 불러일으켰어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I gave him books to read, but after a page or two he would put the book down and stare miserably into space.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 읽을 책을 주었지만, 한두 페이지 읽고 나면 책을 내려놓고 비참하게 허공을 바라보곤 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To come together or unite with something.

senses.gloss: To connect or combine into one; to put together.
senses.example: The plumber joined the two ends of the broken pipe.

senses.gloss: To come together; to meet.
senses.example: Parallel lines never join.

senses.gloss: To enter into association or alliance, to unite in a common purpose.
senses.example: […]Nature and Fortune ioyn’d to make thee great.

examples.text: I got him to join the American Legion and he used to stand high there.
examples.translation_ko: 그를 재향군인회에 가입시켰더니 거기서 꽤 높은 지위에 올랐어.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Rather ashamed that on my first appearance I had stayed so late, I joined the last of Gatsby’s guests, who were clustered around him.
examples.translation_ko: 첫 방문에서 이렇게 늦게까지 머물렀다는 것이 다소 부끄러워서, 나는 개츠비 주위에 모여 있던 마지막 손님들에게 합류했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He seemed to see nothing, and did not notice that I had joined him till I touched him on the arm.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아무것도 보지 못하는 것 같았고, 내가 그의 팔을 건드릴 때까지 내가 그에게 다가온 것도 눈치채지 못했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But he made her promise that when she had buried him—did I tell you that I dug his grave with my own hands, for none of the natives would approach the infected house, and we buried him, she and I, sewn up in three pareos joined together, under the mango-tree—he made her promise that she would set fire to the house and not leave it till it was burned to the ground and not a stick remained.”
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그는 아타에게 자신을 매장한 후—내가 내 손으로 그의 무덤을 팠다고 말했던가, 원주민들은 아무도 감염된 집에 접근하려 하지 않았기에, 우리가, 그녀와 내가, 세 장의 파레오를 이어 붙인 천에 그를 싸서 망고나무 아래 묻었다—집에 불을 지르고 완전히 타서 재가 되고 나무 조각 하나도 남지 않을 때까지 그 자리를 떠나지 말라고 약속하게 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To provide food or drink to someone.

senses.gloss: An act of putting the ball or shuttlecock in play in various games.
senses.example: Whose serve is it?

senses.gloss: A portion of food or drink, a serving.
senses.example: Smirnoff Appleback was a finished drink, comprising a 50ml serve of Smirnoff, with ice and lemonade or ginger ale and equating to 1.9 units.

senses.gloss: An impressive presentation (especially of a person's appearance).
senses.example: That white eyeliner is such a serve.

examples.text: A pair of stage twins, who turned out to be the girls in yellow, did a baby act in costume, and champagne was served in glasses bigger than finger-bowls.
examples.translation_ko: 무대 쌍둥이 한 쌍이 나타났는데, 알고 보니 노란 옷을 입은 그 소녀들이었고, 의상을 입고 아기 연기를 했으며, 샴페인은 핑거볼보다 큰 잔에 담겨 나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The first supper—there would be another one after midnight—was now being served, and Jordan invited me to join her own party, who were spread around a table on the other side of the garden.
examples.translation_ko: 첫 번째 만찬—자정 후에 또 다른 만찬이 있을 예정이었다—이 이제 막 시작되었고, 조던은 나를 자신의 일행에 합류하자고 초대했는데, 그들은 정원 반대편 테이블 주위에 흩어져 앉아 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I supposed he had gone back to the shabby attic which served him as a studio.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아마 화실로 쓰고 있던 그 초라한 다락방으로 돌아갔을 것이라 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But the impression is fleeting, and serves only to give a greater acuteness to the enjoyment of the moment.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그런 인상은 순간적이며, 다만 현재 순간의 즐거움을 더욱 예리하게 만들어줄 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: The commander of a ship or aircraft.

senses.gloss: A chief or leader.
