examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Americans, while willing, even eager, to be serfs, have always been obstinate about being peasantry.
examples.translation_ko: 미국인들은 농노가 되는 것은 기꺼이, 심지어 열망하면서도, 소작농이 되는 것에 대해서는 언제나 완고하게 거부해왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His red face was shining with sweat, and he had a look of comic agitation, but there was in his round, surprised eyes an eager light.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 붉은 얼굴은 땀으로 번들거렸고, 우스꽝스럽게 동요한 표정을 짓고 있었지만, 그의 둥글고 놀란 눈에는 간절한 빛이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Whenever she went out—and compassion for her misadventure made her friends eager to entertain her—she bore a demeanour that was perfect.
examples.translation_ko: 외출할 때마다—그녀의 불운에 대한 동정심으로 친구들이 그녀를 대접하려 애썼다—그녀는 완벽한 태도를 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English altogeder, altogedere, equivalent to al- (“all”) + together. Cognate with Scots awthegither (“altogether”), Middle High German ...
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is complete or total.

senses.gloss: Completely, wholly, or without exception.
senses.example: Police did not seem altogether satisfied with my alibi.

senses.gloss: On the whole; with everything considered.
senses.example: Altogether, I'm sorry it happened.

senses.gloss: With everything included.
senses.example: Altogether, your bill comes to $6.99.

examples.text: The murmur trembled on the verge of coherence, sank down, mounted excitedly, and then ceased altogether.
examples.translation_ko: 그 중얼거림은 무슨 말인지 알아들을 듯 말 듯 떨리다가 가라앉았다가 다시 흥분되게 높아지더니 완전히 멈췄다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “It wasn’t altogether satisfactory.”
examples.translation_ko: "완전히 만족스럽지는 않았거든."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I did not altogether believe my eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 내 눈을 완전히 믿을 수가 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English usualli, equivalent to usual + -ly. Displaced native Old English ġewunelīċe.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is the normal or expected state of affairs.

senses.gloss: Most of the time; less than always, but more than occasionally.
senses.example: Except for one or two days a year, he usually walks to work.

senses.gloss: Under normal conditions.

examples.text: You see, I usually find myself among strangers because I drift here and there trying to forget the sad things that happened to me.”
examples.translation_ko: 아시다시피, 나는 보통 낯선 사람들 사이에 있게 되는데, 내게 일어난 슬픈 일들을 잊으려고 이곳저곳을 떠돌아다니기 때문입니다."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Usually her voice came over the wire as something fresh and cool, as if a divot from a green golf-links had come sailing in at the office window, but this morning it seemed harsh and dry.
examples.translation_ko: 평소 그녀의 목소리는 전화선을 타고 신선하고 시원하게 들려왔는데, 마치 푸른 골프장에서 떼어낸 잔디 조각이 사무실 창문으로 날아든 것 같았지만, 이날 아침에는 거칠고 메마르게 들렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His face, usually so rosy, was now strangely mottled.
examples.translation_ko: 평소 그렇게 장밋빛이던 그의 얼굴이 이제는 이상하게 얼룩덜룩했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Miss Waterford was giving a tea-party, and her small room was more than usually full.
examples.translation_ko: 워터포드 양이 다과회를 열고 있었는데, 그녀의 작은 방은 평소보다 더욱 붐볐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English rawe, raw, rau, from Old English hrēaw (“raw, uncooked”), from Proto-West Germanic *hrau, from Proto-Germanic *hrawaz, *hrēwaz ...
definition_en: Uncooked or unprocessed.

senses.gloss: (of food) Not cooked.
senses.example: There's nothing but raw fish in the freezer.

senses.gloss: Subsisting on, or pertaining to, a diet of raw food.
senses.example: I was 100% raw from 2014 until early 2018.

senses.gloss: Not treated or processed; in a natural state, unrefined, unprocessed. (of materials, products, etc.)
senses.example: raw cane sugar

examples.text: After half an hour, the sun shone again, and the grocer’s automobile rounded Gatsby’s drive with the raw material for his servants’ dinner—I felt sure he wouldn’t eat a spoonful.
examples.translation_ko: 30분 후 해가 다시 비치자, 식료품상의 자동차가 개츠비의 진입로를 돌아 그의 하인들 저녁 식사 재료를 가지고 왔다—그는 한 숟가락도 먹지 않을 것이 분명했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He must have looked up at an unfamiliar sky through frightening leaves and shivered as he found what a grotesque thing a rose is and how raw the sunlight was upon the scarcely created grass.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 무서운 나뭇잎 사이로 낯선 하늘을 올려다보았을 것이고, 장미가 얼마나 기괴한 것인지, 겨우 자라난 풀 위의 햇빛이 얼마나 날것인지 깨달으며 몸서리쳤을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She looked upon life as an opportunity for writing novels and the public as her raw material.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 인생을 소설을 쓸 기회로, 대중을 자신의 원재료로 여겼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When he had seen her he was taken into another room and given dinner—raw fish, fried bananas, and chicken—que sais-je, the typical dinner of the indigène—and while he was eating it he saw a young girl being driven away from the door in tears.
examples.translation_ko: 할머니를 진찰한 후 그는 다른 방으로 안내되어 저녁을 대접받았는데—생선회, 튀긴 바나나, 닭고기—뭐 그런 것들로, 전형적인 원주민 식사였다—그가 식사를 하고 있는데 어떤 젊은 소녀가 문 앞에서 울면서 쫓겨나는 것을 보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English framen, fremen, fremmen (“to construct, build, strengthen, refresh, perform, execute, profit, avail”), from Old English framian...
definition_en: A structure of wood or metal to hold a window or door.

senses.gloss: To fit, as for a specific end or purpose; make suitable or comfortable; adapt; adjust.
senses.example: The human mind is framed to be influenced.

senses.gloss: To construct by fitting together or uniting various parts; fabricate by union of constituent parts.
senses.example:
Nature that fram’d vs of foure Elements,
Warring within our breaſts for regiment,
Doth teach vs all to haue aſpyring minds:

senses.gloss: To bring or put into form or order; adjust the parts or elements of; compose; contrive; plan; devise.
senses.example: As for America’s constitution, speaking as the court’s originalist-in-chief, all that mattered was what its words meant when it was framed.

examples.text: They must look queer in their garish frames on the walls of the peasant house.
examples.translation_ko: 농가 벽에 걸린 화려한 액자 속에서 그 그림들은 분명 어색해 보일 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a deep, resonant voice, fitted to his massive frame, and a keen sense of the dramatic.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 거대한 체구에 어울리는 깊고 울림 있는 목소리와 예리한 극적 감각을 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French artistique, from artiste + -ique. By surface analysis, artist + -ic.
definition_en: Having or showing a good sense of art.

senses.gloss: Having or revealing creative skill.
Relating to or characteristic of art or artists.
Aesthetically pleasing.

examples.text: He informed me that he was in the “artistic game,” and I gathered later that he was a photographer and had made the dim enlargement of Mrs. Wilson’s mother which hovered like an ectoplasm on the wall.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자신이 "예술계"에 종사한다고 알려주었는데, 나중에 알고 보니 그는 사진사였고 벽에 유령처럼 걸려 있는 윌슨 부인의 어머니 사진을 흐릿하게 확대한 것도 그의 작품이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was deliberately artistic.
examples.translation_ko: 의도적으로 예술적인 분위기였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was chaste, artistic, and dull.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 단정하고 예술적이었지만 따분했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fredom, freedom, from Old English frēodōm (“freedom, state of free-will, charter, emancipation, deliverance”), from Proto-West ...
definition_en: The power or right to act, speak, or think as one wants without being controlled or restrained.

senses.gloss: The state of being free.
senses.example: Having recently been released from prison, he didn't know what to do with his newfound freedom.

senses.gloss: The lack of a specific constraint, or of constraints in general; a state of being free, unconstrained.
senses.example: Freedom of speech is a basic democratic value.

senses.gloss: The right or privilege of unrestricted use or access
senses.example: Freedom of a city

examples.text: He had casually conferred on me the freedom of the neighbourhood.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 무심코 나에게 이 동네의 자유를 선사해 주었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His family were enormously wealthy—even in college his freedom with money was a matter for reproach—but now he’d left Chicago and come East in a fashion that rather took your breath away: for instance, he’d brought down a string of polo ponies from Lake Forest.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 가문은 엄청나게 부유했다—대학 시절에도 그의 돈 쓰는 방식은 비난거리였다—하지만 이제 그는 시카고를 떠나 동부로 온 방식이 숨이 막힐 정도였다: 예를 들어, 레이크 포레스트에서 폴로 조랑말 한 떼를 끌고 내려온 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Why should I give him his freedom?”
examples.translation_ko: "내가 왜 그에게 자유를 주어야 하죠?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You rejoice in your freedom, and you feel that at last you can call your soul your own.
examples.translation_ko: 자유를 만끽하며, 마침내 네 영혼을 온전히 네 것이라고 부를 수 있다고 느끼겠지.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From mis- + fortune.
definition_en: A circumstance or event that is unfortunate.

senses.gloss: Bad luck.
senses.example: The worst tour I have ever had the misfortune to experience.

senses.gloss: An undesirable event such as an accident.
senses.example: She had to come to terms with a number of misfortunes.

examples.text: You’re the most loathsome beast that it’s ever been my misfortune to meet.
examples.translation_ko: 당신은 내가 불행하게도 만난 사람 중 가장 역겨운 짐승이에요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was taken aback by her assumption that I knew all about her domestic misfortune.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 그녀의 가정 불화에 대해 모든 것을 알고 있다고 단정하는 그녀의 태도에 나는 당황했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English exercise, from Old French exercise, from Latin exercitium.
definition_en: Physical activity to maintain or improve health.

senses.gloss: Any activity designed to develop or hone a skill or ability.
senses.example: The teacher told us that the next exercise is to write an essay.

senses.gloss: Activity intended to improve physical, or sometimes mental, strength and fitness.
senses.example: Swimming is good exercise.

senses.gloss: A setting in action or practicing; employment in the proper mode of activity; exertion; application; use.
senses.example: The law guarantees us the free exercise of our rights.

examples.text: I don’t take enough exercise.
examples.translation_ko: 운동을 충분히 하지 않아요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I can’t imagine a more wonderful exercise of it than to move the souls of men to pity or terror.”
examples.translation_ko: 사람들의 영혼을 연민이나 공포로 움직이는 것보다 더 멋진 권력의 행사는 상상할 수 없다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English obligen, from Old French obligier, obliger, from Latin obligō, obligāre, from ob- + ligō. Doublet of obligate, taken straight f...
definition_en: Obligate or require someone to do something.

senses.gloss: To constrain someone by force or by social, moral or legal means.
senses.example: I am obliged to report to the police station every week.

senses.gloss: To do (someone) a service or favour (hence, originally, creating an obligation).
senses.example: He obliged me by not parking his car in the drive.

senses.gloss: To be indebted to someone.
senses.example: I am obliged to you for your recent help.

examples.text: “I’m much obliged but I couldn’t take on any more work.”
examples.translation_ko: "고맙긴 하지만 더 이상 일을 맡을 수는 없어요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But I wanted to leave things in order and not just trust that obliging and indifferent sea to sweep my refuse away.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 나는 모든 일을 정리하고 떠나고 싶었고, 그저 친절하고 무관심한 바다가 내 찌꺼기들을 쓸어가 주리라 믿고만 있을 수는 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: You felt that you obliged her by accepting her sympathy.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 동정을 받아들임으로써 당신이 그녀에게 호의를 베푸는 것 같은 느낌이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I took them to oblige Monsieur Stroeve, and I said I would sell them if I could.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브 씨를 도와드리려고 그림들을 맡았고, 팔 수 있으면 팔겠다고 말했을 뿐입니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English mel, from Old English mǣl (“measure, time, occasion, set time, time for eating, meal”), from Proto-West Germanic *māl, from Pro...
definition_en: A single act of eating.

senses.gloss: Food that is prepared and eaten, usually at a specific time, and usually in a comparatively large quantity (as opposed to a snack).
senses.example: Breakfast is the morning meal, lunch is the noon meal, and dinner, or supper, is the evening meal.

senses.gloss: Food served or eaten as a repast.
senses.example: This is the meal pleasantly set . . . . this is the meat and drink for natural hunger, / It is for the wicked just the same as the righteous . . . .

senses.gloss: A break taken by a police officer in order to eat.
senses.example: “I was on meal when I heard the call on the radio and recognized the address. What the hell?”

examples.text: “I’d like a decent meal.”
examples.translation_ko: "제대로 된 식사를 하고 싶어."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You can have your meals here.
examples.translation_ko: 식사는 여기서 할 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English trimen, trymen, trümen, from Old English trymman (“to make firm; strengthen”), from Proto-West Germanic *trummjan, from Proto-G...
definition_en: To cut or shape something to a smaller size.

senses.gloss: To reduce slightly; to cut; especially, to remove excess.
senses.example: He trimmed his beard before the interview.

senses.gloss: To decorate or adorn; especially of a Christmas tree.
senses.example: They traditionally trim the tree on Christmas Eve.

senses.gloss: To adjust the positions of control surfaces, sometimes using trim tabs, so as to modify or eliminate the aircraft's tendency to pitch, roll, or yaw when the cockpit controls are released.

examples.text: His tanned skin was drawn attractively tight on his face and his short hair looked as though it were trimmed every day.
examples.translation_ko: 그을린 피부가 얼굴에 매력적으로 팽팽하게 당겨져 있었고, 짧은 머리는 매일 다듬는 것처럼 보였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Wellington is trim and neat and English; it reminds you of a seaport town on the South Coast.
examples.translation_ko: 웰링턴은 단정하고 깔끔하며 영국적이다. 남해안의 항구 도시를 연상시킨다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She made an appointment, and I went to the trim little house on Campden Hill which she now inhabited.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 약속을 잡아주어서 나는 그녀가 지금 살고 있는 캠든 힐의 단정한 작은 집으로 갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English browe, from Old English brū, from Proto-West Germanic *brāwu, from Proto-Germanic *brūwō, from Proto-Indo-European *h₃bʰrúHs (“...
definition_en: The upper part of the eye or face.

senses.gloss: The bony ridge over the eyes, upon which the eyebrows are located.
The eyebrow.
senses.example: And his arch’d brow, pulled o’er his eyes, / With solemn proof proclaims him wise.

senses.gloss: The forehead.
senses.example: Mr. Banks’ panama hat was in one hand, while the other drew a handkerchief across his perspiring brow.

examples.text: She showed a surprising amount of character about it too—looked at the coroner with determined eyes under that corrected brow of hers, and swore that her sister had never seen Gatsby, that her sister was completely happy with her husband, that her sister had been into no mischief whatever.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 이 일에 대해 놀라울 정도로 의연함을 보였다—교정한 눈썹 아래 단호한 눈으로 검시관을 바라보며, 언니는 개츠비를 본 적이 없다고, 언니는 남편과 완전히 행복했다고, 언니는 어떤 잘못도 저지르지 않았다고 맹세했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had his mother’s candid brow and fine, reflective eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 어머니의 솔직한 이마와 아름답고 사려 깊은 눈을 닮았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She was very pale now, and her fine brow was dark and lowering.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 이제 매우 창백했고, 아름다운 이마는 어둡고 험악해 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English charme, from Old French charme (“chant, magic spell”), from Latin carmen (“song, incantation”).
definition_en: A quality that makes something or someone attractive and enjoyable.

senses.gloss: An object, act or words believed to have magic power (usually carries a positive connotation).
senses.example: a charm against evil

senses.gloss: The ability to persuade, delight or arouse admiration.
senses.example: He had great personal charm.

senses.gloss: A small trinket on a bracelet or chain, etc., traditionally supposed to confer luck upon the wearer.
senses.example: She wears a charm bracelet on her wrist.

examples.text: It was full of money—that was the inexhaustible charm that rose and fell in it, the jingle of it, the cymbals’ song of it … High in a white palace the king’s daughter, the golden girl …
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 돈으로 가득했다—그 안에서 솟아오르고 가라앉는 무궁무진한 매력, 그것의 짤랑거림, 그것의 심벌즈 노래가 바로 그것이었다 … 하얀 궁전 높은 곳의 왕의 딸, 황금빛 소녀가 …
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Perhaps her naivete was her greatest charm.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 그녀의 순진함이 가장 큰 매력이었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She looked at him with the grave cheerfulness which was one of her charms.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그녀의 매력 중 하나인 진지한 명랑함으로 그를 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English boren, from Old English borian (“to pierce”), from Proto-West Germanic *borōn, from Proto-Germanic *burōną.
Compare Danish bore...
definition_en: To make someone feel tired or annoyed by talking too much.

senses.gloss: To inspire boredom in somebody.
senses.example: to bore someone to death

senses.gloss: To make a hole through something.
senses.example: On June 8, 1872, the London & North Western Railway obtained powers to quadruple its main line, and a new tunnel was bored for the up and down slow lines.

senses.gloss: To make a hole with, or as if with, a boring instrument; to cut a circular hole by the rotary motion of a tool.
senses.example: to bore for water or oil

examples.text: “Does he bore you?”
examples.translation_ko: "당신은 지루하지 않나요?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Her face was set, and he saw that he was only boring her.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 얼굴은 굳어 있었고, 그는 자신이 그녀를 지겹게 하고 있을 뿐이라는 것을 깨달았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Abbreviation of chatter. The bird sense refers to the sound of its call.
definition_en: A brief conversation or talk.

senses.gloss: To be engaged in informal conversation.
senses.example: She chatted with her friend in the cafe.

senses.gloss: To talk more than a few words.
senses.example: I met my old friend in the street, so we chatted for a while.

senses.gloss: To talk of; to discuss.
senses.example: They chatted politics for a while.

examples.text: We smoked and chatted.
examples.translation_ko: 담배를 피우며 담소를 나누었지요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We began to chat about vintages and tobacco.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 포도주 연도와 담배에 대해 이야기하기 시작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English wast, waste (“a waste”, noun), from Anglo-Norman, Old Northern French wast, waste (“a waste”), from Frankish *wōstī (“a waste”)...
definition_en: To use or spend something carelessly.

senses.gloss: Excess of material, useless by-products, or damaged, unsaleable products; garbage; rubbish.
Excrement or urine.
senses.example: The cage was littered with animal waste.

senses.gloss: A wasteland; an uninhabited desolate region; a wilderness or desert.
senses.example: The pampas of Argentina and the chilly wastes of Patagonia, like the prairies and deserts of North America, were largely shunned by Spanish settlers until the 1870s.

examples.text: He was busy, and could waste no more time on us.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 바빴고, 우리에게 더 이상 시간을 낭비할 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was not a man with whom it was worth while wasting politeness.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 예의를 차릴 가치가 있는 사람이 아니었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French relief (“assistance”), from Old French relever (“to relieve”), from Latin relevare (“to raise up, make light”). See also relieve.
definition_en: A feeling of being less worried or anxious.

senses.gloss: The removal of stress or discomfort.
senses.example: I sighed with relief when I found out that my daughter hadn't got lost, but was waiting for me at home.

senses.gloss: The feeling associated with the removal of stress or discomfort.
senses.example: DfT's action was greeted with great relief in many quarters.

senses.gloss: Release from a post or duty, as when replaced by another.

examples.text: Doubtless there was a certain struggle and a certain relief.
examples.translation_ko: 분명 어떤 투쟁과 어떤 안도감이 있었을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was a great relief, and I tried very hard to die, but I seemed to bear an enchanted life.
examples.translation_ko: 정말 다행이었어. 나는 죽으려고 무척 애썼지만, 마법에 걸린 목숨을 타고난 것 같았거든.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They met with indifference, and would part with relief.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 무관심하게 만났고, 안도감을 느끼며 헤어질 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Here and there was an Italian cabinet surmounted with Delft, and here and there a bas-relief.
examples.translation_ko: 여기저기에는 델프트 도자기를 올린 이탈리아식 캐비닛이 있었고, 또 여기저기에는 부조가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French social, from Latin sociālis (“of or belonging to a companion or companionship or association, social”), from socius (“a companio...
definition_en: Relating to society or its organization.

senses.gloss: Being extroverted or outgoing.
senses.example: James is a very social guy; he knows lots of people.

senses.gloss: Of or relating to society.
senses.example: Teresa feels uncomfortable in certain social situations.

senses.gloss: Relating to social media or social networks.
senses.example: social gaming

examples.text: It was, of course, a purely social function.
examples.translation_ko: 물론 순전히 사교적인 모임이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was impossible to keep up our social pretences any longer.
examples.translation_ko: 더 이상 사교적인 체면을 유지하는 것은 불가능했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Balti پولو (polo, “ball”). Cognate with Tibetan པོ་ལོ (po lo), ཕོ་ལོང (pho long), སྤོ་ལོ (spo lo, “ball”).
definition_en: A sport played on horseback with a long-handled stick.

senses.gloss: A ball game where two teams of players on horseback use long-handled mallets to propel the ball along the ground and into their opponent's goal.
senses.example: There were polo fields – sometimes green, sometimes brown – where in the old days, people had actually played that strange game that seems like a drunken bet about golf and horse riding.

senses.gloss: The game of ice polo, one of the ancestors of ice hockey; a similar game played on the ice, or on a prepared floor, by players wearing skates.
A polo shirt.
senses.example: Then on the second floor there is the creepy boy’s section, which had little headless mannequins in premium polos ($39.50), rugby shirts ($49.50) and a precocious leather pilot jacket for $148.

examples.text: “Mrs. Buchanan … and Mr. Buchanan—” After an instant’s hesitation he added: “the polo player.”
examples.translation_ko: "뷰캐넌 부인… 그리고 뷰캐넌 씨—" 잠깐 망설인 후 그가 덧붙였다. "폴로 선수 말입니다."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But evidently the sound of it pleased Gatsby for Tom remained “the polo player” for the rest of the evening.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 분명히 그 말의 울림이 개츠비의 마음에 들었던 모양이었다. 톰은 그날 저녁 내내 "폴로 선수"로 남아 있었으니까.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The K.C. told us of a case he was engaged in, and the Colonel talked about polo.
examples.translation_ko: 왕실 변호사는 자신이 맡고 있는 사건에 대해 말했고, 대령은 폴로에 대해 이야기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I remembered from my previous meeting with him that he had a foolish face, and was proud of the fact that for the ten years before he left the army he had played polo three days a week.
examples.translation_ko: 이전에 만났을 때 그가 어리석은 얼굴을 하고 있었다는 것과, 군대를 떠나기 전 십 년 동안 일주일에 사흘씩 폴로를 쳤다는 사실을 자랑스러워했다는 것이 기억났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English clubbe, from Old Norse klubba, klumba (“cudgel”), from Proto-Germanic *klumpô (“clip, clasp; clump, lump; log, block”...
definition_en: A group of people with a shared interest or activity.

senses.gloss: An association of members joining together for some common purpose, especially sports or recreation.
The fees associated with belonging to such a club.
senses.example: He can have no right to the benefits of Society, who will not pay his Club towards the Support of it.

senses.gloss: A heavy object, often a kind of stick, intended for use as a bludgeoning weapon or a plaything.

examples.text: A massive and lethargic woman, who had been urging Daisy to play golf with her at the local club tomorrow, spoke in Miss Baedeker’s defence:
examples.translation_ko: 덩치가 크고 나른한 여자가 데이지에게 내일 동네 클럽에서 골프를 치자고 권하고 있었는데, 베데커 양을 변호하며 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was Jordan Baker; she often called me up at this hour because the uncertainty of her own movements between hotels and clubs and private houses made her hard to find in any other way.
examples.translation_ko: 조던 베이커였다. 그녀는 호텔과 클럽, 개인 저택들을 오가는 자신의 행적이 불분명해서 다른 방법으로는 찾기 어려웠기 때문에 종종 이 시간에 내게 전화를 걸었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When in an hour they crowded into a cab to go home, I strolled idly to my club.
examples.translation_ko: 한 시간 후 그들이 마차에 몰려 타고 집으로 돌아갈 때, 나는 한가롭게 클럽으로 걸어갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: My husband said he went to the club three or four nights a week to play bridge.
examples.translation_ko: 남편이 일주일에 서너 번 클럽에 가서 브리지를 친다고 했거든요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The verb is derived from earlier glimse (obsolete), from Middle English glimsen (“to dazzle; to glisten; to glance with the eyes”), possibly from O...
definition_en: A brief or casual look at something.

senses.gloss: To see or view (someone, or something tangible) briefly and incompletely.
To perceive (something intangible) briefly and incompletely.
senses.example: I have only begun to glimpse the magnitude of the problem.

senses.gloss: Chiefly followed by at or upon: to look at briefly and incompletely; to glance.
senses.example: The door always opens directly into the kitchen, without any vestibule; and, glimpsing in, you see that a cottager's life must be the very plainest and homeliest that ever was lived by men and women.

examples.text: He doesn’t know very much about Tom, though he says he’s read a Chicago paper for years just on the chance of catching a glimpse of Daisy’s name.”
examples.translation_ko: 그는 톰에 대해 별로 아는 게 없지만, 데이지의 이름을 언뜻이라도 볼 기회를 노려 시카고 신문을 수년간 읽어왔다고 말했다."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Then the valley of ashes opened out on both sides of us, and I had a glimpse of Mrs. Wilson straining at the garage pump with panting vitality as we went by.
examples.translation_ko: 그러자 잿빛 골짜기가 우리 양쪽으로 펼쳐졌고, 우리가 지나갈 때 윌슨 부인이 숨을 헐떡이며 활기차게 주유소 펌프질을 하는 모습이 눈에 들어왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I had a fleeting glimpse of a pursuit of the ineffable.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 형언할 수 없는 것을 추구하는 모습을 잠깐 엿보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was perhaps a little lonely, and it was with a touch of envy that I thought of the pleasant family life of which I had had a glimpse.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 아마도 조금 외로웠던 것 같고, 잠깐 엿본 그 즐거운 가정생활을 생각하며 약간의 부러움을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From happy + -ness.
definition_en: A state of being happy.

senses.gloss: The emotion of being happy; joy; elation.
senses.example: Yes, Aline, true happiness comes of true love, and true love should be independent of external influences.

senses.gloss: Prosperity, thriving, wellbeing.
Good luck; good fortune.
senses.example: All happineſſe bechance to thee in Millaine.

examples.text: “I’m p-paralysed with happiness.”
examples.translation_ko: "나는 행복해서 마-마비가 될 지경이야."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As I went over to say goodbye I saw that the expression of bewilderment had come back into Gatsby’s face, as though a faint doubt had occurred to him as to the quality of his present happiness.
examples.translation_ko: 작별 인사를 하러 다가가면서 나는 개츠비의 얼굴에 다시 당황스러운 표정이 떠오르는 것을 보았다. 마치 지금 자신이 느끼는 행복의 본질에 대해 희미한 의구심이 든 것처럼.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He spoke to her of the happiness of their life.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀에게 그들의 행복한 삶에 대해 이야기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I’m grateful for all the happiness you gave me in the past.”
examples.translation_ko: 당신이 과거에 내게 준 모든 행복에 감사합니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English grave, grafe, from Old English græf, grafu (“cave, grave, trench”), from Proto-West Germanic *grab, from Proto-Germanic *grabą,...
definition_en: A place where a dead body is buried.

senses.gloss: An excavation in the earth as a place of burial.
senses.example: Let mee not be ashamed, O Lord, for I haue called vpon thee: let the wicked be ashamed, and let them be silent in the graue.

senses.gloss: Any place of interment.
Any place containing one or more corpses.

examples.text: I felt that Strickland had kept his secret to the grave.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 자신의 비밀을 무덤까지 가져갔다는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She looked at him with the grave cheerfulness which was one of her charms.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그녀의 매력 중 하나인 진지한 명랑함으로 그를 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From earlier len (with excrescent -d, as in sound, round, etc.), from Middle English lenen, lænen, from Old English lǣnan (“to lend; give, grant, l...
definition_en: To give someone temporary use of something.

senses.gloss: To allow to be used by someone temporarily, on condition that it or its equivalent will be returned.
senses.example: I will only lend you my car if you fill up the tank.

senses.gloss: To make a loan.
To be suitable or applicable, to fit.
senses.example: Poems do not lend themselves to translation easily.

examples.text: “Did you really think I’d lend you money?”
examples.translation_ko: "정말로 내가 자네에게 돈을 빌려줄 거라고 생각했나?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: One day he asked me to lend him fifty francs.
examples.translation_ko: 어느 날 그가 나에게 50프랑을 빌려달라고 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English distance, distaunce, destance (“disagreement, dispute; discrimination; armed conflict; hostility; trouble; space between two po...
definition_en: The amount of space between two points.

senses.gloss: An amount of space between points (often geographical points), usually (but not necessarily) measured along a straight line.
senses.example: [O]bservations on the eclipses of Jupiter's satellites have demonstrated that light takes up no more than 8′ 7″ in passing from the sun to the earth, a distance of 95,000,000 miles.

senses.gloss: Chiefly in by a distance: a space of more than 30 lengths (about 80 yards or 7.3 metres) between two racehorses finishing a race, used to describe the margin of victory; also (archaic), any space of 240 yards (about 219.5 metres) on a racecourse.
Chiefly in from a distance: a place which is far away or remote; specifically (especially painting), a more remote part of a landscape or view as contrasted with the foreground.
senses.example: From a distance, you look like my friend / Even though we are at war / From a distance, I just cannot comprehend / What all this fighting's for // […] // God is watching us / From a distance

examples.text: We saw the three or four automobiles and the crowd when we were still some distance away.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 아직 꽤 멀리 떨어져 있을 때 서너 대의 자동차와 군중을 보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Compared to the great distance that had separated him from Daisy it had seemed very near to her, almost touching her.
examples.translation_ko: 그를 데이지로부터 갈라놓았던 그 먼 거리에 비하면, 그 불빛은 그녀에게 아주 가까이 있는 것처럼, 거의 그녀에게 닿을 듯이 보였었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As they stand they are like the figures in an old tapestry; they do not separate themselves from the background, and at a distance seem to lose their pattern, so that you have little but a pleasing piece of colour.
examples.translation_ko: 지금 상태로는 그들은 오래된 태피스트리 속 인물들 같다. 배경에서 분리되지 않고, 멀리서 보면 무늬가 흐려져서 그저 보기 좋은 색채 덩어리 정도로만 보인다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The beauty of the island is unveiled as diminishing distance shows you in distincter shape its lovely peaks, but it keeps its secret as you sail by, and, darkly inviolable, seems to fold itself together in a stony, inaccessible grimness.
examples.translation_ko: 거리가 줄어들면서 섬의 아름다운 봉우리들이 더욱 뚜렷한 모습을 드러내며 섬의 아름다움이 펼쳐지지만, 배가 지나쳐 갈 때에도 섬은 여전히 비밀을 간직한 채 어둡고 신성불가침한 모습으로 돌처럼 굳고 접근할 수 없는 험상궂음 속에 몸을 감싸고 있는 듯하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French concerner, from Medieval Latin concernō, concernere (“I distinguish, have respect to”), from Latin concernō (“I mix, si...
definition_en: To feel worried or anxious about something.

senses.gloss: That which affects one’s welfare or happiness. A matter of interest to someone.
senses.example: Mark’s health was of great concern to Connie.

senses.gloss: The placement of interest or worry on a subject.
senses.example: Most people in Australia have no concern for the recent events in London.

senses.gloss: A worry; a sense that something may be wrong; an identification of a possible problem.
senses.example: Let me know if you have any questions or concerns about the document.

examples.text: Mrs. Wilson was first concerned with the dog.
examples.translation_ko: 윌슨 부인은 먼저 개를 돌보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I don’t want to pry into what doesn’t concern me.
examples.translation_ko: 저와 상관없는 일에 참견하고 싶지 않습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I felt a certain shyness at referring to matters which were no concern of mine.
examples.translation_ko: 나와는 상관없는 일에 대해 언급하는 것이 어딘지 부끄러웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English message, from Old French message, from Early Medieval Latin missāticum, derived from Latin mittere (“send”), ultimately from Pr...
definition_en: A communication or information conveyed.

senses.gloss: A communication, or what is communicated; any concept or information conveyed.
senses.example: We've just received an urgent message from the President.

senses.gloss: An underlying theme or conclusion to be drawn from something.
senses.example: The main message of the novel is that time heals all wounds.

senses.gloss: An errand.
senses.example: I had been on a message for my father, and was walking home along the road, when I saw a tall, fine lassie coming over the bogland on the right hand side of the road.

examples.text: No telephone message arrived, but the butler went without his sleep and waited for it until four o’clock—until long after there was anyone to give it to if it came.
examples.translation_ko: 전화는 오지 않았지만 집사는 잠도 자지 않고 네 시까지 기다렸다—전화가 와도 전해줄 사람이 아무도 없게 된 지 한참이 지난 후까지.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I tried to think about Gatsby then for a moment, but he was already too far away, and I could only remember, without resentment, that Daisy hadn’t sent a message or a flower.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 잠시 개츠비를 생각해보려 했지만, 그는 이미 너무 멀리 가 있었고, 나는 원망 없이 다만 데이지가 편지 한 통이나 꽃 한 송이도 보내지 않았다는 것만 기억할 수 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Dirk, filled with compassion, begged her to take the message at once.
examples.translation_ko: 연민으로 가득 찬 더크는 그녀에게 당장 그 말을 전해달라고 애원했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I gave the boy a message for Ata that I would come whenever she sent for me.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 소년에게 아타에게 전할 말을 맡겼다. 그녀가 부르면 언제든 오겠다고.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Variant of usque, abbreviation of usquebaugh (compare obsolete whiskybae), from Scottish Gaelic uisge-beatha (“water of life”), calque of Medieval ...
definition_en: A type of strong alcoholic liquor distilled from fermented grain mash.

senses.gloss: Alternative form of whiskey, an alcoholic liquor distilled from fermented grain, usually aged in oak barrels, (particularly) Scotch; a drink of this liquor.

examples.text: The Colonel gulped down his whisky.
examples.translation_ko: 대령은 위스키를 단숨에 들이켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The Colonel asked for a whisky-and-soda.
examples.translation_ko: 대령은 위스키 소다를 달라고 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English stiff, stiffe, stif, from Old English stīf, from Proto-West Germanic *stīf, from Proto-Germanic *stīfaz, from Proto-Indo-Europe...
definition_en: Having or showing a lack of flexibility.

senses.gloss: Rigid; hard to bend; inflexible.
senses.example: You have discovered the corpse of Captain Willem of the MSV Majesty. His stiff fingers are wrapped tightly around a small datapad.

senses.gloss: Inflexible; rigid.
Formal in behavior; unrelaxed.

examples.text: “I’m stiff,” she complained, “I’ve been lying on that sofa for as long as I can remember.”
examples.translation_ko: "몸이 뻣뻣해." 그녀가 불평했다. "기억하는 한 계속 저 소파에 누워 있었거든."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He set down the receiver and came toward us, glistening slightly, to take our stiff straw hats.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 수화기를 내려놓고 살짝 땀에 젖은 채로 우리 쪽으로 다가와 딱딱한 밀짚모자를 받아들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There were no flowers, and various knick-knacks, put away during the summer, had not been replaced; there was something cheerless and stiff about the room which had always seemed so friendly; it gave you an odd feeling, as though someone were lying dead on the other side of the wall.

examples.translation_ko: 그가 힘없이 우리를 욕하는 동안 우리는 그에게 옷을 입히고, 아래층으로 내려가게 하고, 마차에 태워서, 마침내 스트루브의 작업실로 데려갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English facioun, from Anglo-Norman fechoun (compare Jersey Norman faichon), variant of Old French faceon, fazon, façon (“fash...
definition_en: A popular style or way of dressing.

senses.gloss: A current (constantly changing) trend, favored for frivolous rather than practical, logical, or intellectual reasons.
Popular trends, especially in clothing; the industry that designs clothing and sometimes other related items.
senses.example: Check out the latest in fashion.

senses.gloss: A style or manner in which something is done.
senses.example:
Ophelia: My lord, he hath importuned me with love in honourable fashion.
Lord Polonius: Ay, fashion you may call it; go to, go to.

examples.text: His family were enormously wealthy—even in college his freedom with money was a matter for reproach—but now he’d left Chicago and come East in a fashion that rather took your breath away: for instance, he’d brought down a string of polo ponies from Lake Forest.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 가문은 엄청나게 부유했다—대학 시절에도 그의 돈 쓰는 방식은 비난거리였다—하지만 이제 그는 시카고를 떠나 동부로 온 방식이 숨이 막힐 정도였다: 예를 들어, 레이크 포레스트에서 폴로 조랑말 한 떼를 끌고 내려온 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Why are you idling in this disgraceful fashion?”
examples.translation_ko: "왜 이렇게 한심하게 빈둥거리고 있는 거야?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Beauty is something wonderful and strange that the artist fashions out of the chaos of the world in the torment of his soul.
examples.translation_ko: 아름다움이란 예술가가 영혼의 고통 속에서 세상의 혼돈으로부터 빚어내는 경이롭고 신비한 것이오.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English conscience, from Old French conscience, from Latin conscientia (“knowledge within oneself”), from consciens, present participle...
definition_en: The part of the mind that makes judgments about right and wrong.

senses.gloss: The ethical or moral sense of right and wrong, chiefly as it affects a person’s own behaviour and forms their attitude to their past actions.
senses.example: Your conscience is your highest authority.

senses.gloss: A personification of the moral sense of right and wrong, usually in the form of a person, a being or merely a voice that gives moral lessons and advices.
Consciousness; thinking; awareness, especially self-awareness.

examples.text: I had the appetite of youth and he of a hardened conscience.
examples.translation_ko: 나에게는 젊음의 식욕이 있었고 그에게는 무감각해진 양심의 식욕이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Nor with such a man could you expect the appeal to conscience to be effective.
examples.translation_ko: 그런 사람에게는 양심에 호소하는 것이 효과적일 거라고 기대할 수도 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English torture, from Old French torture, from Late Latin tortūra (“a twisting, writhing, of bodily pain, a griping colic;” in Medieval...
definition_en: To cause severe physical or mental suffering.

senses.gloss: The infliction of severe pain or anguish, especially as an interrogation technique or punishment; (usually in the plural) a technique, method, or device which is designed to inflict such anguish.
senses.example: People confess to anything under torture.

senses.gloss: Severe pain or anguish, of mind or body.
An unpleasant sensation or its infliction: embarrassment, heartache, etc.
senses.example: Every time she says 'goodbye' it is torture!

examples.text: Perhaps she got enjoyment out of the torture she inflicted.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 그녀는 자신이 가하는 고문에서 즐거움을 얻었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Supposing your wife died, wouldn’t you be tortured by remorse?”
examples.translation_ko: 만약 당신 아내가 죽는다면, 후회로 괴로워하지 않겠는가?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English ston, stone, stan, from Old English stān, from Proto-West Germanic *stain, from Proto-Germanic *stainaz, from Proto-Indo-Europe...
definition_en: A small rock or pebble.

senses.gloss: A hard earthen substance that can form rocks; especially, such substance when regarded as a building material.
senses.example: The first day of the weeke, commeth Mary Magdalene earely when it was yet darke, vnto the Sepulchre, and seeth the stone taken away from the Sepulchre.

senses.gloss: A piece of such material: a rock or a pebble.
A gemstone, a jewel, especially a diamond.
senses.example: […]Ineſtimable Stones, vnvalewed Iewels[…]

examples.text: On the white steps an obscene word, scrawled by some boy with a piece of brick, stood out clearly in the moonlight, and I erased it, drawing my shoe raspingly along the stone.
examples.translation_ko: 하얀 계단에는 어떤 소년이 벽돌 조각으로 갈겨쓴 외설스러운 말이 달빛 아래 선명하게 드러나 있었고, 나는 신발로 돌을 거칠게 문지르며 그것을 지웠다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Can the law get blood out of a stone?
examples.translation_ko: "법이 돌에서 피를 짜낼 수 있겠는가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We came to a stone bridge over a shallow river, and we stopped for a few minutes to see the native boys bathing.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 얕은 강 위의 돌다리에 이르렀고, 잠시 멈춰 서서 원주민 소년들이 목욕하는 모습을 구경했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bitterli, biterli, biterliche, from Old English biterlīċe, bitterlīċe (“bitterly”), equivalent to bitter + -ly. Cognate with Ge...
definition_en: Feeling or expressing bitter resentment.

senses.gloss: In a bitter manner.
senses.example: Heidi threw herself down beside Clara's chair and began to cry bitterly.

senses.gloss: Extremely
senses.example: On a bitterly cold evening at Wembley, the Lionesses knew only victory would be enough to keep alive Team GB's hopes of competing in Paris.

examples.text: However, that was my fault, for he was one of those who used to sneer most bitterly at Gatsby on the courage of Gatsby’s liquor, and I should have known better than to call him.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그건 내 잘못이었다. 그는 개츠비의 술에 힘입어 개츠비를 가장 신랄하게 비웃곤 했던 사람 중 하나였는데, 나는 그에게 전화를 걸지 말았어야 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Then his face grew bitterly scornful.
examples.translation_ko: 그러자 그의 얼굴에 씁쓸한 경멸의 빛이 떠올랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When I told him that I meant to live in Paris for a while, and had taken an apartment, he reproached me bitterly for not having let him know.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 한동안 파리에서 살 예정이며 아파트를 구했다고 말하자, 그는 미리 알려주지 않았다며 몹시 원망했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English quik, quic, from Old English cwic (“alive”), from Proto-West Germanic *kwiku, from Proto-Germanic *kwikwaz, from Proto-Indo-Eur...
definition_en: Having or showing a rapid quality.

senses.gloss: Moving with speed, rapidity or swiftness, or capable of doing so; rapid; fast.
senses.example: I ran to the station – but I wasn't quick enough.

senses.gloss: Occurring in a short time; happening or done rapidly.
senses.example: That was a quick meal.

senses.gloss: Lively, fast-thinking, witty, intelligent.
senses.example: You have to be very quick to be able to compete in ad-lib theatrics.

examples.text: “Come here quick!”
examples.translation_ko: "빨리 이리 와!"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was a long silence on the other end of the wire, followed by an exclamation … then a quick squawk as the connection was broken.
examples.translation_ko: 전화선 저편에서 긴 침묵이 흘렀고, 이어서 감탄사가 터져 나왔다… 그러고는 연결이 끊어지면서 날카로운 잡음이 들렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I can learn quicker than I could when I was eighteen.”
examples.translation_ko: "열여덟 살 때보다 지금이 더 빨리 배울 수 있어."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was quick to discover talent, and his praise was generous.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 재능을 재빨리 발견해내는 눈이 있었고, 칭찬을 아끼지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French, from Medieval Latin sensatio, from Latin sensus.
definition_en: A strong and pleasant feeling or emotion.

senses.gloss: A physical feeling or perception from something that comes into contact with the body; something sensed.
Excitation of sensory organs.
senses.example: In the dead state all is apparently without motion. No agent within indicates design, intelligence, or foresight: there is no respiration; […] no sensation; […]

senses.gloss: A widespread reaction of interest or excitement.
senses.example: Young Derby's odd genius developed remarkably, and in his eighteenth year his collected nightmare-lyrics made a real sensation when issued under the title Azathoth and Other Horrors.

examples.text: If you read the papers you know there was a big sensation.”
examples.translation_ko: 신문을 읽으신 분들은 아시겠지만 대단한 센세이션을 일으켰던 곡입니다."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He smiled with jovial condescension, and added: “Some sensation!”
examples.translation_ko: 그는 쾌활하면서도 거만한 미소를 지으며 덧붙였다. "정말 대단한 센세이션이었죠!"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had the sensation that here was the abode of pain.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 이곳이 고통의 거처라는 느낌을 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His eyes grew accustomed to the darkness, and now he was seized by an overwhelming sensation as he stared at the painted walls.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 눈이 어둠에 익숙해지자, 칠해진 벽을 바라보며 압도적인 감각에 사로잡혔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English chyn, from Old English ċinn (“chin”), from Proto-West Germanic *kinnu, from Proto-Germanic *kinnuz (“chin”), from Proto-Indo-Eu...
definition_en: The lower front part of the face.

senses.gloss: The bottom of a face, (specifically) the typically jutting jawline below the mouth.
Talk.
A lie, a falsehood.

examples.text: Then he sat down, rigidly, his elbow on the arm of the sofa and his chin in his hand.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 소파 팔걸이에 팔꿈치를 올리고 손으로 턱을 괸 채 경직되게 앉았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I glanced at Daisy, who was staring terrified between Gatsby and her husband, and at Jordan, who had begun to balance an invisible but absorbing object on the tip of her chin.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 개츠비와 남편 사이에서 겁에 질린 채 바라보고 있는 데이지와, 턱끝에 보이지 않지만 흥미로운 무언가의 균형을 맞추기 시작한 조던을 흘끗 보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She had a bold hooked nose and three chins.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 굵직한 매부리코와 삼중턱을 가지고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Her arms were like legs of mutton, her breasts like giant cabbages; her face, broad and fleshy, gave you an impression of almost indecent nakedness, and vast chin succeeded to vast chin.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 팔은 양다리 같았고, 가슴은 거대한 양배추 같았다. 넓고 살찐 얼굴은 거의 외설스러울 정도로 적나라한 인상을 주었고, 거대한 턱 아래로 또 다른 거대한 턱이 이어졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French intolerable, from Latin intolerābilis. By surface analysis, in- + tolerable.
definition_en: Extremely unpleasant or unacceptable.

senses.gloss: Not tolerable; not capable of being borne or endured.
Extremely offensive or insulting.
senses.example: It is an intolerable sound that sets spoons tinkling in saucers and windowpanes vibrating.

senses.gloss: Extremely worn and degraded, to the point of being unsafe.

examples.text: When they convinced her of this, she immediately fainted, as if that was the intolerable part of the affair.
examples.translation_ko: 사람들이 그녀에게 이 사실을 납득시키자, 그녀는 즉시 기절했는데, 마치 그것이야말로 이 사건에서 참을 수 없는 부분인 것처럼 보였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The thought of her suffering was intolerable.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 고통받았을 생각을 하니 견딜 수가 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She clasped her hands over her heart as though its beating were intolerable.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 심장 박동이 견딜 수 없다는 듯 가슴에 두 손을 모았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *dwóh₁
From Medieval Latin indīviduālis, from Latin indīviduum (“an indivisible thing”), neuter of indīviduus (“indivisible, undivided”),...
definition_en: A single person or thing considered separately from others.

senses.gloss: A person considered alone, rather than as belonging to a group of people.
senses.example: He is an unusual individual.

senses.gloss: A single physical human being as a legal subject, as opposed to a legal person such as a corporation.
senses.example: Every individual is equal before and under the law and has the right to the equal protection and equal benefit of the law without discrimination […].

senses.gloss: An object, be it a thing or an agent, as contrasted to a class.
senses.example: It is typically held that chairs, trees, rocks, people and many of the so-called ‘everyday’ objects we encounter can be regarded as individuals.

examples.text: Then, very gradually, part by part, a pale, dangling individual stepped out of the wreck, pawing tentatively at the ground with a large uncertain dancing shoe.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 아주 천천히, 조금씩 조금씩, 창백하고 축 늘어진 한 사내가 잔해에서 빠져나와 크고 불안정한 댄스화로 땅을 더듬거리며 조심스럽게 디뎠다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It is the very strong link that attaches the individual to the whole.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 개인을 전체에 결속시키는 매우 강력한 고리다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He is no longer an individual, but a thing, an instrument to some purpose foreign to his ego.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 더 이상 개인이 아니라 하나의 사물, 자신의 자아와는 무관한 어떤 목적을 위한 도구가 되어버린다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pryde, pride, from Old English prȳde, prȳte (“pride”) (compare Old Norse prýði (“bravery, pomp”)), derivative of Old English pr...
definition_en: To feel a sense of satisfaction or pleasure.

senses.gloss: A sense of one's own worth; reasonable self-esteem and satisfaction (in oneself, in one's work, one's family, etc).
senses.example: He swelled with pride as he held the trophy. His family watched with pride from the bleachers.

senses.gloss: An unreasonable overestimation of one's own superiority in terms of talents, or looks, wealth, importance, etc., which comes across as being haughty, lofty, and often showing contempt of others; exaggerated self-worth.
Proud or disdainful behavior or treatment that reflects such an attitude (of haughtiness); arrogance.
senses.example: Pride goeth before the fall.

examples.text: He glowed with happy pride.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 행복한 자부심으로 얼굴을 빛냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then, in pride and contempt, he destroyed it.”
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 자부심과 경멸 속에서 그것을 파괴했습니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English nervous (“composed of or incorporating nerves”), from Latin nervōsus (“nervous; sinewy; energetic, vigorous”), from nervus (“ne...
definition_en: Feeling or showing anxiety or unease.

senses.gloss: Full of sinews.
Having strong or prominent sinews; sinewy, muscular.
senses.example: [T]here is nothing in marble equal to the Venus of Medici, for ſoftneſs and tenderneſs; as there is nothing ſo ſtrong and nervous, as the Hercules Farneſe.

senses.gloss: Of a piece of writing, literary style etc.: forceful, powerful.
senses.example: Nervous, clear, and striking, was almost all that he uttered […].

examples.text: You see, when we left New York she was very nervous
examples.translation_ko: 있잖아, 뉴욕을 떠날 때 데이지가 몹시 신경이 예민해져 있었거든
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was worried now—there was a quality of nervous despair in Daisy’s letters.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 그는 걱정이 되었다. 데이지의 편지에는 신경질적인 절망의 기색이 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Mrs. Strickland was plainly nervous.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인은 명백히 초조해하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English boote, bote (“shoe”), from Old French bote (“a high, thick shoe”). Of obscure origin, but probably related to Old French bot (“...
definition_en: A part of a shoe that covers the foot and lower leg.

senses.gloss: A heavy shoe that covers part of the leg.
A kind of sports shoe worn by players of certain games such as cricket and football (historically in the form of boots, now shorter, but still called the same).
A blow with the foot; a kick.

examples.text: Almost before I had grasped her meaning there was the flutter of a dress and the crunch of leather boots, and Tom and Daisy were back at the table.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 그녀의 말뜻을 채 파악하기도 전에 드레스가 바스락거리고 가죽 부츠가 바닥을 밟는 소리가 났고, 톰과 데이지가 다시 식탁으로 돌아왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The lamplight, bright on his boots and dull on the autumn-leaf yellow of her hair, glinted along the paper as she turned a page with a flutter of slender muscles in her arms.
examples.translation_ko: 램프 불빛이 그의 구두 위에서는 밝게, 그녀의 가을 낙엽 같은 노란 머리카락 위에서는 흐릿하게 비치며, 그녀가 가느다란 팔 근육을 살짝 움직여 페이지를 넘길 때마다 종이 위로 반짝였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You can bet your boots I’d have routed her out fast enough.”
examples.translation_ko: "내가 갔다면 그 여자를 금세 찾아냈을 텐데."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The air was heavy with the dust beaten up by the heavy boots of the men, and gray with smoke.
examples.translation_ko: 공기는 남자들의 무거운 부츠가 일으킨 먼지로 탁했고, 담배 연기로 회색빛을 띠었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English tine, tyne (“very small”) + -y. Perhaps from tine.
definition_en: Extremely small in size or amount.

senses.gloss: Very small.

examples.text: After a moment I discovered his tiny eyes in the half-darkness.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 후 나는 어스름한 어둠 속에서 그의 작은 눈을 발견했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Daisy watched him and laughed, her sweet, exciting laugh; a tiny gust of powder rose from her bosom into the air.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지는 그를 바라보며 웃었다. 달콤하고 흥미진진한 웃음이었다. 그녀의 가슴에서 작은 분가루가 공중으로 날아올랐다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He’s living in one tiny room in the most squalid way.
examples.translation_ko: 가장 더러운 환경의 작은 방 하나에서 살고 있어.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They had but the studio, a bedroom, and a tiny kitchen.
examples.translation_ko: 그들에게는 화실과 침실, 그리고 작은 부엌뿐이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English gaspen, gayspen (“to gape, outbreathe”), related to and likely derived from Old Norse geispa (“to yawn”) or its descendant Dani...
definition_en: A sudden intake of breath.

senses.gloss: To draw in the breath suddenly, as if from a shock.
senses.example: The audience gasped as the magician disappeared.

senses.gloss: To breathe quickly or in a labored manner, as after exertion; to respire with heaving of the breast; to pant.
senses.example: We were all gasping when we reached the summit.

senses.gloss: To speak in a breathless manner.
senses.example: The old man gasped his last few words.

examples.text: He gave a gasp.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 숨을 헐떡였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Stroeve gave a little gasp.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브가 작게 숨을 헐떡였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English helples, from Old English *helplēas (“helpless”) from Proto-Germanic *helpōlausaz, equivalent to help + -less. Compare Dutch hu...
definition_en: Lacking the power to help oneself or others.

senses.gloss: Unable to defend oneself.
senses.example:
Rana Thanoptis: Are we good? Can I go?
Shepard: You conducted brutal experiments on helpless test subjects. You helped Saren. You don't get to live.

etymology: From incessant + -ly.
definition_en: Continuing to happen or be done without stopping.

senses.gloss: In a manner without pause or stop, especially to the point of annoyance; not ceasing.

examples.text: I couldn’t sleep all night; a foghorn was groaning incessantly on the Sound, and I tossed half-sick between grotesque reality and savage, frightening dreams.

examples.text: Tom talked incessantly, exulting and laughing, but his voice was as remote from Jordan and me as the foreign clamour on the sidewalk or the tumult of the elevated overhead.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I suppose no artist achieves completely the realisation of the dream that obsesses him, and Strickland, harassed incessantly by his struggle with technique, managed, perhaps, less than others to express the vision that he saw with his mind’s eye; but in Tahiti the circumstances were favourable to him; he found in his surroundings the accidents necessary for his inspiration to become effective, and his later pictures give at least a suggestion of what he sought.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 예술가도 자신을 사로잡는 꿈을 완전히 실현하지는 못하는 법이고, 기법과의 끊임없는 투쟁에 시달린 스트릭랜드는 아마도 다른 이들보다도 더 적게 자신이 마음의 눈으로 본 환상을 표현해냈을 것이다. 하지만 타히티에서는 상황이 그에게 유리했다. 그는 주변 환경에서 자신의 영감이 효과를 발휘하는 데 필요한 우연들을 발견했고, 그의 후기 작품들은 적어도 그가 추구했던 것의 암시를 보여준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.translation_ko: 개츠비의 악명은 그의 환대를 받아들여 그의 과거에 대한 권위자가 된 수백 명의 사람들에 의해 퍼져나가 여름 내내 커져서, 뉴스거리가 되기 직전까지 이르렀다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Someone with a positive manner, perhaps a detective, used the expression “madman” as he bent over Wilson’s body that afternoon, and the adventitious authority of his voice set the key for the newspaper reports next morning.
examples.translation_ko: 단호한 태도의 누군가가, 아마 형사였을 텐데, 그날 오후 윌슨의 시체 위로 몸을 굽히며 "광인"이라는 표현을 썼고, 그의 목소리가 지닌 우연한 권위가 다음 날 아침 신문 보도의 논조를 결정했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: In a few weeks the authorities received his resignation of the coveted position on the staff.
examples.translation_ko: 몇 주 후 병원 당국은 그가 모두가 탐내던 스태프 자리를 사임한다는 통보를 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The subject was grateful, and the industrious Weitbrecht-Rotholz in his imposing monograph[2] has been able to give a remarkable list of authorities.
examples.translation_ko: 주제는 매력적이었고, 부지런한 바이트브레히트-로톨츠는 그의 인상적인 단행본에서 주목할 만한 전거 목록을 제시할 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From late Middle English seldom, alteration of earlier selden, from Old English seldan (“seldom”), from Proto-West Germanic *seldanā, from Proto-Ge...
definition_en: Used to indicate that something happens infrequently.

senses.gloss: Infrequently, rarely.
senses.example: They seldom come here now.

examples.text: The men were seldom eccentric in appearance.
examples.translation_ko: 남자들은 외모가 별난 경우가 드물었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Here Strickland lived, coming seldom to Papeete, on the produce of the land.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 이곳에서 살았는데, 파페에테에는 좀처럼 나가지 않고 땅에서 나는 것으로 생활했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English ignoraunce, ignorance, from
From Old French ignorance, from Latin ignōrantia. By surface analysis, ignor(e) + -ance.
definition_en: Lack of knowledge or understanding.

senses.gloss: The condition of being uninformed or uneducated; lack of knowledge or information.
senses.example: She shows total ignorance about the topic at hand.

senses.gloss: Sins committed through ignorance.

examples.text: It is the bravado of ignorance.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 무지에서 나오는 허세일 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Their ignorance is better than all our knowledge.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 무지가 우리의 모든 지식보다 낫다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed into late Middle English from Old French extreme, from Latin extrēmus, the superlative of exter.
definition_en: Exceeding the normal or average limit.

senses.gloss: Of a place, the most remote, farthest or outermost.
senses.example: At the extreme edges, the coating is very thin.

senses.gloss: In the greatest or highest degree; intense.
senses.example: He has an extreme aversion to needles, and avoids visiting the doctor.

senses.gloss: Excessive, or far beyond the norm.
senses.example: His extreme love of model trains showed in the rails that criscrossed his entire home.

examples.text: I picked it up with a weary bend and handed it back to her, holding it at arm’s length and by the extreme tip of the corners to indicate that I had no designs upon it—but everyone near by, including the woman, suspected me just the same.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 지친 몸을 구부려 그것을 주워 그녀에게 돌려주었는데, 팔을 쭉 뻗고 모서리 끝만 잡아서 내가 그것에 대해 어떤 욕심도 없다는 것을 보여주려 했지만, 그 여자를 포함해 근처에 있던 모든 사람들은 똑같이 나를 의심했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was cruel that his extreme unhappiness should have in it something of buffoonery.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 극도의 불행 속에 어딘가 우스꽝스러운 면이 있다는 것은 잔인한 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: With the superciliousness of extreme youth, I put thirty-five as the utmost limit at which a man might fall in love without making a fool of himself.
examples.translation_ko: 극도로 젊은 나이의 거만함으로, 나는 남자가 바보가 되지 않고 사랑에 빠질 수 있는 최대 한계를 서른다섯으로 잡았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English example, exaumple, from Old French example, essaumple, from Latin exemplum (“sample, pattern, specimen, copy for imitation, etc...
definition_en: A specific instance or illustration used to explain or demonstrate something.

senses.gloss: Something that is representative of all such things in a group.
Something that serves to illustrate or explain a rule.
Something that serves as a pattern of behaviour to be imitated (a good example) or not to be imitated (a bad example).
senses.example: Nelson Mandela was an example for many to follow.

examples.text: Who now, for example, thinks of George Crabbe?
examples.translation_ko: 예를 들어, 지금 누가 조지 크래브를 생각하겠는가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose it was a very pretty example of the triumph of spirit over matter, and so my digression has at least the advantage of a moral.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 이것은 정신이 물질을 이기는 승리의 아주 좋은 본보기였을 것이고, 그러니 내 곁가지 이야기도 최소한 교훈이라는 장점은 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English famous, from Anglo-Norman famous, from Latin fāmōsus, equivalent to fame + -ous. Displaced native Old English hlīsful.
definition_en: Well-known or celebrated.

senses.gloss: Well known.
senses.example:
By this my ſword that conquer’d Perſea,
Thy fall ſhall make me famous through the world:

senses.gloss: In the public eye.
senses.example: Some people are only famous within their city.

examples.text: “It’s one of the most famous colleges in the world.”
examples.translation_ko: "세계에서 가장 유명한 대학 중 하나야."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I’d a little rather not be the polo player,” said Tom pleasantly, “I’d rather look at all these famous people in—in oblivion.”
examples.translation_ko: "나는 폴로 선수보다는," 톰이 유쾌하게 말했다, "차라리 이 모든 유명한 사람들을 망각 속에서 바라보고 싶어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I wanted no one to take notice of me, so that I could observe these famous creatures at my ease and listen to the clever things they said.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 아무도 내게 주의를 기울이지 않기를 바랐다. 그래야 이 유명한 인물들을 편안히 관찰하고 그들이 하는 기발한 말들을 들을 수 있을 테니까.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Maurice Huret in his famous article gave an outline of Charles Strickland’s life which was well calculated to whet the appetites of the inquiring.
examples.translation_ko: 모리스 위레는 그의 유명한 기사에서 찰스 스트릭랜드의 생애 개요를 제시했는데, 이는 탐구하는 이들의 호기심을 자극하기에 충분히 계산된 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin gratus (“pleasing, agreeable”) + -ful, morphologically grate + -ful.
definition_en: Feeling thankful for something.

senses.gloss: Appreciative; thankful.
senses.example: I'm grateful that you helped me out.

senses.gloss: Pleasing, welcome.
senses.example: […] grateful underfoot was the damp and slightly yielding beach, from which the waves seemed just retired.

examples.text: By six o’clock Michaelis was worn out, and grateful for the sound of a car stopping outside.
examples.translation_ko: 여섯 시가 되자 미카엘리스는 지쳐 있었고, 밖에서 차가 멈추는 소리에 고마움을 느꼈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I’m grateful for all the happiness you gave me in the past.”
examples.translation_ko: 당신이 과거에 내게 준 모든 행복에 감사합니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was a thoroughly dull party from the beginning, but if you will come I shall be uncommonly grateful.
examples.translation_ko: 처음부터 끝까지 지독히 따분한 파티가 될 텐데, 그래도 와주신다면 정말 고맙겠어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From surprise + -ing.
definition_en: More than expected or unusual.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of surprise

examples.text: I was startled, naturally, but the really surprising thing was that it hadn’t happened before.
examples.translation_ko: 당연히 나는 깜짝 놀랐지만, 정말 놀라운 것은 이런 일이 전에 일어나지 않았다는 사실이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As for Tom, the fact that he “had some woman in New York” was really less surprising than that he had been depressed by a book.
examples.translation_ko: 톰의 경우, 그가 "뉴욕에 어떤 여자를 두고 있다"는 사실은 그가 책 때문에 우울해했다는 것보다 실제로는 덜 놀라운 일이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It seemed to me that I was on the threshold of a surprising adventure.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 놀라운 모험의 문턱에 서 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In the first place his red beard, ragged and untrimmed, hid much of his face, and his hair was long; but the most surprising change in him was his extreme thinness.
examples.translation_ko: 우선 그의 붉은 수염이 거칠고 다듬어지지 않아 얼굴의 상당 부분을 가리고 있었고, 머리카락도 길었다. 하지만 그에게서 가장 놀라운 변화는 극도로 말라빠진 모습이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English inventen, borrowed from Old French inventer, from Latin inventus, perfect passive participle of inveniō (“come upon, meet with,...
definition_en: To create or design something new.

senses.gloss: To design a new process or mechanism.
senses.example: After weeks of hard work, I invented a new way to alphabetize matchbooks.

senses.gloss: To create something fictional for a particular purpose.
senses.example: I knew I had to invent an excuse, and quickly.

senses.gloss: To come upon; to find; to discover.
senses.example: Far off he wonders, what them makes so glad, / If Bacchus merry fruit they did inuent [...].

examples.text: His lips moved silently for a moment as he invented, “ ‘George B. Wilson at the Gasoline Pump,’ or something like that.”
examples.translation_ko: 그가 지어내면서 잠시 입술을 조용히 움직였다. "'주유소의 조지 B. 윌슨' 같은 걸로요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: So he invented just the sort of Jay Gatsby that a seventeen-year-old boy would be likely to invent, and to this conception he was faithful to the end.
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 그는 열일곱 살 소년이 만들어낼 법한 바로 그런 제이 개츠비를 창조했고, 이 개념에 끝까지 충실했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: If I were writing a novel, rather than narrating such facts as I know of a curious personality, I should have invented much to account for this change of heart.
examples.translation_ko: 만약 내가 기이한 인물에 대해 아는 사실들을 서술하는 것이 아니라 소설을 쓰고 있다면, 이런 마음의 변화를 설명하기 위해 많은 것을 지어냈을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It seizes with avidity upon any incidents, surprising or mysterious, in the career of those who have at all distinguished themselves from their fellows, and invents a legend to which it then attaches a fanatical belief.
examples.translation_ko: 인간은 동료들과 조금이라도 구별되는 사람들의 생애에서 놀랍거나 신비로운 사건들을 탐욕스럽게 붙잡고는, 그것에 광신적인 믿음을 부여하는 전설을 만들어낸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English legende, from Old French legende, from Medieval Latin legenda (“a legend, story, especially the lives of the saints”), from Lat...
definition_en: A story or tradition that is passed down through generations.

senses.gloss: the life story of a saint (such stories are often embellished, but any kind is called a legend)
senses.example: As a child she had nothing to read but the legends of early Christian martyrs.

senses.gloss: A story of unknown origin describing plausible but extraordinary past events.
senses.example: The legend of Troy was discovered to have a historical basis.

senses.gloss: A plausible story set in the historical past, but whose historicity is uncertain.
senses.example: the legend of Robin Hood

examples.text: “Orderi di Danilo,” ran the circular legend, “Montenegro, Nicolas Rex.”
examples.translation_ko: "오르데리 디 다닐로"라고 원형 문구가 새겨져 있었고, "몬테네그로, 니콜라스 렉스"라고 적혀 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Contemporary legends such as the “underground pipeline to Canada” attached themselves to him, and there was one persistent story that he didn’t live in a house at all, but in a boat that looked like a house and was moved secretly up and down the Long Island shore.
examples.translation_ko: "캐나다로 통하는 지하 파이프라인" 같은 당대의 전설들이 그에게 붙어다녔고, 그가 집에 사는 게 아니라 집처럼 생긴 배에 살면서 롱아일랜드 해안을 따라 은밀히 오가고 있다는 끈질긴 소문도 하나 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The incidents of the legend become the hero’s surest passport to immortality.
examples.translation_ko: 전설 속 사건들은 영웅이 불멸에 이르는 가장 확실한 여권이 된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In due course a legend arose of such circumstantiality that the wise historian would hesitate to attack it.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 너무나 구체적인 전설이 생겨나서, 현명한 역사가라면 그것을 공격하기를 주저할 정도가 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Anglo-Norman outrageus, Middle French outrageus, from outrage; equivalent to outrage + -ous.
definition_en: Excessively bad or shocking.

senses.gloss: Violating morality or decency; provoking indignation or affront.
Transgressing reasonable limits; extravagant, immoderate.
senses.example: Audience members praised McKellen, best known for Shakespearean roles and as Gandalf in The Lord of the Rings, for his show-stealing turn as Twankey in a series of outrageous glitzy dresses.

senses.gloss: Shocking; exceeding conventional behaviour; provocative.
senses.example: "It's something I really am quite nervous about," he admits, before adding, with relish: "You have to be a bit outrageous and challenging sometimes."

examples.text: There is so much in his character which is strange that I feel it would complete the picture if his views were outrageous.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 성격에는 기이한 면이 너무 많아서, 그의 견해까지 터무니없다면 그 인물상이 완성될 것 같은 느낌이 든다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: If I have succeeded at all in giving the complicated impression that Strickland made on me, it will not seem outrageous to say that I felt he was at once too great and too small for love.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드가 내게 준 복잡한 인상을 어느 정도라도 전달하는 데 성공했다면, 그가 사랑하기에는 동시에 너무 위대하면서도 너무 소심했다고 내가 느꼈다고 말해도 터무니없지 않을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French attaque, derived from the verb attaquer, from Italian attaccare (“to join, attach”) (used in attaccare battaglia (“to join bat...
definition_en: To launch a surprise attack on someone or something.

senses.gloss: An attempt to cause damage, injury to, or death of an opponent or enemy.
senses.example: From 1906 to 1960, there were forty-six recorded shark attacks, half of which were fatal.

senses.gloss: Any of several specific maneuvers, skills, or special abilities that a character can use to inflict damage against opponents.
An attempt to detract from the worth or credibility of, a person, position, idea, object, or thing, by physical, verbal, emotional, or other assault.
senses.example: They claimed the censorship of the article was an attack on free speech.

examples.text: Malice cannot touch us, nor envy attack.
examples.translation_ko: 악의도 우리를 건드릴 수 없고, 질투도 우리를 공격할 수 없습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He judged that the disease had already attacked the vocal chords.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 병이 이미 성대를 침범했다고 판단했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English removen, from Anglo-Norman remover, removeir, from Old French remouvoir, from Latin removēre, from re- + movēre (“to move”), eq...
definition_en: To take or move something away from a place.

senses.gloss: To delete.
To move from one place to another, especially to take away.
senses.example: He removed the marbles from the bag.

senses.gloss: To replace a dish within a course.

examples.text: Daisy was my second cousin once removed, and I’d known Tom in college.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지는 나의 재종 사촌이었고, 톰은 대학에서 알고 지낸 사이였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We all looked in silence at Mrs. Wilson, who removed a strand of hair from over her eyes and looked back at us with a brilliant smile.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 모두 조용히 윌슨 부인을 바라보았다. 그녀는 눈을 가린 머리카락 한 올을 치우고는 환한 미소를 지으며 우리를 돌아보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His garb of woe suggested that he had lost in one catastrophe every relation he had in the world, even to cousins by marriage twice removed.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 상복 차림새는 마치 한 번의 재앙으로 이 세상의 모든 친척들을, 심지어 두 다리 건너 인척까지도 잃었다는 듯한 인상을 주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He saw her roll down her sleeves and remove her apron—the apron hung on a peg behind the door—and take the bottle of oxalic acid and go with it into the bedroom.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀가 소매를 내리고 앞치마를 벗는 모습을 보았다—그 앞치마는 문 뒤 못에 걸려 있었다—그리고 옥살산 병을 들고 침실로 들어가는 모습을.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sauf, safe, saf, saaf, from Old French sauf, saulf, salf (“safe”), from Latin salvus (“whole, safe”), from Proto-Italic *salwos...
definition_en: Free from danger or risk.

senses.gloss: Not in danger; out of harm's reach.
senses.example: You’ll be safe from the storm here in the cabin.

senses.gloss: Free from risk.
senses.example: It’s safe to eat this berry.

senses.gloss: Providing protection from danger; providing shelter.
senses.example: We have to find a safe spot, where we can hide out until this is over.

examples.text: “You said a bad driver was only safe until she met another bad driver?
examples.translation_ko: "나쁜 운전자는 다른 나쁜 운전자를 만나기 전까지만 안전하다고 하셨잖아요?
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It never occurred to me that one man could start to play with the faith of fifty million people—with the single-mindedness of a burglar blowing a safe.
examples.translation_ko: 한 사람이 5천만 명의 믿음을 가지고 장난을 칠 수 있다는 것은—금고를 터뜨리는 도둑의 일편단심으로—내게는 전혀 생각해본 적이 없는 일이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She had abandoned the safe shelter of her husband’s protection and the comfortable ease of a well-provided establishment for what she could not but see was an extreme hazard.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 남편의 보호라는 안전한 피난처와 넉넉한 살림의 편안함을 버리고, 누가 봐도 극도로 위험한 일에 뛰어든 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Dr. Weitbrecht-Rotholz belongs to that school of historians which believes that human nature is not only about as bad as it can be, but a great deal worse; and certainly the reader is safer of entertainment in their hands than in those of the writers who take a malicious pleasure in representing the great figures of romance as patterns of the domestic virtues.

senses.gloss: That which limits the extent of anything; limit, extremity, bound, boundary, terminus.
senses.example: "Alright, look...we can spend the holidays with your parents, but this time it will be on my terms."

senses.gloss: A chronological limitation or restriction, a limited timespan.
senses.example: The term of a lease agreement is the period of time during which the lease is effective, and may be fixed, periodic, or of indefinite duration.

senses.gloss: Any of the binding conditions or promises in a legal contract.
senses.example: Be sure to read the terms and conditions before signing.

examples.text: She was effectually prevented, but she wasn’t on speaking terms with her family for several weeks.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 효과적으로 저지당했지만, 몇 주 동안 가족과 말도 섞지 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Most of the confidences were unsought—frequently I have feigned sleep, preoccupation, or a hostile levity when I realized by some unmistakable sign that an intimate revelation was quivering on the horizon; for the intimate revelations of young men, or at least the terms in which they express them, are usually plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions.

etymology: From Middle English motif, from Anglo-Norman motif, Middle French motif, and their source, Late Latin motivum (“motive, moving cause”), neuter of m...
definition_en: A reason for doing something.

senses.gloss: An idea or communication that makes one want to act, especially from spiritual sources; a divine prompting.
senses.example: there's something in a woman beyond all human delight; a magnetic virtue, a charming quality, an occult and powerful motive.

senses.gloss: An incentive to act in a particular way; a reason or emotion that makes one want to do something; anything that prompts a choice of action.
senses.example: Many of them at first seemed kind to him, but it turned out their motives were not entirely altruistic.

senses.gloss: A limb or other bodily organ that can move.
senses.example: every joint and motive of her body

etymology: From Middle English egernesse, egrenesse; equivalent to eager + -ness.
definition_en: A strong desire to do or achieve something.

senses.gloss: The state or quality of being eager; ardent desire.
Tartness, sourness.

examples.text: He waited, looking at me with suppressed eagerness.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 억누른 열망으로 나를 바라보며 기다렸다.
