examples.text: He was saying some last word to her, but the eagerness in his manner tightened abruptly into formality as several people approached him to say goodbye.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀에게 마지막 말을 건네고 있었지만, 몇몇 사람들이 작별 인사를 하러 다가오자 그의 태도에서 드러나던 간절함이 갑자기 격식을 차린 모습으로 굳어졌다.

examples.text: It was charming to be welcomed with so much eagerness.
examples.translation_ko: 그토록 열렬하게 환영받는다는 것은 정말 기분 좋은 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There is a singular fascination in watching the eagerness with which the learned author ferrets out every circumstance which may throw discredit on his hero.
examples.translation_ko: 박식한 저자가 자신의 주인공에게 불명예를 안겨줄 수 있는 모든 정황을 열심히 파헤치는 모습을 지켜보는 것에는 묘한 매력이 있다.

etymology: From Middle English cruelte, from Old French crualté (French cruauté), from Latin crudelitas. By surface analysis, cruel + -ty.
definition_en: The act of treating someone or something with cruelty.

senses.gloss: An indifference to suffering or pleasure in inflicting suffering.
A cruel act.
senses.example: Gay songwriter behind bars! Needs sincere letter to help ease the tension from cruelties inside the joint.

examples.text: I have an idea that there was some cruelty in her indifference.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 무관심에는 어떤 잔혹함이 있었다는 생각이 든다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I wondered what an abyss of cruelty she must have looked into that in horror she refused to live.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 공포에 질려 살기를 거부할 만큼 어떤 잔혹함의 심연을 들여다보았을까 궁금했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Relating to a person's character or identity.

senses.gloss: Pertaining to persons (human beings as opposed to things or animals).
Of or pertaining to a particular person; relating to, or affecting, an individual, or each of many individuals
senses.example: personal values; personal desire

senses.gloss: Dealing with subjects about which one wishes (or people usually wish) to maintain privacy or discretion; not for public view; sensitive, intimate.

definition_en: To suggest or advise something as being good or suitable.

senses.gloss: To bestow commendation on; to represent favourably; to suggest, endorse or encourage as an appropriate choice.
senses.example: The board recommends Philips, given his ample experience in similar positions.

senses.gloss: To make acceptable; to attract favor to.

senses.gloss: Accompanied with, or causing, anxiety; worrying.

etymology: From Middle English relesen, relessen, from Old French relaisser (variant of relascher).

examples.text: Of their elders some, by imitating the antics of youth, strive to persuade themselves that their day is not yet over; they shout with the lustiest, but the war cry sounds hollow in their mouth; they are like poor wantons attempting with pencil, paint and powder, with shrill gaiety, to recover the illusion of their spring.
examples.translation_ko: 기성세대 중 일부는 젊은이들의 우스꽝스러운 행동을 흉내 내며 자신들의 시대가 아직 끝나지 않았다고 스스로를 설득하려 애쓴다. 그들은 가장 힘차게 외치지만, 그 전투 함성은 그들의 입에서 공허하게 울릴 뿐이다. 마치 불쌍한 창녀들이 연필과 물감과 분칠로, 날카로운 쾌활함으로 자신들의 봄날이라는 환상을 되찾으려 애쓰는 것과 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A false impression or idea that is not based on reality.

senses.gloss: Anything that seems to be something that it is not.
senses.example: We saw what looked like a tiger among the trees, but it was an illusion caused by the shadows of the branches.

senses.gloss: A misapprehension; a belief in something that is in fact not true.
senses.example: Jane has this illusion that John is in love with her.

senses.gloss: A magician’s trick.

examples.text: Indeed, I was unconvinced that Robert Strickland did not share their illusion.
examples.translation_ko: 실제로 로버트 스트릭랜드도 그들의 착각을 공유하고 있는 것은 아닌지 확신할 수 없었다.

examples.text: they say nothing to me: to my mind they know too much and feel too obviously; I cannot stomach the heartiness with which they slap me on the back or the emotion with which they hurl themselves on my bosom; their passion seems to me a little anaemic and their dreams a trifle dull.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 내게 아무것도 말해주지 않는다. 내가 보기에 그들은 너무 많이 알고 너무 뻔하게 느낀다. 나는 그들이 내 등을 두드리는 그 호탕함이나 내 품에 몸을 던지는 그 감정을 견딜 수 없다. 그들의 열정은 내게 다소 빈혈기가 있어 보이고 그들의 꿈은 조금 따분해 보인다.

senses.example: my poor dear duke[…], in consequence of the excitement created in his august bosom by her frantic violence and grief, had a fit in which I very nigh lost him.

senses.gloss: The protected interior or inner part of something; the area enclosed as by an embrace.

examples.translation_ko: 그의 열정은 진실했고 비평은 예리했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The verb is derived from Middle English ridden (“to remove debris, obstructions, etc., from (a place), to clear; to complete (something unfinished)...
definition_en: To get rid of something unwanted

senses.gloss: Followed by of: to free (oneself or someone, or a place) from an annoyance or hindrance.
senses.example: I’m glad to be rid of that stupid nickname.

senses.gloss: Followed by away, from, or out of: to remove (oneself or someone, or something, that is annoying, troublesome, or unwanted).
senses.example: Worst of all though were the leeches. The soldiers had managed to rid them from the camp interiors, but once you ventured out on patrol and into the wetlands, they were everywhere.

senses.gloss: Often followed by from, of, or out of: to free or release, or to rescue or save, (oneself or someone, or something).
senses.example: Then comes ſhe [Juliet] to me [Friar Laurence], / And vvith vvild lookes bid me deuiſe ſome meane / To rid her from this ſecond mariage: / Or in my Cell there vvould ſhe kill her ſelfe.

examples.text: Then he went into the jewellery store to buy a pearl necklace—or perhaps only a pair of cuff buttons—rid of my provincial squeamishness forever.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 진주 목걸이를 사러—아니면 아마도 커프스 단추 한 쌍을 사러—보석상에 들어갔고, 나의 촌스러운 까다로움은 영원히 사라졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It would be an excuse to be rid of him.
examples.translation_ko: 그를 떼어놓을 핑계가 될 터였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Shall I get rid of Strickland for you?”
examples.translation_ko: "내가 스트릭랜드를 쫓아내 드릴까요?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fond, fonned, past participle of fonnen (“to be foolish, be simple, dote”), equivalent to fon + -ed. More at fon.
definition_en: Having a warm and affectionate feeling towards someone or something.

senses.gloss: Having a liking or affection (for).
senses.example: I am fond of this song!

senses.gloss: Affectionate.
senses.example: a fond farewell

senses.gloss: Indulgent, doting.
senses.example: I have fond grandparents who spoil me.

examples.text: I’m very fond of him.”
examples.translation_ko: 저는 그를 무척 좋아해요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “But aren’t you fond of them?
examples.translation_ko: "하지만 당신은 그 아이들을 사랑하지 않나요?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English warnen, warnien (“to warn; admonish”), from Old English warnian (“to take heed; warn”), from Proto-Germanic *warnōną (“to warn;...
definition_en: Give a warning or notice to someone.

senses.gloss: To make (someone) aware of impending danger, evil, etc.
senses.example: We waved a flag to warn the oncoming traffic about the accident.

senses.gloss: To notify or inform (someone, about something).
senses.example: I warned him he'd be getting a huge box of birthday presents from me.

senses.gloss: To summon (someone) to or inform of a formal meeting or duty.
senses.example: [...] the plaintiff fraudulently warned the meeting for November 15, giving only five days' notice [...]

examples.text: “Don’t bring Tom,” I warned her.
examples.translation_ko: "톰은 데려오지 마." 내가 그녀에게 당부했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Remember Biloxi,” Jordan warned her.
examples.translation_ko: "빌록시를 기억해." 조던이 그녀에게 경고했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “It’s only decent to warn you that you will be bored to extinction.
examples.translation_ko: "미리 경고해드리는 게 예의겠지만, 지루해서 죽을 지경이 되실 거예요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When the mail-boat, stopping for twenty-four hours on its way from Wellington to San Francisco, blew the whistle that warned the passengers to get on board, Tiaré clasped me to her vast bosom, so that I seemed to sink into a billowy sea, and pressed her red lips to mine.
examples.translation_ko: 웰링턴에서 샌프란시스코로 가는 도중 이십사 시간 정박하는 우편선이 승객들에게 승선하라는 경적을 울렸을 때, 티아레는 나를 그녀의 거대한 품에 안아서 마치 내가 물결치는 바다 속으로 빠져드는 것 같았고, 그녀의 붉은 입술을 내 입술에 눌렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin bis in diē.
definition_en: To offer or propose a price for something.

senses.gloss: twice a day, two times per day
senses.example: It has been repeatedly documented that moving patients from a TID dosing regimen to BID or OD vastly improves compliance, and thus the medicine's effectiveness.

examples.text: Those who went farther than Chicago would gather in the old dim Union Station at six o’clock of a December evening, with a few Chicago friends, already caught up into their own holiday gaieties, to bid them a hasty goodbye.
examples.translation_ko: 시카고보다 더 먼 곳으로 가는 사람들은 12월 어느 저녁 6시에 낡고 어스름한 유니언 역에 모여들곤 했는데, 이미 저마다의 휴일 흥겨움에 빠져 있던 시카고 친구 몇 명과 함께 성급한 작별 인사를 나누었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The last words he said to me when I bade him good-night were:
examples.translation_ko: 내가 그에게 안녕히 주무시라고 인사할 때 그가 내게 한 마지막 말은 이것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She made no secret of her desires, and I was bidden to translate.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 자신의 욕망을 숨기지 않았고, 나는 통역을 하라는 부탁을 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French plan (“a ground-plot of a building”), from plan (“flat”), a later form of the vernacular plain, from Latin planus (“flat, plan...
definition_en: A detailed proposal for doing something.

senses.gloss: A drawing showing technical details of a building, machine, etc., with unwanted details omitted, and often using symbols rather than detailed drawing to represent doors, valves, etc.
senses.example: The plans for many important buildings were once publicly available.

senses.gloss: A set of intended actions, usually mutually related, through which one expects to achieve a goal.
senses.example: He didn't really have a plan; he had a goal and a habit of control.

senses.gloss: A two-dimensional drawing of a building as seen from above with obscuring or irrelevant details such as roof removed, or of a floor of a building, revealing the internal layout; as distinct from the elevation.
senses.example: Seen in plan, the building had numerous passageways not apparent to visitors.

examples.text: He had made no plans.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아무런 계획도 세우지 못했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We must first think of some plan.
examples.translation_ko: 우선 어떤 계획을 세워야 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Attested since 1588, borrowed from Spanish tabaco. The Spanish word could be from Arabic طُبَّاق (ṭubbāq, “Dittrichia viscosa”) or from a Caribbean...
definition_en: A plant whose leaves are used to make cigarettes and other products.

senses.gloss: Any plant of the genus Nicotiana.
Leaves of Nicotiana tabacum and some other species cultivated and harvested to make cigarettes, cigars, snuff, for smoking in pipes or for chewing.
senses.example: Tobacco-settlement bonds are a tribute both to the inventiveness of bankers and the childlike impatience of politicians.

senses.gloss: A variety of tobacco.
senses.example: Tobaccos from the Connecticut Valley were used for wrapping cigars.

examples.text: The Dancies came, too, and S. B. Whitebait, who was well over sixty, and Maurice A. Flink, and the Hammerheads, and Beluga the tobacco importer, and Beluga’s girls.
examples.translation_ko: 댄시 가족도 왔고, 예순이 훨씬 넘은 S. B. 화이트베이트와 모리스 A. 플링크, 그리고 해머헤드 가족과 담배 수입업자 벨루가, 그리고 벨루가의 여자들도 왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We began to chat about vintages and tobacco.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 포도주 연도와 담배에 대해 이야기하기 시작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There was a tin of tobacco on the table, and, taking out his pipe, he filled it.
examples.translation_ko: 테이블 위에 담배통이 있었는데, 그는 파이프를 꺼내어 담배를 채웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English examinen, examenen, from Old French examiner, from Latin exāmināre.
definition_en: Investigate or study something carefully.

senses.gloss: To observe or inspect carefully or critically.
senses.example: He examined the crime scene for clues.

senses.gloss: To check the health or condition of something or someone.
senses.example: The doctor examined the patient.

senses.gloss: To determine the aptitude, skills or qualifications of someone by subjecting them to an examination.

examples.text: They stood side by side examining it.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 나란히 서서 그것을 살펴보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As we entered he wheeled excitedly around and examined Jordan from head to foot.
examples.translation_ko: 우리가 들어서자 그는 흥분해서 몸을 돌리더니 조던을 머리끝부터 발끝까지 살펴보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I welcomed the opportunity to examine him at my ease.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그를 여유롭게 관찰할 기회를 반겼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I had nothing to say and so sat silent, trying politely to show interest in the conversation; and because I thought no one was in the least concerned with me, examined Strickland at my ease.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 할 말이 없어서 조용히 앉아 있으면서 대화에 관심을 보이려고 정중하게 애썼고, 아무도 나에게는 조금도 신경 쓰지 않는다고 생각했기 때문에 편안하게 스트릭랜드를 관찰했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English schort, short, from Old English sċeort, sċort (“short”), from Proto-West Germanic *skurt, from Proto-Germanic *skurtaz (“short”...
definition_en: Having a relatively small length.

senses.gloss: Having a small distance from one end or edge to another, either horizontally or vertically.
Of comparatively small height.
Having little duration.
senses.example: Our meeting was a short six minutes today. Every day for the past month it’s been at least twenty minutes long.

examples.text: He gave a short laugh.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 짧게 웃었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His hair was reddish, cut very short, and his eyes were small, blue or grey.
examples.translation_ko: 머리카락은 적갈색으로 아주 짧게 깎았고, 눈은 작으며 파란색 또는 회색이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French prospereus, from Old French prosperer, from Latin prosperō (“I cause to succeed”), from Old Latin pro spere (“according to expec...
definition_en: Having a lot of money and being successful.

senses.gloss: Characterized by success.
senses.example: Trading Babe Ruth was far more prosperous for the Yankees than for the Red Sox.

senses.gloss: Well off; affluent.
senses.example: He was raised in a very prosperous household.

senses.gloss: Favorable.
senses.example: He chose a prosperous lottery number that evening.

examples.text: I was immediately struck by the number of young Englishmen dotted about; all well dressed, all looking a little hungry, and all talking in low, earnest voices to solid and prosperous Americans.
examples.translation_ko: 곳곳에 흩어져 있는 젊은 영국인들의 수가 즉시 내 눈에 띄었다. 모두 옷을 잘 차려입었고, 모두 약간 굶주린 듯 보였으며, 모두 든든하고 부유한 미국인들에게 낮고 진지한 목소리로 말을 걸고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: You were fairly prosperous.
examples.translation_ko: 당신은 꽤 잘살고 있었지.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He looked more than ever like a prosperous bagman.
examples.translation_ko: 그 어느 때보다 성공한 외판원 같아 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From in- + numerable; from Middle English innumerable, from Latin innumerābilis, from in- + numerābilis.
definition_en: Too numerous to count or be numbered.

senses.gloss: Not capable of being counted, enumerated, or numbered.
senses.example: The casualties of the Second World War were so great that they are innumerable.

senses.gloss: Of a very high number; extremely numerous.

examples.text: When she moved about there was an incessant clicking as innumerable pottery bracelets jingled up and down upon her arms.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 움직일 때마다 팔에 끼고 있는 수많은 도자기 팔찌들이 위아래로 부딪히며 끊임없이 딸랑거리는 소리가 났다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The flowers were unnecessary, for at two o’clock a greenhouse arrived from Gatsby’s, with innumerable receptacles to contain it.
examples.translation_ko: 꽃은 필요 없었다. 두 시에 개츠비네에서 온실이 도착했는데, 꽃을 담을 그릇들이 셀 수 없이 많았기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: That must be the story of innumerable couples, and the pattern of life it offers has a homely grace.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 수많은 부부들의 이야기일 것이고, 그것이 제시하는 삶의 패턴에는 소박한 우아함이 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Once they each of them earned a franc by loading trucks with innumerable boxes of oranges that had been dumped down on the quay.
examples.translation_ko: 한번은 부두에 쌓아놓은 수많은 오렌지 상자를 트럭에 싣는 일로 각자 1프랑씩 벌었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French classe, from Latin classis (“a class or division of the people, assembly of people, the whole body of citizens called to arms, t...
definition_en: A group of people with similar characteristics or interests.

senses.gloss: A group, collection, category or set sharing characteristics or attributes.
senses.example: The new Ford Fiesta is set to be best in the 'small family' class.

senses.gloss: A social grouping, based on job, wealth, etc. In Britain, society is commonly split into three main classes: upper class, middle class and working class.
The division of society into classes.
senses.example: Jane Austen's works deal with class in 18th-century England.

examples.text: He told me he was president of your class at Yale.”
examples.translation_ko: 예일에서 자네 학급 회장이었다고 내게 말했거든."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The Stricklands were an average family in the middle class.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 가족은 중산층의 평범한 가정이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: For the last year I’ve been going to some classes at night.”
examples.translation_ko: 작년부터 밤에 수업을 듣고 있어요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English contrarie, compare French contraire, from Old French contraire, from Latin contrārius (“opposite, opposed, contrary”), from con...
definition_en: A person or thing that is opposed to another.

senses.gloss: Opposite; in an opposite direction; in opposition; adverse.
senses.example: contrary winds

senses.gloss: Opposed; contradictory; inconsistent.
Given to opposition; perverse; wayward.
senses.example: a contrary disposition; a contrary child

examples.text: On the contrary, they were merely casual events in a crowded summer, and, until much later, they absorbed me infinitely less than my personal affairs.
examples.translation_ko: 오히려 그것들은 분주한 여름 속의 우연한 사건들에 불과했고, 훨씬 나중까지도 내 개인적인 일들보다 훨씬 덜 나를 사로잡았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I racked my brain, but could in no way account for an action so contrary to my conception of him.
examples.translation_ko: 머리를 쥐어짜봤지만, 내가 생각하는 그의 성격과 정반대인 그런 행동을 도무지 설명할 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Nonsense,” I answered promptly; “I don’t disapprove of the boa-constrictor; on the contrary, I’m interested in his mental processes.”
examples.translation_ko: "말도 안 되는 소리군요." 나는 즉시 대답했다. "나는 보아뱀을 못마땅하게 여기지 않습니다. 오히려 그놈의 정신적 과정에 흥미를 느끼죠."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English ashamed, aschamed, from Old English āsċamod, past participle of Old English āsċamian (“to be ashamed”), equivalent to a- + sham...
definition_en: Feeling embarrassed or guilty about something.

senses.gloss: Feeling shame or guilt.
senses.example: Be ashamed to die until you have won some victory for humanity.

examples.text: Rather ashamed that on my first appearance I had stayed so late, I joined the last of Gatsby’s guests, who were clustered around him.
examples.translation_ko: 첫 방문에서 이렇게 늦게까지 머물렀다는 것이 다소 부끄러워서, 나는 개츠비 주위에 모여 있던 마지막 손님들에게 합류했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You don’t seem in the least ashamed.”
examples.translation_ko: "당신은 조금도 부끄러워하지 않는군요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Won’t you be ashamed when you feel in your heart the desire for comfort and sympathy?
examples.translation_ko: 마음속에서 위안과 동정에 대한 욕구를 느낄 때 부끄럽지 않겠는가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English odde, od (“odd (not even); leftover after division into pairs”), from Old Norse oddi (“odd, third or additional number; triangl...
definition_en: Not even or normal.

senses.gloss: Differing from what is usual, ordinary or expected.
senses.example: She slept in, which was very odd.

senses.gloss: Peculiar, singular and strange in looks or character; eccentric, bizarre.
Without a corresponding mate in a pair or set; unmatched; (of a pair or set) mismatched.
senses.example: Optimistically, he had a corner of a drawer for odd socks.

examples.text: Michaelis didn’t see anything odd in that, and he gave Wilson a dozen reasons why his wife might have bought the dog-leash.
examples.translation_ko: 미카엘리스는 그것에서 이상한 점을 찾지 못했고, 윌슨의 아내가 개목줄을 샀을 만한 이유를 열두 가지나 들어주었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There were often odd jobs to be got about the fish-market.
examples.translation_ko: 어시장 근처에서는 종종 잡일거리를 구할 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He received us in a room that might have been in a house in a provincial town in France, and the one or two Polynesian curios had an odd look.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 프랑스의 어느 지방 도시 집에 있을 법한 방에서 우리를 맞이했는데, 한두 점의 폴리네시아 골동품이 묘하게 어울리지 않아 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lack, lakke, lak, from Old English *læc (“deficiency, lack, want”), from Proto-West Germanic *lak, from Proto-Germanic *laką, *...
definition_en: A deficiency or shortage of something.

senses.gloss: A deficiency or need (of something desirable or necessary); an absence, want, dearth.
senses.example: I went to a shrink, to analyze my dreams. He said it's lack of sex that's bringing me down.

senses.gloss: A defect or failing; moral or spiritual degeneracy.

examples.text: He discussed the most intimate matters with a complete lack of self-consciousness.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 가장 사적인 문제들도 전혀 자의식 없이 이야기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose it was commonplace in me that I felt slightly outraged at his lack of spirit.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 기개 없는 모습에 내가 약간 분개한 것은 아마도 내 속물근성 때문이었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pound, from Old English pund (“a pound, weight”), from Proto-West Germanic *pund, from Proto-Germanic *pundą (“pound, weight”),...
definition_en: A unit of weight or currency.

senses.gloss: Ellipsis of pound weight.
Various non-English units of measure.
A unit of weight in various measurement systems.

examples.text: I’ve got about a hundred pounds.”
examples.translation_ko: "백 파운드 정도 있어."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She’s got two or three hundred pounds and the furniture.”
examples.translation_ko: 그녀에게는 2백에서 3백 파운드와 가구가 있어."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Back-formation from confused, from Middle English confused (“frustrated, ruined”), from Anglo-Norman confus, from Latin cōnfūsus, past participle o...
definition_en: To cause someone to become confused or unclear about something.

senses.gloss: to puzzle, perplex, baffle, bewilder (somebody); to afflict by being complicated, contradictory, or otherwise difficult to understand
senses.example: It confused me when I went to the office and nobody was there, but then I realised it was Sunday.

senses.gloss: To mix up, muddle up (one thing with another); to mistake (one thing for another).
senses.example: People who say "hola" to Italians are confusing Italian with Spanish.

senses.gloss: To mix thoroughly; to confound; to disorder.

examples.text: Confused, he stared at us as we laughed.
examples.translation_ko: 당황한 그는 웃고 있는 우리를 멍하니 바라보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The relentless beating heat was beginning to confuse me and I had a bad moment there before I realized that so far his suspicions hadn’t alighted on Tom.

examples.translation_ko: 잠시 후 정신을 차린 그는 우리를 위해 거대한 특허 캐비닛 두 개를 열어 보였는데, 그 안에는 그의 수많은 정장과 가운과 넥타이들이, 그리고 벽돌처럼 쌓인 셔츠들이 열두 개씩 높이 포개져 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her gown was dowdy and expensive.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 드레스는 촌스럽고 비쌌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Her hair, not yet very gray, was becomingly arranged, and her black gown was modish.
examples.translation_ko: 아직 그리 희지 않은 머리카락은 보기 좋게 정리되어 있었고, 검은 드레스는 세련되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From vital + -ity, from Middle French vitalité, from Latin vitalitas (“vital force, life”), from vitalis (“vital”); see vital.
definition_en: The state of being full of energy and life.

senses.gloss: The capacity to live and develop.
Energy or vigour.
That which distinguishes living from nonliving things; life, animateness.

examples.text: The intense vitality that had been so remarkable in the garage was converted into impressive hauteur.
examples.translation_ko: 차고에서 그토록 두드러졌던 강렬한 활력이 인상적인 오만함으로 바뀌었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The mouth was wide open and ripped a little at the corners, as though she had choked a little in giving up the tremendous vitality she had stored so long.
examples.translation_ko: 입은 크게 벌어져 있었고 양쪽 끝이 조금 찢어져 있었는데, 마치 그토록 오랫동안 간직해온 엄청난 생명력을 포기하면서 조금 질식한 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There is in the streets of the poorer quarters of Paris a thronging vitality which excites the blood and prepares the soul for the unexpected.
examples.translation_ko: 파리의 가난한 동네 거리에는 피를 끓게 하고 영혼을 예상치 못한 일에 대비시키는 활기찬 생명력이 넘쳐흐른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English twinclen, twynclen, from Old English twinclian (“to twinkle”), equivalent to twink (“to wink; blink; twinkle”) + -le (frequenta...
definition_en: To shine with a faint, intermittent light.

senses.gloss: To shine with a flickering light; to glimmer.
senses.example: We could see the lights of the village twinkling in the distance.

senses.gloss: To be bright with delight.
senses.example: His shrewd little eyes twinkled roguishly.

senses.gloss: To bat, blink or wink the eyes.
senses.example: The Owl Fell a Moping and Twinkling.

examples.text: On Sunday morning while church bells rang in the villages alongshore, the world and its mistress returned to Gatsby’s house and twinkled hilariously on his lawn.
examples.translation_ko: 일요일 아침 해안가 마을들에서 교회 종소리가 울려 퍼지는 동안, 세상과 그 정부는 개츠비의 집으로 돌아와 그의 잔디밭에서 유쾌하게 반짝였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When he realized what I was talking about, that there were twinkle-bells of sunshine in the room, he smiled like a weather man, like an ecstatic patron of recurrent light, and repeated the news to Daisy.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 무슨 말을 하는지 깨달았을 때, 방 안에 햇살이 반짝이고 있다는 것을 알았을 때, 그는 일기예보관처럼, 되돌아온 빛에 황홀해하는 후원자처럼 미소를 지으며 그 소식을 데이지에게 되풀이했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His eyes twinkled.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 눈이 반짝였다.

examples.text: His eyes twinkled.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 눈이 반짝였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From prepare + -ed.
definition_en: Well-planned and ready for a situation.

senses.gloss: Disposed, willing, ready (to do something).
senses.example: The journalist interviewed an eye-witness who was not prepared to disclose his identity.

examples.text: I was not prepared to feel any great sympathy for her.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그녀에게 큰 동정심을 느낄 준비가 되어 있지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Does that mean that you’re prepared to take her back?”
examples.translation_ko: "그럼 그녀를 다시 받아들일 준비가 되어 있다는 뜻인가요?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bon, from Old English bān (“bone, tusk; the bone of a limb”), from Proto-Germanic *bainą (“bone”), from *bainaz (“straight”), p...
definition_en: A hard white tissue that forms the skeleton of a person or animal.

senses.gloss: A composite material consisting largely of calcium phosphate and collagen and making up the skeleton of most vertebrates.
Any of the components of an endoskeleton, made of this material.
senses.example: No Trophee, Sword, nor Hatchment o're his bones.

senses.gloss: A bone of a fish; a fishbone.

examples.text: He was nothing but skin and bone.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 뼈와 가죽만 남은 상태였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I am in the position of a biologist who from a single bone must reconstruct not only the appearance of an extinct animal, but its habits.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 뼈 하나로부터 멸종된 동물의 외모뿐만 아니라 그 습성까지 재구성해야 하는 생물학자의 처지에 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English worien, werien, wirien, wirwen, wyryȝen (“to choke, strangle”), from Old English wyrġan, from Proto-Germanic *wurgijaną, from P...
definition_en: Feel anxious or troubled about something.

senses.gloss: To be troubled; to give way to mental anxiety or doubt.
senses.example: So you go along for a long time / And nothing seems to worry your mind / But what it adds up to / It's the side effect / That finally gets to you

senses.gloss: Disturb the peace of mind of; afflict with mental agitation or distress; to exercise.
senses.example: Your tone of voice worries me.

senses.gloss: To harass; to irritate or distress.
senses.example: The President was worried into military action by persistent advisors.

examples.text: Don’t worry.
examples.translation_ko: 걱정하지 마세요.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Something worried me.
examples.translation_ko: 뭔가 걱정스러웠다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Are you sure it won’t begin to worry you?
examples.translation_ko: 정말로 그런 것들이 당신을 괴롭히기 시작하지 않을 거라고 확신하나요?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English enducen, borrowed from Latin indūcere (“lead in, bring in, introduce”), from in + dūcō (“lead, conduct”). Compare also abduce, ...
definition_en: To cause or lead to a particular feeling or situation.

senses.gloss: To lead by persuasion or influence; incite or prevail upon.
To cause, bring about, lead to.
senses.example: His meditation induced a compromise. Opium induces sleep.

senses.gloss: To induce the labour of (a pregnant woman).

examples.text: “Your wife says that nothing you can do will ever induce her to divorce you.
examples.translation_ko: "당신 부인은 당신이 무엇을 하든 절대로 이혼해주지 않겠다고 말했습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I forced him to eat, and after luncheon I induced him to lie down, but he could not sleep.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 억지로 그에게 음식을 먹게 했고, 점심 후에는 누워서 쉬도록 했지만 그는 잠들 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From definite + -ly.
definition_en: Used to emphasize that something is certain or true.

senses.gloss: Without question and beyond doubt.
senses.example: Joe definitely doesn't know how to drive a tractor.

senses.gloss: In a definite manner; decisively.
senses.example: And the Nose definitely turned away.

examples.text: “I know,” he said definitely.
examples.translation_ko: "나는 알고 있어." 그가 단호하게 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her frightened eyes told that whatever intentions, whatever courage she had had, were definitely gone.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 겁에 질린 눈은 어떤 의도든, 어떤 용기든 그녀가 가지고 있던 것들이 완전히 사라져버렸음을 말해주었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: You can put any possibility of that definitely out of your head.”
examples.translation_ko: 그런 가능성은 아예 머릿속에서 지워버리시기 바랍니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From deliberate + -ly.
definition_en: Done with careful thought and intention.

senses.gloss: Intentionally, or after deliberation; not accidentally.
senses.example: He deliberately broke that, didn't he?

senses.gloss: Taking one's time, slowly and carefully.
senses.example: After being called upon, he strode deliberately up to the blackboard.

examples.text: When I passed the ash-heaps on the train that morning I had crossed deliberately to the other side of the car.
examples.translation_ko: 그날 아침 기차로 재더미를 지날 때 나는 일부러 객차 반대편으로 건너갔었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her grey, sun-strained eyes stared straight ahead, but she had deliberately shifted our relations, and for a moment I thought I loved her.
examples.translation_ko: 햇빛에 지친 그녀의 회색 눈동자가 정면을 응시하고 있었지만, 그녀는 의도적으로 우리 사이의 관계를 바꿔놓았고, 순간 나는 그녀를 사랑한다고 생각했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was deliberately artistic.
examples.translation_ko: 의도적으로 예술적인 분위기였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I spoke as deliberately as I could.
examples.translation_ko: 가능한 한 신중하게 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Having or feeling too many people around.

senses.gloss: Containing a dense pack or mass of something; teeming.
senses.example:
Although it's always crowded
You still can find some room
For broken-hearted lovers
To cry there in their gloom.

examples.text: As the waiter brought my change I caught sight of Tom Buchanan across the crowded room.
examples.translation_ko: 웨이터가 거스름돈을 가져오자 나는 붐비는 방 건너편에서 톰 뷰캐넌을 발견했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: On the contrary, they were merely casual events in a crowded summer, and, until much later, they absorbed me infinitely less than my personal affairs.
examples.translation_ko: 오히려 그것들은 분주한 여름 속의 우연한 사건들에 불과했고, 훨씬 나중까지도 내 개인적인 일들보다 훨씬 덜 나를 사로잡았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I paid for what we had drunk, and we made our way to a cheap restaurant, crowded and gay, where we dined with pleasure.
examples.translation_ko: 우리가 마신 것의 값을 치르고, 붐비고 활기찬 값싼 식당으로 가서 즐겁게 저녁을 먹었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The Rue Bouterie is a narrow street of one-storeyed houses, each house consisting of but one room; they are like the booths in a crowded fair or the cages of animals in a circus.
examples.translation_ko: 부테리 거리는 단층집들이 늘어선 좁은 길인데, 각 집은 방 하나로만 이루어져 있었다. 마치 붐비는 장터의 노점이나 서커스의 동물 우리 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin medium, neuter of medius (“middle”), from Proto-Italic *meðjos, from Proto-Indo-European *médʰyos (“between”). Compare middle. ...
definition_en: A person who claims to have psychic abilities.

senses.gloss: The material of the surrounding environment, e.g. solid, liquid, gas, vacuum, or a specific substance such as a solvent.
The materials or empty space through which signals, waves, or forces pass.
senses.example: VVhether any other Liquours, being made Mediums, cauſe a Diuerſity of Sound from Water, it may bee tried: […]

senses.gloss: A format for communicating or presenting information.

examples.text: “A medium?”
examples.translation_ko: "영매?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Do you mean you’ve been to a medium?” inquired Jordan humorously.
examples.translation_ko: "혹시 영매한테 갔다 온 거예요?" 조던이 우스갯소리로 물었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But whereas his medium was paint, mine has been life.”
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그의 매개체가 물감이었다면, 나의 것은 삶 그 자체였다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “I wonder if you haven’t mistaken your medium,” I said.
examples.translation_ko: "당신이 매체를 잘못 선택한 것은 아닐까요?" 내가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pleasauntly; equivalent to pleasant + -ly.
definition_en: In a pleasant manner.

senses.gloss: In a pleasant manner; so as to achieve a pleasant result.
senses.example: He smiled pleasantly at passersby.

senses.gloss: Lightly
Ludicrously; facetiously.
senses.example: In workhouses, pleasantly so named, because work cannot be done in them.

examples.text: “I’d a little rather not be the polo player,” said Tom pleasantly, “I’d rather look at all these famous people in—in oblivion.”
examples.translation_ko: "나는 폴로 선수보다는," 톰이 유쾌하게 말했다, "차라리 이 모든 유명한 사람들을 망각 속에서 바라보고 싶어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Tom and Miss Baker, with several feet of twilight between them, strolled back into the library, as if to a vigil beside a perfectly tangible body, while, trying to look pleasantly interested and a little deaf, I followed Daisy around a chain of connecting verandas to the porch in front.
examples.translation_ko: 톰과 베이커 양은 그들 사이에 몇 피트의 황혼을 두고, 마치 완전히 실체가 있는 시신 곁에서 철야를 하듯 서재로 천천히 걸어 들어갔고, 나는 유쾌하게 관심 있어 하면서 약간 귀가 먹은 척하려 애쓰며 데이지를 따라 연결된 베란다들을 지나 앞쪽 현관으로 갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Life was ordered too pleasantly.
examples.translation_ko: 삶은 너무나 기분 좋게 정돈되어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I put his answer as pleasantly as I could.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그의 대답을 가능한 한 부드럽게 전했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English unable, unabel, unhable, unhabil, equivalent to un- + able.
definition_en: Lacking the ability or power to do something.

senses.gloss: Not able; lacking a certain ability.
senses.example: Are you unable to mind your own business or something?

examples.text: She must have broken her rule against drinking that night, for when she arrived she was stupid with liquor and unable to understand that the ambulance had already gone to Flushing.
examples.translation_ko: 그날 밤 그녀는 평소 금주 원칙을 어겼던 모양이었는데, 도착했을 때 술에 취해 멍한 상태였고 구급차가 이미 플러싱으로 떠났다는 것을 이해하지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She has a small mind, and she resents the abstract which she is unable to grasp.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 마음이 좁고, 자신이 이해할 수 없는 추상적인 것들을 원망한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When I had asked him what first gave him the idea of being a painter, he was unable or unwilling to tell me.
examples.translation_ko: 처음 화가가 되겠다는 생각을 하게 된 계기가 무엇이냐고 물었을 때, 그는 말할 수 없거나 말하고 싶어 하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + willing.
definition_en: Reluctant or unwilling to do something.

senses.gloss: Not willing; reluctant
senses.example: an unwilling servant

examples.text: When I had asked him what first gave him the idea of being a painter, he was unable or unwilling to tell me.
examples.translation_ko: 처음 화가가 되겠다는 생각을 하게 된 계기가 무엇이냐고 물었을 때, 그는 말할 수 없거나 말하고 싶어 하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The sight of him brought back to me all the horror which I was not unwilling to forget, and I felt in me a sudden repulsion for the cause of it.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 모습을 보자 잊고 싶었던 모든 공포가 되살아났고, 그 원인에 대한 갑작스러운 혐오감이 내 안에서 솟구쳤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English determinen, from Old French determiner, French déterminer, from Latin determināre (“to bound, limit, prescribe, fix, determine”...
definition_en: Decide or settle on a course of action.

senses.gloss: To set the boundaries or limits of.
senses.example: The knowledge of men hitherto hath been determined by the view or sight.

senses.gloss: To ascertain definitely; to figure out, find out, or conclude by analyzing, calculating, or investigating.
To fix the form or character of; to shape; to prescribe imperatively; to regulate; to settle.
senses.example: something divinely beautiful […] that at some time or other might influence or even determine her course of life

examples.text: He wanted to go and he didn’t see that Mr. Sloane had determined he shouldn’t.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 가고 싶어했지만 슬론 씨가 그를 데려가지 않기로 마음먹었다는 것을 눈치채지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I saw that for some reason of his own he was determined not to come, so I stood up.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 어떤 이유로든 오지 않기로 결심한 것을 보고 나는 일어섰다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: During his sea faring days he had cruised the South Seas, and he determined now to seek his fortune there.
examples.translation_ko: 항해하던 시절 그는 남태평양을 누볐기에, 이제 그곳에서 운을 찾기로 결심했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: If, seized by an intolerable boredom, he had determined to be a painter merely to break with irksome ties, it would have been comprehensible, and commonplace; but commonplace is precisely what I felt he was not.
examples.translation_ko: 만약 참을 수 없는 권태감에 사로잡혀 성가신 속박에서 벗어나려는 목적만으로 화가가 되기로 결심했다면, 그것은 이해할 만하고 평범한 일이었을 것이다. 하지만 평범함이야말로 그에게는 전혀 어울리지 않는다고 내가 느끼는 바였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The noun is derived from Middle English eg, egg, egge (“egg of a domestic or wild fowl; egg of a snake”) [and other forms] (originally Northern Eng...
definition_en: A roundish body produced by female birds for reproduction.

senses.gloss: The edible egg (sense 1.1) of a domestic fowl such as a duck, goose, or, especially, a chicken; (uncountable) the contents of such an egg or eggs used as food.
senses.example: We made a big omelette with three eggs.

senses.gloss: A food item shaped to resemble an egg (sense 1.1.1), such as a chocolate egg.
An approximately spherical or ellipsoidal body produced by birds, insects, reptiles, and other animals, housing the embryo within a membrane or shell during its development.
senses.example: [T]hinke him as a Serpents egge, / VVhich hatch'd, vvould as his kinde grovv mischieuous; / And kill him in the ſhell.

examples.text: My house was at the very tip of the egg, only fifty yards from the Sound, and squeezed between two huge places that rented for twelve or fifteen thousand a season.
examples.translation_ko: 내 집은 달걀의 맨 끝에 있었고, 사운드에서 겨우 50야드 떨어져 있었으며, 한 시즌에 1만 2천에서 1만 5천 달러에 임대되는 거대한 저택 두 채 사이에 끼어 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They are not perfect ovals—like the egg in the Columbus story, they are both crushed flat at the contact end—but their physical resemblance must be a source of perpetual wonder to the gulls that fly overhead.
examples.translation_ko: 그것들은 완전한 타원형이 아니었다. 콜럼버스 이야기의 달걀처럼 접촉면 끝이 모두 납작하게 눌려 있었지만, 그 물리적 유사성은 머리 위를 나는 갈매기들에게 영원한 경이의 원천임에 틀림없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His body was shaped like a huge duck’s egg; and his eyes, sharp, blue, and good-natured, rested now and then with self-satisfaction on his enormous paunch.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 몸은 거대한 오리알 모양이었고, 날카롭고 푸른 선량한 눈은 때때로 자신의 엄청난 배를 자족스럽게 내려다보았다.

examples.text: The cuckoo lays its egg in the strange bird’s nest, and when the young one is hatched it shoulders its foster-brothers out and breaks at last the nest that has sheltered it.
examples.translation_ko: 뻐꾸기는 다른 새의 둥지에 알을 낳고, 새끼가 부화하면 양부모의 새끼들을 밀어내고 마침내 자신을 보살펴준 둥지를 부숴버린다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bird, brid, from Old English bridd (“chick, fledgling, chicken”), of uncertain origin (see Old English bridd for more). Origina...
definition_en: A type of warm-blooded animal that can fly.

senses.gloss: An animal of the clade (traditionally class) Aves in the phylum Chordata, characterized by being warm-blooded, having feathers and wings usually capable of flight, having a beaked mouth, and laying eggs.
senses.example: Ducks and sparrows are birds.

senses.gloss: A chicken or turkey used as food.
senses.example: Pitch in and help me stuff the bird if you want Thanksgiving dinner.

senses.gloss: A man, fellow.
senses.example: "Ah, he's a funny bird," said Phaedra, throwing a leg over the sill.

examples.text: The shadow of a tree fell abruptly across the dew and ghostly birds began to sing among the blue leaves.
examples.translation_ko: 나무 그림자가 이슬 위로 갑자기 떨어지고 유령 같은 새들이 푸른 잎사귀 사이에서 노래하기 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There’s a bird on the lawn that I think must be a nightingale come over on the Cunard or White Star Line.
examples.translation_ko: 잔디밭에 새 한 마리가 있는데 큐나드나 화이트 스타 라인을 타고 건너온 나이팅게일인 것 같아요.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The pirate birds were screeching among the leaves of the palms.
examples.translation_ko: 해적새들이 야자수 잎사귀 사이에서 날카롭게 울어댔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You felt that a bird would speak in these tones if it could speak English.
examples.translation_ko: 새가 영어를 할 수 있다면 바로 이런 톤으로 말할 것 같다는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English seely, sēlī, from Old English sǣliġ, ġesǣliġ (“lucky, fortunate”), from Proto-West Germanic *sālīg, from *sāli; equivalent to s...
definition_en: Foolish or absurd.

senses.gloss: Laughable or amusing through foolishness or a foolish appearance.
senses.example: Well sir, I have a silly walk and I'd like to obtain a Government grant to help me develop it.

senses.gloss: Absurdly large.
senses.example: He cannot achieve celebrity by covering himself with diamonds... or by giving a silly price for a hack.

senses.gloss: Good; pious.
senses.example: The King of Spaine is counted very ſtrong, and the Pope is counted very ſtrong, because they haue a ſtrong hand to perſecute the ſilly ones of leſus Chriſt.

examples.text: “Don’t be silly; it’s just two minutes to four.”
examples.translation_ko: "바보 같은 소리 마세요. 4시까지 2분밖에 안 남았어요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I shook hands with him; it seemed silly not to, for I felt suddenly as though I were talking to a child.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그와 악수를 했다. 그러지 않는 것이 바보 같아 보였기 때문이었는데, 갑자기 마치 어린아이와 이야기하고 있는 것 같은 기분이 들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “How can you be so silly?
examples.translation_ko: "어떻게 그렇게 바보 같은 소리를 할 수 있어?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose he thought me very silly.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내가 아주 바보 같다고 생각했을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Having a strong unpleasant smell due to decay.

senses.gloss: Of perishable items, overridden with bacteria and other infectious agents.
senses.example: If you leave a bin unattended for a few weeks, the rubbish inside will turn rotten.

senses.gloss: In a state of decay.
senses.example: The floors were damaged and the walls were rotten.

senses.gloss: Cruel, mean or immoral.
senses.example: That man is a rotten father.

examples.text: “You’re a rotten driver,” I protested.
examples.translation_ko: "당신은 형편없는 운전자예요." 내가 항의했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “They’re a rotten crowd,” I shouted across the lawn.
examples.translation_ko: "그들은 썩어빠진 무리야!" 나는 잔디밭 너머로 소리쳤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I don’t care; it’s rotten nonsense.”
examples.translation_ko: "상관없어. 완전히 헛소리야."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You seem to have had a rotten time in Paris.
examples.translation_ko: 파리에서는 지독하게 고생한 것 같은데.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French effectif, from Latin effectīvus (“productive; effective”), from efficiō (“I make; I bring about”), equivalent to effect + -ive.
definition_en: Having a strong and positive effect.

senses.gloss: Having the power to produce a required effect or effects.
senses.example: The pill is an effective method of birth control.

senses.gloss: Producing a decided or decisive effect.
senses.example: The president delivered an effective speech!

senses.gloss: Efficient, serviceable, or operative, available for useful work.
senses.example: How long does it take to make a bunch of civilians an effective military force?

examples.text: Nor with such a man could you expect the appeal to conscience to be effective.
examples.translation_ko: 그런 사람에게는 양심에 호소하는 것이 효과적일 거라고 기대할 수도 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Sometimes it seems as if they grudge the longevity which postpones their chance of an effective scene.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 그들이 효과적인 장면을 연출할 기회를 미루는 장수를 원망하는 것처럼 보이기도 한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From conscious + -ness.
definition_en: The state of being aware of one's surroundings and thoughts.

senses.gloss: The state or trait of having cognition and sensation; cognition and sensation themselves.
senses.example: To lose consciousness after striking one's head

senses.gloss: The fact of having knowledge of a particular fact or matter; cognizance.
Acute awareness (of something) and belief in its communal relevance.
senses.example: the development of a feminist consciousness

examples.text: So engrossed was she that she had no consciousness of being observed, and one emotion after another crept into her face like objects into a slowly developing picture.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 너무나 몰입해 있어서 누군가 자신을 지켜보고 있다는 것을 전혀 의식하지 못했고, 천천히 현상되는 사진 속으로 사물들이 나타나듯 하나씩 하나씩 감정들이 그녀의 얼굴에 스며들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Or perhaps I had merely grown used to it, grown to accept West Egg as a world complete in itself, with its own standards and its own great figures, second to nothing because it had no consciousness of being so, and now I was looking at it again, through Daisy’s eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 아니면 내가 단지 그것에 익숙해진 것일 수도 있다. 웨스트에그를 그 자체로 완전한 세계로 받아들이게 되었고, 그곳만의 기준과 위대한 인물들이 있으며, 그런 의식 자체가 없기 때문에 그 어떤 것에도 뒤지지 않는다고 여기게 되었는데, 이제 데이지의 눈을 통해 다시 바라보고 있는 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He discussed the most intimate matters with a complete lack of self-consciousness.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 가장 사적인 문제들도 전혀 자의식 없이 이야기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It gave me the impression you get when you are sitting next door to a room that you know is empty, but in which, you know not why, you have a dreadful consciousness that notwithstanding there is someone.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 마치 옆방이 비어 있다는 것을 알면서도, 왜인지 모르게 그럼에도 불구하고 누군가 있다는 무서운 의식을 갖게 될 때 느끼는 그런 인상을 주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: One who counts.

senses.gloss: A reckoner; someone who collects data by counting; an enumerator.
An object (now especially a small disc) used in counting or keeping count, or as a marker in games, etc.
senses.example: He rolled a six on the dice, so moved his counter forward six spaces.

examples.text: “Then you ought to leave it alone,” countered Doctor Civet.
examples.translation_ko: "그럼 그냥 내버려둬야지." 시베트 박사가 반박했다.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 태도는 활기찼고, 그녀의 좋은 교양은 군인이 아니라면 점원이나 다름없다는 확신을 간신히 감추고 있었다.

examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 내게 돌아서더니, 한 옥타브 낮아진 목소리로 방 안을 전율하는 경멸감으로 가득 채웠다. "우리가 왜 시카고를 떠났는지 아세요?
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He lowered his eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 눈을 내리깔았다.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From desperate + -ly.
definition_en: Used to express a strong feeling of urgency or need.

senses.gloss: In a desperate manner; without regard to danger or safety; recklessly.

senses.gloss: extremely

examples.translation_ko: 그는 한 줌의 공기라도 붙잡으려는 듯, 그녀가 자신에게 사랑스럽게 만들어준 그 장소의 한 조각이라도 구하려는 듯 필사적으로 손을 뻗었다.

examples.text: She gave no sign that she hated Strickland so desperately.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 스트릭랜드를 그토록 절망적으로 미워한다는 기색을 전혀 드러내지 않았다.

senses.gloss: A competitive sporting event such as a boxing meet (commonly called a "bout"), a baseball game, or a cricket match.

senses.gloss: Any contest or trial of strength or skill, or to determine superiority.

senses.gloss: Someone with a measure of an attribute equaling or exceeding the object of comparison.

examples.text: Suddenly she threw the cigarette and the burning match on the carpet.
examples.translation_ko: 갑자기 그녀는 담배와 타고 있는 성냥을 카펫 위에 던져버렸다.

examples.text: He lit Daisy’s cigarette from a trembling match, and sat down with her on a couch far across the room, where there was no light save what the gleaming floor bounced in from the hall.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 떨리는 성냥으로 데이지의 담배에 불을 붙여주고, 복도에서 반짝이는 마루로 튕겨 들어오는 빛 외에는 아무 불빛도 없는 방 저편 소파에 그녀와 함께 앉았다.

examples.text: “Haven’t you got a match, you fool?”
examples.translation_ko: "성냥 하나 없어, 이 바보야?"

examples.text: I struck a match, and looked about for a candle.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 성냥을 켜고 촛불을 찾아 주위를 둘러보았다.

definition_en: To cause someone to suffer great pain or distress.

senses.gloss: A catapult or other kind of war-engine.
Torture, originally as inflicted by an instrument of torture.
Any extreme pain, anguish or misery, either physical or mental.
senses.example: He was bitter from the torments of the divorce.

examples.text: I saw a tormented spirit striving for the release of expression.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 표현의 해방을 위해 몸부림치는 고뇌에 찬 영혼을 보았다.

examples.text: I should have made Strickland’s marriage a long torment from which escape was the only possible issue.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 스트릭랜드의 결혼을 도피만이 유일한 해결책인 긴 고통으로 만들었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English beeste, beste, from Old French beste (French bête), from Latin bēstia (“animal, beast”); many cognates – see bēstia.
definition_en: A wild or ferocious animal.

senses.gloss: A domestic animal, especially a bovine farm animal.

senses.gloss: All non-human animals seen as a group.
senses.example: Language is what separates man and beast.

senses.gloss: A monstrously unusual and dangerous animal.

examples.text: “Women are strange little beasts,” he said to Dr. Coutras.
examples.translation_ko: "여자들은 이상한 작은 짐승들이야." 그가 쿠트라 박사에게 말했다.

examples.text: You’re the most loathsome beast that it’s ever been my misfortune to meet.
examples.translation_ko: 당신은 내가 불행하게도 만난 사람 중 가장 역겨운 짐승이에요.

etymology: From Middle English importaunce, from Middle French importance, from Medieval Latin importantia. By surface analysis, import (“to be important”) + ...
definition_en: The quality of being important or having a significant effect.

significance or prominence.
personal status or standing.

examples.text: And besides, I’m different; I’m not of any importance.”
examples.translation_ko: 게다가 저는 달라요. 저는 중요한 사람이 아니거든요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Because women can do nothing except love, they’ve given it a ridiculous importance.
examples.translation_ko: 여자들은 사랑 말고는 할 줄 아는 게 없으니까, 사랑을 우스꽝스럽게 중요하게 만들어버렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: The ability or power to do something.

senses.gloss: The ability to hold, receive, or absorb
A measure of such ability; volume
The maximum amount that can be held
senses.example: It was hauling a capacity load.

examples.text: In various unrevealed capacities he had come in contact with such people, but always with indiscernible barbed wire between.
examples.translation_ko: 여러 알려지지 않은 자격으로 그는 그런 사람들과 접촉했지만, 항상 그들 사이에는 보이지 않는 철조망이 있었다.

examples.text: For over a year he had been beating his way along the south shore of Lake Superior as a clam-digger and a salmon-fisher or in any other capacity that brought him food and bed.
examples.translation_ko: 일 년이 넘도록 그는 슈피리어 호수 남쪽 연안을 따라 조개 캐는 일꾼이나 연어잡이 어부로, 혹은 먹을 것과 잠자리를 구할 수 있는 어떤 일이든 하며 떠돌아다녔다.

examples.text: She was a little ashamed of her courage and business capacity, but delighted that she was going to dine the next night with a K.C. who lived in South Kensington.

examples.text: He had a sweet and generous nature, and yet was always blundering; a real feeling for what was beautiful and the capacity to create only what was commonplace; a peculiar delicacy of sentiment and gross manners.

definition_en: Agree to or approve of something.

senses.gloss: To express willingness, to give permission.

senses.gloss: To cause to sign a consent form.

examples.translation_ko: 하지만 베이커 양이 친절하게도 이 일에 대해 자네와 이야기해 주겠다고 동의했어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

definition_en: To combine different things together.
