senses.gloss: To combine (items from two or more sources normally kept separate).
senses.example: to mix business with pleasure

senses.gloss: To form by mingling; to produce by the stirring together of ingredients; to concoct from different parts.
senses.example: Yellow and blue paint mix to make green.

examples.text: “There’s nothing to get mixed up in.
examples.translation_ko: "끼어들 일은 없습니다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I can’t do it—I can’t get mixed up in it,” he said.
examples.translation_ko: "못 하겠어요—거기 끼어들 수 없어요." 그가 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Several people have suggested that she should go on the stage, but of course I couldn’t consent to that, I know all the chief dramatists, and I could get her a part to-morrow, but I shouldn’t like her to mix with all sorts of people.”
examples.translation_ko: "여러 사람이 그 아이가 무대에 서야 한다고 제안했지만, 물론 나는 동의할 수 없었어요. 나는 주요 극작가들을 모두 알고 있고, 내일이라도 그 아이에게 역할을 구해줄 수 있지만, 온갖 부류의 사람들과 어울리게 하고 싶지는 않거든요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English robben, from Anglo-Norman robber, from Late Latin raubāre, from Frankish *raubōn (compare Dutch roven) and Old High German roub...
definition_en: To take something from someone by force or stealth.

senses.gloss: To steal from, especially using force or violence.
senses.example: He robbed three banks before he was caught.

senses.gloss: To deprive of, or withhold from, unjustly or injuriously; to defraud.
senses.example: The best way to rob a bank is to own one.

senses.gloss: To deprive (of).
senses.example: Working all day robs me of any energy to go out in the evening.

examples.text: For all I knew he was going to rob the house in a moment; I wouldn’t have been surprised to see sinister faces, the faces of “Wolfshiem’s people,” behind him in the dark shrubbery.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 아는 한 그는 당장이라도 그 집을 털 작정일지도 몰랐다. 어두운 관목 뒤에서 음험한 얼굴들, "울프샤임의 사람들" 얼굴이 나타나도 나는 놀라지 않았을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Strickland’s injurious calm robbed Stroeve of the rest of his self-control.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드의 모독적인 침착함이 스트루브의 남은 자제력마저 앗아갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I felt that she was possessed by some shapeless dread which robbed her of all self-control.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 형체 없는 어떤 두려움에 사로잡혀 자제력을 완전히 잃은 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French ignorant. By surface analysis, ignore + -ant.
definition_en: Lacking knowledge or education.

senses.gloss: Unknowledgeable or uneducated; characterized by ignorance.
senses.example: The ignorant peasant, without fault, is greater than the philosopher with many; for what is genius or courage without an heart?

senses.gloss: Not knowing (a fact or facts), unaware (of something).
senses.example: That night he slept the sleep of happiness, blissfully ignorant that he had placed the letters in the wrong envelopes.

senses.gloss: Ill-mannered, crude.
senses.example: His manner was at best off-hand, at worst totally ignorant.

examples.text: He knew women early, and since they spoiled him he became contemptuous of them, of young virgins because they were ignorant, of the others because they were hysterical about things which in his overwhelming self-absorption he took for granted.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 일찍부터 여자들을 알았고, 여자들이 그를 응석받이로 키웠기 때문에 그녀들을 경멸하게 되었다. 젊은 처녀들은 무지하다고, 다른 여자들은 그의 압도적인 자기도취 속에서 그가 당연하게 여기는 것들에 대해 히스테리를 부린다고 여겼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You know, we English are so dreadfully ignorant.
examples.translation_ko: "아시다시피 우리 영국인들은 정말 무지하기 짝이 없어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: And let us seek the love of simple, ignorant people.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 단순하고 무지한 사람들의 사랑을 구해보자.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English slippen, probably from Middle Low German slippen, from Old Saxon *slippian, from Proto-West Germanic *slippjan, from Proto-Germ...
definition_en: To fall or move unintentionally.

senses.gloss: To lose one’s traction on a slippery surface; to slide due to a lack of friction.
To err.
senses.example: There is one that slippeth in his speach, but not from his heart, and who is he that hath not offended with his tongue?

senses.gloss: To accidentally reveal a secret or otherwise say something unintentionally.

examples.text: “I just slip it on sometimes when I don’t care what I look like.”
examples.translation_ko: "내가 어떻게 보이든 상관없을 때나 대충 걸치는 거예요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His wife and his mistress, until an hour ago secure and inviolate, were slipping precipitately from his control.
examples.translation_ko: 한 시간 전까지만 해도 안전하고 침범당할 수 없었던 그의 아내와 정부가 그의 통제에서 급격히 빠져나가고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The sweat made them constantly slip down.
examples.translation_ko: 땀 때문에 안경이 계속 미끄러져 내렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English houshold. By surface analysis, house + hold.
Cognate with Scots houshald, housald, housell, howsell (“household”), Dutch huisho...
definition_en: A group of people living together as a family.

senses.gloss: Collectively, all the persons who live in a given house; a family including attendants, servants etc.; a domestic or family establishment.
senses.example: Although I was a member of the royal household, I was not among the privileged few who were trained for rule.

senses.gloss: Entirety of work and management required to sustain the household.
Legal or culturally determined unit of people living together.

examples.text: There was something very charming in his little household.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 작은 가정에는 매우 매력적인 무언가가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suspected that for the figures had sat his household above Taravao, and the woman and the baby were Ata and his first son.
examples.translation_ko: 인물들의 모델로는 타라바오 위쪽에 있던 그의 가족이 앉았을 것이고, 여인과 아기는 아타와 그의 첫째 아들이었을 것이라고 나는 짐작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lengeren, frequentative of lengen (“to stay, dwell, tarry”), from Old English lenġan (“to lengthen, delay, extend”), from Proto...
definition_en: Remain or stay for a short time after something has finished.

senses.gloss: To stay or remain in a place or situation, especially as if unwilling to depart or not easily able to do so.
senses.example: It takes into account […] predictions of how long radioactive contaminants will linger in the soil and water near the nuclear facility.

senses.gloss: To remain alive or existent although still proceeding toward death or extinction; to die gradually.
senses.example: During his absence the queen fell ill, and after lingering for some time she died.

senses.gloss: To consider or contemplate for a period of time; to engage in analytic thinking or discussion.
senses.example: Trump doesn't linger on the poll.

examples.text: But Jordan lingered for a moment more.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 조던은 잠시 더 머뭇거렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Jordan’s party were calling impatiently to her from the porch, but she lingered for a moment to shake hands.
examples.translation_ko: 조던의 일행이 현관에서 성급하게 그녀를 부르고 있었지만, 그녀는 잠시 머물며 악수를 나누었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His eyes lingered on his picture.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 시선이 자신의 그림에 머물렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He dragged himself up the stairs; his feet seemed unwilling to carry him; and outside the door he lingered for a long time, trying to summon up courage to go in.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 계단을 질질 끌며 올라갔다. 발이 그를 나르기를 거부하는 것 같았고, 문 밖에서 오랫동안 머뭇거리며 안으로 들어갈 용기를 내려고 애썼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English resisten, from Middle French resister and Old French resistre, and their source, Latin resistere, from re- + sistere (“cause to...
definition_en: To oppose or withstand something.

senses.gloss: To attempt to counter the actions or effects of.
senses.example: Seeing the British establishment struggle with the financial sector is like watching an alcoholic who still resists the idea that something drastic needs to happen for him to turn his life around.

senses.gloss: To withstand the actions of.
To oppose; to refuse to accept.

examples.text: Do you think she could resist?”
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 참을 수 있을 거라고 생각하나?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was by now so worn out that he could not resist my firmness.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 그는 너무 지쳐서 내 단호함에 저항할 수도 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English marble, marbre; from Anglo-Norman and Old French marbre, from Latin marmor, from Ancient Greek μάρμαρος (mármaros), p...
definition_en: A type of metamorphic rock used for sculpture and building.

senses.gloss: A metamorphic rock of crystalline limestone.
senses.example: Open thy marble jaws, O tomb / And hide me, earth, in thy dark womb.

senses.gloss: A small ball used in games, originally of marble but now usually of glass or ceramic.
Statues made from marble.
senses.example: The Elgin Marbles were originally part of the temple of the Parthenon.

examples.text: Then I went out of the room and down the marble steps into the rain, leaving them there together.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 나는 방을 나와 대리석 계단을 내려 빗속으로 걸어 나갔다. 그들을 그곳에 함께 남겨둔 채.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was strange to reach the marble steps and find no stir of bright dresses in and out the door, and hear no sound but bird voices in the trees.
examples.translation_ko: 대리석 계단에 다다라서도 문 안팎으로 화려한 드레스들의 움직임을 찾을 수 없고, 나무 위 새들의 지저귐 외에는 아무 소리도 들리지 않는 것이 이상했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He brought out a picture of two curly-headed Italian urchins playing marbles.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 구슬치기를 하는 곱슬머리 이탈리아 꼬마 두 명을 그린 그림을 꺼내왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Medieval Latin brutalis (“savage, stupid”), from Latin brūtus (“dull, stupid”).
definition_en: Extremely harsh or violent.

senses.gloss: Savagely violent, vicious, ruthless, or cruel, often in an unintelligent manner.
senses.example: What began as a zeitgeisty outlaw romp in the Uncool Britannia of the 1990s is now reborn as a scabrous and brutal black comedy about middle-aged male disappointment and fear of death.

senses.gloss: Crude or unfeeling in manner or speech.
Harsh; unrelenting.

examples.text: I received the impression of a life intense and brutal, savage, multicoloured, and vivacious.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 강렬하고 잔혹하며, 야만적이고 다채로우며 생기 넘치는 삶의 인상을 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I do not think he was any gentler here, less selfish or less brutal, but the circumstances were more favourable.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 여기서 더 온화해졌거나 덜 이기적이거나 덜 잔인해졌다고는 생각하지 않지만, 상황이 더 유리했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English ragged, from North Germanic. Compare with Old Norse rǫgvaðr (“tufted”) and Norwegian ragget (“shaggy”).
definition_en: Having a rough or uneven edge or surface.

senses.gloss: In tatters, having the texture broken.
senses.example: a ragged coat

senses.gloss: Having rough edges; jagged or uneven
senses.example: ragged rocks

senses.gloss: Harsh-sounding; having an unpleasant noise

examples.text: Then he returned the wallet and pulled from his pocket a ragged old copy of a book called Hopalong Cassidy.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 지갑을 도로 넣고 주머니에서 『호팔롱 캐시디』라는 책의 너덜너덜한 낡은 판본을 꺼냈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We both looked down at the grass—there was a sharp line where my ragged lawn ended and the darker, well-kept expanse of his began.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 둘 다 잔디를 내려다보았다. 내 너덜너덜한 잔디밭이 끝나는 곳과 그의 어둡고 잘 가꾸어진 넓은 잔디밭이 시작되는 곳 사이에는 뚜렷한 경계선이 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Bananas with their great ragged leaves, like the tattered habiliments of an empress in adversity, grew close up to the house.
examples.translation_ko: 역경에 처한 여제의 너덜너덜한 의복 같은 크고 너덜거리는 잎사귀를 가진 바나나 나무들이 집 바로 옆까지 자라고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In the first place his red beard, ragged and untrimmed, hid much of his face, and his hair was long; but the most surprising change in him was his extreme thinness.
examples.translation_ko: 우선 그의 붉은 수염이 거칠고 다듬어지지 않아 얼굴의 상당 부분을 가리고 있었고, 머리카락도 길었다. 하지만 그에게서 가장 놀라운 변화는 극도로 말라빠진 모습이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Used to express a strong feeling or emphasis

examples.text: “Stroeve,” I said.
examples.translation_ko: "스트루브." 내가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In ten minutes Stroeve, panting, came back.
examples.translation_ko: 십 분 후 스트루브가 헐떡거리며 돌아왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sterven (“to die, perish”), from Old English steorfan (“to die, perish”), from Proto-West Germanic *sterban, from Proto-Germani...
definition_en: To die from lack of food.

senses.gloss: To die because of lack of food or of not eating.
senses.example: "When all of you starve to death, Shasta, don't come crying to me, that's all."

senses.gloss: To suffer severely because of lack of food or of not eating.
senses.example: ..., and the little half-starved, stunted girl of twelve, with her brown arms and steady, unerring aim, will hammer out half a bundle, IS. 6½d.

senses.gloss: To be very hungry.
senses.example: I was starving so I wrote S.O.S. on the desert island using rocks.

examples.text: “I am half starved.”
examples.translation_ko: "실제로 반쯤 굶어 죽어가고 있어."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was half starved.”
examples.translation_ko: 반쯤 굶어 죽을 뻔했으니까."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English licour, from Anglo-Norman licour, from Latin liquor (“fluidity, liquidness, a fluid, a liquid”), from liquere (“to be fluid or ...
definition_en: A liquid substance for drinking.

senses.gloss: A liquid, a fluid.
senses.example:
Dreaming when Dawn's Left Hand was in the Sky
I heard a Voice within the Tavern cry,
"Awake, my Little ones, and fill the Cup
Before Life's Liquor in its Cup be dry."

senses.gloss: A drinkable liquid.
A liquid obtained by cooking meat or vegetables (or both).

examples.text: Sometimes in the course of gay parties women used to rub champagne into his hair; for himself he formed the habit of letting liquor alone.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 흥겨운 파티 중에 여자들이 그의 머리에 샴페인을 비비곤 했지만, 그 자신은 술을 멀리하는 습관을 기르게 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: However, that was my fault, for he was one of those who used to sneer most bitterly at Gatsby on the courage of Gatsby’s liquor, and I should have known better than to call him.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그건 내 잘못이었다. 그는 개츠비의 술에 힘입어 개츠비를 가장 신랄하게 비웃곤 했던 사람 중 하나였는데, 나는 그에게 전화를 걸지 말았어야 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I changed my mind: it was not liquor that had driven him to this obvious desperation.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 생각을 바꿨다. 그를 이런 명백한 절망으로 몰아넣은 것은 술이 아니었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He told me of the long hours he spent walking about the Boulevard de la Madeleine on the look-out for Englishmen, preferably the worse for liquor, who desired to see things which the law forbade.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 마들렌 대로를 오랜 시간 걸어 다니며 영국인들, 특히 술에 취해 법으로 금지된 것들을 보고 싶어하는 영국인들을 찾아다녔던 이야기를 들려주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English valey, valeye, from Anglo-Norman valey, Old French valee (compare French vallée), from Latin vallēs/vallis. Doublet of vlei and...
definition_en: A low area of land between hills or mountains.

senses.gloss: An elongated depression cast between hills or mountains, often with a river flowing through it.
senses.example: The Indus River valley was the site of an ancient civilization.

senses.gloss: An area which drains itself into a river.
Any structure resembling one, e.g. the interior angle formed by the intersection of two sloping roof planes.

examples.text: Then the valley of ashes opened out on both sides of us, and I had a glimpse of Mrs. Wilson straining at the garage pump with panting vitality as we went by.
examples.translation_ko: 그러자 잿빛 골짜기가 우리 양쪽으로 펼쳐졌고, 우리가 지나갈 때 윌슨 부인이 숨을 헐떡이며 활기차게 주유소 펌프질을 하는 모습이 눈에 들어왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The valley of ashes is bounded on one side by a small foul river, and, when the drawbridge is up to let barges through, the passengers on waiting trains can stare at the dismal scene for as long as half an hour.
examples.translation_ko: 잿빛 골짜기는 한쪽으로 더러운 작은 강에 둘러싸여 있고, 바지선을 통과시키려고 도개교가 올라가면 기다리는 기차의 승객들은 30분이나 되는 동안 그 음울한 광경을 바라볼 수 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Sometimes I’ve thought of an island lost in a boundless sea, where I could live in some hidden valley, among strange trees, in silence.
examples.translation_ko: "때로는 끝없는 바다에 잃어버린 섬을 생각해봤다. 그곳 어딘가 숨겨진 계곡에서, 기이한 나무들 사이에서, 고요 속에 살 수 있는 곳을."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was told that that was what they called the Englishman, a painter, who lived with Ata up in the valley seven kilometres from where they were.
examples.translation_ko: 그들이 있던 곳에서 7킬로미터 떨어진 계곡에서 아타와 함께 사는 영국인 화가를 그렇게 부른다는 대답을 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From dim + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is seen or perceived faintly.

senses.gloss: In a dim manner; not clearly.
senses.example: "The evil is for those benighted ones who will have none of it; seeing the light the true believers worship, as the fishes see the stars, but dimly."

examples.text: Dimly I heard someone murmur “Blessed are the dead that the rain falls on,” and then the owl-eyed man said “Amen to that,” in a brave voice.
examples.translation_ko: 희미하게 누군가 "비 맞는 죽은 자는 복이 있나니"라고 중얼거리는 소리가 들렸고, 그러자 부엉이 눈의 남자가 용감한 목소리로 "아멘"이라고 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: This is a valley of ashes—a fantastic farm where ashes grow like wheat into ridges and hills and grotesque gardens; where ashes take the forms of houses and chimneys and rising smoke and, finally, with a transcendent effort, of ash-grey men, who move dimly and already crumbling through the powdery air.
examples.translation_ko: 이곳이 바로 잿빛 골짜기다—재가 밀처럼 자라나 능선과 언덕과 기괴한 정원을 이루는 환상적인 농장이며, 재가 집과 굴뚝과 피어오르는 연기의 형태를 취하고, 마침내 초월적인 노력으로 재빛 회색 사내들의 모습까지 만들어내는 곳이다. 그들은 가루 같은 공기 속에서 희미하게 움직이며 이미 부서져가고 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was obscure, perhaps, but I thought that I saw dimly his meaning.
examples.translation_ko: 모호한 말이었지만, 그의 뜻을 어렴풋이 알 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I dimly perceived a bed in the corner, and I wondered whether the light would disclose lying on it a dead body.
examples.translation_ko: 구석에 침대가 어렴풋이 보였는데, 불을 켜면 그 위에 시체가 누워 있는 모습이 드러날지도 모른다는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French sombre (“dark”), from Old French sombre, from a verb *sombrer or Latin sub- + umbra. Compare Spanish sombra (“shade; dark part...
definition_en: Having a serious and gloomy quality.

senses.gloss: Dark; gloomy; shadowy, dimly lit.
Dull or dark in colour or brightness.
Melancholic, gloomy, dreary, dismal; grim.
senses.example: The dinner was silent and sombre; happily it was also short.

examples.text: The friends looked out at us with the tragic eyes and short upper lips of southeastern Europe, and I was glad that the sight of Gatsby’s splendid car was included in their sombre holiday.
examples.translation_ko: 친구들은 동남유럽인 특유의 비극적인 눈과 짧은 윗입술로 우리를 바라보았고, 개츠비의 화려한 자동차가 그들의 음울한 휴일에 포함된 광경이 나는 기뻤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They seemed to possess a sombre passion of their own.
examples.translation_ko: 그것들만의 음울한 열정을 품고 있는 듯했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Here all the decencies of civilisation are swept away, and you feel that men are face to face with a sombre reality.
examples.translation_ko: 이곳에서는 문명의 모든 체면이 쓸려나가고, 인간이 음울한 현실과 정면으로 마주하고 있음을 느끼게 된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From the earlier (nautical) term brise, brize (“breeze”), from Middle English brees (“wind”). Ultimate origin obscure.
Variously supposed to derive...
definition_en: A gentle current of air.

senses.gloss: A light, gentle wind.
senses.example: The breeze rustled the papers on her desk.

senses.gloss: Any activity that is easy, not testing or difficult.
senses.example: After studying Latin, Spanish was a breeze.

senses.gloss: Wind blowing across a cricket match, whatever its strength.

examples.text: A breeze stirred the grey haze of Daisy’s fur collar.
examples.translation_ko: 산들바람이 데이지의 회색 털 칼라를 살랑거렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Daisy and Jordan lay upon an enormous couch, like silver idols weighing down their own white dresses against the singing breeze of the fans.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지와 조던은 거대한 소파에 누워 있었는데, 선풍기의 노랫소리 같은 바람에 맞서 하얀 드레스를 눌러 입은 은빛 우상들 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The breeze was laden still with the pleasant odours of the land.
examples.translation_ko: 바람에는 여전히 육지의 향긋한 냄새가 실려 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You feel like a disembodied spirit, immaterial; and you seem to be able to touch beauty as though it were a palpable thing; and you feel an intimate communion with the breeze, and with the trees breaking into leaf, and with the iridescence of the river.
examples.translation_ko: 마치 육체를 벗어난 영혼처럼, 비물질적인 존재가 된 기분이야. 그리고 아름다움을 마치 만질 수 있는 실체인 것처럼 손에 닿을 수 있을 것 같고, 산들바람과, 잎을 틔우는 나무들과, 강물의 무지갯빛과 친밀한 교감을 나누는 것 같아.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French offendre, from Latin offendō (“strike, blunder, commit an offense”), from ob- (“against”) + *fendō (“strike”).
definition_en: To cause someone to feel angry or upset.

senses.gloss: To hurt the feelings of; to displease; to make angry; to insult.
senses.example: Your accusations offend me deeply.

senses.gloss: To feel or become offended; to take insult.
senses.example: Don't worry. I don't offend easily.

senses.gloss: To physically harm, pain.
senses.example: Strong light offends the eye.

examples.text: He thought you might be offended.
examples.translation_ko: 당신이 기분 나빠할까 봐 걱정했어요.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I wondered if I had said anything to offend him.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 그의 기분을 상하게 하는 말을 했나 싶었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: If I’ve done anything to offend you I beg you to forgive me.
examples.translation_ko: 만약 내가 당신 기분을 상하게 한 일이 있다면 용서해 달라고 빌게요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was constantly offending Dirk Stroeve so bitterly that he flung away, vowing he would never speak to him again; but there was a solid force in Strickland that attracted the fat Dutchman against his will, so that he came back, fawning like a clumsy dog, though he knew that his only greeting would be the blow he dreaded.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 끊임없이 더크 스트루브를 몹시 화나게 해서 스트루브가 다시는 그와 말하지 않겠다고 맹세하며 뛰쳐나가게 만들었지만, 스트릭랜드에게는 뚱뚱한 네덜란드인의 의지와는 반대로 그를 끌어당기는 확고한 힘이 있어서, 스트루브는 자신을 맞이할 것이 두려워하는 매질뿐이라는 것을 알면서도 서툰 개처럼 아첨하며 다시 돌아오곤 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English constant, from Old French constant, from Latin constantem, accusative of constans, from cōnstāre (“to stand firm”). Displaced n...
definition_en: Remaining the same over time.

senses.gloss: Unchanged through time or space; permanent.
Consistently recurring over time; persistent.
Steady in purpose, action, feeling, etc.
senses.example: His gifts, his constant courtship, nothing gained.

examples.text: But his heart was in a constant, turbulent riot.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그의 마음은 끊임없이 격렬하게 요동쳤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The bottle of whisky—a second one—was now in constant demand by all present, excepting Catherine, who “felt just as good on nothing at all.”
examples.translation_ko: 위스키 한 병—두 번째 병—은 이제 그 자리에 있던 모든 사람들이 끊임없이 찾았는데, "아무것도 안 마셔도 충분히 기분 좋다"던 캐서린만은 예외였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was the constant lover, and though she grew old, losing her rounded lines and her fair comeliness, to him she would certainly never alter.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 변함없는 연인이었고, 그녀가 나이 들어 둥근 몸매와 아름다운 용모를 잃더라도 그에게는 결코 변하지 않을 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: To them he was no more than a beach-comber in constant need of money, remarkable only for the peculiarity that he painted pictures which seemed to them absurd; and it was not till he had been dead for some years and agents came from the dealers in Paris and Berlin to look for any pictures which might still remain on the island, that they had any idea that among them had dwelt a man of consequence.
examples.translation_ko: 그들에게 그는 늘 돈이 궁한 해변 부랑자에 불과했고, 다만 그들이 보기에 터무니없어 보이는 그림을 그린다는 기이함으로만 주목받았을 뿐이었다. 그가 죽은 지 몇 년이 지나 파리와 베를린의 화상들이 보낸 중개인들이 섬에 남아 있을지도 모를 그림들을 찾으러 왔을 때서야, 그들은 자신들 사이에 중요한 인물이 살았었다는 사실을 깨달았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lether, from Old English leþer (“leather”), from Proto-West Germanic *leþr, from Proto-Germanic *leþrą (“leather”), possibly bo...
definition_en: A strong and flexible material made from animal hides.

senses.gloss: A tough material produced from the skin of animals, by tanning or similar process, used e.g. for clothing.
A piece of the above used for polishing.
A cricket ball or football.
senses.example: The goalee made a frantic grab as the leather spun clean past him, but he was just a second too late, and Joe had scored for Redcliff.

examples.text: He felt the hot, green leather of the seat.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 좌석의 뜨겁고 초록색인 가죽을 느꼈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was nothing in it but a small, expensive dog-leash, made of leather and braided silver.
examples.translation_ko: 그 안에는 가죽과 은실로 짠 작고 비싼 개목줄 외에는 아무것도 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was too cold to sit outside, and we took our places on leather benches within.
examples.translation_ko: 밖에 앉기에는 너무 추워서, 우리는 안쪽 가죽 벤치에 자리를 잡았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From a- + head. Perhaps originally a nautical term, "beyond the head (of a ship)", then drifting into more general English usage where it is used t...
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is happening or will happen before something else.

senses.gloss: At or towards the front; in the direction one is facing or moving.
senses.example: The island was directly ahead.

senses.gloss: So as to be further advanced, either spatially or in an abstract sense; to be superior.
senses.example: He finished two laps ahead of me.

senses.gloss: In or for the future.
senses.example: There may be tough times ahead.

examples.text: “Jimmy was bound to get ahead.
examples.translation_ko: "지미는 성공할 운명이었어요.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Ahead lay the scalloped ocean and the abounding blessed isles.
examples.translation_ko: 앞쪽으로는 물결치는 바다와 풍요로운 축복받은 섬들이 펼쳐져 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Stroeve ran up the stairs ahead of me, and when I reached the top floor I found him talking to a workman in his shirt-sleeves who had opened a door at which Stroeve had knocked.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브가 나보다 앞서 계단을 뛰어올라갔고, 내가 맨 위층에 도착했을 때 그가 셔츠 차림의 일꾼과 이야기하고 있는 것을 보았다. 스트루브가 노크한 문을 그 일꾼이 열어준 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English candel, from Old English candel (“candle”), borrowed from Latin candēla (“candle”), from Latin candeō (“be white, bright, shini...
definition_en: A light source consisting of a wick or wicks immersed in a combustible substance.

senses.gloss: A light source consisting of a wick embedded in a solid, flammable substance such as wax, tallow, or paraffin.
senses.example: light a candle

senses.gloss: The protruding, removable portion of a filter, particularly a water filter.
A unit of luminous intensity, now replaced by the SI unit candela.

examples.text: “Why candles?” objected Daisy, frowning.
examples.translation_ko: "왜 촛불이에요?" 데이지가 얼굴을 찌푸리며 반박했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Among the broken fragments of the last five minutes at table I remember the candles being lit again, pointlessly, and I was conscious of wanting to look squarely at everyone, and yet to avoid all eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 식탁에서의 지난 5분간의 산산조각 난 파편들 사이에서 나는 촛불이 다시 켜지는 것을, 아무 의미 없이, 기억하고 있으며, 모든 사람을 똑바로 바라보고 싶으면서도 동시에 모든 시선을 피하고 싶다는 생각이 든다는 것을 의식했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I struck a match, and looked about for a candle.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 성냥을 켜고 촛불을 찾아 주위를 둘러보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Besides what I had suggested, he brought candles, and meat-juice, and a spirit-lamp.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 제안한 것들 외에도 그는 양초와 육즙, 그리고 알코올 램프를 가져왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From state + -ment.
definition_en: A declaration or assertion of fact.

senses.gloss: A declaration or remark.
senses.example: make a statement

senses.gloss: A presentation of opinion or position.
A document that summarizes financial activity.
senses.example: a bank statement

examples.text: “Why—any statement to give out.”
examples.translation_ko: "그러니까—발표할 성명 같은 것 말입니다."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A caddy retracted his statement, and the only other witness admitted that he might have been mistaken.
examples.translation_ko: 캐디가 자신의 진술을 철회했고, 유일한 다른 목격자도 자신이 잘못 보았을 수도 있다고 인정했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He said all this slowly, detaching statement from statement with a little awkward silence, and he kept his kind, foolish eyes fixed on mine.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 이 모든 말을 천천히 했고, 어색한 침묵으로 문장과 문장 사이를 끊어가며 말했으며, 친절하고 어리석은 눈을 내 눈에 고정시키고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I presumed that Strickland knew what had happened, for someone must have been to see him from the police, and he must have made his statement.
examples.translation_ko: 경찰에서 누군가 그를 만나러 왔을 것이고 그가 진술을 했을 테니, 스트릭랜드는 무슨 일이 일어났는지 알고 있으리라 짐작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From hasty + -ly.
definition_en: Done quickly or in a hurry.

senses.gloss: In a hasty manner; quickly or hurriedly.
senses.example: Eudemis moved hastily but as unobtrusively as he could through the gaping crowd[.]

senses.gloss: Soon, shortly.
senses.example: she with liquors strong his eyes did steepe, / That nothing should him hastily awake [...].

examples.text: “Oh, I will,” he broke out hastily.
examples.translation_ko: "아, 그럴게요." 그가 성급하게 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: My incredulity was submerged in fascination now; it was like skimming hastily through a dozen magazines.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 내 의심은 매혹감에 완전히 잠겨버렸다. 마치 수십 권의 잡지를 성급하게 훑어보는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: he said hastily.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 성급하게 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From draw (“to move by pulling”) + -er; compare French tiroir. Attested from the 16th century.
definition_en: A movable container for storing or holding things.

senses.gloss: An open-topped box that can be slid in and out of the cabinet that contains it, used for storing clothing or other articles.
senses.example: He knelt down and began shoving the drawer into the slot; the rail was misaligned so he banged it with the heel of his hand. It stuck.

senses.gloss: A side panel containing supplementary content.
Attributive form of drawers.
senses.example: The Sikh code of conduct does not restrict how Sikhs dress, except that they must wear kashera (drawer-type, cotton tie-able underwear) and a turban.

examples.text: “Which drawer?”
examples.translation_ko: "어느 서랍요?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “That drawer—that one.”
examples.translation_ko: "그 서랍—저거 말이야."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The knives and forks were put away in a drawer.
examples.translation_ko: 나이프와 포크는 서랍에 정리되어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He went to the drawer in which he kept his money and took out several bank-notes.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 돈을 보관하던 서랍으로 가서 지폐 몇 장을 꺼냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English symply, symplely; equivalent to simple + -ly, with *-lely simplified to -ly by haplology.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is straightforward or uncomplicated.

senses.gloss: In a simple way or state; considered in or by itself; without addition; alone.
Plainly; without art or subtlety
Foolishly; stupidly.

examples.text: “It was … simply amazing,” she repeated abstractedly.
examples.translation_ko: "정말… 놀라웠어요." 그녀가 멍하니 되뇌었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But there was a change in Gatsby that was simply confounding.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 개츠비에게는 정말 당황스러운 변화가 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I couldn’t let her live in those circumstances—I simply couldn’t.”
examples.translation_ko: "그녀를 그런 환경에서 살게 할 수는 없었어요. 정말 그럴 수 없었다고요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The emotions common to most of us simply did not exist in him, and it was as absurd to blame him for not feeling them as for blaming the tiger because he is fierce and cruel.
examples.translation_ko: 우리 대부분에게 공통된 감정들이 그에게는 아예 존재하지 않았으며, 그런 감정을 느끼지 못한다고 그를 탓하는 것은 호랑이가 사납고 잔혹하다고 탓하는 것만큼이나 어리석은 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Recorded since 1432 as Middle English resulten, from Medieval Latin resultare, in Classical Latin "to spring forward, rebound", the frequentative o...
definition_en: The outcome of a particular action or set of circumstances.

senses.gloss: To proceed, spring up or rise, as a consequence, from facts, arguments, premises, combination of circumstances, consultation, thought or endeavor.
senses.example: Pleasure and peace do naturally result from a holy and good life.

senses.gloss: To have as a consequence; to lead to; to bring about
senses.example: This measure will result in good or in evil.

senses.gloss: To return to the proprietor (or heirs) after a reversion.

examples.text: And the result was she hardly knew what she was saying.”
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 그녀는 자신이 무슨 말을 하고 있는지 거의 알지 못했어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was the result of the six years during which he had been painting.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 그가 그림을 그려온 6년간의 결과물이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was not so much puzzled by Blanche Stroeve’s action, for I saw in that merely the result of a physical appeal.
examples.translation_ko: 블랑슈 스트루브의 행동이 그리 이해하기 어렵지는 않았다. 거기서 나는 단순히 육체적 매력이 불러일으킨 결과를 보았을 뿐이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sinistre (“unlucky”), from Old French senestre, sinistre (“left”), from Latin sinister (“left hand”).
definition_en: Having or showing a threatening or unpleasant quality.

senses.gloss: Inauspicious, ominous, unlucky, illegitimate (as in bar sinister).
senses.example:
All the several ills that visit earth,
Brought forth by night, with a sinister birth.

senses.gloss: Evil or seemingly evil; indicating lurking danger or harm.
senses.example: sinister influences

senses.gloss: Of the left side.
senses.example: Before the train had stopped he had decorated his sinister shirt-cuff with the inscription, ‘J. P. Huddle, The Warren, Tilfield, near Slowborough.’

examples.text: I could see nothing sinister about him.
examples.translation_ko: 그에게서 불길한 것은 아무것도 찾을 수 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And with this doubt, his whole statement fell to pieces, and I wondered if there wasn’t something a little sinister about him, after all.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 의심과 함께 그의 말 전체가 산산조각 났고, 나는 결국 그에게 뭔가 조금 불길한 면이 있는 것은 아닌지 궁금해졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: By day it is merely sordid, but at night, lit only by the lamps in the little huts, the street has a sinister beauty.
examples.translation_ko: 낮에는 그저 더러울 뿐이지만, 밤이 되어 작은 오두막들의 등불만이 거리를 비출 때면 음산한 아름다움을 띤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His appearance was wild and uncouth; there was aloofness in his eyes and sensuality in his mouth; he was big and strong; he gave the impression of untamed passion; and perhaps she felt in him, too, that sinister element which had made me think of those wild beings of the world’s early history when matter, retaining its early connection with the earth, seemed to possess yet a spirit of its own.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 모습은 거칠고 조야했다. 그의 눈에는 냉담함이, 입에는 관능이 있었다. 그는 크고 강했으며, 길들여지지 않은 열정의 인상을 주었다. 그리고 아마도 그녀는 그에게서도 그 불길한 요소를 느꼈을 것이다. 그것은 물질이 대지와의 초기 연결을 유지하며 아직 고유한 정신을 지니고 있는 듯했던 세계 초기 역사의 야생 존재들을 떠올리게 했던 바로 그 요소였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French inevitable, from Latin inēvītābilis (“unavoidable”), from in- + ēvītābilis (“avoidable”), from ēvītāre (“to avoid”), from ē- (“o...
definition_en: Something that is certain to happen.

senses.gloss: Impossible to avoid or prevent.
senses.example: We were going so fast that the collision was inevitable.

senses.gloss: Predictable or always happening.
senses.example: My outburst met with the inevitable punishment.

examples.text: I remembered, of course, that the World’s Series had been fixed in 1919, but if I had thought of it at all I would have thought of it as a thing that merely happened, the end of some inevitable chain.
examples.translation_ko: 물론 나는 1919년 월드시리즈가 조작되었다는 것을 기억하고 있었지만, 그것에 대해 생각해본 적이 있다면 그저 일어난 일, 어떤 필연적인 연쇄의 끝 정도로 여겼을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Gatsby asked me to wait until he was free, and I lingered in the garden until the inevitable swimming party had run up, chilled and exalted, from the black beach, until the lights were extinguished in the guestrooms overhead.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비가 자신이 자유로워질 때까지 기다려달라고 부탁했고, 나는 정원에서 어쩔 수 없이 벌어지는 수영 파티가 검은 해변에서 몸을 떨며 들뜬 채로 뛰어올 때까지, 위층 객실들의 불빛이 꺼질 때까지 머뭇거렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was inevitable.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 피할 수 없는 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I think, even, he hated the inevitable partner in his debauchery.
examples.translation_ko: 심지어 그는 자신의 방탕한 행위에 불가피하게 동반되는 상대방까지도 미워했던 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English concepcioun, borrowed from Old French conception, from Latin conceptiō (“a comprehending, a collection, composition, an express...
definition_en: The formation of an idea or plan.

senses.gloss: The act of conceiving.
The state of being conceived; the beginning.
The fertilization of an ovum by a sperm to form a zygote.

examples.text: The truth was that Jay Gatsby of West Egg, Long Island, sprang from his Platonic conception of himself.
examples.translation_ko: 사실 롱아일랜드 웨스트에그의 제이 개츠비는 자기 자신에 대한 플라톤적 개념에서 탄생한 것이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: What could you make of that, except to suspect some intensity in his conception of the affair that couldn’t be measured?
examples.translation_ko: 그 말로 무엇을 알 수 있겠는가, 다만 그 사건에 대한 그의 생각에 측정할 수 없는 어떤 강렬함이 있다고 짐작할 뿐이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was a man without any conception of gratitude.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 감사라는 개념 자체가 없는 사람이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I racked my brain, but could in no way account for an action so contrary to my conception of him.
examples.translation_ko: 머리를 쥐어짜봤지만, 내가 생각하는 그의 성격과 정반대인 그런 행동을 도무지 설명할 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin indicātus, perfect passive participle of indicō (“to point out, indicate”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from in- (“in, to”...
definition_en: Show or suggest the presence of something.

senses.gloss: To point out; to discover; to direct to a knowledge of; to show; to make known.
senses.example: The guard blew his whistle to indicate imminent departure.

senses.gloss: To show or manifest by symptoms.
senses.example: Great prostration of strength indicates the use of stimulants.

senses.gloss: To point to as the proper remedies.
senses.example: It was strange to buy things I used to consider luxuries but were now medically indicated, like air conditioning and well-made shoes.

examples.text: he cried, needlessly indicating the direction.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 굳이 방향을 가리키며 외쳤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Gatsby indicated a gorgeous, scarcely human orchid of a woman who sat in state under a white-plum tree.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 흰 자두나무 아래 당당하게 앉아 있는, 거의 인간 같지 않을 정도로 화려한 난초 같은 여인을 가리켰다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I could have wished that Strickland had used some other phrase to indicate his refusal.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드가 거절의 뜻을 표할 때 다른 표현을 썼더라면 좋았을 텐데.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Mrs. Strickland and Mrs. Ronaldson looked down with a slightly pious expression which indicated, I felt sure, that they thought the quotation was from Holy Writ.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인과 로널드슨 부인은 약간 경건한 표정으로 고개를 숙였는데, 그 인용구가 성경에서 나온 것이라고 생각하고 있음이 분명했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English issue, from Old French issue (“an exit, a way out”), feminine past participle of issir (“to exit”), from Latin exeō (“go out, e...
definition_en: A problem or difficulty that needs to be dealt with.

senses.gloss: A movement of soldiers towards an enemy, a sortie.
The outflow of a bodily fluid, particularly (now rare) in abnormal amounts.
senses.example: And behold, a woman which was diseased with an issue of blood twelue yeeres, came behinde him [Jesus], and touched the hemme of his garment.

senses.gloss: The bodily fluid drained through a natural or artificial issue.
senses.example: For she doted upon their paramours, whose flesh is as the flesh of asses, and whose issue is like the issue of horses.

examples.text: “To be continued,” she said, tossing the magazine on the table, “in our very next issue.”
examples.translation_ko: "다음 호에 계속됩니다." 그녀가 잡지를 탁자 위에 던지며 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For some time confused and intriguing sounds had issued from a long, many-windowed room which overhung the terrace.
examples.translation_ko: 한동안 테라스 위로 돌출된 길고 창문이 많은 방에서 어수선하고 흥미로운 소리들이 흘러나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He made movements with his lips as though he were speaking, but no sound issued from them.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 무언가 말하려는 듯 입술을 움직였지만, 아무 소리도 나오지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I should have made Strickland’s marriage a long torment from which escape was the only possible issue.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 스트릭랜드의 결혼을 도피만이 유일한 해결책인 긴 고통으로 만들었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From breath + -less.
definition_en: Without breath or gasping for air.

senses.gloss: Having difficulty breathing; gasping.
That makes one hold one's breath (with excitement etc.).
senses.example: The plane buzzed on at a breathless speed. Bob had been in a plane before, and he had no fear. Indeed, but for the strange circumstances, he would have enjoyed that breathless rush through space.

senses.gloss: Not breathing; dead or apparently so.

examples.text: When they met again, two days later, it was Gatsby who was breathless, who was, somehow, betrayed.
examples.translation_ko: 이틀 후 그들이 다시 만났을 때, 숨이 가빠하고 있는 것은, 어떻게든 배신당한 것은 개츠비였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But what gave it an air of breathless intensity, was that Daisy lived there—it was as casual a thing to her as his tent out at camp was to him.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그 집에 숨 막히는 강렬함을 부여한 것은 데이지가 그곳에 살고 있다는 사실이었다—그것은 그에게 캠프의 텐트가 그런 것처럼 그녀에게는 자연스러운 일이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They are sensual with an unashamed violence that leaves you breathless.
examples.translation_ko: 그것들은 숨이 막힐 정도로 부끄러움 없는 격렬함으로 관능적이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She was evidently a copious talker, and now poured forth a breathless stream of anecdote and comment.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 분명히 말이 많은 사람이었고, 지금도 숨 가쁘게 일화와 논평을 쏟아내고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Recorded since circa 1374 as Middle English nerve, from Medieval Latin nervus (“nerve”), from Latin nervus (“sinew”). Doublet of neuron and sinew.
definition_en: A bundle of nerve fibers that transmit signals to and from the brain.

senses.gloss: A bundle of neurons with their connective tissue sheaths, blood vessels and lymphatics.
senses.example: The nerves can be seen through the skin.

senses.gloss: A neuron.
A vein in a leaf; a grain in wood.
senses.example: Some plants have ornamental value because of their contrasting nerves.

examples.text: Well, first Daisy turned away from the woman toward the other car, and then she lost her nerve and turned back.
examples.translation_ko: 글쎄, 처음에 데이지는 그 여자를 피해 반대편 차 쪽으로 핸들을 돌렸는데, 그러다가 겁이 나서 다시 돌아섰어.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her face, above a spotted dress of dark blue crêpe-de-chine, contained no facet or gleam of beauty, but there was an immediately perceptible vitality about her as if the nerves of her body were continually smouldering.
examples.translation_ko: 짙은 남색 크레이프 드 신 소재의 얼룩진 드레스 위로 드러난 그녀의 얼굴에는 아름다움의 편린이나 광채 같은 것은 전혀 없었지만, 마치 온몸의 신경이 끊임없이 타오르고 있는 듯한 즉각적으로 감지되는 활력이 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Good Heavens, my nerves are all distraught,” he said.
examples.translation_ko: "맙소사, 내 신경이 완전히 엉망이군." 그가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You scold yourself; you know it is only your nerves—and yet, and yet...
examples.translation_ko: 스스로를 꾸짖어본다. 그저 신경 때문이라는 것을 안다. 그런데도, 그런데도...
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English restles, restelees, from Old English ræstlēas, equivalent to rest + -less.
definition_en: Feeling or showing a lack of calm or peace.

senses.gloss: Not allowing or affording rest.
senses.example: The night before his wedding was a restless one.

senses.gloss: Without rest; unable to be still or quiet; uneasy; continually moving.
senses.example: He was a restless child.

senses.gloss: Not satisfied to be at rest or in peace; averse to repose; eager for change; discontented.
senses.example: A restless ambition.

examples.text: I enjoyed the counter-raid so thoroughly that I came back restless.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그 반격을 너무나 철저히 즐겨서 불안한 마음으로 돌아왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Gatsby’s foot beat a short, restless tattoo and Tom eyed him suddenly.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비의 발이 짧고 불안하게 바닥을 두드렸고 톰이 갑자기 그를 노려보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Looking back, I am vexed that I made such a fool of myself; I suppose the last restless nights had shaken my nerves more than I knew.
examples.translation_ko: 돌이켜보니 내가 그토록 바보 같은 짓을 했다는 사실이 화가 났다. 아마도 지난 며칠간의 잠 못 이룬 밤들이 내가 생각했던 것보다 더 심하게 신경을 상하게 했던 모양이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested in Thomas Browne's Religio Medici (1643) in sense 1, ostensibly from New Latin suīcīdium, from suī (genitive reflexive pronoun) + -c...
definition_en: The act of intentionally causing one's own death.

senses.gloss: The act of intentionally killing oneself.
senses.example: Other global taboos, such as sex and suicide, manifest themselves widely online, with websites offering suicide guides and Hot XXX Action seconds away at the click of a button. […]

senses.gloss: A particular instance of a person intentionally killing oneself, or of multiple people doing so.
senses.example: There had been half a dozen mysterious suicides which had been investigated by Scotland Yard.

senses.gloss: A person who has intentionally killed themself.
senses.example: "I remember one suicide," she said to Philip, "who threw himself into the Thames."

examples.text: “Do you want to commit suicide?”
examples.translation_ko: "자살하려고 작정했나?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her methodicalness made her suicide more deliberate.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 체계적인 성격이 자살을 더욱 의도적인 것으로 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She was going to have a baby, and she tried to commit suicide.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 아이를 가지게 되었고, 자살을 시도했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pees, pes, pais, borrowed from Anglo-Norman peis and Old French pais (“peace”), from Latin pāx (“peace”), from Proto-Indo-Europ...
definition_en: A state of quiet and tranquility.

senses.gloss: A state of tranquility, quiet, and harmony; absence of violence.
senses.example: Our lounge strives to maintain an environment of peace for the comfort of our customers.

senses.gloss: A state free of oppressive and unpleasant thoughts and emotions.
senses.example: The safety equipment will give me some peace of mind.

senses.gloss: Death.
senses.example:
’Twere best at once to sink to peace,
⁠Like birds the charming serpent draws,
⁠To drop head-foremost in the jaws
Of vacant darkness and to cease.

examples.text: It gave him no peace.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 그에게 평안을 주지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “She says she only wants to be left in peace.”
examples.translation_ko: "그냥 조용히 내버려 두었으면 좋겠다고 하네요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English aloud, a loude (“aloud”), equivalent to a- + loud or a- + loude (“sound”).
definition_en: Spoken loudly.

senses.gloss: With a loud voice, or great noise; loudly; audibly.
senses.example: Try speaking aloud rather than whispering.

senses.gloss: Audibly, as opposed to silently/quietly.
senses.example: speaking aloud rather than thinking thoughts privately

examples.text: “We won’t be late if we start now,” she insisted aloud.
examples.translation_ko: "지금 출발하면 늦지 않을 거예요." 그녀가 큰 소리로 고집했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I laughed aloud as the yolks of their eyeballs rolled toward us in haughty rivalry.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 눈동자가 거만한 경쟁심을 담고 우리 쪽으로 굴러오자 나는 큰 소리로 웃었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His father was a spare old man, his hands gnarled after the work of a lifetime, silent and upright; in the evening he read the paper aloud, while his wife and daughter (now married to the captain of a fishing smack), unwilling to lose a moment, bent over their sewing.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 아버지는 마른 노인으로, 평생의 노동으로 거칠어진 손을 가졌으며, 과묵하고 꼿꼿했다. 저녁이면 그는 신문을 소리 내어 읽었고, 그의 아내와 딸(지금은 어선 선장과 결혼했다)은 한 순간도 허비하지 않으려는 듯 바느질에 몰두했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English greef, gref, from Old French grief (“grave, heavy, grievous, sad”), from Latin gravis (“heavy, grievous, sad”). Doublet of grave.
definition_en: A feeling of great sadness or loss.

senses.gloss: Suffering, hardship.
senses.example: The neighbour's teenage give me grief every time they see me.

senses.gloss: Emotional pain, generally arising from misfortune, significant personal loss, bereavement, misconduct of oneself or others, etc.; sorrow; sadness.
senses.example: She was worn out from so much grief.

senses.gloss: A cause or instance of sorrow or pain; that which afflicts or distresses; a trial.
senses.example: Surely, he hath borne our griefs, and carried our sorrows.

examples.text: So Wilson was reduced to a man “deranged by grief” in order that the case might remain in its simplest form.
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 윌슨은 사건이 가장 단순한 형태로 남을 수 있도록 "슬픔에 미친 남자"로 축소되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The abnormal mind is quick to detect and attach itself to this quality when it appears in a normal person, and so it came about that in college I was unjustly accused of being a politician, because I was privy to the secret griefs of wild, unknown men.
examples.translation_ko: 비정상적인 정신은 이런 자질이 정상적인 사람에게서 나타날 때 재빨리 알아채고 달라붙는 법이어서, 대학 시절 나는 정치꾼이라는 부당한 누명을 썼다. 거칠고 낯선 남자들의 은밀한 고통을 알고 있었기 때문이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Poor soul, she was so proud; and though it nearly broke her heart to part from me, she smiled, and would not show me her grief.
examples.translation_ko: 불쌍한 어머니는 너무나 자랑스러워하셨지만, 저와 헤어지는 것이 가슴 아프셨을 텐데도 웃으시며 슬픔을 내색하지 않으셨어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Grief and jealousy and rage seized him, and he cried out hoarsely; he was inarticulate; he clenched his fists and raised them threateningly at an invisible enemy.
examples.translation_ko: 슬픔과 질투와 분노가 그를 사로잡았고, 그는 쉰 목소리로 외쳤다. 말이 제대로 나오지 않았다. 주먹을 꽉 쥐고 보이지 않는 적을 향해 위협적으로 치켜들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English eternal, from Old French eternal, from Late Latin aeternālis, from Latin aeternus (“eternal”), from aevum (“age”). Displaced na...
definition_en: Lasting forever or for a very long time.

senses.gloss: Lasting forever; unending.
senses.example: Thy smoking altar shall be fat with food / Of incense and the grateful steam of blood; / Burnt-offerings morn and evening shall be thine, / And fires eternal in thy temple shine.

senses.gloss: Existing outside time; as opposed to sempiternal, existing within time but everlastingly.
Constant; perpetual; ceaseless; ever-present.

examples.text: It was one of those rare smiles with a quality of eternal reassurance in it, that you may come across four or five times in life.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 영원한 안심을 주는 품격을 지닌 드문 미소 중 하나였는데, 평생에 네다섯 번 마주칠까 말까 한 그런 미소였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It faced—or seemed to face—the whole eternal world for an instant, and then concentrated on you with an irresistible prejudice in your favour.
examples.translation_ko: 그 미소는 순간 영원한 세상 전체를 마주하는 듯—아니 정말로 마주하는 듯—보이다가, 그러고는 당신에게 유리한 거부할 수 없는 편견을 품고 당신에게 집중되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I see you as the eternal pilgrim to some shrine that perhaps does not exist.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 당신을 아마도 존재하지 않을지도 모르는 어떤 성지를 향한 영원한 순례자로 봅니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was not only the bold simplification of the drawing which showed so rich and so singular a personality; it was not only the painting, though the flesh was painted with a passionate sensuality which had in it something miraculous; it was not only the solidity, so that you felt extraordinarily the weight of the body; there was also a spirituality, troubling and new, which led the imagination along unsuspected ways, and suggested dim empty spaces, lit only by the eternal stars, where the soul, all naked, adventured fearful to the discovery of new mysteries.
examples.translation_ko: 그토록 풍부하고 독특한 개성을 보여주는 것은 단지 대담한 소묘의 단순화만이 아니었다. 단지 회화 기법만도 아니었다. 비록 살결이 기적적인 무언가를 담은 열정적인 관능미로 그려졌지만 말이다. 단지 육체의 무게감을 놀라울 정도로 느끼게 하는 견고함만도 아니었다. 거기에는 또한 불안하고 새로운 영성이 있어서, 상상력을 예상치 못한 길로 이끌고, 영원한 별들만이 비추는 희미하고 공허한 공간들을 암시했다. 그곳에서 벌거벗은 영혼이 새로운 신비의 발견을 향해 두려워하며 모험을 떠나는 곳을.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English dekke, borrowed from Middle Dutch dec (“roof, covering”), from Middle Dutch decken, from Old Dutch thecken, from Proto-West Ger...
definition_en: To furnish or equip with a deck.

senses.gloss: Any raised flat surface that can be walked on: a balcony; a porch; a raised patio; a flat rooftop.
The floorlike covering of the horizontal sections, or compartments, of a ship or boat. Small vessels have only one deck; larger ships have two or three decks.
senses.example: to swab the deck

senses.gloss: A main aeroplane surface, especially of a biplane or multiplane.

examples.text: To young Gatz, resting on his oars and looking up at the railed deck, that yacht represented all the beauty and glamour in the world.
examples.translation_ko: 노를 멈추고 난간이 있는 갑판을 올려다보는 젊은 개츠에게 그 요트는 세상의 모든 아름다움과 화려함을 상징했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had thrown himself into it with a creative passion, adding to it all the time, decking it out with every bright feather that drifted his way.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 창조적인 열정으로 그 환상에 몸을 던졌고, 끊임없이 거기에 무언가를 보태면서, 자신에게 떠밀려 오는 모든 찬란한 깃털로 그것을 치장했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I’d been scrubbing the deck, and all at once a chap said to me: ‘Why, there it is.’
examples.translation_ko: "갑판을 문지르고 있었는데, 갑자기 한 녀석이 내게 말했어요. '어, 저기 있네.'
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The false emphasis with which they try to deck their worthless thoughts blunts their susceptibilities.
examples.translation_ko: 그들이 자신의 무가치한 생각을 치장하려고 사용하는 거짓된 강조는 그들의 감수성을 무디게 만든다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From complete + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is done or achieved fully.

senses.gloss: In a complete manner; thoroughly.
senses.example: Please completely fill in the box for your answer, using a number 2 pencil.

senses.gloss: To the fullest extent or degree; totally.
senses.example: He is completely mad.

examples.text: I hardly know where I am when I hear about a thing like this and am completely knocked down and out.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 일에 대해 들으면 제가 어디에 있는지도 모르겠고 완전히 넘어져서 기진맥진해집니다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The only completely stationary object in the room was an enormous couch on which two young women were buoyed up as though upon an anchored balloon.
examples.translation_ko: 방에서 완전히 정지해 있는 유일한 물건은 거대한 소파였는데, 그 위에 두 젊은 여자가 마치 정박한 기구 위에라도 떠 있는 듯 올라앉아 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “It just happens that I am a completely normal man.”
examples.translation_ko: "나는 그저 완전히 정상적인 남자일 뿐이다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose no artist achieves completely the realisation of the dream that obsesses him, and Strickland, harassed incessantly by his struggle with technique, managed, perhaps, less than others to express the vision that he saw with his mind’s eye; but in Tahiti the circumstances were favourable to him; he found in his surroundings the accidents necessary for his inspiration to become effective, and his later pictures give at least a suggestion of what he sought.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 예술가도 자신을 사로잡는 꿈을 완전히 실현하지는 못하는 법이고, 기법과의 끊임없는 투쟁에 시달린 스트릭랜드는 아마도 다른 이들보다도 더 적게 자신이 마음의 눈으로 본 환상을 표현해냈을 것이다. 하지만 타히티에서는 상황이 그에게 유리했다. 그는 주변 환경에서 자신의 영감이 효과를 발휘하는 데 필요한 우연들을 발견했고, 그의 후기 작품들은 적어도 그가 추구했던 것의 암시를 보여준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English hospitalite, from Old French hospitalité (modern French hospitalité), from Latin hospitālitās (“hospitality”), from hospitālis ...
definition_en: The quality of being welcoming and generous to guests.

senses.gloss: The act or service of welcoming, receiving, hosting, or entertaining guests; an appropriate attitude of openness, respect, and generosity toward guests.
senses.example: Please thank our hosts for their hospitality during the week that we stayed.

senses.gloss: The business of providing catering, lodging and entertainment service; the industry which includes the operation of hotels, restaurants, and similar enterprises.
senses.example: After graduating from college, she found a job in hospitality.

senses.gloss: The food, drink, and entertainment given to customers by a company or organization or provided to visitors by a private host.

examples.text: I thanked him for his hospitality.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그의 환대에 감사를 표했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Gatsby’s notoriety, spread about by the hundreds who had accepted his hospitality and so become authorities upon his past, had increased all summer until he fell just short of being news.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비의 악명은 그의 환대를 받아들여 그의 과거에 대한 권위자가 된 수백 명의 사람들에 의해 퍼져나가 여름 내내 커져서, 뉴스거리가 되기 직전까지 이르렀다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When the doors of the Asile de Nuit were closed to them, Strickland and Captain Nichols sought the hospitality of Tough Bill.
examples.translation_ko: 아질 드 뉘의 문이 그들에게 닫혔을 때, 스트릭랜드와 니콜스 선장은 터프 빌의 환대를 구했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Hospitality was a passion with her, and there was no one on the island who need go without a dinner when there was anything to eat at the Hôtel de la Fleur.
examples.translation_ko: 손님 접대는 그녀의 열정이었고, 플뢰르 호텔에 먹을 것이 있는 한 섬에서 저녁을 굶어야 하는 사람은 아무도 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English gardener, either calqued or loaned from Anglo-Norman and Old Northern French gardinier.
See garden, and compare German Gärtner ...
definition_en: A person who cultivates and maintains gardens.

senses.gloss: One who gardens; one who grows plants or cultivates a garden.
senses.example: "Ponder the fact that God has made you a gardener, to root out vice and to plant virtue." — St. Catherine of Siena

senses.gloss: A coachman who drives badly.
senses.example: Get on, gardener! Get on, you slow and clumsy coachman. The allusion is to a man who is both gardener and coachman.

examples.text: The gardener, the last one of Gatsby’s former servants, came to the foot of the steps.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비의 옛 하인들 중 마지막 남은 정원사가 계단 아래로 다가왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: With scarcely a word said, four of us, the chauffeur, butler, gardener, and I hurried down to the pool.
examples.translation_ko: 거의 말도 없이 우리 넷—운전기사, 집사, 정원사, 그리고 나—이 서둘러 수영장으로 내려갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Their brain is seething with ideas, and they can only tell you that the umbrella of the gardener’s aunt is in the house.
examples.translation_ko: 머릿속에는 온갖 생각들이 끓어오르는데, 정작 할 수 있는 말이라고는 정원사 아주머니의 우산이 집에 있다는 것뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English nere, ner, from Old English nēar (“nearer”, comparative of nēah (“nigh”), the superlative would become next), influenced by Old...
definition_en: Located close to something.

senses.gloss: Physically close.
senses.example: I can't see near objects very clearly without my glasses.

senses.gloss: Close in time.
senses.example: The end is near.

senses.gloss: Closely connected or related.
senses.example: The deceased man had no near relatives.

examples.text: Then we came near, and I seemed to recognise it.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 가까이 다가가니, 그곳을 알아보는 것 같았어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: A chapter of my life was closed, and I felt a little nearer to inevitable death.
examples.translation_ko: 내 인생의 한 장이 막을 내렸고, 나는 피할 수 없는 죽음에 조금 더 가까워진 기분이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: By surface analysis, overwhelm + -ing.
definition_en: Extremely difficult to handle or manage.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of overwhelm

examples.text: To my overwhelming surprise the living-room was deserted.
examples.translation_ko: 놀랍게도 거실에는 아무도 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He knew women early, and since they spoiled him he became contemptuous of them, of young virgins because they were ignorant, of the others because they were hysterical about things which in his overwhelming self-absorption he took for granted.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 일찍부터 여자들을 알았고, 여자들이 그를 응석받이로 키웠기 때문에 그녀들을 경멸하게 되었다. 젊은 처녀들은 무지하다고, 다른 여자들은 그의 압도적인 자기도취 속에서 그가 당연하게 여기는 것들에 대해 히스테리를 부린다고 여겼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I felt an overwhelming compassion.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 압도적인 연민을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was genius, and it was stupendous and overwhelming.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 천재성이었고, 경이롭고 압도적이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin persistentem, present participle of persistō (“continue steadfastly”). By surface analysis, persist + -ent.
definition_en: Continuing to exist or be present over a long period of time.

senses.gloss: Obstinately refusing to give up or let go.
senses.example: She has had a persistent cough for weeks.

senses.gloss: Insistently repetitive.
senses.example: There was a persistent knocking on the door.

senses.gloss: Indefinitely continuous.
senses.example: There have been persistent rumours for years.

examples.text: All the cars have the left rear wheel painted black as a mourning wreath, and there’s a persistent wail all night along the north shore.”
examples.translation_ko: 모든 자동차의 왼쪽 뒷바퀴에 조화 대신 검은 페인트를 칠해놓았고, 밤새도록 북쪽 해안을 따라 애절한 곡소리가 끊이지 않아."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I followed him over a low whitewashed railroad fence, and we walked back a hundred yards along the road under Doctor Eckleburg’s persistent stare.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그를 따라 낮은 하얀 철도 울타리를 넘어 에클버그 박사의 끈질긴 시선 아래 길을 따라 백 야드쯤 되돌아 걸었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But it is unfortunate that I can give no description of the arduous steps by which he reached such mastery over his art as he ever acquired; for if I could show him undaunted by failure, by an unceasing effort of courage holding despair at bay, doggedly persistent in the face of self-doubt, which is the artist’s bitterest enemy, I might excite some sympathy for a personality which, I am all too conscious, must appear singularly devoid of charm.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그가 자신의 예술에서 그 정도의 숙련에 이르기까지 거쳐야 했던 험난한 과정을 묘사할 수 없다는 것은 유감스러운 일이다. 만약 내가 실패에 굴복하지 않고, 끊임없는 용기의 노력으로 절망을 물리치며, 예술가의 가장 쓰라린 적인 자기 의심 앞에서도 완고하게 버텨내는 그의 모습을 보여줄 수 있다면, 매력이 현저히 부족해 보일 수밖에 없다는 것을 나 자신도 너무나 잘 알고 있는 이 인물에 대해 어느 정도 동정심을 불러일으킬 수 있을 텐데 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Move through the air without landing.

senses.gloss: To keep (something, such as an aircraft) in a stationary state in the air.
Of a bird: to shelter (chicks) under its body and wings; (by extension) of a thing: to cover or surround (something).
Of a bird or insect: to flap (its wings) so it can remain stationary in the air.
senses.example: Thus have I lain conceal'd like a vvinter Fly, hoping for ſome bleſt Sun-Shine to vvarm me into Life again, and make me hover my flagging VVings; […]

examples.text: A silver curve of the moon hovered already in the western sky.
examples.translation_ko: 은빛 초승달이 이미 서쪽 하늘에 떠 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Tom Buchanan, who had been hovering restlessly about the room, stopped and rested his hand on my shoulder.
examples.translation_ko: 방 안을 안절부절못하며 서성이던 톰 뷰캐넌이 걸음을 멈추고 내 어깨에 손을 올렸다.

examples.text: His thoughts floated then serenely in the empyrean, and he felt towards her the horror that perhaps the painted butterfly, hovering about the flowers, feels to the filthy chrysalis from which it has triumphantly emerged.
examples.translation_ko: 그때 그의 사상은 천상계에서 고요히 떠돌았고, 꽃들 주위를 맴도는 아름다운 나비가 자신이 승리를 거두며 빠져나온 더러운 번데기에 대해 느끼는 것과 같은 혐오감을 그녀에게 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To become visible or apparent.

senses.gloss: To come into view.
To come out of a situation, object, or a liquid.
senses.example: He emerged unscathed from the accident.

senses.gloss: To become known.
senses.example: Gradually the truth emerged.

examples.text: She nodded and moved away from him just as George Wilson emerged with two chairs from his office door.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 고개를 끄덕이며 그에게서 멀어졌는데, 마침 조지 윌슨이 사무실 문에서 의자 두 개를 들고 나왔다.

examples.translation_ko: 잠시 후 주인이 가게 안쪽에서 나와 움푹 들어간 눈으로 차를 바라보았다.

examples.translation_ko: 그때 그의 사상은 천상계에서 고요히 떠돌았고, 꽃들 주위를 맴도는 아름다운 나비가 자신이 승리를 거두며 빠져나온 더러운 번데기에 대해 느끼는 것과 같은 혐오감을 그녀에게 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Having a bright yellow color.

senses.gloss: Made of, or relating to, gold.
senses.example: She wore a golden crown.

senses.gloss: Having a color or other richness suggestive of gold.
senses.example: Under a golden sun.

senses.gloss: Of a beverage, flavoured or colored with turmeric.

examples.text: With Jordan’s slender golden arm resting in mine, we descended the steps and sauntered about the garden.
examples.translation_ko: 조던의 가느다란 황금빛 팔이 내 팔에 기대어진 채, 우리는 계단을 내려가 정원을 거닐었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The rain was still falling, but the darkness had parted in the west, and there was a pink and golden billow of foamy clouds above the sea.
examples.translation_ko: 비는 여전히 내리고 있었지만 서쪽 하늘의 어둠은 걷혀 있었고, 바다 위로 분홍빛과 황금빛 거품구름이 물결치고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Nor is it vouchsafed to man in the flesh to know aught that more nearly suggests the approach to the golden realms of fancy than the approach to Tahiti.
examples.translation_ko: 육신을 지닌 인간에게는 환상의 황금 영역으로 다가가는 것보다 더 가깝게 느껴지는 것을 아는 것이 허락되지 않으니, 그것은 바로 타히티로 다가가는 것이다.

senses.gloss: The concept of a sail or sails, as if a substance.

senses.gloss: The power harnessed by a sail or sails, or the use of this power for travel or transport.

examples.text: Twice Strickland refused a berth on tramps sailing for the United States, and once on a collier going to Newcastle.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 미국으로 가는 화물선의 일자리를 두 번 거절했고, 뉴캐슬로 가는 석탄선의 일자리도 한 번 거절했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A ridge of rocks or coral near the surface of the sea.

senses.gloss: A chain or range of rocks, sand, or coral lying at or near the surface of the water.
A large vein of auriferous quartz; hence, any body of rock yielding valuable ore.

examples.text: He used to go fishing on the reef.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 산호초에서 낚시를 하곤 했다.

examples.text: Our trees have prospered, and there is shell on my reef.
examples.translation_ko: 우리 나무들은 잘 자랐고, 내 암초에는 조개껍데기가 있다.

definition_en: A body of water partially enclosed by land but usually with a wide mouth connecting it to the open sea.

senses.gloss: A body of water (especially the sea) contained by a concave shoreline.
senses.example: This hotel has a great view across the bay.

senses.gloss: A bank or dam to keep back water.

examples.text: “Gatsby bought that house so that Daisy would be just across the bay.”
examples.translation_ko: "개츠비가 그 집을 산 건 데이지가 바로 만 건너편에 있게 하려고였어요."

examples.text: “If it wasn’t for the mist we could see your home across the bay,” said Gatsby.

An event or a situation which is inevitable in the fullness of time.

examples.text: Dr. Weitbrecht-Rotholz belongs to that school of historians which believes that human nature is not only about as bad as it can be, but a great deal worse; and certainly the reader is safer of entertainment in their hands than in those of the writers who take a malicious pleasure in representing the great figures of romance as patterns of the domestic virtues.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French requerre (French: requérir), from Latin requīrō (“I require, seek, ask for”).
definition_en: To need or demand something.

senses.gloss: To demand, to insist upon (having); to call for authoritatively.
senses.example: "I am Miss Newbury," I announced, "and I require to be shown to my room immediately, if you please."

senses.gloss: Naturally to demand (something) as indispensable; to need, to call for as necessary.
senses.example: A weapon small enough to put on a missile would require uranium enriched to more than 90% U-235.

senses.gloss: To demand (of someone) to do something.
senses.example: It is required (of me) that I give evidence in court.

examples.text: It requires a very lively passion to steel me to my own ridicule.
examples.translation_ko: 내 자신이 우스꽝스러워 보이는 것을 감수하려면 매우 강렬한 열정이 필요하다.

examples.text: Tiaré introduced me to him, and he handed me his card, a large card on which was printed René Brunot, and underneath, Capitaine au Long Cours.

examples.text: Gone were the Morris papers and gone the severe cretonnes, gone were the Arundel prints that had adorned the walls of her drawing-room in Ashley Gardens; the room blazed with fantastic colour, and I wondered if she knew that those varied hues, which fashion had imposed upon her, were due to the dreams of a poor painter in a South Sea island.
examples.translation_ko: 모리스 벽지도 사라지고 엄숙한 크레톤 천도 사라졌으며, 애슐리 가든스의 응접실 벽을 장식했던 아런델 판화들도 모두 사라졌다. 이제 그 방은 환상적인 색채로 눈부시게 빛났는데, 유행이 그녀에게 강요한 그 다채로운 색조들이 남태평양 어느 섬의 가난한 화가의 꿈에서 비롯된 것임을 그녀가 알고 있는지 나는 궁금했다.

definition_en: A person who is studying at a school or university.

senses.gloss: A person who studies or learns about a particular subject.

senses.gloss: A person who is formally enrolled at a school, a college or university, or another educational institution.

senses.gloss: A person who is enrolled at a college or university (as contrasted with a pupil or schoolchild attending a primary or secondary school).

senses.gloss: An attitude or a feeling of distaste or aversion.

senses.gloss: An individual vote showing disapproval of, or lack of support for, something posted on the Internet.

etymology: From Middle English carfulli, carefulliche, from Old English carfullīċe, ċearfullīċe (“carefully, diligently”), equivalent to careful + -ly.

senses.gloss: Sorrowfully.

senses.gloss: With care; attentively, circumspectly.

senses.gloss: Conscientiously, painstakingly, fastidiously, meticulously

examples.translation_ko: 이 일행은 어수선하지 않고 품위 있는 동질성을 유지했으며, 시골의 침착한 귀족층을 대표하는 역할을 자임했다—이스트에그가 웨스트에그를 내려다보며 그곳의 현란한 유쾌함을 조심스럽게 경계하고 있었다.

etymology: From Middle English labor, labour, labur, from Old French labor (modern labeur) and its etymon, Latin labor.
definition_en: Physical or mental effort needed to do something.

senses.gloss: Effort expended on a particular task; toil, work.

senses.gloss: That which requires hard work for its accomplishment; that which demands effort.
senses.example: Being a labour of so great difficulty, the exact performance thereof we may rather wish than look for.

senses.gloss: Workers in general; the working class, the workforce; sometimes specifically the labour movement, organised labour.

examples.text: Only the poet or the saint can water an asphalt pavement in the confident anticipation that lilies will reward his labour.
examples.translation_ko: 오직 시인이나 성인만이 백합이 자신의 노고에 보답할 것이라는 확신을 품고 아스팔트 포장도로에 물을 뿌릴 수 있다.

examples.text: Ah, mon cher monsieur, they talk of the blessedness of labour, and it is a meaningless phrase, but to me it has the most intense significance.

definition_en: The ability to acquire and apply knowledge and skills.

definition_en: The maximum amount that something can be.

senses.gloss: A restriction; a bound beyond which one may not go.
senses.example: There are several existing limits to executive power.

senses.gloss: A value to which a sequence converges. Equivalently, the common value of the upper limit and the lower limit of a sequence: if the upper and lower limits are different, then the sequence has no limit (i.e., does not converge).

senses.gloss: Any of several abstractions of this concept of limit.
senses.example: Category theory defines a very general concept of limit.

examples.text: Man’s desire for the approval of his fellows is so strong, his dread of their censure so violent, that he himself has brought his enemy within his gates; and it keeps watch over him, vigilant always in the interests of its master to crush any half-formed desire to break away from the herd.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham
