examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 소년 시절부터 강한 소명 의식이 있었지만 아버지의 뜻에 짓눌리거나 생계를 꾸려야 하는 필요에 희생되었다고 보여주었을 것이다. 그가 삶의 속박에 조바심을 내는 모습을 그렸을 것이고, 예술에 대한 열정과 자신의 지위에 따른 의무 사이의 갈등에서 그에 대한 동정심을 불러일으킬 수 있었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English stikke (“stick, rod, twig”), from Old English sticca (“rod, twig”), from Proto-West Germanic *stikkō, from Proto-Germanic *stik...
definition_en: A small thin piece of wood or other material used for a particular purpose.

senses.gloss: A small, thin branch from a tree or bush; a twig; a branch.
senses.example: The beaver's dam was made out of sticks.

senses.gloss: A relatively long, thin piece of wood, of any size.
senses.example: I found several good sticks in the brush heap.

senses.gloss: A timber board, especially a two by four (inches).
senses.example: I found enough sticks in dumpsters at construction sites to build my shed.

examples.text: I got him a job once or twice, but he couldn’t stick to anything.
examples.translation_ko: 한두 번 일자리도 구해줬지만 오래 버티지 못했어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “I think you’d have been wiser if you’d hit her over the head with a stick.
examples.translation_ko: "차라리 막대기로 그 여자 머리를 한 대 쳤다면 더 현명했을 텐데요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pouerles, powerles, equivalent to power + -less.
definition_en: Lacking power or control.

senses.gloss: Lacking sufficient power or strength.
senses.example: Frank desperately wanted to help. To do something. Anything. But he was powerless to stop what was about to happen.

senses.gloss: Lacking legal authority.
senses.example: The traffic warden was powerless to stop me driving away.

senses.gloss: Without electricity or electrical power.
senses.example: During the storm, the entire neighborhood was left powerless for several hours

examples.text: They said something that words were powerless to utter.
examples.translation_ko: 그것들은 말로는 표현할 힘이 없는 무언가를 말하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The satyr in him suddenly took possession, and he was powerless in the grip of an instinct which had all the strength of the primitive forces of nature.
examples.translation_ko: 그 안의 사티로스가 갑자기 그를 사로잡았고, 그는 자연의 원시적 힘만큼 강력한 본능의 지배 앞에서 무력했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sotil, soubtil, subtil, borrowed from Old French soutil, subtil, from Latin subtīlis (“fine, thin, slender, delicate”); probabl...
definition_en: Having or showing a delicate and precise understanding.

senses.gloss: Hard to grasp; not obvious or easily understood.
Barely noticeable, not obvious, indistinct.
senses.example: The difference is subtle, but you can hear it if you listen carefully.

senses.gloss: Cleverly contrived.

examples.text: But I can still read the grey names, and they will give you a better impression than my generalities of those who accepted Gatsby’s hospitality and paid him the subtle tribute of knowing nothing whatever about him.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 나는 여전히 그 회색빛 이름들을 읽을 수 있고, 그것들은 개츠비의 환대를 받아들이면서도 그에 대해서는 전혀 아무것도 모른다는 미묘한 경의를 표했던 사람들에 대해 내 일반론보다 더 나은 인상을 줄 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Those who think that a man betrays his character nowhere more clearly than when he is playing a game might on this draw subtle inferences.
examples.translation_ko: 게임을 할 때만큼 사람의 성격이 명확하게 드러나는 때는 없다고 생각하는 사람들이라면 이것으로부터 미묘한 추론을 할 수 있을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Oh, I think that’s awfully subtle,” said the Colonel, putting into the word all the contempt he felt for a quality so alien to the traditions of his calling.
examples.translation_ko: "오, 그건 너무 미묘한 생각이군요." 대령이 말했다. 자신의 직업 전통과는 너무나 동떨어진 그런 성질에 대해 느끼는 모든 경멸을 그 말에 담으면서.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English rage, from Anglo-Norman rage, from Late Latin rabia, from Classical Latin rabiēs (“anger, fury”). Doublet of rabies.
Displaced ...
definition_en: A strong and uncontrolled feeling of anger.

senses.gloss: Violent uncontrolled anger.
senses.example: […] rage is not only impotent by definition, it is the mode in which impotence becomes active in its last stage of final despair.

senses.gloss: A current fashion or fad.
senses.example: Miniskirts were all the rage back then.

senses.gloss: An exciting and boisterous party.
senses.example: That evening, Felix and Trish Homer invited me to the Sundancer for "a bit of a rage."

examples.text: You drink till you’re blind with rage.”
examples.translation_ko: 분노로 눈이 멀 때까지 마시는 거야."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Because she’s weak, she has a rage for domination, and nothing less will satisfy her.
examples.translation_ko: 약하기 때문에 지배욕에 사로잡혀 있고, 그것보다 못한 것으로는 만족하지 않는다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A slight but noticeable shaking or quivering.

senses.gloss: A tremble.

examples.text: But he wouldn’t eat, and the glass of milk spilled from his trembling hand.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그는 먹으려 하지 않았고, 떨리는 손에서 우유 한 잔이 쏟아졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He lit Daisy’s cigarette from a trembling match, and sat down with her on a couch far across the room, where there was no light save what the gleaming floor bounced in from the hall.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 떨리는 성냥으로 데이지의 담배에 불을 붙여주고, 복도에서 반짝이는 마루로 튕겨 들어오는 빛 외에는 아무 불빛도 없는 방 저편 소파에 그녀와 함께 앉았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She went on in a low and trembling voice:
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 낮고 떨리는 목소리로 계속했다:
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then he told me, in a trembling voice, with the tears pouring down his cheeks, how he had gone up to her, trying to take her in his arms, but she had drawn away and begged him not to touch her.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 떨리는 목소리로, 뺨에 눈물을 흘리며, 어떻게 그녀에게 다가가 품에 안으려 했지만 그녀가 몸을 피하며 자신을 만지지 말아달라고 애원했는지 말해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English granten, graunten, grantien, grauntien, from Anglo-Norman granter, graunter, from Old French granter, graunter, graanter, grean...
definition_en: Give permission or authorization for something.

senses.gloss: To give (permission or wish).
senses.example: He was granted permission to attend the meeting.

senses.gloss: To give (bestow upon or confer, particularly in answer to prayer or request).
senses.example: In order to grant the rich these pleasures, the social contract is reconfigured. The welfare state is dismantled. […]

senses.gloss: To agree with (someone) on (something); to accept (something) for the sake of argument; to admit to (someone) that (something) is true.
senses.example: The universe exists, said the father: somebody must have made it. If that somebody exists, said I, somebody must have made him. I grant that for the sake of argument, said the Oratorian.

examples.text: Taking our scepticism for granted, he rushed to the bookcases and returned with Volume One of the Stoddard Lectures.
examples.translation_ko: 우리의 회의적인 반응을 당연하게 여기며, 그는 서가로 달려가서 스토다드 강연집 1권을 들고 돌아왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He knew women early, and since they spoiled him he became contemptuous of them, of young virgins because they were ignorant, of the others because they were hysterical about things which in his overwhelming self-absorption he took for granted.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 일찍부터 여자들을 알았고, 여자들이 그를 응석받이로 키웠기 때문에 그녀들을 경멸하게 되었다. 젊은 처녀들은 무지하다고, 다른 여자들은 그의 압도적인 자기도취 속에서 그가 당연하게 여기는 것들에 대해 히스테리를 부린다고 여겼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I don’t deny that perhaps Amy took her husband a little too much for granted.
examples.translation_ko: "에이미가 남편을 너무 당연하게 여겼을지도 모른다는 점은 부인하지 않습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Granting that you owed him no gratitude, were you obliged to go out of your way to take his wife from him?
examples.translation_ko: "자네가 그에게 고마워할 필요가 없다고 치더라도, 굳이 나서서 그의 아내를 빼앗을 의무라도 있었나?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English trak, tracke, from Old French trac (“track of horses, trail, trace”), of uncertain origin. Likely from a Germanic source, eithe...
definition_en: A mark or path made by something moving.

senses.gloss: A mark left by something that has passed along.
senses.example: Follow the track of the ship.

senses.gloss: A mark or impression left by the foot, either of man or animal.
senses.example: The fox tracks were still visible in the snow.

senses.gloss: The entire lower surface of the foot; said of birds, etc.

examples.text: It was a few days before the Fourth of July, and a grey, scrawny Italian child was setting torpedoes in a row along the railroad track.
examples.translation_ko: 독립기념일 며칠 전이었는데, 회색빛 깡마른 이탈리아 아이가 철로를 따라 폭죽들을 일렬로 놓고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And last the murky yellow cars of the Chicago, Milwaukee and St. Paul railroad looking cheerful as Christmas itself on the tracks beside the gate.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 마지막으로 개찰구 옆 선로에서 크리스마스 그 자체만큼이나 명랑해 보이는 시카고, 밀워키 앤드 세인트폴 철도의 탁한 노란색 객차들을.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “In that case he has a positive genius for covering up his tracks.”
examples.translation_ko: "그렇다면 그는 자신의 행적을 감추는 데 정말 천재적인 재능이 있는 셈이군요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English singulerly; equivalent to singular + -ly.
definition_en: Used to describe something that is unique or exceptional.

senses.gloss: Strangely; oddly.
senses.example: He behaved most singularly when we met him last night.

senses.gloss: Extremely; remarkably.
senses.example: "There were scraps of verse. I do not profess to be a judge of such things, but they appeared to me to be singularly wanting in merit."

senses.gloss: In the singular number; in terms of a single thing.

examples.text: He was left with his singularly appropriate education; the vague contour of Jay Gatsby had filled out to the substantiality of a man.
examples.translation_ko: 그에게 남은 것은 그 독특하게도 적절한 교육뿐이었다. 제이 개츠비의 모호한 윤곽이 한 남자의 실체로 채워진 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I noticed that he seemed singularly disconsolate.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 유난히 의기소침해 보인다는 것을 알아차렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I could not find out how this had arisen, but, singularly enough, it created much sympathy for Mrs. Strickland, and at the same time gave her not a little prestige.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 이야기가 어떻게 생겨났는지는 알 수 없었지만, 이상하게도 이 소문은 스트릭랜드 부인에 대한 많은 동정심을 불러일으키는 동시에 그녀에게 적지 않은 명성을 안겨주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English penyles, penylees; equivalent to penny + -less. Compare Old Norse penningalauss (“penniless”).
definition_en: Having no money.

senses.gloss: Lacking even the smallest amount of money.
senses.example: In societies without national insurance of any kind, almshouses are the last refuge of penniless people.

senses.gloss: Abstaining from the use of penny coins, despite having fully decimalized currency, via rounding of cash transactions (but not necessarily of cashless ones).
senses.example: Canada became a penniless country in 2013 simply by rounding its cash transactions to the nearest nickel but otherwise not changing anything.

examples.text: The day-coach—he was penniless now—was hot.
examples.translation_ko: 보통 객차는—그는 이제 무일푼이었다—더웠다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: However glorious might be his future as Jay Gatsby, he was at present a penniless young man without a past, and at any moment the invisible cloak of his uniform might slip from his shoulders.
examples.translation_ko: 제이 개츠비로서의 그의 미래가 아무리 영광스러울지라도, 현재 그는 과거가 없는 무일푼 청년이었고, 언제든 군복이라는 보이지 않는 망토가 그의 어깨에서 미끄러져 떨어질 수 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Colonel MacAndrew had not exaggerated when he said she would be penniless, and it was necessary for her to earn her own living as quickly as she could.
examples.translation_ko: 맥앤드류 대령이 그녀가 무일푼이 될 것이라고 말했을 때 과장한 것이 아니었고, 그녀로서는 가능한 한 빨리 스스로 생계를 꾸려나가야 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Here they made friends with others in as desperate condition as themselves, and when they were penniless and the night was bitter cold, they were glad to borrow from anyone who had earned a stray franc during the day the price of a roof over their heads.
examples.translation_ko: 이곳에서 그들은 자신들과 마찬가지로 절망적인 처지에 있는 다른 사람들과 친구가 되었고, 무일푼이 되어 밤이 혹독하게 추울 때면 하루 동안 프랑 한 닢이라도 번 사람에게서 머리 위에 지붕 하나 얹을 돈을 기꺼이 빌렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The adjective is borrowed from Middle French panique, a word itself borrowed from Ancient Greek πανικός (panikós, “pertaining to Pan”); Pan, the Gr...
definition_en: A sudden feeling of fear or anxiety.

senses.gloss: Alternative letter-case form of Panic (“pertaining to the Greek god Pan”).
Of fear, fright, etc: overwhelming or sudden.
senses.example:
Terrified, he looked down from the skies
 At the waves, and panic blackness filled his eyes.

senses.gloss: Pertaining to or resulting from overwhelming fear or fright.
senses.example:
No Dangers threatned, but they ſmil'd to meet
 The pannick French-men trembling at their Feet.

examples.text: “You don’t understand,” said Gatsby, with a touch of panic.
examples.translation_ko: "당신은 이해하지 못해요." 개츠비가 약간 당황한 기색으로 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I did, old sport,” he said automatically, “but I lost most of it in the big panic—the panic of the war.”
examples.translation_ko: "그랬지, 형씨," 그가 기계적으로 말했다, "하지만 대공황 때 대부분을 잃었어—전쟁 때 공황 말이야."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was seized with panic.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 공황에 사로잡혔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I saw that he was panic-stricken.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 공포에 질려 있다는 것을 알 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French alterer (French altérer), from Medieval Latin alterāre (“to make other”), from Latin alter (“the other”), from al- (seen in alius (...
definition_en: To make different or change something.

senses.gloss: To change the form or structure of.
senses.example: It gilds all objects, but it alters none.

senses.gloss: To become different.
senses.example: […] Passing the song of the hermit bird and the tallying song of my soul, / Victorious song, death’s outlet song, yet varying ever-altering song, […]

senses.gloss: To tailor clothes to make them fit.

examples.text: I was going to wear it tonight, but it was too big in the bust and had to be altered.
examples.translation_ko: 오늘 밤에 입으려고 했는데 가슴 부분이 너무 커서 수선을 맡겨야 했어요.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Nothing that you can say will make me alter it.”
examples.translation_ko: 당신이 무슨 말을 해도 바뀌지 않을 거예요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Strickland was indifferent to his surroundings, and he had lived in the other’s studio without thinking of altering a thing.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 주변 환경에 무관심했고, 다른 사람의 작업실에서 살면서도 그 어떤 것 하나 바꿀 생각을 하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From late Middle English emploien, imploien, emplien (“to apply to a specific purpose”), from Anglo-Norman emploier, Old French emploiier (“to enta...
definition_en: Use someone or something for a particular purpose.

senses.gloss: To retain (someone) as an employee.
senses.example: Our company employs hundreds of people.

senses.gloss: To provide (someone) with a new job; to hire.
senses.example: Yesterday our local garage employed a new mechanic.

senses.gloss: To use (someone or something) for a job or task.
senses.example: The burglar employed a jemmy to get in.

examples.text: He was employed in a vague personal capacity—while he remained with Cody he was in turn steward, mate, skipper, secretary, and even jailor, for Dan Cody sober knew what lavish doings Dan Cody drunk might soon be about, and he provided for such contingencies by reposing more and more trust in Gatsby.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 애매한 개인적 자격으로 고용되었다—코디와 함께 있는 동안 그는 번갈아 가며 사환, 항해사, 선장, 비서, 심지어 간수 역할까지 했는데, 술에 취하지 않은 댄 코디는 술에 취한 댄 코디가 곧 어떤 방탕한 짓을 벌일지 알고 있었고, 그런 상황에 대비해 개츠비에게 점점 더 많은 신뢰를 맡겼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: No one will employ you now.
examples.translation_ko: 이제는 아무도 당신을 고용하려 하지 않을 거야.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: During a strike he had been employed as a house-painter.
examples.translation_ko: 파업 중에는 집 페인트칠하는 일을 했었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English silk, sylk, selk, selc, from Old English sioloc, seoloc, seolc (“silk”). The immediate source is uncertain; it probably reached...
definition_en: A soft, smooth fabric made from silk fibers.

senses.gloss: A fine fiber excreted by the silkworm or other arthropod (such as a spider).
senses.example: The thread made of silk was barely visible.

senses.gloss: A fine, soft cloth woven from silk fibers.
Anything which resembles silk, such as the filiform styles of the female flower of maize, or the seed covering of bombaxes.

examples.text: A massage and a wave, and a collar for the dog, and one of those cute little ashtrays where you touch a spring, and a wreath with a black silk bow for mother’s grave that’ll last all summer.
examples.translation_ko: 마사지에 파마, 개 목걸이, 그리고 스프링을 누르면 되는 그 귀여운 재떨이, 엄마 무덤에 놓을 검은 실크 리본 달린 화환도 하나—여름 내내 갈 거야.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He took out a pile of shirts and began throwing them, one by one, before us, shirts of sheer linen and thick silk and fine flannel, which lost their folds as they fell and covered the table in many-coloured disarray.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 셔츠 더미를 꺼내어 우리 앞에 하나씩 던지기 시작했다. 순수한 린넨과 두꺼운 실크, 고급 플란넬로 만든 셔츠들이 떨어지면서 주름이 펴지며 테이블을 형형색색으로 어지럽게 덮었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There were bits of old brocade on the walls, and the piano was covered with a piece of silk, beautiful and tarnished; in one corner was a copy of the Venus of Milo, and in another of the Venus of the Medici.

examples.translation_ko: "내 선택은 이미 끝났어요." 그녀가 무기력한 목소리로 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: For choice he sat on a kitchen chair without arms.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 되도록 팔걸이 없는 부엌 의자에 앉았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The verb is from Middle English folden, from Old English fealdan, from Proto-West Germanic *falþan, from Proto-Germanic *falþaną (“to fold”), from ...
definition_en: To bend or crease something so that it folds in half.

senses.gloss: To bend (any thin material, such as paper) over so that it comes in contact with itself.
To make the proper arrangement (in a thin material) by bending.
senses.example: If you fold the sheets, they'll fit more easily in the drawer.

senses.gloss: To draw or coil (one’s arms, a snake’s body, etc.) around something so as to enclose or embrace it.

examples.text: I folded the paper and put it down beside me.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 신문을 접어서 옆에 내려놓았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Ata’s property was right away in a fold of the mountain.
examples.translation_ko: 아타의 집은 산 접힌 곳 저 멀리에 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sourrounden (“to submerge, overflow”), from Middle French souronder, suronder, from Late Latin superundō, from super + undō (“t...
definition_en: To be on all sides of something or someone.

senses.gloss: To encircle something or simultaneously extend in all directions.
senses.example: and this way they get rid of those grand and stubborn opinions that surround them.

senses.gloss: To enclose or confine something on all sides so as to prevent escape.
To pass around; to travel about; to circumnavigate.
senses.example: to surround the world

examples.text: We got up, and he led me on to the verandah which surrounded his house.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 일어나서 그가 나를 자신의 집을 둘러싼 베란다로 안내했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Strickland was distinguished from most Englishmen by his perfect indifference to comfort; it did not irk him to live always in one shabby room; he had no need to be surrounded by beautiful things.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 안락함에 대한 완전한 무관심으로 대부분의 영국인들과 구별되었다. 항상 초라한 방 하나에서 사는 것이 그를 괴롭히지 않았고, 아름다운 것들에 둘러싸여 있을 필요도 느끼지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English *frightenen, equivalent to fright + -en.
definition_en: To make someone feel frightened or afraid.

senses.gloss: To cause to feel fear; to scare; to cause to feel alarm or fright.
senses.example: Avery puts a sheet over her head, pretending to be a ghost to frighten Emily.

senses.gloss: To become scared or alarmed.
senses.example: Be sneaky. Fish frighten easily.

examples.text: He told her those things in a way that frightened her—that made it look as if I was some kind of cheap sharper.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 그녀에게 그런 식으로 말한 것이 그녀를 겁먹게 했어—마치 내가 어떤 싸구려 사기꾼인 것처럼 보이게 만들었다고.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It must have frightened her.
examples.translation_ko: 그것이 그녀를 두렵게 했을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You nearly frightened me out of my wits.”
examples.translation_ko: "당신 때문에 혼이 빠질 뻔했소."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French advertissement (“statement calling attention”), compare French avertissement (“warning”). See advertise. Equivalent to advertise...
definition_en: A public notice or announcement to promote a product or service.

senses.gloss: A commercial solicitation designed to sell some commodity, service or similar.
senses.example: Companies try to sell their products using advertisements in form of placards, television spots and print publications.

senses.gloss: A public notice.
senses.example: The city council placed an advertisement in the local newspaper to inform its residents of the forthcoming roadworks.

senses.gloss: A recommendation of a particular product, service or person.
senses.example: The good manners and intelligence of the students are an advertisement for the school.

examples.text: “You know the advertisement of the man—”
examples.translation_ko: "그 남자 광고 말이에요—"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “That’s an advertisement,” Michaelis assured him.
examples.translation_ko: "그건 광고판이에요." 미카엘리스가 그를 안심시켰다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Then he happened on a job to translate the advertisements of patent medicines which were sent broadcast to the medical profession in England.
examples.translation_ko: 그러던 중 그는 영국의 의료계에 광고로 뿌려지는 특허 의약품 광고를 번역하는 일자리를 우연히 얻게 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French réalité (“quality of being real”), from Middle French realité (“property, possession”), from Medieval Latin reālitās, from Late Latin r...
definition_en: The state of things as they actually exist.

senses.gloss: The state of being actual or real; realness.
senses.example: The reality of the crash scene on TV dawned upon him only when he saw the victim was no actor but his friend.

senses.gloss: The real world.
senses.example: A man very often fancies that he understands a critic, when in reality he does not comprehend his meaning.

senses.gloss: A real entity, event, or other fact.
senses.example: The ultimate reality of life is that it ends in death.

examples.text: I couldn’t sleep all night; a foghorn was groaning incessantly on the Sound, and I tossed half-sick between grotesque reality and savage, frightening dreams.
examples.translation_ko: 밤새 잠을 이룰 수 없었다. 해협에서 안개 경적이 끊임없이 울어댔고, 나는 기괴한 현실과 야만스럽고 무서운 꿈 사이에서 반쯤 병든 채로 뒤척였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For a while these reveries provided an outlet for his imagination; they were a satisfactory hint of the unreality of reality, a promise that the rock of the world was founded securely on a fairy’s wing.
examples.translation_ko: 한동안 이런 몽상들은 그의 상상력의 출구가 되어주었다. 그것들은 현실의 비현실성에 대한 만족스러운 암시였고, 세상이라는 바위가 요정의 날개 위에 단단히 세워져 있다는 약속이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He lived in a dream, and the reality meant nothing to him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 꿈속에서 살았고, 현실은 그에게 아무 의미가 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Here all the decencies of civilisation are swept away, and you feel that men are face to face with a sombre reality.
examples.translation_ko: 이곳에서는 문명의 모든 체면이 쓸려나가고, 인간이 음울한 현실과 정면으로 마주하고 있음을 느끼게 된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From dis- + approve.
definition_en: Express disapproval or dislike of something.

senses.gloss: To condemn; to consider wrong or inappropriate; used with of.
senses.example: She disapproves of rap music because of its sometimes aggressive lyrics.

senses.gloss: To have or express an unfavorable opinion.
senses.example: Green washing schemes of corporations are disapproved by Greenpeace activists.

senses.gloss: To refuse to approve; reject.

examples.text: It was the only compliment I ever gave him, because I disapproved of him from beginning to end.
examples.translation_ko: 그것이 내가 그에게 한 유일한 칭찬이었다. 나는 처음부터 끝까지 그를 못마땅하게 여겼기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I liked to walk up Fifth Avenue and pick out romantic women from the crowd and imagine that in a few minutes I was going to enter into their lives, and no one would ever know or disapprove.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 5번가를 걸어 올라가며 군중 속에서 낭만적인 여인들을 골라내어, 몇 분 후면 내가 그들의 삶 속으로 들어갈 것이고 아무도 알지 못하거나 반대하지 않을 것이라고 상상하기를 좋아했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I’m afraid you disapprove of me?”
examples.translation_ko: "당신이 나를 못마땅하게 여기는 것 같은데요?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “It’s only right that you shouldn’t disapprove of me.
examples.translation_ko: "당신이 나를 못마땅하게 여기지 않는 것이 당연합니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The noun is from Middle English scold(e), skald(e), first attested in the 12th or 13th century (as scold, scolde, skolde, skald). The verb is from ...
definition_en: To criticize or scold someone severely.

senses.gloss: A person who habitually scolds, in particular a troublesome and angry woman.
senses.example: Consider the contrast with the United States, where deficit scolds dominated Beltway discourse in 2010–2011 but never managed to dictate the terms of political debate […]

examples.text: “You young men think you can force your way in here any time,” she scolded.
examples.translation_ko: "젊은 남자들은 언제든지 여기 마음대로 들어올 수 있다고 생각하는군요." 그녀가 꾸짖었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Then there were bloody towels upon the bathroom floor, and women’s voices scolding, and high over the confusion a long broken wail of pain.
examples.translation_ko: 그러자 화장실 바닥에는 피 묻은 수건들이 있었고, 여자들의 꾸짖는 소리가 들렸으며, 그 혼란 위로 길고 끊어진 고통의 울음소리가 높이 울려 퍼졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His face fell, and he pouted his lips like a scolded child.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 얼굴이 침울해졌고, 꾸중 들은 아이처럼 입술을 삐죽 내밀었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You scold yourself; you know it is only your nerves—and yet, and yet...
examples.translation_ko: 스스로를 꾸짖어본다. 그저 신경 때문이라는 것을 안다. 그런데도, 그런데도...
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English proven, from Old English prōfian (“to esteem, regard as, evince, try, prove”) and Old French prover (“to prove”), both from Lat...
definition_en: To show or demonstrate the truth of something.

senses.gloss: To demonstrate that something is true or viable; to give proof for; to bear out; to testify.
senses.example: I will prove that my method is more effective than yours.

senses.gloss: To turn out; to manifest.
senses.example: It proved to be a cold day.

senses.gloss: To turn out to be.
senses.example: Have an exit strategy should your calculations prove incorrect.

examples.text: It’s all scientific stuff; it’s been proved.”
examples.translation_ko: "모든 게 과학적인 내용이야. 증명된 거라고."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “After all, there’s nothing to prove that she is unhappy.
examples.translation_ko: "결국 그녀가 불행하다는 증거는 아무것도 없잖아요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She proved herself not only a capable, but a devoted nurse.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 자신이 유능할 뿐만 아니라 헌신적인 간병인임을 증명했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English uncerteyn; equivalent to un- + certain.
definition_en: Lacking a clear or definite idea of something.

senses.gloss: Not certain; unsure.
senses.example: Conſider man without the protection and conduct of a ſuperior Being, and he is ſecure of nothing that he enjoys in this world, and uncertain of every thing that he hopes for.

senses.gloss: Not known for certain; questionable.
senses.example: Tomorrow's weather is uncertain.

senses.gloss: Not yet determined; undecided.

examples.text: Finally he got up and informed me, in an uncertain voice, that he was going home.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 그는 일어나서 집에 가겠다고 불안한 목소리로 내게 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Then, very gradually, part by part, a pale, dangling individual stepped out of the wreck, pawing tentatively at the ground with a large uncertain dancing shoe.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 아주 천천히, 조금씩 조금씩, 창백하고 축 늘어진 한 사내가 잔해에서 빠져나와 크고 불안정한 댄스화로 땅을 더듬거리며 조심스럽게 디뎠다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was of uncertain temper.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 변덕스러운 성격이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He is shut in a tower of brass, and can communicate with his fellows only by signs, and the signs have no common value, so that their sense is vague and uncertain.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 황동 탑에 갇혀 있어서, 동료들과는 오직 신호로만 소통할 수 있는데, 그 신호들은 공통된 가치가 없어서 의미가 모호하고 불확실하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English welthy, welþi, equivalent to wealth + -y. Cognate with Middle Dutch weldech, weeldech (“magnificent, luscious, lavish”).
definition_en: Having a lot of money or valuable possessions.

senses.gloss: Possessing financial wealth; rich.
senses.example: Gleefully and legally intruding upon the sanctum of the wealthy linksters, we walked the mitigation meadows.

senses.gloss: Abundant in quality or quantity; profuse.

examples.text: “I am the son of some wealthy people in the Middle West—all dead now.
examples.translation_ko: "나는 중서부의 부유한 집안 아들이오—지금은 모두 세상을 떠났지만.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was hard to realize that a man in my own generation was wealthy enough to do that.
examples.translation_ko: 내 또래의 남자가 그런 일을 할 만큼 부유하다는 것을 실감하기가 어려웠다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Most of them have found their way into museums, and the rest are the treasured possessions of wealthy amateurs.
examples.translation_ko: 그 그림들 대부분은 박물관으로 들어갔고, 나머지는 부유한 수집가들의 소중한 소장품이 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: formerly in the possession of a wealthy manufacturer at Lille, who fled from that city on the approach of the Germans, is now in the National Gallery at Stockholm.
examples.translation_ko: 예전에 릴의 부유한 제조업자가 소유했던 것으로, 독일군이 접근하자 그 도시에서 도망친 그가 남긴 이 작품은 지금 스톡홀름 국립미술관에 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin connectere (“fasten together”), from con- (“together”) + nectere (“bind”), which is cognate with English knot and English knit.
definition_en: To join or link something to another.

senses.gloss: To join (to another object): to attach, or to be intended to attach or capable of attaching, to another object.
senses.example: I think this piece connects to that piece over there.

senses.gloss: To join: to attach, or to be intended to attach or capable of attaching, to each other.
senses.example: Both roads have the same name, but they don't connect: they're on opposite sides of the river, and there's no bridge there.

senses.gloss: To arrive at an intended target; to land.
senses.example: When that roundhouse kick connected with his temple it sent him flying across the room.

examples.text: It wasn’t until then that I connected this Gatsby with the officer in her white car.
examples.translation_ko: 그제서야 나는 이 개츠비를 그녀의 하얀 차에 탔던 그 장교와 연결지을 수 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Tom and Miss Baker, with several feet of twilight between them, strolled back into the library, as if to a vigil beside a perfectly tangible body, while, trying to look pleasantly interested and a little deaf, I followed Daisy around a chain of connecting verandas to the porch in front.
examples.translation_ko: 톰과 베이커 양은 그들 사이에 몇 피트의 황혼을 두고, 마치 완전히 실체가 있는 시신 곁에서 철야를 하듯 서재로 천천히 걸어 들어갔고, 나는 유쾌하게 관심 있어 하면서 약간 귀가 먹은 척하려 애쓰며 데이지를 따라 연결된 베란다들을 지나 앞쪽 현관으로 갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For the next month, occupied with my own affairs, I saw no one connected with this lamentable business, and my mind ceased to be occupied with it.
examples.translation_ko: 그 다음 한 달 동안 내 일에 바빠서 이 비참한 사건과 관련된 사람은 아무도 만나지 않았고, 내 마음도 더 이상 그 일에 사로잡히지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The absurdity that clung to everything connected with Dirk Stroeve gave it a curious note, like an unresolved discord, but made it somehow more modern, more human; like a rough joke thrown into a serious scene, it heightened the poignancy which all beauty has.
examples.translation_ko: 더크 스트루브와 관련된 모든 것에 달라붙은 우스꽝스러움이 해결되지 않은 불협화음처럼 기묘한 색채를 더했지만, 그것이 오히려 더 현대적이고 더 인간적으로 만들었다. 진지한 장면에 던져진 거친 농담처럼, 그것은 모든 아름다움이 지닌 애절함을 더욱 고조시켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English usual, from Old French usuel, from Latin ūsuālis (“for use, fit for use, also of common use, customary, common, ordinary, usual...
definition_en: Being or done according to what is normal or expected.

senses.gloss: Most commonly occurring; typical.
senses.example: The preference of a boy to a girl is a usual occurrence in some parts of China.

examples.text: Then he gave the sardonic smile which was usual with him.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 평소와 같은 냉소적인 미소를 지었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Once some women, venturing nearer than usual to the plantation, saw her washing clothes in the brook, and they threw stones at her.
examples.translation_ko: 한번은 몇몇 여자들이 평소보다 농장에 가까이 다가와서 그녀가 개울에서 빨래하는 모습을 보고는 그녀에게 돌을 던졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English hunten, from Old English huntian (“to hunt”), from Proto-West Germanic *huntōn (“to hunt, capture”), possibly from Proto-Indo-E...
definition_en: To search for and follow or pursue game.

senses.gloss: To find or search for an animal in the wild with the intention of killing the animal for its meat or for sport.
senses.example: State Wildlife Management areas often offer licensed hunters the opportunity to hunt on public lands.

senses.gloss: To try to find something; search (for).
senses.example: The little girl was hunting for shells on the beach.

senses.gloss: To drive; to chase; with down, from, away, etc.
senses.example: to hunt down a criminal

examples.text: His house had never seemed so enormous to me as it did that night when we hunted through the great rooms for cigarettes.
examples.translation_ko: 그날 밤 담배를 찾아 큰 방들을 뒤지며 돌아다닐 때만큼 그의 집이 거대하게 느껴진 적이 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I wanted to explain that I’d hunted for him early in the evening and to apologize for not having known him in the garden.
examples.translation_ko: 저녁 일찍부터 그를 찾아다녔다는 것과 정원에서 그를 알아보지 못한 것에 대해 사과하고 싶었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I tried to make Stroeve understand that it was absurd to hunt vaguely about Paris.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 스트루브에게 파리를 막연히 돌아다니며 찾는 것은 터무니없는 일이라고 이해시키려 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: What they felt the lack of most bitterly was tobacco, and Captain Nichols, for his part, could not do without it; he took to hunting the “Can o’ Beer,” for cigarette-ends and the butt-end of cigars which the promenaders of the night before had thrown away.
examples.translation_ko: 그들이 가장 절실하게 그리워한 것은 담배였는데, 니콜스 선장은 특히 담배 없이는 견딜 수 없었다. 그는 "깡 오 비어"를 뒤져서 전날 밤 산책객들이 버린 담배꽁초와 시가 꽁초를 찾아다니기 시작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English perceiven, borrowed from Old French percevoir, perceveir, from Latin percipiō, past participle perceptus (“take hold of, obtain...
definition_en: Understand or become aware of something through the senses.

senses.gloss: To become aware of, through the physical senses, to see; to understand.
senses.example: Go from the presence of a foolish man, when thou perceivest not in him the lips of knowledge.

senses.gloss: To interpret something in a particular way.
senses.example: John was perceived to be a coward by his comrades

examples.text: But above the grey land and the spasms of bleak dust which drift endlessly over it, you perceive, after a moment, the eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg.

definition_en: To inhale and exhale air.

senses.gloss: To draw air into (inhale), and expel air from (exhale), the lungs in order to extract oxygen and excrete waste gases.
To take in needed gases and expel waste gases in a similar way.

senses.gloss: To inhale (a gas) to sustain life.
senses.example: While life as we know it depends on oxygen, scientists have speculated that alien life forms might breathe chlorine or methane.

examples.text: With an effort Wilson left the shade and support of the doorway and, breathing hard, unscrewed the cap of the tank.

definition_en: Impossible to explain or understand.

senses.gloss: Impossible to explain; not easily accounted for.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her expression was curiously familiar—it was an expression I had often seen on women’s faces, but on Myrtle Wilson’s face it seemed purposeless and inexplicable until I realized that her eyes, wide with jealous terror, were fixed not on Tom, but on Jordan Baker, whom she took to be his wife.

examples.translation_ko: "뷰캐넌 부인… 그리고 뷰캐넌 씨—" 잠깐 망설인 후 그가 덧붙였다. "폴로 선수 말입니다."

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: After a moment’s hesitation, Strickland scrambled to his feet, and together they went to the Bouchée de Pain, where the hungry are given a wedge of bread, which they must eat there and then, for it is forbidden to take it away; and then to the Cuillère de Soupe, where for a week, at eleven and four, you may get a bowl of thin, salt soup.

examples.translation_ko: 그곳에서도 나는 그 천장을 그린 사람의 위대함에 경외감을 느꼈다.

senses.gloss: Not occupied or in current use.
senses.example: We could rent out the spare room.

examples.text: Even when the East excited me most, even when I was most keenly aware of its superiority to the bored, sprawling, swollen towns beyond the Ohio, with their interminable inquisitions which spared only the children and the very old—even then it had always for me a quality of distortion.
examples.translation_ko: 동부가 나를 가장 흥분시켰을 때조차, 오하이오 너머 지루하고 무질서하게 뻗어나간 부풀어 오른 도시들에 비해 동부가 얼마나 우월한지를 가장 예리하게 깨달았을 때조차—어린아이들과 아주 늙은이들만을 제외하고는 끝없는 캐묻기를 일삼는 그런 도시들에 비해서 말이다—그럴 때조차 동부는 나에게 언제나 뒤틀린 무언가의 성질을 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I think he boxed a little in his spare time.
examples.translation_ko: 여가 시간에는 권투를 조금 했던 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You’ll be spared at least the worst privations.”
examples.translation_ko: 적어도 최악의 궁핍은 면하게 될 거야."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From bore + -ed.
definition_en: Feeling listless and uninterested.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of bore

examples.text: “Chester, I think you could do something with her,” she broke out, but Mr. McKee only nodded in a bored way, and turned his attention to Tom.
examples.translation_ko: "체스터, 저 여자로 뭔가 할 수 있을 것 같은데." 그녀가 불쑥 말했지만, 맥키 씨는 지루한 듯 고개만 끄덕이고는 톰에게 관심을 돌렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The bored haughty face that she turned to the world concealed something—most affectations conceal something eventually, even though they don’t in the beginning—and one day I found what it was.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 세상을 향해 보이는 지루하고 거만한 얼굴은 무언가를 감추고 있었다—대부분의 가식은 결국 무언가를 감추게 마련이다. 처음에는 그렇지 않더라도—그리고 어느 날 나는 그것이 무엇인지 알게 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “‘But are you never bored or lonely?’ I asked.
examples.translation_ko: "'하지만 지루하거나 외롭지는 않습니까?' 내가 물었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But perhaps this is very fanciful; and it may be that she was merely bored with her husband and went to Strickland out of a callous curiosity.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 이런 생각은 지나치게 공상적일지도 모른다. 그녀는 단지 남편에게 지루함을 느껴서 냉혹한 호기심으로 스트릭랜드에게 간 것일 수도 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From obsolete Middle English verb devoiden, from Old French desvuidier (“to empty out”) (compare French dévider).
definition_en: Lacking or devoid of something.

senses.gloss: Completely without; having none of.
senses.example: I went searching for a knife, but the kitchen was devoid of anything sharper than a spoon.

examples.text: Miss Baker and I exchanged a short glance consciously devoid of meaning.
examples.translation_ko: 베이커 양과 나는 의도적으로 아무 의미도 담지 않은 짧은 시선을 주고받았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The meeting had been devoid of incident.
examples.translation_ko: 그 만남은 별다른 사건이 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Love is never quite devoid of sentimentality, and Strickland was the least inclined to that infirmity of any man I have known.
examples.translation_ko: 사랑에는 언제나 감상이 어느 정도 섞여 있기 마련인데, 스트릭랜드는 내가 아는 사람 중에서 그런 나약함에 가장 빠지지 않는 인물이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sunni, from Old English *sunniġ. Cognate with West Frisian sinnich, Low German sünnig, sonnig, Dutch zonnig, German sonnig. Equ...
definition_en: Having a lot of sunlight.

senses.gloss: Featuring a lot of sunshine.
senses.example: Whilst it may be sunny today, the weather forecast is predicting rain.

senses.gloss: Receiving a lot of sunshine.
senses.example: the sunny side of a hill

senses.gloss: Cheerful.
senses.example: a person with a sunny disposition

examples.text: We talked for a few minutes on the sunny porch.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 햇살 가득한 현관에서 몇 분간 이야기를 나누었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The day was fine and sunny, and I felt in myself a more acute delight in life.
examples.translation_ko: 날씨는 맑고 화창했으며, 나는 삶에 대한 더욱 예리한 기쁨을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: My thoughts wandered, and I thought of the sunny beaches of Brittany and the freshness of the sea.
examples.translation_ko: 생각이 딴 곳으로 흘러가면서 브르타뉴의 햇살 가득한 해변과 바다의 상쾌함을 떠올렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bolle, from Old English bolla, bolle (“bowl, cup, pot, beaker, measure”), from Proto-West Germanic *bollā, from Proto-Germanic ...
definition_en: A rounded container for holding food or liquids.

senses.gloss: A roughly hemispherical container used to hold, mix or present food, such as salad, fruit or soup, or other items.
As much as is held by a bowl.
senses.example: You can’t have any more soup – you’ve had three bowls already.

senses.gloss: A dish comprising a mix of different foods, not all of which need be cooked, served in a bowl.
senses.example: This restaurant offers a number of different bowls.

examples.text: I had taken two finger-bowls of champagne, and the scene had changed before my eyes into something significant, elemental, and profound.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 샴페인을 핑거볼로 두 잔이나 마셨고, 내 눈앞의 광경이 의미 있고 원초적이며 심오한 무언가로 변해 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A pair of stage twins, who turned out to be the girls in yellow, did a baby act in costume, and champagne was served in glasses bigger than finger-bowls.
examples.translation_ko: 무대 쌍둥이 한 쌍이 나타났는데, 알고 보니 노란 옷을 입은 그 소녀들이었고, 의상을 입고 아기 연기를 했으며, 샴페인은 핑거볼보다 큰 잔에 담겨 나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: By my side was the empty bowl in which the concierge had brought me my café au lait and the fragment of croissant which I had not had appetite enough to eat.
examples.translation_ko: 내 곁에는 관리인이 가져다준 카페오레를 마신 빈 그릇과 식욕이 없어서 다 먹지 못한 크루아상 조각이 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: After a moment’s hesitation, Strickland scrambled to his feet, and together they went to the Bouchée de Pain, where the hungry are given a wedge of bread, which they must eat there and then, for it is forbidden to take it away; and then to the Cuillère de Soupe, where for a week, at eleven and four, you may get a bowl of thin, salt soup.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 망설인 후 스트릭랜드는 비틀거리며 일어났고, 둘은 함께 부셰 드 팽으로 갔다. 그곳에서는 굶주린 자들에게 빵 한 조각을 주는데, 그 자리에서 바로 먹어야 했다. 가져가는 것은 금지되어 있었기 때문이다. 그다음에는 퀴예르 드 수프로 갔는데, 그곳에서는 일주일 동안 열한 시와 네 시에 묽고 짠 수프 한 그릇을 얻을 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin distractus, from distrahō (“to pull apart”), from dis- + trahō (“to pull”).
definition_en: To divert someone's attention from something.

senses.gloss: To divert the attention of.
senses.example: The crowd was distracted by a helicopter hovering over the stadium when the only goal of the game was scored.

senses.gloss: To make crazy or insane; to drive to distraction.
senses.example:
By Heav’ns, ſuch Virtues, join’d with ſuch Succeſs,
Diſtract my very Soul: Our Father’s Fortune
Wou’d almoſt tempt us to renounce his Precepts.

examples.text: Michaelis made a clumsy attempt to distract him.
examples.translation_ko: 미카엘리스는 서툴게 그의 주의를 돌리려 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He spoke as though I were a child that needed to be distracted.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 마치 주의를 돌려줘야 할 아이를 대하듯 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Stroeve could not bear to be alone, and I exhausted myself in efforts to distract him.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 혼자 있는 것을 견딜 수 없어 했고, 나는 그의 마음을 달래려 애쓰다가 지쳐버렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English awake, a shortened form of awaken (“awakened, awake”), past participle of Middle English awaken (“to awaken”). See verb below. ...
definition_en: To be conscious and alert.

senses.gloss: Not asleep; conscious.
senses.example: By quarter to six all this had me so awake and agitated that even the Balinese wind chimes that I hung up in the garden to relax me began to sound like Big Ben.

senses.gloss: Alert, aware.
senses.example: They were awake to the possibility of a decline in sales.

examples.text: Mr. McKee awoke from his doze and started in a daze toward the door.
examples.translation_ko: 맥키 씨는 졸음에서 깨어나 멍한 상태로 문 쪽으로 걸어갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Wilson was quieter now, and Michaelis went home to sleep; when he awoke four hours later and hurried back to the garage, Wilson was gone.
examples.translation_ko: 윌슨은 이제 더 조용해졌고, 미카엘리스는 집에 가서 잠을 잤다. 네 시간 후 깨어나 서둘러 정비소로 돌아왔을 때, 윌슨은 사라져 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: In the morning when I awoke he was still asleep.
examples.translation_ko: 아침에 잠에서 깨어났을 때 그는 아직 잠들어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I remember that on my first morning I awoke early, and when I came on to the terrace of the hotel no one was stirring.
examples.translation_ko: 첫날 아침 일찍 잠에서 깨어 호텔 테라스로 나왔을 때 아무도 움직이지 않고 있었던 것이 기억난다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English herse, hers, herce, from Old French herce, from Medieval Latin hercia, from Latin herpicem, hirpex; ultimately from Oscan 𐌇𐌉𐌓𐌐𐌖...
definition_en: A vehicle for carrying a coffin in a funeral procession.

senses.gloss: A framework of wood or metal placed over the coffin or tomb of a deceased person, and covered with a pall; also, a temporary canopy bearing wax lights and set up in a church, under which the coffin was placed during the funeral ceremonies.
A grave, coffin, tomb, or sepulchral monument.
senses.example: who lies beneath this sculptured hearse

senses.gloss: A bier or handbarrow for conveying the dead to the grave.
senses.example: Set down, set down your honourable load, / If honour may be shrouded in a hearse.

examples.text: A dead man passed us in a hearse heaped with blooms, followed by two carriages with drawn blinds, and by more cheerful carriages for friends.
examples.translation_ko: 꽃으로 뒤덮인 영구차에 실린 죽은 자가 우리를 지나쳤고, 블라인드를 내린 두 대의 마차가 뒤따랐으며, 친구들을 태운 더 밝은 마차들이 그 뒤를 이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: About five o’clock our procession of three cars reached the cemetery and stopped in a thick drizzle beside the gate—first a motor hearse, horribly black and wet, then Mr. Gatz and the minister and me in the limousine, and a little later four or five servants and the postman from West Egg, in Gatsby’s station wagon, all wet to the skin.
examples.translation_ko: 다섯 시쯤 되어 세 대의 차로 이루어진 우리 행렬이 묘지에 도착해 문 옆에서 멈춰 섰다. 부슬부슬 내리는 비 속에서—맨 앞에는 끔찍하도록 검고 비에 젖은 영구차가, 그 다음에는 개츠 씨와 목사 그리고 내가 탄 리무진이, 그리고 조금 뒤에는 웨스트에그에서 온 하인 네다섯 명과 우편배달부가 개츠비의 스테이션 왜건을 타고 왔는데, 모두 뼛속까지 젖어 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Dirk and I alone followed the hearse to the cemetery.
examples.translation_ko: 디르크와 나만이 영구차를 따라 묘지까지 갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Now and then I caught sight of the swaying hearse in front of us, and our own driver urged his pair so that we might not remain behind.
examples.translation_ko: 때때로 앞에서 흔들리는 영구차가 눈에 띄었고, 우리 마부도 뒤처지지 않으려고 말 두 마리를 재촉했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English horse, hors, from Old English hors (“horse”), from Proto-West Germanic *hors, *hross, from Proto-Germanic *hrussą (“horse”), fr...
definition_en: A large, hoofed, herbivorous mammal.

senses.gloss: Any member of the species Equus ferus, including the Przewalski's horse and the extinct Equus ferus ferus.
Any current or extinct animal of the family Equidae, including zebras and asses.
senses.example: These bone features, distinctive in the zebra, are actually present in all horses.

senses.gloss: Cavalry soldiers (sometimes capitalized when referring to an official category).
senses.example: We should place two units of horse and one of foot on this side of the field.

examples.text: “I haven’t got a horse,” said Gatsby.
examples.translation_ko: "말이 없습니다." 개츠비가 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The horses, needless to say, were not mentioned again.
examples.translation_ko: 말할 것도 없이, 말들은 다시 언급되지 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We went at a foot-pace, but on the way back we trotted, and there was something to my mind singularly horrible in the way the driver of the hearse whipped up his horses.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 걸음걸이로 갔지만, 돌아오는 길에는 속보로 갔는데, 영구차 마부가 말들에게 채찍을 가하는 모습이 내 마음에는 묘하게 끔찍하게 느껴졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French civilisation, equivalent to civilise + -ation or civil + -isation.
definition_en: A complex human society with a high level of social organization.

senses.gloss: UK, Ireland, Australia, New Zealand, South Africa, Hong Kong, and Commonwealth spelling of civilization.

examples.text: They sounded strangely in the tropical night thousands of miles from civilisation.
examples.translation_ko: 문명에서 수천 마일 떨어진 열대의 밤에 그 선율들은 이상하게 들렸습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Here all the decencies of civilisation are swept away, and you feel that men are face to face with a sombre reality.
examples.translation_ko: 이곳에서는 문명의 모든 체면이 쓸려나가고, 인간이 음울한 현실과 정면으로 마주하고 있음을 느끼게 된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A flat dish used for serving or eating food.

senses.gloss: A slightly curved but almost flat dish from which food is served or eaten.
senses.example: I filled my plate from the bountiful table.

senses.gloss: Such dishes collectively.
senses.example: A valuable collection of silver plate was donated to the museum.

senses.gloss: The contents of such a dish.
senses.example: I ate a plate of beans.

examples.text: Daisy and Tom were sitting opposite each other at the kitchen table, with a plate of cold fried chicken between them, and two bottles of ale.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지와 톰이 부엌 테이블에서 서로 마주 앉아 있었고, 그들 사이에는 차가운 프라이드치킨 한 접시와 맥주 두 병이 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I remember a still-life of oranges on a plate, and I was bothered because the plate was not round and the oranges were lop-sided.
examples.translation_ko: 접시 위에 놓인 오렌지들을 그린 정물화가 기억나는데, 접시가 둥글지 않고 오렌지들이 비뚤어져 있어서 나는 거슬렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: On a rack were the plates that she had used for dinner on the night of her quarrel with Strickland, and they had been carefully washed.
examples.translation_ko: 선반에는 스트릭랜드와 다툰 밤 저녁 식사 때 그녀가 사용했던 접시들이 놓여 있었는데, 깨끗이 씻어져 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English [Term?], borrowed from Old French triumphe, from Latin triumphus (“triumphal procession”), ultimately from Ancient Greek θρίαμβ...
definition_en: A victory or achievement that is celebrated.

senses.gloss: A conclusive success following an effort, conflict, or confrontation of obstacles; victory; conquest.
senses.example: the triumph of knowledge

senses.gloss: A magnificent and imposing ceremonial performed in honor of a victor.
Any triumphal procession; a pompous exhibition; a stately show or pageant.
senses.example: We are ready, & our daughter heere, / In honour of whoſe Birth, theſe Triumphs are, / Sits heere like Beauties child,

examples.text: It’s a triumph.
examples.translation_ko: 대단한 성과야.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The groups change more swiftly, swell with new arrivals, dissolve and form in the same breath; already there are wanderers, confident girls who weave here and there among the stouter and more stable, become for a sharp, joyous moment the centre of a group, and then, excited with triumph, glide on through the sea-change of faces and voices and colour under the constantly changing light.
examples.translation_ko: 무리들은 더욱 빠르게 변화하고, 새로 도착한 사람들로 부풀어 오르고, 해체되었다가 같은 숨결 안에서 다시 형성되었다. 이미 방랑자들이 있었는데, 자신만만한 소녀들이 더 든든하고 안정적인 사람들 사이를 이리저리 누비며, 날카롭고 즐거운 순간 동안 무리의 중심이 되었다가, 승리에 들뜬 채 끊임없이 변하는 빛 아래서 얼굴과 목소리와 색채의 바다 같은 변화 속을 미끄러져 나아갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: At last he came upon what he sought, a large scraper, and he pounced on it with a cry of triumph.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 그가 찾던 것, 큰 스크래퍼를 발견했고, 승리의 외침과 함께 그것을 움켜잡았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose it was a very pretty example of the triumph of spirit over matter, and so my digression has at least the advantage of a moral.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 이것은 정신이 물질을 이기는 승리의 아주 좋은 본보기였을 것이고, 그러니 내 곁가지 이야기도 최소한 교훈이라는 장점은 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English reaccion, from Old French reaction, from Latin reāctiō, from the verb reagō, from re- (“again”) + agō (“to act”); mor...
definition_en: A strong feeling of dislike or opposition.

senses.gloss: An action or statement in response to a stimulus or other event.
senses.example: The announcement of the verdict brought a violent reaction.

senses.gloss: A transformation in which one or more substances is converted into another by combination or decomposition.
senses.example: In this reaction, the acid and base will neutralize each other, producing a salt.

senses.gloss: Reactionary politics; a period in which reactionary thought or politics is resurgent or dominant.

examples.text: He spoke as if Daisy’s reaction was the only thing that mattered.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 마치 데이지의 반응만이 중요한 것처럼 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Now, in the reaction, he was running down like an over-wound clock.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 그 반작용으로, 그는 태엽을 너무 감은 시계처럼 서서히 멈춰가고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I stood by, at a loss, like a stranger in a land where the reactions of man to familiar things are all different from those he has known.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 어찌할 바를 모르고 그 자리에 서 있었다. 마치 익숙한 것들에 대한 인간의 반응이 자신이 알던 것과 모두 다른 낯선 땅의 이방인처럼.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I had an idea that Dirk, a man of greater emotional reactions than depth of feeling, would soon forget; and Blanche’s life, begun with who knows what bright hopes and what dreams, might just as well have never been lived.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 감정의 깊이보다는 반응이 더 격렬한 남자인 더크가 곧 잊어버리리라는 생각이 들었다. 그리고 누가 알겠는가, 어떤 밝은 희망과 꿈으로 시작되었을 블랑슈의 인생은 아예 살지 않았던 것과 다름없을지도 모른다는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A unit of language that expresses a complete thought.

senses.gloss: The decision or judgement of a jury or court; a verdict.
senses.example: The court returned a sentence of guilt in the first charge, but innocence in the second.

senses.gloss: The judicial order for a punishment to be imposed on a person convicted of a crime.
senses.example: The judge declared a sentence of death by hanging for the infamous child rapist.

senses.gloss: A punishment imposed on a person convicted of a crime.

examples.text: After she had obliterated four years with that sentence they could decide upon the more practical measures to be taken.
examples.translation_ko: 그 한마디로 4년의 세월을 지워버린 후에야 그들은 더 현실적인 조치들을 결정할 수 있을 터였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We hadn’t reached West Egg village before Gatsby began leaving his elegant sentences unfinished and slapping himself indecisively on the knee of his caramel-coloured suit.
examples.translation_ko: 웨스트에그 마을에 도착하기도 전에 개츠비는 우아한 문장들을 끝맺지 못한 채 남겨두기 시작했고, 캐러멜색 양복 무릎을 우유부단하게 치기 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Dr. Coutras had delivered sentence of death on many men, and he could never overcome the horror with which it filled him.
examples.translation_ko: 쿠트라 박사는 수많은 사람에게 사형선고를 내려왔지만, 그때마다 느끼는 공포감을 결코 극복할 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But neither here nor elsewhere do I pretend to give his exact words; his vocabulary was small, and he had no gift for framing sentences, so that one had to piece his meaning together out of interjections, the expression of his face, gestures and hackneyed phrases.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 여기서든 다른 곳에서든 나는 그의 정확한 말을 전한다고 주장하지는 않는다. 그의 어휘는 빈약했고 문장을 구성하는 재능도 없어서, 감탄사와 표정, 몸짓, 그리고 진부한 구절들을 짜맞춰 그의 의미를 파악해야 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French colossal, formed from Latin colossus, from Ancient Greek κολοσσός (kolossós, “giant statue”).
definition_en: Extremely large or impressive.

senses.gloss: Extremely large or on a great scale.
senses.example: A single puppy can make a colossal mess.

senses.gloss: Amazingly spectacular; extraordinary; epic.

examples.text: But he knew that he was in Daisy’s house by a colossal accident.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그는 자신이 엄청난 우연으로 데이지의 집에 있다는 것을 알고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Possibly it had occurred to him that the colossal significance of that light had now vanished forever.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 그 불빛이 지녔던 엄청난 의미가 이제 영원히 사라져버렸다는 생각이 그에게 떠올랐을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Even I, in my colossal ignorance, could not but feel that here, trying to express itself, was real power.
examples.translation_ko: 무지몽매한 나조차도 여기서 자신을 표현하려 애쓰는 것이 진정한 힘이라는 것을 느끼지 않을 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

A similarly framed structure with a platform or enclosed area on top, used as a lookout for spotting fires, plane crashes, fugitives, etc.
A water tower.

examples.text: His eyes went over it, every arched door and square tower.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 시선이 집 전체를 훑었다, 아치형 문과 사각형 탑 하나하나를.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Turning a corner, I saw that it was Gatsby’s house, lit from tower to cellar.
examples.translation_ko: 모퉁이를 돌자 그것이 개츠비의 집임을 알 수 있었는데, 탑 꼭대기부터 지하실까지 환하게 불이 켜져 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He is shut in a tower of brass, and can communicate with his fellows only by signs, and the signs have no common value, so that their sense is vague and uncertain.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 황동 탑에 갇혀 있어서, 동료들과는 오직 신호로만 소통할 수 있는데, 그 신호들은 공통된 가치가 없어서 의미가 모호하고 불확실하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

The female cousin or cousin-in-law of one’s parent.
A woman of an older generation than oneself, especially a friend of one's parents, by means of fictive kin.

examples.translation_ko: 모든 숙모와 숙부들이 마치 내게 맞는 예비학교를 고르듯 상의를 했고, 마침내 매우 진지하고 망설이는 표정으로 "음—그래"라고 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Their brain is seething with ideas, and they can only tell you that the umbrella of the gardener’s aunt is in the house.
examples.translation_ko: 머릿속에는 온갖 생각들이 끓어오르는데, 정작 할 수 있는 말이라고는 정원사 아주머니의 우산이 집에 있다는 것뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Completely or entirely.

senses.gloss: Completely; entirely; to the fullest extent.

examples.text: The idea is if we don’t look out the white race will be—will be utterly submerged.
examples.translation_ko: 요점은 우리가 조심하지 않으면 백인종이—백인종이 완전히 매몰될 거라는 거야.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I woke up out of the ether with an utterly abandoned feeling, and asked the nurse right away if it was a boy or a girl.
examples.translation_ko: 마취에서 깨어나니 완전히 버림받은 기분이 들어서, 간호사에게 곧바로 아들인지 딸인지 물어봤지.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The final impression I received was of a prodigious effort to express some state of the soul, and in this effort, I fancied, must be sought the explanation of what so utterly perplexed me.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 마지막으로 받은 인상은 영혼의 어떤 상태를 표현하려는 엄청난 노력이었고, 나를 그토록 완전히 당황시킨 것의 해답도 바로 이 노력에서 찾아야 한다고 생각했다.

senses.gloss: To force, constrain, or coerce.

examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 목소리가 끊어지는 순간, 내 관심과 믿음을 강요하던 것이 멈추자, 나는 그녀가 한 말의 근본적인 거짓됨을 느꼈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Before I could reply that he was my neighbour dinner was announced; wedging his tense arm imperatively under mine, Tom Buchanan compelled me from the room as though he were moving a checker to another square.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 내 이웃이라고 대답하기도 전에 저녁 식사가 준비되었다고 알려왔다. 톰 뷰캐넌은 긴장한 팔을 강압적으로 내 팔 밑에 끼워 넣고는 마치 체커 말을 다른 칸으로 옮기듯 나를 방에서 끌어냈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was as though he had become aware of the soul of the universe and were compelled to express it.
examples.translation_ko: 마치 그가 우주의 영혼을 깨닫게 되어 그것을 표현하지 않을 수 없게 된 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.example: She was the mistress of the estate-mansion, and owned the horses.

senses.gloss: A female head of household.
A female teacher.
senses.example: games mistress

examples.text: His wife and his mistress, until an hour ago secure and inviolate, were slipping precipitately from his control.
examples.translation_ko: 한 시간 전까지만 해도 안전하고 침범당할 수 없었던 그의 아내와 정부가 그의 통제에서 급격히 빠져나가고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There is always a halt there of at least a minute, and it was because of this that I first met Tom Buchanan’s mistress.
examples.translation_ko: 그곳에서는 항상 최소한 1분은 정차하는데, 바로 그 때문에 나는 톰 뷰캐넌의 정부를 처음 만나게 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I do not know how I have deserved to have a wife who was the perfect friend and helpmate, the perfect mistress and the perfect mother.”
examples.translation_ko: 나는 완벽한 친구이자 동반자, 완벽한 아내이자 완벽한 어머니인 부인을 둘 자격이 내게 있는지 모르겠다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: As a mistress she did not then exist for him, but only as a model; and then there were long hours in which they lived side by side in silence.
examples.translation_ko: 애인으로서 그녀는 그때 그에게 존재하지 않았고, 오직 모델로서만 존재했다. 그리고 그들이 나란히 침묵 속에서 지내는 긴 시간들이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: A series of interconnected things.

senses.gloss: A series of stores or businesses with the same brand name.

examples.translation_ko: 그것은 몬테네그로의 따뜻한 작은 심장에서 우러나온 이 찬사를 불러일으킨 일련의 국가적 상황들을 충분히 이해하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I remembered, of course, that the World’s Series had been fixed in 1919, but if I had thought of it at all I would have thought of it as a thing that merely happened, the end of some inevitable chain.
examples.translation_ko: 물론 나는 1919년 월드시리즈가 조작되었다는 것을 기억하고 있었지만, 그것에 대해 생각해본 적이 있다면 그저 일어난 일, 어떤 필연적인 연쇄의 끝 정도로 여겼을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They are as little their own masters as the slaves chained to the benches of a galley.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 갤리선의 노 젓는 자리에 사슬로 묶인 노예들과 마찬가지로 자신의 주인이 아닙니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Perhaps she knew with her intelligence that the chains she forged only aroused his instinct of destruction, as the plate-glass window makes your fingers itch for half a brick; but her heart, incapable of reason, made her continue on a course she knew was fatal.
examples.translation_ko: 아마 그녀는 자신의 지성으로 알고 있었을 것이다. 자신이 만드는 사슬이 오히려 그의 파괴 본능만 자극할 뿐이라는 것을, 마치 판유리창이 사람으로 하여금 벽돌 반 조각을 집어 던지고 싶은 충동을 불러일으키는 것처럼 말이다. 하지만 이성을 잃은 그녀의 마음은 치명적이라는 것을 알면서도 그 길을 계속 걷게 만들었다.

examples.text: Most of those reports were a nightmare—grotesque, circumstantial, eager, and untrue.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For in men, as a rule, love is but an episode which takes its place among the other affairs of the day, and the emphasis laid on it in novels gives it an importance which is untrue to life.
examples.translation_ko: 일반적으로 남자들에게 사랑이란 하루의 다른 일들 사이에 자리 잡는 하나의 에피소드에 불과한데, 소설에서 그것에 부여하는 강조는 삶의 진실과 맞지 않는 중요성을 부여하기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The conversation proceeded, and I marvelled at the tact with which Mr. Van Busche Taylor avoided all subjects that might have been in the least embarrassing, and at the ingenuity with which Mrs. Strickland, without saying a word that was untrue, insinuated that her relations with her husband had always been perfect.
examples.translation_ko: 대화가 이어졌고, 나는 반 부셰 테일러 씨가 조금이라도 난처할 수 있는 모든 주제를 피해가는 재치와, 스트릭랜드 부인이 거짓말은 한 마디도 하지 않으면서도 남편과의 관계가 항상 완벽했다고 넌지시 암시하는 교묘함에 감탄했다.

examples.translation_ko: 어떤 여자는 검은 속옷에 살색 스타킹을 신고 있고, 어떤 여자는 노랗게 염색한 곱슬머리를 하고 짧은 모슬린 원피스를 입어 마치 어린 소녀처럼 차려입었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Tom talked incessantly, exulting and laughing, but his voice was as remote from Jordan and me as the foreign clamour on the sidewalk or the tumult of the elevated overhead.
examples.translation_ko: 톰은 쉴 새 없이 떠들며 의기양양해하고 웃어댔지만, 그의 목소리는 조던과 나에게 인도의 시끄러운 외국인들의 소음이나 머리 위 고가철도의 소란만큼이나 멀게 들렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Here, on this remote island, he seemed to have aroused none of the detestation with which he was regarded at home, but compassion rather; and his vagaries were accepted with tolerance.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The demon which possessed him was exorcised at last, and with the completion of the work, for which all his life had been a painful preparation, rest descended on his remote and tortured soul.

senses.gloss: Somebody who possesses great bravery and carries out extraordinary or noble deeds.

The protagonist in a work of fiction.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There was here, maybe, the opportunity for a modern version of the hero who for the good of mankind exposes himself to the agonies of the damned.
examples.translation_ko: 여기에는 인류의 선을 위해 자신을 저주받은 자들의 고통에 내맡기는 영웅의 현대적 판본을 위한 기회가 있었을지도 모른다.

definition_en: A payment or gift given to a superior as a sign of respect or loyalty.

senses.gloss: An acknowledgment of gratitude, respect or admiration; an accompanying gift.
senses.example: Please accept this as a tribute of our thanks.

senses.gloss: An homage made in a body of work to another work or creator.

senses.gloss: A payment made by one nation to another in submission.

examples.text: Almost any exhibition of complete self-sufficiency draws a stunned tribute from me.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It appreciated fully the chain of national circumstances which had elicited this tribute from Montenegro’s warm little heart.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 몬테네그로의 따뜻한 작은 심장에서 우러나온 이 찬사를 불러일으킨 일련의 국가적 상황들을 충분히 이해하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It may be that you do not like his art, but at all events you can hardly refuse it the tribute of your interest.
examples.translation_ko: 당신이 그의 예술을 좋아하지 않을 수도 있지만, 어쨌든 관심이라는 찬사는 거부하기 어려울 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A person who admires or respects someone or something.

senses.gloss: One who admires.
senses.example: Deven is an enthusiastic admirer of The Beatles.

senses.gloss: One who is romantically attracted to someone.
senses.example: Although he has a number of admirers, he prefers to remain single.

examples.text: I was his first admirer in the islands.”

examples.text: Dr. Weitbrecht-Rotholz was an enthusiastic admirer of Charles Strickland, and there was no danger that he would whitewash him.
examples.translation_ko: 바이트브레히트-로톨츠 박사는 찰스 스트릭랜드의 열렬한 찬미자였으므로, 그가 스트릭랜드를 미화할 위험은 전혀 없었다.

senses.gloss: Frequent repetition of the same behavior; way of behavior common to many; ordinary manner; habitual practice; method of doing, living or behaving.
senses.example: Moved beyond his custom, Gama said

senses.gloss: Habitual buying of goods from one same vendor.
senses.example: Let him have your custom, but not your votes.

senses.gloss: The habitual patrons (i.e. customers) of a business; business support.

examples.text: Everything is done with a great deal of bustle, the unloading of the baggage, the examination of the customs; and everyone seems to smile at you.
examples.translation_ko: 짐을 내리고 세관 검사를 받는 모든 일이 매우 분주하게 이루어지며, 모든 사람이 당신에게 미소를 짓는 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose Velasquez was a better painter than El Greco, but custom stales one’s admiration for him: the Cretan, sensual and tragic, proffers the mystery of his soul like a standing sacrifice.
examples.translation_ko: 벨라스케스가 엘 그레코보다 더 뛰어난 화가였을 것이라고 생각하지만, 관습이 그에 대한 감탄을 진부하게 만든다. 반면 관능적이고 비극적인 크레타 출신 화가는 제단 위의 제물처럼 자신의 영혼의 신비를 내보인다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A person who writes poetry.

senses.gloss: A person who writes poems.
A person with a creative or romantic imagination.

examples.text: Then came the French Revolution and the Napoleonic Wars, and the poets sang new songs.
examples.translation_ko: 그러다 프랑스 혁명과 나폴레옹 전쟁이 일어났고, 시인들은 새로운 노래를 불렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Only the poet or the saint can water an asphalt pavement in the confident anticipation that lilies will reward his labour.
examples.translation_ko: 오직 시인이나 성인만이 백합이 자신의 노고에 보답할 것이라는 확신을 품고 아스팔트 포장도로에 물을 뿌릴 수 있다.

definition_en: Extremely beautiful or impressive

senses.gloss: To heat (a substance) in a container so as to convert it into a gas which then condenses in solid form on cooler parts of the container; (generally) to change (a solid substance) into a gas without breaking down or passing through the liquid state by heating it gently.
senses.example: The aſhes either of Pit-Coal, or Sea-Coal, make no Efferveſcence vvith Alkalies or Acids. VVhence the ſaline Principle is altogether volatile, and ſublimed avvay by the fire.

senses.gloss: To obtain or purify (a substance) in this manner.
senses.example: [I]t [niter, or sodium carbonate] Calcineth, Sublimeth and Diſſolveth Minerals and Metals.

senses.gloss: To raise (someone or an intangible thing) to a state of (especially moral or spiritual) excellence; to exalt.
senses.example: […] Bob's countenance was sublimed by his recent interview, like that of a priest just come from the penetralia of the temple.

examples.text: Stroeve was sublime.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 숭고했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Those great works of his have the calm of the sublime; but here, notwithstanding beauty, was something troubling.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 위대한 작품들에는 숭고함의 고요함이 있다. 하지만 여기에는 아름다움에도 불구하고 뭔가 불안하게 하는 것이 있었다.

definition_en: Relating to or characterized by sex.

senses.gloss: Arising from the fact of being male or female; pertaining to sex or gender, or to the social relations between the sexes.
senses.example: Women face sexual discrimination in the workplace.

senses.gloss: Capable of sexual reproduction; sexed, sexuate.
Pertaining to sexual intercourse or other intimate physical contact.

examples.text: I suppose that art is a manifestation of the sexual instinct.

definition_en: A strong and often unaccountable interest or attraction.

senses.gloss: The act of bewitching, or enchanting
senses.example: Little disappointed, then, she turned attention to "Chat of the Social World," gossip which exercised potent fascination upon the girl's intelligence.

senses.gloss: The state or condition of being fascinated.
senses.example: To my fascination, the skies turned all kinds of colours.

senses.gloss: Something which fascinates.
senses.example: Life after death had always been a great fascination to him.

examples.text: My incredulity was submerged in fascination now; it was like skimming hastily through a dozen magazines.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: To pursue his secret has something of the fascination of a detective story.

definition_en: A piece of writing that is published in a newspaper or magazine.

senses.gloss: A piece of nonfiction writing such as a story, report, opinion piece, or entry in a newspaper, magazine, journal, encyclopedia, etc.
An object, a member of a group or class.
senses.example: an article of clothing

senses.gloss: A part of speech that indicates, specifies and limits a noun (a, an, or the in English). In some languages the article may appear as an ending (e.g. definite article in Swedish) or there may be none (e.g. Russian, Pashto).
senses.example:
‘A song called “Freak Like Me” by the Sugababes,’ said Jesse.
‘Just Sugababes, no article,’ the man said, enjoying the stunned reaction on Jesse’s face.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was not till four years after Strickland’s death that Maurice Huret wrote that article in the Mercure de France which rescued the unknown painter from oblivion and blazed the trail which succeeding writers, with more or less docility, have followed.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To save someone or something from a difficult situation.

senses.gloss: To save from any violence, danger or evil.
senses.example: The well-trained team rescued everyone after the avalanche.

senses.gloss: To free or liberate from confinement or other physical restraint.
senses.example: to rescue a prisoner from the enemy

senses.gloss: To recover forcibly, especially from a siege.

examples.text: Again he made no reply, but the driver of our carriage came to my rescue.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 또다시 대답하지 않았지만, 마차 운전사가 나를 구해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I felt so shy that I could think of nothing to say, but Mrs. Strickland came to my rescue.
examples.translation_ko: 너무 어색해서 할 말이 떠오르지 않았는데, 스트릭랜드 부인이 나를 구해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To make a strong impression on someone.

senses.gloss: To affect (someone) strongly and often favourably.
senses.example: You impressed me with your command of Urdu.

senses.gloss: To make an impression, to be impressive.
senses.example: Henderson impressed in his first game as captain.

senses.gloss: To produce a vivid impression of (something).
senses.example: That first view of the Eiger impressed itself on my mind.

examples.text: Now that I look back I am more than ever impressed by Stroeve’s acuteness.
examples.translation_ko: 지금 돌이켜보니 스트루브의 예리함에 더욱 감탄하게 된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Their technique impressed him, but I fancy that he thought their attitude commonplace.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 기법은 인상적이었지만, 그는 그들의 태도가 평범하다고 생각하는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin comprehensibilis.
definition_en: Clearly understandable.

senses.gloss: Able to be comprehended.

examples.text: It is a grotesque misapprehension which sees in art no more than a craft comprehensible perfectly only to the craftsman: art is a manifestation of emotion, and emotion speaks a language that all may understand.
examples.translation_ko: 예술을 장인만이 완전히 이해할 수 있는 기예 이상으로 보지 않는 것은 기괴한 오해이다. 예술은 감정의 발현이며, 감정은 모든 사람이 이해할 수 있는 언어로 말하기 때문이다.

definition_en: A means of communicating in words, symbols, or signs.

senses.gloss: A body of words, and set of methods of combining them (called a grammar), understood by a community and used as a form of communication.
senses.example: The English and German languages are both members of the West Germanic language family.

senses.gloss: The ability to communicate using words.
senses.example: the gift of language

senses.gloss: A sublanguage: the slang of a particular community or jargon of a particular specialist field.
senses.example: legal language; the language of chemistry

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We are like people living in a country whose language they know so little that, with all manner of beautiful and profound things to say, they are condemned to the banalities of the conversation manual.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 마치 어떤 나라에 살면서도 그 나라 말을 거의 모르는 사람들과 같아서, 아름답고 심오한 말을 하고 싶어도 회화 교본의 진부한 표현들로 만족해야 하는 신세다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A method or skill used to achieve a particular result.

senses.gloss: The practical aspects of a given art, occupation etc.; formal requirements.
senses.example: Brahms, after realizing that the technique of the piano was developing along mistaken lines, and his own danger of stereotyping his style, keeps away from it for most of his middle age [...].

senses.gloss: Practical ability in some given field or practice, often as opposed to creativity or imaginative skill.
senses.example: Yet those who packed concert halls to listen to him sing, as Indians did for over six decades, rarely mentioned his technique.

senses.gloss: A method of achieving something or carrying something out, especially one requiring some skill or knowledge.
senses.example: They said executives were warned about one technique nicknamed "carpet karaoke", which involved bending deportees over in aircraft seats to silence them.

examples.text: First of all I was taken aback by what seemed to me the clumsiness of his technique.
examples.translation_ko: 무엇보다 먼저 나를 당황하게 한 것은 그의 기법이 서투르다고 여겨진 점이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Their technique impressed him, but I fancy that he thought their attitude commonplace.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 기법은 인상적이었지만, 그는 그들의 태도가 평범하다고 생각하는 것 같았다.

definition_en: Deserving or receiving admiration.

senses.gloss: Deserving of the highest esteem or admiration; estimable.
senses.example: It's admirable that Shelley overcame her handicap and excelled in her work.

senses.gloss: Good or heroic.
senses.example: The act of putting out the burning fires was admirable.

examples.text: “Admirable advice,” I answered.
examples.translation_ko: "훌륭한 조언이군요." 내가 대답했다.

senses.gloss: To grow plants, notably crops.

senses.gloss: To nurture; to foster; to tend.
senses.example: They tried to cultivate an interest in learning among their students.

senses.gloss: To turn or stir soil in preparation for planting or as a method of weed control between growing crop plants.
