examples.translation_ko: 망고와 바나나, 오렌지, 그리고 이름 모를 과일들이 쌓여 있는 그림이었는데, 언뜻 보기에는 충분히 무해한 그림이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English innocent, from Old French innocent, inocent, borrowed from Latin innocēns (“harmless, inoffensive”), from in- (“not”) + nocēns,...
definition_en: Free from guilt or wrongdoing.

senses.gloss: Free from guilt, sin, or immorality.
senses.example: I'm sure there's an innocent explanation for all this.

senses.gloss: Bearing no legal responsibility for a wrongful act.
Without wrongful intent; accidental or in good faith.
senses.example: He didn't mean anything by it; it was an innocent mistake.

examples.text: Our life is simple and innocent.
examples.translation_ko: 우리의 삶은 단순하고 순수합니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The Colonel stared into vacancy, and I wondered whether anyone could be quite so innocent of guile as he looked.
examples.translation_ko: 대령은 허공을 바라보았고, 나는 과연 누군가가 저렇게 보이는 만큼 순진무구할 수 있을까 하는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English personally, personely, personallich, personaliche, equivalent to personal + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is done or experienced directly by the speaker.

senses.gloss: In a personal manner.
In person.
senses.example: 'There's a boy here who wants to speak to Miss Clara personally,' he announced.

senses.gloss: Concerning oneself.
senses.example: I'm really annoyed with her, personally.

examples.text: “But if I weren’t personally concerned I should be sorry at the waste.
examples.translation_ko: "하지만 내가 개인적으로 관련되지 않았다면 그런 낭비가 안타까웠을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “There’s no harm in a kick in the hindquarters when your belly’s full,” said Captain Nichols, “and personally I never take it in bad part.
examples.translation_ko: "배가 부를 때 엉덩이에 발길질 한 번 당하는 건 별일 아니야." 니콜스 선장이 말했다. "개인적으로 나는 그런 걸 나쁘게 받아들이지 않아.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From unpleasant + -ness.
definition_en: A state or quality of being unpleasant.

senses.gloss: The property of being unpleasant or disagreeable.
senses.example: Given the behaviour of the members, who do normally come to Lord’s, this seemed a bizarre attempt to offload the unpleasantness on hoi polloi taking advantage of some rare £25 tickets.

senses.gloss: An unpleasant behaviour, occurrence, etc.

examples.text: “I’m just going to wait here and see if he tries to bother her about that unpleasantness this afternoon.
examples.translation_ko: "여기서 기다리면서 그가 오늘 오후 그 불쾌한 일로 그녀를 괴롭히려 하는지 지켜볼 생각이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There were the same people, or at least the same sort of people, the same profusion of champagne, the same many-coloured, many-keyed commotion, but I felt an unpleasantness in the air, a pervading harshness that hadn’t been there before.
examples.translation_ko: 같은 사람들, 아니 적어도 같은 부류의 사람들이 있었고, 샴페인도 똑같이 풍성했으며, 똑같이 화려하고 다채로운 소란이 있었지만, 공기 중에 불쾌함이 느껴졌다. 전에는 없던 거친 기운이 전체를 감싸고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But it was nice to see that any unpleasantness he had endured in his native land had not impaired his ardent patriotism.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 고국에서 겪었던 어떤 불쾌한 일도 그의 열렬한 애국심을 손상시키지 못했다는 것은 보기 좋은 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Personally I think it was rash of Mr. Strickland, in refuting the account which had gained belief of a certain “unpleasantness” between his father and mother, to state that Charles Strickland in a letter written from Paris had described her as “an excellent woman,” since Dr. Weitbrecht-Rotholz was able to print the letter in facsimile, and it appears that the passage referred to ran in fact as follows: God damn my wife.
examples.translation_ko: 개인적으로 나는 스트릭랜드 씨가 아버지와 어머니 사이의 어떤 "불쾌한 일"에 대해 널리 믿어진 설명을 반박하면서, 찰스 스트릭랜드가 파리에서 보낸 편지에서 어머니를 "훌륭한 여성"이라고 묘사했다고 진술한 것은 경솔했다고 생각한다. 왜냐하면 바이트브레히트-로톨츠 박사가 그 편지를 복사본으로 인쇄할 수 있었고, 언급된 구절이 실제로는 다음과 같이 되어 있었음이 밝혀졌기 때문이다: 젠장할 내 아내.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed into Middle English from Old French passage, from passer (“to pass”).
definition_en: A section of a book or document.

senses.gloss: A paragraph or section of text or music with particular meaning.
senses.example: passage of scripture

senses.gloss: Part of a path or journey.
senses.example: He made his passage through the trees carefully, mindful of the stickers.

senses.gloss: An incident or episode.
senses.example: But there are those who do not feel that the sordid passages of life should be kept off the stage. It is a matter of opinion.

examples.text: He worked his passage on a sailing vessel that was making the trip from Auckland to San Francisco, and he arrived with a box of paints, an easel, and a dozen canvases.
examples.translation_ko: 오클랜드에서 샌프란시스코로 가는 범선에서 일하며 배삯을 벌었고, 물감 상자와 이젤, 캔버스 열두 장을 가지고 도착했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They are strangers in their birthplace, and the leafy lanes they have known from childhood or the populous streets in which they have played, remain but a place of passage.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 태어난 곳에서조차 이방인이며, 어린 시절부터 알아온 나뭇잎 우거진 골목길이나 뛰어놀던 번화한 거리들도 그저 지나가는 장소일 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English referren, from Old French referer, from Latin referre. The noun (used in journalism) is from the verb. Doublet of relate. See a...
definition_en: To mention or direct someone to something.

senses.gloss: To direct the attention of (someone toward something)
senses.example: The shop assistant referred me to the help desk on ground floor.

senses.gloss: To submit to (another person or group) for consideration; to send or direct elsewhere.
senses.example: He referred the matter to the principal.

senses.gloss: To place in or under by a mental or rational process; to assign to, as a class, a cause, source, a motive, reason, or ground of explanation.
senses.example: He referred the phenomena to electrical disturbances.

examples.text: Of course I knew what they were referring to, but I wasn’t even vaguely engaged.
examples.translation_ko: 물론 그들이 무엇을 말하는지 알고 있었지만, 나는 어렴풋이라도 약혼한 상태가 아니었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: From the moment I telephoned news of the catastrophe to West Egg village, every surmise about him, and every practical question, was referred to me.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 웨스트에그 마을에 그 참사 소식을 전화로 알린 순간부터, 그에 대한 모든 추측과 모든 실질적인 문제가 나에게 맡겨졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I felt a certain shyness at referring to matters which were no concern of mine.
examples.translation_ko: 나와는 상관없는 일에 대해 언급하는 것이 어딘지 부끄러웠다.

definition_en: A person who has a deep understanding of the mysteries of life and the universe.

senses.gloss: Of, or relating to mystics, mysticism or occult mysteries; mystical.
senses.example: a mystic dance

senses.gloss: Mysterious and strange; arcane, obscure or enigmatic.
senses.example:
Tho’ truths in manhood darkly join,
⁠Deep-seated in our mystic frame,
⁠We yield all blessing to the name
Of Him that made them current coin; […]

examples.text: No mystic ever saw deeper meaning in common things.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 신비주의자도 평범한 사물에서 이보다 더 깊은 의미를 보지는 못했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was like the mystic seeking to describe the ineffable.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 형언할 수 없는 것을 묘사하려는 신비주의자 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French ineffable (modern French ineffable), from Latin ineffābilis, from in- (“not”) + effor (“utter”) + -bilis (“-able”).
definition_en: Too great or beautiful to be expressed in words.

senses.gloss: Beyond expression in words; unspeakable.
senses.example: As Alan Watts (1961) wrote, it involves trying to speak the unspeakable, scrute the inscrutable and eff the ineffable.

senses.gloss: Forbidden to be uttered; taboo.

examples.text: A universe of ineffable gaudiness spun itself out in his brain while the clock ticked on the washstand and the moon soaked with wet light his tangled clothes upon the floor.
examples.translation_ko: 세면대 위의 시계가 째깍거리고 달빛이 바닥에 어지럽게 흩어진 그의 옷가지들을 축축한 빛으로 적시는 동안, 형언할 수 없이 화려한 우주가 그의 뇌 속에서 펼쳐졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I had a fleeting glimpse of a pursuit of the ineffable.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 형언할 수 없는 것을 추구하는 모습을 잠깐 엿보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was like the mystic seeking to describe the ineffable.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 형언할 수 없는 것을 묘사하려는 신비주의자 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English warm, werm, from Old English wearm, from Proto-West Germanic *warm, from Proto-Germanic *warmaz, either from Proto-Indo-Europea...
definition_en: To make or become warm.

senses.gloss: Of a somewhat high temperature, often but not always connoting that the high temperature is pleasant rather than uncomfortable.
senses.example: The tea is still warm.

senses.gloss: Friendly and with affection.
senses.example: We have a warm friendship.

senses.gloss: Having a color in the part of the visible electromagnetic spectrum between red and yellow-green.

examples.text: Though it was October, the evening was warm, and the tables on the pavement were crowded.
examples.translation_ko: 10월이었지만 저녁은 따뜻했고, 보도의 테이블들은 사람들로 붐볐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Her brother-in-law, Colonel MacAndrew, stood in front of the fireplace, warming his back at an unlit fire.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 시숙인 맥앤드류 대령은 벽난로 앞에 서서 불이 켜지지 않은 난로에 등을 대고 몸을 따뜻하게 하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From amaze + -ing, from Old English āmasian.
definition_en: Extremely impressive or surprising.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of amaze
senses.example: Sheffield is an amazing athlete, how much of the amazing is provided from the Chemlab.

examples.text: “It was … simply amazing,” she repeated abstractedly.
examples.translation_ko: "정말… 놀라웠어요." 그녀가 멍하니 되뇌었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I’ve just heard the most amazing thing,” she whispered.
examples.translation_ko: "방금 정말 놀라운 얘기를 들었어요." 그녀가 속삭였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His industry has been amazing.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 근면함은 놀라울 정도였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: As a rule she was so calm; her agitation now was amazing.
examples.translation_ko: 평소 그녀는 매우 침착했는데, 지금의 동요는 놀라울 정도였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A written or printed request for payment.

senses.gloss: A written list or inventory. (Now obsolete except in specific senses or set phrases; bill of lading, bill of goods, etc.)
A document, originally sealed; a formal statement or official memorandum. (Now obsolete except with certain qualifying words; bill of health, bill of sale etc.)
A draft of a law, presented to a legislature for enactment; a proposed or projected law.
senses.example: Mr. Speaker, on behalf of the Prime Minister, I beg to introduce a bill entitled[…]

examples.text: I had a woman up here last week to look at my feet, and when she gave me the bill you’d of thought she had my appendicitis out.”
examples.translation_ko: 지난주에 한 여자를 불러서 내 발을 봐달라고 했는데, 계산서를 받고 보니 맹장수술이라도 해준 줄 알겠더라고."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She never turned her customers out of her house because they did not pay their bills.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 숙박비를 내지 못한다고 해서 손님들을 내쫓는 일이 결코 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She used him with the same affability as those of her clients who paid their bills once a week.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 일주일에 한 번씩 숙박비를 내는 다른 손님들과 똑같이 친절하게 그를 대했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English hasard, from Old French hasart (“a game of dice”) (noun), hasarder (verb), from Arabic اَلزَّهْر (az-zahr, “the dice”). Compare...
definition_en: A source of danger or risk.

senses.gloss: The chance of suffering harm; danger, peril, risk of loss.
senses.example: He encountered the enemy at the hazard of his reputation and life.

senses.gloss: An obstacle or other feature which causes risk or danger; originally in sports, and now applied more generally.
senses.example: The video game involves guiding a character on a skateboard past all kinds of hazards.

senses.gloss: An obstacle or other feature that presents a risk or danger that justifies the driver in taking action to avoid it.

examples.text: “Why don’t you go over to him, Amy?” hazarded the Colonel.
examples.translation_ko: "에이미, 그에게 가보는 게 어때?" 대령이 조심스럽게 제안했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I have said already that but for the hazard of a journey to Tahiti I should doubtless never have written this book.
examples.translation_ko: 타히티로의 우연한 여행이 아니었다면 나는 분명 이 책을 쓰지 않았을 것이라고 이미 말한 바 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French, from Latin severus (“severe, serious, grave in demeanor”).
definition_en: Extremely unpleasant or serious.

senses.gloss: Very bad or intense.
senses.example: Parkinsonism, at its severest, presents itself as an akinetic amimia (as opposed to certain cortical disorders which are amimic akinesias).

senses.gloss: Strict or harsh.
senses.example: a severe taskmaster

senses.gloss: Sober, plain in appearance, austere.
senses.example: a severe old maiden aunt

examples.text: It was very severe.
examples.translation_ko: 매우 엄숙한 분위기였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But there is in my nature a strain of asceticism, and I have subjected my flesh each week to a more severe mortification.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 내 성격에는 금욕적인 면이 있어서, 매주 내 육신을 더욱 혹독한 고행에 내맡겨왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Anglo-Norman failer, from Old French faillir (“to fail”).
definition_en: The state or fact of not succeeding.

senses.gloss: State or condition of not meeting a desirable or intended objective, opposite of success.
senses.example: For Liverpool, their season will now be regarded as a relative disappointment after failure to add the FA Cup to the Carling Cup and not mounting a challenge to reach the Champions League places.

senses.gloss: A condition in which a specified organ does not function well enough to support life.
senses.example: heart failure

senses.gloss: Omission to do something, whether or not it was attempted, especially something that ought to have been done.

examples.text: On the last night, with my trunk packed and my car sold to the grocer, I went over and looked at that huge incoherent failure of a house once more.
examples.translation_ko: 마지막 밤, 트렁크를 싸고 차를 식료품점 주인에게 판 후, 나는 그 거대하고 지리멸렬한 실패작 같은 집을 다시 한 번 보러 갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The moral I draw is that the writer should seek his reward in the pleasure of his work and in release from the burden of his thought; and, indifferent to aught else, care nothing for praise or censure, failure or success.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 얻는 교훈은 작가란 자신의 작업에서 오는 기쁨과 사상의 짐에서 벗어나는 해방감에서 보상을 찾아야 한다는 것이다. 그 밖의 모든 것에는 무관심하게, 칭찬이나 비난, 실패나 성공 따위는 아랑곳하지 말고.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He left it on his marriage, and settled down on a small property he had near Quimper to live for the rest of his days in peace; but the failure of an attorney left him suddenly penniless, and neither he nor his wife was willing to live in penury where they had enjoyed consideration.
examples.translation_ko: 결혼과 함께 해군을 떠나 캥페르 근처에 있는 작은 영지에 정착하여 평생을 평화롭게 살려 했지만, 변호사의 파산으로 갑자기 무일푼이 되었고, 그와 아내 모두 한때 존경받던 곳에서 궁핍하게 사는 것을 원치 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Make a great effort to achieve something.

senses.gloss: To try to achieve a result; to make strenuous effort; to try earnestly and persistently.
senses.example: He strove to excel.

senses.gloss: To struggle in opposition; to be in contention or dispute; to contend; to contest.
senses.example: to strive against fate

senses.gloss: To vie; to compete as a rival.

 Of Daphne, by Orontes and the inspired
 Castalian spring, might with this paradise
 Of Eden strive.

examples.text: I saw a tormented spirit striving for the release of expression.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 표현의 해방을 위해 몸부림치는 고뇌에 찬 영혼을 보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The only thing that seemed clear to me—and perhaps even this was fanciful—was that he was passionately striving for liberation from some power that held him.
examples.translation_ko: 내게 분명해 보이는 유일한 것은—그리고 아마 이것조차 공상일지도 모르지만—그가 자신을 붙잡고 있는 어떤 힘으로부터의 해방을 열정적으로 추구하고 있다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Lacking substance or content.

senses.gloss: A small valley between mountains.
senses.example: He built himself a cabin in a hollow high up in the Rockies.

senses.gloss: A sunken area on a surface.
senses.example: the hollow of the hand

senses.gloss: An unfilled space in something solid; a cavity, natural or artificial.
senses.example: a hollow in a tree trunk

examples.text: After a moment the proprietor emerged from the interior of his establishment and gazed hollow-eyed at the car.

examples.text: In the Argonne Forest I took the remains of my machine-gun battalion so far forward that there was a half mile gap on either side of us where the infantry couldn’t advance.
examples.translation_ko: 아르곤 숲에서 나는 기관총 대대의 잔여 병력을 너무 앞으로 밀고 나가서 양쪽으로 보병이 전진할 수 없는 반 마일의 공백이 생겼지.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When we had done discussing the merits of the latest book, it was natural to wonder how many copies had been sold, what advance the author had received, and how much he was likely to make out of it.
examples.translation_ko: 최신작의 장점에 대한 논의를 마치고 나면, 얼마나 많은 부수가 팔렸는지, 작가가 얼마의 선인세를 받았는지, 그 책으로 얼마나 벌 것 같은지 궁금해하는 것이 자연스러웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Nothing ever happened in that little town, left behind by the advance of civilisation, and one year followed the next till death came, like a friend, to give rest to those who had laboured so diligently.
examples.translation_ko: 문명의 발전에서 뒤처진 그 작은 마을에서는 아무 일도 일어나지 않았고, 해가 바뀌고 또 바뀌어 마침내 죽음이 친구처럼 찾아와 그토록 부지런히 일해온 사람들에게 안식을 주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English comparen, from Old French comparer, from Latin comparare (“to prepare, procure”), from compar (“like or equal to another”), fro...
definition_en: To examine and note the similarities and differences between things.

senses.gloss: To assess the similarities and differences between two or more things ["to compare X with Y"]. Having made the comparison of X with Y, one might have found it similar to Y or different from Y.
senses.example: Compare the tiger's coloration with that of the zebra.

senses.gloss: To declare two things to be similar in some respect ["to compare X to Y"].
senses.example: Astronomers have compared comets to dirty snowballs.

senses.gloss: To form the three degrees of comparison of (an adjective).
senses.example: We compare "good" as "good", "better", "best".

examples.text: Compared to the great distance that had separated him from Daisy it had seemed very near to her, almost touching her.
examples.translation_ko: 그를 데이지로부터 갈라놓았던 그 먼 거리에 비하면, 그 불빛은 그녀에게 아주 가까이 있는 것처럼, 거의 그녀에게 닿을 듯이 보였었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was never satisfied with what he had done; it seemed to him of no consequence compared with the vision that obsessed his mind.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자신이 한 작업에 결코 만족하지 않았다. 그의 마음을 사로잡은 환상에 비하면 그것은 아무것도 아닌 것처럼 여겨졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He felt always the furious hatred that must seize a man condemned when he compared himself with the doctor, sane and healthy, who had the inestimable privilege of life.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 항상 사형선고를 받은 자가 느낄 수밖에 없는 맹렬한 증오를 느꼈다. 정신이 온전하고 건강하며 삶이라는 헤아릴 수 없는 특권을 누리는 의사와 자신을 비교할 때마다 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English arguen, from Old French arguer, from Latin arguere (“to declare, show, prove, make clear, reprove, accuse”), q.v. for more. Dis...
definition_en: Express disagreement or debate.

senses.gloss: To show grounds for concluding (that); to indicate, imply.
senses.example: Yusuf Bangura argues that the contractocracy thesis merely falls within what he called "third option" explanation.

senses.gloss: To debate, disagree, or discuss opposing or differing viewpoints; to controvert; to wrangle.
senses.example: He also argued for stronger methods to be used against China.

senses.gloss: To have an argument, a quarrel.

examples.text: “We can’t argue about it here,” Tom said impatiently, as a truck gave out a cursing whistle behind us.
examples.translation_ko: "여기서 말다툼할 수는 없어." 뒤에서 트럭이 욕설 섞인 경적을 울리자 톰이 짜증스럽게 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I don’t think it’s so much that,” argued Lucille sceptically; “It’s more that he was a German spy during the war.”
examples.translation_ko: "그런 건 아닌 것 같아요." 루실이 회의적으로 반박했다. "전쟁 중에 독일 스파이였다는 게 더 맞을 거예요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But again I held my tongue, for who am I to argue with a knight?
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 나는 다시 입을 다물었다. 기사 작위를 받은 사람과 누가 나서서 논쟁을 벌이겠는가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then we would speak of this publisher and of that, comparing the generosity of one with the meanness of another; we would argue whether it was better to go to one who gave handsome royalties or to another who “pushed” a book for all it was worth.
examples.translation_ko: 그러면 우리는 이 출판사 저 출판사 이야기를 하며, 한 곳의 후함과 다른 곳의 인색함을 비교했다. 후한 인세를 주는 곳으로 갈지, 아니면 책을 있는 힘껏 "밀어주는" 다른 곳으로 갈지 논쟁을 벌이기도 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English welcome, wolcume, wulcume, wilcume, from Old English wilcuma (“a wished-for guest”; compare also wilcume (“welcome!”, interject...
definition_en: To receive or greet someone warmly.

senses.gloss: Whose arrival is a cause of joy; received with gladness; admitted willingly to the house, entertainment, or company.
senses.example: a welcome visitor

senses.gloss: Producing gladness.
senses.example: a welcome turn of events;  welcome news

senses.gloss: Followed by to: free to have or enjoy gratuitously.
senses.example: You are welcome to the use of my library.

examples.text: I welcomed the opportunity.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그 기회를 반겼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I welcomed the opportunity to examine him at my ease.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그를 여유롭게 관찰할 기회를 반겼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From awk (“odd, clumsy”) + -ward. Compare Middle English aukeward (“in the wrong direction”).
definition_en: Lacking grace or coordination.

senses.gloss: Lacking dexterity in the use of the hands, or of instruments.
senses.example: John was awkward at performing the trick. He'll have to practice to improve.

senses.gloss: Not easily managed or effected; embarrassing.
senses.example: That was an extremely awkward moment. Everyone was watching.

senses.gloss: Lacking social skills, or uncomfortable with social interaction.
senses.example: I'm very awkward at parties.

examples.text: To myself my entrance seemed excessively awkward.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 보기에 내 등장은 지나치게 어색해 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He said all this slowly, detaching statement from statement with a little awkward silence, and he kept his kind, foolish eyes fixed on mine.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 이 모든 말을 천천히 했고, 어색한 침묵으로 문장과 문장 사이를 끊어가며 말했으며, 친절하고 어리석은 눈을 내 눈에 고정시키고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English propre, from Anglo-Norman proper, propre, Old French propre (French: propre), from Latin proprius.
definition_en: Being suitable or correct for a particular purpose.

senses.gloss: Suited or acceptable to the purpose or circumstances; fit, suitable.
senses.example: the proper time to plant potatoes

senses.gloss: Following the established standards of behavior or manners; correct or decorous.
senses.example: a very proper young lady

senses.gloss: Such that the preimage of every compact set is compact.

examples.text: “You know already that I have no proper pride.”
examples.translation_ko: "내게 제대로 된 자존심이 없다는 건 이미 알고 있잖아."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It represented Stroeve’s idea of the proper environment for an artist.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 화가에게 어울리는 적절한 환경에 대한 스트루브의 생각을 보여주는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lyoun, lion, leon, borrowed from Old French lion, from Latin leō, (accusative: leōnem), from Ancient Greek λέων (léōn), of uncl...
definition_en: A large carnivorous mammal with a shaggy mane.

senses.gloss: A big cat, Panthera leo, native to Africa, India and formerly much of Europe.
senses.example: Tigers and lions share a common ancestor from a few million years ago.

senses.gloss: A male lion, as opposed to a lioness, which is characterized by having a flowing shaggy mane and taking little part in hunting, which can be done cooperatively.
Any of various extant and extinct big cats, especially the mountain lion.

examples.text: Do you not see the thickening of your features and a look—how shall I describe it?—the books call it lion-faced.
examples.translation_ko: 얼굴 윤곽이 두꺼워지고 어떤 표정이—어떻게 표현해야 할까요—의학서에서는 사자상이라고 부르는 모습이 보이지 않습니까.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She held their weakness for lions in good-humoured contempt, but played to them her part of the distinguished woman of letters with decorum.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 유명인사들에 대한 그들의 약점을 선량한 경멸로 바라보았지만, 품위 있는 여류 문인이라는 자신의 역할을 예의에 맞게 연기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English dwellen (“delay, live, remain, persist”), from Old English dwellan (“to mislead, deceive; be led into error, stray”), from Prot...
definition_en: Live or stay in a particular place.

senses.gloss: A period of time in which a system or component remains in a given state.
A brief pause in the motion of part of a mechanism to allow an operation to be completed.
A planned delay in a timed control program.

examples.text: The Army and Navy Stores are a bond of union between all who dwell between the river and St. James’s Park.
examples.translation_ko: 육해군 상점은 강과 세인트 제임스 공원 사이에 사는 모든 사람들 사이의 결속의 끈이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I feel that by dwelling on some trick of speech or some queer habit I should be able to give them a significance peculiar to themselves.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 말버릇이나 기이한 습관을 자세히 묘사한다면 그들만의 독특한 의미를 부여할 수 있을 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English periode, from Middle French periode, from Medieval Latin periodus, from Ancient Greek περίοδος (períodos, “circuit, orbit, a re...
definition_en: A length of time.

senses.gloss: A length of time.
senses.example: There was a period of confusion following the announcement.

senses.gloss: A length of time in history seen as a single coherent entity; an epoch, era.
senses.example: Food rationing continued in the post-war period.

senses.gloss: The punctuation mark “.” (indicating the ending of a sentence or marking an abbreviation).
senses.example: ‘You know, a period? The black spot at the end of a sentence — what do you call them over there?’

examples.text: A brewer had built it early in the “period” craze, a decade before, and there was a story that he’d agreed to pay five years’ taxes on all the neighbouring cottages if the owners would have their roofs thatched with straw.
examples.translation_ko: 한 양조업자가 10년 전 "시대풍" 열풍이 한창일 때 그 집을 지었는데, 이웃집 오두막 주인들이 지붕을 짚으로 이어주기만 하면 5년치 세금을 대신 내주겠다고 약속했다는 이야기가 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We went upstairs, through period bedrooms swathed in rose and lavender silk and vivid with new flowers, through dressing-rooms and poolrooms, and bathrooms with sunken baths—intruding into one chamber where a dishevelled man in pyjamas was doing liver exercises on the floor.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 위층으로 올라가서 장미색과 라벤더색 비단으로 둘러싸이고 싱싱한 꽃들로 화사한 시대별 침실들을 지나고, 화장실과 당구장, 그리고 움푹 파인 욕조가 있는 욕실들을 지나갔다—한 방에서는 잠옷 차림의 헝클어진 남자가 바닥에서 간 운동을 하고 있어서 우리가 침입하게 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The dining-room was in the good taste of the period.
examples.translation_ko: 식당은 그 시대의 좋은 취향으로 꾸며져 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose his life during this period was romantic, but he certainly saw no romance in it.
examples.translation_ko: 이 시기 그의 삶은 낭만적이었을 것이라고 생각하지만, 그 자신은 분명히 그 속에서 어떤 낭만도 보지 못했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *dwóh₁
From Middle English wode, from Old English wudu, widu (“wood, forest, grove; tree; timber”), from Proto-West Germanic *widu, from ...
definition_en: A material made from trees.

senses.gloss: The substance making up the central part of the trunk and branches of a tree. Used as a material for construction, to manufacture various items, etc. or as fuel.
senses.example: This table is made of wood.

senses.gloss: The wood from a particular species of tree.
senses.example: Teak is much used for outdoor benches, but a number of other woods are also suitable, such as ipé, redwood, etc.

senses.gloss: A forested or wooded area.
senses.example: A wood beyond this moor was viewed as a border area in the seventeenth century.

examples.text: Did he dream of the nymph flying through the woods of Greece with the satyr in hot pursuit?
examples.translation_ko: 그는 사티로스의 뜨거운 추격을 받으며 그리스 숲속을 달아나는 님프를 꿈꾸고 있는 것일까?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There was a high dado of white wood and a green paper on which were etchings by Whistler in neat black frames.
examples.translation_ko: 높은 흰색 나무 벽판이 있었고, 녹색 벽지 위에는 휘슬러의 동판화들이 단정한 검은 액자에 걸려 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English designen, from Old French designer, from Latin designō (“I mark out, point out, describe, design, contrive”), from de- (or dis-...
definition_en: A plan or drawing created to achieve a specific goal.

senses.gloss: A specification of an object or process, referring to requirements to be satisfied and thus conditions to be met for them to solve a problem.
A plan (with more or less detail) for the structure and functions of an artifact, building or system.
senses.example: The initial design of the park was rejected for being too expensive.

senses.gloss: A pattern, as an element of a work of art or architecture.
senses.example: We're working on some new designs for our range of summer shirts

examples.text: On buffet tables, garnished with glistening hors-d’oeuvre, spiced baked hams crowded against salads of harlequin designs and pastry pigs and turkeys bewitched to a dark gold.
examples.translation_ko: 반짝이는 오르되브르로 장식된 뷔페 테이블 위에는 향신료를 넣어 구운 햄들이 할리퀸 무늬의 샐러드들과 어깨를 맞대고 있었고, 페이스트리로 만든 돼지와 칠면조들이 짙은 황금빛으로 마법에 걸린 듯 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I picked it up with a weary bend and handed it back to her, holding it at arm’s length and by the extreme tip of the corners to indicate that I had no designs upon it—but everyone near by, including the woman, suspected me just the same.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 지친 몸을 구부려 그것을 주워 그녀에게 돌려주었는데, 팔을 쭉 뻗고 모서리 끝만 잡아서 내가 그것에 대해 어떤 욕심도 없다는 것을 보여주려 했지만, 그 여자를 포함해 근처에 있던 모든 사람들은 똑같이 나를 의심했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her flat was always neat and cheerful, gay with flowers, and the chintzes in the drawing-room, notwithstanding their severe design, were bright and pretty.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 아파트는 언제나 깔끔하고 밝았으며, 꽃들로 화사했고, 응접실의 무늬 있는 면직물들도 엄격한 디자인에도 불구하고 밝고 예뻤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The green curtains with their peacock design, hung in straight lines, and the green carpet, in the pattern of which pale rabbits frolicked among leafy trees, suggested the influence of William Morris.
examples.translation_ko: 공작 무늬가 있는 녹색 커튼이 곧게 드리워져 있었고, 창백한 토끼들이 잎이 무성한 나무들 사이에서 뛰노는 무늬의 녹색 카펫은 윌리엄 모리스의 영향을 시사했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English streight, streght, streiȝt, the past participle of strecchen (“to stretch”), from Old English streċċan (past participle ġestrea...
definition_en: Direct and straightforward.

senses.gloss: Not crooked, curly, or bent; having a constant direction throughout its length.
senses.example: The other people, I presume, are supposed to be standing to attention, but they're all smiling at me. The lines are not even straight.

senses.gloss: Direct, undeviating.
senses.example: He had no time to set himself, but his throw was straight and true. Pick slid in, spikes high, and Schang tagged him in the ribs a foot or two from the plate.

senses.gloss: Perfectly horizontal or vertical; not diagonal or oblique.
senses.example: There's nothing more annoying than taking a great picture, only to find that the horizon isn't straight.

examples.text: And do you know, I walked straight there, and when I saw it, I recognised it at once.”
examples.translation_ko: 그런데 있잖아요, 나는 곧장 그곳으로 걸어갔고, 그 호텔을 보자마자 단번에 알아봤어요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But one evening when I was passing along the Avenue de Clichy in front of the café which Strickland frequented and which I now avoided, I ran straight into him.
examples.translation_ko: 그런데 어느 날 저녁 스트릭랜드가 자주 가던, 그래서 내가 이제는 피하고 있던 카페 앞 클리시 거리를 지나가다가 그와 정면으로 마주쳤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English avys, from Old French avis, from the phrase ce m'est a vis ("in my view"), where vis is from Latin visus, past participle of vi...
definition_en: Guidance or recommendation given to someone.

senses.gloss: An opinion offered to guide behavior in an effort to be helpful.
senses.example: She was offered various pieces of advice on what to do.

senses.gloss: Deliberate consideration; knowledge.
senses.example:
How shall I dote on her with more advice,
 That thus without advice begin to love her?

senses.gloss: Information or news given; intelligence
senses.example: late advices from France

examples.text: In my younger and more vulnerable years my father gave me some advice that I’ve been turning over in my mind ever since.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 더 어리고 더 연약했던 시절, 아버지는 내게 조언을 하나 해주셨는데, 그 후로 지금까지 나는 그 말을 마음속에서 되새기고 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The door that I pushed open, on the advice of an elevator boy, was marked “The Swastika Holding Company,” and at first there didn’t seem to be anyone inside.
examples.translation_ko: 엘리베이터 보이의 안내를 받아 밀고 들어간 문에는 "스와스티카 지주회사"라는 간판이 붙어 있었는데, 처음에는 안에 아무도 없는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Admirable advice,” I answered.
examples.translation_ko: "훌륭한 조언이군요." 내가 대답했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: To a young man like myself his advice and guidance were of incomparable value.
examples.translation_ko: 나 같은 젊은이에게 그의 조언과 지도는 비할 데 없이 소중했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: By surface analysis, amuse + -ing.
definition_en: Causing amusement or laughter.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of amuse

examples.text: “She finds them amusing.
examples.translation_ko: "재미있어 하거든요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “I don’t see anything very amusing in that.”
examples.translation_ko: "그게 그렇게 우스운 일인지 모르겠는데."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English heighte, heiȝþe, from Old English hēahþu, hēhþo, hīehþu (“height”), Proto-West Germanic *hauhiþu, from Proto-Germanic *hauhiþō ...
definition_en: The distance or level above the ground.

senses.gloss: The vertical distance from the ground to the highest part of a standing person or animal (withers in the case of a horse).
senses.example: — What's your height? — 180 centimetres.

senses.gloss: The minimum distance from a vertex of a triangle to (the extension of) the edge opposite, namely along a line perpendicular to the edge.
senses.example: The area of a triangle is "a half base times height".

senses.gloss: Bare, not covered by clothing.

senses.gloss: Lacking some clothing; clothed only in underwear.
Glib, without decoration, put bluntly.
senses.example: This is the naked truth.

examples.text: He was clean shaven, and his large face looked uncomfortably naked.
examples.translation_ko: 수염을 깨끗이 밀어서 큰 얼굴이 불편할 정도로 드러나 보였다.

examples.text: She was suckling a new-born child, and another child, stark naked, was playing at her feet.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: Flat, level.

senses.gloss: Ordinary; lacking adornment or ornamentation; unembellished.
senses.example: He was dressed simply in plain black clothes.

senses.gloss: Of just one colour; lacking a pattern.

examples.text: His manner made his answer quite plain, and the girl threw back her head with a sudden gesture.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 태도만으로도 대답은 충분히 명확했고, 소녀는 갑작스러운 몸짓으로 고개를 뒤로 젖혔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She sat down and I began to chat with her; but, it was plain that her interest was in Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 앉자 나는 그녀와 이야기를 나누기 시작했지만, 그녀의 관심이 스트릭랜드에게 있다는 것은 분명했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: The acquisition of title to, or property in, anything for a price; buying for money or its equivalent.
senses.example: They offer a free hamburger with the purchase of a drink.

senses.gloss: That which is obtained for a price in money or its equivalent.
senses.example: He was pleased with his latest purchase.

senses.gloss: That which is obtained, got or acquired, in any manner, honestly or dishonestly; property; possession; acquisition.

examples.text: Throwing a regal homecoming glance around the neighbourhood, Mrs. Wilson gathered up her dog and her other purchases, and went haughtily in.
examples.translation_ko: 동네를 둘러보며 여왕이 개선하듯 당당한 눈길을 던진 윌슨 부인은 개와 다른 물건들을 챙겨 들고 거만하게 안으로 들어갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I reflected that French paper was bad, and that, foiled of my purpose, I need not burden myself with a purchase that I did not need.
examples.translation_ko: 프랑스 종이는 질이 좋지 않다는 생각이 들었고, 목적이 좌절된 마당에 굳이 필요하지도 않은 물건을 사서 짐이 될 필요는 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But on my last day in town, coming out of the Stores, I met her with her son and daughter; like myself, she had been making her final purchases before leaving London, and we were both hot and tired.
examples.translation_ko: 그런데 런던에서의 마지막 날, 백화점에서 나오는 길에 그녀를 아들, 딸과 함께 만났다. 나처럼 그녀도 런던을 떠나기 전 마지막 쇼핑을 하고 있었고, 우리 둘 다 덥고 지쳐 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English idely, ydelly, idelliche, from Old English īdellīċe, equivalent to idle + -ly.
definition_en: In a lazy or careless manner.

senses.gloss: Without specific purpose, intent or effort.
senses.example: I idly played with the paper, not even realizing I was folding it into a paper airplane.

senses.gloss: In an idle manner.

examples.text: When in an hour they crowded into a cab to go home, I strolled idly to my club.
examples.translation_ko: 한 시간 후 그들이 마차에 몰려 타고 집으로 돌아갈 때, 나는 한가롭게 클럽으로 걸어갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I wandered about looking at the pictures I knew so well, and let my fancy play idly with the emotions they suggested.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그토록 잘 알고 있는 그림들을 보며 이리저리 거닐었고, 그 그림들이 불러일으키는 감정에 한가로이 상상을 맡겼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A feeling of discontent and resentment towards someone who has something you desire.

senses.gloss: Resentful desire of something possessed by another or others (but not limited to material possessions).
senses.example: Theodorus assures Socrates that no envy will prevent the Stranger from responding

senses.gloss: An object of envious notice or feeling.
senses.example:
Blacke Foryst of Despayr, taking photos of the band
 Put 'em up on Myspace you're the envy of the land

senses.gloss: Hatred, enmity, ill-feeling.
senses.example:
But let me tell the World,
 If he out-liue the enuie of this day,
 England did neuer owe so sweet a hope,
 So much misconstrued in his Wantonnesse.

examples.text: Malice cannot touch us, nor envy attack.
examples.translation_ko: 악의도 우리를 건드릴 수 없고, 질투도 우리를 공격할 수 없습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I envied men who had seen with their own eyes the sights that Captain Nichols described.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 니콜스 선장이 묘사한 광경들을 직접 눈으로 본 사람들이 부러웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A level of quality or achievement that is considered normal or acceptable.

senses.gloss: Falling within an accepted range of size, amount, power, quality, etc.
Growing alone as a free-standing plant; not trained on a post etc.
senses.example: There are women who cannot grow alone as standard trees;—for whom the support and warmth of some wall, some paling, some post, is absolutely necessary […].

senses.gloss: Having recognized excellence or authority.
senses.example: standard works in history; standard authors

examples.text: “Is it standard shift?” demanded Tom.
examples.translation_ko: "수동변속기야?" 톰이 다그쳤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The one on my right was a colossal affair by any standard—it was a factual imitation of some Hôtel de Ville in Normandy, with a tower on one side, spanking new under a thin beard of raw ivy, and a marble swimming pool, and more than forty acres of lawn and garden.
examples.translation_ko: 내 오른쪽에 있는 것은 어떤 기준으로 보아도 거대한 건물이었다. 노르망디의 어떤 시청사를 사실적으로 모방한 것으로, 한쪽에는 탑이 있고, 어린 담쟁이덩굴의 얇은 수염 아래 번쩍번쩍 새것이었으며, 대리석 수영장과 40에이커가 넘는 잔디밭과 정원이 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Perhaps Charles Strickland was dull judged by a standard that demanded above all things verbal scintillation; but his intelligence was adequate to his surroundings, and that is a passport, not only to reasonable success, but still more to happiness.
examples.translation_ko: 무엇보다 언변의 번뜩임을 요구하는 기준으로 판단한다면 찰스 스트릭랜드는 둔했을지도 모르지만, 그의 지성은 자신의 환경에 충분했고, 그것은 합리적인 성공뿐만 아니라 더 나아가 행복으로 가는 통행증이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Sufficient but not excessive.

senses.gloss: Equal to or fulfilling some requirement.

examples.text: After all, in any other walk in life it doesn’t matter if you’re not very good; you can get along quite comfortably if you’re just adequate; but it’s different with an artist.”
examples.translation_ko: 결국 다른 어떤 분야에서든 그리 뛰어나지 않아도 상관없어. 그저 적당하기만 해도 꽤 편안하게 살아갈 수 있거든. 하지만 예술가는 달라."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Though his means were adequate to the needs of himself and his wife, he certainly had no money to waste; but now he was wantonly extravagant in the purchase of delicacies, out of season and dear, which might tempt Strickland’s capricious appetite.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 수입은 자신과 아내의 필요를 충족시키기에 충분했지만, 확실히 낭비할 돈은 없었다. 하지만 이제 그는 스트릭랜드의 변덕스러운 식욕을 돋울 수 있는 진미들을 사는 데 방탕하게 돈을 썼는데, 그것들은 제철이 아니어서 비쌌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English tradicioun, from Old French tradicion, from Latin trāditiō, from the verb trādō. Doublet of treason.
definition_en: A custom or belief that is passed down from previous generations.

senses.gloss: A part of culture that is passed from person to person or generation to generation, possibly differing in detail from family to family, such as the way to celebrate holidays.
senses.example: After breakfast, Charles Macdoodle told Lady Mary that it was a tradition in the family that those rumbling carriages on the terrace betokened death.

senses.gloss: A commonly held system.
An established or distinctive style or method
senses.example: Following tradition, the victorious athlete runs a lap around the track.

examples.text: It is a family tradition.”

examples.translation_ko: 캐러웨이 가문은 일종의 씨족이고, 우리는 버클루 공작의 후손이라는 전통을 가지고 있지만, 우리 혈통의 실제 창시자는 할아버지의 형으로, 1851년에 이곳에 와서 남북전쟁에 대리인을 보내고 아버지가 오늘날까지 이어가고 있는 철물 도매업을 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Oh, I think that’s awfully subtle,” said the Colonel, putting into the word all the contempt he felt for a quality so alien to the traditions of his calling.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I pictured their lives, troubled by no untoward adventure, honest, decent, and, by reason of those two upstanding, pleasant children, so obviously destined to carry on the normal traditions of their race and station, not without significance.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Having or showing a calm and peaceful quality.

senses.gloss: calm and quiet; peaceful; tranquil
senses.example: The ant has made himself illustrious / Through constant industry industrious. / So what? / Would you be calm and placid / If you were full of formic acid?

examples.text: Strickland remained placid.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 평온함을 유지했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: How did I know what were the thoughts and emotions behind that placid brow and those cool gray eyes?
examples.translation_ko: 그 평온한 이마와 차가운 회색 눈동자 뒤에 어떤 생각과 감정이 숨어 있는지 내가 어떻게 알 수 있겠는가?

examples.text: It was obvious at a glance that he was in a high fever.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A distinctive feature or quality of someone or something.

senses.gloss: Being a distinguishing feature of a person or thing.

examples.text: The fact that he had never changed suggested a sluggishness of habit which seemed to me characteristic.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 한 번도 장소를 바꾸지 않았다는 사실은 그의 특징으로 보이는 습관의 게으름을 시사했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a characteristic sentimentality about the day and wanted to pass it among his friends with suitable ceremonies.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그날에 대해 특유의 감상적인 마음을 품고 있었고, 적절한 의식과 함께 친구들 사이에서 그날을 보내고 싶어 했다.

A device, incorporating a ratchet, used to torture victims by stretching them beyond their natural limits.
senses.example: During the troubles of the fifteenth century, a rack was introduced into the Tower, and was occasionally used under the plea of political necessity.

examples.translation_ko: 머리를 쥐어짜봤지만, 내가 생각하는 그의 성격과 정반대인 그런 행동을 도무지 설명할 수 없었다.

examples.text: On a rack were the plates that she had used for dinner on the night of her quarrel with Strickland, and they had been carefully washed.
examples.translation_ko: 선반에는 스트릭랜드와 다툰 밤 저녁 식사 때 그녀가 사용했던 접시들이 놓여 있었는데, 깨끗이 씻어져 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A talk or discourse on a particular subject.

senses.gloss: The ability to speak; the faculty of uttering words or articulate sounds and vocalizations to communicate.
senses.example: He had a bad speech impediment.

senses.gloss: The act of speaking, a certain style of it.
senses.example: It was hard to hear his speech over the noise.

senses.gloss: A formal session of speaking, especially a long oral message given publicly by one person.
senses.example: The candidate made some ambitious promises in his campaign speech.

examples.text: It was the kind of voice that the ear follows up and down, as if each speech is an arrangement of notes that will never be played again.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 귀가 오르락내리락 따라가게 되는 그런 목소리였다. 마치 각각의 말이 다시는 연주되지 않을 음표들의 배열인 것처럼.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Precisely at that point it vanished—and I was looking at an elegant young roughneck, a year or two over thirty, whose elaborate formality of speech just missed being absurd.
examples.translation_ko: 바로 그 순간 미소는 사라졌고—나는 서른을 한두 살 넘긴 우아한 젊은 건달을 바라보고 있었는데, 그의 정교한 격식 차린 말투는 우스꽝스러워 보이기 일보 직전이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Holding his hostess’ hand, he made her a graceful, though perhaps too elaborate, speech of thanks, and left us.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 여주인의 손을 잡고 우아하지만 다소 과장된 감사 인사를 건넨 뒤 우리를 떠났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I feel that by dwelling on some trick of speech or some queer habit I should be able to give them a significance peculiar to themselves.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 말버릇이나 기이한 습관을 자세히 묘사한다면 그들만의 독특한 의미를 부여할 수 있을 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To divide or keep apart.

senses.gloss: To divide (a thing) into separate parts.
senses.example: Separate the articles from the headings.

senses.gloss: To disunite from a group or mass; to disconnect.
senses.example: From the fine gold I separate the allay [alloy].

senses.gloss: To cause (things or people) to be separate.

examples.translation_ko: 그를 데이지로부터 갈라놓았던 그 먼 거리에 비하면, 그 불빛은 그녀에게 아주 가까이 있는 것처럼, 거의 그녀에게 닿을 듯이 보였었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
