examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The notion originated with Daisy’s suggestion that we hire five bathrooms and take cold baths, and then assumed more tangible form as “a place to have a mint julep.”
examples.translation_ko: 이 생각은 데이지가 욕실 다섯 개를 빌려서 찬물로 목욕을 하자고 제안한 데서 시작되었다가, "민트 줄렙을 마실 장소"라는 좀 더 구체적인 형태로 발전했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her black dress, simple to austerity, suggested her bereaved condition, and I was innocently astonished that notwithstanding a real emotion she was able to dress the part she had to play according to her notions of seemliness.
examples.translation_ko: 금욕적일 만큼 소박한 검은 드레스는 그녀의 상중임을 말해주었고, 진정한 감정에도 불구하고 그녀가 품위에 대한 자신의 관념에 따라 자신이 연기해야 할 역할에 맞게 옷차림을 할 수 있다는 사실에 나는 순진하게도 놀랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I do not know how he had come upon the notion of going to the South Seas, though I remember that his imagination had long been haunted by an island, all green and sunny, encircled by a sea more blue than is found in Northern latitudes.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 어떻게 남태평양으로 가겠다는 생각을 하게 되었는지는 모르겠지만, 온통 푸르고 햇살 가득한, 북방 지역에서는 볼 수 없는 더욱 푸른 바다에 둘러싸인 섬이 오랫동안 그의 상상을 사로잡고 있었다는 것은 기억한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French brut, from Old French brut, from Latin brūtus (“dull, stupid, insensible”), an Oscan loanword, from Proto-Indo-European *gʷréh₂u...
definition_en: A person who is extremely cruel or violent.

senses.gloss: Without reason or intelligence (of animals).
senses.example: a brute beast

senses.gloss: Characteristic of unthinking animals; senseless, unreasoning (of humans).
senses.example: A creature […] not prone / And brute as other creatures, but endued / With sanctity of reason.

senses.gloss: Unconnected with intelligence or thought; purely material, senseless.
senses.example: the brute earth; the brute powers of nature

examples.text: That’s what I get for marrying a brute of a man, a great, big, hulking physical specimen of a—”
examples.translation_ko: 야만적인 남자, 크고 거대하고 우람한 육체의 표본 같은—그런 사람과 결혼한 대가가 이거네요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Brutes,” I said.
examples.translation_ko: "짐승들이군요." 내가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Her voice trembled a little, and I felt a brute even to hesitate.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 목소리가 약간 떨렸고, 나는 망설이는 것만으로도 짐승 같은 기분이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English goodnesse, godnesse, from Old English gōdnes (“goodness; virtue; kindness”), from Proto-West Germanic *gōdnassī (“goodness”), e...
definition_en: Expressing approval or admiration.

senses.gloss: The state or characteristic of being good.
senses.example: Rich, raisiny, smoky, coffee goodness: that is the flavor of urfa biber.

senses.gloss: The good, nutritional, healthy part or content of something.
God.
senses.example: Thank goodness that the war is over!

examples.text: “Oh, for goodness sake, let me be.
examples.translation_ko: "아, 제발 그만 놔둬요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “For goodness sake, hold your tongue,” she interrupted, tears of annoyance in her eyes.
examples.translation_ko: "제발 입 좀 다물어요." 그녀가 짜증스러운 눈물을 글썽이며 말을 끊었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English clenchen, from Old English clenċan (“to clinch; hold fast”), a variant of Old English clenġan (“to adhere; remain”), from Proto...
definition_en: To hold or squeeze something tightly with one's teeth.

senses.gloss: To grip or hold fast.
senses.example: Clinch the pointed spear.

senses.gloss: To close tightly.
senses.example: He clenched his fist in anger.

senses.gloss: Alternative form of clinch (“bend and hammer a nail”).

examples.text: Mr. McKee was asleep on a chair with his fists clenched in his lap, like a photograph of a man of action.
examples.translation_ko: 맥키 씨는 의자에서 잠들어 있었는데, 무릎 위에 주먹을 꽉 쥔 채로 있는 모습이 마치 행동하는 남자의 사진 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I clenched my hands, seeking to control my irritation.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 주먹을 꽉 쥐고 짜증을 억누르려 애썼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She struggled for self-control, and I saw her hands clench and unclench spasmodically.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 자제력을 되찾으려 애썼고, 나는 그녀의 손이 경련적으로 주먹을 쥐었다 폈다 하는 것을 보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English paynful, peinful, peynful, paynefull, peynefull, equivalent to pain + -ful. Compare Danish pinefuld (“painful”).
definition_en: Causing or feeling physical pain.

senses.gloss: Causing pain or distress, either physical or mental.
senses.example: A rackingly painful disease that affects the joints and finally cripples, it is caused by an imbalance of uric acid in the system.

senses.gloss: Afflicted or suffering with pain (of a body part or, formerly, of a person).
Requiring effort or labor; difficult, laborious.

examples.text: It was dreadfully painful.
examples.translation_ko: 정말 고통스러운 광경이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He gulped, and put his hand to his heart to ease its painful beating.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 목을 꿀꺽 삼키고, 고통스럽게 뛰는 심장을 달래려고 가슴에 손을 얹었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English smothe, smethe, from Old English smēþe, smōþ, both from Proto-West Germanic *smanþī, of unknown origin. Cognate with Scots smui...
definition_en: To make something smooth

senses.gloss: Having a texture that lacks friction. Not rough.
senses.example: Teaching that’s done by talking seems to have one rough path and another part which is smoother.

senses.gloss: Without difficulty, problems, or unexpected consequences or incidents.
senses.example: We hope for a smooth transition to the new system.

senses.gloss: Bland; glib.
senses.example: This feeling, grounded on the experience of centuries of oppression, was not to be allayed by smooth explanations on the part of the advocates of the Constitution.

examples.text: Daisy took the brush with delight, and smoothed her hair, whereupon Gatsby sat down and shaded his eyes and began to laugh.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지는 기뻐하며 빗을 집어 들고 머리를 빗었고, 그러자 개츠비는 앉아서 눈을 가리고는 웃기 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Mrs. MacAndrew smoothed down the lap of her gown, and gold bangles fell over her wrists.
examples.translation_ko: 맥앤드류 부인은 무릎 위의 드레스를 매만졌고, 금팔찌들이 손목 위로 흘러내렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: If he’ll come back now everything can be smoothed over, and no one will know anything about it.”
examples.translation_ko: 지금 돌아온다면 모든 일이 원만하게 해결될 수 있고, 아무도 이 일에 대해 알지 못할 거예요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English wheraboutes, equivalent to whereabout + -s (adverbial suffix).
definition_en: The place or location where someone is found.

senses.gloss: In, at or near what location.
senses.example: Whereabouts do you live?

examples.text: As soon as I arrived I made an attempt to find my host, but the two or three people of whom I asked his whereabouts stared at me in such an amazed way, and denied so vehemently any knowledge of his movements, that I slunk off in the direction of the cocktail table—the only place in the garden where a single man could linger without looking purposeless and alone.
examples.translation_ko: 도착하자마자 나는 주인을 찾으려고 했지만, 그의 행방을 물어본 두세 사람이 너무나 놀란 표정으로 나를 쳐다보며 그의 움직임에 대해 아는 바가 없다고 격렬하게 부인하는 바람에, 나는 칵테일 테이블 쪽으로 슬금슬금 물러났다. 정원에서 혼자 있는 남자가 목적 없고 외로워 보이지 않으면서 머물 수 있는 유일한 장소였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: With that queer idea of his to keep his whereabouts secret, it was unlikely that, on leaving, he had said where he was going.
examples.translation_ko: 자신의 행방을 비밀로 하려는 그 기이한 생각 때문에, 떠날 때 어디로 가는지 말했을 가능성은 희박했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had some reason to conceal the fact that he had run away with a woman, and he was using every precaution to hide her whereabouts.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 어떤 여자와 함께 도망쳤다는 사실을 숨길 이유가 있었고, 그녀의 행방을 감추기 위해 온갖 주의를 기울이고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Originated 1542, from Classical Latin cynicus (“Cynic/cynic”, adjective) + -al. By surface analysis, cynic + -al. In reference to dogs, with allusi...
definition_en: Having a negative or skeptical attitude towards people and things.

senses.gloss: Of or relating to the belief that human actions are motivated only or primarily by base desires or selfishness.
senses.example: I hope it is no very cynical asperity not to confess obligations where no benefit has been received.

senses.gloss: Skeptical of the integrity, sincerity, or motives of others.
Bitterly or jadedly distrustful or contemptuous; mocking.

examples.text: The undergraduate nodded in a cynical, melancholy way.
examples.translation_ko: 그 대학생은 냉소적이고 우울한 방식으로 고개를 끄덕였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Well, I’ve had a very bad time, Nick, and I’m pretty cynical about everything.”
examples.translation_ko: "글쎄, 닉, 나는 정말 힘든 시간을 보냈고, 모든 것에 대해 꽤 냉소적이 되었어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His partner, in a violent letter, sent to his bank, had taunted him with hiding his whereabouts: and Strickland, in a cynical and humourous reply, had told his partner exactly where to find him.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 동업자가 은행으로 보낸 격렬한 편지에서 그가 행방을 숨기고 있다고 비난했는데, 스트릭랜드는 냉소적이고 유머러스한 답장으로 동업자에게 자신을 어디서 찾을 수 있는지 정확히 알려주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: My first thought was that she had come to the end of her forbearance with his infatuation for Strickland, and, goaded by the latter’s cynical behaviour, had insisted that he should be turned out.
examples.translation_ko: 내 첫 번째 생각은 그녀가 스트릭랜드에 대한 남편의 맹목적 열정을 더 이상 참을 수 없게 되었고, 스트릭랜드의 냉소적인 행동에 자극받아 그를 내쫓아야 한다고 고집을 부렸으리라는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French suite. See also the doublet suit.
definition_en: A set of rooms or apartments that are connected and share facilities.

senses.gloss: A group or train of attendants, servants etc.; a retinue.
senses.example: [A]s to men, we shall live altogether at the Duc de Romagnecourt's, his suite of servants will be ours.

senses.gloss: A connected series or succession of objects; a number of things used or classed together.
senses.example: Secondly, I continue to base my concepts on intensive study of a limited suite of collections, rather than superficial study of every packet that comes to hand.

senses.gloss: A group of connected rooms, usually separable from other rooms by means of access.
senses.example: The Presidential suite is well appointed and allows for good security.

examples.text: “It’s a swell suite,” whispered Jordan respectfully, and everyone laughed.
examples.translation_ko: "정말 멋진 스위트룸이네요." 조던이 공손하게 속삭였고, 모두가 웃었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And we all took the less explicable step of engaging the parlour of a suite in the Plaza Hotel.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 우리는 모두 설명하기 어려운 행동을 했다—플라자 호텔 스위트룸의 응접실을 빌린 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The drawing-room at the Hôtel de la Fleur was a small room, with a cottage piano, and a suite of mahogany furniture, covered in stamped velvet, neatly arranged around the walls.
examples.translation_ko: 호텔 드 라 플뢰르의 응접실은 작은 방으로, 소형 피아노 한 대와 도장을 찍은 벨벳으로 덮인 마호가니 가구 한 벌이 벽을 따라 단정하게 배치되어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I imagined that she saw her husband installed in a luxurious suite of rooms, dining at one smart restaurant after another, and she pictured his days spent at race-meetings and his evenings at the play.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그녀가 남편이 호화로운 객실에 머물며 고급 레스토랑을 전전하고, 낮에는 경마장에서 저녁에는 극장에서 시간을 보내는 모습을 상상하고 있으리라 짐작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English brest, from Old English brēost, from Proto-West Germanic *breust, from Proto-Germanic *breustą, from Proto-Indo-European *bʰrew...
definition_en: The front part of the body between the neck and the abdomen.

senses.gloss: Either of the two organs on the front of a female human's chest, which contain the mammary glands; also the analogous organs in males.
senses.example: Tanya’s breasts grew remarkably during pregnancy.

senses.gloss: The chest, or front of the human thorax.
senses.example: The Wedding-Guest here beat his breast, / For he heard the loud bassoon.

senses.gloss: A section of clothing covering the breast area.
senses.example: By the time he reached the War Memorial damp had soaked through the breasts of his shirt.

examples.text: Anger struggled in her breast with misery.
examples.translation_ko: 분노와 비참함이 그녀의 가슴속에서 격렬하게 맞부딪쳤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The suggestion sent a ray of hope in all their breasts, but I would have nothing to do with it.
examples.translation_ko: 이 추측은 모든 사람의 가슴에 한 줄기 희망을 보냈지만, 나는 그런 생각에 동조하고 싶지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English miserie, from Old French miserie (modern: misère), from Latin miseria, from miser, equivalent to miser + -y. Doublet of misère.
definition_en: A state of unhappiness or suffering.

senses.gloss: Great unhappiness; extreme pain of body or mind; wretchedness; distress; woe.
senses.example: Ever since his wife left him you can see the misery on his face.

senses.gloss: A bodily ache or pain.
senses.example: [...] and I had a misery in my left breast and shoulder. I was hurt, but knew not how or how much.

senses.gloss: Cause of misery; calamity; misfortune.

examples.text: Anger struggled in her breast with misery.
examples.translation_ko: 분노와 비참함이 그녀의 가슴속에서 격렬하게 맞부딪쳤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose he had some idea that the sight of his misery would touch her.
examples.translation_ko: 자신의 비참한 모습을 보면 그녀의 마음이 움직일 거라는 생각이 있었던 모양이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English frely, freelich, from Old English frēolīc (“free, freeborn, glorious, stately, magnificent, noble, beautiful, charming”), equiv...
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is done without restriction or control.

senses.gloss: Free; frank.
Generous; noble; excellent; beautiful; lovely.

examples.text: The tears coursed down her cheeks—not freely, however, for when they came into contact with her heavily beaded eyelashes they assumed an inky colour, and pursued the rest of their way in slow black rivulets.
examples.translation_ko: 눈물이 그녀의 뺨을 타고 흘러내렸다—하지만 자유롭게 흐르지는 못했는데, 구슬이 촘촘히 박힌 속눈썹에 닿자 잉크 색깔을 띠게 되어 느린 검은 물줄기가 되어 나머지 길을 이어갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She was weeping freely.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 펑펑 울고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His temper was certainly no better when he arrived, perspiring freely and thirsty.
examples.translation_ko: 땀을 뻘뻘 흘리며 목이 마른 채로 도착했을 때 그의 기분은 확실히 나아지지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English erande, erende, from Old English ǣrende, from Proto-West Germanic *ārundī (“message, errand”).
definition_en: A task or errand to be done.

senses.gloss: A mission or quest.
senses.example: What will ye, said King Arthur, and what is your errand?

senses.gloss: A mundane mission of no great consequence, concerning household or business affairs (dropping items by, doing paperwork, going to a friend's house, etc.)
senses.example: The errands before he could start the project included getting material at the store and getting the tools he had lent his neighbors.

senses.gloss: The purpose of such a journey.

examples.text: During the journey I thought over my errand with misgiving.
examples.translation_ko: 여행하는 동안 나는 불안한 마음으로 내 임무를 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She never even changed the hour of her errands or sought an alternative route.
examples.translation_ko: 심지어 심부름 가는 시간을 바꾸거나 다른 길을 찾으려 하지도 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From calm + -ly.
definition_en: In a calm manner.

senses.gloss: In a calm manner; coolly.
senses.example: She ran to the door and there beheld the ragged street urchin calmly playing his organ.

examples.text: “Yes,” admitted the child calmly.
examples.translation_ko: "네." 아이가 차분히 인정했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Wha’s matter?” he inquired calmly.
examples.translation_ko: "무슨 일이야?" 그가 차분하게 물었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Now that I was free from the spectacle of Mrs. Strickland’s distress I could consider the matter more calmly.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 스트릭랜드 부인의 고통스러운 모습에서 벗어나자 나는 그 문제를 더 냉정하게 생각할 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English trippen (“tread or step lightly and nimbly, skip, dance”), perhaps from Old French triper (“to hop or dance around, strike with...
definition_en: A journey or excursion.

senses.gloss: A journey; an excursion or jaunt.
senses.example: We made a trip to the beach.

senses.gloss: A stumble or misstep.
senses.example: He was injured due to a trip down the stairs.

senses.gloss: An error; a failure; a mistake.
senses.example: Each seeming trip, and each digressive start.

examples.text: Next day at five o’clock she married Tom Buchanan without so much as a shiver, and started off on a three months’ trip to the South Seas.
examples.translation_ko: 다음 날 다섯 시에 그녀는 조금의 떨림도 없이 톰 뷰캐넌과 결혼했고, 남태평양으로 석 달간의 신혼여행을 떠났다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He came back from France when Tom and Daisy were still on their wedding trip, and made a miserable but irresistible journey to Louisville on the last of his army pay.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 톰과 데이지가 아직 신혼여행 중일 때 프랑스에서 돌아와, 마지막 남은 군인 월급으로 루이빌까지 비참하지만 거부할 수 없는 여행을 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But there was something of an adventure in my trip, and my spirits rose as I approached Paris.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 내 여행에는 모험의 기운이 있었고, 파리에 가까워질수록 내 기분은 들뜨기 시작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He worked his passage on a sailing vessel that was making the trip from Auckland to San Francisco, and he arrived with a box of paints, an easel, and a dozen canvases.
examples.translation_ko: 오클랜드에서 샌프란시스코로 가는 범선에서 일하며 배삯을 벌었고, 물감 상자와 이젤, 캔버스 열두 장을 가지고 도착했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Ancient Greek δραματικός (dramatikós), from δρᾶμα (drâma, “drama, play”), from δράω (dráō, “I do, accomplish”). By surface analysis, drama + -...
definition_en: Characterized by or full of drama.

senses.gloss: Of or relating to the drama.
senses.example: Monteverde found the conditions of dramatic music more favourable to his experiments than those of choral music, in which both voices and ears are at their highest sensibility to discord.

senses.gloss: Striking in appearance or effect.
senses.example: Poland has made some dramatic gains in education in the past decade.

senses.gloss: Having a powerful, expressive singing voice.

examples.text: This was a permanent move, said Daisy over the telephone, but I didn’t believe it—I had no sight into Daisy’s heart, but I felt that Tom would drift on forever seeking, a little wistfully, for the dramatic turbulence of some irrecoverable football game.
examples.translation_ko: 이번에는 영구적인 이주라고 데이지가 전화로 말했지만, 나는 믿지 않았다—데이지의 마음속을 들여다볼 수는 없었지만, 톰은 영원히 떠돌아다닐 것 같았다, 되찾을 수 없는 어떤 미식축구 경기의 극적인 격동을 조금은 그리워하며 찾아서.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had a deep, resonant voice, fitted to his massive frame, and a keen sense of the dramatic.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 거대한 체구에 어울리는 깊고 울림 있는 목소리와 예리한 극적 감각을 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She must be a woman of complicated character, and there was something dramatic in the contrast of that with her demure appearance.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 분명 복잡한 성격의 소유자였고, 그런 면과 그녀의 얌전한 외모 사이의 대조에는 뭔가 극적인 것이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English delicacie, from Middle English delicat, from Latin delicatus.
definition_en: A subtle and refined quality or characteristic.

senses.gloss: The quality of being delicate.
Something appealing, usually a pleasing food, especially a choice dish of a certain culture suggesting rarity and refinement.
senses.example: a Chinese delicacy

senses.gloss: Fineness or elegance of construction or appearance.

examples.text: A succulent hash arrived, and Mr. Wolfshiem, forgetting the more sentimental atmosphere of the old Metropole, began to eat with ferocious delicacy.
examples.translation_ko: 맛있는 해시가 나왔고, 울프샤임 씨는 옛 메트로폴의 감상적인 분위기는 잊은 채 사나우면서도 우아하게 먹기 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I made up my mind to see Strickland the following evening, for I felt instinctively that the hour must be chosen with delicacy.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 다음 날 저녁에 스트릭랜드를 만나기로 마음먹었다. 그 시간은 세심하게 선택해야 한다고 본능적으로 느꼈기 때문이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a sweet and generous nature, and yet was always blundering; a real feeling for what was beautiful and the capacity to create only what was commonplace; a peculiar delicacy of sentiment and gross manners.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 다정하고 관대한 성품을 지녔으면서도 늘 실수를 저질렀고, 아름다운 것에 대한 진정한 감각을 가졌으면서도 평범한 것만 창조할 수 있는 능력밖에 없었으며, 독특하게 섬세한 감성과 조야한 매너를 함께 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French enquerre, from en- + querre (“to search, to look for”), from Latin quaerere, of uncertain origin, but possibly from Proto-Italic *k...
definition_en: To ask for information or details about something.

senses.gloss: British English form of inquire.
senses.example: He enquired about the availability of rental bicycles in the town.

examples.text: I enquired.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 물었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I enquired at my hotel for that in which Charles Strickland was living.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 호텔에서 찰스 스트릭랜드가 머물고 있는 곳을 물어보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English ningkiling, nyngkiling (“hint, slight indication; mention, whisper”), and then either:
* possibly a variant of nikking, nyckyng...
definition_en: A slight or vague idea of something.

senses.gloss: Usually preceded by forms of to give: a slight hint, implication, or suggestion given., A vague idea about something.
senses.example: A passage from one of her [Rosa Luxemberg's] letters written from prison to a young friend, Dr. Hans Diefenbacker, in the spring of 1917 will suffice to give an inkling of this passion: [...]

senses.gloss: Often preceded by forms of to get or to have: an imprecise idea or slight knowledge of something; a suspicion.
senses.example: Of the thing that sustains him through trials man has no inkling, much less knowledge, at the time.

senses.gloss: A desire, an inclination.

examples.text: I asked myself if Mrs. Strickland had any inkling of the facts.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 스트릭랜드 부인이 사실을 조금이라도 눈치채고 있는지 자문해보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Damn it all,” I said, more violently because I had an inkling my motive was none too creditable, “I don’t want to know you.”
examples.translation_ko: "젠장," 내 동기가 그리 떳떳하지 못하다는 것을 어렴풋이 알았기에 더욱 격렬하게 말했다. "당신을 알고 싶지 않습니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fame, from Old French fame (“celebrity, renown”), itself borrowed from Latin fāma (“talk, rumor, report, reputation”), from Pro...
definition_en: Gain widespread recognition or reputation.

senses.gloss: Something said or reported; gossip, rumour.
senses.example: There went a fame in Heav'n that he ere long / Intended to create, and therein plant / A generation, whom his choice regard / Should favour […].

senses.gloss: One's reputation.
The state of being famous or well-known and spoken of, especially for something positive.
senses.example: I find thou art no less than fame hath bruited.

examples.text: “Who makes fame?
examples.translation_ko: "명성을 만드는 게 누구인가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Don’t you want fame?
examples.translation_ko: "명성을 원하지 않습니까?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French modeste, from Latin modestus.
definition_en: Showing humility and modesty.

senses.gloss: Not bragging or boasting about oneself or one's achievements; unpretentious, humble.
Small, moderate in size.
senses.example: He earns a modest amount of money.

senses.gloss: Pure and delicate from a sense of propriety.
senses.example: modest thoughts or language

examples.text: I looked in often on the Stroeves, and sometimes shared their modest fare.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브 부부를 자주 찾아갔고, 때로는 그들의 소박한 식사를 함께했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: My own hotel was modest enough, but it was magnificent in comparison with this.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 묵고 있는 호텔도 소박한 편이었지만, 이곳과 비교하면 호화로웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From be- + draggle.
definition_en: To wet or soil with mud or mire.

senses.gloss: To make (something) wet and limp, especially by dragging it along the ground.

examples.text: He looked suddenly bedraggled.
examples.translation_ko: 갑자기 초라해 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was dressed in a bedraggled suit of khaki, and his hands would have been all the better for a wash.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 너덜너덜한 카키색 양복을 입고 있었고, 손은 씻었다면 훨씬 나았을 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Great beauty or magnificence.

senses.gloss: British, Canadian, Ireland, South Africa, Australian, and New Zealand standard spelling of splendor.

examples.text: He came alive to me, delivered suddenly from the womb of his purposeless splendour.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내게 생생하게 다가왔다, 목적 없는 화려함의 자궁에서 갑자기 태어난 듯이.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had reached an age where death no longer has the quality of ghastly surprise, and when he looked around him now for the first time and saw the height and splendour of the hall and the great rooms opening out from it into other rooms, his grief began to be mixed with an awed pride.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 죽음이 더 이상 끔찍한 놀라움의 성질을 갖지 않는 나이에 이르렀고, 이제 처음으로 주위를 둘러보며 현관의 높이와 화려함, 그리고 거기서 다른 방들로 이어지는 큰 방들을 보았을 때, 그의 슬픔은 경외하는 자부심과 뒤섞이기 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was not here that Charles Strickland lived in guilty splendour with the unknown charmer for whose sake he had abandoned honour and duty.
examples.translation_ko: 찰스 스트릭랜드가 명예와 의무를 버리고까지 택한 정체불명의 요부와 함께 죄스러운 호사를 누리며 살고 있는 곳은 바로 여기가 아니었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Murea, the sister isle, comes into view in rocky splendour, rising from the desert sea mysteriously, like the unsubstantial fabric of a magic wand.
examples.translation_ko: 자매 섬인 무레아가 바위투성이의 장관을 이루며 시야에 들어온다. 신비롭게 사막 같은 바다에서 솟아오르는 모습이 마치 마법 지팡이가 만들어낸 실체 없는 직물 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English vexen, from Old French vexer, from Latin vexāre (“disturb, agitate, annoy”). Doublet of quake. Displaced native Old English dre...
definition_en: Cause annoyance or worry.

senses.gloss: To annoy, irritate.
senses.example: Billy's professor was vexed by his continued failure to improve his grades.

senses.gloss: To cause (mental) suffering to; to distress.
senses.example:
I vex my heart with fancies dim:
⁠He still outstript me in the race;
⁠It was but unity of place
That made me dream I rank’d with him.

senses.gloss: To trouble aggressively, to harass.
senses.example: In that tyme Herode the kynge layed hondes on certayne of the congregaciõ, to vexe them.

examples.text: I was slightly vexed.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 약간 짜증이 났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Sweetheart, have I vexed you?
examples.translation_ko: "여보, 내가 당신을 화나게 했나요?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English narow, narowe, narewe, narwe, naru, from Old English nearu (“narrow, strait, confined, constricted, not spacious, limited, pett...
definition_en: Not wide or broad.

senses.gloss: Having a small width; not wide; having opposite edges or sides that are close, especially by comparison to length or depth.
senses.example: a narrow hallway

senses.gloss: Of little extent; very limited; circumscribed.
senses.example: The Jews were but a small nation, and confined to a narrow compass in the world.

senses.gloss: Restrictive; without flexibility or latitude.
senses.example: a narrow interpretation

examples.text: I walked up narrow stairs, and on the landing found a sort of box, glassed in, within which were a desk and a couple of chairs.
examples.translation_ko: 좁은 계단을 올라가니 층계참에 유리로 둘러싸인 일종의 박스 같은 공간이 있었는데, 그 안에는 책상과 의자 두 개가 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The Rue Bouterie is a narrow street of one-storeyed houses, each house consisting of but one room; they are like the booths in a crowded fair or the cages of animals in a circus.
examples.translation_ko: 부테리 거리는 단층집들이 늘어선 좁은 길인데, 각 집은 방 하나로만 이루어져 있었다. 마치 붐비는 장터의 노점이나 서커스의 동물 우리 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First appears c. 1646 in a publication by Thomas Browne, from New Latin ēlectricus (“electrical; of amber”), from ēlectrum (“amber”) + -icus (“adje...
definition_en: Relating to electricity.

senses.gloss: Of, relating to, produced by, operated with, or utilising electricity; electrical.
senses.example: While Britain continues to argue about how to deliver affordable electrification and decarbonisation, Swiss railways have been 100% electric since the 1960s.

senses.gloss: Of or relating to an electronic version of a musical instrument that has an acoustic equivalent.
Being emotionally thrilling; electrifying.
senses.example: And bold / Electric Pindar, quick as fear, / With race-dust on his cheeks, and clear / Slant startled eyes that seemed to hear // The chariot rounding the last goal, / to hurtle past it in his soul.

examples.text: All the lights were going on in West Egg now; the electric trains, men-carrying, were plunging home through the rain from New York.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 웨스트에그의 모든 불빛이 켜지고 있었다. 사람들을 실어 나르는 전기 기차들이 뉴욕에서 비를 뚫고 집으로 돌진하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We pushed aside curtains that were like pavilions, and felt over innumerable feet of dark wall for electric light switches—once I tumbled with a sort of splash upon the keys of a ghostly piano.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 천막 같은 커튼들을 밀어젖히고, 전등 스위치를 찾아 어둠 속 벽면을 끝없이 더듬었다—한 번은 유령 같은 피아노 건반 위에 철퍼덕 소리를 내며 넘어지기도 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was no one about, but under an electric bell was written Garcon.
examples.translation_ko: 주변에는 아무도 없었지만, 전기 벨 아래에는 '보이'라고 적혀 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From suspicious + -ly.
definition_en: Having or showing a reason to suspect something.

senses.gloss: In a way suggesting suspicion.
senses.example: The police officer looked at her suspiciously.

senses.gloss: In a way that arouses suspicion.
senses.example: She was behaving very suspiciously.

senses.gloss: Causing suspicion.
senses.example: Suspiciously, he had taken out an insurance policy on his wife just months earlier.

examples.text: Some dim impulse moved the policeman to look suspiciously at Tom.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 막연한 직감이 경찰관으로 하여금 톰을 의심스럽게 바라보게 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Wondering if he were sick I went over to find out—an unfamiliar butler with a villainous face squinted at me suspiciously from the door.
examples.translation_ko: 혹시 아픈 것은 아닌지 궁금해서 알아보러 갔는데—악인 같은 얼굴을 한 낯선 집사가 문에서 나를 의심스럽게 째려보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The waiter looked at me suspiciously as I made my way upstairs.
examples.translation_ko: 웨이터는 내가 위층으로 올라가는 것을 의심스러운 눈으로 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “What is it that thou art saying to the doctor?” asked Ata suspiciously.
examples.translation_ko: "박사에게 무슨 말을 하고 있는 거야?" 아타가 의심스럽게 물었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English dressing, dressinge, dressynge, equivalent to dress + -ing.
definition_en: A mixture of ingredients used to add flavor or texture to food.

senses.gloss: Material applied to a wound for protection or therapy.
senses.example: She removed Stranleigh’s coat with a dexterity that aroused his imagination. The elder woman returned with dressings and a sponge, which she placed on a chair.

senses.gloss: A sauce, especially a cold one for salads.
senses.example: I was even more excited to tailor it with a choice of dressings — blue cheese, ranch, French, Russian, Italian, creamy Italian.

senses.gloss: Something added to the soil as a fertilizer etc.

examples.text: Sometimes a shadow moved against a dressing-room blind above, gave way to another shadow, an indefinite procession of shadows, who rouged and powdered in an invisible glass.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 위층 탈의실 블라인드 너머로 그림자가 움직이다가 다른 그림자에게 자리를 내주었고, 보이지 않는 거울 앞에서 연지와 분을 바르는 모호한 그림자들의 행렬이 이어졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Recovering himself in a minute he opened for us two hulking patent cabinets which held his massed suits and dressing-gowns and ties, and his shirts, piled like bricks in stacks a dozen high.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 후 정신을 차린 그는 우리를 위해 거대한 특허 캐비닛 두 개를 열어 보였는데, 그 안에는 그의 수많은 정장과 가운과 넥타이들이, 그리고 벽돌처럼 쌓인 셔츠들이 열두 개씩 높이 포개져 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Three flights up a Woman in a dressing-gown, with touzled hair, opened a door and looked at me silently as I passed.
examples.translation_ko: 3층을 올라가니 헝클어진 머리에 가운을 입은 여자가 문을 열고 내가 지나가는 것을 말없이 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English shaven, schaven, from Old English sċafan (“to shave, scrape, shred, polish”), from Proto-West Germanic *skaban, from ...
definition_en: To remove hair from the skin.

senses.gloss: To make (the head, skin etc.) bald or (the hair) shorter by using a tool such as a razor or electric clippers to cut the hair close to the skin.
To cut anything in this fashion.
senses.example: The Lab'rer vvith the bending Scythe is ſeen / Shaving the Surface of the vvaving Green; […]

senses.gloss: To remove hair from one's face by this means.
senses.example: I had little time to shave this morning.

examples.text: Once more it was pouring, and my irregular lawn, well-shaved by Gatsby’s gardener, abounded in small muddy swamps and prehistoric marshes.
examples.translation_ko: 다시 비가 쏟아지고 있었고, 개츠비의 정원사가 깔끔하게 깎아놓은 내 울퉁불퉁한 잔디밭은 작은 진흙 웅덩이들과 원시시대 늪지들로 가득했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had just shaved, for there was a white spot of lather on his cheekbone, and he was most respectful in his greeting to everyone in the room.
examples.translation_ko: 방금 면도를 했는지 광대뼈에 하얀 비누거품이 한 점 묻어 있었고, 방 안의 모든 사람에게 극도로 정중하게 인사를 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had not shaved for a couple of days.
examples.translation_ko: 이틀 정도 면도를 하지 않은 상태였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He wore an old Norfolk jacket, and he had not shaved for several days.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 낡은 노퍽 재킷을 입고 있었고, 며칠째 면도를 하지 않은 상태였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + tidy.
definition_en: Not neat or organized.

senses.gloss: Sloppy.
senses.example: I have never seen such an untidy bedroom!

senses.gloss: Disorganized.
senses.example: His finances were in an untidy state when he died.

examples.text: He looked at me for a minute or two, pulling his untidy beard.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 헝클어진 수염을 잡아당기며 한두 분간 나를 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When last I saw him he was spruce enough, but he looked ill at ease: now, untidy and ill-kempt, he looked perfectly at home.
examples.translation_ko: 마지막으로 그를 봤을 때는 말끔한 차림이었지만 어색해 보였는데, 지금은 단정하지 못하고 지저분한 모습이지만 오히려 완전히 편안해 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From bowl + -er.
definition_en: A person who bowls, typically with a ball.

senses.gloss: One who engages in the sport of bowling.
The player currently bowling.
A player selected mainly for their bowling ability.

examples.text: He put on a bowler hat much in need of brushing.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 솔질이 절실히 필요한 중절모를 썼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was dressed in the deepest mourning, and on his bowler was a broad black band.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 깊은 상복을 입고 있었고, 중절모에는 넓은 검은 띠를 둘렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French précéder, from Latin praecēdō, from prae- + cēdō.
definition_en: Come before something in time or order.

senses.gloss: To go before, go in front of.
senses.example: Cultural genocide precedes physical genocide.

senses.gloss: To cause to be preceded; to preface; to introduce.
senses.example: It has been usual to precede hostilities by a public declaration communicated to the enemy.

senses.gloss: To have higher rank than (someone or something else).

examples.text: With a reluctant backward glance the well-disciplined child held to her nurse’s hand and was pulled out the door, just as Tom came back, preceding four gin rickeys that clicked full of ice.

examples.translation_ko: 나는 파리에 수백 번 가봤지만, 파리는 언제나 나에게 흥분의 전율을 안겨준다. 나는 모험의 문턱에 서 있다는 느낌 없이는 파리의 거리를 걸을 수가 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English translaten (“to transport, translate, transform”), from Anglo-Norman translater, from Latin trānslātus, perfect passive partici...
definition_en: To change the form or meaning of something.

senses.gloss: To change spoken words or written text (of a book, document, movie, etc.) from one language to another.
senses.example: Hans translated my novel into Welsh.

senses.gloss: To provide a translation of spoken words or written text in another language; to be, or be capable of being, rendered in another language.
senses.example: Hans translated for us while we were in Marrakesh.

senses.gloss: To express spoken words or written text in a different (often clearer or simpler) way in the same language; to paraphrase, to rephrase, to restate.

examples.text: She made no secret of her desires, and I was bidden to translate.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 자신의 욕망을 숨기지 않았고, 나는 통역을 하라는 부탁을 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When I translated this, Strickland shrugged his shoulders impatiently.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 이를 번역해주자 스트릭랜드는 짜증스럽게 어깨를 으쓱했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English teye (“cord, chain”), from Old English tēag, tēah (“cord, chain”), from Proto-West Germanic *taugu, from Proto-Germanic *taugō,...
definition_en: A cord or strip of fabric worn around the neck.

senses.gloss: A knot; a fastening.
A knot of hair, as at the back of a wig.
A necktie (item of clothing consisting of a strip of cloth tied around the neck). See also bow tie, black tie.

examples.text: I cannot come down now as I am tied up in some very important business and cannot get mixed up in this thing now.
examples.translation_ko: 지금은 매우 중요한 일에 얽매여 있어서 내려갈 수 없고 지금 이 일에 연루될 수도 없습니다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: An hour later the front door opened nervously, and Gatsby in a white flannel suit, silver shirt, and gold-coloured tie, hurried in.
examples.translation_ko: 한 시간 후 현관문이 조심스럽게 열리더니, 흰 플란넬 정장에 은색 셔츠, 금색 넥타이를 맨 개츠비가 서둘러 들어왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: If, seized by an intolerable boredom, he had determined to be a painter merely to break with irksome ties, it would have been comprehensible, and commonplace; but commonplace is precisely what I felt he was not.
examples.translation_ko: 만약 참을 수 없는 권태감에 사로잡혀 성가신 속박에서 벗어나려는 목적만으로 화가가 되기로 결심했다면, 그것은 이해할 만하고 평범한 일이었을 것이다. 하지만 평범함이야말로 그에게는 전혀 어울리지 않는다고 내가 느끼는 바였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sheltron, sheldtrume (“roof or wall formed by locked shields”), from Old English sċildtruma, sċyldtruma (“a phalanx, company (o...
definition_en: Provide temporary protection from the elements.

senses.gloss: A place where a person or animal may find protection from the elements (especially rain, storms, or cold) sometimes as a place to sleep (such as a cave).
senses.example: The band of explorers found a shelter behind the waterfall, which they rested at for three days.

senses.gloss: A bare-bones above-ground structure meant to provide temporary cover from the elements; usually small and with no door to close.
senses.example: bus shelter

senses.gloss: A place for protection from deadly conditions outside, including military assault; usually partly or fully underground.
senses.example: tornado shelter

examples.text: This was the master of a sailors’ boarding-house, a huge mulatto with a heavy fist, who gave the stranded mariner food and shelter till he found him a berth.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 선원 하숙집 주인으로, 거대한 혼혈인이었는데 주먹이 무거웠고, 좌초된 선원들에게 일자리를 찾아줄 때까지 음식과 잠자리를 제공해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The cuckoo lays its egg in the strange bird’s nest, and when the young one is hatched it shoulders its foster-brothers out and breaks at last the nest that has sheltered it.
examples.translation_ko: 뻐꾸기는 다른 새의 둥지에 알을 낳고, 새끼가 부화하면 양부모의 새끼들을 밀어내고 마침내 자신을 보살펴준 둥지를 부숴버린다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English ruyne, ruine, from Old French ruine, from Latin ruīna (“overthrow, ruin”), from ruō (“I fall down, tumble, sink in ruin, rush”).
definition_en: A destroyed or abandoned building.

senses.gloss: The remains of a destroyed or dilapidated construction, such as a house or castle.
senses.example: Not only is Jerusalem not a ruin, but she is at the height of her glory compared to all of Jewish history!

senses.gloss: The state of being a ruin, destroyed or decayed.
senses.example: The monastery has fallen into ruin.

senses.gloss: Something that leads to serious trouble or destruction.
senses.example: Gambling has been the ruin of many.

examples.text: On a chance we tried an important-looking door, and walked into a high Gothic library, panelled with carved English oak, and probably transported complete from some ruin overseas.
examples.translation_ko: 우연히 중요해 보이는 문을 열어보았더니, 조각된 영국산 참나무로 벽을 두른 높은 고딕 양식의 서재로 들어서게 되었는데, 아마도 해외의 어떤 폐허에서 통째로 옮겨온 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I suppose it escaped your memory that you’d ruined his life?”
examples.translation_ko: "당신이 그의 인생을 망쳐놓았다는 사실을 잊어버린 모양이군요?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: And I think that was the vision that had remained with him always, dazzling his eyes so that he could not see the truth; and notwithstanding the brutality of fact, he continued to see with the eyes of the spirit an Italy of romantic brigands and picturesque ruins.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 내 생각에 그 환상이 언제나 그와 함께 남아 있어서 그의 눈을 현혹시켜 진실을 보지 못하게 했던 것 같다. 현실의 잔혹함에도 불구하고 그는 계속해서 영혼의 눈으로 낭만적인 도적들과 그림 같은 폐허가 있는 이탈리아를 보고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pouerful, powarfull. By surface analysis, power + -ful.
definition_en: Having or showing great physical or mental strength.

senses.gloss: Having, or capable of exerting, power or influence.
senses.example: Earth is surrounded by a magnetosphere — an invisible bubble of magnetism generated by the powerful churning of molten metals at Earth’s core.

senses.gloss: Leading to many or important deductions.
senses.example: a powerful set of postulates

senses.gloss: Large; capacious; said of veins of ore.

examples.text: Then he made a harsh sound in his throat, and with a violent thrusting movement of his powerful arms pushed his way through.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 목구멍에서 거친 소리를 내더니, 강인한 팔로 격렬하게 밀어젖히며 사람들 사이를 헤치고 들어갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her husband, among various physical accomplishments, had been one of the most powerful ends that ever played football at New Haven—a national figure in a way, one of those men who reach such an acute limited excellence at twenty-one that everything afterward savours of anticlimax.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 남편은 여러 신체적 재능 중에서도 뉴헤이븐에서 미식축구를 했던 가장 강력한 엔드 중 한 명이었다—어떤 면에서는 전국적인 인물이었고, 스물한 살에 그토록 예리하고 제한적인 탁월함에 도달해서 그 이후의 모든 것이 김빠진 뒷맛을 남기는 그런 부류의 남자였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “He was a powerful fellow, Tough Bill, but he didn’t quite like the look of Charlie, so he began cursing him.
examples.translation_ko: "터프 빌은 힘센 놈이었지만 찰리의 모습이 영 마음에 들지 않았나 봐, 그래서 욕을 하기 시작했어."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But how strange it was that the creative instinct should seize upon this dull stockbroker, to his own ruin, perhaps, and to the misfortune of such as were dependent on him; and yet no stranger than the way in which the spirit of God has seized men, powerful and rich, pursuing them with stubborn vigilance till at last, conquered, they have abandoned the joy of the world and the love of women for the painful austerities of the cloister.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 창조적 본능이 이 따분한 주식중개인을 사로잡아, 아마도 그 자신을 파멸로 이끌고 그에게 의존하는 사람들을 불행하게 만든다는 것이 얼마나 기이한 일인가. 그러나 하나님의 영이 권력 있고 부유한 사람들을 사로잡아 완강한 경계심으로 그들을 추적하다가 마침내 그들을 굴복시켜 세상의 기쁨과 여인의 사랑을 버리고 수도원의 고통스러운 금욕생활로 향하게 하는 방식보다 더 기이하지는 않다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin obsessus, perfect passive participle of obsideō (“sit on or in, remain, besiege”), from ob (“before”) + sedeō (“I sit”); see sit, sessio...
definition_en: To think about something constantly and often in a way that is not healthy.

senses.gloss: To be preoccupied with a single topic or emotion.
senses.example: Some people are obsessed with sports.

senses.gloss: To dominate the thoughts of someone.
senses.example: Thoughts of her obsess my every waking moment.

senses.gloss: To think or talk obsessively about.
senses.example: Stop obsessing over it, will you!

examples.text: “Do you know how men can be so obsessed by love that they are deaf and blind to everything else in the world?
examples.translation_ko: "사랑에 사로잡힌 남자들이 세상의 다른 모든 것에 귀머거리가 되고 눈멀어버리는 경우를 아시나요?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But to my practical mind it remained to be seen whether the passion which obsessed him would be justified of its works.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 실용적인 내 마음으로는 그를 사로잡은 열정이 그 결과물로 정당화될 수 있을지 지켜봐야 한다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From hurried + -ly.
definition_en: Done quickly and with a sense of urgency.

senses.gloss: In a hurried manner.
senses.example: But Johnson [...] hurriedly [c]hanged his plea to guilty.

examples.text: “Oh, sure,” agreed Wilson hurriedly, and went toward the little office, mingling immediately with the cement colour of the walls.
examples.translation_ko: "아, 물론이죠." 윌슨이 서둘러 대답하며 작은 사무실 쪽으로 향했는데, 즉시 벽의 시멘트 색깔과 하나가 되어버렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She would not answer; she walked hurriedly, with averted face.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 대답하지 않았다. 얼굴을 돌린 채 서둘러 걸어갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Hurriedly he took the key out of his pocket, opened, and walked in.
examples.translation_ko: 서둘러 주머니에서 열쇠를 꺼내 문을 열고 안으로 들어갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French exposer (“to lay open, set forth”), from Latin expōnō (“set forth”), with contamination from poser (“to lay, place”). D...
definition_en: Reveal or make known a secret.

senses.gloss: To reveal, uncover, make visible, bring to light, introduce (to).
To subject photographic film to light thereby recording an image.
To abandon, especially an unwanted baby in the wilderness.
senses.example: This they do, as a rule, by exposing the child or throwing it into the sea.

examples.text: His pretentiousness will only expose his vacuity.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 허세는 오직 그의 공허함만을 드러낼 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There was here, maybe, the opportunity for a modern version of the hero who for the good of mankind exposes himself to the agonies of the damned.
examples.translation_ko: 여기에는 인류의 선을 위해 자신을 저주받은 자들의 고통에 내맡기는 영웅의 현대적 판본을 위한 기회가 있었을지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English outrage, from Old French outrage, oultrage (“excess”), from Vulgar Latin *ultrāticum ("a going beyond"), derived from Latin ult...
definition_en: A strong feeling of anger or shock at something that is considered wrong or unfair.

senses.gloss: An excessively violent or vicious attack; an atrocity.
An offensive, immoral or indecent act.
The resentful, indignant, or shocked anger aroused by such acts.

examples.text: It was impossible to make him understand that one might be outraged by his callous selfishness.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 냉혹한 이기심에 분개할 수도 있다는 것을 그에게 이해시키는 것은 불가능했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The character of a scoundrel, logical and complete, has a fascination for his creator which is an outrage to law and order.
examples.translation_ko: 논리적이고 완전한 악한의 성격은 창조자에게 법과 질서에 대한 모독이라 할 만한 매혹을 안겨준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: 1398, “making,” from Old French, from Latin efficientem, nominative efficiēns, participle of efficere (“work out, accomplish”) (see effect). Meanin...
definition_en: Having the ability to produce desired results with minimal waste of time, money, or effort.

senses.gloss: Making good, thorough, or careful use of resources; not consuming extra. Especially, making good use of time or energy.
senses.example: An efficient process would automate all the routine work.

senses.gloss: Expressing the proportion of consumed energy that was successfully used in a process; the ratio of useful output to total input.
senses.example: The motor is only 20% efficient at that temperature.

senses.gloss: Causing effects, producing results; bringing into being; initiating change (rare except in philosophical and legal expression efficient cause = causative factor or agent).
senses.example: Ownership, maintenance, or use of the automobile need not be the direct and efficient cause of the injury sustained

examples.text: I am certain that he was an efficient one.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 유능한 경찰관이었으리라고 나는 확신한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She was so efficient that it was certain she would make a success of the adventure.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 너무나 유능해서 이 모험을 성공시킬 것이 확실했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French superiour, from Latin superior (“higher, upper”).
definition_en: Having greater prestige or importance.

senses.gloss: Of high standard or quality.
Greater in size or power.
Beyond the power or influence of; too great or firm to be subdued or affected by.
senses.example: There is not in earth a spectacle more worthy […]than a brave man superior to his sufferings.

examples.text: His eyes narrowed and his mouth widened slightly with the ghost of a superior “Hm!”
examples.translation_ko: 그의 눈이 가늘어지고 입가에 우월감이 서린 "흠!" 하는 표정의 흔적과 함께 입술이 살짝 벌어졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was dancing now on the canvas in the garden; old men pushing young girls backward in eternal graceless circles, superior couples holding each other tortuously, fashionably, and keeping in the corners—and a great number of single girls dancing individually or relieving the orchestra for a moment of the burden of the banjo or the traps.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 정원의 캔버스 위에서는 춤이 한창이었다. 늙은 남자들이 젊은 여자들을 영원히 우아하지 못한 원을 그리며 뒤로 밀어내고, 잘난 체하는 커플들이 서로를 비틀어 안고 멋을 부리며 구석에 머물러 있고, 수많은 독신 여자들이 혼자 춤을 추거나 잠시 오케스트라의 밴조나 드럼 연주를 대신하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Strickland was just the man to rise superior to circumstances, when they were such as to occasion despondency in most; but whether this was due to equanimity of soul or to contradictoriness it would be difficult to say.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 대부분의 사람들이 절망에 빠질 만한 상황에서도 그것을 초월해 일어서는 그런 사람이었다. 하지만 이것이 마음의 평정 때문인지 아니면 반골 기질 때문인지는 판단하기 어려웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Mrs. Strickland’s sister was older than she, not unlike her, but more faded; and she had the efficient air, as though she carried the British Empire in her pocket, which the wives of senior officers acquire from the consciousness of belonging to a superior caste.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인의 언니는 그녀보다 나이가 많았고, 그녀와 닮았지만 더 초췌해 보였다. 그리고 마치 대영제국을 주머니에 넣고 다니는 듯한 유능한 분위기를 풍겼는데, 이는 고위 장교의 부인들이 우월한 계급에 속한다는 의식에서 우러나오는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English kene (“bold, brave, sharp”), from Old English cēne (“keen, fierce, bold, brave, warlike, powerful; learned, clever, wise”), fro...
definition_en: Having or showing a strong and enthusiastic interest.

senses.gloss: Often with a prepositional phrase, or with to and an infinitive: showing a quick and ardent responsiveness or willingness; eager, enthusiastic, interested.
senses.example: I’m keen on computers.

senses.gloss: Fierce, intense, vehement.
senses.example: This boy has a keen appetite.

senses.gloss: Having a fine edge or point; sharp.
senses.example: Come thick Night, / And pall thee in the dunneſt ſmoake of Hell, / That my keene Knife ſee not the Wound it makes, / Nor Heauen peepe through the Blanket of the darke, / To cry, hold, hold.

examples.text: “Did you never know that he was keen on that sort of thing.”
examples.translation_ko: "그가 그런 일에 열중한다는 걸 전혀 모르셨나요?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a deep, resonant voice, fitted to his massive frame, and a keen sense of the dramatic.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 거대한 체구에 어울리는 깊고 울림 있는 목소리와 예리한 극적 감각을 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Ancient Greek καταστροφή (katastrophḗ), from καταστρέφω (katastréphō, “I overturn”), from κατά (katá, “down, against”) + στρέφω (stréphō, “I t...
definition_en: A sudden and severe event that causes great damage or loss.

senses.gloss: Any large and disastrous event of great significance.
senses.example: The Chernobyl disaster was a catastrophe.

senses.gloss: A disaster beyond expectations.
The dramatic event that initiates the resolution of the plot; the dénouement.
senses.example: Pat : he comes like the Cataſtrophe of the old Comedie : my Cue is villanous Melancholly, with a ſighe like Tom o’ Bedlam.

examples.text: From the moment I telephoned news of the catastrophe to West Egg village, every surmise about him, and every practical question, was referred to me.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 웨스트에그 마을에 그 참사 소식을 전화로 알린 순간부터, 그에 대한 모든 추측과 모든 실질적인 문제가 나에게 맡겨졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I foresee some terrible catastrophe.”
examples.translation_ko: "끔찍한 재앙이 닥칠 것 같아요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His garb of woe suggested that he had lost in one catastrophe every relation he had in the world, even to cousins by marriage twice removed.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 상복 차림새는 마치 한 번의 재앙으로 이 세상의 모든 친척들을, 심지어 두 다리 건너 인척까지도 잃었다는 듯한 인상을 주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Synchronically equivalent to tight + -en. From Middle English tighten, from Old English tyhtan, thus originally unrelated to tight (Old English *þi...
definition_en: To make something tighter or more secure.

senses.gloss: To make tighter.
senses.example: Please tighten that screw a quarter-turn.

senses.gloss: To become tighter.
senses.example: That joint is tightening as the wood dries.

senses.gloss: To make money harder to borrow or obtain.
senses.example: If the government doesn't tighten the money supply, inflation is certain to be harsh.

examples.text: Watching Tom, I saw the wad of muscle back of his shoulder tighten under his coat.
examples.translation_ko: 톰을 지켜보던 나는 그의 어깨 뒤쪽 근육 덩어리가 코트 아래에서 굳어지는 것을 보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was saying some last word to her, but the eagerness in his manner tightened abruptly into formality as several people approached him to say goodbye.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀에게 마지막 말을 건네고 있었지만, 몇몇 사람들이 작별 인사를 하러 다가오자 그의 태도에서 드러나던 간절함이 갑자기 격식을 차린 모습으로 굳어졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Mrs. MacAndrew tightened her lips.
examples.translation_ko: 맥앤드류 부인이 입술을 꽉 다물었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English spot, spotte, partially from Middle Dutch spotte (“spot, speck”), and partially merging with Middle English splot, from Old Eng...
definition_en: A small mark or patch on the skin.

senses.gloss: A round or irregular patch on the surface of a thing having a different color, texture etc. and generally round in shape.
senses.example: The leopard is noted for the spots of color in its fur.

senses.gloss: A stain or disfiguring mark.
senses.example: I have tried everything, and I can’t get this spot out.

senses.gloss: A pimple, papule or pustule.
senses.example: That morning, I saw that a spot had come up on my chin.

examples.text: A spot of colour rose suddenly to Mrs. Strickland’s pale cheeks.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인의 창백한 뺨에 갑자기 붉은 기가 돌았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You’d better stand there,” he said, pointing to a spot from which, presumably, he fancied I could see to best advantage what he had to show me.
examples.translation_ko: "저기 서 있는 게 좋겠소." 그가 말했다. 아마도 그가 보여주려는 것을 내가 가장 잘 볼 수 있으리라고 생각하는 자리를 가리키면서.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From 16th-century criminal slang, perhaps from Middle English bet (“something better, advantage, luck”), from Old English bet, bett (“better”, adve...
definition_en: Place a wager or make a prediction.

senses.gloss: A wager, an agreement between two parties that a stake (usually money) will be paid by the loser to the winner (the winner being the one who correctly forecast the outcome of an event).
senses.example: Dylan owes Fletcher $30 from an unsuccessful bet.

senses.gloss: A candidate (for elections and pageants) or competitor (in multinational sports).
Indicating a degree of certainty, or that something can be relied upon.
senses.example: It’s a safe bet that it will rain tomorrow.

examples.text: I’ll bet he killed a man.”
examples.translation_ko: 분명히 사람을 죽인 적이 있을 거예요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Walter could have you up on the betting laws too, but Wolfshiem scared him into shutting his mouth.”
examples.translation_ko: "월터는 도박법으로도 자네를 고발할 수 있었지만, 울프샤임이 겁을 줘서 입을 다물게 했어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I bet he found it hell to paint.”
examples.translation_ko: "그 자식은 그림 그리는 게 지옥 같았을 거야."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You can bet your boots I’d have routed her out fast enough.”
examples.translation_ko: "내가 갔다면 그 여자를 금세 찾아냈을 텐데."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Clipping of whim-wham.
definition_en: A sudden or unexplained idea or feeling.

senses.gloss: A fanciful impulse, or sudden change of idea.
senses.example: “You’re either with me or you’re against me” became Dany’s credo, and those against her were an ever-changing multitude to be determined solely by her whims.

senses.gloss: A large capstan or vertical drum turned by horse power or steam power, for raising ore or water, etc., from mines, or for other purposes

examples.text: As a matter of fact, he had no such facilities—he had no comfortable family standing behind him, and he was liable at the whim of an impersonal government to be blown anywhere about the world.
examples.translation_ko: 사실 그에게는 그런 능력이 없었다—그를 뒷받침해줄 든든한 가문도 없었고, 비정한 정부의 변덕에 따라 세계 어디든 날려갈 수 있는 처지였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “If it’s just a whim, he’ll get over it.”
examples.translation_ko: "단순한 변덕이라면 곧 정신을 차릴 거예요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But it was the whim I could not understand.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 내가 이해할 수 없었던 것은 그 변덕이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From cool + -ly (adverbial suffix).
definition_en: In a cool manner.

senses.gloss: At a moderately low temperature.
senses.example: The wind blew coolly.

senses.gloss: In a cool, unpanicked or collected manner.
senses.example: Graham secured victory with five minutes left, coolly lifting the ball over Asmir Begovic.

senses.gloss: With calm impudence.
senses.example: They walked in, not even wearing masks, and coolly robbed the bank of twelve thousand pounds.

examples.text: Gatsby hesitated, then added, coolly: “He’s the man who fixed the World’s Series back in 1919.”
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 잠시 망설이더니 차갑게 덧붙였다. "1919년 월드시리즈를 조작한 장본인이야."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But young men didn’t—at least in my provincial inexperience I believed they didn’t—drift coolly out of nowhere and buy a palace on Long Island Sound.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 젊은 남자들이—적어도 내 시골뜨기 경험으로는 그렇지 않다고 믿었는데—아무 데서나 태연히 나타나 롱아일랜드 해협에 궁전을 사지는 않는 법이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Not out of charity,” I answered coolly.
examples.translation_ko: "동정심에서가 아니야." 나는 냉정하게 대답했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Mrs. MacAndrew looked at her sister coolly.
examples.translation_ko: 맥앤드류 부인은 언니를 차갑게 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sexe (“gender”), from Old French sexe (“genitals; gender”), from Latin sexus (“gender; gender traits; males or females; genital...
definition_en: The state or fact of being male or female.

senses.gloss: A category into which sexually-reproducing organisms are divided on the basis of their reproductive roles in their species; the system of such categories, which can differ by organism or by taxonomic branch.
senses.example: The effect of the medication is dependent upon age, sex, and other factors.

senses.gloss: Another category, especially of humans and especially based on sexuality or gender roles.
senses.example: I have encountered officers who believe a woman got a better assignment or somehow "got over" because of her sex.

senses.gloss: The members of such a category, taken collectively.
senses.example: the fairer sex

examples.text: Who am I that I should seek to unravel the mysterious intricacies of sex?
examples.translation_ko: 성의 신비로운 복잡함을 풀어내려 하다니, 내가 누구란 말인가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is possible that Strickland hated the normal release of sex because it seemed to him brutal by comparison with the satisfaction of artistic creation.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드가 성적 욕구의 정상적인 해소를 증오했던 것은, 그것이 예술적 창조의 만족감에 비해 야만적으로 보였기 때문일 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French miserable, from Old French, from Latin miserabilis, equivalent to miser + -able.
definition_en: Feeling or showing great unhappiness.

senses.gloss: In a state of misery: very sad, ill, or poor.
senses.example: The secret of being miserable is to have leisure to bother about whether you are happy or not. The cure for it is occupation, because occupation means pre-occupation

senses.gloss: Very bad (at something); unskilled, incompetent; hopeless.
senses.example: He's good at some sports, like tennis, but he's just miserable at football.

senses.gloss: Of the weather, extremely unpleasant due to being cold, wet, overcast, etc.

examples.text: He followed me wildly into the kitchen, closed the door, and whispered: “Oh, God!” in a miserable way.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 미친 듯이 나를 따라 부엌으로 들어와서 문을 닫고는 비참한 목소리로 속삭였다. "오, 하느님!"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He came back from France when Tom and Daisy were still on their wedding trip, and made a miserable but irresistible journey to Louisville on the last of his army pay.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 톰과 데이지가 아직 신혼여행 중일 때 프랑스에서 돌아와, 마지막 남은 군인 월급으로 루이빌까지 비참하지만 거부할 수 없는 여행을 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I should like him to die miserable, poor, and starving, without a friend.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 비참하게, 가난하게, 굶주리며, 친구 하나 없이 죽었으면 좋겠어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Panting a little in his haste, he told her how miserable he was; he besought her to have mercy on him; he promised, if she would forgive him, to do everything she wanted.
examples.translation_ko: 서두르느라 약간 숨을 헐떡이며, 그는 자신이 얼마나 비참한지 말했다. 그녀에게 자비를 베풀어 달라고 간청했다. 그녀가 용서해 준다면 그녀가 원하는 것은 무엇이든 하겠다고 약속했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Feeling let down or unfulfilled.

senses.gloss: Defeated of expectations or hope; experiencing disappointment; let down.
senses.example: After all his anticipation, the trip left him deeply disappointed.

senses.gloss: Having had a marriage proposal rejected.
Expressing or indicating disappointment.
senses.example: a disappointed tone / face / silence

examples.text: “No?” Mr. Wolfshiem seemed disappointed.
examples.translation_ko: "아닌가요?" 울프샤임 씨가 실망한 듯했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I think I was a little disappointed in her.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그녀에게 조금 실망한 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I am disappointed that I cannot report any extravagances in his opinions on the old masters.
examples.translation_ko: 거장들에 대한 그의 견해에서 별다른 기행을 보고할 수 없다는 것이 실망스럽다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French humiliation, from Late Latin humiliatio, from humiliare (“to humiliate”); see humiliate.
definition_en: The act of humiliating someone or something.

senses.gloss: The act of humiliating or humbling someone; abasement of pride; mortification.
The state of being humiliated, humbled or reduced to lowliness or submission.

examples.text: Daisy went upstairs to wash her face—too late I thought with humiliation of my towels—while Gatsby and I waited on the lawn.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지가 세수를 하러 위층으로 올라갔는데—너무 늦었지만 나는 수건 생각에 굴욕감을 느꼈다—개츠비와 나는 잔디밭에서 기다렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Now, Tough Bill was not the man to put up with humiliation at the hands of a common sailor.
examples.translation_ko: 터프 빌은 평범한 선원에게 굴욕을 당하고 참고 넘어갈 사람이 아니었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He noticed that his wife had remained perfectly still, and to be made ridiculous before her increased his humiliation.
examples.translation_ko: 아내가 꼼짝도 하지 않고 가만히 서 있는 것을 보니, 그녀 앞에서 우스꽝스러운 꼴이 된 것이 굴욕감을 더욱 크게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pure, pur, from Old French pur, from Latin pūrus (“clean, free from dirt or filth, unmixed, plain”), from Proto-Indo-European *...
definition_en: Free from impurities or contamination.

senses.gloss: Free of flaws or imperfections; unsullied.
senses.example: Such was the origin of a friendship as warm and pure as any that ancient or modern history records.

senses.gloss: Free of foreign material or pollutants.
senses.example: "Hetch Hetchy water is the purest, wholly unpolluted, and forever unpollutable."

senses.gloss: Free of immoral behavior or qualities; clean.
senses.example: Laye hondes sodenly on no man nether be part taker of wother mens synnes. Kepe thy silfe pure.

examples.text: His bedroom was the simplest room of all—except where the dresser was garnished with a toilet set of pure dull gold.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 침실은 모든 방 중에서 가장 소박했다. 다만 화장대가 순금으로 된 화장 도구 세트로 장식되어 있는 것만 빼고는.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I can tell you why he left his wife—from pure selfishness and nothing else whatever.”
examples.translation_ko: "그가 왜 아내를 떠났는지 말씀드릴 수 있어요. 순전히 이기심 때문이고 다른 이유는 전혀 없습니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “I’ll tell you what must seem strange, that when it’s over you feel so extraordinarily pure.
examples.translation_ko: "이상하게 보일지도 모르지만, 그 모든 게 끝나고 나면 놀라울 정도로 순수한 기분이 든다는 걸 말해주겠어.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sours, from Old French sorse (“rise, beginning, spring, source”), from sors, past participle of sordre, sourdre, from Latin sur...
definition_en: The origin or point of supply of something.

senses.gloss: The person, place, or thing from which something (information, goods, etc.) comes or is acquired.
senses.example: The accused refused to reveal the source of the illegal drugs she was selling.

senses.gloss: Spring; fountainhead; wellhead; any collection of water on or under the surface of the ground in which a stream originates.
senses.example: The main sources of the Euphrates River are the Karasu and Murat Rivers.

senses.gloss: A reporter's informant.

examples.text: Just why these inventions were a source of satisfaction to James Gatz of North Dakota, isn’t easy to say.
examples.translation_ko: 노스다코타 출신 제임스 개츠에게 이런 지어낸 이야기들이 왜 만족의 원천이었는지는 쉽게 말하기 어렵다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They are not perfect ovals—like the egg in the Columbus story, they are both crushed flat at the contact end—but their physical resemblance must be a source of perpetual wonder to the gulls that fly overhead.
examples.translation_ko: 그것들은 완전한 타원형이 아니었다. 콜럼버스 이야기의 달걀처럼 접촉면 끝이 모두 납작하게 눌려 있었지만, 그 물리적 유사성은 머리 위를 나는 갈매기들에게 영원한 경이의 원천임에 틀림없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: From what I’ve been able to gather from certain sources that I can’t tell you, I know that he didn’t leave England by himself.”
examples.translation_ko: "내가 말할 수 없는 특정한 소식통들로부터 알아낸 바에 따르면, 그가 혼자서 영국을 떠나지 않았다는 것을 알고 있다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French passagier with intrusive n (see etymology of messenger).
definition_en: A person traveling in or on a vehicle.

senses.gloss: One who rides or travels in a vehicle, but who does not operate it and is not a member of the crew.
Somebody in a team who does not do their fair share of the work.
A young hunting bird that can fly and is taken while it is still in its first year.

examples.text: The valley of ashes is bounded on one side by a small foul river, and, when the drawbridge is up to let barges through, the passengers on waiting trains can stare at the dismal scene for as long as half an hour.
examples.translation_ko: 잿빛 골짜기는 한쪽으로 더러운 작은 강에 둘러싸여 있고, 바지선을 통과시키려고 도개교가 올라가면 기다리는 기차의 승객들은 30분이나 되는 동안 그 음울한 광경을 바라볼 수 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We were like tram-cars running on their lines from terminus to terminus, and it was possible to calculate within small limits the number of passengers they would carry.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 종점에서 종점까지 정해진 노선을 달리는 전차 같았고, 얼마나 많은 승객을 태울지도 어느 정도 계산할 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was perhaps ten years later that one morning on board ship, about to land at Alexandria, I was bidden to line up with the other passengers for the doctor’s examination.
examples.translation_ko: 아마 십 년쯤 지난 후였을 것이다. 어느 날 아침 알렉산드리아에 상륙하려던 배 위에서, 나는 다른 승객들과 함께 줄을 서서 의사의 검진을 받으라는 지시를 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English morwe, morwen, from Old English morgen, from Proto-West Germanic *morgan, *morgin, from Proto-Germanic *murganaz, *murginaz; co...
definition_en: The day following the present one.

senses.gloss: The next or following day.
Morning.
senses.example: For quotations using this term, see Citations:morrow.

examples.text: “I’m starting to-morrow.
examples.translation_ko: "내일 떠납니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I’ll come and fetch them to-morrow.”
examples.translation_ko: 내일 가져가러 오겠소."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fourtenyght, fourtene nyght, from Old English fēowertīene niht (literally “fourteen nights"; the Anglo-Saxons counted by nights...
definition_en: A period of 14 days.

senses.gloss: A period of 2 weeks.
senses.example: On being kicked the girl fell desperately in love with Henri, and for a fortnight they lived together and spent a thousand francs of Henri's money.

examples.text: At least once a fortnight a corps of caterers came down with several hundred feet of canvas and enough coloured lights to make a Christmas tree of Gatsby’s enormous garden.
examples.translation_ko: 적어도 보름에 한 번은 출장 요리사들이 수백 피트의 캔버스와 개츠비의 거대한 정원을 크리스마스트리로 만들 만큼 충분한 색색의 전구를 가지고 내려왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Yes, I’ve known it for a fortnight.
examples.translation_ko: "네, 2주 전부터 알고 있었어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In point of fact, I met Strickland before I had been a fortnight in Paris.
examples.translation_ko: 사실 나는 파리에 온 지 보름도 되기 전에 스트릭랜드를 만났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French modelle, from Old Italian modello, from Vulgar Latin *modellus, diminutive form of modulus (“measure, standard”), diminutive of ...
definition_en: A person or thing that is considered to be a good example of something.

senses.gloss: A person who serves as a human template for artwork or fashion.
A person, usually an attractive male or female, who is hired to show items or goods to the public, such as items that are given away as prizes on a TV game show.
A representation of a physical object.
senses.example: The boy played with a model of a World War II fighter plane. The biology teacher passed a large plastic model of the atomic structure of DNA around the classroom.

examples.text: I can get my models here just as well as in Rome.”
examples.translation_ko: 로마에서와 마찬가지로 여기서도 모델을 구할 수 있거든요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: No, he said; he liked to have his models under his hand.
examples.translation_ko: 아니라고 그가 말했다. 모델들을 손 닿는 곳에 두고 있는 게 좋다고 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Origin uncertain. Perhaps from French s'allonger (“to lie down”). Compare French longer (“to walk along”). Compare also German lungern (“to hang or...
definition_en: To relax or sit comfortably.

senses.gloss: To relax; to spend time lazily; to stand, sit, or recline, in an indolent manner.
senses.example: We like to spend our Sundays lounging about at home in our pyjamas.

senses.gloss: To walk or go in a leisurely manner.
senses.example: As she lounged past Leila's car she cast an insolent glance at the Irish girl.

examples.text: Mr. Sloane didn’t enter into the conversation, but lounged back haughtily in his chair; the woman said nothing either—until unexpectedly, after two highballs, she became cordial.
examples.translation_ko: 슬론 씨는 대화에 끼어들지 않고 의자에 거만하게 기대어 앉아 있었고, 그 여자 역시 아무 말이 없었다—하지만 뜻밖에도 하이볼 두 잔을 마신 후 다정해졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was painting a group of Italian peasants, in the costume of the Campagna, lounging on the steps of a Roman church.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 캄파냐 지방의 의상을 입은 이탈리아 농민들이 로마의 한 교회 계단에 늘어져 있는 모습을 그리고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I led a very regular life, working in the morning, and in the afternoon lounging about the gardens of the Luxembourg or sauntering through the streets.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 매우 규칙적인 생활을 했는데, 오전에는 일을 하고 오후에는 룩셈부르크 정원을 어슬렁거리거나 거리를 산책했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French genereux, and its source, Latin generōsus (“of noble birth”), from genus (“race, stock”).
definition_en: Having a willingness to give and share freely.

senses.gloss: A spending or consuming, often a disbursement of funds.
senses.example: She went to great expense to ensure her children would get the best education.

senses.gloss: The elimination or consumption of something, sometimes with the notion of loss or damage to the thing eliminated.

senses.gloss: Loss.

examples.text: He writhed under the jokes, practical and otherwise, which were perpetually made at his expense, and yet never ceased, it seemed wilfully, to expose himself to them.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 끊임없이 자신을 희생양으로 삼아 벌어지는 실제적이든 그렇지 않든 온갖 농담들 때문에 괴로워했지만, 마치 일부러 그러는 것처럼 보일 정도로 자신을 그런 상황에 계속 노출시키는 일을 멈추지 않았다.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From possible + -ly.
definition_en: Used to express a possibility or uncertainty.

senses.gloss: Perhaps; indicates that the proposition may be true (is not certainly false) regardless of any facts or circumstances known to, stated by or implied by the speaker.
senses.example: Possibly, they will make gains in the midterm elections.

senses.gloss: In the realm of possibility; indicates that the action may successfully be performed (is not impossible) regardless of any facts or circumstances known to, stated by or implied by the speaker that might limit the performance.
