examples.translation_ko: 이 친구는 정말 벨라스코군.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: You see, he’s regular tough underneath it all.”
examples.translation_ko: 알고 보면 그 사람도 꽤 강인한 면이 있거든요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I led a very regular life, working in the morning, and in the afternoon lounging about the gardens of the Luxembourg or sauntering through the streets.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 매우 규칙적인 생활을 했는데, 오전에는 일을 하고 오후에는 룩셈부르크 정원을 어슬렁거리거나 거리를 산책했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English idel, ydel, from Old English īdel, from Proto-West Germanic *īdal, from Proto-Germanic *īdalaz. Cognate with Dutch ijdel (“vain...
definition_en: to be inactive or not working

senses.gloss: Empty, vacant.
Not being used appropriately; not occupied; (of time) with no, no important, or not much activity.
senses.example: idle hours

senses.gloss: Not engaged in any occupation or employment; unemployed; inactive; doing nothing in particular.
senses.example: idle workmen

examples.text: “Why are you idling in this disgraceful fashion?”
examples.translation_ko: "왜 이렇게 한심하게 빈둥거리고 있는 거야?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “There are more cafés in Paris than one, at which to trifle away an idle hour.”
examples.translation_ko: "파리에는 한가한 시간을 보낼 수 있는 카페가 한 곳만 있는 것은 아니니까요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fare, from a merger of Old English fær (“journey, road”) and faru (“journey, companions, baggage”), from Proto-Germanic *farą a...
definition_en: The cost or price of something.

senses.gloss: A going; journey; travel; voyage; course; passage.
Money paid for a transport ticket.
senses.example: train fare

senses.gloss: A paying passenger, especially in a taxi.

examples.text: One of the taxi drivers in the village never took a fare past the entrance gate without stopping for a minute and pointing inside; perhaps it was he who drove Daisy and Gatsby over to East Egg the night of the accident, and perhaps he had made a story about it all his own.
examples.translation_ko: 마을의 택시 기사 중 한 명은 정문을 지날 때마다 잠시 멈춰 서서 안쪽을 가리키곤 했다. 아마 사고가 난 그날 밤 데이지와 개츠비를 이스트에그까지 태워다 준 것도 그였을 것이고, 그 일에 대해 자신만의 이야기를 만들어냈을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I looked in often on the Stroeves, and sometimes shared their modest fare.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브 부부를 자주 찾아갔고, 때로는 그들의 소박한 식사를 함께했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: During his sea faring days he had cruised the South Seas, and he determined now to seek his fortune there.
examples.translation_ko: 항해하던 시절 그는 남태평양을 누볐기에, 이제 그곳에서 운을 찾기로 결심했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: In English (recorded only since 1656, but until the 19th century stigmatized as 'Scottish') apparently from narration.
definition_en: To tell or describe a story.

senses.gloss: To relate (a story or series of events) in speech or writing.
senses.example: narrate a story

senses.gloss: To give an account.
senses.example: narrate the meeting

examples.text: When I had narrated his lamentable death I ceased.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 비참한 죽음을 이야기하고 나서 나는 말을 멈췄다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The perfect seriousness with which he narrated his misfortunes convulsed me with laughter, and this added to Mrs. Stroeve’s irritation.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 자신의 불행을 이야기하는 완전히 진지한 태도가 나를 웃음으로 경련시켰고, 이것이 스트루브 부인의 짜증을 더했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French irritation, from Latin irrītātiō, from irrītāre (“to excite”).
definition_en: A feeling of annoyance or displeasure.

senses.gloss: The act of irritating or annoying.
senses.example: What irritation causes you to be so moody?

senses.gloss: The state of being irritated.
A thing or person that annoys.

examples.text: I clenched my hands, seeking to control my irritation.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 주먹을 꽉 쥐고 짜증을 억누르려 애썼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: All his irritation was gone, and he felt—eh bien, oui, je ne le nie pas—he felt an overwhelming pity.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 모든 짜증은 사라졌고, 그는—에 비앙, 위, 즈 느 르 니 파—압도적인 연민을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English flikeren (“to flutter”), from Old English flicerian, flicorian (“to flutter”), from Proto-West Germanic *flikurōn.
Akin to Sate...
definition_en: To shine or burn with an unsteady light.

senses.gloss: An unsteady flash of light.
senses.example: the flicker of the dying candle

senses.gloss: A short moment.
senses.example: a flicker of hope

examples.text: I began to like New York, the racy, adventurous feel of it at night, and the satisfaction that the constant flicker of men and women and machines gives to the restless eye.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 뉴욕을 좋아하기 시작했다. 밤의 생생하고 모험적인 느낌과, 끊임없이 깜박이는 남녀와 기계들이 불안한 눈에 주는 만족감을 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Slenderly, languidly, their hands set lightly on their hips, the two young women preceded us out on to a rosy-coloured porch, open toward the sunset, where four candles flickered on the table in the diminished wind.
examples.translation_ko: 날씬하고 나른하게, 손을 가볍게 허리에 얹은 채 두 젊은 여인이 우리보다 먼저 장밋빛 베란다로 나갔다. 석양을 향해 열린 그곳에서는 바람이 잦아든 가운데 테이블 위의 네 개의 촛불이 흔들리고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A smile flickered in his eyes, and he stirred his absinthe in silence.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 눈에 미소가 스쳤고, 그는 조용히 압생트를 저었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English flen, from Old English flēon, from Proto-Germanic *fleuhaną, from Proto-Indo-European *plewk-, *plew- (“to fly, flow, run”).
Co...
definition_en: Run away quickly

senses.gloss: To run away; to escape.
senses.example: The prisoner tried to flee, but was caught by the guards.

senses.gloss: To escape from.
senses.example: Many people fled the country as war loomed.

senses.gloss: To disappear quickly; to vanish; to fleet.
senses.example: Ethereal products flee once freely exposed to air.

examples.text: They fled in terror.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 공포에 질려 달아났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He walked up, and a little boy, playing unconcernedly in the sunshine, started at his approach and fled quickly away: to him the stranger was the enemy.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 걸어가자 햇빛 속에서 태평하게 놀고 있던 어린 소년이 그의 접근에 깜짝 놀라며 재빨리 달아났다. 그 아이에게 낯선 사람은 적이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English gentil (“courteous, noble”), from Old French gentil (“high-born, noble”), from Latin gentilis (“of the same family or clan”), f...
definition_en: Having or showing a soft and kind nature.

senses.gloss: Tender and amiable; of a considerate or kindly disposition.
senses.example: Stuart is a gentle man; he would never hurt you.

senses.gloss: Soft and mild rather than hard or severe.
senses.example: I felt something touch my shoulder; it was gentle and a little slimy.

senses.gloss: Docile and easily managed.
senses.example: We had a gentle swim in the lake.

examples.text: The Swede is adept at the gentle pastime of fishing in troubled waters.
examples.translation_ko: 스웨덴인은 혼란한 상황에서 이득을 취하는 온화한 오락에 능숙하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Let us be silent, content in our little corner, meek and gentle like them.
examples.translation_ko: 그들처럼 온순하고 부드럽게, 우리의 작은 구석에서 조용히 만족하며 지내자.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Surprised or frightened suddenly.

senses.gloss: Surprised and slightly frightened.

examples.text: For a moment a phrase tried to take shape in my mouth and my lips parted like a dumb man’s, as though there was more struggling upon them than a wisp of startled air.
examples.translation_ko: 한순간 어떤 구절이 내 입에서 형태를 잡으려 했고, 내 입술은 벙어리의 입술처럼 벌어졌다, 마치 놀란 공기의 한 줄기보다 더 많은 것이 그 위에서 몸부림치고 있는 것처럼.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was startled and amazed.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 깜짝 놀라며 어리둥절해했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I smiled, for his appearance, so rotund and yet so startled, could never fail to excite a smile, and then as I came nearer
examples.translation_ko: 나는 미소를 지었다. 그토록 둥글둥글하면서도 놀란 듯한 그의 모습은 언제나 미소를 자아내지 않을 수 없었기 때문이다. 그런데 가까이 다가가면서
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English simplicite, from Old French simplicite, from Latin simplicitās, from simplex (“simple”). See simple. Partially displaced native...
definition_en: The state of being simple and unadorned.

senses.gloss: The quality or state of being unmixed or uncompounded
senses.example: the simplicity of metals or of earths

senses.gloss: The quality or state of being not complex, or of consisting of few parts.
senses.example: the simplicity of a machine

senses.gloss: Lack of sharpness of mind; lack of ability to think using complex ideas; stupidity

examples.text: She saw something awful in the very simplicity she failed to understand.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 자신이 이해하지 못하는 바로 그 단순함 속에서 끔찍한 무언가를 보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Sometimes they came and went without having met Gatsby at all, came for the party with a simplicity of heart that was its own ticket of admission.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 개츠비를 전혀 만나지도 못한 채 왔다 갔다 하기도 했는데, 그 자체가 입장권이 되는 순수한 마음으로 파티에 왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He and his wife made a picture which the imagination gratefully dwelt upon, and the simplicity of his love for her had a deliberate grace.
examples.translation_ko: 그와 그의 아내는 상상력이 기꺼이 머물고 싶어 하는 그림을 만들어냈고, 그녀에 대한 그의 사랑의 순수함에는 의도적인 우아함이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I thought of the happy life that pair had led in the cosy studio in Montmartre, Stroeve and his wife, their simplicity, kindness, and hospitality; it seemed to me cruel that it should have been broken to pieces by a ruthless chance; but the cruellest thing of all was that in fact it made no great difference.
examples.translation_ko: 몽마르트르의 아늑한 화실에서 스트루브와 그의 아내가 보냈던 행복한 나날들, 그들의 순박함과 친절함, 그리고 후한 인정을 생각해보니, 무자비한 우연에 의해 그 모든 것이 산산조각 난 것이 잔혹하게 느껴졌다. 하지만 무엇보다 잔혹한 것은 사실 그것이 별로 중요하지 않다는 점이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English affection, affeccion, affeccioun, from Old French affection, from Latin affectiōnem, from affectiō; equivalent to affect + -ion.
definition_en: A feeling of liking or loving someone.

senses.gloss: The act of affecting or acting upon.

The state of being affected, especially: a change in, or alteration of, the emotional state of a person or other animal, caused by a subjective affect (a subjective feeling or emotion), which arises in response to a stimulus which may result from either thought or perception.
An attribute; a quality or property; a condition.

examples.text: I tried to show by my expression that I expected no affection.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 아무런 호감도 기대하지 않는다는 표정을 지으려 애썼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For a moment the last sunshine fell with romantic affection upon her glowing face; her voice compelled me forward breathlessly as I listened—then the glow faded, each light deserting her with lingering regret, like children leaving a pleasant street at dusk.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 동안 마지막 햇살이 낭만적인 애정으로 그녀의 빛나는 얼굴에 내려앉았다. 그녀의 목소리는 내가 숨을 죽이고 듣는 동안 나를 앞으로 이끌었다—그러다 그 빛이 사라지고, 모든 광채가 아쉬운 듯 그녀를 떠났다. 마치 황혼녘 즐거운 거리를 떠나는 아이들처럼.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I could understand how his wife must feel for him, and I was glad that her affection was so tender.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 아내가 그를 어떻게 생각할지 이해할 수 있었고, 그녀의 애정이 그토록 다정한 것이 기뻤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They say a woman always remembers her first lover with affection; but perhaps she does not always remember him.
examples.translation_ko: 여자는 언제나 첫 연인을 애정 어린 마음으로 기억한다고들 하지만, 어쩌면 항상 기억하는 건 아닐지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cerymonye, from Latin caerimonia or caeremonia, later often cerimonia (“sacredness, reverence, a sacred rite”).
definition_en: A formal or official event.

senses.gloss: A ritual, with religious or cultural significance.
senses.example: Under certain circumstances there are few hours in life more agreeable than the hour dedicated to the ceremony known as afternoon tea.

senses.gloss: An official gathering to celebrate, commemorate, or otherwise mark some event.
senses.example: a graduation ceremony, an opening ceremony

senses.gloss: A formal socially established behaviour, often in relation to people of different ranks; formality.
senses.example: They went into the bars and interrupted the drinking, hustling the men out without ceremony.

examples.text: The music had died down as the ceremony began and now a long cheer floated in at the window, followed by intermittent cries of “Yea—ea—ea!” and finally by a burst of jazz as the dancing began.
examples.translation_ko: 의식이 시작되면서 음악이 잦아들었고, 이제 긴 환호성이 창문으로 흘러들어왔다. 이어서 간헐적인 "예—에—에!" 소리가 들렸고, 마침내 춤이 시작되자 재즈가 터져 나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You enter without ceremony,” said Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: "예의도 없이 들어오는군." 스트릭랜드가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Ata is a sensible girl, and she doesn’t expect any ceremony before the Mayor.
examples.translation_ko: 아타는 분별 있는 아이고, 시장 앞에서 무슨 의식을 치르길 바라지도 않아.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English rof, from Old English hrōf (“roof, ceiling; top, summit; heaven, sky”), from Proto-Germanic *hrōfą (“roof”).
definition_en: The top covering of a building.

senses.gloss: The external covering at the top of a building.
senses.example: The roof was blown off by the tornado.

senses.gloss: The top external level of a building.
senses.example: Let's go up to the roof.

senses.gloss: The upper part of a cavity.
senses.example: The palate is the roof of the mouth.

examples.text: A brewer had built it early in the “period” craze, a decade before, and there was a story that he’d agreed to pay five years’ taxes on all the neighbouring cottages if the owners would have their roofs thatched with straw.
examples.translation_ko: 한 양조업자가 10년 전 "시대풍" 열풍이 한창일 때 그 집을 지었는데, 이웃집 오두막 주인들이 지붕을 짚으로 이어주기만 하면 5년치 세금을 대신 내주겠다고 약속했다는 이야기가 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Already it was deep summer on roadhouse roofs and in front of wayside garages, where new red petrol-pumps sat out in pools of light, and when I reached my estate at West Egg I ran the car under its shed and sat for a while on an abandoned grass roller in the yard.
examples.translation_ko: 길가 여관 지붕 위와 도로변 주유소 앞에는 이미 한여름이 깊게 내려앉아 있었고, 새빨간 주유기들이 불빛 웅덩이 속에 자리 잡고 있었다. 웨스트에그에 있는 내 집에 도착해서는 차를 차고 밑에 넣어두고 마당의 버려진 잔디 롤러 위에 잠시 앉아 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I could only see that it was an attic, with a sloping roof; and a faint glimmer, no more than a less profound obscurity, came from a skylight.
examples.translation_ko: 경사진 지붕을 가진 다락방이라는 것만 알 수 있었고, 천창에서 희미한 빛이 새어 들어왔는데 그것도 그저 덜 짙은 어둠에 불과했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Here they made friends with others in as desperate condition as themselves, and when they were penniless and the night was bitter cold, they were glad to borrow from anyone who had earned a stray franc during the day the price of a roof over their heads.
examples.translation_ko: 이곳에서 그들은 자신들과 마찬가지로 절망적인 처지에 있는 다른 사람들과 친구가 되었고, 무일푼이 되어 밤이 혹독하게 추울 때면 하루 동안 프랑 한 닢이라도 번 사람에게서 머리 위에 지붕 하나 얹을 돈을 기꺼이 빌렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English crakken, craken, from Old English cracian (“to resound, crack”), from Proto-West Germanic *krakōn, from Proto-Germanic *krakōną...
definition_en: To make a sudden loud noise by breaking or splitting.

senses.gloss: To form cracks.
senses.example: It's been so dry, the ground is starting to crack.

senses.gloss: To break apart under force, stress, or pressure.
senses.example: When I tried to stand on the chair, it cracked.

senses.gloss: To become debilitated by psychological pressure.
senses.example: Anyone would crack after being hounded like that.

examples.text: His temper cracked a little.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 성질이 조금 터져 나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was a photograph of the house, cracked in the corners and dirty with many hands.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 집 사진이었는데, 모서리가 갈라지고 여러 손을 거치면서 더러워져 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Stroeve, his voice cracking with emotion, went up to him.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 감정에 북받쳐 목소리가 갈라진 채 그에게 다가갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was about ten o’ clock at night; I had been dining by myself at a restaurant, and having returned to my small apartment, was sitting in my parlour, reading I heard the cracked tinkling of the bell, and, going into the corridor, opened the door.
examples.translation_ko: 밤 열 시쯤이었다. 나는 식당에서 혼자 저녁을 먹고 작은 아파트로 돌아와 응접실에 앉아 책을 읽고 있었는데, 종이 갈라진 소리로 딸랑거리는 것을 듣고 복도로 나가 문을 열었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English, borrowed from Old French contenir, from Latin continēre (“to hold or keep together, comprise, contain”), combined form of con-...
definition_en: To hold or include something inside.

senses.gloss: To hold inside.
senses.example: The brown box contains three stacks of books.

senses.gloss: To include as a part.
senses.example: Most of the meals they offer contain meat.

senses.gloss: To put constraints upon; to restrain; to confine; to keep within bounds.
senses.example: I'm so excited, I can hardly contain myself!

examples.text: The flowers were unnecessary, for at two o’clock a greenhouse arrived from Gatsby’s, with innumerable receptacles to contain it.
examples.translation_ko: 꽃은 필요 없었다. 두 시에 개츠비네에서 온실이 도착했는데, 꽃을 담을 그릇들이 셀 수 없이 많았기 때문이다.

examples.text: One of the three shops it contained was for rent and another was an all-night restaurant, approached by a trail of ashes; the third was a garage—Repairs.

examples.text: It seemed to break oddly on the silence.
examples.translation_ko: 그 목소리는 고요함을 이상하게 깨뜨리는 것 같았다.

senses.example: A sheet of paper measuring eight and one-half inches wide by eleven inches high is a popular item in commerce.

examples.text: His parents were shiftless and unsuccessful farm people—his imagination had never really accepted them as his parents at all.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 부모는 게으르고 성공하지 못한 농민들이었는데—그의 상상력은 그들을 자신의 부모로 진정 받아들인 적이 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had often spoken to me of the silent town, somewhere up in the north of Holland, where his parents still lived.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 네덜란드 북부 어딘가에 있는 조용한 마을에 대해 자주 이야기했는데, 그곳에는 아직도 그의 부모가 살고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin splendidus, from splendere (“to shine”) + -idus (“adjective forming suffix”).
definition_en: Extremely impressive or attractive.

senses.gloss: Possessing or displaying splendor; shining; very bright.
senses.example: a splendid sun

senses.gloss: Gorgeous; magnificent; sumptuous; of remarkable beauty.
senses.example: a splendid palace

senses.gloss: Brilliant, excellent, of a very high standard.
senses.example: "We've fallen on our feet and no mistake," said Peter. "This is going to be perfectly splendid. That old chap will let us do anything we like."

examples.text: I agreed that it was splendid.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 정말 훌륭하다고 동의했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The friends looked out at us with the tragic eyes and short upper lips of southeastern Europe, and I was glad that the sight of Gatsby’s splendid car was included in their sombre holiday.
examples.translation_ko: 친구들은 동남유럽인 특유의 비극적인 눈과 짧은 윗입술로 우리를 바라보았고, 개츠비의 화려한 자동차가 그들의 음울한 휴일에 포함된 광경이 나는 기뻤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Rich merchants, sending their wares to the distant Indies, had lived in them calm and prosperous lives, and in their decent decay they kept still an aroma of their splendid past.
examples.translation_ko: 먼 인도로 상품을 보내던 부유한 상인들이 그 집들에서 평온하고 풍요로운 삶을 살았고, 품위 있게 낡아가는 가운데서도 여전히 찬란했던 과거의 향기를 간직하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In a handsome gold frame was a copy of Velasquez’ Innocent X., that Stroeve had made in Rome, and placed so as to make the most of their decorative effect were a number of Stroeve’s pictures, all in splendid frames.
examples.translation_ko: 화려한 금테 액자에는 스트루브가 로마에서 그린 벨라스케스의 '인노첸트 10세' 복제품이 걸려 있었고, 장식 효과를 최대한 살리도록 배치된 곳곳에는 모두 훌륭한 액자에 담긴 스트루브의 그림들이 여러 점 걸려 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English feeld, feld, from Old English feld, from Proto-West Germanic *felþu, from Proto-Germanic *felþuz (“field”), ultimately from Pro...
definition_en: An area of land covered with grass or other herbaceous plants.

senses.gloss: A land area free of woodland, cities, and towns; an area of open country.
senses.example: There are several species of wild flowers growing in this field.

senses.gloss: The open country near or belonging to a town or city.
A wide, open space that is used to grow crops or to hold farm animals, usually enclosed by a fence, hedge or other barrier.
senses.example: There were some cows grazing in a field.

examples.text: Cody was fifty years old then, a product of the Nevada silver fields, of the Yukon, of every rush for metal since seventy-five.
examples.translation_ko: 코디는 그때 쉰 살이었는데, 네바다 은광과 유콘, 그리고 1875년 이후 벌어진 모든 광물 러시의 산물이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He did not know that it was already behind him, somewhere back in that vast obscurity beyond the city, where the dark fields of the republic rolled on under the night.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그것이 이미 자신의 뒤편 어딘가에, 도시 너머 광막한 어둠 속에, 공화국의 어두운 들판이 밤하늘 아래 끝없이 펼쳐진 곳에 있다는 것을 알지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: You could wander along the canal till you came to broad green fields, with windmills here and there, in which cattle, black and white, grazed lazily.
examples.translation_ko: 운하를 따라 걸어가다 보면 넓고 푸른 들판이 나타났고, 여기저기 풍차가 서 있는 가운데 흑백 얼룩의 소들이 느긋하게 풀을 뜯고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English ripe, rype, from Old English rīpe (“ripe, mature”), from Proto-West Germanic *rīpī, from Proto-Germanic *rīpijaz, *rīpiz, from ...
definition_en: Fully grown or mature.

senses.gloss: Ready for reaping or gathering; having attained perfection; mature.
senses.example: ripe grain

senses.gloss: Advanced to the state of fitness for use; mellow.
senses.example: ripe cheese

senses.gloss: Having attained its full development; mature; perfected.
senses.example:
When you're ripe
You'll bleed out of control

examples.text: There was a ripe mystery about it, a hint of bedrooms upstairs more beautiful and cool than other bedrooms, of gay and radiant activities taking place through its corridors, and of romances that were not musty and laid away already in lavender but fresh and breathing and redolent of this year’s shining motorcars and of dances whose flowers were scarcely withered.
examples.translation_ko: 그 집에는 무르익은 신비로움이 있었다. 위층의 침실들이 다른 침실들보다 더 아름답고 시원하다는 암시, 복도를 통해 벌어지는 유쾌하고 찬란한 활동들, 그리고 곰팡내 나며 이미 라벤더 향 속에 묻혀버린 것이 아니라 올해의 빛나는 자동차들의 향기와 꽃이 아직 시들지 않은 무도회의 향기로 신선하고 생생하게 숨 쉬는 로맨스들의 암시가 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He swarmed up a tree, and presently threw down a ripe nut.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 나무를 재빨리 올라가더니 곧 익은 열매 하나를 던져 내렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He remained fat, and his round, red cheeks shone like ripe apples.
examples.translation_ko: 여전히 뚱뚱했고, 동그랗고 붉은 뺨은 잘 익은 사과처럼 윤이 났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: (early 17th century) From a Romance language, see French concentrer, Italian concentràre, Spanish concentrar; alternatively from Medieval Latin/New...
definition_en: Focus one's attention or effort on something.

senses.gloss: To bring to, or direct toward, a common center; to unite more closely; to gather into one body, mass, or force.
senses.example: to concentrate the attention

senses.gloss: To increase the strength and diminish the bulk of, as of a liquid or an ore; to intensify, by getting rid of useless material; to condense.
senses.example: to concentrate by washing

senses.gloss: To approach or meet in a common center; to consolidate.
senses.example: Population tends to concentrate in cities.

examples.text: He concentrated with an effort.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 애써 정신을 집중했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Well, you come,” she urged, concentrating on Gatsby.
examples.translation_ko: "자, 오세요." 그녀가 개츠비에게 시선을 집중하며 재촉했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was excited by the encounter, and my fancy worked busily while I sought to concentrate myself on the game I was playing.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그 만남에 흥분했고, 게임에 집중하려고 애쓰는 동안 상상력이 분주하게 돌아갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English draggen (“to drag”), early Middle English dragen (“to draw, carry”), confluence of Old English dragan (“to drag, draw, draw one...
definition_en: To pull or move something slowly and heavily.

senses.gloss: Resistance of a fluid to something moving through it.
senses.example: When designing cars, manufacturers have to take drag into consideration.

senses.gloss: Any force acting in opposition to the motion of an object.
senses.example: A high thrust-to-weight ratio helps a rocket to overcome the effects of gravity drag.

senses.gloss: The bottom part of a sand casting mold.

examples.text: At eleven o’clock a man in a raincoat, dragging a lawn-mower, tapped at my front door and said that Mr. Gatsby had sent him over to cut my grass.
examples.translation_ko: 열한 시에 비옷을 입고 잔디깎이를 끌고 온 남자가 현관문을 두드리며 개츠비 씨가 내 잔디를 깎으라고 자신을 보냈다고 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Captain Nichols dragged Strickland, bleeding from a wound in his arm, his clothes in rags, into the street.
examples.translation_ko: 니콜스 선장은 팔에 상처를 입고 피를 흘리며 옷이 너덜너덜해진 스트릭랜드를 거리로 끌어냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The sun-baked streets seemed to give back the heat that had beat down on them during the day, and the passers-by dragged their feet along them wearily.
examples.translation_ko: 햇볕에 달궈진 거리들은 하루 종일 내리쬔 열기를 되돌려 보내는 듯했고, 지나가는 사람들은 지친 발걸음을 질질 끌며 걸어갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English dumb (“silent, speechless, mute, ineffectual”), from Old English dumb (“silent, speechless, mute, unable to speak”), from Proto...
definition_en: Lacking the power of speech or unable to speak.

senses.gloss: Unable to speak; lacking power of speech (kept in "deaf, dumb, and blind").
senses.example: His younger brother was born dumb, and communicated with sign language.

senses.gloss: Not talkative; taciturn or unwilling to speak.
Having no input or voice in running things.

examples.text: He’s so dumb he doesn’t know he’s alive.”
examples.translation_ko: "너무 바보라서 자기가 살아 있는지도 모르거든."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You think I’m pretty dumb, don’t you?” he suggested.
examples.translation_ko: "내가 꽤 바보 같다고 생각하지?" 그가 넌지시 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He might have been struck dumb.
examples.translation_ko: 벙어리가 된 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin distortum, past participle of distorqueō (“to twist, torture, distort”).
definition_en: To change or twist something so that it is not accurate or true.

senses.gloss: To bring something out of shape, to misshape.
To become misshapen.
To give a false or misleading account of; pervert.
senses.example: In their articles, journalists sometimes distort the truth.

examples.text: After Gatsby’s death the East was haunted for me like that, distorted beyond my eyes’ power of correction.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비가 죽은 후 동부는 나에게 그런 식으로 사로잡혀 있었다. 내 눈이 바로잡을 수 있는 힘을 넘어서도록 뒤틀려 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When I came back they had both disappeared, so I sat down discreetly in the living-room and read a chapter of Simon Called Peter—either it was terrible stuff or the whisky distorted things, because it didn’t make any sense to me.
examples.translation_ko: 돌아와 보니 둘 다 사라져 있어서, 나는 거실에 조심스럽게 앉아 『시몬이라 불린 베드로』를 한 장 읽었다. 그 책이 형편없는 내용이었는지 위스키가 사물을 왜곡시켰는지, 도무지 이해가 되지 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The magnifying-glasses he wore distorted them.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 쓴 돋보기가 눈을 일그러뜨리고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He did not hesitate to simplify or to distort if he could get nearer to that unknown thing he sought.
examples.translation_ko: 자신이 추구하는 미지의 것에 더 가까이 다가갈 수 있다면 단순화하거나 왜곡하는 것도 서슴지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French acide, from Latin acidus (“sour, acid”), from aceō (“I am sour”). Doublet of agita and acetic.
definition_en: A substance that is sour to the taste and has a pH of less than 7.

senses.gloss: Sour, sharp, or biting to the taste; tart; having the taste of vinegar.
senses.example: acid fruits or liquors

senses.gloss: Sour-tempered.
senses.example: His response was harsh and acid.

senses.gloss: Of or pertaining to an acid; acidic.
senses.example: acid soils

examples.text: Her mouth and chin were all burnt by the acid.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 입과 턱은 모두 산에 타서 상처투성이였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There was a bottle of oxalic acid on the table.”
examples.translation_ko: 탁자 위에는 옥살산 병이 놓여 있었고요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French sofa, ultimately from Arabic صُفَّة (ṣuffa, “a long seat made of stone or brick, covered with rich carpets and cushions and us...
definition_en: A piece of furniture for sitting or lying on.

senses.gloss: A raised area of a building's floor, usually covered with carpeting, used for sitting.
An upholstered seat with a raised back and one or two raised ends, long enough to comfortably accommodate two or more people.
senses.example: He bought a big sofa two days before his relatives arrived.

examples.text: Then he sat down, rigidly, his elbow on the arm of the sofa and his chin in his hand.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 소파 팔걸이에 팔꿈치를 올리고 손으로 턱을 괸 채 경직되게 앉았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I’m stiff,” she complained, “I’ve been lying on that sofa for as long as I can remember.”
examples.translation_ko: "몸이 뻣뻣해." 그녀가 불평했다. "기억하는 한 계속 저 소파에 누워 있었거든."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His volubility had left him at last, and he sank down wearily on my sofa.
examples.translation_ko: 그토록 수다스럽던 그가 마침내 말문이 막혔고, 지친 듯 내 소파에 털썩 주저앉았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was the picture of a woman lying on a sofa, with one arm beneath her head and the other along her body; one knee was raised, and the other leg was stretched out.
examples.translation_ko: 소파에 누워 있는 여인의 그림이었는데, 한 팔은 머리 밑에 베고 다른 팔은 몸을 따라 늘어뜨린 채였다. 한쪽 무릎은 세우고 다른 쪽 다리는 쭉 뻗어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Late Middle English acute (“of a disease or fever: starting suddenly and lasting for a short time; of a humour: irritating, sharp”), from Lati...
definition_en: Having or showing a sharp and sudden quality.

senses.gloss: Brief, quick, short.
senses.example: It was an acute event.

senses.gloss: High or shrill.
senses.example: an acute accent or tone

senses.gloss: Intense; sensitive; sharp.
senses.example: She had an acute sense of honour

examples.text: There was something pathetic in his concentration, as if his complacency, more acute than of old, was not enough to him any more.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 집중하는 모습에는 뭔가 애처로운 구석이 있었다. 마치 예전보다 더욱 예민해진 그의 자기만족이 이제는 그에게 충분하지 않은 것처럼.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her husband, among various physical accomplishments, had been one of the most powerful ends that ever played football at New Haven—a national figure in a way, one of those men who reach such an acute limited excellence at twenty-one that everything afterward savours of anticlimax.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 남편은 여러 신체적 재능 중에서도 뉴헤이븐에서 미식축구를 했던 가장 강력한 엔드 중 한 명이었다—어떤 면에서는 전국적인 인물이었고, 스물한 살에 그토록 예리하고 제한적인 탁월함에 도달해서 그 이후의 모든 것이 김빠진 뒷맛을 남기는 그런 부류의 남자였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The day was fine and sunny, and I felt in myself a more acute delight in life.
examples.translation_ko: 날씨는 맑고 화창했으며, 나는 삶에 대한 더욱 예리한 기쁨을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: To the acute observer no one can produce the most casual work without disclosing the innermost secrets of his soul.
examples.translation_ko: 예리한 관찰자에게는 누구든 아무리 대수롭지 않은 작품이라도 만들면서 자신의 영혼 깊숙한 비밀을 드러내지 않을 수 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English appropriaten, from appropriat (“appropriated”) + -en, borrowed from Latin appropriātus, perfect passive participle of appropriō...
definition_en: Suitable for the occasion or situation.

senses.gloss: To take to oneself; to claim or use, especially as by an exclusive right.
senses.example: Let no man appropriate the use of a common benefit.

senses.gloss: To set apart for, or assign to, a particular person or use, especially in exclusion of all others; with to or for.
senses.example: A spot of ground is appropriated for a garden.

senses.gloss: To annex (for example a benefice, to a spiritual corporation, as its property).
senses.example: Some [benefices] were appropriated to secular ecclesiastical corporations

examples.text: He was left with his singularly appropriate education; the vague contour of Jay Gatsby had filled out to the substantiality of a man.
examples.translation_ko: 그에게 남은 것은 그 독특하게도 적절한 교육뿐이었다. 제이 개츠비의 모호한 윤곽이 한 남자의 실체로 채워진 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I think he hardly knew what he was saying, for when I asked him what business he was in he answered: “That’s my affair,” before he realized that it wasn’t an appropriate reply.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자신이 무슨 말을 하는지 거의 모르는 것 같았다. 내가 무슨 사업을 하느냐고 묻자 그는 "그건 내 일이야"라고 대답했다가, 그것이 적절한 답변이 아니라는 걸 깨달았기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I made an appropriate rejoinder, and he smiled wanly.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 적절한 대답을 했고, 그는 쓸쓸하게 미소를 지었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Brueghel gave me the impression of a man striving to express in one medium feelings more appropriate to expression in another, and it may be that it was the obscure consciousness of this that excited Strickland’s sympathy.
examples.translation_ko: 브뤼헐은 내게 한 매체로 다른 매체에 더 적합한 감정을 표현하려고 애쓰는 사람이라는 인상을 주었는데, 아마도 이런 막연한 의식이 스트릭랜드의 공감을 불러일으켰을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English glisnen, glistnen, from Old English glisnian, itself from Proto-West Germanic *glisnōn, while ultimately deriving from Proto-Ge...
definition_en: Shine with a faintly sparkling light.

senses.gloss: To reflect light with a glittering luster; to sparkle, coruscate, glint or flash.
senses.example: The sun was fierce, the land seemed to glisten and drip with steam.

examples.text: He set down the receiver and came toward us, glistening slightly, to take our stiff straw hats.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 수화기를 내려놓고 살짝 땀에 젖은 채로 우리 쪽으로 다가와 딱딱한 밀짚모자를 받아들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: On buffet tables, garnished with glistening hors-d’oeuvre, spiced baked hams crowded against salads of harlequin designs and pastry pigs and turkeys bewitched to a dark gold.
examples.translation_ko: 반짝이는 오르되브르로 장식된 뷔페 테이블 위에는 향신료를 넣어 구운 햄들이 할리퀸 무늬의 샐러드들과 어깨를 맞대고 있었고, 페이스트리로 만든 돼지와 칠면조들이 짙은 황금빛으로 마법에 걸린 듯 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His kind eyes glistened.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 다정한 눈이 반짝였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Tears glistened in her eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 눈에 눈물이 반짝였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English horribly, horribely, horribliche, horriblelyche, equivalent to horrible + -ly.
definition_en: Used to describe something that is very unpleasant or frightening.

senses.gloss: In a horrible way; very badly.
senses.example: The beginning art students displayed their horribly executed paintings with hopeful faces.

senses.gloss: To an extreme degree or extent.
senses.example: Then everything went horribly wrong.

senses.gloss: With a very bad effect.
senses.example: Horribly, as he was dying, his eyes reddened.

examples.text: A pause; it endured horribly.
examples.translation_ko: 침묵이 흘렀다. 끔찍할 정도로 길게.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: About five o’clock our procession of three cars reached the cemetery and stopped in a thick drizzle beside the gate—first a motor hearse, horribly black and wet, then Mr. Gatz and the minister and me in the limousine, and a little later four or five servants and the postman from West Egg, in Gatsby’s station wagon, all wet to the skin.
examples.translation_ko: 다섯 시쯤 되어 세 대의 차로 이루어진 우리 행렬이 묘지에 도착해 문 옆에서 멈춰 섰다. 부슬부슬 내리는 비 속에서—맨 앞에는 끔찍하도록 검고 비에 젖은 영구차가, 그 다음에는 개츠 씨와 목사 그리고 내가 탄 리무진이, 그리고 조금 뒤에는 웨스트에그에서 온 하인 네다섯 명과 우편배달부가 개츠비의 스테이션 왜건을 타고 왔는데, 모두 뼛속까지 젖어 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He felt horribly sick.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 끔찍하게 속이 메스꺼웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The stench that assailed him turned him horribly sick.
examples.translation_ko: 그를 덮친 악취가 그를 끔찍하게 메스껍게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English tin, from Old English tin, from Proto-West Germanic *tin, from Proto-Germanic *tiną.
definition_en: A chemical element with the symbol Sn and atomic number 50.

senses.gloss: A malleable, ductile, metallic element, resistant to corrosion, with atomic number 50 and symbol Sn.
An airtight container, made of tin or another metal, used to preserve food, or hold a liquid or some other product.
senses.example: a tin of baked beans; a tobacco tin; a tin of shoe polish

senses.gloss: A metal pan used for baking, roasting, storing food, etc.
senses.example: muffin tin

examples.text: A reluctant elevator boy went for a box full of straw and some milk, to which he added on his own initiative a tin of large, hard dog biscuits—one of which decomposed apathetically in the saucer of milk all afternoon.
examples.translation_ko: 마지못해 하는 엘리베이터 보이가 짚으로 가득한 상자와 우유를 가져왔는데, 거기에 자기 판단으로 크고 딱딱한 개 비스킷 통을 하나 더했다. 그 비스킷 중 하나는 오후 내내 우유 접시에서 맥없이 풀어져 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was a tin of tobacco on the table, and, taking out his pipe, he filled it.
examples.translation_ko: 테이블 위에 담배통이 있었는데, 그는 파이프를 꺼내어 담배를 채웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Under a cover were the remains of a piece of cheese, and in a tin box was a crust of bread.
examples.translation_ko: 덮개 아래에는 치즈 조각이 남아 있었고, 양철 상자 안에는 빵 껍질이 들어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Late Middle English in the sense of "stunted tree," a variant of shrub, possibly under Old Norse influence.
definition_en: A small bushy tree or a rough surface.

senses.gloss: Mean; dirty; contemptible; scrubby.
senses.example: No little scrub joint shall come on my board.

examples.text: “I’d been scrubbing the deck, and all at once a chap said to me: ‘Why, there it is.’
examples.translation_ko: "갑판을 문지르고 있었는데, 갑자기 한 녀석이 내게 말했어요. '어, 저기 있네.'
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was a ring of land round a deep lagoon, uninhabited, and covered only with scrub and wild guava.
examples.translation_ko: 그곳은 깊은 석호를 둘러싼 고리 모양의 땅으로, 사람이 살지 않았고 관목과 야생 구아바만이 덮고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English wildely, wijldeli, wildeliche, equivalent to wild + -ly.
definition_en: Used to describe something that is done or happens in a completely uncontrolled and unpredictable way.

senses.gloss: In a wild, uncontrolled manner.
senses.example: He swung wildly at the guy's head, but ended up on the floor.

senses.gloss: To a ridiculous or extreme degree; extremely.
senses.example: wildly exagerrated

examples.text: He followed me wildly into the kitchen, closed the door, and whispered: “Oh, God!” in a miserable way.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 미친 듯이 나를 따라 부엌으로 들어와서 문을 닫고는 비참한 목소리로 속삭였다. "오, 하느님!"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He looked around him wildly, as if the past were lurking here in the shadow of his house, just out of reach of his hand.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 과거가 집 그림자 속 어딘가에 숨어 있으면서 손에 닿지 않는 곳에 있는 것처럼, 미친 듯이 주위를 둘러보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He looked round wildly for some instrument; he wanted to hack the picture to pieces; it should not exist another minute.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 무언가 도구를 찾아 미친 듯이 주위를 둘러보았다. 그림을 산산조각 내고 싶었다. 그 그림이 단 일 분이라도 더 존재해서는 안 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I saw him, with my mind’s eye, on the schooner on which he worked, wearing nothing but a pair of dungarees; and at night, when the boat sailed along easily before a light breeze, and the sailors were gathered on the upper deck, while the captain and the supercargo lolled in deck-chairs, smoking their pipes, I saw him dance with another lad, dance wildly, to the wheezy music of the concertina.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 마음의 눈으로 그를 보았다. 그가 일하던 스쿠너호에서 작업복 바지 한 벌만 걸친 채로 있는 모습을, 그리고 밤에 배가 가벼운 바람을 받으며 순조롭게 항해할 때, 선원들이 상갑판에 모여 있고 선장과 화물 담당관이 갑판 의자에 기대어 파이프 담배를 피우고 있을 때, 그가 다른 젊은이와 함께 아코디언의 쌕쌕거리는 음악에 맞춰 격렬하게 춤추는 모습을.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From in- + coherent.
definition_en: Lacking coherence or logical connection.

senses.gloss: Not making logical sense; not logically connected or consistent.
senses.example: When we confronted her, she gave us a hasty, incoherent explanation.

senses.gloss: Not holding together physically; loose; unconnected.
senses.example: […] sooner, may all the Material World crumble into Incoherent Atoms, or relapse into the Abyss of Nothingness, than that any Conclusion, thus deduced, can be False […]

senses.gloss: Not cohering socially, not united.
senses.example: I was glad, now, to be out of Karhide, an incoherent land driven towards violence by a paranoid, pregnant king and an egomaniac Regent.

examples.text: About three o’clock the quality of Wilson’s incoherent muttering changed—he grew quieter and began to talk about the yellow car.
examples.translation_ko: 세 시쯤 되어 윌슨의 횡설수설하는 중얼거림의 성질이 바뀌었다. 그는 더 조용해지더니 노란 차에 대해 이야기하기 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: On the last night, with my trunk packed and my car sold to the grocer, I went over and looked at that huge incoherent failure of a house once more.
examples.translation_ko: 마지막 밤, 트렁크를 싸고 차를 식료품점 주인에게 판 후, 나는 그 거대하고 지리멸렬한 실패작 같은 집을 다시 한 번 보러 갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Stroeve tried to talk to me about the picture, but he was incoherent, and I had to guess at what he meant.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 그 그림에 대해 나와 이야기하려 했지만, 말이 앞뒤가 맞지 않아서 나는 그의 뜻을 짐작해야 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English ferful, fervol, equivalent to fear + -ful.
definition_en: Feeling or showing fear.

senses.gloss: Frightening; causing fear.
senses.example:
Sirs, stop their mouths, let them not speak to me,
But let them hear what fearful words I utter.

senses.gloss: Tending to fear; timid.
senses.example: a fearful boy

senses.gloss: Terrible; shockingly bad.

examples.text: His life was strangely divorced from material things, and it was as though his body at times wreaked a fearful revenge on his spirit.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 삶은 물질적인 것들과 이상하게 분리되어 있었고, 마치 그의 육체가 때때로 그의 정신에 무서운 복수를 가하는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was the work of a man who had delved into the hidden depths of nature and had discovered secrets which were beautiful and fearful too.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 자연의 숨겨진 깊은 곳까지 파고들어 아름답고 동시에 두려운 비밀들을 발견한 사람의 작품이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lyghtly, liȝtliche, lihtliche, from Old English lēohtlīċe, equivalent to light + -ly.
definition_en: Used to describe something that is done or happens with little force or effort.

senses.gloss: In a light manner.
senses.example: As a teacher, I don't take rudeness in class lightly.

examples.text: “Well, other people are,” she said lightly.
examples.translation_ko: "글쎄, 다른 사람들이 조심하니까요." 그녀가 가볍게 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I said lightly that I had heard nothing at all, and a few minutes later I got up to go home.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 아무것도 듣지 못했다고 가볍게 말했고, 몇 분 후 집에 가려고 일어났다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But one fact he made clear to me; people talk of beauty lightly, and having no feeling for words, they use that one carelessly, so that it loses its force; and the thing it stands for, sharing its name with a hundred trivial objects, is deprived of dignity.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그가 내게 분명히 해준 사실이 하나 있었다. 사람들은 아름다움에 대해 가볍게 말하고, 언어에 대한 감각이 없어서 그 단어를 함부로 사용하므로 그 힘을 잃게 만든다는 것이었다. 그리고 그 단어가 가리키는 대상은 수많은 하찮은 것들과 이름을 공유하게 되어 존엄성을 박탈당한다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sadnesse, equivalent to sad + -ness.
definition_en: A feeling of sadness or sorrow.

senses.gloss: The state or emotion of being sad.
senses.example:
But sorrow that is couch'd in seeming gladness
Is like that mirth fate turns to sudden sadness.

senses.gloss: An event in one's life that causes sadness.
senses.example: She has experienced many sadnesses in her forty years.

examples.text: “Tom’s getting very profound,” said Daisy, with an expression of unthoughtful sadness.
examples.translation_ko: "톰이 아주 심오해지고 있네요." 데이지가 생각 없는 슬픔의 표정을 지으며 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For Daisy was young and her artificial world was redolent of orchids and pleasant, cheerful snobbery and orchestras which set the rhythm of the year, summing up the sadness and suggestiveness of life in new tunes.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지는 젊었고 그녀의 인위적인 세계는 난초 향기로 가득했으며, 유쾌하고 명랑한 속물근성과 한 해의 리듬을 만들어내는 오케스트라들로 넘쳐났는데, 그것들은 삶의 슬픔과 암시를 새로운 선율로 요약해냈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was young still, and in a few years he would look back on all his misery with a sadness in which there would be something not unpleasurable.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아직 젊었고, 몇 년 후면 자신의 모든 비참함을 돌아보며 불쾌하지만은 않은 무언가가 담긴 슬픔을 느끼게 될 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is like the sadness which you may see in the jester’s eyes when a merry company is laughing at his sallies; his lips smile and his jokes are gayer because in the communion of laughter he finds himself more intolerably alone.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 유쾌한 일행이 어릿광대의 농담에 웃고 있을 때 그의 눈에서 볼 수 있는 슬픔과 같다. 웃음의 교감 속에서 자신이 더욱 견딜 수 없을 만큼 외롭다는 것을 깨닫기 때문에 그의 입술은 미소 짓고 농담은 더욱 경쾌해진다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
Uncertain. From either:
* Earlier English roger (“a begging vagabond who pretends to be a poor scholar from Oxford or Cambridge”), possibly from La...
definition_en: A person who plays or behaves in a dishonest or unscrupulous way.

senses.gloss: A scoundrel, rascal or unprincipled, deceitful, and unreliable person.
senses.example: “… No rogue e’er felt the halter draw, with a good opinion of the law, and perhaps my own detestation of the law arises from my having frequently broken it. […]”

senses.gloss: A mischievous scamp.
senses.example: Ah, you sweet little rogue, you!

senses.gloss: A vagrant.

examples.text: The rogue, like the artist and perhaps the gentleman, belongs to no class.
examples.translation_ko: 악한은 예술가나 신사와 마찬가지로 어떤 계급에도 속하지 않는다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They moved quickly, following my smallest gesture, and they gave him the look of a very thorough rogue.
examples.translation_ko: 그 눈은 재빠르게 움직이며 내 작은 몸짓까지 따라왔고, 그래서 그는 아주 철저한 악한처럼 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English destroyen, from Old French destruire, Vulgar Latin *destrugō, from Classical Latin dēstruō, from dē- (“un-, de-”) + struō (“I b...
definition_en: To cause something to be completely ruined or damaged.

senses.gloss: To damage beyond use or repair; to damage (something) to the point that it effectively ceases to exist.
senses.example: The earthquake destroyed several apartment complexes.

senses.gloss: To neutralize, undo a property or condition.
senses.example: Smoking destroys the natural subtlety of the palate.

senses.gloss: To put down or euthanize.
senses.example: Destroying a rabid dog is required by law.

examples.text: “Destroyed?”
examples.translation_ko: "파괴되었다고요?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then, in pride and contempt, he destroyed it.”
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 자부심과 경멸 속에서 그것을 파괴했습니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English snacchen, snecchen, from Old English *snæċċan, *sneċċan, from Proto-West Germanic *snakkijan, from Proto-Germanic *snakkijaną, ...
definition_en: To take or seize something quickly and often secretly.

senses.gloss: To grasp and remove quickly.
senses.example: He snatched up the phone.

senses.gloss: To attempt to seize something suddenly.
senses.example: to snatch at a rope

senses.gloss: To take or seize hastily, abruptly, or without permission or ceremony.
senses.example: to snatch a kiss

examples.text: He stretched out his hand desperately as if to snatch only a wisp of air, to save a fragment of the spot that she had made lovely for him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 한 줌의 공기라도 붙잡으려는 듯, 그녀가 자신에게 사랑스럽게 만들어준 그 장소의 한 조각이라도 구하려는 듯 필사적으로 손을 뻗었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He snatched the book from me and replaced it hastily on its shelf, muttering that if one brick was removed the whole library was liable to collapse.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내게서 책을 낚아채더니 서둘러 제자리에 꽂으면서, 벽돌 하나만 빼내도 도서관 전체가 무너질 수 있다고 중얼거렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He snatched you from the jaws of death.”
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자네를 죽음의 문턱에서 구해냈다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The bush was encroaching, and it looked as though very soon the primeval forest would regain possession of that strip of land which had been snatched from it at the cost of so much labour.
examples.translation_ko: 덤불이 침범해 들어오고 있었고, 그토록 많은 노동의 대가로 빼앗았던 이 땅을 원시림이 곧 다시 차지할 것 같아 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English lust, from Old English lust (“lust, pleasure, longing”), from Proto-West Germanic *lustu, from Proto-Germanic *lustuz.
Akin to ...
definition_en: A strong desire or craving for something.

senses.gloss: A feeling of strong desire, especially such a feeling driven by sexual arousal.
senses.example: Seeing Leslie fills me with a passionate lust.

senses.gloss: A general want or longing, not necessarily sexual.
senses.example: The boarders hide their lust to go home.

senses.gloss: A delightful cause of joy, pleasure.
senses.example: An ideal son is his father's lasting lust.

examples.text: I know lust.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 욕정을 안다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The hideous lust that pervades the air is oppressive and horrible, and yet there is something mysterious in the sight which haunts and troubles you.
examples.translation_ko: 공기를 가득 채운 추악한 욕정이 숨막히고 끔찍하지만, 그 광경에는 사람을 사로잡고 마음을 어지럽히는 신비로운 무언가가 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English graspen, grapsen, craspen (“to grope; feel around”), from Old English *grǣpsian, from Proto-West Germanic *graipisōn, from Prot...
definition_en: To take or hold something firmly with one's hand.

senses.gloss: To grip; to take hold, particularly with the hand.
senses.example: How few! yet how they creep / Through my fingers to the deep, / While I weep—while I weep! / O God! can I not grasp / Them with a tighter clasp?

senses.gloss: To understand.
senses.example: I have never been able to grasp the concept of infinity.

senses.gloss: To take advantage of something, to seize, to jump at a chance.

examples.text: He had come a long way to this blue lawn, and his dream must have seemed so close that he could hardly fail to grasp it.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 이 푸른 잔디밭까지 먼 길을 왔고, 그의 꿈은 너무 가까이 있어서 그것을 붙잡지 못할 리 없어 보였을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Almost before I had grasped her meaning there was the flutter of a dress and the crunch of leather boots, and Tom and Daisy were back at the table.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 그녀의 말뜻을 채 파악하기도 전에 드레스가 바스락거리고 가죽 부츠가 바닥을 밟는 소리가 났고, 톰과 데이지가 다시 식탁으로 돌아왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She has a small mind, and she resents the abstract which she is unable to grasp.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 마음이 좁고, 자신이 이해할 수 없는 추상적인 것들을 원망한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin contemptus (whence contempt) + -ous.
definition_en: Showing or feeling contempt.

senses.gloss: Showing contempt; expressing disdain; showing a lack of respect.
senses.example: I don't know that guy, but he just gave me a contemptuous look.

senses.gloss: Worthy of contempt; contemptible.

examples.text: I knew now why her face was familiar—its pleasing contemptuous expression had looked out at me from many rotogravure pictures of the sporting life at Asheville and Hot Springs and Palm Beach.
examples.translation_ko: 이제야 그녀의 얼굴이 왜 낯익었는지 알 것 같았다—그 매력적이면서도 경멸적인 표정을 애슈빌과 핫스프링스, 팜비치의 스포츠계 소식을 다룬 수많은 사진판화에서 본 적이 있었던 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was on my way to get roaring drunk from sheer embarrassment when Jordan Baker came out of the house and stood at the head of the marble steps, leaning a little backward and looking with contemptuous interest down into the garden.
examples.translation_ko: 순전한 당황감 때문에 만취할 참이었는데, 조던 베이커가 집에서 나와 대리석 계단 꼭대기에 서서 약간 뒤로 몸을 기대고 경멸적인 관심으로 정원을 내려다보고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He stopped in front of my chair, and stood looking down at me with an expression in which I read a contemptuous amazement.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내 의자 앞에 멈춰 서서 경멸적인 놀라움이 담긴 표정으로 나를 내려다보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English crawlen, crewlen, creulen, crallen, *cravelen, from Old Norse krafla (compare Danish kravle (“to crawl, creep”), Swedish kravla...
definition_en: Move slowly on hands and feet.

senses.gloss: To creep; to move slowly on hands and knees, or by dragging the body along the ground.
senses.example: Clutching my wounded side, I crawled back to the trench.

senses.gloss: To move forward slowly, with frequent stops.
senses.example: The rush-hour traffic crawled around the bypass.

senses.gloss: To act in a servile manner.
senses.example: Don’t come crawling to me with your useless apologies!

examples.text: On the green Sound, stagnant in the heat, one small sail crawled slowly toward the fresher sea.
examples.translation_ko: 더위에 정체된 푸른 해협 위로, 작은 돛 하나가 더 시원한 바다를 향해 천천히 기어가고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Occasionally a line of grey cars crawls along an invisible track, gives out a ghastly creak, and comes to rest, and immediately the ash-grey men swarm up with leaden spades and stir up an impenetrable cloud, which screens their obscure operations from your sight.
examples.translation_ko: 때때로 회색 화차들이 한 줄로 보이지 않는 선로를 따라 기어가다가 섬뜩한 삐걱거리는 소리를 내며 멈춰 선다. 그러면 즉시 재빛 회색 사내들이 납덩이 같은 삽을 들고 우르르 몰려와 뚫을 수 없는 먼지 구름을 일으켜, 그들의 모호한 작업을 시야에서 가려버린다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Sooner or later you’ll be ill and tired and old, and then you’ll crawl back into the herd.
examples.translation_ko: 조만간 당신도 병들고 지치고 늙을 것이고, 그때가 되면 무리 속으로 기어 돌아갈 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There is the rustle of the myriad animals on the beach, all the little shelled things that crawl about ceaselessly, and there is the noisy scurrying of the land-crabs.
examples.translation_ko: 해변에는 무수한 동물들이 바스락거리는 소리가 있고, 끊임없이 기어다니는 온갖 조개껍데기를 가진 작은 생물들이 있으며, 육지게들이 시끄럽게 뛰어다니는 소리가 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English conveien, from Old French conveier (French convoyer), from Vulgar Latin *convio, from Classical Latin via (“way”). Compare convoy.
definition_en: To communicate or express something.

senses.gloss: To move (something) from one place to another.
senses.example: Air conveys sound. Water is conveyed through the pipe.

senses.gloss: To take or carry (someone) from one place to another.
senses.example:
[…] the false Tyrant seiz’d the Princely Maid,
And to a Lodge in distant Woods convey’d;

senses.gloss: To communicate; to make known; to portray.
senses.example: to convey an impression; to convey information

examples.text: His speaking voice, a gruff husky tenor, added to the impression of fractiousness he conveyed.
examples.translation_ko: 거칠고 쉰 테너인 그의 목소리는 그가 풍기는 성급함의 인상을 더했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It understood you just so far as you wanted to be understood, believed in you as you would like to believe in yourself, and assured you that it had precisely the impression of you that, at your best, you hoped to convey.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 당신이 이해받고 싶어 하는 만큼만 당신을 이해했고, 당신이 자신을 믿고 싶어 하는 대로 당신을 믿어주었으며, 당신이 최선의 모습일 때 전달하고 싶어 했던 바로 그 인상을 자신이 받았다고 확신시켜 주었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was under an intolerable necessity to convey something that he felt, and he created them with that intention alone.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자신이 느끼는 무언가를 전달해야 한다는 참을 수 없는 필요에 사로잡혀 있었고, 오직 그 의도만으로 작품들을 창조했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We seek pitifully to convey to others the treasures of our heart, but they have not the power to accept them, and so we go lonely, side by side but not together, unable to know our fellows and unknown by them.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 가슴속 보물을 다른 사람들에게 전하려고 애처롭게 애쓰지만, 그들에게는 그것을 받아들일 힘이 없어서, 우리는 나란히 있으면서도 함께하지 못한 채 외롭게 살아간다. 동료들을 알 수도 없고 그들에게 알려질 수도 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English fan, inherited from Old English fann (“a winnowing, fan”), derived from Latin vannus (“fan for winnowing grain”), der...
definition_en: To make or cause to make a strong current of air.

senses.gloss: A hand-held device consisting of concertinaed material, or slats of material, gathered together at one end, that may be opened out into the shape of a sector of a circle and waved back and forth in order to move air towards oneself and cool oneself.
An electrical or mechanical device for moving air, used for cooling people, machinery, etc.
senses.example: He didn't switch on the fan because the temperature was 15 degrees Celsius.

senses.gloss: The action of fanning; agitation of the air.
senses.example: "If I cannot be of service, then I certainly don't wish to impose," said McGinty, with a quick fan of breeze that indicated a sweeping bow.

examples.text: In a well-fanned Forty-second Street cellar I met Gatsby for lunch.
examples.translation_ko: 환기가 잘 되는 42번가 지하실에서 나는 개츠비와 점심을 함께했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Daisy and Jordan lay upon an enormous couch, like silver idols weighing down their own white dresses against the singing breeze of the fans.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지와 조던은 거대한 소파에 누워 있었는데, 선풍기의 노랫소리 같은 바람에 맞서 하얀 드레스를 눌러 입은 은빛 우상들 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A latent gift might reveal itself on acquaintance with the painters and writers whose society his wife sought; or domestic incompatability might turn him upon himself; a love affair might fan into bright flame a fire which I could have shown smouldering dimly in his heart.
examples.translation_ko: 잠재된 재능이 그의 아내가 사귀던 화가들과 작가들과의 교제를 통해 드러날 수도 있었을 것이고, 가정 불화가 그를 자기 내면으로 돌리게 했을 수도 있었을 것이며, 연애 사건이 그의 마음속에서 희미하게 타오르고 있던 불씨를 밝은 불꽃으로 부채질했을 수도 있었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: According to the gracious custom of the island, presents were given me by the persons with whom I had been thrown in contact—baskets made of the leaves of the cocoa-nut tree, mats of pandanus, fans; and Tiaré gave me three little pearls and three jars of guava-jelly made with her own plump hands.
examples.translation_ko: 섬의 우아한 관습에 따라, 내가 인연을 맺었던 사람들이 나에게 선물을 주었다—코코넛 나무 잎으로 만든 바구니, 판다누스로 짠 돗자리, 부채들이었고, 티아레는 작은 진주 세 개와 자신의 통통한 손으로 직접 만든 구아바 젤리 세 병을 주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin pressūra.
definition_en: The force exerted on a surface by an object or fluid.

senses.gloss: A pressing; a force applied to a surface.
senses.example: Apply pressure to the wound to stop the bleeding.

senses.gloss: A contrasting force or impulse of any kind
senses.example: the pressure of poverty; the pressure of taxes; the pressure of motives on the mind; the pressure of civilization.

senses.gloss: Distress.
senses.example: She has felt pressure lately because her boss expects her to get the job done by the first.

examples.text: Luckily the clock took this moment to tilt dangerously at the pressure of his head, whereupon he turned and caught it with trembling fingers, and set it back in place.
examples.translation_ko: 다행히 바로 그 순간 시계가 그의 머리 압력에 위험하게 기울었고, 그러자 그는 몸을 돌려 떨리는 손가락으로 시계를 붙잡아 제자리에 다시 놓았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She was feeling the pressure of the world outside, and she wanted to see him and feel his presence beside her and be reassured that she was doing the right thing after all.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 바깥세상의 압박을 느끼고 있었고, 그를 보고 곁에서 그의 존재를 느끼며 자신이 결국 옳은 일을 하고 있다는 확신을 얻고 싶었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: An effective story might also have been made by bringing him into contact with some old painter whom the pressure of want or the desire for commercial success had made false to the genius of his youth, and who, seeing in Strickland the possibilities which himself had wasted, influenced him to forsake all and follow the divine tyranny of art.
examples.translation_ko: 궁핍의 압박이나 상업적 성공에 대한 욕망 때문에 젊은 시절의 천재성을 배반한 늙은 화가와 그를 접촉시켜, 그 화가가 스트릭랜드에게서 자신이 낭비한 가능성을 보고 모든 것을 버리고 예술의 신성한 폭정을 따르도록 영향을 미치게 함으로써 효과적인 이야기를 만들 수도 있었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From lonely + -ness.
definition_en: A feeling of sadness because one has no friends or company.

senses.gloss: A feeling of depression resulting from being alone or from having no companions.
senses.example:
Loneliness got a mind of its own
The more people around, the more you feel alone

senses.gloss: The condition or state of being alone or having no companions.
senses.example: Hitherto all things that have bin nam’d, were approv’d of God to be very good: lonelines is the first thing which Gods eye nam’d not good […]

senses.gloss: The state of being unfrequented or devoid of human activity (of a place or time).
senses.example: In addition, the very loneliness of the road had its charm for him; since only at rare intervals is house seen by its side, and rarer still living creature encountered upon it.

examples.text: Thirty—the promise of a decade of loneliness, a thinning list of single men to know, a thinning briefcase of enthusiasm, thinning hair.
examples.translation_ko: 서른—외로움의 십 년에 대한 약속, 알고 지낼 독신 남자들의 줄어드는 명단, 열정이 담긴 서류가방의 얇아짐, 그리고 빠져가는 머리카락.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: At the enchanted metropolitan twilight I felt a haunting loneliness sometimes, and felt it in others—poor young clerks who loitered in front of windows waiting until it was time for a solitary restaurant dinner—young clerks in the dusk, wasting the most poignant moments of night and life.
examples.translation_ko: 마법에 걸린 듯한 대도시의 황혼 속에서 나는 때때로 마음을 사로잡는 외로움을 느꼈고, 다른 이들에게서도 그것을 느꼈다—창문 앞에서 어슬렁거리며 혼자 식당에서 저녁을 먹을 시간이 될 때까지 기다리는 가난한 젊은 사무원들—황혼 속의 젊은 사무원들이 밤과 인생의 가장 애절한 순간들을 허비하고 있는 것을.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: If in the loneliness of his studio he wrestled desperately with the Angel of the Lord he never allowed a soul to divine his anguish.
examples.translation_ko: 작업실의 고독 속에서 주님의 천사와 필사적으로 씨름했을지라도, 그는 그 누구도 자신의 고뇌를 눈치채지 못하게 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It would not surprise you if, as you came near seeking for an opening in the reef, it vanished suddenly from your view, and nothing met your gaze but the blue loneliness of the Pacific.
examples.translation_ko: 암초 사이의 틈을 찾아 가까이 다가갈 때 섬이 갑자기 시야에서 사라져버리고, 눈앞에는 태평양의 푸른 적막만이 펼쳐진다 해도 놀랄 일이 아닐 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English anoyen, from Old French anoier (“to bother, disturb”), from Late Latin inodiāre (“to make loathsome”), derived from Latin odium...
definition_en: To cause annoyance or irritation.

senses.gloss: To disturb or irritate, especially by continued or repeated acts; to bother with unpleasant deeds.
senses.example: Marc loved his sister, but when she annoyed him he wanted to switch her off.

senses.gloss: To do something to upset or anger someone; to be troublesome.
To molest; to harm; to injure.
senses.example: to annoy an army by impeding its march, or by a cannonade

examples.text: This annoyed me.
examples.translation_ko: 이것이 나를 짜증나게 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He won’t annoy you.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 당신을 괴롭히지는 않을 거요.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But I dare say he said it to annoy, and if he did he certainly succeeded.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 아마 그는 상대방을 짜증나게 하려고 그런 말을 했을 것이고, 만약 그것이 목적이었다면 분명히 성공했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English magik, magyk, from Old French magique (noun and adjective), from Latin magicus (adjective), magica (noun use of feminine form o...
definition_en: Having or showing a special power to do something that seems impossible.

senses.gloss: The supernatural forces which are drawn on in such a ritual.
A specific ritual or procedure associated with such magic; a spell; a magical ability.
senses.example: "I am the master of mighty magics."

senses.gloss: The ability to cast a magic spell.
senses.example: I learned a new magic after rescuing the tree fairy.

examples.text: He seemed on a sudden to have entered a magic world.
examples.translation_ko: 갑자기 마법의 세계에 들어선 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It brought to his mind vague recollections of black magic.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 마음속에 흑마술에 대한 막연한 기억들이 떠올랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A place where ships can dock and be repaired.

senses.gloss: Standard spelling of harbor.
senses.example: In West Wales it has never been possible until recently to exploit the magnificent natural harbour of Milford Haven, for there was no industrial hinterland.

examples.text: He loved to moon about the harbour talking to the natives.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 항구를 어슬렁거리며 원주민들과 이야기하는 것을 좋아했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You double down to the harbour, my lad,” said the Captain to Strickland, “and sign on.
examples.translation_ko: "항구로 뛰어가서 승선 계약을 맺어," 선장이 스트릭랜드에게 말했다. "자네 서류는 있잖아."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Attested ca. 1715, of uncertain origin. Said to be derived from dialectal scoon (“to skim over water”). Compare also shunt (“to cause to move (sudd...
definition_en: A type of sailing ship or a large glass for serving drinks.

senses.gloss: A sailing ship with two or more masts, all with fore-and-aft sails; if two masted, having a foremast and a mainmast.
senses.example: In addition to the square-rigged sailing ships, the schooners were the second largest group of large sailing vessels.

senses.gloss: A glass for drinking a large measure of sherry.
senses.example: Boycott any pub that bans work clothes, allows customers to reserve tables or only sells beer in schooners. That is less a pub, more a private members’ club.

senses.gloss: A glass of beer, of a size which varies between states (Wikipedia).
senses.example: For a true Adelaide experience, head for the bar and order a schooner of Coopers, the local brew, or a glass of SA′s impressive wine.

examples.text: I have come to Tahiti now to buy a schooner.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이제 타히티에 와서 스쿠너를 한 척 사려고 한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I have heard that the boy works on one of Cameron’s schooners.
examples.translation_ko: 그 아이는 카메론의 스쿠너 중 한 척에서 일한다고 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Having a fixed or restricted amount.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of limit

examples.text: Suddenly I wasn’t thinking of Daisy and Gatsby any more, but of this clean, hard, limited person, who dealt in universal scepticism, and who leaned back jauntily just within the circle of my arm.
examples.translation_ko: 갑자기 나는 더 이상 데이지와 개츠비를 생각하지 않고 있었다. 대신 이 깨끗하고 단단하고 한정적인 사람을, 보편적 회의주의를 다루며 내 팔이 그리는 원 안에서 당당하게 몸을 뒤로 기댄 이 사람을 생각하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was rather literary in college—one year I wrote a series of very solemn and obvious editorials for the Yale News—and now I was going to bring back all such things into my life and become again that most limited of all specialists, the “well-rounded man.”
examples.translation_ko: 대학 시절 나는 꽤 문학적이었다—한 해 동안 예일 뉴스에 매우 진부하고 뻔한 사설들을 연재하기도 했다—그리고 이제 나는 그런 모든 것들을 내 삶으로 다시 불러들여서, 모든 전문가 중에서도 가장 제한적인 존재인 "교양인"이 되려고 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I recognised my friend’s limited vocabulary, and I prepared to regard Captain Nichols as a trustworthy witness.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 내 친구의 제한된 어휘를 알아차렸고, 니콜스 선장을 믿을 만한 증인으로 여길 준비가 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Perhaps a shortening of truckle, related to Latin trochus (“iron hoop, wheel”) from Ancient Greek τροχός (trokhós).
definition_en: A large vehicle for transporting goods.

senses.gloss: A small wheel or roller, specifically the wheel of a gun carriage.
The ball on top of a flagpole.

On a wooden mast, a circular disc (or sometimes a rectangle) of wood near or at the top of the mast, usually with holes or sheaves to reeve signal halyards; also a temporary or emergency place for a lookout. "Main" refers to the mainmast, whereas a truck on another mast may be called (on the mizzenmast, for example) "mizzen-truck".

examples.text: “We can’t argue about it here,” Tom said impatiently, as a truck gave out a cursing whistle behind us.
examples.translation_ko: "여기서 말다툼할 수는 없어." 뒤에서 트럭이 욕설 섞인 경적을 울리자 톰이 짜증스럽게 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Once they each of them earned a franc by loading trucks with innumerable boxes of oranges that had been dumped down on the quay.
examples.translation_ko: 한번은 부두에 쌓아놓은 수많은 오렌지 상자를 트럭에 싣는 일로 각자 1프랑씩 벌었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: After Strickland’s death certain of his effects were sold by auction in the market-place at Papeete, and she went to it herself because there was among the truck an American stove she wanted.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드가 죽은 후 그의 유품 일부가 파페에테 시장에서 경매에 부쳐졌는데, 그녀가 원하던 미국제 난로가 잡동사니 중에 섞여 있어서 직접 경매에 참석했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Learned borrowing from Latin pervādō.
definition_en: Spread throughout or affect something

senses.gloss: To be in every part of; to spread through; permeate.
senses.example: Cruel wars pervade history.

examples.text: He felt their presence all about the house, pervading the air with the shades and echoes of still vibrant emotions.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 집 안 곳곳에서 그들의 존재를 느꼈고, 여전히 생생한 감정들의 그림자와 메아리가 공기를 가득 채우고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Just as Daisy’s house had always seemed to him more mysterious and gay than other houses, so his idea of the city itself, even though she was gone from it, was pervaded with a melancholy beauty.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They were sombre blues, opaque like a delicately carved bowl in lapis lazuli, and yet with a quivering lustre that suggested the palpitation of mysterious life; there were purples, horrible like raw and putrid flesh, and yet with a glowing, sensual passion that called up vague memories of the Roman Empire of Heliogabalus; there were reds, shrill like the berries of holly—one thought of Christmas in England, and the snow, the good cheer, and the pleasure of children—and yet by some magic softened till they had the swooning tenderness of a dove’s breast; there were deep yellows that died with an unnatural passion into a green as fragrant as the spring and as pure as the sparkling water of a mountain brook.
examples.translation_ko: 청금석으로 정교하게 조각한 그릇처럼 불투명한 음울한 청색들이 있었는데, 그러면서도 신비로운 생명의 고동을 암시하는 떨리는 광택을 띠고 있었다. 날것의 썩은 살점처럼 끔찍한 자주색들이 있었는데, 그러면서도 헬리오가발루스 시대 로마 제국의 막연한 기억을 불러일으키는 타오르는 관능적 열정을 품고 있었다. 호랑가시나무 열매처럼 날카로운 적색들이 있었는데—영국의 크리스마스와 눈, 즐거운 축제, 아이들의 기쁨을 떠올리게 했다—그러면서도 어떤 마법에 의해 부드러워져서 비둘기 가슴의 황홀한 부드러움을 지니고 있었다. 부자연스러운 열정으로 죽어가면서 봄처럼 향기롭고 산골 시냇물처럼 맑고 반짝이는 초록으로 변해가는 깊은 황색들이 있었다.

examples.text: Before me stretched the portentous, menacing road of a new decade.
examples.translation_ko: 내 앞에는 불길하고 위협적인 새로운 십 년의 길이 펼쳐져 있었다.

examples.text: Thirty—the promise of a decade of loneliness, a thinning list of single men to know, a thinning briefcase of enthusiasm, thinning hair.

definition_en: To enclose (an object) completely in any flexible, thin material such as fabric or paper.

senses.gloss: To enclose (an object) completely in any flexible, thin material such as fabric or paper.
senses.example: Christmas gifts are commonly known to be wrapped in paper.

senses.gloss: To enclose or coil around an object or organism, as a form of grasping.
senses.example: A snake wraps itself around its prey.

senses.gloss: To conceal by enveloping or enfolding; to hide.

examples.text: “She had it wrapped in tissue paper on her bureau.”

examples.translation_ko: 나는 잔디밭 가장자리를 따라 되돌아가서 자갈길을 조용히 지나 베란다 계단을 발끝으로 올라갔다.

etymology: From Middle English discrete, from Old French discret, from Latin discrētus, from past participle of discernere. Doublet of discrete.
definition_en: Having or showing a careful and thoughtful choice about what to do or say.

senses.gloss: Respectful of privacy or secrecy; exercising caution in order to avoid causing embarrassment; quiet; diplomatic.
senses.example: With a discreet gesture, she reminded him to mind his manners.

senses.gloss: Not drawing attention, anger or challenge; inconspicuous.

examples.text: “It’d be more discreet to go to Europe.”
examples.translation_ko: "유럽으로 가는 게 더 신중할 텐데."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was a matter upon which he was reticent, and with persons of his kind a direct question is never very discreet.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 이 문제에 대해 말을 아꼈고, 그런 부류의 사람들에게 직접적인 질문은 결코 신중하지 못한 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I do not speak of that greatness which is achieved by the fortunate politician or the successful soldier; that is a quality which belongs to the place he occupies rather than to the man; and a change of circumstances reduces it to very discreet proportions.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 운 좋은 정치가나 성공한 군인이 성취하는 그런 위대함을 말하는 것이 아니다. 그것은 그 사람 자체보다는 그가 차지하는 지위에 속하는 성질이며, 상황이 바뀌면 아주 초라한 규모로 축소되고 만다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: The relationship between two quantities or amounts.

senses.gloss: A quantity of something that is part of the whole amount or number.
Harmonious relation of parts to each other or to the whole.
Proper or equal share.
senses.example: Let the women[…]do the same things in their proportions and capacities.

examples.text: The thing approached the proportions of a scandal—then died away.
examples.translation_ko: 그 일은 스캔들에 가까운 규모로 번져갔다가 사그라들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The daughter of a native and an English sea-captain settled in Tahiti, when I knew her she was a woman of fifty, who looked older, and of enormous proportions.
examples.translation_ko: 타히티에 정착한 원주민과 영국인 선장 사이에서 태어난 딸로, 내가 그녀를 알았을 때 그녀는 쉰 살의 여인이었는데 나이보다 늙어 보였고 거대한 체구를 하고 있었다.

examples.text: I do not speak of that greatness which is achieved by the fortunate politician or the successful soldier; that is a quality which belongs to the place he occupies rather than to the man; and a change of circumstances reduces it to very discreet proportions.
