etymology: From Middle English market, from late Old English market (“market”) and Anglo-Norman markiet (Old French marchié), Old Saxon markat, and/or Old Nor...
definition_en: A place where people buy and sell goods.

senses.gloss: A gathering of people for the purchase and sale of merchandise, often periodic at a set time.
senses.example: The right to hold a weekly market was an invaluable privilege not given to all towns in the Middle Ages.

senses.gloss: A relatively spacious outdoor or covered site where traders set up stalls, either temporarily or permanently or semi-permanently, and buyers browse the merchandise.
senses.example: This site on North Street used to be the market, until it was redeveloped.

senses.gloss: Any physical store selling groceries, such as a grocery store or convenience store.
senses.example: Stop by the market on your way home and pick up some milk.

examples.text: There were often odd jobs to be got about the fish-market.
examples.translation_ko: 어시장 근처에서는 종종 잡일거리를 구할 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The Prime Minister out of office is seen, too often, to have been but a pompous rhetorician, and the General without an army is but the tame hero of a market town.
examples.translation_ko: 관직에서 물러난 총리는 너무나 자주 허풍스러운 웅변가에 불과했음이 드러나고, 군대 없는 장군은 시골 장터의 길들여진 영웅일 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English authentik, from Old French autentique, from Latin authenticus, from Ancient Greek αὐθεντικός (authentikós, “principal, genuine”...
definition_en: Genuine or true to the original.

senses.gloss: Of the same origin as claimed; genuine.
senses.example: The experts confirmed it was an authentic signature.

senses.gloss: Conforming to reality and therefore worthy of trust, reliance, or belief.
senses.example: an authentic writer; an authentic portrait; authentic information

senses.gloss: Designating a mode having the final as the lowest note.

examples.text: To my astonishment, the thing had an authentic look.
examples.translation_ko: 놀랍게도 그것은 진짜처럼 보였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The greatness of Charles Strickland was authentic.
examples.translation_ko: 찰스 스트릭랜드의 위대함은 진정한 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: And when such as had come in contact with Strickland in the past, writers who had known him in London, painters who had met him in the cafés of Montmartre, discovered to their amazement that where they had seen but an unsuccessful artist, like another, authentic genius had rubbed shoulders with them there began to appear in the magazines of France and America a succession of articles, the reminiscences of one, the appreciation of another, which added to Strickland’s notoriety, and fed without satisfying the curiosity of the public.
examples.translation_ko: 과거에 스트릭랜드와 접촉했던 사람들, 런던에서 그를 알았던 작가들, 몽마르트르의 카페에서 그를 만났던 화가들이 자신들이 그저 또 다른 실패한 예술가로만 보았던 곳에서 진정한 천재가 어깨를 스쳤다는 사실을 놀랍게 발견하자, 프랑스와 미국의 잡지들에 연이어 기사들이 나타나기 시작했다. 한 사람의 회상, 다른 사람의 평가가 스트릭랜드의 명성을 더했고, 대중의 호기심을 만족시키지는 못한 채 부채질했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From eccentric + -ity.
definition_en: The quality of being eccentric or unconventional.

senses.gloss: The quality of being eccentric or odd; any eccentric behaviour.
The ratio, constant for any particular conic section, of the distance of a point from the focus to its distance from the directrix.
senses.example: For an ellipse, the eccentricity is the ratio of the distance from the center to a focus divided by the length of the semi-major axis.

senses.gloss: The eccentricity of the conic section (usually an ellipse) defined by the orbit of a given object around a reference object (such as that of a planet around the sun).

examples.text: The time has passed when he was an object of ridicule, and it is no longer a mark of eccentricity to defend or of perversity to extol him.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 조롱거리였던 시절은 지났고, 그를 옹호하는 것이 더 이상 괴짜의 표시도 아니고 그를 찬양하는 것이 비뚤어진 성향의 표시도 아니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was obvious that he had no social gifts, but these a man can do without; he had no eccentricity even, to take him out of the common run; he was just a good, dull, honest, plain man.
examples.translation_ko: 그에게 사교적 재능이 없다는 것은 분명했지만, 남자라면 그런 것 없이도 살 수 있다. 하지만 그를 평범한 부류에서 벗어나게 해줄 별난 구석조차 없었다. 그는 그저 선량하고, 따분하고, 정직하고, 수수한 남자였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English defenden, from Old French defendre, deffendre (Modern French défendre), from Latin dēfendō (“to ward off”), from Proto-Italic *...
definition_en: To protect or defend against attack.

senses.gloss: To ward off attacks against; to fight to protect; to guard.
To support by words or writing; to vindicate, talk in favour of.
senses.example: Justice Elena Kagan on Thursday defended the code of conduct the Supreme Court created last year, but conceded there needs to be a way to enforce the rules for it to be more effective.

senses.gloss: To make legal defence of; to represent (the accused).
senses.example: Philip Miles, defending, said: "This was a single instance, there was no allegation of continuing behaviour over a long period of time."

examples.text: It passed, and he began to talk excitedly to Daisy, denying everything, defending his name against accusations that had not been made.
examples.translation_ko: 그것도 지나가고, 그는 데이지에게 흥분해서 말하기 시작했다. 모든 것을 부인하며, 제기되지도 않은 비난들로부터 자신의 명예를 변호했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The Chink was not backward to defend himself, and a very lively quarrel ensued.
examples.translation_ko: 중국인도 뒤지지 않고 자신을 변호했고, 매우 격렬한 말다툼이 벌어졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The time has passed when he was an object of ridicule, and it is no longer a mark of eccentricity to defend or of perversity to extol him.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 조롱거리였던 시절은 지났고, 그를 옹호하는 것이 더 이상 괴짜의 표시도 아니고 그를 찬양하는 것이 비뚤어진 성향의 표시도 아니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Latin decoratio: compare French décoration.
Morphologically decorate + -ion
definition_en: An object or design added to make something more attractive.

senses.gloss: The act of adorning, embellishing, or honoring; ornamentation.
Any item that adorns, enriches, or beautifies; something added by way of embellishment or ornamentation.
Specifically, any mark of honor to be worn upon the person, as a medal, cross, or ribbon of an order of knighthood, bestowed for services in war, great achievements in literature, art, etc.

examples.text: I was promoted to be a major, and every Allied government gave me a decoration—even Montenegro, little Montenegro down on the Adriatic Sea!”
examples.translation_ko: 나는 소령으로 진급했고, 모든 연합국 정부가 나에게 훈장을 줬지—심지어 몬테네그로, 아드리아 해 연안의 작은 몬테네그로까지!"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “For a long time I could not get out of my head the recollection of the extraordinary decoration with which Strickland had covered the walls of his house,” he said reflectively.
examples.translation_ko: "오랫동안 스트릭랜드가 자신의 집 벽에 그린 그 놀라운 장식에 대한 기억을 머릿속에서 지워낼 수가 없었습니다." 그가 회상하듯 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The artist, painter, poet, or musician, by his decoration, sublime or beautiful, satisfies the aesthetic sense; but that is akin to the sexual instinct, and shares its barbarity: he lays before you also the greater gift of himself.
examples.translation_ko: 예술가, 화가, 시인, 음악가는 숭고하거나 아름다운 장식을 통해 미적 감각을 만족시킨다. 하지만 그것은 성적 본능과 유사하며 그 야만성을 공유한다. 그는 또한 자신이라는 더 큰 선물을 당신 앞에 내놓는다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Ellipsis of detective police.
definition_en: A person who investigates crimes and solves mysteries.

senses.gloss: A police officer tasked with collecting evidence and information in order to solve a crime; an investigator.
A person employed to find information not otherwise available to the public.

examples.text: Someone with a positive manner, perhaps a detective, used the expression “madman” as he bent over Wilson’s body that afternoon, and the adventitious authority of his voice set the key for the newspaper reports next morning.
examples.translation_ko: 단호한 태도의 누군가가, 아마 형사였을 텐데, 그날 오후 윌슨의 시체 위로 몸을 굽히며 "광인"이라는 표현을 썼고, 그의 목소리가 지닌 우연한 권위가 다음 날 아침 신문 보도의 논조를 결정했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: To pursue his secret has something of the fascination of a detective story.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 비밀을 추적하는 일에는 추리소설 같은 매혹이 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The books he liked were queer; sometimes I would find him poring over the poems of Mallarme, and he read them as a child reads, forming the words with his lips, and I wondered what strange emotion he got from those subtle cadences and obscure phrases; and again I found him absorbed in the detective novels of Gaboriau.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 좋아하는 책들은 기이했다. 때로는 말라르메의 시집을 열심히 들여다보고 있는 그를 발견하곤 했는데, 그는 아이가 읽듯 입술로 단어를 따라 읽었고, 나는 그가 그 미묘한 운율과 모호한 구절들에서 어떤 기묘한 감정을 얻는지 궁금했다. 또 어떤 때는 가보리오의 탐정소설에 빠져 있는 그를 발견하기도 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English oblivion, from Anglo-Norman oblivion, from Latin oblīviō (“forgetfulness”), from oblivisci (“to forget”).
definition_en: A state of being forgotten or ignored.

senses.gloss: The state of forgetting completely, of being oblivious, unconscious, unaware, as when sleeping, drunk, or dead.
senses.example: He regularly drank himself into oblivion.

senses.gloss: The state of being completely forgotten, of being reduced to a state of non-existence, extinction, or nothingness, including through war and destruction. (Figuratively) for an area like hell, a wasteland.
senses.example: Due to modern technology, many more people and much more information will not slip into oblivion, contrary to what happened throughout history until now.

senses.gloss: A form of purgatory.

examples.text: Tom appeared from his oblivion as we were sitting down to supper together.
examples.translation_ko: 우리가 함께 저녁을 먹으려고 앉을 때 톰이 망각에서 나타났다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I’d a little rather not be the polo player,” said Tom pleasantly, “I’d rather look at all these famous people in—in oblivion.”
examples.translation_ko: "나는 폴로 선수보다는," 톰이 유쾌하게 말했다, "차라리 이 모든 유명한 사람들을 망각 속에서 바라보고 싶어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was not till four years after Strickland’s death that Maurice Huret wrote that article in the Mercure de France which rescued the unknown painter from oblivion and blazed the trail which succeeding writers, with more or less docility, have followed.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드가 죽은 지 4년이 지나서야 모리스 위레가 메르퀴르 드 프랑스지에 그 기사를 써서 무명의 화가를 망각에서 구해내고, 후속 작가들이 다소간의 순종으로 따라간 길을 개척했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English trailen, from Old French trailler (“to tow; pick up the scent of a quarry”), from Vulgar Latin *tragulāre (“to drag”), from Lat...
definition_en: A path or track made by people or animals.

senses.gloss: To follow behind (someone or something); to tail (someone or something).
senses.example: The hunters trailed their prey deep into the woods.

senses.gloss: To drag (something) behind on the ground.
senses.example: You'll get your coat all muddy if you trail it around like that.

senses.gloss: To leave (a trail of).
senses.example: He walked into the house, soaking wet, and trailed water all over the place.

examples.text: One of the three shops it contained was for rent and another was an all-night restaurant, approached by a trail of ashes; the third was a garage—Repairs.
examples.translation_ko: 그곳에 있는 세 개의 상점 중 하나는 임대용이었고, 다른 하나는 재 더미 사이의 오솔길을 따라 들어가는 24시간 식당이었다. 세 번째는 정비소였다—수리업.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I know very little about painting, and I wander along trails that others have blazed for me.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 회화에 대해 아는 것이 거의 없고, 다른 사람들이 닦아놓은 길을 따라 걸을 뿐이다.

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French critique, from Latin criticus, from Ancient Greek κριτικός (kritikós, “of or for judging, able to discern”), from κρίνω...
definition_en: A person who expresses a professional opinion on the merits or faults of something.

senses.gloss: A person who appraises the works of others.
senses.example: Following its publication, the novel received widespread acclaim from literary critics.

senses.gloss: A specialist in judging works of art.
One who criticizes; a person who finds fault.
senses.example: When an author has many beauties consistent with virtue, piety, and truth, let not little critics exalt themselves, and shower down their ill nature.

examples.text: “Mr. Van Busche Taylor is the distinguished American critic.
examples.translation_ko: "반 부셰 테일러 씨는 저명한 미국 비평가예요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But I will allow that the critic who has not a practical knowledge of technique is seldom able to say anything on the subject of real value, and my ignorance of painting is extreme.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 기법에 대한 실용적 지식이 없는 비평가는 진정한 가치가 있는 말을 거의 할 수 없다는 점은 인정하겠으며, 회화에 대한 나의 무지는 극심하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English extravagaunt, from Middle French extravagant and its etymon Medieval Latin extravagans, past participle of extravagor...
definition_en: Excessively expensive or elaborate.

senses.gloss: Exceeding the bounds of something; roving; hence, foreign.
senses.example: The extravagant and erring spirit hies / To his confine.

senses.gloss: Extreme; wild; excessive; unrestrained.
senses.example: extravagant acts, praise, or abuse

senses.gloss: Exorbitant

examples.text: Tough Bill’s fare was seldom extravagant, and you rose from his table almost as hungry as you sat down, but for some days they had good reason to regret it.
examples.translation_ko: 터프 빌의 식사는 좀처럼 풍성하지 않아서 그의 식탁에서 일어날 때는 앉았을 때와 거의 마찬가지로 배가 고팠지만, 며칠 동안 그들은 그것을 그리워할 충분한 이유가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Though his means were adequate to the needs of himself and his wife, he certainly had no money to waste; but now he was wantonly extravagant in the purchase of delicacies, out of season and dear, which might tempt Strickland’s capricious appetite.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 수입은 자신과 아내의 필요를 충족시키기에 충분했지만, 확실히 낭비할 돈은 없었다. 하지만 이제 그는 스트릭랜드의 변덕스러운 식욕을 돋울 수 있는 진미들을 사는 데 방탕하게 돈을 썼는데, 그것들은 제철이 아니어서 비쌌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English juggement, borrowed from Old French jugement, from Late Latin iūdicāmentum, from Latin iūdicō. Partially displaced doom. By sur...
definition_en: The act of forming an opinion or making a decision about something.

senses.gloss: The act of judging.
senses.example: The key to the situation was judgment of the role the railways could play in modern times.

senses.gloss: The power or faculty of performing such operations; especially, when unqualified, the faculty of judging or deciding rightly, justly, or wisely.
senses.example: a man of judgment / a man of good judgment

senses.gloss: The conclusion or result of judging; an opinion; a decision.
senses.example:
Not from the stars do I my judgment pluck;
And yet methinks I have astronomy […]

examples.text: I thought he was reserving his judgment till the end.
examples.translation_ko: 끝까지 다 본 다음에 판단을 내리려는 거라고 생각했어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I think I have never known a man whose judgment was surer.
examples.translation_ko: 그만큼 확실한 판단력을 가진 사람을 나는 본 적이 없다고 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English confirmen, confermen, from Old French confermer, from Latin cōnfirmāre (“to make firm, strengthen, establish”), from con- (“tog...
definition_en: To make certain or sure of something.

senses.gloss: To strengthen; to make firm or resolute.
To administer the sacrament of confirmation on (someone).
senses.example: Elizabeth, daughter of Henry VIII, was baptized and confirmed at the age of three days.

senses.gloss: To assure the accuracy of previous statements.

examples.text: “Of course you will,” confirmed Daisy.
examples.translation_ko: "물론 그럴 거야." 데이지가 확신에 찬 목소리로 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Someone who had been driving a little behind us confirmed this, and the policeman turned away.
examples.translation_ko: 우리 뒤에서 조금 떨어져 운전하던 누군가가 이를 확인해 주었고, 경찰관은 돌아섰다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For a long time no critic has enjoyed in France a more incontestable authority, and it was impossible not to be impressed by the claims he made; they seemed extravagant; but later judgments have confirmed his estimate, and the reputation of Charles Strickland is now firmly established on the lines which he laid down.
examples.translation_ko: 오랫동안 프랑스에서 그보다 더 확실한 권위를 누린 비평가는 없었고, 그가 제기한 주장에 감명받지 않을 수 없었다. 그 주장들은 과장된 것처럼 보였지만, 후의 판단들이 그의 평가를 확증했고, 찰스 스트릭랜드의 명성은 이제 그가 제시한 노선 위에 확고히 자리 잡았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fermely; equivalent to firm + -ly.
definition_en: In a firm or fixed position.

senses.gloss: In a firm or definite or strong manner.
senses.example: She corrected him firmly but gently.

senses.gloss: Securely.
senses.example: Tie the rope firmly to the post.

senses.gloss: Definitively.
senses.example: This was widely interpreted to mean that slavery was once more firmly illegal in England.

examples.text: But they knew then, I firmly believe.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그때 그들은 알고 있었다고 나는 확신한다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He walked quickly over to Wilson and, standing in front of him, seized him firmly by the upper arms.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 재빨리 윌슨에게 다가가서 그의 앞에 서더니 그의 팔뚝을 단단히 붙잡았다.

etymology: From Middle English establissen, from Old French establiss-, stem of some of the conjugated forms of establir, (Modern French établir), from Latin ...
definition_en: To make or set up something officially.

senses.gloss: To make stable or firm; to confirm.
senses.example: Once it [a snowdrop variety] became established, some bulbs were lifted and passed on to be chipped (i.e. cut into small pieces and grown on).

senses.gloss: To form; to found; to institute; to set up in business.
senses.example: But with thee will I establish my covenant; and thou shalt come into the ark, thou, and thy sons, and thy wife, and thy sons' wives with thee.

senses.gloss: To appoint or adopt, as officers, laws, regulations, guidelines, etc.; to enact; to ordain.

examples.text: Amid the welcome confusion of cups and cakes a certain physical decency established itself.
examples.translation_ko: 찻잔과 케이크들의 반가운 혼란 속에서 어떤 육체적 품위가 자리를 잡았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Two shining arrogant eyes had established dominance over his face and gave him the appearance of always leaning aggressively forward.
examples.translation_ko: 빛나는 오만한 두 눈이 그의 얼굴을 지배하고 있어서, 그에게는 항상 공격적으로 몸을 앞으로 기울이는 듯한 인상을 주었다.

etymology: The noun is derived from Middle English stile, stel, stele, stiel, stiele, stil, still, stille, styele, style, styill, styll, styyl (“writing tool,...
definition_en: A particular way of doing something or a distinctive quality of someone's appearance.

senses.gloss: A sharp stick used for writing on clay tablets or other surfaces; a stylus; (by extension, obsolete) an instrument used to write with ink; a pen.
senses.example: Thus while his Thoughts the lingring Day beguile, / To gentle Arcite let us turn our Style; [...]

senses.gloss: A tool with a sharp point used in engraving; a burin, a graver, a stylet, a stylus.
senses.example: From Job xix. 24. it appears to have been usual in his day, to write or engrave upon Plates of Lead, which might easily be done with a Pen, or Graver, or Style of Iron, or other hard metal.

senses.gloss: The gnomon or pin of a sundial, the shadow of which indicates the hour.

examples.text: It was a very small room, overcrowded with furniture of the style which the French know as Louis Philippe.
examples.translation_ko: 매우 작은 방이었는데, 프랑스인들이 루이 필리프 양식이라고 부르는 스타일의 가구들로 빼곡했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I admire their polish—their youth is already so accomplished that it seems absurd to speak of promise—I marvel at the felicity of their style; but with all their copiousness (their vocabulary suggests that they fingered Roget’s Thesaurus in their cradles)
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그들의 세련됨을 감탄한다—그들의 젊음은 이미 너무나 완성되어 있어서 장래성을 운운하는 것조차 우스꽝스러워 보인다—나는 그들 문체의 적절함에 경탄한다. 하지만 그 모든 풍부함에도 불구하고 (그들의 어휘력을 보면 요람에서부터 로제의 유의어 사전을 만지작거렸던 것 같다)
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From out + line.
definition_en: A brief summary or description of the main points.

senses.gloss: A line marking the boundary of an object figure.
The outer shape of an object or figure.
senses.example: From this point of vantage, we were able to gain an impression of the massive outlines of the main structure, and its intricate maze of girders.

senses.gloss: A sketch or drawing in which objects are delineated in contours without shading.
senses.example: Painters, by their outlines, colours, lights, and shadows, represent the same in their pictures.

examples.text: And I looked up and I saw the outline of the island.
examples.translation_ko: 고개를 들어보니 섬의 윤곽이 보였어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Maurice Huret in his famous article gave an outline of Charles Strickland’s life which was well calculated to whet the appetites of the inquiring.
examples.translation_ko: 모리스 위레는 그의 유명한 기사에서 찰스 스트릭랜드의 생애 개요를 제시했는데, 이는 탐구하는 이들의 호기심을 자극하기에 충분히 계산된 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English degre, borrowed from Old French degré (French: degré), itself from Latin gradus, with the prefix de-.
definition_en: A unit of measurement for temperature or a level of achievement.

senses.gloss: A stage of proficiency or qualification in a course of study, now especially an award bestowed by a university/college, as a certification of academic achievement. (In the United States, can include secondary schools.)
senses.example: She has two bachelor's degrees and is studying towards a master's degree.

senses.gloss: A unit of measurement of angle equal to ¹⁄₃₆₀ of a circle's circumference.
senses.example: A right angle is a ninety-degree angle.

senses.gloss: A unit of measurement of temperature on any of several scales, such as Celsius or Fahrenheit.
senses.example: 212 degrees Fahrenheit is equal to 100 degrees Celsius.

examples.text: It occurred to me that he had been very slowly bending toward her all evening to attain this proximity, and even while I watched I saw him stoop one ultimate degree and kiss at her cheek.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 저녁 내내 아주 천천히 그녀 쪽으로 몸을 기울여 이런 근접함을 얻으려 했다는 생각이 들었고, 내가 지켜보는 동안에도 그가 마지막으로 한 번 더 몸을 굽혀 그녀의 뺨에 입을 맞추는 것을 보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There were three married couples and Jordan’s escort, a persistent undergraduate given to violent innuendo, and obviously under the impression that sooner or later Jordan was going to yield him up her person to a greater or lesser degree.
examples.translation_ko: 세 쌍의 부부와 조던의 에스코트가 있었는데, 그는 격렬한 빈정거림을 일삼는 끈질긴 대학생으로, 조던이 조만간 어느 정도든 자신에게 몸을 맡길 것이라고 확신하고 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: With his disinterested passion for art, he had a real desire to call the attention of the wise to a talent which was in the highest degree original; but he was too good a journalist to be unaware that the “human interest” would enable him more easily to effect his purpose.
examples.translation_ko: 예술에 대한 사심 없는 열정으로, 그는 최고도로 독창적인 재능에 현명한 이들의 관심을 끌고자 하는 진정한 욕망을 가지고 있었다. 하지만 그는 너무나 훌륭한 저널리스트여서 '인간적 흥미'가 자신의 목적을 더 쉽게 달성하게 해줄 것임을 모르지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Small restaurants serving coffee and light meals.

senses.gloss: plural of café

examples.text: His acquaintances resented the fact that he turned up in popular cafés with her and, leaving her at a table, sauntered about, chatting with whomsoever he knew.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 지인들은 그가 인기 있는 카페에 그녀와 함께 나타나서는 그녀를 테이블에 남겨두고 아는 사람이면 누구와든 수다를 떨며 어슬렁거리는 것을 못마땅해했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “There are more cafés in Paris than one, at which to trifle away an idle hour.”
examples.translation_ko: "파리에는 한가한 시간을 보낼 수 있는 카페가 한 곳만 있는 것은 아니니까요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: And when such as had come in contact with Strickland in the past, writers who had known him in London, painters who had met him in the cafés of Montmartre, discovered to their amazement that where they had seen but an unsuccessful artist, like another, authentic genius had rubbed shoulders with them there began to appear in the magazines of France and America a succession of articles, the reminiscences of one, the appreciation of another, which added to Strickland’s notoriety, and fed without satisfying the curiosity of the public.
examples.translation_ko: 과거에 스트릭랜드와 접촉했던 사람들, 런던에서 그를 알았던 작가들, 몽마르트르의 카페에서 그를 만났던 화가들이 자신들이 그저 또 다른 실패한 예술가로만 보았던 곳에서 진정한 천재가 어깨를 스쳤다는 사실을 놀랍게 발견하자, 프랑스와 미국의 잡지들에 연이어 기사들이 나타나기 시작했다. 한 사람의 회상, 다른 사람의 평가가 스트릭랜드의 명성을 더했고, 대중의 호기심을 만족시키지는 못한 채 부채질했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English feden, from Old English fēdan (“to feed”), from Proto-West Germanic *fōdijan, from Proto-Germanic *fōdijaną (“to feed”), from P...
definition_en: Provide food for animals or a machine.

senses.gloss: To give (someone or something) food to eat.
senses.example: Feed the dog every evening.

senses.gloss: To eat (usually of animals).
senses.example: Spiders feed on gnats and flies.

senses.gloss: To give (someone or something) to (someone or something else) as food.
senses.example: Don't feed him too much; he's still a baby.

examples.text: I told her that if she wanted writers she must feed them well.”
examples.translation_ko: 작가들을 초대하려면 잘 먹여야 한다고 그녀에게 말했거든요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She raised his head to give him food, and it was heavy against her hand; when she had fed him she wiped his sensual mouth and his red beard.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그에게 음식을 먹이려고 그의 머리를 들어올렸는데, 그것은 그녀의 손에 무겁게 기대어졌다. 그에게 음식을 먹인 후 그녀는 그의 관능적인 입과 붉은 수염을 닦아주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *tréyes
From the Middle English verb protesten, from Old French protester, from Latin prōtestārī, from prō + testor, from testis (“witnes...
definition_en: A public expression of dissent or disapproval.

senses.gloss: To make a strong objection.
senses.example: How dare you, I protest!

senses.gloss: To affirm (something).
senses.example: I protest my innocence.

senses.gloss: To object to.

examples.text: It is the protest of romance against the commonplace of life.
examples.translation_ko: 이는 평범한 삶에 맞서는 낭만의 항거이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She flashed a smile at me, and, protesting an engagement with her dentist, jauntily walked on.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 나에게 미소를 번뜩 지어 보이고는, 치과 의사와 약속이 있다고 변명하며 경쾌하게 걸어갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Late Latin īrōnicus, from Ancient Greek εἰρωνικός (eirōnikós). Compare Middle French, ironique, equivalent to irony + -ic.
definition_en: Contrasting or incongruous with what is expected.

senses.gloss: Characterized by or constituting (any kind of) irony.
senses.example: It's somewhat ironic to have a wave of smog right on Earth Day.

senses.gloss: Odd or coincidental; strange.
senses.example: It's ironic that we are eating a sandwich in Sandwich, Massachusetts.

senses.gloss: Acting in an unserious and teasing manner.
senses.example: Don't take it personally. We're just being ironic.

examples.text: His eyes had an ironic smile in them.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 눈에는 비꼬는 듯한 미소가 떠올라 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I think there would have been something ironic in the picture of the successful old man, rich and honoured, living in another the life which he, though knowing it was the better part, had not had the strength to pursue.
examples.translation_ko: 성공한 늙은이가 부유하고 존경받으며 살면서, 더 나은 길임을 알면서도 추구할 힘이 없었던 삶을 다른 사람 안에서 살아가는 모습에는 뭔가 아이러니한 것이 있었을 것이라고 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From obscure + -ly.
definition_en: In a way that is not clearly understood.

senses.gloss: In an obscure manner.

examples.text: Blinking away the brightness of the street outside, my eyes picked him out obscurely in the anteroom, talking to another man.
examples.translation_ko: 밖 거리의 밝은 빛을 깜빡이며 떨쳐내자, 내 눈에 어렴풋이 들어온 것은 대기실에서 다른 남자와 이야기를 나누고 있는 그의 모습이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was when curiosity about Gatsby was at its highest that the lights in his house failed to go on one Saturday night—and, as obscurely as it had begun, his career as Trimalchio was over.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비에 대한 호기심이 절정에 달했을 때, 어느 토요일 밤 그의 집에 불이 켜지지 않았다—그리고 그토록 모호하게 시작되었듯이, 트리말키오로서의 그의 경력도 끝이 났다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Charles Strickland lived obscurely.
examples.translation_ko: 찰스 스트릭랜드는 무명으로 살았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English historian, historien, from Old French historien, from Latin historia (“story, history”), equivalent to history + -ian. More at ...
definition_en: A person who studies and writes about history.

senses.gloss: A writer of history.
One who studies or researches history.
senses.example: If this is what real people and societies are like, then it may be appropriate for historians to represent their subjects' lives in storylike form.

senses.gloss: One who recounts their own medical history.
senses.example: The patient is unconscious when the syncopal event takes place and therefore is a poor historian.

examples.text: But a wise historian is precisely what the Rev. Robert Strickland is not.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 로버트 스트릭랜드 목사는 정확히 현명한 역사가가 아니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In due course a legend arose of such circumstantiality that the wise historian would hesitate to attack it.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 너무나 구체적인 전설이 생겨나서, 현명한 역사가라면 그것을 공격하기를 주저할 정도가 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From consider + -able.
definition_en: Of a size or amount that is noticeable or significant.

senses.gloss: Significant; worth considering.
senses.example: Soon I became a considerable figure in the music industry.

senses.gloss: Large in amount.
senses.example: With the cutting out of the previous recovery times for electrification work, curtailment of station times and acceleration, considerable reductions have been made in the overall schedules.

examples.text: The sharp jut of a wall accounted for the detachment of the wheel, which was now getting considerable attention from half a dozen curious chauffeurs.
examples.translation_ko: 벽의 날카로운 돌출부가 바퀴 분리의 원인이었는데, 그 바퀴는 지금 호기심 많은 운전사 여섯 명으로부터 상당한 관심을 받고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Sometimes a man survives a considerable time from an era in which he had his place into one which is strange to him, and then the curious are offered one of the most singular spectacles in the human comedy.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 어떤 사람이 자신의 자리가 있던 시대에서 낯선 시대로 상당한 시간을 버텨내며 살아남기도 하는데, 그러면 호기심 많은 이들에게 인간 희극에서 가장 기이한 광경 중 하나가 제공된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He wrote his biography[3] avowedly to “remove certain misconceptions which had gained currency” in regard to the later part of his father’s life, and which had “caused considerable pain to persons still living.”
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아버지 생애의 후반부에 관해 "널리 퍼진 특정한 오해들을 불식시키고" "아직 생존해 있는 사람들에게 상당한 고통을 안겨준" 것들을 바로잡기 위해 공공연히 전기를 썼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English comunly; equivalent to common + -ly.
definition_en: Used or done by most people.

senses.gloss: As a rule; frequently; usually.
In common; familiarly.

examples.text: It is obvious that there was much in the commonly received account of Strickland’s life to embarrass a respectable family.
examples.translation_ko: 일반적으로 알려진 스트릭랜드의 생애에는 점잖은 가문을 당황시킬 만한 내용이 많았다는 것이 분명하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He made one laugh sometimes by speaking the truth, but this is a form of humour which gains its force only by its unusualness; it would cease to amuse if it were commonly practised.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 때로 진실을 말함으로써 사람들을 웃게 만들었지만, 이런 형태의 유머는 그 드문 성격으로만 힘을 얻는 것이어서, 만약 흔히 행해진다면 재미를 잃을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French embarrasser (“to embarrass; to block, obstruct”), from Spanish embarazar, from Portuguese embaraçar, from em- (“in”) (from Lat...
definition_en: Make someone feel ashamed or foolish.

senses.gloss: to humiliate; to disrupt somebody's composure or comfort with acting publicly or freely; to abash.
senses.example: The crowd's laughter and jeers embarrassed him.

senses.gloss: To hinder from liberty of movement; to impede; to obstruct.
senses.example: The motion was advanced in order to embarrass the progress of the bill.

senses.gloss: To involve in difficulties concerning money matters; to encumber with debt; to beset with urgent claims or demands.
senses.example: A man or his business is embarrassed when he cannot meet his pecuniary engagements.

examples.text: “You’re just embarrassed, that’s all,” and luckily I added: “Daisy’s embarrassed too.”
examples.translation_ko: "그냥 당황한 거야, 그게 다야." 그리고 다행히 나는 덧붙였다. "데이지도 당황하고 있어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It is obvious that there was much in the commonly received account of Strickland’s life to embarrass a respectable family.
examples.translation_ko: 일반적으로 알려진 스트릭랜드의 생애에는 점잖은 가문을 당황시킬 만한 내용이 많았다는 것이 분명하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Sometimes he embarrassed his wife, and the only time I saw her put out of countenance was when he insisted on telling me that he had taken a purge, and went into somewhat realistic details on the subject.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 그가 아내를 당황하게 만들었는데, 내가 그녀가 얼굴을 붉히는 것을 본 유일한 때는 그가 자신이 설사약을 먹었다고 고집스럽게 내게 말하면서 그 주제에 대해 다소 사실적인 세부사항까지 늘어놓았을 때였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
Borrowed from Middle French amusement, from amuser + -ment.
Morphologically amuse + -ment
definition_en: A feeling of enjoyment or entertainment.

senses.gloss: Entertainment.
senses.example: To my great amusement, the dog kept on chasing its tail and yelped when it bit it.

senses.gloss: An activity that is entertaining or amusing, such as dancing, gunning, or fishing.
senses.example: "What a charming amusement for young people this is, Mr. Darcy! There is nothing like dancing after all. I consider it as one of the first refinements of polished society."

examples.text: Once there they were introduced by somebody who knew Gatsby, and after that they conducted themselves according to the rules of behaviour associated with an amusement park.
examples.translation_ko: 일단 그곳에 가면 개츠비를 아는 누군가가 소개해주었고, 그 후로는 놀이공원에서 통용되는 행동 규칙에 따라 행동했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I noticed that now and then his eyes rested on me with a faint smile of amusement.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그의 눈이 때때로 희미한 재미있다는 듯한 미소와 함께 나에게 머물러 있는 것을 알아챘다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I have read this work with a good deal of amusement, and upon this I congratulate myself, since it is colourless and dull.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이 작품을 상당히 재미있게 읽었는데, 이는 축하할 일이다. 왜냐하면 이 책은 무미건조하고 따분하기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested in 1548; borrowed from Latin congrātulātus, the perfect active participle of Latin grātulor (“to wish joice, rejoice (with); to cong...
definition_en: Express warm congratulations to someone.

senses.gloss: To express one’s sympathetic pleasure or joy to the person(s) it is felt for; to felicitate.
senses.example: Remind me to congratulate Dave and Lisa on their wedding.

senses.gloss: To consider oneself fortunate in some matter.
senses.example: I congratulated myself on the success of my plan.

examples.text: Mrs. Strickland might congratulate herself that her party was a success.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인은 자신의 파티가 성공적이라고 자축해도 좋았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I have read this work with a good deal of amusement, and upon this I congratulate myself, since it is colourless and dull.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이 작품을 상당히 재미있게 읽었는데, 이는 축하할 일이다. 왜냐하면 이 책은 무미건조하고 따분하기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English science, scyence, borrowed from Old French science, escience, from Latin scientia (“knowledge”), from sciens, the present parti...
definition_en: The study of the natural world based on evidence.

senses.gloss: A particular discipline or branch of knowledge that is natural, measurable or consisting of systematic principles rather than intuition or technical skill.
senses.example: Of course in my opinion Social Studies is more of a science than an art.

senses.gloss: Specifically the natural sciences.
senses.example: My favorite subjects at school are science, mathematics, and history.

senses.gloss: Knowledge gained through study or practice; mastery of a particular discipline or area.
senses.example: Shakespeare's deep and accurate science in mental philosophy

examples.text: Maybe you don’t believe that, but science—”
examples.translation_ko: 믿지 않을지도 모르지만, 과학이—"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “—And we’ve produced all the things that go to make civilization—oh, science and art, and all that.
examples.translation_ko: "—그리고 우리는 문명을 이루는 모든 것들을 만들어냈다—오, 과학과 예술, 그런 모든 것들을 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The modern clergyman has acquired in his study of the science which I believe is called exegesis an astonishing facility for explaining things away, but the subtlety with which the Rev. Robert Strickland has “interpreted” all the facts in his father’s life which a dutiful son might find it inconvenient to remember must surely lead him in the fullness of time to the highest dignities of the Church.
examples.translation_ko: 현대의 성직자들은 주석학이라고 불리는 학문 연구를 통해 사물을 해명해버리는 놀라운 능력을 습득했지만, 로버트 스트릭랜드 목사가 효성스러운 아들로서 기억하기 불편할 수 있는 아버지 생애의 모든 사실들을 "해석"해낸 그 교묘함은 분명 때가 되면 그를 교회의 최고 지위에 올려놓을 것이다.

etymology: From Middle English facilite, from Middle French facilité, and its source, Latin facilitās. By surface analysis, facile + -ity. Doublet of faculty.
definition_en: A building or equipment that provides a particular service.

senses.gloss: The fact of being easy, or easily done; absence of difficulty; simplicity.
senses.example: Clytomachus affirmed, that he could never understand by the writings of Carneades, what opinion he was of. Why hath Epicurus interdicted facility unto his Sectaries?

senses.gloss: Dexterity of speech or action; skill, talent.
senses.example: The facility she shows in playing the violin is unrivalled.

senses.gloss: The physical means or contrivances to make something (especially a public service) possible; the required equipment, infrastructure, location etc.
senses.example: Transport facilities in Bangkok are not sufficient to prevent frequent traffic collapses during rush hour.

examples.text: As a matter of fact, he had no such facilities—he had no comfortable family standing behind him, and he was liable at the whim of an impersonal government to be blown anywhere about the world.
examples.translation_ko: 사실 그에게는 그런 능력이 없었다—그를 뒷받침해줄 든든한 가문도 없었고, 비정한 정부의 변덕에 따라 세계 어디든 날려갈 수 있는 처지였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Tiaré mingled French with English in her conversation, for she used both languages with equal facility.
examples.translation_ko: 티아레는 대화할 때 프랑스어와 영어를 섞어서 썼는데, 두 언어 모두 똑같이 능숙하게 구사했다.

etymology: From Middle English galant, galaunt, from Old French galant (“courteous; dashing; brave”), present participle of galer (“to rejoice; make merry”), ...
definition_en: Showing courage and courtesy.

senses.gloss: Brave, valiant, courteous, especially with regard to male attitudes towards women.
senses.example: That gallant spirit hath aspired the clouds.

senses.gloss: honorable.
grand, noble.

examples.text: These gallant words which seem so novel to those that speak them were said in accents scarcely changed a hundred times before.
examples.translation_ko: 말하는 이들에게는 참신해 보이는 이런 용감한 말들이 이미 백 번도 더 거의 똑같은 억양으로 되풀이되었던 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I saw him, the sea gray under the mistral and foam-flecked, watching the vanishing coast of France, which he was destined never to see again; and I thought there was something gallant in his bearing and dauntless in his soul.
examples.translation_ko: 미스트랄 바람 아래 회색빛을 띤 바다에 거품이 일렁이는 가운데, 다시는 보지 못할 운명인 프랑스 해안이 사라져가는 것을 바라보는 그의 모습이 눈에 보였다. 그리고 그의 자세에는 용감함이, 그의 영혼에는 불굴의 정신이 있다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English chele, chile, from Old English ċiele, ċele (“cold; coldness”), from Proto-West Germanic *kali, from Proto-Germanic *kaliz, from...
definition_en: A feeling of coldness or a state of being calm and relaxed.

senses.gloss: A moderate, but uncomfortable and penetrating coldness.
senses.example: There was a chill in the air.

senses.gloss: A sudden penetrating sense of cold, especially one that causes a brief trembling nerve response through the body; the trembling response itself; often associated with illness: fevers and chills, or susceptibility to illness.
senses.example: Close the window or you'll catch a chill.

senses.gloss: An uncomfortable and numbing sense of fear, dread, anxiety, or alarm, often one that is sudden and usually accompanied by a trembling nerve response resembling the body's response to biting cold.
senses.example: Despite the heat, he felt a chill as he entered the crime scene.

examples.text: I was a little chilled by Mrs. Strickland’s exclusiveness.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 스트릭랜드 부인의 배타적인 태도에 다소 서늘함을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It chilled me a little that Mrs. Strickland should be concerned with gossip, for I did not know then how great a part is played in women’s life by the opinion of others.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인이 남의 시선을 의식한다는 사실이 나를 다소 서늘하게 했는데, 당시 나는 다른 사람들의 평가가 여성의 삶에서 얼마나 큰 비중을 차지하는지 알지 못했기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham
