definition_en: A tool with a heavy head used for pounding or breaking.

senses.gloss: A tool with a heavy head and a handle used for pounding.
senses.example: Bobby used a hammer and nails to fix the two planks together

senses.gloss: The act of using a hammer to hit something.
senses.example: The nail is too loose—give it a hammer.

senses.gloss: The malleus, a small bone of the middle ear.

examples.text: And on Mondays eight servants, including an extra gardener, toiled all day with mops and scrubbing-brushes and hammers and garden-shears, repairing the ravages of the night before.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 월요일마다 정원사 한 명을 추가로 포함해 여덟 명의 하인들이 걸레와 솔과 망치와 정원 가위를 들고 하루 종일 애써서 전날 밤의 참상을 복구했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I wondered if the poor devil had been hammered on the Stock Exchange or run over by an omnibus.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그 불쌍한 자가 증권거래소에서 큰 손실을 입었거나 마차에 치였나 하고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is due to no accident that when one of his most important works, The Woman of Samaria,[4] was sold at Christie’s shortly after the discussion which followed the publication of Mr. Strickland’s biography, it fetched £235 less than it had done nine months before when it was bought by the distinguished collector whose sudden death had brought it once more under the hammer.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 씨의 전기 출간 이후 벌어진 논란 직후 그의 가장 중요한 작품 중 하나인 《사마리아 여인》이 크리스티 경매장에서 팔렸을 때, 9개월 전 저명한 수집가가 구입했을 때보다 235파운드나 낮은 가격을 기록한 것은 결코 우연이 아니다. 그 수집가의 갑작스러운 죽음으로 이 작품이 다시 경매대에 오르게 된 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French originalité. By surface analysis, original + -ity.
definition_en: The quality of being original and unique.

senses.gloss: The quality of being original or novel.
The capacity to think independently or be inventive.
senses.example: Originality may be the capacity to look at the same facts and see new explanations.

senses.gloss: Something original.

examples.text: I think that my taste is good, but I am conscious that it has no originality.
examples.translation_ko: 내 취향이 좋다고 생각하지만, 독창성이 없다는 것을 의식하고 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I wish I could say that I recognised at once their beauty and their great originality.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그 그림들의 아름다움과 위대한 독창성을 단번에 알아보았다고 말할 수 있으면 좋겠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English brusshe, from Old French broisse (Modern French brosse), from Vulgar Latin *brustia, from Frankish *bursti, from Proto-Germanic...
definition_en: To clean or smooth a surface with a brush.

senses.gloss: An implement consisting of multiple more or less flexible bristles or other filaments attached to a handle, used for any of various purposes including cleaning, painting, and arranging hair.
The act of brushing something.
senses.example: She gave her hair a quick brush.

senses.gloss: A piece of conductive material, usually carbon, serving to maintain electrical contact between the stationary and rotating parts of a machine.

examples.text: Tough Bill not only paid for the canvas, colours, and brushes, but gave Strickland a pound of smuggled tobacco into the bargain.
examples.translation_ko: 터프 빌은 캔버스와 물감, 붓값을 지불했을 뿐만 아니라 덤으로 밀수 담배 1파운드까지 스트릭랜드에게 주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Perhaps Charles Strickland’s power and originality would scarcely have sufficed to turn the scale if the remarkable mythopoeic faculty of mankind had not brushed aside with impatience a story which disappointed all its craving for the extraordinary.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 찰스 스트릭랜드의 힘과 독창성만으로는 균형을 뒤바꾸기에 충분하지 않았을 것이다. 만약 인류의 놀라운 신화 창조 능력이 비범한 것에 대한 모든 갈망을 실망시키는 이야기를 성급하게 밀어내지 않았다면 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English impacience, from Old French impacience (modern French impatience), from Latin impatientia. By surface analysis, im- +...
definition_en: A feeling of irritation or annoyance at having to wait.

senses.gloss: The quality of being impatient; lacking patience; restlessness and intolerance of delays; anxiety and eagerness, especially to begin something.

examples.text: He remembered how often he had waited for a minute or two on the landing to get his breath after the ascent, and how absurdly his impatience to see Blanche had taken it away again.
examples.translation_ko: 계단을 오르고 나서 숨을 고르기 위해 층계참에서 1, 2분 기다리곤 했던 일들이 떠올랐고, 블랑슈를 보고 싶은 조급함이 그 숨을 다시 가쁘게 만들었던 것도 우스울 정도였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I tried to persuade myself than an obscure feeling of revolt had been gradually coming to a head in his slow mind, but to challenge this was the undoubted fact that he had never shown any impatience with the monotony of his life.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 둔한 정신 속에서 막연한 반항심이 서서히 고조되어 왔다고 스스로를 설득해보려 했지만, 이에 반박하는 명백한 사실은 그가 자신의 단조로운 삶에 대해 한 번도 조바심을 보인 적이 없다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French desapointer (compare French désappointer); .
definition_en: To fail to meet someone's expectations or hopes.

senses.gloss: To sadden or displease (someone) by underperforming, or by not delivering something promised or hoped for.
senses.example: His lack of respect disappointed her.

senses.gloss: To deprive (someone of something expected or hoped for).
senses.example: Disappointed of immediate promotion he was now more … well, relaxed […]

senses.gloss: To fail to meet (an expectation); to fail to fulfil (a hope).
senses.example: […] a change in prices and rewards, as measured in money, generally affects different classes unequally […] and redistributes Fortune’s favours so as to frustrate design and disappoint expectation.

examples.text: It was sharply different from the West, where an evening was hurried from phase to phase towards its close, in a continually disappointed anticipation or else in sheer nervous dread of the moment itself.
examples.translation_ko: 서부와는 확연히 달랐다. 서부에서는 저녁이 단계를 거쳐 종료를 향해 서둘러 흘러갔고, 그 과정은 끊임없이 실망스러운 기대감이나 아니면 그 순간 자체에 대한 순전한 신경질적 공포로 점철되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: During the evening we played innumerable games of piquet, and bravely, not to disappoint my efforts, he tried to appear interested.
examples.translation_ko: 저녁에는 끝없이 피케 게임을 했고, 내 노력을 헛되게 하지 않으려고 용감하게 관심 있는 척 애썼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Perhaps Charles Strickland’s power and originality would scarcely have sufficed to turn the scale if the remarkable mythopoeic faculty of mankind had not brushed aside with impatience a story which disappointed all its craving for the extraordinary.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 찰스 스트릭랜드의 힘과 독창성만으로는 균형을 뒤바꾸기에 충분하지 않았을 것이다. 만약 인류의 놀라운 신화 창조 능력이 비범한 것에 대한 모든 갈망을 실망시키는 이야기를 성급하게 밀어내지 않았다면 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English palme, from Old English palm, palma (“palm-tree, palm-branch”), from Latin palma (“palm-tree, palm-branch, palm of the hand”), ...
definition_en: The inner surface of the hand.

senses.gloss: Any of various evergreen trees from the family Palmae or Arecaceae, which are mainly found in the tropics.
A branch or leaf of the palm, anciently borne or worn as a symbol of victory or rejoicing.
senses.example: A great multitude […] stood before the throne, and before the Lamb, clothed with white robes, and palmes in their hands.

senses.gloss: Triumph; victory.

examples.text: He reached in his pocket, and a piece of metal, slung on a ribbon, fell into my palm.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 주머니에 손을 넣더니 리본에 매달린 금속 조각 하나가 내 손바닥에 떨어졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The pirate birds were screeching among the leaves of the palms.
examples.translation_ko: 해적새들이 야자수 잎사귀 사이에서 날카롭게 울어댔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Behind is a tropical Landscape with palm-trees, bananas, etc. 60 in.
examples.translation_ko: 뒤편에는 야자수, 바나나 등이 있는 열대 풍경이 펼쳐져 있다. 60인치.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English malicious, from Old French malicios, from Latin malitiōsus, from malitia (“malice”), from malus (“bad”). Displaced native Middl...
definition_en: Having or showing a wish to do harm to others.

senses.gloss: Intending to do harm; characterized by spite and malice.
senses.example: He was sent off for a malicious tackle on Jones.

examples.text: I had never heard her more malicious about our common friends.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 우리 공통 친구들에 대해 그토록 악의에 찬 말을 하는 것을 들어본 적이 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Strickland’s eyes rested on him, and there was in them a malicious expression.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드의 눈이 그에게 머물렀고, 그 안에는 악의적인 표정이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + lucky.
definition_en: Having or showing a tendency to experience bad luck.

senses.gloss: Unfortunate, marked by misfortune.
senses.example: By random chance alone, 99 times out of 100, the Lions should have won an NFL or NFC championship. Worse for arguably the league’s unluckiest fan base, the Lions haven’t really been competitive.

senses.gloss: Inauspicious.
Having ill luck.

examples.text: Dirk Stroeve was one of those unlucky persons whose most sincere emotions are ridiculous.
examples.translation_ko: 더크 스트루브는 가장 진실한 감정조차 우스꽝스럽게 보이는 불운한 사람들 중 하나였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But the bed I made up for myself was sufficiently uncomfortable to give me a wakeful night, and I thought a good deal of what the unlucky Dutchman had told me.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 내가 마련한 잠자리는 충분히 불편해서 밤새 잠을 설쳤고, 나는 그 불운한 네덜란드인이 내게 들려준 이야기를 곰곰히 생각해보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested around 1300. From Middle English acusen, from Old French acuser, from Latin accūsō (“to call to account, accuse”), from ad (“to”) + ...
definition_en: To blame or charge someone with a wrongdoing.

senses.gloss: To find fault with, blame, censure.
senses.example: We are accused of having persuaded Austria and Sardinia to lay down their arms when their differences might have involved the Powers of Europe in contention.

senses.gloss: To charge with having committed a crime or offence.
senses.example: For the U.S. President to be impeached, he must be accused of a high crime or misdemeanor.

senses.gloss: To make an accusation against someone.

examples.text: “I do leave it alone,” affirmed the accused hollowly.
examples.translation_ko: "나는 내버려두고 있어요." 비난받은 여자가 공허하게 단언했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The abnormal mind is quick to detect and attach itself to this quality when it appears in a normal person, and so it came about that in college I was unjustly accused of being a politician, because I was privy to the secret griefs of wild, unknown men.
examples.translation_ko: 비정상적인 정신은 이런 자질이 정상적인 사람에게서 나타날 때 재빨리 알아채고 달라붙는 법이어서, 대학 시절 나는 정치꾼이라는 부당한 누명을 썼다. 거칠고 낯선 남자들의 은밀한 고통을 알고 있었기 때문이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And on the strength of peccadillos, reprehensible in an author, but excusable in a son, the Anglo-Saxon race is accused of prudishness, humbug, pretentiousness, deceit, cunning, and bad cooking.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 작가로서는 비난받을 만하지만 아들로서는 용서할 만한 사소한 잘못들을 근거로, 앵글로색슨 민족은 경직성, 허위, 허세, 기만, 교활함, 그리고 형편없는 요리 실력으로 고발당한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From pretentious + -ness.
definition_en: Excessive pride or self-importance.

senses.gloss: The quality of being pretentious.
senses.example: Possibly her sheer pretentiousness, or that she knew everything about everything, or maybe because she treated her reporters like underoxygenated platypies.

examples.text: His pretentiousness will only expose his vacuity.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 허세는 오직 그의 공허함만을 드러낼 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I think in those days we were a little shy of our emotions, and the fear of ridicule tempered the more obvious forms of pretentiousness.
examples.translation_ko: 그 시절 우리는 감정 표현에 다소 수줍어했고, 조롱당할까 하는 두려움이 노골적인 허세를 누그러뜨렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cunning, kunning, konnyng, alteration of earlier Middle English cunninde, kunnende, cunnand, from Old English cunnende, present...
definition_en: A clever or skillful person.

senses.gloss: Sly; crafty; clever in surreptitious behaviour.
senses.example: They are resolved to be cunning; let others run the hazard of being sincere.

senses.gloss: Skillful, artful.
senses.example: Tis beauty truly blent, whose red and white / Nature's own sweet and cunning hand laid on.

senses.gloss: Wrought with, or exhibiting, skill or ingenuity; ingenious.
senses.example: cunning work

examples.text: He was very cunning, but it was evidently this that he was aiming at.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 매우 교활했지만, 분명히 이것이 그가 노리는 바였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was dexterous to make him comfortable, and he exercised a cunning of which I should never have thought him capable to induce him to take the medicines prescribed by the doctor.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 스트릭랜드를 편안하게 해주는 데 능숙했고, 의사가 처방한 약을 먹도록 유도하기 위해 내가 그에게서 전혀 기대하지 못했을 교활함을 발휘했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Ancient Greek ἐνθουσιαστικός (enthousiastikós), from either ἐνθουσιασμός (enthousiasmós) or ἐνθουσιάζω (enthousiázō) + -τικός (-tikós).
definition_en: Showing a lot of enthusiasm and interest.

senses.gloss: With zealous fervor; excited, motivated.
senses.example: an enthusiastic lover of art

senses.gloss: Relating to enthusiasm, or divine possession.

examples.text: The bar is in full swing, and floating rounds of cocktails permeate the garden outside, until the air is alive with chatter and laughter, and casual innuendo and introductions forgotten on the spot, and enthusiastic meetings between women who never knew each other’s names.
examples.translation_ko: 바는 한창 붐비고 있었고, 칵테일을 든 무리들이 바깥 정원으로 떠다니며 스며들어, 공기는 수다와 웃음소리, 그리고 무심한 풍자와 그 자리에서 잊혀지는 소개, 서로의 이름도 모르는 여자들 사이의 열광적인 만남으로 살아 숨쉬고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Dr. Weitbrecht-Rotholz was an enthusiastic admirer of Charles Strickland, and there was no danger that he would whitewash him.
examples.translation_ko: 바이트브레히트-로톨츠 박사는 찰스 스트릭랜드의 열렬한 찬미자였으므로, 그가 스트릭랜드를 미화할 위험은 전혀 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When I left Rome I corresponded with him, and about once in two months received from him long letters in queer English, which brought before me vividly his spluttering, enthusiastic, gesticulating conversation.
examples.translation_ko: 로마를 떠난 후 나는 그와 편지를 주고받았는데, 두 달에 한 번 정도 그로부터 이상한 영어로 쓰인 긴 편지를 받았고, 그 편지는 더듬거리며 열정적으로 몸짓을 섞어가며 나누던 그의 대화를 생생하게 떠올리게 해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Late Latin dēspicābilis, from Latin dēspicor, a variant of dēspiciō (“I despise”), from de (“down”) + speciō (“I look at, behold”). First atte...
definition_en: Extremely wicked or contemptible.

senses.gloss: Fit or deserving to be despised; contemptible; mean.
senses.example: The physical penis is consumed by despicable fish, animals of the turgid depths, but the higher phallus, the image of resurrection through the goddess, is fashioned as a sacred icon.

examples.text: Somehow, that seemed a despicable occupation.
examples.translation_ko: 어쩐지 그것은 비열한 일처럼 보였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: You have a despicable character.”
examples.translation_ko: 당신은 비열한 성격의 소유자니까요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had an unerring eye for the despicable motive in actions that had all the appearance of innocence.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 순진해 보이는 행동들 속에서 비열한 동기를 찾아내는 데 있어 절대 틀리지 않는 안목을 가지고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English confounden (“destroy, ruin, perplex”), from Anglo-Norman cunfundre and Old French confondre, from Latin cōnfundō (“to mingle, m...
definition_en: To confuse or puzzle someone.

senses.gloss: To perplex or puzzle.
To stun or amaze.
To fail to see the difference; to mix up; to confuse right and wrong.

examples.text: But there was a change in Gatsby that was simply confounding.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 개츠비에게는 정말 당황스러운 변화가 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: If he is well enough to paint, he is well enough to have come down to Taravao and save me this confounded walk.
examples.translation_ko: 그림을 그릴 만큼 건강하다면, 타라바오까지 내려와서 나로 하여금 이 빌어먹을 걸음을 걷지 않게 할 만큼은 건강한 거 아닌가.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His heart warms to him when he can bring forward some example of cruelty or meanness, and he exults like an inquisitor at the auto da fé of an heretic when with some forgotten story he can confound the filial piety of the Rev. Robert Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 잔혹함이나 비열함의 사례를 제시할 수 있을 때면 그의 마음이 따뜻해지고, 잊혀진 이야기로 로버트 스트릭랜드 목사의 효성을 당황시킬 수 있을 때면 마치 종교재판관이 이단자의 화형식에서 환호하듯 의기양양해한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French transaction, from Old French transaccion, from Late Latin transactio.
definition_en: A financial or commercial deal.

senses.gloss: The act of conducting or carrying out (business, negotiations, plans).
senses.example: The transaction was made on Friday with the supplier.

senses.gloss: A deal or business agreement.
An exchange or trade, as of ideas, money, goods, etc.
senses.example: I made the transaction with the vendor as soon as she showed me the pearls.

examples.text: I wondered if this partnership had included the World’s Series transaction in 1919.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이 동업 관계에 1919년 월드시리즈 거래도 포함되어 있었는지 궁금했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The transactions in Montana copper that made him many times a millionaire found him physically robust but on the verge of soft-mindedness, and, suspecting this, an infinite number of women tried to separate him from his money.
examples.translation_ko: 그를 수백만장자로 만들어준 몬태나 구리 거래는 그의 몸은 건장하게 만들었지만 정신은 나약해지기 직전까지 몰고 갔고, 이를 눈치챈 수많은 여자들이 그의 돈을 빼앗으려 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Nothing has been too small to escape him, and you may be sure that if Charles Strickland left a laundry bill unpaid it will be given you in extenso, and if he forebore to return a borrowed half-crown no detail of the transaction will be omitted.
examples.translation_ko: 아무리 사소한 것도 그의 눈을 피해가지 못했으며, 찰스 스트릭랜드가 세탁비를 미납했다면 그것도 빠짐없이 상세히 기록될 것이고, 빌린 반크라운을 돌려주지 않았다면 그 거래의 어떤 세부사항도 빠뜨리지 않을 것이라고 확신해도 좋다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: At least by 1422, from late Middle English omitten, borrowed from Latin omittō (“to let go”), from ob- + mittō (“to send”), but also had the connot...
definition_en: Leave out or exclude something.

senses.gloss: To leave out or exclude.
To fail to perform.
To delete or remove; to strike.
senses.example: In the Criminal Justice and Public Order Act 1994, omit sections 146(4) and 147(3) (homosexual acts as grounds for dismissal from the crew of merchant ships).

examples.text: He had omitted nothing that could make his wife despise him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아내로 하여금 자신을 경멸하게 만들 수 있는 것이라면 하나도 빠뜨리지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He regretted that he had done this, and blamed himself that he had omitted the other.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 이것을 했던 것을 후회하고, 저것을 빠뜨린 것을 자책했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + necessary.
definition_en: Not needed or required.

senses.gloss: Not needed or necessary.
senses.example: The automatic child-frightener made clowns unnecessary.

senses.gloss: Done in addition to requirements; unrequired.

examples.text: The flowers were unnecessary, for at two o’clock a greenhouse arrived from Gatsby’s, with innumerable receptacles to contain it.
examples.translation_ko: 꽃은 필요 없었다. 두 시에 개츠비네에서 온실이 도착했는데, 꽃을 담을 그릇들이 셀 수 없이 많았기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When so much has been written about Charles Strickland, it may seem unnecessary that I should write more.
examples.translation_ko: 찰스 스트릭랜드에 대해 이미 그토록 많은 글이 쓰였는데, 내가 더 쓸 필요가 있을까 싶기도 하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I thought it unnecessary to say anything of Ata and her boy, but for the rest I was as accurate as I could be.
examples.translation_ko: 아타와 그녀의 아들에 대해서는 굳이 말할 필요가 없다고 생각했지만, 나머지는 가능한 한 정확하게 전했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From infrequent + -ly or in- + frequently.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something happens or is done not often.

senses.gloss: Not frequently.

examples.text: During the summer I met Mrs. Strickland not infrequently.
examples.translation_ko: 여름 동안 나는 스트릭랜드 부인을 자주 만났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I saw Strickland not infrequently, and now and then played chess with him.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 스트릭랜드를 자주 만났고, 가끔 그와 체스를 두기도 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French narratif.
definition_en: A story or account of events.

senses.gloss: Telling a story.
Overly talkative; garrulous.
senses.example: But wise through time, and narrative with age.

senses.gloss: Of or relating to narration.
senses.example: the narrative thrust of a film

examples.text: Tiaré broke off her narrative and addressed herself to me reflectively.
examples.translation_ko: 티아레는 이야기를 멈추고 생각에 잠긴 채 나에게 말을 건넸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But I wish I could give here the pictures, coloured and racy, which Captain Nichols’ vivid narrative offered to the imagination.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 니콜스 선장의 생생한 이야기가 상상력에 제공했던 그 다채롭고 흥미진진한 그림들을 여기서 보여줄 수 있다면 좋겠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English refuge, from Old French refuge, from Latin refugium, from re- + fugiō (“flee”). Doublet of refugium.
definition_en: A place of safety or shelter.

senses.gloss: A state of safety, protection or shelter.
senses.example: Rocks, dens, and caves! But I in none of these / Find place or refuge.

senses.gloss: A place providing safety, protection or shelter.
Something or someone turned to for safety or assistance; a recourse or resort.
senses.example: Since its conception, the European Union has been a haven for those seeking refuge from war, persecution and poverty in other parts of the world.

examples.text: But I seek refuge in no such excuses.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 나는 그런 변명에 기대지 않는다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I left him the last word, and sought refuge in a shrug of the shoulders and taciturnity.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 마지막 말을 양보하고, 어깨를 으쓱하며 침묵 속으로 도피했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English publicen (by analogy with banish, finish), from Old French publier, from Latin publicare (“to make public, show or tell to the ...
definition_en: To make information or a work known to the public.

senses.gloss: To issue (something, such as printed work) for distribution and/or sale.
senses.example: The Times published the investigative piece about the governor both in print and online.

senses.gloss: To announce to the public.
senses.example: The Secretary of Health and Human Services published a press release on May 22, 2013.

senses.gloss: To issue the work of (an author).
senses.example: Grove Press published many avant-garde authors.

examples.text: The fact that gossip had published the banns was one of the reasons I had come East.
examples.translation_ko: 소문이 결혼 예고를 발표해버린 것이 내가 동부로 온 이유 중 하나였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It may be that among them a more fervid Keats, a more ethereal Shelley, has already published numbers the world will willingly remember.
examples.translation_ko: 그들 중에는 더욱 열정적인 키츠, 더욱 천상적인 셸리가 이미 세상이 기꺼이 기억할 작품들을 발표했을지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is a salutary discipline to consider the vast number of books that are written, the fair hopes with which their authors see them published, and the fate which awaits them.
examples.translation_ko: 얼마나 많은 책들이 쓰이는지, 저자들이 얼마나 희망에 부풀어 출간을 바라보는지, 그리고 그 책들을 기다리는 운명이 무엇인지 생각해보는 것은 유익한 수행이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English awaiten, from Old Northern French awaitier (“to lie in wait for, watch, observe”), originally especially with a hostile sense; ...
definition_en: To expect or wait for something to happen.

senses.gloss: To wait for.
senses.example: I await your reply to my letter.

senses.gloss: To expect.
To be in store for; to be ready or in waiting for.
senses.example: Glorious rewards await the good in heaven; eternal suffering awaits mortal sinners in hell.

examples.text: Then she flounced over to the dog, kissed it with ecstasy, and swept into the kitchen, implying that a dozen chefs awaited her orders there.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 개에게 뛰어가서 황홀하게 입을 맞추고는 부엌으로 휩쓸려 들어갔는데, 마치 그곳에서 수십 명의 요리사가 자신의 명령을 기다리고 있다는 듯했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Honours and wealth awaited him.
examples.translation_ko: 명예와 부가 그를 기다리고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is a salutary discipline to consider the vast number of books that are written, the fair hopes with which their authors see them published, and the fate which awaits them.
examples.translation_ko: 얼마나 많은 책들이 쓰이는지, 저자들이 얼마나 희망에 부풀어 출간을 바라보는지, 그리고 그 책들을 기다리는 운명이 무엇인지 생각해보는 것은 유익한 수행이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English composicioun, borrowed from Old French composicion, from Latin compositiō, compositiōnem.
definition_en: A combination of different elements to create a whole.

senses.gloss: The act of putting together; assembly.
A mixture or compound; the result of composing.
The proportion of different parts to make a whole.
senses.example: And as for the perfume which thou shalt make, ye shall not make to yourselves according to the composition thereof: it shall be unto thee holy for the Lord.

examples.text: The nature of Mr. Tostoff’s composition eluded me, because just as it began my eyes fell on Gatsby, standing alone on the marble steps and looking from one group to another with approving eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 토스토프 씨의 작품이 어떤 성격인지는 알 수 없었다. 곡이 시작되자마자 내 시선이 개츠비에게 향했기 때문이다. 그는 대리석 계단에 홀로 서서 이 무리 저 무리를 흡족한 눈으로 바라보고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: From floor to ceiling the walls were covered with a strange and elaborate composition.
examples.translation_ko: 바닥부터 천장까지 벽면은 기이하고 정교한 구성으로 뒤덮여 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: And if I may judge from the reviews, many of these books are well and carefully written; much thought has gone to their composition; to some even has been given the anxious labour of a lifetime.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 서평들로 판단해보건대, 이런 책들 중 많은 수가 잘 쓰이고 정성스럽게 쓰인 것들이다. 구성에 많은 생각이 들어갔고, 어떤 것들에는 평생에 걸친 애타는 노력이 바쳐지기까지 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English aught, ought, from Old English āht, āwiht, from ā (“always", "ever”) + wiht (“thing", "creature”). More at wight.
definition_en: A small amount or quantity.

senses.gloss: Anything whatsoever, any part.
senses.example: There was Eru, the One, who in Arda is called Ilúvatar; and he made first the Ainur, the Holy Ones, that were the offspring of his thought, and they were with him before aught else was made.

examples.text: But I should be thrice a fool if I did it for aught but my own entertainment.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 내 자신의 즐거움이 아닌 다른 목적으로 그런다면 나는 세 번이나 바보가 될 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Nor is it vouchsafed to man in the flesh to know aught that more nearly suggests the approach to the golden realms of fancy than the approach to Tahiti.
examples.translation_ko: 육신을 지닌 인간에게는 환상의 황금 영역으로 다가가는 것보다 더 가깝게 느껴지는 것을 아는 것이 허락되지 않으니, 그것은 바로 타히티로 다가가는 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French tumultuous (modern French tumultueux), from Latin tumultuōsus (“restless, turbulent”), from tumultus (“disturbance, uproar, violent...
definition_en: Characterized by or marked by loud and violent disturbance.

senses.gloss: Characterized by loud, confused noise.
senses.example: "Flynn! Flynn! Mike Flynn!" came surging a tumultuous roar from the crowd.

senses.gloss: Causing or characterized by tumult; chaotic, disorderly, turbulent.
senses.example: In his first address to a joint session of Congress, after a tumultuous first month in office, Mr [Donald] Trump delivered a conventional speech in a conventional manner.

examples.text: Fifty feet from the door a dozen headlights illuminated a bizarre and tumultuous scene.
examples.translation_ko: 문에서 오십 피트 떨어진 곳에서 십여 개의 헤드라이트가 기괴하고 소란스러운 광경을 비추고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The prolonged and tumultuous argument that ended by herding us into that room eludes me, though I have a sharp physical memory that, in the course of it, my underwear kept climbing like a damp snake around my legs and intermittent beads of sweat raced cool across my back.
examples.translation_ko: 우리를 그 방으로 몰아넣은 길고 소란스러운 논쟁의 내용은 기억나지 않지만, 그 과정에서 내 속옷이 축축한 뱀처럼 다리를 타고 올라왔고 간헐적으로 땀방울이 등을 시원하게 흘러내렸다는 생생한 신체적 기억은 남아 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The younger generation, conscious of strength and tumultuous, have done with knocking at the door; they have burst in and seated themselves in our seats.
examples.translation_ko: 자신들의 힘을 자각하고 격정적인 젊은 세대는 문을 두드리는 일 따위는 그만두었다. 그들은 문을 부수고 들어와 우리 자리에 앉아 버렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English foreseen, forseen, from Old English foresēon; equivalent to fore- + see. Similar formations in Dutch voorzien, German vorsehen,...
definition_en: Predict or anticipate something.

senses.gloss: To perceive (a situation or event) in advance.
senses.example: "I foresee in this," he says, "the breaking up of our profession."

senses.gloss: To provide.
senses.example: Great shoals of people, which go on to populate, without foreseeing means of life.

examples.text: “I foresee some terrible catastrophe.”
examples.translation_ko: "끔찍한 재앙이 닥칠 것 같아요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They remember that they too trod down a sated generation, with just such clamor and with just such scorn, and they foresee that these brave torch-bearers will presently yield their place also.
examples.translation_ko: 그들도 한때 바로 그런 소란과 바로 그런 경멸로 물린 세대를 짓밟았음을 기억하고, 이 용감한 횃불 든 자들도 머지않아 자신들의 자리를 내주게 되리라는 것을 내다본다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English accent, from Medieval Latin accentus and Old French accent, acent, both from Latin accentus, past participle of accinō (“sing t...
definition_en: A distinctive way of pronouncing a language.

senses.gloss: A higher-pitched or stronger (louder or longer) articulation of a particular syllable of a word or phrase in order to distinguish it from the others or to emphasize it.
senses.example: In the word "careful", the accent is placed on the first syllable.

senses.gloss: Emphasis or importance in general.
senses.example: At this hotel, the accent is on luxury.

senses.gloss: A mark or character used in writing, in order to indicate the place of the spoken accent, or to indicate the nature or quality of the vowel marked.
senses.example: The name Cézanne is written with an acute accent.

examples.text: She spoke them with a singing accent which was not unpleasing.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 노래하듯 억양을 넣어 말했는데, 그것이 불쾌하지는 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: These gallant words which seem so novel to those that speak them were said in accents scarcely changed a hundred times before.
examples.translation_ko: 말하는 이들에게는 참신해 보이는 이런 용감한 말들이 이미 백 번도 더 거의 똑같은 억양으로 되풀이되었던 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English renderen, rendren, from Old French rendre (“render, give back”), from Late Latin rendere, from Latin reddere (“make, give back”).
definition_en: To make or provide something that is needed.

senses.gloss: To cause to become.
senses.example: The shot rendered her immobile.

senses.gloss: To interpret, give an interpretation or rendition of.
senses.example: The pianist rendered the Beethoven sonata beautifully.

senses.gloss: To translate into another language.
senses.example: to render Latin into English

examples.text: But, because the offer was obviously and tactlessly for a service to be rendered, I had no choice except to cut him off there.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그 제안이 명백히 그리고 무례하게도 어떤 봉사를 해달라는 것이었기 때문에, 나는 그 자리에서 그를 말리는 것 외에는 선택의 여지가 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I thought that was the best service I could render him.
examples.translation_ko: 그것이 내가 그에게 해줄 수 있는 최선의 도움이라고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was a famous poet in his day, and the world recognised his genius with a unanimity which the greater complexity of modern life has rendered infrequent.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 당대의 유명한 시인이었고, 세상은 현대 생활의 복잡성으로 인해 드물어진 만장일치로 그의 천재성을 인정했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English willyngly, wyllyngly (“intentionally, deliverately; freely, gladly”), from Old English willendlīċe (“diligently”), equivalent t...
definition_en: Done or made with a willingness to do something.

senses.gloss: Of one’s own free will; freely and spontaneously.
senses.example: Now this is a process of the mind or thought, of which I would willingly know the foundation.

examples.text: He accepted willingly my invitation to remain for a few days in my apartment.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 며칠간 내 아파트에 머물자는 내 제안을 기꺼이 받아들였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She saw shrewdly that the world is quickly bored by the recital of misfortune, and willingly avoids the sight of distress.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 세상이 불행담을 듣는 것을 금세 지겨워하고 고통받는 모습을 기꺼이 외면한다는 것을 예리하게 간파하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested from 1300, from Middle English merveile, from Old French merveille (“a wonder”), from Vulgar Latin *miribilia, from Latin mīrābilia ...
definition_en: Be amazed or astonished.

senses.gloss: That which causes wonder; a prodigy; a portent.
senses.example: The mysteries of this wonderful universe rise more palpable upon the departing spirit, so soon to mingle with their marvels.

senses.gloss: wonder, astonishment.
senses.example: Use lessens marvel.

examples.text: Perhaps some unbelievable guest would arrive, a person infinitely rare and to be marvelled at, some authentically radiant young girl who with one fresh glance at Gatsby, one moment of magical encounter, would blot out those five years of unwavering devotion.
examples.translation_ko: 어쩌면 믿을 수 없는 손님이 도착할지도 모른다. 무한히 드물고 경탄할 만한 사람, 개츠비를 향한 신선한 한 번의 시선으로, 마법 같은 만남의 한 순간으로 흔들림 없는 다섯 해의 헌신을 지워버릴 진정으로 빛나는 젊은 여인이.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I admire their polish—their youth is already so accomplished that it seems absurd to speak of promise—I marvel at the felicity of their style; but with all their copiousness (their vocabulary suggests that they fingered Roget’s Thesaurus in their cradles)
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그들의 세련됨을 감탄한다—그들의 젊음은 이미 너무나 완성되어 있어서 장래성을 운운하는 것조차 우스꽝스러워 보인다—나는 그들 문체의 적절함에 경탄한다. 하지만 그 모든 풍부함에도 불구하고 (그들의 어휘력을 보면 요람에서부터 로제의 유의어 사전을 만지작거렸던 것 같다)
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The conversation proceeded, and I marvelled at the tact with which Mr. Van Busche Taylor avoided all subjects that might have been in the least embarrassing, and at the ingenuity with which Mrs. Strickland, without saying a word that was untrue, insinuated that her relations with her husband had always been perfect.
examples.translation_ko: 대화가 이어졌고, 나는 반 부셰 테일러 씨가 조금이라도 난처할 수 있는 모든 주제를 피해가는 재치와, 스트릭랜드 부인이 거짓말은 한 마디도 하지 않으면서도 남편과의 관계가 항상 완벽했다고 넌지시 암시하는 교묘함에 감탄했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Learned borrowing from Medieval Latin vocābulārium. Doublet of vocabularium.
definition_en: A collection of words and their meanings.

senses.gloss: A usually alphabetized and explained collection of words e.g. of a particular field, or prepared for a specific purpose, often for learning.
The collection of words a person knows and uses.
senses.example: My Russian vocabulary is very limited.

senses.gloss: The stock of words used in a particular field.
senses.example: The vocabulary of social sciences is often incomprehensible to ordinary people.

examples.text: I recognised my friend’s limited vocabulary, and I prepared to regard Captain Nichols as a trustworthy witness.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 내 친구의 제한된 어휘를 알아차렸고, 니콜스 선장을 믿을 만한 증인으로 여길 준비가 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I admire their polish—their youth is already so accomplished that it seems absurd to speak of promise—I marvel at the felicity of their style; but with all their copiousness (their vocabulary suggests that they fingered Roget’s Thesaurus in their cradles)
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그들의 세련됨을 감탄한다—그들의 젊음은 이미 너무나 완성되어 있어서 장래성을 운운하는 것조차 우스꽝스러워 보인다—나는 그들 문체의 적절함에 경탄한다. 하지만 그 모든 풍부함에도 불구하고 (그들의 어휘력을 보면 요람에서부터 로제의 유의어 사전을 만지작거렸던 것 같다)
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English trifle, trifel, triful, trefle, truyfle, trufful, from Old French trufle (“mockery”), a byform of trufe, truffe (“deception”), ...
definition_en: Not very important or serious.

senses.gloss: An English dessert made from a mixture of thick custard, fruit, sponge cake, jelly and whipped cream.
senses.example: It is interesting to watch the surface joviality on screen while racism is layered between courses like soggy trifles.

senses.gloss: Anything that is of little importance or worth.
senses.example: ‘And all about a rattle!’ said Alice, still hoping to make them a little ashamed of fighting for such a trifle.

senses.gloss: An insignificant amount of money.
senses.example: “It was bad of me then not to send the fifteen hundred dollars. I assumed it would be a trifle.” / “Well, until a few months ago it was a trifle.”

definition_en: Honest and straightforward in speech or actions.

senses.gloss: Impartial and free from prejudice.

senses.gloss: Straightforward, open and sincere.
senses.example: Sam Altman, the chief executive and co-founder of OpenAI, has been ousted from his own company after its board accused him of “being not consistently candid in his communications”.

senses.gloss: Not posed or rehearsed.
senses.example: Will the introduction of supplementary flash or flood intrude on a candid picture situation or ruin the mood?

examples.text: He had his mother’s candid brow and fine, reflective eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 어머니의 솔직한 이마와 아름답고 사려 깊은 눈을 닮았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She looked at me with those pleasant eyes of hers, which had remained as candid and as sympathetic as they had been more than twenty years before.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 이십여 년 전과 똑같이 솔직하고 따뜻했던 그 다정한 눈으로 나를 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A large or excessive amount of something.

examples.text: There were the same people, or at least the same sort of people, the same profusion of champagne, the same many-coloured, many-keyed commotion, but I felt an unpleasantness in the air, a pervading harshness that hadn’t been there before.

examples.text: Ata’s father had planted crotons round his property, and they grew in coloured profusion, gay and brilliant; they fenced the land with flame.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Her hair, thick and dark like her mother’s, fell over her shoulders in fine profusion, and she had the same kindly expression and sedate, untroubled eyes.

examples.text: The rain poured down his thick glasses, and he took them off and wiped them to see the protecting canvas unrolled from Gatsby’s grave.
examples.translation_ko: 비가 그의 두꺼운 안경에 쏟아져 내렸고, 그는 안경을 벗어 닦으며 개츠비의 무덤을 덮은 방수포를 바라보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She said this not disparagingly, but affectionately rather, as though, by acknowledging the worst about him, she wished to protect him from the aspersions of her friends.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 이 말을 경멸조로 한 것이 아니라 오히려 애정을 담아 했다. 마치 그의 최악의 면을 인정함으로써 친구들의 비난으로부터 그를 보호하려는 듯했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: That is an emotion in which tenderness is an essential part, but Strickland had no tenderness either for himself or for others; there is in love a sense of weakness, a desire to protect, an eagerness to do good and to give pleasure—if not unselfishness, at all events a selfishness which marvellously conceals itself; it has in it a certain diffidence.
examples.translation_ko: 사랑이란 다정함이 필수적인 부분을 차지하는 감정인데, 스트릭랜드에게는 자신에 대해서든 타인에 대해서든 다정함이라는 것이 없었다. 사랑에는 나약함이 있고, 보호하고자 하는 욕구가 있으며, 선을 행하고 기쁨을 주려는 열망이 있다—비이기적이라고 할 수는 없을지라도, 적어도 놀랍도록 교묘하게 자신을 감추는 이기심이 있다. 사랑에는 어떤 수줍음이 깃들어 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Late Latin typicalis, from Latin typicus (“typical”), from Ancient Greek τυπικός (tupikós, “of or pertaining to a type, conformable, typical”)...
definition_en: Typical of something is what you would normally expect.

senses.gloss: Capturing the overall sense of a thing.
Characteristically representing something by form, group, idea or type.
Normal, average; to be expected.
senses.example: One typical Grecian kiln engorged one thousand muleloads of juniper wood in a single burn. Fifty such kilns would devour six thousand metric tons of trees and brush annually.

examples.text: “He’s on the Stock Exchange, and he’s a typical broker.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Each one talked to his neighbour; to his neighbour on the right during the soup, fish, and entree; to his neighbour on the left during the roast, sweet, and savoury.
examples.translation_ko: 각자 옆 사람과 이야기했다. 수프와 생선, 앙트레 요리 때는 오른쪽 옆 사람과, 로스트와 디저트, 짭짤한 요리 때는 왼쪽 옆 사람과 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A food or dish that is not sweet.

senses.gloss: Alternative form of savory.

examples.text: Each one talked to his neighbour; to his neighbour on the right during the soup, fish, and entree; to his neighbour on the left during the roast, sweet, and savoury.
examples.translation_ko: 각자 옆 사람과 이야기했다. 수프와 생선, 앙트레 요리 때는 오른쪽 옆 사람과, 로스트와 디저트, 짭짤한 요리 때는 왼쪽 옆 사람과 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: From morning till night you saw her sitting on a low chair in the kitchen, surrounded by a Chinese cook and two or three native girls, giving her orders, chatting sociably with all and sundry, and tasting the savoury messes she devised.
examples.translation_ko: 아침부터 밤까지 그녀는 부엌의 낮은 의자에 앉아 중국인 요리사 한 명과 원주민 소녀 두세 명에게 둘러싸인 채 지시를 내리고, 이런저런 사람들과 정겹게 수다를 떨며, 자신이 만들어낸 맛있는 요리들을 맛보고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French crédit (“belief, trust”), from Latin crēditum (“a loan, credit”), neuter of crēditus, past participle of crēdere (“to b...
definition_en: A form of recognition or reward for something done.

senses.gloss: To believe; to put credence in.
senses.example: Someone said there were over 100,000 people there, but I can't credit that.

senses.gloss: To add to an account.
senses.example: Credit accounts receivable with the amount of the invoice.

senses.gloss: To acknowledge the contribution of.
senses.example: I credit the town council with restoring the shopping district.

examples.text: I bought a dozen volumes on banking and credit and investment securities, and they stood on my shelf in red and gold like new money from the mint, promising to unfold the shining secrets that only Midas and Morgan and Maecenas knew.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 은행업과 신용과 투자증권에 관한 책을 열두 권 샀는데, 그것들은 조폐국에서 갓 나온 새 돈처럼 빨갛고 금빛으로 내 책장에 서 있으면서, 오직 미다스와 모건과 마이케나스만이 알고 있던 빛나는 비밀들을 펼쳐 보이겠다고 약속하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He showed a skill I should never have credited him with in finding the places where the unhappy Dutchman was most sensitive.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 불행한 네덜란드인이 가장 예민해하는 부분을 찾아내는 솜씨를 보여주었는데, 나는 그에게 그런 재능이 있으리라고는 전혀 생각지 못했었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I no longer wondered that Mrs. Strickland felt a certain embarrassment about him; he was scarcely a credit to a woman who wanted to make herself a position in the world of art and letters.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인이 그에 대해 어느 정도 당혹감을 느끼는 것이 더 이상 이상하지 않았다. 예술과 문학계에서 자신의 지위를 구축하려는 여성에게 그는 별로 도움이 되지 않는 남편이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French attractif, from Late Latin attractivus, equivalent to attract + -ive.
definition_en: Having a pleasing appearance or charm.

senses.gloss: Causing attraction; having the quality of attracting by inherent force.
Having the power of charming or alluring by agreeable qualities; enticing.
senses.example: That's a very attractive offer.

senses.gloss: Pleasing or appealing to the senses, especially of a potential romantic partner.
senses.example: He is an attractive fellow with a trim figure.

examples.text: I wondered what she found so attractive in Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 스트릭랜드에게서 무엇을 그토록 매력적으로 느끼는지 궁금했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They were even more attractive than their photographs had suggested, and she was right to be proud of them.
examples.translation_ko: 아이들은 사진에서 본 것보다 훨씬 더 매력적이었고, 그녀가 자랑스러워할 만했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English agreable, from Old French agreable. Equivalent to agree + -able.
definition_en: Pleasing or acceptable to someone.

senses.gloss: Able to agree; possible to be agreed.
senses.example: an agreeable contract

senses.gloss: Pleasant to the senses or the mind; pleasing, satisfying, palatable.
senses.example: a man with agreeable manners

senses.gloss: Willing; ready to agree or consent.
senses.example: These Frenchmen give unto the said captain of Calais a great sum of money, so that he will be but content and agreeable that they may enter into the said town.

examples.text: When anyone spoke to him he invariably laughed in an agreeable, colourless way.
examples.translation_ko: 누군가 그에게 말을 걸면 언제나 상냥하지만 특색 없는 방식으로 웃어댔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was very agreeable under the trees.
examples.translation_ko: 나무 아래는 매우 기분 좋았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: My friend’s appearance suggested that he was now in the same predicament, and I prepared myself to cultivate an agreeable acquaintance.
examples.translation_ko: 내 친구의 외모로 보아 지금도 같은 곤경에 처해 있는 것 같았고, 나는 유쾌한 지인 관계를 가꿔나갈 준비를 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From enormous + -ly.
definition_en: Extremely large or great in degree.

senses.gloss: Extremely, greatly: to an enormous degree.
senses.example: Gloria is enormously pleased with our progress.

senses.gloss: Shockingly.

examples.text: His family were enormously wealthy—even in college his freedom with money was a matter for reproach—but now he’d left Chicago and come East in a fashion that rather took your breath away: for instance, he’d brought down a string of polo ponies from Lake Forest.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 가문은 엄청나게 부유했다—대학 시절에도 그의 돈 쓰는 방식은 비난거리였다—하지만 이제 그는 시카고를 떠나 동부로 온 방식이 숨이 막힐 정도였다: 예를 들어, 레이크 포레스트에서 폴로 조랑말 한 떼를 끌고 내려온 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They had little private jokes of their own which, unintelligible to the outsider, amused them enormously.
examples.translation_ko: 그들만의 작은 농담들이 있었는데, 외부인에게는 이해할 수 없는 것들이었지만 그들 자신에게는 엄청나게 재미있는 것들이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Now that his influence has so enormously affected modern painting, now that others have charted the country which he was among the first to explore, Strickland’s pictures, seen for the first time, would find the mind more prepared for them; but it must be remembered that I had never seen anything of the sort.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 그의 영향력이 현대 회화에 엄청난 변화를 가져왔고, 이제 다른 화가들이 그가 최초로 탐험한 영역을 지도로 그려놓은 지금, 스트릭랜드의 그림들을 처음 보는 사람이라면 더 준비된 마음으로 받아들일 수 있을 것이다. 하지만 당시 나는 그런 류의 작품을 본 적이 전혀 없었다는 점을 기억해야 한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From uneasy + -ness.
definition_en: A feeling of unease or discomfort.

senses.gloss: The state of being uneasy, nervous or restless.
An anxious state of mind; anxiety.
senses.example: Finding that the afternoon coach was gone, and finding that his uneasiness grew into positive alarm, as obstacles came in his way, he resolved to follow in a post-chaise.

examples.text: When Dr. Coutras arrived at the plantation he was seized with a feeling of uneasiness.
examples.translation_ko: 쿠트라 박사가 농장에 도착했을 때 그는 불안한 기분에 사로잡혔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then a strange uneasiness would seize the Captain; he would look at his watch and sigh.
examples.translation_ko: 그러면 이상한 불안감이 선장을 사로잡았다. 그는 시계를 보고 한숨을 쉬었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From in- + calculable.
definition_en: Too great to be measured or calculated.

senses.gloss: Impossible to calculate.
Too much, too vast, or too numerous to enable computation.
senses.example: The loss the National Library suffered from the fire is incalculable.

senses.gloss: Of a person's mood or character, etc.: impossible to predict.
senses.example: He is incalculable when he's drunk. He can turn from an amiable person into a violent horror in a moment.

examples.text: What would happen now in the dim, incalculable hours?
examples.translation_ko: 이제 어둡고 헤아릴 수 없는 시간들 속에서 무슨 일이 일어날까?
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But because I have learnt that man is incalculable, I should not at this time of day be so surprised by the news that reached me when in the early autumn I returned to London.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 인간이란 예측할 수 없는 존재라는 것을 배웠기 때문에, 이른 가을 런던으로 돌아왔을 때 내게 전해진 소식에 지금이라면 그렇게 놀라지는 않을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But if one could be certain of nothing in dealing with creatures so incalculable as human beings, there were explanations of Blanche Stroeve’s behaviour which were at all events plausible.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 인간처럼 예측 불가능한 존재들을 다룰 때는 아무것도 확신할 수 없다 해도, 블랑슈 스트루브의 행동에 대해서는 최소한 그럴듯한 설명들이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French (voiture) omnibus (“(carriage) for all”), from Latin omnibus (“for all”), dative plural of omnis (“all”).
definition_en: A large public vehicle that carries many passengers.

senses.gloss: A bus (vehicle for transporting large numbers of people along roads).
senses.example: Baldrick, I want you to take this [money] and go out, and buy a turkey so large you'd think its mother had been rogered by an omnibus.

senses.gloss: An anthology of previously released material linked together by theme or author, especially in book form.
A broadcast programme consisting of all of the episodes of a serial that have been shown in the previous week.
senses.example: The omnibus edition of The Archers is broadcast every Sunday morning at 11.00.

examples.text: On weekends his Rolls-Royce became an omnibus, bearing parties to and from the city between nine in the morning and long past midnight, while his station wagon scampered like a brisk yellow bug to meet all trains.
examples.translation_ko: 주말이면 그의 롤스로이스가 버스가 되어 아침 아홉 시부터 자정을 훌쩍 넘어서까지 일행들을 도시로 실어 나르고 데려왔고, 그의 스테이션 왜건은 민첩한 노란 벌레처럼 분주히 돌아다니며 모든 기차를 마중했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: for theatres and newspapers, and the rumble of omnibuses on the cobbled pavements?’
examples.translation_ko: 극장이나 신문, 자갈길 위로 굴러가는 마차들의 소음 같은 것들 말입니다.'
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I wondered if the poor devil had been hammered on the Stock Exchange or run over by an omnibus.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그 불쌍한 자가 증권거래소에서 큰 손실을 입었거나 마차에 치였나 하고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French courbe (“curve, curved object”), from Latin curvus (“bent, crooked, curved”). Doublet of curve.
definition_en: A strip of metal fixed to the edge of a road or path.

senses.gloss: A concrete margin along the edge of a road; a kerb (UK, Australia, New Zealand)
A raised margin along the edge of something, such as a well or the eye of a dome, as a strengthening.
Something that checks or restrains; a restraint.
senses.example: The same also is that burning mention’d by S. Paul, whereof mariage ought to be the remedy; the Flesh hath other naturall and easie curbs which are in the power of any temperate man..

examples.text: I stopped at the curb.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 길가에 멈춰 섰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Miss Waterford certainly felt that she could not do her subject justice on the curb of Jermyn Street, and so, like an artist, flung the bare fact at me and declared that she knew no details.
examples.translation_ko: 워터포드 양은 저민 가의 길가에서는 자신의 화제를 제대로 다룰 수 없다고 생각했던 것이 분명했고, 그래서 예술가답게 나에게 사실만을 던져주고는 자세한 내용은 모른다고 단언했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English injustice, from Old French injustice, from Latin iniustitia. Equivalent to in- + justice. Displaced native Old English unrihtwī...
definition_en: The state of being unjust or unfair.

senses.gloss: Absence of justice; unjustice.
Violation of the rights of another person or people.
senses.example: Silence in the face of gross injustice, or support for it, or even active involvement therein, comes at a price.

senses.gloss: Unfairness; the state of not being fair or just.

examples.text: “He did me an injustice, for I too know what it is to have dreams.
examples.translation_ko: "그는 나를 오해했다. 나 역시 꿈이 무엇인지 알고 있으니까.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He hinted at undeserved misfortune, and there is no doubt that he looked upon himself as the victim of injustice.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 부당한 불행을 암시했고, 자신을 불의의 희생자로 여기고 있음에는 의심의 여지가 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English obstinat(e) (“obstinate, stubborn”), from Latin obstinātus, perfect passive participle of obstinō (“set one's mind fi...
definition_en: Refusing to change one's opinion or course of action.

senses.gloss: Stubbornly adhering to an opinion, purpose, or course, usually with implied unreasonableness; persistent.
senses.example: From this consideration it is that we have derived the custom, in times of war, to punish […] those who are obstinate to defend a place that by the rules of war is not tenable […]

senses.gloss: Not easily subdued or removed.
Typical of an obstinate person; fixed and unmoving.
senses.example: He had the same pile of curly hair, but he was clean-shaven with a heavy, obstinate jowl.

examples.text: Americans, while willing, even eager, to be serfs, have always been obstinate about being peasantry.
examples.translation_ko: 미국인들은 농노가 되는 것은 기꺼이, 심지어 열망하면서도, 소작농이 되는 것에 대해서는 언제나 완고하게 거부해왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I’m as obstinate as he is, and I’ll never divorce him.
examples.translation_ko: 나도 그 사람만큼 고집이 세니까, 절대 이혼해주지 않을 거야.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I could not do her the injustice of supposing that so trifling a circumstance would have prevented her from giving them, but she was obstinate.
examples.translation_ko: 그런 사소한 상황이 그녀가 세부사항을 말하는 것을 막았으리라고 생각하는 것은 그녀에게 불공평한 일이었지만, 그녀는 완고했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From jaunty + -ly.
definition_en: Done with a carefree and lighthearted air.

senses.gloss: In an airy, showy, or affected manner.
In a dapper or stylish manner.
In an ostentatiously self-confident manner.
senses.example: [He] walked quite jauntily across the courtyard to the distant door, his sandals clacking against the marble.

examples.text: Suddenly I wasn’t thinking of Daisy and Gatsby any more, but of this clean, hard, limited person, who dealt in universal scepticism, and who leaned back jauntily just within the circle of my arm.
examples.translation_ko: 갑자기 나는 더 이상 데이지와 개츠비를 생각하지 않고 있었다. 대신 이 깨끗하고 단단하고 한정적인 사람을, 보편적 회의주의를 다루며 내 팔이 그리는 원 안에서 당당하게 몸을 뒤로 기댄 이 사람을 생각하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She was dressed to play golf, and I remember thinking she looked like a good illustration, her chin raised a little jauntily, her hair the colour of an autumn leaf, her face the same brown tint as the fingerless glove on her knee.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 골프를 치러 가는 차림이었는데, 턱을 약간 경쾌하게 치켜들고, 머리카락은 가을 낙엽 색깔이며, 얼굴은 무릎 위에 놓인 손가락 없는 장갑과 같은 갈색 빛깔인 그녀가 마치 훌륭한 삽화 같다는 생각이 들었던 것을 기억한다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She flashed a smile at me, and, protesting an engagement with her dentist, jauntily walked on.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 나에게 미소를 번뜩 지어 보이고는, 치과 의사와 약속이 있다고 변명하며 경쾌하게 걸어갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Extremely surprised or shocked.

senses.gloss: Surprised, startled, confused, or taken aback, particularly when also indignant.
senses.example: We were shocked to see how ill she was.

senses.gloss: Suffering from shock.
senses.example: The patient is shocked.

senses.gloss: Affected, altered, or transformed by one or more shock waves.
senses.example: shocked quartz

examples.text: Daisy was not a Catholic, and I was a little shocked at the elaborateness of the lie.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지는 가톨릭 신자가 아니었기에, 나는 그 정교한 거짓말에 조금 충격을 받았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But, though they drew back the sheet and looked at Gatsby with shocked eyes, his protest continued in my brain:
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그들이 시트를 걷어내고 충격에 찬 눈으로 개츠비를 바라보는 동안에도, 그의 간청은 내 머릿속에서 계속 울려 퍼졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But I was a little shocked.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 나는 조금 충격을 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *úd
From Middle English utmost, utemest [and other forms], from Old English ūtmest, ūtemest [and other forms], from ūt, ūte (“out; outdoo...
definition_en: Greatest or most extreme degree.

senses.gloss: Situated at the most distant limit; farthest, outermost.
senses.example: the utmost limits of the land

senses.gloss: The most extreme; greatest, ultimate.
senses.example: the utmost assiduity

examples.text: “What do you mean?” cried Mrs. Strickland, with the utmost astonishment.
examples.translation_ko: "무슨 말씀이세요?" 스트릭랜드 부인이 극도로 놀라며 소리쳤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: With the superciliousness of extreme youth, I put thirty-five as the utmost limit at which a man might fall in love without making a fool of himself.
examples.translation_ko: 극도로 젊은 나이의 거만함으로, 나는 남자가 바보가 되지 않고 사랑에 빠질 수 있는 최대 한계를 서른다섯으로 잡았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French agitation, from Latin agitātiō (“movement, agitation”).
definition_en: A state of intense emotional excitement or disturbance.

senses.gloss: The act of agitating, or the state of being agitated; the state of being disrupted with violence, or with irregular action; commotion.
senses.example: During a storm the sea is in agitation.

senses.gloss: A disturbance of personal tranquillity; disturbance of someone's peace of mind.
senses.example: She causes great agitation within me.

senses.gloss: Excitement of public feeling by discussion, appeals, etc.
senses.example: the antislavery agitation

examples.text: As a rule she was so calm; her agitation now was amazing.
examples.translation_ko: 평소 그녀는 매우 침착했는데, 지금의 동요는 놀라울 정도였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was likely enough that in the agitation of the moment my note had escaped her memory.
examples.translation_ko: 그 순간의 동요 속에서 내 편지를 잊어버렸을 가능성이 충분했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From part + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is only partly true or applicable.

senses.gloss: In part, or to some degree, but not completely.
senses.example: They had partly finished the house, so they could move in before winter; the car was partly visible in the garage.

examples.text: There was a sound within, and the door was partly opened.
examples.translation_ko: 안에서 소리가 나더니 문이 조금 열렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The blinds were partly drawn to darken the room, and Mrs. Strickland was sitting with her back to the light.
examples.translation_ko: 방을 어둡게 하려고 블라인드가 반쯤 내려져 있었고, 스트릭랜드 부인은 등을 빛에 대고 앉아 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English interrupcioun, from Old French interrupcion, from Latin interruptio.
definition_en: A break or pause in a continuous activity.

senses.gloss: The act of interrupting, or the state of being interrupted.
the act of breaking into someone else’s speech.
A time interval during which there is a cessation of something.

examples.text: When, almost immediately, the telephone rang inside and the butler left the porch Daisy seized upon the momentary interruption and leaned towards me.
examples.translation_ko: 거의 즉시 집 안에서 전화벨이 울리고 집사가 현관을 떠나자, 데이지는 그 순간적인 중단을 틈타 내 쪽으로 몸을 기울였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I fancied that the Colonel resented the interruption.
examples.translation_ko: 대령이 방해받는 것을 못마땅해한다는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We arranged to spend an evening together for old time’s sake, and when I agreed to dine with him, he proposed that he should ask nobody else, so that we could chat without interruption.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 옛정을 나누며 저녁 시간을 함께 보내기로 했고, 내가 그와 식사하기로 하자 그는 다른 사람은 부르지 말자고 제안했다. 그래야 방해받지 않고 이야기할 수 있다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From re- + place.
definition_en: To put something in the place of another.

senses.gloss: To restore to a former place, position, condition, etc.; to put back.
senses.example: When you've finished using the telephone, please replace the handset.

senses.gloss: To refund; to repay; to pay back.
senses.example: You can take what you need from the petty cash, but you must replace it tomorrow morning.

senses.gloss: To supply or substitute an equivalent with.
senses.example: I replaced my car with a newer model.

examples.text: He snatched the book from me and replaced it hastily on its shelf, muttering that if one brick was removed the whole library was liable to collapse.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내게서 책을 낚아채더니 서둘러 제자리에 꽂으면서, 벽돌 하나만 빼내도 도서관 전체가 무너질 수 있다고 중얼거렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: My Finn informed me that Gatsby had dismissed every servant in his house a week ago and replaced them with half a dozen others, who never went into West Egg village to be bribed by the tradesmen, but ordered moderate supplies over the telephone.
examples.translation_ko: 내 핀란드인 가정부는 개츠비가 일주일 전에 집의 모든 하인들을 해고하고 여섯 명 정도의 다른 사람들로 교체했다고 알려주었는데, 이들은 상인들에게 매수당할 일이 없도록 웨스트에그 마을에 나가지 않고 전화로만 적당한 생필품을 주문했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There were no flowers, and various knick-knacks, put away during the summer, had not been replaced; there was something cheerless and stiff about the room which had always seemed so friendly; it gave you an odd feeling, as though someone were lying dead on the other side of the wall.
examples.translation_ko: 꽃도 없었고, 여름 동안 치워두었던 여러 장식품들도 제자리에 돌아오지 않았다. 언제나 그토록 친근하게 느껴졌던 방에는 뭔가 쓸쓸하고 경직된 분위기가 있었다. 마치 벽 너머에서 누군가 죽어 누워 있는 것 같은 기묘한 느낌을 주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From black + guard, thought to have referred originally to the scullions and lower menials of a court, or of a nobleman's household, who wore black...
definition_en: A contemptible or despicable person.

senses.gloss: The lowest servant in a household charged with pots, pans, and other kitchen equipment.
An unprincipled, contemptible person; an untrustworthy person.
A man who uses foul language in front of a woman (typically a woman of high standing).

examples.text: “All we know is that the blackguard’s gone to Paris.”
examples.translation_ko: "우리가 아는 건 그 악한이 파리로 갔다는 것뿐이야."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You don’t care if people think you an utter blackguard?
examples.translation_ko: "사람들이 당신을 완전한 악한이라고 생각해도 상관없다는 말입니까?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Used in English since the 16th century. Via Middle French moustache from Italian mostaccio, from Early Medieval Latin mustācium, from Byzantine Gre...
definition_en: A growth of hair on the upper lip.

senses.gloss: A growth of facial hair between the nose and the upper lip.
senses.example: The Stan Lee fly, or Daptolestes leei, which is said to share his characteristic sunglasses and white moustache

senses.gloss: A curly bracket, { or }.
senses.example: In this example, the first is a string of text that contains the name property in double curly brackets (or “mustaches”)—this is the syntax for a tag.

examples.text: I’d been writing letters once a week and signing them: “Love, Nick,” and all I could think of was how, when that certain girl played tennis, a faint moustache of perspiration appeared on her upper lip.
examples.translation_ko: 일주일에 한 번씩 편지를 써서 "사랑을 담아, 닉"이라고 서명해왔는데, 내가 생각할 수 있는 것이라고는 그 여자가 테니스를 칠 때 윗입술에 희미하게 맺히는 땀방울뿐이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was a tall, lean man of fifty, with a drooping moustache and grey hair.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 늘어진 콧수염과 회색 머리를 한 쉰 살의 키 크고 마른 남자였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was a very lean man, of no more than average height, with gray hair cut short and a stubbly gray moustache.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 매우 마른 사내로, 평균 키 정도였고, 회색 머리를 짧게 깎았으며 거칠거칠한 회색 콧수염을 기르고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Feeling great pleasure or joy.

senses.gloss: Greatly pleased.
senses.example: Number forty-seven said to number three: / You're the cutest jailbird I ever did see. / I sure would be delighted with your company. / Come on and do the jailhouse rock with me.

senses.gloss: Filled with wonder and delight.

examples.text: “Certainly; I’d be delighted to have you.”
examples.translation_ko: "물론이죠. 기꺼이 모셔드리겠습니다."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I shall be delighted to do it.”
examples.translation_ko: 기꺼이 하겠습니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then he gave a cry of delighted surprise and drew me in.
examples.translation_ko: 그러다가 기뻐하며 놀라는 소리를 지르고는 나를 안으로 끌어들였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English thrasshen, a dialectal variant of thresshen, threshen (whence the modern English thresh), from Old English þrescan, from Proto-...
definition_en: to hit or beat violently

senses.gloss: To beat mercilessly.
senses.example: But in the town it was well known, when they got home at night, their fat and psychopathic wives would thrash them within inches of their lives.

senses.gloss: To defeat utterly.
senses.example: Pardew made five changes to the side that thrashed West Ham 5-0 on Wednesday - with players such as James Perch and Alan Smith given the chance to underline their case for a regular starting berth.

senses.gloss: To thresh.

examples.text: I’d thrash him within an inch of his life.”
examples.translation_ko: 죽기 직전까지 두들겨 패 주겠어."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “My first husband, Captain Johnson, used to thrash me regularly.
examples.translation_ko: "내 첫 번째 남편인 존슨 선장은 나를 늘 때렸어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin dīrectus, perfect passive participle of dīrigō (“straighten, direct”), from dis- (“asunder, in pieces, apart, in two”) + regō (...
definition_en: Straightforward and to the point.

senses.gloss: Proceeding without deviation or interruption.
Straight; not crooked, oblique, or circuitous; leading by the short or shortest way to a point or end.
senses.example: the most direct route between two buildings

senses.gloss: Straightforward; sincere.
senses.example: Be even and direct with me.

examples.text: It was a matter upon which he was reticent, and with persons of his kind a direct question is never very discreet.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 이 문제에 대해 말을 아꼈고, 그런 부류의 사람들에게 직접적인 질문은 결코 신중하지 못한 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is always distressing when outraged morality does not possess the strength of arm to administer direct chastisement on the sinner.
examples.translation_ko: 분노한 도덕심이 죄인에게 직접적인 응징을 가할 만한 완력을 갖추지 못했을 때는 언제나 안타까운 법이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sinne, synne, sunne, zen, from Old English synn (“sin”), from Proto-West Germanic *sunnju, from Proto-Germanic *sunjō (“truth, ...
definition_en: The act of doing something considered wrong or immoral.

senses.gloss: A violation of divine will or religious law.
senses.example: As a Christian, I think this is a sin against God.

senses.gloss: Sinfulness, depravity, iniquity.
A misdeed or wrong.

examples.text: I did not then know the besetting sin of woman, the passion to discuss her private affairs with anyone who is willing to listen.
examples.translation_ko: 그때 나는 여자들의 고질적인 죄악, 즉 기꺼이 들어줄 사람이라면 누구에게든 자신의 사생활을 털어놓고 싶어 하는 열정을 알지 못했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The nurse looked at him with her calm, kind eyes, which had seen all the horror and pain of the world, and yet, filled with the vision of a world without sin, remained serene.
examples.translation_ko: 간호사는 세상의 모든 공포와 고통을 보아왔으면서도, 죄 없는 세상에 대한 환상으로 가득 차 여전히 평온함을 유지하고 있는 차분하고 친절한 눈으로 그를 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English assumpcioun, from Medieval Latin assumptio (“a taking up (into heaven)”) and Latin assumptio (“a taking up, adoption, the minor...
definition_en: The act of taking something for granted or assuming it to be true.

senses.gloss: The act of assuming, or taking to or upon oneself; the act of taking up or adopting.
senses.example: His assumption of secretarial duties was timely.

senses.gloss: The act of taking for granted, or supposing a thing without proof; a supposition; an unwarrantable claim.
senses.example: Their assumption of his guilt disqualified them from jury duty.

senses.gloss: The thing supposed; a postulate, or proposition assumed; a supposition.
senses.example: No doubt a finite evaluative argument must make some unargued evaluative assumptions, just as finite factual arguments must make some unargued factual assumptions.

examples.text: The supercilious assumption was that on Sunday afternoon I had nothing better to do.
examples.translation_ko: 일요일 오후에 내가 딱히 할 일이 없을 거라는 건방진 추정이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was taken aback by her assumption that I knew all about her domestic misfortune.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 그녀의 가정 불화에 대해 모든 것을 알고 있다고 단정하는 그녀의 태도에 나는 당황했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I am a little shy of any assumption of moral indignation; there is always in it an element of self-satisfaction which makes it awkward to anyone who has a sense of humour.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 도덕적 분노라는 것을 가정하는 일을 다소 꺼린다. 거기에는 언제나 자기만족의 요소가 들어있어서, 유머 감각이 있는 사람에게는 어색하게 느껴지기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From wan + -ly.
definition_en: In a weak or feeble manner.

senses.gloss: In a wan or pale manner.
senses.example: […] [he] spent a lot of time wanly imagining how warm and secure marriage must make men feel […]

examples.text: “Nothing happened,” he said wanly.
examples.translation_ko: "아무 일도 없었어." 그가 힘없이 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She smiled wanly.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 힘없이 미소를 지었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I made an appropriate rejoinder, and he smiled wanly.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 적절한 대답을 했고, 그는 쓸쓸하게 미소를 지었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English þrusten, from Old Norse þrysta, from Proto-Germanic *þrustijaną, possibly from Proto-Indo-European *trewd-.
definition_en: To push or drive something forward with force.

senses.gloss: An attack made by moving the sword parallel to its length and landing with the point.
senses.example: Pierre was a master swordsman, and could parry the thrusts of lesser men with barely a thought.

senses.gloss: A push, stab, or lunge forward (the act thereof.)
senses.example: The cutpurse tried to knock her satchel from her hands, but she avoided his thrust and yelled, "Thief!"

senses.gloss: The force generated by propulsion, as in a jet engine.
senses.example: Spacecraft are engineering marvels, designed to resist the thrust of liftoff, as well as the reverse pressure of the void.

examples.text: Since these confidences were thrust on me, I saw no harm in asking a few questions.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 비밀 이야기를 들려주는 마당에 몇 가지 질문을 해도 무방하다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She thrust into his hand a crumpled piece of newspaper, and when he opened it he found in it a hundred-franc note.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그의 손에 구겨진 신문지 조각을 밀어 넣었고, 그것을 펼쳐보니 안에 백 프랑 지폐가 들어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French improbable, from im- + probable.
definition_en: Unlikely to happen or exist.

senses.gloss: Not likely to be true.
senses.example: It's highly improbable that aliens abducted you.

senses.gloss: Not likely to happen.
senses.example: Due to the loss of power, it is improbable that we will begin on time.

examples.text: It seemed so improbable.
examples.translation_ko: 너무나 있을 법하지 않은 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was more than improbable; it was incredible.
examples.translation_ko: 있을 법하지 않은 정도가 아니라 믿을 수 없는 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English proof, from Old French prove, from Late Latin proba (“a proof”), from Latin probō (“to prove”); see prove; compare also the dou...
definition_en: Evidence or demonstration of something's existence or truth.

senses.gloss: An effort, process, or operation designed to establish or discover a fact or truth; an act of testing; a test; a trial.
senses.example:
France I more praise and love; you are, my lord,
Yourself for horsemanship much famed; and there
You shall have many proofs to shew your skill.

senses.gloss: The degree of evidence which convinces the mind of any truth or fact, and produces belief; a test by facts or arguments which induce, or tend to induce, certainty of the judgment; conclusive evidence; demonstration.
senses.example:
Faith, faith is an island in the setting sun
But proof, yes
Proof is the bottom line for everyone

senses.gloss: The quality or state of having been proved or tried; firmness or hardness which resists impression, or does not yield to force; impenetrability of physical bodies.

examples.text: “Well, the first thing is to get our proofs.
examples.translation_ko: "우선 증거부터 확보해야 해.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His cordiality was proof that he knew I had no wish to speak to him.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 다정한 태도는 내가 그와 말하고 싶어 하지 않는다는 것을 그가 알고 있다는 증거였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From direct + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is happening or being done immediately.

senses.gloss: In a direct manner; in a straight line or course.
senses.example: He drove directly to the office, and didn't stop off at the petrol station.

senses.gloss: In a straightforward way; without anything intervening; not by secondary but by direct means.
senses.example: I'm sick of asking you to fire him; I'll just do it directly.

senses.gloss: Plainly, without circumlocution or ambiguity; absolutely; in express terms.
senses.example: I'm going to tell Natalie directly that I love her.

examples.text: His eyes, meanwhile, roved very slowly all around the room—he completed the arc by turning to inspect the people directly behind.
examples.translation_ko: 한편 그의 눈은 방 안을 아주 천천히 훑었다—몸을 돌려 바로 뒤쪽 사람들까지 살펴보며 한 바퀴를 완성했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I drove from the station directly to Gatsby’s house and my rushing anxiously up the front steps was the first thing that alarmed anyone.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 역에서 곧장 개츠비의 집으로 차를 몰고 가서 불안하게 현관 계단을 뛰어올라갔는데, 그것이 누군가를 처음으로 놀라게 한 일이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She did not answer directly.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 직접적으로 대답하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Predicted or anticipated something.

senses.gloss: simple past of foresee

examples.text: Something impelled him to go to the studio, some obscure desire for self-torture, and yet he dreaded the anguish that he foresaw.
examples.translation_ko: 무언가가 그를 화실로 향하게 했다. 자기 자신을 괴롭히려는 어떤 막연한 욕망이었지만, 동시에 그는 예상되는 고통을 두려워했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Strickland seemed to bear in his heart strange harmonies and unadventured patterns, and I foresaw for him an end of torture and despair.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 마음속에 기묘한 화음과 아직 시도되지 않은 무늬들을 품고 있는 것 같았고, 나는 그에게 고통과 절망의 종말이 기다리고 있음을 예감했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A message or signal that warns of a possible danger.

senses.gloss: present participle of warn

examples.text: I was about to speak when she sat up alertly and said “Sh!” in a warning voice.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 말하려던 참에 그녀가 경계하듯 몸을 일으키며 경고하는 목소리로 "쉿!" 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I had no warning—nothing.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 아무런 경고도 받지 못했다—아무것도.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I could not imagine that he had had no warning.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 아무런 징조도 눈치채지 못했다는 것이 믿어지지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin recēns (genitive recentis).
definition_en: Happening or done not long ago.

senses.gloss: Having happened a short while ago.
Up-to-date; not old-fashioned or dated.
Having done something a short while ago that distinguishes them as what they are called.
senses.example: The cause has several hundred recent donors.

examples.text: In a basket swung from his neck cowered a dozen very recent puppies of an indeterminate breed.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 목에 걸린 바구니 안에는 품종을 알 수 없는 갓 태어난 강아지 십여 마리가 웅크리고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Accustomed to the drawing of the old masters, and convinced that Ingres was the greatest draughtsman of recent times, I thought that Strickland drew very badly.
examples.translation_ko: 고전 거장들의 소묘에 익숙하고 앵그르가 근세 최고의 소묘가라고 확신하던 나는 스트릭랜드가 그림을 매우 못 그린다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She went on, talking somewhat at random, now of the recent past, then of their first meeting and their marriage; but presently I began to form a fairly coherent picture of their lives; and it seemed to me that my surmises had not been incorrect.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 계속해서 다소 두서없이 이야기했는데, 때로는 최근 일들을, 때로는 그들의 첫 만남과 결혼에 대해 말했다. 하지만 곧 나는 그들의 삶에 대한 상당히 일관된 그림을 그릴 수 있게 되었고, 내 추측이 틀리지 않았던 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Clipping of adventure.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was never put out by Strickland’s rudeness; if it was merely sullen, he appeared not to notice it; if it was aggressive, he only chuckled.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I wondered what a stranger would have taken him to be, sitting there in his old Norfolk jacket and his unbrushed bowler; his trousers were baggy, his hands were not clean; and his face, with the red stubble of the unshaved chin, the little eyes, and the large, aggressive nose, was uncouth and coarse.
examples.translation_ko: 낡은 노퍽 재킷과 솔질하지 않은 중절모를 쓰고 그곳에 앉아 있는 그를 보고 낯선 사람이라면 무엇이라고 생각했을까 궁금했다. 바지는 헐렁했고, 손은 깨끗하지 않았으며, 면도하지 않은 턱의 붉은 수염, 작은 눈, 크고 공격적인 코가 있는 얼굴은 거칠고 조야했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: A coffin.

examples.text: I saw the skins of tigers flaming in his palace on the Grand Canal; I saw him opening a chest of rubies to ease, with their crimson-lighted depths, the gnawings of his broken heart.

examples.text: “Now that you’ve got that off your chest, let’s go and have dinner.”
