examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was an extraordinary figure, with his red beard and matted hair, and his great hairy chest.
examples.translation_ko: 붉은 수염과 헝클어진 머리, 그리고 털이 무성한 넓은 가슴을 한 그의 모습은 기이했다.

examples.text: I dare say it would have been more seemly to decline this proposal.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 제안을 거절하는 것이 더 체면에 맞았을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It seemed to me a little ungracious to decline an invitation of that sort, and I ascribed his refusal to lack of money.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: Feelings, especially tender feelings, as apart from reason or judgment, or of a weak or foolish kind.
senses.example: Good decision-making is not governed by mere sentiment.

examples.text: Certainly not those who expect from it only decorous sentiments and normal emotions.
examples.translation_ko: 분명히 마음에서 품위 있는 감정과 정상적인 감정만을 기대하는 사람들은 그럴 수 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a sweet and generous nature, and yet was always blundering; a real feeling for what was beautiful and the capacity to create only what was commonplace; a peculiar delicacy of sentiment and gross manners.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 다정하고 관대한 성품을 지녔으면서도 늘 실수를 저질렀고, 아름다운 것에 대한 진정한 감각을 가졌으면서도 평범한 것만 창조할 수 있는 능력밖에 없었으며, 독특하게 섬세한 감성과 조야한 매너를 함께 지니고 있었다.

senses.gloss: Strangely, oddly.

examples.text: Tom and Daisy stared, with that peculiarly unreal feeling that accompanies the recognition of a hitherto ghostly celebrity of the movies.
examples.translation_ko: 톰과 데이지는 지금까지 영화 속에서만 유령처럼 존재했던 유명인을 실제로 마주했을 때 느끼는 그 특유의 비현실적인 감정과 함께 그를 바라보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was balancing himself on the dashboard of his car with that resourcefulness of movement that is so peculiarly American—that comes, I suppose, with the absence of lifting work in youth and, even more, with the formless grace of our nervous, sporadic games.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자동차 계기판에 몸을 기대며 균형을 잡고 있었는데, 그 민첩한 몸놀림은 참으로 미국적이었다. 젊은 시절 육체노동을 하지 않았기 때문이겠지만, 더 나아가 우리의 신경질적이고 산발적인 게임들이 주는 형태 없는 우아함 때문이리라.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But the fear of not being able to carry it through effectively has always made me shy of assuming the moral attitude; and in this case the certainty that my sentiments would be lost on Strickland made it peculiarly embarrassing to utter them.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 효과적으로 해낼 수 없을지도 모른다는 두려움 때문에 나는 늘 도덕적 자세를 취하는 것을 꺼려했고, 이 경우에는 내 감정이 스트릭랜드에게 전혀 통하지 않을 것이 확실했기에 그것을 입 밖에 내는 것이 특히 난처했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: Very sure of something; positive.

senses.gloss: Self-assured, self-reliant, sure of oneself.

senses.example: I was rated as the most confident ruffian, for daring to approach her room at that hour of night.

examples.text: “The last one was the one I met you at,” answered the girl, in an alert confident voice.

examples.text: The groups change more swiftly, swell with new arrivals, dissolve and form in the same breath; already there are wanderers, confident girls who weave here and there among the stouter and more stable, become for a sharp, joyous moment the centre of a group, and then, excited with triumph, glide on through the sea-change of faces and voices and colour under the constantly changing light.

examples.translation_ko: 그것이 내가 그에게 한 유일한 칭찬이었다. 나는 처음부터 끝까지 그를 못마땅하게 여겼기 때문이다.

examples.text: “After all, it was rather a compliment she was paying you.”
examples.translation_ko: "결국 그녀가 당신에게 찬사를 보낸 것이나 다름없었잖소."

examples.text: “Anyhow, he gives large parties,” said Jordan, changing the subject with an urban distaste for the concrete.

examples.translation_ko: 인간이 자신의 유령 같은 마음속에 쌓아둘 수 있는 것에는 그 어떤 불길이나 신선함도 맞설 수 없다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A mango grew in front of the house, and at the edge of the clearing were two flamboyants, twin trees, that challenged the gold of the cocoa-nuts with their scarlet flowers.
examples.translation_ko: 집 앞에는 망고나무가 자라고 있었고, 개간지 가장자리에는 두 그루의 플람보얀트가 쌍둥이처럼 서서 주홍빛 꽃으로 코코넛의 황금빛에 맞서고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I tried to persuade myself than an obscure feeling of revolt had been gradually coming to a head in his slow mind, but to challenge this was the undoubted fact that he had never shown any impatience with the monotony of his life.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 둔한 정신 속에서 막연한 반항심이 서서히 고조되어 왔다고 스스로를 설득해보려 했지만, 이에 반박하는 명백한 사실은 그가 자신의 단조로운 삶에 대해 한 번도 조바심을 보인 적이 없다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *dwóh₁
From Middle English devisen, devysen, from Old French deviser, from Vulgar Latin devisō, from Latin dīvisō, frequentative of dīvidō.
definition_en: Plan or invent a new idea.

senses.gloss: To use one’s intellect to plan or design (something).
senses.example: to devise an argument; to devise a machine, or a new system of writing

senses.gloss: To leave (property) in a will.
To form a scheme; to lay a plan; to contrive; to consider.
senses.example: I thought, devised, and Pallas heard my prayer.

examples.text: I expect that Shakespeare devised Iago with a gusto which he never knew when, weaving moonbeams with his fancy, he imagined Desdemona.
examples.translation_ko: 셰익스피어가 달빛을 상상력으로 엮어 데스데모나를 창조할 때는 결코 느끼지 못했던 열정으로 이아고를 고안해냈으리라 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: At last, because I was romantic, I devised an explanation which I acknowledged to be far-fetched, but which was the only one that in any way satisfied me.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 낭만적인 성향의 나는 억지스럽다고 스스로 인정하면서도, 어떻게든 나를 만족시킬 수 있는 유일한 설명을 고안해냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *wréh₂ds
From Middle English rote, root, roote (“the underground part of a plant”), from late Old English rōt, from Old Norse rót (Icelan...
definition_en: To find the origin or cause of something.

senses.gloss: The part of a plant, generally underground, that anchors and supports the plant body, absorbs and stores water and nutrients, and in some plants is able to perform vegetative reproduction.
senses.example: This tree's roots can go as deep as twenty metres underground.

senses.gloss: A root vegetable.
senses.example: [...] two fields which should have been sown with roots in the early summer were not sown because the ploughing had not been completed early enough.

senses.gloss: The part of a tooth extending into the bone holding the tooth in place.
senses.example: Root damage is a common problem of overbrushing.

examples.text: The child, relinquished by the nurse, rushed across the room and rooted shyly into her mother’s dress.
examples.translation_ko: 유모가 놓아준 아이는 방을 가로질러 달려와서는 수줍게 어머니의 드레스에 얼굴을 묻었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But the doctor gave a gasp, he was rooted to the floor, and he stared with all his eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 의사는 숨을 헐떡이며 바닥에 뿌리박힌 듯 서서 눈을 크게 뜨고 응시했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was this: I asked myself whether there was not in his soul some deep-rooted instinct of creation, which the circumstances of his life had obscured, but which grew relentlessly, as a cancer may grow in the living tissues, till at last it took possession of his whole being and forced him irresistibly to action.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 이런 것이었다. 나는 그의 영혼 깊숙한 곳에 창조의 본능이 뿌리박혀 있었던 것은 아닐까 하고 자문해보았다. 그의 삶의 환경이 그 본능을 가려왔지만, 암이 살아있는 조직에서 자라나듯 그것이 무자비하게 성장하여 마침내 그의 존재 전체를 장악하고 그를 거부할 수 없는 행동으로 내몰았던 것은 아닐까.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Late Latin creativus, from Latin creō. Equivalent to create + -ive. Displaced native Old English orþanclīċ.
definition_en: Having or showing an ability to create new and original ideas.

senses.gloss: Tending to create things, or having the ability to create; often, excellently, in a novel fashion, or any or all of these.
senses.example: a creative dramatist who avoids cliche

senses.gloss: Original, expressive and imaginative.
senses.example: a creative new solution to an old problem

senses.gloss: A type of set of natural numbers, related to mathematical logic.
senses.example: a creative set

examples.text: He had thrown himself into it with a creative passion, adding to it all the time, decking it out with every bright feather that drifted his way.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 창조적인 열정으로 그 환상에 몸을 던졌고, 끊임없이 거기에 무언가를 보태면서, 자신에게 떠밀려 오는 모든 찬란한 깃털로 그것을 치장했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: This responsiveness had nothing to do with that flabby impressionability which is dignified under the name of the “creative temperament”—it was an extraordinary gift for hope, a romantic readiness such as I have never found in any other person and which it is not likely I shall ever find again.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 반응성은 "창조적 기질"이라는 이름으로 포장되는 그 나약한 감수성과는 아무 관련이 없었다. 그것은 희망에 대한 비범한 재능이었고, 내가 다른 어떤 사람에게서도 발견한 적이 없고 앞으로도 발견할 가능성이 없는 낭만적 준비 자세였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But how strange it was that the creative instinct should seize upon this dull stockbroker, to his own ruin, perhaps, and to the misfortune of such as were dependent on him; and yet no stranger than the way in which the spirit of God has seized men, powerful and rich, pursuing them with stubborn vigilance till at last, conquered, they have abandoned the joy of the world and the love of women for the painful austerities of the cloister.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 창조적 본능이 이 따분한 주식중개인을 사로잡아, 아마도 그 자신을 파멸로 이끌고 그에게 의존하는 사람들을 불행하게 만든다는 것이 얼마나 기이한 일인가. 그러나 하나님의 영이 권력 있고 부유한 사람들을 사로잡아 완강한 경계심으로 그들을 추적하다가 마침내 그들을 굴복시켜 세상의 기쁨과 여인의 사랑을 버리고 수도원의 고통스러운 금욕생활로 향하게 하는 방식보다 더 기이하지는 않다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English deceyven, desayven, dissayven, from Old French decever, decevoir, from Latin dēcipiō (“to deceive; beguile; entrap”), from dē- ...
definition_en: To give false information to someone in order to trick them.

senses.gloss: To trick or mislead.
senses.example: It feels painful to begin seeing clearly, that you’ve been deceived by the very people and institutions you trusted to guide you.

examples.text: I’ve never been so deceived in a man as I was in George Rainey.
examples.translation_ko: 조지 레이니만큼 나를 속인 남자는 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When people say they do not care what others think of them, for the most part they deceive themselves.
examples.translation_ko: 사람들이 남의 시선 따위는 신경 쓰지 않는다고 말할 때, 대부분은 자기 자신을 속이고 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From approve + -al.
definition_en: The act of giving or receiving approval.

senses.gloss: An expression granting permission; an indication of agreement with a proposal; an acknowledgement that a person, thing, or event meets requirements.
senses.example: I need to get an approval on this purchase order.

senses.gloss: An expression of favorable acceptance and encouragement; a compliment that also condones.
senses.example: Words of approval never seem to come from him.

senses.gloss: Something mailed by a seller to a collector to match their stated interests; the collector can approve of or return the item.

examples.text: I imagine that she had never looked with approval on her sister’s leaning towards persons who cultivated the arts.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 언니가 예술을 추구하는 사람들에게 기울이는 관심을 결코 좋게 보지 않았던 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Generally they mean only that they will do as they choose, in the confidence that no one will know their vagaries; and at the utmost only that they are willing to act contrary to the opinion of the majority because they are supported by the approval of their neighbours.
examples.translation_ko: 일반적으로 그들이 의미하는 바는 아무도 자신의 변덕을 알지 못할 것이라는 확신 속에서 자기 마음대로 행동하겠다는 것이고, 기껏해야 이웃들의 찬성에 힘입어 다수의 의견에 반하는 행동을 기꺼이 하겠다는 것일 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + conventional.
definition_en: Not conforming to conventional standards or practices.

senses.gloss: Not adhering to custom, convention, or accepted standards.
Out of the ordinary.
Atypical.

examples.text: It is not difficult to be unconventional in the eyes of the world when your unconventionality is but the convention of your set.
examples.translation_ko: 당신의 비관습성이 단지 당신이 속한 집단의 관습에 불과할 때, 세상 사람들 눈에 비관습적으로 보이는 것은 어려운 일이 아니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: No one runs so hurriedly to the cover of respectability as the unconventional woman who has exposed herself to the slings and arrows of outraged propriety.
examples.translation_ko: 분별없는 행동으로 세상의 분노와 비난에 자신을 노출시킨 파격적인 여자만큼 체면치레라는 은신처로 급히 달려가는 사람은 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English afforthen, aforthen, avorthien, from earlier iforthen, iforthien, ȝeforthien, from Old English forþian, ġeforþian (“to further,...
definition_en: Be able to pay for something.

senses.gloss: To incur, stand, or bear without serious detriment, as an act which might under other circumstances be injurious; (usually after an expression of ability, as could, able, difficult) to be able or rich enough; to spare.
senses.example: I think we can afford the extra hour it will take.  We can only afford to buy a small car at the moment.

senses.gloss: To offer, provide, or supply, as in selling, granting or expending, with profit, or without too great a loss.
senses.example: Alfred affords his goods cheaper than Bantock.

senses.gloss: To give forth; to supply, yield, or produce as the natural result, fruit, or issue.
senses.example: Grapes afford wine.  Olives afford oil.  The earth affords fruit.  The sea affords an abundant supply of fish.

examples.text: He could afford to control himself now.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 그는 자신을 통제할 여유가 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It affords you then an inordinate amount of self-esteem.
examples.translation_ko: 그러면 당신은 엄청난 자존감을 얻게 된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I do not consider that the cigars and whisky he consumed at my expense (he always refused cocktails, since he was practically a teetotaller), and the few dollars, borrowed with a civil air of conferring a favour upon me, that passed from my pocket to his, were in any way equivalent to the entertainment he afforded me.
examples.translation_ko: 내 돈으로 그가 소비한 시가와 위스키(그는 사실상 금주가였기 때문에 칵테일은 항상 거절했다), 그리고 내게 호의를 베푸는 듯한 정중한 태도로 빌려간 몇 달러가 내 주머니에서 그의 주머니로 넘어간 것이 그가 내게 선사한 즐거움과 결코 동등하다고 생각하지 않는다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Verb from Middle English grippen, from Old English grippan, from a Proto-Germanic *gripjaną (compare Old High German gripfen); compare the related ...
definition_en: A firm hold or grasp of something.

senses.gloss: To take hold (of), particularly with the hand.
senses.example: That suitcase is heavy, so grip the handle firmly.

senses.gloss: To figuratively take hold of or grasp.
senses.example: We need to grip this problem, not shut our eyes and hope it goes away.

senses.gloss: Of an emotion or situation: to have a strong effect upon.
senses.example: As the water level began to rise, I was gripped by panic.

examples.text: Blanche Stroeve was in the cruel grip of appetite.
examples.translation_ko: 블랑슈 스트루브는 욕망의 잔혹한 지배를 받고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The satyr in him suddenly took possession, and he was powerless in the grip of an instinct which had all the strength of the primitive forces of nature.
examples.translation_ko: 그 안의 사티로스가 갑자기 그를 사로잡았고, 그는 자연의 원시적 힘만큼 강력한 본능의 지배 앞에서 무력했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin centrālis, from centrum (“centre”), from Ancient Greek κέντρον (kéntron); by surface analysis, centre + -al.
definition_en: Relating to or situated at the center.

senses.gloss: Being in the centre.
senses.example: The network had no central ownership or controller; and it did only one thing – transfer data packets from one edge of the network to their destination at another edge.

senses.gloss: Having or containing the centre of something.
Being very important, or key to something.
senses.example: Cleverley was a central figure as England took the lead inside three minutes. He saw his shot handled by Moldovan defender Simion Bulgaru and Lampard drilled home the penalty in trademark fashion.

examples.text: I tried four times; finally an exasperated central told me the wire was being kept open for long distance from Detroit.
examples.translation_ko: 네 번이나 시도했지만, 마침내 짜증이 난 교환원이 디트로이트에서 오는 장거리 전화 때문에 회선을 열어두고 있다고 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A maid began opening the upper windows of his house, appeared momentarily in each, and, leaning from the large central bay, spat meditatively into the garden.
examples.translation_ko: 하녀 한 명이 그의 집 위층 창문들을 열기 시작했고, 각 창문마다 잠깐씩 모습을 드러내더니, 가운데 큰 출창에서 몸을 내밀고는 생각에 잠긴 듯 정원으로 침을 뱉었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It is the spy seated in the central stronghold of the ego.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 자아의 중심 요새에 앉아 있는 스파이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English herde, heerde, heorde, from Old English hierd, heord (“herd, flock; keeping, care, custody”), from Proto-West Germanic *herdu, ...
definition_en: A group of animals, especially cattle or sheep.

senses.gloss: A number of domestic animals assembled together under the watch or ownership of a keeper.
senses.example: a herd of cattle

senses.gloss: Any collection of animals gathered or travelling in a company.
senses.example: Zakouma is the last place on Earth where you can see more than a thousand elephants on the move in a single, compact herd.

senses.gloss: A crowd, a mass of people or things; a rabble.
senses.example: You can never interest the common herd in the abstract question.

examples.text: You know how natives love to herd together.
examples.translation_ko: 원주민들이 얼마나 함께 모여 있기를 좋아하는지 당신도 알 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Sooner or later you’ll be ill and tired and old, and then you’ll crawl back into the herd.
examples.translation_ko: 조만간 당신도 병들고 지치고 늙을 것이고, 그때가 되면 무리 속으로 기어 돌아갈 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English linke, lenke, from a merger of Old English hlenċe, hlenċa (“ring; chainlink”) and Old Norse *hlenkr, hlekkr (“ring; chain”); bo...
definition_en: A connection or relationship between two things.

senses.gloss: A connection between places, people, events, things, or ideas.
senses.example: The mayor’s assistant serves as the link to the media.

senses.gloss: One element of a chain or other connected series.
senses.example: The third link of the silver chain needs to be resoldered.

senses.gloss: Abbreviation of hyperlink.
senses.example: The link on the page points to the sports scores.

examples.text: Usually her voice came over the wire as something fresh and cool, as if a divot from a green golf-links had come sailing in at the office window, but this morning it seemed harsh and dry.
examples.translation_ko: 평소 그녀의 목소리는 전화선을 타고 신선하고 시원하게 들려왔는데, 마치 푸른 골프장에서 떼어낸 잔디 조각이 사무실 창문으로 날아든 것 같았지만, 이날 아침에는 거칠고 메마르게 들렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When the “Jazz History of the World” was over, girls were putting their heads on men’s shoulders in a puppyish, convivial way, girls were swooning backward playfully into men’s arms, even into groups, knowing that someone would arrest their falls—but no one swooned backward on Gatsby, and no French bob touched Gatsby’s shoulder, and no singing quartets were formed with Gatsby’s head for one link.
examples.translation_ko: "재즈 세계사"가 끝나자, 여자들은 강아지처럼 다정하게 남자들의 어깨에 머리를 기대고 있었고, 장난스럽게 남자들의 팔 속으로, 심지어 무리 속으로 몸을 맡기며 뒤로 쓰러져갔다. 누군가가 자신들의 낙하를 막아줄 것을 알고 있었기 때문이다. 하지만 아무도 개츠비에게 몸을 맡기며 뒤로 쓰러지지 않았고, 어떤 프렌치 단발머리도 개츠비의 어깨에 닿지 않았으며, 개츠비를 한 고리로 하여 사중창단이 만들어지지도 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It is the very strong link that attaches the individual to the whole.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 개인을 전체에 결속시키는 매우 강력한 고리다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English sclave, from Old French sclave, from Medieval Latin sclavus (“slave”), from Late Latin Sclavus (“Slav”), traditionall...
definition_en: A person who is owned or controlled by another.

senses.gloss: A person who is held in servitude as the property of another person, and whose labor (and often also whose body and life) is subject to the owner's volition and control.
A drudge; one who labors or is obliged (e.g. by prior contract) to labor like a slave with limited rights, e.g. an indentured servant.
An abject person.
senses.example: Art thou the ſlaue that with thy breath haſt kill'd / Mine innocent child?

examples.text: They are as little their own masters as the slaves chained to the benches of a galley.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 갤리선의 노 젓는 자리에 사슬로 묶인 노예들과 마찬가지로 자신의 주인이 아닙니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You should have lived at a time when women were chattels and men the masters of slaves,” I said.
examples.translation_ko: "당신은 여자가 재산이고 남자가 노예의 주인이던 시대에 태어났어야 했군요." 내가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From earlier swey (“to fall, swoon”), from Middle English sweyen, from Old Norse sveigja (“to bend, bow”), from Proto-Germanic *swaigijaną (compare...
definition_en: A gentle or subtle movement from side to side.

senses.gloss: The act of swaying; a swaying motion; a swing or sweep of a weapon.
A rocking or swinging motion.
senses.example: The old song caused a little sway in everyone in the room.

senses.gloss: Influence, weight, or authority that inclines to one side
senses.example: I doubt I'll hold much sway with someone so powerful.

examples.text: Stroeve hid his face in his hands and swayed backwards and forwards, groaning.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 두 손으로 얼굴을 가리고 앞뒤로 몸을 흔들며 신음했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Now and then I caught sight of the swaying hearse in front of us, and our own driver urged his pair so that we might not remain behind.
examples.translation_ko: 때때로 앞에서 흔들리는 영구차가 눈에 띄었고, 우리 마부도 뒤처지지 않으려고 말 두 마리를 재촉했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English senior, from Latin senior (“older”), comparative form of senex (“old”); see senate. Doublet of seigneur, seignior, senhor, seño...
definition_en: Older or more experienced

examples.text: It’s mostly merchants who buy them, and rich tradesmen.
examples.translation_ko: 주로 상인들과 부유한 장사꾼들이 사죠.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He reminded you of those jolly, fat merchants that Rubens painted.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 루벤스가 그린 그 쾌활하고 뚱뚱한 상인들을 연상시켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From daze + -le, a frequentative form.
definition_en: To dazzle someone is to impress or overwhelm them with something.

senses.gloss: To confuse or overpower the sight of (someone or something, such as a sensor) by means of excessive brightness.
senses.example: Dazzled by the headlights of the lorry, the deer stopped in the middle of the street.

senses.gloss: To render incapable of thinking clearly; to overwhelm with showiness or brilliance.
senses.example: The delegates were dazzled by the originality of his arguments.

senses.gloss: To be overpowered by light; to be confused by excess of brightness.
senses.example: […] I dare not trust these Eyes; / They Dance in Mists, and dazle with surprize.

examples.text: I spent my Saturday nights in New York because those gleaming, dazzling parties of his were with me so vividly that I could still hear the music and the laughter, faint and incessant, from his garden, and the cars going up and down his drive.
examples.translation_ko: 토요일 밤마다 나는 뉴욕에서 보냈다. 그의 그 찬란하고 눈부신 파티들이 너무나 생생하게 내 안에 남아 있어서, 여전히 그의 정원에서 들려오는 희미하고 끊임없는 음악과 웃음소리, 그리고 그의 진입로를 오르내리는 자동차 소리를 들을 수 있었기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The colour dazzles you.
examples.translation_ko: 그 색채가 눈을 부시게 한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: And I think that was the vision that had remained with him always, dazzling his eyes so that he could not see the truth; and notwithstanding the brutality of fact, he continued to see with the eyes of the spirit an Italy of romantic brigands and picturesque ruins.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 내 생각에 그 환상이 언제나 그와 함께 남아 있어서 그의 눈을 현혹시켜 진실을 보지 못하게 했던 것 같다. 현실의 잔혹함에도 불구하고 그는 계속해서 영혼의 눈으로 낭만적인 도적들과 그림 같은 폐허가 있는 이탈리아를 보고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From picture + -esque, a calque of French pittoresque, from picture (“a picture, painting”).
definition_en: Having a charming or picturesque quality.

senses.gloss: Resembling or worthy of a picture or painting; having the qualities of a picture or painting; pleasingly beautiful.
senses.example: We looked down onto a beautiful, picturesque sunset over the ocean.

senses.gloss: Strikingly graphic or vivid; having striking and vivid imagery.
senses.example: picturesque language

examples.text: I thought of those cold scenes of his, with their picturesque peasants and cypresses and olive-trees.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그림 같은 농부들과 사이프러스 나무, 올리브 나무가 있는 그의 차가운 풍경화들을 떠올렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I discovered that in Paris he had been painting just the same stale, obviously picturesque things that he had painted for years in Rome.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 파리에서도 로마에서 수년간 그려왔던 것과 똑같은 진부하고 뻔히 그림 같은 소재들을 그리고 있었다는 사실을 알게 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bagge, from Old Norse baggi (“bag, pack, satchel, bundle”) (whence also Old French bague (“bundle, package, sack”)); related to...
definition_en: A flexible container made of fabric or other material.

senses.gloss: A soft container made out of cloth, paper, thin plastic, etc. and open at the top, used to hold food, commodities, and other goods.

A container made of leather, plastic, or other material, usually with a handle or handles, in which you carry personal items, or clothes or other things that you need for travelling. Includes shopping bags, schoolbags, suitcases, briefcases, handbags, backpacks, etc.
One's preference.
senses.example: Acid House is not my bag: I prefer the more traditional styles of music.

examples.text: Wild rumours were circulating about her—how her mother had found her packing her bag one winter night to go to New York and say goodbye to a soldier who was going overseas.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀에 대한 황당한 소문들이 돌고 있었다—어느 겨울밤 어머니가 그녀를 발견했는데, 해외로 떠나는 한 군인에게 작별 인사를 하러 뉴욕에 가려고 가방을 싸고 있었다는 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His eyes leaked continuously with excitement, and when I took the bag and umbrella from his hands he began to pull so incessantly at his sparse grey beard that I had difficulty in getting off his coat.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 눈에서는 흥분으로 인해 계속 눈물이 흘렀고, 내가 그의 손에서 가방과 우산을 받아들자 성긴 회색 수염을 끊임없이 잡아당기기 시작해서 외투를 벗기는 데 애를 먹었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I imagine that a pickpocket, proud of his light fingers, must feel a sort of indignation with the careless woman who leaves in a cab a vanity-bag with all her jewels in it.
examples.translation_ko: 손재주가 뛰어난 소매치기라면, 보석을 모두 넣어둔 화장품 가방을 택시에 부주의하게 두고 내리는 여자에게 일종의 분노를 느낄 것이라고 나는 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English juel, jewel, juwel, jeuel, jowel, from Anglo-Norman juel, from Old French jouel, joel, joïel, hence French joyau, of uncertain ...
definition_en: A precious stone or gem.

senses.gloss: A precious or semi-precious stone; gem, gemstone.
A valuable object used for personal ornamentation, especially one made of precious metals and stones; a piece of jewellery.
senses.example: Iachimo: 'Tis plate of rare device, and jewels / Of rich and exquisite form, their values great.

senses.gloss: Anything precious or valuable.
senses.example: Galveston was the jewel of Texas prior to the hurricane.

examples.text: Her hand, which dangles over the side, sparkles cold with jewels.
examples.translation_ko: 옆으로 늘어뜨린 그녀의 손이 보석들로 차갑게 반짝인다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “After that I lived like a young rajah in all the capitals of Europe—Paris, Venice, Rome—collecting jewels, chiefly rubies, hunting big game, painting a little, things for myself only, and trying to forget something very sad that had happened to me long ago.”
examples.translation_ko: "그 후 나는 유럽의 모든 수도에서 젊은 라자처럼 살았습니다. 파리, 베니스, 로마에서 보석을 수집하고—주로 루비였죠—대형 사냥을 하고, 그림도 조금 그리고, 모든 것을 오직 나 자신만을 위해 하면서, 오래전에 내게 일어난 매우 슬픈 일을 잊으려 애썼습니다."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I imagine that a pickpocket, proud of his light fingers, must feel a sort of indignation with the careless woman who leaves in a cab a vanity-bag with all her jewels in it.
examples.translation_ko: 손재주가 뛰어난 소매치기라면, 보석을 모두 넣어둔 화장품 가방을 택시에 부주의하게 두고 내리는 여자에게 일종의 분노를 느낄 것이라고 나는 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From the Middle English tragedie, from the Old French tragedie, from the Latin tragoedia, from the Ancient Greek τραγῳδία (tragōidía, “epic play, t...
definition_en: A serious play or drama that ends unhappily.

senses.gloss: A drama or similar work, in which the main character is brought to ruin or otherwise suffers the extreme consequences of some tragic flaw or weakness of character.
The genre of such works, and the art of producing them.
A disastrous event, especially one involving great loss of life or injury.
senses.example: After the terrible tragedy of the Triangle Shirtwaist Fire in 1911, which killed 146 New York garment workers, proper fire drilling was considered a necessity.

examples.text: His life was a tragedy written in the terms of knockabout farce.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 인생은 막장 희극의 형식으로 쓰인 비극이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was puzzled by him, and I was eager to see how he regarded the tragedy he had caused in the lives of people who had used him with so much kindness.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 나를 당황스럽게 했고, 나는 그토록 친절하게 대해준 사람들의 삶에 그가 초래한 비극을 어떻게 바라보는지 간절히 알고 싶었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English galery, gallerye, from Middle French galerie, gallerie, from Old French galerie, gallerie (“a long portico, a gallery”), from M...
definition_en: A room or space for displaying art.

senses.gloss: An institution, building, or room for the exhibition and conservation of important objects, especially works of art.
senses.example: In the gallery are displayed genuine artifacts dug up from the site, and in the gift shop you can buy a replica as a souvenir.

senses.gloss: An establishment that buys, sells, and displays works of art.
senses.example: Some of her best work can be yours: it is available at a gallery, if you can afford it.

senses.gloss: The uppermost seating area projecting from the rear or side walls of a theater, concert hall, or auditorium.
senses.example: We could afford the less expensive seats in the gallery.

examples.text: I sauntered into the long gallery, and there suddenly saw Stroeve.
examples.translation_ko: 긴 회랑으로 들어서서 천천히 걷다가 갑자기 스트루브를 보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But though so bad a painter, he had a very delicate feeling for art, and to go with him to picture-galleries was a rare treat.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그토록 형편없는 화가였음에도 불구하고, 그는 예술에 대한 매우 섬세한 감각을 지니고 있었고, 그와 함께 미술관을 다니는 것은 더없는 즐거움이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A person who is sure of something.

senses.gloss: comparative form of sure: more sure

examples.text: “One thing’s sure and nothing’s surer
examples.translation_ko: "한 가지는 확실하고 그보다 더 확실한 건 없어
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: On the other hand, no garage man who had seen him ever came forward, and perhaps he had an easier, surer way of finding out what he wanted to know.
examples.translation_ko: 반면에 그를 본 적이 있는 정비소 직원은 아무도 나서지 않았고, 아마 그는 자신이 알고 싶어 하는 것을 알아낼 더 쉽고 확실한 방법이 있었을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I think I have never known a man whose judgment was surer.
examples.translation_ko: 그만큼 확실한 판단력을 가진 사람을 나는 본 적이 없다고 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English educaten, from educat(e) (“educated”, also used as the past participle of educaten) + -en (verb-forming suffix), from Latin ēdu...
definition_en: To teach or instruct someone.

senses.gloss: To instruct or train.
senses.example: Wang said such changes to the Baishui glacier provide the chance to educate visitors about global warming.

examples.text: He hurried the phrase “educated at Oxford,” or swallowed it, or choked on it, as though it had bothered him before.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 "옥스퍼드에서 교육받았다"는 말을 서둘러 내뱉거나, 삼켜버리거나, 목에 걸린 듯 했는데, 마치 전에도 그 말 때문에 곤란을 겪었던 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was brought up in America but educated at Oxford, because all my ancestors have been educated there for many years.
examples.translation_ko: 미국에서 자랐지만 옥스퍼드에서 교육받았소. 내 조상들이 수년간 모두 그곳에서 교육받아왔기 때문이오.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And he was better educated than most painters.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 그는 대부분의 화가들보다 교양이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin gesticulatus, past participle of gesticulor (“to gesticulate”), from gesticulus (“a mimic gesture”), diminutive of gestus (“gesture”), f...
definition_en: Make gestures to convey meaning

senses.gloss: To make gestures or motions, as in speaking.
senses.example: ... groups of dancers were wheeling, plunging, and gesticulating while the ogre, more aphasic than before, mumbled at full strength ...

senses.gloss: To say or express through gestures.
senses.example: […]the TV programme Friends is influencing not only the way Irish people speak but also how they gesticulate. Now almost every utterance is accompanied by arms outstretched and palms turned upwards."

examples.text: And the crowd that throngs the wharf as the steamer draws alongside is gay and debonair; it is a noisy, cheerful, gesticulating crowd.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 기선이 접안할 때 부두에 몰려든 군중은 명랑하고 쾌활하다. 시끄럽고 유쾌하며 몸짓을 크게 하는 군중이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It made the Marseilles that I knew, gesticulating and sunny, with its comfortable hotels and its restaurants crowded with the well-to-do, tame and commonplace.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 내가 알던 마르세유를, 몸짓을 하며 햇살 가득한, 안락한 호텔들과 부유한 사람들로 붐비는 식당들이 있는 그 마르세유를 시시하고 평범하게 만들어버렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English swete, swet, swate, swote, from Old English swāt, from Proto-Germanic *swait-, *swaitą, from Proto-Indo-European *swoyd- (“to s...
definition_en: To produce sweat as a result of physical exertion or heat.

senses.gloss: Fluid that exits the body through pores in the skin usually due to physical stress and/or high temperature for the purpose of regulating body temperature and removing certain compounds from the circulation.
The state of one who sweats; diaphoresis.
senses.example: Just thinking about the interview tomorrow puts me into a nervous sweat.

senses.gloss: Hard work; toil.

examples.text: The sweat made them constantly slip down.
examples.translation_ko: 땀 때문에 안경이 계속 미끄러져 내렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His red face was shining with sweat, and he had a look of comic agitation, but there was in his round, surprised eyes an eager light.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 붉은 얼굴은 땀으로 번들거렸고, 우스꽝스럽게 동요한 표정을 짓고 있었지만, 그의 둥글고 놀란 눈에는 간절한 빛이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pore, from Old French pore, from Latin porus, from Ancient Greek πόρος (póros, “passage”). Displaced native English sweat hole ...
definition_en: A small opening or hole in the skin.

senses.gloss: A tiny opening in the skin.
senses.example: I could sense the sweat dripping out of all my pores.

senses.gloss: By extension any small opening or interstice, especially one of many, or one allowing the passage of a fluid.
senses.example: the pores of a rock.

examples.text: The very phrases were worn so threadbare that they evoked no image except that of a turbaned “character” leaking sawdust at every pore as he pursued a tiger through the Bois de Boulogne.
examples.translation_ko: 그 문구들은 너무 낡아빠져서 부아 드 불로뉴에서 호랑이를 쫓는 터번을 쓴 '인물'이 온몸의 구멍마다 톱밥을 흘리는 모습 외에는 아무런 이미지도 떠올리지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was heart-broken because he had no whisky, wanted to make coffee for me, racked his brain for something he could possibly do for me, and beamed and laughed, and in the exuberance of his delight sweated at every pore.
examples.translation_ko: 위스키가 없다며 가슴 아파하고, 나를 위해 커피를 끓이려 하고, 내게 뭔가 해줄 일이 없나 머리를 쥐어짜며, 환하게 웃고 기뻐하다가 흥분한 나머지 온몸에서 땀을 뻘뻘 흘렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The books he liked were queer; sometimes I would find him poring over the poems of Mallarme, and he read them as a child reads, forming the words with his lips, and I wondered what strange emotion he got from those subtle cadences and obscure phrases; and again I found him absorbed in the detective novels of Gaboriau.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 좋아하는 책들은 기이했다. 때로는 말라르메의 시집을 열심히 들여다보고 있는 그를 발견하곤 했는데, 그는 아이가 읽듯 입술로 단어를 따라 읽었고, 나는 그가 그 미묘한 운율과 모호한 구절들에서 어떤 기묘한 감정을 얻는지 궁금했다. 또 어떤 때는 가보리오의 탐정소설에 빠져 있는 그를 발견하기도 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English balled, ballid, bald (“bald”), of uncertain origin. Probably formed from Middle English bal, balle (“ball, round object, knoll,...
definition_en: Having little or no hair on the head.

senses.gloss: Having little or no hair, fur, or feathers.
Having little or no hair on the head, or having a large area of bare scalp on top of the head.
senses.example: a bald man with a moustache

senses.gloss: Of animals, having areas (of fur or plumage) that are colored white, especially on the head.

examples.text: The doctor was a stout man in shabby clothes, and when he took off his hat I noticed that he was very bald.
examples.translation_ko: 의사는 남루한 옷을 입은 뚱뚱한 남자였는데, 모자를 벗었을 때 나는 그가 매우 대머리라는 것을 알아차렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was a fat little man, with short legs, young still—he could not have been more than thirty—but prematurely bald.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 다리가 짧은 뚱뚱한 소남자였는데, 아직 젊었지만—서른을 넘지 않았을 것이다—일찍 대머리가 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English rim, rym, rime, from Old English rima (“rim, edge, border, bank, coast”), from Proto-Germanic *rimô, *rembô (“edge, border”), p...
definition_en: To form or be shaped into a ring around the edge of something.

senses.gloss: An edge around something, especially when circular.
senses.example: That's... our galaxy. We're beyond the rim.

senses.gloss: A wheelrim.
senses.example: About an hour later, she noticed an all black Phantom with tints and chrome rims riding slowly through the car lot.

senses.gloss: A semicircular copydesk.
senses.example: On the rim are copy editors who edit stories for accuracy, brevity and clarity.

examples.text: He went out of the room calling “Ewing!” and returned in a few minutes accompanied by an embarrassed, slightly worn young man, with shell-rimmed glasses and scanty blond hair.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 "유잉!"을 부르며 방을 나갔다가 몇 분 후 당황한 기색이 역력한, 약간 지쳐 보이는 젊은 남자를 데리고 돌아왔다. 그는 뿔테 안경을 쓰고 있었고 금발 머리는 성성했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His gold-rimmed spectacles were still on his nose.
examples.translation_ko: 금테 안경이 여전히 코에 걸려 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His eyes were blue and round too, he wore large gold-rimmed spectacles, and his eyebrows were so fair that you could not see them.
examples.translation_ko: 눈도 파랗고 둥글었으며, 큰 금테 안경을 쓰고 있었는데, 눈썹이 너무 연해서 보이지 않을 정도였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From curl + -y.
definition_en: Having a wavy or curved shape.

senses.gloss: Having curls.
Curling in a direction, as opposed to straight (quotation marks or apostrophes)
Complicated and difficult; knotty.
senses.example: Often, the job will throw you a curly problem that will cause the unprepared to fail, so it is best to prepare an investigative plan before starting work.

examples.text: He brought out a picture of two curly-headed Italian urchins playing marbles.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 구슬치기를 하는 곱슬머리 이탈리아 꼬마 두 명을 그린 그림을 꺼내왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Some wear black shifts and flesh-coloured stockings; some with curly hair, dyed yellow, are dressed like little girls in short muslin frocks.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 여자는 검은 속옷에 살색 스타킹을 신고 있고, 어떤 여자는 노랗게 염색한 곱슬머리를 하고 짧은 모슬린 원피스를 입어 마치 어린 소녀처럼 차려입었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French lamentable, from Latin lāmentābilis (“full of sorrow, mournful; deplorable”), from lāmentor (“lament”), from lāmenta (“wailing, ...
definition_en: Causing or expressing regret or sorrow.

definition_en: A structure built out over water, typically for loading and unloading ships.

examples.text: Once they each of them earned a franc by loading trucks with innumerable boxes of oranges that had been dumped down on the quay.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I spent long hours in the Louvre, the most friendly of all galleries and the most convenient for meditation; or idled on the quays, fingering second-hand books that I never meant to buy.

definition_en: The expression or appearance of a person's face.

senses.gloss: Appearance, especially the features and expression of the face.
senses.example: But Richmond, his grandfather's darling, after one thoughtful glance cast under his lashes at that uncompromising countenance appeared to lose himself in his own reflections.

senses.gloss: Favour; support; encouragement.
senses.example: All feared and obeyed him; to use his roads we must have his countenance.

senses.gloss: Superficial appearance; show; pretense.
senses.example: The election being done, he made countenance of great discontent thereat.

examples.text: Looked at from a distance, however, the hen resolved itself into a bonnet, and the countenance of a stout old lady beamed down into the room.
examples.translation_ko: 그러나 멀리서 보니 그 암탉은 모자로 변했고, 통통한 노부인의 얼굴이 방 안을 향해 환하게 미소 짓고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He is not embarrassed by the sans gene of the hobo, nor put out of countenance by the etiquette of the prince.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 부랑자의 뻔뻔함에 당황하지도 않고, 왕자의 예법에 기죽지도 않는다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Sometimes he embarrassed his wife, and the only time I saw her put out of countenance was when he insisted on telling me that he had taken a purge, and went into somewhat realistic details on the subject.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 그가 아내를 당황하게 만들었는데, 내가 그녀가 얼굴을 붉히는 것을 본 유일한 때는 그가 자신이 설사약을 먹었다고 고집스럽게 내게 말하면서 그 주제에 대해 다소 사실적인 세부사항까지 늘어놓았을 때였다.

definition_en: Express a strong feeling of loyalty or devotion.

senses.gloss: A solemn promise to perform some act, or behave in a specified manner, especially a promise to live and act in accordance with the rules of a religious order.
senses.example: The old hermit, up in the mountains, took a vow of silence.

senses.gloss: A declaration or assertion.
A votive offering.
senses.example: There are also waxen vows, that represent other parts of the body mixed with them; but of these there are few in comparison of the number of the Priapi.

examples.text: I wondered what those friends of mine would say who demanded vast studios, and vowed they could not work unless all the conditions were to their liking.
examples.translation_ko: 거대한 화실을 요구하며 모든 조건이 마음에 들지 않으면 작업할 수 없다고 맹세하던 내 친구들이 이것을 보면 뭐라고 할까 궁금했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I knew her capable of temper, for all the calmness of her manner; and if Stroeve still refused, she might easily have flung out of the studio with vows never to return.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 침착한 태도에도 불구하고 나는 그녀가 화를 낼 수 있는 성격임을 알고 있었다. 만약 스트루브가 계속 거절한다면, 그녀는 다시는 돌아오지 않겠다고 맹세하며 화실에서 뛰쳐나갔을지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: By surface analysis, greet + -ing.
definition_en: A message or expression of goodwill on meeting someone.

senses.gloss: A conventional phrase used to start a letter or conversation or otherwise to acknowledge a person's arrival or presence.
senses.example: It's polite to begin a letter with a greeting, but this practice is less common in email.

senses.gloss: The action of the verb to greet.

examples.text: He had just shaved, for there was a white spot of lather on his cheekbone, and he was most respectful in his greeting to everyone in the room.
examples.translation_ko: 방금 면도를 했는지 광대뼈에 하얀 비누거품이 한 점 묻어 있었고, 방 안의 모든 사람에게 극도로 정중하게 인사를 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was characteristic of him to display geniality with anyone who showed a disinclination to meet him, and the coolness of my greeting can have left him in little doubt of that.
examples.translation_ko: 자신을 만나기 꺼리는 기색을 보이는 사람에게는 누구든 친근함을 과시하는 것이 그의 특징이었고, 내가 차갑게 인사한 것만 봐도 그는 충분히 눈치챘을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was constantly offending Dirk Stroeve so bitterly that he flung away, vowing he would never speak to him again; but there was a solid force in Strickland that attracted the fat Dutchman against his will, so that he came back, fawning like a clumsy dog, though he knew that his only greeting would be the blow he dreaded.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 끊임없이 더크 스트루브를 몹시 화나게 해서 스트루브가 다시는 그와 말하지 않겠다고 맹세하며 뛰쳐나가게 만들었지만, 스트릭랜드에게는 뚱뚱한 네덜란드인의 의지와는 반대로 그를 끌어당기는 확고한 힘이 있어서, 스트루브는 자신을 맞이할 것이 두려워하는 매질뿐이라는 것을 알면서도 서툰 개처럼 아첨하며 다시 돌아오곤 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English obligacioun, from Old French obligacion, from Latin obligatio, obligationem, from obligatum (past participle of obligare), from...
definition_en: A duty or responsibility to do something.

senses.gloss: The act of binding oneself by a social, legal, or moral tie to someone.
A social, legal, or moral requirement, duty, contract, or promise that compels someone to follow or avoid a particular course of action.
senses.example: I feel I'm under obligation to attend my sister's wedding, even though we have a very frosty relationship.

senses.gloss: A course of action imposed by society, law, or conscience by which someone is bound or restricted.

examples.text: The voice in the hall rose high with annoyance: “Very well, then, I won’t sell you the car at all … I’m under no obligations to you at all … and as for your bothering me about it at lunch time, I won’t stand that at all!”
examples.translation_ko: 복도에서 들려오는 목소리가 짜증스럽게 높아졌다. "좋아, 그럼 차는 아예 안 팔겠어... 나는 당신에게 아무런 의무도 없다고... 그리고 점심시간에 이런 일로 나를 귀찮게 하는 건 절대 참을 수 없어!"

senses.gloss: The thing to be done as agent for another.
senses.example: I have three commissions for the city.

examples.text: I accepted a commission as first lieutenant when it began.

examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 웨스트에그에 경악했다. 브로드웨이가 롱아일랜드의 한 어촌 마을에 낳아놓은 이 전례 없는 "장소"에—오래된 완곡어법 아래서 거슬려하는 거친 활력과, 주민들을 무에서 무로 가는 지름길로 몰아가는 지나치게 뻔뻔한 운명에 경악했다.

senses.gloss: Marked by extreme and violent energy.

senses.gloss: Without defence; undefended.

definition_en: Extremely surprised or impressed.

senses.gloss: Astonished or confounded with fear, surprise, or wonder; greatly surprised (often with ensuing adpositions e.g. at, with, or by).
senses.example:
1917, Frederic Harrison, The Mill on the Floss. Vol. IX. Harvard Classics Shelf of Fiction
we are amazed by forked flashes of wisdom

examples.text: As soon as I arrived I made an attempt to find my host, but the two or three people of whom I asked his whereabouts stared at me in such an amazed way, and denied so vehemently any knowledge of his movements, that I slunk off in the direction of the cocktail table—the only place in the garden where a single man could linger without looking purposeless and alone.
examples.translation_ko: 도착하자마자 나는 주인을 찾으려고 했지만, 그의 행방을 물어본 두세 사람이 너무나 놀란 표정으로 나를 쳐다보며 그의 움직임에 대해 아는 바가 없다고 격렬하게 부인하는 바람에, 나는 칵테일 테이블 쪽으로 슬금슬금 물러났다. 정원에서 혼자 있는 남자가 목적 없고 외로워 보이지 않으면서 머물 수 있는 유일한 장소였다.

etymology: Inherited from Middle English worschippe, worthschipe, from Old English weorþsċiepe. Cognate with Scots worschip (“worship”).
definition_en: To show respect and admiration for a person or thing.

senses.gloss: The devotion accorded to a deity or to a sacred object.
senses.example: Polytheistic theology and worship had to go underground.

senses.gloss: The adoration (or latria) owed to God alone, as greater than the hyperveneration / hyper-veneration (or hyperdulia) that is given to Saint Mary only and the veneration (or dulia) accorded to all other Roman Catholic saints.
The religious ceremonies that express this devotion.
senses.example: The worſhip of God is an eminent part of Religion; and Prayer, which is often in Scripture expreſſed by ſeeking God, and calling upon his Name, is a chief part of Religious Worſhip.

examples.text: “I’ve worshipped you as no woman was ever worshipped before.
examples.translation_ko: "당신을 그 어떤 여자도 받아본 적 없을 만큼 숭배했는데.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I longed to possess a Sisley and a Degas, and I worshipped Manet.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 시슬레와 드가의 작품을 소유하고 싶어 했고, 마네를 숭배했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Having a smooth and curved shape.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of round

examples.text: After half an hour, the sun shone again, and the grocer’s automobile rounded Gatsby’s drive with the raw material for his servants’ dinner—I felt sure he wouldn’t eat a spoonful.
examples.translation_ko: 30분 후 해가 다시 비치자, 식료품상의 자동차가 개츠비의 진입로를 돌아 그의 하인들 저녁 식사 재료를 가지고 왔다—그는 한 숟가락도 먹지 않을 것이 분명했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was rather literary in college—one year I wrote a series of very solemn and obvious editorials for the Yale News—and now I was going to bring back all such things into my life and become again that most limited of all specialists, the “well-rounded man.”
examples.translation_ko: 대학 시절 나는 꽤 문학적이었다—한 해 동안 예일 뉴스에 매우 진부하고 뻔한 사설들을 연재하기도 했다—그리고 이제 나는 그런 모든 것들을 내 삶으로 다시 불러들여서, 모든 전문가 중에서도 가장 제한적인 존재인 "교양인"이 되려고 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was the constant lover, and though she grew old, losing her rounded lines and her fair comeliness, to him she would certainly never alter.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 변함없는 연인이었고, 그녀가 나이 들어 둥근 몸매와 아름다운 용모를 잃더라도 그에게는 결코 변하지 않을 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: The state of being orderly and well organized.

senses.gloss: The fact of having a regular, proper and systematic arrangement.
senses.example: Voltaire had drawn on Newton to demonstrate an allegedly divine orderliness in the natural world which left no space for God's intervention in human affairs [...].

examples.text: There was a pleasing grace in the orderliness of their lives.

examples.text: He told me of his childhood in the tidy brick house, and of his mother’s passionate orderliness.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 나에게 말끔한 벽돌집에서 보낸 어린 시절과 어머니의 열정적인 정리정돈 습관에 대해 이야기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

homework

examples.text: Ata continued to do the housework, and I gave him his meals as I said I would.
examples.translation_ko: 아타는 계속 집안일을 했고, 나는 약속한 대로 그에게 식사를 제공했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was married to an American woman, obese and slatternly, fallen to this pass by Heaven knows what process of degradation, and every day the boarders took it in turns to help her with the housework.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 미국인 여자와 결혼했는데, 비만하고 단정치 못한 여자로 하늘만이 아는 어떤 타락의 과정을 거쳐 이런 처지에 떨어진 사람이었고, 매일 하숙생들이 돌아가며 그녀의 집안일을 도왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: By surface analysis, market + -ing.
definition_en: The process of promoting and selling products or services.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of market

examples.text: “She’d gone out to do the marketing.”
examples.translation_ko: "장을 보러 나갔어요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She had done her marketing from day to day, buying only what was strictly needful, so that nothing was left over from one day to the next.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 날마다 장을 보면서 꼭 필요한 것만 사서, 하루에서 다음 날로 넘어가는 것이 아무것도 없도록 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sewen, seowen, sowen, from Old English siwian, seowian, seowan (“to sew, mend, patch, knit together, link, unite”), from Proto-...
definition_en: To sew or join things together with thread.

senses.gloss: To use a needle to pass thread repeatedly through (pieces of fabric) in order to join them together.
senses.example: Balls were first made of grass or leaves held together by strings, and later of pieces of animal skin sewn together and stuffed with feathers or hay.

senses.gloss: To use a needle to pass thread repeatedly through pieces of fabric in order to join them together.
Followed by into: to enclose by sewing.
senses.example: to sew money into a bag

examples.text: Mrs. Stroeve sewed, and I thought I recognised the shirt she was mending as Strickland’s.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브 부인은 바느질을 하고 있었는데, 그녀가 꿰매고 있는 셔츠가 스트릭랜드의 것인 듯했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Mrs. Stroeve did all the housework herself; and while Dirk painted bad pictures, she went marketing, cooked the luncheon, sewed, occupied herself like a busy ant all the day; and in the evening sat in the studio, sewing again, while Dirk played music which I am sure was far beyond her comprehension.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브 부인은 모든 집안일을 혼자 했다. 더크가 형편없는 그림을 그리는 동안 그녀는 장을 보러 나가고, 점심을 요리하고, 바느질을 하며, 하루 종일 부지런한 개미처럼 바쁘게 움직였다. 저녁이면 화실에 앉아 다시 바느질을 하고, 더크는 그녀가 이해하기에는 분명 너무 어려운 음악을 연주했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From sentimental + -ity.
definition_en: Excessive emotional attachment or sentimental feeling.

senses.gloss: An act or state of being sentimental.

examples.text: Through all he said, even through his appalling sentimentality, I was reminded of something—an elusive rhythm, a fragment of lost words, that I had heard somewhere a long time ago.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 한 모든 말을 통해, 심지어 그의 끔찍한 감상주의를 통해서도, 나는 무언가를 떠올렸다—오래전 어디선가 들었던 것 같은 애매한 리듬, 잃어버린 말들의 한 조각을.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had a characteristic sentimentality about the day and wanted to pass it among his friends with suitable ceremonies.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그날에 대해 특유의 감상적인 마음을 품고 있었고, 적절한 의식과 함께 친구들 사이에서 그날을 보내고 싶어 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Love is never quite devoid of sentimentality, and Strickland was the least inclined to that infirmity of any man I have known.
examples.translation_ko: 사랑에는 언제나 감상이 어느 정도 섞여 있기 마련인데, 스트릭랜드는 내가 아는 사람 중에서 그런 나약함에 가장 빠지지 않는 인물이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From suit + -able.
definition_en: Suitable for a particular purpose or occasion.

senses.gloss: Having sufficient or the required properties for a certain purpose or task; appropriate to a certain occasion.
senses.example: Doctors told Matthew Parker’s family there was only a 1% chance of finding a suitable donor for Matthew because his body had rejected a previous transplant.

examples.text: Perhaps both were trying to put down in paint ideas which were more suitable to literature.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 둘 다 문학에 더 적합한 사상을 그림으로 옮겨 놓으려 했던 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a characteristic sentimentality about the day and wanted to pass it among his friends with suitable ceremonies.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그날에 대해 특유의 감상적인 마음을 품고 있었고, 적절한 의식과 함께 친구들 사이에서 그날을 보내고 싶어 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English felowschipe, felawshipe, felaȝschyp, equivalent to fellow + -ship; or perhaps adapted from Old Norse félagskapr, félagsskapr (“...
definition_en: A close and friendly relationship between people who share similar interests or activities.

senses.gloss: A company of people that share the same interest or aim.
senses.example: The Fellowship of the Ring

senses.gloss: Company, companions; a group of people or things following another.
A feeling of friendship, relatedness or connection between people.
senses.example: The grace of the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of God and the fellowship of the Holy Spirit be with you all.

examples.text: But at the moment he was all heartiness and good-fellowship.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그 순간 그는 온통 다정함과 친근함 그 자체였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They belonged to all the countries in the world, but this was no bar to good-fellowship; for they felt themselves freemen of a country whose frontiers include them all, the great country of Cockaine.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 세계 각국 출신이었지만, 이것이 우정에 장애가 되지는 않았다. 그들은 모든 나라를 국경 안에 포함하는 위대한 나라, 코케인의 자유민이라고 스스로를 여겼기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From unwilling + -ly or un- + willingly.
definition_en: Reluctant or unwilling to do something.

senses.gloss: In an unwilling or uncooperative manner.
senses.example: Mai unwillingly starts her journey, wondering how she, still dependent on her parents, can possibly be a reliable companion to her frail grandmother.

examples.text: He watched while the two men standing closest glanced at each other and went unwillingly into the room.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 가장 가까이 서 있던 두 남자가 서로 눈을 마주치며 마지못해 방으로 들어가는 것을 지켜보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He waited a moment longer, hoping I’d begin a conversation, but I was too absorbed to be responsive, so he went unwillingly home.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내가 대화를 시작하기를 바라며 잠시 더 기다렸지만, 나는 너무 몰두해 있어서 반응할 수 없었고, 그래서 그는 마지못해 집으로 돌아갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Stroeve accompanied me unwillingly.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 마지못해 나를 따라왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French oposite, from Latin oppositus, perfect passive participle of oppōnō (“I oppose”). Compare oppose.
definition_en: The state or position of being directly facing away from something.

senses.gloss: Located directly across from something else, or from each other.
senses.example: She saw him walking on the opposite side of the road.

senses.gloss: Of leaves and flowers, positioned directly across from each other on a stem.
Facing in the other direction.
senses.example: They were moving in opposite directions.

examples.text: “It seems that pretty soon the earth’s going to fall into the sun—or wait a minute—it’s just the opposite—the sun’s getting colder every year.
examples.translation_ko: "곧 지구가 태양 속으로 떨어질 것 같은데—아니 잠깐—정반대군—해가 해마다 더 차가워지고 있다는 거였어.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When I came opposite her house that morning her white roadster was beside the kerb, and she was sitting in it with a lieutenant I had never seen before.
examples.translation_ko: 그날 아침 내가 그녀의 집 맞은편에 이르렀을 때 그녀의 흰 로드스터가 길가에 서 있었고, 그녀는 내가 전에 본 적 없는 중위와 함께 차에 앉아 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She was not certain where he lived, but it was in one of the three houses opposite.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그가 어디 사는지 확실하지는 않지만 맞은편 세 집 중 하나라고 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Show preference or kindness to someone.

senses.gloss: British standard spelling of favor.
senses.example: I need a favour. Could you lend me £5 until tomorrow, please?

examples.text: Luck favoured us, and in the first we tried the concierge told us that we should find him on the top floor.
examples.translation_ko: 운이 따라주어서 첫 번째로 들어간 집에서 관리인이 맨 위층에서 찾을 수 있을 거라고 알려주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It did not generally carry a doctor, but one of the senior surgeons at the hospital knew a director of the line, and Abraham was taken as a favour.
examples.translation_ko: 그 배는 보통 의사를 태우지 않았지만, 병원의 선임 외과의 중 한 명이 그 선박회사의 이사를 알고 있어서 아브라함이 특별히 승선할 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English werkman, from Old English weorcmann (“workman”), from Proto-West Germanic *werkamann, from Proto-Germanic *werkamann- (“workman...
definition_en: A person who works with their hands.

senses.gloss: A man who labours for wages.
senses.example: He laid the foundation stone on August 1 1847, and then set around 2,000 workmen loose on the undertaking. The station opened exactly one year later on August 1 1848.

senses.gloss: An artisan or craftsman.

examples.text: It started because she passed so close to some workmen that our fender flicked a button on one man’s coat.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 일꾼들을 너무 가까이 지나치는 바람에 우리 차의 흙받이가 한 남자의 코트 단추를 건드렸기 때문이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Just as the latter was getting uneasy, some workmen came past the door bound for his restaurant, and Michaelis took the opportunity to get away, intending to come back later.
examples.translation_ko: 미카엘리스가 불안해하기 시작할 무렵, 몇몇 일꾼들이 그의 식당으로 향하며 문 앞을 지나갔고, 미카엘리스는 그 기회를 틈타 나중에 다시 오겠다는 생각으로 그곳을 떠났다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Stroeve ran up the stairs ahead of me, and when I reached the top floor I found him talking to a workman in his shirt-sleeves who had opened a door at which Stroeve had knocked.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브가 나보다 앞서 계단을 뛰어올라갔고, 내가 맨 위층에 도착했을 때 그가 셔츠 차림의 일꾼과 이야기하고 있는 것을 보았다. 스트루브가 노크한 문을 그 일꾼이 열어준 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English handel, handle, from Old English handle (“a handle”), from *handulā. See verb below. Cognate with Danish handel (“a handle”).
definition_en: A part of an object that is used to grasp or turn it.

senses.gloss: The part of an object which is (designed to be) held in the hand when used or moved.
senses.example: But first they were gonna stop in Las Vegas / It's off to Las Vegas / To check out the lounges / Pull a few handles

senses.gloss: An instrument for effecting a purpose (either literally or figuratively); a tool, or an opportunity or pretext.
senses.example: Indeed, at the beginning of the session he was careful to make "no declarations of what might hereafter be measures, so as to give anybody a handle for fixing him down to any particular system."

senses.gloss: The gross amount of wagering within a given period of time or for a given event at one of more establishments.
senses.example: The daily handle of a Las Vegas casino is typically millions of dollars.

examples.text: “It’s a nice yellow one,” said Wilson, as he strained at the handle.
examples.translation_ko: "멋진 노란색이에요." 윌슨이 손잡이를 힘껏 돌리며 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He turned the handle and entered.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 손잡이를 돌리고 들어갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I tried the handle, and found the door unlocked.
examples.translation_ko: 손잡이를 돌려보니 문이 잠겨 있지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English disclosen, from Middle French desclos, from Old French desclore, itself from Vulgar Latin disclaudere, from Latin dis- + claude...
definition_en: Reveal information that was previously secret.

senses.gloss: To open up, unfasten.
senses.example: The estrich layeth her eggs under sand, where the heat of the discloseth them.

senses.gloss: To uncover, physically expose to view.
senses.example: Its brown curtain was only half drawn, disclosing the elegant legs, clad in transparent black, of a female seated inside.

senses.gloss: To expose to the knowledge of others; to make known, state openly, reveal (something).
senses.example: Disclosing to a child his or her own HIV-positive status is yet another complicated process. Who should disclose and when and how that person should do it are prominent questions […]

examples.text: They seemed to me ugly, but they suggested without disclosing a secret of momentous significance.
examples.translation_ko: 그림들은 내게 추하게 보였지만, 중대한 의미를 지닌 비밀을 드러내지 않은 채 암시하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I dimly perceived a bed in the corner, and I wondered whether the light would disclose lying on it a dead body.
examples.translation_ko: 구석에 침대가 어렴풋이 보였는데, 불을 켜면 그 위에 시체가 누워 있는 모습이 드러날지도 모른다는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English warmth, warmeth, wermþe, from Old English *wiermþu (“warmth”), from Proto-West Germanic *warmiþu (“warmness; warmth”), correspo...
definition_en: A feeling of being warm or a quality of something that is warm.

senses.gloss: A moderate degree of heat; the sensation of being warm.
Friendliness, kindness or affection.
Fervor, intensity of emotion or expression.
senses.example: "You don't know him—don't pronounce an opinion upon him," I said with warmth.

examples.text: I think that voice held him most, with its fluctuating, feverish warmth, because it couldn’t be over-dreamed—that voice was a deathless song.
examples.translation_ko: 내 생각에는 그 목소리가 그를 가장 사로잡았던 것 같다. 그 변화무쌍하고 열병 같은 따스함으로—왜냐하면 그 목소리만큼은 꿈으로도 넘어설 수 없었기 때문이다. 그 목소리는 불멸의 노래였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She was only extemporizing, but a stirring warmth flowed from her, as if her heart was trying to come out to you concealed in one of those breathless, thrilling words.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그저 즉흥적으로 말하고 있었지만, 마치 그녀의 마음이 숨 막히고 전율적인 말들 속에 숨어서 당신에게 다가오려 하는 것처럼, 감동적인 온기가 그녀에게서 흘러나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Strickland was lying in the bed, uncomfortably because it was too small for him, and he had put all his clothes over him for warmth.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 침대에 누워 있었는데, 침대가 그에게는 너무 작아서 불편해 보였고, 추위를 막으려고 옷을 모두 몸 위에 덮어놓고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Lived or resided in a place.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of dwell
senses.example: Unless the Lord had been my help, my soul had almost dwelt in silence.

examples.text: His eyes dwelt for a moment on a large can within reach of an outstretched arm.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 시선이 팔을 뻗으면 닿을 거리에 있는 큰 통에 잠시 머물렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His father was a carpenter, and they dwelt in a little old red-brick house, neat and clean, by the side of a sluggish canal.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 아버지는 목수였고, 그들은 완만한 운하 옆에 있는 깔끔하고 깨끗한 작은 낡은 붉은 벽돌집에 살고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English febly; equivalent to feeble + -ly, euphonically blending -le and -ly due to difficulty of pronouncing -blely. Compare nimbly, n...
definition_en: In a weak or ineffective manner.

senses.gloss: In a feeble manner.
senses.example: The hurt nigger moaned feebly somewhere nearby, and then fetched a deep sigh that made me mend my pace away from there.

examples.text: but she didn’t say any more, and after a moment I returned rather feebly to the subject of her daughter.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그녀는 더 이상 말하지 않았고, 잠시 후 나는 다소 힘없이 그녀의 딸 이야기로 돌아갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was beating quickly and feebly.
examples.translation_ko: 맥박은 빠르고 약하게 뛰고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We dressed him, while he feebly cursed us, got him downstairs, into a cab, and eventually to Stroeve’s studio.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 힘없이 우리를 욕하는 동안 우리는 그에게 옷을 입히고, 아래층으로 내려가게 하고, 마차에 태워서, 마침내 스트루브의 작업실로 데려갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English filthy, filthi, equivalent to filth + -y.
definition_en: Extremely dirty or unclean.

senses.gloss: Covered with filth; very dirty.
senses.example: The coaches were filthy outside and did not appear to have been painted or washed for years. Inside there were uncomfortable seats covered with a cane-like material.

senses.gloss: Obscene or offensive.
senses.example: Filthy smirking Pat Robertson has come in second in the Iowa Republican caucuses.

senses.gloss: Very unpleasant or disagreeable.

examples.text: “I can’t bear to think of you living in that horrible, filthy attic.
examples.translation_ko: "당신이 그 끔찍하고 더러운 다락방에서 사는 걸 생각하니 견딜 수가 없어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He is alone in a filthy attic, and there is not a soul to look after him.
examples.translation_ko: 더러운 다락방에 혼자 있는데, 돌봐줄 사람이 아무도 없어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English bunche, bonche (“hump, swelling”), of uncertain origin.
Perhaps a variant of *bunge (compare dialectal bung (“heap, grape bunch...
definition_en: A small group of things tied or gathered together.

senses.gloss: A group of similar things, either growing together, or in a cluster or clump, usually fastened together.
senses.example: a bunch of grapes

senses.gloss: The illegitimate supplying of laboratory animals that are act
The peloton; the main group of riders formed during a race.

examples.text: “You’re worth the whole damn bunch put together.”
examples.translation_ko: "당신은 그 빌어먹을 놈들을 다 합친 것보다 훨씬 낫소."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You’re one of that bunch that hangs around with Meyer Wolfshiem—that much I happen to know.
examples.translation_ko: "너는 마이어 울프샤임과 어울리는 그 무리 중 하나야—그 정도는 내가 알고 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: On the easel was a half-finished picture of a smiling Italian peasant, holding a bunch of grapes over the head of a dark-eyed girl.
examples.translation_ko: 이젤 위에는 미소 짓는 이탈리아 농부가 검은 눈의 소녀 머리 위로 포도송이를 들고 있는 반쯤 완성된 그림이 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cyvyl, civil, borrowed from Old French civil, from Latin cīvīlis (“relating to a citizen”), from cīvis (“citizen”). Cognate wit...
definition_en: Relating to citizens or their rights.

senses.gloss: Having to do with people and government office as opposed to the military or religion.
senses.example: She went into civil service because she wanted to help the people.

senses.gloss: Behaving in a reasonable or polite manner; avoiding displays of hostility.
senses.example: It was very civil of him to stop the argument.

senses.gloss: In a peaceful and well-ordered state.
senses.example:
Herein thou haſt done good ſeruice to thy country:
VVere all inhumaine ſlaues ſo ſerued as he,
