examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He told her how passionately he loved her, and reminded her of all the devotion he had lavished upon her.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자신이 얼마나 열정적으로 그녀를 사랑하는지 말했고, 그녀에게 쏟아부었던 모든 헌신을 상기시켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He could not do enough to show his gratitude for the whole-hearted devotion with which she had accepted the burden he laid on her.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자신이 그녀에게 지운 짐을 온 마음으로 받아들인 그녀의 헌신적인 보살핌에 감사를 표하기 위해 온갖 정성을 다했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To stress or give more importance to something.

senses.gloss: Alternative spelling of emphasize.
senses.example: It has emphasised that the proposals do not involve any work on the railway itself, so train services would continue to run throughout.

examples.text: It seemed to emphasise the unconquerable spirit of man.
examples.translation_ko: 그것이 인간의 불굴의 정신을 강조하는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I think I should have emphasised his patience with the unsuitable mate, and the compassion which made him unwilling to throw off the yoke that oppressed him.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 부적절한 배우자에 대한 그의 인내심과, 자신을 억압하는 멍에를 벗어던지기를 꺼리게 만든 연민을 강조했을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English aspect, from Latin aspectus (“look, sight; appearance”), from aspiciō (“see; catch sight of; inspect”), from ad- (“to, towards,...
definition_en: A particular part or feature of something.

senses.gloss: Any specific feature, part, or element of something.
senses.example: Japan's aging population is an important aspect of its economy.

senses.gloss: The way something appears when viewed from a certain direction or perspective.
senses.example: Given the limitations of planar representation[…] The painter is constantly forced to choose one aspect over the other.

senses.gloss: The way something appears when considered from a certain point of view.
senses.example: in certain aspects [ = in certain respects]

examples.text: With enchanting murmurs Daisy admired this aspect or that of the feudal silhouette against the sky, admired the gardens, the sparkling odour of jonquils and the frothy odour of hawthorn and plum blossoms and the pale gold odour of kiss-me-at-the-gate.
examples.translation_ko: 황홀한 중얼거림과 함께 데이지는 하늘을 배경으로 한 봉건적 실루엣의 이런저런 면모를 감탄했고, 정원들과 수선화의 반짝이는 향기, 산사나무와 자두꽃의 거품 같은 향기, 그리고 키스미앳더게이트의 창백한 금빛 향기를 감탄했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: You felt that it was ready to be wafted away on the immaterial air, and death bore all the aspect of a beloved friend.”
examples.translation_ko: 그 영혼은 무형의 대기 속으로 언제든 떠날 준비가 되어 있는 것 같았고, 죽음은 사랑하는 친구의 모든 면모를 지니고 있었다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: With his untidy beard and long hair, his features, always a little larger than life, now emphasised by illness, he had an extraordinary aspect; but it was so odd that it was not quite ugly.
examples.translation_ko: 단정하지 못한 수염과 긴 머리카락, 원래도 평범보다 큰 편이던 이목구비가 이제 병으로 인해 더욱 두드러져 보이는 그의 모습은 기이했다. 하지만 너무 특이해서 오히려 추하지는 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Derived from Middle French sensualité, derived from Late Latin sēnsuālitātem (“sensibility, capacity for sensation”). By surface analysis, sensual ...
definition_en: The quality of being sensual or having a strong appreciation for sensuality.

senses.gloss: The state of being sensual or sensuous.
A preoccupation with sensual pleasure.

examples.text: It was not exactly spirituality that was obvious, though the screen of the flesh seemed almost transparent, because there was in his face an outrageous sensuality; but, though it sounds nonsense, it seemed as though his sensuality were curiously spiritual.
examples.translation_ko: 육체라는 가림막이 거의 투명해 보일 정도였지만, 그의 얼굴에는 노골적인 관능성이 있었기 때문에 정확히 영성이 드러나 보인다고 할 수는 없었다. 하지만 말이 안 되는 소리 같지만, 그의 관능성이 묘하게 영적인 것처럼 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His appearance was wild and uncouth; there was aloofness in his eyes and sensuality in his mouth; he was big and strong; he gave the impression of untamed passion; and perhaps she felt in him, too, that sinister element which had made me think of those wild beings of the world’s early history when matter, retaining its early connection with the earth, seemed to possess yet a spirit of its own.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 모습은 거칠고 조야했다. 그의 눈에는 냉담함이, 입에는 관능이 있었다. 그는 크고 강했으며, 길들여지지 않은 열정의 인상을 주었다. 그리고 아마도 그녀는 그에게서도 그 불길한 요소를 느꼈을 것이다. 그것은 물질이 대지와의 초기 연결을 유지하며 아직 고유한 정신을 지니고 있는 듯했던 세계 초기 역사의 야생 존재들을 떠올리게 했던 바로 그 요소였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English yvel, evel, ivel, uvel, from Old English yfel, from Proto-West Germanic *ubil, from Proto-Germanic *ubilaz (compare Saterland F...
definition_en: A morally bad or wrong action or thing.

senses.gloss: Intending to harm; malevolent.
senses.example: an evil plot to brainwash and even kill innocent people

senses.gloss: Morally corrupt.
senses.example: If something is evil, it is never mandatory.

senses.gloss: Unpleasant, foul (of odor, taste, mood, weather, etc.).
senses.example: Everyone in the tiny, crowded, hot, and evil-smelling kitchen […] has been invited to participate in a moment of history.

examples.text: I had again the feeling that he was possessed of a devil; but you could not say that it was a devil of evil, for it was a primitive force that existed before good and ill.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 다시 그가 악마에게 사로잡혀 있다는 느낌을 받았다. 하지만 그것이 악한 악마라고는 할 수 없었다. 선악이 생기기 이전부터 존재했던 원시적 힘이었기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He recognises in himself an artistic satisfaction in the contemplation of evil which a little startles him; but sincerity forces him to confess that the disapproval he feels for certain actions is not nearly so strong as his curiosity in their reasons.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 악을 관조할 때 느끼는 예술적 만족감을 자신 안에서 인식하며 약간 놀라게 되지만, 솔직함이 그로 하여금 특정 행위들에 대해 느끼는 불쾌감이 그 이유에 대한 호기심만큼 강하지 않다는 것을 고백하게 만든다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English hevely, hevyliche, from Old English hefiġlīċe (“heavily; grievously”), equivalent to heavy + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is done or affected very much.

senses.gloss: With a great weight.
senses.example: heavily burdened

senses.gloss: To a considerable degree, to a great extent.
senses.example: He relied heavily on the data collected by the others.

senses.gloss: In a manner designed for heavy duty.
senses.example: heavily armed soldiers; heavily armoured tanks; heavily reinforced walls

examples.text: “You ought to live in California—” began Miss Baker, but Tom interrupted her by shifting heavily in his chair.
examples.translation_ko: "당신은 캘리포니아에서 살아야—" 베이커 양이 말을 시작했지만, 톰이 의자에서 몸을 크게 움직이며 그녀의 말을 가로막았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The tears coursed down her cheeks—not freely, however, for when they came into contact with her heavily beaded eyelashes they assumed an inky colour, and pursued the rest of their way in slow black rivulets.
examples.translation_ko: 눈물이 그녀의 뺨을 타고 흘러내렸다—하지만 자유롭게 흐르지는 못했는데, 구슬이 촘촘히 박힌 속눈썹에 닿자 잉크 색깔을 띠게 되어 느린 검은 물줄기가 되어 나머지 길을 이어갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Stroeve liked his ease, and in his studio were a couple of heavily upholstered arm-chairs and a large divan.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 안락함을 좋아해서, 그의 작업실에는 푹신한 안락의자 두 개와 큰 소파가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French, from Ottoman Turkish دیوان (divan), from Classical Persian دیوان (dēwān), from Middle Persian d(p)ywʾn' (dēwān, “archive, col...
definition_en: A long, upholstered seat for two or more people.

senses.gloss: A Muslim council of state, specifically that of viziers of the Ottoman Empire that discussed and recommended new laws and law changes to a higher authority (the sultan).
The council chamber where this court is held; (by extension), any court of justice.
Any council or assembly.
senses.example: As I passed, I called at the mad-house; where I found Mac Fane and the scowling keeper in high divan.

examples.text: She was extended full length at her end of the divan, completely motionless, and with her chin raised a little, as if she were balancing something on it which was quite likely to fall.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 긴 의자 끝에서 온몸을 쭉 뻗고 완전히 움직이지 않은 채 턱을 조금 들고 있었는데, 마치 떨어지기 쉬운 무언가를 그 위에 균형잡고 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I had a divan in my sitting-room, and could very well sleep on that.
examples.translation_ko: 거실에 소파가 하나 있었으니 거기서 자는 것쯤은 충분히 괜찮았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Stroeve liked his ease, and in his studio were a couple of heavily upholstered arm-chairs and a large divan.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 안락함을 좋아해서, 그의 작업실에는 푹신한 안락의자 두 개와 큰 소파가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French affectation and its etymon Latin affectātiōnem, from affectō (“I feign”). By surface analysis, affect + -ation.
definition_en: Excessive or affected behavior.

senses.gloss: An attempt to assume or exhibit what is not natural or real; false display; artificial show.
senses.example: This poem is strongly tinctured with those pedantic affectations concerning the passion of love ...

senses.gloss: An unusual mannerism.
An ostentatious fondness for something.
senses.example: Her upper part of decent diſcipline / Shew’d affecation of an ancient line: / And fathers, councils, church and churches head, / Were on her reverend Phylacteries read.

examples.text: The bored haughty face that she turned to the world concealed something—most affectations conceal something eventually, even though they don’t in the beginning—and one day I found what it was.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 세상을 향해 보이는 지루하고 거만한 얼굴은 무언가를 감추고 있었다—대부분의 가식은 결국 무언가를 감추게 마련이다. 처음에는 그렇지 않더라도—그리고 어느 날 나는 그것이 무엇인지 알게 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: No affectation of peculiarity can conceal a commonplace mind.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 기이함의 가식도 평범한 정신을 감출 수는 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Strickland would not go near them, not from any affectation of stoicism, for I found him seated on a three-legged stool when I went into the studio one day and he was alone, but because he did not like them.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 그것들 근처에 가려 하지 않았는데, 금욕주의를 가장하려는 것이 아니었다. 어느 날 내가 작업실에 들어갔을 때 그가 혼자서 다리 셋 달린 의자에 앉아 있는 것을 보았기 때문이다. 그는 단지 그런 것들을 좋아하지 않았을 뿐이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English onhappily, unhappili, unhappily, unhappyly; equivalent to un- + happily or unhappy + -ly.
definition_en: In an unhappy manner.

senses.gloss: Unfortunately; regrettably.
senses.example: Theodore Roosevelt […] added, perhaps unhappily, that he believed the US administration in the Philippines could learn a lot from the Austrian example.

senses.gloss: Through evil fate or chance; wretchedly.
Without happiness; sadly.

examples.text: When Klipspringer had played “The Love Nest” he turned around on the bench and searched unhappily for Gatsby in the gloom.
examples.translation_ko: 클립스프링거가 "사랑의 보금자리"를 연주하고 나서 벤치에서 몸을 돌려 어둠 속에서 개츠비를 불안하게 찾았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But with every word she was drawing further and further into herself, so he gave that up, and only the dead dream fought on as the afternoon slipped away, trying to touch what was no longer tangible, struggling unhappily, undespairingly, toward that lost voice across the room.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그가 말할 때마다 그녀는 점점 더 자기 안으로 움츠러들었고, 그래서 그는 포기할 수밖에 없었다. 오후가 흘러가는 동안 오직 죽은 꿈만이 계속 싸웠다. 더 이상 만질 수 없는 것을 만지려 애쓰며, 방 저편의 잃어버린 목소리를 향해 불행하게, 절망하지 않으면서 몸부림쳤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He glanced unhappily at one of the pictures on the wall.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 벽에 걸린 그림 중 하나를 불안한 눈빛으로 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A room for receiving guests or for socializing.

senses.gloss: Commonwealth standard spelling of parlor.
senses.example: Will you walk into my parlour, said a Spider to a Fly; / 'Tis the prettiest little parlour that ever you did spy.

examples.text: And we all took the less explicable step of engaging the parlour of a suite in the Plaza Hotel.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 우리는 모두 설명하기 어려운 행동을 했다—플라자 호텔 스위트룸의 응접실을 빌린 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For all I know, this picture may still adorn the parlour of the tumbledown little house somewhere near the Quai de la Joliette, and I suppose it could now be sold for fifteen hundred pounds.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 아는 한, 이 그림은 아직도 케 드 라 졸리에트 근처 어딘가에 있는 허름한 작은 집 응접실을 장식하고 있을지도 모르며, 지금이라면 1500파운드에 팔릴 수 있을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was about ten o’ clock at night; I had been dining by myself at a restaurant, and having returned to my small apartment, was sitting in my parlour, reading I heard the cracked tinkling of the bell, and, going into the corridor, opened the door.
examples.translation_ko: 밤 열 시쯤이었다. 나는 식당에서 혼자 저녁을 먹고 작은 아파트로 돌아와 응접실에 앉아 책을 읽고 있었는데, 종이 갈라진 소리로 딸랑거리는 것을 듣고 복도로 나가 문을 열었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French corridor, from Italian corridore (“long passage”) (= corridoio), from correre (“to run”).
definition_en: A long, narrow passage or hallway.

senses.gloss: A narrow hall or passage with rooms leading off it, as in a building or in a railway carriage.
senses.example: Eldridge closed the despatch-case with a snap and, rising briskly, walked down the corridor to his solitary table in the dining-car.

senses.gloss: A restricted tract of land that allows passage between two places.
The covered way lying round the whole compass of the fortifications of a place.

examples.text: There was a ripe mystery about it, a hint of bedrooms upstairs more beautiful and cool than other bedrooms, of gay and radiant activities taking place through its corridors, and of romances that were not musty and laid away already in lavender but fresh and breathing and redolent of this year’s shining motorcars and of dances whose flowers were scarcely withered.
examples.translation_ko: 그 집에는 무르익은 신비로움이 있었다. 위층의 침실들이 다른 침실들보다 더 아름답고 시원하다는 암시, 복도를 통해 벌어지는 유쾌하고 찬란한 활동들, 그리고 곰팡내 나며 이미 라벤더 향 속에 묻혀버린 것이 아니라 올해의 빛나는 자동차들의 향기와 꽃이 아직 시들지 않은 무도회의 향기로 신선하고 생생하게 숨 쉬는 로맨스들의 암시가 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was about ten o’ clock at night; I had been dining by myself at a restaurant, and having returned to my small apartment, was sitting in my parlour, reading I heard the cracked tinkling of the bell, and, going into the corridor, opened the door.
examples.translation_ko: 밤 열 시쯤이었다. 나는 식당에서 혼자 저녁을 먹고 작은 아파트로 돌아와 응접실에 앉아 책을 읽고 있었는데, 종이 갈라진 소리로 딸랑거리는 것을 듣고 복도로 나가 문을 열었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But when we arrived at the hospital, a gaunt, cheerless building, the mere sight of which was enough to make one’s heart sick, and after being directed from this official to that, up endless stairs and through long, bare corridors, found the doctor in charge of the case, we were told that the patient was too ill to see anyone that day.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 우리가 병원에 도착했을 때—보기만 해도 마음이 아플 만큼 을씨년스럽고 삭막한 건물이었다—이 직원에게서 저 직원에게로, 끝없는 계단을 오르고 길고 삭막한 복도를 지나 담당 의사를 찾아갔지만, 환자가 그날은 누구도 만날 수 없을 만큼 위중하다는 말을 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From hysteric + -al, from Latin hystericus, from Ancient Greek ὑστερικός (husterikós, “suffering in the womb, hysterical”), from ῠ̔στέρᾱ (hŭstérā, ...
definition_en: Extremely emotional or irrational.

senses.gloss: Of, or arising from hysteria.
senses.example: An event of this nature, a marriage, or a refusal, or a proposal, thrills through a whole household of women, and sets all their hysterical sympathies at work.

senses.gloss: Having, or prone to having hysterics.
Provoking uncontrollable laughter.

examples.text: He knew women early, and since they spoiled him he became contemptuous of them, of young virgins because they were ignorant, of the others because they were hysterical about things which in his overwhelming self-absorption he took for granted.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 일찍부터 여자들을 알았고, 여자들이 그를 응석받이로 키웠기 때문에 그녀들을 경멸하게 되었다. 젊은 처녀들은 무지하다고, 다른 여자들은 그의 압도적인 자기도취 속에서 그가 당연하게 여기는 것들에 대해 히스테리를 부린다고 여겼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You’re an hysterical ass,” I said a little impatiently.
examples.translation_ko: "자네는 히스테리를 부리는 바보야." 나는 약간 성가신 듯 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Moreover, to him the affair was commonplace; it was just an hysterical woman who had quarrelled with her lover and taken poison; it was constantly happening.
examples.translation_ko: 게다가 그에게 이 일은 흔한 일이었다. 연인과 다투고 독을 먹은 히스테리적인 여자일 뿐이었고, 늘 일어나는 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English whistel, whistil, whistle, from Old English hwistle, from the verb (see below).
definition_en: To make a high-pitched sound with the tongue.

senses.gloss: A device designed to be placed in the mouth and blown, or driven by steam or some other mechanism, to make a whistling sound.
An act of whistling.
A shrill, high-pitched sound made by whistling.

examples.text: He made the parcel and he whistled a tune.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 소포를 만들며 콧노래를 불렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He went on whistling as though it had nothing to do with him.”
examples.translation_ko: 마치 자신과는 상관없는 일이라는 듯 계속 휘파람을 불었다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *h₁én
The verb is borrowed from Middle French implorer (modern French implorer (“to beg, plead, implore”)), or directly from its etymon L...
definition_en: Beg or plead urgently for something.

senses.gloss: To beg or plead for (something) earnestly or urgently; to beseech.
senses.example: The man told his story with many tears, and produced a letter written in the king's hand, and addressed to no particular person, but imploring the aid of all good Englishmen.

senses.gloss: To beg or plead that (someone) earnestly or urgently do something; to beseech, to entreat.
senses.example: A prayer lies bound in me / And implores a god, / And implores a name.

senses.gloss: Often followed by for (a thing) or of (a person): to express an earnest or urgent plea.
senses.example: "Do not let me think of them too often, too much, too fondly," I implored; […]

examples.text: Eluding Jordan’s undergraduate, who was now engaged in an obstetrical conversation with two chorus girls, and who implored me to join him, I went inside.
examples.translation_ko: 지금 두 코러스 걸과 산부인과 얘기에 열중하며 나에게 합류하라고 애원하는 조던의 대학생을 피해 나는 안으로 들어갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He implored her not to leave him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀에게 자신을 떠나지 말아달라고 간청했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Have mercy on her,” he implored him.
examples.translation_ko: "그녀에게 자비를 베풀어 주세요." 그가 애원했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English mercy, merci, from Anglo-Norman merci (compare continental Old French merci, mercit), from Latin mercēs (“wages, fee, price”), ...
definition_en: Compassionate treatment of those who are guilty.

senses.gloss: Relenting; forbearance to cause or allow harm to another.
senses.example: She took mercy on him and quit embarrassing him.

senses.gloss: Forgiveness or compassion, especially toward those less fortunate.
senses.example: Have mercy on the poor and assist them if you can.

senses.gloss: A tendency toward forgiveness, pity, or compassion.
senses.example: Mercy is one of his many virtues.

examples.text: “Have mercy on her,” he implored him.
examples.translation_ko: "그녀에게 자비를 베풀어 주세요." 그가 애원했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is a mercy when it runs its course quickly.”
examples.translation_ko: 빨리 진행되어 끝나는 것이 차라리 자비로운 일이지요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English stakeren, from Old Norse stakra (“to push, stagger”). Cognate with dialectal Danish stagre.
definition_en: To walk unsteadily or be shocked.

senses.gloss: An unsteady movement of the body in walking or standing as if one were about to fall; a reeling motion.
senses.example: the stagger of a drunken man

senses.gloss: A disease of horses and other animals, attended by reeling, unsteady gait or sudden falling.
senses.example: parasitic staggers

senses.gloss: Bewilderment; perplexity.

examples.text: The idea staggered me.
examples.translation_ko: 그 생각만으로도 나는 충격에 휩싸였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He staggered to his feet, but still he would not let her go.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 비틀거리며 일어났지만, 여전히 그녀를 놓아주려 하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Strickland was taken by surprise and he staggered, but he was very strong, even after his illness, and in a moment, he did not exactly know how, Stroeve found himself on the floor.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 불의의 일격에 비틀거렸지만, 병을 앓은 후에도 여전히 힘이 셌고, 순식간에 어떻게 된 일인지도 모르는 사이에 스트루브는 바닥에 나뒹굴고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English tumblen (“to fall over and over again, tumble”), frequentative of Middle English tumben (“to fall, leap, dance”), from Old Engl...
definition_en: Fall or drop suddenly.

senses.gloss: A fall, especially end over end.
senses.example: I took a tumble down the stairs and broke my tooth.

senses.gloss: A disorderly heap.
An act of sexual intercourse.
senses.example: When you've just had a tumble between the sheets and are feeling rumpled and lazy, she may want to get up so she can make the bed.

examples.text: There must have been moments even that afternoon when Daisy tumbled short of his dreams—not through her own fault, but because of the colossal vitality of his illusion.
examples.translation_ko: 그날 오후에도 분명 데이지가 그의 꿈에 미치지 못하는 순간들이 있었을 것이다—그녀 자신의 잘못이 아니라, 그의 환상이 지닌 거대한 생명력 때문에.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We pushed aside curtains that were like pavilions, and felt over innumerable feet of dark wall for electric light switches—once I tumbled with a sort of splash upon the keys of a ghostly piano.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 천막 같은 커튼들을 밀어젖히고, 전등 스위치를 찾아 어둠 속 벽면을 끝없이 더듬었다—한 번은 유령 같은 피아노 건반 위에 철퍼덕 소리를 내며 넘어지기도 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His spectacles had tumbled off in the struggle, and he could not immediately see them.
examples.translation_ko: 몸싸움 중에 안경이 떨어져서 당장 찾을 수가 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English gronen, granen, from Old English grānian (“to groan; lament; murmur”), from Proto-West Germanic *grainōn, from Proto-Germanic *...
definition_en: To make a low, sad sound.

senses.gloss: A low, mournful sound uttered in pain or grief.
A low, guttural sound uttered in frustration, disapproval, or ecstasy.
A low creaking sound from applied pressure or weight.

examples.text: She heard someone groaning.
examples.translation_ko: 누군가 신음하는 소리가 들렸대요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Oh, my dear,” he groaned at last, “how can you be so cruel?”
examples.translation_ko: "오, 여보," 그가 마침내 신음하듯 말했다. "어떻게 그렇게 잔인할 수 있어?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English instant (“infinitely short period of time”), from Old French instant (“assiduous, at hand”, adjective), from Latin īnstāns, īns...
definition_en: A moment or a very short period of time.

senses.gloss: A very short period of time; a moment.
senses.example: She paused for only an instant, which was just enough time for John to change the subject.

senses.gloss: A single, usually precise, point in time.
senses.example: The instant the alarm went off, he fled the building.

senses.gloss: A beverage or food which has been pre-processed to reduce preparation time, especially instant coffee.

examples.text: There was an instant of complete silence, but when Tough Bill threw himself on Strickland the lust of battle seized them all, and in a moment there was a confused scrimmage.
examples.translation_ko: 순간 완전한 정적이 흘렀지만, 터프 빌이 스트릭랜드에게 달려들자 싸움의 욕망이 모든 이를 사로잡았고, 순식간에 혼란스러운 난투가 벌어졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She had not yielded for an instant to the enervating charm of the tropics, but contrariwise was more active, more worldly, more decided than anyone in a temperate clime would have thought it possible to be.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 열대 지방의 나른한 매력에 한 순간도 굴복하지 않았으며, 오히려 온대 기후에 사는 누구라도 가능하리라 생각했을 것보다 더 활동적이고, 더 세속적이고, 더 단호했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From resent + -ment, after Middle French and French ressentiment (in Old French as recentement), from an archaic usage of the verb ressentir via Ol...
definition_en: A feeling of indignant discontent.

senses.gloss: Anger or displeasure stemming from belief that one has been wronged or betrayed by others; indignation.
senses.example: Amongst the most violent against him was Mrs. Bennet, whose dislike of his general behaviour, was sharpened into particular resentment, by his having slighted one of her daughters.

senses.gloss: The state of holding something in the mind as a subject of contemplation, or of being inclined to reflect upon it; feeling; impression.
senses.example: It is a greater wonder that so many of them die, with so little resentment of their danger.

senses.gloss: Satisfaction; gratitude.
senses.example: The Council taking notice of the many good services performed by Mr. John Milton […] have thought fit to declare their resentment and good acceptance of the same.

examples.text: I tried to think about Gatsby then for a moment, but he was already too far away, and I could only remember, without resentment, that Daisy hadn’t sent a message or a flower.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 잠시 개츠비를 생각해보려 했지만, 그는 이미 너무 멀리 가 있었고, 나는 원망 없이 다만 데이지가 편지 한 통이나 꽃 한 송이도 보내지 않았다는 것만 기억할 수 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He seemed to bear no resentment.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아무런 원망도 품지 않는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “It must be reassuring to you to know that you certainly run no risk of incurring the resentment of the women you come in contact with,” I retorted.
examples.translation_ko: "당신과 접촉하는 여자들의 원한을 살 위험은 전혀 없다는 걸 아니 안심이 되겠군요." 내가 쏘아붙였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English blyndnes, blyndnesse, from Old English blindnes (“blindness”), equivalent to blind + -ness.
definition_en: A condition of being unable to see.

senses.gloss: The condition of being blind; unable to see.
senses.example: DHPG […] is effective in fighting Cytomegalovirus (CMV), a common virus which, for PWAs, can cause CMV retinitis — a condition which can lead to blindness within weeks.

senses.gloss: Want of intellectual or moral discernment; mental darkness; ignorance, heedlessness.
concealment

examples.text: Evidently some wild wag of an oculist set them there to fatten his practice in the borough of Queens, and then sank down himself into eternal blindness, or forgot them and moved away.
examples.translation_ko: 분명히 어떤 괴짜 안과의사가 퀸스 구에서 장사를 늘리려고 그것들을 거기 세워놓았다가, 자신은 영원한 실명 속으로 가라앉거나 아니면 그것들을 잊어버리고 다른 곳으로 이사를 간 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Now something occurred to him that he had not told me before; now he discussed what he ought to have said instead of what he did say; then he lamented his blindness.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 전에 내게 말하지 않았던 것이 떠오르기도 하고, 이제 실제로 한 말 대신 했어야 할 말을 논하기도 하고, 그러다가 자신의 맹목을 한탄하기도 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But the blindness of love led her to believe what she wanted to be true, and her love was so great that it seemed impossible to her that it should not in return awake an equal love.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 사랑의 맹목이 그녀로 하여금 믿고 싶은 것을 믿게 만들었고, 그녀의 사랑이 너무나 컸기에 그것이 똑같은 사랑을 불러일으키지 않는다는 것은 불가능해 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham
