senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of lose

examples.text: For the present he seemed quite lost.
examples.translation_ko: 당장은 그가 완전히 길을 잃은 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I lived at the Hôtel de la Fleur, and Mrs. Johnson, the proprietress, had a sad story to tell of lost opportunity.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 호텔 드 라 플뢰르에 머물렀는데, 여관 주인인 존슨 부인에게는 놓친 기회에 대한 슬픈 이야기가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English vīne, from Anglo-Norman vigne, from Vulgar Latin vīnia, from Latin vīnea (“vines in a vineyard”), from vīneus (“related to wine...
definition_en: A plant that produces grapes or other fruit.

senses.gloss: Any plant whose stem requires support and which climbs by tendrils or twining.
Any plant the stem of which creeps along the ground.
A stem of such plants, especially when thick and rope-like; a liana.
senses.example: I could have easily been in the Congo. Trees, Tarzan-like vines, creepy crawlies, spiders and more spiders.

examples.text: Tom stopped beside the porch and looked up at the second floor, where two windows bloomed with light among the vines.
examples.translation_ko: 톰은 현관 옆에 차를 세우고 이층을 올려다보았는데, 덩굴 사이로 두 개의 창문이 불빛으로 피어나고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The lawn started at the beach and ran towards the front door for a quarter of a mile, jumping over sundials and brick walks and burning gardens—finally when it reached the house drifting up the side in bright vines as though from the momentum of its run.
examples.translation_ko: 잔디밭은 해변에서 시작되어 정문까지 4분의 1마일을 달려갔는데, 해시계와 벽돌길과 타오르는 듯한 정원들을 뛰어넘더니 마침내 집에 다다라서는 달려온 탄력으로 밝은 덩굴이 되어 건물 옆면을 타고 올라갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It is a passive feeling capable of being roused for any object, as the vine can grow on any tree; and the wisdom of the world recognises its strength when it urges a girl to marry the man who wants her with the assurance that love will follow.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 포도덩굴이 어떤 나무에든 자랄 수 있듯이 어떤 대상에든 불러일으킬 수 있는 수동적인 감정이다. 그리고 세상의 지혜는 그 힘을 인정하기에 소녀에게 자신을 원하는 남자와 결혼하라고 권하며 사랑은 뒤따라올 것이라고 확신시킨다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English chacen, from Anglo-Norman chacer, Old French chacier, from Vulgar Latin *captiāre, from Latin captāre, frequentative of capere....
definition_en: A person or animal that is being pursued.

senses.gloss: The act of one who chases another; a pursuit.
A hunt; the act of hunting; the pursuit of game.
A children's game where one player chases another.
senses.example: So we played chase up and down the concourses of the airport.

examples.text: Gray clouds chased one another across the sky.
examples.translation_ko: 회색 구름들이 하늘을 가로질러 서로를 쫓아갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They chased one another with shrill cries and laughter, and their bodies, brown and wet, gleamed in the sunlight.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 날카로운 외침과 웃음소리를 내며 서로를 쫓아다녔고, 갈색의 젖은 몸이 햇빛에 반짝였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pursuyte, from Old French poursuite, from the verb porsuir (“to pursue”).
definition_en: The act of pursuing or chasing something.

senses.gloss: The act of pursuing.
senses.example: Unremitting pursuit of wealth doesn't bring happiness, particularly if successful.

senses.gloss: A hobby or recreational activity, done regularly.
A discipline in track cycling where two opposing teams start on opposite sides of the track and try to catch their opponents.

examples.text: I had a fleeting glimpse of a pursuit of the ineffable.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 형언할 수 없는 것을 추구하는 모습을 잠깐 엿보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Did he dream of the nymph flying through the woods of Greece with the satyr in hot pursuit?
examples.translation_ko: 그는 사티로스의 뜨거운 추격을 받으며 그리스 숲속을 달아나는 님프를 꿈꾸고 있는 것일까?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English costen, from Old French coster, couster (“to cost”), from Medieval Latin cōstō, from Latin cōnstō (“stand together”).
definition_en: The amount of money required to buy or maintain something.

senses.gloss: To incur a charge of; to require payment of a (specified) price.
senses.example: This shirt cost $50, while this was cheaper at only $30.

senses.gloss: To cause something to be lost; to cause the expenditure or relinquishment of.
senses.example: Trying to rescue the man from the burning building cost them their lives.

senses.gloss: To require to be borne or suffered; to cause.
senses.example: LUKE: "That little droid is going to cost me a lot of trouble."

examples.text: I would not have given the cost of postage for the picture.
examples.translation_ko: 저는 그 그림에 우편료만큼의 값어치도 매기지 않았을 것입니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was not strange that he should so heartlessly have betrayed his friends’ confidence, nor that he hesitated not at all to gratify a whim at the cost of another’s misery.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 친구의 신뢰를 그토록 무정하게 배신한 것도, 다른 사람의 불행을 대가로 자신의 변덕을 채우는 데 조금도 주저하지 않은 것도 이상할 게 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English tygre, in part from Old English tigras (pl.), in part from Anglo-Norman tigre, both from Latin tigris, from Ancient Greek τίγρι...
definition_en: A large carnivorous mammal with orange and black stripes.

senses.gloss: Panthera tigris, a large predatory mammal of the cat family, indigenous to Asia.
A male tiger; as opposed to a tigress.
senses.example: Coordinate term: tigress

senses.gloss: A sabre-toothed tiger (any felid in subfamily †Machairodontinae).

examples.text: I saw the skins of tigers flaming in his palace on the Grand Canal; I saw him opening a chest of rubies to ease, with their crimson-lighted depths, the gnawings of his broken heart.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 대운하의 그의 궁전에서 호랑이 가죽들이 타오르는 것을 보았고, 그가 루비 상자를 열어 진홍빛 깊이로 상처받은 마음의 아픔을 달래는 것을 보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The very phrases were worn so threadbare that they evoked no image except that of a turbaned “character” leaking sawdust at every pore as he pursued a tiger through the Bois de Boulogne.
examples.translation_ko: 그 문구들은 너무 낡아빠져서 부아 드 불로뉴에서 호랑이를 쫓는 터번을 쓴 '인물'이 온몸의 구멍마다 톱밥을 흘리는 모습 외에는 아무런 이미지도 떠올리지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The emotions common to most of us simply did not exist in him, and it was as absurd to blame him for not feeling them as for blaming the tiger because he is fierce and cruel.
examples.translation_ko: 우리 대부분에게 공통된 감정들이 그에게는 아예 존재하지 않았으며, 그런 감정을 느끼지 못한다고 그를 탓하는 것은 호랑이가 사납고 잔혹하다고 탓하는 것만큼이나 어리석은 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From absorb + -ing.
definition_en: Having or showing the ability to absorb something.

senses.gloss: Engrossing, that sustains someone's interest.
senses.example: an absorbing pursuit

senses.gloss: Allowing a process to enter it, but not to leave it.

examples.text: I glanced at Daisy, who was staring terrified between Gatsby and her husband, and at Jordan, who had begun to balance an invisible but absorbing object on the tip of her chin.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 개츠비와 남편 사이에서 겁에 질린 채 바라보고 있는 데이지와, 턱끝에 보이지 않지만 흥미로운 무언가의 균형을 맞추기 시작한 조던을 흘끗 보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Until long habit has blunted the sensibility, there is something disconcerting to the writer in the instinct which causes him to take an interest in the singularities of human nature so absorbing that his moral sense is powerless against it.
examples.translation_ko: 오랜 습관이 감수성을 무디게 만들기 전까지는, 인간 본성의 특이한 면에 빠져들어 도덕적 감각마저 무력하게 만드는 본능이 작가에게는 당황스러운 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Love is absorbing; it takes the lover out of himself; the most clear-sighted, though he may know, cannot realise that his love will cease; it gives body to what he knows is illusion, and, knowing it is nothing else, he loves it better than reality.
examples.translation_ko: 사랑은 모든 것을 흡수한다. 사랑하는 사람을 자기 자신으로부터 벗어나게 한다. 아무리 명석한 사람이라도 자신의 사랑이 끝날 것임을 알면서도 그것을 실감하지 못한다. 사랑은 환상임을 알면서도 그것에 실체를 부여하고, 그것이 환상에 불과함을 알면서도 현실보다 더 사랑한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English foreyn, forein, from Old French forain, from Vulgar Latin *forānus (“outsider, outlander”), from Latin forās (“outside, outdoor...
definition_en: Belonging to or characteristic of a country other than one's own.

senses.gloss: Located outside a country or place, especially one's own.
senses.example: He liked visiting foreign cities.

senses.gloss: Originating from, characteristic of, belonging to, or being a citizen of a country or place other than the one under discussion.
senses.example: There are many more foreign students in Europe since the Erasmus scheme started.

senses.gloss: Relating to a different nation.
senses.example: foreign policy; foreign navies

examples.text: Tom talked incessantly, exulting and laughing, but his voice was as remote from Jordan and me as the foreign clamour on the sidewalk or the tumult of the elevated overhead.
examples.translation_ko: 톰은 쉴 새 없이 떠들며 의기양양해하고 웃어댔지만, 그의 목소리는 조던과 나에게 인도의 시끄러운 외국인들의 소음이나 머리 위 고가철도의 소란만큼이나 멀게 들렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He is no longer an individual, but a thing, an instrument to some purpose foreign to his ego.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 더 이상 개인이 아니라 하나의 사물, 자신의 자아와는 무관한 어떤 목적을 위한 도구가 되어버린다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I could not believe that he would ever suffer that possession of himself which love is; he could never endure a foreign yoke.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 사랑이라는 자기 자신에 대한 지배를 당할 리는 없다고 나는 생각했다. 그는 결코 타인의 멍에를 견딜 수 없는 사람이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: 14th century, via Old French and Latin from Ancient Greek ἀγωνία (agōnía, “emulation, competition, struggle”), from ἀγών (agṓn, “contest”). Specifi...
definition_en: Intense physical or mental suffering.

senses.gloss: Extreme pain.
senses.example: When the weight fell on her foot, she cried out in agony.

senses.gloss: The sufferings of Jesus Christ in the Garden of Gethsemane (often capitalized).
senses.example: And being in an agonie, he prayed more earneſtly,[…].

senses.gloss: Violent contest or striving.
senses.example: The world is convulsed by the agonies of great nations.

examples.text: The agony of it drove him up from the bed and out of the room.
examples.translation_ko: 그 고통이 그를 침대에서 일으켜 방 밖으로 내몰았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There was here, maybe, the opportunity for a modern version of the hero who for the good of mankind exposes himself to the agonies of the damned.
examples.translation_ko: 여기에는 인류의 선을 위해 자신을 저주받은 자들의 고통에 내맡기는 영웅의 현대적 판본을 위한 기회가 있었을지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English veyn, from Old French vain, from Latin vānus (“empty”).
definition_en: Having or showing too much pride in one's appearance or abilities.

senses.gloss: Overly proud of oneself, especially concerning appearance; having a high opinion of one's own accomplishments with slight reason.
senses.example: Every writer is a narcissist. This does not mean that he is vain; it only means that he is hopelessly self-absorbed.

senses.gloss: Having no real substance, value, or importance; empty; void; worthless; unsatisfying.
senses.example: Vain wisdom all, and false philosophy.

senses.gloss: Effecting no purpose; pointless, futile.
senses.example: vain toil    a vain attempt

examples.text: It was vain to seek the analysis of his emotion.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 감정을 분석하려는 시도는 헛된 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Dirk, with his vain lamentations, had begun to bore me, and I avoided his society.
examples.translation_ko: 헛된 한탄만 늘어놓는 더크가 지겨워지기 시작했고, 나는 그와의 만남을 피했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Old French temptacion, from Latin temptatio
Morphologically tempt + -ation
definition_en: A strong attraction to something that is wrong or forbidden.

senses.gloss: The act of tempting.
The condition of being tempted.
Something attractive, tempting or seductive; an inducement, seducement, or enticement.

examples.text: He had no such temptation.
examples.translation_ko: 그에게는 그런 유혹 자체가 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I do not think he resisted the temptation of giving her an account of his troubles.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 그녀에게 자신의 고민을 털어놓고 싶은 유혹을 뿌리치지 못했으리라고 나는 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French tolerance, from Latin tolerantia (“endurance”), from tolerans, present participle of Latin tolerō (“endure”).
definition_en: The ability to accept or tolerate something unpleasant.

senses.gloss: The ability to endure pain or hardship; endurance.
The ability or practice of tolerating; an acceptance of or patience with the beliefs, opinions or practices of others; a lack of bigotry.
The ability of the body (or other organism) to resist the action of a poison, to cope with a dangerous drug or to survive infection by an organism.

examples.text: And, after boasting this way of my tolerance, I come to the admission that it has a limit.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 이렇게 나의 관용에 대해 자랑한 후에, 나는 그것에도 한계가 있다는 것을 인정하게 된다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There is no cruelty greater than a woman’s to a man who loves her and whom she does not love; she has no kindness then, no tolerance even, she has only an insane irritation.
examples.translation_ko: 자신을 사랑하지만 자신은 사랑하지 않는 남자에게 보이는 여자의 잔혹함보다 더한 잔혹함은 없다. 그때 여자에게는 친절함도 없고 관용조차 없으며, 오직 광적인 짜증만이 있을 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Here, on this remote island, he seemed to have aroused none of the detestation with which he was regarded at home, but compassion rather; and his vagaries were accepted with tolerance.
examples.translation_ko: 여기, 이 외딴 섬에서 그는 고국에서 받았던 그런 혐오감을 불러일으키지 않는 것 같았고, 오히려 동정을 받았다. 그리고 그의 기행들도 관용으로 받아들여졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English carpenter, from Anglo-Norman carpenter (compare Old French charpentier), from Late Latin carpentārius (“a carpenter”), from Lat...
definition_en: A person who makes or repairs things with wood.

senses.gloss: A person skilled at carpentry, the trade of cutting and joining timber in order to construct buildings or other structures.

A senior rating in ships responsible for all the woodwork onboard; in the days of sail, a warrant officer responsible for the hull, masts, spars and boats of a ship, and whose responsibility was to sound the well to see if the ship was making water.
A two-wheeled carriage.

examples.text: “My father wished me to become a carpenter like himself.
examples.translation_ko: "아버지는 내가 아버지처럼 목수가 되기를 바라셨습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His father was a carpenter, and they dwelt in a little old red-brick house, neat and clean, by the side of a sluggish canal.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 아버지는 목수였고, 그들은 완만한 운하 옆에 있는 깔끔하고 깨끗한 작은 낡은 붉은 벽돌집에 살고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From lazy + -ly.
definition_en: Done slowly and without much effort.

senses.gloss: In a lazy manner.
senses.example: She lazily scrubbed the pot, but without some real elbow grease it wasn't going to get clean.

senses.gloss: In a slow manner.
senses.example: Her ensign dropped limp like a rag; the muzzles of the long eight-inch guns stuck out all over the low hull; the greasy, slimy swell swung her up lazily and let her down, swaying her thin masts.

examples.text: As we passed over the dark bridge her wan face fell lazily against my coat’s shoulder and the formidable stroke of thirty died away with the reassuring pressure of her hand.
examples.translation_ko: 우리가 어두운 다리를 건널 때 그녀의 창백한 얼굴이 나른하게 내 코트 어깨에 기대었고, 서른이라는 무시무시한 충격은 그녀 손의 든든한 압박감과 함께 사라져갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Some lean lazily against the side-posts, humming to themselves or calling to the passer-by in a raucous voice, and some listlessly read.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 여자들은 문설주에 나른하게 기대어 혼자 콧노래를 부르거나 지나가는 사람에게 쉰 목소리로 소리를 지르고 있었고, 어떤 여자들은 무기력하게 책을 읽고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You could wander along the canal till you came to broad green fields, with windmills here and there, in which cattle, black and white, grazed lazily.
examples.translation_ko: 운하를 따라 걸어가다 보면 넓고 푸른 들판이 나타났고, 여기저기 풍차가 서 있는 가운데 흑백 얼룩의 소들이 느긋하게 풀을 뜯고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *h₂ébōl
Proto-Germanic *aplaz
Proto-West Germanic *applu
Old English æppel
Middle English appel
English apple
Th...
definition_en: A sweet, typically red fruit.

senses.gloss: The fruit of the tree Malus domestica, chiefly with a green, red, or yellow skin, cultivated in temperate climates for cidermaking, cooking, and eating.
senses.example: Close by and under cover, I watched the juicing process. Apples were washed, then tipped, stalks and all, into the crusher and reduced to pulp.

senses.gloss: Often with a qualifying word: any fruit or vegetable, or any other thing (such as a cone or gall) produced by a plant, especially if from a tree and similar to the fruit of Malus domestica (sense 1.1).
senses.example: custard apple    rose apple    thorn apple

senses.gloss: Ellipsis of Adam's apple (“the lump in the throat, usually more noticeable in men than in women; the laryngeal prominence”).
senses.example: The apple in his neck bobbles as he gulps. “You've got to be kidding.” / “No, I'm not. Your inheritance amounts to maybe three hundred thousand dollars."

examples.text: While we admired he brought more and the soft rich heap mounted higher—shirts with stripes and scrolls and plaids in coral and apple-green and lavender and faint orange, with monograms of indian blue.
examples.translation_ko: 우리가 감탄하는 동안 그는 더 많은 셔츠를 가져왔고, 부드럽고 값진 더미는 더욱 높아져갔다—산호색과 연두색과 라벤더색과 연한 주황색의 줄무늬와 소용돌이와 격자무늬가 있는 셔츠들, 인디언 블루 모노그램이 새겨진 것들이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He remained fat, and his round, red cheeks shone like ripe apples.
examples.translation_ko: 여전히 뚱뚱했고, 동그랗고 붉은 뺨은 잘 익은 사과처럼 윤이 났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I saw a neat little old woman, with cheeks like apples, toiling away from morning to night, through the long years, to keep her house trim and spruce.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 사과 같은 볼을 한 단정한 작은 노부인이 긴 세월 동안 아침부터 밤까지 쉬지 않고 일하며 집을 깔끔하고 단정하게 유지하는 모습을 떠올렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Formerly spelt janty, from French gentil. See gentle, and compare genty. Doublet of genteel, gentile, and gentle.
definition_en: A carefree and lively quality.

senses.gloss: Airy; showy; finical.
Characterized by an affected or fantastical manner.
Dapper or stylish.
senses.example: He wore a jaunty outfit that was all the rage.

examples.text: “Please come and see me … Phone book … Under the name of Mrs. Sigourney Howard … My aunt …” She was hurrying off as she talked—her brown hand waved a jaunty salute as she melted into her party at the door.
examples.translation_ko: "꼭 저를 보러 와요… 전화번호부에… 시구어니 하워드 부인 이름으로… 제 이모예요…" 그녀는 말하면서 서둘러 떠나갔다—그녀의 갈색 손이 경쾌한 경례를 흔들며 문가의 일행 속으로 사라져갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She wasn’t able to endure being at a disadvantage and, given this unwillingness, I suppose she had begun dealing in subterfuges when she was very young in order to keep that cool, insolent smile turned to the world and yet satisfy the demands of her hard, jaunty body.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 불리한 처지에 놓이는 것을 견딜 수 없었고, 그런 성격 때문에 아주 어릴 때부터 속임수를 쓰기 시작했을 것이다. 세상을 향해서는 그 차갑고 건방진 미소를 유지하면서도, 동시에 자신의 단단하고 당당한 몸이 요구하는 것들을 만족시키기 위해서 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had great neatness of person, and he continued to wear his spruce black coat and his bowler hat, always a little too small for him, in a dapper, jaunty manner.
examples.translation_ko: 몸단장을 매우 깔끔하게 했고, 언제나 자신에게는 조금 작은 중절모와 함께 단정한 검은 코트를 말쑥하고 경쾌하게 차려입고 다녔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sorow, sorwe, sorghe, sorȝe, from Old English sorg, sorh (“care, anxiety, sorrow, grief”), from Proto-West Germanic *sorgu, fro...
definition_en: A feeling of sadness or regret.

senses.gloss: unhappiness, woe
senses.example: The safe and general antidote against sorrow is employment.

senses.gloss: (usually in plural) An instance or cause of unhappiness.
senses.example: Parting is such sweet sorrow.

examples.text: No—Gatsby turned out all right at the end; it is what preyed on Gatsby, what foul dust floated in the wake of his dreams that temporarily closed out my interest in the abortive sorrows and short-winded elations of men.
examples.translation_ko: 아니다. 개츠비는 결국 괜찮았다. 개츠비를 괴롭힌 것, 그의 꿈의 항적에 떠다니던 더러운 먼지가 인간들의 유산된 슬픔과 숨 가쁜 환희에 대한 내 관심을 일시적으로 차단했던 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I could not help it; I put Stroeve and his sorrows out of my mind.
examples.translation_ko: 어쩔 수 없었다. 나는 스트루브와 그의 슬픔을 마음에서 지워버렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was getting something of a paunch, and sorrow had no effect on it.
examples.translation_ko: 배가 나오기 시작했는데, 슬픔은 그것에 아무런 영향도 미치지 못했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Feeling or showing strong dislike or distaste.

senses.gloss: Filled with disgust.
senses.example: The sight of the squirming mass of maggots left me disgusted.

examples.text: Their interest rather touched me and made them less remotely rich—nevertheless, I was confused and a little disgusted as I drove away.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 관심이 오히려 내 마음을 건드렸고 그들을 덜 동떨어진 부자로 느끼게 했다—그럼에도 불구하고 차를 몰고 떠나면서 나는 혼란스럽고 약간 역겨웠다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: At last I was disgusted with him, and I got a divorce.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 나는 그가 역겨워져서 이혼했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was disgusted with him, and if I had had an opportunity should have been glad to tell him so, but I saw no object in seeking him out for the purpose.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 역겨웠고, 기회가 있었다면 기꺼이 그에게 그런 말을 해주었을 것이지만, 굳이 그를 찾아가서 그런 말을 할 이유는 없다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English exultacion, from Old French exultacion, from Latin exsultātiō, exsultātiōnem.
definition_en: A feeling of great joy or triumph.

senses.gloss: The act of exulting; great joy at success or victory, or at any advantage gained; rapturous delight

examples.text: He literally glowed; without a word or a gesture of exultation a new well-being radiated from him and filled the little room.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 말 그대로 빛이 났다. 한 마디 말이나 기쁨의 몸짓도 없이 새로운 행복감이 그에게서 뿜어져 나와 작은 방을 가득 채웠다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Something seemed to twist his heart, and suddenly he felt an exultation, a sense of wonderful freedom.
examples.translation_ko: 무언가가 그의 심장을 비틀어놓는 것 같았고, 갑자기 그는 환희와 놀라운 자유감을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I always tried my best to beat Strickland, because he was a player who despised the opponent he vanquished; his exultation in victory made defeat more difficult to bear.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 항상 스트릭랜드를 이기려고 최선을 다했는데, 그는 자신이 이긴 상대를 경멸하는 선수였기 때문이다. 승리에 대한 그의 득의양양함은 패배를 더욱 견디기 어렵게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: By surface analysis, follow + -ing.
definition_en: Following something or someone closely

senses.gloss: Coming next, either in sequence or in time.
senses.example: See the following section.

senses.gloss: About to be specified.
senses.example: The following words have no definition[…]

senses.gloss: Blowing in the direction of travel, as opposed to headwind; downwind.
senses.example: The following wind sped us on our way.

examples.text: He had intended, probably, to take what he could and go—but now he found that he had committed himself to the following of a grail.
examples.translation_ko: 아마 그는 얻을 수 있는 것을 취하고 떠날 작정이었을 것이다—하지만 이제 그는 성배를 좇는 일에 자신을 바쳤다는 것을 깨달았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Tom was evidently perturbed at Daisy’s running around alone, for on the following Saturday night he came with her to Gatsby’s party.
examples.translation_ko: 톰은 데이지가 혼자 돌아다니는 것을 분명히 못마땅해했던 모양이다. 그 다음 토요일 밤에는 그녀와 함께 개츠비의 파티에 왔기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: You will always find him at the following address:
examples.translation_ko: 당신은 언제든 다음 주소에서 그를 찾을 수 있을 것이다:
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Recorded since 1375, from Latin lāmentātiō (“wailing, moaning, weeping”), from the deponent verb lāmentor, from lāmentum (“wail; wailing”), itself ...
definition_en: A feeling of sorrow or regret.

senses.gloss: The act of lamenting.
A sorrowful cry; a lament.
Specifically, mourning.

examples.text: Dirk, with his vain lamentations, had begun to bore me, and I avoided his society.
examples.translation_ko: 헛된 한탄만 늘어놓는 더크가 지겨워지기 시작했고, 나는 그와의 만남을 피했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There must have been something terrible in his face, for suddenly they all burst out into loud cries and lamentation.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 얼굴에 무언가 끔찍한 것이 있었음에 틀림없었다. 갑자기 그들이 모두 큰 소리로 울부짖으며 통곡을 터뜨렸기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From fresh + -ness.
definition_en: The state of being fresh.

senses.gloss: The state or quality of being fresh.

examples.text: No amount of fire or freshness can challenge what a man can store up in his ghostly heart.
examples.translation_ko: 인간이 자신의 유령 같은 마음속에 쌓아둘 수 있는 것에는 그 어떤 불길이나 신선함도 맞설 수 없다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She had caught a cold, and it made her voice huskier and more charming than ever, and Gatsby was overwhelmingly aware of the youth and mystery that wealth imprisons and preserves, of the freshness of many clothes, and of Daisy, gleaming like silver, safe and proud above the hot struggles of the poor.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 감기에 걸려 있었는데, 그 때문에 목소리가 더욱 허스키하고 매혹적이 되었고, 개츠비는 부가 가두고 보존하는 젊음과 신비로움을, 수많은 옷들의 신선함을, 그리고 은처럼 빛나며 가난한 자들의 뜨거운 몸부림 위에서 안전하고 당당한 데이지를 압도적으로 의식했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: My thoughts wandered, and I thought of the sunny beaches of Brittany and the freshness of the sea.
examples.translation_ko: 생각이 딴 곳으로 흘러가면서 브르타뉴의 햇살 가득한 해변과 바다의 상쾌함을 떠올렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English spillen, from Old English spillan, spildan (“to kill, destroy, waste”), from Proto-West Germanic *spilþijan, from Proto-Germani...
definition_en: To cause something to fall or flow out.

senses.gloss: To drop something so that it spreads out or makes a mess; to accidentally pour.
senses.example: I spilled some sticky juice on the kitchen floor.

senses.gloss: To spread out or fall out, as above.
senses.example: Some sticky juice spilled onto the kitchen floor.

senses.gloss: To overflow out of a designated area.
senses.example: The crowd spilled onto Maple Avenue.

examples.text: But he wouldn’t eat, and the glass of milk spilled from his trembling hand.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그는 먹으려 하지 않았고, 떨리는 손에서 우유 한 잔이 쏟아졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Laughter is easier minute by minute, spilled with prodigality, tipped out at a cheerful word.
examples.translation_ko: 웃음은 분마다 더 쉬워져서, 아낌없이 쏟아지고, 유쾌한 한마디에 터져 나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He gulped down a mouthful, and some of it was spilt on his shirt-front.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 한 모금을 꿀꺽 삼켰고, 물 일부가 셔츠 앞가슴에 흘러내렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English endeles, from Old English endelēas (“endless”), from Proto-Germanic *andijalausaz (“endless”), equivalent to end + -less.
definition_en: Having no end or limit.

senses.gloss: Having no end.
senses.example: endless time; endless praise

senses.gloss: Extending indefinitely.
senses.example: an endless line

senses.gloss: Too much or many to be exhausted; an extremely high number or amount of; immeasurable, innumerable.
senses.example: In 1903, [Albert Shhoenhut] announced his Humpty Dumpty circus, with over 20 figures and animals, each with six joints enabling them to be put into endless positions.

examples.text: After two years I remember the rest of that day, and that night and the next day, only as an endless drill of police and photographers and newspaper men in and out of Gatsby’s front door.
examples.translation_ko: 2년이 지난 지금 그날 나머지와 그날 밤, 그리고 다음 날을 기억해보면 개츠비의 현관문을 드나드는 경찰과 사진기자들과 신문기자들의 끝없는 행진만이 떠오른다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As I walked up the endless stairs of the house in which Strickland lived, I confess that I was a little excited.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드가 살고 있는 집의 끝없는 계단을 올라가면서, 나는 솔직히 조금 흥분되어 있었다고 고백한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But when we arrived at the hospital, a gaunt, cheerless building, the mere sight of which was enough to make one’s heart sick, and after being directed from this official to that, up endless stairs and through long, bare corridors, found the doctor in charge of the case, we were told that the patient was too ill to see anyone that day.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 우리가 병원에 도착했을 때—보기만 해도 마음이 아플 만큼 을씨년스럽고 삭막한 건물이었다—이 직원에게서 저 직원에게로, 끝없는 계단을 오르고 길고 삭막한 복도를 지나 담당 의사를 찾아갔지만, 환자가 그날은 누구도 만날 수 없을 만큼 위중하다는 말을 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English chargen, from Old French chargier, from Late Latin carricō (“to load”), from Latin carrus (“a car, wagon”); see car. Doublet of...
definition_en: A sum of money owed or due to be paid.

senses.gloss: The amount of money levied for a service.
senses.example: There will be a charge of five dollars.

senses.gloss: A ground attack against a prepared enemy.
senses.example: Pickett's Charge; the Charge of the Light Brigade

senses.gloss: A forceful forward movement.
senses.example: Abou Diaby should have added Arsenal's fourth in the 50th minute after he danced round a host of defenders on a charge towards goal

examples.text: The Asile de Nuit is a large stone building where pauper and vagabond may get a bed for a week, provided their papers are in order and they can persuade the friars in charge that they are workingmen.
examples.translation_ko: 아질 드 뉘는 거대한 석조 건물로, 빈민과 부랑자들이 서류만 제대로 갖추고 관리하는 수사들에게 자신이 노동자임을 납득시킬 수 있다면 일주일간 잠자리를 얻을 수 있는 곳이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They lived with him a month, sleeping with a dozen others, Swedes, negroes, Brazilians, on the floor of the two bare rooms in his house which he assigned to his charges; and every day they went with him to the Place Victor Gélu, whither came ships’ captains in search of a man.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 그와 함께 한 달을 살았는데, 스웨덴인, 흑인, 브라질인 등 십여 명과 함께 그가 하숙생들에게 배정한 집 안의 두 개 빈 방 바닥에서 잠을 잤고, 매일 그와 함께 빅토르 젤뤼 광장으로 가서 사람을 구하러 온 선장들을 만났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English curraunt, borrowed from Old French curant (French courant), present participle of courre (“to run”), from Latin currere (“to ru...
definition_en: Happening or existing at the present time.

senses.gloss: The generally unidirectional movement of a gas or fluid.
senses.example: The mantle is important to our discussion in that its viscous nature can conduct convection currents that have effects on the crust upon which we live.

senses.gloss: The part of a fluid that moves continuously in a certain direction, especially (oceanography) ellipsis of ocean current.
The amount of electric charge flowing in each unit of time.
senses.example: CGS: esu/second (esu/s)

examples.text: So we beat on, boats against the current, borne back ceaselessly into the past.
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 우리는 계속 노를 젓는다, 끊임없이 과거로 밀려나면서도 물살을 거슬러.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It created profound astonishment, and wild rumours were current.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 깊은 충격을 불러일으켰고, 온갖 터무니없는 소문들이 돌았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was obvious that to him Blanche Stroeve was only a unit to be added to the statistical list of attempted suicides in the city of Paris during the current year.
examples.translation_ko: 그에게 블랑슈 스트루브는 올해 파리 시에서 일어난 자살 시도 통계 목록에 추가될 하나의 단위에 불과한 것이 분명했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English myserablie; equivalent to miserable + -ly.
definition_en: Used to express a strong feeling of sadness or disappointment.

senses.gloss: In a miserable manner.
senses.example: fail miserably

examples.text: He sat down miserably, as if I had pushed him, and simultaneously there was the sound of a motor turning into my lane.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내가 밀어붙인 것처럼 비참하게 주저앉았고, 동시에 내 골목으로 자동차가 들어서는 소리가 들렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Very romantic,” he said, and then miserably to me: “If it’s light enough after dinner, I want to take you down to the stables.”
examples.translation_ko: "아주 낭만적이지." 그가 말하고는 나에게 우울하게 덧붙였다. "저녁 식사 후에 충분히 밝다면 마구간으로 데려가고 싶어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I gave him books to read, but after a page or two he would put the book down and stare miserably into space.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 읽을 책을 주었지만, 한두 페이지 읽고 나면 책을 내려놓고 비참하게 허공을 바라보곤 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Late Middle English vocal, borrowed from Latin vōcālis (“uttering a voice, sounding, speaking”), from vōx (“a voice, sound, tone”) + -ālis (“-al”, ...
definition_en: Relating to the voice or singing.

senses.gloss: Used in the production of speech sounds.
senses.example: vocal apparatus

senses.gloss: Relating to, composed or arranged for, or sung by the human voice.

Consisting of, or characterized by, voice, or tone produced in the larynx, which may be modified, either by resonance, as in the case of the vowels, or by obstructive action, as in certain consonants, such as v, l, etc., or by both, as in the nasals m, n, ng.

examples.text: “It appears that her vocal cords have been burnt by the acid.”
examples.translation_ko: "산에 의해 성대가 타버린 것 같습니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He judged that the disease had already attacked the vocal chords.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 병이 이미 성대를 침범했다고 판단했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
Borrowed from French console (“bracket”, noun), from consoler (“to console, to comfort”, verb).
Sense of “bracket” either due to a bracket alleviat...
definition_en: To comfort or reassure someone.

senses.gloss: A stand-alone cabinet designed to stand on the floor; especially, one integrated with home entertainment equipment, such as a TV or stereo system.
senses.example: The film's music blared from the console.

senses.gloss: A desk-like cabinet, table, or stand upon which controls, instruments, and displays are mounted.
The keyboard and screen of a computer or other electronic device.

examples.text: My own house was an eyesore, but it was a small eyesore, and it had been overlooked, so I had a view of the water, a partial view of my neighbour’s lawn, and the consoling proximity of millionaires—all for eighty dollars a month.
examples.translation_ko: 내 집은 눈에 거슬리는 것이었지만, 작게 눈에 거슬리는 것이었고, 간과되어 있었기 때문에 나는 물을 볼 수 있었고, 이웃의 잔디밭을 부분적으로 볼 수 있었으며, 백만장자들의 위안이 되는 근접성을 누릴 수 있었다. 모든 것이 한 달에 80달러였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When he had gone halfway he turned around and stared at the scene—his wife and Catherine scolding and consoling as they stumbled here and there among the crowded furniture with articles of aid, and the despairing figure on the couch, bleeding fluently, and trying to spread a copy of Town Tattle over the tapestry scenes of Versailles.
examples.translation_ko: 중간쯤 갔을 때 그는 돌아서서 그 광경을 바라보았다—그의 아내와 캐서린이 빽빽한 가구들 사이를 이리저리 비틀거리며 구호용품을 들고 꾸짖기도 하고 달래기도 하는 모습, 그리고 소파 위에서 절망에 빠진 채 피를 줄줄 흘리며 베르사유 태피스트리 장면 위에 《타운 태틀》 한 부를 펼쳐 덮으려 애쓰는 모습을.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The nurse was pitiful to his distress, but she had little to say that could console him.
examples.translation_ko: 간호사는 그의 괴로움을 불쌍히 여겼지만, 그를 위로할 만한 말은 거의 해줄 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French formalité. equivalent to formal + -ity.
definition_en: A formal or official quality.

senses.gloss: The state of being formal.
Something said or done as a matter of form.
A customary ritual without substance, real consequence, or unique meaning.
senses.example: The examination for priesthood is no mere formality, so we have to study well.

examples.text: He was saying some last word to her, but the eagerness in his manner tightened abruptly into formality as several people approached him to say goodbye.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀에게 마지막 말을 건네고 있었지만, 몇몇 사람들이 작별 인사를 하러 다가오자 그의 태도에서 드러나던 간절함이 갑자기 격식을 차린 모습으로 굳어졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Precisely at that point it vanished—and I was looking at an elegant young roughneck, a year or two over thirty, whose elaborate formality of speech just missed being absurd.
examples.translation_ko: 바로 그 순간 미소는 사라졌고—나는 서른을 한두 살 넘긴 우아한 젊은 건달을 바라보고 있었는데, 그의 정교한 격식 차린 말투는 우스꽝스러워 보이기 일보 직전이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The circumstances of Blanche Stroeve’s death necessitated all manner of dreadful formalities, but at last we were allowed to bury her.
examples.translation_ko: 블랑슈 스트루브의 죽음으로 인해 온갖 끔찍한 절차들을 거쳐야 했지만, 마침내 우리는 그녀를 매장할 수 있게 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cimiterie, from Old French cimitiere, from Medieval Latin cimitērium, from Late Latin coemētērium, from Ancient Greek κοιμητήρι...
definition_en: A place for burying the dead.

senses.gloss: A place where the dead are buried; a graveyard or memorial park.
senses.example: […] the cemetery – which people of shattering wit like Sampson never tired of calling ‘the dead centre of town’ […]

examples.text: As we started through the gate into the cemetery I heard a car stop and then the sound of someone splashing after us over the soggy ground.
examples.translation_ko: 묘지 문을 통과해 들어가기 시작할 때 차 한 대가 멈춰 서는 소리가 들렸고, 이어서 누군가 질척한 땅을 첨벙거리며 우리를 따라오는 소리가 들렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: About five o’clock our procession of three cars reached the cemetery and stopped in a thick drizzle beside the gate—first a motor hearse, horribly black and wet, then Mr. Gatz and the minister and me in the limousine, and a little later four or five servants and the postman from West Egg, in Gatsby’s station wagon, all wet to the skin.
examples.translation_ko: 다섯 시쯤 되어 세 대의 차로 이루어진 우리 행렬이 묘지에 도착해 문 옆에서 멈춰 섰다. 부슬부슬 내리는 비 속에서—맨 앞에는 끔찍하도록 검고 비에 젖은 영구차가, 그 다음에는 개츠 씨와 목사 그리고 내가 탄 리무진이, 그리고 조금 뒤에는 웨스트에그에서 온 하인 네다섯 명과 우편배달부가 개츠비의 스테이션 왜건을 타고 왔는데, 모두 뼛속까지 젖어 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Dirk and I alone followed the hearse to the cemetery.
examples.translation_ko: 디르크와 나만이 영구차를 따라 묘지까지 갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English trotten, from Old French trotter, troter (“to go, trot”), from Medieval Latin *trottō, *trotō (“to go”), from Frankish *trottōn...
definition_en: To walk or move at a slow pace.

senses.gloss: A gait of a person or animal faster than a walk but slower than a run.
senses.example: Waziri’s warriors marched at a rapid trot through the jungle in the direction of the village.

senses.gloss: A brisk journey or progression.
senses.example: We often take the car and have a trot down to the beach.

senses.gloss: A gait of a four-legged animal between walk and canter, a diagonal gait (in which diagonally opposite pairs of legs move together).
senses.example: Dogs have a variety of gaits. Most dogs have the walk, trot, pace, and gallop.

examples.text: Tom and I shook hands, the rest of us exchanged a cool nod, and they trotted quickly down the drive, disappearing under the August foliage just as Gatsby, with hat and light overcoat in hand, came out the front door.
examples.translation_ko: 톰과 나는 악수를 나누었고, 나머지는 차가운 목례를 주고받았다. 그들은 차도를 따라 재빨리 달려 내려가 8월의 무성한 잎사귀 아래로 사라졌는데, 바로 그때 개츠비가 모자와 가벼운 외투를 손에 든 채 현관문으로 나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For several weeks I didn’t see him or hear his voice on the phone—mostly I was in New York, trotting around with Jordan and trying to ingratiate myself with her senile aunt—but finally I went over to his house one Sunday afternoon.
examples.translation_ko: 몇 주 동안 나는 그를 보지도 못했고 전화로 그의 목소리를 듣지도 못했다. 대부분 나는 뉴욕에 있으면서 조던과 함께 돌아다니며 그녀의 노망든 고모에게 잘 보이려고 애쓰고 있었다. 하지만 마침내 어느 일요일 오후 그의 집으로 찾아갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We went at a foot-pace, but on the way back we trotted, and there was something to my mind singularly horrible in the way the driver of the hearse whipped up his horses.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 걸음걸이로 갔지만, 돌아오는 길에는 속보로 갔는데, 영구차 마부가 말들에게 채찍을 가하는 모습이 내 마음에는 묘하게 끔찍하게 느껴졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cariage, from Old Northern French cariage, from carier (“to carry”).
definition_en: A vehicle with four wheels, typically horse-drawn.

senses.gloss: The act of conveying; carrying.
senses.example: The remainder of the men were employed in unbarreling our Pork and stringing it on poles for convenience of carriage, and carrying our Batteaux from the river to the pond.

senses.gloss: A means of conveyance.
A (mostly four-wheeled) lighter vehicle chiefly designed to transport people, generally drawn by horse power.
senses.example: The carriage ride was very romantic.

examples.text: A dead man passed us in a hearse heaped with blooms, followed by two carriages with drawn blinds, and by more cheerful carriages for friends.
examples.translation_ko: 꽃으로 뒤덮인 영구차에 실린 죽은 자가 우리를 지나쳤고, 블라인드를 내린 두 대의 마차가 뒤따랐으며, 친구들을 태운 더 밝은 마차들이 그 뒤를 이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She was a slender, small-breasted girl, with an erect carriage, which she accentuated by throwing her body backward at the shoulders like a young cadet.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 날씬하고 가슴이 작은 소녀였는데, 꼿꼿한 자세를 하고 있었고, 젊은 사관생도처럼 어깨를 뒤로 젖혀 그 자세를 더욱 강조했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Again he made no reply, but the driver of our carriage came to my rescue.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 또다시 대답하지 않았지만, 마차 운전사가 나를 구해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: By surface analysis, mourn + -ing.
definition_en: A period of grief or sorrow.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of mourn

examples.text: All the cars have the left rear wheel painted black as a mourning wreath, and there’s a persistent wail all night along the north shore.”
examples.translation_ko: 모든 자동차의 왼쪽 뒷바퀴에 조화 대신 검은 페인트를 칠해놓았고, 밤새도록 북쪽 해안을 따라 애절한 곡소리가 끊이지 않아."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was dressed in the deepest mourning, and on his bowler was a broad black band.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 깊은 상복을 입고 있었고, 중절모에는 넓은 검은 띠를 둘렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His plumpness and his red, fat cheeks made his mourning not a little incongruous.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 통통한 몸매와 붉고 살찐 볼은 그의 상복 차림을 적잖이 어울리지 않게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin mania, from Ancient Greek μανία (manía, “madness”).
definition_en: A state of extreme excitement or enthusiasm.

senses.gloss: Violent derangement of mind; madness; insanity.
Excessive or unreasonable desire; insane passion affecting one or many people; fanaticism.
senses.example: One of the manias of the present day, which especially excites my spleen, is the locomotive rage which seems to possess all ranks—that necessity of going out of town in the summer...

senses.gloss: The state of abnormally elevated or irritable mood, arousal, and/or energy levels.

examples.text: It is her mania.
examples.translation_ko: 그것이 아내의 고질병이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is my mania.’
examples.translation_ko: 그게 제 버릇이에요.'
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English upright, uppryght, upriht, from Old English upriht (“upright; erect”), from Proto-Germanic *upprehtaz, equivalent to up- + righ...
definition_en: Standing or behaving correctly and honestly.

senses.gloss: Vertical; erect.
senses.example: Upright posture evolved well before an enlarged brain in hominids.

senses.gloss: In its proper orientation; not overturned.
senses.example: My brother didn't get angry when his son knocked over the lamp; he simply called the boy over and helped him set it upright again.

senses.gloss: Greater in height than breadth.

examples.text: Wilson’s eyes fell upon Tom; he started up on his tiptoes and then would have collapsed to his knees had not Tom held him upright.
examples.translation_ko: 윌슨의 시선이 톰에게 떨어졌다. 그는 발끝으로 일어서려 했지만 톰이 붙잡지 않았다면 무릎을 꿇고 주저앉았을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She held herself upright.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 꼿꼿이 몸을 세우고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His father was a spare old man, his hands gnarled after the work of a lifetime, silent and upright; in the evening he read the paper aloud, while his wife and daughter (now married to the captain of a fishing smack), unwilling to lose a moment, bent over their sewing.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 아버지는 마른 노인으로, 평생의 노동으로 거칠어진 손을 가졌으며, 과묵하고 꼿꼿했다. 저녁이면 그는 신문을 소리 내어 읽었고, 그의 아내와 딸(지금은 어선 선장과 결혼했다)은 한 순간도 허비하지 않으려는 듯 바느질에 몰두했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English prise, from Old French prise (“a taking, capture, a seizure, a thing seized, a prize, booty, also hold, purchase”), past partic...
definition_en: A thing that is given as a reward for winning or achieving something.

senses.gloss: That which is taken from another; something captured; a thing seized by force, stratagem, or superior power.
senses.example:
[…] wherefore he now begunne
To challenge her anew, as his owne prize,
Whom formerly he had in battell wonne,

senses.gloss: Anything captured by a belligerent using the rights of war; especially, property captured at sea in virtue of the rights of war, as a vessel.
An honour or reward striven for in a competitive contest; anything offered to be competed for, or as an inducement to, or reward of, effort.
senses.example: I fought and conquer’d, yet have lost the prize.

examples.text: I got prizes for it at school.
examples.translation_ko: 학교에서 그것으로 상도 받았고요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He got the prizes and the scholarships that I went in for.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 노렸던 상과 장학금을 모두 그가 차지했거든.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From scholar + -ship.
definition_en: A grant or payment made to support the study of a student.

senses.gloss: A grant-in-aid to a student.
senses.example: There is a significant investment in scholarships and fellowships and traineeships, so that we are also making sure that we’re investing in domestic work force.

senses.gloss: The character or qualities of a scholar.
The activity, methods or attainments of a scholar.

examples.text: He got the prizes and the scholarships that I went in for.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 노렸던 상과 장학금을 모두 그가 차지했거든.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: And they sent me to Amsterdam to try for a scholarship, and I won it.
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 그분들이 저를 암스테르담으로 보내 장학금 시험을 치르게 했고, 제가 합격했어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
Borrowed from Middle French impulser, from Latin impulsus.
For spelling, as in pulse, the -e (on -lse) is so the end is pronounced /ls/, rather tha...
definition_en: A sudden strong and unreflective urge to do something.

senses.gloss: A thrust; a push; a sudden force that impels.
senses.example:
c. 1715-1716, Samuel Clarke, letter to Gottfried Wilhelm Leibniz
All spontaneous animal motion is performed by mechanical impulse.

senses.gloss: A wish or urge, particularly a sudden one prompting action.
senses.example: The impulse to learn drove me to study night and day.

senses.gloss: The integral of force over time.
senses.example: The total impulse from the impact will depend on the kinetic energy of the projectile.

examples.text: Some dim impulse moved the policeman to look suspiciously at Tom.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 막연한 직감이 경찰관으로 하여금 톰을 의심스럽게 바라보게 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Moved by an irresistible impulse, Gatsby turned to Tom, who had accepted the introduction as a stranger.
examples.translation_ko: 억누를 수 없는 충동에 이끌려 개츠비는 자신을 낯선 사람으로 받아들인 톰에게 몸을 돌렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had an impulse to run down the stairs after me and beg me to go in with him; he had a feeling that there was somebody in the studio.
examples.translation_ko: 계단을 뛰어내려가 나를 쫓아가서 함께 들어가 달라고 애원하고 싶은 충동이 들었다. 작업실에 누군가 있다는 느낌이 들었던 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English gracious, from Old French gracieus, from Latin gratiosus, from gratia (“esteem, favor”). See grace. Displaced native Old Englis...
definition_en: Showing kindness and consideration.

senses.gloss: kind and warmly courteous
tactful
compassionate

examples.text: He cared nothing for those things which with most people make life gracious and beautiful.
examples.translation_ko: 대부분의 사람들에게 삶을 우아하고 아름답게 만들어주는 것들에 대해 그는 전혀 개의치 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: What had happened could only be a dream, a frightful dream; and when he turned the key and opened the door, he would see her bending slightly over the table in the gracious attitude of the woman in Chardin’s Benedicite, which always seemed to him so exquisite.
examples.translation_ko: 일어난 일은 꿈, 끔찍한 꿈일 뿐이었다. 열쇠를 돌려 문을 열면 샤르댕의 「식사 기도」 속 여인의 우아한 자세로 테이블 위에 살짝 몸을 굽히고 있는 그녀를 보게 될 것이었다. 그 자세는 언제나 그에게 너무도 아름다워 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English forke (“digging fork”), from Old English force, forca (“forked instrument used to torture”), from Proto-West Germanic *furkō (“...
definition_en: A utensil with two or more prongs for picking up food.

senses.gloss: A utensil with spikes used to put solid food into the mouth, or to hold food down while cutting.
Any of several types of pronged tools for use on farms, in fields, or in the garden or lawn, such as a smaller hand fork for weeding or a larger one for turning over the soil.
Such a pronged tool having a long straight handle, generally for two-handed use, as used for digging, lifting, mucking, pitching, etc.

examples.text: So he waited, listening for a moment longer to the tuning-fork that had been struck upon a star.
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 그는 기다렸다, 별 위에서 울린 음차의 소리를 잠시 더 들으면서.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The knives and forks were put away in a drawer.
examples.translation_ko: 나이프와 포크는 서랍에 정리되어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a sudden vision of her standing in the kitchen—it was hardly larger than a cupboard—washing the plates and glasses, the forks and spoons, giving the knives a rapid polish on the knife-board; and then putting everything away, giving the sink a scrub, and hanging the dish-cloth up to dry—it was there still, a gray torn rag; then looking round to see that everything was clean and nice.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 갑자기 그녀가 부엌에 서 있는 모습이 눈에 떠올랐다—찬장보다 조금 클 뿐인 그 부엌에서 접시와 잔들, 포크와 숟가락을 씻고, 칼판에 칼들을 재빠르게 닦아내고, 그런 다음 모든 것을 제자리에 정리하고, 개수대를 문지르고, 행주를 걸어 말리는—그 행주는 아직도 거기 있었다, 회색빛 너덜너덜한 걸레가—그리고 나서 모든 것이 깨끗하고 말끔한지 둘러보는 모습이.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From frighten + -ing.
definition_en: Causing fear or anxiety.

senses.gloss: Causing fear; of capable of causing fear; scary.
senses.example: Riding the rollercoaster was a frightening experience.

senses.gloss: Awful, terrible, very bad.

examples.text: I couldn’t sleep all night; a foghorn was groaning incessantly on the Sound, and I tossed half-sick between grotesque reality and savage, frightening dreams.
examples.translation_ko: 밤새 잠을 이룰 수 없었다. 해협에서 안개 경적이 끊임없이 울어댔고, 나는 기괴한 현실과 야만스럽고 무서운 꿈 사이에서 반쯤 병든 채로 뒤척였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He must have looked up at an unfamiliar sky through frightening leaves and shivered as he found what a grotesque thing a rose is and how raw the sunlight was upon the scarcely created grass.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 무서운 나뭇잎 사이로 낯선 하늘을 올려다보았을 것이고, 장미가 얼마나 기괴한 것인지, 겨우 자라난 풀 위의 햇빛이 얼마나 날것인지 깨달으며 몸서리쳤을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her self-possession was frightening.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 침착함은 무서울 정도였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cloth, clath, from Old English clāþ (“cloth, clothes, covering, sail”), from Proto-Germanic *klaiþą (“garment”), perhaps from P...
definition_en: A piece of fabric used for clothing or other purposes.

senses.gloss: A fabric, usually made of woven, knitted, or felted fibres or filaments, such as used in dressing, decorating, cleaning or other practical use.
senses.example: There were other types of looms for producing various specialised types of cloth, for example fustians and velvets, but there is not space here to discuss these.

senses.gloss: Specifically, a tablecloth, especially as spread before a meal or removed afterwards.
senses.example: One day he came, as I thought accidentally, to dinner. My huſband was very much engaged in buſineſs, and quitted the room ſoon after the cloth was removed.

senses.gloss: A piece of cloth used for a particular purpose.
senses.example: Wipe the surface with a cloth dampened with mineral spirits in order to remove the sanding dust, then brush on a full coat of varnish.

examples.text: Tom came out of the house wrapping a quart bottle in a towel, followed by Daisy and Jordan wearing small tight hats of metallic cloth and carrying light capes over their arms.
examples.translation_ko: 톰이 수건에 1쿼트짜리 병을 감싸 들고 집에서 나왔고, 뒤따라 데이지와 조던이 금속 천으로 된 작고 꼭 맞는 모자를 쓰고 가벼운 망토를 팔에 걸친 채 나왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When his wife, a tall, lovely creature in cloth of gold, had left us, I remarked laughingly on the change in his present circumstances from those when we had both been medical students.
examples.translation_ko: 금실로 짠 옷을 입은 키 크고 아름다운 그의 아내가 자리를 뜨자, 나는 우리가 둘 다 의대생이었던 시절과 지금 그의 처지가 얼마나 달라졌는지 웃으며 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a sudden vision of her standing in the kitchen—it was hardly larger than a cupboard—washing the plates and glasses, the forks and spoons, giving the knives a rapid polish on the knife-board; and then putting everything away, giving the sink a scrub, and hanging the dish-cloth up to dry—it was there still, a gray torn rag; then looking round to see that everything was clean and nice.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 갑자기 그녀가 부엌에 서 있는 모습이 눈에 떠올랐다—찬장보다 조금 클 뿐인 그 부엌에서 접시와 잔들, 포크와 숟가락을 씻고, 칼판에 칼들을 재빠르게 닦아내고, 그런 다음 모든 것을 제자리에 정리하고, 개수대를 문지르고, 행주를 걸어 말리는—그 행주는 아직도 거기 있었다, 회색빛 너덜너덜한 걸레가—그리고 나서 모든 것이 깨끗하고 말끔한지 둘러보는 모습이.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin decorātus + -ive. Cognate with French décoratif.
definition_en: Used to add beauty or interest.

senses.gloss: That serves to decorate

examples.text: “Great art is always decorative.”
examples.translation_ko: "위대한 예술은 언제나 장식적입니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Yes; they’re so essentially decorative.”
examples.translation_ko: "그렇습니다. 본질적으로 장식적이거든요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French atmosphère, from New Latin atmosphaera, from Ancient Greek ἀτμός (atmós, “steam”) + σφαῖρα (sphaîra, “sphere”); corresponding ...
definition_en: The surrounding air or a particular feeling or mood.

senses.gloss: The gases surrounding the Earth or any astronomical body.
senses.example: To most people, the huge ice sheets of Antarctica and Greenland are merely water that once was snow. To glaciologists and climatologists, they are storehouses of the Earth's former atmospheres.

senses.gloss: The air in a particular place.
senses.example: The last hue of crimson had died away in the west, and the depth of the rich purple atmosphere was unbroken.

senses.gloss: The conditions (such as music, illumination etc.) that can influence the mood felt in an environment.

examples.text: A succulent hash arrived, and Mr. Wolfshiem, forgetting the more sentimental atmosphere of the old Metropole, began to eat with ferocious delicacy.
examples.translation_ko: 맛있는 해시가 나왔고, 울프샤임 씨는 옛 메트로폴의 감상적인 분위기는 잊은 채 사나우면서도 우아하게 먹기 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There is an atmosphere that is at once intense and tragic.
examples.translation_ko: 그곳에는 강렬하면서도 비극적인 분위기가 감돈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had never lost his appreciation for the romantic atmosphere of a studio, and though now the sight of it was like a stab in his heart, without thinking what he was at, he changed slightly the position of a Louis XV. table which was one of his treasures.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 작업실의 낭만적인 분위기에 대한 감상을 결코 잃지 않았고, 지금 그 광경이 가슴을 찌르는 듯했지만, 자신이 무엇을 하고 있는지도 모른 채 그의 보물 중 하나인 루이 15세 양식 탁자의 위치를 살짝 바꾸었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English tresour, from Old French tresor (“treasury”), from Latin thēsaurus (“treasure”), from Ancient Greek θησαυρός (thēsaur...
definition_en: A valuable or precious object.

senses.gloss: A collection of valuable things; accumulated wealth; a stock of money, jewels, etc.
senses.example: It seems there was a worm that slept upon a pile of treasure, which it had zealously heaped up under a stone bluff.

senses.gloss: A term of endearment.
The female genitals; pudenda.

examples.text: Unconsciously, perhaps, we treasure the power we have over people by their regard for our opinion of them, and we hate those upon whom we have no such influence.
examples.translation_ko: 무의식적으로, 아마도 우리는 다른 사람들이 우리에 대한 평가를 신경 쓴다는 점에서 그들에 대해 갖는 힘을 소중히 여기며, 그런 영향력이 전혀 통하지 않는 사람들을 미워한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We seek pitifully to convey to others the treasures of our heart, but they have not the power to accept them, and so we go lonely, side by side but not together, unable to know our fellows and unknown by them.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 가슴속 보물을 다른 사람들에게 전하려고 애처롭게 애쓰지만, 그들에게는 그것을 받아들일 힘이 없어서, 우리는 나란히 있으면서도 함께하지 못한 채 외롭게 살아간다. 동료들을 알 수도 없고 그들에게 알려질 수도 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fist, from Old English fȳst (“fist”), from Proto-West Germanic *fūsti, of uncertain origin. Cognate with Saterland Frisian Fääs...
definition_en: A closed hand used for punching or gripping.

senses.gloss: A hand with the fingers clenched or curled inward.
senses.example: The boxer's fists rained down on his opponent in the last round.

senses.gloss: The pointing hand symbol ☞.
The characteristic signaling rhythm of an individual telegraph or CW operator when sending Morse code.

examples.text: Mr. McKee was asleep on a chair with his fists clenched in his lap, like a photograph of a man of action.
examples.translation_ko: 맥키 씨는 의자에서 잠들어 있었는데, 무릎 위에 주먹을 꽉 쥔 채로 있는 모습이 마치 행동하는 남자의 사진 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: This was the master of a sailors’ boarding-house, a huge mulatto with a heavy fist, who gave the stranded mariner food and shelter till he found him a berth.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 선원 하숙집 주인으로, 거대한 혼혈인이었는데 주먹이 무거웠고, 좌초된 선원들에게 일자리를 찾아줄 때까지 음식과 잠자리를 제공해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Grief and jealousy and rage seized him, and he cried out hoarsely; he was inarticulate; he clenched his fists and raised them threateningly at an invisible enemy.
examples.translation_ko: 슬픔과 질투와 분노가 그를 사로잡았고, 그는 쉰 목소리로 외쳤다. 말이 제대로 나오지 않았다. 주먹을 꽉 쥐고 보이지 않는 적을 향해 위협적으로 치켜들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English dim, dym, from Old English dim, dimm (“dim, dark, gloomy; wretched, grievous, sad, unhappy”), from Proto-West Germanic *dimm, f...
definition_en: Lacking brightness or intensity.

senses.gloss: Not bright or colorful.
senses.example: The lighting was too dim for me to make out his facial features.

senses.gloss: Not smart or intelligent.
senses.example: He may be a bit dim, but he's not entirely stupid.

senses.gloss: Indistinct, hazy or unclear.
senses.example: His vision grew dimmer as he aged.

examples.text: The light was dim, and after the brilliant sunshine for a while he could see nothing.
examples.translation_ko: 실내는 어둑했고, 찬란한 햇빛에 익숙해진 눈으로는 한동안 아무것도 보이지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Perhaps some deep-rooted atavism urges the wanderer back to lands which his ancestors left in the dim beginnings of history.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 깊이 뿌리박힌 어떤 선조 회귀 본능이 방랑자를 역사의 어스름한 태초에 조상들이 떠났던 땅으로 되돌아가게 하는 것일지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: from discover + -ery, on the pattern of the pair recover, recovery. Displaced native Old English onfundennes.
definition_en: The act of finding or learning something new.

senses.gloss: Something discovered.
senses.example: This latest discovery should eventually lead to much better treatments for disease.

senses.gloss: The discovering of new things.
senses.example: The purpose of the voyage was discovery.

senses.gloss: An act of uncovering or revealing something; a revelation.

examples.text: I stared at him and then at Tom, who had made a parallel discovery less than an hour before—and it occurred to me that there was no difference between men, in intelligence or race, so profound as the difference between the sick and the well.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그를 바라보다가 톰을 바라보았다. 톰은 한 시간도 채 되지 않아 비슷한 사실을 발견했던 것이다. 그때 나는 지능이나 인종보다도 아픈 자와 건강한 자 사이의 차이만큼 인간들 사이에 깊은 차이는 없다는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
