examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She wanted to bring me down to her level; she cared nothing for me, she only wanted me to be hers.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 나를 자신의 수준으로 끌어내리고 싶어했다. 나 자체에는 관심이 없었고, 단지 내가 자신의 소유가 되기만을 원했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From use + -less.
definition_en: Lacking any practical or useful quality.

senses.gloss: Without use or possibility to be used.
senses.example: This fork's prongs are bent. It's useless now.

senses.gloss: Unhelpful, not useful; pointless (of an action).
senses.example: I think it's useless to keep this discussion going. It's like talking to a brick wall.

senses.gloss: Good-for-nothing; not dependable.
senses.example: Bill never mows the lawn, takes out the trash or anything. He's useless, but I love him anyways.

examples.text: It all seemed useless and inane.
examples.translation_ko: 모든 것이 무의미하고 공허해 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “It’s as useless to talk to you about these things as to describe colours to a man who was born blind.”
examples.translation_ko: "이런 일에 대해 당신과 이야기하는 것은 태어날 때부터 눈먼 사람에게 색깔을 설명하는 것만큼이나 무용해."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + important.
definition_en: Not significant or worthy of attention.

senses.gloss: petty; not important or noteworthy

examples.text: “Old sport, the dance is unimportant.”
examples.translation_ko: "형씨, 댄스 파티는 중요하지 않아."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was unimportant.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 중요하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But we’ve talked about her quite enough; she was an entirely unimportant person.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그녀에 대해서는 충분히 얘기했으니, 그녀는 전혀 중요하지 않은 사람이었어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The verb is derived from Middle English yernen, yern (“to express or feel desire; to desire, long or wish for; to lust after; to ask or demand for”...
definition_en: Feel a strong desire for something.

senses.gloss: To have a strong desire for something or to do something; to long for or to do something.
senses.example: All I yearn for is a simple life.

senses.gloss: To long for something in the past with melancholy or nostalgia.
senses.example: Having shaken the dust of the ugly new South Africa from his feet, is he yearning for the South Africa of the old days, when Eden was still possible?

senses.gloss: Of music, words, etc.: to express strong desire or longing.
senses.example: The music, yearning like a God in pain, / She scarcely heard: […]

examples.text: Sooner or later the human being in you will yearn for the common bonds of humanity.”
examples.translation_ko: 조만간 당신 안의 인간적인 면이 인간다운 유대를 갈망하게 될 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Do you not yearn sometimes for the light of the streets in Paris or London, the companionship of your friends, and equals, que sais-je?
examples.translation_ko: 파리나 런던의 거리 불빛이, 친구들과 동료들과의 교제가, 뭐라고 할까, 그런 것들이 그립지 않습니까?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fleten (“to float”), from Old English flēotan (“to float”), from Proto-Germanic *fleutaną, from Proto-Indo-European *plewd-. By...
definition_en: Lasting for a very short time.

senses.gloss: Passing quickly; of short duration.
senses.example: And I am inspired afresh to pursue the stunning beauty of Christ rather than the fleeting beauty of this world.

examples.text: I had a fleeting glimpse of a pursuit of the ineffable.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 형언할 수 없는 것을 추구하는 모습을 잠깐 엿보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But the impression is fleeting, and serves only to give a greater acuteness to the enjoyment of the moment.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그런 인상은 순간적이며, 다만 현재 순간의 즐거움을 더욱 예리하게 만들어줄 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English revēlen, from Old French reveler, from Latin revēlāre (“to reveal, uncover”), from re- (“back, again”) + vēlāre (“to cover”), f...
definition_en: To make something known or visible.

senses.gloss: The outer side of a window or door frame.
A revelation; an uncovering of what was hidden in the scene or story.
senses.example: The comedian had been telling us about his sleep being disturbed by noise. Then came the reveal: he was sleeping on a bed in a department store.

examples.text: It transpired after a confused five minutes that the man had heard Gatsby’s name around his office in a connection which he either wouldn’t reveal or didn’t fully understand.
examples.translation_ko: 혼란스러운 5분이 지나고 나서야 그 남자가 사무실에서 개츠비의 이름을 어떤 연관성으로 들었다는 것이 밝혀졌는데, 그는 그것을 밝히려 하지 않거나 완전히 이해하지 못하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A man’s work reveals him.
examples.translation_ko: 사람의 작품은 그 사람을 드러낸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: A latent gift might reveal itself on acquaintance with the painters and writers whose society his wife sought; or domestic incompatability might turn him upon himself; a love affair might fan into bright flame a fire which I could have shown smouldering dimly in his heart.
examples.translation_ko: 잠재된 재능이 그의 아내가 사귀던 화가들과 작가들과의 교제를 통해 드러날 수도 있었을 것이고, 가정 불화가 그를 자기 내면으로 돌리게 했을 수도 있었을 것이며, 연애 사건이 그의 마음속에서 희미하게 타오르고 있던 불씨를 밝은 불꽃으로 부채질했을 수도 있었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English deliveren, from Anglo-Norman and Old French delivrer, from Latin dē + līberō (“to set free”).
Compare typologically dispatch, a...
definition_en: To give or bring something to someone.

senses.gloss: To set free from restraint or danger.
senses.example: The hostage was delivered from her captors and thus preserved from any danger.

senses.gloss: To assist in the birth of.
senses.example: the doctor delivered the baby

senses.gloss: To assist (a female) in bearing, that is, in bringing forth (a child).
senses.example: the duchess was delivered of a son

examples.text: He came alive to me, delivered suddenly from the womb of his purposeless splendour.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내게 생생하게 다가왔다, 목적 없는 화려함의 자궁에서 갑자기 태어난 듯이.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But in his book or his picture the real man delivers himself defenceless.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 자신의 책이나 그림에서 진짜 그 사람은 무방비 상태로 자신을 내보인다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Dr. Coutras had delivered sentence of death on many men, and he could never overcome the horror with which it filled him.
examples.translation_ko: 쿠트라 박사는 수많은 사람에게 사형선고를 내려왔지만, 그때마다 느끼는 공포감을 결코 극복할 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From profound + -ly.
definition_en: Having or showing a deep understanding of something.

senses.gloss: With depth, meaningfully.
senses.example: He thought and wrote profoundly.

senses.gloss: Very importantly.
senses.example: More profoundly, it has shaken our most fundamental assumptions.

senses.gloss: Deeply; very; strongly or forcefully.
senses.example: From his childhood, she was profoundly troubled.

examples.text: He was profoundly affected by the fact that Tom was there.
examples.translation_ko: 톰이 그곳에 있다는 사실에 그는 깊이 동요했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They had never been closer in their month of love, nor communicated more profoundly one with another, than when she brushed silent lips against his coat’s shoulder or when he touched the end of her fingers, gently, as though she were asleep.
examples.translation_ko: 한 달간의 사랑 동안 그들이 이보다 더 가까웠던 적도, 더 깊이 마음을 나눈 적도 없었다. 그녀가 조용히 입술을 그의 코트 어깨에 대거나, 그가 마치 그녀가 잠든 것처럼 부드럽게 그녀의 손끝을 어루만질 때보다도.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His Olympia seemed to me the greatest picture of modern times, and Le Déjeuner sur l’Herbe moved me profoundly.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 《올림피아》는 내게 근대 최고의 그림으로 여겨졌고, 《풀밭에서의 점심》은 나를 깊이 감동시켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English descripcioun, from Old French description and its etymon, Latin dēscrīptiō, noun of action of dēscrībō (“I describe”).
definition_en: A written account of the characteristics of someone or something.

senses.gloss: A sketch or account of anything in words; a portraiture or representation in language; an enumeration of the essential qualities of a thing or species.
senses.example: give a verbal description of the events

senses.gloss: The act of describing; a delineation by marks or signs.
A set of characteristics by which someone or something can be recognized.
senses.example: The zoo had no lions, tigers, or cats of any description.

examples.text: He recognised Strickland by the description.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 묘사를 듣고 스트릭랜드임을 알아보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Descriptions of pictures are always dull, and these, besides, are familiar to all who take an interest in such things.
examples.translation_ko: 그림에 대한 묘사는 언제나 지루하고, 게다가 이런 것들에 관심이 있는 사람이라면 누구나 잘 아는 작품들이기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English forest, from Old French forest, from Early Medieval Latin forestis, likely from Frankish or Proto-West Germanic *furh...
definition_en: A large area of land covered with trees.

senses.gloss: A dense uncultivated tract of trees and undergrowth, larger than woods.
Any dense collection or amount.
senses.example: Squealing and still propelled by the kick, the calf scrabbled through the forest of legs and into the open.

senses.gloss: A defined area of land set aside in England as royal hunting ground or for other privileged use; all such areas.
senses.example: […] in places such as the Forest of Bowland there is hardly a tree in sight and much of the area is a vast tract of almost barren gritstone hills and peat moorland.

examples.text: He had a vague impression of a great primeval forest and of naked people walking beneath the trees.
examples.translation_ko: 거대한 원시림과 나무 아래를 걸어다니는 벌거벗은 사람들의 모습이 어렴풋이 눈에 들어왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There were two or three pictures of the forest at Fontainebleau and several of streets in Paris: my first feeling was that they might have been painted by a drunken cabdriver.
examples.translation_ko: 퐁텐블로 숲을 그린 그림이 두세 점 있었고 파리 거리를 그린 그림이 몇 점 있었는데, 처음 든 생각은 술 취한 마차꾼이 그린 것 같다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bras, bres, from Old English bræs (“brass, bronze”), of uncertain origin. Perhaps representing a backformation from Proto-Germa...
definition_en: A yellowish-brown alloy of copper and zinc.

senses.gloss: A memorial or sepulchral tablet usually made of brass or latten: a monumental brass.
Fittings, utensils, or other items made of brass.
A class of wind instruments, usually made of metal (such as brass), that use vibrations of the player's lips to produce sound; a band or the section of an orchestra that features such instruments.
senses.example: A few measures later, the brass comes in strong!

examples.text: Before I could answer, Daisy came out of the house and two rows of brass buttons on her dress gleamed in the sunlight.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 대답하기도 전에 데이지가 집에서 나왔고, 그녀 드레스의 두 줄 놋단추가 햇빛에 반짝였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: In the main hall a bar with a real brass rail was set up, and stocked with gins and liquors and with cordials so long forgotten that most of his female guests were too young to know one from another.
examples.translation_ko: 메인 홀에는 진짜 황동 난간이 달린 바가 설치되어 있었고, 진과 리큐어, 그리고 너무 오래전에 잊혀진 코디얼들로 가득 채워져 있어서 그의 여성 손님들 대부분은 너무 어려서 하나하나를 구별할 줄도 몰랐다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He is shut in a tower of brass, and can communicate with his fellows only by signs, and the signs have no common value, so that their sense is vague and uncertain.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 황동 탑에 갇혀 있어서, 동료들과는 오직 신호로만 소통할 수 있는데, 그 신호들은 공통된 가치가 없어서 의미가 모호하고 불확실하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Adapted borrowing of Latin commūnicāt- (past participial stem of commūnicō (“share, impart; make common”)) + -ate (verb-forming suffix), from commū...
definition_en: To share or exchange information.

senses.gloss: To impart or transmit (information or knowledge) to someone; to make known, to tell.
senses.example: It is vital that I communicate this information to you.

senses.gloss: To impart or transmit (an intangible quantity, substance); to give a share of.
senses.example: to communicate motion by means of a crank

senses.gloss: To pass on (a disease) to another person, animal etc.
senses.example: The disease was mainly communicated via rats and other vermin.

examples.text: They had never been closer in their month of love, nor communicated more profoundly one with another, than when she brushed silent lips against his coat’s shoulder or when he touched the end of her fingers, gently, as though she were asleep.
examples.translation_ko: 한 달간의 사랑 동안 그들이 이보다 더 가까웠던 적도, 더 깊이 마음을 나눈 적도 없었다. 그녀가 조용히 입술을 그의 코트 어깨에 대거나, 그가 마치 그녀가 잠든 것처럼 부드럽게 그녀의 손끝을 어루만질 때보다도.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The weakness of your body communicated itself to your soul.
examples.translation_ko: 육체의 나약함이 영혼에까지 전해진 것입니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He is shut in a tower of brass, and can communicate with his fellows only by signs, and the signs have no common value, so that their sense is vague and uncertain.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 황동 탑에 갇혀 있어서, 동료들과는 오직 신호로만 소통할 수 있는데, 그 신호들은 공통된 가치가 없어서 의미가 모호하고 불확실하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: In late Middle English (circa 1400) as masse in the sense of "lump, quantity of matter", from Anglo-Norman masse, in Old French attested from the 1...
definition_en: A large amount or quantity of something.

senses.gloss: A quantity of matter cohering so as to make one body, or an aggregation of particles or things which collectively make one body or quantity, usually of considerable size.
senses.example: […] and because a deep mass of continual sea is slower stirred to rage.

senses.gloss: Precious metal, especially gold or silver.
senses.example: Right in the midst the Goddesse selfe did stand / Upon an altar of some costly masse […].

senses.gloss: A measure of the inertia of a mass of matter, one of four fundamental properties of matter. SI unit of mass: kilogram.

examples.text: I walked out the back way—just as Gatsby had when he had made his nervous circuit of the house half an hour before—and ran for a huge black knotted tree, whose massed leaves made a fabric against the rain.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 뒷문으로 나갔다—30분 전 개츠비가 불안하게 집 주위를 돌았을 때와 똑같은 길로—그리고 거대한 검은 옹이 박힌 나무로 달려갔는데, 그 무성한 잎사귀들이 빗줄기를 막는 천막을 이루고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Upstairs, in the solemn echoing drive she let four taxicabs drive away before she selected a new one, lavender-coloured with grey upholstery, and in this we slid out from the mass of the station into the glowing sunshine.
examples.translation_ko: 위층 엄숙하고 메아리치는 차도에서 그녀는 네 대의 택시를 보내고 나서야 새 택시 한 대를 골랐는데, 회색 실내 장식에 라벤더색 차체였고, 우리는 그 차를 타고 역의 인파를 빠져나와 찬란한 햇살 속으로 미끄러져 나갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Facts were nothing to him, for beneath the mass of irrelevant incidents he looked for something significant to himself.
examples.translation_ko: 사실들은 그에게 아무것도 아니었다. 무관한 사건들의 더미 아래에서 그는 자신에게 의미 있는 무언가를 찾고 있었기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From ir- + relevant.
definition_en: Not related to the matter at hand.

senses.gloss: Not at all related: totally unrelated, wholly unconnected, completely inapplicable.
Not usefully related: not associated in any way that is important or useful to the context being discussed: not materially applicable; having connections not applicable in the present situation.
Not relevant, as
senses.example: Andy Kirby said that, on her second day in his class, Velvet declared algebra irrelevant to her life and strolled out the door. "Haven't seen her since," he said.

examples.text: (I’ve heard it said that Daisy’s murmur was only to make people lean toward her; an irrelevant criticism that made it no less charming.)
examples.translation_ko: (데이지의 속삭임은 사람들로 하여금 그녀 쪽으로 몸을 기울이게 하려는 것뿐이라는 말을 들은 적이 있다. 그런 엉뚱한 비판이 그녀의 매력을 조금이라도 덜어주지는 못했지만.)
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Facts were nothing to him, for beneath the mass of irrelevant incidents he looked for something significant to himself.
examples.translation_ko: 사실들은 그에게 아무것도 아니었다. 무관한 사건들의 더미 아래에서 그는 자신에게 의미 있는 무언가를 찾고 있었기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It would seem that my visit to this remote island should immediately revive my interest in Strickland, but the work I was engaged in occupied my attention to the exclusion of something that was irrelevant, and it was not till I had been there some days that I even remembered his connection with it.
examples.translation_ko: 이 외딴 섬을 방문한 것이 곧바로 스트릭랜드에 대한 내 관심을 되살려야 할 것 같았지만, 내가 몰두하고 있던 일이 관련 없는 것들을 배제하고 내 주의를 온통 사로잡고 있었기에, 며칠이 지나서야 비로소 그와 이 섬의 연관성을 떠올렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin significans, present participle of significare, from signum (“sign”) + ficare (“do, make”), variant of facere.
definition_en: Having or showing a great deal of importance.

senses.gloss: Signifying something; carrying meaning.
senses.example: a significant word or sound

senses.gloss: Having a noticeable or major effect.
senses.example: That was a significant step in the right direction.

senses.gloss: Reasonably large in number or amount.

examples.text: I had taken two finger-bowls of champagne, and the scene had changed before my eyes into something significant, elemental, and profound.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 샴페인을 핑거볼로 두 잔이나 마셨고, 내 눈앞의 광경이 의미 있고 원초적이며 심오한 무언가로 변해 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Facts were nothing to him, for beneath the mass of irrelevant incidents he looked for something significant to himself.
examples.translation_ko: 사실들은 그에게 아무것도 아니었다. 무관한 사건들의 더미 아래에서 그는 자신에게 의미 있는 무언가를 찾고 있었기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The years during which he was struggling to acquire proficiency in a difficult art were monotonous, and I do not know that there was anything significant in the shifts to which he was put to earn enough money to keep him.
examples.translation_ko: 어려운 예술에서 숙련도를 쌓기 위해 고군분투했던 그 세월들은 단조로웠고, 생계를 유지할 만큼 돈을 벌기 위해 그가 해야 했던 온갖 일들에 특별한 의미가 있었다고는 생각하지 않는다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English flawme, blend of Old French flame and flambe, flamble, the first from Latin flamma, the second from Latin flammula, diminutive ...
definition_en: A small, glowing piece of burning material.

senses.gloss: The visible part of fire; a stream of burning vapour or gas, emitting light and heat.
A romantic partner or lover in a usually short-lived but passionate affair.
senses.example: I could copy out yards of rhapsody to Lord George Poynings, her old flame, in which she addressed him by the most affectionate names.

senses.gloss: An aggressively insulting criticism or remark.
senses.example: Flames are, unfortunately, a fact of USENET life. It's a rare USENET regular who hasn't been shaken to the foundations with anger at something some jerk has posted.

examples.text: You have an impression of coloured movement against the flaming blue of the sky.
examples.translation_ko: 타오르는 푸른 하늘을 배경으로 색색의 움직임이 펼쳐지는 인상을 받는다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Ata’s father had planted crotons round his property, and they grew in coloured profusion, gay and brilliant; they fenced the land with flame.
examples.translation_ko: 아타의 아버지는 자신의 땅 둘레에 크로톤을 심어놓았는데, 그것들이 화려한 색깔로 무성하게 자라나 밝고 찬란했다. 그 나무들이 불꽃처럼 땅을 둘러쌌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To burn slowly and quietly.

senses.gloss: Alternative form of smolder.
senses.example: Lightning may blast and blacken, but it rarely gives rise to widespread fire. Decaying vegetation may occasionally smoulder with the heat of its fermentation, but this again rarely results in flames.

senses.gloss: To smother; to suffocate; to choke.
senses.example: In any event Scheurs (1997: 188) acknowledged that the Stockholm conference recognized and respected sovereignty but also mentioned that it sought to restrict it and not smoulder it.

examples.text: Her face, above a spotted dress of dark blue crêpe-de-chine, contained no facet or gleam of beauty, but there was an immediately perceptible vitality about her as if the nerves of her body were continually smouldering.
examples.translation_ko: 짙은 남색 크레이프 드 신 소재의 얼룩진 드레스 위로 드러난 그녀의 얼굴에는 아름다움의 편린이나 광채 같은 것은 전혀 없었지만, 마치 온몸의 신경이 끊임없이 타오르고 있는 듯한 즉각적으로 감지되는 활력이 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: In a little while nothing remained but smouldering embers, and a great masterpiece existed no longer.
examples.translation_ko: 얼마 지나지 않아 그을린 재만 남았고, 위대한 걸작은 더 이상 존재하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: A latent gift might reveal itself on acquaintance with the painters and writers whose society his wife sought; or domestic incompatability might turn him upon himself; a love affair might fan into bright flame a fire which I could have shown smouldering dimly in his heart.
examples.translation_ko: 잠재된 재능이 그의 아내가 사귀던 화가들과 작가들과의 교제를 통해 드러날 수도 있었을 것이고, 가정 불화가 그를 자기 내면으로 돌리게 했을 수도 있었을 것이며, 연애 사건이 그의 마음속에서 희미하게 타오르고 있던 불씨를 밝은 불꽃으로 부채질했을 수도 있었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A change or movement from one position to another.

senses.gloss: A movement to do something, a beginning.
An act of shifting; a slight movement or change.
senses.example: The generational shift Mr. Obama once embodied is, in fact, well under way, but it will not change Washington as quickly — or as harmoniously — as a lot of voters once hoped.

senses.gloss: A share, a portion assigned on division.

examples.text: The women wore nothing but a shift.
examples.translation_ko: 여자들은 속옷 한 장만 걸치고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Some wear black shifts and flesh-coloured stockings; some with curly hair, dyed yellow, are dressed like little girls in short muslin frocks.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 여자는 검은 속옷에 살색 스타킹을 신고 있고, 어떤 여자는 노랗게 염색한 곱슬머리를 하고 짧은 모슬린 원피스를 입어 마치 어린 소녀처럼 차려입었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Distant or detached in manner or attitude.

senses.gloss: At or from a distance, but within view, or at a small distance; apart; away.
senses.example:
The noise approaches, tho' our palace stood
 Aloof from streets, encompass'd with a wood

senses.gloss: Without sympathy; unfavorably.

examples.text: They may spend their whole lives aliens among their kindred and remain aloof among the only scenes they have ever known.
examples.translation_ko: 평생을 친족들 사이에서 이방인으로 보내고, 지금껏 알아온 유일한 풍경들 속에서도 동떨어져 지낼지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When Blanche saw that, notwithstanding his moments of passion, Strickland remained aloof, she must have been filled with dismay, and even in those moments I surmise that she realised that to him
examples.translation_ko: 블랑슈는 스트릭랜드가 열정적인 순간들에도 불구하고 여전히 냉담하게 거리를 두고 있다는 것을 깨달았을 때 절망감에 사로잡혔을 것이고, 심지어 그런 순간들에도 그에게 자신은
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A period of time between two events or points.

senses.gloss: A distance in space.
senses.example: 'Twixt host and host but narrow space was left, / A dreadful interval.

senses.gloss: A period of time.
senses.example: the interval between contractions during childbirth

senses.gloss: The difference (a ratio or logarithmic measure) in pitch between two notes, often referring to those two pitches themselves (otherwise known as a dyad).

examples.text: One of the men was talking with curious intensity to a young actress, and his wife, after attempting to laugh at the situation in a dignified and indifferent way, broke down entirely and resorted to flank attacks—at intervals she appeared suddenly at his side like an angry diamond, and hissed: “You promised!” into his ear.
examples.translation_ko: 남자 중 한 명이 젊은 여배우와 이상할 정도로 열심히 이야기하고 있었고, 그의 아내는 처음에는 품위 있고 무관심한 태도로 그 상황을 웃어넘기려 했지만 결국 완전히 무너져 측면 공격에 나섰다—때때로 그녀는 화난 다이아몬드처럼 갑자기 그의 곁에 나타나 "약속했잖아!"라고 그의 귀에 쏘아붙였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: After all, there are twenty-four hours in the day, and the summits of emotion can only be reached at rare intervals.
examples.translation_ko: 결국 하루는 스물네 시간이고, 감정의 절정은 드문 순간에만 도달할 수 있는 법이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But even during the brief intervals in which they are in love, men do other things which distract their mind; the trades by which they earn their living engage their attention; they are absorbed in sport; they can interest themselves in art.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 사랑에 빠져 있는 짧은 순간들 중에도 남자들은 마음을 딴 데로 돌리는 다른 일들을 한다. 생계를 위한 직업이 그들의 관심을 끌고, 스포츠에 몰두하며, 예술에 흥미를 느낄 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English equal, from Latin aequālis. Doublet of aequalis and egal.
definition_en: Having the same amount or degree.

senses.gloss: The same in value (status, merit, etc): having or deserving the same rights or treatment.
senses.example: We hold that all men are created equal and are thus equal under the law.

senses.gloss: The same in all respects that matter practically; interchangeable, fungible, or (even sometimes) identical for practical purposes.
senses.example: Equal conditions should produce equal results.

senses.gloss: Exactly identical, having the same value.
senses.example: All right angles are equal.

examples.text: Tiaré mingled French with English in her conversation, for she used both languages with equal facility.
examples.translation_ko: 티아레는 대화할 때 프랑스어와 영어를 섞어서 썼는데, 두 언어 모두 똑같이 능숙하게 구사했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Do you not yearn sometimes for the light of the streets in Paris or London, the companionship of your friends, and equals, que sais-je?
examples.translation_ko: 파리나 런던의 거리 불빛이, 친구들과 동료들과의 교제가, 뭐라고 할까, 그런 것들이 그립지 않습니까?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From tragic + -ally.
definition_en: Happening or resulting in a sad or unfortunate outcome.

senses.gloss: In a tragic manner.

examples.text: Gatsby, pale as death, with his hands plunged like weights in his coat pockets, was standing in a puddle of water glaring tragically into my eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 죽음처럼 창백한 얼굴로 두 손을 추처럼 코트 주머니에 깊숙이 찔러 넣은 채, 물웅덩이에 서서 비극적인 눈빛으로 나를 노려보고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The “death car” as the newspapers called it, didn’t stop; it came out of the gathering darkness, wavered tragically for a moment, and then disappeared around the next bend.
examples.translation_ko: 신문에서 "죽음의 차"라고 부른 그 차는 멈추지 않았다. 짙어지는 어둠 속에서 나타나 비극적으로 잠깐 흔들리더니 다음 모퉁이 너머로 사라져버렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It is an irony that they should so tragically have affected others.
examples.translation_ko: 그런 것들이 다른 사람들에게 그토록 비극적인 영향을 끼쳤다는 것은 아이러니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To be made up of something.

senses.gloss: To be.
senses.example: District number twenty-five (25) shall consist the counties of Tompkins, Seneca and Yates.

senses.gloss: To exist or be compatible.
senses.example: All things do not consist by Christ today, and all the way back to Adam all things have not consisted by Christ.

examples.text: His real life consisted of dreams and of tremendously hard work.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 진짜 삶은 꿈과 엄청나게 힘든 작업으로 이루어져 있었다.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: The state or process of becoming more focused or intense.

senses.gloss: The direction of attention to a specific object.
The act, process or product of reducing the volume of a liquid, as by evaporation.
The act or process of removing the dress of ore and of reducing the valuable part to smaller compass, as by currents of air or water.

examples.text: There was something pathetic in his concentration, as if his complacency, more acute than of old, was not enough to him any more.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 집중하는 모습에는 뭔가 애처로운 구석이 있었다. 마치 예전보다 더욱 예민해진 그의 자기만족이 이제는 그에게 충분하지 않은 것처럼.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A stout, middle-aged man, with enormous owl-eyed spectacles, was sitting somewhat drunk on the edge of a great table, staring with unsteady concentration at the shelves of books.
examples.translation_ko: 거대한 부엉이 눈 같은 안경을 쓴 건장하고 중년의 남자가 큰 탁자 모서리에 다소 취한 채로 앉아서, 불안정한 집중력으로 책장들을 응시하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They have a faculty of concentration on that which occupies them at the moment, and it irks them if one encroaches on the other.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 그 순간 자신을 사로잡고 있는 것에 집중하는 능력이 있으며, 한 영역이 다른 영역을 침범하면 짜증을 낸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Used to describe something that is done with great success or victory.

senses.gloss: In a triumphant manner.
senses.example: “Another double,” said the old lady: triumphantly making a memorandum of the circumstance, by placing one sixpence and a battered halfpenny, under the candlestick.

examples.text: he cried triumphantly.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 의기양양하게 외쳤다.

examples.translation_ko: "보셨죠." 캐서린이 의기양양하게 소리쳤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His thoughts floated then serenely in the empyrean, and he felt towards her the horror that perhaps the painted butterfly, hovering about the flowers, feels to the filthy chrysalis from which it has triumphantly emerged.
examples.translation_ko: 그때 그의 사상은 천상계에서 고요히 떠돌았고, 꽃들 주위를 맴도는 아름다운 나비가 자신이 승리를 거두며 빠져나온 더러운 번데기에 대해 느끼는 것과 같은 혐오감을 그녀에게 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From self + -ish. Compare Danish selvisk (“selfish”), Swedish självisk (“selfish”).
definition_en: Having or showing a concern only for oneself.

senses.gloss: Holding one's own self-interest as the standard for decision making.
Having excessive or exclusive regard and concern for one's own well-being, profit or pleasure, with little or no consideration for others.
Of video game characters: relying on their own actions and capabilities to be effective in the game, rather than on other characters.

examples.text: “Never heard anything so selfish in my life.”
examples.translation_ko: "평생 이렇게 이기적인 소리는 처음 들어봐요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I do not think he was any gentler here, less selfish or less brutal, but the circumstances were more favourable.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 여기서 더 온화해졌거나 덜 이기적이거나 덜 잔인해졌다고는 생각하지 않지만, 상황이 더 유리했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It seems strange even to myself, when I have described a man who was cruel, selfish, brutal and sensual, to say that he was a great idealist.
examples.translation_ko: 잔인하고 이기적이며 야만적이고 관능적인 한 남자를 묘사해놓고서 그가 위대한 이상주의자였다고 말하는 것은, 나 자신에게도 이상하게 느껴진다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Abundant or plentiful in amount.

senses.gloss: Vast in quantity or number, profuse, abundant; taking place on a large scale.
senses.example: He drank a copious amount of vodka, and passed out.

senses.gloss: Having an abundant supply.
Full of thought, information, or matter; exuberant in words, expression, or style.

examples.text: I never heard her speak, but it may be that in private she had a copious conversation.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 말하는 것을 들어본 적은 없지만, 사적인 자리에서는 말이 많았을지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She was evidently a copious talker, and now poured forth a breathless stream of anecdote and comment.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 분명히 말이 많은 사람이었고, 지금도 숨 가쁘게 일화와 논평을 쏟아내고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Suitable for a particular purpose or occasion.

senses.gloss: Suitable; proper
senses.example: You have nothing to say about it. I'll do exactly as I see fit.

senses.gloss: Adapted to a purpose or environment.
senses.example: survival of the fittest

senses.gloss: In good shape; physically well.
senses.example: You don't have to be a good climber for Kilimanjaro, but you do have to be fit.

examples.text: “I thought he knew something about breeding, but he wasn’t fit to lick my shoe.”
examples.translation_ko: "교양이 있는 사람인 줄 알았는데, 내 신발이나 핥을 자격도 없는 놈이었어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had a deep, resonant voice, fitted to his massive frame, and a keen sense of the dramatic.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 거대한 체구에 어울리는 깊고 울림 있는 목소리와 예리한 극적 감각을 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He seemed to see his fellow-creatures grotesquely, and he was angry with them because they were grotesque; life was a confusion of ridiculous, sordid happenings, a fit subject for laughter, and yet it made him sorrowful to laugh.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 동료 인간들을 기괴하게 보는 듯했고, 그들이 기괴하다는 이유로 화를 냈다. 삶은 우스꽝스럽고 추잡한 일들의 혼란이었고, 웃음거리가 될 만한 소재였지만, 그럼에도 웃는다는 것이 그를 슬프게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Polynesia + -an.
definition_en: Relating to the Pacific islanders of Polynesia.

senses.gloss: Of, from, or pertaining to Polynesia.

examples.text: They belonged to a Polynesian garden of the Hesperides.
examples.translation_ko: 그것들은 폴리네시아의 헤스페리데스 정원에 속한 것들이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He received us in a room that might have been in a house in a provincial town in France, and the one or two Polynesian curios had an odd look.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 프랑스의 어느 지방 도시 집에 있을 법한 방에서 우리를 맞이했는데, 한두 점의 폴리네시아 골동품이 묘하게 어울리지 않아 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: The act of beginning something.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of open

examples.text: He was never quite still; there was always a tapping foot somewhere or the impatient opening and closing of a hand.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 결코 완전히 가만히 있지 못했다. 어디선가 항상 발을 두드리거나 손을 조급하게 쥐었다 폈다 하곤 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And when we steamed slowly out of the lagoon, making our way gingerly through the opening in the reef, and then steered for the open sea, a certain melancholy fell upon me.
examples.translation_ko: 우리가 석호에서 천천히 빠져나와 산호초 틈새를 조심스럽게 통과한 다음 망망대해를 향해 나아갔을 때, 어떤 우울함이 나를 사로잡았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It would not surprise you if, as you came near seeking for an opening in the reef, it vanished suddenly from your view, and nothing met your gaze but the blue loneliness of the Pacific.
examples.translation_ko: 암초 사이의 틈을 찾아 가까이 다가갈 때 섬이 갑자기 시야에서 사라져버리고, 눈앞에는 태평양의 푸른 적막만이 펼쳐진다 해도 놀랄 일이 아닐 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: Referring to the final stage of French Gothic architecture from the 14th to the 16th centuries.
senses.example: The nave and central tower, more flamboyant in design, were finished early in the sixteenth century after the original plan.

senses.gloss: Of a blade: forged in a wavy, undulating pattern, like a flame-bladed sword or a kris.

examples.text: A mango grew in front of the house, and at the edge of the clearing were two flamboyants, twin trees, that challenged the gold of the cocoa-nuts with their scarlet flowers.
examples.translation_ko: 집 앞에는 망고나무가 자라고 있었고, 개간지 가장자리에는 두 그루의 플람보얀트가 쌍둥이처럼 서서 주홍빛 꽃으로 코코넛의 황금빛에 맞서고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The schooners moored to the quay are trim and neat, the little town along the bay is white and urbane, and the flamboyants, scarlet against the blue sky, flaunt their colour like a cry of passion.
examples.translation_ko: 부두에 정박한 스쿠너들은 단정하고 깔끔하며, 만 따라 늘어선 작은 마을은 하얗고 세련되어 있고, 푸른 하늘을 배경으로 한 진홍빛 플람보얀트들은 열정의 외침처럼 색채를 뽐내고 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English scarlet, scarlat, borrowed from Old French escarlate (“a type of cloth”), from Medieval Latin scarlatum (“scarlet cloth”), of u...
definition_en: A bright red color.

senses.gloss: A brilliant red colour sometimes tinged with orange.
Cloth of a scarlet color.
senses.example: All her household are clothed with scarlet.

examples.text: A mango grew in front of the house, and at the edge of the clearing were two flamboyants, twin trees, that challenged the gold of the cocoa-nuts with their scarlet flowers.
examples.translation_ko: 집 앞에는 망고나무가 자라고 있었고, 개간지 가장자리에는 두 그루의 플람보얀트가 쌍둥이처럼 서서 주홍빛 꽃으로 코코넛의 황금빛에 맞서고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The schooners moored to the quay are trim and neat, the little town along the bay is white and urbane, and the flamboyants, scarlet against the blue sky, flaunt their colour like a cry of passion.
examples.translation_ko: 부두에 정박한 스쿠너들은 단정하고 깔끔하며, 만 따라 늘어선 작은 마을은 하얗고 세련되어 있고, 푸른 하늘을 배경으로 한 진홍빛 플람보얀트들은 열정의 외침처럼 색채를 뽐내고 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From steam + -er. The steamer duck or steamer (sense 6.2) is apparently named for its resemblance to a paddle steamer when swimming rapidly.
definition_en: A type of steam-powered locomotive or a vessel that uses steam power.

senses.gloss: A vessel in which articles are subjected to the action of steam, as in washing and in various processes of manufacture.
A cooking appliance that cooks by steaming.
A steam fire engine, that is, a steam boiler and engine driving a pump, which are all mounted on wheels.

examples.text: And the crowd that throngs the wharf as the steamer draws alongside is gay and debonair; it is a noisy, cheerful, gesticulating crowd.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 기선이 접안할 때 부두에 몰려든 군중은 명랑하고 쾌활하다. 시끄럽고 유쾌하며 몸짓을 크게 하는 군중이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Before he entered upon his new duties he wished to take a holiday, and, having no private means, he went as surgeon on a tramp steamer to the Levant.
examples.translation_ko: 새로운 직무를 시작하기 전에 그는 휴가를 보내고 싶었는데, 개인 재산이 없었던 그는 레반트 행 화물선에 선의로 승선했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From along + side; compare alongsides.
definition_en: Next to something or someone.

senses.gloss: Along the side; by the side; side by side; abreast.
senses.example: Ahoy! Bring your boat alongside.

examples.text: The word “sensuous” had the effect of further disquieting Tom, but before he could invent a protest the coupé came to a stop, and Daisy signalled us to draw up alongside.
examples.translation_ko: "관능적"이라는 말이 톰을 더욱 불안하게 만들었지만, 그가 반박할 말을 생각해내기도 전에 쿠페가 멈춰 섰고, 데이지가 우리에게 옆으로 차를 대라고 신호를 보냈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: With fenders spread like wings we scattered light through half Astoria—only half, for as we twisted among the pillars of the elevated I heard the familiar “jug-jug-spat!” of a motorcycle, and a frantic policeman rode alongside.
examples.translation_ko: 날개처럼 펼쳐진 흙받이로 아스토리아 절반에 빛을 흩뿌리며 달렸다—절반만이었다. 고가철도 기둥들 사이를 누비며 달리는데 익숙한 "덜컹덜컹-탁!" 하는 오토바이 소리가 들렸고, 다급한 경찰관이 나란히 달려왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And the crowd that throngs the wharf as the steamer draws alongside is gay and debonair; it is a noisy, cheerful, gesticulating crowd.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 기선이 접안할 때 부두에 몰려든 군중은 명랑하고 쾌활하다. 시끄럽고 유쾌하며 몸짓을 크게 하는 군중이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English comber, camber, equivalent to comb + -er.
definition_en: A person who combs or carded wool.

senses.gloss: A person who combs wool, etc.
A machine that combs wool, etc.
A long, curving wave breaking on the shore.
senses.example: The mighty combers crashed down with long echoing reverberations like the roar of great cannons, followed by the ominous swish of broken water rushing across the reef in mad clouds of foam and spray.

examples.text: The society of beach-combers always repays the small pains you need be at to enjoy it.
examples.translation_ko: 해변의 부랑자들과 어울리는 사회는 그들을 즐기기 위해 들이는 작은 수고를 언제나 보상해준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The Chink’s Head was a name the beach-combers gave to a wretched inn off the Rue Bouterie, kept by a one-eyed Chinaman, where for six sous you could sleep in a cot and for three on the floor.
examples.translation_ko: 중국인 머리라는 곳은 해변의 부랑자들이 루 부트리 거리 근처의 한심한 여관에 붙인 이름이었는데, 외눈박이 중국인이 운영하는 곳으로 6수를 내면 침대에서, 3수를 내면 바닥에서 잘 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English rigide, from Latin rigidus (“stiff”), from rigeō (“I am stiff”). Compare rigor. Merged with Middle English rigged, rygged, rugg...
definition_en: Having a fixed shape and not able to be bent.

senses.gloss: Stiff, rather than flexible.
Having inflexible thoughts, opinions, or beliefs.
Fixed, rather than moving.
senses.example: A sunflower, four more, one bowed, and horses in the distance standing rigid and still as toys.

examples.text: Probably it had been tactful to leave Daisy’s house, but the act annoyed me, and her next remark made me rigid.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지의 집을 떠난 것은 아마 현명한 처사였겠지만, 그 행동이 나를 짜증나게 했고, 그녀의 다음 말은 나를 경직시켰다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: At that time there was no rigid sequestration on the islands, and lepers, if they chose, were allowed to go free.
examples.translation_ko: 그 당시 섬에는 엄격한 격리 조치가 없었고, 나병 환자들은 원한다면 자유롭게 돌아다닐 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I should be sorry if my conscience, insisting on a rigid attention to the matter in hand, forced me to dismiss him in a couple of lines.
examples.translation_ko: 양심이 당면한 문제에 엄격하게 집중하라고 재촉하여 그를 두어 줄로 대충 넘어가게 만든다면 유감스러울 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English monk, from Old English munuc, from Proto-West Germanic *munik, from Late Latin monicus, variant of monachus, from Ancient Greek...
definition_en: A man who has dedicated his life to a religious order.

senses.gloss: A male member of a monastic order who has devoted his life for religious service.
senses.example: In clusters on the plain, like cowlless monks at matins, sat the vultures that had settled on the corpse of the hyena impaled by the female rhino […]

senses.gloss: In earlier usage, an eremite or hermit devoted to solitude, as opposed to a cenobite, who lived communally.
A male who leads an isolated life; a loner, a hermit.

examples.text: He and Strickland were assigned to different rooms, and when, thrown out of bed at five in the morning by a stalwart monk, he had made his bed and washed his face, Strickland had already disappeared.
examples.translation_ko: 그와 스트릭랜드는 서로 다른 방에 배정되었고, 새벽 다섯 시에 건장한 수사에게 침대에서 쫓겨나 잠자리를 정리하고 세수를 마쳤을 때, 스트릭랜드는 이미 사라진 후였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But he did not have a chance to speak to him, since, as he entered the common-room, a monk came in with a huge Bible in his arms, mounted a pulpit which was at the end of the room, and began the service which the wretched outcasts had to endure as the price of their lodging.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그와 말을 나눌 기회는 없었다. 공동실에 들어서자마자 한 수사가 거대한 성경을 품에 안고 들어와 방 끝에 있는 강단에 올라가서, 이 비참한 버림받은 자들이 잠자리의 대가로 견뎌야 하는 예배를 시작했기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English hungry, from Old English hungriġ, from Proto-West Germanic *hungrug, from Proto-Germanic *hungrugaz (“hungry”); equivalent to h...
definition_en: Feeling a strong need to eat.

senses.gloss: Affected by hunger; having the physical need for food.
senses.example: My kids go to bed hungry every night because I haven’t got much money for food.

senses.gloss: Causing hunger.
senses.example: All this gardening is hungry work.

senses.gloss: Eager; having an avid desire or appetite for something.
senses.example: young and hungry

examples.text: I was immediately struck by the number of young Englishmen dotted about; all well dressed, all looking a little hungry, and all talking in low, earnest voices to solid and prosperous Americans.
examples.translation_ko: 곳곳에 흩어져 있는 젊은 영국인들의 수가 즉시 내 눈에 띄었다. 모두 옷을 잘 차려입었고, 모두 약간 굶주린 듯 보였으며, 모두 든든하고 부유한 미국인들에게 낮고 진지한 목소리로 말을 걸고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Tough Bill’s fare was seldom extravagant, and you rose from his table almost as hungry as you sat down, but for some days they had good reason to regret it.
examples.translation_ko: 터프 빌의 식사는 좀처럼 풍성하지 않아서 그의 식탁에서 일어날 때는 앉았을 때와 거의 마찬가지로 배가 고팠지만, 며칠 동안 그들은 그것을 그리워할 충분한 이유가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: After a moment’s hesitation, Strickland scrambled to his feet, and together they went to the Bouchée de Pain, where the hungry are given a wedge of bread, which they must eat there and then, for it is forbidden to take it away; and then to the Cuillère de Soupe, where for a week, at eleven and four, you may get a bowl of thin, salt soup.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 망설인 후 스트릭랜드는 비틀거리며 일어났고, 둘은 함께 부셰 드 팽으로 갔다. 그곳에서는 굶주린 자들에게 빵 한 조각을 주는데, 그 자리에서 바로 먹어야 했다. 가져가는 것은 금지되어 있었기 때문이다. 그다음에는 퀴예르 드 수프로 갔는데, 그곳에서는 일주일 동안 열한 시와 네 시에 묽고 짠 수프 한 그릇을 얻을 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From race (“having a characteristic taste (of wines, fruits, etc.)”) + -y.
definition_en: A spicy or racy novel.

senses.gloss: Mildly risqué.
senses.example: She wore a racy dress that was just barely appropriate for the occasion.

senses.gloss: Having a strong flavor indicating origin; of distinct characteristic taste; tasting of the soil.
senses.example: a racy wine

senses.gloss: Exciting to the mind by a strong or distinctive character of thought or language; peculiar and piquant; fresh and lively.

examples.text: I began to like New York, the racy, adventurous feel of it at night, and the satisfaction that the constant flicker of men and women and machines gives to the restless eye.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 뉴욕을 좋아하기 시작했다. 밤의 생생하고 모험적인 느낌과, 끊임없이 깜박이는 남녀와 기계들이 불안한 눈에 주는 만족감을 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When Michaelis’s testimony at the inquest brought to light Wilson’s suspicions of his wife I thought the whole tale would shortly be served up in racy pasquinade—but Catherine, who might have said anything, didn’t say a word.
examples.translation_ko: 심문에서 미카엘리스의 증언이 아내에 대한 윌슨의 의혹을 드러냈을 때, 나는 이 모든 이야기가 곧 자극적인 풍자문으로 각색되리라 생각했다—하지만 무엇이든 말할 수 있었던 캐서린은 한마디도 하지 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But I wish I could give here the pictures, coloured and racy, which Captain Nichols’ vivid narrative offered to the imagination.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 니콜스 선장의 생생한 이야기가 상상력에 제공했던 그 다채롭고 흥미진진한 그림들을 여기서 보여줄 수 있다면 좋겠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English savage, from Old French sauvage, salvage (“wild, untamed”), from Late Latin salvāticus, alteration of Latin silvāticus (“wild”,...
definition_en: Being extremely violent or aggressive.

senses.gloss: Wild; not cultivated or tamed.
senses.example: a savage wilderness

senses.gloss: Barbaric; not civilized.
senses.example: savage manners

senses.gloss: Primitive; lacking complexity or sophistication.

examples.text: I couldn’t sleep all night; a foghorn was groaning incessantly on the Sound, and I tossed half-sick between grotesque reality and savage, frightening dreams.
examples.translation_ko: 밤새 잠을 이룰 수 없었다. 해협에서 안개 경적이 끊임없이 울어댔고, 나는 기괴한 현실과 야만스럽고 무서운 꿈 사이에서 반쯤 병든 채로 뒤척였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I remember the portrait of him up in Gatsby’s bedroom, a grey, florid man with a hard, empty face—the pioneer debauchee, who during one phase of American life brought back to the Eastern seaboard the savage violence of the frontier brothel and saloon.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비의 침실에 걸려 있던 그의 초상화가 기억난다. 회색빛에 혈색이 좋은, 딱딱하고 공허한 얼굴을 한 남자—미국 역사의 한 시기 동안 변방 매춘굴과 술집의 야만적 폭력을 동부 해안으로 되가져온 선구적 방탕아였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I received the impression of a life intense and brutal, savage, multicoloured, and vivacious.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 강렬하고 잔혹하며, 야만적이고 다채로우며 생기 넘치는 삶의 인상을 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin vīvāx, vīvāci- (“lively, vigorous”) + -ous, from vīvere (“to live”).
definition_en: Having a lively and energetic personality.

senses.gloss: Lively and animated; full of life and energy.
Long-lived.
Difficult to kill.

examples.text: I received the impression of a life intense and brutal, savage, multicoloured, and vivacious.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 강렬하고 잔혹하며, 야만적이고 다채로우며 생기 넘치는 삶의 인상을 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I shall not tell what Dr. Coutras related to me in his words, but in my own, for I cannot hope to give at second hand any impression of his vivacious delivery.
examples.translation_ko: 쿠트라 박사가 내게 들려준 이야기를 그의 말 그대로 전하지는 않고 내 방식으로 전하겠다. 그의 생생한 화법을 간접적으로나마 전달할 자신이 없기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The noun is derived from Late Middle English birth (“(nautical) bearing away or off, clearance, berth”). Further etymology uncertain, but probably ...
definition_en: A place to sleep or stay on a ship or train.

senses.gloss: A place for a vessel to lie at anchor or to moor.
A room in a vessel in which the officers or company mess (“eat together”) and reside; also, a room or other place in a vessel for storage.
A place on a vessel to sleep, especially a bed on the side of a cabin.
senses.example: By what I then thought to be great good luck I had succeeded in getting a three-berth cabin for myself and my little boy alone—Nos. 45, 46, 47—on the starboard side of the ship.

examples.text: Twice Strickland refused a berth on tramps sailing for the United States, and once on a collier going to Newcastle.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 미국으로 가는 화물선의 일자리를 두 번 거절했고, 뉴캐슬로 가는 석탄선의 일자리도 한 번 거절했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: This was the master of a sailors’ boarding-house, a huge mulatto with a heavy fist, who gave the stranded mariner food and shelter till he found him a berth.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 선원 하숙집 주인으로, 거대한 혼혈인이었는데 주먹이 무거웠고, 좌초된 선원들에게 일자리를 찾아줄 때까지 음식과 잠자리를 제공해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English wage, from Anglo-Norman wage, from Old Northern French wage, a northern variant of Old French gauge, guage (whence modern Frenc...
definition_en: The amount of money that an employee is paid for their work.

senses.gloss: An amount of money paid to a worker for a specified quantity of work, usually calculated on an hourly basis and expressed in an amount of money per hour.
senses.example: Before her promotion, her wages were 20% less.

examples.text: I knew he was starving, but I offered him good wages.”
examples.translation_ko: 그가 굶고 있다는 걸 알았지만, 좋은 임금을 제안했어요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I saw Strickland was thinking of it, so I said to him: ‘I’ve given her good wages and she’s saved them, and the captains and the first mates she’s known have given her a little something now and then.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드가 그것을 생각하고 있는 게 보여서 나는 그에게 말했다. "나는 그녀에게 좋은 임금을 줬고 그녀는 그걸 모아뒀어. 그리고 그녀가 알던 선장들과 일등 항해사들이 가끔씩 조금씩 용돈을 줬지.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bere, from Old English bēor (“beer”) (Oxford OED notes: "rare, except in poetry"), from Proto-West Germanic *beuʀ, from Proto-G...
definition_en: A type of alcoholic beverage made from fermented barley malt.

senses.gloss: An alcoholic drink fermented from starch material, commonly barley malt; often with hops or some other substance (like gruit) to impart a bitter flavor.
senses.example: Beer is brewed all over the world.

senses.gloss: A fermented extract of the roots and other parts of various plants, as spruce, ginger, sassafras, etc.
A solution produced by steeping plant materials in water or another fluid.

examples.text: He lurched against a table at which three soldiers were sitting and knocked over a glass of beer.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 세 명의 군인이 앉아 있는 테이블에 비틀거리며 부딪혀 맥주잔을 넘어뜨렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The waiter, an undersized youth with a flat, spotty face, hurried to and fro carrying a tray laden with glasses of beer.
examples.translation_ko: 키가 작고 얼굴이 납작하며 여드름투성이인 젊은 웨이터가 맥주잔들을 가득 실은 쟁반을 들고 이리저리 바쁘게 뛰어다녔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English male, from Anglo-Norman male, Old French male (“bag, wallet”), from Frankish *malha (“bag”), from Proto-Germanic *malhō (“bag, ...
definition_en: A system for sending letters and packages.

senses.gloss: A bag or wallet.
senses.example:
Open the Males, yet guard the treaſure ſure.
Lay out our golden wedges to the view,
That their reflexions may amaze the Perſeans.

senses.gloss: A bag containing letters to be delivered by post.
The (physical) material conveyed by the postal service.
senses.example: Don't forget to pick up the mail on your way.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her face was sad and lovely with bright things in it, bright eyes and a bright passionate mouth, but there was an excitement in her voice that men who had cared for her found difficult to forget: a singing compulsion, a whispered “Listen,” a promise that she had done gay, exciting things just a while since and that there were gay, exciting things hovering in the next hour.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 얼굴은 슬프면서도 사랑스러웠고, 밝은 눈과 밝고 열정적인 입술 같은 빛나는 것들로 가득했지만, 그녀의 목소리에는 한때 그녀를 사랑했던 남자들이 좀처럼 잊기 어려워하는 흥분이 담겨 있었다. 노래하듯 사람을 끌어당기는 힘, 속삭이는 "들어봐"라는 말, 그리고 조금 전까지 즐겁고 흥미진진한 일들을 해왔으며 다음 시간에도 그런 일들이 기다리고 있다는 약속 같은 것이.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Evidemment, it is not exciting on my island, and we are very far from the world—imagine, it takes me four days to come to Tahiti—but we are happy there.
examples.translation_ko: "물론 우리 섬에서는 흥미진진한 일이 없고, 세상과는 아주 멀리 떨어져 있습니다. 상상해 보세요, 타히티까지 오는 데 나흘이나 걸린답니다. 하지만 우리는 그곳에서 행복합니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French floride (“flourishing”), from Latin floridus (“flowery, blooming”). Doublet of Florida.
definition_en: Having a rich or elaborate quality.

senses.gloss: Having a rosy or pale red colour; ruddy.
Elaborately ornate; flowery.
In a blatant, vivid, or highly disorganized state.
senses.example: florid psychosis

examples.text: I had expected that Mr. Gatsby would be a florid and corpulent person in his middle years.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 개츠비 씨가 중년의 혈색 좋고 뚱뚱한 사람일 거라고 예상했었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I remember the portrait of him up in Gatsby’s bedroom, a grey, florid man with a hard, empty face—the pioneer debauchee, who during one phase of American life brought back to the Eastern seaboard the savage violence of the frontier brothel and saloon.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비의 침실에 걸려 있던 그의 초상화가 기억난다. 회색빛에 혈색이 좋은, 딱딱하고 공허한 얼굴을 한 남자—미국 역사의 한 시기 동안 변방 매춘굴과 술집의 야만적 폭력을 동부 해안으로 되가져온 선구적 방탕아였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His complexion was florid and his hair white.
examples.translation_ko: 안색은 붉으락했고 머리는 하얗게 세어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English provincial, from Old French provincial, from Latin prōvinciālis (“of a province”), equivalent to province + -ial.
definition_en: Relating to a province or provincial administration.

senses.gloss: Of or pertaining to a province.
senses.example: a provincial government

senses.gloss: Constituting a province.
Exhibiting the ways or manners of a province; characteristic of the inhabitants of a province.
senses.example: […] fond of exhibiting provincial airs and graces.

examples.text: Then he went into the jewellery store to buy a pearl necklace—or perhaps only a pair of cuff buttons—rid of my provincial squeamishness forever.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 진주 목걸이를 사러—아니면 아마도 커프스 단추 한 쌍을 사러—보석상에 들어갔고, 나의 촌스러운 까다로움은 영원히 사라졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But young men didn’t—at least in my provincial inexperience I believed they didn’t—drift coolly out of nowhere and buy a palace on Long Island Sound.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 젊은 남자들이—적어도 내 시골뜨기 경험으로는 그렇지 않다고 믿었는데—아무 데서나 태연히 나타나 롱아일랜드 해협에 궁전을 사지는 않는 법이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He received us in a room that might have been in a house in a provincial town in France, and the one or two Polynesian curios had an odd look.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 프랑스의 어느 지방 도시 집에 있을 법한 방에서 우리를 맞이했는데, 한두 점의 폴리네시아 골동품이 묘하게 어울리지 않아 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English local, from Late Latin locālis (“belonging to a place”), possibly also via Old French local; ultimately from Latin locus (“a pl...
definition_en: Relating to a particular place or area.

senses.gloss: From or in a nearby location.
senses.example: We prefer local produce.

senses.gloss: Connected directly to a particular computer, processor, etc.; able to be accessed offline.
senses.example: local disk drive

senses.gloss: Having limited scope (either lexical or dynamic); only accessible within a certain portion of a program.

examples.text: A massive and lethargic woman, who had been urging Daisy to play golf with her at the local club tomorrow, spoke in Miss Baedeker’s defence:
examples.translation_ko: 덩치가 크고 나른한 여자가 데이지에게 내일 동네 클럽에서 골프를 치자고 권하고 있었는데, 베데커 양을 변호하며 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Something in his leisurely movements and the secure position of his feet upon the lawn suggested that it was Mr. Gatsby himself, come out to determine what share was his of our local heavens.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 여유로운 움직임과 잔디밭 위에 안정되게 자리 잡은 발의 위치로 보아 그것은 개츠비 씨 본인인 것 같았다. 우리 지역 하늘의 몫이 자신에게 얼마나 되는지 알아보러 나온 것이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For some minutes there was an exchange of courtesies and some local gossip about the island, the prospects of copra and the vanilla crop; then we came to the object of my visit.
examples.translation_ko: 몇 분간 서로 예의를 갖춘 인사와 섬의 근황, 코프라와 바닐라 작황에 대한 지역 소식을 주고받은 후, 우리는 내 방문 목적으로 화제를 돌렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lepre, leprosy, from Old French [Term?], from Latin leprae, lepra, from Ancient Greek λέπρα (lépra).
definition_en: A person suffering from leprosy.

senses.gloss: A person who has leprosy, a person suffering from Hansen's disease.
Synonym of outcast: A person who is shunned, a pariah.

examples.text: “When you look at yourself in the glass you see the typical appearance of the leper.”
examples.translation_ko: "거울을 들여다보면 전형적인 나병 환자의 모습이 보일 겁니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: As she opened the door he smelt the sickly sweet smell which makes the neighbourhood of the leper nauseous.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 문을 열자 나병환자 근처에서 나는 역겨운 달콤하고 비릿한 냄새가 그의 코를 찔렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French hostile, from Latin hostīlis, from hostis (“enemy”). Displaced Old English fēondlīċ.
definition_en: Showing a desire to harm or fight.

senses.gloss: Not friendly; appropriate to an enemy; showing the disposition of an enemy; showing ill will and malevolence or a desire to thwart and injure.
senses.example: a hostile force

senses.gloss: Aggressive; antagonistic.
Unwilling.

examples.text: But when I’d shouted “hello” several times in vain, an argument broke out behind a partition, and presently a lovely Jewess appeared at an interior door and scrutinized me with black hostile eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 내가 "안녕하세요"라고 몇 번 소리쳐도 대답이 없자, 칸막이 뒤에서 말다툼이 벌어졌고, 곧 아름다운 유대인 여성이 안쪽 문에 나타나 검고 적대적인 눈으로 나를 살펴보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Most of the confidences were unsought—frequently I have feigned sleep, preoccupation, or a hostile levity when I realized by some unmistakable sign that an intimate revelation was quivering on the horizon; for the intimate revelations of young men, or at least the terms in which they express them, are usually plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions.
examples.translation_ko: 대부분의 고백은 내가 원하지 않은 것들이었다—친밀한 폭로가 수평선에서 떨리고 있다는 확실한 징조를 알아챘을 때, 나는 종종 잠든 척, 딴 생각에 빠진 척, 혹은 적대적인 경박함을 가장했다. 젊은 남자들의 친밀한 폭로는, 적어도 그들이 그것을 표현하는 방식은, 대개 표절에 가깝고 명백한 억압으로 인해 흠이 있기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was something hostile in the air which made him hesitate, and he felt that invisible forces barred his way.
examples.translation_ko: 공기 중에는 그를 주저하게 만드는 적대적인 무언가가 있었고, 보이지 않는 힘들이 그의 길을 가로막고 있다고 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Variant of cord, with spelling alteration due to Latin chorda (“cord”), ultimately from Ancient Greek χορδή (khordḗ, “string of gut, the string of ...
definition_en: A group of notes sounded simultaneously.

senses.gloss: A harmonic set of three or more notes that is heard as if sounding simultaneously.
senses.example: He struck the opening chords of the passage; but this time Irene's voice was silent. Victor stopped in the middle of an arpeggio.

senses.gloss: A line segment between two points of a curve.
A horizontal member of a truss.

examples.text: From the ballroom beneath, muffled and suffocating chords were drifting up on hot waves of air.
examples.translation_ko: 아래층 무도회장에서 뜨거운 공기의 물결을 타고 무겁고 숨막히는 화음들이 떠올라왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As Tom took up the receiver the compressed heat exploded into sound and we were listening to the portentous chords of Mendelssohn’s Wedding March from the ballroom below.
examples.translation_ko: 톰이 수화기를 들자 압축된 열기가 소리로 터져 나왔고, 우리는 아래층 무도회장에서 울려 퍼지는 멘델스존의 결혼행진곡의 장엄한 화음을 듣고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He judged that the disease had already attacked the vocal chords.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 병이 이미 성대를 침범했다고 판단했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Ultimately from Proto-Germanic *stam- (“to trip up; to stammer, stutter”), thereby related to German stumm (“mute”), Dutch stom (“dumb”). Doublet o...
definition_en: To walk or move unsteadily.

senses.gloss: A fall, trip or substantial misstep.
senses.example: I went to his aid. As he said, a board in the floor was loose. His stepping on it unawares had caused his stumble.

senses.gloss: An error or blunder.
senses.example: She owns up to early stumbles, such as bottles being mislabeled.

senses.gloss: A clumsy walk.

examples.text: The living-room was crowded to the doors with a set of tapestried furniture entirely too large for it, so that to move about was to stumble continually over scenes of ladies swinging in the gardens of Versailles.
examples.translation_ko: 거실은 문간까지 태피스트리 가구 세트로 빼곡했는데, 그 방에 비해 너무 큰 가구들이어서 돌아다니려면 베르사유 정원에서 그네 타는 귀부인들의 장면 위로 계속 발이 걸렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When he had gone halfway he turned around and stared at the scene—his wife and Catherine scolding and consoling as they stumbled here and there among the crowded furniture with articles of aid, and the despairing figure on the couch, bleeding fluently, and trying to spread a copy of Town Tattle over the tapestry scenes of Versailles.
examples.translation_ko: 중간쯤 갔을 때 그는 돌아서서 그 광경을 바라보았다—그의 아내와 캐서린이 빽빽한 가구들 사이를 이리저리 비틀거리며 구호용품을 들고 꾸짖기도 하고 달래기도 하는 모습, 그리고 소파 위에서 절망에 빠진 채 피를 줄줄 흘리며 베르사유 태피스트리 장면 위에 《타운 태틀》 한 부를 펼쳐 덮으려 애쓰는 모습을.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Sometimes he had to stumble along the bed of the stream, and sometimes he had to push through shrubs, dense and thorny; often he was obliged to climb over rocks in order to avoid the hornet-nests that hung on the trees over his head.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 개울바닥을 따라 비틀거리며 걸어야 했고, 때로는 빽빽하고 가시가 많은 관목들을 헤치고 나아가야 했다. 머리 위 나무에 매달린 말벌집을 피하기 위해 바위를 기어올라야 하는 경우도 자주 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English climben, from Old English climban (“to climb”), from Proto-West Germanic *klimban, from Proto-Germanic *klimbaną (“to climb, go...
definition_en: To move upward by using hands and feet.

senses.gloss: To ascend; rise; to go up.
senses.example: Prices climbed steeply.

senses.gloss: To mount; to move upwards on.
senses.example: climbing a tree

senses.gloss: To scale; to get to the top of something.
senses.example: He is a curly-haired schoolboy barely in his teens, but 13-year-old Jordan Romero from California has become the youngest person to climb Mount Everest.

examples.text: The prolonged and tumultuous argument that ended by herding us into that room eludes me, though I have a sharp physical memory that, in the course of it, my underwear kept climbing like a damp snake around my legs and intermittent beads of sweat raced cool across my back.
examples.translation_ko: 우리를 그 방으로 몰아넣은 길고 소란스러운 논쟁의 내용은 기억나지 않지만, 그 과정에서 내 속옷이 축축한 뱀처럼 다리를 타고 올라왔고 간헐적으로 땀방울이 등을 시원하게 흘러내렸다는 생생한 신체적 기억은 남아 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Out of the corner of his eye Gatsby saw that the blocks of the sidewalks really formed a ladder and mounted to a secret place above the trees—he could climb to it, if he climbed alone, and once there he could suck on the pap of life, gulp down the incomparable milk of wonder.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 눈길 한편으로 보도블록들이 실제로는 사다리를 이루며 나무들 위 어떤 비밀스러운 곳으로 올라간다는 것을 깨달았다—혼자서 오른다면 그곳에 닿을 수 있을 것이고, 일단 그곳에 이르면 생명의 젖을 빨고 경이로움의 비할 데 없는 젖을 들이킬 수 있을 것이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Sometimes he had to stumble along the bed of the stream, and sometimes he had to push through shrubs, dense and thorny; often he was obliged to climb over rocks in order to avoid the hornet-nests that hung on the trees over his head.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 개울바닥을 따라 비틀거리며 걸어야 했고, 때로는 빽빽하고 가시가 많은 관목들을 헤치고 나아가야 했다. 머리 위 나무에 매달린 말벌집을 피하기 위해 바위를 기어올라야 하는 경우도 자주 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Adapted borrowing of Latin tremendus (“fearful, terrible”, gerundive of tremō (“to tremble”)) + -ous. Doublet of tremend.
definition_en: Extremely good or impressive.

senses.gloss: Awe-inspiring; terrific.
Notable for its size, power, or excellence.
senses.example: Van Beethoven's ninth symphony is a tremendous piece of music.

senses.gloss: Extremely large (in amount, extent, degree, etc.) or great
senses.example: There was a tremendous outpouring of support.

examples.text: This tremendous detail was to be cleared up at last.
examples.translation_ko: 이 엄청난 세부사항이 마침내 밝혀질 참이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The mouth was wide open and ripped a little at the corners, as though she had choked a little in giving up the tremendous vitality she had stored so long.
examples.translation_ko: 입은 크게 벌어져 있었고 양쪽 끝이 조금 찢어져 있었는데, 마치 그토록 오랫동안 간직해온 엄청난 생명력을 포기하면서 조금 질식한 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was tremendous, sensual, passionate; and yet there was something horrible there, too, something which made him afraid.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 엄청나고, 관능적이고, 열정적이었다. 그러면서도 거기에는 무언가 끔찍한 것, 그를 두렵게 만드는 무언가가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English coment, comment, from Old French coment (“commentary”), from Late Latin commentum (“comment, interpretation”), from Classical L...
definition_en: A statement or remark about something.

senses.gloss: A spoken or written remark.
senses.example: I have no comment on that.

senses.gloss: The act of commenting.
senses.example: People bled to death like gentlemen in an operating room or expired without comment in an oxygen tent.

senses.gloss: The part of a sentence that provides new information regarding the current theme.

examples.text: When I had finished she told me without comment that she was engaged to another man.
examples.translation_ko: 내 이야기가 끝나자 그녀는 아무 말 없이 다른 남자와 약혼했다고 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: All night the saxophones wailed the hopeless comment of the “Beale Street Blues” while a hundred pairs of golden and silver slippers shuffled the shining dust.
examples.translation_ko: 밤새도록 색소폰들이 "빌 스트리트 블루스"의 절망적인 논평을 울부짖는 동안, 수백 켤레의 금색과 은색 슬리퍼들이 반짝이는 먼지를 휘저었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She was evidently a copious talker, and now poured forth a breathless stream of anecdote and comment.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 분명히 말이 많은 사람이었고, 지금도 숨 가쁘게 일화와 논평을 쏟아내고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *de
The verb is derived from Middle English descenden (“to move downwards, fall, descend; to slope downwards; to go from a better to a wo...
definition_en: To move downward or come down from a higher place.

senses.gloss: To pass from a higher to a lower part of (something, such as a flight of stairs or a slope); to go down along or upon.
senses.example: they descended the river in boats

senses.gloss: Of a flight of stairs, a road, etc.: to lead down (a hill, a slope, etc.).
senses.example: They took the steep path that descends the hill down to the beach.

senses.gloss: To move (someone or something) from a higher to a lower place or position; to bring or send (someone or something) down.

examples.text: With Jordan’s slender golden arm resting in mine, we descended the steps and sauntered about the garden.
examples.translation_ko: 조던의 가느다란 황금빛 팔이 내 팔에 기대어진 채, 우리는 계단을 내려가 정원을 거닐었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The Carraways are something of a clan, and we have a tradition that we’re descended from the Dukes of Buccleuch, but the actual founder of my line was my grandfather’s brother, who came here in fifty-one, sent a substitute to the Civil War, and started the wholesale hardware business that my father carries on today.
examples.translation_ko: 캐러웨이 가문은 일종의 씨족이고, 우리는 버클루 공작의 후손이라는 전통을 가지고 있지만, 우리 혈통의 실제 창시자는 할아버지의 형으로, 1851년에 이곳에 와서 남북전쟁에 대리인을 보내고 아버지가 오늘날까지 이어가고 있는 철물 도매업을 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The demon which possessed him was exorcised at last, and with the completion of the work, for which all his life had been a painful preparation, rest descended on his remote and tortured soul.
examples.translation_ko: 그를 사로잡았던 악마가 마침내 쫓겨났고, 평생을 고통스러운 준비 과정으로 보낸 그 작업이 완성되면서 그의 외롭고 고통받던 영혼에 안식이 내려왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From delicate + -ly.
definition_en: Done with great care and precision.

senses.gloss: In a delicate manner; exquisitely.
senses.example: The gingerbread was delicately, if imprecisely, captured by the brushstrokes.

senses.gloss: Tactfully.
senses.example: He approached the main subject delicately.

examples.text: she asked delicately.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 조심스럽게 물었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The straw seats of the car hovered on the edge of combustion; the woman next to me perspired delicately for a while into her white shirtwaist, and then, as her newspaper dampened under her fingers, lapsed despairingly into deep heat with a desolate cry.
examples.translation_ko: 객차의 짚으로 만든 좌석들은 연소 직전까지 달아올랐고, 내 옆의 여자는 한동안 하얀 블라우스 속으로 우아하게 땀을 흘리다가, 손가락 아래 신문지가 축축해지자 절망적인 비명과 함께 깊은 더위 속으로 무력하게 빠져들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They were sombre blues, opaque like a delicately carved bowl in lapis lazuli, and yet with a quivering lustre that suggested the palpitation of mysterious life; there were purples, horrible like raw and putrid flesh, and yet with a glowing, sensual passion that called up vague memories of the Roman Empire of Heliogabalus; there were reds, shrill like the berries of holly—one thought of Christmas in England, and the snow, the good cheer, and the pleasure of children—and yet by some magic softened till they had the swooning tenderness of a dove’s breast; there were deep yellows that died with an unnatural passion into a green as fragrant as the spring and as pure as the sparkling water of a mountain brook.
examples.translation_ko: 청금석으로 정교하게 조각한 그릇처럼 불투명한 음울한 청색들이 있었는데, 그러면서도 신비로운 생명의 고동을 암시하는 떨리는 광택을 띠고 있었다. 날것의 썩은 살점처럼 끔찍한 자주색들이 있었는데, 그러면서도 헬리오가발루스 시대 로마 제국의 막연한 기억을 불러일으키는 타오르는 관능적 열정을 품고 있었다. 호랑가시나무 열매처럼 날카로운 적색들이 있었는데—영국의 크리스마스와 눈, 즐거운 축제, 아이들의 기쁨을 떠올리게 했다—그러면서도 어떤 마법에 의해 부드러워져서 비둘기 가슴의 황홀한 부드러움을 지니고 있었다. 부자연스러운 열정으로 죽어가면서 봄처럼 향기롭고 산골 시냇물처럼 맑고 반짝이는 초록으로 변해가는 깊은 황색들이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sparkel, sparkle, sparcle, equivalent to spark + -le (diminutive suffix). In some modern uses deverbal from etymology 2 below.
definition_en: To shine brightly with a brief flash of light.

senses.gloss: A little spark; a scintillation.
senses.example: The shock was sufficiently strong to strike out some sparkles of his fiery temper.

senses.gloss: Brilliance; luster.
senses.example: the sparkle of a diamond

senses.gloss: Liveliness; vivacity.
senses.example: the sparkle of his conversation over dinner

examples.text: Her hand, which dangles over the side, sparkles cold with jewels.
examples.translation_ko: 옆으로 늘어뜨린 그녀의 손이 보석들로 차갑게 반짝인다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: With enchanting murmurs Daisy admired this aspect or that of the feudal silhouette against the sky, admired the gardens, the sparkling odour of jonquils and the frothy odour of hawthorn and plum blossoms and the pale gold odour of kiss-me-at-the-gate.
examples.translation_ko: 황홀한 중얼거림과 함께 데이지는 하늘을 배경으로 한 봉건적 실루엣의 이런저런 면모를 감탄했고, 정원들과 수선화의 반짝이는 향기, 산사나무와 자두꽃의 거품 같은 향기, 그리고 키스미앳더게이트의 창백한 금빛 향기를 감탄했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They were sombre blues, opaque like a delicately carved bowl in lapis lazuli, and yet with a quivering lustre that suggested the palpitation of mysterious life; there were purples, horrible like raw and putrid flesh, and yet with a glowing, sensual passion that called up vague memories of the Roman Empire of Heliogabalus; there were reds, shrill like the berries of holly—one thought of Christmas in England, and the snow, the good cheer, and the pleasure of children—and yet by some magic softened till they had the swooning tenderness of a dove’s breast; there were deep yellows that died with an unnatural passion into a green as fragrant as the spring and as pure as the sparkling water of a mountain brook.
