examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A strong unpleasant smell.

senses.gloss: Alternative spelling of odor.

examples.text: With enchanting murmurs Daisy admired this aspect or that of the feudal silhouette against the sky, admired the gardens, the sparkling odour of jonquils and the frothy odour of hawthorn and plum blossoms and the pale gold odour of kiss-me-at-the-gate.
examples.translation_ko: 황홀한 중얼거림과 함께 데이지는 하늘을 배경으로 한 봉건적 실루엣의 이런저런 면모를 감탄했고, 정원들과 수선화의 반짝이는 향기, 산사나무와 자두꽃의 거품 같은 향기, 그리고 키스미앳더게이트의 창백한 금빛 향기를 감탄했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They were heavy with tropical odours.
examples.translation_ko: 열대의 향기가 짙게 배어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The breeze was laden still with the pleasant odours of the land.
examples.translation_ko: 바람에는 여전히 육지의 향긋한 냄새가 실려 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Partly from Middle English visiter, visitere, equivalent to visit + -er; and partly from Middle English visitour, from Anglo-Norman visitour, from ...
definition_en: A person who visits a place.

senses.gloss: Someone who visits someone else; someone staying as a guest.
senses.example: The Riley Packaging plant in Uganda is quite a sight. From wall to wall and floor to ceiling, it is crammed with vast rolls of paper. A visitor feels like an ant gazing at stacks of toilet rolls.

senses.gloss: Someone who pays a visit to a specific place or event; a sightseer or tourist.
senses.example: Belgrade knew how to show visitors a good time, thanks to its fashionable, somewhat raucous nightclub and bar scene.

senses.gloss: Someone, or a team, that is playing away from home.
senses.example: But, somewhat against the run of play, Craddock fired the visitors ahead, volleying a low effort beyond Simon Mignolet after Sunderland twice failed to clear attempted crosses from Stephen Hunt.

examples.text: I went back to the drawing-room and thought for an instant that they were chance visitors, all these official people who suddenly filled it.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 응접실로 돌아갔는데, 갑자기 그곳을 가득 채운 이 모든 공무원들이 우연히 찾아온 방문객들인 것처럼 순간 착각했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: So naturally Michaelis tried to find out what had happened, but Wilson wouldn’t say a word—instead he began to throw curious, suspicious glances at his visitor and ask him what he’d been doing at certain times on certain days.
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 미카엘리스는 당연히 무슨 일이 일어났는지 알아내려고 했지만, 윌슨은 한 마디도 하지 않았다—대신 방문객을 향해 이상하고 의심스러운 눈길을 던지기 시작하며 특정한 날 특정한 시간에 무엇을 하고 있었는지 물어보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When I was ushered into the drawing-room I found that Mrs. Strickland had a visitor, and when I discovered who he was, I guessed that I had been asked to come at just that time not without intention.
examples.translation_ko: 응접실로 안내되었을 때 스트릭랜드 부인에게 손님이 와 있었는데, 그가 누구인지 알고 보니 내가 바로 그 시간에 오도록 초대받은 것이 우연이 아니라는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Coined between 1300 and 1350 from Middle English repairen, from Middle French reparer, from Latin reparō (“renew, repair”).
definition_en: To fix or mend something that is broken.

senses.gloss: To restore to good working order, fix, or improve damaged condition; to mend; to remedy.
senses.example: to repair a house, a road, a shoe, a ship

senses.gloss: To make amends for, as for an injury, by an equivalent; to indemnify for.
senses.example: to repair a loss or damage

examples.text: Then he gave instructions that the open car wasn’t to be taken out under any circumstances—and this was strange, because the front right fender needed repair.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 오픈카는 어떤 경우에도 밖으로 빼내지 말라고 지시했는데, 앞쪽 오른편 펜더를 수리해야 했기 때문에 이상한 일이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And on Mondays eight servants, including an extra gardener, toiled all day with mops and scrubbing-brushes and hammers and garden-shears, repairing the ravages of the night before.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 월요일마다 정원사 한 명을 추가로 포함해 여덟 명의 하인들이 걸레와 솔과 망치와 정원 가위를 들고 하루 종일 애써서 전날 밤의 참상을 복구했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: If you haven’t read his book your education has been shamefully neglected, and you must repair the omission at once.
examples.translation_ko: 그분의 책을 읽지 않으셨다면 교양이 부끄럽게 부족한 거니까, 당장 그 빈틈을 메우셔야 해요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English graceful; equivalent to grace + -ful.
definition_en: Having or showing a pleasing and elegant quality.

senses.gloss: Having or showing grace in movement, shape, or proportion.
senses.example: She is a graceful dancer.

senses.gloss: Magnanimous, lacking arrogance or complaint; gracious.
senses.example: The athlete's graceful acceptance of the controversial second-place finish won the admiration of the spectators.

senses.gloss: Gradual and non-disruptive.

examples.text: I remember being surprised by his graceful, conservative foxtrot—I had never seen him dance before.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 우아하고 절제된 폭스트롯에 놀랐던 기억이 난다—그가 춤추는 모습을 본 적이 없었기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His head leaned back so far that it rested against the face of a defunct mantelpiece clock, and from this position his distraught eyes stared down at Daisy, who was sitting, frightened but graceful, on the edge of a stiff chair.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 머리는 너무 뒤로 젖혀져 고장 난 벽난로 시계 면에 닿아 있었고, 그 자세에서 그의 당황한 눈이 데이지를 내려다보고 있었다. 데이지는 딱딱한 의자 끝에 겁에 질렸지만 우아하게 앉아 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Holding his hostess’ hand, he made her a graceful, though perhaps too elaborate, speech of thanks, and left us.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 여주인의 손을 잡고 우아하지만 다소 과장된 감사 인사를 건넨 뒤 우리를 떠났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The obsolete sense of “quota”, from Medieval Latin quotātiō, from Latin quotāre, is attested from the 15th century. The sense “fragment of verbal e...
definition_en: A passage or phrase repeated from another text.

senses.gloss: A fragment of a human expression that is repeated by somebody else, for example from literature or a famous speech.
senses.example: "Where they burn books, they will also burn people" is a famous quotation from Heinrich Heine.

senses.gloss: The act of quoting someone or something.
senses.example: In his mature works, [Chinary] Ung pays regular homage to Cambodian music by evoking its ambience without resorting to quotation of specific Cambodian melodies.

senses.gloss: A price that has been quoted for buying or selling.
senses.example: Let's get a quotation for repairing the roof before we decide whether it's worth doing.

examples.text: Up in the city, I tried for a while to list the quotations on an interminable amount of stock, then I fell asleep in my swivel-chair.
examples.translation_ko: 도시에서 나는 한동안 끝없이 많은 주식의 시세를 정리하려 애쓰다가 회전의자에서 잠이 들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Mrs. Strickland and Mrs. Ronaldson looked down with a slightly pious expression which indicated, I felt sure, that they thought the quotation was from Holy Writ.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인과 로널드슨 부인은 약간 경건한 표정으로 고개를 숙였는데, 그 인용구가 성경에서 나온 것이라고 생각하고 있음이 분명했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: A quotation from the Bible came to my lips, but I held my tongue, for I know that clergymen think it a little blasphemous when the laity poach upon their preserves.
examples.translation_ko: 성경 구절이 입가에 맴돌았지만, 나는 입을 다물었다. 성직자들은 평신도가 자신들의 영역을 침범하는 것을 다소 신성모독적이라고 여긴다는 것을 알고 있었기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French reserver, from Latin reservō (“to reserve, retain”).
definition_en: The act of reserving or keeping back; reservation; exception.

senses.gloss: The act of reserving or keeping back; reservation; exception.
senses.example: The book is on reserve.

senses.gloss: Restraint of freedom in words or actions; backwardness; caution in personal behavior.
A natural resource known to exist but not currently exploited.
senses.example: New oil reserves are continuously being discovered, but not as fast as the existing ones are running out.

examples.text: Reserving judgements is a matter of infinite hope.
examples.translation_ko: 판단을 유보한다는 것은 무한한 희망의 문제다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I think that he would have acknowledged anything now, without reserve, but he wanted to talk about Daisy.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 그는 거리낌 없이 무엇이든 인정했을 것 같았지만, 그가 하고 싶어 한 이야기는 데이지에 관한 것이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology:
From Middle English westerne, from Old English westerne, from Proto-Germanic *westrōnijaz.
By surface analysis, west + -ern.
definition_en: Of, facing, situated in, or related to the west.

senses.gloss: Of, facing, situated in, or related to the west.
senses.example: the western approaches

senses.gloss: Blowing from the west; westerly.
Occidental.

examples.text: A silver curve of the moon hovered already in the western sky.
examples.translation_ko: 은빛 초승달이 이미 서쪽 하늘에 떠 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: My family have been prominent, well-to-do people in this Middle Western city for three generations.
examples.translation_ko: 우리 가문은 이 중서부 도시에서 삼 대에 걸쳐 저명하고 유복한 사람들이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: Borrowed from Irish clann (“offspring, children of the family”) and Scottish Gaelic clann, both from Old Irish cland, borrowed from Old Welsh plant...
definition_en: A group of people all descended from a common ancestor, in fact or belief, especially when the exact genealogies are not known.

senses.gloss: A group of people all descended from a common ancestor, in fact or belief, especially when the exact genealogies are not known.
A traditional social group of families in the Scottish Highlands having a common hereditary chieftain.
Any group defined by family ties with some sort of political unity.

examples.text: His voice was solemn, as if the memory of that sudden extinction of a clan still haunted him.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 목소리는 엄숙했는데, 마치 일족이 갑작스럽게 전멸한 기억이 아직도 그를 괴롭히는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And the Hornbeams and the Willie Voltaires, and a whole clan named Blackbuck, who always gathered in a corner and flipped up their noses like goats at whosoever came near.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 혼빔 가족과 윌리 볼테어 가족, 그리고 블랙벅이라는 성씨의 온 일족이 있었는데, 이들은 항상 구석에 모여서 가까이 오는 사람이면 누구든 염소처럼 코를 치켜세우곤 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English delaien, borrowed from Anglo-Norman delaier, Old French deslaier, from des- + Old French laier (“to leave”), a conflation of Ol...
definition_en: A period of time before an event occurs; the act of delaying; procrastination; lingering inactivity.

senses.gloss: A period of time before an event occurs; the act of delaying; procrastination; lingering inactivity.
senses.example: the delay before the echo of a sound

senses.gloss: An audio effects unit that introduces a controlled delay.
senses.example: The 8-bit sound quality of many early delays did indeed leave a lot to be desired (compare this to the 16-bit digital technology of CDs)

senses.gloss: Synonym of promise (“object representing delayed result”).

examples.text: Father agreed to finance me for a year, and after various delays I came East, permanently, I thought, in the spring of twenty-two.
examples.translation_ko: 아버지는 일 년간 자금을 대주기로 동의했고, 여러 차례 지연 끝에 나는 1922년 봄, 영구히 정착할 생각으로 동부에 왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Several times he turned his head and looked back for their car, and if the traffic delayed them he slowed up until they came into sight.
examples.translation_ko: 몇 번이나 고개를 돌려 그들의 차를 뒤돌아보았고, 교통체증으로 그들이 늦어지면 그들이 보일 때까지 속도를 늦췄다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English center, centre, from Middle French centre, from Latin centrum, from Ancient Greek κέντρον (kéntron), from κεντεῖν (kenteîn, “to...
definition_en: Alternative spelling of center.

senses.gloss: Alternative spelling of center.

examples.text: Gatsby stood in the centre of the crimson carpet and gazed around with fascinated eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 진홍색 카펫 한가운데 서서 매혹된 눈으로 주위를 둘러보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Instead of being the warm centre of the world, the Middle West now seemed like the ragged edge of the universe—so I decided to go East and learn the bond business.
examples.translation_ko: 세상의 따뜻한 중심지였던 중서부가 이제는 우주의 너덜너덜한 가장자리처럼 느껴졌다. 그래서 나는 동부로 가서 채권업을 배우기로 결심했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

definition_en: Strangely unconventional; highly unusual and different from common experience, often in an extravagant, fantastic, and/or conspicuous way.

senses.gloss: Strangely unconventional; highly unusual and different from common experience, often in an extravagant, fantastic, and/or conspicuous way.

examples.text: The most insignificant of Strickland’s works suggests a personality which is strange, tormented, and complex; and it is this surely which prevents even those who do not like his pictures from being indifferent to them; it is this which has excited so curious an interest in his life and character.

definition_en: A skill or activity requiring special training and practice.

examples.text: He had learnt his craft at the school of Alexander Pope, and he wrote moral stories in rhymed couplets.

examples.text: It is a grotesque misapprehension which sees in art no more than a craft comprehensible perfectly only to the craftsman: art is a manifestation of emotion, and emotion speaks a language that all may understand.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: With his disinterested passion for art, he had a real desire to call the attention of the wise to a talent which was in the highest degree original; but he was too good a journalist to be unaware that the “human interest” would enable him more easily to effect his purpose.
examples.translation_ko: 예술에 대한 사심 없는 열정으로, 그는 최고도로 독창적인 재능에 현명한 이들의 관심을 끌고자 하는 진정한 욕망을 가지고 있었다. 하지만 그는 너무나 훌륭한 저널리스트여서 '인간적 흥미'가 자신의 목적을 더 쉽게 달성하게 해줄 것임을 모르지 않았다.

examples.text: His parents were shiftless and unsuccessful farm people—his imagination had never really accepted them as his parents at all.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And when such as had come in contact with Strickland in the past, writers who had known him in London, painters who had met him in the cafés of Montmartre, discovered to their amazement that where they had seen but an unsuccessful artist, like another, authentic genius had rubbed shoulders with them there began to appear in the magazines of France and America a succession of articles, the reminiscences of one, the appreciation of another, which added to Strickland’s notoriety, and fed without satisfying the curiosity of the public.
examples.translation_ko: 과거에 스트릭랜드와 접촉했던 사람들, 런던에서 그를 알았던 작가들, 몽마르트르의 카페에서 그를 만났던 화가들이 자신들이 그저 또 다른 실패한 예술가로만 보았던 곳에서 진정한 천재가 어깨를 스쳤다는 사실을 놀랍게 발견하자, 프랑스와 미국의 잡지들에 연이어 기사들이 나타나기 시작했다. 한 사람의 회상, 다른 사람의 평가가 스트릭랜드의 명성을 더했고, 대중의 호기심을 만족시키지는 못한 채 부채질했다.

senses.example: ‘It's rather like a beautiful Inverness cloak one has inherited. Much too good to hide away, so one wears it instead of an overcoat and pretends it's an amusing new fashion.’

senses.gloss: That which conceals; a disguise or pretext.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The ironic philosopher reflects with a smile that Sir Walter Raleigh is more safely inshrined in the memory of mankind because he set his cloak for the Virgin Queen to walk on than because he carried the English name to undiscovered countries.
examples.translation_ko: 아이러니한 철학자는 미소를 지으며 생각한다. 월터 롤리 경이 인류의 기억 속에 더욱 안전하게 자리 잡은 것은 미지의 땅에 영국의 이름을 전파했기 때문이 아니라, 처녀 여왕이 걸을 수 있도록 자신의 망토를 깔아드렸기 때문이라고.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From scant + -y.
definition_en: Meager or insufficient in amount.

senses.gloss: Somewhat less than is needed in amplitude or extent.
senses.example: A girl dressed in scanty clothing

senses.gloss: Sparing; niggardly; parsimonious; stingy.
senses.example: In illustrating a point of difficulty, be not too scanty of words.

examples.text: He went out of the room calling “Ewing!” and returned in a few minutes accompanied by an embarrassed, slightly worn young man, with shell-rimmed glasses and scanty blond hair.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 "유잉!"을 부르며 방을 나갔다가 몇 분 후 당황한 기색이 역력한, 약간 지쳐 보이는 젊은 남자를 데리고 돌아왔다. 그는 뿔테 안경을 쓰고 있었고 금발 머리는 성성했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It is not strange, then, that those who wrote of him should have eked out their scanty recollections with a lively fancy, and it is evident that there was enough in the little that was known of him to give opportunity to the romantic scribe; there was much in his life which was strange and terrible, in his character something outrageous, and in his fate not a little that was pathetic.
examples.translation_ko: 따라서 그에 대해 쓴 사람들이 빈약한 기억을 생생한 상상력으로 보완했다는 것은 이상한 일이 아니며, 그에 대해 알려진 적은 것들 속에도 낭만적인 필사자에게 기회를 줄 만한 충분한 소재가 있었음이 분명하다. 그의 삶에는 기이하고 끔찍한 것들이 많았고, 그의 성격에는 터무니없는 면이 있었으며, 그의 운명에는 적지 않은 비극적 요소가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From mis- + conception.
definition_en: A mistaken or incorrect idea about something.

senses.gloss: A mistaken belief, a wrong idea.
senses.example: There are several common misconceptions about the theory of relativity.

examples.text: So I take advantage of this short halt, while Gatsby, so to speak, caught his breath, to clear this set of misconceptions away.
examples.translation_ko: 그래서 나는 개츠비가 말하자면 숨을 고르는 이 짧은 휴지를 이용해서 이런 오해들을 말끔히 정리해두려고 한다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He wrote his biography[3] avowedly to “remove certain misconceptions which had gained currency” in regard to the later part of his father’s life, and which had “caused considerable pain to persons still living.”
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아버지 생애의 후반부에 관해 "널리 퍼진 특정한 오해들을 불식시키고" "아직 생존해 있는 사람들에게 상당한 고통을 안겨준" 것들을 바로잡기 위해 공공연히 전기를 썼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From respect + -able.
definition_en: Having or showing a sense of what is right and proper.

senses.gloss: Deserving respect.
senses.example: His accomplishments, morals, loyalty, and stature make him a respectable person.

senses.gloss: Decent; satisfactory.
senses.example: Turn up to the interview wearing something respectable.  She plays a respectable game of chess.  He got a respectable B+ on his last exam.

senses.gloss: Moderately well-to-do.

examples.text: The quarter was not fashionable; it was not even respectable.
examples.translation_ko: 그 지역은 고급스럽지도 않았고, 심지어 점잖지도 않은 곳이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is obvious that there was much in the commonly received account of Strickland’s life to embarrass a respectable family.
examples.translation_ko: 일반적으로 알려진 스트릭랜드의 생애에는 점잖은 가문을 당황시킬 만한 내용이 많았다는 것이 분명하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From colour + -less.
definition_en: Having no colour.

senses.gloss: Having little or no colour.
senses.example: The wide prospect up stream was grey and lowering, the long still-distant waterfront of Dundee, and the Fife shore were alike colourless, and there was ample evidence of rough weather not far ahead.

senses.gloss: Water white.
Lacking in interest or variety.

examples.text: When anyone spoke to him he invariably laughed in an agreeable, colourless way.
examples.translation_ko: 누군가 그에게 말을 걸면 언제나 상냥하지만 특색 없는 방식으로 웃어댔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I have read this work with a good deal of amusement, and upon this I congratulate myself, since it is colourless and dull.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이 작품을 상당히 재미있게 읽었는데, 이는 축하할 일이다. 왜냐하면 이 책은 무미건조하고 따분하기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Extremely surprising or impressive.

senses.gloss: Causing astonishment.
senses.example: astonishing display

examples.text: The fact was infinitely astonishing to him, and I recognized first the unusual quality of wonder, and then the man—it was the late patron of Gatsby’s library.
examples.translation_ko: 그 사실이 그에게는 무한히 놀라운 일이었고, 나는 먼저 그 특이한 경이로움의 성질을, 그다음에 그 사람을—개츠비의 서재를 애용했던 그 사람임을 알아보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The modern clergyman has acquired in his study of the science which I believe is called exegesis an astonishing facility for explaining things away, but the subtlety with which the Rev. Robert Strickland has “interpreted” all the facts in his father’s life which a dutiful son might find it inconvenient to remember must surely lead him in the fullness of time to the highest dignities of the Church.
examples.translation_ko: 현대의 성직자들은 주석학이라고 불리는 학문 연구를 통해 사물을 해명해버리는 놀라운 능력을 습득했지만, 로버트 스트릭랜드 목사가 효성스러운 아들로서 기억하기 불편할 수 있는 아버지 생애의 모든 사실들을 "해석"해낸 그 교묘함은 분명 때가 되면 그를 교회의 최고 지위에 올려놓을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sotilte, from Old French sutilté, inherited from Latin subtīlitās, from subtīlis (“subtle”). Equivalent to subtle + -ty. Double...
definition_en: A subtle or delicate quality.

senses.gloss: The quality of being scarcely noticeable or difficult to discern. (of things)
senses.example: the subtlety of the Mona Lisa’s smile

senses.gloss: The quality of being done in a clever way that is not obvious or not direct; the quality of being carefully thought out. (of things)
senses.example: the subtlety of a writer’s analysis / of a singer’s phrasing

senses.gloss: The quality of being able to achieve one's aims through clever, delicate or indirect methods. (of people)
senses.example: With all his usual subtlety, he quietly fixed the problem before anyone else noticed it.

examples.text: But who can fathom the subtleties of the human heart?
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 누가 인간 마음의 미묘함을 헤아릴 수 있겠는가?

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French inconvenient, from Latin inconvenientem.
definition_en: Causing trouble or difficulty.

senses.gloss: not convenient

examples.text: “It’s quite obvious that it would be much easier to nurse him here,” I said, “but of course it would be very inconvenient.
examples.translation_ko: "물론 여기서 간병하는 게 훨씬 쉬울 거라는 건 분명하지만," 내가 말했다, "당연히 매우 불편할 겁니다.

definition_en: The state of being full or complete.

senses.gloss: Being full; completeness.
The degree to which a space is full.
The degree to which fate has become known.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They would grow old insensibly; they would see their son and daughter come to years of reason, marry in due course—the one a pretty girl, future mother of healthy children; the other a handsome, manly fellow, obviously a soldier; and at last, prosperous in their dignified retirement, beloved by their descendants, after a happy, not unuseful life, in the fullness of their age they would sink into the grave.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 자연스럽게 늙어갈 것이고, 아들과 딸이 분별력을 갖는 나이가 되어 때가 되면 결혼하는 것을 보게 될 것이다. 하나는 예쁜 소녀로 건강한 아이들의 미래 어머니가 되고, 다른 하나는 잘생기고 남자다운 청년으로 분명히 군인이 될 것이다. 그리고 마침내 품위 있는 은퇴 생활에서 번영하며 후손들의 사랑을 받다가, 행복하고 무익하지 않은 삶을 마친 후 충분한 나이에 무덤으로 들어갈 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French hasardeux, equivalent to hazard + -ous.
definition_en: posing a risk or danger

senses.gloss: Risky; dangerous; with the nature of a hazard.
Of or involving chance.

examples.text: It is hazardous to play poker with them, but their ingenuity adds a peculiar excitement to the best game in the world.
examples.translation_ko: 그들과 포커를 치는 것은 위험하지만, 그들의 기발함은 세상에서 가장 훌륭한 게임에 독특한 흥미를 더해준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was a hazardous, though maybe a gallant thing to do, since it is probable that the legend commonly received has had no small share in the growth of Strickland’s reputation; for there are many who have been attracted to his art by the detestation in which they held his character or the compassion with which they regarded his death; and the son’s well-meaning efforts threw a singular chill upon the father’s admirers.
examples.translation_ko: 이는 위험하지만 어쩌면 용감한 일이었다. 왜냐하면 일반적으로 알려진 전설이 스트릭랜드의 명성 성장에 적지 않은 몫을 했을 가능성이 있기 때문이다. 그의 인격에 대한 혐오나 그의 죽음에 대한 연민 때문에 그의 예술에 끌린 사람들이 많았는데, 아들의 선의에서 우러난 노력은 아버지의 추종자들에게 묘한 냉기를 던져주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English probable, from Old French probable, from Latin probābilis (“that may be proved, credible”), from probāre (“to test, examine”); ...
definition_en: Likely to happen or be true.

senses.gloss: Likely or most likely to be true.
senses.example: It's probable that it will rain tomorrow.

senses.gloss: Likely to happen.
senses.example: With all the support we have, success is looking probable.

senses.gloss: Supporting, or giving ground for, belief, but not demonstrating.
senses.example: From an examination of the Teutonic words for "temple" Grimm has made it probable that amongst the Germans the oldest sanctuaries were natural woods.

examples.text: I thought it probable enough that Blanche Stroeve would not continue to find life with Strickland tolerable, but one of the falsest of proverbs is that you must lie on the bed that you have made.
examples.translation_ko: 블랑슈 스트루브가 스트릭랜드와의 생활을 계속 견딜 수 있으리라고는 생각하지 않았지만, '자신이 깐 자리에는 자신이 누워야 한다'는 속담만큼 거짓된 것도 없다.

etymology: From grow + -th (abstract nominal suffix). Compare Old Frisian grēd ("meadow, pasture"; > North Frisian greyde (“growth, pasture”)), Middle High Ge...
definition_en: The process of becoming or growing larger.

senses.gloss: An increase in size, number, value, or strength.
Ellipsis of economic growth.
senses.example: Growth was dampened by a softening of the global economy in 2001, but picked up in the subsequent years due to strong growth in China.

senses.gloss: An increase in psychological strength or resilience; an increased ability to overcome adversity.
senses.example: Struggle, disappointment, and criticism all contribute to a person's growth.

examples.text: A small, flat-nosed Jew raised his large head and regarded me with two fine growths of hair which luxuriated in either nostril.

definition_en: A strong feeling of dislike or hatred.

senses.gloss: Hate coupled with disgust; abhorrence.

senses.example: Neckties are a real detestation for them.

examples.text: Here, on this remote island, he seemed to have aroused none of the detestation with which he was regarded at home, but compassion rather; and his vagaries were accepted with tolerance.

etymology: From New Latin biographia, formed from Ancient Greek βίος (bíos, “life”) + γράφω (gráphō, “write”).
definition_en: A written account of someone's life.

senses.gloss: A person's life story, especially one published.
senses.example: There are many biographies of Benjamin Franklin.

senses.gloss: The art of writing this kind of story.

examples.text: It is due to no accident that when one of his most important works, The Woman of Samaria,[4] was sold at Christie’s shortly after the discussion which followed the publication of Mr. Strickland’s biography, it fetched £235 less than it had done nine months before when it was bought by the distinguished collector whose sudden death had brought it once more under the hammer.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 씨의 전기 출간 이후 벌어진 논란 직후 그의 가장 중요한 작품 중 하나인 《사마리아 여인》이 크리스티 경매장에서 팔렸을 때, 9개월 전 저명한 수집가가 구입했을 때보다 235파운드나 낮은 가격을 기록한 것은 결코 우연이 아니다. 그 수집가의 갑작스러운 죽음으로 이 작품이 다시 경매대에 오르게 된 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: For my part, I should be sorry to think that there was nothing between Anthony and Cleopatra but an economic situation; and it will require a great deal more evidence than is ever likely to be available, thank God, to persuade me that Tiberius was as blameless a monarch as King George V. Dr. Weitbrecht-Rotholz has dealt in such terms with the Rev. Robert Strickland’s innocent biography that it is difficult to avoid feeling a certain sympathy for the unlucky parson.
examples.translation_ko: 내 생각으로는 안토니우스와 클레오파트라 사이에 경제적 상황 외에는 아무것도 없었다고 여기는 것은 유감스러운 일이다. 그리고 티베리우스가 조지 5세만큼 흠잡을 데 없는 군주였다고 나를 설득하려면, 다행히도 결코 입수될 가능성이 없는 것보다 훨씬 더 많은 증거가 필요할 것이다. 바이트브레히트-로톨츠 박사는 로버트 스트릭랜드 목사의 순진한 전기를 그런 식으로 다루었기 때문에 그 불운한 목사에게 어느 정도 동정심을 느끼지 않을 수 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cravinge, from Old English crafing (“claim, demand”); equivalent to crave + -ing.
definition_en: A strong desire for something.

senses.gloss: A strong desire; yearning.
senses.example: The craving for cuteness is a psychological phenomenon that originally had the purpose of increasing the chances of a baby to survive […]

examples.text: I believed him capable of uprooting from his heart, though it might be with agony, so that he was left battered and ensanguined, anything that came between himself and that uncomprehended craving that urged him constantly to he knew not what.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 자신과 그 이해할 수 없는 갈망 사이를 가로막는 것이라면 무엇이든, 비록 그것이 고통스럽더라도, 자신이 만신창이가 되고 피투성이가 될지라도, 자신의 마음에서 뿌리째 뽑아낼 수 있는 사람이라고 믿었다. 그 갈망은 끊임없이 그를 자신도 모르는 무언가를 향해 내몰고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Perhaps Charles Strickland’s power and originality would scarcely have sufficed to turn the scale if the remarkable mythopoeic faculty of mankind had not brushed aside with impatience a story which disappointed all its craving for the extraordinary.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 찰스 스트릭랜드의 힘과 독창성만으로는 균형을 뒤바꾸기에 충분하지 않았을 것이다. 만약 인류의 놀라운 신화 창조 능력이 비범한 것에 대한 모든 갈망을 실망시키는 이야기를 성급하게 밀어내지 않았다면 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From misgive, from mis- + give, from Middle English give (“suggest, given”). Compare given and what gives.
definition_en: A feeling of doubt or apprehension about something.

senses.gloss: doubt, apprehension, a feeling of dread
senses.example: In the night, or the gloomy chambers of the day, fears and misgivings wax strong, but out in the sunlight there is, for a time, cessation even of the terror of death.

examples.text: During the journey I thought over my errand with misgiving.
examples.translation_ko: 여행하는 동안 나는 불안한 마음으로 내 임무를 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: And presently Dr. Weitbrecht-Rotholz produced the work which finally set at rest the misgivings of all lovers of art.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 마침내 바이트브레히트-로톨츠 박사가 모든 예술 애호가들의 의구심을 완전히 잠재운 작품을 발표했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English reder, redar, redere, redare, from Old English rēdere, rǣdere (“a reader; scholar; diviner”), from Proto-West Germanic *rādāri,...
definition_en: A person who reads books or other written material.

senses.gloss: A person who reads.
senses.example: an early reader, a talented reader

senses.gloss: A person who reads a publication.
senses.example: 10,000 weekly readers

senses.gloss: A person who recites literary works, usually to an audience.

examples.text: Heaven knows what pains the author has been at, what bitter experiences he has endured and what heartache suffered, to give some chance reader a few hours’ relaxation or to while away the tedium of a journey.
examples.translation_ko: 하늘만이 아시겠지만, 저자가 얼마나 고생했을지, 얼마나 쓰라린 경험을 견뎠을지, 얼마나 가슴 아파했을지를, 그저 우연한 독자 한 명에게 몇 시간의 휴식을 주거나 여행의 지루함을 달래주기 위해서 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Dr. Weitbrecht-Rotholz belongs to that school of historians which believes that human nature is not only about as bad as it can be, but a great deal worse; and certainly the reader is safer of entertainment in their hands than in those of the writers who take a malicious pleasure in representing the great figures of romance as patterns of the domestic virtues.
examples.translation_ko: 바이트브레히트-로톨츠 박사는 인간의 본성이 가능한 한 나쁠 뿐만 아니라 그보다 훨씬 더 나쁘다고 믿는 역사학파에 속한다. 확실히 독자들은 로맨스의 위대한 인물들을 가정적 미덕의 모범으로 묘사하는 데 악의적 쾌감을 느끼는 작가들보다는 이런 사람들의 손에서 더 안전하게 즐거움을 얻을 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English vertu, virtue, borrowed from Anglo-Norman vertu, virtu, from Latin virtus (“manliness, bravery, worth, moral excellence”), from...
definition_en: A quality considered morally excellent or admirable.

senses.gloss: Accordance with moral principles; conformity of behaviour or thought with the strictures of morality; good moral conduct.
senses.example: Without virtue, there is no freedom.

senses.gloss: A particular manifestation of moral excellence in a person; an admirable quality.
senses.example: Some men are modest, and seem to take pains to hide their virtues; and, from a natural distance and reserve in their tempers, scarce suffer their good qualities to be known […].

senses.gloss: Specifically, each of several qualities held to be particularly important, including the four cardinal virtues, the three theological virtues, or the seven virtues opposed to the seven deadly sins.
senses.example: The divine virtues of truth and equity are the only bands of friendship, the only supports of society.

examples.text: Everyone suspects himself of at least one of the cardinal virtues, and this is mine: I am one of the few honest people that I have ever known.
examples.translation_ko: 누구나 자신에게 적어도 하나의 추기경 덕목이 있다고 생각하는데, 내 것은 이것이다. 나는 내가 아는 몇 안 되는 정직한 사람 중 하나다.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French economique, from Latin oeconomicus, from Ancient Greek οἰκονομικός (oikonomikós, “skilled with household management”).
definition_en: Relating to the production and distribution of wealth.

senses.gloss: Pertaining to an economy.
Frugal; cheap (in the sense of representing good value); economical.
Pertaining to the study of money and its movement.

examples.text: I might have spoken of the economic position of woman, of the contract, tacit and overt, which a man accepts by his marriage, and of much else; but I felt that there was only one point which really signified.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 여성의 경제적 지위나, 남자가 결혼으로써 받아들이는 암묵적이고 명시적인 계약, 그리고 그 밖의 여러 가지에 대해 말할 수도 있었지만, 정말 중요한 것은 오직 한 가지뿐이라고 느꼈다.

etymology: From Middle English evidence, from Old French [Term?], from Latin evidentia (“clearness, in Late Latin a proof”), from evidens (“clear, evident”); ...
definition_en: Facts or information used to decide a question or support an argument.

senses.gloss: Facts or observations presented in support of an assertion.
senses.example: There is no evidence that anyone was here earlier.

senses.gloss: Anything admitted by a court to prove or disprove alleged matters of fact in a trial.
One who bears witness.
senses.example: He recapitulated the Sybil’s story word by word, with the air of a man who is cross-examining an evidence, and trying to make him contradict himself.

examples.text: It is not thus that the Church in its great days dealt with evidence that was unwelcome.
examples.translation_ko: 전성기의 교회가 달갑지 않은 증거를 이런 식으로 다루지는 않았다.

etymology: From Middle English persoun, from Anglo-Norman, Old French persone (“parson, person”), from Medieval Latin persona (“parson, person”), from Latin p...
definition_en: A clergyman who is in charge of a local church.

senses.gloss: An Anglican cleric having full legal control of a parish under ecclesiastical law.
A Protestant minister.
A Roman Catholic priest of an independent parish church.
senses.example:
a lewde curate,
A parson benyfyced
But nothynge well advysed.

examples.text: There entered a tall man in khaki, with the parson’s collar, handsome in a somewhat heavy fashion, but with the frank eyes that I remembered in him as a boy.
examples.translation_ko: 목사복 칼라를 한 카키색 군복의 키 큰 남자가 들어왔는데, 다소 둔중한 느낌이지만 잘생긴 편이었고, 내가 그를 소년으로 기억하던 때의 그 솔직한 눈빛을 그대로 지니고 있었다.

etymology: From Middle English trecherie, from Old French tricherie, trecherie, from tricher, trichier (“to cheat”).
definition_en: Disloyal or deceitful behavior.

senses.gloss: Deliberate, often calculated, disregard for trust or faith.
senses.example: Suddenly, in the midst of high-camp treachery and sleuthery, each character does a star turn, breaking out in song.

senses.gloss: The act of violating the confidence of another, usually for personal gain.
Treason.

examples.text: His decent reticence is branded as hypocrisy, his circumlocutions are roundly called lies, and his silence is vilified as treachery.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 품위 있는 침묵은 위선으로 낙인찍히고, 그의 완곡한 표현은 거짓말이라고 단정되며, 그의 침묵은 배신으로 비난받는다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The ridicule he had endured for years seemed now to weigh him down, and the final blow of Blanche’s treachery had robbed him of the resiliency which had made him take it so gaily.
examples.translation_ko: 수년간 견뎌온 조롱이 이제 그를 짓누르는 듯했고, 블랑슈의 배신이라는 마지막 일격이 그동안 그로 하여금 그 모든 것을 유쾌하게 받아들일 수 있게 해주던 회복력을 앗아가 버렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Origin unknown; the Oxford English Dictionary (OED) states that “the facts as to its origin appear to have been lost, even before the word became c...
definition_en: A person or thing that is considered to be deceitful or hypocritical.

senses.gloss: A hoax, jest, or prank.
A fraud or sham; (uncountable) hypocrisy.
A cheat, fraudster, or hypocrite.
senses.example: "It is an open admission," he cried. "What more do you want? The fellow is a self-confessed humbug. We have only to return home and report him as the brazen imposter that he is."

examples.text: “What’s the good of trying to humbug me?”
examples.translation_ko: "나를 속이려 해봤자 무슨 소용이 있겠어?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: And on the strength of peccadillos, reprehensible in an author, but excusable in a son, the Anglo-Saxon race is accused of prudishness, humbug, pretentiousness, deceit, cunning, and bad cooking.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 작가로서는 비난받을 만하지만 아들로서는 용서할 만한 사소한 잘못들을 근거로, 앵글로색슨 민족은 경직성, 허위, 허세, 기만, 교활함, 그리고 형편없는 요리 실력으로 고발당한다.

etymology: From cook + -ing. The noun and adjective follow from the verb. The use of the word cooking to describe cheap bitter was popularized by the title ch...
definition_en: The act of preparing food.

senses.gloss: The process of preparing food by using heat.
senses.example: The cooking took a long time. Fionn built a spit from the ash that the salmon had knocked down.

senses.gloss: An instance of preparing food by using heat.
senses.example: Historian Madeleine Pelner Cosman addresses the multiple cookings of single dishes in medieval recipes. Why would a veal stew require four changes of pot and five separate cookings?

senses.gloss: One's ability to prepare food; cookery.
senses.example: Azie is a charming and attentive host. His cooking is excellent and the meals he prepares seem healthy and nutritious.

examples.text: She was sitting on her haunches in the lean-to that served her as kitchen, watching some mess cooking in a pot.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 부엌으로 쓰는 쪽마루에 쪼그리고 앉아 냄비에서 끓고 있는 무언가를 지켜보고 있었다.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From white + wash.
definition_en: To cover or conceal something by applying a white coating.

senses.gloss: A lime and water mixture for painting walls and fences bright white.
senses.example: For walls plaster gave a smooth white surface; or if it was not sufficiently white, or had become discoloured, it could be brightened up with a coat of whitewash or paint.

senses.gloss: A complete victory or series of victories without suffering any losses; a clean sweep.
senses.example: For the first time in a long time, Australia are being threatened with the prospect of a 5-0 whitewash

senses.gloss: A campaign to paper over unfavorable elements; (everyday life) pretense.

examples.text: I followed him over a low whitewashed railroad fence, and we walked back a hundred yards along the road under Doctor Eckleburg’s persistent stare.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그를 따라 낮은 하얀 철도 울타리를 넘어 에클버그 박사의 끈질긴 시선 아래 길을 따라 백 야드쯤 되돌아 걸었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Dr. Weitbrecht-Rotholz was an enthusiastic admirer of Charles Strickland, and there was no danger that he would whitewash him.
examples.translation_ko: 바이트브레히트-로톨츠 박사는 찰스 스트릭랜드의 열렬한 찬미자였으므로, 그가 스트릭랜드를 미화할 위험은 전혀 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Clipping of psychotic and psychopath + -o (“person with characteristic”). Compare sicko.
definition_en: A person with a mental disorder characterized by abnormal behavior.

senses.gloss: Psychotic, psychopathic, or (broadly) otherwise insane.
senses.example: Oh, she's sweet but a psycho / A little bit psycho / At night she's screamin' / "I'm-ma-ma-ma out my mind"

examples.text: The mystic sees the ineffable, and the psycho-pathologist the unspeakable.
examples.translation_ko: 신비주의자는 형언할 수 없는 것을 보고, 정신병리학자는 말할 수 없는 것을 본다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was a psycho-pathologist, as well as a student of art, and the subconscious had few secrets from him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 예술 연구자인 동시에 정신병리학자였으며, 무의식이 그에게 숨기는 비밀은 거의 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From pathology + -ist.
definition_en: A doctor who specializes in the study and diagnosis of disease by examining tissues and cells.

senses.gloss: An expert in pathology; a specialist who examines samples of body tissues for diagnostic or forensic purpose.

examples.text: The mystic sees the ineffable, and the psycho-pathologist the unspeakable.

examples.translation_ko: 그는 예술 연구자인 동시에 정신병리학자였으며, 무의식이 그에게 숨기는 비밀은 거의 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From sub- + conscious.
definition_en: Relating to or being a part of the mind that operates below the level of conscious awareness.

senses.gloss: Occuring in the part of our mind that we are not normally aware of.
senses.example: The sense of smell can be a subconscious influence on our actions.

senses.gloss: Partially conscious.

examples.text: He was a psycho-pathologist, as well as a student of art, and the subconscious had few secrets from him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 예술 연구자인 동시에 정신병리학자였으며, 무의식이 그에게 숨기는 비밀은 거의 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It may be that in his rogues the writer gratifies instincts deep-rooted in him, which the manners and customs of a civilised world have forced back to the mysterious recesses of the subconscious.
examples.translation_ko: 작가는 자신의 악역들을 통해 문명 세계의 예의와 관습에 의해 잠재의식의 신비로운 깊은 곳으로 밀려난, 자신 안에 깊이 뿌리박힌 본능들을 충족시키는 것일지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From mean + -ness.
definition_en: A quality of being mean or unkind.

senses.gloss: The condition, or quality, of being mean (any of its definitions)
senses.example: This figure is of a later date, by the meanness of the workmanship.

senses.gloss: A mean act.
senses.example: There are enough meannesses in everyone — ourselves included — to make for us a contemptible world, if we select the meannesses and let our minds dwell upon them.

examples.text: His heart warms to him when he can bring forward some example of cruelty or meanness, and he exults like an inquisitor at the auto da fé of an heretic when with some forgotten story he can confound the filial piety of the Rev. Robert Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 잔혹함이나 비열함의 사례를 제시할 수 있을 때면 그의 마음이 따뜻해지고, 잊혀진 이야기로 로버트 스트릭랜드 목사의 효성을 당황시킬 수 있을 때면 마치 종교재판관이 이단자의 화형식에서 환호하듯 의기양양해한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then we would speak of this publisher and of that, comparing the generosity of one with the meanness of another; we would argue whether it was better to go to one who gave handsome royalties or to another who “pushed” a book for all it was worth.
examples.translation_ko: 그러면 우리는 이 출판사 저 출판사 이야기를 하며, 한 곳의 후함과 다른 곳의 인색함을 비교했다. 후한 인세를 주는 곳으로 갈지, 아니면 책을 있는 힘껏 "밀어주는" 다른 곳으로 갈지 논쟁을 벌이기도 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French exulter, from Latin exsultō, frequentative of exsiliō (“jump up”), from ex- + saliō (“jump, leap”).
definition_en: Feel or express great joy or triumph.

senses.gloss: To rejoice; to be very happy, especially in triumph; to triumph (over).
senses.example: I took a deep breath; a locomotive howled across-the darkness, Mobile-bound. So were we. I took off my shirt and exulted.

examples.text: Tom talked incessantly, exulting and laughing, but his voice was as remote from Jordan and me as the foreign clamour on the sidewalk or the tumult of the elevated overhead.
examples.translation_ko: 톰은 쉴 새 없이 떠들며 의기양양해하고 웃어댔지만, 그의 목소리는 조던과 나에게 인도의 시끄러운 외국인들의 소음이나 머리 위 고가철도의 소란만큼이나 멀게 들렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His heart warms to him when he can bring forward some example of cruelty or meanness, and he exults like an inquisitor at the auto da fé of an heretic when with some forgotten story he can confound the filial piety of the Rev. Robert Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 잔혹함이나 비열함의 사례를 제시할 수 있을 때면 그의 마음이 따뜻해지고, 잊혀진 이야기로 로버트 스트릭랜드 목사의 효성을 당황시킬 수 있을 때면 마치 종교재판관이 이단자의 화형식에서 환호하듯 의기양양해한다.

etymology: From Ancient Greek αὐτός (autós, “self”), metanalyzed from auto- in words such as automatic, autopilot, and automobile.
definition_en: A self-propelled road vehicle.

senses.gloss: Clipping of automatic (of a gearbox/transmission).
senses.example: It's an auto sedan which we picked up from a wholesaler locally.

examples.text: “Auto hit her.
examples.translation_ko: "자동차가 그녀를 쳤어요.

examples.text: His heart warms to him when he can bring forward some example of cruelty or meanness, and he exults like an inquisitor at the auto da fé of an heretic when with some forgotten story he can confound the filial piety of the Rev. Robert Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 잔혹함이나 비열함의 사례를 제시할 수 있을 때면 그의 마음이 따뜻해지고, 잊혀진 이야기로 로버트 스트릭랜드 목사의 효성을 당황시킬 수 있을 때면 마치 종교재판관이 이단자의 화형식에서 환호하듯 의기양양해한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From intimate + -ly.
definition_en: In a close and personal manner.

senses.gloss: In an intimate manner.

examples.text: What would we not give for the reminiscences of someone who had been as intimately acquainted with El Greco as I was with Strickland?
examples.translation_ko: 내가 스트릭랜드를 알았던 것만큼 엘 그레코를 친밀하게 알았던 누군가의 회상록이 있다면 우리가 그것을 얻기 위해 무엇을 아끼겠는가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I knew him more intimately than most: I met him first before ever he became a painter, and I saw him not infrequently during the difficult years he spent in Paris; but I do not suppose I should ever have set down my recollections if the hazards of the war had not taken me to Tahiti.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 대부분의 사람들보다 그를 더 친밀하게 알고 있었다. 그가 화가가 되기 전에 처음 만났고, 그가 파리에서 보낸 힘든 시절 동안 자주 만났다. 하지만 전쟁의 우연한 기회가 나를 타히티로 데려가지 않았다면 내 회상을 기록으로 남기려 하지 않았을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Late Middle English notoryous, from Medieval Latin nōtōrius (“evident, known; famous, well-known; infamous”), from Latin nōtus (“known, recogn...
definition_en: Known or famous for being very bad or unpleasant.

senses.gloss: Of a person or entity: generally or widely known for something negative; infamous.
senses.example: The U.S. is notorious for spending oodles on health care, but health care has little to do with stopping the spread of infectious diseases.

senses.gloss: Of an act, situation, etc.: blameworthy in an obvious and offensive way; blatant, flagrant.
senses.example: [H]e vvas Charg'd upon Oath, vvith having been a Party in a notorious Robbery, Burglary, and Murther, committed ſo and ſo, in ſuch a Place, and on ſuch a Day.

senses.gloss: Generally or widely known; of common knowledge; famous or well-known.
senses.example: Of Cham is the name Chemmis in Aegipt; and Ammon the Idol and Oracle ſo notorious.

examples.text: A celebrated tenor had sung in Italian, and a notorious contralto had sung in jazz, and between the numbers people were doing “stunts” all over the garden, while happy, vacuous bursts of laughter rose toward the summer sky.
examples.translation_ko: 유명한 테너가 이탈리아어로 노래를 불렀고, 악명 높은 콘트랄토가 재즈를 불렀으며, 곡과 곡 사이에는 사람들이 정원 곳곳에서 "묘기"를 부리고 있었고, 행복하고 공허한 웃음소리가 터져 나와 여름 하늘로 치솟았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There, as is notorious, he spent the last years of his life; and there I came across persons who were familiar with him.
examples.translation_ko: 널리 알려진 바와 같이 그는 그곳에서 생의 마지막 몇 년을 보냈고, 나는 그곳에서 그를 잘 알던 사람들을 만났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English superfluous, from Latin superfluus (“superfluous”), from superfluō (“overflow”), from super (“above, more than, over”) + fluō (...
definition_en: Exceeding what is necessary or required.

senses.gloss: In excess of what is required or sufficient.
senses.example: With a full rain suit, carrying an umbrella may be superfluous.

examples.text: That request seemed superfluous when I wrote it.
examples.translation_ko: 그 편지를 쓸 때는 그런 요청이 불필요해 보였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: If they who believe in Strickland’s greatness are right, the personal narratives of such as knew him in the flesh can hardly be superfluous.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드의 위대함을 믿는 사람들이 옳다면, 그를 직접 알았던 사람들의 개인적인 증언이 불필요할 리는 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English aqueynten, acointen, from Old French acointier, from Early Medieval Latin accognitāre, from Late Latin accognitus, past partici...
definition_en: Make someone familiar with something or someone.

senses.gloss: To furnish or give experimental knowledge of; to make (one) know; to make familiar.
senses.example: I think you should acquaint him with the realities of the situation.

senses.gloss: To communicate notice to; to inform; let know.
senses.example: He went directly, sign'd the indentures, was put into the ship, and came over, never writing a line to acquaint his friends what was become of him.

senses.gloss: To familiarize; to accustom.
senses.example:
October 2 1642, Isaac Basire, letter to John Evelyn
What success it may further have I shall acquaint you at my coming over

examples.text: What would we not give for the reminiscences of someone who had been as intimately acquainted with El Greco as I was with Strickland?
examples.translation_ko: 내가 스트릭랜드를 알았던 것만큼 엘 그레코를 친밀하게 알았던 누군가의 회상록이 있다면 우리가 그것을 얻기 위해 무엇을 아끼겠는가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose that he clung to Captain Nichols because he was acquainted with those parts, and it was Captain Nichols who persuaded him that he would be more comfortable in Tahiti.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 니콜스 선장에게 매달린 것은 선장이 그 지역 사정에 밝았기 때문이었고, 타히티에서 더 편안하게 지낼 수 있을 것이라고 설득한 것도 니콜스 선장이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Late Latin praeceptum, form of praecipiō (“to teach”), from Latin prae (“pre-”) + capiō (“take”).
definition_en: A principle or rule of conduct.

senses.gloss: A rule or principle, especially one governing personal conduct.
senses.example: Precept guides, but example draws.

senses.gloss: A written command, especially a demand for payment.
An order issued by one local authority to another specifying the rate of tax to be charged on its behalf.

examples.text: She looked upon venery as the natural occupation for men and women, and was ever ready with precept and example from her own wide experience.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 연애를 남녀의 자연스러운 일로 여겼고, 자신의 풍부한 경험에서 나온 교훈과 실례를 들려주기를 언제나 마다하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I forget who it was that recommended men for their soul’s good to do each day two things they disliked: it was a wise man, and it is a precept that I have followed scrupulously; for every day I have got up and I have gone to bed.
examples.translation_ko: 영혼의 건강을 위해 매일 싫어하는 일 두 가지를 하라고 권한 사람이 누구였는지 기억나지 않지만, 그는 현명한 사람이었고 나는 그 교훈을 철저히 따라왔다. 매일 잠자리에서 일어나고 잠자리에 들었으니까.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English [Term?], from Anglo-Norman, from Old French descipline, from Latin disciplina (“instruction”), from discipulus (“pupil”), influ...
definition_en: A branch of knowledge or a field of study.

senses.gloss: An enforced compliance or control.
senses.example: The masters looked unusually stern, but it was the sternness of thought rather than of discipline.

senses.gloss: A systematic method of obtaining obedience.
senses.example: Endure hardship as discipline; God is treating you as his children. For what children are not disciplined by their father?

senses.gloss: A state of order based on submission to authority.
senses.example: Their wildness lose, and, quitting nature's part, / Obey the rules and discipline of art.

examples.text: An officer’s got to think about discipline.”
examples.translation_ko: "장교라면 규율을 생각해야 하거든."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is a salutary discipline to consider the vast number of books that are written, the fair hopes with which their authors see them published, and the fate which awaits them.
examples.translation_ko: 얼마나 많은 책들이 쓰이는지, 저자들이 얼마나 희망에 부풀어 출간을 바라보는지, 그리고 그 책들을 기다리는 운명이 무엇인지 생각해보는 것은 유익한 수행이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin taedium, from taedēre (“to weary”).
definition_en: A feeling of listlessness and boredom.

senses.gloss: Boredom or tediousness; ennui.
senses.example: Nothing actual ever suits pure expectation and such purity of expectation is a great source of tedium.

examples.text: To avoid the tedium of dining tête-à-tête, to give their servants a rest, because there was no reason to refuse, because they were “owed” a dinner.
examples.translation_ko: 둘만의 지루한 식사를 피하기 위해, 하인들에게 휴식을 주기 위해, 거절할 이유가 없어서, 저녁 식사를 "빚졌기" 때문에.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Heaven knows what pains the author has been at, what bitter experiences he has endured and what heartache suffered, to give some chance reader a few hours’ relaxation or to while away the tedium of a journey.
examples.translation_ko: 하늘만이 아시겠지만, 저자가 얼마나 고생했을지, 얼마나 쓰라린 경험을 견뎠을지, 얼마나 가슴 아파했을지를, 그저 우연한 독자 한 명에게 몇 시간의 휴식을 주거나 여행의 지루함을 달래주기 위해서 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lyftyme, equivalent to life + time. Cognate with Icelandic líftími (“lifetime”). Compare also Saterland Frisian Lieuwendstied, ...
definition_en: The period of time during which someone or something exists.

senses.gloss: The duration of the life of someone or something.
senses.example: comes with a lifetime warranty

senses.gloss: A long period of time.
senses.example: I've been waiting a lifetime for a train.

examples.text: And if I may judge from the reviews, many of these books are well and carefully written; much thought has gone to their composition; to some even has been given the anxious labour of a lifetime.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 서평들로 판단해보건대, 이런 책들 중 많은 수가 잘 쓰이고 정성스럽게 쓰인 것들이다. 구성에 많은 생각이 들어갔고, 어떤 것들에는 평생에 걸친 애타는 노력이 바쳐지기까지 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His father was a spare old man, his hands gnarled after the work of a lifetime, silent and upright; in the evening he read the paper aloud, while his wife and daughter (now married to the captain of a fishing smack), unwilling to lose a moment, bent over their sewing.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 아버지는 마른 노인으로, 평생의 노동으로 거칠어진 손을 가졌으며, 과묵하고 꼿꼿했다. 저녁이면 그는 신문을 소리 내어 읽었고, 그의 아내와 딸(지금은 어선 선장과 결혼했다)은 한 순간도 허비하지 않으려는 듯 바느질에 몰두했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From 1350–1400 Middle English censure, from Old French, from Latin censūra (“censor's office or assessment”), from censēre (“to consider, to assess...
definition_en: Official criticism or disapproval.

senses.gloss: The act of blaming, criticizing, or condemning as wrong; reprehension.
senses.example: Both the censure and the praise were merited.

senses.gloss: Official reprimand.
A judicial or ecclesiastical sentence or reprimand; condemnatory judgment.
senses.example: [E]xcommunication […] being the chief ecclesiastical censure

examples.text: The moral I draw is that the writer should seek his reward in the pleasure of his work and in release from the burden of his thought; and, indifferent to aught else, care nothing for praise or censure, failure or success.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 얻는 교훈은 작가란 자신의 작업에서 오는 기쁨과 사상의 짐에서 벗어나는 해방감에서 보상을 찾아야 한다는 것이다. 그 밖의 모든 것에는 무관심하게, 칭찬이나 비난, 실패나 성공 따위는 아랑곳하지 말고.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Man’s desire for the approval of his fellows is so strong, his dread of their censure so violent, that he himself has brought his enemy within his gates; and it keeps watch over him, vigilant always in the interests of its master to crush any half-formed desire to break away from the herd.
examples.translation_ko: 동료들의 인정을 받고자 하는 인간의 욕망은 너무나 강하고, 그들의 비난을 두려워하는 마음은 너무나 격렬해서, 인간은 스스로 적을 성문 안으로 불러들였다. 그 적은 항상 경계를 늦추지 않고 그를 감시하며, 주인의 이익을 위해 무리에서 벗어나려는 어떤 미약한 욕망이라도 짓밟으려 한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English eldre, from Old English eldra, yldra, ieldra, from Proto-Germanic *alþizô. The vowel change from a to e triggered by the follow...
definition_en: A person who is older than another.

senses.gloss: comparative degree of old: older, greater than another in age or seniority.
senses.example: My elder brother just got married.

examples.text: The only painter that interested him who was at all unexpected was Brueghel the Elder.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 관심을 보인 화가 중에서 다소 뜻밖이었던 유일한 인물은 브뤼헐 대부였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Of their elders some, by imitating the antics of youth, strive to persuade themselves that their day is not yet over; they shout with the lustiest, but the war cry sounds hollow in their mouth; they are like poor wantons attempting with pencil, paint and powder, with shrill gaiety, to recover the illusion of their spring.
examples.translation_ko: 기성세대 중 일부는 젊은이들의 우스꽝스러운 행동을 흉내 내며 자신들의 시대가 아직 끝나지 않았다고 스스로를 설득하려 애쓴다. 그들은 가장 힘차게 외치지만, 그 전투 함성은 그들의 입에서 공허하게 울릴 뿐이다. 마치 불쌍한 창녀들이 연필과 물감과 분칠로, 날카로운 쾌활함으로 자신들의 봄날이라는 환상을 되찾으려 애쓰는 것과 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English poudre, pouder, pouldre, borrowed from Old French poudre, poldre, puldre, from Latin pulverem, accusative singular of Latin pul...
definition_en: A dry powder or powdered substance.

senses.gloss: The fine particles which are the result of reducing a dry substance by pounding, grinding, or triturating, or the result of decay; dust.
senses.example: Let them stop fretting about vegetables denied by the weather and eat chilli powder. Just explain to them that they really shouldn’t think about spiralising it, because that doesn’t work.

senses.gloss: A mixture of fine dry, sweet-smelling particles applied to the face or other body parts, to reduce shine or to alleviate chaffing.
senses.example: She was redolent of violet sachet powder, and had warm, soft, white hands, but she danced divinely, moving as smoothly as the tide coming in.

senses.gloss: An explosive mixture used in gunnery, blasting, etc.; gunpowder.
senses.example: Tut, tut, good enough to toſſe: foode for Powder, foode for Powder: they'll fill a Pit, as well as better: tuſh man, mortall men, mortall men.

examples.text: She had dried her eyes and powdered her nose.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 눈물을 닦고 코에 분을 발랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Of their elders some, by imitating the antics of youth, strive to persuade themselves that their day is not yet over; they shout with the lustiest, but the war cry sounds hollow in their mouth; they are like poor wantons attempting with pencil, paint and powder, with shrill gaiety, to recover the illusion of their spring.
examples.translation_ko: 기성세대 중 일부는 젊은이들의 우스꽝스러운 행동을 흉내 내며 자신들의 시대가 아직 끝나지 않았다고 스스로를 설득하려 애쓴다. 그들은 가장 힘차게 외치지만, 그 전투 함성은 그들의 입에서 공허하게 울릴 뿐이다. 마치 불쌍한 창녀들이 연필과 물감과 분칠로, 날카로운 쾌활함으로 자신들의 봄날이라는 환상을 되찾으려 애쓰는 것과 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English mokkery, from Anglo-Norman mokerie, mokery and Middle French mocquerie, moquerie, from moquer, moker (“to mock”) + -erie (“-ery...
definition_en: A joke or act intended to mock or ridicule someone.

senses.gloss: The action of mocking; ridicule, derision.
Something so lacking in necessary qualities as to inspire ridicule; a laughing-stock.
Something insultingly imitative; an offensively futile action, gesture etc.

examples.text: In their chastened smile is an indulgent mockery.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 차분한 미소에는 관대한 조롱이 담겨 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I seemed to see in them a hint of mockery; it was true that Stroeve had the head of the husband who is deceived.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 눈빛에서 조롱의 기색을 엿볼 수 있는 것 같았다. 스트루브는 정말로 속임을 당하는 남편의 얼굴을 하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English berer, berere, from Old English berere (attested in Old English wæterberere (“waterbearer”)), equivalent to bear + -er.
definition_en: A person who carries or holds something.

senses.gloss: One who, or that which, bears, sustains, or carries.
senses.example: The slightest manifestation of sympathy or justice toward a person of color, was denounced as abolitionism; and the name of abolitionist, subjected its bearer to frightful liabilities.

senses.gloss: Someone who helps carry the coffin or a dead body during a funeral procession.
senses.example: The deep shadows of the porch swallowed up priest, corpse and bearers […]

senses.gloss: One who possesses a cheque, bond, or other notes promising payment.
senses.example: I promise to pay the bearer on demand.

examples.text: It is fitting that the bearer of important tidings should be rewarded.
examples.translation_ko: 중요한 소식을 전하는 자는 보상을 받는 것이 마땅하오.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They remember that they too trod down a sated generation, with just such clamor and with just such scorn, and they foresee that these brave torch-bearers will presently yield their place also.
examples.translation_ko: 그들도 한때 바로 그런 소란과 바로 그런 경멸로 물린 세대를 짓밟았음을 기억하고, 이 용감한 횃불 든 자들도 머지않아 자신들의 자리를 내주게 되리라는 것을 내다본다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From backward + -s. See also -s (“used in the formation of certain adverbs: backwards, downwards, inwards, etc.”).
definition_en: Moving or directed in the opposite direction from which something is normally done.

senses.gloss: Synonym of backward; see usage notes there.

examples.text: The pendulum swings backwards and forwards.
examples.translation_ko: 진자는 앞뒤로 흔들린다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Stroeve hid his face in his hands and swayed backwards and forwards, groaning.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 두 손으로 얼굴을 가리고 앞뒤로 몸을 흔들며 신음했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From forward + -s (adverbial suffix).
definition_en: Moving or directed forward.

senses.gloss: Synonym of forward (most senses).

examples.text: The pendulum swings backwards and forwards.
examples.translation_ko: 진자는 앞뒤로 흔들린다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Stroeve hid his face in his hands and swayed backwards and forwards, groaning.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 두 손으로 얼굴을 가리고 앞뒤로 몸을 흔들며 신음했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *tréyes
From Middle English travelen (“to make a laborious journey, travel”) from Middle Scots travailen (“to toil, work, travel”), alter...
definition_en: To go from one place to another.

senses.gloss: To be on a journey, often for pleasure or business and with luggage; to go from one place to another.
senses.example: John seems to spend as much time travelling as he does in the office.

senses.gloss: To pass from one place to another; to move or transmit.
senses.example: Soundwaves can travel through water.

senses.gloss: To move illegally by walking or running without dribbling the ball.

examples.text: The circle is ever travelled anew.
examples.translation_ko: 원은 언제나 새롭게 그려진다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They love to travel and they love to gossip, but they do not care to walk, and for weeks at a time
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 여행을 좋아하고 수다떨기를 좋아하지만, 걷기는 싫어해서 몇 주씩
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English onew, of newe, from Old English of niowe. By surface analysis, a- (“of, from”) + new.
definition_en: Again or once more.

senses.gloss: Again, once more; afresh, in a new way, newly.
senses.example: Each morning, opportunity—like the sun—dawns anew.

examples.text: The circle is ever travelled anew.
examples.translation_ko: 원은 언제나 새롭게 그려진다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She settled in two tiny rooms in Westminster, and faced the world anew.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 웨스트민스터의 작은 방 두 칸에 정착하여 세상을 새롭게 맞섰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Anglo-Norman survivre, Old French survivre, from Late Latin supervivere (“to outlive”), from Latin super (“over”) + vivere (“to live”), akin t...
definition_en: To remain alive or in existence.

senses.gloss: Of a person, to continue to live; to remain alive.
senses.example: Whether by a miracle or by good luck, all twenty passengers survived.

senses.gloss: Of an object or concept, to continue to exist.
senses.example: This town has been hit by two hurricanes, but it survives.

senses.gloss: To live past (a life-threatening event)
senses.example: Whether by a miracle or by good luck, all twenty passengers survived the crash.

examples.text: A wafer of a moon was shining over Gatsby’s house, making the night fine as before, and surviving the laughter and the sound of his still glowing garden.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비의 집 위로 얇은 초승달이 빛나고 있었고, 밤을 전처럼 아름답게 만들며, 아직도 환하게 빛나는 그의 정원에서 흘러나오는 웃음소리와 소음을 견뎌내고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Sometimes a man survives a considerable time from an era in which he had his place into one which is strange to him, and then the curious are offered one of the most singular spectacles in the human comedy.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 어떤 사람이 자신의 자리가 있던 시대에서 낯선 시대로 상당한 시간을 버텨내며 살아남기도 하는데, 그러면 호기심 많은 이들에게 인간 희극에서 가장 기이한 광경 중 하나가 제공된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French poème, from Latin poēma, from Ancient Greek ποίημα (poíēma), from ποιέω (poiéō, “I make”). Displaced native Old English lēoþ.
definition_en: A piece of writing that has a creative or imaginative style.

senses.gloss: A literary piece written in verse.
A piece of writing in the tradition of poetry, an instance of poetry.
A piece of poetic writing, that is with an intensity or depth of expression or inspiration greater than is usual in prose.

examples.text: But the odes of Keats and of Wordsworth, a poem or two by Coleridge, a few more by Shelley, discovered vast realms of the spirit that none had explored before.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 키츠와 워즈워스의 송가들, 콜리지의 시 한두 편, 셸리의 몇 편 더 많은 작품들은 그 누구도 전에 탐험해보지 못한 정신의 광대한 영역들을 발견해냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The books he liked were queer; sometimes I would find him poring over the poems of Mallarme, and he read them as a child reads, forming the words with his lips, and I wondered what strange emotion he got from those subtle cadences and obscure phrases; and again I found him absorbed in the detective novels of Gaboriau.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 좋아하는 책들은 기이했다. 때로는 말라르메의 시집을 열심히 들여다보고 있는 그를 발견하곤 했는데, 그는 아이가 읽듯 입술로 단어를 따라 읽었고, 나는 그가 그 미묘한 운율과 모호한 구절들에서 어떤 기묘한 감정을 얻는지 궁금했다. 또 어떤 때는 가보리오의 탐정소설에 빠져 있는 그를 발견하기도 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English rewme, realme, reaume, from Old French reaume, realme, reialme (“kingdom”), of unclear origins. A postulated *rēgālimen (“domai...
definition_en: A kingdom or domain ruled by a monarch.

senses.gloss: An otherworldly dimension or domain — magical, ethereal, or otherwise — usually ruled or created by a mystical character.
The spiritual state of which God is the head; the Kingdom of Heaven.
A territory or state, as ruled by an absolute authority, especially by a king; a kingdom.
senses.example:
1913, Leslie Alexander Toke, Catholic Encyclopedia, "St. Dunstan",
Then seeing his life was threatened he fled the realm and crossed over to Flanders, […]

examples.text: Nor is it vouchsafed to man in the flesh to know aught that more nearly suggests the approach to the golden realms of fancy than the approach to Tahiti.
examples.translation_ko: 육신을 지닌 인간에게는 환상의 황금 영역으로 다가가는 것보다 더 가깝게 느껴지는 것을 아는 것이 허락되지 않으니, 그것은 바로 타히티로 다가가는 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But the odes of Keats and of Wordsworth, a poem or two by Coleridge, a few more by Shelley, discovered vast realms of the spirit that none had explored before.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 키츠와 워즈워스의 송가들, 콜리지의 시 한두 편, 셸리의 몇 편 더 많은 작품들은 그 누구도 전에 탐험해보지 못한 정신의 광대한 영역들을 발견해냈다.

etymology: From Middle French explorer, from Latin explōrāre (“to investigate, search out”), itself said to be originally a hunters' term meaning "to set up a...
definition_en: To investigate or examine something.

senses.gloss: To seek for something or after someone.
To examine or investigate something systematically.
senses.example: The committee has been exploring alternative solutions to the problem at hand.

senses.gloss: To travel somewhere in search of discovery.
senses.example: It was around that time that the expedition began exploring the Arctic Circle.

examples.text: But the odes of Keats and of Wordsworth, a poem or two by Coleridge, a few more by Shelley, discovered vast realms of the spirit that none had explored before.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 키츠와 워즈워스의 송가들, 콜리지의 시 한두 편, 셸리의 몇 편 더 많은 작품들은 그 누구도 전에 탐험해보지 못한 정신의 광대한 영역들을 발견해냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Now that his influence has so enormously affected modern painting, now that others have charted the country which he was among the first to explore, Strickland’s pictures, seen for the first time, would find the mind more prepared for them; but it must be remembered that I had never seen anything of the sort.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 그의 영향력이 현대 회화에 엄청난 변화를 가져왔고, 이제 다른 화가들이 그가 최초로 탐험한 영역을 지도로 그려놓은 지금, 스트릭랜드의 그림들을 처음 보는 사람이라면 더 준비된 마음으로 받아들일 수 있을 것이다. 하지만 당시 나는 그런 류의 작품을 본 적이 전혀 없었다는 점을 기억해야 한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From desultory + -ly.
definition_en: In a desultory manner; without purpose or direction.

senses.gloss: In a desultory fashion.
senses.example: She had been working desultorily on her book for several years.

examples.text: I have read desultorily the writings of the younger generation.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 젊은 세대의 글들을 두서없이 읽어왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I read a page here and there, and made acquaintance with a great many authors whom I was content to know thus desultorily.
examples.translation_ko: 여기저기서 한 페이지씩 읽어가며, 이런 식으로 두서없이 알게 되는 것으로 만족하는 수많은 작가들과 친분을 쌓았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Pole + -ish. Doublet of Poylish.
definition_en: A person from Poland.

senses.gloss: Of, from or native to Poland, or relating to the Polish language.
senses.example: A far-right Polish MP has extinguished candles on a menorah lit for Hanukah in Poland’s parliament, disrupting proceedings before a planned vote of confidence in the new government.

examples.text: I admire their polish—their youth is already so accomplished that it seems absurd to speak of promise—I marvel at the felicity of their style; but with all their copiousness (their vocabulary suggests that they fingered Roget’s Thesaurus in their cradles)
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그들의 세련됨을 감탄한다—그들의 젊음은 이미 너무나 완성되어 있어서 장래성을 운운하는 것조차 우스꽝스러워 보인다—나는 그들 문체의 적절함에 경탄한다. 하지만 그 모든 풍부함에도 불구하고 (그들의 어휘력을 보면 요람에서부터 로제의 유의어 사전을 만지작거렸던 것 같다)
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a sudden vision of her standing in the kitchen—it was hardly larger than a cupboard—washing the plates and glasses, the forks and spoons, giving the knives a rapid polish on the knife-board; and then putting everything away, giving the sink a scrub, and hanging the dish-cloth up to dry—it was there still, a gray torn rag; then looking round to see that everything was clean and nice.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 갑자기 그녀가 부엌에 서 있는 모습이 눈에 떠올랐다—찬장보다 조금 클 뿐인 그 부엌에서 접시와 잔들, 포크와 숟가락을 씻고, 칼판에 칼들을 재빠르게 닦아내고, 그런 다음 모든 것을 제자리에 정리하고, 개수대를 문지르고, 행주를 걸어 말리는—그 행주는 아직도 거기 있었다, 회색빛 너덜너덜한 걸레가—그리고 나서 모든 것이 깨끗하고 말끔한지 둘러보는 모습이.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English stomak, from Old French estomac, from Latin stomachus, from Ancient Greek στόμαχος (stómakhos), from στόμα (stóma, “mouth”).
La...
definition_en: To feel or experience nausea.

senses.gloss: An organ in animals that stores food in the process of digestion.
senses.example: Our stomachs and livers have an enzyme known as alcohol dehydrogenase that breaks down ethanol to make it less toxic for our bodies, said Atlanta gastroenterologist Dr. Preston Stewart.

senses.gloss: The belly.
senses.example: Why did you hit me in the stomach?

senses.gloss: Pride, haughtiness.
senses.example: This sort of crying[…] proceeding from pride, obstinacy, and stomach, the will, where the fault lies, must be bent.

examples.text: I could not stomach his weakness, and he saw my disapproval.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그의 나약함이 역겨웠고, 그는 내 못마땅함을 알아챘다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: they say nothing to me: to my mind they know too much and feel too obviously; I cannot stomach the heartiness with which they slap me on the back or the emotion with which they hurl themselves on my bosom; their passion seems to me a little anaemic and their dreams a trifle dull.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 내게 아무것도 말해주지 않는다. 내가 보기에 그들은 너무 많이 알고 너무 뻔하게 느낀다. 나는 그들이 내 등을 두드리는 그 호탕함이나 내 품에 몸을 던지는 그 감정을 견딜 수 없다. 그들의 열정은 내게 다소 빈혈기가 있어 보이고 그들의 꿈은 조금 따분해 보인다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From hearty + -ness.
definition_en: The quality of being hearty or robust.

senses.gloss: The quality of being hearty.

examples.text: But at the moment he was all heartiness and good-fellowship.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그 순간 그는 온통 다정함과 친근함 그 자체였다.

definition_en: Lacking sufficient red blood cells or hemoglobin.

senses.gloss: Alternative spelling of anemic.
senses.example: The educated man of the twentieth century is not anaemic, languishing in a washed-out, wan vitality.

examples.text: He was a blond, spiritless man, anaemic, and faintly handsome.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 금발에 기운 없는 남자로, 빈혈기가 있으면서도 어딘지 잘생긴 구석이 있었다.

etymology: From Middle English singularite, from Old French singularité, from Late Latin singulāritās (“singleness”), from Latin singulāris (“single”). By sur...
definition_en: A point of infinite density or a hypothetical future event that brings about profound change.

senses.gloss: The state of being singular, distinct, peculiar, uncommon or unusual.
senses.example: A sub-cultural style or artifact, when adopted by the mainstream, loses its singularity. Once bell-bottoms became fashionable they were no longer a "gay style."

senses.gloss: An unusual action or behaviour.
A point where all parallel lines meet.

examples.text: It is long since I frequented it, and if the novels that describe its present singularities are accurate much in it is now changed.
examples.translation_ko: 그곳을 드나든 지 오래되었고, 현재의 특이한 모습들을 묘사한 소설들이 정확하다면 많은 것이 지금은 바뀌었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Until long habit has blunted the sensibility, there is something disconcerting to the writer in the instinct which causes him to take an interest in the singularities of human nature so absorbing that his moral sense is powerless against it.
examples.translation_ko: 오랜 습관이 감수성을 무디게 만들기 전까지는, 인간 본성의 특이한 면에 빠져들어 도덕적 감각마저 무력하게 만드는 본능이 작가에게는 당황스러운 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English crude, borrowed from Latin crūdus (“raw, bloody, uncooked, undigested, crude”). Doublet of crudo, from Italian. Cognate with Ol...
definition_en: Not refined or processed.

senses.gloss: In a natural, untreated state.
senses.example: crude oil

senses.gloss: Characterized by simplicity, especially something not carefully or expertly made.
senses.example: a crude shelter

senses.gloss: Lacking concealing elements.
senses.example: a crude truth

examples.text: The colour seemed to me extraordinarily crude.
examples.translation_ko: 색채가 내게는 극도로 조잡해 보였다.

examples.text: I do not believe that there was in that genteel Bohemia an intensive culture of chastity, but I do not remember so crude a promiscuity as seems to be practised in the present day.

definition_en: Having or showing the quality of being hypocritical.

senses.gloss: Characterized by hypocrisy or being a hypocrite.

examples.text: “Of course it would be hypocritical for me to pretend that I regret what Abraham did.
examples.translation_ko: "물론 아브라함이 한 일을 후회하지 않는다고 가식을 부리는 것은 위선일 것이다.

examples.text: We did not think it hypocritical to draw over our vagaries the curtain of a decent silence.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 자신의 방탕함을 품위 있는 침묵의 장막으로 가리는 것을 위선이라고 생각하지 않았다.

etymology: From Middle English spade, from Old English spada, spade, spadu (“spade”), from Proto-Germanic *spadô. Doublet of spatha, spathe, and épée.
definition_en: A tool used for digging or moving soil.

senses.gloss: A garden tool with a handle and a flat blade for digging. Not to be confused with a shovel which is used for moving earth or other materials.
senses.example: "[...] And not a single spade has gone in the ground - not a single mile of track built."

senses.gloss: A cutting instrument used in flensing a whale.
A device for terminating an electrical conductor resembling a small spade.

examples.text: Occasionally a line of grey cars crawls along an invisible track, gives out a ghastly creak, and comes to rest, and immediately the ash-grey men swarm up with leaden spades and stir up an impenetrable cloud, which screens their obscure operations from your sight.
examples.translation_ko: 때때로 회색 화차들이 한 줄로 보이지 않는 선로를 따라 기어가다가 섬뜩한 삐걱거리는 소리를 내며 멈춰 선다. 그러면 즉시 재빛 회색 사내들이 납덩이 같은 삽을 들고 우르르 몰려와 뚫을 수 없는 먼지 구름을 일으켜, 그들의 모호한 작업을 시야에서 가려버린다.

examples.text: The spade was not invariably called a bloody shovel.
examples.translation_ko: 삽을 언제나 빌어먹을 삽이라고 부르지는 않았다.

etymology: Borrowed from Latin excursio (“a running out, an inroad, invasion, a setting out, beginning of a speech”), from excurrere (“to run out”), from ex (...
definition_en: A short trip or journey for pleasure.

senses.gloss: A brief recreational trip; a journey out of the usual way.
senses.example: While driving home I took an excursion and saw some deer.

senses.gloss: A field trip.
A wandering from the main subject: a digression.
senses.example: Now all his ponderings, however excursive, wheeled round Isabel as their center; and back to her they came again from every excursion; and again derived some new, small germs for wonderment.

examples.text: When I came back from the East last autumn I felt that I wanted the world to be in uniform and at a sort of moral attention forever; I wanted no more riotous excursions with privileged glimpses into the human heart.
examples.translation_ko: 지난 가을 동부에서 돌아왔을 때 나는 세상이 영원히 제복을 입고 도덕적 차렷 자세를 취하기를 바랐다. 인간의 마음을 특권적으로 엿보는 소란스러운 모험은 더 이상 원하지 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I lived near Victoria Station, and I recall long excursions by bus to the hospitable houses of the literary.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 빅토리아 역 근처에 살았는데, 문인들의 호의적인 집들을 버스로 찾아가던 긴 여행들이 기억난다.

etymology: From Middle English ussher, uscher, usscher, from Anglo-Norman usser and Old French ussier, uissier (“porter, doorman”) (compare French huissier), ...
definition_en: To introduce or escort someone formally.

senses.gloss: A person, in a church, cinema etc., who escorts people to their seats.
A male escort at a wedding.
A doorkeeper in a courtroom.

examples.text: In my timidity I wandered up and down the street while I screwed up my courage to ring the bell; and then, sick with apprehension, was ushered into an airless room full of people.
examples.translation_ko: 소심한 나는 벨을 누를 용기를 내면서 거리를 이리저리 헤맸고, 그러다가 불안에 떨며 사람들로 가득한 답답한 방으로 안내되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When I was ushered into the drawing-room I found that Mrs. Strickland had a visitor, and when I discovered who he was, I guessed that I had been asked to come at just that time not without intention.
