etymology: From air + -less.
definition_en: Lacking air or having little air.

senses.gloss: Lacking or being without air.
Lacking air circulation.
With air that is stale.

examples.text: They were dark and airless.
examples.translation_ko: 계단은 어둡고 공기가 탁했다.

etymology: From excessive + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is done or experienced to a great degree.

senses.gloss: To an excessive degree.
senses.example: The application form was excessively complicated.

senses.gloss: In excess.
senses.example: He smoked excessively.

examples.text: To myself my entrance seemed excessively awkward.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 보기에 내 등장은 지나치게 어색해 보였다.

examples.text: I was introduced to this celebrated person after that one, and the kind words they said about my book made me excessively uncomfortable.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이런저런 유명인사들에게 소개되었고, 그들이 내 책에 대해 해준 친절한 말들이 나를 몹시 불편하게 만들었다.

 *gʷṓws

definition_en: A yellowish fatty substance used for cooking and as a spread.

senses.gloss: A soft, fatty foodstuff made by churning the cream of milk (generally cow's milk).
Any of various foodstuffs made from other foods or oils, similar in consistency to, eaten like or intended as a substitute for butter (preceded by the name of the food used to make it).

senses.gloss: Any of various substances made from other (especially plant-based) oils or fats, used in moisturizers, cosmetics, etc.
senses.example: Butters such as cocoa, illippe, kokum, mango, murumuru, sal (shorea) and shea occur naturally and are obtained directly from the plant.

examples.text: I never ceased to be fascinated by their persistence in eating buttered toast with their gloves on, and I observed with admiration the unconcern with which they wiped their fingers on their chair when they thought no one was looking.

definition_en: Protective clothing or equipment worn to prevent injury.

senses.gloss: British standard spelling of armor.

examples.text: I longed to pierce his armour of complete indifference.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I have a recollection of large, unbending women with great noses and rapacious eyes, who wore their clothes as though they were armour; and of little, mouse-like spinsters, with soft voices and a shrewd glance.
examples.translation_ko: 커다란 코와 탐욕스러운 눈을 가진 키 크고 완고한 여자들이 기억난다. 그들은 옷을 마치 갑옷처럼 입고 다녔다. 그리고 부드러운 목소리와 예리한 눈빛을 가진 쥐 같은 작은 노처녀들도 있었다.

definition_en: To attract and hold someone's attention strongly.

senses.gloss: To evoke an intense interest or attraction in someone.
senses.example: The flickering TV fascinated the cat.

senses.gloss: To make someone hold motionless; to spellbind.
senses.example: We were fascinated by the potter's skill.

senses.gloss: To be irresistibly charming or attractive to.
senses.example: Her gait fascinates all men.

examples.text: You feel I know not what primitive force which repels and yet fascinates you.
examples.translation_ko: 당신은 밀어내면서도 동시에 매혹시키는, 형언할 수 없는 원시적 힘을 느낀다.

definition_en: A covering for the hand, typically made of leather or fabric.

senses.gloss: An item of clothing, covering all or part of the hand and fingers, but usually allowing independent movement of the fingers.
senses.example: I wore gloves to keep my hands warm.

senses.gloss: A baseball mitt.
The ability to catch a hit ball.
senses.example: Frederico had a great glove, but he couldn't hit a curveball, so he never broke into the pros.

etymology: From Middle French revenge, a derivation from revenger, from Old French revengier (possibly influenced by Old Occitan revènge (“revenge, comeback”)...
definition_en: A feeling of hatred and a desire to hurt someone who has wronged you.

senses.gloss: Any form of personal, retaliatory action against an individual, institution, or group for some alleged or perceived harm or injustice.
senses.example: Indifference is the sweetest revenge.

senses.gloss: A win by a previous loser.
senses.example: “I'm through with all pawn-games,” I laughed. “Come, let us have a game of lansquenet. Either I will take a farewell fall out of you or you will have your sevenfold revenge”.

examples.text: His life was strangely divorced from material things, and it was as though his body at times wreaked a fearful revenge on his spirit.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 삶은 물질적인 것들과 이상하게 분리되어 있었고, 마치 그의 육체가 때때로 그의 정신에 무서운 복수를 가하는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It must have been bad for the furniture, but I suppose the hostess took her revenge on the furniture of her friends when, in turn, she visited them.
examples.translation_ko: 가구에는 좋지 않았겠지만, 안주인도 차례로 친구들을 방문할 때 그들의 가구로 복수를 했으리라 생각한다.

etymology: First appears c. 1581. Origin uncertain, probably literally "little poorly dressed woman," formed from doue, "poorly dressed woman". Possibly also ...
definition_en: Unfashionably dressed or looking old-fashioned.

senses.gloss: Plain and unfashionable in style or dress.
Lacking stylishness or neatness; shabby.
senses.example: [...she was] a perfect saint amongst women, but so dreadfully dowdy that she reminded one of a badly bound hymn-book.

examples.text: Her gown was dowdy and expensive.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 드레스는 촌스럽고 비쌌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Some of them were dressed fashionably, and they said they couldn’t for the life of them see why you should be dowdy just because you had written a novel; if you had a neat figure you might as well make the most of it, and a smart shoe on a small foot had never prevented an editor from taking your “stuff.”
examples.translation_ko: 그들 중 일부는 멋지게 차려입고 다녔는데, 소설을 썼다고 해서 왜 촌스럽게 입어야 하는지 도무지 모르겠다고 말했다. 몸매가 좋다면 최대한 살려야 하고, 작은 발에 신은 멋진 구두가 편집자로 하여금 당신의 '작품'을 거절하게 만든 적은 없다는 것이었다.

definition_en: A person who edits written material.

senses.gloss: A person who edits or makes changes to documents.
A copy editor.
A person who edited a specific document.
senses.example: John Johnson wrote this term paper and the editor was Joan Johnson.

examples.text: Then we would talk of agents and the offers they had obtained for us; of editors and the sort of contributions they welcomed, how much they paid a thousand, and whether they paid promptly or otherwise.

etymology: From Middle French epigramme, from Latin epigramma, from Ancient Greek ἐπίγραμμα (epígramma, “inscription”).
definition_en: A short witty saying or phrase.

senses.gloss: An inscription in stone.
A brief but witty saying.
A short, witty or pithy poem.

examples.text: This isn’t just an epigram—life is much more successfully looked at from a single window, after all.
examples.translation_ko: 이것은 단순한 경구가 아니다—결국 인생은 하나의 창문에서 바라볼 때 훨씬 더 성공적으로 보이는 법이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: In those days conversation was still cultivated as an art; a neat repartee was more highly valued than the crackling of thorns under a pot; and the epigram, not yet a mechanical appliance by which the dull may achieve a semblance of wit, gave sprightliness to the small talk of the urbane.
examples.translation_ko: 그 시절에는 대화가 여전히 하나의 예술로 여겨졌다. 기지 있는 응답은 가시나무가 솥 밑에서 타닥거리는 소리보다 더 높이 평가되었고, 아직 둔한 자들이 재치 있는 척하는 기계적 장치가 되지 않은 경구는 교양인들의 담소에 활기를 불어넣었다.

definition_en: Relating to machines or machinery.

senses.gloss: Characteristic of someone who does manual labour for a living; coarse, vulgar.
senses.example: all manner of silks were already become so vile and abject, that was any man seene to weare them, he was presently judged to be some countrie fellow, or mechanicall man.

senses.gloss: Related to mechanics (the design and construction of machines).

etymology: A variant of urban + -ane (a variant of -an (suffix meaning ‘of or pertaining to’ forming adjectives)). Urban is borrowed from Middle French urbain...
definition_en: Having a sophisticated and cultured air.

senses.gloss: Of a person (usually a man): having refined manners; courteous, polite, suave.
senses.example: Our people must have some control over our destiny," reasons Wilma Muth, an urbane woman who serves as Inyo County supervisor.

senses.gloss: Of an act, expression, etc.: suited to a person of refined manners; elegant, sophisticated.
senses.example: To guests, a servant should not sour-faced by, / But do the honours with a mind urbane.

senses.gloss: Obsolete spelling of urban (“of, pertaining to, or characteristic of a city or town, or life in such a place; living in a city or town; having authority or jurisdiction over a city or town”).
senses.example: Raising, through just gradation, savage life / To rustic, and the rustic to urbane.

examples.text: The schooners moored to the quay are trim and neat, the little town along the bay is white and urbane, and the flamboyants, scarlet against the blue sky, flaunt their colour like a cry of passion.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In those days conversation was still cultivated as an art; a neat repartee was more highly valued than the crackling of thorns under a pot; and the epigram, not yet a mechanical appliance by which the dull may achieve a semblance of wit, gave sprightliness to the small talk of the urbane.
examples.translation_ko: 그 시절에는 대화가 여전히 하나의 예술로 여겨졌다. 기지 있는 응답은 가시나무가 솥 밑에서 타닥거리는 소리보다 더 높이 평가되었고, 아직 둔한 자들이 재치 있는 척하는 기계적 장치가 되지 않은 경구는 교양인들의 담소에 활기를 불어넣었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From scintillate + -ion.
definition_en: A brief flash of light, especially one caused by the interaction between a particle and a material.

senses.gloss: A flash of light; a spark.
The twinkling of a star or other celestial body caused by turbulence in the Earth's atmosphere.
The flash of light produced by something (especially a phosphor) when it absorbs ionizing radiation.

examples.text: It is sad that I can remember nothing of all this scintillation.
examples.translation_ko: 이 모든 번뜩이는 대화를 하나도 기억하지 못한다는 것이 안타깝다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Perhaps Charles Strickland was dull judged by a standard that demanded above all things verbal scintillation; but his intelligence was adequate to his surroundings, and that is a passport, not only to reasonable success, but still more to happiness.
examples.translation_ko: 무엇보다 언변의 번뜩임을 요구하는 기준으로 판단한다면 찰스 스트릭랜드는 둔했을지도 모르지만, 그의 지성은 자신의 환경에 충분했고, 그것은 합리적인 성공뿐만 아니라 더 나아가 행복으로 가는 통행증이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Made or designed in a particular style.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of fashion

examples.text: By God, I may be old-fashioned in my ideas, but women run around too much these days to suit me.
examples.translation_ko: 맙소사, 내 생각이 구식일지도 모르지만, 요즘 여자들은 내 성에 차지 않을 정도로 너무 돌아다닌다고.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Some were modern and some were old-fashioned.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 것들은 현대적이었고 어떤 것들은 구식이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin agēns, present active participle of agere (“to drive, lead, conduct, manage, perform, do”).
definition_en: A person who acts on behalf of another.

senses.gloss: One who exerts power, or has the power to act.
One who acts for, or in the place of, another (the principal), by that person's authority; someone entrusted to act on behalf of or in behalf of another, such as to transact business for them.
A person who looks for work for another person and brokers a deal between the hiree and hirer.

examples.text: Then we would talk of agents and the offers they had obtained for us; of editors and the sort of contributions they welcomed, how much they paid a thousand, and whether they paid promptly or otherwise.
examples.translation_ko: 그러면 우리는 에이전트들과 그들이 우리를 위해 따낸 제안들에 대해, 편집자들과 그들이 환영하는 기고문의 종류, 천 단어당 얼마를 지불하는지, 그리고 그들이 즉시 지불하는지 아닌지에 대해 이야기하곤 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: To them he was no more than a beach-comber in constant need of money, remarkable only for the peculiarity that he painted pictures which seemed to them absurd; and it was not till he had been dead for some years and agents came from the dealers in Paris and Berlin to look for any pictures which might still remain on the island, that they had any idea that among them had dwelt a man of consequence.
examples.translation_ko: 그들에게 그는 늘 돈이 궁한 해변 부랑자에 불과했고, 다만 그들이 보기에 터무니없어 보이는 그림을 그린다는 기이함으로만 주목받았을 뿐이었다. 그가 죽은 지 몇 년이 지나 파리와 베를린의 화상들이 보낸 중개인들이 섬에 남아 있을지도 모를 그림들을 찾으러 왔을 때서야, 그들은 자신들 사이에 중요한 인물이 살았었다는 사실을 깨달았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From prompt + -ly.
definition_en: Done or happening quickly and efficiently.

senses.gloss: Both soon and quickly.
senses.example: […] the ducklings nestled down inside it and promptly fell asleep.

senses.gloss: Exactly at a specific time.
senses.example: The sale will begin on January 28th, promptly at 9 a.m.

examples.text: “Nonsense,” I answered promptly; “I don’t disapprove of the boa-constrictor; on the contrary, I’m interested in his mental processes.”
examples.translation_ko: "말도 안 되는 소리군요." 나는 즉시 대답했다. "나는 보아뱀을 못마땅하게 여기지 않습니다. 오히려 그놈의 정신적 과정에 흥미를 느끼죠."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then we would talk of agents and the offers they had obtained for us; of editors and the sort of contributions they welcomed, how much they paid a thousand, and whether they paid promptly or otherwise.
examples.translation_ko: 그러면 우리는 에이전트들과 그들이 우리를 위해 따낸 제안들에 대해, 편집자들과 그들이 환영하는 기고문의 종류, 천 단어당 얼마를 지불하는지, 그리고 그들이 즉시 지불하는지 아닌지에 대해 이야기하곤 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Learned borrowing from Latin decōrum, neuter form of decōrus (“proper, decent”).
definition_en: Proper behavior or manners.

senses.gloss: Appropriate social behavior.
senses.example: It was sort of a finishing school. You know, to teach proper social decorum and so on and so forth.

senses.gloss: A convention of social behavior.

examples.text: Her husband played his part with decorum.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 남편은 품위 있게 자신의 역할을 해냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She held their weakness for lions in good-humoured contempt, but played to them her part of the distinguished woman of letters with decorum.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 유명인사들에 대한 그들의 약점을 선량한 경멸로 바라보았지만, 품위 있는 여류 문인이라는 자신의 역할을 예의에 맞게 연기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cathedral, chathedral, cathiderall, from Old French [Term?], from Latin cathedrālis, from cathedra + -ālis, from Ancient Greek ...
definition_en: A large and impressive church, typically the main church of a diocese.

senses.gloss: Relating to the office of a bishop or an archbishop.

examples.text: When I arrived, a little late, because in my fear of being too early I had walked three times round the cathedral, I found the party already complete.
examples.translation_ko: 너무 일찍 도착할까 봐 대성당 주위를 세 바퀴나 돌았기 때문에 조금 늦게 도착했을 때, 일행은 이미 다 모여 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She had a flat in Westminster, overlooking the unfinished cathedral, and because we lived in the same neighbourhood we felt friendly disposed to one another.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 웨스트민스터에 미완성 대성당이 내려다보이는 아파트를 가지고 있었고, 같은 동네에 살았기 때문에 우리는 서로 친근감을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French disposer.
definition_en: Get rid of something unwanted or unnecessary.

senses.gloss: To eliminate or to get rid of something.
senses.example: I dispose of my trash in the garbage can.

senses.gloss: To distribute or arrange; to put in place.
senses.example: By disposing the driving power over a number of cars instead of concentrating it in a single locomotive a great advance was made towards a high rate of acceleration.

senses.gloss: To deal out; to assign to a use.
senses.example: what he designed to bestow on her funeral, he would rather dispose among the poor

examples.text: As we walked across the moonlight gravel to the porch he disposed of the situation in a few brisk phrases.
examples.translation_ko: 달빛이 비치는 자갈길을 건너 현관으로 걸어가면서 그는 몇 마디 간결한 말로 상황을 정리했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She had a flat in Westminster, overlooking the unfinished cathedral, and because we lived in the same neighbourhood we felt friendly disposed to one another.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 웨스트민스터에 미완성 대성당이 내려다보이는 아파트를 가지고 있었고, 같은 동네에 살았기 때문에 우리는 서로 친근감을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English unyoun, from Old French union, from Late Latin ūniō, ūniōnem (“oneness, unity”), from Latin ūnus (“one”). Doublet of unio.
definition_en: A state of being joined or united.

senses.gloss: The act of uniting or joining two or more things into one.
The state of being united or joined; a state of unity or harmony.
Something united, or made one; something formed by a combination or coalition of parts or members; a confederation; a consolidated body; a league.

examples.text: The Army and Navy Stores are a bond of union between all who dwell between the river and St. James’s Park.
examples.translation_ko: 육해군 상점은 강과 세인트 제임스 공원 사이에 사는 모든 사람들 사이의 결속의 끈이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: To give my story coherence I should describe the progress of their tragic union, but I know nothing of the three months during which they lived together.
examples.translation_ko: 내 이야기에 일관성을 부여하려면 그들의 비극적 결합이 어떻게 진행되었는지 묘사해야 하겠지만, 그들이 함께 살았던 석 달 동안에 대해서는 아무것도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English frok, frokke, from Old French froc (“frock, a monk's gown or habit”), perhaps via Medieval Latin hrocus, roccus, rocus (“a coat...
definition_en: Dress someone informally

senses.gloss: A dress, a piece of clothing, which consists of a skirt and a cover for the upper body.
An outer garment worn by priests and other clericals; a habit.
A sailor's jersey.

examples.text: Some wear black shifts and flesh-coloured stockings; some with curly hair, dyed yellow, are dressed like little girls in short muslin frocks.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 여자는 검은 속옷에 살색 스타킹을 신고 있고, 어떤 여자는 노랗게 염색한 곱슬머리를 하고 짧은 모슬린 원피스를 입어 마치 어린 소녀처럼 차려입었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Miss Waterford, torn between the aestheticism of her early youth, when she used to go to parties in sage green, holding a daffodil, and the flippancy of her maturer years, which tended to high heels and Paris frocks, wore a new hat.
examples.translation_ko: 워터포드 양은 세이지 그린 옷을 입고 수선화를 들고 파티에 다니던 젊은 시절의 미학주의와, 하이힐과 파리 드레스를 선호하는 성숙한 나이의 경박함 사이에서 갈등하며 새 모자를 쓰고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English whisperen, from Old English hwisprian (“to mutter, murmur, whisper”), from Proto-West Germanic *hwisprōn, from Proto-Germanic *...
definition_en: A soft quiet sound or voice.

senses.gloss: The act of speaking in a quiet voice, especially without vibration of the vocal cords.
senses.example: I spoke in a near whisper.

senses.gloss: A rumor.
senses.example: There are whispers of rebellion all around.

senses.gloss: A faint trace or hint (of something).
senses.example: The soup had just a whisper of basil.

examples.text: “Is there anyone else she wants to see?” asked Dirk, in a voice so low it was almost a whisper.
examples.translation_ko: "다른 사람 중에 만나고 싶어하는 사람이 있나요?" 더크가 거의 속삭임에 가까운 낮은 목소리로 물었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Mrs. Jay, aware that impropriety is the soul of wit, made observations in tones hardly above a whisper that might well have tinged the snowy tablecloth with a rosy hue.
examples.translation_ko: 부적절함이야말로 재치의 영혼이라는 것을 아는 제이 부인은 하얀 식탁보를 장밋빛으로 물들일 만한 말들을 속삭이듯 낮은 목소리로 내뱉었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested around 1472. From Middle English absurdite, then from either Middle French absurdité, or from Late Latin absurditas (“dissonance, in...
definition_en: The quality of being absurd or unreasonable.

senses.gloss: That which is absurd; an absurd action; a logical contradiction.
The quality of being absurd or inconsistent with obvious truth, reason, or sound judgment.
senses.example: Neither [Jones][…] nor I (in 1966) could conceive of reducing our "science" to the ultimate absurdity of reading Finnish newspapers almost a century and a half old in order to establish "priority."

senses.gloss: Dissonance.

examples.text: Richard Twining bubbled over with quaint absurdities, and George Road, conscious that he need not exhibit a brilliancy which was almost a by-word, opened his mouth only to put food into it.
examples.translation_ko: 리처드 트와이닝은 기발한 우스갯소리로 넘쳐났고, 거의 대명사가 된 자신의 재치를 굳이 뽐낼 필요가 없다는 것을 아는 조지 로드는 오직 음식을 넣기 위해서만 입을 열었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The absurdity that clung to everything connected with Dirk Stroeve gave it a curious note, like an unresolved discord, but made it somehow more modern, more human; like a rough joke thrown into a serious scene, it heightened the poignancy which all beauty has.
examples.translation_ko: 더크 스트루브와 관련된 모든 것에 달라붙은 우스꽝스러움이 해결되지 않은 불협화음처럼 기묘한 색채를 더했지만, 그것이 오히려 더 현대적이고 더 인간적으로 만들었다. 진지한 장면에 던져진 거친 농담처럼, 그것은 모든 아름다움이 지닌 애절함을 더욱 고조시켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin exhibitus, perfect passive participle of exhibeō (“I hold forth, present, show, display”), from ex (“out of, from”) + habeō (“I have, ho...
definition_en: Show or display something.

senses.gloss: To display or show (something) for others to see, especially at an exhibition or contest.
senses.example: He wanted to exhibit his baseball cards.

senses.gloss: To demonstrate.
senses.example: The players exhibited great skill.

senses.gloss: To submit (a physical object) to a court as evidence.
senses.example: I now exhibit this bloody hammer.

examples.text: Richard Twining bubbled over with quaint absurdities, and George Road, conscious that he need not exhibit a brilliancy which was almost a by-word, opened his mouth only to put food into it.
examples.translation_ko: 리처드 트와이닝은 기발한 우스갯소리로 넘쳐났고, 거의 대명사가 된 자신의 재치를 굳이 뽐낼 필요가 없다는 것을 아는 조지 로드는 오직 음식을 넣기 위해서만 입을 열었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They pinched and saved so that I should have enough to live on, and when my first picture was exhibited they came to Amsterdam to see it, my father and mother and my sister, and my mother cried when she looked at it.”
examples.translation_ko: 가족들은 제가 생활할 수 있을 만큼 충분한 돈을 마련하려고 허리띠를 졸라매며 저축했고, 제 첫 작품이 전시되었을 때는 아버지와 어머니, 누이가 그것을 보러 암스테르담까지 오셨는데, 어머니는 그 그림을 보고 우셨어요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English plump, plompe, a borrowing from Middle Dutch plomp or Middle Low German plump. Cognate with Saterland Frisian plump (“plump”).
definition_en: Having a soft and rounded shape.

senses.gloss: Having a full and rounded shape; chubby, somewhat overweight.
senses.example: a plump baby; plump cheeks

senses.gloss: Fat.
Sudden and without reservation; blunt; direct; downright.
senses.example: I've said so haven't I? Plump and plain.

examples.text: She was a woman of thirty-seven, rather tall and plump, without being fat; she was not pretty, but her face was pleasing, chiefly, perhaps, on account of her kind brown eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 서른일곱 살의 여자로, 키가 큰 편이고 통통했지만 뚱뚱하지는 않았다. 예쁘지는 않았지만 얼굴이 호감형이었는데, 아마도 친절한 갈색 눈 때문이었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: According to the gracious custom of the island, presents were given me by the persons with whom I had been thrown in contact—baskets made of the leaves of the cocoa-nut tree, mats of pandanus, fans; and Tiaré gave me three little pearls and three jars of guava-jelly made with her own plump hands.
examples.translation_ko: 섬의 우아한 관습에 따라, 내가 인연을 맺었던 사람들이 나에게 선물을 주었다—코코넛 나무 잎으로 만든 바구니, 판다누스로 짠 돗자리, 부채들이었고, 티아레는 작은 진주 세 개와 자신의 통통한 손으로 직접 만든 구아바 젤리 세 병을 주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + affected.
definition_en: Not influenced or changed by something.

senses.gloss: Not affected or changed.
senses.example: Since I work from home, I was unaffected by the office move.

senses.gloss: Lacking pretense or affectation; natural.
senses.example: Mr. Bingley was good-looking and gentlemanlike; he had a pleasant countenance, and easy, unaffected manners.

examples.text: Only Gatsby, the man who gives his name to this book, was exempt from my reaction—Gatsby, who represented everything for which I have an unaffected scorn.
examples.translation_ko: 오직 개츠비만이, 이 책에 제목을 준 그 남자만이 내 반감에서 예외였다. 내가 꾸밈없는 경멸을 품고 있는 모든 것을 대변하는 개츠비였는데도 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She was the only woman of the three whose face was free of make-up, and by contrast with the others she seemed simple and unaffected.
examples.translation_ko: 세 여자 중에서 화장을 하지 않은 사람은 그녀뿐이었고, 다른 사람들과 대조적으로 그녀는 소박하고 꾸밈없어 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From leaf + -y.
definition_en: A plant with leaves.

senses.gloss: covered with leaves
senses.example: leafy trees

senses.gloss: containing much foliage
senses.example: a leafy avenue

senses.gloss: in the form of leaves (of some material)

examples.text: They are strangers in their birthplace, and the leafy lanes they have known from childhood or the populous streets in which they have played, remain but a place of passage.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 태어난 곳에서조차 이방인이며, 어린 시절부터 알아온 나뭇잎 우거진 골목길이나 뛰어놀던 번화한 거리들도 그저 지나가는 장소일 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The green curtains with their peacock design, hung in straight lines, and the green carpet, in the pattern of which pale rabbits frolicked among leafy trees, suggested the influence of William Morris.
examples.translation_ko: 공작 무늬가 있는 녹색 커튼이 곧게 드리워져 있었고, 창백한 토끼들이 잎이 무성한 나무들 사이에서 뛰노는 무늬의 녹색 카펫은 윌리엄 모리스의 영향을 시사했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English harmles, from Old English *hearmlēas, from Proto-Germanic *harmalausaz (“without harm; harmless”), equivalent to harm + -less.
...
definition_en: A person or thing that causes no harm.

senses.gloss: Incapable of causing harm or danger; safe.
Not intended to harm; inoffensive.
Unharmed.

examples.text: Looking back, I think that Mrs. Strickland was the most harmless of all the lion-hunters that pursue their quarry from the rarefied heights of Hampstead to the nethermost studios of Cheyne Walk.
examples.translation_ko: 돌이켜보면, 스트릭랜드 부인은 햄프스테드의 고고한 높이에서부터 체인 워크의 가장 밑바닥 화실까지 사냥감을 쫓아다니는 모든 사자 사냥꾼들 중에서 가장 무해한 존재였다고 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: A pleasant, hospitable woman, with a harmless craze for the small lions of literary society; a rather dull man, doing his duty in that state of life in which a merciful Providence had placed him; two nice-looking, healthy children.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of read

examples.text: Strickland, according to Captain Nichols, did not use exactly the words I have given, but since this book is meant for family reading I have thought it better, at the expense of truth, to put into his mouth expressions familiar to the domestic circle.
examples.translation_ko: 니콜스 선장에 따르면, 스트릭랜드는 내가 방금 인용한 표현을 정확히 사용하지는 않았다. 하지만 이 책이 가정에서 읽힐 것을 염두에 두고 있으므로, 진실을 희생하더라도 가정에서 익숙한 표현을 그의 입에 담는 것이 낫다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She had a real passion for reading (rare in her kind, who for the most part are more interested in the author than in his book, in the painter than in his pictures), and she invented a world of the imagination in which she lived with a freedom she never acquired in the world of every day.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 독서에 대한 진정한 열정을 가지고 있었는데(그녀와 같은 부류에서는 드문 일이었다. 대부분은 책보다는 작가에게, 그림보다는 화가에게 더 관심이 있었으니까), 상상의 세계를 창조해서 그 안에서 일상 세계에서는 결코 얻지 못했던 자유로움을 누리며 살았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From dramatic + -ally.
definition_en: Used to describe something that is done or happens in a dramatic way.

senses.gloss: In a dramatic manner.

examples.text: He stopped, somewhat dramatically, and stretched out his arm.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 다소 극적으로 멈춰 서서 팔을 뻗었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She saw them dramatically, and really seemed herself to live a larger life because she entertained them and visited them in their fastnesses.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그들을 극적으로 바라보았고, 그들을 접대하고 그들의 요새를 방문함으로써 정말로 자신이 더 큰 삶을 살고 있는 것처럼 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A quality of being fast or swift.

senses.gloss: The quality or state of being strongly attached; firmness, secureness, tenacity.
senses.example: [T]his is the ſure, infallible Teſt of Love, that the Meaſure of its Strength is to be taken by the Faſtneſs of its Hold.

The quality or state of moving quickly; quickness, rapidity, swiftness.

[Frog:] Why are all of us fleein'? What dire peril threatens our sylvan fastness?
 [Bug:] Just run! Your fastness shouldn't be too slow.

examples.text: Ten miles away the island of Murea, like some high fastness of the Holy Grail, guarded its mystery.
examples.translation_ko: 십 마일 떨어진 무레아 섬이 성배의 높은 요새처럼 그 신비를 지키고 있었다.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French théorie, from Late Latin theōria, from Ancient Greek θεωρία (theōría, “contemplation, divine perspective, speculation, a looking...
definition_en: A proposed explanation for a set of phenomena.

senses.gloss: A description of an event or system that is considered to be accurate.
senses.example: As they encrease the hatred of vice in some, so doe they enlarge the theory of wickednesse in all.

senses.gloss: A coherent statement or set of ideas that explains observed facts or phenomena and correctly predicts new facts or phenomena not previously observed, or which sets out the laws and principles of something known or observed; a hypothesis confirmed by observation, experiment etc.
senses.example: The world would need additional decades [...] before the Big Bang would begin to move from interesting idea to established theory.

senses.gloss: The underlying principles or methods of a given technical skill, art etc., as opposed to its practice.
senses.example: Lopukhov wrote a number of books and articles on ballet theory, as well as his memoirs.

examples.text: Their moral eccentricities, like their oddities of dress, their wild theories and paradoxes, were an entertainment which amused her, but had not the slightest influence on her convictions.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 도덕적 기행과 복장의 기이함, 거친 이론들과 역설들은 그녀를 즐겁게 해주는 오락거리였지만, 그녀의 신념에는 조금도 영향을 미치지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I feel the need to ascribe to him fantastic theories about his predecessors, and it is with a certain sense of disillusion that I confess he thought about them pretty much as does everybody else.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 선배 화가들에 대한 기상천외한 이론들을 부여하고 싶은 욕구를 느끼는데, 그가 그들에 대해 다른 사람들과 거의 똑같이 생각했다고 고백하는 것은 어느 정도 환멸감을 준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French formidable, from Latin formīdābilis (“formidable, terrible”), from formīdō (“fear, dread”).
definition_en: Extremely impressive or intimidating.

senses.gloss: Causing fear, dread, awe, or discouragement as a result of size, strength, or some other impressive feature; commanding respect; causing wonder or astonishment.
Difficult to defeat or overcome.
senses.example: a formidable opponent

examples.text: As we passed over the dark bridge her wan face fell lazily against my coat’s shoulder and the formidable stroke of thirty died away with the reassuring pressure of her hand.
examples.translation_ko: 우리가 어두운 다리를 건널 때 그녀의 창백한 얼굴이 나른하게 내 코트 어깨에 기대었고, 서른이라는 무시무시한 충격은 그녀 손의 든든한 압박감과 함께 사라져갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I went now and then to pleasant little luncheons at her flat, and to rather more formidable tea-parties.
examples.translation_ko: 가끔 그녀의 아파트에서 열리는 즐거운 소규모 점심 모임에 참석했고, 좀 더 격식을 차린 다과회에도 나갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: c. 1325–75. From Middle English guide, from the Old French guide, from Old Occitan guida, from guidar, from Frankish *wītan (“to show the way, lead...
definition_en: To show or direct the way.

senses.gloss: Someone who guides, especially someone hired to show people around a place or an institution and offer information and explanation, or to lead them through dangerous terrain.
senses.example: The guide led us around the museum and explained the exhibits.

senses.gloss: A document or book that offers information or instruction; guidebook.
A sign that guides people; guidepost.

examples.text: I was very young, and perhaps she liked the idea of guiding my virgin steps on the hard road of letters; while for me it was pleasant to have someone I could go to with my small troubles, certain of an attentive ear and reasonable counsel.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 아주 젊었고, 아마 그녀는 문학이라는 험난한 길에서 순진한 내 발걸음을 이끌어준다는 생각을 좋아했을 것이다. 한편 나로서는 사소한 고민거리가 생겼을 때 찾아가서 관심 있게 들어주고 합리적인 조언을 해줄 사람이 있다는 것이 즐거웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He told me with grim humour of the time he had spent acting as guide to Cockneys who wanted to see the night side of life in Paris; it was an occupation that appealed to his sardonic temper and somehow or other he had acquired a wide acquaintance with the more disreputable quarters of the city.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 파리의 밤의 세계를 구경하고 싶어 하는 런던 서민들의 안내자 노릇을 했던 시절을 냉혹한 유머로 내게 들려주었다. 그것은 그의 냉소적인 성격에 어울리는 직업이었고, 어떻게 해서인지 그는 도시의 더 불명예스러운 지역들과 폭넓은 친분을 쌓고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English attentif, attentijf, from Old French attentif.
definition_en: Paying close attention to details.

senses.gloss: Paying attention; noticing, watching, listening, or attending closely.
senses.example: She is an attentive listener, but does not like to talk much.

senses.gloss: Courteous; mindful.
senses.example: a husband attentive to his wife’s needs

examples.text: You need no laborious steps to enter upon familiarity with them, and you can earn not only their confidence, but their gratitude, by turning an attentive ear to their discourse.
examples.translation_ko: 그들과 친해지기 위해 번거로운 단계를 거칠 필요가 없으며, 그들의 이야기에 귀 기울여주기만 해도 신뢰는 물론 감사까지 얻을 수 있다.

examples.text: At last he came upon what he sought, a large scraper, and he pounced on it with a cry of triumph.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 그가 찾던 것, 큰 스크래퍼를 발견했고, 승리의 외침과 함께 그것을 움켜잡았다.

examples.text: It is a charming faculty, but one often abused by those who are conscious of its possession: for there is something ghoulish in the avidity with which they will pounce upon the misfortune of their friends so that they may exercise their dexterity.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “He’d be a bit surly sometimes, but when we hadn’t had a bite since morning, and we hadn’t even got the price of a lie down at the Chink’s, he’d be as lively as a cricket.”
examples.translation_ko: "가끔 좀 뚱한 적은 있었지만, 아침부터 한 입도 못 먹고 중국인 숙소에서 잘 돈도 없을 때도 귀뚜라미처럼 활기찼거든요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From reflect + -ive.
definition_en: Having or showing a thoughtful and careful consideration of one's actions.

senses.gloss: That reflects, or redirects back to the source.
senses.example: Mirrors are reflective.

senses.gloss: Pondering, especially thinking back on the past.
senses.example: He always becomes reflective in preparation for the new year.

senses.gloss: That reveals or shows; revealing; indicative of.

examples.text: He had his mother’s candid brow and fine, reflective eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 어머니의 솔직한 이마와 아름답고 사려 깊은 눈을 닮았다.

examples.text: She paused, looking at him with those reflective eyes of hers, which now were so different to him.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 잠시 말을 멈추고 그 사색적인 눈으로 그를 바라보았는데, 그 눈빛은 이제 그에게 전혀 다르게 느껴졌다.

definition_en: Showing a willingness to help or please others.

senses.gloss: Having a kind personality; kind, warmhearted, sympathetic.
senses.example: A kindly old man sits on the park bench every afternoon feeding pigeons.

senses.gloss: Favourable, gentle, pleasant, tidy, auspicious, beneficent.
senses.example: Lead, kindly Light, amid th' encircling gloom, / ⁠Lead Thou me on

senses.gloss: Lawful.

examples.text: Her hair, thick and dark like her mother’s, fell over her shoulders in fine profusion, and she had the same kindly expression and sedate, untroubled eyes.

examples.text: It was a slow smile, starting and sometimes ending in the eyes; it was very sensual, neither cruel nor kindly, but suggested rather the inhuman glee of the satyr.

examples.text: I do not know why I had expected her to be somehow changed; she wore the same gray dress that she wore so often, neat and becoming, and her brow was as candid, her eyes as untroubled, as when I had been used to see her occupied with her household duties in the studio.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “They’re both of them the image of you,” I said.
examples.translation_ko: "두 아이 모두 어머니를 쏙 빼닮았군요." 내가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From shy + -ness.
definition_en: A feeling of nervousness or awkwardness in social situations.

senses.gloss: The quality of being shy; a fear of social interactions.
senses.example: Her shyness kept her from asking him to the prom.

examples.text: I felt a certain shyness at referring to matters which were no concern of mine.
examples.translation_ko: 나와는 상관없는 일에 대해 언급하는 것이 어딘지 부끄러웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She smiled to cover her shyness, and I fancied she had a fear that I would make the sort of gibe that such a confession could hardly have failed to elicit from Rose Waterford.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 수줍음을 감추려고 미소를 지었는데, 나는 그녀가 내가 로즈 워터포드라면 그런 고백을 듣고 틀림없이 했을 법한 조롱을 할까 봐 두려워하는 것 같다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Tease or mock someone with a witty remark.

senses.gloss: Alternative spelling of gybe.
Alternative spelling of jibe (“facetious or insulting remark”).
senses.example: But an ugly eruption of racist gibes against some of its young Black players was a reminder that not everyone glories in the diverse portrait of the country that this team reflects.

examples.text: I felt sure he was seeking for some gibe, could think of none, and so was forced to silence.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 비꼬는 말을 찾고 있지만 떠오르지 않아서 어쩔 수 없이 침묵할 수밖에 없다고 확신했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She smiled to cover her shyness, and I fancied she had a fear that I would make the sort of gibe that such a confession could hardly have failed to elicit from Rose Waterford.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 수줍음을 감추려고 미소를 지었는데, 나는 그녀가 내가 로즈 워터포드라면 그런 고백을 듣고 틀림없이 했을 법한 조롱을 할까 봐 두려워하는 것 같다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From late Middle English, borrowed from Latin extinctio (“extinction, annihilation”), from extinguere, past participle extinctus (“to extinguish”);...
definition_en: The state of being extinct.

senses.gloss: The action of making or becoming extinct; annihilation.
senses.example: Dr. Manuel: You're wasting your time. The age of humanity is over. Our extinction is inevitable.

senses.gloss: The absorption or scattering of electromagnetic radiation emitted by astronomical objects by intervening dust and gas before it reaches the observer.
The inability to perceive multiple stimuli simultaneously.

examples.text: His voice was solemn, as if the memory of that sudden extinction of a clan still haunted him.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 목소리는 엄숙했는데, 마치 일족이 갑작스럽게 전멸한 기억이 아직도 그를 괴롭히는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “It’s only decent to warn you that you will be bored to extinction.
examples.translation_ko: "미리 경고해드리는 게 예의겠지만, 지루해서 죽을 지경이 되실 거예요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From thorough + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is done completely or very effectively.

senses.gloss: In a thorough or complete manner.
senses.example: He went out in the rain and came back thoroughly drenched.

examples.text: I enjoyed the counter-raid so thoroughly that I came back restless.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그 반격을 너무나 철저히 즐겨서 불안한 마음으로 돌아왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was a thoroughly dull party from the beginning, but if you will come I shall be uncommonly grateful.
examples.translation_ko: 처음부터 끝까지 지독히 따분한 파티가 될 텐데, 그래도 와주신다면 정말 고맙겠어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English geste (“idle tale”), from Old French geste (“acts, exploits”), from Latin gesta (“acts, deeds”). Doublet of gest.
definition_en: A humorous or ironic remark.

senses.gloss: An act performed for amusement; a joke.
senses.example: I made that comment in jest; it wasn't serious.

senses.gloss: Someone or something that is ridiculed; the target of a joke.
senses.example: Your majesty, stop him before he makes you the jest of the court.

senses.gloss: A deed; an action; a gest.
senses.example: the jests or actions of princes

examples.text: “You are jesting,” said Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: "농담하시는군요." 스트릭랜드가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Turning to him gaily, she attempted a small jest.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 명랑하게 남편 쪽으로 돌아서며 작은 농담을 시도했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English assemblen, from Old French assembler (“to assemble”), from Medieval Latin assimulāre (“to bring together”), from ad- + simulō (...
definition_en: To gather or put together into a single group.

senses.gloss: To put together.
senses.example: He assembled the model ship.

senses.gloss: To gather as a group.
senses.example: The parents assembled in the school hall.

senses.gloss: To translate from assembly language to machine code.

examples.text: Then the natives would assemble with spears, and with much shouting would transfix the great startled things as they hurried down to the sea.
examples.translation_ko: 그러면 원주민들이 창을 들고 모여들어 큰 소리를 지르며 바다로 서둘러 내려가는 놀란 큰 물고기들을 찔러 잡았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When at last we were all assembled, waiting for dinner to be announced, I reflected, while I chatted with the woman I had been asked to “take in,” that civilised man practises a strange ingenuity in wasting on tedious exercises the brief span of his life.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 모든 사람이 모여 저녁 식사 시간이 알려지기를 기다리고 있을 때, 나는 "에스코트"해달라고 부탁받은 여자와 이야기를 나누면서 문명인이라는 존재가 짧은 인생을 지루한 일들로 낭비하는 데 기묘한 재주를 발휘한다는 생각을 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: English tedi(um) + -ous, from Old French tedieus, from Late Latin taediōsus, from Latin taedium (“weariness, tedium”).
definition_en: Extremely dull and uninteresting.

senses.gloss: Boring, monotonous, time-consuming, wearisome, livelong.
senses.example: John Gilpin's ſpouse ſaid to her dear, / Though wedded we have been / Theſe twice ten tedious years, yet we / No holiday have ſeen.

examples.text: My friends pursued their course with uneventfulness; they had no longer any surprises for me, and when I met them I knew pretty well what they would say; even their love-affairs had a tedious banality.
examples.translation_ko: 내 친구들은 평온하게 자신들의 길을 걸어갔다. 그들에게서 더 이상 놀랄 만한 것은 없었고, 만날 때마다 그들이 무슨 말을 할지 거의 알 수 있었다. 심지어 그들의 연애사조차 지루할 만큼 뻔했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When at last we were all assembled, waiting for dinner to be announced, I reflected, while I chatted with the woman I had been asked to “take in,” that civilised man practises a strange ingenuity in wasting on tedious exercises the brief span of his life.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 모든 사람이 모여 저녁 식사 시간이 알려지기를 기다리고 있을 때, 나는 "에스코트"해달라고 부탁받은 여자와 이야기를 나누면서 문명인이라는 존재가 짧은 인생을 지루한 일들로 낭비하는 데 기묘한 재주를 발휘한다는 생각을 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English purely, equivalent to pure + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is done or thought of without any mixture or addition.

senses.gloss: Wholly; really, completely.
senses.example: I am fascinated by the entire scene, I purely am.

senses.gloss: Solely; exclusively; merely, simply.
senses.example: "But this meal tonight is not a date, not in the traditional sense. It's purely platonic, I assure you."

senses.gloss: Chastely, innocently; in a sinless manner, without fault.
senses.example: faith and troth, / Strain'd purely from all hollow bias drawing: / Bids thee with most diuine integritie, / From heart of very heart, great Hector welcome.

examples.text: It was, of course, a purely social function.
examples.translation_ko: 물론 순전히 사교적인 모임이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “It’s a purely professional interest you take in me?”
examples.translation_ko: "나에 대한 관심이 순전히 직업적인 것이군요?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French function, from Old French fonction, from Latin functiō (“performance, execution”), from functus, perfect participle of fungor (“...
definition_en: A set of rules that explains what a function does.

senses.gloss: What something does or is used for.
A professional or official position.
An official or social occasion.
senses.example: Our hotel is hosting a function for all the warehouse workers on the night of April 18.

examples.text: Instead of rambling, this party had preserved a dignified homogeneity, and assumed to itself the function of representing the staid nobility of the countryside—East Egg condescending to West Egg and carefully on guard against its spectroscopic gaiety.
examples.translation_ko: 이 일행은 어수선하지 않고 품위 있는 동질성을 유지했으며, 시골의 침착한 귀족층을 대표하는 역할을 자임했다—이스트에그가 웨스트에그를 내려다보며 그곳의 현란한 유쾌함을 조심스럽게 경계하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was, of course, a purely social function.
examples.translation_ko: 물론 순전히 사교적인 모임이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Used to indicate that something is being spoken more loudly.

senses.gloss: comparative form of loud: more loud
senses.example: The sound of a hard-working diesel engine pierces the damp Yorkshire air. It gets louder, until a bright red High Speed Train cuts through the gloom.

examples.text: There was never a pause, and the noise grew louder.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시의 침묵도 없었고, 소음은 더욱 커졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Her laughter was the most catching I ever heard; it would begin, a low peal in her throat, and would grow louder and louder till her whole vast body shook.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 웃음소리는 내가 들어본 것 중 가장 전염성이 강했다. 목구멍 깊은 곳에서 낮게 울려 퍼지기 시작해서 점점 커져가다가 마침내 그녀의 거대한 몸 전체가 흔들릴 정도가 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old English port, borrowed from Latin portus (“port, harbour”), ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *pértus (“crossing”) (and thus a distant d...
definition_en: A location on a coast or shore

senses.gloss: A place on the coast at which ships can shelter, or dock to load and unload cargo or passengers.
senses.example: peering in maps for ports and piers and roads

senses.gloss: A town or city containing such a place, a port city.

The left-hand side of a vessel, including aircraft, when one is facing the front. Used to unambiguously refer to directions relative to the vessel structure, rather than to a person or object on board.

examples.text: He passed round the port again and handed us cigars.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 포트 와인을 다시 돌리고 우리에게 시가를 건넸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The ship was only in port for six hours, and in the evening Captain Nichols watched the vanishing smoke from her funnels as she ploughed East through the wintry sea.
examples.translation_ko: 배는 단 여섯 시간만 항구에 정박했고, 저녁이 되자 니콜스 선장은 겨울 바다를 가로질러 동쪽으로 나아가는 배의 굴뚝에서 피어오르는 연기가 사라지는 것을 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From clumsy + -ly.
definition_en: Done with a lack of skill or care.

senses.gloss: In a clumsy manner or way; without care or finesse, often hurriedly or awkwardly.
senses.example: But, bowing with sketchily joined hands, they smiled their way clumsily out, down to the darkness.

examples.text: It was as though he found in the chaos of the universe a new pattern, and were attempting clumsily, with anguish of soul, to set it down.
examples.translation_ko: 마치 그가 우주의 혼돈 속에서 새로운 패턴을 발견하고, 영혼의 고뇌와 함께 서투르게 그것을 기록하려 애쓰고 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was bigger than I expected: I do not know why I had imagined him slender and of insignificant appearance; in point of fact he was broad and heavy, with large hands and feet, and he wore his evening clothes clumsily.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내가 예상했던 것보다 덩치가 컸다. 왜 그를 날씬하고 보잘것없는 외모로 상상했는지 모르겠지만, 실제로는 어깨가 넓고 체구가 무거웠으며, 손과 발이 컸고, 연미복을 어색하게 입고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- (“not”) + gainly (“graceful; becoming; proper, suitable; gracious, kindly”) (from gain (“dexterous; convenient, easy, handy; suitable”), f...
definition_en: Unusually awkward or clumsy.

senses.gloss: Clumsy; lacking grace.
senses.example: His body, though thin, looked oversized and ungainly, his limbs poorly knit together; he appeared to conquer his tendency to awkwardness by making only the smallest, most deliberate of movements.

senses.gloss: Difficult to move or to manage; unwieldy.
Unsuitable; unprofitable.
senses.example: For as she could not, alas, select / Twixt ye goodlie and ungainlie, / Why of course 'twas Actions must direct / Her goode opinion,—mainlie.

examples.text: The portraits were a little larger than life-size, and this gave them an ungainly look.
examples.translation_ko: 초상화들은 실물보다 조금 더 큰 크기였는데, 그래서 어색해 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was a man of forty, not good-looking, and yet not ugly, for his features were rather good; but they were all a little larger than life-size, and the effect was ungainly.
examples.translation_ko: 마흔 살 남자로, 잘생기지도 못생기지도 않았는데, 이목구비 자체는 나쁘지 않았지만 모든 것이 실제보다 조금씩 크게 느껴져서 전체적으로 어색한 느낌이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English dusty, dusti, from Old English dūstiġ, dystiġ, dȳstiġ (“dusty”), equivalent to dust + -y. Cognate with Dutch donzig (“cottony, ...
definition_en: Covered with dust.

senses.gloss: Covered with dust.
senses.example: a dusty carpet

senses.gloss: Powdery and resembling dust.
Grey or greyish.
senses.example: a dusty peach color

examples.text: Tom threw on both brakes impatiently, and we slid to an abrupt dusty stop under Wilson’s sign.
examples.translation_ko: 톰은 성급하게 브레이크를 밟았고, 우리는 윌슨의 간판 아래에서 갑작스럽게 먼지를 일으키며 멈춰 섰다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The season was drawing to its dusty end, and everyone I knew was arranging to go away.
examples.translation_ko: 계절은 먼지투성이 끝자락으로 치달아가고 있었고, 내가 아는 사람들은 모두 떠날 준비를 하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English coste (“rib; side of the body, flank; side of a building; face of a solid figure; coast, shore; bay, gulf; sea; concavity, holl...
definition_en: A long piece of land along the edge of a sea or lake.

senses.gloss: The edge of the land where it meets an ocean, sea, gulf, bay, or large lake.
senses.example: The rocky coast of Maine has few beaches.

senses.gloss: The side or edge of something.
senses.example: And the Coaſt towards which the lines KL and VX are drawn, may be call’d the Coaſt of unuſual Refraction.

senses.gloss: A region of land; a district or country.
senses.example: P. Crescentius, in his lib. 1 de agric. cap. 5, is very copious in this subject, how a house should be wholesomely sited, in a good coast, good air, wind, etc.

examples.text: Mrs. Strickland was taking her family to the coast of Norfolk, so that the children might have the sea and her husband golf.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인은 가족들과 함께 노퍽 해안으로 가려고 했는데, 아이들은 바다를, 남편은 골프를 즐길 수 있도록 하기 위해서였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I saw him, the sea gray under the mistral and foam-flecked, watching the vanishing coast of France, which he was destined never to see again; and I thought there was something gallant in his bearing and dauntless in his soul.
examples.translation_ko: 미스트랄 바람 아래 회색빛을 띤 바다에 거품이 일렁이는 가운데, 다시는 보지 못할 운명인 프랑스 해안이 사라져가는 것을 바라보는 그의 모습이 눈에 보였다. 그리고 그의 자세에는 용감함이, 그의 영혼에는 불굴의 정신이 있다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Mid-15th century; from Middle English alacrite, from Latin alacritās, from alacer (“brisk”) + -itās (“-ity”).
definition_en: Quick and eager movement or action.

senses.gloss: Eagerness; liveliness; enthusiasm.
senses.example: This evening, however, he was struck by the beaming alacrity of the aide-de-camp's greeting.

senses.gloss: Promptness; speed.
senses.example: Not just that, but if the inlet of a turbopump impeller runs dry, it would overspeed with blinding alacrity.

examples.text: Not only her face, but her whole body, gave a sense of alacrity.
examples.translation_ko: 얼굴뿐만 아니라 온몸이 기민함을 드러내고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I think Mrs. Strickland was glad to show me her children, and she accepted my invitation with alacrity.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인은 나에게 자신의 아이들을 보여주고 싶어하는 것 같았고, 기꺼이 내 제안을 받아들였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From devote + -ed.
definition_en: Showing loyalty and dedication to a person or cause.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of devote

examples.text: They seemed devoted to one another.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 서로에게 헌신적인 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She proved herself not only a capable, but a devoted nurse.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 자신이 유능할 뿐만 아니라 헌신적인 간병인임을 증명했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + intelligible.
definition_en: Not able to be understood.

senses.gloss: Not intelligible; unable to be understood.
senses.example: Unintelligible announcements on station loudspeakers are both irritating and confusing.

examples.text: Forms leaned together in the taxis as they waited, and voices sang, and there was laughter from unheard jokes, and lighted cigarettes made unintelligible circles inside.
examples.translation_ko: 택시들이 기다리는 동안 형체들이 서로 기대어 있었고, 목소리들이 노래했으며, 들리지 않는 농담에서 웃음소리가 났고, 불 켜진 담배들이 안에서 알아볼 수 없는 원을 그렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They had little private jokes of their own which, unintelligible to the outsider, amused them enormously.
examples.translation_ko: 그들만의 작은 농담들이 있었는데, 외부인에게는 이해할 수 없는 것들이었지만 그들 자신에게는 엄청나게 재미있는 것들이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + toward (“to + -ward”).
definition_en: Unfavorable or unexpected

senses.gloss: Unfavourable, adverse, or disadvantageous.
senses.example: No untoward effects were reported; however, this was not a blinded or controlled study.

senses.gloss: Unruly, troublesome; not easily guided.
Unseemly, improper.
senses.example: “I have a suspicion that someone is trying to recategorize my generosity to ex-girlfriends as something more untoward,” Gaetz said. As only he could.

examples.text: This was the first suggestion that anything untoward had happened.
examples.translation_ko: 이것이 뭔가 좋지 않은 일이 일어났다는 첫 번째 암시였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I pictured their lives, troubled by no untoward adventure, honest, decent, and, by reason of those two upstanding, pleasant children, so obviously destined to carry on the normal traditions of their race and station, not without significance.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그들의 삶을 그려보았다. 뜻밖의 모험으로 괴로워하지 않고, 정직하고 품위 있으며, 자신들의 인종과 지위의 정상적인 전통을 이어갈 운명이 분명한 그 두 건실하고 사랑스러운 아이들 덕분에 의미 없지 않은 삶을.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English destinen, from Old French destiner. Doublet of destinate.
definition_en: Decide or plan the course of something.

senses.gloss: to preordain
to assign something (especially finance) for a particular use
to attribute a particular destination

examples.text: I saw him, the sea gray under the mistral and foam-flecked, watching the vanishing coast of France, which he was destined never to see again; and I thought there was something gallant in his bearing and dauntless in his soul.
examples.translation_ko: 미스트랄 바람 아래 회색빛을 띤 바다에 거품이 일렁이는 가운데, 다시는 보지 못할 운명인 프랑스 해안이 사라져가는 것을 바라보는 그의 모습이 눈에 보였다. 그리고 그의 자세에는 용감함이, 그의 영혼에는 불굴의 정신이 있다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I pictured their lives, troubled by no untoward adventure, honest, decent, and, by reason of those two upstanding, pleasant children, so obviously destined to carry on the normal traditions of their race and station, not without significance.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그들의 삶을 그려보았다. 뜻밖의 모험으로 괴로워하지 않고, 정직하고 품위 있으며, 자신들의 인종과 지위의 정상적인 전통을 이어갈 운명이 분명한 그 두 건실하고 사랑스러운 아이들 덕분에 의미 없지 않은 삶을.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French retirement, from retirer (“withdraw, retire”); corresponding to retire + -ment.
definition_en: The state of stopping work and receiving a pension.

senses.gloss: An act of retiring; withdrawal.
The state of being retired; seclusion.
A place of seclusion or privacy; a retreat.
senses.example: When her mother frowned, and her friend looked cool, she would steal to this retirement, where human foot seldom trod […].

examples.text: Mrs. Strickland was the daughter of an Indian civilian, who on his retirement had settled in the depths of the country, but it was his habit every August to take his family to Eastbourne for change of air; and it was here, when she was twenty, that she met Charles Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인은 인도 문관의 딸이었는데, 그는 은퇴 후 시골 깊숙한 곳에 정착했지만 매년 8월이면 가족을 데리고 이스트본으로 전지요양을 가는 것이 습관이었다. 그리고 바로 이곳에서 그녀가 스무 살 때 찰스 스트릭랜드를 만났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They would grow old insensibly; they would see their son and daughter come to years of reason, marry in due course—the one a pretty girl, future mother of healthy children; the other a handsome, manly fellow, obviously a soldier; and at last, prosperous in their dignified retirement, beloved by their descendants, after a happy, not unuseful life, in the fullness of their age they would sink into the grave.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 자연스럽게 늙어갈 것이고, 아들과 딸이 분별력을 갖는 나이가 되어 때가 되면 결혼하는 것을 보게 될 것이다. 하나는 예쁜 소녀로 건강한 아이들의 미래 어머니가 되고, 다른 하나는 잘생기고 남자다운 청년으로 분명히 군인이 될 것이다. 그리고 마침내 품위 있는 은퇴 생활에서 번영하며 후손들의 사랑을 받다가, 행복하고 무익하지 않은 삶을 마친 후 충분한 나이에 무덤으로 들어갈 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English homly, hoomly, hamely (“domestic, familiar, plain, unattractive”), from Old English *hāmlīċ (“of the home, domestic”), from Pro...
definition_en: Having a plain and unpretentious quality.

senses.gloss: Characteristic of, belonging to, or befitting a home; domestic, cozy.
senses.example: Mowgli: "Oh, don't worry Chota, it may not be homely, but I can warm it up."

senses.gloss: Lacking in beauty or elegance, plain in appearance, physically unattractive.
senses.example: You see, she sees herself as a starlet; I see her as a sturdy, healthy but decidedly homely kid.

senses.gloss: On intimate or friendly terms with (someone); familiar; at home (with a person); intimate.
senses.example: With all these men I was right homely, and communed with them long and oft.

examples.text: That must be the story of innumerable couples, and the pattern of life it offers has a homely grace.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 수많은 부부들의 이야기일 것이고, 그것이 제시하는 삶의 패턴에는 소박한 우아함이 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The streets were wide and empty; for two hundred years the place had been dying, but the houses had the homely stateliness of their time.
examples.translation_ko: 거리는 넓고 텅 비어 있었다. 이백 년 동안 그 마을은 쇠락해가고 있었지만, 집들은 그 시대의 소박한 위엄을 간직하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French riveret (“little stream”) or from Italian rivoletto, from Italian rivo, from Latin rivus.
definition_en: A small stream of water.

senses.gloss: A small stream; a streamlet; a gill.
senses.example: A rivulet of tears ran down his face.

senses.gloss: Perizoma affinitatum, a geometrid moth.

examples.text: The tears coursed down her cheeks—not freely, however, for when they came into contact with her heavily beaded eyelashes they assumed an inky colour, and pursued the rest of their way in slow black rivulets.
examples.translation_ko: 눈물이 그녀의 뺨을 타고 흘러내렸다—하지만 자유롭게 흐르지는 못했는데, 구슬이 촘촘히 박힌 속눈썹에 닿자 잉크 색깔을 띠게 되어 느린 검은 물줄기가 되어 나머지 길을 이어갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It reminds you of a placid rivulet, meandering smoothly through green pastures and shaded by pleasant trees, till at last it falls into the vasty sea; but the sea is so calm, so silent, so indifferent, that you are troubled suddenly by a vague uneasiness.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 푸른 목초지를 구불구불 흘러가며 아름다운 나무들의 그늘을 받다가 마침내 광활한 바다로 떨어지는 고요한 시냇물을 연상시킨다. 하지만 그 바다가 너무나 잔잔하고, 너무나 조용하고, 너무나 무관심해서 갑자기 막연한 불안감에 사로잡히게 된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English kinken, kynken, from Old English *cincian (attested in cincung), from Proto-West Germanic *kinkōn, from Proto-Germanic *kinkōną...
definition_en: A sudden or unexpected twist or turn.

senses.gloss: To laugh loudly.
To gasp for breath as in a severe fit of coughing.

examples.text: I suppose there was some kink in Abraham.
examples.translation_ko: 아브라함에게는 뭔가 비뚤어진 구석이 있었던 모양이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Perhaps it is only by a kink in my nature, strong in me even in those days, that I felt in such an existence, the share of the great majority, something amiss.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 그 당시에도 내 안에 강하게 자리 잡고 있던 내 성격의 비뚤어진 면 때문일 것이다. 나는 대다수가 누리는 그런 삶에서 뭔가 잘못된 것을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From a- + miss.
definition_en: Not quite right or satisfactory.

senses.gloss: Wrong; faulty; out of order; improper or otherwise incorrect.
senses.example: He suspected something was amiss.

examples.text: In England and France he was the square peg in the round hole, but here the holes were any sort of shape, and no sort of peg was quite amiss.
examples.translation_ko: 영국과 프랑스에서 그는 둥근 구멍에 끼워 넣으려는 네모난 못이었지만, 여기서는 구멍들이 온갖 모양이었고 어떤 못도 완전히 맞지 않는 것은 아니었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Perhaps it is only by a kink in my nature, strong in me even in those days, that I felt in such an existence, the share of the great majority, something amiss.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 그 당시에도 내 안에 강하게 자리 잡고 있던 내 성격의 비뚤어진 면 때문일 것이다. 나는 대다수가 누리는 그런 삶에서 뭔가 잘못된 것을 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Causing alarm or concern.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of alarm

examples.text: Gatsby looked with vacant eyes through a copy of Clay’s Economics, starting at the Finnish tread that shook the kitchen floor, and peering towards the bleared windows from time to time as if a series of invisible but alarming happenings were taking place outside.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 클레이 경제학 책을 멍하니 들여다보며, 부엌 바닥을 흔드는 핀란드산 발걸음 소리에 놀라고는, 때때로 흐릿한 창문 쪽을 힐끗 보았는데 마치 밖에서 보이지 않지만 불길한 일들이 연달아 벌어지고 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There seemed to me something alarming in such easy delights.
examples.translation_ko: 그토록 손쉬운 즐거움에는 뭔가 섬뜩한 구석이 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From dangerous + -ly.
definition_en: Causing or involving danger.

senses.gloss: In a dangerous manner.
senses.example: Add in nominations for Django Unchained, The Master and Moonrise Kingdom, and the Academy Awards look dangerously close to being about rewarding the actual best films of the year. Don't tell anyone.

examples.text: Luckily the clock took this moment to tilt dangerously at the pressure of his head, whereupon he turned and caught it with trembling fingers, and set it back in place.
examples.translation_ko: 다행히 바로 그 순간 시계가 그의 머리 압력에 위험하게 기울었고, 그러자 그는 몸을 돌려 떨리는 손가락으로 시계를 붙잡아 제자리에 다시 놓았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: In my heart was a desire to live more dangerously.
examples.translation_ko: 내 마음속에는 더 위험하게 살고 싶은 욕망이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Having an irregular or broken edge.

senses.gloss: Unevenly cut; having the texture of something so cut.
Having a rough quality.
Of an array, having a different cardinality in each dimension, such that a representation on paper would appear uneven.

examples.text: I was not unprepared for jagged rocks and treacherous shoals if I could only have change—change and the excitement of the unforeseen.
examples.translation_ko: 변화만 있다면—변화와 예측할 수 없는 것들의 흥분만 있다면, 나는 들쭉날쭉한 바위와 위험한 암초도 각오하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: With its jagged outline it is like a Monseratt of the Pacific, and you may imagine that there Polynesian knights guard with strange rites mysteries unholy for men to know.
examples.translation_ko: 들쭉날쭉한 윤곽선을 가진 그 섬은 태평양의 몬세라트 같으며, 그곳에서 폴리네시아의 기사들이 인간이 알아서는 안 될 불경한 신비를 기이한 의식으로 지키고 있다고 상상할 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French trecheros, tricheros (“deceitful”), equivalent to treacher + -ous. See treacher.
definition_en: Having a tendency to cause harm or danger.

senses.gloss: Exhibiting treachery.
senses.example: I see the wife misused by her husband, I see the treacherous seducer of young women, / I mark the ranklings of jealousy and unrequited love attempted to be hid […]

senses.gloss: Deceitful; inclined to betray.
Unreliable; dangerous.
senses.example: a treacherous mountain trail

examples.text: I was not unprepared for jagged rocks and treacherous shoals if I could only have change—change and the excitement of the unforeseen.
examples.translation_ko: 변화만 있다면—변화와 예측할 수 없는 것들의 흥분만 있다면, 나는 들쭉날쭉한 바위와 위험한 암초도 각오하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I had said all I had to say on the subject that had brought me to Paris, and though I felt it in a manner treacherous to Mrs. Strickland not to pursue it, I could not struggle against his indifference.
examples.translation_ko: 나를 파리로 이끈 문제에 대해 할 말은 다 했고, 그것을 계속 추궁하지 않는 것이 어떤 면에서 스트릭랜드 부인에게 배신하는 것 같았지만, 그의 무관심에 맞서 싸울 수는 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English schold, scholde, from Old English sċeald (“shallow”), perhaps from Proto-Germanic *skalidaz, past participle of *skaljaną (“to ...
definition_en: A shallow area of water where the sea bed is exposed at low tide.

senses.gloss: Shallow.
senses.example: shoal water

examples.text: There was a little stream that ran not far away, in which he bathed, and down this on occasion would come a shoal of fish.
examples.translation_ko: 멀지 않은 곳에 작은 개울이 흘렀는데, 그는 거기서 목욕을 했고, 때로는 그 개울로 물고기 떼가 내려오곤 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was not unprepared for jagged rocks and treacherous shoals if I could only have change—change and the excitement of the unforeseen.
examples.translation_ko: 변화만 있다면—변화와 예측할 수 없는 것들의 흥분만 있다면, 나는 들쭉날쭉한 바위와 위험한 암초도 각오하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested in 1604, in modern sense since 1665, from Ancient Greek ἰδιοσυγκρασία (idiosunkrasía, “one’s own temperament”), from ἴδιος (ídios, “...
definition_en: A peculiar or individual characteristic of a person.

senses.gloss: A behavior or way of thinking that is characteristic of a person.
A language or behaviour that is particular to an individual or group.
A peculiar individual reaction to a generally innocuous substance or factor.

examples.text: But I suppose that everyone’s conception of the passion is formed on his own idiosyncrasies, and it is different with every different person.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 누구나 열정에 대한 개념은 자신만의 특성에 따라 형성되는 것이고, 사람마다 모두 다른 법이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I have been able to invest them with none of those characteristics which make the persons of a book exist with a real life of their own; and, wondering if the fault is mine, I rack my brains to remember idiosyncrasies which might lend them vividness.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그들에게 책 속 인물들이 고유한 실제 생명력을 갖게 해주는 특성들을 부여하지 못했다. 혹시 내 잘못인가 싶어서, 그들을 생생하게 만들어줄 수 있는 특이한 점들을 기억해내려고 머리를 쥐어짠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English tapestrie, from Old French tapisserie (“tapestry”), from Ancient Greek τάπης (tápēs), from an Iranian source.
definition_en: A decorative fabric with a design or picture woven into it.

senses.gloss: A heavy woven cloth, often with decorative pictorial designs, normally hung on walls.
Anything with variegated or complex details.
senses.example: European adventurers found themselves within a watery world, a tapestry of streams, channels, wetlands, lakes and lush riparian meadows enriched by floodwaters from the Mississippi River.

examples.text: When he had gone halfway he turned around and stared at the scene—his wife and Catherine scolding and consoling as they stumbled here and there among the crowded furniture with articles of aid, and the despairing figure on the couch, bleeding fluently, and trying to spread a copy of Town Tattle over the tapestry scenes of Versailles.
examples.translation_ko: 중간쯤 갔을 때 그는 돌아서서 그 광경을 바라보았다—그의 아내와 캐서린이 빽빽한 가구들 사이를 이리저리 비틀거리며 구호용품을 들고 꾸짖기도 하고 달래기도 하는 모습, 그리고 소파 위에서 절망에 빠진 채 피를 줄줄 흘리며 베르사유 태피스트리 장면 위에 《타운 태틀》 한 부를 펼쳐 덮으려 애쓰는 모습을.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As they stand they are like the figures in an old tapestry; they do not separate themselves from the background, and at a distance seem to lose their pattern, so that you have little but a pleasing piece of colour.
examples.translation_ko: 지금 상태로는 그들은 오래된 태피스트리 속 인물들 같다. 배경에서 분리되지 않고, 멀리서 보면 무늬가 흐려져서 그저 보기 좋은 색채 덩어리 정도로만 보인다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From back + ground. Compare backstory.
definition_en: The part of a scene or image that is behind the main subject.

senses.gloss: Less important or less noticeable in a scene or system.
senses.example: background noise

examples.text: A dim background started to take shape behind him, but at her next remark it faded away.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 뒤로 희미한 배경이 윤곽을 드러내기 시작했지만, 그녀의 다음 말에 그것은 사라져버렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: As they stand they are like the figures in an old tapestry; they do not separate themselves from the background, and at a distance seem to lose their pattern, so that you have little but a pleasing piece of colour.
examples.translation_ko: 지금 상태로는 그들은 오래된 태피스트리 속 인물들 같다. 배경에서 분리되지 않고, 멀리서 보면 무늬가 흐려져서 그저 보기 좋은 색채 덩어리 정도로만 보인다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Late Latin essentiālis, from Latin essentia (“being, essence”).
definition_en: Necessary for something to exist or be done.

senses.gloss: Necessary.
senses.example: Thus, research-based resources with the potential to assist teachers prepare secondary students for tertiary education are essential.

senses.gloss: Very important; of high importance.
senses.example: In order to grant the rich these pleasures, the social contract is reconfigured. The welfare state is dismantled. Essential public services are cut so that the rich may pay less tax. […]

senses.gloss: Necessary for survival but not synthesized by the organism, thus needing to be ingested.

examples.text: They are like cells in the body, essential, but, so long as they remain healthy, engulfed in the momentous whole.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 몸속의 세포와 같았다. 필수적이지만, 건강한 상태를 유지하는 한 거대한 전체에 묻혀 있는 존재들이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: That is an emotion in which tenderness is an essential part, but Strickland had no tenderness either for himself or for others; there is in love a sense of weakness, a desire to protect, an eagerness to do good and to give pleasure—if not unselfishness, at all events a selfishness which marvellously conceals itself; it has in it a certain diffidence.
examples.translation_ko: 사랑이란 다정함이 필수적인 부분을 차지하는 감정인데, 스트릭랜드에게는 자신에 대해서든 타인에 대해서든 다정함이라는 것이 없었다. 사랑에는 나약함이 있고, 보호하고자 하는 욕구가 있으며, 선을 행하고 기쁨을 주려는 열망이 있다—비이기적이라고 할 수는 없을지라도, 적어도 놀랍도록 교묘하게 자신을 감추는 이기심이 있다. 사랑에는 어떤 수줍음이 깃들어 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From moment (“weight, importance”) + -ous.
definition_en: Having great importance or significance.

senses.gloss: Outstanding in importance, of great consequence.
senses.example: The last train ran on December 31, 1932, almost unnoticed, for it coincided with the running of the last steam passenger train down the main line from London to Brighton, a much more momentous event.

examples.text: They seemed to me ugly, but they suggested without disclosing a secret of momentous significance.
