senses.gloss: An order or command.

examples.text: Then he gave instructions that the open car wasn’t to be taken out under any circumstances—and this was strange, because the front right fender needed repair.
examples.translation_ko: 그러고는 오픈카는 어떤 경우에도 밖으로 빼내지 말라고 지시했는데, 앞쪽 오른편 펜더를 수리해야 했기 때문에 이상한 일이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I have given Anne your instructions, and dinner will be ready for you and the children when you come.
examples.translation_ko: 앤에게 당신이 지시한 대로 말해두었고, 당신과 아이들이 돌아오면 저녁이 준비되어 있을 거야.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Old English post (“pillar, door-post”) and Latin postis (“a post, a door-post”) through Old French. .
definition_en: Send or deliver by mail.

senses.gloss: A long dowel or plank protruding from the ground; a fencepost; a lightpost.
senses.example: ram a post into the ground

senses.gloss: A stud; a two-by-four.
A pole in a battery.

examples.text: I shall post this letter on my arrival.
examples.translation_ko: 도착하면 이 편지를 부칠 거야.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Some lean lazily against the side-posts, humming to themselves or calling to the passer-by in a raucous voice, and some listlessly read.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 여자들은 문설주에 나른하게 기대어 혼자 콧노래를 부르거나 지나가는 사람에게 쉰 목소리로 소리를 지르고 있었고, 어떤 여자들은 무기력하게 책을 읽고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English dredfully, dradefullich, dredefullich; equivalent to dreadful + -ly.
definition_en: Used to express strong dislike or disapproval.

senses.gloss: In a dreadful manner; terribly.
senses.example: The smellful old heathen was snoring dreadfully.

senses.gloss: Exceptionally, eminently, very much.
senses.example: That restaurant seems dreadfully expensive.

examples.text: It was dreadfully painful.
examples.translation_ko: 정말 고통스러운 광경이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “You know, we English are so dreadfully ignorant.
examples.translation_ko: "아시다시피 우리 영국인들은 정말 무지하기 짝이 없어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From in- + sincerity.
definition_en: Lack of sincerity or genuineness.

senses.gloss: Property of being insincere, lacking sincerity or truthfulness.
senses.example: His insincerity was obvious to all; he was neither honest nor believable.

examples.text: The instant her voice broke off, ceasing to compel my attention, my belief, I felt the basic insincerity of what she had said.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 목소리가 끊어지는 순간, 내 관심과 믿음을 강요하던 것이 멈추자, 나는 그녀가 한 말의 근본적인 거짓됨을 느꼈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It throws a shadow of insincerity over their most deeply felt emotions.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 그들의 가장 진실한 감정에까지 위선의 그림자를 드리운다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
Etymology tree
Proto-Indo-European *bʰeg-der.
Proto-Germanic *bankiz
Proto-West Germanic *banki
Lombardic bankbor.
Italian bancabor.
Middle French ...
definition_en: An institution that provides financial services.

senses.gloss: An institution where one can place and borrow money and take care of financial affairs.
A branch office of such an institution.
An underwriter or controller of a card game.

examples.text: He went to the drawer in which he kept his money and took out several bank-notes.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 돈을 보관하던 서랍으로 가서 지폐 몇 장을 꺼냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His partner, in a violent letter, sent to his bank, had taunted him with hiding his whereabouts: and Strickland, in a cynical and humourous reply, had told his partner exactly where to find him.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 동업자가 은행으로 보낸 격렬한 편지에서 그가 행방을 숨기고 있다고 비난했는데, 스트릭랜드는 냉소적이고 유머러스한 답장으로 동업자에게 자신을 어디서 찾을 수 있는지 정확히 알려주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English derkly, derkely, derkliche, derkeliche; equivalent to dark + -ly. Compare Old English deorclīċe, a parallel formation.
definition_en: In a dark manner.

senses.gloss: With insufficient light for easy discernment or comprehension.
senses.example: I could make out his image darkly.

senses.gloss: With a dark appearance.
senses.example: He saw how the candlesticks shone darkly in the vicinity of the diamond flames in Shevele's ears and on her silk dress collar.

senses.gloss: In a manner which is not readily visible or noticeable; inconspicuously.

examples.text: She flushed darkly.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 얼굴이 시뻘겋게 달아올랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The beauty of the island is unveiled as diminishing distance shows you in distincter shape its lovely peaks, but it keeps its secret as you sail by, and, darkly inviolable, seems to fold itself together in a stony, inaccessible grimness.
examples.translation_ko: 거리가 줄어들면서 섬의 아름다운 봉우리들이 더욱 뚜렷한 모습을 드러내며 섬의 아름다움이 펼쳐지지만, 배가 지나쳐 갈 때에도 섬은 여전히 비밀을 간직한 채 어둡고 신성불가침한 모습으로 돌처럼 굳고 접근할 수 없는 험상궂음 속에 몸을 감싸고 있는 듯하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English luxurious, from Old French luxurios (modern French luxurieux), from Latin lū̆xuriōsus (“rank, luxuriant, profuse, excessive, im...
definition_en: Extremely comfortable or elegant.

senses.gloss: Very fine in quality and comfortable.
senses.example: a luxurious hotel suite

senses.gloss: Enjoying the pleasures of luxury, accustomed to luxury.
senses.example: Invalids, and luxurious persons, require more artificial arrangements for travelling on the camel.

examples.text: They were extravagantly luxurious.
examples.translation_ko: 그것들은 지나칠 정도로 호화로웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I imagined that she saw her husband installed in a luxurious suite of rooms, dining at one smart restaurant after another, and she pictured his days spent at race-meetings and his evenings at the play.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그녀가 남편이 호화로운 객실에 머물며 고급 레스토랑을 전전하고, 낮에는 경마장에서 저녁에는 극장에서 시간을 보내는 모습을 상상하고 있으리라 짐작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English helthe, from Old English hǣlþ, from Proto-West Germanic *hailiþu, from Proto-Germanic *hailiþō, from Proto-Germanic *...
definition_en: The state of being free from illness or injury.

senses.gloss: The state of being free from physical or psychological disease, illness, or malfunction; wellness.
senses.example: Her mental health is really affected by stressful environments.

senses.gloss: A state of well-being or balance, often physical but sometimes also mental and social; the overall level of function of an organism from the cellular (micro) level to the social (macro) level.
senses.example: The directors are concerned about the financial health of the project.

senses.gloss: Physical condition.

examples.text: There was so much to read, for one thing, and so much fine health to be pulled down out of the young breath-giving air.
examples.translation_ko: 우선 읽을 것이 너무나 많았고, 젊고 생기를 주는 공기에서 끌어낼 수 있는 건강함도 너무나 많았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His health will never stand it.”
examples.translation_ko: 몸이 견디지 못할 거예요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English contradiccioun, contradiction, from Old French contradiction, from Latin contrādictiō, from contrādīcō (“speak against”).
definition_en: A statement that contradicts another statement or a fact.

senses.gloss: The act of contradicting.
senses.example: His contradiction of the proposal was very interesting.

senses.gloss: A statement that contradicts itself, i.e., a statement that claims that the same thing is true and that it is false at the same time and in the same senses of the terms.
senses.example: There is a contradiction in what you say: she can't be both married and single.

senses.gloss: A logical inconsistency among two or more elements or propositions.
senses.example: Marx believed that the contradictions of capitalism would lead to socialism.

examples.text: Who could resolve the contradiction?
examples.translation_ko: 누가 이런 모순을 해결할 수 있겠는가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was puzzled by the contradictions that I saw in her behaviour.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 행동에서 보인 모순들이 나를 당황스럽게 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: The state of being sufficient or adequate.

senses.gloss: The quality or condition of being sufficient.
An adequate amount.
senses.example: But the Eastern front of the Allies was far more vulnerable. Russia could not begin to supply herself with a sufficiency of large guns and of heavy munitionment for them.

examples.text: Almost any exhibition of complete self-sufficiency draws a stunned tribute from me.
examples.translation_ko: 완전한 자족의 모습은 거의 언제나 내게서 놀란 듯한 찬사를 이끌어낸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was evident that she had been prepared to weep, for she had provided herself with a sufficiency of handkerchiefs; I admired her forethought, but in retrospect it made her tears perhaps less moving.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 울 준비를 해왔다는 것은 분명했다. 충분한 양의 손수건을 준비해왔기 때문이었다. 나는 그녀의 선견지명에 감탄했지만, 돌이켜보니 그것이 그녀의 눈물을 덜 감동적으로 만들었을지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Late Middle English perturben (“to disturb (someone) mentally, disquiet; to cause disorder to (something), confuse; to hinder (something)”), f...
definition_en: Cause trouble or disturbance.

senses.gloss: To disturb; to bother or unsettle.
To slightly modify the motion of an object.
To modify the motion of a body by exerting a gravitational force.

examples.text: Tom was evidently perturbed at Daisy’s running around alone, for on the following Saturday night he came with her to Gatsby’s party.
examples.translation_ko: 톰은 데이지가 혼자 돌아다니는 것을 분명히 못마땅해했던 모양이다. 그 다음 토요일 밤에는 그녀와 함께 개츠비의 파티에 왔기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I could not decide whether she desired the return of her husband because she loved him, or because she dreaded the tongue of scandal; and I was perturbed by the suspicion that the anguish of love contemned was alloyed in her broken heart with the pangs, sordid to my young mind, of wounded vanity.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 남편을 사랑해서 그의 귀환을 바라는 것인지, 아니면 세간의 험담이 두려워서인지 판단할 수 없었다. 그리고 경멸당한 사랑의 고뇌가 그녀의 상처받은 마음에서 상처받은 허영심의 고통과 뒤섞여 있다는 의혹이 나를 불안하게 했다. 그 허영심의 고통은 어린 내 마음에는 천박한 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Late Latin contradictorius, from Latin contradico.
definition_en: Expressing or containing a contradiction.

senses.gloss: That contradicts something, such as an argument.
That is itself a contradiction.
senses.example: Our attitudes toward sharks are contradictory. We fear them and yet we seek them out.

senses.gloss: That is diametrically opposed to something.
senses.example: Schemes […] contradictory to common sense.

examples.text: What a cruel practical joke old Nature played when she flung so many contradictory elements together, and left the man face to face with the perplexing callousness of the universe.
examples.translation_ko: 자연이라는 늙은 존재가 그토록 많은 모순된 요소들을 한데 뒤섞어놓고는, 인간을 우주의 당혹스러운 냉혹함과 마주하게 내버려둔 것이야말로 얼마나 잔인한 현실적 농담인가.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I had not yet learnt how contradictory is human nature; I did not know how much pose there is in the sincere, how much baseness in the noble, nor how much goodness in the reprobate.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 아직 인간의 본성이 얼마나 모순적인지 배우지 못했다. 진실한 것 속에 얼마나 많은 가식이 있는지, 고귀한 것 속에 얼마나 많은 비열함이 있는지, 타락한 자 속에 얼마나 많은 선량함이 있는지 알지 못했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French somptueux, from Latin sumptuōsus, from sūmptus (“cost, charge, expense”), from sumō (“I take”) + -tus (noun formation suffix).
definition_en: Extremely luxurious or elaborate.

senses.gloss: Magnificent, luxurious, splendid.
senses.example: Cabaye pulled all the strings in a dominant home performance and capped a majestic individual display with a sumptuous first-time finish into the far corner for his second goal of the afternoon.

examples.text: It had occurred to me that this shadow of a garage must be a blind, and that sumptuous and romantic apartments were concealed overhead, when the proprietor himself appeared in the door of an office, wiping his hands on a piece of waste.
examples.translation_ko: 이 정비소의 그림자 같은 곳은 위장일 뿐이고, 위층에는 호화롭고 낭만적인 방들이 숨겨져 있을 것이라는 생각이 들었는데, 바로 그때 사장이 사무실 문간에 나타나 헝겊 조각으로 손을 닦고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I had understood from Mrs. Strickland that it was a large and sumptuous place at the back of the Rue de Rivoli.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인에게서 들은 바로는 리볼리 가 뒤편에 있는 크고 호화로운 곳이라고 했는데 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English directorie, dyrectorye, from Medieval Latin dīrectōrium. Doublet of directorium.
definition_en: A list or table of names, addresses, and phone numbers.

senses.gloss: A list of names, addresses etc, of specific classes of people or organizations, often in alphabetical order or in some classification.
senses.example: look up an address in the directory

senses.gloss: A structured listing of the names and characteristics of the files on a storage device.
A virtual container in a computer's file system, in which files and other directories may be stored. The files and subdirectories in a directory are usually related.

examples.text: We looked it out in the directory.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 전화번호부를 뒤져보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I called for a directory and looked out the bakers.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 전화번호부를 달라고 해서 제빵소들을 찾아보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin subserviens, present active of subservio (“I serve under”).
definition_en: Showing a willingness to obey or be controlled by others.

senses.gloss: Useful in an inferior capacity.
Obsequiously submissive.

examples.text: And man, subservient to interests he has persuaded himself are greater than his own, makes himself a slave to his taskmaster.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 인간은 자신보다 더 위대하다고 스스로를 설득한 이익에 굴복하여, 자신을 그 주인의 노예로 만든다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was a street of small shops subservient to the needs of poor people, and about the middle of it, on the left as I walked down, was the Hôtel des Belges.
examples.translation_ko: 그곳은 가난한 사람들의 필요를 충족시키는 작은 상점들이 늘어선 거리였고, 내가 걸어 내려가면서 보니 거리 중간쯤 왼쪽에 벨기에 호텔이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English comparisoun, from Old French comparison, from Latin comparātiō, from comparātus, perfect passive participle of comparō.
definition_en: A process or act of comparing two or more things.

senses.gloss: The act of comparing or the state or process of being compared.
senses.example: to bring a thing into comparison with another

senses.gloss: An evaluation of the similarities and differences of one or more things relative to some other or each other.
senses.example: He made a careful comparison of the available products before buying anything.

senses.gloss: With a negation, the state of being similar or alike.
senses.example: There really is no comparison between the performance of today's computers and those of a decade ago.

examples.text: My own hotel was modest enough, but it was magnificent in comparison with this.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 묵고 있는 호텔도 소박한 편이었지만, 이곳과 비교하면 호화로웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is possible that Strickland hated the normal release of sex because it seemed to him brutal by comparison with the satisfaction of artistic creation.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드가 성적 욕구의 정상적인 해소를 증오했던 것은, 그것이 예술적 창조의 만족감에 비해 야만적으로 보였기 때문일 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English gilty, gulty, from Old English gyltiġ (“offending, guilty”); equivalent to guilt + -y.
definition_en: Feeling or showing that one has done something wrong.

senses.gloss: Responsible for a dishonest act.
senses.example: He was guilty of cheating at cards.

senses.gloss: Judged to have committed a crime.
senses.example: The guilty man was led away.

senses.gloss: Having a sense of guilt.
senses.example: Do you have a guilty conscience?

examples.text: Wilson was so sick that he looked guilty, unforgivably guilty—as if he had just got some poor girl with child.
examples.translation_ko: 윌슨은 너무 아파서 죄책감에 사로잡힌 것처럼, 용서받을 수 없을 만큼 죄스러운 것처럼 보였다. 마치 어떤 불쌍한 소녀를 임신시킨 것처럼 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was not here that Charles Strickland lived in guilty splendour with the unknown charmer for whose sake he had abandoned honour and duty.
examples.translation_ko: 찰스 스트릭랜드가 명예와 의무를 버리고까지 택한 정체불명의 요부와 함께 죄스러운 호사를 누리며 살고 있는 곳은 바로 여기가 아니었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English porter, portere, portier, borrowed from Anglo-Norman portour and Old French porteor, from Late Latin portātor, from past partic...
definition_en: A person who carries luggage or goods.

senses.gloss: A person who carries luggage and related objects.
senses.example: By the time I reached the train station I was exhausted, but fortunately there was a porter waiting.

senses.gloss: An ant having the specialized role of carrying.
One who ports software (makes it usable on another platform).
senses.example: […] useful only if you are a Perl porter or implementor and you want to check the efficiency of the hashing algorithm.

examples.text: There was a bench outside, on which it might be presumed the night porter passed uneasy nights.
examples.translation_ko: 밖에는 벤치가 하나 있었는데, 아마도 야간 수위가 불편한 밤을 보내는 곳인 듯했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But he found his traps waiting for him in the porter’s lodge, and the concierge told him that Blanche had gone out.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그는 관리사무소에서 자신의 짐들이 기다리고 있는 것을 발견했고, 관리인은 블랑슈가 외출했다고 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From slip + -er.
definition_en: A type of footwear that is typically worn indoors.

senses.gloss: A low soft shoe that can be slipped on and off easily.
Such a shoe intended for indoor use; a bedroom or house slipper.
senses.example: Get out of bed, put on your slippers, and come downstairs.

senses.gloss: A flip-flop (type of rubber sandal).

examples.text: All night the saxophones wailed the hopeless comment of the “Beale Street Blues” while a hundred pairs of golden and silver slippers shuffled the shining dust.
examples.translation_ko: 밤새도록 색소폰들이 "빌 스트리트 블루스"의 절망적인 논평을 울부짖는 동안, 수백 켤레의 금색과 은색 슬리퍼들이 반짝이는 먼지를 휘저었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was in shirt-sleeves and carpet slippers.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 셔츠 차림에 실내화를 신고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From earlier sixt, from Middle English sixte, from Old English siexta, from Proto-Germanic *sehstô, equivalent to six + -th (ordinal suffix).
definition_en: Being the sixth in a series or sequence.

senses.gloss: The ordinal form of the number six.
senses.example: As this sixth edition is published in 2011, it is exactly 25 years since the publication of the first edition in 1986. That, in itself, is a very sobering thought, for all kinds of reasons.

examples.text: On the sixth floor.”
examples.translation_ko: 6층에요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: At length I reached the sixth floor, and knocked at the door numbered thirty-two.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 6층에 도착해서 32번이라고 적힌 문을 두드렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From wash + stand.
definition_en: A piece of furniture for washing hands or face.

senses.gloss: A table containing a basin and a pitcher of water for washing.
In a stable or garage, a place in the floor prepared so that carriages or automobiles may be washed there and the water run off.
senses.example: Washstand in an Electric Garage. […] In a few garages arrangements are made for washing cars in any position on the storage floor, so that it is not necessary to move them on to and off the washrack.

examples.text: A universe of ineffable gaudiness spun itself out in his brain while the clock ticked on the washstand and the moon soaked with wet light his tangled clothes upon the floor.
examples.translation_ko: 세면대 위의 시계가 째깍거리고 달빛이 바닥에 어지럽게 흩어진 그의 옷가지들을 축축한 빛으로 적시는 동안, 형언할 수 없이 화려한 우주가 그의 뇌 속에서 펼쳐졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was a large wooden bedstead on which was a billowing red eiderdown, and there was a large wardrobe, a round table, a very small washstand, and two stuffed chairs covered with red rep.
examples.translation_ko: 붉은 솜이불이 부풀어 오른 큰 나무 침대가 하나 있었고, 큰 옷장과 둥근 탁자, 아주 작은 세면대, 그리고 붉은 모직으로 덮인 쿠션 의자 두 개가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English luxurie, from Old French luxurie, from Latin luxuria (“rankness, luxury”), from luxus (“extravagance, luxury”).
definition_en: A high standard or quality of something.

senses.gloss: Very wealthy and comfortable surroundings; the state of being that they create.
senses.example: Near-synonyms: splendor, grandeur, grandness, decadence

senses.gloss: Something desirable but expensive and that one can live without.
senses.example: “[…] We are engaged in a great work, a treatise on our river fortifications, perhaps? But since when did army officers afford the luxury of amanuenses in this simple republic? […]”

senses.gloss: Something that is pleasant and desirable but not necessary in life (whether expensive or not).

examples.text: Her porch was bright with the bought luxury of star-shine; the wicker of the settee squeaked fashionably as she turned toward him and he kissed her curious and lovely mouth.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 베란다는 돈으로 산 별빛의 사치로 환하게 빛났고, 그녀가 그를 향해 몸을 돌리자 긴 의자의 고리버들이 멋스럽게 삐걱거렸으며, 그는 그녀의 신비롭고 사랑스러운 입술에 입맞춤했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was no sign of the abandoned luxury that Colonel MacAndrew had so confidently described.
examples.translation_ko: 맥앤드류 대령이 그토록 자신 있게 묘사했던 방탕한 사치의 흔적은 어디에도 보이지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From confident + -ly.
definition_en: Feeling or showing complete trust in one's abilities.

senses.gloss: In a confident manner; with confidence; with strong assurance; positively.
senses.example: Alice confidently stepped up on the platform to give her maiden speech as CEO.

examples.text: This seemed to reassure him and he continued more confidently.
examples.translation_ko: 이 말이 그를 안심시키는 듯했고 그는 더 자신 있게 계속했다.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French jacquet, diminutive of Old French jaque.
definition_en: A short coat typically worn for warmth.

senses.gloss: A piece of clothing worn on the upper body outside a shirt or blouse, often waist length to thigh length.
A piece of a person's suit, beside trousers and, sometimes, waistcoat; coat (US)
A protective or insulating cover for an object (e.g. a book, hot water tank, bullet.)

examples.text: He wore an old Norfolk jacket, and he had not shaved for several days.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 낡은 노퍽 재킷을 입고 있었고, 며칠째 면도를 하지 않은 상태였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I wondered what a stranger would have taken him to be, sitting there in his old Norfolk jacket and his unbrushed bowler; his trousers were baggy, his hands were not clean; and his face, with the red stubble of the unshaved chin, the little eyes, and the large, aggressive nose, was uncouth and coarse.
examples.translation_ko: 낡은 노퍽 재킷과 솔질하지 않은 중절모를 쓰고 그곳에 앉아 있는 그를 보고 낯선 사람이라면 무엇이라고 생각했을까 궁금했다. 바지는 헐렁했고, 손은 깨끗하지 않았으며, 면도하지 않은 턱의 붉은 수염, 작은 눈, 크고 공격적인 코가 있는 얼굴은 거칠고 조야했다.

definition_en: A person who is biologically male.

senses.gloss: Belonging to the sex which typically produces sperm, or to the gender which is typically associated with it.
senses.example: We got the hang of [caring for a baby], Kate and I, with some quiet, surprising guidance from a gentle male nurse whose touching lack of intrusion was so instinctive as to seem part of the pattern.

senses.gloss: Characteristic of this sex/gender. (Compare masculine, manly.)
senses.example: stereotypically male interests, an insect with typically male coloration

senses.gloss: Tending to lead to or regulate the development of sexual characteristics typical of this sex.
senses.example: the male chromosome; like testes, ovaries also produce testosterone and some other male hormones

examples.text: There were clerks and shopgirls; old fellows who might have stepped out of the pages of Honore de Balzac; members, male and female, of the professions which make their profit of the frailties of mankind.

examples.text: It was a vision of the beginnings of the world, the Garden of Eden, with Adam and Eve—que sais-je?—it was a hymn to the beauty of the human form, male and female, and the praise of Nature, sublime, indifferent, lovely, and cruel.

senses.gloss: Belonging to the sex which typically produces eggs (ova), or to the gender which is typically associated with it.

senses.example: A travelling shot of a harbour view near Sydney's White Bay moves into a domestic interior as a female voice says, 'There was nowhere else to live except alone.'

etymology: From Middle English sugre, sucre, from Middle French sucre, from Old French çucre (circa 13th century), from Old Italian zucchero (or another verna...
definition_en: A sweet white or brownish powder used as a food ingredient.

senses.gloss: Sucrose in the form of small crystals, obtained from sugar cane or sugar beet and used to sweeten food and drink.
senses.example: Even in extreme cases such as chemical pollution in the Florida Everglades from heavily subsidized sugar farming, strong regulations are routinely blocked by industry.

senses.gloss: A specific variety of sugar.
Any of various small carbohydrates that are used by organisms to store energy.
senses.example: Although H. bertonii relies on scale insects to prepare its parasitism site on plants, it directly absorbs and utilizes plant sugars.

examples.text: Over the great bridge, with the sunlight through the girders making a constant flicker upon the moving cars, with the city rising up across the river in white heaps and sugar lumps all built with a wish out of nonolfactory money.
examples.translation_ko: 거대한 다리 위로, 철골 사이로 스며든 햇빛이 달리는 자동차들 위에 끊임없이 깜박이고, 강 건너편으로는 도시가 하얀 더미와 각설탕 덩어리처럼 솟아올라 있었는데, 모두 냄새 없는 돈으로 소망을 담아 지어진 것들이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The absinthe came, and with due solemnity we dropped water over the melting sugar.
examples.translation_ko: 압생트가 나왔고, 우리는 의식을 치르듯 녹아가는 설탕 위에 물을 떨어뜨렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Learned borrowing from Latin lūdicrus. First attested in 1619.
definition_en: Extremely foolish or absurd.

senses.gloss: Idiotic or unthinkable, often to the point of being funny; amusing by being plainly incongruous or absurd.
senses.example: He made a ludicrous attempt to run for office.

examples.text: It made my position complicated, not to say ludicrous.
examples.translation_ko: 이는 내 입장을 복잡하게 만들었고, 우스꽝스럽게 만들기까지 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When he told me this he put his hand to his cheek as though he still felt the smart of the blow, and in his eyes was a pain that was heartrending and an amazement that was ludicrous.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 내게 이 이야기를 할 때 그는 아직도 그 타격의 아픔을 느끼는 듯 손을 뺨에 갖다 댔고, 그의 눈에는 가슴 아픈 고통과 우스꽝스러운 놀라움이 담겨 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French hortatoire, from Latin hortor (“encourage”).
definition_en: Encouraging or advising someone to do something.

senses.gloss: Giving exhortation or advice; encouraging.
senses.example: Inextricably from its analyses and polemic, above all, The Communist Manifesto is hortatory, ‘a call to arms in the service of the revolution’.

examples.text: The words were ordinary enough, and to my mind there was in them something so hortatory that I almost smiled.
examples.translation_ko: 그 말들은 충분히 평범했고, 내 생각에는 그 안에 너무나 설교조인 무언가가 있어서 나는 거의 미소를 지을 뻔했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was prepared to be persuasive, touching, and hortatory, admonitory and expostulating, if need be vituperative even, indignant and sarcastic; but what the devil does a mentor do when the sinner makes no bones about confessing his sin?
examples.translation_ko: 나는 설득적이고 감동적이며 훈계하는 태도로, 필요하다면 꾸짖고 항의하며, 심지어 신랄하게 비난하고 분개하며 비꼬는 자세까지 취할 준비가 되어 있었다. 하지만 죄인이 자신의 죄를 스스럼없이 고백해버릴 때 도대체 스승은 무엇을 해야 한단 말인가?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English, from Old French contract, from Latin contractum, past participle of contrahere (“to bring together, to bring about, to conclud...
definition_en: A legally binding agreement between two or more parties.

senses.gloss: An agreement between two or more parties, to perform a specific job or work order, often temporary or of fixed duration and usually governed by a written agreement.
senses.example: sign a contract

senses.gloss: An agreement which the law will enforce in some way. A legally binding contract must contain at least one promise, i.e., a commitment or offer, by an offeror to and accepted by an offeree to do something in the future. A contract is thus executory rather than executed.
The document containing such an agreement.

examples.text: I might have spoken of the economic position of woman, of the contract, tacit and overt, which a man accepts by his marriage, and of much else; but I felt that there was only one point which really signified.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 여성의 경제적 지위나, 남자가 결혼으로써 받아들이는 암묵적이고 명시적인 계약, 그리고 그 밖의 여러 가지에 대해 말할 수도 있었지만, 정말 중요한 것은 오직 한 가지뿐이라고 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: One day they had a stroke of luck: one of the boarding-masters got a contract to paint a tramp that had come in from Madagascar round the Cape of Good Hope, and they spent several days on a plank hanging over the side, covering the rusty hull with paint.
examples.translation_ko: 어느 날 그들에게 행운이 찾아왔다. 하숙집 주인 중 한 명이 희망봉을 돌아 마다가스카르에서 온 화물선에 페인트칠을 하는 계약을 따냈고, 그들은 며칠 동안 배 옆구리에 매달린 널빤지 위에서 녹슨 선체에 페인트를 칠했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From late 17th century French effronterie, from effronté (“shameless, insolent”), from Old French esfronté, from Vulgar Latin *exfrontātus. Compare...
definition_en: The quality of being extremely bold or impudent.

senses.gloss: Insolent and shameless audacity.
senses.example: We even had the effrontery to suggest that he should leave the country.

senses.gloss: An act of insolent and shameless audacity.
senses.example: Any refusal to salute the president shall be counted as an effrontery.

examples.text: He was generous, and the needy, laughing at him because he believed so naively their stories of distress, borrowed from him with effrontery.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 관대했고, 궁핍한 사람들은 그가 자신들의 곤경담을 순진하게 믿는다고 비웃으면서도 뻔뻔스럽게 그에게서 돈을 빌렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The matter was immensely serious for all the parties concerned, but there was in the manner of his answer such a cheerful effrontery that I had to bite my lips in order not to laugh.
examples.translation_ko: 관련된 모든 당사자들에게는 엄청나게 심각한 문제였지만, 그의 대답하는 태도에는 너무나 명랑한 뻔뻔함이 있어서 나는 웃음이 터지지 않도록 입술을 깨물어야 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Extremely unpleasant or repulsive.

senses.gloss: Worthy of, or causing, abhorrence, as a thing of evil omen; odious in the utmost degree; very hateful; detestable; loathsome; execrable.
Excessive, large (used as an intensifier).
Very bad or inferior.

examples.text: “He’s abominable.”
examples.translation_ko: "혐오스러운 놈이지."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I reminded myself that his behaviour was abominable.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그의 행동이 가증스럽다고 스스로에게 상기시켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English swyn, swin, from Old English swīn, from Proto-West Germanic *swīn, from Proto-Germanic *swīną, from an adjectival form of Proto...
definition_en: A group of domestic or feral pigs.

senses.gloss: A pig (the animal).
The Zimmerman farm introduced swine to their husbandry.
A contemptible person (plural swine or swines).

examples.text: “Everyone will think you a perfect swine.”
examples.translation_ko: "모든 사람이 당신을 완전한 인간 쓰레기라고 생각할 텐데요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Well, Charlie stuck it for a bit, then he stepped forward and he just said: ‘Get out, you bloody swine.’
examples.translation_ko: 글쎄, 찰리는 잠시 참고 있다가 앞으로 나서서 이렇게 말했어. '꺼져, 이 더러운 돼지 같은 놈아.'

etymology: From Middle English, from Old French, from stem of Late Latin prōtectiō (“a covering over”), from Latin prōtēctus, perfect passive participle of pr...
definition_en: The act of protecting something or someone from harm.

senses.gloss: The process of keeping (something or someone) safe.
senses.example: Raincoats give protection from rain.

senses.gloss: The state of being safe.
A means of keeping or remaining safe.

examples.text: “I suppose the law has some protection to offer them.”
examples.translation_ko: "법이 그들에게 어느 정도 보호를 제공할 것이라고 생각한다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She had abandoned the safe shelter of her husband’s protection and the comfortable ease of a well-provided establishment for what she could not but see was an extreme hazard.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 남편의 보호라는 안전한 피난처와 넉넉한 살림의 편안함을 버리고, 누가 봐도 극도로 위험한 일에 뛰어든 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Cause to become narrow or restricted.

senses.gloss: To make strait; to narrow or confine to a smaller space.
senses.example: The channel straitened the river through the town, made it flow faster, and caused more flooding upstream.

senses.gloss: To restrict or diminish, especially financially.
senses.example: Rising costs put those on fixed incomes in straitened circumstances.

senses.gloss: Misspelling of straighten.

examples.text: It was true that his hotel pointed to the most straitened circumstances.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 머물고 있는 호텔을 보면 정말로 극도로 궁핍한 상황임이 분명했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was a very modest position that he occupied, and there was about him an air of straitened circumstance.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 맡고 있는 직책은 매우 소박한 것이었고, 그에게는 궁핍한 처지의 분위기가 감돌았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A person who mocks or teases others.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of mock

examples.text: He was perfectly cool, and his eyes kept that mocking smile which made all I said seem rather foolish.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 완전히 침착했고, 그의 눈에는 내가 하는 말을 모두 바보스럽게 만드는 조롱하는 미소가 계속 떠올라 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He stood before me, motionless, with a mocking smile in his eyes; but for all that, for a moment I had an inkling of a fiery, tortured spirit, aiming at something greater than could be conceived by anything that was bound up with the flesh.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내 앞에 움직이지 않고 서서 눈에 조롱하는 미소를 띠고 있었다. 하지만 그럼에도 불구하고 한순간 나는 육체에 얽매인 그 어떤 것으로도 상상할 수 없는 더 위대한 무언가를 추구하는, 불타오르고 고뇌하는 영혼의 기미를 감지했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English feynen, feinen, borrowed from Old French feindre (“to pretend”), from Latin fingere (“to form, shape, invent”). Compare French ...
definition_en: Pretend to have a feeling or quality that you do not really have.

senses.gloss: To make a false show or pretence of; to counterfeit or simulate.
senses.example: The pupil feigned sickness on the day of his exam.

senses.gloss: To imagine; to invent; to pretend to do something.
senses.example: He feigned that he had gone home at the appointed time.

senses.gloss: To make an action as if doing one thing, but actually doing another, for example to trick an opponent; to feint.

examples.text: Most of the confidences were unsought—frequently I have feigned sleep, preoccupation, or a hostile levity when I realized by some unmistakable sign that an intimate revelation was quivering on the horizon; for the intimate revelations of young men, or at least the terms in which they express them, are usually plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions.
examples.translation_ko: 대부분의 고백은 내가 원하지 않은 것들이었다—친밀한 폭로가 수평선에서 떨리고 있다는 확실한 징조를 알아챘을 때, 나는 종종 잠든 척, 딴 생각에 빠진 척, 혹은 적대적인 경박함을 가장했다. 젊은 남자들의 친밀한 폭로는, 적어도 그들이 그것을 표현하는 방식은, 대개 표절에 가깝고 명백한 억압으로 인해 흠이 있기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He looked at me with an astonishment that was certainly not feigned.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 분명히 꾸며낸 것이 아닌 놀라움으로 나를 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From uproarious + -ly.
definition_en: Causing or characterized by loud and uncontrolled laughter.

senses.gloss: In an uproarious manner.
senses.example: From the first frames, it reveals itself as an outrageously, uproariously sexed-up piece of work, stylishly directed by Alfonso Cuaron from a script by his brother Carlos.

examples.text: He laughed so uproariously that people sitting near us looked round, and some of them began to laugh too.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 너무 요란하게 웃어서 우리 근처에 앉은 사람들이 돌아보았고, 그들 중 몇몇도 따라 웃기 시작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Round the room people were sitting at table, here half a dozen sailors uproariously drunk, there a group of soldiers; and in the middle, crowded together, couples were dancing.
examples.translation_ko: 방 안 곳곳의 테이블에는 사람들이 앉아 있었는데, 한쪽에는 술에 만취한 선원 여섯 명이 떠들어대고 있었고, 다른 쪽에는 군인들이 무리를 이루고 있었다. 그리고 가운데서는 커플들이 빽빽이 모여 춤을 추고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Learned borrowing from Latin ingenuus (“of noble character, frank”). Doublet of ingenu.
definition_en: Having or showing a natural and sincere quality.

senses.gloss: Naive and trusting.
Demonstrating childlike simplicity.
senses.example:
"Do you mean to say you didn't leave your wife for another woman?"
"Of course not."
"On your word of honour?"
I don't know why I asked for that. It was very ingenuous of me.

senses.gloss: Unsophisticated; clumsy or obvious.
senses.example: There was nothing more I dared say. My ingenuous attempts to lie my way out of trouble had only served to get me in deeper and deeper.

examples.text: It was very ingenuous of me.
examples.translation_ko: 참으로 순진한 질문이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I should have liked you better if you hadn’t made that ingenuous appeal to my sympathies.”
examples.translation_ko: "당신이 내 동정심에 그렇게 순진하게 호소하지 않았다면 더 좋아했을 텐데."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English miracle, from Old French miracle, from Latin mīrāculum (“object of wonder”), from mīror (“to wonder at”), from mīrus (“wonderfu...
definition_en: A surprising and welcome event or situation that is not explicable by natural laws.

senses.gloss: An event that appears inexplicable by the laws of nature and so is held to be supernatural in origin.
senses.example: Many religious beliefs are based on miracles.

senses.gloss: A fortunate outcome that prevails despite overwhelming odds against it.
senses.example: It was a miracle that I survived that ditching in the high waves because I had my seat belt and shoulder harness unbuckled in anticipation of bailing out.

senses.gloss: An awesome and exceptional example of something.
senses.example: It was a miracle of engineering that made possible, with the cheap electricity the dam generated, another kind of miracle: the bizarre, superilluminated city of Las Vegas, Nevada.

examples.text: Her kitchen was a miracle of clean brightness.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 부엌은 깨끗하고 밝은 기적 같은 공간이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Of course a miracle may happen, and you may be a great painter, but you must confess the chances are a million to one against it.
examples.translation_ko: "물론 기적이 일어날 수도 있고, 당신이 위대한 화가가 될 수도 있겠지만, 그럴 가능성은 백만 분의 일이라는 걸 인정해야 할 거야.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Derived from Old French folie (“madness”), from the adjective fol (“mad, insane”).
definition_en: A foolish or senseless act.

senses.gloss: Foolishness that results from a lack of foresight or lack of practicality.
senses.example: It would be folly to walk all that way, knowing the shops are probably shut by now.

senses.gloss: Thoughtless action resulting in tragic consequence.
senses.example: The purchase of Alaska from Russia was termed Seward's folly.

senses.gloss: A fanciful building built for purely ornamental reasons.
senses.example: A luncheonette in the shape of a coffee cup is particularly conspicuous, as is intended of an architectural duck or folly.

examples.text: “I don’t see why, unless it’s folly to say the obvious.”
examples.translation_ko: "뻔한 얘기를 하는 게 어리석은 일이 아니라면, 왜 그런지 모르겠군."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The experience of life shows that people are constantly doing things which must lead to disaster, and yet by some chance manage to evade the result of their folly.
examples.translation_ko: 인생 경험을 보면 사람들은 끊임없이 재앙으로 이어질 수밖에 없는 일들을 저지르면서도, 어떤 우연한 기회로 자신의 어리석음이 초래할 결과를 피해 나간다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English swymmen, from Old English swimman (“to swim, float”) (class III strong verb; past tense swamm, past participle geswummen), from...
definition_en: To move through water using the arms and legs.

senses.gloss: To move through the water, without touching the bottom; to propel oneself in water by natural means.
senses.example: We were now all upon a Level, as to our travelling; being unshipp’d, for our Bark would swim no farther, and she was too heavy to carry on our Backs […]

senses.gloss: To become immersed in, or as if in, or flooded with, or as if with, a liquid
senses.example: swimming in self-pity

senses.gloss: To move around freely because of excess space.
senses.example: A fam'd Sur-tout he wears, which once was blue, / And his foot swims in a capacious shoe.

examples.text: They can swim as well as the natives.
examples.translation_ko: 원주민들만큼 수영을 잘합니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When a man falls into the water it doesn’t matter how he swims, well or badly: he’s got to get out or else he’ll drown.”
examples.translation_ko: 사람이 물에 빠지면 헤엄을 잘 치든 못 치든 상관없어. 나오지 않으면 익사하고 말 테니까."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English spit, a shortening of despit (whence despite), from Old French despit, from Latin dēspectum (“looking down on”), from Latin dēs...
definition_en: A feeling of bitter anger or resentment.

senses.gloss: Ill will or hatred toward another, accompanied with the desire to unjustifiably irritate, annoy, or thwart; a want to disturb or put out another; mild malice
senses.example: He was so filled with spite for his ex-wife, his brother was afraid of what he might do.

senses.gloss: Vexation; chagrin; mortification.
senses.example: "The time is out of joint: O cursed spite."

examples.text: In spite of the wives’ agreement that such malevolence was beyond credibility, the dispute ended in a short struggle, and both wives were lifted, kicking, into the night.
examples.translation_ko: 그런 악의가 믿을 수 없을 정도라는 아내들의 의견 일치에도 불구하고, 다툼은 짧은 몸싸움으로 끝났고, 두 아내 모두 발길질을 하며 밤 속으로 끌려나갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was real passion in his voice, and in spite of myself I was impressed.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 목소리에는 진정한 열정이 담겨 있었고, 나도 모르게 감동을 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Having a strong and favorable impression.

senses.gloss: strongly affected, especially favourably
senses.example: I was impressed with the cleanliness of the hotel.

senses.gloss: stamped, under pressure
compelled to serve in a military force

examples.text: I was strangely impressed.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이상하게 감명을 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There was real passion in his voice, and in spite of myself I was impressed.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 목소리에는 진정한 열정이 담겨 있었고, 나도 모르게 감동을 받았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English uncouth, from Old English uncūþ (“unknown; unfamiliar; strange”), from Proto-West Germanic *unkunþ, from Proto-Germanic *unkunþ...
definition_en: Lacking refinement or polish.

senses.gloss: Unfamiliar, strange, foreign.
senses.example: There was a delicious sensation of mingled security and awe with which I looked down, from my giddy height, on the monsters of the deep at their uncouth gambols.

senses.gloss: Clumsy, awkward.
Unrefined, crude.
senses.example: I don't want to associate with uncouth people.

examples.text: I wondered what a stranger would have taken him to be, sitting there in his old Norfolk jacket and his unbrushed bowler; his trousers were baggy, his hands were not clean; and his face, with the red stubble of the unshaved chin, the little eyes, and the large, aggressive nose, was uncouth and coarse.
examples.translation_ko: 낡은 노퍽 재킷과 솔질하지 않은 중절모를 쓰고 그곳에 앉아 있는 그를 보고 낯선 사람이라면 무엇이라고 생각했을까 궁금했다. 바지는 헐렁했고, 손은 깨끗하지 않았으며, 면도하지 않은 턱의 붉은 수염, 작은 눈, 크고 공격적인 코가 있는 얼굴은 거칠고 조야했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His appearance was wild and uncouth; there was aloofness in his eyes and sensuality in his mouth; he was big and strong; he gave the impression of untamed passion; and perhaps she felt in him, too, that sinister element which had made me think of those wild beings of the world’s early history when matter, retaining its early connection with the earth, seemed to possess yet a spirit of its own.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 모습은 거칠고 조야했다. 그의 눈에는 냉담함이, 입에는 관능이 있었다. 그는 크고 강했으며, 길들여지지 않은 열정의 인상을 주었다. 그리고 아마도 그녀는 그에게서도 그 불길한 요소를 느꼈을 것이다. 그것은 물질이 대지와의 초기 연결을 유지하며 아직 고유한 정신을 지니고 있는 듯했던 세계 초기 역사의 야생 존재들을 떠올리게 했던 바로 그 요소였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English a-fresche, equivalent to a- + fresh. Compare Old English afersċean (“to freshen; become fresh”).
definition_en: Freshly or anew.

senses.gloss: Anew; again; once more.
senses.example: We ditched the original design and decided to start afresh.

examples.text: “She’s willing to forget everything that’s happened and start afresh.
examples.translation_ko: "부인은 지금까지 일어난 모든 일을 잊고 새로 시작할 용의가 있습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I gave up my small apartment, sold my few belongings, and resolved to start afresh.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 작은 아파트를 정리하고 얼마 안 되는 소지품을 팔아치운 뒤, 새롭게 시작하기로 결심했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English certeynte (“surety”), from Anglo-Norman certeinte, from Old French certeinete, from Vulgar Latin *certānitās, from Latin certus.
definition_en: A state of being absolutely sure about something.

senses.gloss: The state of being certain.
senses.example: The certainty of punishment is the truest security against crimes.

senses.gloss: An instance of being certain.
A fact or truth unquestionably established.
senses.example: There is a certainty attainable. A certainty of feeling will arise through the very contemplation of Jesus. But there is also attainable a certainty of Reason.

examples.text: “I wonder if I could write on a desert island, with the certainty that no eyes but mine would ever see what I had written.”
examples.translation_ko: "아무도 보지 않을 것이라는 확신 속에서, 오직 내 눈만이 내가 쓴 것을 볼 무인도에서 글을 쓸 수 있을까 하는 생각이 든다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But the fear of not being able to carry it through effectively has always made me shy of assuming the moral attitude; and in this case the certainty that my sentiments would be lost on Strickland made it peculiarly embarrassing to utter them.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 효과적으로 해낼 수 없을지도 모른다는 두려움 때문에 나는 늘 도덕적 자세를 취하는 것을 꺼려했고, 이 경우에는 내 감정이 스트릭랜드에게 전혀 통하지 않을 것이 확실했기에 그것을 입 밖에 내는 것이 특히 난처했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English hardenen, equivalent to hard + -en. Cognate with Danish hærdne (“to harden; cure”), Swedish hårdna (“to harden”), Norwegian her...
definition_en: Become stronger or more resistant.

senses.gloss: To become hard.
To make something hard or harder.
To strengthen.

examples.text: His brown, hardening body lived naturally through the half-fierce, half-lazy work of the bracing days.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 갈색으로 단단해진 몸은 상쾌한 나날의 반은 격렬하고 반은 나른한 일을 통해 자연스럽게 살아갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I had the appetite of youth and he of a hardened conscience.
examples.translation_ko: 나에게는 젊음의 식욕이 있었고 그에게는 무감각해진 양심의 식욕이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English taverne, from Old French taverne (“wine shop”), from Latin taberna (“inn”). Doublet of taberna and taverna.
definition_en: A building where food and drink are served.

senses.gloss: A restaurant or bar.
A building containing a bar licensed to sell alcoholic drinks, and offering sleeping accommodations for travelers.
senses.example: At one of the way-stations on his long journey a barmaid at a tavern speaks to Gilgamesh and tries to give him common sense on the human condition.

examples.text: Then we went to a tavern to have coffee and liqueurs.
examples.translation_ko: 그다음 우리는 커피와 리큐어를 마시러 선술집에 갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There were a number of harlots in the tavern: some were sitting with men, others by themselves; and presently I noticed that one of these was looking at us.
examples.translation_ko: 선술집에는 여러 명의 창녀들이 있었는데, 어떤 이들은 남자들과 함께 앉아 있고 어떤 이들은 혼자 있었다. 그런데 곧 그중 한 명이 우리를 바라보고 있다는 것을 알아챘다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Unadapted borrowing from French liqueur. Doublet of liquor.
definition_en: A sweet, flavored liquid used in cooking and as a digestif after meals.

senses.gloss: A flavored alcoholic beverage that is usually very sweet and contains a high percentage of alcohol.

examples.text: Then we went to a tavern to have coffee and liqueurs.
examples.translation_ko: 그다음 우리는 커피와 리큐어를 마시러 선술집에 갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We had all the champagne we could drink and liqueurs to follow.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 마실 수 있는 만큼 샴페인을 마셨고, 그 다음엔 리큐어까지 들이켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English temperament, borrowed from Middle French tempérament, from Latin temperāmentum.
definition_en: A person's natural disposition or character.

senses.gloss: A person's usual manner of thinking, behaving or reacting.
senses.example: President Taft did not have the temperament either to dominate or to work with his Congress.

senses.gloss: A tendency to become irritable or angry.
The altering of certain intervals from their correct values in order to improve the moving from key to key.

examples.text: To a certain temperament the situation might have seemed intriguing—my own instinct was to telephone immediately for the police.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 성격의 사람에게는 이 상황이 흥미진진해 보일 수도 있었겠지만, 내 본능은 즉시 경찰에 전화를 거는 것이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It requires the feminine temperament to repeat the same thing three times with unabated zest.
examples.translation_ko: 같은 말을 세 번 반복해도 열정이 식지 않으려면 여성적 기질이 필요하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From rough + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is approximate or not exact.

senses.gloss: In a rough manner; without kindness, softness, or gentleness.
senses.example: They treated the prisoners roughly [...] slashing pitilessly with their whips to drive them as wretched animals before them.

senses.gloss: Unevenly or irregularly.
Without precision or exactness; imprecisely but close to in quantity or amount; approximately.
senses.example: Of the roughly 400 emerging infectious diseases that have been identified since 1940, more than 60% are zoonotic: ie they came from animals. Throughout history this has been common.

examples.text: “Let’s have some gas!” cried Tom roughly.
examples.translation_ko: "기름 좀 넣어줘!" 톰이 거칠게 소리쳤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “That sort of thing makes me sick,” he said roughly.
examples.translation_ko: "그런 식의 일은 역겹다." 그가 거칠게 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From bore + -dom.
definition_en: A feeling of listlessness and boredom.

senses.gloss: The state of being bored.
senses.example: […]only last Sunday, my Lady, in the desolation of Boredom and the clutch of Giant Despair, almost hated her own maid for being in spirits.

senses.gloss: An instance or period of being bored; a bored state.
senses.example: See more citations at boredoms.

examples.text: Gatsby, his hands still in his pockets, was reclining against the mantelpiece in a strained counterfeit of perfect ease, even of boredom.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 두 손을 주머니에 넣은 채 벽난로 선반에 기대어 있었는데, 완벽한 여유로움, 아니 지루함까지 가장하려 애쓰는 모습이 어색했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: If, seized by an intolerable boredom, he had determined to be a painter merely to break with irksome ties, it would have been comprehensible, and commonplace; but commonplace is precisely what I felt he was not.
examples.translation_ko: 만약 참을 수 없는 권태감에 사로잡혀 성가신 속박에서 벗어나려는 목적만으로 화가가 되기로 결심했다면, 그것은 이해할 만하고 평범한 일이었을 것이다. 하지만 평범함이야말로 그에게는 전혀 어울리지 않는다고 내가 느끼는 바였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English irkesome, irksum, equivalent to irk + -some, or perhaps continuing (in altered form) from Old English weorcsum (“painful, hurtf...
definition_en: Causing annoyance or frustration.

senses.gloss: Marked by irritation or annoyance; disagreeable; troublesome by reason of long continuance or repetition
senses.example: He has this irksome habit of racing up to red lights, so he has to brake heavily.

examples.text: It was irksome.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 성가신 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: If, seized by an intolerable boredom, he had determined to be a painter merely to break with irksome ties, it would have been comprehensible, and commonplace; but commonplace is precisely what I felt he was not.
examples.translation_ko: 만약 참을 수 없는 권태감에 사로잡혀 성가신 속박에서 벗어나려는 목적만으로 화가가 되기로 결심했다면, 그것은 이해할 만하고 평범한 일이었을 것이다. 하지만 평범함이야말로 그에게는 전혀 어울리지 않는다고 내가 느끼는 바였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Obtained or brought something.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of fetch

examples.text: “All that seems to me very far-fetched,” she said acidly.
examples.translation_ko: "그런 말씀은 모두 너무 억지스럽게 들립니다." 그녀가 신랄하게 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: At last, because I was romantic, I devised an explanation which I acknowledged to be far-fetched, but which was the only one that in any way satisfied me.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 낭만적인 성향의 나는 억지스럽다고 스스로 인정하면서도, 어떻게든 나를 만족시킬 수 있는 유일한 설명을 고안해냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English creacion, creacioun, creation, from Old French creacion (French création), from Latin creātiō, creātiōnis; equivalent to create...
definition_en: The act of creating something.

senses.gloss: Something created such as an invention or artwork.
senses.example: I think the manufacturer was so ashamed of its creation that it didn't put its name on it!

senses.gloss: The act of creating something.
senses.example: The restructure resulted in the creation of a number of shared services.

definition_en: A person employed to obtain secret information about an organization or government.

senses.gloss: A person who secretly watches and examines the actions of other individuals or organizations and gathers information on them (usually to gain an advantage).
senses.example:
The dead leap at the throat, destroy
The meaning of the day; dark forms
Have scaled your walls, and spies betray
Old secrets to amorphous swarms.

senses.gloss: A defensive player assigned to cover an offensive backfield player man-to-man when they are expected to engage in a running play, but the offensive player does not run with the ball immediately.

examples.text: “I don’t think it’s so much that,” argued Lucille sceptically; “It’s more that he was a German spy during the war.”
examples.translation_ko: "그런 건 아닌 것 같아요." 루실이 회의적으로 반박했다. "전쟁 중에 독일 스파이였다는 게 더 맞을 거예요."

examples.text: It is the spy seated in the central stronghold of the ego.

etymology: From Latin ego (“I”). Chosen by Freud’s translator as a translation of his use of German Ich as a noun for this concept from the pronoun ich (“I”)....
definition_en: The part of the mind that knows and reflects on itself.

senses.gloss: The self, especially with a sense of self-importance.
The most central part of the mind, which mediates with one's surroundings.
senses.example: ‘Everything begins with “I”, you mean. Which is ego,’ said Tom, placing an ankle behind his ear, ‘not id.’

senses.gloss: A person's self-esteem and opinion of themselves.
senses.example: My columns in the early days of the Labour government often featured John Prescott, who was in charge of transport as part of a mega-department created to match his ego.

examples.text: It is the spy seated in the central stronghold of the ego.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 자아의 중심 요새에 앉아 있는 스파이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He is no longer an individual, but a thing, an instrument to some purpose foreign to his ego.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 더 이상 개인이 아니라 하나의 사물, 자신의 자아와는 무관한 어떤 목적을 위한 도구가 되어버린다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To look at someone with admiration or adoration.

senses.gloss: A young deer.
A pale brown colour tinted with yellow, like that of a fawn.
The young of an animal; a whelp.
senses.example: she [the tigress] rageth upon the shore and the sands, for the losse of her fawnes

examples.text: At last, like a courtier fawning on the royal stick that is laid about his shoulders, he prides himself on the sensitiveness of his conscience.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was constantly offending Dirk Stroeve so bitterly that he flung away, vowing he would never speak to him again; but there was a solid force in Strickland that attracted the fat Dutchman against his will, so that he came back, fawning like a clumsy dog, though he knew that his only greeting would be the blow he dreaded.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 끊임없이 더크 스트루브를 몹시 화나게 해서 스트루브가 다시는 그와 말하지 않겠다고 맹세하며 뛰쳐나가게 만들었지만, 스트릭랜드에게는 뚱뚱한 네덜란드인의 의지와는 반대로 그를 끌어당기는 확고한 힘이 있어서, 스트루브는 자신을 맞이할 것이 두려워하는 매질뿐이라는 것을 알면서도 서툰 개처럼 아첨하며 다시 돌아오곤 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From sensitive + -ness.
definition_en: The quality of being easily affected or offended.

senses.gloss: The quality or degree of being sensitive.
The ability to perceive sensation.
The ability to be aware of (and, usually, react with regard to) the feelings of others.

examples.text: It is a melody that he sings to you, and to hear it again in your own heart you want knowledge and sensitiveness and imagination.”
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 예술가가 당신에게 들려주는 선율이며, 당신 마음속에서 그 선율을 다시 듣기 위해서는 지식과 감수성과 상상력이 필요하오."

examples.translation_ko: 마침내 자신의 어깨를 내리치는 왕의 지팡이에 아첨하는 신하처럼, 그는 자신의 양심이 예민한 것을 자랑스러워한다.

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French urgent (“pressing, impelling”), from Latin urgēns, from urgēre (“to press”), from Proto-Indo-European *werǵʰ- (“bind, s...
definition_en: Requiring immediate attention.

senses.gloss: Requiring immediate attention.
senses.example: An urgent appeal was sent out for assistance.

senses.gloss: Of people: insistent, solicitous.
senses.example: My kind friends here are most affectionately urgent with me to prolong my stay […].

examples.text: It was the first time he had called on me, though I had gone to two of his parties, mounted in his hydroplane, and, at his urgent invitation, made frequent use of his beach.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 나를 찾아온 것은 이번이 처음이었다. 나는 그의 파티에 두 번 참석했고, 그의 수상비행기를 타봤으며, 그의 간곡한 권유로 그의 해변을 자주 이용했건만.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When I reached London I found waiting for me an urgent request that I should go to Mrs. Strickland’s as soon after dinner as I could.
examples.translation_ko: 런던에 도착했을 때, 저녁 식사 후 가능한 한 빨리 스트릭랜드 부인을 찾아달라는 긴급한 부탁이 나를 기다리고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English playnly, pleinly, pleyneliche, equivalent to plain + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is clear or obvious.

senses.gloss: In a plain manner; simply; basically.
senses.example: She decorated the room plainly but neatly.

senses.gloss: Obviously; clearly.
senses.example: You will see that ours is plainly the better method.

examples.text: Mrs. Strickland was plainly nervous.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인은 명백히 초조해하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Her hair, brown and abundant, was plainly done, her face was very pale, and her features were good without being distinguished.
examples.translation_ko: 갈색의 풍성한 머리카락은 소박하게 빗어 올렸고, 얼굴은 매우 창백했으며, 이목구비는 뛰어나지는 않지만 단정했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English hatter; equivalent to hat + -er.
definition_en: A person who makes and sells hats.

senses.gloss: A person who makes, sells, or repairs hats.
A person who lives alone in the bush.
senses.example:
Lonely hut where drought’s eternal, suffocating atmosphere
Where the God-forgotten hatter dreams of city life and beer.

senses.gloss: A miner who works by himself.

examples.text: “He must be as mad as a hatter,” exclaimed the Colonel.
examples.translation_ko: "완전히 미쳤군!" 대령이 외쳤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “The Captain must have thought you as mad as a hatter,” I smiled.
examples.translation_ko: "선장은 당신을 완전히 미친 사람으로 생각했을 거예요." 내가 웃으며 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English chaf, from Old English ċeaf, from Proto-West Germanic *kaf. Cognate with Scots caff, Saterland Frisian Sääf, West Frisian tsjêf...
definition_en: Separate grain from chaff.

senses.gloss: The inedible parts of a grain-producing plant.
senses.example: To separate out the chaff, early cultures tossed baskets of grain into the air and let the wind blow away the lighter chaff.

senses.gloss: Straw or hay cut up fine for the food of cattle.
Any excess or unwanted material, resource, or person; anything worthless.
senses.example: Who that has prided himself on his spiritual strength has not seen it humbled to the dust? A knowledge of religion, as distinguished from experience, seems but chaff in such moments of trial.

examples.text: We used to chaff him.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 그를 놀리곤 했어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I was on the point of chaffing him on his state.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 상태를 놀려줄 참이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin incongruus, from in- (“not”) + congruus (“congruent”), equivalent to in- + congruous.
definition_en: Not harmonious or consistent with its surroundings.

senses.gloss: Not similar or congruent; not matching or fitting in.
senses.example: A slightly incongruous note is struck by the National Westminster Bank beside the Vine [pub], a tiny dolls' house of a building, about the size of a garden shed, in herringbone-patterned brick.

senses.gloss: Of two numbers, with respect to a third, such that their difference can not be divided by it without a remainder.
senses.example: 20 and 25 are incongruous with respect to 4.

examples.text: His plumpness and his red, fat cheeks made his mourning not a little incongruous.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 통통한 몸매와 붉고 살찐 볼은 그의 상복 차림을 적잖이 어울리지 않게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I thought it could hardly have failed to strike them that there was something incongruous in him.
examples.translation_ko: 그들이 그에게서 뭔가 어울리지 않는 구석이 있다는 것을 눈치채지 못했을 리 없다고 나는 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From derisive + -ly.
definition_en: In a mocking or scornful manner.

senses.gloss: In a derisive manner; demeaningly, mockingly.

examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 "교양"을 비웃듯이 말했다.

examples.translation_ko: "그리고 훌륭한 요리사이기도 하고." 스트릭랜드가 조롱하듯 덧붙였다.

etymology:
Etymology tree
English mind
English -ed
English minded
From mind + -ed. Compare Old English -mōd (“minded”), Old English ġehyġd (“minded; disposed”).
definition_en: Having a particular opinion or attitude.

senses.gloss: Having or exemplifying a mind of the stated type, nature or inclination.
senses.example: Downtown merchants can’t condone sending the spend-minded to Lancaster Mall, where they can park without fear in mega-macadam lots.

senses.gloss: Having a preference for doing something; having a likelihood, or disposition to carry out an act.
senses.example: I am minded to refuse the request.

examples.text: I wouldn’t have minded sacrifices.
examples.translation_ko: 희생도 마다하지 않았을 거예요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But no one was more single-minded than Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 스트릭랜드만큼 한 가지에만 몰두하는 사람은 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: Unwillingness or inability to believe; doubt about the truth or verisimilitude of something; disbelief.

senses.gloss: Religious disbelief; lack of faith.

etymology: From Latin praeposterus (“with the hinder part before, reversed, inverted, perverted”), from prae (“before”) + posterus (“coming after”).
definition_en: Extremely foolish or unreasonable.

senses.gloss: Absurd, or contrary to common sense.
senses.example: Leading the attack on the president's very citizenship is the professional vulgarian Donald Trump, who gets away with the kind of preposterous, race-based comments granted few black public figures.

examples.text: It’s a preposterous attempt to try to live only for yourself and by yourself.

definition_en: To travel from one place to another by a particular path.

senses.gloss: A course or way which is traveled or passed.

senses.gloss: A regular itinerary of stops, or the path followed between these stops, such as for delivery or passenger transportation.

senses.gloss: A road or path; often specifically a highway.

examples.translation_ko: 심지어 심부름 가는 시간을 바꾸거나 다른 길을 찾으려 하지도 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin squalidus, from squalere (“to be rough or dirty”).
definition_en: Having or showing a lack of cleanliness and comfort.

senses.gloss: Extremely dirty and unpleasant.
Showing a contemptible lack of moral standards.
senses.example: A squalid attempt to buy votes.

examples.text: He looked round the squalid attic in dismay.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 더러운 다락방을 둘러보며 경악했다.

senses.gloss: A beam of light or radiation.

One of the spheromeres of a radiate, especially one of the arms of a starfish or an ophiuran.

examples.text: The suggestion sent a ray of hope in all their breasts, but I would have nothing to do with it.

examples.translation_ko: "그런 말씀은 모두 너무 억지스럽게 들립니다." 그녀가 신랄하게 말했다.

examples.translation_ko: "만약 그렇다면, 동업자에게 자신의 주소를 알려주는 바보 같은 짓은 하지 않았을 거야." 나는 신랄하게 반박했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Not belonging to a particular country or region.

senses.gloss: A person, animal, plant, or other thing which is from outside the family, group, organization, or territory under consideration.
A citizen or national of another sovereign state.
senses.example: Aliens are aliens because of persecution or war or hardship or famine.

senses.gloss: A mischievous or suspicious foreigner.

examples.text: They may spend their whole lives aliens among their kindred and remain aloof among the only scenes they have ever known.
examples.translation_ko: 평생을 친족들 사이에서 이방인으로 보내고, 지금껏 알아온 유일한 풍경들 속에서도 동떨어져 지낼지도 모른다.

etymology: From Middle English callyng, kallyng, kalland, from Old English *cealliende and Old Norse kallandi, equivalent to call + -ing.
definition_en: A summons or invitation to a particular place.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of call

examples.text: This was not without its use in the calling which she had decided to follow.
examples.translation_ko: 이것은 그녀가 따르기로 결심한 직업에서 쓸모가 없지 않았다.

examples.text: “Oh, I think that’s awfully subtle,” said the Colonel, putting into the word all the contempt he felt for a quality so alien to the traditions of his calling.

etymology: From Middle English pallour, from Old French palor (“paleness, pallor”), from Latin pallor, from palleō (“look pale, blanch”).
definition_en: A pale or unhealthy appearance of the skin.

senses.gloss: Unnatural paleness, especially as a sign of sickness or distress.

examples.text: The sky had still the pallor of dawn, and there was a ghostly silence on the lagoon.
examples.translation_ko: 하늘은 여전히 새벽의 창백함을 띠고 있었고, 석호에는 유령 같은 정적이 흘렀다.

senses.gloss: Deep-seated and/or long-term animosity or ill will about something or someone, especially due to perceived mistreatment.
senses.example: to have, hold, or bear a grudge against someone

examples.text: After all, you can’t grudge me that.”
examples.translation_ko: 그 정도는 허락해 주셔야죠."

examples.text: Sometimes it seems as if they grudge the longevity which postpones their chance of an effective scene.

etymology: From Latin postpōnō (“I put after; I postpone”) from post (“after”) + pōnō (“I put; I place”), compare forestall.

senses.gloss: To delay or put off an event, appointment, etc.
To place after in order; to deem less important.
senses.example: Why should the See of Antioch, that most ancient and truly Apostolical Church, where the Christian name began […] be postponed to Alexandria?
