examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Sometimes it seems as if they grudge the longevity which postpones their chance of an effective scene.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 그들이 효과적인 장면을 연출할 기회를 미루는 장수를 원망하는 것처럼 보이기도 한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A person who has not eaten for a long time.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of starve

examples.text: I should like him to die miserable, poor, and starving, without a friend.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 비참하게, 가난하게, 굶주리며, 친구 하나 없이 죽었으면 좋겠어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The two buildings are placed far apart, so that only the starving should be tempted to make use of them.
examples.translation_ko: 두 건물은 멀리 떨어져 있어서 오직 굶주린 자들만이 그곳을 이용하려는 유혹을 받도록 되어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English roten, rotten, from Old English rotian (“to rot, become corrupted, ulcerate, putrefy”), from Proto-West Germanic *rot...
definition_en: To decay or become rotten.

senses.gloss: To suffer decomposition due to biological action, especially by fungi or bacteria.
senses.example: The apple left in the cupboard all that time had started to rot.

senses.gloss: To decline in function or utility.
senses.example: Your brain will rot if you spend so much time on the computer, Tony!

senses.gloss: To (cause to) deteriorate in any way, as in morals; to corrupt.

examples.text: I hope he’ll rot with some loathsome disease.
examples.translation_ko: 끔찍한 병에 걸려 썩어 죽기를 바라요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: No one would go near now to gather the cocoa-nuts, and they lay rotting on the ground.
examples.translation_ko: 이제는 아무도 코코넛을 따러 가려 하지 않았고, 코코넛들은 땅에서 썩어가고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From vindictive + -ness.
definition_en: A strong desire for revenge.

senses.gloss: The condition of being vindictive; a malevolent desire for revenge.

examples.text: He knew Tough Bill’s vindictiveness.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 터프 빌의 복수심을 알고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I expected then people to be more of a piece than I do now, and I was distressed to find so much vindictiveness in so charming a creature.
examples.translation_ko: 그때 나는 지금보다 사람들이 더 일관성 있을 거라고 기대했고, 그토록 매력적인 여인에게서 그런 복수심을 발견하게 되어 괴로웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English motle, from Anglo-Norman motteley (“parti-colored”), from Old English mot (“speck”). Doublet of mote. The English word can be a...
definition_en: Diverse or multicolored.

senses.gloss: Comprising greatly varied elements, to the point of incongruity.
senses.example: I met a fool i' th' forest, / A motley' fool.

senses.gloss: Having many colours; variegated.

examples.text: I did not realise how motley are the qualities that go to make up a human being.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 인간을 구성하는 자질들이 얼마나 뒤섞여 있는지 깨닫지 못했던 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: A motley crowd saunters along the streets—Lascars off a P. and O., blond Northmen from a Swedish barque, Japanese from a man-of-war, English sailors, Spaniards, pleasant-looking fellows from a French cruiser, negroes off an American tramp.
examples.translation_ko: 잡다한 군중이 거리를 어슬렁거리며 걸어간다—P&O 기선에서 내린 라스카르족들, 스웨덴 범선에서 온 금발의 북유럽 사람들, 군함에서 나온 일본인들, 영국 선원들, 스페인 사람들, 프랑스 순양함에서 온 호감형 젊은이들, 미국 화물선에서 내린 흑인들.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English charite, from Old French charité, cherte, chariteit, cariteit, from Latin cāritās.
definition_en: The act of giving money or time to help those in need.

senses.gloss: An organization, the objective of which is to carry out a charitable purpose.
The goods or money given to those in need.
Benevolence to others less fortunate than ourselves; the providing of goods or money to those in need.

examples.text: “Not out of charity,” I answered coolly.
examples.translation_ko: "동정심에서가 아니야." 나는 냉정하게 대답했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Now I am well aware that pettiness and grandeur, malice and charity, hatred and love, can find place side by side in the same human heart.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 나는 소심함과 위대함, 악의와 자선, 증오와 사랑이 같은 인간의 마음속에 나란히 자리할 수 있다는 것을 잘 알고 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English haterede, hatrede (“hatred”), from hate (“hate”) + -rede (“suffix denoting state or condition”), equivalent to hate + -red; com...
definition_en: A strong feeling of dislike or hostility.

senses.gloss: Strong aversion; intense dislike.
senses.example: Fears and hatreds pay no attention to facts.

examples.text: Now I am well aware that pettiness and grandeur, malice and charity, hatred and love, can find place side by side in the same human heart.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 나는 소심함과 위대함, 악의와 자선, 증오와 사랑이 같은 인간의 마음속에 나란히 자리할 수 있다는 것을 잘 알고 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He felt always the furious hatred that must seize a man condemned when he compared himself with the doctor, sane and healthy, who had the inestimable privilege of life.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 항상 사형선고를 받은 자가 느낄 수밖에 없는 맹렬한 증오를 느꼈다. 정신이 온전하고 건강하며 삶이라는 헤아릴 수 없는 특권을 누리는 의사와 자신을 비교할 때마다 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French responsable, from Old French responsable, responsible, formed from the root of Latin responsus, from respondere. The spelling of...
definition_en: Having a sense of duty or obligation to take care of something.

senses.gloss: Having the duty of taking care of something; answerable for an act performed or for its consequences; accountable; amenable, especially legally or politically.
senses.example: Parents are responsible for their child's behaviour.

senses.gloss: Being a primary cause of a situation or action and thus able to be blamed or credited for it.
senses.example: Who is responsible for this mess?

senses.gloss: Answerable to (a superior).

examples.text: At first I was surprised and confused; then, as he lay in his house and didn’t move or breathe or speak, hour upon hour, it grew upon me that I was responsible, because no one else was interested—interested, I mean, with that intense personal interest to which everyone has some vague right at the end.
examples.translation_ko: 처음에는 놀랍고 당황스러웠다. 그러나 그가 집에 누워 움직이지도, 숨쉬지도, 말하지도 않은 채 시간이 흘러가면서, 내가 책임져야 한다는 생각이 점점 커져갔다. 다른 누구도 관심이 없었기 때문이었다. 내 말은, 모든 사람이 마지막에 어렴풋이나마 가질 권리가 있는 그런 강렬하고 개인적인 관심 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You know, I’m not sure that your husband is quite responsible for his actions.
examples.translation_ko: "있잖아요, 당신 남편이 자신의 행동에 대해 온전히 책임질 수 있는 상태인지 확신이 서지 않아요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English spell, spel, from Old English spell (“news, story”), from Proto-Germanic *spellą (“speech, account, tale”), from Proto-Indo-Eur...
definition_en: A word or phrase that is spoken to try to make something happen.

senses.gloss: Words or a formula supposed to have magical powers.
senses.example: He cast a spell to cure warts.

senses.gloss: A magical effect or influence induced by an incantation or formula.
senses.example: under a spell

senses.gloss: Speech, discourse.

examples.text: The spell was broken.
examples.translation_ko: 마법이 깨졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It’s as though someone had cast a spell over him.
examples.translation_ko: 마치 누군가 그에게 마법을 걸어놓은 것 같습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Late Latin vacantia. Doublet of vacance.
definition_en: A position or place that is empty or unoccupied.

senses.gloss: An unoccupied position or job.
senses.example: Whenever there is a vacancy in the office of the Vice President, the President shall nominate a Vice President who shall take office upon confirmation by a majority vote of both Houses of Congress.

senses.gloss: An available room in a hotel; guest house, etc.
Empty space.
senses.example: Sky was set above earth, land ringed with sea, / Chaos retired to its own vacancy ….

examples.text: The Colonel stared into vacancy, and I wondered whether anyone could be quite so innocent of guile as he looked.
examples.translation_ko: 대령은 허공을 바라보았고, 나는 과연 누군가가 저렇게 보이는 만큼 순진무구할 수 있을까 하는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Strickland was a weird figure as he lay there, thinner than ever, with his ragged red beard and his eyes staring feverishly into vacancy; his illness seemed to have made them larger, and they had an unnatural brightness.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 그곳에 누워 있는 모습이 기괴했는데, 전보다 더욱 야위어서 헝클어진 붉은 수염과 열에 들뜬 눈으로 허공을 응시하고 있었다. 병으로 인해 눈이 더 커진 것 같았고, 부자연스럽게 빛나고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English gile, from Anglo-Norman gile, from Old French guile (“deception”), from Frankish *wīl (“ruse”), from Proto-Germanic *wīlą, from...
definition_en: Cunning or deceitful behavior.

senses.gloss: Astuteness often marked by a certain sense of cunning or artful deception.
senses.example: Estonia were struggling to get to grips with the game while Ireland were showing a composure and guile that demonstrated their experience in play-off ties.

senses.gloss: Deceptiveness, deceit, fraud, duplicity, dishonesty.
senses.example: Jesus saw Nathanael coming to him, and saith of him, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom is no guile!

examples.text: The Colonel stared into vacancy, and I wondered whether anyone could be quite so innocent of guile as he looked.
examples.translation_ko: 대령은 허공을 바라보았고, 나는 과연 누군가가 저렇게 보이는 만큼 순진무구할 수 있을까 하는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It cannot be said that they are without guile, but they have a tolerant respect for the law, when the law is supported by strength.
examples.translation_ko: 그들에게 간계가 없다고는 할 수 없지만, 법이 힘으로 뒷받침될 때는 법에 대해 관대한 존경심을 보인다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English hertles, herteles, from Old English heortlēas (“without courage; listless”), equivalent to heart + -less. Cognate with German h...
definition_en: Lacking kindness or compassion.

senses.gloss: Without feeling, emotion, or concern for others; uncaring; cruel.
senses.example: His heartless actions and cold manner left her saddened and feeling alone.

senses.gloss: Without a physical heart.
Listless, unenthusiastic.
senses.example: Near-synonyms: spiritless, unhearty

examples.text: “But that doesn’t prevent the fact that Charles Strickland is a heartless beast.”
examples.translation_ko: "하지만 그렇다고 해서 찰스 스트릭랜드가 무정한 짐승이라는 사실이 바뀌는 건 아니에요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I feared he would think it heartless if I read, so I sat by the window, smoking a pipe, till he felt inclined to speak.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 책을 읽으면 냉정하다고 생각할까 봐 걱정되어, 나는 창가에 앉아 파이프 담배를 피우며 그가 말하고 싶어할 때까지 기다렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French detenir. Cognate with Italian detenere, Portuguese deter, Romanian deține, and Spanish detener.
definition_en: To hold someone or something back from leaving a place.

senses.gloss: To keep someone from proceeding by holding them back or making claims on their attention.
To put under custody.
To keep back or from; to withhold.
senses.example: Detain not the wages of the hireling.

examples.text: Neither wit nor whisky could detain him then.
examples.translation_ko: 그럴 때면 재치도 위스키도 그를 붙잡을 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When, saying I was tired, I rose to go, Mrs. Strickland made no attempt to detain me.
examples.translation_ko: 피곤하다며 일어나 가려고 하자, 스트릭랜드 부인은 나를 붙잡으려 하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: The way someone behaves or conducts themselves.

senses.gloss: UK, Australia, New Zealand, Ireland, and Commonwealth spelling of demeanor.

examples.text: Whenever she went out—and compassion for her misadventure made her friends eager to entertain her—she bore a demeanour that was perfect.
examples.translation_ko: 외출할 때마다—그녀의 불운에 대한 동정심으로 친구들이 그녀를 대접하려 애썼다—그녀는 완벽한 태도를 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He spoke with the accent of New England, and there was about his demeanour a bloodless frigidity which made me ask myself why on earth he was busying himself with Charles Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 뉴잉글랜드 억양으로 말했고, 그의 태도에는 피 한 방울 없는 냉담함이 있어서 나는 도대체 왜 이 사람이 찰스 스트릭랜드에게 관심을 갖는지 의아했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Late Latin circulātus, perfect passive participle of Late Latin circulō (“to make circular, encircle”) (see -ate (verb-forming suffix...
definition_en: To move or flow freely from place to place.

senses.gloss: to move in circles or through a circuit
to cause (a person or thing) to move in circles or through a circuit
to move from person to person, as at a party
senses.example: In both the 2005 and 2013 papal elections there were whispers circulating that back in 1976 Francis had failed to help the two priests in their hour of need.

examples.text: Wild rumours were circulating about her—how her mother had found her packing her bag one winter night to go to New York and say goodbye to a soldier who was going overseas.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀에 대한 황당한 소문들이 돌고 있었다—어느 겨울밤 어머니가 그녀를 발견했는데, 해외로 떠나는 한 군인에게 작별 인사를 하러 뉴욕에 가려고 가방을 싸고 있었다는 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I discovered presently that a peculiar story was circulating among her friends.
examples.translation_ko: 얼마 후 나는 그녀의 친구들 사이에서 기묘한 이야기가 돌고 있다는 것을 알게 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English dauncer, dawncere, dancere, equivalent to dance + -er.
definition_en: A person who dances professionally or as a hobby.

senses.gloss: A person who dances, usually as a hobby, an occupation, or a profession.
senses.example: I'm a terrible dancer.

senses.gloss: A stripper.
Synonym of garreter (“a thief who used housetops to enter by garret windows”).
senses.example: [A]bout 40 were burglars, "dancers," "garreters," and other adepts with the skeleton keys.

examples.text: The dancers stopped suddenly still.
examples.translation_ko: 춤추던 사람들이 갑자기 멈춰 섰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They said that Charles Strickland had become infatuated with a French dancer, whom he had first seen in the ballet at the Empire, and had accompanied her to Paris.
examples.translation_ko: 사람들은 찰스 스트릭랜드가 엠파이어 극장의 발레에서 처음 본 프랑스 무용수에게 빠져서 그녀와 함께 파리로 갔다고 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French prestige (“illusion, fascination, enchantment, prestige”), from Latin praestīgium (“a delusion, an illusion”). Despite the phonetic sim...
definition_en: High social status or respect.

senses.gloss: The quality of how good the reputation of something or someone is, how favourably something or someone is regarded.
senses.example: Oxford has a university of very high prestige.

senses.gloss: Delusion; illusion; trick.
senses.example: That faith which, we are told, was founded on a rock, impregnable to the assaults of men and demons; to the sophisms of infidelity, and the prestiges of imposture!

examples.text: His power depended on his prestige, and first one, then another, of the sailors who lived in his house told them that he had sworn to do Strickland in.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 권력은 위신에 달려 있었고, 그의 집에 사는 선원들이 하나둘씩 스트릭랜드를 해치우겠다고 맹세했다는 소문을 퍼뜨렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I could not find out how this had arisen, but, singularly enough, it created much sympathy for Mrs. Strickland, and at the same time gave her not a little prestige.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 이야기가 어떻게 생겨났는지는 알 수 없었지만, 이상하게도 이 소문은 스트릭랜드 부인에 대한 많은 동정심을 불러일으키는 동시에 그녀에게 적지 않은 명성을 안겨주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French banalité, from banal, equivalent to banal + -ity.
definition_en: The quality of being commonplace or ordinary.

senses.gloss: The quality of being banal.
Something which is banal.
A feudal right or obligation, especially the obligation for a peasant to grind grain at the lord's mill, or the profits accruing from such rights.
senses.example: In fact corvées, champarts, and rights of banality not only continued but had been increased in the course of the seventeenth century.

examples.text: My friends pursued their course with uneventfulness; they had no longer any surprises for me, and when I met them I knew pretty well what they would say; even their love-affairs had a tedious banality.
examples.translation_ko: 내 친구들은 평온하게 자신들의 길을 걸어갔다. 그들에게서 더 이상 놀랄 만한 것은 없었고, 만날 때마다 그들이 무슨 말을 할지 거의 알 수 있었다. 심지어 그들의 연애사조차 지루할 만큼 뻔했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We are like people living in a country whose language they know so little that, with all manner of beautiful and profound things to say, they are condemned to the banalities of the conversation manual.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 마치 어떤 나라에 살면서도 그 나라 말을 거의 모르는 사람들과 같아서, 아름답고 심오한 말을 하고 싶어도 회화 교본의 진부한 표현들로 만족해야 하는 신세다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From belong + -ing.
definition_en: A feeling of being part of a group or community.

senses.gloss: The feeling that one belongs.
senses.example: I have a feeling of belonging in London.

senses.gloss: Something physical that is owned.
senses.example: Make sure you take all your belongings when you leave.

senses.gloss: Family; relations; household.
senses.example: As soon as the principal personages were seated, the verandah of the house was filled silently by the muffled-up forms of Lakamba’s female belongings.

examples.text: I gave up my small apartment, sold my few belongings, and resolved to start afresh.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 작은 아파트를 정리하고 얼마 안 되는 소지품을 팔아치운 뒤, 새롭게 시작하기로 결심했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had no great difficulty in leaving the ship, and in twenty-four hours, with all his belongings, he was on shore.
examples.translation_ko: 배에서 내리는 것은 그리 어렵지 않았고, 이십사 시간 만에 그는 모든 소지품을 가지고 육지에 발을 디뎠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English type (“symbol, figure, emblem”), from Latin typus, from Ancient Greek τύπος (túpos, “mark, impression, type”), from τύπτω (túpt...
definition_en: Classify or categorize something.

senses.gloss: A grouping based on shared characteristics; a class.
senses.example: This type of plane can handle rough weather more easily than that type of plane.

senses.gloss: An individual considered typical of its class, one regarded as typifying a certain profession, environment, etc.
senses.example: "I just peeked out toward the restaurant and there are a lot of Navy types in there. I'd hate for you to get in trouble on your last night in Europe."

senses.gloss: An individual that represents the ideal for its class; an embodiment.
senses.example: Altogether he was the type of low ruffianism — as ill-conditioned a looking brute as ever ginned a hare.

examples.text: She had made a success of her business, and now had an office in Chancery Lane; she did little typing herself, but spent her time correcting the work of the four girls she employed.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 사업에 성공해서 이제 챈서리 레인에 사무실을 두고 있었다. 타이핑은 거의 직접 하지 않고, 고용한 네 명의 여직원들이 한 일을 교정하는 데 시간을 보냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She was a woman of twenty-eight, I should think, though of a type whose age is always doubtful; for she cannot have looked different when she was twenty, and at forty would look no older.
examples.translation_ko: 스물여덟 살 정도로 보였는데, 나이를 가늠하기 어려운 부류의 여자였다. 스무 살 때도 지금과 다르지 않았을 것이고, 마흔이 되어도 더 늙어 보이지 않을 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From neat + -ness.
definition_en: The quality of being tidy and well-organized.

senses.gloss: The state of being neat.
senses.example: Both engines and carriages were maintained in admirable cleanliness, and a very high standard of neatness characterised the permanent way and lineside buildings.

examples.text: He had great neatness of person, and he continued to wear his spruce black coat and his bowler hat, always a little too small for him, in a dapper, jaunty manner.
examples.translation_ko: 몸단장을 매우 깔끔하게 했고, 언제나 자신에게는 조금 작은 중절모와 함께 단정한 검은 코트를 말쑥하고 경쾌하게 차려입고 다녔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She had had the idea of giving it a certain daintiness, and she made much use of blue and red inks; she bound the copy in coarse paper, that looked vaguely like watered silk, in various pale colours; and she had acquired a reputation for neatness and accuracy.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 일에 어떤 우아함을 부여한다는 아이디어를 갖고 있어서 파란색과 빨간색 잉크를 많이 사용했고, 물결무늬 비단처럼 보이는 거친 종이로 원고를 다양한 연한 색깔로 제본했으며, 정확하고 깔끔하다는 평판을 얻고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Perhaps from Middle English ruschen, russchen (“to rush, startle, make a loud rushing noise”), from Old English hrysċan (“to jolt, startle”), from ...
definition_en: A sudden movement or action.

senses.gloss: A sudden forward motion.
senses.example: A gentleman of his train spurred up his horse, and, with a violent rush, severed him from the duke.

senses.gloss: A surge.
senses.example: A rush of business can be difficult to handle effectively for its unexpected volume.

senses.gloss: General haste.
senses.example: Many errors were made in the rush to finish.

examples.text: On a sudden the police rushed in, and everyone who could made for the door.
examples.translation_ko: 갑자기 경찰이 들이닥치자 도망칠 수 있는 자는 모두 문으로 향했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She was pleased to be able to tell you that her son was at Cambridge, and it was with a little laugh that she spoke of the rush of dances to which her daughter, just out, was invited.
examples.translation_ko: 아들이 케임브리지에 다니고 있다고 말할 수 있어서 기뻤고, 막 사교계에 데뷔한 딸이 무도회 초대를 잇달아 받고 있다는 이야기를 할 때는 작은 웃음을 지었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *pénkʷe
From Middle English fifthe, fifte, fift, from Old English fīfta (“fifth”), from Proto-Germanic *fimftô (“fifth”) or *femftô, equi...
definition_en: Being the ordinal number for five.

senses.gloss: The ordinal form of the number five.

examples.text: I couldn’t guess what Daisy and Tom were thinking, but I doubt if even Miss Baker, who seemed to have mastered a certain hardy scepticism, was able utterly to put this fifth guest’s shrill metallic urgency out of mind.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지와 톰이 무슨 생각을 하고 있는지 짐작할 수 없었지만, 어떤 완고한 회의주의를 터득한 것 같은 베이커 양조차도 이 다섯 번째 손님의 날카롭고 금속적인 긴박함을 마음에서 완전히 떨쳐낼 수는 없었으리라고 생각한다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I quickly found myself a tiny apartment on the fifth floor of a house in the Rue des Dames, and for a couple of hundred francs bought at a second-hand dealer’s enough furniture to make it habitable.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 담 거리의 한 건물 5층에 있는 조그만 아파트를 재빨리 구했고, 중고품 상인에게서 2백 프랑을 주고 살 만한 가구들을 사서 거주할 수 있게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin genuīnus (“innate, native, natural”), from genus, from Proto-Indo-European *ǵenh₁-.
definition_en: Sincerely made or expressed.

senses.gloss: Belonging to, or proceeding from the original stock; native
Not counterfeit, spurious, false, or adulterated
senses.example: a genuine text; a genuine production; genuine materials; genuine friendship

examples.text: He had a genuine enthusiasm for the commonplace.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 평범한 것에 대한 진정한 열정을 가지고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There was in my soul a perfectly genuine horror of Strickland, and side by side with it a cold curiosity to discover his motives.
examples.translation_ko: 내 영혼 속에는 스트릭랜드에 대한 진심어린 공포가 있었고, 그와 나란히 그의 동기를 알아내고자 하는 차가운 호기심이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To feel or show no concern about something.

examples.text: His soul palpitating with love of art, he painted the models who hung about the stairway of Bernini in the Piazza de Spagna, undaunted by their obvious picturesqueness; and his studio was full of canvases on which were portrayed moustachioed, large-eyed peasants in peaked hats, urchins in becoming rags, and women in bright petticoats.
examples.translation_ko: 예술에 대한 사랑으로 가슴이 뛰는 그는 스파냐 광장의 베르니니 계단 주변에서 어슬렁거리는 모델들을 그렸는데, 그들의 뻔한 그림 같은 모습에도 굴복하지 않았다. 그의 작업실은 뾰족한 모자를 쓴 콧수염 난 큰 눈의 농부들, 보기 좋게 너덜너덜한 옷을 입은 꼬마들, 그리고 화려한 페티코트를 입은 여인들을 그린 캔버스들로 가득했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But it is unfortunate that I can give no description of the arduous steps by which he reached such mastery over his art as he ever acquired; for if I could show him undaunted by failure, by an unceasing effort of courage holding despair at bay, doggedly persistent in the face of self-doubt, which is the artist’s bitterest enemy, I might excite some sympathy for a personality which, I am all too conscious, must appear singularly devoid of charm.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그가 자신의 예술에서 그 정도의 숙련에 이르기까지 거쳐야 했던 험난한 과정을 묘사할 수 없다는 것은 유감스러운 일이다. 만약 내가 실패에 굴복하지 않고, 끊임없는 용기의 노력으로 절망을 물리치며, 예술가의 가장 쓰라린 적인 자기 의심 앞에서도 완고하게 버텨내는 그의 모습을 보여줄 수 있다면, 매력이 현저히 부족해 보일 수밖에 없다는 것을 나 자신도 너무나 잘 알고 있는 이 인물에 대해 어느 정도 동정심을 불러일으킬 수 있을 텐데 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English yrchoun, irchoun (“hedgehog; sea urchin”), from Old Northern French irechon, from Vulgar Latin *ērīciōnem, from Latin ericius. ...
definition_en: To steal or plunder.

senses.gloss: A mischievous child.
A street urchin, a child who lives, or spends most of their time, in the streets.
senses.example: And the urchins that stand with their thievish eyes / Forever on watch ran off each with a prize.

senses.gloss: A sea urchin.

examples.text: He brought out a picture of two curly-headed Italian urchins playing marbles.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 구슬치기를 하는 곱슬머리 이탈리아 꼬마 두 명을 그린 그림을 꺼내왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His soul palpitating with love of art, he painted the models who hung about the stairway of Bernini in the Piazza de Spagna, undaunted by their obvious picturesqueness; and his studio was full of canvases on which were portrayed moustachioed, large-eyed peasants in peaked hats, urchins in becoming rags, and women in bright petticoats.
examples.translation_ko: 예술에 대한 사랑으로 가슴이 뛰는 그는 스파냐 광장의 베르니니 계단 주변에서 어슬렁거리는 모델들을 그렸는데, 그들의 뻔한 그림 같은 모습에도 굴복하지 않았다. 그의 작업실은 뾰족한 모자를 쓴 콧수염 난 큰 눈의 농부들, 보기 좋게 너덜너덜한 옷을 입은 꼬마들, 그리고 화려한 페티코트를 입은 여인들을 그린 캔버스들로 가득했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cipres, from Old French cipres (French cyprès), from Late Latin cypressus; compare Hebrew גֹּפֶר (gōp̄er), the name of the tree...
definition_en: A coniferous evergreen tree with scale-like leaves.

senses.gloss: An evergreen coniferous tree with flattened shoots bearing small scale-like leaves, whose dark foliage is sometimes associated with mourning, in family Cupressaceae, especially the genera Cupressus and Chamaecyparis.
senses.example: The plain appears like paradiſe reſtored, where the proud cypreſs and tall arreca ſeem walking by the margin of the paſſing ſtream..

examples.text: I thought of those cold scenes of his, with their picturesque peasants and cypresses and olive-trees.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그림 같은 농부들과 사이프러스 나무, 올리브 나무가 있는 그의 차가운 풍경화들을 떠올렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Sometimes they lounged at the steps of a church, and sometimes dallied among cypresses against a cloudless sky; sometimes they made love by a Renaissance well-head, and sometimes they wandered through the Campagna by the side of an ox-waggon.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 그들이 교회 계단에 기대어 있었고, 때로는 구름 한 점 없는 하늘을 배경으로 사이프러스 나무들 사이에서 한가로이 시간을 보냈다. 때로는 르네상스 시대 우물가에서 사랑을 나누었고, 때로는 소가 끄는 마차 옆에서 캄파냐 평원을 거닐었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cloudeles, equivalent to cloud + -less.
definition_en: Having no clouds.

senses.gloss: Without any clouds.
senses.example: a cloudless day

examples.text: On the verandah the air was scented with the heavy perfume of the tiare, and overhead the Southern Cross shone in a cloudless sky.
examples.translation_ko: 베란다에는 티아레 꽃의 진한 향기가 공기를 감쌌고, 머리 위로는 구름 한 점 없는 하늘에 남십자성이 빛나고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Sometimes they lounged at the steps of a church, and sometimes dallied among cypresses against a cloudless sky; sometimes they made love by a Renaissance well-head, and sometimes they wandered through the Campagna by the side of an ox-waggon.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 그들이 교회 계단에 기대어 있었고, 때로는 구름 한 점 없는 하늘을 배경으로 사이프러스 나무들 사이에서 한가로이 시간을 보냈다. 때로는 르네상스 시대 우물가에서 사랑을 나누었고, 때로는 소가 끄는 마차 옆에서 캄파냐 평원을 거닐었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From trade + -s- + -man.
definition_en: A person who trades or works with their hands.

senses.gloss: A skilled manual worker (implied male).
One who trades; a shopkeeper.

examples.text: My Finn informed me that Gatsby had dismissed every servant in his house a week ago and replaced them with half a dozen others, who never went into West Egg village to be bribed by the tradesmen, but ordered moderate supplies over the telephone.
examples.translation_ko: 내 핀란드인 가정부는 개츠비가 일주일 전에 집의 모든 하인들을 해고하고 여섯 명 정도의 다른 사람들로 교체했다고 알려주었는데, 이들은 상인들에게 매수당할 일이 없도록 웨스트에그 마을에 나가지 않고 전화로만 적당한 생필품을 주문했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It’s mostly merchants who buy them, and rich tradesmen.
examples.translation_ko: 주로 상인들과 부유한 장사꾼들이 사죠.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From French idéal, from Late Latin ideālis (“existing in idea”), by surface analysis, idea + -al, from Latin idea (“idea”); see idea.
In mathematic...
definition_en: A perfect or theoretical standard against which others can be judged.

senses.gloss: Pertaining to ideas, or to a given idea.
Existing only in the mind; conceptual, imaginary.
senses.example: At first, he began to doubt the reality of his adventures, but the acute pain in his shoulders when he attempted to rise, assured him that the kicking of the goblins was certainly not ideal.

senses.gloss: Optimal; being the best possibility.

examples.text: She is occupied with material things, and she is jealous of the ideal.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 물질적인 것들에만 관심이 있고, 이상을 질투한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was an ideal that he painted—a poor one, common and shop-soiled, but still it was an ideal; and it gave his character a peculiar charm.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 그린 것은 이상향이었다. 비록 빈약하고 평범하며 진부한 이상향이었지만, 그래도 이상향은 이상향이었다. 그리고 그것이 그의 인격에 독특한 매력을 부여했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From naive + -ly.
definition_en: Assuming things will work out without any problems.

senses.gloss: In a naive manner.

examples.text: He was generous, and the needy, laughing at him because he believed so naively their stories of distress, borrowed from him with effrontery.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 관대했고, 궁핍한 사람들은 그가 자신들의 곤경담을 순진하게 믿는다고 비웃으면서도 뻔뻔스럽게 그에게서 돈을 빌렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Though he had suffered so much from the ridicule of his friends, Dirk Stroeve, eager for praise and naively self-satisfied, could never resist displaying his work.
examples.translation_ko: 친구들의 조롱으로 그토록 고통받았으면서도, 더크 스트루브는 칭찬에 목말라하고 순진하게 자기만족에 빠져 있어서 자신의 작품을 보여주는 일을 결코 참을 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From emotion + -al.
definition_en: Relating to emotions or the emotional state.

senses.gloss: Of or relating to the emotions.
senses.example: emotional crisis

senses.gloss: Characterized by emotion.
Determined by strong emotion rather than purely logical reasoning.
senses.example: emotional decision

examples.text: He was very emotional, yet his feeling, so easily aroused, had in it something absurd, so that you accepted his kindness, but felt no gratitude.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 매우 감정적이었지만, 그토록 쉽게 동요하는 그의 감정에는 우스꽝스러운 면이 있어서, 사람들은 그의 친절을 받아들이면서도 고마움을 느끼지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I had an idea that Dirk, a man of greater emotional reactions than depth of feeling, would soon forget; and Blanche’s life, begun with who knows what bright hopes and what dreams, might just as well have never been lived.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 감정의 깊이보다는 반응이 더 격렬한 남자인 더크가 곧 잊어버리리라는 생각이 들었다. 그리고 누가 알겠는가, 어떤 밝은 희망과 꿈으로 시작되었을 블랑슈의 인생은 아예 살지 않았던 것과 다름없을지도 모른다는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English but, butte (“goal, mark, butt of land”), from Old English byt, bytt (“small piece of land”) and *butt (attested in diminutive O...
definition_en: The rear end of a person or animal.

senses.gloss: The whole buttocks and pelvic region that includes one's private parts.
senses.example: I can see your butt.

senses.gloss: Body; self.
senses.example: Get your butt to the car.

senses.gloss: The buttocks or anus (used as a minced oath in idiomatic expressions; less objectionable than arse/ass).
senses.example: Get up off your butt and get to work.

examples.text: Nature had made him a butt, but had denied him insensibility.
examples.translation_ko: 자연은 그를 조롱거리로 만들어놓고는 무감각함은 주지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: What they felt the lack of most bitterly was tobacco, and Captain Nichols, for his part, could not do without it; he took to hunting the “Can o’ Beer,” for cigarette-ends and the butt-end of cigars which the promenaders of the night before had thrown away.
examples.translation_ko: 그들이 가장 절실하게 그리워한 것은 담배였는데, 니콜스 선장은 특히 담배 없이는 견딜 수 없었다. 그는 "깡 오 비어"를 뒤져서 전날 밤 산책객들이 버린 담배꽁초와 시가 꽁초를 찾아다니기 시작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French farce (“farce (style of humor); stuffing”) (in the latter sense, via Middle English fars, farsse), from Old French fars...
definition_en: A comedy that is silly or absurd.

senses.gloss: A style of humor marked by broad improbabilities with little regard to regularity or method.
A motion picture or play featuring this style of humor.
senses.example: The farce that we saw last night had us laughing and shaking our heads at the same time.

senses.gloss: A situation abounding with ludicrous incidents.
senses.example: The first month of labor negotiations was a farce.

examples.text: His life was a tragedy written in the terms of knockabout farce.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 인생은 막장 희극의 형식으로 쓰인 비극이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It passed through my mind that the whole thing was a stupendous, incomprehensible farce.
examples.translation_ko: 이 모든 것이 엄청나고 이해할 수 없는 희극이라는 생각이 머릿속을 스쳐 지나갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English delicat, from Latin dēlicātus (“giving pleasure, delightful, soft, luxurious, delicate, (in Medieval Latin also) fine, slender”...
definition_en: Very sensitive to change or easily damaged.

senses.gloss: Easily damaged or requiring careful handling.
senses.example: Those clothes are made from delicate lace.

senses.gloss: Characterized by a fine structure or thin lines.
senses.example: Her face was delicate.

senses.gloss: Intended for use with fragile items.
senses.example: Set the washing machine to the delicate cycle.

examples.text: We passed a barrier of dark trees, and then the façade of Fifty-Ninth Street, a block of delicate pale light, beamed down into the park.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 어두운 나무들의 장벽을 지나쳤고, 그러자 59번가의 정면이, 섬세하고 창백한 빛의 한 구획이 공원 아래로 환하게 비쳐 내렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But though so bad a painter, he had a very delicate feeling for art, and to go with him to picture-galleries was a rare treat.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그토록 형편없는 화가였음에도 불구하고, 그는 예술에 대한 매우 섬세한 감각을 지니고 있었고, 그와 함께 미술관을 다니는 것은 더없는 즐거움이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From critic + -ism.
definition_en: A statement expressing disapproval or dislike.

senses.gloss: The act of criticising; a critical judgment passed or expressed
senses.example: The politician received a lot of public criticism for his controversial stance on the issue.

senses.gloss: A critical observation or detailed examination and review.
senses.example: The politician received several detailed criticisms of his stance on the issue.

examples.text: (I’ve heard it said that Daisy’s murmur was only to make people lean toward her; an irrelevant criticism that made it no less charming.)
examples.translation_ko: (데이지의 속삭임은 사람들로 하여금 그녀 쪽으로 몸을 기울이게 하려는 것뿐이라는 말을 들은 적이 있다. 그런 엉뚱한 비판이 그녀의 매력을 조금이라도 덜어주지는 못했지만.)
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His enthusiasm was sincere and his criticism acute.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 열정은 진실했고 비평은 예리했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To be of the same kind or nature as.

examples.text: They may spend their whole lives aliens among their kindred and remain aloof among the only scenes they have ever known.
examples.translation_ko: 평생을 친족들 사이에서 이방인으로 보내고, 지금껏 알아온 유일한 풍경들 속에서도 동떨어져 지낼지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was not, like most of them, ignorant of kindred arts, and his taste for music and literature gave depth and variety to his comprehension of painting.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 대부분의 화가들처럼 관련 예술 분야에 무지하지 않았고, 음악과 문학에 대한 그의 취향은 회화에 대한 그의 이해에 깊이와 다양성을 더해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French varieté (“variety”) (modern French variété (“variety; genre, type”)) or directly from its etymon Latin varietās (“difference; di...
definition_en: A type or kind of something.

senses.gloss: A deviation or difference.
An animal or plant (or a group of such animals or plants) with characteristics causing it to differ from other animals or plants of the same species; a strain or cultivar.
senses.example: Jim is a nurseryman, specialising in clematis, and he has built up a business exporting 150 varieties to countries all over the world.

senses.gloss: A rank in a taxonomic classification below species and (if present) subspecies, and above form; hence, an organism of that rank.
senses.example: Capsicum annuum var. glabriusculum is a variety of Capsicum annuum commonly known as chiltepin or Indian pepper.

examples.text: I was within and without, simultaneously enchanted and repelled by the inexhaustible variety of life.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 안에 있으면서 동시에 밖에 있었고, 삶의 무궁무진한 다양성에 매혹되면서 동시에 반발감을 느꼈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was not, like most of them, ignorant of kindred arts, and his taste for music and literature gave depth and variety to his comprehension of painting.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 대부분의 화가들처럼 관련 예술 분야에 무지하지 않았고, 음악과 문학에 대한 그의 취향은 회화에 대한 그의 이해에 깊이와 다양성을 더해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French compréhension, from Latin comprehensiō (“taking together”), from com- (“with, together”) + prehendō (“take”).
definition_en: The ability to understand and interpret written or spoken language.

senses.gloss: A thorough understanding.
senses.example: Students will be tested on their comprehension of sentences in the foreign language.

senses.gloss: The totality of intensions, that is, attributes, characters, marks, properties, or qualities, that the object possesses, or else the totality of intensions that are pertinent to the context of a given discussion.
A compact syntax for generating a collection in some programming languages, traditionally lists in functional programming languages.

examples.text: He was not, like most of them, ignorant of kindred arts, and his taste for music and literature gave depth and variety to his comprehension of painting.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 대부분의 화가들처럼 관련 예술 분야에 무지하지 않았고, 음악과 문학에 대한 그의 취향은 회화에 대한 그의 이해에 깊이와 다양성을 더해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Mrs. Stroeve did all the housework herself; and while Dirk painted bad pictures, she went marketing, cooked the luncheon, sewed, occupied herself like a busy ant all the day; and in the evening sat in the studio, sewing again, while Dirk played music which I am sure was far beyond her comprehension.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브 부인은 모든 집안일을 혼자 했다. 더크가 형편없는 그림을 그리는 동안 그녀는 장을 보러 나가고, 점심을 요리하고, 바느질을 하며, 하루 종일 부지런한 개미처럼 바쁘게 움직였다. 저녁이면 화실에 앉아 다시 바느질을 하고, 더크는 그녀가 이해하기에는 분명 너무 어려운 음악을 연주했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English incomparable, from Middle French incomparable, from Old French [Term?], from Latin incomparābilis. By surface analysis, in- + c...
definition_en: Unmatched or superior to all others.

senses.gloss: Not comparable.
So much better than another as to be beyond comparison.
senses.example: I know of nothing in all drama more incomparable from the point of view of art, nothing more suggestive in its subtlety of observation, than Shakespeare's drawing of Rosencrantz and Guildenstern.

examples.text: Out of the corner of his eye Gatsby saw that the blocks of the sidewalks really formed a ladder and mounted to a secret place above the trees—he could climb to it, if he climbed alone, and once there he could suck on the pap of life, gulp down the incomparable milk of wonder.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 눈길 한편으로 보도블록들이 실제로는 사다리를 이루며 나무들 위 어떤 비밀스러운 곳으로 올라간다는 것을 깨달았다—혼자서 오른다면 그곳에 닿을 수 있을 것이고, 일단 그곳에 이르면 생명의 젖을 빨고 경이로움의 비할 데 없는 젖을 들이킬 수 있을 것이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: To a young man like myself his advice and guidance were of incomparable value.
examples.translation_ko: 나 같은 젊은이에게 그의 조언과 지도는 비할 데 없이 소중했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From vivid + -ly.
definition_en: Describing or characterized by vividness.

senses.gloss: In a vivid manner.

examples.text: I spent my Saturday nights in New York because those gleaming, dazzling parties of his were with me so vividly that I could still hear the music and the laughter, faint and incessant, from his garden, and the cars going up and down his drive.
examples.translation_ko: 토요일 밤마다 나는 뉴욕에서 보냈다. 그의 그 찬란하고 눈부신 파티들이 너무나 생생하게 내 안에 남아 있어서, 여전히 그의 정원에서 들려오는 희미하고 끊임없는 음악과 웃음소리, 그리고 그의 진입로를 오르내리는 자동차 소리를 들을 수 있었기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When I left Rome I corresponded with him, and about once in two months received from him long letters in queer English, which brought before me vividly his spluttering, enthusiastic, gesticulating conversation.
examples.translation_ko: 로마를 떠난 후 나는 그와 편지를 주고받았는데, 두 달에 한 번 정도 그로부터 이상한 영어로 쓰인 긴 편지를 받았고, 그 편지는 더듬거리며 열정적으로 몸짓을 섞어가며 나누던 그의 대화를 생생하게 떠올리게 해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From sew + -ing.
definition_en: The act of sewing or the skill of working with a needle and thread.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of sew

examples.text: His wife was seated near the stove at her sewing, and she rose as I came in.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 아내는 난로 근처에 앉아 바느질을 하고 있다가 내가 들어오자 일어났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His father was a spare old man, his hands gnarled after the work of a lifetime, silent and upright; in the evening he read the paper aloud, while his wife and daughter (now married to the captain of a fishing smack), unwilling to lose a moment, bent over their sewing.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 아버지는 마른 노인으로, 평생의 노동으로 거칠어진 손을 가졌으며, 과묵하고 꼿꼿했다. 저녁이면 그는 신문을 소리 내어 읽었고, 그의 아내와 딸(지금은 어선 선장과 결혼했다)은 한 순간도 허비하지 않으려는 듯 바느질에 몰두했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English quysshyn, from later Old French coissin (modern coussin), from Vulgar Latin *coxīnus (“seat pad”), derived from Latin coxa (“hi...
definition_en: A soft pad used for comfort or support.

senses.gloss: A throw pillow.
A thin, flat pad used on hard chairs and sometimes toilet seats.
A soft mass of material stuffed into a cloth bag, used for comfort or support.

examples.text: “What wonderful cushions you have,” said Mr. Van Busche Taylor.
examples.translation_ko: "정말 멋진 쿠션들이군요." 반 부셰 테일러 씨가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He sat me down in a chair, patting me as though I were a cushion, pressed cigars upon me, cakes, wine.
examples.translation_ko: 나를 의자에 앉히며 쿠션을 두드리듯 내 몸을 토닥거리고, 시가와 케이크와 포도주를 억지로 권했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *h₁eǵʰs
From Middle English menden (“to cure; to do good to, benefit; to do or make better, improve; to get better, recover; to keep in a...
definition_en: To repair or fix something.

senses.gloss: To physically repair (something that is broken, defaced, decayed, torn, or otherwise damaged).
senses.example: My trousers have a big rip in them and need mending.

senses.gloss: To add fuel to (a fire).
senses.example: He mended the fire and turned the meat on the greenwood racks.

senses.gloss: To correct or put right (an error, a fault, etc.); to rectify, to remedy.
senses.example: [S]he peered into her handbag mirror to mend her rouge: […]

examples.text: Mrs. Stroeve sewed, and I thought I recognised the shirt she was mending as Strickland’s.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브 부인은 바느질을 하고 있었는데, 그녀가 꿰매고 있는 셔츠가 스트릭랜드의 것인 듯했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Meanwhile, Mrs. Stroeve sat quietly mending her stockings, without talking, and she listened to all he said with a quiet smile on her lips.
examples.translation_ko: 한편 스트루브 부인은 조용히 앉아서 말없이 스타킹을 꿰매고 있었는데, 그가 하는 말을 모두 입가에 잔잔한 미소를 띠며 듣고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From stock (“cover with material”) + -ing. Corruption of old plural -en, i.e. stocken, now singular.
definition_en: A type of hosiery that covers the foot and leg.

senses.gloss: A soft garment, usually knit or woven, worn on the foot and lower leg under shoes or other footwear.
senses.example: a pair of stockings

senses.gloss: A large, sock-like bag used to store small Christmas gifts, typically hung on a mantelpiece.
A broad ring of a different fur colour on the lower part of the leg of a quadruped.

examples.text: Meanwhile, Mrs. Stroeve sat quietly mending her stockings, without talking, and she listened to all he said with a quiet smile on her lips.
examples.translation_ko: 한편 스트루브 부인은 조용히 앉아서 말없이 스타킹을 꿰매고 있었는데, 그가 하는 말을 모두 입가에 잔잔한 미소를 띠며 듣고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Some wear black shifts and flesh-coloured stockings; some with curly hair, dyed yellow, are dressed like little girls in short muslin frocks.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 여자는 검은 속옷에 살색 스타킹을 신고 있고, 어떤 여자는 노랗게 염색한 곱슬머리를 하고 짧은 모슬린 원피스를 입어 마치 어린 소녀처럼 차려입었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Learned borrowing from Latin affectiōnātus. By surface analysis, affection + -ate (adjective-forming suffix). Doublet of aficionado.
definition_en: Showing or feeling love and kindness.

senses.gloss: Having affection or warm regard; loving; fond.
senses.example: She eulogised her always warm and affectionate brother.

senses.gloss: Characterised by or proceeding from affection; indicating love; tender.
senses.example: the affectionate care of a parent; an affectionate countenance; an affectionate message; affectionate language

senses.gloss: Eager; passionate; strongly inclined toward something.

examples.text: “Don’t be affectionate before strangers, Dirk,” she said.
examples.translation_ko: "낯선 사람들 앞에서 애정 표현은 하지 마세요, 더크." 그녀가 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Poor pantaloon, he was not an object to excite love, but the smile in her eyes was affectionate, and it was possible that her reserve concealed a very deep feeling.
examples.translation_ko: 불쌍한 어릿광대, 그는 사랑을 불러일으킬 만한 대상은 아니었지만, 그녀의 눈에 담긴 미소는 다정했고, 그녀의 차분함이 아주 깊은 감정을 숨기고 있을 가능성도 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From comely + -ness (“the quality of being”).
definition_en: The quality of being attractive and pleasing.

senses.gloss: Quality of being comely; beauty, attractiveness.

examples.text: She was not the ravishing creature that his love-sick fancy saw, but she had a grave comeliness.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그의 사랑에 병든 상상이 그려낸 황홀한 피조물은 아니었지만, 엄숙한 아름다움을 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was the constant lover, and though she grew old, losing her rounded lines and her fair comeliness, to him she would certainly never alter.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 변함없는 연인이었고, 그녀가 나이 들어 둥근 몸매와 아름다운 용모를 잃더라도 그에게는 결코 변하지 않을 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested about 1380. From Middle English abundaunt, habundaunt, aboundant, from Anglo-Norman abundant, from Old French abondant, from Latin a...
definition_en: Having or showing a large amount of something.

senses.gloss: Fully sufficient; found in copious supply; in great quantity; overflowing.
senses.example: Blackberries are abundant in this part of the country in October, so we always make lots of jam.

senses.gloss: Richly supplied; wealthy; possessing in great quantity.
senses.example: Abundant in goodness and truth.

senses.gloss: Being an abundant number, i.e. less than the sum of all of its divisors except itself.

examples.text: Her hair, brown and abundant, was plainly done, her face was very pale, and her features were good without being distinguished.
examples.translation_ko: 갈색의 풍성한 머리카락은 소박하게 빗어 올렸고, 얼굴은 매우 창백했으며, 이목구비는 뛰어나지는 않지만 단정했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He must have acquired experiences which would form abundant material for a picaresque novel of modern Paris, but he remained aloof, and judging from his conversation there was nothing in those years that had made a particular impression on him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 현대 파리를 배경으로 한 피카레스크 소설의 풍부한 소재가 될 만한 경험들을 쌓았을 것이다. 하지만 그는 초연함을 유지했고, 그의 대화로 판단해보건대 그 세월 동안 그에게 특별한 인상을 남긴 것은 아무것도 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Rebracketing of napron (a napron → an apron), from Middle English naperoun, napron, apron, from Old French napperon, diminutive of nappe (“tableclo...
definition_en: To cover or protect with an apron.

senses.gloss: An article of clothing worn over the front of the torso and/or legs for protection from spills; also historically worn by Freemasons and as part of women's fashion.
The short cassock ordinarily worn by English bishops.
The paved area of an airport, especially the area where aircraft park away from a terminal.

examples.text: He saw her roll down her sleeves and remove her apron—the apron hung on a peg behind the door—and take the bottle of oxalic acid and go with it into the bedroom.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀가 소매를 내리고 앞치마를 벗는 모습을 보았다—그 앞치마는 문 뒤 못에 걸려 있었다—그리고 옥살산 병을 들고 침실로 들어가는 모습을.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But when Stroeve spoke of Chardin it was not without reason, and she reminded me curiously of that pleasant housewife in her mob-cap and apron whom the great painter has immortalised.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 스트루브가 샤르댕을 언급한 것은 이유가 없지 않았고, 그녀는 그 위대한 화가가 불멸의 작품으로 남긴 모자를 쓰고 앞치마를 두른 그 다정한 주부를 기묘하게 연상시켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English upbringinge, equivalent to upbring + -ing.
definition_en: The process of educating and training a child.

senses.gloss: The traits acquired during one's childhood training
The raising or training of a child.
senses.example: Through her upbringing, Mildred's father had carefully programmed her to expect very little from life.

examples.text: Though she was English, I could not exactly place her, and it was not obvious from what rank in society she sprang, what had been her upbringing, or how she had lived before her marriage.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 영국인이었지만, 나는 그녀의 정확한 출신을 알 수 없었고, 그녀가 어떤 사회 계층 출신인지, 어떤 교육을 받았는지, 결혼 전에 어떻게 살았는지도 분명하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His wife’s tidiness was one of the traits which had so much pleased him; his own upbringing had given him a tender sympathy for the delight in orderliness; and when he had seen her instinctive desire to put each thing in its appointed place it had given him a little warm feeling in his heart.
examples.translation_ko: 아내의 정돈된 생활은 그를 그토록 기쁘게 했던 특징 중 하나였다. 그 자신의 성장 배경이 질서를 좋아하는 마음에 대한 따뜻한 공감을 심어주었고, 모든 것을 제자리에 두려는 그녀의 본능적인 욕구를 보았을 때 그의 마음에 작은 따뜻함을 안겨주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Roman.
definition_en: Relating to ancient Rome or its culture.

senses.gloss: Upright, as opposed to italic.
senses.example: In some early printed Bibles quoted text is indicated by changing the font from roman to italic.

senses.gloss: Of or related to the Latin alphabet or roman numerals.

examples.text: “She was a governess in the family of some Roman prince, and the son of the house seduced her.
examples.translation_ko: "그녀는 어떤 로마 귀족 집안의 가정교사였는데, 그 집 아들이 그녀를 유혹했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was painting a group of Italian peasants, in the costume of the Campagna, lounging on the steps of a Roman church.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 캄파냐 지방의 의상을 입은 이탈리아 농민들이 로마의 한 교회 계단에 늘어져 있는 모습을 그리고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Latin criticus + -al, from Ancient Greek κριτικός (kritikós, “of or for judging, able to discern”), from
κρίνω (krínō, “I separate, judge”); a...
definition_en: Having or showing a careful and detailed analysis of something.

senses.gloss: Inclined to find fault or criticize.
senses.example: A good teacher is fair but critical.

senses.gloss: Pertaining to, or indicating, a crisis or turning point.
senses.example: This is a critical moment.

senses.gloss: Extremely important.
senses.example: It's critical that you deliver this on time.

examples.text: I had heard some story of her too, a critical, unpleasant story, but what it was I had forgotten long ago.
examples.translation_ko: 나도 그녀에 대한 이야기를 들은 적이 있었다. 비판적이고 불쾌한 이야기였지만, 그것이 무엇이었는지는 오래전에 잊어버렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was strange that his critical sense, so accurate and unconventional when he dealt with the work of others, should be satisfied in himself with what was hackneyed and vulgar beyond belief.
examples.translation_ko: 다른 사람의 작품을 다룰 때는 그토록 정확하고 독창적이던 그의 비판적 안목이, 자신의 경우에는 믿을 수 없을 만큼 진부하고 저속한 것에 만족한다는 사실이 이상했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English displayen, from Anglo-Norman despleier and Old French despleier, desploiier, from Medieval Latin displicare (“to unfold, displa...
definition_en: Show or present something.

senses.gloss: A show or spectacle.
senses.example: The trapeze artist put on an amazing acrobatic display.

examples.text: There entered a tall man in khaki, with the parson’s collar, handsome in a somewhat heavy fashion, but with the frank eyes that I remembered in him as a boy.
examples.translation_ko: 목사복 칼라를 한 카키색 군복의 키 큰 남자가 들어왔는데, 다소 둔중한 느낌이지만 잘생긴 편이었고, 내가 그를 소년으로 기억하던 때의 그 솔직한 눈빛을 그대로 지니고 있었다.

definition_en: A person you love or are fond of.

senses.gloss: A person very much liked or loved by someone, especially when both partners are young.

senses.gloss: A term of endearment, especially for a girlfriend, fiancée, or wife.

senses.gloss: A long, thin and flexible form of material, generally with a round cross-section, used in sewing, weaving or in the construction of string.
A continued theme or idea.

etymology: From Anglo-Norman resumer, Middle French resumer, from Latin resumere, from re- + sumere (“to take”).
definition_en: To summarize or recount something briefly.

senses.gloss: To take back possession of (something)
senses.example: Ladies and gentlemen, please resume your seats.

senses.gloss: To summarise.
senses.example: He […] used to say that each separate death had taught him something new about death, and that he was going to resume this knowledge in a philosophic essay about dying.

senses.gloss: To start (something) again that has been stopped or paused from the point at which it was stopped or paused; continue, carry on.

examples.text: “She really ought to get away from him,” resumed Catherine to me.

senses.gloss: An examination of catechumens, in the last week of Lent, who were to receive baptism on Easter Day.

examples.text: He had just shaved, for there was a white spot of lather on his cheekbone, and he was most respectful in his greeting to everyone in the room.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: After a moment’s hesitation, Strickland scrambled to his feet, and together they went to the Bouchée de Pain, where the hungry are given a wedge of bread, which they must eat there and then, for it is forbidden to take it away; and then to the Cuillère de Soupe, where for a week, at eleven and four, you may get a bowl of thin, salt soup.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 망설인 후 스트릭랜드는 비틀거리며 일어났고, 둘은 함께 부셰 드 팽으로 갔다. 그곳에서는 굶주린 자들에게 빵 한 조각을 주는데, 그 자리에서 바로 먹어야 했다. 가져가는 것은 금지되어 있었기 때문이다. 그다음에는 퀴예르 드 수프로 갔는데, 그곳에서는 일주일 동안 열한 시와 네 시에 묽고 짠 수프 한 그릇을 얻을 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English tidy, tydy, tidi (“timely, seasonal, opportune”), from tide (“time”) + -y. Cognate with Saterland Frisian tiedig (“timely, earl...
definition_en: Neat and organized.

senses.gloss: Arranged neatly and in order.
senses.example: She always kept her desk immaculately tidy; nothing was ever out of place.

senses.gloss: Not messy; neat and controlled.
senses.example: Keep Britain tidy by picking up litter.

senses.gloss: Satisfactory; comfortable.

examples.text: He told me of his childhood in the tidy brick house, and of his mother’s passionate orderliness.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 나에게 말끔한 벽돌집에서 보낸 어린 시절과 어머니의 열정적인 정리정돈 습관에 대해 이야기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When in luck he was able to make a tidy sum; but the shabbiness of his clothes at last frightened the sight-seers, and he could not find people adventurous enough to trust themselves to him.
examples.translation_ko: 운이 좋을 때는 제법 괜찮은 돈을 벌 수 있었지만, 마침내 그의 남루한 옷차림이 관광객들을 겁주게 되어 그를 믿고 따라갈 만큼 모험심 있는 사람들을 찾을 수 없게 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English aventurous, aunterous, auntrous, from Old French aventuros (whence French aventureux). By surface analysis, adventure + -ous.
definition_en: Having a desire for adventure and travel.

senses.gloss: Inclined to adventure; willing to take risks; prone to embark on hazardous enterprises; daring.
senses.example: The San Juan market is Mexico City's most famous deli of exotic meats, where an adventurous shopper can hunt down hard-to-find critters such as ostrich, wild boar and crocodile.

senses.gloss: Full of risks; risky; liable to be in danger; requiring courage; rash.
senses.example: take an adventurous viewpoint

examples.text: I began to like New York, the racy, adventurous feel of it at night, and the satisfaction that the constant flicker of men and women and machines gives to the restless eye.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 뉴욕을 좋아하기 시작했다. 밤의 생생하고 모험적인 느낌과, 끊임없이 깜박이는 남녀와 기계들이 불안한 눈에 주는 만족감을 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When in luck he was able to make a tidy sum; but the shabbiness of his clothes at last frightened the sight-seers, and he could not find people adventurous enough to trust themselves to him.
examples.translation_ko: 운이 좋을 때는 제법 괜찮은 돈을 벌 수 있었지만, 마침내 그의 남루한 옷차림이 관광객들을 겁주게 되어 그를 믿고 따라갈 만큼 모험심 있는 사람들을 찾을 수 없게 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From unwilling + -ness.
definition_en: A lack of willingness to do something.

senses.gloss: The property of being unwilling.

examples.text: She wasn’t able to endure being at a disadvantage and, given this unwillingness, I suppose she had begun dealing in subterfuges when she was very young in order to keep that cool, insolent smile turned to the world and yet satisfy the demands of her hard, jaunty body.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 불리한 처지에 놓이는 것을 견딜 수 없었고, 그런 성격 때문에 아주 어릴 때부터 속임수를 쓰기 시작했을 것이다. 세상을 향해서는 그 차갑고 건방진 미소를 유지하면서도, 동시에 자신의 단단하고 당당한 몸이 요구하는 것들을 만족시키기 위해서 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: So far as I could make out, he painted with great difficulty, and in his unwillingness to accept help from anyone lost much time in finding out for himself the solution of technical problems which preceding generations had already worked out one by one.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 알아본 바로는, 그는 매우 어렵게 그림을 그렸고, 누구의 도움도 받으려 하지 않는 고집 때문에 이전 세대들이 이미 하나씩 해결해놓은 기술적 문제들의 해답을 스스로 찾아내느라 많은 시간을 허비했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English oblivious, from Latin oblīviōsus (“forgetful, oblivious”), formed from oblīvium (“forgetfulness, oblivion”) + -ōsus (“full of, ...
definition_en: Unaware of one's surroundings or a situation.

senses.gloss: Lacking awareness; unmindful; unaware, unconscious of.
senses.example: Your grandmother is completely oblivious to her surroundings.

senses.gloss: Forgetful.
senses.example: He's hopelessly oblivious, always forgetting his appointments.

examples.text: Each night he added to the pattern of his fancies until drowsiness closed down upon some vivid scene with an oblivious embrace.
examples.translation_ko: 매일 밤 그는 자신의 환상의 무늬에 새로운 것을 더해갔고, 마침내 졸음이 어떤 생생한 장면을 망각의 품에 안을 때까지 계속되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I had the feeling that he worked on a canvas with all the force of his violent personality, oblivious of everything in his effort to get what he saw with the mind’s eye; and then, having finished, not the picture perhaps, for I had an idea that he seldom brought anything to completion, but the passion that fired him, he lost all care for it.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 캔버스 앞에서 작업할 때는 마음의 눈으로 본 것을 얻어내려는 노력에 모든 것을 잊은 채, 격렬한 성격의 온 힘을 다해 그림을 그린다는 느낌이 들었다. 그리고 나서 그림을 완성하고 나면—아마 그림 자체가 아니라, 그는 어떤 것도 완성까지 가져가는 일이 드물다는 생각이 들었기 때문이다—그를 불타오르게 했던 열정이 끝나고 나면, 그는 그 작품에 대한 모든 관심을 잃어버렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin completio, completionem, from complere (“to fill up, complete”); comparable to English complete + -ion.
definition_en: The act of making something complete.

senses.gloss: The act or state of being or making something complete; conclusion, accomplishment.
The conclusion of an act of conveyancing concerning the sale of a property.
A forward pass that is successfully caught by the intended receiver.

examples.text: The demon which possessed him was exorcised at last, and with the completion of the work, for which all his life had been a painful preparation, rest descended on his remote and tortured soul.
examples.translation_ko: 그를 사로잡았던 악마가 마침내 쫓겨났고, 평생을 고통스러운 준비 과정으로 보낸 그 작업이 완성되면서 그의 외롭고 고통받던 영혼에 안식이 내려왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English proces, from Old French procés (“journey”), from Latin prōcessus (“course, progression”), nominalization of prōcēdō (“proceed, ...
definition_en: A series of actions or operations undertaken to achieve an end.

senses.gloss: A series of events leading to a result or product.
senses.example: This product of last month's quality standards committee is quite good, even though the process was flawed.

senses.gloss: The set of procedures used in the manufacture of a product, especially in the food and chemical industries.
A path or succession of states through which a system passes.

examples.text: “Nonsense,” I answered promptly; “I don’t disapprove of the boa-constrictor; on the contrary, I’m interested in his mental processes.”
examples.translation_ko: "말도 안 되는 소리군요." 나는 즉시 대답했다. "나는 보아뱀을 못마땅하게 여기지 않습니다. 오히려 그놈의 정신적 과정에 흥미를 느끼죠."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was married to an American woman, obese and slatternly, fallen to this pass by Heaven knows what process of degradation, and every day the boarders took it in turns to help her with the housework.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 미국인 여자와 결혼했는데, 비만하고 단정치 못한 여자로 하늘만이 아는 어떤 타락의 과정을 거쳐 이런 처지에 떨어진 사람이었고, 매일 하숙생들이 돌아가며 그녀의 집안일을 도왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From dry + -ly.
definition_en: In a dry manner; without enthusiasm or emotion.

senses.gloss: In a dry manner.

examples.text: He smiled dryly, but said nothing.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 씁쓸하게 미소를 지었지만 아무 말도 하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He smiled dryly and pulled his beard.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 씁쓸하게 미소를 지으며 수염을 쓰다듬었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From nature + -ed.
definition_en: Having a particular quality or character.

senses.gloss: Having or possessing the specified disposition or temperament.

examples.text: His body was shaped like a huge duck’s egg; and his eyes, sharp, blue, and good-natured, rested now and then with self-satisfaction on his enormous paunch.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 몸은 거대한 오리알 모양이었고, 날카롭고 푸른 선량한 눈은 때때로 자신의 엄청난 배를 자족스럽게 내려다보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I do not know that it was attractive, but it lit up his face, changing the expression, which was generally sombre, and gave it a look of not ill-natured malice.
examples.translation_ko: 그것이 매력적이었는지는 확실하지 않지만, 그의 얼굴을 환하게 밝혀 평소 침울했던 표정을 바꾸어 놓으며 악의 없는 악의에 찬 모습을 보여주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Ancient Greek ἀναχωρητής (anakhōrētḗs, “anchorite”), from ἀναχωρέω (anakhōréō, “to withdraw, retire”), via Latin anchorēta, a variant of anach...
definition_en: A person who lives a solitary life of prayer and contemplation.

senses.gloss: One who lives in isolation or seclusion, especially for religious reasons; hermit.
senses.example:
“Haven't you been in love since you came to Paris?”
“I haven't got time for that sort of nonsense. Life isn't long enough for love and art.”
“Your appearance doesn't suggest the anchorite.”

examples.text: “Your appearance doesn’t suggest the anchorite.”
examples.translation_ko: "당신 외모는 은둔자 같지 않은데요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He lived in Paris more lonely than an anchorite in the deserts of Thebes.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 파리에서 테베 사막의 은둔자보다도 더 외롭게 살았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From searching + -ly.
definition_en: Examining or investigating something carefully.

senses.gloss: In a searching manner.
senses.example: He stared at me searchingly, trying to determine if I was lying.

examples.text: She sat down, glanced searchingly at Miss Baker and then at me, and continued: “I looked outdoors for a minute, and it’s very romantic outdoors.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 자리에 앉더니 베이커 양을 살피듯 바라보고 나서 나를 보며 말을 이었다. "잠깐 밖을 내다봤는데, 밖이 정말 낭만적이에요.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I paused, and I looked at him searchingly.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 말을 멈추고 그를 예리하게 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English rejoicen, rejoisen, from Old French resjoir. Doublet of rejoy. Compare French réjouir; Spanish regocijar; Portuguese regozijar;...
definition_en: Feel or express great happiness.

senses.gloss: To be very happy, be delighted, exult; to feel joy.
senses.example: Leicester closed out the win to spark emotional scenes as those inside Wembley rejoiced in a landmark victory.

senses.gloss: To have (someone) as a lover or spouse; to enjoy sexually.
To make happy, exhilarate.
senses.example: Were he [Cain] alive, it would rejoice his soul to see what mischief it had made.

examples.text: You rejoice in your freedom, and you feel that at last you can call your soul your own.
examples.translation_ko: 자유를 만끽하며, 마침내 네 영혼을 온전히 네 것이라고 부를 수 있다고 느끼겠지.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I had a lively picture of Captain Nichols flying headlong down a narrow gangway before the uplifted foot of an angry mate, and, like a true Englishman, rejoicing in the spirit of the Mercantile Marine.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 니콜스 선장이 성난 항해사의 치켜든 발에 쫓겨 좁은 갑판길을 머리부터 내달리는 생생한 모습을 그려보았고, 진정한 영국인답게 상선대의 기개에 기뻐했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The adjective is derived from Late Middle English immaterial, inmateriall (“incorporeal; spiritual”), from Middle French immateriel (“not material”...
definition_en: Not relevant to the matter at hand.

senses.gloss: Having no matter or substance; incorporeal.
senses.example: Some believe that because ghosts are immaterial, they can pass through walls.

senses.gloss: Of the nature of the soul or spirit; spiritual.
Of no importance; inconsequential, insignificant, unimportant.

examples.text: You felt that it was ready to be wafted away on the immaterial air, and death bore all the aspect of a beloved friend.”
examples.translation_ko: 그 영혼은 무형의 대기 속으로 언제든 떠날 준비가 되어 있는 것 같았고, 죽음은 사랑하는 친구의 모든 면모를 지니고 있었다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You feel like a disembodied spirit, immaterial; and you seem to be able to touch beauty as though it were a palpable thing; and you feel an intimate communion with the breeze, and with the trees breaking into leaf, and with the iridescence of the river.
examples.translation_ko: 마치 육체를 벗어난 영혼처럼, 비물질적인 존재가 된 기분이야. 그리고 아름다움을 마치 만질 수 있는 실체인 것처럼 손에 닿을 수 있을 것 같고, 산들바람과, 잎을 틔우는 나무들과, 강물의 무지갯빛과 친밀한 교감을 나누는 것 같아.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French palpable and its source, Latin palpābilis, which is from palpō (“to touch softly”) + -bilis.
definition_en: Clearly noticeable or tangible.

senses.gloss: Capable of being touched, felt or handled; touchable, tangible.
senses.example: The force of her horror must have been palpable in the air, because Jorge's eyes opened as she raised the bayonet up. "Fina?"

senses.gloss: Obvious or easily perceived; noticeable.
senses.example: By Thursday, there was a palpable sense of frustration with the opposition’s strategy on the streets of Caracas, people in the capital said.

senses.gloss: That can be detected by palpation.

examples.text: The silence of the studio seemed to gather body, so that it became an almost palpable presence.
examples.translation_ko: 작업실의 정적이 실체를 갖춘 듯 응축되어 거의 만질 수 있을 정도의 존재감이 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You feel like a disembodied spirit, immaterial; and you seem to be able to touch beauty as though it were a palpable thing; and you feel an intimate communion with the breeze, and with the trees breaking into leaf, and with the iridescence of the river.
examples.translation_ko: 마치 육체를 벗어난 영혼처럼, 비물질적인 존재가 된 기분이야. 그리고 아름다움을 마치 만질 수 있는 실체인 것처럼 손에 닿을 수 있을 것 같고, 산들바람과, 잎을 틔우는 나무들과, 강물의 무지갯빛과 친밀한 교감을 나누는 것 같아.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English comunioun, communyoun, from Anglo-Norman comunion or Middle French communion, from Ecclesiastical Latin commūniō (“communion”),...
definition_en: A shared or joint participation in a particular activity.

senses.gloss: A joining together of minds or spirits; a mental connection.
Holy Communion; the Eucharist.
senses.example: It is with the day of her first communion that this narrative of mine begins.

senses.gloss: A form of ecclesiastical unity between the Roman Catholic Church and another, so that the latter is considered part of the former.

examples.text: It is like the sadness which you may see in the jester’s eyes when a merry company is laughing at his sallies; his lips smile and his jokes are gayer because in the communion of laughter he finds himself more intolerably alone.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 유쾌한 일행이 어릿광대의 농담에 웃고 있을 때 그의 눈에서 볼 수 있는 슬픔과 같다. 웃음의 교감 속에서 자신이 더욱 견딜 수 없을 만큼 외롭다는 것을 깨닫기 때문에 그의 입술은 미소 짓고 농담은 더욱 경쾌해진다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You feel like a disembodied spirit, immaterial; and you seem to be able to touch beauty as though it were a palpable thing; and you feel an intimate communion with the breeze, and with the trees breaking into leaf, and with the iridescence of the river.
examples.translation_ko: 마치 육체를 벗어난 영혼처럼, 비물질적인 존재가 된 기분이야. 그리고 아름다움을 마치 만질 수 있는 실체인 것처럼 손에 닿을 수 있을 것 같고, 산들바람과, 잎을 틔우는 나무들과, 강물의 무지갯빛과 친밀한 교감을 나누는 것 같아.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French meditacion, from Latin meditatio, from meditatus, the past participle of meditārī (“to meditate, to think over, consider”), itself ...
definition_en: A state of deep thought or concentration.

senses.gloss: A devotional exercise of, or leading to, contemplation.

Any of various types of achieving more or less altered states of consciousness, such as vacancy of mind or prolonged contemplation on a single sensation or thought, through relaxed or focused mental and physical activity generally of a nonstrenuous and non–substance-induced nature.
A contemplative discourse, often on a religious or philosophical subject.
senses.example: Her book is less a cookbook than a meditation on the craft of cookery.

examples.text: I should have thought it needed a good deal of character to throw up a career after half an hour’s meditation, because you saw in another way of living a more intense significance.
examples.translation_ko: 삼십 분 정도 생각해본 뒤에 다른 삶의 방식에서 더 강렬한 의미를 발견했다는 이유로 자신의 경력을 포기하는 것이야말로 상당한 인격을 필요로 하는 일이라고 나는 생각했을 텐데.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I spent long hours in the Louvre, the most friendly of all galleries and the most convenient for meditation; or idled on the quays, fingering second-hand books that I never meant to buy.
examples.translation_ko: 루브르에서 오랜 시간을 보냈는데, 그곳은 모든 미술관 중에서 가장 친근하고 명상하기에 가장 편리한 곳이었다. 아니면 센 강변에서 빈둥거리며 살 생각도 없는 헌책들을 뒤적거렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English king, kyng, from Old English cyng, cyning (“king”), from Proto-West Germanic *kuning, from Proto-Germanic *kuningaz, *kunungaz ...
definition_en: The supreme ruler of a kingdom.

senses.gloss: A male monarch; a man who heads a monarchy; in an absolute monarchy, the supreme ruler of his nation.
senses.example: Henry VIII was the king of England from 1509 to 1547.

senses.gloss: The monarch with the most power and authority in a monarchy, regardless of sex.
senses.example: Hatshepsut was ruling as a king, not queen and she needed to be recognised as such.

senses.gloss: A powerful or majorly influential person; someone who holds the preeminent position.
senses.example: Howard Stern styled himself as the "king of all media".

examples.text: It was full of money—that was the inexhaustible charm that rose and fell in it, the jingle of it, the cymbals’ song of it … High in a white palace the king’s daughter, the golden girl …
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 돈으로 가득했다—그 안에서 솟아오르고 가라앉는 무궁무진한 매력, 그것의 짤랑거림, 그것의 심벌즈 노래가 바로 그것이었다 … 하얀 궁전 높은 곳의 왕의 딸, 황금빛 소녀가 …
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was a dinner for a King when he brought in a huge dish of it, succulent with tomatoes, and we ate it together with the good household bread and a bottle of red wine.
examples.translation_ko: 토마토로 맛을 낸 커다란 접시의 스파게티를 가져올 때면 그야말로 왕의 만찬이었고, 우리는 그것을 집에서 만든 좋은 빵과 적포도주 한 병과 함께 먹었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French succulent, from Latin succulentus.
definition_en: Having a thick, fleshy texture.

senses.gloss: Juicy or lush.
senses.example: “Ah. Good evening, sir. Can I interest you in a meal? A succulent Chinese meal?”

senses.gloss: Luscious or delectable.
senses.example: The peaceful revolution was achieved in the United States following 1820, largely under the guise of succulent phrases and legal technicalities.

senses.gloss: Having fleshy leaves or other tissues that store water.

examples.text: A succulent hash arrived, and Mr. Wolfshiem, forgetting the more sentimental atmosphere of the old Metropole, began to eat with ferocious delicacy.
examples.translation_ko: 맛있는 해시가 나왔고, 울프샤임 씨는 옛 메트로폴의 감상적인 분위기는 잊은 채 사나우면서도 우아하게 먹기 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was a dinner for a King when he brought in a huge dish of it, succulent with tomatoes, and we ate it together with the good household bread and a bottle of red wine.
examples.translation_ko: 토마토로 맛을 낸 커다란 접시의 스파게티를 가져올 때면 그야말로 왕의 만찬이었고, 우리는 그것을 집에서 만든 좋은 빵과 적포도주 한 병과 함께 먹었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested in 1731; borrowed from Medieval Latin accentuātus, perfect passive participle of accentuō (see -ate (verb-forming suffix)), from Lat...
definition_en: To emphasize or stress something.

senses.gloss: To pronounce with an accent or vocal stress.
To bring out distinctly; to make more noticeable or prominent; to emphasize.
senses.example: Soft girl makeup, as the name suggests is a pastel, sweet style that focuses on accentuating natural features with a signature element being blush and faux freckles.

senses.gloss: To mark with a written accent.

examples.text: She was a slender, small-breasted girl, with an erect carriage, which she accentuated by throwing her body backward at the shoulders like a young cadet.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 날씬하고 가슴이 작은 소녀였는데, 꼿꼿한 자세를 하고 있었고, 젊은 사관생도처럼 어깨를 뒤로 젖혀 그 자세를 더욱 강조했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But I thought that was perhaps no more than a natural reserve accentuated by the verbose frankness of her husband.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그것은 아마도 남편의 수다스러운 솔직함 때문에 더욱 두드러져 보이는 천성적인 내성적 성격에 불과할 것이라고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From serious + -ness.
definition_en: The quality of being serious and responsible.

senses.gloss: The state or quality of being serious.
senses.example: “[…] She takes the whole thing with desperate seriousness. But the others are all easy and jovial—thinking about the good fare that is soon to be eaten, about the hired fly, about anything.”

examples.text: The perfect seriousness with which he narrated his misfortunes convulsed me with laughter, and this added to Mrs. Stroeve’s irritation.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 자신의 불행을 이야기하는 완전히 진지한 태도가 나를 웃음으로 경련시켰고, 이것이 스트루브 부인의 짜증을 더했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I could not help laughing at this remark, made in all seriousness; but he went on, walking up and down the room like a caged beast, intent on expressing what he felt, but found such difficulty in putting coherently.
examples.translation_ko: 진지하게 내뱉은 이 말에 웃음을 참을 수 없었지만, 그는 계속해서 우리에 갇힌 짐승처럼 방 안을 오가며 자신이 느끼는 것을 표현하려 애썼다. 하지만 일관성 있게 말로 옮기는 데 큰 어려움을 겪고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To wrinkle or pucker the lips or face.

senses.gloss: To pinch or wrinkle (especially a body part); to squeeze inwardly, to dimple or fold.
senses.example: Now the skin was puckered into a million wrinkles, and on the shapeless face was the stamp of unutterable age.

examples.text: His forehead was all puckered, and his red mouth set in a pout.
examples.translation_ko: 이마에는 주름이 잔뜩 잡혔고, 붉은 입술은 삐죽하게 내밀어져 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His round eyes grew rounder still, and his brow puckered in dismay as he saw that she was angry.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 동그란 눈이 더욱 동그래졌고, 그녀가 화났다는 것을 보자 그의 이마가 당황해서 주름졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English anoyaunce (rare form of noyaunce), from Old French anuiance, anoiance, from the verb anuier (“to cause problems”), eq...
definition_en: A feeling of displeasure or frustration.

senses.gloss: That which annoys.
senses.example: Having to wait 45 minutes for the bus is a real annoyance, but it's the only way to get to work.

senses.gloss: An act or instance of annoying.
The psychological state of being annoyed or irritated.
senses.example: feeling mild annoyance

examples.text: The voice in the hall rose high with annoyance: “Very well, then, I won’t sell you the car at all … I’m under no obligations to you at all … and as for your bothering me about it at lunch time, I won’t stand that at all!”
examples.translation_ko: 복도에서 들려오는 목소리가 짜증스럽게 높아졌다. "좋아, 그럼 차는 아예 안 팔겠어... 나는 당신에게 아무런 의무도 없다고... 그리고 점심시간에 이런 일로 나를 귀찮게 하는 건 절대 참을 수 없어!"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “For goodness sake, hold your tongue,” she interrupted, tears of annoyance in her eyes.
examples.translation_ko: "제발 입 좀 다물어요." 그녀가 짜증스러운 눈물을 글썽이며 말을 끊었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pouten, probably from Scandinavian (compare Norwegian pute (“pillow, cushion”), dial. Swedish puta (“to be puffed out”), Danish...
definition_en: Express displeasure by pouting.

senses.gloss: To push out one's lips.
To thrust itself outward; to be prominent.
To be or pretend to be ill-tempered; to sulk.

examples.text: His face fell, and he pouted his lips like a scolded child.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 얼굴이 침울해졌고, 꾸중 들은 아이처럼 입술을 삐죽 내밀었다.
