examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A foolish or annoying person.

examples.text: “I’m interested in the young men, but voyons, you yourself, Monsieur Stroeve, you don’t think there’s any talent there.”
examples.translation_ko: "젊은 화가들에게는 관심이 있지만, 보세요, 스트루브 씨, 당신 자신도 거기에 재능이 있다고 생각하지 않잖아요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “He did not come much to Papeete after that, and about a year later it chanced that I had to go to that part of the island for I forgot what business, and when I had finished it I said to myself: ‘Voyons, why should I not go and see that poor Strickland?’
examples.translation_ko: "그 후로는 파페에테에 별로 오지 않았는데, 약 일 년 뒤에 우연히 무슨 일인지는 잊었지만 섬의 그 지역에 갈 일이 생겼어요. 일을 마치고 나서 혼자 생각했죠. '그런데 왜 그 불쌍한 스트릭랜드를 찾아가 보지 않을까?'
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English abstract, borrowed from Latin abstractus, perfect passive participle of abstrahō (“draw away”), formed from abs- (“away”) + tra...
definition_en: To express or represent an idea in a general way without giving details.

senses.gloss: An abridgement or summary of a longer publication.
senses.example: An analysis and abstract of every treatise he had read.

senses.gloss: Concentrated essence of a product.
A powdered solid extract of a medicinal substance mixed with lactose.

examples.text: She has a small mind, and she resents the abstract which she is unable to grasp.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 마음이 좁고, 자신이 이해할 수 없는 추상적인 것들을 원망한다.

examples.text: Sometimes he would sit silent and abstracted, taking no notice of anyone; and at others, when he was in a good humour, he would talk in his own halting way.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Causing or characterized by a sudden stop.

senses.gloss: Prone to pauses or breaks; hesitant; broken.
senses.example: Him we enlisted at Para, on the recommendation of the steamship company, on whose vessels he had learned to speak a halting English.

examples.text: I fancy that Strickland saw vaguely some spiritual meaning in material things that was so strange that he could only suggest it with halting symbols.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 물질적인 것들 속에서 너무나 기이한 어떤 정신적 의미를 막연히 보았기에, 더듬거리는 상징으로만 그것을 암시할 수 있었던 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Sometimes he would sit silent and abstracted, taking no notice of anyone; and at others, when he was in a good humour, he would talk in his own halting way.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Late Latin sarcasmus, from Ancient Greek σαρκασμός (sarkasmós, “a sneer”), from σαρκάζω (sarkázō, “I gnash the teeth (in anger)”, literally “I...
definition_en: A sharp, often ironic or sarcastic remark.

senses.gloss: Use of acerbic language to mock or convey contempt, often using irony and (in speech) often marked by overemphasis and sneering.
An individual act of the above.

examples.text: Strickland employed not the rapier of sarcasm but the bludgeon of invective.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 풍자라는 가는 검이 아니라 욕설이라는 몽둥이를 사용했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He never said a clever thing, but he had a vein of brutal sarcasm which was not ineffective, and he always said exactly what he thought.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 결코 재치 있는 말을 하지 않았지만, 나름대로 효과적인 잔인한 비꼼의 재주가 있었고, 항상 자신이 생각하는 바를 정확히 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From susceptible + -ity.
definition_en: The state of being susceptible to something.

senses.gloss: The condition of being susceptible; vulnerability.
senses.example: It has been reported that periparturient cows undergo a period of immunosuppression of various immunological parameters associated with a high susceptibility to uterine and mammary infections […]

senses.gloss: emotional sensitivity.
senses.example: The eyes were large and black, and had the moonlight's melancholy, with that tearful lustre which is the certain sign of keen susceptibility.

senses.gloss: Being vulnerable to a treatment (usually an antibiotic or antifungal); also, the degree of such vulnerability (i.e., weak, moderate, or strong).

examples.text: He was indifferent to the susceptibilities of others, and when he wounded them was amused.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 다른 사람들의 감정에 무관심했고, 상처를 주면 오히려 재미있어 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The false emphasis with which they try to deck their worthless thoughts blunts their susceptibilities.
examples.translation_ko: 그들이 자신의 무가치한 생각을 치장하려고 사용하는 거짓된 강조는 그들의 감수성을 무디게 만든다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Possibly from an alteration of clumsed (“benumbed”) or from clumse (“a stupid fellow; lout”) + -y. More at clumse.
definition_en: Having a lack of skill or coordination.

senses.gloss: Awkward, lacking coordination, not graceful, not dextrous.
senses.example: He's very clumsy. I wouldn't trust him with carrying the dishes.

senses.gloss: Not elegant or well-planned, lacking tact or subtlety.
senses.example: It is a clumsy solution, but it might work for now.

senses.gloss: Awkward or inefficient in use or construction, difficult to handle or manage especially because of shape.

examples.text: Michaelis made a clumsy attempt to distract him.
examples.translation_ko: 미카엘리스는 서툴게 그의 주의를 돌리려 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was constantly offending Dirk Stroeve so bitterly that he flung away, vowing he would never speak to him again; but there was a solid force in Strickland that attracted the fat Dutchman against his will, so that he came back, fawning like a clumsy dog, though he knew that his only greeting would be the blow he dreaded.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 끊임없이 더크 스트루브를 몹시 화나게 해서 스트루브가 다시는 그와 말하지 않겠다고 맹세하며 뛰쳐나가게 만들었지만, 스트릭랜드에게는 뚱뚱한 네덜란드인의 의지와는 반대로 그를 끌어당기는 확고한 힘이 있어서, 스트루브는 자신을 맞이할 것이 두려워하는 매질뿐이라는 것을 알면서도 서툰 개처럼 아첨하며 다시 돌아오곤 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French sensitif, from Medieval Latin sensitivus.
definition_en: Having or showing a quick and deep emotional response.

senses.gloss: Having the faculty of sensation; pertaining to the senses.
senses.example: The sensitive faculty most part overrules reason, the soul is carried hoodwinked, and the understanding captive like a beast.

senses.gloss: Responsive to stimuli.
Easily offended, upset, or hurt.
senses.example: Max is very sensitive; he cried today because of the bad news.

examples.text: There was a sardonic sincerity in Strickland which made me sensitive to anything that might suggest a pose.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드에게는 냉소적인 진실함이 있어서, 나로 하여금 가식적으로 보일 수 있는 어떤 것에도 민감하게 반응하게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He showed a skill I should never have credited him with in finding the places where the unhappy Dutchman was most sensitive.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 불행한 네덜란드인이 가장 예민해하는 부분을 찾아내는 솜씨를 보여주었는데, 나는 그에게 그런 재능이 있으리라고는 전혀 생각지 못했었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A domesticated mammal with a thick woolly coat.

senses.gloss: A woolly ruminant of the genus Ovis.
A member of the domestic species Ovis aries, the most well-known species of Ovis.
A timid, shy person who is easily led by others.

examples.text: I wouldn’t have been surprised to see a great flock of white sheep turn the corner.
examples.translation_ko: 모퉁이를 돌아 하얀 양떼가 나타나도 놀라지 않았을 것이다.

etymology: From Old English hider, from Proto-Germanic *hidrê. Cognate with Latin citer.
definition_en: Used to indicate a direction or movement towards the speaker.

senses.gloss: To this place, to here.
senses.example: He went hither and thither.

senses.gloss: over here

examples.text: It urged him hither and thither.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 그를 이리저리 몰아댔다.

examples.translation_ko: 그는 겁에 질린 양이 이리저리 목적 없이 뛰어다니는 모습을 연상시켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English deliberat(e), borrowed from Latin dēlīberātus, perfect passive participle of dēlīberō (“to consider, weigh well”) (se...
definition_en: Thoughtfully planned or done.

senses.gloss: Done on purpose; intentional.
senses.example: a deliberate attempt to cover up his crime

senses.gloss: Formed with deliberation; carefully considered; not sudden or rash.
senses.example: a deliberate opinion; a deliberate measure or result

senses.gloss: Of a person, weighing facts and arguments with a view to a choice or decision; carefully considering the probable consequences of a step; slow in determining.
senses.example: The jury took eight hours to come to its deliberate verdict.

examples.text: Her methodicalness made her suicide more deliberate.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 체계적인 성격이 자살을 더욱 의도적인 것으로 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He and his wife made a picture which the imagination gratefully dwelt upon, and the simplicity of his love for her had a deliberate grace.
examples.translation_ko: 그와 그의 아내는 상상력이 기꺼이 머물고 싶어 하는 그림을 만들어냈고, 그녀에 대한 그의 사랑의 순수함에는 의도적인 우아함이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French piédestal, itself borrowed from Italian piedistallo (literally “foot stand”). Spelling influenced by Latin pēs, pedem.
definition_en: A base or support for something, typically raised above the ground.

senses.gloss: The base or foot of a column, statue, vase, lamp.
A place of reverence or honor.
senses.example: He has put his mother on a pedestal. You can't say a word against her.

senses.gloss: A casting secured to the frame of a truck of a railcar and forming a jaw for holding a journal box.

examples.text: Dozing against the pedestal of a statue, he saw Strickland again.
examples.translation_ko: 동상 받침대에 기대어 졸고 있는 스트릭랜드를 다시 발견했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: If she had any sense of humour, it must amuse her that he should place her on a pedestal and worship her with such an honest idolatry, but even while she laughed she must have been pleased and touched.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀에게 유머 감각이 조금이라도 있었다면, 그가 자신을 받들어 모시며 그토록 순진한 우상숭배로 숭배하는 모습이 우스웠을 것이다. 하지만 웃으면서도 기뻐하고 감동했을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Considered to be morally or legally correct.

senses.gloss: Having a justification.
senses.example: The act was fully justified.

senses.gloss: Of text, arranged on a page or a computer screen such that the left and right ends of all lines within paragraphs are aligned, with the space between words adjusted as necessary. Also called fully justified to contrast with left-justified and right-justified.

examples.text: I couldn’t forgive him or like him, but I saw that what he had done was, to him, entirely justified.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그를 용서할 수도 좋아할 수도 없었지만, 그가 한 일이 그에게는 전적으로 정당한 것이었다는 걸 알 수 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He played with taste, but with more feeling than was always justified, and into his music poured all his honest, sentimental, exuberant soul.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 품위 있게 연주했지만, 때로는 정당화되기 어려울 만큼 감정을 담아 연주했고, 그의 음악에는 그의 순수하고 감상적이며 열정적인 영혼이 모두 쏟아져 나왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English heightenen, hyghtenen, equivalent to height + -en (verbal suffix).
definition_en: Make or become greater

senses.gloss: To make high; to raise higher; to elevate.
senses.example: Black Bridge, near Machynlleth, is being heightened by one metre in a £3.6 million project to reduce delays caused by flooding.

senses.gloss: To advance, increase, augment, make larger, more intense, stronger etc.
senses.example: to heighten beauty

examples.text: If personality is an unbroken series of successful gestures, then there was something gorgeous about him, some heightened sensitivity to the promises of life, as if he were related to one of those intricate machines that register earthquakes ten thousand miles away.
examples.translation_ko: 인격이란 것이 성공적인 몸짓들의 끊어지지 않는 연속이라면, 그에게는 뭔가 화려한 면이 있었다. 삶의 약속들에 대한 고조된 감수성이 있었는데, 마치 만 마일 떨어진 곳의 지진을 감지하는 정교한 기계들 중 하나와 연결되어 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The absurdity that clung to everything connected with Dirk Stroeve gave it a curious note, like an unresolved discord, but made it somehow more modern, more human; like a rough joke thrown into a serious scene, it heightened the poignancy which all beauty has.
examples.translation_ko: 더크 스트루브와 관련된 모든 것에 달라붙은 우스꽝스러움이 해결되지 않은 불협화음처럼 기묘한 색채를 더했지만, 그것이 오히려 더 현대적이고 더 인간적으로 만들었다. 진지한 장면에 던져진 거친 농담처럼, 그것은 모든 아름다움이 지닌 애절함을 더욱 고조시켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Causing or feeling shame or embarrassment.

senses.gloss: Liable to humiliate, degrade, shame or embarrass someone.
senses.example: The most rapid and most seductive transition in all human nature is that which attends the palliation of a ravenous appetite. There is something humiliating about it.

examples.text: That answer of his seemed to me strangely humiliating.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 그런 대답이 나에게는 이상하리만큼 굴욕적으로 느껴졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Stroeve had set up a Christmas-tree in his studio, and I suspected that we should both find absurd little presents hanging on its festive branches; but he was shy about seeing Strickland again; it was a little humiliating to forgive so easily insults so outrageous, and he wished me to be present at the reconciliation on which he was determined.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 자신의 화실에 크리스마스트리를 세워놓았는데, 나는 우리 둘 다 그 축제 같은 가지들에 매달린 우스꽝스러운 작은 선물들을 발견하게 될 것이라고 짐작했다. 하지만 그는 스트릭랜드를 다시 만나는 것을 부끄러워했다. 그토록 터무니없는 모욕을 그렇게 쉽게 용서하는 것은 다소 굴욕적인 일이었고, 그는 자신이 결심한 화해의 자리에 내가 함께 있기를 바랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From stuff + -y.
definition_en: Having a lot of mucus or being congested.

senses.gloss: Poorly ventilated; partially plugged.
senses.example: I can’t smell very well today – I have a stuffy nose.

senses.gloss: Uncomfortably warm without sufficient air circulation.
senses.example: We all sat in stuffy classrooms and had men in tweedy sportscoats ruin our afternoons.

senses.gloss: Stout; mettlesome; resolute.

examples.text: It was hot and stuffy, and the air was gray with smoke.
examples.translation_ko: 안은 덥고 답답했으며, 공기는 담배 연기로 회색빛이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Dirk was going home to dinner, and I proposed to find a doctor and bring him to see Strickland; but when we got down into the street, fresh after the stuffy attic, the Dutchman begged me to go immediately to his studio.
examples.translation_ko: 디르크는 저녁 식사를 하러 집으로 가려 했고, 나는 의사를 찾아 스트릭랜드를 진찰하게 하자고 제안했다. 하지만 답답한 다락방을 나와 상쾌한 거리로 내려왔을 때, 네덜란드인은 즉시 자신의 작업실로 가자고 간청했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English occasionally, occasionaly, occasyoneely, occasyonly, equivalent to occasional + -ly.
definition_en: Used at irregular intervals.

senses.gloss: On occasion: at relatively infrequent intervals, from time to time, sometimes.
senses.example: Flames could still be seen from town flaring up occasionally on a hill dotted with emergency vehicles.

senses.gloss: On an occasion, accidentally, by chance.
senses.example: I had met Lord Ossory in the forenoon, who had come to town occasionally.

senses.gloss: On the occasion of something else happening; incidentally, by the way.
senses.example: I think it is plain, that Origen, whatever Character he may have occaſionally given of this Book, did not judge it any part of the Canon...

examples.text: Occasionally a line of grey cars crawls along an invisible track, gives out a ghastly creak, and comes to rest, and immediately the ash-grey men swarm up with leaden spades and stir up an impenetrable cloud, which screens their obscure operations from your sight.
examples.translation_ko: 때때로 회색 화차들이 한 줄로 보이지 않는 선로를 따라 기어가다가 섬뜩한 삐걱거리는 소리를 내며 멈춰 선다. 그러면 즉시 재빛 회색 사내들이 납덩이 같은 삽을 들고 우르르 몰려와 뚫을 수 없는 먼지 구름을 일으켜, 그들의 모호한 작업을 시야에서 가려버린다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Strickland did not come, but presently we saw the French painter who occasionally played chess with him.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 오지 않았지만, 곧 가끔 그와 체스를 두던 프랑스 화가를 보게 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English bakere, from Old English bæcere (“baker”), from Proto-Germanic *bakārijaz (“baker”), equivalent to bake + -er. Cognat...
definition_en: A person who bakes bread and other baked goods.

senses.gloss: A person who bakes and sells bread, cakes and similar items.
A portable oven for baking.
An apple suitable for baking.
senses.example: Wealthys and McIntoshes are not good bakers.

examples.text: I called for a directory and looked out the bakers.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 전화번호부를 달라고 해서 제빵소들을 찾아보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Suddenly I remembered that he had got his commission to paint a portrait through the baker from whom he bought his bread, and it struck me that there one might find his address.
examples.translation_ko: 문득 그가 빵을 사던 제빵사를 통해 초상화 그리는 일을 의뢰받았던 것이 생각났고, 거기서 그의 주소를 알아낼 수 있을 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Not locked or secured.

senses.gloss: Not secured or protected by a lock.
senses.example: an unlocked computer file

senses.gloss: Not bound to any particular carrier.
senses.example: an unlocked iPhone

examples.text: Someone started to ask me questions, but I broke away and going upstairs looked hastily through the unlocked parts of his desk—he’d never told me definitely that his parents were dead.
examples.translation_ko: 누군가 내게 질문을 하기 시작했지만, 나는 그들을 뿌리치고 위층으로 올라가 그의 책상에서 잠기지 않은 부분들을 서둘러 뒤져보았다—그는 부모님이 돌아가셨다고 확실히 말해준 적이 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I tried the handle, and found the door unlocked.
examples.translation_ko: 손잡이를 돌려보니 문이 잠겨 있지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English obscurite, obscuryte, from Middle French obscurité and its etymon Latin obscūritās. By surface analysis, obscure + -ity.
definition_en: A state of being little known or understood.

senses.gloss: Darkness; the absence of light.
The state of being unknown; a thing that is unknown.
The quality of being difficult to understand; a thing that is difficult to understand.

examples.text: He did not know that it was already behind him, somewhere back in that vast obscurity beyond the city, where the dark fields of the republic rolled on under the night.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그것이 이미 자신의 뒤편 어딘가에, 도시 너머 광막한 어둠 속에, 공화국의 어두운 들판이 밤하늘 아래 끝없이 펼쳐진 곳에 있다는 것을 알지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I could only see that it was an attic, with a sloping roof; and a faint glimmer, no more than a less profound obscurity, came from a skylight.
examples.translation_ko: 경사진 지붕을 가진 다락방이라는 것만 알 수 있었고, 천창에서 희미한 빛이 새어 들어왔는데 그것도 그저 덜 짙은 어둠에 불과했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From harsh + -ly.
definition_en: Used to describe something that is severe or unpleasant.

senses.gloss: In a harsh manner; severely.
senses.example:
The traveller hears me now and then,
⁠And sometimes harshly will he speak:
⁠‘This fellow would make weakness weak,
And melt the waxen hearts of men.’

examples.text: “What do I owe you?” demanded Tom harshly.
examples.translation_ko: "얼마를 드리면 됩니까?" 톰이 거칠게 물었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Strickland’s voice, coming out of the darkness, harshly, made me start.
examples.translation_ko: 어둠 속에서 거칠게 터져 나온 스트릭랜드의 목소리에 나는 깜짝 놀랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French palette. Doublet of pallet.
definition_en: A range of colors or a flat surface used for mixing and applying paint.

senses.gloss: A thin board on which a painter lays and mixes colours.
The range of colors in a given work or item or body of work.
senses.example: The unified colour palette of reds, blues, and yellows used throughout the signage matches that of the institution’s logo and letterhead.

senses.gloss: The range of tones or tone colors in a given musical composition or performance.

examples.text: On the table, crowded with paints, palette-knives, and litter of all kinds, was the end of a candle.
examples.translation_ko: 물감과 팔레트 나이프, 온갖 잡동사니로 어수선한 테이블 위에 촛불 한 토막이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The doctor, wondering irritably why they behaved so strangely, entered, and there found Strickland cleaning his palette.
examples.translation_ko: 의사는 그들이 왜 그렇게 이상하게 행동하는지 짜증스럽게 궁금해하며 안으로 들어갔고, 그곳에서 스트릭랜드가 팔레트를 닦고 있는 것을 발견했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English grape, from Old French grape, grappe, crape (“cluster of fruit or flowers, bunch of grapes”), from graper, craper (“to pick gra...
definition_en: A small, round or oval fruit that grows in clusters.

senses.gloss: A small, round, smooth-skinned edible fruit, usually purple, red, or green, that grows in bunches on vines of genus Vitis.
senses.example: Grapes give us whole-fruit snacks, grape juice, raisins, wine, and more.

senses.gloss: A woody vine of genus Vitis that bears clusters of grapes; a grapevine.
senses.example: wild grape covering the back slope

senses.gloss: Any of various fruits or plants with varying resemblances to those of genus Vitis but belonging to other genera; their edibility varies.
senses.example: sea grape; tail grape

examples.text: I suggested that he should get a thermometer, and a few grapes, and some bread.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 체온계와 포도 몇 송이, 그리고 빵을 사오라고 제안했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: On the easel was a half-finished picture of a smiling Italian peasant, holding a bunch of grapes over the head of a dark-eyed girl.
examples.translation_ko: 이젤 위에는 미소 짓는 이탈리아 농부가 검은 눈의 소녀 머리 위로 포도송이를 들고 있는 반쯤 완성된 그림이 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English clatren (“to make a rattling sound”), from Old English *clatrian (attested as the Late Old English gerund clatrung), of onomato...
definition_en: Make a loud rattling noise.

senses.gloss: To make a rattling sound.
senses.example: [Hoop-and-stick] was not a little gentleman's game but was played by boys in heavy boots making a terrific noise as they clattered along on the pavements at quite a speed.

senses.gloss: To chatter noisily or rapidly.
senses.example: Here is a great deale of good matter, / loſt for lacke of telling, / Now ſicker I see, thou doeſt but clatter: / harme may come of melling.

senses.gloss: To hit; to smack.
senses.example: “An Orange bitch clattered seven shades of shite out of her,” Padraig eagerly piped up.

examples.text: Stroeve, glad to make himself useful, clattered down the stairs.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 자신이 도움이 될 수 있다는 것에 기뻐하며 계단을 쿵쿵거리며 내려갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He lifted his arm as though to strike, and then, opening his hand, let it fall with a clatter to the ground.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 치려는 듯 팔을 들어올렸다가 손을 펼치며 그것을 바닥에 떨어뜨려 덜컹거리는 소리를 냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English mete, from Old English mete (“food”), from Proto-West Germanic *mati, from Proto-Germanic *matiz (“food”), from Proto-Indo-Euro...
definition_en: A type of food obtained from animals.

senses.gloss: The flesh (muscle tissue) of an animal used as food.
senses.example: A large portion of domestic meat production comes from animals raised on factory farms.

senses.gloss: A type of meat, by anatomic position and provenance.
senses.example: The butchery's profit rate on various meats varies greatly.

senses.gloss: Food, for animals or humans, especially solid food. See also meat and drink.
senses.example: The way she said ‘dinner’ and the way she said ‘champagne’ gave meat and liquid their exact difference[…].

examples.text: Besides what I had suggested, he brought candles, and meat-juice, and a spirit-lamp.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 제안한 것들 외에도 그는 양초와 육즙, 그리고 알코올 램프를 가져왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then they cut out the copra and put it into sacks, and the women would carry it down to the trader at the village by the lagoon, and he would give in exchange for it rice and soap and tinned meat and a little money.
examples.translation_ko: 그런 다음 코프라를 잘라내어 자루에 담았고, 여자들이 그것을 석호 옆 마을의 상인에게 가져다주면 그는 그 대신 쌀과 비누와 통조림 고기, 그리고 약간의 돈을 주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English jus, juis, from Old French jus, jous, from Latin jūs (“broth, soup, sauce”), from Proto-Indo-European *yéwHs, from *yewH- (“to ...
definition_en: The liquid part of a fruit or plant.

senses.gloss: A liquid from a plant, especially fruit.
senses.example: Squeeze the orange and some juice will come out.

senses.gloss: A beverage made of juice.
senses.example: I’d like two orange juices please.

senses.gloss: A soft drink.

examples.text: There was a machine in the kitchen which could extract the juice of two hundred oranges in half an hour if a little button was pressed two hundred times by a butler’s thumb.
examples.translation_ko: 부엌에는 집사의 엄지손가락으로 작은 버튼을 이백 번 누르면 삼십 분 안에 오렌지 이백 개의 즙을 짜낼 수 있는 기계가 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Besides what I had suggested, he brought candles, and meat-juice, and a spirit-lamp.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 제안한 것들 외에도 그는 양초와 육즙, 그리고 알코올 램프를 가져왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English cherefulnes; equivalent to cheerful + -ness.
definition_en: A feeling or expression of happiness and joy.

senses.gloss: The state of being cheerful; joy.
senses.example: Or he that exhorteth, on exhortation: he that giueth, let him doe it with simplicitie: hee that ruleth, with diligence: hee that sheweth mercy, with cheerefulnesse.

examples.text: Her cheerfulness was the cheerfulness of despair.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 명랑함은 절망의 명랑함이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She looked at him with the grave cheerfulness which was one of her charms.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그녀의 매력 중 하나인 진지한 명랑함으로 그를 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English thinking, thynkynge, thenkyng, equivalent to think + -ing.
definition_en: The process of forming opinions or making decisions.

senses.gloss: Thought; gerund of think.
senses.example: What is your thinking on this subject?

examples.text: But I am slow-thinking and full of interior rules that act as brakes on my desires, and I knew that first I had to get myself definitely out of that tangle back home.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 나는 생각이 느리고 욕망에 제동을 거는 내적 규칙들로 가득한 사람이어서, 먼저 고향에서의 그 얽힌 관계를 확실히 정리해야 한다는 것을 알고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I shouldn’t sleep a wink for thinking of him.”
examples.translation_ko: 그 생각을 하면 한숨도 잘 수 없을 거예요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: The care and support of patients, especially those who are ill or injured.

senses.gloss: In the state of suckling young, lactating.
senses.example: The nursing bear wouldn't move far until her cubs were older.

senses.gloss: Referring to nurses.
senses.example: The nursing staff worked overtime at the hospital.

examples.text: “I have no objection to your nursing him.”
examples.translation_ko: "당신이 그를 간병하는 것에 대해서는 반대하지 않습니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When we went again to the hospital we saw a nursing sister.
examples.translation_ko: 다시 병원에 갔을 때 우리는 간호사를 만났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English distaunt, from Old French distant, from Latin distāns.
definition_en: Far away from something or someone.

senses.gloss: Far off (physically, logically or mentally).
senses.example: We heard a distant rumbling but didn't pay any more attention to it. She was surprised to find that her fiancé was a distant relative of hers. His distant look showed that he was not listening to me.

senses.gloss: Emotionally unresponsive or unwilling to express genuine feelings.
senses.example: Ever since our argument, she has been totally distant toward me.

senses.gloss: Imported into a cable television system from a different market (and thus possibly incurring a copyright royalty).
senses.example: Finally, there will be those unusual situations where a signal is distant to part of a CATV system and local to the rest of it.

examples.text: Her voice was cold and distant.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 목소리는 차갑고 냉담했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Rich merchants, sending their wares to the distant Indies, had lived in them calm and prosperous lives, and in their decent decay they kept still an aroma of their splendid past.
examples.translation_ko: 먼 인도로 상품을 보내던 부유한 상인들이 그 집들에서 평온하고 풍요로운 삶을 살았고, 품위 있게 낡아가는 가운데서도 여전히 찬란했던 과거의 향기를 간직하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English likken, from Old English liccian, from Proto-West Germanic *likkōn, from Proto-Germanic *likkōną, from Proto-Indo-European *ley...
definition_en: To touch or taste with the tongue.

senses.gloss: To stroke with the tongue.
senses.example: The cat licked its fur.

senses.gloss: To lap; to take in with the tongue.
senses.example: She licked the last of the honey off the spoon before washing it.

senses.gloss: To beat with repeated blows.
senses.example: "What a curious kind of a fool a girl is! Never been licked in school! Shucks! What's a licking! That's just like a girl -- they're so thin-skinned and chicken-hearted. […]"

examples.text: “I thought he knew something about breeding, but he wasn’t fit to lick my shoe.”
examples.translation_ko: "교양이 있는 사람인 줄 알았는데, 내 신발이나 핥을 자격도 없는 놈이었어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He showed that he despised you, and you lick his hand.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 당신을 경멸한다는 걸 보여줬는데, 당신은 그의 손을 핥고 있어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French tolerant, from Latin tolerans, present participle of tolerō (“endure”).
definition_en: Showing willingness to accept or respect differences.

senses.gloss: Tending to permit, allow, understand, or accept something.
senses.example: He's pretty tolerant of different political views, but don't ask him about religion.

senses.gloss: Tending to withstand or survive.
senses.example: These plants are tolerant of drought and sunlight.

examples.text: We should be very tolerant with them, and very patient.”
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 그들에게 매우 관대하고 인내심을 가져야 해."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It cannot be said that they are without guile, but they have a tolerant respect for the law, when the law is supported by strength.
examples.translation_ko: 그들에게 간계가 없다고는 할 수 없지만, 법이 힘으로 뒷받침될 때는 법에 대해 관대한 존경심을 보인다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French terrifier, from Latin terrificare.
definition_en: To fill with fear or terror.

senses.gloss: To frighten greatly; to fill with terror.
To menace or intimidate.
senses.example:
Your men are valiant but their number few,
And cannot terrifie his mightie hoſt, […]

senses.gloss: To make terrible.

examples.text: I glanced at Daisy, who was staring terrified between Gatsby and her husband, and at Jordan, who had begun to balance an invisible but absorbing object on the tip of her chin.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 개츠비와 남편 사이에서 겁에 질린 채 바라보고 있는 데이지와, 턱끝에 보이지 않지만 흥미로운 무언가의 균형을 맞추기 시작한 조던을 흘끗 보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I don’t know why, but there’s something in him that terrifies me.
examples.translation_ko: 이유는 모르겠지만, 그에게는 나를 공포에 떨게 하는 무언가가 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Origin uncertain, perhaps an alteration of chavel, or a frequentive of sheaf.
definition_en: A sudden, involuntary movement of the body, typically caused by cold or fear.

senses.gloss: To tremble or shake, especially when cold or frightened.
senses.example: They stood outside for hours, shivering in the frosty air.

senses.gloss: To cause to shake or tremble, as a sail, by steering close to the wind.

examples.text: A shiver passed through her.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 몸에 전율이 스쳐 지나갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Though he was hot from walking, he shivered.
examples.translation_ko: 걸어서 몸이 달아올랐는데도 그는 몸을 떨었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From exhaust + -ed.
definition_en: Feeling extremely tired.

senses.gloss: Very tired; zonked (out).
senses.example: The exhausted man fell asleep immediately.

senses.gloss: Depleted of resources.
senses.example: The exhausted mine was worthless once all the ore had been extracted.

senses.gloss: Emptied of contents, especially of air; that has been made into a vacuum.
senses.example: A man can live in thick air, but perishes in an exhausted receiver.

examples.text: He was absolutely exhausted.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 완전히 지쳐 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was so exhausted by the time we arrived that he allowed us to put him to bed without a word.
examples.translation_ko: 도착했을 때 그는 너무 지쳐서 한 마디 말도 없이 우리가 그를 침대에 눕히도록 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English enquery, from the Old French verb enquerre, from Latin inquīrō, composed of in- (“in, at, on; into”) + quaerō (“I seek, look fo...
definition_en: An official investigation or a formal request for information.

senses.gloss: The act of inquiring; a seeking of information by asking questions; interrogation; a question or questioning.
A search for truth, information, or knowledge; examination of facts or principles; research; investigation; inquest.
senses.example: Scientific inquiry

examples.text: At this inquiry she sat up and opened her eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 이 질문에 그녀는 몸을 일으켜 세우고 눈을 떴다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was not that he was exacting and querulous; on the contrary, he never complained, he asked for nothing, he was perfectly silent; but he seemed to resent the care that was taken of him; he received all inquiries about his feelings or his needs with a jibe, a sneer, or an oath.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 까다롭고 불평이 많아서가 아니었다. 오히려 그는 결코 불평하지 않았고, 아무것도 요구하지 않았으며, 완전히 조용했다. 하지만 그는 자신을 돌봐주는 것을 못마땅해하는 것 같았다. 그의 기분이나 필요한 것에 대한 모든 문의를 비꼬거나 냉소하거나 욕설로 받아넘겼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French détestable. By surface analysis, detest + -able.
definition_en: Extremely unpleasant or hateful

senses.gloss: Stimulating disgust or detestation; offensive; shocking.

examples.text: “I think you’re detestable.
examples.translation_ko: "당신이 혐오스럽습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I found him detestable, and as soon as he was out of danger I had no hesitation in telling him so.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 혐오스러웠고, 그가 위험에서 벗어나자마자 주저 없이 그에게 그렇게 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin dexter (“right, ready”) + -ous. Displaced native Old English handcræftiġ.
definition_en: Having or showing skill with your hands.

senses.gloss: Skillful with one's hands.
senses.example: She is pleasingly dexterous with the chopsticks, and keeps one hand lying palm up on her lap. Pinched with just the right pressure between the sticks; funny how plump women have that delicate touch.

senses.gloss: Skillful in some specific thing.
senses.example: We went frequently out with this boat a-fishing; and as I was most dexterous to catch fish for him, he never went without me.

senses.gloss: Agile; flexible; able to move fluidly and gracefully.

examples.text: He was dexterous to make him comfortable, and he exercised a cunning of which I should never have thought him capable to induce him to take the medicines prescribed by the doctor.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 스트릭랜드를 편안하게 해주는 데 능숙했고, 의사가 처방한 약을 먹도록 유도하기 위해 내가 그에게서 전혀 기대하지 못했을 교활함을 발휘했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Then she caught sight of a cat trying to get at a dish of prawns on the kitchen table, and with a dexterous gesture and a lively volley of abuse flung a book at its scampering tail.
examples.translation_ko: 그때 부엌 탁자 위 새우 접시에 손을 대려는 고양이가 눈에 띄자, 그녀는 능숙한 손놀림과 요란한 욕설을 퍼부으며 달아나는 고양이 꼬리를 향해 책을 집어던졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From tact + -ful.
definition_en: Having or showing a careful and thoughtful way of dealing with people.

senses.gloss: Possessing tact; able to deal with people in a sensitive manner.

examples.text: Probably it had been tactful to leave Daisy’s house, but the act annoyed me, and her next remark made me rigid.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지의 집을 떠난 것은 아마 현명한 처사였겠지만, 그 행동이 나를 짜증나게 했고, 그녀의 다음 말은 나를 경직시켰다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I shall never forget the tactful patience with which he persuaded him to take nourishment.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 스트릭랜드로 하여금 영양분을 섭취하도록 설득한 재치 있는 인내심을 결코 잊지 못할 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From vehement + -ly.
definition_en: Expressed with strong emotion or conviction.

senses.gloss: In a vehement manner; expressing with a strong or forceful attitude.
senses.example: vehemently opposed

examples.text: As soon as I arrived I made an attempt to find my host, but the two or three people of whom I asked his whereabouts stared at me in such an amazed way, and denied so vehemently any knowledge of his movements, that I slunk off in the direction of the cocktail table—the only place in the garden where a single man could linger without looking purposeless and alone.
examples.translation_ko: 도착하자마자 나는 주인을 찾으려고 했지만, 그의 행방을 물어본 두세 사람이 너무나 놀란 표정으로 나를 쳐다보며 그의 움직임에 대해 아는 바가 없다고 격렬하게 부인하는 바람에, 나는 칵테일 테이블 쪽으로 슬금슬금 물러났다. 정원에서 혼자 있는 남자가 목적 없고 외로워 보이지 않으면서 머물 수 있는 유일한 장소였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was nothing in her to remind you that she had so vehemently struggled against her husband’s wish to bring Strickland to the studio.
examples.translation_ko: 남편이 스트릭랜드를 작업실로 데려오려는 뜻에 그토록 격렬하게 반대했던 그녀의 모습을 떠올리게 하는 구석은 전혀 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English needeful, nedeful, from Old English nēodful (“necessary; earnest; zealous”). Equivalent to need + -ful. Cognate with Dutch nood...
definition_en: Necessary or required.

senses.gloss: Needed; necessary; mandatory; requisite; indispensable.
Needy; in need.
senses.example: […] where his active benevolence was ever found in cheerful co-operation for the cause of the humble & needful orphan […]

examples.text: She insisted on doing her share of the offices needful to the sick.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 환자에게 필요한 일들을 자신이 맡아서 하겠다고 고집했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She had done her marketing from day to day, buying only what was strictly needful, so that nothing was left over from one day to the next.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 날마다 장을 보면서 꼭 필요한 것만 사서, 하루에서 다음 날로 넘어가는 것이 아무것도 없도록 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English werde, wierde, wirde, wyrede, wurde, from Old English wyrd (“fate”), from Proto-West Germanic *wurdi, from Proto-Germanic *wurd...
definition_en: Unconventional or strange.

senses.gloss: Having an unusually strange character or behaviour.
senses.example: There are lots of weird people in this place.

senses.gloss: Deviating from the normal; bizarre.
senses.example: It was quite weird to bump into all my ex-girlfriends on the same day.

senses.gloss: Relating to weird fiction ("a macabre subgenre of speculative fiction").
senses.example: a weird story

examples.text: I must have felt pretty weird by that time, because I could think of nothing except the luminosity of his pink suit under the moon.
examples.translation_ko: 그때쯤 나는 꽤 이상한 기분이었던 것 같다. 달빛 아래 그의 분홍색 양복이 내는 광채 외에는 아무것도 생각할 수 없었기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Strickland was a weird figure as he lay there, thinner than ever, with his ragged red beard and his eyes staring feverishly into vacancy; his illness seemed to have made them larger, and they had an unnatural brightness.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 그곳에 누워 있는 모습이 기괴했는데, 전보다 더욱 야위어서 헝클어진 붉은 수염과 열에 들뜬 눈으로 허공을 응시하고 있었다. 병으로 인해 눈이 더 커진 것 같았고, 부자연스럽게 빛나고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English unnatural, unnaturel, equivalent to un- + natural.
definition_en: Not occurring or existing in nature.

senses.gloss: Not natural.
Not occurring in nature, the environment or atmosphere
Going against nature; perverse.
senses.example: One mother, when she heard that her daughter intended to take up medicine, retired to her room and wept, bewailing the fact that she had given birth to an "unnatural daughter."

examples.text: Strickland was a weird figure as he lay there, thinner than ever, with his ragged red beard and his eyes staring feverishly into vacancy; his illness seemed to have made them larger, and they had an unnatural brightness.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 그곳에 누워 있는 모습이 기괴했는데, 전보다 더욱 야위어서 헝클어진 붉은 수염과 열에 들뜬 눈으로 허공을 응시하고 있었다. 병으로 인해 눈이 더 커진 것 같았고, 부자연스럽게 빛나고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They were sombre blues, opaque like a delicately carved bowl in lapis lazuli, and yet with a quivering lustre that suggested the palpitation of mysterious life; there were purples, horrible like raw and putrid flesh, and yet with a glowing, sensual passion that called up vague memories of the Roman Empire of Heliogabalus; there were reds, shrill like the berries of holly—one thought of Christmas in England, and the snow, the good cheer, and the pleasure of children—and yet by some magic softened till they had the swooning tenderness of a dove’s breast; there were deep yellows that died with an unnatural passion into a green as fragrant as the spring and as pure as the sparkling water of a mountain brook.
examples.translation_ko: 청금석으로 정교하게 조각한 그릇처럼 불투명한 음울한 청색들이 있었는데, 그러면서도 신비로운 생명의 고동을 암시하는 떨리는 광택을 띠고 있었다. 날것의 썩은 살점처럼 끔찍한 자주색들이 있었는데, 그러면서도 헬리오가발루스 시대 로마 제국의 막연한 기억을 불러일으키는 타오르는 관능적 열정을 품고 있었다. 호랑가시나무 열매처럼 날카로운 적색들이 있었는데—영국의 크리스마스와 눈, 즐거운 축제, 아이들의 기쁨을 떠올리게 했다—그러면서도 어떤 마법에 의해 부드러워져서 비둘기 가슴의 황홀한 부드러움을 지니고 있었다. 부자연스러운 열정으로 죽어가면서 봄처럼 향기롭고 산골 시냇물처럼 맑고 반짝이는 초록으로 변해가는 깊은 황색들이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested in 1502. From Middle French ironie, from Old French, from Latin īrōnīa, from Ancient Greek εἰρωνεία (eirōneía, “irony, pretext”), fr...
definition_en: A situation or event that is opposite of what one would expect.

senses.gloss: The quality of a statement that, when taken in context, may actually mean something different from, or the opposite of, what is written literally; the use of words expressing something other than their literal intention, often in a humorous context.
senses.example: A principal virtue of Rorty's recognition of both the lightminded and the serious side of irony is to urge us in that direction.

senses.gloss: An ironic statement.
Dramatic irony: a theatrical effect in which the meaning of a situation, or some incongruity in the plot, is understood by the audience, but not by the characters in the play.

examples.text: It is an irony that they should so tragically have affected others.
examples.translation_ko: 그런 것들이 다른 사람들에게 그토록 비극적인 영향을 끼쳤다는 것은 아이러니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Once I saw that his eyes were fixed on Blanche Stroeve, and there was in them a curious irony.
examples.translation_ko: 한번은 그의 시선이 블랑슈 스트루브에게 고정되어 있는 것을 보았는데, 그 눈빛에는 묘한 아이러니가 담겨 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French spiritualité, from Late Latin spīrituālitās.
definition_en: The quality of being spiritual or concerned with the nature of the soul.

senses.gloss: The quality or state of being spiritual.
senses.example: Much of our spirituality and comfort in public worship depends on the state of mind in which we come.

senses.gloss: Concern for that which is unseen and intangible, as opposed to physical or mundane.
Appreciation for religious values.

examples.text: It was not exactly spirituality that was obvious, though the screen of the flesh seemed almost transparent, because there was in his face an outrageous sensuality; but, though it sounds nonsense, it seemed as though his sensuality were curiously spiritual.
examples.translation_ko: 육체라는 가림막이 거의 투명해 보일 정도였지만, 그의 얼굴에는 노골적인 관능성이 있었기 때문에 정확히 영성이 드러나 보인다고 할 수는 없었다. 하지만 말이 안 되는 소리 같지만, 그의 관능성이 묘하게 영적인 것처럼 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was not only the bold simplification of the drawing which showed so rich and so singular a personality; it was not only the painting, though the flesh was painted with a passionate sensuality which had in it something miraculous; it was not only the solidity, so that you felt extraordinarily the weight of the body; there was also a spirituality, troubling and new, which led the imagination along unsuspected ways, and suggested dim empty spaces, lit only by the eternal stars, where the soul, all naked, adventured fearful to the discovery of new mysteries.
examples.translation_ko: 그토록 풍부하고 독특한 개성을 보여주는 것은 단지 대담한 소묘의 단순화만이 아니었다. 단지 회화 기법만도 아니었다. 비록 살결이 기적적인 무언가를 담은 열정적인 관능미로 그려졌지만 말이다. 단지 육체의 무게감을 놀라울 정도로 느끼게 하는 견고함만도 아니었다. 거기에는 또한 불안하고 새로운 영성이 있어서, 상상력을 예상치 못한 길로 이끌고, 영원한 별들만이 비추는 희미하고 공허한 공간들을 암시했다. 그곳에서 벌거벗은 영혼이 새로운 신비의 발견을 향해 두려워하며 모험을 떠나는 곳을.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Back-formation from Middle English part-takinge, part-takynge (“a sharing; partaking”), a calque of Latin particeps (“participating”); equivalent t...
definition_en: Share or participate in something.

senses.gloss: To take part in an activity; to participate.
senses.example: Brutes partake in this faculty.

senses.gloss: To take a share or portion.
senses.example: Will you partake of some food?

senses.gloss: To have something of the properties, character, or office.
senses.example: The people are encouraged to perceive their liberation in historic terms and to trust that new events will partake of past glories.

examples.text: and I tried to go, but Tom and Gatsby insisted with competitive firmness that we remain—as though neither of them had anything to conceal and it would be a privilege to partake vicariously of their emotions.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 자리를 뜨려 했지만, 톰과 개츠비는 경쟁적인 단호함으로 우리가 남아 있어야 한다고 고집했다—마치 둘 다 숨길 것이 없고 그들의 감정을 간접적으로나마 함께 나누는 것이 특권이라도 되는 양.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He seemed to partake of those obscure forces of nature which the Greeks personified in shapes part human and part beast, the satyr and the faun.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그리스인들이 반인반수의 모습으로 의인화했던 자연의 모호한 힘들, 즉 사티로스나 파우누스 같은 존재들과 닮아 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old English wābegān (“beset by woe”), from wā (“woe”) + begān (“to beset, to surround”). Equivalent to woe + begone (past participle of bego).
definition_en: Unhappy or unfortunate

senses.gloss: In a deplorable state.
senses.example: The 44-year-old Prokhorov, the second-richest man in Russia, is expected to assume control of the woebegone Nets within the next few weeks.

senses.gloss: Filled with or deeply affected by woe.

examples.text: He looked woebegone and yet ridiculous, like a man who has fallen into the water with all his clothes on, and, being rescued from death, frightened still, feels that he only looks a fool.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 옷을 다 입은 채로 물에 빠졌다가 죽음에서 구조되어 여전히 겁에 질린 채, 자신이 바보처럼 보일 뿐이라는 것을 깨닫는 사람처럼 비참하면서도 우스꽝스러워 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He thought nothing of it, but when he went out to get into his trap and drive home, he saw her again, standing a little way off; she looked at him with a woebegone air, and tears streamed down her cheeks.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 별로 신경 쓰지 않았지만, 밖으로 나가 마차에 올라 집으로 돌아가려 할 때 그 소녀를 다시 보았는데, 조금 떨어진 곳에 서서 슬픈 표정으로 그를 바라보며 뺨에 눈물을 흘리고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To annoy or disturb someone repeatedly.

senses.gloss: To annoy (someone) frequently or systematically; to pester.
senses.example: Scottie, a precocious 10-year old,^([sic]) wears provocatively sloganed T-shirts and harasses her peers by text message.

senses.gloss: To persistently bother (someone, or a group of people) physically or psychologically when such behaviour is illegal and/or unwanted, especially over an extended period.
senses.example: I am gay and have AIDS and would very much like to write to someone. It is vey lonely here and they seem to think I'm going to die soon, though I wonder if they aren't just harassing me.

senses.gloss: To put excessive burdens upon (someone); to subject (someone) to anxieties.
senses.example: To harass good people is no different than speaking ill of them.

examples.text: His round blue eyes looked harassed behind his glasses.
examples.translation_ko: 안경 너머로 그의 둥근 파란 눈이 괴로워 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose no artist achieves completely the realisation of the dream that obsesses him, and Strickland, harassed incessantly by his struggle with technique, managed, perhaps, less than others to express the vision that he saw with his mind’s eye; but in Tahiti the circumstances were favourable to him; he found in his surroundings the accidents necessary for his inspiration to become effective, and his later pictures give at least a suggestion of what he sought.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 예술가도 자신을 사로잡는 꿈을 완전히 실현하지는 못하는 법이고, 기법과의 끊임없는 투쟁에 시달린 스트릭랜드는 아마도 다른 이들보다도 더 적게 자신이 마음의 눈으로 본 환상을 표현해냈을 것이다. 하지만 타히티에서는 상황이 그에게 유리했다. 그는 주변 환경에서 자신의 영감이 효과를 발휘하는 데 필요한 우연들을 발견했고, 그의 후기 작품들은 적어도 그가 추구했던 것의 암시를 보여준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From disgrace + -ful.
definition_en: Causing or showing shame.

senses.gloss: Bringing or warranting disgrace; shameful.
senses.example: From Zoilus to Dennis, no disgracefuller outrage on taste had been committed.

senses.gloss: Giving offense to moral sensibilities and injurious to reputation.
senses.example: To a good golfer a shank is disgracefuller than being dead drunk or in jail.

examples.text: “Why are you idling in this disgraceful fashion?”
examples.translation_ko: "왜 이렇게 한심하게 빈둥거리고 있는 거야?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I saw that Mrs. Strickland had forgotten that she had ever done anything so disgraceful as to work for her living.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인은 자신이 생계를 위해 일했다는 그토록 수치스러운 일을 한 적이 있다는 사실을 잊어버린 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fonne, fon (“foolish, simple, silly”) or fonnen (“make a fool of”), from Middle English fonne (“a fool, dupe”), probably of Nor...
definition_en: Enjoyable or amusing.

senses.gloss: Amusement, enjoyment or pleasure.
senses.example: Grafting your boss's face onto the hind end of a donkey is fun, but serious fun is when you create the impossible and it looks real.

senses.gloss: Playful, often noisy, activity.

examples.text: “It was great fun to do.”
examples.translation_ko: "그걸 그리는 게 정말 재미있었어."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I thought it would be fun.
examples.translation_ko: 재미있을 것 같았어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French destachier, from the same root as attach; compare French détacher and Portuguese and Spanish destacar.
definition_en: Separate from a group or connection.

senses.gloss: To take apart from; to take off.
senses.example: to detach the tag from a newly purchased garment

senses.gloss: To separate for a special object or use.
senses.example: to detach a ship from a fleet, or a company from a regiment

senses.gloss: To come off something.
senses.example: Now that the zipper has detached, my winter coat won't keep me very warm.

examples.text: He said all this slowly, detaching statement from statement with a little awkward silence, and he kept his kind, foolish eyes fixed on mine.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 이 모든 말을 천천히 했고, 어색한 침묵으로 문장과 문장 사이를 끊어가며 말했으며, 친절하고 어리석은 눈을 내 눈에 고정시키고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It may be that in order to realise the romance of life you must have something of the actor in you; and, capable of standing outside yourself, you must be able to watch your actions with an interest at once detached and absorbed.
examples.translation_ko: 인생의 낭만을 깨닫기 위해서는 배우의 기질이 어느 정도 있어야 하는 것일지도 모른다. 자신을 객관화할 수 있어야 하고, 초연하면서도 몰입된 관심으로 자신의 행동을 지켜볼 수 있어야 하는 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Deverbal from look out.
definition_en: A place or position from which to observe something.

senses.gloss: A vantage point with a view of the surrounding area.
A session of watching for an approaching enemy, police, etc.
senses.example: We kept a lookout all night, but nobody came.

senses.gloss: A person on watch for approaching enemy, police, danger, etc.
senses.example: The raid failed when the lookout noticed the enemy group.

examples.text: That’s his lookout.”
examples.translation_ko: 그건 그 사람이 알아서 할 일이에요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: If she had to put up with certain inconveniences it was her own lookout.”
examples.translation_ko: 불편을 감수해야 한다면 그건 그녀 자신이 알아서 할 일이었다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Compound of school + boy.
definition_en: A young boy who attends school.

senses.gloss: A boy attending school.

examples.text: He stood like a schoolboy with whom a master is finding fault.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 선생님께 꾸중을 듣는 학생처럼 서 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He looked like an overblown schoolboy, and though I felt so sorry for him, I could hardly help laughing.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 덩치만 큰 남학생 같아 보였고, 나는 그가 너무 불쌍했지만 웃음을 참기가 힘들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A person who is seated.

senses.gloss: A period during which one is seated for a specific purpose.
senses.example: Due to the sheer volume of guests, we had to have two sittings for the meal.

senses.gloss: A seance or other session with a medium or fortuneteller.
senses.example: "It's not always easy to get him, and of course a small fee, a guinea I think, is usual, but if you wanted a sitting I could work it." "You think him genuine?" Atkinson shrugged his shoulders.

senses.gloss: A special seat allotted to a seat-holder, at church, etc.

examples.text: I led the way into my sitting room and asked him to sit down.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 거실로 안내하며 그에게 앉으라고 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I had a divan in my sitting-room, and could very well sleep on that.
examples.translation_ko: 거실에 소파가 하나 있었으니 거기서 자는 것쯤은 충분히 괜찮았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To flow or move slowly and steadily.

senses.gloss: A very thin river.
senses.example: The brook had shrunk to a mere trickle.

senses.gloss: A very thin flow; the sound of such a flow.
senses.example: The tap of the washbasin in my bedroom is leaking and the trickle drives me mad at night.

examples.text: He gave a little gasp, and the tears began to trickle down his round cheeks.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 작게 헐떡이더니 눈물이 동그란 뺨을 타고 흘러내리기 시작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.translation_ko: 순간 스트릭랜드의 의연함이 흔들렸고, 그의 두 눈에 눈물이 고여 뺨을 따라 천천히 흘러내렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From calm + -ness.
definition_en: A state of being peaceful and untroubled.

senses.gloss: The state of being calm; tranquillity; silence.
The product of being calm.

examples.text: However, as calmness wasn’t an end in itself, I made an excuse at the first possible moment, and got to my feet.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 평온함 자체가 목적은 아니었으므로, 나는 가능한 첫 순간에 핑계를 대고 자리에서 일어났다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I knew her capable of temper, for all the calmness of her manner; and if Stroeve still refused, she might easily have flung out of the studio with vows never to return.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 침착한 태도에도 불구하고 나는 그녀가 화를 낼 수 있는 성격임을 알고 있었다. 만약 스트루브가 계속 거절한다면, 그녀는 다시는 돌아오지 않겠다고 맹세하며 화실에서 뛰쳐나갔을지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Express discontent or pain with a low sound.

senses.gloss: A low, mournful cry of pain, sorrow or pleasure.

senses.gloss: A lament or sorrow.
senses.example: to make one's moan

examples.text: “You don’t understand,” he moaned.
examples.translation_ko: "당신은 이해하지 못해." 그가 신음했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: “Oh, I don’t know,” he moaned, seizing his head with his hands.
examples.translation_ko: "아, 모르겠어요." 그는 두 손으로 머리를 감싸며 신음했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Make a careless mistake.

senses.gloss: A clumsy or embarrassing mistake.
A very bad move, usually caused by some tactical oversight.
Confusion; bewilderment; trouble; disturbance; clamour.

examples.text: He had a sweet and generous nature, and yet was always blundering; a real feeling for what was beautiful and the capacity to create only what was commonplace; a peculiar delicacy of sentiment and gross manners.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 다정하고 관대한 성품을 지녔으면서도 늘 실수를 저질렀고, 아름다운 것에 대한 진정한 감각을 가졌으면서도 평범한 것만 창조할 수 있는 능력밖에 없었으며, 독특하게 섬세한 감성과 조야한 매너를 함께 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I supposed that for some reason or other—and Heaven knows what ingenuity men exercise to torment themselves—Dirk had got it into his head that his wife cared for Strickland, and with his genius for blundering he might quite well have offended her so that, to anger him, perhaps, she had taken pains to foster his suspicion.
examples.translation_ko: 무슨 이유에서인지—하늘만이 아시겠지만 사람들이 자신을 괴롭히기 위해 얼마나 기발한 수를 쓰는지—더크는 아내가 스트릭랜드를 좋아한다는 생각을 머릿속에 집어넣었고, 실수를 저지르는 그의 천재적 재능으로 아내의 기분을 상하게 했을 수도 있었으며, 그래서 아내가 그를 화나게 하려고 일부러 그의 의심을 부추겼을지도 모른다고 나는 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English humble, from Old French humble, umble, humle, from Latin humilis (“low, slight, hence mean, humble”) (compare Greek χαμηλός (kh...
definition_en: Showing modest or lowly behavior.

senses.gloss: Not pretentious or magnificent; unpretending; unassuming.

senses.gloss: Having a low opinion of oneself; not proud, arrogant, or assuming; modest.
senses.example:
She ſhould be humble, who would pleaſe;
 And ſhe muſt ſuffer, who can love.

examples.translation_ko: 바보짓을 했다면 굽실거리며 사과해야지.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A package or bundle of goods.

senses.gloss: A package wrapped for shipment.
senses.example: I saw a brown paper parcel on my doorstep.

senses.gloss: An individual consignment of cargo for shipment, regardless of size and form.
An individual item appearing on an invoice or receipt (only in the phrase bill of parcels).

examples.text: He made the parcel and he whistled a tune.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 소포를 만들며 콧노래를 불렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You remember I fetched from his room what I thought he needed, and he asked Blanche for a piece of paper and some string to make a parcel.”
examples.translation_ko: 자네도 기억하겠지만 내가 그의 방에서 필요할 것 같은 물건들을 가져왔었는데, 그가 블랑슈에게 종이 한 장과 끈을 달라고 해서 보따리를 만들려고 했다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Extremely surprised or shocked.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of astound

examples.text: He was astounded.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 경악했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I believed him now, and I was astounded.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 그의 말을 믿었고, 경악했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From passionate + -ly.
definition_en: Feeling or showing strong enthusiasm and excitement.

senses.gloss: In a passionate manner.

examples.text: He told her how passionately he loved her, and reminded her of all the devotion he had lavished upon her.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자신이 얼마나 열정적으로 그녀를 사랑하는지 말했고, 그녀에게 쏟아부었던 모든 헌신을 상기시켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The only thing that seemed clear to me—and perhaps even this was fanciful—was that he was passionately striving for liberation from some power that held him.
examples.translation_ko: 내게 분명해 보이는 유일한 것은—그리고 아마 이것조차 공상일지도 모르지만—그가 자신을 붙잡고 있는 어떤 힘으로부터의 해방을 열정적으로 추구하고 있다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Causing or capable of causing harm.

senses.gloss: Causing physical harm or injury; harmful, hurtful.
Causing harm to one's reputation; invidious, defamatory, libelous, slanderous.

examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드의 모독적인 침착함이 스트루브의 남은 자제력마저 앗아갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I knew from what I had heard that she was a woman of violent passions; and that injurious blow that she had given Dirk, the man who had loved her so devotedly, betrayed a sudden temper and a horrid cruelty.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 들은 바로는 그녀가 격렬한 감정의 소유자라는 것을 알고 있었다. 그리고 그토록 헌신적으로 자신을 사랑했던 남자 더크에게 가한 그 해로운 타격은 갑작스러운 성질과 끔찍한 잔혹함을 드러내는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A feeling of admiration for someone or something.

senses.gloss: an attitude of consideration or high regard
senses.example: He is an intellectual giant, and I have great respect for him.

senses.gloss: good opinion, honor, or admiration
Polite greetings, often offered as condolences after a death.
senses.example: The mourners paid their last respects to the deceased poet.

examples.text: He went up to her quickly and fell on his knees before her, seizing her hands: he abandoned all self-respect.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 재빨리 그녀에게 다가가 그녀 앞에 무릎을 꿇고 그녀의 손을 붙잡았다. 그는 모든 자존심을 포기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It cannot be said that they are without guile, but they have a tolerant respect for the law, when the law is supported by strength.
examples.translation_ko: 그들에게 간계가 없다고는 할 수 없지만, 법이 힘으로 뒷받침될 때는 법에 대해 관대한 존경심을 보인다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Variant form of by, from Old English bī (“being near”).
definition_en: A farewell or a dismissal.

senses.gloss: The position of a person or team in a tournament or competition who draws no opponent in a particular round so advances to the next round unopposed, or is awarded points for a win in a league table; also the phantom opponent of such a person or team.
senses.example: Craig's Crew plays the bye next week.

senses.gloss: An extra scored when the batsmen take runs after the ball has passed the striker without hitting either the bat or the batsman.
A thing not directly aimed at; a secondary or subsidiary object, course, path, undertaking, issue, etc.
senses.example: The Synod of Dort in some points condemneth, upon the by, even the discipline of the Church of England.

etymology: From logic + -al.
definition_en: Based on reason and sound argument.

senses.gloss: In agreement with the principles of logic; sequacious.
senses.example: To provide convincing arguments, we need to first address the issues of concern, list the facts, and then use logical reasoning to help people have a better understanding of the issue.

senses.gloss: Reasonable.
senses.example:
I won't lie about what I did
I cut her head off and threw it in a ditch
Why I only kept the body was a logical choice
I threw away the head because I hated the sound of her voice

senses.gloss: Of or pertaining to logic.
senses.example: It's not logical, it's God!

examples.text: “I dare say that’s logical,” I smiled, “but most men are made differently, and they can’t.”
examples.translation_ko: "논리적으로는 그럴 수도 있겠지만," 나는 미소를 지었다. "대부분의 남자들은 다르게 만들어져서 그럴 수가 없다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The character of a scoundrel, logical and complete, has a fascination for his creator which is an outrage to law and order.
examples.translation_ko: 논리적이고 완전한 악한의 성격은 창조자에게 법과 질서에 대한 모독이라 할 만한 매혹을 안겨준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From sudden + -ness.
definition_en: The quality of being sudden.

senses.gloss: The state of being sudden.
senses.example: The suddenness with which the solemn quiet had been broken in upon, had chaced from his remembrance the horrid phantom;—it now recurred to it, with two-fold force, and a shudder crept all over him.

examples.text: At this point Miss Baker said: “Absolutely!” with such suddenness that I started—it was the first word she had uttered since I came into the room.
examples.translation_ko: 이때 베이커 양이 "그럼요!"라고 갑자기 외쳤다. 너무 갑작스러워서 나는 깜짝 놀랐다. 내가 이 방에 들어온 후 그녀가 한 첫 마디였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was puzzling over the suddenness of the whole affair.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이 모든 일이 갑작스럽게 벌어진 것에 대해 곰곰 생각하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + consciously, and more rarely, from unconscious + -ly.
definition_en: Not aware of one's actions or feelings.

senses.gloss: In an unconscious manner; unknowingly

examples.text: There was a pencil on the table, and unconsciously he drew a head on the blotting-paper.
examples.translation_ko: 탁자 위에 연필이 하나 있었는데, 그는 무의식중에 흡지 위에 머리 하나를 그렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Unconsciously, perhaps, we treasure the power we have over people by their regard for our opinion of them, and we hate those upon whom we have no such influence.
examples.translation_ko: 무의식적으로, 아마도 우리는 다른 사람들이 우리에 대한 평가를 신경 쓴다는 점에서 그들에 대해 갖는 힘을 소중히 여기며, 그런 영향력이 전혀 통하지 않는 사람들을 미워한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English blot (“blot, spot, stain, blemish”). Perhaps from Old Norse *blettr (“blot, stain”) (only attested in documents from after Old ...
definition_en: To mark or stain something with a dark spot.

senses.gloss: A blemish, spot or stain made by a coloured substance.
senses.example:
[…] He was blind; he could not see the stars
Glinting among the wraiths of wandering cloud;
Queer blots of colour, purple, scarlet, green,
Flickered and faded in his drowning eyes.

senses.gloss: A stain on someone's reputation or character; a disgrace.
senses.example: The only blot on this service is that of its Kentish Town connections, which throughout the day in many cases just miss the St. Pancras-Luton stopping trains.

senses.gloss: A method of transferring proteins, DNA or RNA, onto a carrier.

examples.text: Perhaps some unbelievable guest would arrive, a person infinitely rare and to be marvelled at, some authentically radiant young girl who with one fresh glance at Gatsby, one moment of magical encounter, would blot out those five years of unwavering devotion.
examples.translation_ko: 어쩌면 믿을 수 없는 손님이 도착할지도 모른다. 무한히 드물고 경탄할 만한 사람, 개츠비를 향한 신선한 한 번의 시선으로, 마법 같은 만남의 한 순간으로 흔들림 없는 다섯 해의 헌신을 지워버릴 진정으로 빛나는 젊은 여인이.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There was a pencil on the table, and unconsciously he drew a head on the blotting-paper.
examples.translation_ko: 탁자 위에 연필이 하나 있었는데, 그는 무의식중에 흡지 위에 머리 하나를 그렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English frightful (“afraid”), from Old English forhtfull (“fainthearted, timorous”). Equivalent to fright + -ful.
definition_en: Extremely frightening or unpleasant.

senses.gloss: Afraid, frightened.
senses.example: Ðis frigtful ðus a-biden,

senses.gloss: Timid, fearful, easily frightened.
senses.example: See how the frightful herds run from the wood.

senses.gloss: Genuinely horrific, awful, or alarming.

examples.text: Oh, if you knew the frightful anguish in my heart.”
examples.translation_ko: 아, 제 마음속의 끔찍한 고통을 당신이 안다면요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: What had happened could only be a dream, a frightful dream; and when he turned the key and opened the door, he would see her bending slightly over the table in the gracious attitude of the woman in Chardin’s Benedicite, which always seemed to him so exquisite.
examples.translation_ko: 일어난 일은 꿈, 끔찍한 꿈일 뿐이었다. 열쇠를 돌려 문을 열면 샤르댕의 「식사 기도」 속 여인의 우아한 자세로 테이블 위에 살짝 몸을 굽히고 있는 그녀를 보게 될 것이었다. 그 자세는 언제나 그에게 너무도 아름다워 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bitternesse, biternesse, from Old English biternes (“bitterness; grief”), equivalent to bitter + -ness.
definition_en: A strong unpleasant feeling of discontent or resentment.

senses.gloss: The quality of having a bitter taste.
The quality of feeling bitter; acrimony, resentment; the quality of exhibiting such feelings.
senses.example: the bitterness of his words

senses.gloss: The quality of eliciting a bitter, humiliating or harsh feeling.
senses.example: Nothing could assuage the bitterness of their defeat.

examples.text: I looked at her mouth for an expression that could give me a clue to what she felt; I watched her eyes for some tell-tale flash, some hint of dismay or bitterness; I scanned her brow for any passing line that might indicate a settling emotion.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그녀가 무엇을 느끼는지 단서를 얻을 수 있는 표정을 찾아 그녀의 입을 살펴보았고, 무언가를 드러내는 번뜩임이나 당황이나 괴로움의 기색을 찾아 그녀의 눈을 지켜보았으며, 마음속 감정이 굳어지는 것을 나타낼 수도 있는 순간적인 주름살을 찾아 그녀의 이마를 살폈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He chose his moment carefully, and tried to make his request sound casual; but he could not master the trembling of his voice; and he felt himself that into words that he wished to seem jovial and friendly there crept the bitterness of his jealousy.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 신중하게 때를 골라 자신의 부탁이 무심한 듯 들리도록 애썼지만, 떨리는 목소리를 억누를 수 없었다. 그리고 유쾌하고 친근하게 들리기를 바랐던 말에 질투의 쓰라림이 스며드는 것을 스스로 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From Middle English preparacion, from Middle French preparacion, from Latin praeparatio, praeparationem.
Morphologically prepare + -ation
definition_en: The act of making something ready for use or a situation.

senses.gloss: The act of preparing or getting ready.
senses.example: I went over my notes in preparation for the exam.

senses.gloss: The state of being prepared; readiness.
A substance, especially a remedy, that is prepared.
senses.example: The traditional remedy is a bitter preparation made from steamed herbs.

examples.text: He had not expected Strickland to take him up on the spot and make his preparations to go there and then; above all, he had not expected his wife’s decision to go with him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 스트릭랜드가 즉석에서 받아들여 당장 떠날 준비를 하리라고는 예상하지 못했고, 무엇보다 아내가 함께 가겠다고 결심하리라고는 전혀 예상하지 못했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The demon which possessed him was exorcised at last, and with the completion of the work, for which all his life had been a painful preparation, rest descended on his remote and tortured soul.
examples.translation_ko: 그를 사로잡았던 악마가 마침내 쫓겨났고, 평생을 고통스러운 준비 과정으로 보낸 그 작업이 완성되면서 그의 외롭고 고통받던 영혼에 안식이 내려왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English respounse, respons, from Old French respons, respuns, responce, ultimately from the Latin respōnsum, a nominal use of the neute...
definition_en: A reaction or answer to a question or situation.

senses.gloss: An answer or reply, or something in the nature of an answer or reply.
The act of responding or replying; reply: as, to speak in response to a question.
An oracular answer.

examples.text: He hadn’t once ceased looking at Daisy, and I think he revalued everything in his house according to the measure of response it drew from her well-loved eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 한순간도 데이지에게서 시선을 떼지 않았고, 그녀의 사랑스러운 눈동자에서 나타나는 반응의 정도에 따라 집 안의 모든 것을 다시 평가하고 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I do not suppose she had ever really cared for her husband, and what I had taken for love was no more than the feminine response to caresses and comfort which in the minds of most women passes for it.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 남편을 진정으로 사랑한 적은 없었을 것이고, 내가 사랑이라고 여겼던 것은 애무와 안락함에 대한 여성적 반응에 지나지 않았을 것이다. 대부분의 여성들 마음속에서는 그것이 사랑으로 통한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English rousen, from Anglo-Norman reuser, ruser, originally used in English of hawks shaking the feathers of the body, from Latin recūs...
definition_en: To wake or stir someone from sleep.

senses.gloss: An arousal.
The sounding of a bugle in the morning after reveille, to signal that soldiers are to rise from bed, often the rouse.

examples.text: “But I guess Strickland was an ugly customer when he was roused,” said Captain Nichols, reflectively.
examples.translation_ko: "하지만 스트릭랜드가 화가 나면 만만치 않은 상대였을 거야." 니콜스 선장이 곰곰히 생각하며 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is a passive feeling capable of being roused for any object, as the vine can grow on any tree; and the wisdom of the world recognises its strength when it urges a girl to marry the man who wants her with the assurance that love will follow.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 포도덩굴이 어떤 나무에든 자랄 수 있듯이 어떤 대상에든 불러일으킬 수 있는 수동적인 감정이다. 그리고 세상의 지혜는 그 힘을 인정하기에 소녀에게 자신을 원하는 남자와 결혼하라고 권하며 사랑은 뒤따라올 것이라고 확신시킨다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English attraccioun, from Old French attraction, from Latin attractio from past participle of attrahō (= ad + trahō), equivalent to att...
definition_en: A strong feeling of liking or wanting something.

senses.gloss: The tendency to attract.
senses.example: The Moon is held in its orbit by the attraction of the Earth's gravity.

senses.gloss: The feeling of being attracted (to something).
senses.example: I felt a strange attraction towards the place.

senses.gloss: Sexual or romantic desire (especially for a specified individual, kind of person, etc).

examples.text: I suspected that Blanche Stroeve’s violent dislike of Strickland had in it from the beginning a vague element of sexual attraction.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 블랑슈 스트루브가 스트릭랜드를 격렬하게 싫어하는 마음 속에 처음부터 막연한 성적 끌림의 요소가 있었다고 의심했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: All that was healthy and natural, all that clung to happy relationships and the simple joys of simple men, shrunk from them in dismay; and yet a fearful attraction was in them, and, like the fruit on the Tree of the Knowledge of Good and Evil they were terrible with the possibilities of the Unknown.
examples.translation_ko: 건강하고 자연스러운 모든 것, 행복한 인간관계와 소박한 사람들의 단순한 기쁨에 매달리는 모든 것이 경악하며 그것들로부터 움츠러들었다. 그러나 그 안에는 무서운 매력이 있었고, 선악과처럼 미지의 가능성으로 인해 끔찍했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From intimate + -cy.
definition_en: A close and affectionate relationship between people.

senses.gloss: Feeling or atmosphere of closeness and openness towards someone else, often but not necessarily involving sexuality.
senses.example: […] there was keen intimacy between the dog and the man.

senses.gloss: Intimate relationship.
senses.example: “I have always thought it a very foolish intimacy,” said Mr. Knightley presently, “though I have kept my thoughts to myself; but I now perceive that it will be a very unfortunate one for Harriet […]”

senses.gloss: Intimate detail, (item of) intimate information.
senses.example: He recognized the tone as the one used by friendly sisters to discuss the infirmities of their husbands. It was Shama’s plea to a sister to exchange intimacies, to show support.

examples.text: There was an unmistakable air of natural intimacy about the picture, and anybody would have said that they were conspiring together.
examples.translation_ko: 그 광경에는 자연스러운 친밀감이 분명히 배어 있었고, 누가 봐도 둘이 함께 무언가를 꾸미고 있다고 말했을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And then I fancy that the daily intimacy with the sick man moved her strangely.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 나는 병든 남자와의 일상적인 친밀감이 그녀를 이상하게 감동시켰다고 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lyme, lim, from Old English lim (“limb, branch”), from Proto-West Germanic *limu, from Proto-Germanic *limuz (“branch, limb”). ...
definition_en: A part of the body that is attached to the main part.

senses.gloss: A major appendage of human or animal, used for locomotion (such as an arm, leg or wing).
senses.example:
UUhoſe hands are made to gripe a warlike Lance—
Their ſhoulders broad, for complet armour fit,
Their lims more large and of a bigger ſize
Than all the brats yſprong from Typhons loins:

senses.gloss: A branch of a tree.
The part of the bow, from the handle to the tip.

examples.text: He lay on his back limply, as though all the strength had gone out of his limbs, and presently I saw that he had fallen asleep.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 마치 팔다리에서 모든 힘이 빠진 것처럼 축 늘어져 등을 대고 누워 있었고, 곧 그가 잠들어버린 것을 나는 알 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She washed his limbs; they were covered with thick hair; and when she dried his hands, even in his weakness they were strong and sinewy.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그의 팔다리를 씻어주었다. 그것들은 짙은 털로 덮여 있었다. 그리고 그의 손을 말려줄 때, 쇠약해진 상태에서도 그 손들은 강하고 힘줄이 발달해 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English nimphe, from Old English nymphē and Old French nimphe, both from Latin nympha (“nymph, bride”), from Ancient Greek νύμφη (númph...
definition_en: A mythological female nature spirit.

senses.gloss: Any female nature spirit associated with water, forests, grotto, wind, etc.
A young girl, especially one who is attractive, beautiful or graceful.
The larva of certain insects.

examples.text: “This is a nice restaurant here,” said Mr. Wolfshiem, looking at the presbyterian nymphs on the ceiling.
examples.translation_ko: "여기 참 좋은 식당이군요." 울프샤임 씨가 천장의 장로교도 요정들을 바라보며 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Did he dream of the nymph flying through the woods of Greece with the satyr in hot pursuit?
examples.translation_ko: 그는 사티로스의 뜨거운 추격을 받으며 그리스 숲속을 달아나는 님프를 꿈꾸고 있는 것일까?
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From fancy + -ful.
definition_en: Having or showing a tendency to imagine things that are not real.

senses.gloss: Imaginative or fantastic; ignoring reality.
senses.example: It was fanciful to suppose that all he had to do would be to stride into a top law firm and he would be hired on the spot.

senses.gloss: Unreal or imagined.

examples.text: But perhaps this is very fanciful; and it may be that she was merely bored with her husband and went to Strickland out of a callous curiosity.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 이런 생각은 지나치게 공상적일지도 모른다. 그녀는 단지 남편에게 지루함을 느껴서 냉혹한 호기심으로 스트릭랜드에게 간 것일 수도 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The only thing that seemed clear to me—and perhaps even this was fanciful—was that he was passionately striving for liberation from some power that held him.
examples.translation_ko: 내게 분명해 보이는 유일한 것은—그리고 아마 이것조차 공상일지도 모르지만—그가 자신을 붙잡고 있는 어떤 힘으로부터의 해방을 열정적으로 추구하고 있다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin callōsus (“hard-skinned”), from callum (“hardened skin”) + -ōsus.
definition_en: Having or showing a lack of feeling or concern for others.

senses.gloss: Emotionally hardened; unfeeling and indifferent to the suffering/feelings of others.
senses.example: She was so callous that she could criticise a cancer patient for wearing a wig.

senses.gloss: Having calluses, or relating to calluses.

examples.text: It was impossible to make him understand that one might be outraged by his callous selfishness.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 냉혹한 이기심에 분개할 수도 있다는 것을 그에게 이해시키는 것은 불가능했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But perhaps this is very fanciful; and it may be that she was merely bored with her husband and went to Strickland out of a callous curiosity.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 이런 생각은 지나치게 공상적일지도 모른다. 그녀는 단지 남편에게 지루함을 느껴서 냉혹한 호기심으로 스트릭랜드에게 간 것일 수도 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English snare, from Old English snearu (“snare, noose”), from Proto-West Germanic *snarhā, from Proto-Germanic *snarhǭ (“a sling; loop;...
definition_en: A device for catching or holding something, especially an animal.

senses.gloss: A trap (especially one made from a loop of wire, string, or leather).
senses.example: He felt a snare tightening around his throat; he gasped and threw a leg out of the bed, where it jerked for a second or two, thumping the steel frame, and died.

senses.gloss: A mental or psychological trap.
senses.example: They were devious war aims, and Allenby’s campaign was fought with a maximum of snare and subterfuge.

senses.gloss: A loop of cord used in obstetric cases, to hold or to pull a fetus from the mother animal.

examples.text: With infinite patience she prepared to snare me and bind me.
examples.translation_ko: 무한한 인내심으로 그녀는 나를 덫에 걸어 묶어두려 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham
