examples.text: She may have had no particular feeling for him, but succumbed to his wish from propinquity or idleness, to find then that she was powerless in a snare of her own contriving.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그에 대해 특별한 감정이 없었을지도 모르지만, 가까이 있다는 이유로 혹은 무료함 때문에 그의 바람에 굴복했다가, 자신이 스스로 만든 올가미에서 벗어날 수 없음을 깨달았을 수도 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fers, fiers, borrowed from Old French fers (“wild", "ferocious”), nominative of fer, from Latin ferus (“wild", "untamed”).
definition_en: Showing a strong and uncontrolled emotion.

senses.gloss: Exceedingly violent, severe, ferocious, cruel or savage.
senses.example: A fierce storm battered the coast.

senses.gloss: Resolute or strenuously active.
senses.example: We made a fierce attempt to escape.

senses.gloss: Threatening in appearance or demeanor.
senses.example: The lion gave a fierce roar.

examples.text: His brown, hardening body lived naturally through the half-fierce, half-lazy work of the bracing days.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 갈색으로 단단해진 몸은 상쾌한 나날의 반은 격렬하고 반은 나른한 일을 통해 자연스럽게 살아갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The emotions common to most of us simply did not exist in him, and it was as absurd to blame him for not feeling them as for blaming the tiger because he is fierce and cruel.
examples.translation_ko: 우리 대부분에게 공통된 감정들이 그에게는 아예 존재하지 않았으며, 그런 감정을 느끼지 못한다고 그를 탓하는 것은 호랑이가 사납고 잔혹하다고 탓하는 것만큼이나 어리석은 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French trait (“line, feature”), from Latin tractus (“drawing, pulling”), from Latin trahō. Doublet of tract.
definition_en: A distinctive quality or characteristic of someone's personality.

senses.gloss: An identifying characteristic, habit or trend.
senses.example: inherited traits and acquired traits

senses.gloss: An uninstantiable collection of methods that provides functionality to a class by using the class’s own interface.
senses.example: Traits are somewhat between an interface and a mixin.

examples.text: These were not traits which I could imagine in Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 특성들은 내가 스트릭랜드에게서 상상할 수 있는 것들이 아니었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His wife’s tidiness was one of the traits which had so much pleased him; his own upbringing had given him a tender sympathy for the delight in orderliness; and when he had seen her instinctive desire to put each thing in its appointed place it had given him a little warm feeling in his heart.
examples.translation_ko: 아내의 정돈된 생활은 그를 그토록 기쁘게 했던 특징 중 하나였다. 그 자신의 성장 배경이 질서를 좋아하는 마음에 대한 따뜻한 공감을 심어주었고, 모든 것을 제자리에 두려는 그녀의 본능적인 욕구를 보았을 때 그의 마음에 작은 따뜻함을 안겨주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English yok, yoke, ȝok from Old English ġeoc (“yoke”), from Proto-Germanic *juką (“yoke”), from Proto-Indo-European *yugóm (“yoke”), fr...
definition_en: A frame or bar used to join two animals together.

senses.gloss: A bar or frame by which two oxen or other draught animals are joined at their necks enabling them to pull a cart, plough, etc.; (by extension) a device attached to a single draught animal for the same purpose.
senses.example: A yearling bullock to thy name ſhall ſmoke, / Untam'd, unconſcious of the galling yoke, / With ample forehead, and yet tender horns / Whoſe budding honours ductile gold adorns.

senses.gloss: A pole carried on the neck and shoulders of a person, used for carrying a pair of buckets, etc., one at each end of the pole; a carrying pole.
senses.example: The speaker, who had been carrying a pair of pails on a yoke, deposited them upon the edge of the pavement in front of the inn, and straightened his back to an excruciating perpendicular.

senses.gloss: Any of various devices with crosspieces used to control an aircraft; specifically, the control column.

examples.text: I could not believe that he would ever suffer that possession of himself which love is; he could never endure a foreign yoke.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 사랑이라는 자기 자신에 대한 지배를 당할 리는 없다고 나는 생각했다. 그는 결코 타인의 멍에를 견딜 수 없는 사람이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I think I should have emphasised his patience with the unsuitable mate, and the compassion which made him unwilling to throw off the yoke that oppressed him.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 부적절한 배우자에 대한 그의 인내심과, 자신을 억압하는 멍에를 벗어던지기를 꺼리게 만든 연민을 강조했을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English logge, from Old French loge (“arbour, covered walk-way”), from Frankish *laubijā (“shelter; arbour”), from Proto-West Germanic ...
definition_en: A small building for a particular purpose or group.

senses.gloss: A building for recreational use such as a hunting lodge or a summer cabin.
Ellipsis of porter's lodge: a building or room near the entrance of an estate or building, especially (UK, Canada) as a college mailroom.
senses.example: [H]e walked across Hawthorn Tree Court on his way to the porter's lodge. […] At the lodge he cleared his pigeon-hole.

senses.gloss: A local chapter of some fraternities, such as freemasons.

examples.text: But he found his traps waiting for him in the porter’s lodge, and the concierge told him that Blanche had gone out.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그는 관리사무소에서 자신의 짐들이 기다리고 있는 것을 발견했고, 관리인은 블랑슈가 외출했다고 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: There was one man there who had fallen on adversity, and to him she had given board and lodging for several months.
examples.translation_ko: 그곳에는 불운에 빠진 남자가 한 명 있었는데, 그녀는 그에게 몇 달 동안 숙식을 제공해 주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From way + lay, likely a calque of Middle Dutch wegelagen (“besetting of ways, lying in wait with evil or hostile intent along public ways”). Compa...
definition_en: Attack or ambush someone unexpectedly.

senses.gloss: To lie in wait for and attack from ambush.
To accost or intercept unexpectedly.

examples.text: Ata had waylaid the cart that took the mail into Papeete, and besought the man who drove it to go at once to the doctor.
examples.translation_ko: 아타가 파페에테로 우편을 가져가는 마차를 가로막고, 마차를 모는 사람에게 즉시 의사에게 가달라고 간청했던 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Knowing at what time his wife did her shopping, one day, unable any longer to bear not seeing her, he waylaid her in the street.
examples.translation_ko: 아내가 언제 장을 보러 나가는지 알고 있던 그는, 어느 날 더 이상 그녀를 보지 못하는 것을 견딜 수 없어서 길에서 그녀를 기다렸다가 가로막았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From devoted + -ly.
definition_en: Done with great devotion.

senses.gloss: In a devoted manner.

examples.text: He spluttered out words of apology for any wrong he had committed towards her; he told her he loved her devotedly and begged her to return to him.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자신이 그녀에게 저지른 잘못에 대해 더듬거리며 사과했고, 그녀를 헌신적으로 사랑한다고 말하며 자신에게 돌아와 달라고 애원했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I knew from what I had heard that she was a woman of violent passions; and that injurious blow that she had given Dirk, the man who had loved her so devotedly, betrayed a sudden temper and a horrid cruelty.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 들은 바로는 그녀가 격렬한 감정의 소유자라는 것을 알고 있었다. 그리고 그토록 헌신적으로 자신을 사랑했던 남자 더크에게 가한 그 해로운 타격은 갑작스러운 성질과 끔찍한 잔혹함을 드러내는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Blend of Middle English hasten (verb), (compare Dutch haasten, German hasten, Danish haste, Swedish hasta (“to hasten, rush”)) and Middle English h...
definition_en: A state of being in a hurry.

senses.gloss: Speed; swiftness; dispatch.
senses.example: We were running late so we finished our meal in haste.

senses.gloss: Urgency; sudden excitement of feeling or passion; precipitance; vehemence.
senses.example: I said in my haste, All men are liars.

examples.text: She came in with such a proprietary haste, and looked around so possessively at the furniture that I wondered if she lived here.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 마치 주인이라도 되는 듯 성급하게 들어와서는 가구들을 소유자라도 되는 듯 둘러보았기에, 나는 그녀가 여기 사는 것은 아닌지 궁금했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Panting a little in his haste, he told her how miserable he was; he besought her to have mercy on him; he promised, if she would forgive him, to do everything she wanted.
examples.translation_ko: 서두르느라 약간 숨을 헐떡이며, 그는 자신이 얼마나 비참한지 말했다. 그녀에게 자비를 베풀어 달라고 간청했다. 그녀가 용서해 준다면 그녀가 원하는 것은 무엇이든 하겠다고 약속했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From enjoy + -ment.
definition_en: The pleasure or satisfaction derived from an activity.

senses.gloss: The condition of enjoying anything.
senses.example: Few activities better the enjoyment of a hearty meal eaten in good company.

senses.gloss: An enjoyable state of mind.
An activity that gives pleasure.

examples.text: Perhaps she got enjoyment out of the torture she inflicted.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 그녀는 자신이 가하는 고문에서 즐거움을 얻었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But the impression is fleeting, and serves only to give a greater acuteness to the enjoyment of the moment.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그런 인상은 순간적이며, 다만 현재 순간의 즐거움을 더욱 예리하게 만들어줄 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French canal, from Old French canal, from Latin canālis (“channel; canal”), from canālis (“canal”), from canna (“reed, cane”),...
definition_en: A man-made waterway connecting two larger bodies of water.

senses.gloss: An artificial waterway or artificially improved river used for travel, shipping, or irrigation.
A tubular channel within the body or within a plant.
One of the faint, hazy markings resembling straight lines on early telescopic images of the surface of Mars; see Martian canals

examples.text: His father was a carpenter, and they dwelt in a little old red-brick house, neat and clean, by the side of a sluggish canal.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 아버지는 목수였고, 그들은 완만한 운하 옆에 있는 깔끔하고 깨끗한 작은 낡은 붉은 벽돌집에 살고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: You could wander along the canal till you came to broad green fields, with windmills here and there, in which cattle, black and white, grazed lazily.
examples.translation_ko: 운하를 따라 걸어가다 보면 넓고 푸른 들판이 나타났고, 여기저기 풍차가 서 있는 가운데 흑백 얼룩의 소들이 느긋하게 풀을 뜯고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From boy + -hood.
definition_en: The period of a boy's life.

senses.gloss: The state or period of being a boy.
senses.example:
And boyhood is a summer sun
Whose waning is the dreariest one —
For all we live to know is known
And all we seek to keep hath flown — […]

examples.text: I thought that among those surroundings, with their recollections of his boyhood, Dirk Stroeve would forget his unhappiness.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 소년 시절의 추억이 깃든 그런 환경 속에서라면 더크 스트루브가 자신의 불행을 잊을 수 있으리라고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I think I should have shown a strong vocation in boyhood, crushed by the will of his father or sacrificed to the necessity of earning a living; I should have pictured him impatient of the restraints of life; and in the struggle between his passion for art and the duties of his station I could have aroused sympathy for him.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 소년 시절부터 강한 소명 의식이 있었지만 아버지의 뜻에 짓눌리거나 생계를 꾸려야 하는 필요에 희생되었다고 보여주었을 것이다. 그가 삶의 속박에 조바심을 내는 모습을 그렸을 것이고, 예술에 대한 열정과 자신의 지위에 따른 의무 사이의 갈등에서 그에 대한 동정심을 불러일으킬 수 있었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: By analogy to past participles like torn from tear and sworn from swear.
definition_en: Showing signs of wear and tear.

senses.gloss: Damaged and shabby as a result of much use.
senses.example: Upon this, an unhappy-looking woman, in a sort of mourning, neat, but sadly worn, hid her face behind a meagre bundle, and was heard to sob.

senses.gloss: Worn out; exhausted.
senses.example: Preëminently is the Lake District suited for the jaded and worn, who seek in solitude and amidst scenery unmoiled and unsullied by human artifice, refreshment alike of body and spirit.

examples.text: He went out of the room calling “Ewing!” and returned in a few minutes accompanied by an embarrassed, slightly worn young man, with shell-rimmed glasses and scanty blond hair.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 "유잉!"을 부르며 방을 나갔다가 몇 분 후 당황한 기색이 역력한, 약간 지쳐 보이는 젊은 남자를 데리고 돌아왔다. 그는 뿔테 안경을 쓰고 있었고 금발 머리는 성성했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He might have excited sympathy if he had grown worn and thin.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 초췌해지고 말라갔다면 동정을 받았을지도 모른다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English paunche, from Old Northern French panche, Old French pance (French panse), from Latin pantex.
definition_en: A stomach that is prominent or distended.

senses.gloss: The first compartment of the stomach of a ruminant, the rumen.
The contents of this stomach in a slaughtered animal, viewed as food or a byproduct.
The belly of a human, especially a large, fat protruding one.
senses.example: Since retiring from athletics, he has developed a paunch.

examples.text: He was getting something of a paunch, and sorrow had no effect on it.
examples.translation_ko: 배가 나오기 시작했는데, 슬픔은 그것에 아무런 영향도 미치지 못했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His body was shaped like a huge duck’s egg; and his eyes, sharp, blue, and good-natured, rested now and then with self-satisfaction on his enormous paunch.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 몸은 거대한 오리알 모양이었고, 날카롭고 푸른 선량한 눈은 때때로 자신의 엄청난 배를 자족스럽게 내려다보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English gros (“large, thick, full-bodied; coarse, unrefined, simple”), from Old French gros, from Latin grossus (“big, fat, thick”, in ...
definition_en: Extremely unpleasant or unattractive.

senses.gloss: Highly or conspicuously offensive.
senses.example: a gross mistake; gross injustice; gross negligence; a gross insult

senses.gloss: Excluding any deductions; including all associated amounts.
senses.example: gross domestic product; gross income; gross weight

senses.gloss: Seen without a microscope (usually for a tissue or an organ); at a large scale; not detailed.
senses.example: gross anatomy

examples.text: I am a materialist, and I am a gross, fat man—Falstaff, eh?—the lyrical mode does not become me.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 유물론자이고, 뚱뚱하고 속물적인 인간이다. 팰스태프 같은 놈 말이다. 서정적인 어조는 나에게 어울리지 않는다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He had a sweet and generous nature, and yet was always blundering; a real feeling for what was beautiful and the capacity to create only what was commonplace; a peculiar delicacy of sentiment and gross manners.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 다정하고 관대한 성품을 지녔으면서도 늘 실수를 저질렀고, 아름다운 것에 대한 진정한 감각을 가졌으면서도 평범한 것만 창조할 수 있는 능력밖에 없었으며, 독특하게 섬세한 감성과 조야한 매너를 함께 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Past tense of "bid", to offer or propose something

senses.gloss: simple past of bid
senses.example: Pancho, the major-domo, came up to say that Colonel Morales was waiting below. Appleby bade him bring out cigars and wine, and rose from his seat when Morales came in.

examples.text: Blanche then held out her hand and bade me good-evening.
examples.translation_ko: 그러자 블랑슈가 손을 내밀며 안녕히 가시라고 인사했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I could have killed Strickland then, and I knew that my voice was trembling when I bade the nurse good-bye.
examples.translation_ko: 그때 스트릭랜드를 죽여버리고 싶었고, 간호사에게 작별 인사를 할 때 내 목소리가 떨리고 있다는 것을 알 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From sulky + -ly.
definition_en: In a sulky manner.

senses.gloss: In a sulky manner.
senses.example: By hammering trenchantly on that point, Podson was induced to say sulkily, "Oh, all right, if you're so set on it...I never mentioned it. Hang it, I'm not likely to mention it to anybody, am I?"

examples.text: Only gradually did I become aware that the automobiles which turned expectantly into his drive stayed for just a minute and then drove sulkily away.
examples.translation_ko: 기대에 찬 채 그의 진입로로 들어서는 자동차들이 잠깐만 머물다가 시무룩하게 돌아가는 것을 나는 서서히 깨닫게 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I followed them rather sulkily to the table at which Strickland always sat, and he called for the board and the chessmen.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 다소 뚱한 표정으로 스트릭랜드가 늘 앉던 테이블로 그들을 따라갔고, 그는 체스판과 말을 가져오라고 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed into late Middle English from Late Latin īnscrūtābilis, from in- (“not”) + scrūtō (“to examine”), corresponding to in- + scrutable
definition_en: Difficult to understand or interpret.

senses.gloss: Difficult or impossible to comprehend, fathom, or interpret.
senses.example: His inscrutable theories would years later become the foundation of a whole new science.

examples.text: I do not know to what inscrutable Nirvana you aim.
examples.translation_ko: 당신이 어떤 불가해한 열반을 목표로 하는지 모르겠습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Mrs. Stroeve watched the game with inscrutable face.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브 부인은 헤아릴 수 없는 표정으로 게임을 지켜보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Variant of clew (“a ball of thread or yarn”), from Middle English clewe, from Old English clīewen (“ball”), from Proto-West Germanic *kliuwīn, from...
definition_en: A piece of information that helps solve a problem or puzzle.

senses.gloss: A strand of yarn etc. as used to guide one through a labyrinth; something which points the way, a guide.
senses.example: she had even had in the past a small smug conviction that in the domestic labyrinth she always kept the clue.

senses.gloss: Information which may lead one to a certain point or conclusion.
senses.example: Give me a clue because the question is too vague.

senses.gloss: An object or a kind of indication which may be used as evidence.
senses.example: The detectives were looking for some clues at the scene of the crime.

examples.text: When I imagined that on seeing his pictures I should get a clue to the understanding of his strange character I was mistaken.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 그림들을 보면 그의 기이한 성격을 이해할 단서를 얻을 수 있으리라 생각했던 나는 착각이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I looked at her mouth for an expression that could give me a clue to what she felt; I watched her eyes for some tell-tale flash, some hint of dismay or bitterness; I scanned her brow for any passing line that might indicate a settling emotion.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그녀가 무엇을 느끼는지 단서를 얻을 수 있는 표정을 찾아 그녀의 입을 살펴보았고, 무언가를 드러내는 번뜩임이나 당황이나 괴로움의 기색을 찾아 그녀의 눈을 지켜보았으며, 마음속 감정이 굳어지는 것을 나타낼 수도 있는 순간적인 주름살을 찾아 그녀의 이마를 살폈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English tale, from Old English talu (“tale, series, calculation”), from Proto-West Germanic *talu, from Proto-Germanic *talō (“calculat...
definition_en: A story or account of events.

senses.gloss: A rehearsal of what has occurred; narrative; discourse; statement; history; story.
senses.example: the Canterbury Tales

senses.gloss: A number told or counted off; a reckoning by count; an enumeration.
senses.example: They proceeded with some rigour, these Custodiars; took written inventories, clapt-on seals, exacted everywhere strict tale and measure

senses.gloss: The fraudulent opportunity presented by a confidence man to the mark or victim.

examples.text: When Michaelis’s testimony at the inquest brought to light Wilson’s suspicions of his wife I thought the whole tale would shortly be served up in racy pasquinade—but Catherine, who might have said anything, didn’t say a word.
examples.translation_ko: 심문에서 미카엘리스의 증언이 아내에 대한 윌슨의 의혹을 드러냈을 때, 나는 이 모든 이야기가 곧 자극적인 풍자문으로 각색되리라 생각했다—하지만 무엇이든 말할 수 있었던 캐서린은 한마디도 하지 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I looked at her mouth for an expression that could give me a clue to what she felt; I watched her eyes for some tell-tale flash, some hint of dismay or bitterness; I scanned her brow for any passing line that might indicate a settling emotion.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그녀가 무엇을 느끼는지 단서를 얻을 수 있는 표정을 찾아 그녀의 입을 살펴보았고, 무언가를 드러내는 번뜩임이나 당황이나 괴로움의 기색을 찾아 그녀의 눈을 지켜보았으며, 마음속 감정이 굳어지는 것을 나타낼 수도 있는 순간적인 주름살을 찾아 그녀의 이마를 살폈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French masque (“a covering to hide or protect the face”), from Italian maschera (“mask, disguise”), from (a byform of, see it ...
definition_en: A covering for the face, typically worn to conceal one's identity or to protect oneself from dust, smoke, etc.

senses.gloss: A cover, or partial cover, for the face, used for disguise or protection.
senses.example: a dancer's mask; a fencer's mask; a ball player's mask

senses.gloss: That which disguises; a pretext or subterfuge.
senses.example: Grouchy and wary and tender, he’s a sozzled hedonist seemingly out for himself—though his party-animal facade is just a mask for his bottomless generosity.

senses.gloss: Appearance, likeness.
senses.example:
Come then, pure hands, and bear the head
⁠That sleeps or wears the mask of sleep,
⁠And come, whatever loves to weep,
And hear the ritual of the dead.

examples.text: Her face was a mask that told nothing.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 얼굴은 아무것도 말해주지 않는 가면이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Sometimes people carry to such perfection the mask they have assumed that in due course they actually become the person they seem.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 사람들이 자신이 쓴 가면을 너무나 완벽하게 착용해서 결국 실제로 그들이 보이는 그 사람이 되어버리기도 한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From motion + -less.
definition_en: Completely still or stationary.

senses.gloss: At rest, stationary, immobile, not moving.
senses.example: Nothing was to be seen save flat meadows, cows for the most part feeding unconcernedly, and silvery pollard willows motionless in the warm sunlight.

examples.text: Her hands lay on her lap motionless, one in the other loosely clasped.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 손은 무릎 위에 움직이지 않은 채 놓여 있었고, 한 손이 다른 손을 느슨하게 감싸고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He stood before me, motionless, with a mocking smile in his eyes; but for all that, for a moment I had an inkling of a fiery, tortured spirit, aiming at something greater than could be conceived by anything that was bound up with the flesh.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내 앞에 움직이지 않고 서서 눈에 조롱하는 미소를 띠고 있었다. 하지만 그럼에도 불구하고 한순간 나는 육체에 얽매인 그 어떤 것으로도 상상할 수 없는 더 위대한 무언가를 추구하는, 불타오르고 고뇌하는 영혼의 기미를 감지했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English *establishment, stablishment, stablisshement, from Old French establissement (Modern French établissement), from the verb estab...
definition_en: A large organization or institution that is considered to be powerful and influential.

senses.gloss: The act or process of establishing; a ratifying or ordaining; settlement; confirmation.
senses.example: Since their establishment of the company in 1984, they have grown into a global business.

senses.gloss: The state of being established, founded, etc.; fixed state.
senses.example: The firm celebrated twenty years since their establishment by updating their look.

senses.gloss: That which is established; as a form of government, a permanent organization, business or force, or the place where one is permanently fixed for residence.
senses.example: Pedro's is a fine establishment serving a variety of delicious food.

examples.text: After a moment the proprietor emerged from the interior of his establishment and gazed hollow-eyed at the car.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 후 주인이 가게 안쪽에서 나와 움푹 들어간 눈으로 차를 바라보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She had abandoned the safe shelter of her husband’s protection and the comfortable ease of a well-provided establishment for what she could not but see was an extreme hazard.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 남편의 보호라는 안전한 피난처와 넉넉한 살림의 편안함을 버리고, 누가 봐도 극도로 위험한 일에 뛰어든 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From ready + -ness.
definition_en: The state of being ready to do something.

senses.gloss: The state or degree of being ready; preparedness.
senses.example: readiness for civil emergencies

senses.gloss: Willingness.
senses.example: his readiness to help

examples.text: This responsiveness had nothing to do with that flabby impressionability which is dignified under the name of the “creative temperament”—it was an extraordinary gift for hope, a romantic readiness such as I have never found in any other person and which it is not likely I shall ever find again.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 반응성은 "창조적 기질"이라는 이름으로 포장되는 그 나약한 감수성과는 아무 관련이 없었다. 그것은 희망에 대한 비범한 재능이었고, 내가 다른 어떤 사람에게서도 발견한 적이 없고 앞으로도 발견할 가능성이 없는 낭만적 준비 자세였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It showed an eagerness for adventure, a readiness for the hand-to-mouth, which the care she took of her home and her love of good housewifery made not a little remarkable.
examples.translation_ko: 이는 모험에 대한 열망과 그날그날 살아가는 삶에 대한 각오를 보여주는 것이었는데, 집안을 돌보는 그녀의 세심함과 살림에 대한 애정을 생각하면 적지 않게 놀라운 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English encountren, from Anglo-Norman encountrer, Old French encontrer (“to confront”), from encontre (“against, counter to”), from Lat...
definition_en: A meeting or coming together of two or more people.

senses.gloss: To meet (someone) or find (something), especially unexpectedly.
senses.example: H' incounters Talgol, routs the Bear, / And takes the Fidler Prisoner; / Conveys him to enchanted Castle, / There shuts him fast in wooden Bastile.

senses.gloss: To confront (someone or something) face to face.
To meet one another.
senses.example: […] yet when the brother and the sister had encountered, according to the set appointment, none of these impassionedments had been repeated.

examples.text: Perhaps some unbelievable guest would arrive, a person infinitely rare and to be marvelled at, some authentically radiant young girl who with one fresh glance at Gatsby, one moment of magical encounter, would blot out those five years of unwavering devotion.
examples.translation_ko: 어쩌면 믿을 수 없는 손님이 도착할지도 모른다. 무한히 드물고 경탄할 만한 사람, 개츠비를 향한 신선한 한 번의 시선으로, 마법 같은 만남의 한 순간으로 흔들림 없는 다섯 해의 헌신을 지워버릴 진정으로 빛나는 젊은 여인이.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was excited by the encounter, and my fancy worked busily while I sought to concentrate myself on the game I was playing.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그 만남에 흥분했고, 게임에 집중하려고 애쓰는 동안 상상력이 분주하게 돌아갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English clerli, clerely, clerelych, cleerliche, clerliche, equivalent to clear + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is obvious or easy to understand.

senses.gloss: In a clear manner.
senses.example: He enunciated every syllable clearly.

senses.gloss: Without a doubt; obviously.
senses.example: Clearly, the judge erred in his opinion.

senses.gloss: To a degree clearly discernible.
senses.example: He was clearly wrong on all points but one.

examples.text: On the white steps an obscene word, scrawled by some boy with a piece of brick, stood out clearly in the moonlight, and I erased it, drawing my shoe raspingly along the stone.
examples.translation_ko: 하얀 계단에는 어떤 소년이 벽돌 조각으로 갈겨쓴 외설스러운 말이 달빛 아래 선명하게 드러나 있었고, 나는 신발로 돌을 거칠게 문지르며 그것을 지웠다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Those who think that a man betrays his character nowhere more clearly than when he is playing a game might on this draw subtle inferences.
examples.translation_ko: 게임을 할 때만큼 사람의 성격이 명확하게 드러나는 때는 없다고 생각하는 사람들이라면 이것으로부터 미묘한 추론을 할 수 있을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin inferentia. Morphologically infer + -ence.
definition_en: A conclusion or opinion drawn from evidence or reasoning.

senses.gloss: The act or process of inferring by deduction or induction.
That which is inferred; a truth or proposition drawn from another which is admitted or supposed to be true; a conclusion; a deduction.

examples.text: Those who think that a man betrays his character nowhere more clearly than when he is playing a game might on this draw subtle inferences.
examples.translation_ko: 게임을 할 때만큼 사람의 성격이 명확하게 드러나는 때는 없다고 생각하는 사람들이라면 이것으로부터 미묘한 추론을 할 수 있을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In social intercourse he gives you the surface that he wishes the world to accept, and you can only gain a true knowledge of him by inferences from little actions, of which he is unconscious, and from fleeting expressions, which cross his face unknown to him.
examples.translation_ko: 사교적 교제에서 그는 세상이 받아들이기를 바라는 표면만을 보여주며, 당신은 오직 그가 의식하지 못하는 사소한 행동들과 그도 모르게 얼굴을 스쳐가는 순간적인 표정들로부터 추론해야만 그에 대한 진정한 지식을 얻을 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From private + -cy.
definition_en: The state of being alone and free from public attention.

senses.gloss: The state of being secluded from the presence, sight, or knowledge of others.
senses.example: I need my privacy, so please stay out of my room.

senses.gloss: Freedom from unwanted or undue disturbance of one's private life.
senses.example: It takes a village to rob one of a sense of privacy.

senses.gloss: Freedom from damaging publicity, public scrutiny, surveillance, and disclosure of personal information, usually by a government or a private organization.
senses.example: Privacy is assumed by many to be among common-law rights.

examples.text: At small parties there isn’t any privacy.”
examples.translation_ko: 작은 파티에서는 사생활이라는 게 없어요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I would have given much to be a disembodied spirit so that I could see them in the privacy of the studio and hear what they talked about.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 육체에서 벗어난 영혼이 되어 화실의 은밀한 공간에서 그들을 지켜보고 무슨 이야기를 나누는지 들을 수 있다면 무엇이든 주고 싶었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English colnes, colnesse, from Old English cōlnes, cœ̄lnes, cēlnes (“coolness; cool air, breeze”), from Proto-West Germanic *kōlinassī,...
definition_en: The quality of being cool.

senses.gloss: Moderate chilliness.
senses.example: I know a place of all sweet coolnesses; / a little island, like an emerald, set / in the clear argent of a river, that is / Itself a shining net

senses.gloss: Calmness, confidence, or level-headedness.
senses.example: Luckily for England, they have a world-class striker with a golden touch in [Harry] Kane, who was coolness personified to carefully direct in the winner.

senses.gloss: Conflict or hostility or an instance of such that stands in contrast to expected friendliness or interest.
senses.example: In the midst of enemies, Irish and English, Court treacheries and coolnesses, Strafford depended solely upon Laud, and no one other support.

examples.text: The summer came, breathless and sultry, and even at night there was no coolness to rest one’s jaded nerves.
examples.translation_ko: 여름이 왔다. 숨막히고 무더운 여름이었고, 밤이 되어도 지친 신경을 달래줄 서늘함은 찾아볼 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was characteristic of him to display geniality with anyone who showed a disinclination to meet him, and the coolness of my greeting can have left him in little doubt of that.
examples.translation_ko: 자신을 만나기 꺼리는 기색을 보이는 사람에게는 누구든 친근함을 과시하는 것이 그의 특징이었고, 내가 차갑게 인사한 것만 봐도 그는 충분히 눈치챘을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English baken, from Old English bacan (“to bake”), from Proto-West Germanic *bakan, from Proto-Germanic *bakaną (“to bake”), from Proto...
definition_en: To cook food in an oven.

senses.gloss: To cook (something) in an oven (for someone).
senses.example: I baked a delicious cherry pie.

senses.gloss: To be cooked in an oven.
senses.example: The cake baked at 350°F.

senses.gloss: To be warmed to drying and hardening.
senses.example: The clay baked in the sun.

examples.text: “I don’t want to get stalled in this baking heat.”
examples.translation_ko: "이 찌는 더위에 시동이 꺼지는 건 싫어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The sun-baked streets seemed to give back the heat that had beat down on them during the day, and the passers-by dragged their feet along them wearily.
examples.translation_ko: 햇볕에 달궈진 거리들은 하루 종일 내리쬔 열기를 되돌려 보내는 듯했고, 지나가는 사람들은 지친 발걸음을 질질 끌며 걸어갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English hosely; equivalent to hoarse + -ly.
definition_en: spoken in a hoarse voice

senses.gloss: With a dry, harsh voice.
senses.example: She spoke hoarsely because of her cough.

examples.text: “She’s killed herself,” he said hoarsely.
examples.translation_ko: "그녀가 자살했어요." 그가 쉰 목소리로 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Grief and jealousy and rage seized him, and he cried out hoarsely; he was inarticulate; he clenched his fists and raised them threateningly at an invisible enemy.
examples.translation_ko: 슬픔과 질투와 분노가 그를 사로잡았고, 그는 쉰 목소리로 외쳤다. 말이 제대로 나오지 않았다. 주먹을 꽉 쥐고 보이지 않는 적을 향해 위협적으로 치켜들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English despeyringe, equivalent to despair + -ing.
definition_en: Feeling hopeless and desperate.

senses.gloss: Feeling, expressing, or caused by despair; hopeless.

examples.text: When he had gone halfway he turned around and stared at the scene—his wife and Catherine scolding and consoling as they stumbled here and there among the crowded furniture with articles of aid, and the despairing figure on the couch, bleeding fluently, and trying to spread a copy of Town Tattle over the tapestry scenes of Versailles.
examples.translation_ko: 중간쯤 갔을 때 그는 돌아서서 그 광경을 바라보았다—그의 아내와 캐서린이 빽빽한 가구들 사이를 이리저리 비틀거리며 구호용품을 들고 꾸짖기도 하고 달래기도 하는 모습, 그리고 소파 위에서 절망에 빠진 채 피를 줄줄 흘리며 베르사유 태피스트리 장면 위에 《타운 태틀》 한 부를 펼쳐 덮으려 애쓰는 모습을.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He made despairing gestures with his hands, but still no words came from his mouth.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 절망적인 몸짓을 손으로 해댔지만, 여전히 입에서는 아무 말도 나오지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French oxalique, from Oxalis (“the sorrel plant”).
definition_en: Relating to or containing oxalic acid.

senses.gloss: Of or pertaining to oxalic acid or its derivatives.
senses.example: If not sufficiently purified, a little hydrochloric or oxalic acid, or caustic potash may be put in the water, according as the stains are from grease or from ink.

senses.gloss: Of or pertaining to oxaluria.

examples.text: There was a bottle of oxalic acid on the table.”
examples.translation_ko: 탁자 위에는 옥살산 병이 놓여 있었고요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He saw her roll down her sleeves and remove her apron—the apron hung on a peg behind the door—and take the bottle of oxalic acid and go with it into the bedroom.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀가 소매를 내리고 앞치마를 벗는 모습을 보았다—그 앞치마는 문 뒤 못에 걸려 있었다—그리고 옥살산 병을 들고 침실로 들어가는 모습을.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French ambulance, which replaced hôpital ambulant (“moving hospital”) via the suffix -ance, from Latin ambulō (“to walk; to go about”).
definition_en: A vehicle for transporting sick or injured people to a hospital.

senses.gloss: An emergency vehicle designed for transporting seriously ill or injured people to a hospital.
A mobile field hospital.
A vehicle used for the transportation of dead people, typically to a mortuary.

examples.text: She must have broken her rule against drinking that night, for when she arrived she was stupid with liquor and unable to understand that the ambulance had already gone to Flushing.
examples.translation_ko: 그날 밤 그녀는 평소 금주 원칙을 어겼던 모양이었는데, 도착했을 때 술에 취해 멍한 상태였고 구급차가 이미 플러싱으로 떠났다는 것을 이해하지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And when the ambulance came and they put her on a stretcher, they made me go in the kitchen so that she shouldn’t know I was there.”
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 구급차가 와서 그녀를 들것에 올려놓을 때, 그들은 그녀가 내가 거기 있다는 걸 모르게 하려고 나를 부엌으로 보냈다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From stretch + -er.
definition_en: A device for lifting or moving heavy objects.

senses.gloss: One who, or that which, stretches.
A simple litter designed to carry a sick, injured, or dead person.
senses.example: There, characteristically, he refused to be carried on a stretcher, saying he was too heavy for nurses. He walked in with their support.

senses.gloss: A frame on which a canvas is stretched for painting.
senses.example: A twelve-by-fourteen canvas would not pin in his box, so he had to make a stretcher for it, and very neatly he made it, out of strips of butter-box.

examples.text: In the foreground four solemn men in dress suits are walking along the sidewalk with a stretcher on which lies a drunken woman in a white evening dress.
examples.translation_ko: 전경에는 정장을 차려입은 네 명의 엄숙한 남자들이 들것을 들고 인도를 걸어가고 있는데, 들것 위에는 하얀 이브닝드레스를 입은 술 취한 여자가 누워 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And when the ambulance came and they put her on a stretcher, they made me go in the kitchen so that she shouldn’t know I was there.”
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 구급차가 와서 그녀를 들것에 올려놓을 때, 그들은 그녀가 내가 거기 있다는 걸 모르게 하려고 나를 부엌으로 보냈다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English recoveree, from Old French recovree, from recovrer (“recover”).
definition_en: The process of getting back to a normal state after something has happened.

senses.gloss: The act or process of regaining or repossession of something lost.
A return to normal health.
The act of regaining the natural position after curtseying.

examples.text: He begged me to repeat to her that he loved her still; he would reproach her for nothing, but desired only to help her; he made no claim on her, and on her recovery would not seek to induce her to return to him; she would be perfectly free.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 내게 그녀에게 전해달라고 간청했다. 자신이 여전히 그녀를 사랑한다고, 아무것도 탓하지 않을 테니 단지 도와주고 싶을 뿐이라고, 그녀에게 아무런 요구도 하지 않을 것이며 회복되면 자신에게 돌아오라고 설득하지도 않을 것이라고, 그녀는 완전히 자유로울 것이라고.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Stroeve went twice a day to the hospital to enquire after his wife, who still declined to see him; and came away at first relieved and hopeful because he was told that she seemed to be growing better, and then in despair because, the complication which the doctor had feared having ensued, recovery was impossible.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 하루에 두 번씩 병원에 가서 아직도 그를 만나기를 거부하는 아내의 안부를 물었고, 처음에는 그녀가 나아지고 있는 것 같다는 말을 듣고 안도하며 희망을 품고 돌아왔지만, 의사가 우려했던 합병증이 생겨 회복이 불가능하다는 말을 듣고는 절망에 빠져 돌아왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English mere, mer, from Anglo-Norman meer, from Old French mier, from Latin merus (“pure, unmixed, undiluted”), from Proto-Indo-Europea...
definition_en: Not very great or important

senses.gloss: Just, only; no more than, pure and simple, neither more nor better than might be expected.
senses.example: The mere thought of pineapple on pizza makes me want to throw up.

senses.gloss: Pure, unalloyed .
senses.example: Meere [translating pure] ignorance, and wholy relying on others, was verily more profitable and wiser, than is this verball, and vaine knowledge[…].

senses.gloss: Nothing less than; complete, downright .
senses.example: This freedom of expostulation exalted his mother's ire to meer frenzy […].

examples.text: “As a mere matter of curiosity I wish you’d tell me, have you felt the smallest twinge of remorse for Blanche Stroeve’s death?”
examples.translation_ko: "순전히 호기심에서 묻는 건데, 블랑슈 스트루브의 죽음에 대해 조금이라도 양심의 가책을 느낀 적이 있습니까?"
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But when we arrived at the hospital, a gaunt, cheerless building, the mere sight of which was enough to make one’s heart sick, and after being directed from this official to that, up endless stairs and through long, bare corridors, found the doctor in charge of the case, we were told that the patient was too ill to see anyone that day.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 우리가 병원에 도착했을 때—보기만 해도 마음이 아플 만큼 을씨년스럽고 삭막한 건물이었다—이 직원에게서 저 직원에게로, 끝없는 계단을 오르고 길고 삭막한 복도를 지나 담당 의사를 찾아갔지만, 환자가 그날은 누구도 만날 수 없을 만큼 위중하다는 말을 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From needless + -ly.
definition_en: Done without a good reason.

senses.gloss: In a needless manner.
To a degree or extent beyond what is needed.
senses.example: He was always needlessly anxious about his dog.

senses.gloss: Without need.
senses.example: He worried needlessly about his dog.

examples.text: he cried, needlessly indicating the direction.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 굳이 방향을 가리키며 외쳤다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: At first he thought that Dirk was the cause of the disaster, and he was needlessly brusque with him.
examples.translation_ko: 처음에 그는 디르크가 이 참사의 원인이라고 생각했고, 불필요하게 그에게 무뚝뚝하게 굴었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English fright, furht, from Old English fryhtu, fyrhto (“fright, fear, dread, trembling, horrible sight”), from Proto-Germanic *furhtį̄...
definition_en: A feeling of intense fear or anxiety.

senses.gloss: A state of terror excited by the sudden appearance of danger; sudden and violent fear, usually of short duration; a sudden alarm.
Someone strange, ugly or shocking, producing a feeling of alarm or aversion.
senses.example:
Her maids were old, and if she took a new one,
You might be sure she was a perfect fright;
She did this during even her husband's life
I recommend as much to every wife.

examples.text: At any rate, Miss Baker’s lips fluttered, she nodded at me almost imperceptibly, and then quickly tipped her head back again—the object she was balancing had obviously tottered a little and given her something of a fright.
examples.translation_ko: 어쨌든 베이커 양의 입술이 떨렸고, 거의 알아차릴 수 없을 정도로 내게 고개를 끄덕인 다음, 재빨리 머리를 다시 뒤로 젖혔다. 그녀가 균형을 잡고 있던 물건이 분명히 조금 흔들려서 그녀를 놀라게 한 모양이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It may be that she will get off with a fright.
examples.translation_ko: 그저 놀라는 것으로 끝날 수도 있습니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English draught, draght, draȝt, from Old English *dreaht, *dræht (related to dragan (“to draw, drag”)), from Proto-Germanic *drahtuz, n...
definition_en: A current of air moving through a space.

senses.gloss: Alternative form of draft in some of its senses.
senses.example: She could feel a draught where she was sitting.

senses.gloss: A checker: a game piece used in the game of draughts.
Ale: a type of beer brewed using top-fermenting yeast.

examples.text: Finally I gave him a draught, and he sank into uneasy slumber.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 나는 그에게 수면제를 주었고, 그는 불안한 잠에 빠져들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Ata pierced a hole in it, and the doctor took a long, refreshing draught.
examples.translation_ko: 아타가 구멍을 뚫어주자 의사는 길고 시원한 한 모금을 들이켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English, borrowed from Latin serēnus (“clear, cloudless, untroubled”).
definition_en: Having or showing a calm and peaceful atmosphere.

senses.gloss: Calm, peaceful, unruffled.
senses.example: She looked at her students with joviality and a serene mentality.

senses.gloss: Without worry or anxiety; unaffected by disturbance.
senses.example: I took train and reached Wichita, where my active partner was awaiting me. He had just returned from the Medicine River, and reported everything serene.

senses.gloss: Fair and unclouded (as of the sky); clear; unobscured.
senses.example: A serene sky and verdant fields filled me with ecstasy.

examples.text: To the end his mind remained serene and undisturbed.
examples.translation_ko: 끝까지 그의 마음은 평온하고 흔들리지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The nurse looked at him with her calm, kind eyes, which had seen all the horror and pain of the world, and yet, filled with the vision of a world without sin, remained serene.
examples.translation_ko: 간호사는 세상의 모든 공포와 고통을 보아왔으면서도, 죄 없는 세상에 대한 환상으로 가득 차 여전히 평온함을 유지하고 있는 차분하고 친절한 눈으로 그를 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pilwe, from Old English pylwe, pylu, pyle (“pillow”), from Proto-West Germanic *pulwī (“pillow”), from Latin pulvīnus (“cushion...
definition_en: A cushion for supporting the head or neck while sleeping.

senses.gloss: A soft cushion used to support the head in bed.
Any similar head support used for sleep, such as a neck pillow or a hard porcelain pillow. Example: She slept with her head on the pillow.
A pillow lava.

examples.text: Her pillow is all wet.
examples.translation_ko: 베개가 온통 젖어 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The bedroom looked as though she had just left it: the brushes were neatly placed on the toilet-table, one on each side of the comb; someone had smoothed down the bed on which she had spent her last night in the studio; and her nightdress in a little case lay on the pillow.
examples.translation_ko: 침실은 그녀가 방금 나간 것처럼 보였다. 빗들은 화장대 위에 빗을 사이에 두고 양쪽에 하나씩 가지런히 놓여 있었고, 누군가 그녀가 작업실에서 보낸 마지막 밤을 지낸 침대를 매끄럽게 정리해 놓았으며, 작은 케이스에 든 잠옷이 베개 위에 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English abissus, from Late Latin abyssus (“a bottomless gulf”), from Ancient Greek ἄβυσσος (ábussos, “bottomless”), from ἀ- (a-, “not”)...
definition_en: A very deep part of the ocean or a bottomless pit.

senses.gloss: Hell; the bottomless pit; primeval chaos; a confined subterranean ocean.
senses.example: 'You cannot enter here,' said Gandalf, and the huge shadow halted. 'Go back to the abyss prepared for you! Go back! Fall into the nothingness that awaits you and your Master. Go!'

senses.gloss: A bottomless or unfathomed depth, gulf, or chasm; hence, any deep, immeasurable; any void space.
senses.example: Below is the deep abyss of the Lauterbrunnen valley, and at its head a stately semi-circle of mountains, with the pyramidal Lauterbrunnen Breithorn as the centre-piece.

senses.gloss: Anything infinite, immeasurable, or profound.

examples.text: The immediate contingency overtook him, pulled him back from the edge of theoretical abyss.
examples.translation_ko: 당면한 현실이 그를 덮쳤고, 이론적 심연의 가장자리에서 그를 끌어당겼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I wondered what an abyss of cruelty she must have looked into that in horror she refused to live.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 공포에 질려 살기를 거부할 만큼 어떤 잔혹함의 심연을 들여다보았을까 궁금했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Feeling or showing a sense of relief.

senses.gloss: Experiencing or exhibiting relief; freed from stress or discomfort.
senses.example: She was extremely relieved when the lesson finished.

examples.text: Half an hour later Daisy herself telephoned and seemed relieved to find that I was coming.
examples.translation_ko: 삼십 분 후 데이지가 직접 전화를 걸어왔고, 내가 온다는 말에 안도하는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Stroeve went twice a day to the hospital to enquire after his wife, who still declined to see him; and came away at first relieved and hopeful because he was told that she seemed to be growing better, and then in despair because, the complication which the doctor had feared having ensued, recovery was impossible.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 하루에 두 번씩 병원에 가서 아직도 그를 만나기를 거부하는 아내의 안부를 물었고, 처음에는 그녀가 나아지고 있는 것 같다는 말을 듣고 안도하며 희망을 품고 돌아왔지만, 의사가 우려했던 합병증이 생겨 회복이 불가능하다는 말을 듣고는 절망에 빠져 돌아왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
Borrowed from Middle French complication, from Latin complicatio, complicationem.
Morphologically complicate + -ion
definition_en: A complex or difficult situation.

senses.gloss: The act or process of complicating.
The state of being complicated; intricate or confused relation of parts; complexity.
A person who doesn't fit in with the main scheme of things; an interloper.

examples.text: After the armistice he tried frantically to get home, but some complication or misunderstanding sent him to Oxford instead.
examples.translation_ko: 휴전 후 그는 필사적으로 고향으로 돌아가려 했지만, 어떤 복잡한 사정이나 오해로 인해 대신 옥스퍼드로 가게 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Stroeve went twice a day to the hospital to enquire after his wife, who still declined to see him; and came away at first relieved and hopeful because he was told that she seemed to be growing better, and then in despair because, the complication which the doctor had feared having ensued, recovery was impossible.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 하루에 두 번씩 병원에 가서 아직도 그를 만나기를 거부하는 아내의 안부를 물었고, 처음에는 그녀가 나아지고 있는 것 같다는 말을 듣고 안도하며 희망을 품고 돌아왔지만, 의사가 우려했던 합병증이 생겨 회복이 불가능하다는 말을 듣고는 절망에 빠져 돌아왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French ensu-, stem of some conjugated forms of ensuivre (“follow close upon, come afterward”) (French ensuivre), from Latin īnsequere, fro...
definition_en: Follow or happen as a result

senses.gloss: To follow (a leader, inclination etc.).
senses.example: To ensue his example in doynge the like mischiefe.

senses.gloss: To follow (in time), to be subsequent to.
senses.example: Oh how many changes are like to ensue this reformation!

senses.gloss: To occur afterwards, as a result or effect.
senses.example: Give three freshmen six bottles of wine, and hilarity will ensue.

examples.text: The Chink was not backward to defend himself, and a very lively quarrel ensued.
examples.translation_ko: 중국인도 뒤지지 않고 자신을 변호했고, 매우 격렬한 말다툼이 벌어졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Stroeve went twice a day to the hospital to enquire after his wife, who still declined to see him; and came away at first relieved and hopeful because he was told that she seemed to be growing better, and then in despair because, the complication which the doctor had feared having ensued, recovery was impossible.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 하루에 두 번씩 병원에 가서 아직도 그를 만나기를 거부하는 아내의 안부를 물었고, 처음에는 그녀가 나아지고 있는 것 같다는 말을 듣고 안도하며 희망을 품고 돌아왔지만, 의사가 우려했던 합병증이 생겨 회복이 불가능하다는 말을 듣고는 절망에 빠져 돌아왔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pityful, piteful, piteeful. By surface analysis, pit(i) + -ful.
definition_en: Extremely sad or disappointing.

senses.gloss: So appalling or sad that one feels or should feel sorry for it; eliciting pity.
senses.example: Scotland has a pitiful climate.

senses.gloss: Of an amount or number: very small.
senses.example: A pitiful number of students bothered to turn up.

senses.gloss: Feeling pity; merciful.
senses.example: Straightway, he now goes on to make a full confession; whereupon the mariners became more and more appalled, but still are pitiful.

examples.text: “Even alone I can’t say I never loved Tom,” she admitted in a pitiful voice.
examples.translation_ko: "혼자 있어도 톰을 사랑한 적이 없다고는 말할 수 없어요." 그녀가 애처로운 목소리로 인정했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The nurse was pitiful to his distress, but she had little to say that could console him.
examples.translation_ko: 간호사는 그의 괴로움을 불쌍히 여겼지만, 그를 위로할 만한 말은 거의 해줄 수 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Existing since Middle English entente, from Old French entent or entente, ultimately from Latin intentus. Modified later in spelling to align more ...
definition_en: The aim or intention behind an action.

senses.gloss: Something that is intended.
The state of someone’s mind at the time of committing an offence.

examples.text: The poor woman lay quite still, refusing to speak, with her eyes intent, as though she watched for the coming of death.
examples.translation_ko: 불쌍한 여인은 꼼짝도 하지 않고 누워 있었고, 말하기를 거부한 채 죽음이 다가오는 것을 지켜보기라도 하듯 눈을 집중하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I could not help laughing at this remark, made in all seriousness; but he went on, walking up and down the room like a caged beast, intent on expressing what he felt, but found such difficulty in putting coherently.
examples.translation_ko: 진지하게 내뱉은 이 말에 웃음을 참을 수 없었지만, 그는 계속해서 우리에 갇힌 짐승처럼 방 안을 오가며 자신이 느끼는 것을 표현하려 애썼다. 하지만 일관성 있게 말로 옮기는 데 큰 어려움을 겪고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + conscious.
definition_en: Not aware of one's surroundings or thoughts.

senses.gloss: Not awake; having no awareness (usually as the result of a head injury).
senses.example: After the anesthetist administered the general anesthetic the patient was unconscious.

senses.gloss: Without directed thought or awareness.
senses.example: My sudden fright was an unconscious response.

senses.gloss: engaged in skilled performance without conscious control.
senses.example: Someone who has reeled off a string of baskets will say, "I was unconscious," as if he were following the Zen injunction to be mindful while suspending thought.

examples.text: When she became unconscious they said I might go in.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 의식을 잃자 그들은 내가 들어가도 된다고 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: In social intercourse he gives you the surface that he wishes the world to accept, and you can only gain a true knowledge of him by inferences from little actions, of which he is unconscious, and from fleeting expressions, which cross his face unknown to him.
examples.translation_ko: 사교적 교제에서 그는 세상이 받아들이기를 바라는 표면만을 보여주며, 당신은 오직 그가 의식하지 못하는 사소한 행동들과 그도 모르게 얼굴을 스쳐가는 순간적인 표정들로부터 추론해야만 그에 대한 진정한 지식을 얻을 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pase, from Anglo-Norman pas, Old French pas, and their source, Latin passus. Doublet of pas and fathom; compare also pass. Cogn...
definition_en: A unit of length or a rate at which something moves.

senses.gloss: A step taken with the foot.
The distance covered in a step (or sometimes two), either vaguely or according to various specific set measurements.
senses.example: Even at the duel, standing 10 paces apart, he could have satisfied Aaron’s honor.

senses.gloss: A manner of walking, running or dancing; the rate or style of how someone moves with their feet.
senses.example: Netherlands, one of the pre-tournament favourites, combined their undoubted guile, creativity, pace and attacking quality with midfield grit and organisation.

examples.text: Slackening his pace for a moment, he leaned over and spoke.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 속도를 늦춘 그가 몸을 기울이며 말을 걸었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We went at a foot-pace, but on the way back we trotted, and there was something to my mind singularly horrible in the way the driver of the hearse whipped up his horses.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 걸음걸이로 갔지만, 돌아오는 길에는 속보로 갔는데, 영구차 마부가 말들에게 채찍을 가하는 모습이 내 마음에는 묘하게 끔찍하게 느껴졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English band (also bond), from Old English beand, bænd, bend (“bond, chain, fetter, band, ribbon, ornament, chaplet, crown”),...
definition_en: A group of musicians playing music together.

senses.gloss: A strip of material wrapped around things to hold them together.
senses.example: The Jones man was looking at her hard. Now he reached into the hatch of his vest and fetched out a couple of cigars, everlasting big ones, with gilt bands on them.

senses.gloss: A narrow strip of cloth or other material on clothing, to bind, strengthen, or ornament it.
senses.example: band and gusset and seam

senses.gloss: A strip along the spine of a book where the pages are attached.

examples.text: But I gave it to him and then I lay down and cried to beat the band all afternoon.”
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 양복은 돌려줬고 난 침대에 누워서 오후 내내 목 놓아 울었어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was dressed in the deepest mourning, and on his bowler was a broad black band.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 깊은 상복을 입고 있었고, 중절모에는 넓은 검은 띠를 둘렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English revisite, from Middle French revisiter and Latin revīsitāre. By surface analysis, re + visit.
definition_en: Visit again.

senses.gloss: To visit again.
To reconsider or reexperience something.

examples.text: He stayed there a week, walking the streets where their footsteps had clicked together through the November night and revisiting the out-of-the-way places to which they had driven in her white car.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그곳에서 일주일을 머물며, 십일월 밤 그들의 발걸음이 함께 울려 퍼졌던 거리를 걸었고, 그녀의 하얀 차를 타고 함께 갔던 외진 곳들을 다시 찾았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I think I’d forgotten it all; I seemed to have come so far away from my father’s house that I was shy at the idea of revisiting it; but now I feel it’s my only refuge.”
examples.translation_ko: 모든 것을 잊어버린 것 같았어요. 아버지 집에서 너무 멀리 떨어져 나온 것 같아서 다시 찾아간다는 생각에 주저하게 되었는데, 이제는 그곳이 나의 유일한 피난처라는 생각이 듭니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English sor, from Old English sār (“ache, wound”, noun) and sār (“painful, grievous”, adjective), from Proto-West Germanic *sair, from ...
definition_en: Causing physical pain or discomfort.

senses.gloss: Causing pain or discomfort; painfully sensitive.
senses.example: Her feet were sore from walking so far.

senses.gloss: Sensitive; tender; easily pained, grieved, or vexed; very susceptible of irritation.
senses.example: Malice and hatred are very fretting and vexatious, and apt to make our minds sore and uneasy.

senses.gloss: Dire; distressing.
senses.example: The school was in sore need of textbooks, theirs having been ruined in the flood.

examples.text: I was sore, but not with him so much as with myself.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 마음이 아팠지만, 그보다는 나 자신에게 더 화가 났다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was sore and bruised, and his thoughts went back to the tenderness of his mother’s love.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아프고 상처투성이였으며, 어머니의 따뜻한 사랑이 그리웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bruisen, brusen, brosen, brisen, bresen, from a merger two words, both ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *bʰrews- (“to break”...
definition_en: To become discolored or swollen due to injury.

senses.gloss: To strike (a person), originally with something flat or heavy, but now specifically in such a way as to discolour the skin without breaking it; to contuse.
senses.example: It is as I have spoken: the testing first, next the bruising, and in the last bout the breaking and killing.

senses.gloss: To damage the skin of (fruit or vegetables), in an analogous way.
Of fruit or vegetables, to gain bruises through being handled roughly.
senses.example: Bananas bruise easily.

examples.text: He announced that he had a way of finding out whom the yellow car belonged to, and then he blurted out that a couple of months ago his wife had come from the city with her face bruised and her nose swollen.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 노란 차가 누구 것인지 알아낼 방법이 있다고 선언했고, 그러고는 몇 달 전 자신의 아내가 얼굴에 멍이 들고 코가 부은 채로 도시에서 돌아왔다고 불쑥 털어놓았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was sore and bruised, and his thoughts went back to the tenderness of his mother’s love.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 아프고 상처투성이였으며, 어머니의 따뜻한 사랑이 그리웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English weghen, weȝen, from Old English wegan, from Proto-West Germanic *wegan, from Proto-Germanic *weganą (“to move, carry, weigh”), ...
definition_en: To measure the weight of something.

senses.gloss: To determine the weight of an object.
Often with "out", to measure a certain amount of something by its weight, e.g. for sale.
senses.example: He weighed out two kilos of oranges for a client.

senses.gloss: To determine the intrinsic value or merit of an object, to evaluate.
senses.example: You have been weighed in the balance and found wanting.

examples.text: Daisy and Jordan lay upon an enormous couch, like silver idols weighing down their own white dresses against the singing breeze of the fans.
examples.translation_ko: 데이지와 조던은 거대한 소파에 누워 있었는데, 선풍기의 노랫소리 같은 바람에 맞서 하얀 드레스를 눌러 입은 은빛 우상들 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The ridicule he had endured for years seemed now to weigh him down, and the final blow of Blanche’s treachery had robbed him of the resiliency which had made him take it so gaily.
examples.translation_ko: 수년간 견뎌온 조롱이 이제 그를 짓누르는 듯했고, 블랑슈의 배신이라는 마지막 일격이 그동안 그로 하여금 그 모든 것을 유쾌하게 받아들일 수 있게 해주던 회복력을 앗아가 버렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English childhode, childhod, from Old English ċildhād (“childhood”), equivalent to child + -hood. Compare dialectal Dutch kindheid (“ch...
definition_en: The period of life before adulthood.

senses.gloss: The state of being a child.
The time during which one is a child, from between infancy and puberty.
senses.example: He stood transfixed before the unaccustomed view of London at night time, a vast panorama which reminded him […] of some wood engravings far off and magical, in a printshop in his childhood.

senses.gloss: The early stages of development of something.
senses.example: the childhood of our joy

examples.text: He told me of his childhood in the tidy brick house, and of his mother’s passionate orderliness.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 나에게 말끔한 벽돌집에서 보낸 어린 시절과 어머니의 열정적인 정리정돈 습관에 대해 이야기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They are strangers in their birthplace, and the leafy lanes they have known from childhood or the populous streets in which they have played, remain but a place of passage.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 태어난 곳에서조차 이방인이며, 어린 시절부터 알아온 나뭇잎 우거진 골목길이나 뛰어놀던 번화한 거리들도 그저 지나가는 장소일 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English toilen, toylen, apparently a conflation of Anglo-Norman toiller (“to agitate, stir up, entangle”) (compare Old Northern French ...
definition_en: Work hard and struggle.

senses.gloss: Labour, work, especially of a grueling nature.
senses.example: […] he set to work again and made the snow fly in all directions around him. After some further toil his efforts were rewarded, and a very shabby door-mat lay exposed to view.

senses.gloss: Trouble, strife.
A net or snare; any thread, web, or string spread for taking prey.
senses.example: She had waited overlong, and now it was like that Ailie would escape her toils.

examples.text: And on Mondays eight servants, including an extra gardener, toiled all day with mops and scrubbing-brushes and hammers and garden-shears, repairing the ravages of the night before.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 월요일마다 정원사 한 명을 추가로 포함해 여덟 명의 하인들이 걸레와 솔과 망치와 정원 가위를 들고 하루 종일 애써서 전날 밤의 참상을 복구했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I saw a neat little old woman, with cheeks like apples, toiling away from morning to night, through the long years, to keep her house trim and spruce.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 사과 같은 볼을 한 단정한 작은 노부인이 긴 세월 동안 아침부터 밤까지 쉬지 않고 일하며 집을 깔끔하고 단정하게 유지하는 모습을 떠올렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English meek, meke, meoc, unknown origin, likely related to Old English smēag (“subtle, stealthy, etc.”) and smūgan and possibly a borr...
definition_en: A person who is humble and gentle.

senses.gloss: Humble, non-boastful, modest, meager, or self-effacing.
senses.example: Mrs. Wickam was a meek woman...who was always ready to pity herself, or to be pitied, or to pity anybody else...

senses.gloss: Submissive, dispirited, cowed.
senses.example: What if they were wolves instead of lambs? They'd eat her all the sooner if she was meek to them. Fight or be eaten.

examples.text: She was no longer the meek, soft native girl, but a determined woman.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 더 이상 온순하고 부드러운 원주민 소녀가 아니라 단호한 여자였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Let us be silent, content in our little corner, meek and gentle like them.
examples.translation_ko: 그들처럼 온순하고 부드럽게, 우리의 작은 구석에서 조용히 만족하며 지내자.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Anglo-Norman somoundre, from Old French sumundre, from Latin summonēre, itself from sub + monēre, ultimately from Proto-Indo-European *monéyet...
definition_en: To call or order someone to come.

senses.gloss: To call people together; to convene; to convoke.
senses.example: Silence is primary, summoning presence to itself; so it's a connection to the realm of origin.

senses.gloss: To ask someone to come; to send for.
To order (goods) and have delivered
senses.example: You can summon groceries, alcohol and medicines to your home: chips and vodka on New Year’s Eve, say, and then aspirin on New Year’s Day.

examples.text: But the doctor was out when the summons came, and it was evening when he received it.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 부름이 왔을 때 의사는 외출 중이었고, 그가 전갈을 받은 것은 저녁때였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He dragged himself up the stairs; his feet seemed unwilling to carry him; and outside the door he lingered for a long time, trying to summon up courage to go in.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 계단을 질질 끌며 올라갔다. 발이 그를 나르기를 거부하는 것 같았고, 문 밖에서 오랫동안 머뭇거리며 안으로 들어갈 용기를 내려고 애썼다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin prospectus, past participle of prospicere (“to look forward”), from pro (“before, forward”) + specere, spicere (“to look, to see”), equi...
definition_en: A place or situation that is considered likely to be successful or profitable.

senses.gloss: The region which the eye overlooks at one time; view; scene; outlook.
A picturesque or panoramic view; a landscape; hence, a sketch of a landscape.
senses.example: The wide prospect up stream was grey and lowering, the long still-distant waterfront of Dundee, and the Fife shore were alike colourless, and there was ample evidence of rough weather not far ahead.

senses.gloss: A position affording a fine view; a lookout.
senses.example: Him God beholding from his proſpect high, / Wherein paſt, preſent, future he beholds, / Thus to his onely Son forſeeing ſpake.

examples.text: To see her was a delight that never staled, and even though he had not been out an hour he was as excited at the prospect as if they had been parted for a month.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀를 보는 것은 결코 시들지 않는 기쁨이었고, 한 시간도 나가 있지 않았는데도 마치 한 달 동안 헤어져 있었던 것처럼 설레었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: For some minutes there was an exchange of courtesies and some local gossip about the island, the prospects of copra and the vanilla crop; then we came to the object of my visit.
examples.translation_ko: 몇 분간 서로 예의를 갖춘 인사와 섬의 근황, 코프라와 바닐라 작황에 대한 지역 소식을 주고받은 후, 우리는 내 방문 목적으로 화제를 돌렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English apointen, borrowed from Old French apointier (“to prepare, arrange, lean, place”) (French appointer (“to give a salary, refer a...
definition_en: Choose or select someone for a particular task or position.

senses.gloss: To set, fix or determine (a time or place for something such as a meeting, or the meeting itself) by authority or agreement.
senses.example: We have to wait until they're ready to receive us, and make sure we turn up at the appointed time.

senses.gloss: To name (someone to a post or role).
senses.example: Neal Kwatra, appointed by Cuomo to be the state Democratic Party's chief campaign strategist, was identified by two key Democratic insiders[...]

senses.gloss: To furnish or equip (a place) completely; to provide with all the equipment or furnishings necessary; to fit out.
senses.example: The hotel is beautifully designed and beautifully appointed in a classic, modern style that manages to be both serene and luxurious at the same time.

examples.text: When he was appointed Registrar at Thomas’s I hadn’t a chance of getting on the staff.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 토머스 병원의 레지스트라로 임명되었을 때 나는 스태프가 될 기회조차 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His wife’s tidiness was one of the traits which had so much pleased him; his own upbringing had given him a tender sympathy for the delight in orderliness; and when he had seen her instinctive desire to put each thing in its appointed place it had given him a little warm feeling in his heart.
examples.translation_ko: 아내의 정돈된 생활은 그를 그토록 기쁘게 했던 특징 중 하나였다. 그 자신의 성장 배경이 질서를 좋아하는 마음에 대한 따뜻한 공감을 심어주었고, 모든 것을 제자리에 두려는 그녀의 본능적인 욕구를 보았을 때 그의 마음에 작은 따뜻함을 안겨주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From neat + -ly.
definition_en: Done with care and precision.

senses.gloss: In a neat manner.

examples.text: The drawing-room at the Hôtel de la Fleur was a small room, with a cottage piano, and a suite of mahogany furniture, covered in stamped velvet, neatly arranged around the walls.
examples.translation_ko: 호텔 드 라 플뢰르의 응접실은 작은 방으로, 소형 피아노 한 대와 도장을 찍은 벨벳으로 덮인 마호가니 가구 한 벌이 벽을 따라 단정하게 배치되어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The bedroom looked as though she had just left it: the brushes were neatly placed on the toilet-table, one on each side of the comb; someone had smoothed down the bed on which she had spent her last night in the studio; and her nightdress in a little case lay on the pillow.
examples.translation_ko: 침실은 그녀가 방금 나간 것처럼 보였다. 빗들은 화장대 위에 빗을 사이에 두고 양쪽에 하나씩 가지런히 놓여 있었고, 누군가 그녀가 작업실에서 보낸 마지막 밤을 지낸 침대를 매끄럽게 정리해 놓았으며, 작은 케이스에 든 잠옷이 베개 위에 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham
