definition_en: A room or fixture for urination and defecation.

senses.gloss: A room, enclosed area or single-purpose building containing a fixture or fixtures used for urination and defecation; a bathroom or water closet.
senses.example: Sorry, I was in the toilet.

senses.gloss: A small secondary lavatory having a fixture used for urination and defecation and sink but no bathtub or shower.
A fixture used for urination and defecation, particularly one with a large bowl and ring-shaped seat which uses water to flush the waste material into a septic tank or sewer system.
senses.example: My toilet got clogged. Now the bathroom's flooded.

examples.text: His bedroom was the simplest room of all—except where the dresser was garnished with a toilet set of pure dull gold.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 침실은 모든 방 중에서 가장 소박했다. 다만 화장대가 순금으로 된 화장 도구 세트로 장식되어 있는 것만 빼고는.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The bedroom looked as though she had just left it: the brushes were neatly placed on the toilet-table, one on each side of the comb; someone had smoothed down the bed on which she had spent her last night in the studio; and her nightdress in a little case lay on the pillow.
examples.translation_ko: 침실은 그녀가 방금 나간 것처럼 보였다. 빗들은 화장대 위에 빗을 사이에 두고 양쪽에 하나씩 가지런히 놓여 있었고, 누군가 그녀가 작업실에서 보낸 마지막 밤을 지낸 침대를 매끄럽게 정리해 놓았으며, 작은 케이스에 든 잠옷이 베개 위에 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English thirsti, from Old English þurstiġ, from Proto-Germanic *þurstugaz. Equivalent to thirst + -y. Cognate with Dutch dorstig, Germa...
definition_en: Feeling or showing a need for water.

senses.gloss: Needing to drink water or any liquid that can supply water.
senses.example: After all that work in the hot sun, I am really thirsty.

senses.gloss: Craving alcohol; especially, experiencing some alcohol withdrawal.
senses.example: After all that work on a stupidly maintained spreadsheet, I am really thirsty.

senses.gloss: Causing thirst; giving one a need to drink.
senses.example: Marching is thirsty work.

examples.text: But he felt thirsty, and went into the kitchen to get himself some water.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 목이 말라서 부엌으로 가서 물을 마셨다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His temper was certainly no better when he arrived, perspiring freely and thirsty.
examples.translation_ko: 땀을 뻘뻘 흘리며 목이 마른 채로 도착했을 때 그의 기분은 확실히 나아지지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English cuppeborde, cupbord. Equivalent to cup + board. Phonetic variants show that the /p/ in the original forms had assimil...
definition_en: A piece of furniture with shelves for storing dishes or other household items.

senses.gloss: A board or table used to openly hold and display silver plate and other dishware; a sideboard; a buffet.
senses.example: Now when the maids and pages all were gone, / One onely lampe upon the cubbard burning[…]

senses.gloss: Things displayed on a sideboard; dishware, particularly valuable plate.
senses.example: But howe comme to pas, / Your cupbord that was / Is tourned to glasse, / From syluere to brasse, / From golde to pewter, / Or els to a newter, / To copper, to tyn, / To lede, or alcumyn?

senses.gloss: A cabinet, closet, or other piece of furniture with shelves intended for storing cookware, dishware, or food; similar cabinets or closets used for storing other items.
senses.example: Put the cups back into the cupboard.

examples.text: Finally we came to Gatsby’s own apartment, a bedroom and a bath, and an Adam’s study, where we sat down and drank a glass of some Chartreuse he took from a cupboard in the wall.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 우리는 개츠비의 방에 도착했다. 침실과 욕실, 그리고 아담 양식의 서재가 있었는데, 우리는 그곳에 앉아서 그가 벽장에서 꺼낸 샤르트뢰즈 한 잔을 마셰다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had a sudden vision of her standing in the kitchen—it was hardly larger than a cupboard—washing the plates and glasses, the forks and spoons, giving the knives a rapid polish on the knife-board; and then putting everything away, giving the sink a scrub, and hanging the dish-cloth up to dry—it was there still, a gray torn rag; then looking round to see that everything was clean and nice.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 갑자기 그녀가 부엌에 서 있는 모습이 눈에 떠올랐다—찬장보다 조금 클 뿐인 그 부엌에서 접시와 잔들, 포크와 숟가락을 씻고, 칼판에 칼들을 재빠르게 닦아내고, 그런 다음 모든 것을 제자리에 정리하고, 개수대를 문지르고, 행주를 걸어 말리는—그 행주는 아직도 거기 있었다, 회색빛 너덜너덜한 걸레가—그리고 나서 모든 것이 깨끗하고 말끔한지 둘러보는 모습이.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English pegge, from Middle Dutch pegge (“pin, peg”), from Old Dutch *pigg-, *pegg-, from Proto-Germanic *pig-, *pag- (“peg, stake”), fr...
definition_en: A small metal or plastic device used to fasten or hang something.

senses.gloss: A cylindrical wooden or metal object used to fasten or as a bearing between objects.
A protrusion used to hang things on.
senses.example: Hang your coat on the peg and come in.

senses.gloss: A support; a reason; a pretext.
senses.example: a peg to hang a claim upon

examples.text: In England and France he was the square peg in the round hole, but here the holes were any sort of shape, and no sort of peg was quite amiss.
examples.translation_ko: 영국과 프랑스에서 그는 둥근 구멍에 끼워 넣으려는 네모난 못이었지만, 여기서는 구멍들이 온갖 모양이었고 어떤 못도 완전히 맞지 않는 것은 아니었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He saw her roll down her sleeves and remove her apron—the apron hung on a peg behind the door—and take the bottle of oxalic acid and go with it into the bedroom.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 그녀가 소매를 내리고 앞치마를 벗는 모습을 보았다—그 앞치마는 문 뒤 못에 걸려 있었다—그리고 옥살산 병을 들고 침실로 들어가는 모습을.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French environnement. Compare French environnement. By surface analysis, environ + -ment.
definition_en: The surroundings or conditions in which a particular thing exists or flourishes.

senses.gloss: The surroundings of, and influences on, a particular item of interest.
The natural world or ecosystem.
All the elements that affect a system or its inputs and outputs.

examples.text: It represented Stroeve’s idea of the proper environment for an artist.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 화가에게 어울리는 적절한 환경에 대한 스트루브의 생각을 보여주는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Perhaps when he went to Paris he was too old to fall a victim to the glamour of his environment.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 그가 파리에 갔을 때는 이미 나이가 너무 많아서 그 환경의 매혹에 빠져들 수 없었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
From cabin + -et, influenced by French cabinet.
In sense of “a government group”, compare salon, also named for a room used to gather.
definition_en: A piece of furniture for storing or displaying things.

senses.gloss: A storage closet either separate from, or built into, a wall.
A cupboard.
A source of valuable things; a storehouse.

examples.text: Recovering himself in a minute he opened for us two hulking patent cabinets which held his massed suits and dressing-gowns and ties, and his shirts, piled like bricks in stacks a dozen high.
examples.translation_ko: 잠시 후 정신을 차린 그는 우리를 위해 거대한 특허 캐비닛 두 개를 열어 보였는데, 그 안에는 그의 수많은 정장과 가운과 넥타이들이, 그리고 벽돌처럼 쌓인 셔츠들이 열두 개씩 높이 포개져 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Here and there was an Italian cabinet surmounted with Delft, and here and there a bas-relief.
examples.translation_ko: 여기저기에는 델프트 도자기를 올린 이탈리아식 캐비닛이 있었고, 또 여기저기에는 부조가 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English angrily, equivalent to angry + -ly.
definition_en: Feeling or expressing anger.

senses.gloss: In an angry manner; under the influence of anger.
senses.example: "Leave me alone for once," she said angrily.

examples.text: He flung it back against the wall angrily—what did he mean by leaving it
examples.translation_ko: 그는 화가 나서 캔버스를 벽에 다시 기대어 세웠다—도대체 왜 그것을 거기
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I pressed her, angrily perhaps, but she looked down on the ground and began to cry.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그녀를 다그쳤고, 아마도 화가 나서였을 것이다. 하지만 그녀는 땅을 내려다보며 울기 시작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English scremen, scræmen, probably from a fusion of Middle Dutch scremen (“to yell; shout”) and Old Norse skræma (“to terrify; scare”);...
definition_en: To make a loud, high-pitched cry of pain or fear.

senses.gloss: A loud, emphatic, exclamation of extreme emotion, especially horror, fear, excitement, or anger; it may comprise a word or a sustained, high-pitched vowel sound.
A loud vocalisation of many animals, especially in response to pain or fear.
senses.example: I am tender-hearted by nature, and have found my eyes moist many a time over the scream of a wounded hare.

senses.gloss: A form of singing associated with the metal and screamo styles of music. It is a loud, rough, distorted version of the voice; rather than the normal voice of the singer.

examples.text: When she’s had five or six cocktails she always starts screaming like that.
examples.translation_ko: 칵테일을 대여섯 잔 마시면 항상 저렇게 소리를 지르기 시작해요.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He screamed at the top of his voice.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 목청껏 소리를 질렀다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English frantike, frentik, variant of frenetik, from Old French frenetique, from Late Latin phreneticus, alteration of phreniticus, fro...
definition_en: Extremely anxious or worried.

senses.gloss: Insane, mentally unstable.
senses.example: Master have mercy on my sonne, for he is franticke: and ys sore vexed.

senses.gloss: In a state of panic, worry, frenzy, or rush.
senses.example: They returned the missing child to his frantic mother.

senses.gloss: Extremely energetic.
senses.example: frantic music

examples.text: With fenders spread like wings we scattered light through half Astoria—only half, for as we twisted among the pillars of the elevated I heard the familiar “jug-jug-spat!” of a motorcycle, and a frantic policeman rode alongside.
examples.translation_ko: 날개처럼 펼쳐진 흙받이로 아스토리아 절반에 빛을 흩뿌리며 달렸다—절반만이었다. 고가철도 기둥들 사이를 누비며 달리는데 익숙한 "덜컹덜컹-탁!" 하는 오토바이 소리가 들렸고, 다급한 경찰관이 나란히 달려왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He could see nothing that would serve his purpose; he rummaged about his painting things; somehow he could not find a thing; he was frantic.
examples.translation_ko: 목적에 맞는 것은 아무것도 보이지 않았다. 그는 화구들을 뒤져보았지만 어찌된 일인지 아무것도 찾을 수 없었다. 그는 미쳐버릴 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From scrape + -er.
definition_en: A tool used for scraping or removing material.

senses.gloss: An instrument by which the soles of shoes are cleaned from mud by drawing them across it.
senses.example: There is a scraper as well as a mat, and Mrs. Challenger is most particular.

senses.gloss: An instrument drawn by oxen, horses or a tractor, similar to a plow, that is used for scraping up earth in making or repairing roads, digging cellars, building canals, etc.
An instrument having two or three sharp sides or edges for cleaning the planks, masts, or decks of a ship.

examples.text: I moved a little to see it better, and my foot knocked against the scraper.
examples.translation_ko: 더 잘 보려고 조금 움직였는데, 내 발이 신발 닦개에 부딪혔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: At last he came upon what he sought, a large scraper, and he pounced on it with a cry of triumph.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 그가 찾던 것, 큰 스크래퍼를 발견했고, 승리의 외침과 함께 그것을 움켜잡았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English transporten, a borrowing from Old French transporter (“carry or convey across”), from Latin trānsportō, from trans (“across”) +...
definition_en: To move or convey people or goods from one place to another.

senses.gloss: To carry or bear from one place to another; to remove; to convey.
senses.example: to transport goods; to transport troops

senses.gloss: To deport to a penal colony.
To move (someone) to strong emotion; to carry away.
senses.example: Music transports the soul.

examples.text: On a chance we tried an important-looking door, and walked into a high Gothic library, panelled with carved English oak, and probably transported complete from some ruin overseas.
examples.translation_ko: 우연히 중요해 보이는 문을 열어보았더니, 조각된 영국산 참나무로 벽을 두른 높은 고딕 양식의 서재로 들어서게 되었는데, 아마도 해외의 어떤 폐허에서 통째로 옮겨온 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was as though I were suddenly transported into a world in which the values were changed.
examples.translation_ko: 마치 갑자기 가치관이 바뀐 세계로 옮겨진 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + suspected.
definition_en: Not expected or anticipated.

senses.gloss: Not suspected; not having raised suspicion.
senses.example: The police uncovered his unsuspected drug dealing whilst investigating another matter.

examples.text: He had found, not himself, as the phrase goes, but a new soul with unsuspected powers.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 흔히 말하는 자기 자신을 찾은 것이 아니라, 예상치 못한 힘을 가진 새로운 영혼을 찾았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It was not only the bold simplification of the drawing which showed so rich and so singular a personality; it was not only the painting, though the flesh was painted with a passionate sensuality which had in it something miraculous; it was not only the solidity, so that you felt extraordinarily the weight of the body; there was also a spirituality, troubling and new, which led the imagination along unsuspected ways, and suggested dim empty spaces, lit only by the eternal stars, where the soul, all naked, adventured fearful to the discovery of new mysteries.
examples.translation_ko: 그토록 풍부하고 독특한 개성을 보여주는 것은 단지 대담한 소묘의 단순화만이 아니었다. 단지 회화 기법만도 아니었다. 비록 살결이 기적적인 무언가를 담은 열정적인 관능미로 그려졌지만 말이다. 단지 육체의 무게감을 놀라울 정도로 느끼게 하는 견고함만도 아니었다. 거기에는 또한 불안하고 새로운 영성이 있어서, 상상력을 예상치 못한 길로 이끌고, 영원한 별들만이 비추는 희미하고 공허한 공간들을 암시했다. 그곳에서 벌거벗은 영혼이 새로운 신비의 발견을 향해 두려워하며 모험을 떠나는 곳을.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bold, bolde, bald, beald, from Old English bald, beald (“bold, brave, confident, strong, of good courage, presumptuous, impuden...
definition_en: Showing a willingness to take risks or face challenges.

senses.gloss: Courageous, daring.
senses.example: Bold deeds win admiration and, sometimes, medals.

senses.gloss: Visually striking; conspicuous.
senses.example: the painter's bold use of colour and outline

senses.gloss: Having thicker strokes than the ordinary form of the typeface.
senses.example: Many bold fonts are available on this computer.

examples.text: She had a bold hooked nose and three chins.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 굵직한 매부리코와 삼중턱을 가지고 있었다.

etymology: From the French simplification.
definition_en: The act of making something simpler.

senses.gloss: The act of simplifying or something that has been simplified.
A valid simple argument.

examples.text: I knew nothing of the simplification at which he aimed.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 추구하던 단순화에 대해 전혀 알지 못했다.

etymology: From Middle English weight, weiȝte, weght, wight, from Old English wiht, ġewiht (“weight”), from Proto-Germanic *wihtiz ("weight"; compare *weganą ...
definition_en: The amount of heaviness attributed to an object.

senses.gloss: The downwards force an object experiences due to gravity.
An object used to make something heavier.
A standardized block of metal used in a balance to measure the mass of another object.

examples.text: Gatsby, pale as death, with his hands plunged like weights in his coat pockets, was standing in a puddle of water glaring tragically into my eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 죽음처럼 창백한 얼굴로 두 손을 추처럼 코트 주머니에 깊숙이 찔러 넣은 채, 물웅덩이에 서서 비극적인 눈빛으로 나를 노려보고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was not only the bold simplification of the drawing which showed so rich and so singular a personality; it was not only the painting, though the flesh was painted with a passionate sensuality which had in it something miraculous; it was not only the solidity, so that you felt extraordinarily the weight of the body; there was also a spirituality, troubling and new, which led the imagination along unsuspected ways, and suggested dim empty spaces, lit only by the eternal stars, where the soul, all naked, adventured fearful to the discovery of new mysteries.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From careless + -ly.
definition_en: Done without careful attention to detail.

senses.gloss: Giving the appearance of carelessness; relaxedly.
senses.example: The papers were carelessly strewn on the table.

senses.gloss: Done without care or attention; inattentively.
senses.example: Distracted by the salesperson, he carelessly read the contract.

examples.text: “Oh, that’s all right,” he said carelessly.
examples.translation_ko: "아, 괜찮습니다." 그가 무심하게 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But one fact he made clear to me; people talk of beauty lightly, and having no feeling for words, they use that one carelessly, so that it loses its force; and the thing it stands for, sharing its name with a hundred trivial objects, is deprived of dignity.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그가 내게 분명히 해준 사실이 하나 있었다. 사람들은 아름다움에 대해 가볍게 말하고, 언어에 대한 감각이 없어서 그 단어를 함부로 사용하므로 그 힘을 잃게 만든다는 것이었다. 그리고 그 단어가 가리키는 대상은 수많은 하찮은 것들과 이름을 공유하게 되어 존엄성을 박탈당한다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin emphasis, from Ancient Greek ἔμφασις (émphasis, “significance”), from ἐμφαίνω (emphaínō, “I present, I indicate”), from ἐν- (en-, “in”) ...
definition_en: Importance or stress given to a particular word or phrase.

senses.gloss: Special weight or forcefulness given to something considered important.
senses.example: He paused for emphasis before saying who had won.

senses.gloss: Special attention or prominence given to something.
senses.example: Anglia TV's emphasis is on Norwich and district.

senses.gloss: Prominence given to a syllable or words, by raising the voice or printing in italic or underlined type.
senses.example: He used a yellow highlighter to indicate where to give emphasis in his speech.

examples.text: The false emphasis with which they try to deck their worthless thoughts blunts their susceptibilities.
examples.translation_ko: 그들이 자신의 무가치한 생각을 치장하려고 사용하는 거짓된 강조는 그들의 감수성을 무디게 만든다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: For in men, as a rule, love is but an episode which takes its place among the other affairs of the day, and the emphasis laid on it in novels gives it an importance which is untrue to life.
examples.translation_ko: 일반적으로 남자들에게 사랑이란 하루의 다른 일들 사이에 자리 잡는 하나의 에피소드에 불과한데, 소설에서 그것에 부여하는 강조는 삶의 진실과 맞지 않는 중요성을 부여하기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English blunt, blont, from Old English *blunt, probably of North Germanic origin, possibly related to Old Norse blunda (“to doze”) (> I...
definition_en: To make something dull or less sharp.

senses.gloss: Having a thick edge or point; not sharp.
senses.example: The murderous knife was dull and blunt.

senses.gloss: Dull in understanding; slow of discernment; opposed to acute.
senses.example: His wits are not so blunt.

senses.gloss: Abrupt in address; plain; unceremonious; wanting in the forms of civility; rough in manners or speech.
senses.example: I was taken aback by the blunt admission that he had never liked my company.

examples.text: The false emphasis with which they try to deck their worthless thoughts blunts their susceptibilities.
examples.translation_ko: 그들이 자신의 무가치한 생각을 치장하려고 사용하는 거짓된 강조는 그들의 감수성을 무디게 만든다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Until long habit has blunted the sensibility, there is something disconcerting to the writer in the instinct which causes him to take an interest in the singularities of human nature so absorbing that his moral sense is powerless against it.
examples.translation_ko: 오랜 습관이 감수성을 무디게 만들기 전까지는, 인간 본성의 특이한 면에 빠져들어 도덕적 감각마저 무력하게 만드는 본능이 작가에게는 당황스러운 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + conquerable.
definition_en: Unable to be conquered or defeated.

senses.gloss: Not conquerable; indomitable.
senses.example: Be careful when power comes to thee also, lest thou too shouldst smite in thine anger or thy jealousy, for unconquerable strength is a sore weapon in the hands of erring man.

examples.text: It seemed to emphasise the unconquerable spirit of man.
examples.translation_ko: 그것이 인간의 불굴의 정신을 강조하는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But Stroeve, the unconquerable buffoon, had a love and an understanding of beauty which were as honest and sincere as was his own sincere and honest soul.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 정복할 수 없는 어릿광대 스트루브는 자신의 진실하고 정직한 영혼만큼이나 정직하고 진실한 아름다움에 대한 사랑과 이해를 지니고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English softenen, softnen, equivalent to soft + -en.
definition_en: To become softer or less severe.

senses.gloss: To make something soft or softer.
senses.example: Soften the butter before beating in the sugar.

senses.gloss: To undermine the morale of someone (often soften up).
senses.example: Before the invasion, we softened up the enemy with the artillery.

senses.gloss: To make less harsh
senses.example: Having second thoughts, I softened my criticism.

examples.text: I hoped that the grief which now seemed intolerable would be softened by the lapse of time, and a merciful forgetfulness would help him to take up once more the burden of life.
examples.translation_ko: 지금은 견딜 수 없을 것 같은 슬픔도 시간이 흐르면서 누그러지고, 자비로운 망각이 그로 하여금 다시 한번 삶의 짐을 짊어지는 데 도움이 되기를 바랐다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: They were sombre blues, opaque like a delicately carved bowl in lapis lazuli, and yet with a quivering lustre that suggested the palpitation of mysterious life; there were purples, horrible like raw and putrid flesh, and yet with a glowing, sensual passion that called up vague memories of the Roman Empire of Heliogabalus; there were reds, shrill like the berries of holly—one thought of Christmas in England, and the snow, the good cheer, and the pleasure of children—and yet by some magic softened till they had the swooning tenderness of a dove’s breast; there were deep yellows that died with an unnatural passion into a green as fragrant as the spring and as pure as the sparkling water of a mountain brook.
examples.translation_ko: 청금석으로 정교하게 조각한 그릇처럼 불투명한 음울한 청색들이 있었는데, 그러면서도 신비로운 생명의 고동을 암시하는 떨리는 광택을 띠고 있었다. 날것의 썩은 살점처럼 끔찍한 자주색들이 있었는데, 그러면서도 헬리오가발루스 시대 로마 제국의 막연한 기억을 불러일으키는 타오르는 관능적 열정을 품고 있었다. 호랑가시나무 열매처럼 날카로운 적색들이 있었는데—영국의 크리스마스와 눈, 즐거운 축제, 아이들의 기쁨을 떠올리게 했다—그러면서도 어떤 마법에 의해 부드러워져서 비둘기 가슴의 황홀한 부드러움을 지니고 있었다. 부자연스러운 열정으로 죽어가면서 봄처럼 향기롭고 산골 시냇물처럼 맑고 반짝이는 초록으로 변해가는 깊은 황색들이 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bent-, preterite stem (as in bente, benten, etc.), and Middle English bent, ibent, ybent, past participle forms of Middle Engli...
definition_en: To be curved or twisted.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of bend

examples.text: Dr. Coutras made an effort of will and bent over that battered horror.
examples.translation_ko: 쿠트라 박사는 의지력을 발휘해 그 처참하게 망가진 끔찍한 몰골 위로 몸을 굽혔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But one day, when I was walking along, bent on some errand, I passed Charles Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 그런데 어느 날 볼일이 있어서 길을 걷다가 찰스 스트릭랜드와 마주쳤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English tilte, from Old English *tyltan, *tieltan (“to be unsteady”), related to the adjective tealt (“unsteady”), from Proto-West Germ...
definition_en: To lean or incline to one side.

senses.gloss: To slope or incline (something); to slant.
senses.example: Tilt the barrel to pour out its contents.

senses.gloss: To be at an angle.
senses.example: “Marge Gets A Job” opens with the foundation of the Simpson house tilting perilously to one side, making the family homestead look like the suburban equivalent of the Leaning Tower Of Pisa.

senses.gloss: To charge (at someone) with a lance.
senses.example: At Offham, in Kent, tilting at the quintain provides a climax to the day's revels.

examples.text: Luckily the clock took this moment to tilt dangerously at the pressure of his head, whereupon he turned and caught it with trembling fingers, and set it back in place.

examples.text: Tom deferred that much to the sensibilities of those East Eggers who might be on the train.
examples.translation_ko: 톰은 기차에 탈지도 모르는 이스트에그 사람들의 감정을 그만큼은 배려한 것이었다.

examples.text: Until long habit has blunted the sensibility, there is something disconcerting to the writer in the instinct which causes him to take an interest in the singularities of human nature so absorbing that his moral sense is powerless against it.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: He was an idle, useless scoundrel, who preferred to live with a native woman rather than work for his living like the rest of us.

definition_en: To combine or interlace threads or yarns.

senses.gloss: To form something by passing lengths or strands of material over and under one another.

examples.text: The groups change more swiftly, swell with new arrivals, dissolve and form in the same breath; already there are wanderers, confident girls who weave here and there among the stouter and more stable, become for a sharp, joyous moment the centre of a group, and then, excited with triumph, glide on through the sea-change of faces and voices and colour under the constantly changing light.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It may be that in his rogues the writer gratifies instincts deep-rooted in him, which the manners and customs of a civilised world have forced back to the mysterious recesses of the subconscious.

examples.translation_ko: 몽마르트르의 아늑한 화실에서 스트루브와 그의 아내가 보냈던 행복한 나날들, 그들의 순박함과 친절함, 그리고 후한 인정을 생각해보니, 무자비한 우연에 의해 그 모든 것이 산산조각 난 것이 잔혹하게 느껴졌다. 하지만 무엇보다 잔혹한 것은 사실 그것이 별로 중요하지 않다는 점이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English perce, from conjugated forms of Old French percier such as (jeo) pierce (“I pierce”), probably from Vulgar Latin *pertūsiō, fro...
definition_en: To make a small hole or cut through something.

senses.gloss: To puncture; to break through.
senses.example: What appliance can pierce through the outer layers of a star and test the conditions within?

senses.gloss: To create a hole in the skin for the purpose of inserting jewelry.
senses.example: Can you believe he pierced his tongue?

senses.gloss: to break or interrupt abruptly
senses.example: A scream pierced the silence.

examples.text: I longed to pierce his armour of complete indifference.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 완전한 무관심이라는 그의 갑옷을 뚫고 싶었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Ata pierced a hole in it, and the doctor took a long, refreshing draught.
examples.translation_ko: 아타가 구멍을 뚫어주자 의사는 길고 시원한 한 모금을 들이켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English iren, from Old English īsern, īsærn, īren, īsen, from Proto-West Germanic *īsarn, from Proto-Germanic *īsarną (“iron”), from Pr...
definition_en: A hard, silver-white, ductile metal.

senses.gloss: A common, inexpensive metal, silvery grey when untarnished, that rusts, is attracted by magnets, and is used in making steel: a chemical element having atomic number 26 and symbol Fe.
senses.example: For quotations using this term, see Citations:iron.

senses.gloss: Any material, not a steel, predominantly made of elemental iron.

A tool or appliance made of metal, which is heated and then used to transfer heat to something else; most often a thick piece of metal fitted with a handle and having a flat, roughly triangular bottom, which is heated and used to press wrinkles from clothing, and now usually containing an electrical heating apparatus.

examples.text: The lathe painted to look like iron is seen to be but a lathe.
examples.translation_ko: 철처럼 보이게 칠한 선반도 결국은 그저 선반일 뿐임이 드러난다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She knew what I was talking about, the hussy, and I saw her out of the corner of my eyes listening with all her ears, while she pretended to iron a blouse that she had been washing for me.
examples.translation_ko: 그 뻔뻔한 계집애는 내가 무슨 말을 하는지 알고 있었고, 나를 위해 빨아놓은 블라우스를 다리는 척하면서 귀를 쫑긋 세우고 듣고 있는 모습이 눈 끝에 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From peculiar + -ity.
definition_en: A strange or unusual quality.

senses.gloss: The quality or state of being peculiar; individuality; singularity.
senses.example: The peculiarity of meeting six people on a usually deserted trail only struck me later on.

senses.gloss: That which is peculiar; a special and distinctive characteristic or habit; particularity.
senses.example: I thought Alice and H. J. P. would have fainted at the full spectacle; but we are fast getting used to the little peculiarities of foreigners and I trust they will forgive us many sins in return.

senses.gloss: Exclusive possession or right.

examples.text: No affectation of peculiarity can conceal a commonplace mind.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 기이함의 가식도 평범한 정신을 감출 수는 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: To them he was no more than a beach-comber in constant need of money, remarkable only for the peculiarity that he painted pictures which seemed to them absurd; and it was not till he had been dead for some years and agents came from the dealers in Paris and Berlin to look for any pictures which might still remain on the island, that they had any idea that among them had dwelt a man of consequence.
examples.translation_ko: 그들에게 그는 늘 돈이 궁한 해변 부랑자에 불과했고, 다만 그들이 보기에 터무니없어 보이는 그림을 그린다는 기이함으로만 주목받았을 뿐이었다. 그가 죽은 지 몇 년이 지나 파리와 베를린의 화상들이 보낸 중개인들이 섬에 남아 있을지도 모를 그림들을 찾으러 왔을 때서야, 그들은 자신들 사이에 중요한 인물이 살았었다는 사실을 깨달았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From observe + -er.
definition_en: A person who observes something.

senses.gloss: One who makes observations, monitors or takes notice
senses.example: Most impartial observers agreed that Sampras had not served well.

senses.gloss: One who adheres or follows laws, guidelines, etc.
senses.example: I shall be an observer of the local customs.

senses.gloss: A person sent as a representative, to a meeting or other function to monitor but not to participate
senses.example: The UN sent many observers to the country's first elections.

examples.text: A man in a long duster had dismounted from the wreck and now stood in the middle of the road, looking from the car to the tyre and from the tyre to the observers in a pleasant, puzzled way.
examples.translation_ko: 긴 더스터 코트를 입은 남자가 부서진 차에서 내려 이제 길 한복판에 서서, 차에서 타이어로, 타이어에서 구경꾼들로 시선을 옮기며 기분 좋고 당황한 표정을 짓고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: To the acute observer no one can produce the most casual work without disclosing the innermost secrets of his soul.
examples.translation_ko: 예리한 관찰자에게는 누구든 아무리 대수롭지 않은 작품이라도 만들면서 자신의 영혼 깊숙한 비밀을 드러내지 않을 수 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English threschwolde, threscholde, from Old English þresċold, þerxold, þrexwold (“doorsill, entryway”), from Proto-Germanic *þreskudlaz...
definition_en: The point at which a change or transition takes place.

senses.gloss: The lowermost part of a doorway that one crosses to enter; a sill.
An entrance; the door or gate of a house.
senses.example: Shy. You that did voide your rume vpon my beard, / And foote me as you ſpurne a ſtranger curre / Ouer your threſhold, […]

senses.gloss: Any end or boundary.

examples.text: At first I couldn’t find the source of the high, groaning words that echoed clamorously through the bare garage—then I saw Wilson standing on the raised threshold of his office, swaying back and forth and holding to the doorposts with both hands.
examples.translation_ko: 처음에는 텅 빈 차고에 요란하게 울려 퍼지는 높고 신음하는 말소리의 출처를 찾을 수 없었는데, 그러다가 윌슨이 사무실의 높은 문지방에 서서 앞뒤로 흔들리며 양손으로 문설주를 붙잡고 있는 것을 보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It seemed to me that I was on the threshold of a surprising adventure.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 놀라운 모험의 문턱에 서 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From presume + -ably, presumable + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is assumed or supposed.

senses.gloss: Able to be sensibly presumed.
senses.example: Presumably, he will attend the opening.

examples.text: She had a début after the armistice, and in February she was presumably engaged to a man from New Orleans.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 휴전 후에 사교계에 데뷔했고, 2월에는 뉴올리언스 출신 남자와 약혼한 것으로 알려졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You’d better stand there,” he said, pointing to a spot from which, presumably, he fancied I could see to best advantage what he had to show me.
examples.translation_ko: "저기 서 있는 게 좋겠소." 그가 말했다. 아마도 그가 보여주려는 것을 내가 가장 잘 볼 수 있으리라고 생각하는 자리를 가리키면서.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From an alteration (due to Dutch landschap) of earlier landskip, lantschip, from Middle English *landschippe, *landschapp, from Old English landsċi...
definition_en: A scenic view of the land.

senses.gloss: A portion of land or territory which the eye can comprehend in a single view, including all the objects it contains.
senses.example: Its steel helped build America, from the skyscrapers dotting city landscapes to the cars speeding down highways, to the appliances inside millions of homes.

senses.gloss: A sociological aspect of a physical area.
senses.example: In light of such conceptualisations of the power of linguistic landscapes, we set out to examine the connection between the visual landscape and the spoken landscape in our institution[.]

senses.gloss: A picture representing a real or imaginary scene by land or sea, the main subject being the general aspect of nature, as fields, hills, forests, water, etc.

examples.text: The landscapes puzzled me even more.
examples.translation_ko: 풍경화들은 나를 더욱 당황스럽게 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: The smaller were pictures of still-life and the largest were landscapes.
examples.translation_ko: 작은 것들은 정물화였고 가장 큰 것들은 풍경화였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From re- + production.
definition_en: The process of producing offspring.

senses.gloss: The act of reproducing new individuals biologically.
The act of making copies.
senses.example: Unauthorized reproduction of this article is prohibited.

senses.gloss: A copy of something, as in a piece of art; a duplicate.
senses.example: Jim was proud of the Rembrandt reproduction he owned.

examples.text: And yet on the walls were coloured reproductions of several of Strickland’s best pictures, due to the enterprise of a publisher in Berlin.
examples.translation_ko: 그런데도 벽에는 베를린의 한 출판업자가 기획한 스트릭랜드의 걸작 몇 점을 컬러로 복제한 작품들이 걸려 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Now that I have seen many of them again and the rest are familiar to me in reproductions, I am astonished that at first sight I was bitterly disappointed.
examples.translation_ko: 지금은 그 그림들 중 많은 작품을 다시 보았고 나머지는 복제품으로 익숙해졌는데, 처음 보았을 때 몹시 실망했다는 사실이 놀랍다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From accustom + -ed.
definition_en: Familiar with something through frequent repetition or experience.

senses.gloss: Familiar with something through repeated experience; adapted to existing conditions. (of a person)
senses.example: I am not accustomed to walk(ing) long distances.

senses.gloss: Familiar through use; usual; customary. (of a thing, condition, activity, etc.)
senses.example: The raid, directed as usual by vice squad Sgt. Edward McNelley and featuring the accustomed assortment of vice officers, […]

senses.gloss: Frequented by customers.

examples.text: His eyes grew accustomed to the darkness, and now he was seized by an overwhelming sensation as he stared at the painted walls.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 눈이 어둠에 익숙해지자, 칠해진 벽을 바라보며 압도적인 감각에 사로잡혔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Accustomed to the drawing of the old masters, and convinced that Ingres was the greatest draughtsman of recent times, I thought that Strickland drew very badly.
examples.translation_ko: 고전 거장들의 소묘에 익숙하고 앵그르가 근세 최고의 소묘가라고 확신하던 나는 스트릭랜드가 그림을 매우 못 그린다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English drunken, ydronken, idrunken, from Old English druncen, ġedruncen (“drunk; drunken”), from Proto-Germanic *drunkanaz (“drunken”)...
definition_en: Intoxicated or drunk.

senses.gloss: past participle of drink

examples.text: In the foreground four solemn men in dress suits are walking along the sidewalk with a stretcher on which lies a drunken woman in a white evening dress.
examples.translation_ko: 전경에는 정장을 차려입은 네 명의 엄숙한 남자들이 들것을 들고 인도를 걸어가고 있는데, 들것 위에는 하얀 이브닝드레스를 입은 술 취한 여자가 누워 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There were two or three pictures of the forest at Fontainebleau and several of streets in Paris: my first feeling was that they might have been painted by a drunken cabdriver.
examples.translation_ko: 퐁텐블로 숲을 그린 그림이 두세 점 있었고 파리 거리를 그린 그림이 몇 점 있었는데, 처음 든 생각은 술 취한 마차꾼이 그린 것 같다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Feeling confused or disoriented.

senses.gloss: Baffled, confused, mystified, at a loss, not thinking clearly, or uncertain.
senses.example: He was just standing there, turning this way and that, with a bewildered look on his face.

examples.text: Then the same half-knowing, half-bewildered look came back into his faded eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 그러자 반쯤 아는 듯하면서도 반쯤 당황한 표정이 다시 그의 흐릿한 눈에 떠올랐다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I was perfectly bewildered.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 완전히 어리둥절했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested from 1547, from Late Latin stupendus (“stunning, amazing”), from the verb stupeō (“(I) am stunned”). Doublet of stupend (which is ob...
definition_en: Extremely impressive or amazing.

senses.gloss: Astonishingly great or large; huge; enormous.
senses.example: One cannot appreciate how stupendous the Matterhorn is without seeing it.

senses.gloss: Of stunning excellence or degree; marvelous.
senses.example: The renovator created a stupendous new look for our house.

examples.text: It was genius, and it was stupendous and overwhelming.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 천재성이었고, 경이롭고 압도적이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It passed through my mind that the whole thing was a stupendous, incomprehensible farce.
examples.translation_ko: 이 모든 것이 엄청나고 이해할 수 없는 희극이라는 생각이 머릿속을 스쳐 지나갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From acute + -ness.
definition_en: The quality of being sharp or keen.

senses.gloss: The quality of being acute or pointed
senses.example: the acuteness of an angle

senses.gloss: The faculty of precise discernment or perception; sensitiveness
senses.example: By acuteness of feeling, we perceive small objects or slight impressions.

senses.gloss: Shrillness; high pitch; – said of sounds.

examples.text: Now that I look back I am more than ever impressed by Stroeve’s acuteness.
examples.translation_ko: 지금 돌이켜보니 스트루브의 예리함에 더욱 감탄하게 된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: But the impression is fleeting, and serves only to give a greater acuteness to the enjoyment of the moment.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그런 인상은 순간적이며, 다만 현재 순간의 즐거움을 더욱 예리하게 만들어줄 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English condempnen, from Old French condamner, from Latin condemnāre (“to sentence, condemn, blame”), from com- + damnāre (“to harm, co...
definition_en: To strongly disapprove of or criticize something.

senses.gloss: To strongly criticise or denounce; to excoriate.
senses.example: The president condemned the terrorists.

senses.gloss: To judicially pronounce (someone) guilty.
To judicially announce a verdict upon a finding of guilt; To sentence
senses.example: The judge condemned him to death.

examples.text: He felt always the furious hatred that must seize a man condemned when he compared himself with the doctor, sane and healthy, who had the inestimable privilege of life.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 항상 사형선고를 받은 자가 느낄 수밖에 없는 맹렬한 증오를 느꼈다. 정신이 온전하고 건강하며 삶이라는 헤아릴 수 없는 특권을 누리는 의사와 자신을 비교할 때마다 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We are like people living in a country whose language they know so little that, with all manner of beautiful and profound things to say, they are condemned to the banalities of the conversation manual.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 마치 어떤 나라에 살면서도 그 나라 말을 거의 모르는 사람들과 같아서, 아름답고 심오한 말을 하고 싶어도 회화 교본의 진부한 표현들로 만족해야 하는 신세다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Italian ombrella, umbrella (“parasol, sunshade”), diminutive of ombra (“shade”) (or from a Late Latin or Medieval Latin umbrella), fr...
definition_en: A portable canopy to protect from rain.

senses.gloss: A cloth-covered frame used for protection against rain or sun.
senses.example: Quick, grab that umbrella before you get rained on!

senses.gloss: Anything that provides similar protection.
senses.example: The fighters provide a defensive air umbrella over the battle group.

senses.gloss: Anything that provides similar overarching coverage of a range of concepts, purposes, groups, etc.
senses.example: The test facility was established under the umbrella of the company's quality program.

examples.text: His eyes leaked continuously with excitement, and when I took the bag and umbrella from his hands he began to pull so incessantly at his sparse grey beard that I had difficulty in getting off his coat.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 눈에서는 흥분으로 인해 계속 눈물이 흘렀고, 내가 그의 손에서 가방과 우산을 받아들자 성긴 회색 수염을 끊임없이 잡아당기기 시작해서 외투를 벗기는 데 애를 먹었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Their brain is seething with ideas, and they can only tell you that the umbrella of the gardener’s aunt is in the house.
examples.translation_ko: 머릿속에는 온갖 생각들이 끓어오르는데, 정작 할 수 있는 말이라고는 정원사 아주머니의 우산이 집에 있다는 것뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English necessite, from Old French necessite, from Latin necessitās (“unavoidableness, compulsion, exigency, necessity”), from necesse ...
definition_en: A situation where something is required or essential.

senses.gloss: The quality or state of being necessary, unavoidable, or absolutely requisite.
senses.example: I bought a new table out of necessity. My old one was ruined.

senses.gloss: The condition of being needy; desperate need; lack.
Something necessary; a requisite; something indispensable.
senses.example: A tent is a necessity if you plan on camping.

examples.text: He was under an intolerable necessity to convey something that he felt, and he created them with that intention alone.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 자신이 느끼는 무언가를 전달해야 한다는 참을 수 없는 필요에 사로잡혀 있었고, 오직 그 의도만으로 작품들을 창조했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I think I should have shown a strong vocation in boyhood, crushed by the will of his father or sacrificed to the necessity of earning a living; I should have pictured him impatient of the restraints of life; and in the struggle between his passion for art and the duties of his station I could have aroused sympathy for him.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 소년 시절부터 강한 소명 의식이 있었지만 아버지의 뜻에 짓눌리거나 생계를 꾸려야 하는 필요에 희생되었다고 보여주었을 것이다. 그가 삶의 속박에 조바심을 내는 모습을 그렸을 것이고, 예술에 대한 열정과 자신의 지위에 따른 의무 사이의 갈등에서 그에 대한 동정심을 불러일으킬 수 있었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
Etymology tree
Middle English surrendren
English surrender
From Middle English surrendren, from Old French surrendre, from sur- + rendre (“render”)...
definition_en: Give up or yield to an opponent.

senses.gloss: To give up into the power, control, or possession of another.
To yield (a town, a fortification, etc.) to an enemy.
To give oneself up into the power of another, especially as a prisoner; to submit or give in.
senses.example: Don't shoot! I surrender!

examples.text: “I think I know now why you surrendered to your feeling for Blanche Stroeve,” I said to him.
examples.translation_ko: "이제 당신이 왜 블랑슈 스트루브에 대한 감정에 굴복했는지 알 것 같습니다." 내가 그에게 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: When Strickland suggested that in her surrender to him there was a sense of triumph over Dirk Stroeve, because he had come to her help in her extremity, he opened the door to many a dark conjecture.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드가 블랑슈가 자신에게 몸을 맡긴 것에는 극한 상황에서 자신이 그녀를 도와주었기 때문에 더크 스트루브를 이겼다는 승리감이 있었다고 시사했을 때, 그는 수많은 어두운 추측의 문을 열어젖혔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
Inherited from Middle English pilegrim, from Old French pelegrin, from Latin peregrīnus (“foreigner”). Doublet of peregrine.
The change of /r…r/ to...
definition_en: A traveler or visitor to a place, especially one who is going on a religious pilgrimage.

senses.gloss: One who travels, especially on a journey to visit sites of religious significance.
senses.example: strangers and pilgrims on the earth

senses.gloss: A newcomer.
senses.example: "I wouldn't unfork that horse yet, pilgrim. I want a good look at ya first."

senses.gloss: A silk screen formerly attached to the back of a woman's bonnet to protect the neck.

examples.text: I see you as the eternal pilgrim to some shrine that perhaps does not exist.

senses.gloss: A significant risk, undertaken with a potential gain.
A risky venture.
senses.example: The sailors had taken many gambles with the sea and always won.

examples.text: (“Rot-Gut”) Ferret and the De Jongs and Ernest Lilly—they came to gamble, and when Ferret wandered into the garden it meant he was cleaned out and Associated Traction would have to fluctuate profitably next day.
examples.translation_ko: ("로트-거트") 페렛과 드 용 가족, 어니스트 릴리—이들은 도박을 하러 왔고, 페렛이 정원으로 나가면 그는 털렸다는 뜻이었고 어소시에이티드 트랙션 주식이 다음 날 유리하게 변동해야 했다.

examples.text: Until he married he led the ordinary life of his fellows, gambling mildly on the Exchange, interested to the extent of a sovereign or two on the result of the Derby or the Oxford and Cambridge Race.

senses.gloss: A contiguous area of storage in a file system.

Alluring beauty or charm (often with sex appeal).

examples.text: Perhaps when he went to Paris he was too old to fall a victim to the glamour of his environment.

etymology:
From Middle French coherence, from Latin cohaerentia.
Morphologically cohere + -ence.
definition_en: The quality of being coherent or logical.

senses.gloss: The quality of cohering, or being coherent; internal consistency.

senses.gloss: The quality of forming a unified whole.
A logical arrangement of parts, as in writing.
senses.example: In a lesson on coherence in academic writing, students engaged in the following discussion on the online platform TodaysMeet.

examples.text: The murmur trembled on the verge of coherence, sank down, mounted excitedly, and then ceased altogether.
examples.translation_ko: 그 중얼거림은 무슨 말인지 알아들을 듯 말 듯 떨리다가 가라앉았다가 다시 흥분되게 높아지더니 완전히 멈췄다.

examples.text: To give my story coherence I should describe the progress of their tragic union, but I know nothing of the three months during which they lived together.
examples.translation_ko: 내 이야기에 일관성을 부여하려면 그들의 비극적 결합이 어떻게 진행되었는지 묘사해야 하겠지만, 그들이 함께 살았던 석 달 동안에 대해서는 아무것도 모른다.

definition_en: Used to emphasize the degree or extent of something.

senses.gloss: An incident, action, or time period standing out by itself, but more or less connected with a complete series of events.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I never heard him speak of those whose work had a certain analogy with his own—of Cezanne, for instance, or of Van Gogh; and I doubt very much if he had ever seen their pictures.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 자신의 작품과 어느 정도 유사성을 지닌 화가들—예를 들어 세잔이나 반 고흐—에 대해 이야기하는 것을 들어본 적이 없었다. 그리고 그가 그들의 그림을 본 적이 있는지도 매우 의심스러웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French extravagance, from Medieval Latin extra + vagor (“to wander”).
definition_en: Excessive or extravagant expense or behavior.

senses.gloss: Excessive or superfluous expenditure of money.
Prodigality, as of anger, love, expression, imagination, or demands.
Something extravagant; something done out of extravagance.
senses.example: That luxury car is an extravagance you can't afford.

examples.text: I am disappointed that I cannot report any extravagances in his opinions on the old masters.
examples.translation_ko: 거장들에 대한 그의 견해에서 별다른 기행을 보고할 수 없다는 것이 실망스럽다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: We had looked upon it then as an extravagance to dine in a shabby Italian restaurant in the Westminster Bridge Road.
examples.translation_ko: 그때 우리는 웨스트민스터 브리지 로드의 허름한 이탈리아 식당에서 식사하는 것도 사치라고 여겼었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English *happenynge, *happnynge. By surface analysis, happen + -ing.
definition_en: An event or situation that is happening at the moment.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of happen

examples.text: Gatsby looked with vacant eyes through a copy of Clay’s Economics, starting at the Finnish tread that shook the kitchen floor, and peering towards the bleared windows from time to time as if a series of invisible but alarming happenings were taking place outside.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 클레이 경제학 책을 멍하니 들여다보며, 부엌 바닥을 흔드는 핀란드산 발걸음 소리에 놀라고는, 때때로 흐릿한 창문 쪽을 힐끗 보았는데 마치 밖에서 보이지 않지만 불길한 일들이 연달아 벌어지고 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He seemed to see his fellow-creatures grotesquely, and he was angry with them because they were grotesque; life was a confusion of ridiculous, sordid happenings, a fit subject for laughter, and yet it made him sorrowful to laugh.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 동료 인간들을 기괴하게 보는 듯했고, 그들이 기괴하다는 이유로 화를 냈다. 삶은 우스꽝스럽고 추잡한 일들의 혼란이었고, 웃음거리가 될 만한 소재였지만, 그럼에도 웃는다는 것이 그를 슬프게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From secure + -ly.
definition_en: Done with great care to prevent unauthorized access.

senses.gloss: In a secure manner; without fear or apprehension; without danger.
senses.example: Check all personal items are securely stowed in the overhead lockers.

examples.text: For a while these reveries provided an outlet for his imagination; they were a satisfactory hint of the unreality of reality, a promise that the rock of the world was founded securely on a fairy’s wing.
examples.translation_ko: 한동안 이런 몽상들은 그의 상상력의 출구가 되어주었다. 그것들은 현실의 비현실성에 대한 만족스러운 암시였고, 세상이라는 바위가 요정의 날개 위에 단단히 세워져 있다는 약속이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It is thither that after many wanderings Charles Strickland came, and it is there that he painted the pictures on which his fame most securely rests.
examples.translation_ko: 오랜 방랑 끝에 찰스 스트릭랜드가 도착한 곳이 바로 그곳이었고, 그의 명성을 가장 확고히 떠받치는 그림들을 그린 곳도 바로 거기였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English favourable, from Old French favorable, from Latin favōrābilis, from favor. By surface analysis, favour + -able.
definition_en: Having a positive or advantageous effect.

senses.gloss: Apt to win favour; pleasing.
senses.example: The candidate wearing the business suit made a favourable impression.

senses.gloss: Expressing or indicating favour or goodwill; approving, encouraging.
senses.example: The proposal has received many favourable comments.

senses.gloss: Useful or helpful.
senses.example: We made quick progress, due to favourable winds.

examples.text: I do not think he was any gentler here, less selfish or less brutal, but the circumstances were more favourable.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 여기서 더 온화해졌거나 덜 이기적이거나 덜 잔인해졌다고는 생각하지 않지만, 상황이 더 유리했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I suppose no artist achieves completely the realisation of the dream that obsesses him, and Strickland, harassed incessantly by his struggle with technique, managed, perhaps, less than others to express the vision that he saw with his mind’s eye; but in Tahiti the circumstances were favourable to him; he found in his surroundings the accidents necessary for his inspiration to become effective, and his later pictures give at least a suggestion of what he sought.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 예술가도 자신을 사로잡는 꿈을 완전히 실현하지는 못하는 법이고, 기법과의 끊임없는 투쟁에 시달린 스트릭랜드는 아마도 다른 이들보다도 더 적게 자신이 마음의 눈으로 본 환상을 표현해냈을 것이다. 하지만 타히티에서는 상황이 그에게 유리했다. 그는 주변 환경에서 자신의 영감이 효과를 발휘하는 데 필요한 우연들을 발견했고, 그의 후기 작품들은 적어도 그가 추구했던 것의 암시를 보여준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Having no physical body.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of disembody

examples.text: Unlike Gatsby and Tom Buchanan, I had no girl whose disembodied face floated along the dark cornices and blinding signs, and so I drew up the girl beside me, tightening my arms.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비나 톰 뷰캐넌과 달리, 나에게는 어두운 처마와 눈부신 간판들 사이로 떠다니는 실체 없는 얼굴을 가진 여자가 없었기에, 나는 내 옆의 여자를 끌어당기며 팔에 힘을 주었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It is as though in this far country his spirit, that had wandered disembodied, seeking a tenement, at last was able to clothe itself in flesh.
examples.translation_ko: 마치 이 먼 나라에서 육체 없이 떠돌며 거처를 찾던 그의 영혼이 마침내 살과 피를 입을 수 있게 된 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English garde, from early Middle French or late Old French guarde (“a guardian, warden, keeper”) (whence modern French garde), from the...
definition_en: To protect or watch over someone or something.

senses.gloss: A person who, or thing that, protects or watches over something.
senses.example: The prison guard unlocked the door of the cell. After completing the repairs, he replaced the sump guard.

senses.gloss: A garda; a police officer.
senses.example: The Garda Regulations 1924 required a candidate for appointment as a guard to be able to produce satisfactory references as to his character

senses.gloss: A squad responsible for protecting something.
senses.example: The president inspected the guard of honour.

examples.text: Ten miles away the island of Murea, like some high fastness of the Holy Grail, guarded its mystery.
examples.translation_ko: 십 마일 떨어진 무레아 섬이 성배의 높은 요새처럼 그 신비를 지키고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: With its jagged outline it is like a Monseratt of the Pacific, and you may imagine that there Polynesian knights guard with strange rites mysteries unholy for men to know.
examples.translation_ko: 들쭉날쭉한 윤곽선을 가진 그 섬은 태평양의 몬세라트 같으며, 그곳에서 폴리네시아의 기사들이 인간이 알아서는 안 될 불경한 신비를 기이한 의식으로 지키고 있다고 상상할 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From sea + port.
definition_en: A port for ships and boats.

senses.gloss: A town or harbour with facilities for seagoing ships to dock and take on or discharge cargo.
senses.example: For many years, Oslo had no railway communication with Bergen and Stavanger, the principal seaports on the south-west coast.

examples.text: Wellington is trim and neat and English; it reminds you of a seaport town on the South Coast.
examples.translation_ko: 웰링턴은 단정하고 깔끔하며 영국적이다. 남해안의 항구 도시를 연상시킨다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: His account of their discoveries in the low life of a seaport town would have made a charming book, and in the various characters that came their way the student might easily have found matter for a very complete dictionary of rogues.
examples.translation_ko: 항구 도시의 밑바닥 생활에서 그들이 발견한 것들에 대한 그의 이야기는 매력적인 책 한 권이 되었을 것이고, 그들이 만난 다양한 인물들 속에서 연구자는 아주 완전한 악한들의 사전을 만들 재료를 쉽게 찾을 수 있었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English wynd, wind, from Old English wind (“wind”), from Proto-West Germanic *wind, from Proto-Germanic *windaz, from Proto-Indo-Europe...
definition_en: A natural movement of air.

senses.gloss: Real or perceived movement of atmospheric air usually caused by convection or differences in air pressure.
senses.example: The wind blew through her hair as she stood on the deck of the ship.

senses.gloss: Air artificially put in motion by any force or action.
senses.example: the wind of a cannon ball

senses.gloss: The ability to breathe easily.
senses.example: After the second lap he was already out of wind.

examples.text: Then the wind dropped, and the sea was calm and blue.
examples.translation_ko: 그러다 바람이 잦아들고 바다는 잔잔하고 푸르러졌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Ata’s house stood about eight kilometres from the road that runs round the island, and you went to it along a winding pathway shaded by the luxuriant trees of the tropics.
examples.translation_ko: 아타의 집은 섬을 둘러싸고 있는 길에서 8킬로미터쯤 떨어진 곳에 서 있었는데, 열대의 무성한 나무들이 그늘을 드리운 구불구불한 오솔길을 따라 가야 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English ile, yle (with s added, similar to English island), borrowed from Old French ille, idle, isle, from Latin insula. Not related t...
definition_en: A small island.

senses.gloss: An island, usually very small. Compare with islet.

examples.text: Ahead lay the scalloped ocean and the abounding blessed isles.
examples.translation_ko: 앞쪽으로는 물결치는 바다와 풍요로운 축복받은 섬들이 펼쳐져 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Murea, the sister isle, comes into view in rocky splendour, rising from the desert sea mysteriously, like the unsubstantial fabric of a magic wand.
examples.translation_ko: 자매 섬인 무레아가 바위투성이의 장관을 이루며 시야에 들어온다. 신비롭게 사막 같은 바다에서 솟아오르는 모습이 마치 마법 지팡이가 만들어낸 실체 없는 직물 같다.

etymology: From Middle English rokki, rokky (“rocky”), from rok, rokke (“rock; a rock or stone; large rock by a coast or in the sea; rocky outcrop on a mounta...
definition_en: Having a rugged or rocky quality.

senses.gloss: Abounding in, or full of, rocks; consisting of rocks.
senses.example: a rocky mountain    a rocky shore

senses.gloss: Like a rock; rigid, solid.
Having a habitat around or on rocks.

examples.text: At nine o’clock, one morning late in July, Gatsby’s gorgeous car lurched up the rocky drive to my door and gave out a burst of melody from its three-noted horn.
examples.translation_ko: 7월 말 어느 날 아침 9시, 개츠비의 화려한 자동차가 바위투성이 진입로를 따라 내 문 앞까지 비틀거리며 올라와서는 세 음으로 된 경적에서 선율을 터뜨렸다.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English misteriusly, equivalent to mysterious + -ly.
definition_en: In a mysterious or inexplicable way.

senses.gloss: In a mysterious manner.
senses.example: I put my finger to the side of my nose and nodded mysteriously.

examples.text: Sometimes a man hits upon a place to which he mysteriously feels that he belongs.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 사람이 신비롭게도 자신이 속해 있다고 느끼는 장소를 우연히 발견하기도 한다.

etymology: From Middle English knight, knyght, kniht, from Old English cniht (“boy; servant, knight”), from Proto-West Germanic *kneht.
definition_en: A man of high social status and military rank.

senses.gloss: A young servant or follower; a trained military attendant in service of a lord.
A minor nobleman with an honourable military rank who had served as a page and squire.
An armored and mounted warrior of the Middle Ages.
senses.example: King Arthur and the Knights of the Round Table

examples.text: But again I held my tongue, for who am I to argue with a knight?
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 나는 다시 입을 다물었다. 기사 작위를 받은 사람과 누가 나서서 논쟁을 벌이겠는가?

etymology: From Middle English unholi, unhaliȝ, from Old English unhāliġ, from Proto-Germanic *unhailagaz, equivalent to un- + holy. Cognate with Scots unhaly...
definition_en: Not sacred or divine.

senses.gloss: Not holy; (by extension) evil, impure, or otherwise perverted.
senses.example: The priest's unholy behaviour brought the church into disrepute.

senses.gloss: Dreadful, terrible, excessive, or otherwise atrocious.
senses.example: What an unholy mess your room is in!

examples.text: It was the work of a man who knew things which it is unholy for men to know.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 인간이 알아서는 안 될 것들을 아는 사람의 작품이었다.

examples.text: With its jagged outline it is like a Monseratt of the Pacific, and you may imagine that there Polynesian knights guard with strange rites mysteries unholy for men to know.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Formed under the influence of both diminue (from Old French diminuer, from Latin dīminuo) and minish.
definition_en: To make something smaller or less important.

senses.gloss: To make smaller.
To become less or smaller.
To make appear smaller than in reality; to dismiss as unimportant.

examples.text: His count of enchanted objects had diminished by one.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 간직했던 마법 같은 것들의 수가 하나 줄어든 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The beauty of the island is unveiled as diminishing distance shows you in distincter shape its lovely peaks, but it keeps its secret as you sail by, and, darkly inviolable, seems to fold itself together in a stony, inaccessible grimness.
examples.translation_ko: 거리가 줄어들면서 섬의 아름다운 봉우리들이 더욱 뚜렷한 모습을 드러내며 섬의 아름다움이 펼쳐지지만, 배가 지나쳐 갈 때에도 섬은 여전히 비밀을 간직한 채 어둡고 신성불가침한 모습으로 돌처럼 굳고 접근할 수 없는 험상궂음 속에 몸을 감싸고 있는 듯하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English murmur, murmor, murmour, from Old French murmure (modern French murmure), from Latin murmur (“murmur, humming, muttering, roari...
definition_en: A low, indistinct sound.

senses.gloss: Any low, indistinct sound, like that of running water.
senses.example:
1979: A translation of the Eclogues by Paul Alpers
The windy murmur of the breeze subsides.

senses.gloss: Soft indistinct speech.
senses.example: A murmur arose from the audience.

senses.gloss: The sound made by any condition which produces a noisy, or turbulent, flow of blood through the heart.

examples.text: “A large order,” I murmured.
examples.translation_ko: "대단한 주문이군요." 나는 중얼거렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: Tahiti is a lofty green island, with deep folds of a darker green, in which you divine silent valleys; there is mystery in their sombre depths, down which murmur and plash cool streams, and you feel that in those umbrageous places life from immemorial times has been led according to immemorial ways.
examples.translation_ko: 타히티는 높이 솟은 푸른 섬으로, 더 짙은 녹색의 깊은 주름들이 있어 그 속에 고요한 계곡들이 숨어 있음을 짐작할 수 있다. 그 어둠침침한 깊은 곳에는 신비로움이 깃들어 있고, 그곳으로는 시원한 물줄기가 중얼거리며 철벅거리고 흘러내리며, 그 그늘진 곳에서는 태고적부터 태고의 방식대로 삶이 이어져 왔음을 느끼게 된다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English mery, merie, mirie, myrie, murie, murȝe, from Old English meriġe, miriġe, myriġe, myreġe, myrġe (“pleasing, agreeable; pleasant...
definition_en: Feeling or expressing joy.

senses.gloss: Jolly and full of high spirits; happy.
senses.example: We had a very merry Christmas.

senses.gloss: Festive and full of fun and laughter.
senses.example: Everyone was merry at the party.

senses.gloss: Brisk
senses.example: The play moved along at a merry pace.

examples.text: They had told me he was a merry, light-hearted youth.
examples.translation_ko: 사람들은 그가 명랑하고 쾌활한 청년이었다고 내게 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: It is like the sadness which you may see in the jester’s eyes when a merry company is laughing at his sallies; his lips smile and his jokes are gayer because in the communion of laughter he finds himself more intolerably alone.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 유쾌한 일행이 어릿광대의 농담에 웃고 있을 때 그의 눈에서 볼 수 있는 슬픔과 같다. 웃음의 교감 속에서 자신이 더욱 견딜 수 없을 만큼 외롭다는 것을 깨닫기 때문에 그의 입술은 미소 짓고 농담은 더욱 경쾌해진다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + ashamed.
definition_en: Feeling no shame or guilt.

senses.gloss: feeling or showing no shame, embarrassment or remorse
senses.example: Critics suggest that Fernández, an unashamed populist and nationalist, is seeking to deflect attention from social disharmony at home.

examples.text: A subdued impassioned murmur was audible in the room beyond, and Miss Baker leaned forward unashamed, trying to hear.

definition_en: A structure built out over water, typically for loading and unloading ships.

senses.gloss: An artificial landing place for ships on a riverbank or shore.
senses.example: Out upon the wharfs they came, / Knight and burgher, lord and dame, / And round the prow they read her name, / The Lady of Shalott.

senses.gloss: The bank of a river, or the shore of the sea.
senses.example: the fat weed that roots itself in ease on Lethe wharf

examples.text: And the crowd that throngs the wharf as the steamer draws alongside is gay and debonair; it is a noisy, cheerful, gesticulating crowd.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: One morning the tramp docked at Alexandria, and from the deck he looked at the city, white in the sunlight, and the crowd on the wharf; he saw the natives in their shabby gabardines, the blacks from the Soudan, the noisy throng of Greeks and Italians, the grave Turks in tarbooshes, the sunshine and the blue sky; and something happened to him.
examples.translation_ko: 어느 날 아침 화물선이 알렉산드리아에 정박했고, 갑판에서 그는 햇빛 속에 하얗게 빛나는 도시와 부두의 인파를 바라보았다. 남루한 가바딘을 입은 현지인들, 수단에서 온 흑인들, 시끄러운 그리스인과 이탈리아인 무리, 터부시를 쓴 근엄한 터키인들, 햇살과 푸른 하늘을 보았는데, 그때 그에게 무언가가 일어났다.

definition_en: A state of noisy and busy activity.

senses.gloss: An excited activity; a stir.
A cover to protect and hide the back panel of a computer or other office machine.
A frame worn underneath a woman's skirt, typically only protruding from the rear as opposed to the earlier more circular hoops.

examples.text: The quiet lights in the houses were humming out into the darkness and there was a stir and bustle among the stars.
examples.translation_ko: 집들의 조용한 불빛이 어둠 속으로 윙윙거리며 퍼져나갔고, 별들 사이에서는 술렁임과 분주함이 일고 있었다.

examples.text: Everything is done with a great deal of bustle, the unloading of the baggage, the examination of the customs; and everyone seems to smile at you.
examples.translation_ko: 짐을 내리고 세관 검사를 받는 모든 일이 매우 분주하게 이루어지며, 모든 사람이 당신에게 미소를 짓는 것 같다.

definition_en: Personal belongings carried or transported.

senses.gloss: Portable cases, large bags, and similar equipment for manually carrying, pushing, or pulling personal items while traveling
senses.example: Please put your baggage in the trunk.

senses.gloss: Factors, especially psychological ones, which interfere with a person's ability to function effectively.

senses.gloss: A woman.

examples.text: But she and Tom had gone away early that afternoon, and taken baggage with them.

etymology:

definition_en: A test or assessment of someone's knowledge or skills.

senses.gloss: The act of examining.
Particularly, an inspection by a medical professional to establish the extent and nature of any sickness or injury.

A formal test involving answering written or oral questions under a time constraint and usually without access to textbooks; typically, a large, written test administered to high school and college students covering course material studied in a semester.

examples.text: Everything is done with a great deal of bustle, the unloading of the baggage, the examination of the customs; and everyone seems to smile at you.

etymology: From Middle English lyvere, lyver, from Old English lifer (“liver”), from Proto-West Germanic *libru, from Proto-Germanic *librō, from Proto-Indo-E...
definition_en: The largest internal organ of the body, responsible for detoxification and metabolism.

senses.gloss: A large organ in the body that stores and metabolizes nutrients, destroys toxins and produces bile. It is responsible for thousands of biochemical reactions.
senses.example: Steve Jobs is a famous liver transplant recipient.

senses.gloss: This organ, as taken from animals used as food.
senses.example: I'd like some goose liver pate.

senses.gloss: A dark brown colour, tinted with red and gray, like the colour of liver.

examples.text: We went upstairs, through period bedrooms swathed in rose and lavender silk and vivid with new flowers, through dressing-rooms and poolrooms, and bathrooms with sunken baths—intruding into one chamber where a dishevelled man in pyjamas was doing liver exercises on the floor.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 위층으로 올라가서 장미색과 라벤더색 비단으로 둘러싸이고 싱싱한 꽃들로 화사한 시대별 침실들을 지나고, 화장실과 당구장, 그리고 움푹 파인 욕조가 있는 욕실들을 지나갔다—한 방에서는 잠옷 차림의 헝클어진 남자가 바닥에서 간 운동을 하고 있어서 우리가 침입하게 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You and your liver must decide that between you,” I replied.
examples.translation_ko: "그건 당신과 당신 간이 알아서 결정할 일이지," 내가 답했다.

etymology: From practical + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is almost entirely or nearly the case.

senses.gloss: In practice; in effect or in actuality, though possibly not officially, technically, or legally.
senses.example: Stalin was not technically or legally the head of state but was practically so.

senses.gloss: Almost completely; almost entirely.
senses.example: He was practically uneducated, barely able to read and write a simple sentence.

senses.gloss: With respect to practices or a practice.
senses.example: He wasn't very good with words or numbers; he was more of a practically minded person

examples.text: “I’m practically a teetotaller,” he said, as he poured himself out a good half-tumbler of Canadian Club.
examples.translation_ko: "나는 사실상 금주가야," 그는 캐나디언 클럽을 텀블러 반 정도나 따라 마시며 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I do not consider that the cigars and whisky he consumed at my expense (he always refused cocktails, since he was practically a teetotaller), and the few dollars, borrowed with a civil air of conferring a favour upon me, that passed from my pocket to his, were in any way equivalent to the entertainment he afforded me.
examples.translation_ko: 내 돈으로 그가 소비한 시가와 위스키(그는 사실상 금주가였기 때문에 칵테일은 항상 거절했다), 그리고 내게 호의를 베푸는 듯한 정중한 태도로 빌려간 몇 달러가 내 주머니에서 그의 주머니로 넘어간 것이 그가 내게 선사한 즐거움과 결코 동등하다고 생각하지 않는다.

definition_en: A hard, calcified structure in the mouth used for biting and chewing food.

senses.gloss: A hard, calcareous structure present in the mouth of many vertebrate animals, generally used for biting and chewing food.
A sharp projection on the blade of a saw or similar implement.
A projection on the edge of a gear that meshes with similar projections on adjacent gears, or on the circumference of a cog that engages with a chain.

examples.text: He had been full of the idea so long, dreamed it right through to the end, waited with his teeth set, so to speak, at an inconceivable pitch of intensity.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 너무 오랫동안 그 생각에 사로잡혀 있었고, 끝까지 꿈꿔왔으며, 말하자면 상상할 수 없을 만큼 강렬한 긴장 속에서 이를 악물고 기다려왔던 것이다.

etymology: From astonishing + -ly.
definition_en: Extremely surprising or impressive.

senses.gloss: In an astonishing manner; so as to surprise or astonish.
senses.example: Famous hotels, for instance, are astonishingly commonplace.

senses.gloss: Very; remarkably used as an intensifier.
senses.example: The advertisements made the place look promising, but the food was astonishingly bad.

examples.text: I suppose to European eyes it would have seemed astonishingly sordid.
examples.translation_ko: 유럽인의 눈에는 놀랄 만큼 더럽고 초라해 보였을 것이다.

examples.text: His face was deeply lined, burned brown by long exposure to the sun, and he had a pair of small blue eyes which were astonishingly shifty.

etymology: First attested in 1622. From Italian ingraziare or Medieval Latin *ingratiatus, from Latin in grātiam (“for the favor of”).
definition_en: Gain favor or approval from someone

senses.gloss: To bring oneself into favour with someone by flattering or trying to please them; to insinuate oneself; to worm one's way in.
senses.example: Like many other executives in Silicon Valley, [Meta CEO Mark] Zuckerberg has recently been ingratiating himself with the Trump administration.

senses.gloss: To recommend; to render easy or agreeable.
senses.example: the Sense of this will mightily indear and ingratiate them to us

examples.text: For several weeks I didn’t see him or hear his voice on the phone—mostly I was in New York, trotting around with Jordan and trying to ingratiate myself with her senile aunt—but finally I went over to his house one Sunday afternoon.
examples.translation_ko: 몇 주 동안 나는 그를 보지도 못했고 전화로 그의 목소리를 듣지도 못했다. 대부분 나는 뉴욕에 있으면서 조던과 함께 돌아다니며 그녀의 노망든 고모에게 잘 보이려고 애쓰고 있었다. 하지만 마침내 어느 일요일 오후 그의 집으로 찾아갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He gave me an ingratiating smile.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 비위를 맞추려는 듯한 미소를 지었다.

etymology: Borrowed from French affable, from Latin affābilis, from affor (“I address”), from ad + for (“speak, talk”). See fable.
definition_en: Friendly and approachable in manner.

senses.gloss: Receiving others kindly and conversing with them in a free and friendly manner; friendly, courteous, sociable.
Mild; benign.
senses.example: During more affable weather, the four friends congregate outside, sometimes leaning their hickory chairs against a "catapa" tree[…]

examples.text: They are easy of approach and affable in conversation.
examples.translation_ko: 그들은 접근하기 쉽고 대화에서 상냥하다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: She was civil and affable, but she could hardly conceal her intimate conviction that she was not quite as others were.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 예의 바르고 상냥했지만, 자신이 다른 사람들과는 다르다는 내심의 확신을 거의 감추지 못했다.

etymology:

definition_en: The state of being well known or easily understood.

senses.gloss: The state of being extremely friendly; intimacy.

senses.gloss: Undue intimacy; inappropriate informality, impertinence.
An instance of familiar behaviour.

examples.text: The familiar expression held no more familiarity than the hand which reassuringly brushed my shoulder.
examples.translation_ko: 그 친숙한 표현은 안심시키듯 내 어깨를 스치고 지나간 손길보다도 친숙함이 없었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: You need no laborious steps to enter upon familiarity with them, and you can earn not only their confidence, but their gratitude, by turning an attentive ear to their discourse.
examples.translation_ko: 그들과 친해지기 위해 번거로운 단계를 거칠 필요가 없으며, 그들의 이야기에 귀 기울여주기만 해도 신뢰는 물론 감사까지 얻을 수 있다.

senses.gloss: To use up.
senses.example: The power plant consumes 30 tons of coal per hour.

senses.gloss: To eat.
senses.example: Baby birds consume their own weight in food each day.

senses.gloss: To completely occupy the thoughts or attention of.

definition_en: Discuss or consider something formally.

senses.gloss: To grant as a possession; to bestow.
senses.example: The college has conferred an honorary degree upon the visiting Prime Minister.

senses.gloss: To talk together, to consult, discuss; to collogue.
senses.example: They were in a huddle, conferring about something.

senses.gloss: To compare.

definition_en: Reduce or impair someone's ability or quality.

senses.gloss: To weaken; to affect negatively; to have a diminishing effect on.
senses.example: In 2016, it was announced that Jones had been diagnosed with primary progressive aphasia, a form of dementia that impairs the ability to communicate.

senses.gloss: To grow worse; to deteriorate.
senses.example: Flesh may empaire,[…]but reason can repaire.

examples.text: But it was nice to see that any unpleasantness he had endured in his native land had not impaired his ardent patriotism.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 고국에서 겪었던 어떤 불쾌한 일도 그의 열렬한 애국심을 손상시키지 못했다는 것은 보기 좋은 일이었다.

examples.text: He suffered from dyspepsia, and he might often be seen sucking a tablet of pepsin; in the morning his appetite was poor; but this affliction alone would hardly have impaired his spirits.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 소화불량에 시달렸고, 펩신 정제를 빨고 있는 모습을 자주 볼 수 있었다. 아침에는 식욕이 없었지만, 이런 고통만으로는 그의 기분을 상하게 하기에 충분하지 않았을 것이다.

definition_en: Used to indicate that something happens or is done often.

senses.gloss: For infinitely many terms of the sequence.

examples.text: Most of the confidences were unsought—frequently I have feigned sleep, preoccupation, or a hostile levity when I realized by some unmistakable sign that an intimate revelation was quivering on the horizon; for the intimate revelations of young men, or at least the terms in which they express them, are usually plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I saw him, with my mind’s eye, on the schooner on which he worked, wearing nothing but a pair of dungarees; and at night, when the boat sailed along easily before a light breeze, and the sailors were gathered on the upper deck, while the captain and the supercargo lolled in deck-chairs, smoking their pipes, I saw him dance with another lad, dance wildly, to the wheezy music of the concertina.

examples.text: You would think it not a very suitable picture for a doctor’s consulting-room, but my wife will not have it in the drawing-room.

etymology: From Middle English kerven, from Old English ceorfan, from Proto-West Germanic *kerban, from Proto-Germanic *kerbaną, from Proto-Indo-European *ger...
definition_en: To cut or shape something roughly.

senses.gloss: To cut.
senses.example: My good blade carves the casques of men, / My tough lance thrusteth sure, / My strength is as the strength of ten, / Because my heart is pure.

senses.gloss: To cut meat in order to serve it.
senses.example: You carve the roast and I’ll serve the vegetables.

senses.gloss: To shape to sculptural effect; to produce (a work) by cutting, or to cut (a material) into a finished work, especially with cuts that are curved rather than only straight slices.
senses.example: to carve a name into a tree

examples.text: On a chance we tried an important-looking door, and walked into a high Gothic library, panelled with carved English oak, and probably transported complete from some ruin overseas.
examples.translation_ko: 우연히 중요해 보이는 문을 열어보았더니, 조각된 영국산 참나무로 벽을 두른 높은 고딕 양식의 서재로 들어서게 되었는데, 아마도 해외의 어떤 폐허에서 통째로 옮겨온 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They were sombre blues, opaque like a delicately carved bowl in lapis lazuli, and yet with a quivering lustre that suggested the palpitation of mysterious life; there were purples, horrible like raw and putrid flesh, and yet with a glowing, sensual passion that called up vague memories of the Roman Empire of Heliogabalus; there were reds, shrill like the berries of holly—one thought of Christmas in England, and the snow, the good cheer, and the pleasure of children—and yet by some magic softened till they had the swooning tenderness of a dove’s breast; there were deep yellows that died with an unnatural passion into a green as fragrant as the spring and as pure as the sparkling water of a mountain brook.
examples.translation_ko: 청금석으로 정교하게 조각한 그릇처럼 불투명한 음울한 청색들이 있었는데, 그러면서도 신비로운 생명의 고동을 암시하는 떨리는 광택을 띠고 있었다. 날것의 썩은 살점처럼 끔찍한 자주색들이 있었는데, 그러면서도 헬리오가발루스 시대 로마 제국의 막연한 기억을 불러일으키는 타오르는 관능적 열정을 품고 있었다. 호랑가시나무 열매처럼 날카로운 적색들이 있었는데—영국의 크리스마스와 눈, 즐거운 축제, 아이들의 기쁨을 떠올리게 했다—그러면서도 어떤 마법에 의해 부드러워져서 비둘기 가슴의 황홀한 부드러움을 지니고 있었다. 부자연스러운 열정으로 죽어가면서 봄처럼 향기롭고 산골 시냇물처럼 맑고 반짝이는 초록으로 변해가는 깊은 황색들이 있었다.

definition_en: A feeling of happiness or enthusiasm.

senses.gloss: A cheerful attitude; happiness; a good, happy, or positive mood.
senses.example: I have not that alacrity of spirit, / Nor cheer of mind, that I was wont to have.

senses.gloss: That which promotes good spirits or cheerfulness, especially food and entertainment prepared for a festive occasion.
senses.example: a table loaded with good cheer

senses.gloss: A cry expressing joy, approval or support, such as "hurrah".
senses.example: Three cheers for the birthday boy!

examples.text: The music had died down as the ceremony began and now a long cheer floated in at the window, followed by intermittent cries of “Yea—ea—ea!” and finally by a burst of jazz as the dancing began.
examples.translation_ko: 의식이 시작되면서 음악이 잦아들었고, 이제 긴 환호성이 창문으로 흘러들어왔다. 이어서 간헐적인 "예—에—에!" 소리가 들렸고, 마침내 춤이 시작되자 재즈가 터져 나왔다.
