etymology: From Middle English swoune, swone, from the verb (see below).
definition_en: To faint or lose consciousness

senses.gloss: A faint.
senses.example: She dandled it, and dancet it up and doune, / Not ceasing till she rais'd it from his swoune.

senses.gloss: An infatuation.

examples.text: When the “Jazz History of the World” was over, girls were putting their heads on men’s shoulders in a puppyish, convivial way, girls were swooning backward playfully into men’s arms, even into groups, knowing that someone would arrest their falls—but no one swooned backward on Gatsby, and no French bob touched Gatsby’s shoulder, and no singing quartets were formed with Gatsby’s head for one link.
examples.translation_ko: "재즈 세계사"가 끝나자, 여자들은 강아지처럼 다정하게 남자들의 어깨에 머리를 기대고 있었고, 장난스럽게 남자들의 팔 속으로, 심지어 무리 속으로 몸을 맡기며 뒤로 쓰러져갔다. 누군가가 자신들의 낙하를 막아줄 것을 알고 있었기 때문이다. 하지만 아무도 개츠비에게 몸을 맡기며 뒤로 쓰러지지 않았고, 어떤 프렌치 단발머리도 개츠비의 어깨에 닿지 않았으며, 개츠비를 한 고리로 하여 사중창단이 만들어지지도 않았다.

etymology: From extravagant + -ly.
definition_en: Used to describe something that is excessively elaborate or expensive.

senses.gloss: With lavish expenditure or behaviour; in an extravagant manner.
senses.example: Perhaps nowhere else in insectdom is such an extravagantly flamboyant display of systemized pattern on parade.

examples.text: At any rate Cody asked him a few questions (one of them elicited the brand new name) and found that he was quick and extravagantly ambitious.
examples.translation_ko: 어쨌든 코디는 그에게 몇 가지 질문을 했고(그 중 하나가 그 새로운 이름을 끌어냈다), 그가 영리하고 엄청나게 야심적이라는 것을 알게 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They were extravagantly luxurious.
examples.translation_ko: 그것들은 지나칠 정도로 호화로웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English chapitre, from Old French chapitre, from Latin capitulum (“a chapter of a book, in Medieval Latin also a synod or council”), di...
definition_en: A main division of a book or document.

senses.gloss: One of the main sections into which the text of a book is divided.
senses.example: Detective novel writers try to keep up the suspense until the last chapter.

senses.gloss: A section of a work, a collection of works, or fragments of works, often manuscripts or transcriptions, created by scholars or advocates, not the original authors, to aid in finding portions of the texts.
senses.example: While rubrics do not appear in paper manuscripts, eight paper manuscripts contain chapter titles, which serve the same function as the medieval rubrics.

senses.gloss: An assembly of monks, prebendaries and/or other clergymen connected with a cathedral, conventual or collegiate church, or of a diocese, usually presided over by the dean.

examples.text: When I came back they had both disappeared, so I sat down discreetly in the living-room and read a chapter of Simon Called Peter—either it was terrible stuff or the whisky distorted things, because it didn’t make any sense to me.
examples.translation_ko: 돌아와 보니 둘 다 사라져 있어서, 나는 거실에 조심스럽게 앉아 『시몬이라 불린 베드로』를 한 장 읽었다. 그 책이 형편없는 내용이었는지 위스키가 사물을 왜곡시켰는지, 도무지 이해가 되지 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A chapter of my life was closed, and I felt a little nearer to inevitable death.
examples.translation_ko: 내 인생의 한 장이 막을 내렸고, 나는 피할 수 없는 죽음에 조금 더 가까워진 기분이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From graceful + -ly.
definition_en: Moving with elegance and poise.

senses.gloss: In a graceful manner.

examples.text: She yawned gracefully in my face.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 내 얼굴을 향해 우아하게 하품했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her face, thin and not much lined, was of the sort that ages gracefully, so that you thought in youth she must have been a much handsomer woman than in fact she was.
examples.translation_ko: 야위고 주름이 많지 않은 그녀의 얼굴은 우아하게 나이 드는 부류여서, 젊었을 때는 실제보다 훨씬 더 아름다운 여인이었을 거라는 생각이 들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From mode + -ish.
definition_en: Fashionable and up-to-date in style.

senses.gloss: Conforming with fashion or style.
In the current mode.

examples.text: As we crossed Blackwell’s Island a limousine passed us, driven by a white chauffeur, in which sat three modish negroes, two bucks and a girl.
examples.translation_ko: 블랙웰스 섬을 건널 때 백인 운전사가 모는 리무진이 우리를 지나쳤는데, 그 안에는 멋을 낸 흑인 세 명이 타고 있었다. 남자 둘과 여자 하나였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Her hair, not yet very gray, was becomingly arranged, and her black gown was modish.
examples.translation_ko: 아직 그리 희지 않은 머리카락은 보기 좋게 정리되어 있었고, 검은 드레스는 세련되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: to bend one's knees as a sign of respect or submission

senses.gloss: To rest on one's bent knees, sometimes only one; to move to such a position.
To sink down so that the entrance is level with the pavement, making it easier for passengers to enter.
To cause to kneel.
senses.example: She knelt the doll to fit it into the box.

examples.text: The other car, the one going toward New York, came to rest a hundred yards beyond, and its driver hurried back to where Myrtle Wilson, her life violently extinguished, knelt in the road and mingled her thick dark blood with the dust.
examples.translation_ko: 뉴욕 쪽으로 가던 다른 차는 백 야드쯤 더 가서 멈춰 섰고, 운전자는 서둘러 되돌아와 생명이 처참하게 꺼진 머틀 윌슨이 길바닥에 무릎을 꿇고 진한 검은 피를 먼지와 뒤섞고 있는 곳으로 달려왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Their eyes rested on a nude woman suckling a baby, while a girl was kneeling by their side holding out a flower to the indifferent child.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 시선은 아기에게 젖을 먹이는 나체 여인에게 머물렀는데, 한 소녀가 그들 곁에 무릎을 꿇고 무관심한 아이에게 꽃을 내밀고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From impressive + -ly.
definition_en: Used to describe something that is impressive or of high quality.

senses.gloss: In an impressive manner; forcibly.
senses.example: The words written on the animal were next repeated impressively, and if the dog began to bark, it was a sign that the lover would gain his objective.

examples.text: He touched his head impressively, and I nodded.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 인상적으로 자신의 머리를 만지작거렸고, 나는 고개를 끄덕였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “The mills of God grind slowly, but they grind exceeding small,” he said, somewhat impressively.
examples.translation_ko: "신의 맷돌은 천천히 돌지만, 아주 곱게 간다네." 그가 다소 인상적으로 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From unusual + -ly or un- + usually.
definition_en: In an unusual manner.

senses.gloss: In an unusual manner.
senses.example: She's unusually happy for someone who's just broken her leg.

examples.text: When he came down the steps at last the tanned skin was drawn unusually tight on his face, and his eyes were bright and tired.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 그가 계단을 내려왔을 때 그을린 피부는 얼굴에 유난히 팽팽하게 당겨져 있었고, 눈은 밝으면서도 피로해 보였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He didn’t say any more, but we’ve always been unusually communicative in a reserved way, and I understood that he meant a great deal more than that.
examples.translation_ko: 아버지는 더 이상 말씀하지 않으셨지만, 우리는 늘 절제된 방식으로 유난히 소통이 잘 되는 사이였고, 나는 아버지가 그보다 훨씬 깊은 뜻을 담아 하신 말씀임을 이해했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

definition_en: Alternative spelling of judgment.

senses.gloss: Alternative spelling of judgment.

examples.text: Reserving judgements is a matter of infinite hope.
examples.translation_ko: 판단을 유보한다는 것은 무한한 희망의 문제다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: In consequence, I’m inclined to reserve all judgements, a habit that has opened up many curious natures to me and also made me the victim of not a few veteran bores.
examples.translation_ko: 그 결과 나는 모든 판단을 유보하는 경향이 있는데, 이런 습관 덕분에 많은 기이한 성격의 사람들이 내게 마음을 열었고, 동시에 적지 않은 지긋지긋한 따분한 인물들의 희생양이 되기도 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From un- + mistake + -able.
definition_en: Unique, such that it cannot be mistaken for something else.

senses.gloss: Unique, such that it cannot be mistaken for something else.

examples.text: There was an unmistakable air of natural intimacy about the picture, and anybody would have said that they were conspiring together.
examples.translation_ko: 그 광경에는 자연스러운 친밀감이 분명히 배어 있었고, 누가 봐도 둘이 함께 무언가를 꾸미고 있다고 말했을 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Most of the confidences were unsought—frequently I have feigned sleep, preoccupation, or a hostile levity when I realized by some unmistakable sign that an intimate revelation was quivering on the horizon; for the intimate revelations of young men, or at least the terms in which they express them, are usually plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions.
examples.translation_ko: 대부분의 고백은 내가 원하지 않은 것들이었다—친밀한 폭로가 수평선에서 떨리고 있다는 확실한 징조를 알아챘을 때, 나는 종종 잠든 척, 딴 생각에 빠진 척, 혹은 적대적인 경박함을 가장했다. 젊은 남자들의 친밀한 폭로는, 적어도 그들이 그것을 표현하는 방식은, 대개 표절에 가깝고 명백한 억압으로 인해 흠이 있기 때문이다.

definition_en: A container for arrows, crossbow bolts or darts, such as those fired from a bow, crossbow or blowgun.

senses.example: Arrows were carried in quiver, called also an arrow case, which served for the magazine, arrows for immediate use were worn in the girdle.

senses.gloss: A ready storage location for figurative tools or weapons.
senses.example: He's got lots of sales pitches in his quiver.

senses.gloss: A vulva.

examples.text: The hair in his nostrils quivered slightly, and as he shook his head his eyes filled with tears.
examples.translation_ko: 콧구멍의 털이 살짝 떨렸고, 그가 고개를 흔들자 눈에 눈물이 고였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Most of the confidences were unsought—frequently I have feigned sleep, preoccupation, or a hostile levity when I realized by some unmistakable sign that an intimate revelation was quivering on the horizon; for the intimate revelations of young men, or at least the terms in which they express them, are usually plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions.
examples.translation_ko: 대부분의 고백은 내가 원하지 않은 것들이었다—친밀한 폭로가 수평선에서 떨리고 있다는 확실한 징조를 알아챘을 때, 나는 종종 잠든 척, 딴 생각에 빠진 척, 혹은 적대적인 경박함을 가장했다. 젊은 남자들의 친밀한 폭로는, 적어도 그들이 그것을 표현하는 방식은, 대개 표절에 가깝고 명백한 억압으로 인해 흠이 있기 때문이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: Inherited from Middle English merren, from Old English mierran (“to mar, disturb, confuse; scatter, squander, waste; upset, hinder, obstruct; err”)...
definition_en: To spoil; to ruin; to scathe; to damage.

senses.gloss: To spoil; to ruin; to scathe; to damage.
senses.example: The Court's ability to reinterpret the words in the treaty that do not appeal to it mars its logic, and demeans other words there, most significantly the solemnity of the United States oath.

examples.text: He put his hands in his coat pockets and turned back eagerly to his scrutiny of the house, as though my presence marred the sacredness of the vigil.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 두 손을 코트 주머니에 넣고 열심히 집을 살피는 일로 돌아갔다. 마치 내가 있는 것이 그 신성한 밤샘의 경건함을 해치는 것처럼.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Most of the confidences were unsought—frequently I have feigned sleep, preoccupation, or a hostile levity when I realized by some unmistakable sign that an intimate revelation was quivering on the horizon; for the intimate revelations of young men, or at least the terms in which they express them, are usually plagiaristic and marred by obvious suppressions.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: Borrowed from Latin admissio, admissionis; compare French admission. See admit.
definition_en: The act or practice of admitting.

senses.gloss: The act or practice of admitting.
Permission to enter, or the entrance itself; admittance; entrance; access
senses.example: I request admission for two adults.

senses.gloss: The granting of an argument or position not fully proved; the act of acknowledging something asserted; acknowledgement; concession.

examples.text: And, after boasting this way of my tolerance, I come to the admission that it has a limit.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 이렇게 나의 관용에 대해 자랑한 후에, 나는 그것에도 한계가 있다는 것을 인정하게 된다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Sometimes they came and went without having met Gatsby at all, came for the party with a simplicity of heart that was its own ticket of admission.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 개츠비를 전혀 만나지도 못한 채 왔다 갔다 하기도 했는데, 그 자체가 입장권이 되는 순수한 마음으로 파티에 왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English merssh, from Old English mersċ, merisċ, from Proto-West Germanic *marisk, derived from *mari, equivalent to mere (“sea, body of...
definition_en: An area of low, wet land, often with tall grass or herbaceous plants. (Compare swamp, bog, fen.)

senses.gloss: An area of low, wet land, often with tall grass or herbaceous plants. (Compare swamp, bog, fen.)
senses.example: Many animals live in the marsh.

examples.text: Conduct may be founded on the hard rock or the wet marshes, but after a certain point I don’t care what it’s founded on.
examples.translation_ko: 행동은 단단한 바위 위에 세워질 수도 있고 축축한 늪지 위에 세워질 수도 있지만, 어느 지점을 넘어서면 나는 그것이 무엇 위에 세워졌든 상관하지 않는다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Once more it was pouring, and my irregular lawn, well-shaved by Gatsby’s gardener, abounded in small muddy swamps and prehistoric marshes.
examples.translation_ko: 다시 비가 쏟아지고 있었고, 개츠비의 정원사가 깔끔하게 깎아놓은 내 울퉁불퉁한 잔디밭은 작은 진흙 웅덩이들과 원시시대 늪지들로 가득했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: Inherited from Middle English riotous, from Anglo-Norman riotous; equivalent to riot + -ous.
definition_en: Having the characteristics of a riot.

senses.gloss: Having the characteristics of a riot.
Causing, inciting or taking part in a riot.
Unrestrained and boisterous; degenerate or dissolute.

examples.text: It was on that slender riotous island which extends itself due east of New York—and where there are, among other natural curiosities, two unusual formations of land.
examples.translation_ko: 뉴욕 정동쪽으로 뻗어나간 그 가늘고 떠들썩한 섬에서였는데, 그곳에는 다른 자연의 기이한 것들과 함께 두 개의 특이한 지형이 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When I came back from the East last autumn I felt that I wanted the world to be in uniform and at a sort of moral attention forever; I wanted no more riotous excursions with privileged glimpses into the human heart.
examples.translation_ko: 지난 가을 동부에서 돌아왔을 때 나는 세상이 영원히 제복을 입고 도덕적 차렷 자세를 취하기를 바랐다. 인간의 마음을 특권적으로 엿보는 소란스러운 모험은 더 이상 원하지 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English unbroken, from Old English unġebrocen (“unbroken”), equivalent to un- + broken. Cognate with Dutch ongebroken (“unbroken”), Ger...
definition_en: Whole, not divided into parts.

senses.gloss: Whole, not divided into parts.
senses.example: After the vase had fallen down the flight of stairs we were amazed to find it still unbroken.

senses.gloss: Of a horse, not tamed.
senses.example: There is something majestic about the spirit of an unbroken mustang as it runs wild across the prairie.

senses.gloss: Continuous, without interruption.
senses.example: The team's unbroken winning streak was a record.

examples.text: A waiter knocked and came in with crushed mint and ice but the silence was unbroken by his “thank you” and the soft closing of the door.
examples.translation_ko: 웨이터가 문을 두드리고 들어와 으깬 민트와 얼음을 가져왔지만, 그의 "감사합니다"와 문을 조용히 닫는 소리로도 침묵은 깨지지 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: If personality is an unbroken series of successful gestures, then there was something gorgeous about him, some heightened sensitivity to the promises of life, as if he were related to one of those intricate machines that register earthquakes ten thousand miles away.
examples.translation_ko: 인격이란 것이 성공적인 몸짓들의 끊어지지 않는 연속이라면, 그에게는 뭔가 화려한 면이 있었다. 삶의 약속들에 대한 고조된 감수성이 있었는데, 마치 만 마일 떨어진 곳의 지진을 감지하는 정교한 기계들 중 하나와 연결되어 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: First attested in 1382, with the meaning "causing stillbirth or miscarriage". From Middle English abortif, from Old French abortif, from Latin abor...
definition_en: Produced by abortion; born prematurely and therefore unnatural.

senses.gloss: Produced by abortion; born prematurely and therefore unnatural.
senses.example: an abortive child

senses.gloss: Coming to nothing; failing in its effect. .
senses.example: an abortive attempt

senses.gloss: Imperfectly formed or developed; rudimentary; sterile.
senses.example: an abortive organ

examples.text: His eyes glanced momentarily at me, and his lips parted with an abortive attempt at a laugh.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 시선이 잠깐 나를 향했고, 그의 입술이 웃음을 지으려다 실패한 채 벌어졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: No—Gatsby turned out all right at the end; it is what preyed on Gatsby, what foul dust floated in the wake of his dreams that temporarily closed out my interest in the abortive sorrows and short-winded elations of men.
examples.translation_ko: 아니다. 개츠비는 결국 괜찮았다. 개츠비를 괴롭힌 것, 그의 꿈의 항적에 떠다니던 더러운 먼지가 인간들의 유산된 슬픔과 숨 가쁜 환희에 대한 내 관심을 일시적으로 차단했던 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English actual, actuel (“active”), from Anglo-Norman actuel, actual, and its source Late Latin actuālis (“active, practical”), from Lat...
definition_en: relating to a person's acts or deeds; active, practical

senses.gloss: relating to a person's acts or deeds; active, practical
senses.example: Let your holy and pious intention be actual; that is […] by a special prayer or action, […] given to God.

senses.gloss: Existing in reality, not just potentially; really acted or acting; occurring in fact.
senses.example: the actual cost of goods; the actual case under discussion

senses.gloss: in action at the time being; now existing; current.
senses.example: To my actual feelings it seems incredible that I could ever believe that I believed in Transubstantiation!

examples.text: Sometimes too, he stared around at his possessions in a dazed way, as though in her actual and astounding presence none of it was any longer real.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 그가 자신의 소유물들을 멍한 표정으로 둘러보기도 했는데, 마치 그녀의 실제적이고 놀라운 존재 앞에서는 그 모든 것이 더 이상 현실이 아닌 것처럼 보였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The Carraways are something of a clan, and we have a tradition that we’re descended from the Dukes of Buccleuch, but the actual founder of my line was my grandfather’s brother, who came here in fifty-one, sent a substitute to the Civil War, and started the wholesale hardware business that my father carries on today.
examples.translation_ko: 캐러웨이 가문은 일종의 씨족이고, 우리는 버클루 공작의 후손이라는 전통을 가지고 있지만, 우리 혈통의 실제 창시자는 할아버지의 형으로, 1851년에 이곳에 와서 남북전쟁에 대리인을 보내고 아버지가 오늘날까지 이어가고 있는 철물 도매업을 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

definition_en: The brother or brother-in-law of one’s parent.

senses.gloss: The brother or brother-in-law of one’s parent.
The male cousin of one’s parent.
Used as a fictive kinship title for a close male friend of one's parent or parents.

examples.text: All my aunts and uncles talked it over as if they were choosing a prep school for me, and finally said, “Why—ye-es,” with very grave, hesitant faces.
examples.translation_ko: 모든 숙모와 숙부들이 마치 내게 맞는 예비학교를 고르듯 상의를 했고, 마침내 매우 진지하고 망설이는 표정으로 "음—그래"라고 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I never saw this great-uncle, but I’m supposed to look like him—with special reference to the rather hard-boiled painting that hangs in father’s office.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이 큰아버지를 본 적이 없지만, 그를 닮았다고 여겨진다. 특히 아버지 사무실에 걸린 다소 딱딱한 초상화를 기준으로 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English *special, especial, especiall, from Old French especial (whence also French spécial), from Latin speciālis (from speciēs). In t...
definition_en: Distinguished by a unique, particular, or unusual quality.

senses.gloss: Distinguished by a unique, particular, or unusual quality.
senses.example: a special episode of a television series

senses.gloss: Of particular value or interest; dear; beloved.
senses.example: Everyone is special to someone.

senses.gloss: Of or related to unconventional warfare.
senses.example: special forces, special operations

examples.text: Michaelis had seen this too, but it hadn’t occurred to him that there was any special significance in it.
examples.translation_ko: 미카엘리스도 그것을 보았지만, 거기에 특별한 의미가 있다고는 생각하지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I never saw this great-uncle, but I’m supposed to look like him—with special reference to the rather hard-boiled painting that hangs in father’s office.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 이 큰아버지를 본 적이 없지만, 그를 닮았다고 여겨진다. 특히 아버지 사무실에 걸린 다소 딱딱한 초상화를 기준으로 말이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

definition_en: Preparation.

senses.gloss: Preparation.
A preparatory race or workout.
Abbreviation of preposition.

examples.text: One of my most vivid memories is of coming back West from prep school and later from college at Christmas time.
examples.translation_ko: 내 기억 중 가장 생생한 것 중 하나는 크리스마스 때 예비학교에서, 그리고 나중에는 대학에서 서부로 돌아오던 일이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: All my aunts and uncles talked it over as if they were choosing a prep school for me, and finally said, “Why—ye-es,” with very grave, hesitant faces.
examples.translation_ko: 모든 숙모와 숙부들이 마치 내게 맞는 예비학교를 고르듯 상의를 했고, 마침내 매우 진지하고 망설이는 표정으로 "음—그래"라고 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

definition_en: present participle and gerund of commute

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of commute

examples.text: and there was a face I had noticed on the commuting train.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 통근 열차에서 본 적이 있는 얼굴도 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The practical thing was to find rooms in the city, but it was a warm season, and I had just left a country of wide lawns and friendly trees, so when a young man at the office suggested that we take a house together in a commuting town, it sounded like a great idea.
examples.translation_ko: 실용적으로는 시내에서 방을 구하는 것이었지만, 따뜻한 계절이었고 나는 막 넓은 잔디밭과 정다운 나무들이 있는 고향을 떠나온 터라, 사무실의 한 젊은이가 통근 가능한 마을에서 함께 집을 얻자고 제안했을 때 훌륭한 생각처럼 들렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From card + board.
definition_en: A wood-based material resembling heavy paper, used in the manufacture of boxes, cartons and signs.

senses.gloss: A wood-based material resembling heavy paper, used in the manufacture of boxes, cartons and signs.
Something flat or insubstantial.

examples.text: I thought they’d be a nice durable cardboard.
examples.translation_ko: 튼튼한 판지로 만든 줄 알았는데.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He found the house, a weather-beaten cardboard bungalow at eighty a month, but at the last minute the firm ordered him to Washington, and I went out to the country alone.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 집을 구했는데, 월세 80달러짜리 비바람에 낡은 판지 같은 방갈로였다. 하지만 막판에 회사에서 그를 워싱턴으로 발령 내어, 나는 혼자 교외로 나갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Finn + -ish.
definition_en: Of or pertaining to Finland or the Finns; Finlandic, Finlandish.

senses.gloss: Of or pertaining to Finland or the Finns; Finlandic, Finlandish.
Of or pertaining to the Finnish language.

examples.text: I had a dog—at least I had him for a few days until he ran away—and an old Dodge and a Finnish woman, who made my bed and cooked breakfast and muttered Finnish wisdom to herself over the electric stove.
examples.translation_ko: 개 한 마리가 있었다—적어도 며칠간은 있었는데 도망가 버렸다—그리고 낡은 닷지 한 대와 핀란드 여자 한 명이 있었다. 그녀는 내 침대를 정리하고 아침을 해주며 전기레인지 앞에서 핀란드 격언을 혼잣말로 중얼거렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Gatsby looked with vacant eyes through a copy of Clay’s Economics, starting at the Finnish tread that shook the kitchen floor, and peering towards the bleared windows from time to time as if a series of invisible but alarming happenings were taking place outside.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 클레이 경제학 책을 멍하니 들여다보며, 부엌 바닥을 흔드는 핀란드산 발걸음 소리에 놀라고는, 때때로 흐릿한 창문 쪽을 힐끗 보았는데 마치 밖에서 보이지 않지만 불길한 일들이 연달아 벌어지고 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From invest + -ment.
definition_en: The act of investing, or state of being invested.

senses.gloss: The act of investing, or state of being invested.
senses.example: Giving your children a good education is a wise long-term investment.

senses.gloss: A placement of capital in expectation of deriving income or profit from its use or appreciation.
senses.example: An investment in ink, paper, and steel pens.

senses.gloss: A vestment.
senses.example: Whose white investments figure innocence.

examples.text: I took dinner usually at the Yale Club—for some reason it was the gloomiest event of my day—and then I went upstairs to the library and studied investments and securities for a conscientious hour.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 보통 예일 클럽에서 저녁을 먹었는데—어째서인지 그것이 하루 중 가장 우울한 시간이었다—그러고 나서 위층 도서관으로 올라가 성실하게 한 시간 동안 투자와 증권을 공부했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I bought a dozen volumes on banking and credit and investment securities, and they stood on my shelf in red and gold like new money from the mint, promising to unfold the shining secrets that only Midas and Morgan and Maecenas knew.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 은행업과 신용과 투자증권에 관한 책을 열두 권 샀는데, 그것들은 조폐국에서 갓 나온 새 돈처럼 빨갛고 금빛으로 내 책장에 서 있으면서, 오직 미다스와 모건과 마이케나스만이 알고 있던 빛나는 비밀들을 펼쳐 보이겠다고 약속하고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English extenden, from Anglo-Norman extendre, estendre, from Latin extendō (“I stretch out”).
definition_en: To increase in extent.

senses.gloss: To increase in extent.
To possess a certain extent; to cover an amount of space.
senses.example: The desert extended for miles in all directions.

senses.gloss: To cause to increase in extent.

examples.text: It was on that slender riotous island which extends itself due east of New York—and where there are, among other natural curiosities, two unusual formations of land.
examples.translation_ko: 뉴욕 정동쪽으로 뻗어나간 그 가늘고 떠들썩한 섬에서였는데, 그곳에는 다른 자연의 기이한 것들과 함께 두 개의 특이한 지형이 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She was extended full length at her end of the divan, completely motionless, and with her chin raised a little, as if she were balancing something on it which was quite likely to fall.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 긴 의자 끝에서 온몸을 쭉 뻗고 완전히 움직이지 않은 채 턱을 조금 들고 있었는데, 마치 떨어지기 쉬운 무언가를 그 위에 균형잡고 있는 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From identic + -al.
definition_en: Bearing full likeness by having precisely the same set of characteristics; indistinguishable.

senses.gloss: Bearing full likeness by having precisely the same set of characteristics; indistinguishable.
senses.example: The zygote soon divides into two identical cells.

senses.gloss: Not different or other; not another or others; not different as regards self; selfsame; numerically identical.
senses.example: Nor could I myself look upon this man without some emotion, for he seemed to be the identical person who had picked up the ragged tunic in the lonely wood, and, as a matter of fact, he was!

senses.gloss: Of twins, sharing the same genetic code.

examples.text: They were never quite the same ones in physical person, but they were so identical one with another that it inevitably seemed they had been there before.
examples.translation_ko: 육체적으로는 결코 똑같은 사람들이 아니었지만, 서로 너무나 똑같아서 필연적으로 전에도 여기 왔던 것 같았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From disappoint + -ment.
definition_en: The feeling or state of being disappointed: a feeling of sadness or frustration when something is not as good as one hoped or expected, or when something bad unexpectedly happens.

senses.gloss: The feeling or state of being disappointed: a feeling of sadness or frustration when something is not as good as one hoped or expected, or when something bad unexpectedly happens.
senses.example: Even a trip to beautiful California can cause disappointment.

senses.gloss: An example or the act of disappointing: a circumstance in which a positive expectation is not achieved.
senses.example: The disappointment with our trip to California caused bickering.

senses.gloss: Something or someone that disappoints: that which causes disappointment.
senses.example: Even a trip to beautiful California can be a disappointment.

examples.text: “No, it’s not exactly a police dog,” said the man with disappointment in his voice.
examples.translation_ko: "네, 정확히 경찰견은 아니에요." 남자가 실망한 목소리로 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I had talked with him perhaps half a dozen times in the past month and found, to my disappointment, that he had little to say.
examples.translation_ko: 지난 한 달 동안 그와 대여섯 번 정도 이야기를 나누었는데, 실망스럽게도 그는 할 말이 별로 없다는 것을 알았다.

definition_en: Possessing physical features, behaviors, personality traits or other properties that are mainly attributed to infants and small or cuddly animals; e.g. fair, dainty, round, and soft physical features, disproportionately large eyes and head, playfulness, fragility, helplessness, curiosity or shyness, innocence, affectionate behavior.

senses.gloss: Possessing physical features, behaviors, personality traits or other properties that are mainly attributed to infants and small or cuddly animals; e.g. fair, dainty, round, and soft physical features, disproportionately large eyes and head, playfulness, fragility, helplessness, curiosity or shyness, innocence, affectionate behavior.
senses.example: Our reaction to cute attributes is understood as the way nature ensures mammals care for their young.

senses.gloss: Lovable, charming, attractive or pleasing, especially in a youthful, dainty, quaint or fun-spirited way.
senses.example: Let's go to the mall and look for cute girls.

senses.gloss: Sexually attractive or pleasing; gorgeous.
senses.example: He's got such cute buns.

examples.text: “I think it’s cute,” said Mrs. Wilson enthusiastically.

definition_en: In a haughty manner; with excessive or unwarranted pride.

senses.gloss: In a haughty manner; with excessive or unwarranted pride.
senses.example: He haughtily demanded the best table, even though people looked and wondered who he was.

senses.gloss: To appear again.

etymology: The verb, which is older than the noun, is from Middle English gyngle. Onomatopoeic; compare jangle.
definition_en: The sound of metal or glass clattering against itself.

examples.text: Through this twilight universe Daisy began to move again with the season; suddenly she was again keeping half a dozen dates a day with half a dozen men, and drowsing asleep at dawn with the beads and chiffon of an evening-dress tangled among dying orchids on the floor beside her bed.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The late afternoon sky bloomed in the window for a moment like the blue honey of the Mediterranean—then the shrill voice of Mrs. McKee called me back into the room.
examples.translation_ko: 늦은 오후 하늘이 창가에서 잠깐 지중해의 푸른 꿀처럼 피어올랐다가—맥키 부인의 날카로운 목소리가 나를 다시 방 안으로 불러들였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Latin ianitor (“doorkeeper”).
definition_en: Someone who looks after the maintenance and cleaning of a public building.

senses.gloss: Someone who looks after the maintenance and cleaning of a public building.
A caretaker or custodian; someone who maintains a school building specifically and may serve other administrative roles.
A doorman.

examples.text: Tom rang for the janitor and sent him for some celebrated sandwiches, which were a complete supper in themselves.
examples.translation_ko: 톰은 벨을 눌러 관리인을 불러서 유명한 샌드위치를 가져오라고 시켰는데, 그것만으로도 완전한 저녁식사가 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He stayed there two weeks, dismayed at its ferocious indifference to the drums of his destiny, to destiny itself, and despising the janitor’s work with which he was to pay his way through.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 거기서 이 주간을 머물렀지만, 그의 운명의 북소리에, 운명 그 자체에 대한 대학의 잔혹한 무관심에 실망했고, 학비를 벌기 위해 해야 하는 관리인 일을 혐오했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: Named after its supposed inventor, the Earl of Sandwich (see Sandwich).
definition_en: A dish or foodstuff where at least one piece, but typically two or more pieces, of bread serves as the wrapper or container of some other food.

senses.gloss: A dish or foodstuff where at least one piece, but typically two or more pieces, of bread serves as the wrapper or container of some other food.
senses.example: The most famous place in Copenhagen, Ida Davidsen, has a menu of 190 different kinds of open sandwich.

senses.gloss: Any combination formed by layering one type of material between two layers of some other material.
A layer cake or sandwich cake.
senses.example: […] our local agricultural fair in Warwickshire even has a category for Victoria sandwiches baked by male bakers.

examples.text: Tom rang for the janitor and sent him for some celebrated sandwiches, which were a complete supper in themselves.
examples.translation_ko: 톰은 벨을 눌러 관리인을 불러서 유명한 샌드위치를 가져오라고 시켰는데, 그것만으로도 완전한 저녁식사가 되었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His movements—he was on foot all the time—were afterward traced to Port Roosevelt and then to Gad’s Hill, where he bought a sandwich that he didn’t eat, and a cup of coffee.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 행적은—그는 줄곧 걸어 다녔다—나중에 포트 루즈벨트까지, 그리고 개즈 힐까지 추적되었는데, 그곳에서 그는 먹지도 않은 샌드위치 하나와 커피 한 잔을 샀다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English wacchere, wachere, wacher, equivalent to watch + -er.
definition_en: Someone who observes something closely for professional reasons, such as an analyst or pundit.

senses.gloss: Someone who observes something closely for professional reasons, such as an analyst or pundit.
A political representative aligned with a candidate sent to observe elections to report on irregularities. A scrutineer.
Someone who keeps vigil.

examples.text: It was one of the watchers of the night before who had promised to come back, so he cooked breakfast for three, which he and the other man ate together.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 전날 밤 지켜본 사람들 중 하나로 다시 오겠다고 약속했던 사람이었다. 그래서 그는 세 사람 분의 아침을 준비했고, 자신과 그 다른 사람이 함께 먹었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Yet high over the city our line of yellow windows must have contributed their share of human secrecy to the casual watcher in the darkening streets, and I saw him too, looking up and wondering.
examples.translation_ko: 그러나 도시 높은 곳에 있는 우리의 노란 창문들도 어두워지는 거리의 우연한 구경꾼에게는 인간적인 비밀의 몫을 제공했을 것이고, 나는 그 사람도 보았다, 올려다보며 궁금해하는 모습을.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From in- + exhaustible.
definition_en: Impossible to exhaust; unlimited.

senses.gloss: Impossible to exhaust; unlimited.
senses.example: Henriette and Marie de Mancini, his former inexhaustible themes, seemed to have entirely escaped his memory.

examples.text: I was within and without, simultaneously enchanted and repelled by the inexhaustible variety of life.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 안에 있으면서 동시에 밖에 있었고, 삶의 무궁무진한 다양성에 매혹되면서 동시에 반발감을 느꼈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: It was full of money—that was the inexhaustible charm that rose and fell in it, the jingle of it, the cymbals’ song of it … High in a white palace the king’s daughter, the golden girl …
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 돈으로 가득했다—그 안에서 솟아오르고 가라앉는 무궁무진한 매력, 그것의 짤랑거림, 그것의 심벌즈 노래가 바로 그것이었다 … 하얀 궁전 높은 곳의 왕의 딸, 황금빛 소녀가 …
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From sub- + way.
definition_en: An underground railway, especially for mass transit of people in urban areas.

senses.gloss: An underground railway, especially for mass transit of people in urban areas.
A train that runs on such an underground railway.
senses.example: Just before you leave, the subway comes. You get on. It stops at the next station.

senses.gloss: A rapid transit system, regardless of the elevation of its right of way; a metro system.

examples.text: I was so excited that when I got into a taxi with him I didn’t hardly know I wasn’t getting into a subway train.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 너무 흥분해서 그와 함께 택시에 탔을 때 지하철을 타는 게 아니라는 걸 거의 의식하지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Also from New York were the Chromes and the Backhyssons and the Dennickers and Russel Betty and the Corrigans and the Kellehers and the Dewars and the Scullys and S. W. Belcher and the Smirkes and the young Quinns, divorced now, and Henry L. Palmetto, who killed himself by jumping in front of a subway train in Times Square.
examples.translation_ko: 또한 뉴욕에서는 크롬 가족과 백히슨 가족, 데니커 가족과 러셀 베티, 코리건 가족과 켈레허 가족, 듀어 가족과 스컬리 가족, S. W. 벨처와 스머크 가족, 지금은 이혼한 젊은 퀸 부부, 그리고 타임스 스퀘어에서 지하철 앞으로 뛰어들어 자살한 헨리 L. 팔메토가 왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology:
From Middle English bowe, from Old English boga, Proto-West Germanic *bogō, from Proto-Germanic *bugô.
Cognate with West Frisian bôge, Dutch boog, ...
definition_en: A weapon made of a curved piece of wood or other flexible material whose ends are connected by a string, used for shooting arrows.

senses.gloss: A weapon made of a curved piece of wood or other flexible material whose ends are connected by a string, used for shooting arrows.
A curved bend in a rod or planar surface, or in a linear formation such as a river (see oxbow).
A rod with horsehair (or an artificial substitute) stretched between the ends, used for playing various stringed musical instruments.

translations_zh: 弦樂器的弓 /弦乐器的弓

examples.text: He excused himself with a small bow that included each of us in turn.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 우리 각자를 차례로 포함하는 작은 인사로 양해를 구했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A massage and a wave, and a collar for the dog, and one of those cute little ashtrays where you touch a spring, and a wreath with a black silk bow for mother’s grave that’ll last all summer.
examples.translation_ko: 마사지에 파마, 개 목걸이, 그리고 스프링을 누르면 되는 그 귀여운 재떨이, 엄마 무덤에 놓을 검은 실크 리본 달린 화환도 하나—여름 내내 갈 거야.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology:
From Middle English, back-formation from dazed.
Compare dasask (“to become weary”), with reflexive suffix -sk, Swedish dasa (“lie idly”), and Icela...
definition_en: The state of being dazed

senses.gloss: The state of being dazed
senses.example: He was in a daze.

senses.gloss: A glittering stone.

examples.text: Mr. McKee awoke from his doze and started in a daze toward the door.
examples.translation_ko: 맥키 씨는 졸음에서 깨어나 멍한 상태로 문 쪽으로 걸어갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Sometimes too, he stared around at his possessions in a dazed way, as though in her actual and astounding presence none of it was any longer real.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 그가 자신의 소유물들을 멍한 표정으로 둘러보기도 했는데, 마치 그녀의 실제적이고 놀라운 존재 앞에서는 그 모든 것이 더 이상 현실이 아닌 것처럼 보였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From under- + -wear. Compare Dutch ondergoed, German Unterwäsche, Swedish underkläder.
definition_en: Clothes worn next to the skin, underneath outer clothing.

senses.gloss: Clothes worn next to the skin, underneath outer clothing.
senses.example: Don't scratch and bite, my little bear, you'll soon need bigger underwear.

senses.gloss: Underpants (boxers, briefs, panties, etc) and often bras.

examples.text: … I was standing beside his bed and he was sitting up between the sheets, clad in his underwear, with a great portfolio in his hands.
examples.translation_ko: … 나는 그의 침대 옆에 서 있었고 그는 속옷 차림으로 시트 사이에 앉아 커다란 포트폴리오를 손에 들고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The prolonged and tumultuous argument that ended by herding us into that room eludes me, though I have a sharp physical memory that, in the course of it, my underwear kept climbing like a damp snake around my legs and intermittent beads of sweat raced cool across my back.
examples.translation_ko: 우리를 그 방으로 몰아넣은 길고 소란스러운 논쟁의 내용은 기억나지 않지만, 그 과정에서 내 속옷이 축축한 뱀처럼 다리를 타고 올라왔고 간헐적으로 땀방울이 등을 시원하게 흘러내렸다는 생생한 신체적 기억은 남아 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English moth, moththe, motthe, moght, mohþe, mouȝte, from Old English moþþe, mohþe, mohþa (“any destructive insect larva”), from Proto-...
definition_en: Any flying insect of the order Lepidoptera not in the superfamily Papilionoidea, most species of which are nocturnal and can be distinguished from butterflies by feather-like antennae.

senses.gloss: Any flying insect of the order Lepidoptera not in the superfamily Papilionoidea, most species of which are nocturnal and can be distinguished from butterflies by feather-like antennae.
Anything that gradually and silently eats, consumes, or wastes any other thing.

examples.text: In his blue gardens men and girls came and went like moths among the whisperings and the champagne and the stars.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 푸른 정원에서 남녀들이 속삭임과 샴페인과 별빛 사이로 나방처럼 왔다 갔다 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He had waited five years and bought a mansion where he dispensed starlight to casual moths—so that he could “come over” some afternoon to a stranger’s garden.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 5년을 기다리며 저택을 사서 우연히 찾아든 나방들에게 별빛을 나누어주었다—그저 어느 오후 낯선 이의 정원에 "들를 수" 있기 위해서.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: Abbreviation of extraordinary.
definition_en: Beyond what is due, usual, expected, or necessary; extraneous; additional; supernumerary.

senses.gloss: Beyond what is due, usual, expected, or necessary; extraneous; additional; supernumerary.
senses.example: I don't mind doing some extra work, as long as I get extra pay.

senses.gloss: Extraordinarily good; superior.
Over the top; going beyond what is normal or appropriate, often in a dramatic manner.
senses.example: You unfollowed her for posting cat memes? You're so extra!

examples.text: In this heat every extra gesture was an affront to the common store of life.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 더위에는 조그만 몸짓 하나도 삶의 공동 저장고에 대한 모독이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: And on Mondays eight servants, including an extra gardener, toiled all day with mops and scrubbing-brushes and hammers and garden-shears, repairing the ravages of the night before.
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 월요일마다 정원사 한 명을 추가로 포함해 여덟 명의 하인들이 걸레와 솔과 망치와 정원 가위를 들고 하루 종일 애써서 전날 밤의 참상을 복구했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From cater + -er.
definition_en: A person employed to obtain and maintain the storage of provisions, especially food.

senses.gloss: A person employed to obtain and maintain the storage of provisions, especially food.
senses.example: There is a caterer for the table, whose sleekness of face, rotundity of person, and general air of comfortable well-being, do great honor to the cheer he provides.

senses.gloss: A person or company hired to provide and serve food, usually for a large group and at a location separate from where the food is prepared.
senses.example: Although many hotels work with outside Kosher caterers to provide Kosher services, some have developed their own in-house Kosher catering departments.

examples.text: At least once a fortnight a corps of caterers came down with several hundred feet of canvas and enough coloured lights to make a Christmas tree of Gatsby’s enormous garden.
examples.translation_ko: 적어도 보름에 한 번은 출장 요리사들이 수백 피트의 캔버스와 개츠비의 거대한 정원을 크리스마스트리로 만들 만큼 충분한 색색의 전구를 가지고 내려왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “You’ve dyed your hair since then,” remarked Jordan, and I started, but the girls had moved casually on and her remark was addressed to the premature moon, produced like the supper, no doubt, out of a caterer’s basket.
examples.translation_ko: "그때 이후로 머리를 염색하셨네요," 조던이 말했는데, 나는 깜짝 놀랐지만 소녀들은 이미 무심히 지나가버렸고, 그녀의 말은 마치 만찬처럼 분명 출장업체 바구니에서 나온 듯한 이른 달을 향한 것이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English garnysshen, from Old French garniss-, stem of certain forms of the verb garnir, guarnir, warnir (“to provide, furnish, avert, d...
definition_en: To decorate with ornaments; to adorn; to embellish.

senses.gloss: To decorate with ornaments; to adorn; to embellish.
senses.example: […] the whip […] was garnished with a massive horse’s head of plated metal.

senses.gloss: To ornament with something placed around it.
senses.example: a dish garnished with parsley

senses.gloss: To furnish; to supply.
senses.example: By his spirit he hath garnished the heavens; his hand hath formed the crooked serpent.

examples.text: His bedroom was the simplest room of all—except where the dresser was garnished with a toilet set of pure dull gold.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 침실은 모든 방 중에서 가장 소박했다. 다만 화장대가 순금으로 된 화장 도구 세트로 장식되어 있는 것만 빼고는.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: On buffet tables, garnished with glistening hors-d’oeuvre, spiced baked hams crowded against salads of harlequin designs and pastry pigs and turkeys bewitched to a dark gold.
examples.translation_ko: 반짝이는 오르되브르로 장식된 뷔페 테이블 위에는 향신료를 넣어 구운 햄들이 할리퀸 무늬의 샐러드들과 어깨를 맞대고 있었고, 페이스트리로 만든 돼지와 칠면조들이 짙은 황금빛으로 마법에 걸린 듯 놓여 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

definition_en: Of chief or leading importance; prime, principal.

senses.gloss: Of chief or leading importance; prime, principal.
senses.example: The main office is actually one of the smaller rooms.

senses.gloss: Chief, most important, or principal in extent, size, or strength; consisting of the largest part.
senses.example: main timbers

senses.gloss: Full, sheer, undivided.
senses.example: […] I shall never forget the diabolical sneer which writhed Rashleigh's wayward features, as I was forced from the apartment by the main strength of two of these youthful Titans.

examples.text: In the main hall a bar with a real brass rail was set up, and stocked with gins and liquors and with cordials so long forgotten that most of his female guests were too young to know one from another.
examples.translation_ko: 메인 홀에는 진짜 황동 난간이 달린 바가 설치되어 있었고, 진과 리큐어, 그리고 너무 오래전에 잊혀진 코디얼들로 가득 채워져 있어서 그의 여성 손님들 대부분은 너무 어려서 하나하나를 구별할 줄도 몰랐다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A rope stretched across the main gate and a policeman by it kept out the curious, but little boys soon discovered that they could enter through my yard, and there were always a few of them clustered open-mouthed about the pool.
examples.translation_ko: 정문에 밧줄이 쳐져 있고 경찰관이 호기심 많은 사람들을 막아섰지만, 소년들은 곧 내 마당을 통해 들어올 수 있다는 것을 알아냈고, 언제나 몇 명씩은 수영장 주변에 입을 벌린 채 모여 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

definition_en: A store of goods ready for sale; inventory.

senses.gloss: A store of goods ready for sale; inventory.
senses.example: We have a stock of televisions on hand.

senses.gloss: A supply of anything, stored until used; especially, such a supply that is ready for use.
senses.example: Lay in a stock of wood for the winter season.

senses.gloss: Railroad rolling stock.
senses.example: The Grand Trunk Railway had just purchased a large order of stock from the American Car and Foundry Company.

examples.text: Up in the city, I tried for a while to list the quotations on an interminable amount of stock, then I fell asleep in my swivel-chair.
examples.translation_ko: 도시에서 나는 한동안 끝없이 많은 주식의 시세를 정리하려 애쓰다가 회전의자에서 잠이 들었다.

examples.translation_ko: 메인 홀에는 진짜 황동 난간이 달린 바가 설치되어 있었고, 진과 리큐어, 그리고 너무 오래전에 잊혀진 코디얼들로 가득 채워져 있어서 그의 여성 손님들 대부분은 너무 어려서 하나하나를 구별할 줄도 몰랐다.

definition_en: A colourless non-aged alcoholic liquor made by distilling fermented grains such as barley, corn, oats or rye with juniper berries; the base for many cocktails.

senses.gloss: A colourless non-aged alcoholic liquor made by distilling fermented grains such as barley, corn, oats or rye with juniper berries; the base for many cocktails.

Drawing the best card or combination of cards.
senses.example: Johnny Chan held jack-nine, and hit gin when a queen-ten-eight board was dealt out.

examples.text: With a reluctant backward glance the well-disciplined child held to her nurse’s hand and was pulled out the door, just as Tom came back, preceding four gin rickeys that clicked full of ice.
examples.translation_ko: 잘 훈육된 아이는 아쉬운 듯 뒤를 돌아보며 유모의 손을 잡고 문 밖으로 끌려나갔는데, 바로 그때 톰이 얼음이 가득 담겨 딸랑거리는 진 리키 네 잔을 앞세우고 돌아왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: In the main hall a bar with a real brass rail was set up, and stocked with gins and liquors and with cordials so long forgotten that most of his female guests were too young to know one from another.
examples.translation_ko: 메인 홀에는 진짜 황동 난간이 달린 바가 설치되어 있었고, 진과 리큐어, 그리고 너무 오래전에 잊혀진 코디얼들로 가득 채워져 있어서 그의 여성 손님들 대부분은 너무 어려서 하나하나를 구별할 줄도 몰랐다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: Borrowed from French saxophone, a combination of the surname of its inventor Adolphe Sax (1814–1894) + -o- + -phone (“something that makes a sound”...
definition_en: A single-reed instrument musical instrument of the woodwind family, usually made of brass and with a distinctive loop bringing the bell upwards.

senses.gloss: A single-reed instrument musical instrument of the woodwind family, usually made of brass and with a distinctive loop bringing the bell upwards.
senses.example: I played the saxophone in high school.

senses.gloss: Someone who plays the saxophone; a saxophonist.
senses.example: The saxophones typically sit behind the flutes in a concert band.

examples.text: All night the saxophones wailed the hopeless comment of the “Beale Street Blues” while a hundred pairs of golden and silver slippers shuffled the shining dust.
examples.translation_ko: 밤새도록 색소폰들이 "빌 스트리트 블루스"의 절망적인 논평을 울부짖는 동안, 수백 켤레의 금색과 은색 슬리퍼들이 반짝이는 먼지를 휘저었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: By seven o’clock the orchestra has arrived, no thin five-piece affair, but a whole pitful of oboes and trombones and saxophones and viols and cornets and piccolos, and low and high drums.
examples.translation_ko: 일곱 시가 되자 오케스트라가 도착했는데, 빈약한 다섯 명짜리 악단이 아니라 오보에와 트롬본과 색소폰과 비올라와 코넷과 피콜로, 그리고 저음과 고음 드럼들로 가득한 완전한 오케스트라였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: Borrowed from French salon (“reception room”), from Middle French, from Italian salone (“large hall”), augmented form of sala (“hall”), from Lombar...
definition_en: A large room, especially one used to receive and entertain guests.

senses.gloss: A large room, especially one used to receive and entertain guests.
A gathering of people for a social or intellectual meeting.
An art gallery or exhibition; especially the Paris salon or autumn salon.

examples.text: “Madame expects you in the salon!”
examples.translation_ko: "부인께서 응접실에서 기다리고 계십니다!"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The last swimmers have come in from the beach now and are dressing upstairs; the cars from New York are parked five deep in the drive, and already the halls and salons and verandas are gaudy with primary colours, and hair bobbed in strange new ways, and shawls beyond the dreams of Castile.
examples.translation_ko: 마지막 수영객들이 이제 해변에서 올라와 위층에서 옷을 갈아입고 있었고, 뉴욕에서 온 자동차들이 진입로에 다섯 줄로 주차되어 있었으며, 이미 홀과 살롱과 베란다는 원색들과 기이하고 새로운 방식으로 자른 단발머리, 그리고 카스티야의 꿈을 뛰어넘는 숄들로 화려하게 물들어 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English bobben (“to strike, beat, shake, jog”), of uncertain origin. Compare Scots bob (“to mark, dance with a bobbing motion”), Icelan...
definition_en: To move gently and vertically, in either a single motion or repeatedly up and down, at or near the surface of a body of water, or similar medium.

senses.gloss: To move gently and vertically, in either a single motion or repeatedly up and down, at or near the surface of a body of water, or similar medium.
senses.example: The cork bobbed gently in the calm water.

senses.gloss: To move (something) as though it were bobbing in water.
senses.example: I bobbed my head underwater and saw the goldfish.

senses.gloss: To perform oral sex on someone.
senses.example: She bobbed on his knob.

examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When the “Jazz History of the World” was over, girls were putting their heads on men’s shoulders in a puppyish, convivial way, girls were swooning backward playfully into men’s arms, even into groups, knowing that someone would arrest their falls—but no one swooned backward on Gatsby, and no French bob touched Gatsby’s shoulder, and no singing quartets were formed with Gatsby’s head for one link.
examples.translation_ko: "재즈 세계사"가 끝나자, 여자들은 강아지처럼 다정하게 남자들의 어깨에 머리를 기대고 있었고, 장난스럽게 남자들의 팔 속으로, 심지어 무리 속으로 몸을 맡기며 뒤로 쓰러져갔다. 누군가가 자신들의 낙하를 막아줄 것을 알고 있었기 때문이다. 하지만 아무도 개츠비에게 몸을 맡기며 뒤로 쓰러지지 않았고, 어떤 프렌치 단발머리도 개츠비의 어깨에 닿지 않았으며, 개츠비를 한 고리로 하여 사중창단이 만들어지지도 않았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English round, rounde, from Old Northern French roünt, rund, Old French ront, runt, reont ( > French rond), from both Late Latin retund...
definition_en: Circular or cylindrical; having a circular cross-section in one direction.

senses.gloss: Circular or cylindrical; having a circular cross-section in one direction.
senses.example: We sat at a round table to make conversation easier.

senses.gloss: Spherical; shaped like a ball; having a circular cross-section in more than one direction.
senses.example: The ancient Egyptian demonstrated that the Earth is round, not flat.

senses.gloss: Loosely or approximately circular.
senses.example: a round face, a round belly

examples.text: At her first big golf tournament there was a row that nearly reached the newspapers—a suggestion that she had moved her ball from a bad lie in the semifinal round.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 첫 번째 큰 골프 토너먼트에서 신문에 실릴 뻔한 소동이 있었다—준결승전에서 그녀가 불리한 위치에서 공을 옮겼다는 의혹이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The bar is in full swing, and floating rounds of cocktails permeate the garden outside, until the air is alive with chatter and laughter, and casual innuendo and introductions forgotten on the spot, and enthusiastic meetings between women who never knew each other’s names.
examples.translation_ko: 바는 한창 붐비고 있었고, 칵테일을 든 무리들이 바깥 정원으로 떠다니며 스며들어, 공기는 수다와 웃음소리, 그리고 무심한 풍자와 그 자리에서 잊혀지는 소개, 서로의 이름도 모르는 여자들 사이의 열광적인 만남으로 살아 숨쉬고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From the Latin innuendō (“by nodding”), ablative singular form of innuendum (“a nodding”), gerund of innuō (“I give a nod”).
definition_en: A derogatory hint or reference to, or (often sexual) insinuation about, a person or thing.

senses.gloss: A derogatory hint or reference to, or (often sexual) insinuation about, a person or thing.
senses.example: She made a devious innuendo about her opponent, who was embarrassed.

senses.gloss: A remark that is suggestive of something sexual without stating it explicitly.
senses.example: This is kalaburi, a joking banter that includes stories, jokes, wordplays (puns and double entendres, which are often sexual), and playful innuendo.

senses.gloss: A rhetorical device with an omitted, but obvious conclusion, made to increase the force of an argument.

examples.text: There were three married couples and Jordan’s escort, a persistent undergraduate given to violent innuendo, and obviously under the impression that sooner or later Jordan was going to yield him up her person to a greater or lesser degree.
examples.translation_ko: 세 쌍의 부부와 조던의 에스코트가 있었는데, 그는 격렬한 빈정거림을 일삼는 끈질긴 대학생으로, 조던이 조만간 어느 정도든 자신에게 몸을 맡길 것이라고 확신하고 있는 것 같았다.

etymology: From Middle English picche, piche, pich, from Old English piċ, from Proto-West Germanic *pik, from Latin pix. Cognate with Ancient Greek πίσσα (pís...
definition_en: A sticky, gummy substance secreted by trees; sap.

senses.gloss: A sticky, gummy substance secreted by trees; sap.
senses.example: It is hard to get this pitch off my hand.

senses.gloss: A dark, extremely viscous material still remaining after distilling crude oil and tar.
senses.example: They put pitch on the mast to protect it.

senses.gloss: Pitchstone.

examples.text: He had been full of the idea so long, dreamed it right through to the end, waited with his teeth set, so to speak, at an inconceivable pitch of intensity.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 너무 오랫동안 그 생각에 사로잡혀 있었고, 끝까지 꿈꿔왔으며, 말하자면 상상할 수 없을 만큼 강렬한 긴장 속에서 이를 악물고 기다려왔던 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The lights grow brighter as the earth lurches away from the sun, and now the orchestra is playing yellow cocktail music, and the opera of voices pitches a key higher.
examples.translation_ko: 지구가 태양으로부터 멀어져 가면서 불빛들은 더욱 밝아졌고, 이제 오케스트라는 노란 칵테일 음악을 연주하고 있었으며, 목소리들의 오페라는 한 음계 더 높아졌다.

etymology: Recorded since c. 1374 (displacing Old English toliesan) as Middle English dissolven, from Latin dissolvere (“to loosen up, break apart”) but with ...
definition_en: To terminate a union of multiple members actively, as by disbanding.

senses.gloss: To terminate a union of multiple members actively, as by disbanding.
senses.example: The ruling party or coalition sometimes dissolves parliament early when the polls are favorable, hoping to reconvene with a larger majority.

senses.gloss: To destroy, make disappear.
To liquify, melt into a fluid.
senses.example: as if the world were all dissolved to tears

examples.text: Standing behind him, Michaelis saw with a shock that he was looking at the eyes of Doctor T. J. Eckleburg, which had just emerged, pale and enormous, from the dissolving night.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 뒤에 서 있던 미카엘리스는 충격을 받으며 그가 T. J. 에클버그 박사의 눈을 바라보고 있다는 것을 알았다. 그 눈은 사라져가는 밤으로부터 창백하고 거대하게 막 떠오른 참이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The groups change more swiftly, swell with new arrivals, dissolve and form in the same breath; already there are wanderers, confident girls who weave here and there among the stouter and more stable, become for a sharp, joyous moment the centre of a group, and then, excited with triumph, glide on through the sea-change of faces and voices and colour under the constantly changing light.
examples.translation_ko: 무리들은 더욱 빠르게 변화하고, 새로 도착한 사람들로 부풀어 오르고, 해체되었다가 같은 숨결 안에서 다시 형성되었다. 이미 방랑자들이 있었는데, 자신만만한 소녀들이 더 든든하고 안정적인 사람들 사이를 이리저리 누비며, 날카롭고 즐거운 순간 동안 무리의 중심이 되었다가, 승리에 들뜬 채 끊임없이 변하는 빛 아래서 얼굴과 목소리와 색채의 바다 같은 변화 속을 미끄러져 나아갔다.

definition_en: To move softly, smoothly, or effortlessly.

senses.gloss: To move softly, smoothly, or effortlessly.
senses.example: But it was 37-year-old Giggs who looked like a care-free teenager as he glided across the pitch he knows so well to breathtaking effect.

senses.gloss: To fly unpowered, as of an aircraft. Also relates to gliding birds and flying fish.
senses.example: The tide was out, and we drew up amid the strong bracing smell of seaweed, with gulls screeching, wheeling around, and gliding on the wind.

senses.gloss: To cause to glide.

examples.text: A new world, material without being real, where poor ghosts, breathing dreams like air, drifted fortuitously about … like that ashen, fantastic figure gliding toward him through the amorphous trees.
examples.translation_ko: 새로운 세상, 실재하지 않으면서도 물질적인 세상에서 불쌍한 유령들이 공기처럼 꿈을 들이마시며 우연히 떠돌아다녔다... 무정형의 나무들 사이로 그를 향해 미끄러져 오는 저 잿빛의 환상적인 형체처럼.

etymology: From Middle English leder, ledere, from Old English lǣdere (“leader”), from Proto-West Germanic *laidijārī (“leader”), equivalent to lead + -er. Co...
definition_en: One who goes first.

senses.gloss: One who goes first.
senses.example: Follow the leader.

senses.gloss: One having authority to direct.
senses.example: We elected her team leader.

senses.gloss: One who leads a political party or group of elected party members; sometimes used in titles.
senses.example: Senate Majority Leader

examples.text: There was the boom of a bass drum, and the voice of the orchestra leader rang out suddenly above the echolalia of the garden.
examples.translation_ko: 베이스 드럼이 쿵 울렸고, 오케스트라 지휘자의 목소리가 정원의 메아리 속에서 갑자기 높이 울려 퍼졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A momentary hush; the orchestra leader varies his rhythm obligingly for her, and there is a burst of chatter as the erroneous news goes around that she is Gilda Gray’s understudy from the Follies.
examples.translation_ko: 순간적인 정적이 흘렀다. 오케스트라 지휘자가 그녀를 위해 친절하게 리듬을 바꿔주자, 그녀가 폴리스의 길다 그레이 대역이라는 잘못된 소문이 돌면서 수다소리가 터져 나왔다.

etymology: From Middle English formel, borrowed from Old French formel, from Latin fōrmālis, from fōrma (“form”); equivalent to form + -al.
definition_en: Being in accord with established forms.

senses.gloss: Being in accord with established forms.
senses.example: She spoke formal English, without any dialect.

senses.gloss: Official.
senses.example: I'd like to make a formal complaint.

senses.gloss: Relating to the form or structure of something.
senses.example: Formal linguistics ignores the vocabulary of languages and focuses solely on their grammar.

examples.text: A sudden emptiness seemed to flow now from the windows and the great doors, endowing with complete isolation the figure of the host, who stood on the porch, his hand up in a formal gesture of farewell.
examples.translation_ko: 갑작스러운 공허함이 창문들과 커다란 문들로부터 흘러나오는 듯했고, 현관에 서서 격식을 갖춘 작별 인사로 손을 들고 있는 주인의 모습을 완전한 고립 속에 가두어놓았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: A chauffeur in a uniform of robin’s-egg blue crossed my lawn early that Saturday morning with a surprisingly formal note from his employer: the honour would be entirely Gatsby’s, it said, if I would attend his “little party” that night.
examples.translation_ko: 그 토요일 아침 일찍, 로빈의 알 빛깔 파란 제복을 입은 운전사가 고용주로부터 온 놀랍도록 격식을 갖춘 편지를 들고 내 잔디밭을 가로질러 왔다. 그날 밤 그의 "작은 파티"에 참석해준다면 영광은 전적으로 개츠비의 것이라고 적혀 있었다.

senses.gloss: A native or inhabitant of Germany; a person of German citizenship or nationality.
A member of the Germanic ethnic group which is the most populous ethnic group in Germany; a person of German descent.
A member of a Germanic tribe.
senses.example: Rome was sacked by Germans and the Western Roman Empire collapsed.

examples.text: “I don’t think it’s so much that,” argued Lucille sceptically; “It’s more that he was a German spy during the war.”
examples.translation_ko: "그런 건 아닌 것 같아요." 루실이 회의적으로 반박했다. "전쟁 중에 독일 스파이였다는 게 더 맞을 거예요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We stayed there two days and two nights, a hundred and thirty men with sixteen Lewis guns, and when the infantry came up at last they found the insignia of three German divisions among the piles of dead.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 거기서 이틀 밤낮을 버텼어. 백삼십 명의 병사와 열여섯 정의 루이스 기관총으로 말이야. 마침내 보병들이 올라왔을 때 그들은 시체 더미 사이에서 독일군 세 개 사단의 휘장을 발견했어.

definition_en: Having a small width; not wide; having opposite edges or sides that are close, especially by comparison to length or depth.

senses.gloss: Having a small width; not wide; having opposite edges or sides that are close, especially by comparison to length or depth.
senses.example: a narrow hallway

senses.gloss: Of little extent; very limited; circumscribed.
senses.example: The Jews were but a small nation, and confined to a narrow compass in the world.

senses.gloss: Restrictive; without flexibility or latitude.
senses.example: a narrow interpretation

examples.text: She narrowed her eyes and shivered.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 눈을 가늘게 뜨고 몸을 떨었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His eyes narrowed and his mouth widened slightly with the ghost of a superior “Hm!”
examples.translation_ko: 그의 눈이 가늘어지고 입가에 우월감이 서린 "흠!" 하는 표정의 흔적과 함께 입술이 살짝 벌어졌다.

etymology:
PIE word
 *tréyes
Inherited from Middle English testimonie, from Old French testimonie, from Latin testimōnium (“testimony”).
definition_en: Statements made by a witness in court.

senses.gloss: Statements made by a witness in court.

senses.gloss: To buy up wholesale, especially to buy the whole supply of (a commodity etc.).
To monopolize; to concentrate (something) in the single possession of someone, especially unfairly.
senses.example: Octavian then engrosses for himself proconsular powers for ten years in all the provinces where more than one legion was stationed, giving him effective control of the army

examples.text: They were so engrossed in each other that she didn’t see me until I was five feet away.
examples.translation_ko: 두 사람은 서로에게 너무 빠져 있어서 내가 5피트 거리까지 다가갔는데도 그녀는 나를 보지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: So engrossed was she that she had no consciousness of being observed, and one emotion after another crept into her face like objects into a slowly developing picture.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 너무나 몰입해 있어서 누군가 자신을 지켜보고 있다는 것을 전혀 의식하지 못했고, 천천히 현상되는 사진 속으로 사물들이 나타나듯 하나씩 하나씩 감정들이 그녀의 얼굴에 스며들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From unexpected + -ly or un- + expectedly.
definition_en: In an unexpected manner.

senses.gloss: In an unexpected manner.
senses.example: Other evidence of former ownerships such as notice-boards, number plates, and makers' plates, are often discovered unexpectedly.

examples.text: “Hello, Jordan,” she called unexpectedly.
examples.translation_ko: "안녕, 조던." 그녀가 뜻밖에 불렀다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Mr. Sloane didn’t enter into the conversation, but lounged back haughtily in his chair; the woman said nothing either—until unexpectedly, after two highballs, she became cordial.
examples.translation_ko: 슬론 씨는 대화에 끼어들지 않고 의자에 거만하게 기대어 앉아 있었고, 그 여자 역시 아무 말이 없었다—하지만 뜻밖에도 하이볼 두 잔을 마신 후 다정해졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English hire, hyre, here, hure, from Old English hȳr (“employment for wages; pay for service; interest on money lent”), from Proto-West...
definition_en: A person who has been hired, especially in a cohort.

senses.gloss: A person who has been hired, especially in a cohort.
senses.example: We pair up each of our new hires with one of our original hires.

senses.gloss: The state of being hired, or having a job; employment.
senses.example: When my grandfather retired, he had over twenty mechanics in his hire.

senses.gloss: Payment for the temporary use of something.
senses.example: The sign offered pedalos on hire.

examples.text: The notion originated with Daisy’s suggestion that we hire five bathrooms and take cold baths, and then assumed more tangible form as “a place to have a mint julep.”
examples.translation_ko: 이 생각은 데이지가 욕실 다섯 개를 빌려서 찬물로 목욕을 하자고 제안한 데서 시작되었다가, "민트 줄렙을 마실 장소"라는 좀 더 구체적인 형태로 발전했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He came down with a hundred people in four private cars, and hired a whole floor of the Muhlbach Hotel, and the day before the wedding he gave her a string of pearls valued at three hundred and fifty thousand dollars.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 네 대의 전용 열차에 백 명의 사람들을 데리고 내려와서 뮐바흐 호텔의 한 층 전체를 빌렸고, 결혼식 전날에는 35만 달러 상당의 진주 목걸이를 그녀에게 선물했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English valew, value, from Old French value, feminine past participle of valoir, from Latin valēre (“be strong, be worth”), from Proto-...
definition_en: The quality that renders something desirable or valuable; worth.

senses.gloss: The quality that renders something desirable or valuable; worth.
senses.example: There is tremendous value in a good education.

senses.gloss: The degree of importance given to something.
senses.example: The value of my children's happiness is second only to that of my wife.

senses.gloss: That which is valued or highly esteemed, such as one's morals, morality, or belief system.
senses.example: family values

examples.text: It excited him, too, that many men had already loved Daisy—it increased her value in his eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 많은 남자들이 이미 데이지를 사랑했다는 사실 또한 그를 흥분시켰다—그것은 그의 눈에 그녀의 가치를 높여주었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He came down with a hundred people in four private cars, and hired a whole floor of the Muhlbach Hotel, and the day before the wedding he gave her a string of pearls valued at three hundred and fifty thousand dollars.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 네 대의 전용 열차에 백 명의 사람들을 데리고 내려와서 뮐바흐 호텔의 한 층 전체를 빌렸고, 결혼식 전날에는 35만 달러 상당의 진주 목걸이를 그녀에게 선물했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English gropien, from Old English grāpian, related to grīpan (whence English gripe); compare also grip.
definition_en: To feel with or use the hands; to handle.

senses.gloss: To feel with or use the hands; to handle.

To search or attempt to find something in the dark, or, as a blind person, by feeling; to move about hesitatingly, as in darkness or obscurity; to feel one's way, as with the hands, when one can not see.
senses.example: Through the darkest sky, groping for the light / Like crying for the moon / Never-ending black, forgot what I want / Never felt that hard to me

senses.gloss: To touch (another person) closely and (especially) sexually.
senses.example: The parents found the couple kissing and groping.

examples.text: “Sit down, Daisy,” Tom’s voice groped unsuccessfully for the paternal note.
examples.translation_ko: "앉아, 데이지." 톰의 목소리가 부성적인 어조를 찾으려 했지만 성공하지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She groped around in a wastebasket she had with her on the bed and pulled out the string of pearls.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 침대 위에 가져다 놓은 휴지통을 더듬거리며 진주 목걸이를 꺼냈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

definition_en: simple past and past participle of fascinate

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of fascinate

examples.text: It was touching to see them together—it made you laugh in a hushed, fascinated way.
examples.translation_ko: 그들이 함께 있는 모습을 보는 것은 감동적이었다—숨을 죽이고 매혹된 채로 웃음이 나오게 만드는 그런 광경이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Gatsby stood in the centre of the crimson carpet and gazed around with fascinated eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 진홍색 카펫 한가운데 서서 매혹된 눈으로 주위를 둘러보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

definition_en: A pavilion or portable lodge consisting of skins, canvas, or some strong cloth, stretched and sustained by poles, used for sheltering people from the weather.

senses.gloss: A pavilion or portable lodge consisting of skins, canvas, or some strong cloth, stretched and sustained by poles, used for sheltering people from the weather.
senses.example: We were camping in a three-man tent.

senses.gloss: The representation of a tent used as a bearing.
A portable pulpit set up outside to accommodate worshippers who cannot fit into a church.
senses.example: A splendid tent was erected on the brae north of the town, and round that the countless congregation assembled.

examples.text: At night when you’re asleep Into your tent I’ll creep—”
examples.translation_ko: 밤에 당신이 잠들면 당신의 텐트로 살금살금 들어가리—"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But what gave it an air of breathless intensity, was that Daisy lived there—it was as casual a thing to her as his tent out at camp was to him.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 그 집에 숨 막히는 강렬함을 부여한 것은 데이지가 그곳에 살고 있다는 사실이었다—그것은 그에게 캠프의 텐트가 그런 것처럼 그녀에게는 자연스러운 일이었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From French coïncidence. By surface analysis, coincide + -ence.
definition_en: Of objects, the property of being coincident; occurring at the same time or place.

senses.gloss: Of objects, the property of being coincident; occurring at the same time or place.
Of events, the appearance of a meaningful connection when there is none.
senses.example: That the two writers were born and died on the same day is just a coincidence, although there are many conspiracy theories about it.

senses.gloss: A coincidence point.

examples.text: “But it wasn’t a coincidence at all.”
examples.translation_ko: "하지만 전혀 우연이 아니었어요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “It was a strange coincidence,” I said.
examples.translation_ko: "이상한 우연의 일치군요." 내가 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English barryer, barrere, barryȝer, from Old French barriere (compare French barrière), from Old French barre (“bar”).
definition_en: A structure that bars passage.

senses.gloss: A structure that bars passage.
senses.example: The bus went through a railway barrier and was hit by a train.

senses.gloss: An obstacle or impediment.
senses.example: Even a small fee can be a barrier for some students.

senses.gloss: A boundary or limit.
senses.example: Few marathon runners break the three-hour time barrier.

examples.text: Flushed with his impassioned gibberish, he saw himself standing alone on the last barrier of civilization.
examples.translation_ko: 자신의 격정적인 헛소리에 상기되어, 그는 자신이 문명의 마지막 보루에 홀로 서 있다고 여겼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: We passed a barrier of dark trees, and then the façade of Fifty-Ninth Street, a block of delicate pale light, beamed down into the park.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 어두운 나무들의 장벽을 지나쳤고, 그러자 59번가의 정면이, 섬세하고 창백한 빛의 한 구획이 공원 아래로 환하게 비쳐 내렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From un- + real.
definition_en: Not real or substantial; having no actual presence in reality; lacking the characteristics of reality.

senses.gloss: Not real or substantial; having no actual presence in reality; lacking the characteristics of reality.
senses.example: "The Boy's Uncle made me Real," he said. "That was a great many years ago; but once you are Real you can't become unreal again. It lasts for always."

senses.gloss: very impressive; amazing; unbelievable; incredible; larger or more fantastic than typical of real life.
senses.example: The video includes unreal footage of an eight-metre wave.

examples.text: Tom and Daisy stared, with that peculiarly unreal feeling that accompanies the recognition of a hitherto ghostly celebrity of the movies.
examples.translation_ko: 톰과 데이지는 지금까지 영화 속에서만 유령처럼 존재했던 유명인을 실제로 마주했을 때 느끼는 그 특유의 비현실적인 감정과 함께 그를 바라보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Two o’clock and the whole corner of the peninsula was blazing with light, which fell unreal on the shrubbery and made thin elongating glints upon the roadside wires.
examples.translation_ko: 두 시가 되자 반도의 모퉁이 전체가 빛으로 타오르고 있었는데, 그 빛은 관목들 위로 비현실적으로 내려앉아 길가의 전선들에 가늘고 긴 반짝임을 만들어냈다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology:
Late Middle English, from Low German fummeln, fommeln, fammeln (German fummeln), or Dutch fommelen.
Or, perhaps from a Scandinavian/North Germanic ...
definition_en: To handle nervously or awkwardly.

senses.gloss: To handle nervously or awkwardly.
senses.example: Waiting for the interview, he fumbled with his tie.

senses.gloss: To grope awkwardly in trying to find something
senses.example: He fumbled for his keys.

senses.gloss: To blunder uncertainly.
senses.example: He fumbled through his prepared speech.

examples.text: At least—” He fumbled with a series of beginnings.
examples.translation_ko: 적어도—" 그는 여러 가지 말문을 더듬었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He fumbled at the embroidered coverlet, trying to take it from the bed, and lay down stiffly—was instantly asleep.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 수놓인 침대보를 더듬거리며 침대에서 떼어내려 하다가 뻣뻣하게 누웠고, 곧바로 잠이 들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From sog + -y.
definition_en: Soaked with moisture or other liquid.

senses.gloss: Soaked with moisture or other liquid.
senses.example: "Although we ended up soaked, the feeling of what we achieved and the calories we burned more than made up for soggy hair and clothes. [...]."

examples.text: As we started through the gate into the cemetery I heard a car stop and then the sound of someone splashing after us over the soggy ground.
examples.translation_ko: 묘지 문을 통과해 들어가기 시작할 때 차 한 대가 멈춰 서는 소리가 들렸고, 이어서 누군가 질척한 땅을 첨벙거리며 우리를 따라오는 소리가 들렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: This reminded me that I had forgotten to tell my Finn to come back, so I drove into West Egg Village to search for her among soggy whitewashed alleys and to buy some cups and lemons and flowers.
examples.translation_ko: 그제야 핀란드 여자에게 돌아오라고 말하는 것을 깜빡했다는 생각이 들어서, 웨스트에그 마을로 차를 몰고 가서 축축한 회칠한 골목들 사이에서 그녀를 찾고 컵과 레몬과 꽃을 사왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From nervous + -ly.
definition_en: In a nervous manner; feeling or displaying nervousness.

senses.gloss: In a nervous manner; feeling or displaying nervousness.
senses.example: He paced nervously as he waited for the important phone call.

examples.text: and he must have heard me, for he went on nervously:
examples.translation_ko: 그가 내 소리를 들었음에 틀림없었다. 그는 신경질적으로 말을 이어갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: An hour later the front door opened nervously, and Gatsby in a white flannel suit, silver shirt, and gold-coloured tie, hurried in.
examples.translation_ko: 한 시간 후 현관문이 조심스럽게 열리더니, 흰 플란넬 정장에 은색 셔츠, 금색 넥타이를 맨 개츠비가 서둘러 들어왔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From scrutiny + -ize.
definition_en: To examine something with great care or detail, as to look for hidden or obscure flaws.

senses.gloss: To examine something with great care or detail, as to look for hidden or obscure flaws.
senses.example: to scrutinize the conduct or motives of individuals

senses.gloss: To audit accounts etc in order to verify them.

examples.text: Together we scrutinized the twelve lemon cakes from the delicatessen shop.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 함께 델리카트슨에서 가져온 레몬 케이크 열두 개를 자세히 살펴보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: But when I’d shouted “hello” several times in vain, an argument broke out behind a partition, and presently a lovely Jewess appeared at an interior door and scrutinized me with black hostile eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 내가 "안녕하세요"라고 몇 번 소리쳐도 대답이 없자, 칸막이 뒤에서 말다툼이 벌어졌고, 곧 아름다운 유대인 여성이 안쪽 문에 나타나 검고 적대적인 눈으로 나를 살펴보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From hollow + -ly.
definition_en: in a hollow manner

senses.gloss: in a hollow manner

examples.text: and he added hollowly, “… old sport.”
examples.translation_ko: 그리고 그는 공허하게 덧붙였다. "…형씨."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “I do leave it alone,” affirmed the accused hollowly.
examples.translation_ko: "나는 내버려두고 있어요." 비난받은 여자가 공허하게 단언했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: The noun is from Middle English mist, from Old English mist (“mist; darkness; dimness (of eyesight)”), from Proto-Germanic *mihstaz (“mist, fog”), ...
definition_en: Water or other liquid finely suspended in air. (Compare fog, haze.)

senses.gloss: Water or other liquid finely suspended in air. (Compare fog, haze.)
senses.example: It was difficult to see through the morning mist.

senses.gloss: A layer of fine droplets or particles.
senses.example: There was an oily mist on the lens.

senses.gloss: Anything that dims, darkens, or hinders vision.
senses.example: Alas, I do not have the strength to continue writing. Already, mist veils my eyes.

examples.text: “If it wasn’t for the mist we could see your home across the bay,” said Gatsby.
examples.translation_ko: "안개만 없다면 만 건너편에 있는 당신 집이 보일 텐데요." 개츠비가 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The rain cooled about half-past three to a damp mist, through which occasional thin drops swam like dew.
examples.translation_ko: 세 시 반쯤 되어 비는 그쳤고 축축한 안개가 내렸는데, 그 사이로 가느다란 빗방울들이 이슬처럼 떠다녔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English dew, from Old English dēaw (“dew”), from Proto-West Germanic *dauw, from Proto-Germanic *dawwaz, *dawwą (“dew, moisture”), from...
definition_en: Any moisture from the atmosphere condensed by cool bodies upon their surfaces.

senses.gloss: Any moisture from the atmosphere condensed by cool bodies upon their surfaces.
Moisture in the air that settles on plants, etc in the morning or evening, resulting in drops.
senses.example: Tree don't care what the little bird sings / We go down with the dew in the morning light / The tree don't know what the little bird brings / We go down with the dew in the morning

senses.gloss: An instance of such moisture settling on plants, etc.
senses.example: There was a heavy dew this morning.

examples.text: The rain cooled about half-past three to a damp mist, through which occasional thin drops swam like dew.
examples.translation_ko: 세 시 반쯤 되어 비는 그쳤고 축축한 안개가 내렸는데, 그 사이로 가느다란 빗방울들이 이슬처럼 떠다녔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The shadow of a tree fell abruptly across the dew and ghostly birds began to sing among the blue leaves.
examples.translation_ko: 나무 그림자가 이슬 위로 갑자기 떨어지고 유령 같은 새들이 푸른 잎사귀 사이에서 노래하기 시작했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald
