definition_en: A flammable liquid consisting of a mixture of refined petroleum hydrocarbons, mainly used as a motor fuel; petrol.

senses.gloss: A flammable liquid consisting of a mixture of refined petroleum hydrocarbons, mainly used as a motor fuel; petrol.
senses.example: You can't put gasoline in this car. This car takes diesel fuel.

senses.gloss: Any specific kind of this fuel.
senses.example: He was trying to invent a cleaner-burning gasoline.

senses.gloss: Marijuana, especially very potent or of high quality.

examples.text: “Does the gasoline affect his nose?”
examples.translation_ko: "휘발유 때문에 코가 그런 건가?"
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Then as Doctor T. J. Eckleburg’s faded eyes came into sight down the road, I remembered Gatsby’s caution about gasoline.
examples.translation_ko: 길 아래로 T. J. 에클버그 박사의 바랜 눈이 시야에 들어오자, 나는 개츠비가 휘발유에 대해 주의를 준 것이 생각났다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From mantel + piece.
definition_en: A shelf that is affixed to the wall above a fireplace.

senses.gloss: A shelf that is affixed to the wall above a fireplace.
senses.example: The medium was leaning with her elbow on the mantel piece, austere and aloof.

examples.text: Gatsby, his hands still in his pockets, was reclining against the mantelpiece in a strained counterfeit of perfect ease, even of boredom.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비는 두 손을 주머니에 넣은 채 벽난로 선반에 기대어 있었는데, 완벽한 여유로움, 아니 지루함까지 가장하려 애쓰는 모습이 어색했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: His head leaned back so far that it rested against the face of a defunct mantelpiece clock, and from this position his distraught eyes stared down at Daisy, who was sitting, frightened but graceful, on the edge of a stiff chair.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 머리는 너무 뒤로 젖혀져 고장 난 벽난로 시계 면에 닿아 있었고, 그 자세에서 그의 당황한 눈이 데이지를 내려다보고 있었다. 데이지는 딱딱한 의자 끝에 겁에 질렸지만 우아하게 앉아 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From lucky + -ly.
definition_en: In a lucky manner; by good fortune; fortunately.

senses.gloss: In a lucky manner; by good fortune; fortunately.
senses.example: They luckily escaped injury.

examples.text: “You’re just embarrassed, that’s all,” and luckily I added: “Daisy’s embarrassed too.”

definition_en: The direction towards the pole to the right-hand side of someone facing east, specifically 180°, or (on another celestial object) the direction towards the pole lying on the southern side of the invariable plane.

senses.gloss: The direction towards the pole to the right-hand side of someone facing east, specifically 180°, or (on another celestial object) the direction towards the pole lying on the southern side of the invariable plane.
senses.example: Germany is south of Denmark.

senses.gloss: The southern region or area; the inhabitants thereof.
senses.example: When Nimeiri ended that autonomy in 1983, the south took up arms. This Second Sudanese Civil War ended only after four years of formal talks […]

senses.gloss: In a church: the direction to the right-hand side of a person facing the altar.
senses.example: It was moved from its original location in 1507 hardly a decade after it was completed, to the bottom of the liturgical south aisle along with the free-standing chapel of the relic of the lance.

examples.text: “You follow me to the south side of Central Park, in front of the Plaza.”
examples.translation_ko: "센트럴 파크 남쪽, 플라자 호텔 앞으로 따라와."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: For over a year he had been beating his way along the south shore of Lake Superior as a clam-digger and a salmon-fisher or in any other capacity that brought him food and bed.
examples.translation_ko: 일 년이 넘도록 그는 슈피리어 호수 남쪽 연안을 따라 조개 캐는 일꾼이나 연어잡이 어부로, 혹은 먹을 것과 잠자리를 구할 수 있는 어떤 일이든 하며 떠돌아다녔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English brace, from Old French brace (“arm”), from Latin bracchia, the nominative and accusative plural of bracchium (“arm”).
definition_en: Armor for the arm; vambrace.

senses.gloss: Armor for the arm; vambrace.
A measurement of length, originally representing a person's outstretched arms.
A curved instrument or handle of iron or wood, for holding and turning bits, etc.; a bitstock.
senses.example: a brace and bit

examples.text: His brown, hardening body lived naturally through the half-fierce, half-lazy work of the bracing days.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 갈색으로 단단해진 몸은 상쾌한 나날의 반은 격렬하고 반은 나른한 일을 통해 자연스럽게 살아갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: When we pulled out into the winter night and the real snow, our snow, began to stretch out beside us and twinkle against the windows, and the dim lights of small Wisconsin stations moved by, a sharp wild brace came suddenly into the air.
examples.translation_ko: 우리가 겨울밤 속으로 달려 나가자 진짜 눈이, 우리의 눈이 우리 곁으로 뻗어나가기 시작하며 창문에 반짝였고, 위스콘신의 작은 역들의 희미한 불빛들이 지나쳐 갔을 때, 날카롭고 거친 상쾌함이 갑자기 공기 속으로 스며들었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English destine et al., from Old French destinee, from Latin dēstinō (English destine). Displaced Old English wyrd.
definition_en: That to which any person or thing is destined; a predetermined state; a condition predestined by the Divine or by human will.

senses.gloss: That to which any person or thing is destined; a predetermined state; a condition predestined by the Divine or by human will.
senses.example: Death is the destiny of all mortal men.

senses.gloss: That which is inevitable in the fullness of time.
senses.example: Ain't no use to fight it / Don't tamper with my destiny / Any way you slice it / I'm in the hands of fate, you see

senses.gloss: One's eventual fate (not necessarily inevitable or predestined).
senses.example: Everywhere the atom bombs are dropping / It's the end of all humanity / No more time for last-minute shopping / It's time to face your final destiny

examples.text: He had been coasting along all too hospitable shores for five years when he turned up as James Gatz’s destiny in Little Girl Bay.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 5년 동안 지나치게 호의적인 해안들을 따라 항해하다가 리틀 걸 만에서 제임스 개츠의 운명으로 나타났다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He stayed there two weeks, dismayed at its ferocious indifference to the drums of his destiny, to destiny itself, and despising the janitor’s work with which he was to pay his way through.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 거기서 이 주간을 머물렀지만, 그의 운명의 북소리에, 운명 그 자체에 대한 대학의 잔혹한 무관심에 실망했고, 학비를 벌기 위해 해야 하는 관리인 일을 혐오했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From contingent + -cy (16th century).
definition_en: The quality of being contingent, of happening by chance.

senses.gloss: The quality of being contingent, of happening by chance.
A possibility; something which may or may not happen. A chance occurrence, especially in finance, unexpected expenses.
senses.example: There was also the imperative necessity of creating a reserve fund for unforeseen contingencies, and the question ever present was how was money to be found.

senses.gloss: An amount of money which a party to a contract has to pay to the other party (usually the supplier of a major project to the client) if he or she does not fulfill the contract according to the specification.

examples.text: The immediate contingency overtook him, pulled him back from the edge of theoretical abyss.
examples.translation_ko: 당면한 현실이 그를 덮쳤고, 이론적 심연의 가장자리에서 그를 끌어당겼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: He was employed in a vague personal capacity—while he remained with Cody he was in turn steward, mate, skipper, secretary, and even jailor, for Dan Cody sober knew what lavish doings Dan Cody drunk might soon be about, and he provided for such contingencies by reposing more and more trust in Gatsby.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 애매한 개인적 자격으로 고용되었다—코디와 함께 있는 동안 그는 번갈아 가며 사환, 항해사, 선장, 비서, 심지어 간수 역할까지 했는데, 술에 취하지 않은 댄 코디는 술에 취한 댄 코디가 곧 어떤 방탕한 짓을 벌일지 알고 있었고, 그런 상황에 대비해 개츠비에게 점점 더 많은 신뢰를 맡겼다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: Borrowed from Latin continens, noun use of present participle of continēre (“to contain”).
definition_en: One of the main continuous landmasses, separated by water or geological features, on the surface of a planet, sometimes including its continental shelves and the islands on them.

senses.gloss: One of the main continuous landmasses, separated by water or geological features, on the surface of a planet, sometimes including its continental shelves and the islands on them.
senses.example:
But I should turn mine ears and hear
The moanings of the homeless sea,
⁠The sound of streams that swift or slow
⁠Draw down Æonian hills, and sow
The dust of continents to be; […]

senses.gloss: Each of the traditional main regions into which the Earth’s land surface is divided, including both an extent of mainland and various conventionally associated islands, etc; namely, Africa, Europe, Asia, Australasia/Oceania, North America, South America, and Antarctica.
A large contiguous landmass as opposed to its islands, peninsulas, and so forth; mainland. Also specifically, the Old World continent of Europe–Asia–Africa: see the Continent.
senses.example: No man is an Iland, intire of it ſelfe; euery man is a peece of the Continent, a part of the maine; […]

examples.text: The arrangement lasted five years, during which the boat went three times around the Continent.
examples.translation_ko: 이런 관계는 5년간 지속되었고, 그 동안 배는 대륙을 세 번 돌았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Its vanished trees, the trees that had made way for Gatsby’s house, had once pandered in whispers to the last and greatest of all human dreams; for a transitory enchanted moment man must have held his breath in the presence of this continent, compelled into an aesthetic contemplation he neither understood nor desired, face to face for the last time in history with something commensurate to his capacity for wonder.
examples.translation_ko: 사라진 나무들, 개츠비의 집을 위해 자리를 내준 그 나무들은 한때 인간의 모든 꿈 중에서도 가장 위대하고 마지막인 꿈에 속삭임으로 아첨했었다. 찰나의 황홀한 순간, 인간은 이 대륙 앞에서 숨을 멈췄을 것이다. 자신이 이해하지도 원하지도 않았던 미적 관조에 사로잡힌 채, 역사상 마지막으로 자신의 경이로움을 받아낼 만한 무언가와 마주했던 것이다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English esturne, esterne, from Old English ēasterne (“eastern”), from Proto-Germanic *austrōnijaz (“eastern”), from Proto-Indo-European...
definition_en: Of, facing, situated in, or related to the east.

senses.gloss: Of, facing, situated in, or related to the east.
Blowing from the east; easterly.
Oriental.

examples.text: I see now that this has been a story of the West, after all—Tom and Gatsby, Daisy and Jordan and I, were all Westerners, and perhaps we possessed some deficiency in common which made us subtly unadaptable to Eastern life.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 보니 이것은 결국 서부의 이야기였다—톰과 개츠비, 데이지와 조던 그리고 나, 우리는 모두 서부 사람들이었고, 아마도 우리에게는 동부 생활에 미묘하게 적응하지 못하게 만드는 공통된 결함이 있었던 것 같다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I remember the portrait of him up in Gatsby’s bedroom, a grey, florid man with a hard, empty face—the pioneer debauchee, who during one phase of American life brought back to the Eastern seaboard the savage violence of the frontier brothel and saloon.
examples.translation_ko: 개츠비의 침실에 걸려 있던 그의 초상화가 기억난다. 회색빛에 혈색이 좋은, 딱딱하고 공허한 얼굴을 한 남자—미국 역사의 한 시기 동안 변방 매춘굴과 술집의 야만적 폭력을 동부 해안으로 되가져온 선구적 방탕아였다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Old French, from Italian milione (“million”, from mille (“thousand”, from Latin mille) + -one). Compare -illion.
definition_en: The cardinal number 1 000 000: 10⁶; a thousand thousand.

senses.gloss: The cardinal number 1 000 000: 10⁶; a thousand thousand.
senses.example: Near-synonyms: mega-, M-

senses.gloss: An unspecified very large number.
senses.example: I told you a million times before.

examples.text: He never understood the legal device that was used against him, but what remained of the millions went intact to Ella Kaye.
examples.translation_ko: 그에게 불리하게 사용된 법적 수단이 무엇인지 그는 결코 이해하지 못했지만, 수백만 달러 중 남은 것은 모두 엘라 케이에게 고스란히 돌아갔다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: I don’t mean that he had traded on his phantom millions, but he had deliberately given Daisy a sense of security; he let her believe that he was a person from much the same strata as herself—that he was fully able to take care of her.
examples.translation_ko: 그가 허상의 수백만 달러를 이용했다는 뜻은 아니지만, 그는 의도적으로 데이지에게 안정감을 주었다. 그는 자신이 그녀와 거의 같은 계층의 사람이라고, 그녀를 충분히 돌볼 수 있는 사람이라고 그녀가 믿게 했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle French commocion, from Latin commōtiōnem, accusative singular of commōtiō, from commoveō + -tiō.
definition_en: A state of turbulent motion.

senses.gloss: A state of turbulent motion.
An agitated disturbance or a hubbub.
senses.example: It would seem as if calm were necessary to convulsion; for the tranquillity of the last few months was again to be disturbed by political commotion.

senses.gloss: Sexual excitement.
senses.example: and now, glancing my eyes towards that part of his dress which cover'd the essential object of enjoyment, I plainly discover'd the swell and commotion there

examples.text: “I’ll see if there’s any sign of a commotion.”
examples.translation_ko: "소동의 기미가 있는지 살펴보겠어."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: There were the same people, or at least the same sort of people, the same profusion of champagne, the same many-coloured, many-keyed commotion, but I felt an unpleasantness in the air, a pervading harshness that hadn’t been there before.
examples.translation_ko: 같은 사람들, 아니 적어도 같은 부류의 사람들이 있었고, 샴페인도 똑같이 풍성했으며, 똑같이 화려하고 다채로운 소란이 있었지만, 공기 중에 불쾌함이 느껴졌다. 전에는 없던 거친 기운이 전체를 감싸고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English celebritē, from Old French celebrite (compare French célébrité), from Latin celēbritās.
definition_en: A rite or ceremony.

senses.gloss: A rite or ceremony.
Fame, renown; the state of being famous or talked-about.
A person who has a high degree of recognition by the general population for his or her success or accomplishments; a famous person.

examples.text: “I’ve never met so many celebrities,” Daisy exclaimed.
examples.translation_ko: "이렇게 많은 유명인들을 만나본 적이 없어요." 데이지가 감탄했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: Tom and Daisy stared, with that peculiarly unreal feeling that accompanies the recognition of a hitherto ghostly celebrity of the movies.
examples.translation_ko: 톰과 데이지는 지금까지 영화 속에서만 유령처럼 존재했던 유명인을 실제로 마주했을 때 느끼는 그 특유의 비현실적인 감정과 함께 그를 바라보았다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From genial + -ly.
definition_en: In a genial manner; gaily; cheerfully.

senses.gloss: In a genial manner; gaily; cheerfully.
By genius or nature; naturally.
senses.example: Some men are genially disposed to some opinions.

examples.text: “I read somewhere that the sun’s getting hotter every year,” said Tom genially.
examples.translation_ko: "어디선가 읽었는데 해가 해마다 더 뜨거워지고 있다더군." 톰이 상냥하게 말했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: “Go ahead,” answered Daisy genially, “and if you want to take down any addresses here’s my little gold pencil.”
examples.translation_ko: "그러세요," 데이지가 상냥하게 대답했다, "그리고 주소를 적고 싶으면 여기 내 작은 금연필이 있어요."
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From unsuccessful + -ly or un- + successfully.
definition_en: Not successfully; without success; to no avail.

senses.gloss: Not successfully; without success; to no avail.

examples.text: “Sit down, Daisy,” Tom’s voice groped unsuccessfully for the paternal note.
examples.translation_ko: "앉아, 데이지." 톰의 목소리가 부성적인 어조를 찾으려 했지만 성공하지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: The girl addressed was trying, unsuccessfully, to slump against my shoulder.
examples.translation_ko: 말을 건넨 그 여자는 내 어깨에 몸을 기대려 했지만 성공하지 못했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English herde, heerde, heorde, from Old English hierd, heord (“herd, flock; keeping, care, custody”), from Proto-West Germanic *herdu, ...
definition_en: A number of domestic animals assembled together under the watch or ownership of a keeper.

senses.gloss: A number of domestic animals assembled together under the watch or ownership of a keeper.
senses.example: a herd of cattle

senses.gloss: Any collection of animals gathered or travelling in a company.
senses.example: Zakouma is the last place on Earth where you can see more than a thousand elephants on the move in a single, compact herd.

senses.gloss: A crowd, a mass of people or things; a rabble.
senses.example: You can never interest the common herd in the abstract question.

examples.text: The prolonged and tumultuous argument that ended by herding us into that room eludes me, though I have a sharp physical memory that, in the course of it, my underwear kept climbing like a damp snake around my legs and intermittent beads of sweat raced cool across my back.
examples.translation_ko: 우리를 그 방으로 몰아넣은 길고 소란스러운 논쟁의 내용은 기억나지 않지만, 그 과정에서 내 속옷이 축축한 뱀처럼 다리를 타고 올라왔고 간헐적으로 땀방울이 등을 시원하게 흘러내렸다는 생생한 신체적 기억은 남아 있다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: She was appalled by West Egg, this unprecedented “place” that Broadway had begotten upon a Long Island fishing village—appalled by its raw vigour that chafed under the old euphemisms and by the too obtrusive fate that herded its inhabitants along a shortcut from nothing to nothing.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 웨스트에그에 경악했다. 브로드웨이가 롱아일랜드의 한 어촌 마을에 낳아놓은 이 전례 없는 "장소"에—오래된 완곡어법 아래서 거슬려하는 거친 활력과, 주민들을 무에서 무로 가는 지름길로 몰아가는 지나치게 뻔뻔한 운명에 경악했다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English processioun, borrowed from Old French pourciession, from Latin prōcessiō (“a marching forward, an advance, in Late Latin a reli...
definition_en: The act of progressing or proceeding.

senses.gloss: The act of progressing or proceeding.
senses.example: Yet proof is here of men's unquenched desire / That the procession of their life might be / More equable majestic pure and free; […]

senses.gloss: A group of people or things moving along in an orderly, stately, or solemn manner; a train of persons advancing in order; a retinue.
senses.example: a procession of mourners

senses.gloss: A number of things happening in sequence (in space or in time).

examples.text: Sometimes a shadow moved against a dressing-room blind above, gave way to another shadow, an indefinite procession of shadows, who rouged and powdered in an invisible glass.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 위층 탈의실 블라인드 너머로 그림자가 움직이다가 다른 그림자에게 자리를 내주었고, 보이지 않는 거울 앞에서 연지와 분을 바르는 모호한 그림자들의 행렬이 이어졌다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: About five o’clock our procession of three cars reached the cemetery and stopped in a thick drizzle beside the gate—first a motor hearse, horribly black and wet, then Mr. Gatz and the minister and me in the limousine, and a little later four or five servants and the postman from West Egg, in Gatsby’s station wagon, all wet to the skin.
examples.translation_ko: 다섯 시쯤 되어 세 대의 차로 이루어진 우리 행렬이 묘지에 도착해 문 옆에서 멈춰 섰다. 부슬부슬 내리는 비 속에서—맨 앞에는 끔찍하도록 검고 비에 젖은 영구차가, 그 다음에는 개츠 씨와 목사 그리고 내가 탄 리무진이, 그리고 조금 뒤에는 웨스트에그에서 온 하인 네다섯 명과 우편배달부가 개츠비의 스테이션 왜건을 타고 왔는데, 모두 뼛속까지 젖어 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English pibel (also in pibleston), from Old English papolstān (“pebble-stone”), from Old English *papol, *pyppel, *pæbbel of unknown or...
definition_en: A small stone, especially one rounded by the action of water.

senses.gloss: A small stone, especially one rounded by the action of water.
senses.example:
And trifles for choice matters, worth a sponge;
As children gathering pebbles on the shore.

senses.gloss: A particle from 4 to 64 mm in diameter, following the Wentworth scale.
A small droplet of water intentionally sprayed on the ice that cause irregularities on the surface.

examples.text: The pebbles of the drive crunched under his feet.
examples.translation_ko: 진입로의 자갈이 그의 발걸음에 바스락거렸다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

examples.text: They went upstairs to get ready while we three men stood there shuffling the hot pebbles with our feet.
examples.translation_ko: 그들이 준비하러 위층으로 올라가는 동안 우리 세 남자는 그 자리에 서서 발로 뜨거운 자갈을 비비고 있었다.
examples.author: F. Scott Fitzgerald

etymology: From Middle English furre, forre, from Anglo-Norman forre, fuerre (“a case; sheath”), from Frankish *fōdar, from Proto-West Germanic *fōdr, from Pr...
definition_en: The hairy coat of various mammal species, especially when fine, soft and thick.

senses.gloss: The hairy coat of various mammal species, especially when fine, soft and thick.
The hairy skins of animals used as a material for clothing.
An animal pelt used to make, trim or line clothing.
senses.example: During the colonial period, Britain used Canada as a major source of furs.

examples.text: A breeze stirred the grey haze of Daisy’s fur collar.
examples.translation_ko: 산들바람이 데이지의 회색 털 칼라를 살랑거렸다.

examples.text: I remember the fur coats of the girls returning from Miss This-or-That’s and the chatter of frozen breath and the hands waving overhead as we caught sight of old acquaintances, and the matchings of invitations: “Are you going to the Ordways’?

examples.text: It is a charming faculty, but one often abused by those who are conscious of its possession: for there is something ghoulish in the avidity with which they will pounce upon the misfortune of their friends so that they may exercise their dexterity.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 매력적인 능력이지만, 자신이 그런 능력을 가지고 있다는 것을 의식하는 사람들이 종종 남용하는 것이기도 하다. 친구들의 불행에 탐욕스럽게 달려들어 자신의 솜씨를 발휘하려는 그 열망에는 뭔가 소름끼치는 구석이 있기 때문이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English guschen, gusshen, gosshien, perhaps from Middle Dutch guysen (“to flow out with a gurgling sound, gush”) or Old Norse gusa (“to...
definition_en: To flow or issue suddenly and abundantly.

senses.gloss: A sudden rapid outflow.

examples.text: It gushes forth like an oil-well, and the sympathetic pour out their sympathy with an abandon that is sometimes embarrassing to their victims.
examples.translation_ko: 그것은 유정처럼 솟구쳐 나오고, 동정심 많은 사람들은 때로 피해자들을 당황스럽게 할 정도로 무분별하게 동정을 쏟아낸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bidewen, bideawen; equivalent to be- + dew. Cognate with Dutch bedauwen (“to bedew”), German betauen (“to bedew”).
definition_en: To moisten or sprinkle with dew.

senses.gloss: To make wet with or as if with dew.
senses.example: While sympathetic tears / My cheeks bedew

examples.text: There are bosoms on which so many tears have been shed that I cannot bedew them with mine.
examples.translation_ko: 너무 많은 눈물이 흘러내린 가슴들이 있어서, 나는 그곳에 내 눈물을 더할 수가 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Shortened form of brandywine, from Dutch brandewijn (“burnt wine”). Compare German Brantewein, Branntwein, Danish brændevin.
definition_en: A strong spirit made from fermented fruit juice.

senses.gloss: An alcoholic liquor distilled from wine or fermented fruit juice.
Any variety of brandy.
A glass of brandy.

examples.text: “Milk is very nice, especially with a drop of brandy in it, but the domestic cow is only too glad to be rid of it.
examples.translation_ko: "우유는 아주 좋아요. 특히 브랜디 한 방울 떨어뜨리면 더욱 좋죠. 하지만 집에서 기르는 암소는 그걸 없애버리고 싶어서 안달이에요.

definition_en: A large domesticated mammal often kept on farms for its milk and meat.

senses.gloss: An adult female of the species Bos taurus, especially one that has calved.
senses.example: The whole herd is out to pasture right now — the cows, calves, and heifers are out back, and the bulls are down by the creek.

senses.gloss: Any member of the species Bos taurus regardless of sex or age, including bulls and calves.
senses.example: We saw lots of cows at the farm show, including some surprisingly gigantic bulls.

senses.gloss: Beef: the meat of cattle as food.
senses.example: The only meat I eat is cow.

examples.text: “Milk is very nice, especially with a drop of brandy in it, but the domestic cow is only too glad to be rid of it.

etymology: From Middle English udder, uddyr (also as uther, iddyr), from Old English ūder (“udder; breast”), from Proto-Germanic *ūdarą, from Proto-Indo-Europ...
definition_en: The udder is the organ that produces milk in a female mammal.

senses.gloss: An organ formed of the mammary glands of female quadruped mammals, particularly ruminants such as cattle, goats, sheep and deer.
senses.example: squeeze the udder to get milk

senses.gloss: A woman's breast.

examples.text: A swollen udder is very uncomfortable.”
examples.translation_ko: 부푼 젖통은 아주 불편하거든요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English blister, from Old French blestre, from a Germanic source. Compare Middle Dutch blyster (“swelling”), Old Norse blastr (“a blowi...
definition_en: To form a blister on the skin.

senses.gloss: A small bubble between the layers of the skin that contains watery or bloody fluid and is caused by friction and pressure, burning, freezing, chemical irritation, disease, or infection.
senses.example: Inspect them for rub marks and blisters; tape or bandage rub marks; clean the skin around a blister, use a sterilised needle to puncture it at its outer edge and press out the fluid, then bandage.

senses.gloss: A swelling on a plant.
Something applied to the skin to raise a blister; a vesicatory or other applied medicine.

examples.text: Rose Waterford had a blistering tongue.
examples.translation_ko: 로즈 워터포드는 독설가였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French élégance, from Latin ēlegantia (“exquisiteness; refinement, elegance”).
definition_en: A quality of being refined and stylish.

senses.gloss: Grace, refinement, and beauty in movement, appearance, or manners.
senses.example: The bride was elegance personified.

senses.gloss: Restraint and grace of style.
senses.example: The simple dress had a quiet elegance.

senses.gloss: The beauty of an idea characterized by minimalism and intuitiveness while preserving exactness and precision.
senses.example: The proof of the theorem had a pleasing elegance.

examples.text: She managed her surroundings with elegance.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 주변 환경을 우아하게 꾸며나갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Hindi छींट (chī̃ṭ).
definition_en: A type of printed cotton fabric.

senses.gloss: A painted or stained calico fabric, originally produced in India, and known for its brightly colored designs.
senses.example: The morning air waved to and fro the chintz curtains of a large and, for a London one, a very cheerful-looking room, whose windows opened to the Thames.

examples.text: Her flat was always neat and cheerful, gay with flowers, and the chintzes in the drawing-room, notwithstanding their severe design, were bright and pretty.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 아파트는 언제나 깔끔하고 밝았으며, 꽃들로 화사했고, 응접실의 무늬 있는 면직물들도 엄격한 디자인에도 불구하고 밝고 예뻤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The adjective is derived from Middle English comly, comli, cumly, cumlich (“of a person: beautiful, handsome, etc.; of noble birth, bearing, or cha...
definition_en: Attractive or pleasing to the eye.

senses.gloss: Of a person: attractive or pleasing to look at; beautiful, handsome; also, attractive but not particularly beautiful or handsome.
senses.example: a comely woman

senses.gloss: Of a person, an action, behaviour, etc.: meeting accepted moral or social norms; appropriate, becoming, proper.
senses.example: (A long proceſſion) timely marching home / In comely order to the regal dome.

senses.gloss: Of a thing: beautiful, elegant, well-composed; also, delicate, fine.
senses.example: In ſhootinge at the prickes, haſtye and quicke drawinge is neyther ſure nor yet comely.

examples.text: The meals in the artistic little dining-room were pleasant; the table looked nice, the two maids were trim and comely; the food was well cooked.
examples.translation_ko: 예술적인 작은 식당에서의 식사는 즐거웠다. 식탁은 보기 좋게 차려져 있었고, 두 하녀는 단정하고 예뻤으며, 음식은 잘 요리되어 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From house + keeper.
definition_en: A person responsible for managing and maintaining a household.

senses.gloss: Someone (traditionally a woman) employed to look after the home, typically by managing domestic servants or superintending household management; also someone with equivalent duties in a hotel, institution etc.
senses.example: She was their third housekeeper, but after a month or so she also gave up.

senses.gloss: Someone who manages the running of a home, traditionally the female head of the household.
Someone who keeps to their house; someone who rarely ventures away from home; an unadventurous person, a homebody.
senses.example: I do assure you he is no house-keeper. I have seen him in desperate conflict with savage men, and even with His Majesty's redcoats.

examples.text: It was impossible not to see that Mrs. Strickland was an excellent housekeeper.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드 부인이 훌륭한 주부라는 것을 모를 수가 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The verb is first attested in 1646, the adjective in 1661; borrowed from Latin sēdātus, perfect passive participle of sēdō (“to settle”), see -ate ...
definition_en: Calm and peaceful.

senses.gloss: Remaining composed and dignified, and avoiding too much activity or excitement.
senses.example: Then she saw that they were waving their handkerchiefs; dipping them up and down, with a curiously sedate, formal motion.

senses.gloss: Not overly ornate or showy.
senses.example: The great hotel, with its look of sedate luxury, brooded massively there with people teeming about it.

examples.text: Her hair, thick and dark like her mother’s, fell over her shoulders in fine profusion, and she had the same kindly expression and sedate, untroubled eyes.
examples.translation_ko: 어머니처럼 짙고 검은 머리카락이 어깨 위로 풍성하게 흘러내렸고, 어머니와 같은 친절한 표정과 차분하고 평온한 눈을 하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English blusshen, bluschen, blusschen, blisshen, from Old English blysċan (“to be red; shine”), perhaps from Proto-Germanic *blaskijaną...
definition_en: To become red or flushed in the face due to embarrassment.

senses.gloss: An act of blushing; a pink or red glow on the face caused by embarrassment, shame, shyness, love, etc.
senses.example: It was a sudden revelation, a tinge like a blush which one tried to check and then, as it spread, one yielded to its expansion […]

senses.gloss: A glow; a flush of colour, especially pink or red.
senses.example: Each painting consists of a white aluminum disk, sprayed at the edges with a subtle blush of blue, pink or grey.

senses.gloss: A feeling or appearance of optimism.

examples.text: She smiled, her smile was really very sweet, and she blushed a little; it was singular that a woman of that age should flush so readily.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 미소를 지었는데, 그 미소는 정말로 매우 감미로웠고, 얼굴이 약간 붉어졌다. 그 나이의 여성이 그렇게 쉽게 얼굴을 붉히는 것이 신기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English redily, rediliche. By surface analysis, read(i) + -ly.
definition_en: Available or willing to do something quickly.

senses.gloss: Without unwillingness or hesitation; showing readiness.
senses.example: The suspect readily answered all questions the police officers asked him.

senses.gloss: Without impediment, easily.
senses.example: readily available; readily achievable

examples.text: She smiled, her smile was really very sweet, and she blushed a little; it was singular that a woman of that age should flush so readily.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 미소를 지었는데, 그 미소는 정말로 매우 감미로웠고, 얼굴이 약간 붉어졌다. 그 나이의 여성이 그렇게 쉽게 얼굴을 붉히는 것이 신기했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Innocent and trusting simplicity.

senses.gloss: Alternative spelling of naïveté.

examples.text: Perhaps her naivete was her greatest charm.
examples.translation_ko: 아마도 그녀의 순진함이 가장 큰 매력이었을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The noun is derived from Middle English Philistyne, Philisten [and other forms], from Old English Filistina (genitive plural), from Old French Phil...
definition_en: A person who is uncultured and lacking in refinement.

senses.gloss: A non-Semitic person from ancient Philistia, a region in the southwest Levant in the Middle East.
senses.example: Then the lords of the Philiſtines gathered them together, for to offer a great ſacrifice vnto Dagon their god, and to reioyce; for they ſaid, Our god hath deliuered Samſon our enemy into our hand.

senses.gloss: An opponent (of the speaker, writer, etc); an enemy, a foe.
senses.example: In very truth what could poor old Abbot Hugo do? A frail old man; and the Philistines were upon him,—that is to say, the Hebrews.

senses.gloss: In German universities: a person not associated with the university; a non-academic or non-student; a townsperson.

examples.text: “He’s a perfect philistine.”
examples.translation_ko: "그는 완전한 속물이에요."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From disparaging + -ly.
definition_en: In a way that shows you think someone or something is not good.

senses.gloss: Insultingly.
senses.example: The candidate spoke of his opponent disparagingly.

examples.text: She said this not disparagingly, but affectionately rather, as though, by acknowledging the worst about him, she wished to protect him from the aspersions of her friends.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 이 말을 경멸조로 한 것이 아니라 오히려 애정을 담아 했다. 마치 그의 최악의 면을 인정함으로써 친구들의 비난으로부터 그를 보호하려는 듯했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From affectionate + -ly.
definition_en: Showing or expressing affection.

senses.gloss: In an affectionate manner.
senses.example: Catherine is affectionately known as "Kit Kat" to her friends.

examples.text: She said this not disparagingly, but affectionately rather, as though, by acknowledging the worst about him, she wished to protect him from the aspersions of her friends.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 이 말을 경멸조로 한 것이 아니라 오히려 애정을 담아 했다. 마치 그의 최악의 면을 인정함으로써 친구들의 비난으로부터 그를 보호하려는 듯했다.

etymology: From Latin aspersiōnem, from aspersiō (“sprinkling”).
definition_en: A false or malicious statement that harms someone's reputation.

senses.gloss: An attack on somebody's reputation or good name, often in the phrase to cast aspersions upon….
senses.example: No criminality can be infered or punishment inflicted, but for writing, printing, uttering, or publishing false, scandalous and malicious aspersions against the government.

senses.gloss: A sprinkling, especially of holy water.

examples.text: She said this not disparagingly, but affectionately rather, as though, by acknowledging the worst about him, she wished to protect him from the aspersions of her friends.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 이 말을 경멸조로 한 것이 아니라 오히려 애정을 담아 했다. 마치 그의 최악의 면을 인정함으로써 친구들의 비난으로부터 그를 보호하려는 듯했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English confessioun, from Old French confession, from Latin cōnfessiō, cōnfessiōnem (“confession, acknowledgment, creed or avowal of on...
definition_en: A statement of admission or acknowledgment of a fault or wrongdoing.

senses.gloss: The open admittance of having done something (especially something bad).
senses.example: Without the real murderer's confession, an innocent person could be jailed.

senses.gloss: A formal document providing such an admission.
senses.example: He forced me to sign a confession!

senses.gloss: The disclosure of one's sins to a priest for absolution. In the Roman Catholic Church, it is now also termed the sacrament of reconciliation.
senses.example: I went to confession and now I feel much better about what I had done.

examples.text: She smiled to cover her shyness, and I fancied she had a fear that I would make the sort of gibe that such a confession could hardly have failed to elicit from Rose Waterford.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 수줍음을 감추려고 미소를 지었는데, 나는 그녀가 내가 로즈 워터포드라면 그런 고백을 듣고 틀림없이 했을 법한 조롱을 할까 봐 두려워하는 것 같다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From uncommon + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is not usual or common.

senses.gloss: To an uncommon degree; unusually or extremely.
senses.example: For a gentleman, he was uncommonly rude, but she supposed wearing silk and jade gave him that privilege.

senses.gloss: Not often; on rare occasions.
senses.example: Not uncommonly, I find that I have arrived too late to catch my train.

examples.text: It was a thoroughly dull party from the beginning, but if you will come I shall be uncommonly grateful.
examples.translation_ko: 처음부터 끝까지 지독히 따분한 파티가 될 텐데, 그래도 와주신다면 정말 고맙겠어요.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From neighbour + -ly.
definition_en: Friendly and considerate towards one's neighbors.

senses.gloss: Showing the qualities of a friendly and helpful neighbour.
senses.example: She's so neighbourly that she always holds a welcoming party for new residents.

examples.text: It was only neighbourly to accept.
examples.translation_ko: 이웃 간의 정으로라도 응해야 할 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From facetious + -ness.
definition_en: The quality of being facetious; playful or humorous language.

senses.gloss: The state of being facetious
The product or result of being facetious.

examples.text: Strickland gave the polite little laugh with which people acknowledge a facetiousness in which they see nothing funny, but did not speak.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 전혀 재미있지 않은 농담을 예의상 인정할 때 사람들이 짓는 그런 정중한 웃음을 지었지만, 말은 하지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English spanne, from Old English spann, from Proto-Germanic *spannō (“span, handbreadth”), from Proto-Indo-European *(s)pend- (“to stre...
definition_en: A distance or interval of time between two points.

senses.gloss: The full width of an open hand from the end of the thumb to the end of the little finger used as an informal unit of length.
Any of various traditional units of length approximating this distance, especially the English handspan of 9 inches forming ⅛ fathom and equivalent to 22.86 cm.
A small space or a brief portion of time.
senses.example: He has a short attention span and gets bored within minutes.

examples.text: When at last we were all assembled, waiting for dinner to be announced, I reflected, while I chatted with the woman I had been asked to “take in,” that civilised man practises a strange ingenuity in wasting on tedious exercises the brief span of his life.
examples.translation_ko: 마침내 모든 사람이 모여 저녁 식사 시간이 알려지기를 기다리고 있을 때, 나는 "에스코트"해달라고 부탁받은 여자와 이야기를 나누면서 문명인이라는 존재가 짧은 인생을 지루한 일들로 낭비하는 데 기묘한 재주를 발휘한다는 생각을 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: The top or upper part of something.

examples.text: To avoid the tedium of dining tête-à-tête, to give their servants a rest, because there was no reason to refuse, because they were “owed” a dinner.
examples.translation_ko: 둘만의 지루한 식사를 피하기 위해, 하인들에게 휴식을 주기 위해, 거절할 이유가 없어서, 저녁 식사를 "빚졌기" 때문에.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From inconvenient + -ly.
definition_en: Not conveniently located or situated.

senses.gloss: In an inconvenient manner.

examples.text: The dining-room was inconveniently crowded.
examples.translation_ko: 식당은 불편할 정도로 비좁았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English prosperite, from Old French prosperitet, from Latin prosperitās. Equivalent to prosper + -ity.
definition_en: A state of being successful or flourishing.

senses.gloss: The condition of being prosperous: having good fortune and a fortune.
senses.example: Near-synonym: thriving

examples.text: There was about all of them an air of well-satisfied prosperity.
examples.translation_ko: 그들 모두에게는 만족스러운 번영의 분위기가 감돌았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Used to introduce or lead into a discussion.

senses.gloss: Alternative form of entrée.

examples.text: Each one talked to his neighbour; to his neighbour on the right during the soup, fish, and entree; to his neighbour on the left during the roast, sweet, and savoury.
examples.translation_ko: 각자 옆 사람과 이야기했다. 수프와 생선, 앙트레 요리 때는 오른쪽 옆 사람과, 로스트와 디저트, 짭짤한 요리 때는 왼쪽 옆 사람과 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English rosten, a borrowing from Old French rostir (“to roast, to torture with fire”), from Frankish *rōstijan (“to roast, broil”), fro...
definition_en: A piece of meat cooked over high heat.

senses.gloss: To cook food by heating in an oven or over a fire without covering, resulting in a crisp, possibly even slightly charred appearance.
senses.example: to roast meat on a spit

senses.gloss: To cook by surrounding with hot embers, ashes, sand, etc.
senses.example: to roast a potato in ashes

senses.gloss: To process by drying through exposure to sun or artificial heat.
senses.example: Coffee beans need roasting before use.

examples.text: Each one talked to his neighbour; to his neighbour on the right during the soup, fish, and entree; to his neighbour on the left during the roast, sweet, and savoury.
examples.translation_ko: 각자 옆 사람과 이야기했다. 수프와 생선, 앙트레 요리 때는 오른쪽 옆 사람과, 로스트와 디저트, 짭짤한 요리 때는 왼쪽 옆 사람과 말이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From politic + -al.
definition_en: Relating to the government or politics.

senses.gloss: Concerning or relating to politics, the art and process of governing.
senses.example: Political principles are rarely absolute, as political logic holds an imperfect result by compromise is better than a theoretically perfect abstention from the political process in the opposition.

senses.gloss: Concerning a polity or its administrative components.
senses.example: Good political staff is hard to find, they may neither be ambitious and corrupted by power nor tempted by private sector careers.

senses.gloss: Motivated, especially inappropriately, by political (electoral; or, more generally, power, standing, influence or conflict) calculation.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From petty + -ness.
definition_en: A tendency to be petty or concerned with trivial matters.

senses.gloss: The quality of being petty.
senses.example: The pettiness of the accounting department asking me to save a receipt from a fast-food restaurant was absurd.

senses.gloss: A petty behaviour, attitude, etc.

examples.text: Now I am well aware that pettiness and grandeur, malice and charity, hatred and love, can find place side by side in the same human heart.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 나는 소심함과 위대함, 악의와 자선, 증오와 사랑이 같은 인간의 마음속에 나란히 자리할 수 있다는 것을 잘 알고 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French grandeur, from Old French grandur, from grant (French grand), from Latin grandis (“grown up, great”).
definition_en: A feeling of great pride or admiration.

senses.gloss: The state of being grand or splendid; magnificence.
senses.example: In a tightly choreographed ceremony filled with imperial grandeur, Xi and Putin then walked towards each other and met in the middle, smiling as they shook hands.

senses.gloss: Nobility (state of being noble).
Greatness; largeness; tallness; loftiness.

examples.text: Now I am well aware that pettiness and grandeur, malice and charity, hatred and love, can find place side by side in the same human heart.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 나는 소심함과 위대함, 악의와 자선, 증오와 사랑이 같은 인간의 마음속에 나란히 자리할 수 있다는 것을 잘 알고 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English spiþre, spydyr, spider, spiþer, from Old English spīþra (“spider”), from Proto-West Germanic *spinþrijō, from Proto-Germanic *s...
definition_en: A small, eight-legged arachnid that weaves a web to catch prey.

senses.gloss: Any of various eight-legged, predatory arthropods, of the order Araneae, most of which spin webs to catch prey.
senses.example: Little Miss Muffet, She sat on a tuffet, Eating of curds and whey; There came a little spider, Who sat down beside her, And frighted Miss Muffet away.

senses.gloss: A program which follows links on the World Wide Web in order to gather information.
senses.example: Crawler-based search engines have three major elements. The first is the spider, also called the crawler, which visits a web page, reads it, and then follows links to other pages within the site.

senses.gloss: A float (drink) made by mixing ice-cream and a soda or fizzy drink (such as lemonade).
senses.example: 2002, Katharine Gasparini, Cranberry and vanilla ice cream spider, recipe in Cool Food, page 339.

examples.text: He seems to me to be possessed by some power which is using him for its own ends, and in whose hold he is as helpless as a fly in a spider’s web.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 힘에 사로잡혀 그 힘의 목적을 위해 이용당하고 있는 것 같아요. 거미줄에 걸린 파리처럼 속수무책으로 말이죠.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English webbe, from Old English webb, from Proto-Germanic *wabją, from Proto-Indo-European *webʰ- (“weave”).
definition_en: A network of interconnected pages on the internet.

senses.gloss: The silken structure which a spider builds using silk secreted from the spinnerets at the caudal tip of its abdomen; a spiderweb.
senses.example: The sunlight glistened in the dew on the web.

senses.gloss: Any interconnected set of persons, places, or things, which, when diagrammed, resembles a spider's web.
The part of a baseball mitt between the forefinger and thumb, the webbing.
senses.example: He caught the ball in the web.

examples.text: He seems to me to be possessed by some power which is using him for its own ends, and in whose hold he is as helpless as a fly in a spider’s web.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 힘에 사로잡혀 그 힘의 목적을 위해 이용당하고 있는 것 같아요. 거미줄에 걸린 파리처럼 속수무책으로 말이죠.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From unstable + -ly or un- + stably.
definition_en: Not stable or firm

senses.gloss: In an unstable manner.

examples.text: The soul lives unstably in the body, and is capable of mysterious transformations.
examples.translation_ko: 영혼은 육체 안에서 불안정하게 살아가며, 신비로운 변화를 겪을 수 있는 것이죠.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
Inherited from Middle English transformacioun, from Middle French, from Ecclesiastical Latin trānsfōrmātiō.
Morphologically transform + -ation
definition_en: A change or process of changing something into something different.

senses.gloss: The act of transforming or the state of being transformed.
senses.example: undergo a radical transformation

senses.gloss: A marked change in appearance or character, especially one for the better.

The replacement of the variables in an algebraic expression by their values in terms of another set of variables; a mapping of one space onto another or onto itself; a function that changes the position or direction of the axes of a coordinate system.

examples.text: The soul lives unstably in the body, and is capable of mysterious transformations.
examples.translation_ko: 영혼은 육체 안에서 불안정하게 살아가며, 신비로운 변화를 겪을 수 있는 것이죠.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Hindi बंग्ली (baṅglī, “glass bracelet”).
definition_en: A type of arm or leg jewelry.

senses.gloss: A rigid bracelet or anklet, especially one with no clasp.
senses.example: Mrs. MacAndrew smoothed down the lap of her gown, and gold bangles fell over her wrists.

examples.text: Mrs. MacAndrew smoothed down the lap of her gown, and gold bangles fell over her wrists.
examples.translation_ko: 맥앤드류 부인은 무릎 위의 드레스를 매만졌고, 금팔찌들이 손목 위로 흘러내렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English wrist, from Old English wrist, from Proto-West Germanic *wristu, from Proto-Germanic *wristuz (compare Old Frisian wrist, Low G...
definition_en: The joint connecting the forearm to the hand.

senses.gloss: The complex joint between forearm bones, carpus, and metacarpals where the hand is attached to the arm; the carpus in a narrow sense.
senses.example: With a flick of the wrist, he threw the frisbee to a team-mate.

senses.gloss: A stud or pin which forms a journal.

examples.text: Mrs. MacAndrew smoothed down the lap of her gown, and gold bangles fell over her wrists.
examples.translation_ko: 맥앤드류 부인은 무릎 위의 드레스를 매만졌고, 금팔찌들이 손목 위로 흘러내렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From severe + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate that something is done or experienced to a great degree.

senses.gloss: In a severe manner.
senses.example: Meanwhile the Christian Church from these speculations has kept itself severely apart - as of course representing a unique and divine revelation little concerned or interested in such heathenisms[.]

examples.text: She looked at me severely.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 나를 엄하게 바라보았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From shrewd + -ly.
definition_en: Having or showing a clever and cunning understanding of people and situations.

senses.gloss: In a shrewd manner.

examples.text: She saw shrewdly that the world is quickly bored by the recital of misfortune, and willingly avoids the sight of distress.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 세상이 불행담을 듣는 것을 금세 지겨워하고 고통받는 모습을 기꺼이 외면한다는 것을 예리하게 간파하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From recite + -al.
definition_en: A public performance of music or poetry.

senses.gloss: The act of reciting (the repetition of something that has been memorized); rehearsal
The act of telling the order of events of something in detail the order of events; narration.
That which is recited; a story, narration, account.

examples.text: She saw shrewdly that the world is quickly bored by the recital of misfortune, and willingly avoids the sight of distress.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 세상이 불행담을 듣는 것을 금세 지겨워하고 고통받는 모습을 기꺼이 외면한다는 것을 예리하게 간파하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English misaventure, from Old French mesaventure, equivalent to mis- + adventure.
definition_en: An unfortunate or unexpected event.

senses.gloss: An accidental mishap or misfortune.

examples.text: Whenever she went out—and compassion for her misadventure made her friends eager to entertain her—she bore a demeanour that was perfect.
examples.translation_ko: 외출할 때마다—그녀의 불운에 대한 동정심으로 친구들이 그녀를 대접하려 애썼다—그녀는 완벽한 태도를 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From brazen + -ly.
definition_en: Done with complete disregard for what others think.

senses.gloss: In a brazen (shamelessly shocking and offensive) manner.

examples.text: She was brave, but not too obviously; cheerful, but not brazenly; and she seemed more anxious to listen to the troubles of others than to discuss her own.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 용감했지만 지나치게 티를 내지는 않았고, 명랑했지만 뻔뻔스럽지는 않았으며, 자신의 문제를 논하기보다는 다른 사람들의 고민을 들어주려 애쓰는 것 같았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Derived from Latin contrādictus (“contradicted”), the past participle of contrādīcō (“speak against”) (originally two words).
definition_en: To say or show that something is not true.

senses.gloss: To deny the truth or validity of (a statement or statements).
senses.example: His testimony contradicts hers.

senses.gloss: To oppose (a person) by denying the truth or pertinence of a given statement.
senses.example: Everything he says contradicts me.

senses.gloss: To be contrary to (something).
senses.example:
[…] True indeed it is
That They whom Death has hidden from our sight
Are worthiest of the Mind’s regard; with these
The future cannot contradict the past:

examples.text: “What I mean is, if anyone talks to you about it, please don’t contradict it if they say he eloped with somebody.”
examples.translation_ko: "제 말은, 만약 누군가 당신에게 이 일에 대해 이야기한다면, 그가 누군가와 도망쳤다고 말할 때 부디 부정하지 말아 달라는 뜻입니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Anglo-Norman aloper (“to abduct, run away”), itself borrowed from Proto-West Germanic *andihlaupan (“to run away”). Equivalent to and- + lope ...
definition_en: Run away secretly to get married.

senses.gloss: To run away from home with a paramour.
To run away secretly for the purpose of getting married with one's intended spouse; to marry in a quick or private fashion, especially without a public period of engagement.
senses.example: They knew each other for maybe a month before they eloped in Vegas.

senses.gloss: To run away from home (for any reason).
senses.example: If we'd been a bit quicker, we could have caught Gowan before he eloped

examples.text: “What I mean is, if anyone talks to you about it, please don’t contradict it if they say he eloped with somebody.”
examples.translation_ko: "제 말은, 만약 누군가 당신에게 이 일에 대해 이야기한다면, 그가 누군가와 도망쳤다고 말할 때 부디 부정하지 말아 달라는 뜻입니다."
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French ballet, from Italian balletto (“short dance, ballet”), diminutive form of ballo (“group dance”), from Late Latin ballō (“to da...
definition_en: A classical dance form characterized by elegant movements and precise techniques.

senses.gloss: A classical form of dance.
senses.example: a classically-trained ballet dancer

senses.gloss: A theatrical presentation of such dancing, usually with music, sometimes in the form of a story.
senses.example: Let's go to the ballet in the theatre tomorrow!

senses.gloss: The company of persons who perform this dance.
senses.example: Zara joined the ballet at the age of 14.

examples.text: They said that Charles Strickland had become infatuated with a French dancer, whom he had first seen in the ballet at the Empire, and had accompanied her to Paris.
examples.translation_ko: 사람들은 찰스 스트릭랜드가 엠파이어 극장의 발레에서 처음 본 프랑스 무용수에게 빠져서 그녀와 함께 파리로 갔다고 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English empire, from Old French empire, empere, from Latin imperium, inperium (“command, control, dominion, sovereignty, a dominion, em...
definition_en: A large and powerful state or group of states under a single ruler.

senses.gloss: A political state, often a monarchy, that has achieved a much greater current size than its initial size by conquering surrounding territories, cities or nations.
senses.example: the Russian empire

senses.gloss: A political unit ruled by an emperor or empress.
senses.example: The Empire of Vietnam was a short-lived client state of Japan governing Vietnam between March 11 and August 23, 1945.

senses.gloss: The group of states or other territories that owe allegiance to an imperial power (foreign to them), when distinguished from the native territory of that power; imperial possessions.
senses.example: Since Britain imported mainly foodstuffs from its empire, no preferences could be granted to the colonies without Britain first imposing a tariff on foodstuffs imported from other countries.

examples.text: They said that Charles Strickland had become infatuated with a French dancer, whom he had first seen in the ballet at the Empire, and had accompanied her to Paris.
examples.translation_ko: 사람들은 찰스 스트릭랜드가 엠파이어 극장의 발레에서 처음 본 프랑스 무용수에게 빠져서 그녀와 함께 파리로 갔다고 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin exaggerātus, perfect passive participle of exaggerō (“to heap up, increase, enlarge, magnify, amplify, exaggerate”) (see -ate (...
definition_en: To make or represent something as more serious or important than it really is.

senses.gloss: To overstate, to describe more than the fact.
senses.example: I've told you a billion times not to exaggerate!

examples.text: Colonel MacAndrew had not exaggerated when he said she would be penniless, and it was necessary for her to earn her own living as quickly as she could.
examples.translation_ko: 맥앤드류 대령이 그녀가 무일푼이 될 것이라고 말했을 때 과장한 것이 아니었고, 그녀로서는 가능한 한 빨리 스스로 생계를 꾸려나가야 했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The noun is derived from short + hand (“handwriting; style of penmanship”). The verb is derived from the noun.
definition_en: A written representation of spoken language using abbreviations and symbols.

senses.gloss: A rough and rapid method of writing by substituting symbols for letters, words, etc.
senses.example: Right away you say that nobody learns how to read shorthand. People who want to know shorthand learn how to write it; the reading of it comes by the way.

senses.gloss: Any brief or shortened way of saying or doing something.
senses.example: The jargon becomes a shorthand for these advanced concepts.

examples.text: She made up her mind to profit by her acquaintance with so many writers, and without loss of time began to learn shorthand and typewriting.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그토록 많은 작가들과 아는 사이라는 점을 활용하기로 마음먹고, 시간을 허비하지 않고 속기와 타이핑을 배우기 시작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Back-formation from typewriter.
definition_en: Write using a typewriter.

senses.gloss: To type using a typewriter.

examples.text: She made up her mind to profit by her acquaintance with so many writers, and without loss of time began to learn shorthand and typewriting.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그토록 많은 작가들과 아는 사이라는 점을 활용하기로 마음먹고, 시간을 허비하지 않고 속기와 타이핑을 배우기 시작했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From type + -ist.
definition_en: A person whose job is to type documents or texts.

senses.gloss: A person who types, a clerical worker who writes letters, etc., using a typewriter.

examples.text: Her education made it likely that she would be a typist more efficient than the average, and her story made her claims appealing.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 교육 배경으로 보아 평균보다 유능한 타이피스트가 될 가능성이 높았고, 그녀의 사연은 그녀의 요청을 호소력 있게 만들었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English theires, attested since the 1300s. Equivalent to their + -s (compare -'s); formed by analogy to his. Displaced theirn (from Mid...
definition_en: Belonging to them.

senses.gloss: That or those belonging to them; the possessive case of they, used without a following noun.
senses.example: This luggage is theirs. These passports are also theirs.

senses.gloss: Their house or home.
senses.example: Let's go over to theirs.

examples.text: Her friends promised to send her work, and took care to recommend her to all theirs.
examples.translation_ko: 친구들은 그녀에게 일을 보내주겠다고 약속했고, 자신들의 모든 지인에게도 그녀를 추천해주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English childles; equivalent to child + -less.
definition_en: Having no children.

senses.gloss: Not having any children.
senses.example: I am a lone wolf, a solitary man, wandering through a world in which I have no part. I am wifeless—childless—who is it speaks of the childless as the dead twigs on the tree of life?

examples.text: The MacAndrews, who were childless and in easy circumstances, arranged to undertake the care of the children, and Mrs. Strickland had only herself to provide for.
examples.translation_ko: 자식이 없고 형편이 넉넉한 맥앤드류 부부가 아이들을 돌보기로 했고, 스트릭랜드 부인은 자신만 부양하면 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English undertaken; equivalent to under- + take (after undernim).
definition_en: Take on a task or responsibility.

senses.gloss: To take upon oneself; to start, to embark on (a specific task etc.).
senses.example:
This said, he sat; and expectation held
His look suspense, awaiting who appeared
To second, or oppose, or undertake
The perilous attempt.

senses.gloss: To commit oneself (to an obligation, activity etc.).
senses.example: He undertook to exercise more in future.

senses.gloss: To pass a slower moving vehicle on the curbside rather than on the side closest to oncoming traffic.

examples.text: The MacAndrews, who were childless and in easy circumstances, arranged to undertake the care of the children, and Mrs. Strickland had only herself to provide for.
examples.translation_ko: 자식이 없고 형편이 넉넉한 맥앤드류 부부가 아이들을 돌보기로 했고, 스트릭랜드 부인은 자신만 부양하면 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From uneventful + -ness.
definition_en: The state of being uneventful.

senses.gloss: The quality of being uneventful.
senses.example: But maybe the uneventfulness was merely par for the course.

examples.text: My friends pursued their course with uneventfulness; they had no longer any surprises for me, and when I met them I knew pretty well what they would say; even their love-affairs had a tedious banality.
examples.translation_ko: 내 친구들은 평온하게 자신들의 길을 걸어갔다. 그들에게서 더 이상 놀랄 만한 것은 없었고, 만날 때마다 그들이 무슨 말을 할지 거의 알 수 있었다. 심지어 그들의 연애사조차 지루할 만큼 뻔했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Learned borrowing from Latin terminus (“boundary, limit”). Doublet of term, Terminus, and termon.
definition_en: To bring or come to an end.

senses.gloss: The end or final point of something.
The end point of a transportation system, or the town or city in which it is located.
senses.example: Wuhan is the terminus for cruises to the Yanzi^([sic – meaning Yangtze]) River gorges.

senses.gloss: A boundary or border, or a post or stone marking such a boundary.

examples.text: We were like tram-cars running on their lines from terminus to terminus, and it was possible to calculate within small limits the number of passengers they would carry.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 종점에서 종점까지 정해진 노선을 달리는 전차 같았고, 얼마나 많은 승객을 태울지도 어느 정도 계산할 수 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French correct, from Latin correctus (“improved, amended, correct”), past participle of corrigere, conrigere (“to make straight, make...
definition_en: To make or become accurate.

senses.gloss: Free from error; true; accurate.
senses.example: Your test was completely correct, you get 10 out of 10

senses.gloss: With good manners; well behaved; conforming with accepted standards of behaviour.

examples.text: She had made a success of her business, and now had an office in Chancery Lane; she did little typing herself, but spent her time correcting the work of the four girls she employed.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 사업에 성공해서 이제 챈서리 레인에 사무실을 두고 있었다. 타이핑은 거의 직접 하지 않고, 고용한 네 명의 여직원들이 한 일을 교정하는 데 시간을 보냈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From dainty + -ness.
definition_en: Delicacy or refinement of movement.

senses.gloss: The characteristic of being dainty.
A dainty behaviour or gesture.

examples.text: She had had the idea of giving it a certain daintiness, and she made much use of blue and red inks; she bound the copy in coarse paper, that looked vaguely like watered silk, in various pale colours; and she had acquired a reputation for neatness and accuracy.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 일에 어떤 우아함을 부여한다는 아이디어를 갖고 있어서 파란색과 빨간색 잉크를 많이 사용했고, 물결무늬 비단처럼 보이는 거친 종이로 원고를 다양한 연한 색깔로 제본했으며, 정확하고 깔끔하다는 평판을 얻고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English ynke, from Old French enque, from Latin encaustum (“purple ink used by Roman emperors to sign documents”), from Ancient Greek ἔ...
definition_en: To write or draw with liquid color.

senses.gloss: A pigment (or dye)-based fluid used for writing, printing etc.
senses.example: This form should be filled out in ink.

senses.gloss: A particular type, color or container of this fluid.
The black or dark-colored fluid ejected by squid, octopus etc, as a protective strategy.

examples.text: She had had the idea of giving it a certain daintiness, and she made much use of blue and red inks; she bound the copy in coarse paper, that looked vaguely like watered silk, in various pale colours; and she had acquired a reputation for neatness and accuracy.

senses.gloss: An opponent or enemy.

senses.gloss: One who antagonizes or stirs.

etymology: From thoughtful + -ly.
definition_en: Given careful thought.

senses.gloss: In a thoughtful or pensive manner.
senses.example: 'That button, it suggests possibilities,' said Poirot thoughtfully.

senses.gloss: In a way that shows kindness or consideration for others.

examples.text: Strickland looked at me thoughtfully for nearly a minute.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 거의 1분 동안 나를 곰곰히 바라보았다.

definition_en: Make someone feel ashamed or embarrassed.

senses.gloss: To make ashamed; to embarrass; to destroy the self-possession of, as by exciting suddenly a consciousness of guilt, mistake, or inferiority; to disconcert; to discomfit.
senses.example: The stare seemed to abash Poirot.

senses.gloss: To lose self-possession; to become ashamed.

examples.text: I was not so easily abashed as I had been some years earlier.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French volubile, from Latin volūbilis (“rolling”), from volvō (“roll”).
definition_en: Given to speaking or writing at length and with ease.

senses.gloss: Fluent or having a ready flow of speech.
senses.example: But Wolf Larsen seemed voluble, prone to speech as I had never seen him before. It was as though he were bursting with pent energy which must find an outlet somehow.

senses.gloss: Of thoughts, feelings, or something that is expressed: expressed readily or at length and in a fluent manner.
senses.example: In the daylit corridor he talked with voluble pains of zeal, in duty bound, most fair, most kind, most honest broadbrim.

senses.gloss: Easily rolling or turning; having a fluid, undulating motion.
senses.example: Seen from the west, their sky-line gallops away north and south like a sea-serpent in voluble motion.

examples.text: Stroeve, with voluble tongue, explained how he and I had met, and by what an accident we discovered that we both knew Strickland.
examples.translation_ko: 스트루브는 유창한 말솜씨로 그와 내가 어떻게 만났는지, 그리고 어떤 우연으로 우리 둘 다 스트릭랜드를 안다는 사실을 알게 되었는지 설명했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Speaking foolishly or nonsensically.

senses.gloss: To utter words indistinctly or unintelligibly; to utter inarticulate sounds
senses.example: The men were babbling, so we couldn't make sense of anything.

senses.gloss: To talk incoherently; to utter meaningless words.

senses.example: Radical rather than rhetorical, babble like an oracle

examples.text: He glanced at me once or twice reflectively, but for the most part seemed occupied with his own thoughts; and certainly without Stroeve’s babble the conversation would have been difficult.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 한두 번 생각에 잠긴 듯 나를 흘끗 보았지만, 대부분은 자신의 생각에 잠겨 있는 것 같았다. 스트루브의 수다가 없었다면 대화는 분명 어려웠을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To support or hold something up.

senses.gloss: An object placed against or under another, to support it; anything that supports.
senses.example: They stuck a block of wood under it as a prop.

senses.gloss: The player on either side of the hooker in a scrum.
Any of the seashells in the game of props.

examples.text: When we had ordered our dinner, I propped it against a bottle of St. Galmier and began to read.
examples.translation_ko: 저녁을 주문한 후, 나는 신문을 생갈미에 병에 기대어 세우고 읽기 시작했다.

senses.gloss: Such a work for television, radio or the cinema, usually one that is not a comedy.

senses.gloss: Ellipsis of phonograph record (“a disc, usually made from vinyl, on which sound is recorded and may be replayed on a phonograph”).

etymology: Inherited from Middle English devouren, from Old French devorer (Modern French dévorer), from Latin dēvorō, from vorō.

senses.gloss: To eat quickly, greedily, hungrily, or ravenously.
senses.example: Once constituted, capital reproduces itself faster than output increases. The past devours the future.

senses.gloss: To rapidly destroy, engulf, or lay waste.
senses.example: The fire was devouring the building.

senses.gloss: To take in avidly with the intellect or with one's gaze.
senses.example: She intended to devour the book.

definition_en: Used to emphasize that something is completely true or done.

senses.gloss: Completely and entirely; to the fullest extent; (loosely, exaggeratedly) very; to a great extent.
senses.example: Wholly, in my opinion, this is wrong.

senses.gloss: Exclusively and solely.

definition_en: Having a serious and unpleasant expression.

senses.gloss: Dismal and gloomy, cold and forbidding.
senses.example: Life was grim in many northern industrial towns.

senses.gloss: Rigid and unrelenting.
senses.example: His grim determination enabled him to win.

senses.gloss: Ghastly or sinister.
senses.example: A grim castle overshadowed the village.

senses.gloss: The property of being shabby.

senses.gloss: To raise a corner of the upper lip slightly, especially in scorn.
To utter with a grimace or contemptuous expression; to say sneeringly.

etymology: Borrowed from Latin praescrībere, from prae- (“before, in front”) and scrībere (“to write”).
definition_en: To officially order or recommend a particular treatment.

senses.gloss: To order (a drug or medical device) for use by a particular patient (under licensed authority).
senses.example: The doctor prescribed aspirin.

senses.gloss: To specify by writing as a required procedure or ritual; to lay down authoritatively as a guide, direction, or rule of action.
senses.example: The property meets the criteria prescribed by the regulations.

senses.gloss: To develop or assert a right; to make a claim (by prescription).
senses.example: Most probable that one presentation and 40 years possession thereafter, is sufficient to prescribe a right of patronage.

examples.text: He was dexterous to make him comfortable, and he exercised a cunning of which I should never have thought him capable to induce him to take the medicines prescribed by the doctor.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 스트릭랜드를 편안하게 해주는 데 능숙했고, 의사가 처방한 약을 먹도록 유도하기 위해 내가 그에게서 전혀 기대하지 못했을 교활함을 발휘했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English wantounly, wantounliche, equivalent to wanton + -ly.
definition_en: Done with reckless disregard for consequences.

senses.gloss: in a wanton manner.
senses.example: I believe that I have no enemy on earth, and none surely would have been so wicked as to destroy me wantonly.

examples.text: Though his means were adequate to the needs of himself and his wife, he certainly had no money to waste; but now he was wantonly extravagant in the purchase of delicacies, out of season and dear, which might tempt Strickland’s capricious appetite.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 수입은 자신과 아내의 필요를 충족시키기에 충분했지만, 확실히 낭비할 돈은 없었다. 하지만 이제 그는 스트릭랜드의 변덕스러운 식욕을 돋울 수 있는 진미들을 사는 데 방탕하게 돈을 썼는데, 그것들은 제철이 아니어서 비쌌다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English norisshement, from Middle French, from Old French norissement, from norrir, equivalent to nourish + -ment.
definition_en: Nutritional support or food.

senses.gloss: The act of nourishing or the state of being nourished.
Something that nourishes; food.
senses.example: Many ultraraces do not include much nourishment from organizers.

examples.text: I shall never forget the tactful patience with which he persuaded him to take nourishment.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 스트릭랜드로 하여금 영양분을 섭취하도록 설득한 재치 있는 인내심을 결코 잊지 못할 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English rudenesse, equivalent to rude + -ness.
definition_en: The quality of being rude or impolite.

senses.gloss: The property of being rude.
senses.example: His rudeness was inexcusable.

senses.gloss: A rude remark or behaviour.
senses.example: I'm sick of his rudenesses.

examples.text: He was never put out by Strickland’s rudeness; if it was merely sullen, he appeared not to notice it; if it was aggressive, he only chuckled.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 스트릭랜드의 무례함에 결코 화내지 않았다. 그것이 단순히 뚱한 것이라면 알아차리지 못하는 척했고, 공격적이라면 그저 킬킬 웃을 뿐이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French compétence, from Late Latin competentia. Doublet of competency.
definition_en: The quality of being competent or suitable for a particular task.

senses.gloss: The quality or state of being competent, i.e. able or suitable for a general role.
senses.example: Teachers are now required to teach intercultural communicative competence.

senses.gloss: The quality or state of being able or suitable for a particular task; the quality or state of being competent for a particular task or skill.
The system of linguistic knowledge possessed by native speakers of a language, as opposed to its actual use in concrete situations (performance), cf. linguistic competence.

examples.text: When I remarked on her competence, she told me with that pleasant little smile of hers that for a while she had worked in a hospital.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 그녀의 능숙함에 대해 언급하자, 그녀는 그 특유의 상냥한 미소를 지으며 한동안 병원에서 일한 적이 있다고 말했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English forestallen (“to forestall, intercept, ambush, way-lay”), from forestalle (“a forestalling, interception”), from Old English fo...
definition_en: To prevent or forestall something from happening.

senses.gloss: To prevent, delay or hinder something by taking precautionary or anticipatory measures; to avert.
senses.example: Fred forestalled disaster by his prompt action.

senses.gloss: To preclude or bar from happening, render impossible.
senses.example: In French, an aspired h forestalls elision.

senses.gloss: To purchase the complete supply of a good, particularly foodstuffs, in order to charge a monopoly price.

examples.text: She did not speak to him much, but she was quick to forestall his wants.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀는 그에게 말을 많이 걸지는 않았지만, 그의 필요를 재빨리 미리 채워주었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English bedsyde, bedde syde (also as beddes side, beddes syde), equivalent to bed + -side. Compare German Bettseite (“bedside”).
definition_en: A bed or a place near a bed.

senses.gloss: A position at the side of one's bed.

examples.text: I wondered what she thought during the long darkness as she sat by the bedside.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀가 침대 곁에 앉아 긴 어둠 속에서 무슨 생각을 했을지 나는 궁금했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From feverish + -ly.
definition_en: With a feverish intensity or enthusiasm.

senses.gloss: With excitement and determination.
With speed; rapidly.
senses.example: With nothing else to do, he carried the candle to the front room and began feverishly filling his pipe.

examples.text: Strickland was a weird figure as he lay there, thinner than ever, with his ragged red beard and his eyes staring feverishly into vacancy; his illness seemed to have made them larger, and they had an unnatural brightness.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 그곳에 누워 있는 모습이 기괴했는데, 전보다 더욱 야위어서 헝클어진 붉은 수염과 열에 들뜬 눈으로 허공을 응시하고 있었다. 병으로 인해 눈이 더 커진 것 같았고, 부자연스럽게 빛나고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A sudden loud noise that attracts attention.

examples.text: Her eyes had in them a strange perplexity, and perhaps—but why?—alarm.
examples.translation_ko: 그녀의 눈에는 이상한 당혹감이, 그리고 아마도—하지만 왜?—경계심이 서려 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English surveyen, from Old French sourveoir, surveer (“to oversee”), from sour-, sur- (“over”) + veoir, veeir (“to see”), from Latin vi...
definition_en: Examine or investigate a place or situation.

senses.gloss: The act of surveying; a general view.

senses.gloss: A particular view; an examination, especially an official examination, of a particular group of items, in order to ascertain the condition, quantity, or quality.

senses.gloss: The operation of finding the contour, dimensions, position, or other particulars of any part of the Earth's surface.

examples.text: In a moment Strickland looked away and idly surveyed the ceiling, but she continued to stare at him, and now her look was quite inexplicable.

senses.gloss: A person or animal regarded as resembling a scarecrow (sense 1) in some way; especially, a tall, thin, awkward person; or a person wearing ragged and tattered clothes.

senses.gloss: Synonym of crow scarer (“a farmhand employed to scare birds from the fields”).

examples.text: His clothes hung upon him like rags on a scarecrow.

senses.gloss: See-through, clear; having the property that light passes through it almost undisturbed, such that one can see through it clearly.

To frighten; scare; terrify.

The academic study of chords.

definition_en: A rhythmic flow of sound, especially in speech or music.

senses.gloss: The act or state of declining or sinking.

senses.gloss: The measure or beat of movement.

senses.example: Night has now passed in the Saudi desert and as we hear from Nightline correspondent Forrest Sawyer, the normal cadence of life at the front is about to change.

examples.text: The books he liked were queer; sometimes I would find him poring over the poems of Mallarme, and he read them as a child reads, forming the words with his lips, and I wondered what strange emotion he got from those subtle cadences and obscure phrases; and again I found him absorbed in the detective novels of Gaboriau.

A real or pretended indifference to pleasure or pain; insensibility; impassiveness.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

senses.gloss: Less distant; comparative form of near: more near.

senses.gloss: Causing, feeling, or expressing regret or sorrow, especially in a wry or humorous way.

senses.gloss: Inspiring pity or compassion.
Bad; woeful; deplorable.

examples.text: He gave a little start, and then smiled, but his smile was rueful.

examples.translation_ko: 밤 열 시쯤이었다. 나는 식당에서 혼자 저녁을 먹고 작은 아파트로 돌아와 응접실에 앉아 책을 읽고 있었는데, 종이 갈라진 소리로 딸랑거리는 것을 듣고 복도로 나가 문을 열었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

examples.text: I knew he was of abstemious habit or I should have thought he had been drinking.

senses.gloss: Eagerness, fervor, excessive strong feeling.
