PIE word
 *h₁én
From French enveloppe. The engineering sense is derived from flight envelope. The verb is from the noun.
definition_en: A cover for a letter or document.

senses.gloss: A paper or cardboard wrapper used to enclose small, flat items, especially letters, for mailing.
Something that envelops; a wrapping.
A bag containing the lifting gas of a balloon or airship; fabric that encloses the gas-bags of an airship.

examples.text: I looked at the man before me in his shabby clothes, with his great nose and shining eyes, his red beard and untidy hair; and I had a strange sensation that it was only an envelope, and I was in the presence of a disembodied spirit.
examples.translation_ko: 초라한 옷을 입고 큰 코와 빛나는 눈, 붉은 수염과 헝클어진 머리를 한 내 앞의 남자를 바라보았다. 그리고 이상한 감각이 들었다. 그것은 단지 껍데기일 뿐이고, 나는 육체를 벗어난 영혼 앞에 있다는 느낌이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Old French entrecours, from Late Latin intercursus.
definition_en: Communication or interaction between people.

senses.gloss: Communication, conversation.
senses.example: It might seem that with age places gained upon persons in interest to my mind; and that my pleasure grew in intercourse with things rather than with ideas.

senses.gloss: Dealings between countries.
Dealings with people, including commerce and trade.

examples.text: In social intercourse he gives you the surface that he wishes the world to accept, and you can only gain a true knowledge of him by inferences from little actions, of which he is unconscious, and from fleeting expressions, which cross his face unknown to him.
examples.translation_ko: 사교적 교제에서 그는 세상이 받아들이기를 바라는 표면만을 보여주며, 당신은 오직 그가 의식하지 못하는 사소한 행동들과 그도 모르게 얼굴을 스쳐가는 순간적인 표정들로부터 추론해야만 그에 대한 진정한 지식을 얻을 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English perfeccioun, from Old French perfection, from Latin perfectiō. Displaced native Old English fulfremednes.
definition_en: The state of being flawless or faultless.

senses.gloss: The quality or state of being perfect or complete, so that nothing substandard remains; the highest attainable state or degree of excellence.
senses.example: Think, think about the way of rejection / You're not the only one reaching for perfection / Think, think about the reason you exist / I got something you might not wanna miss

senses.gloss: A quality, endowment, or acquirement completely excellent; an ideal; faultlessness; especially, the divine attribute of complete excellence.
senses.example: No tongue can her perfections tell

senses.gloss: The process or act of establishing official recognition for a legal claim, generally in the context of security interests.

examples.text: Sometimes people carry to such perfection the mask they have assumed that in due course they actually become the person they seem.
examples.translation_ko: 때로는 사람들이 자신이 쓴 가면을 너무나 완벽하게 착용해서 결국 실제로 그들이 보이는 그 사람이 되어버리기도 한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin vacuitās (“empty space, vacancy, vacuity”); equivalent to vacu(ous) + -ity.
definition_en: A state of emptiness or voidness.

senses.gloss: Emptiness.
senses.example: At first glance, Saltburn is classic clash-of-the-classes fare: a tale of social strata, moral vacuity and the seductions of wealth, with a poor boy ushered into his rich friend's kingdom.

senses.gloss: Physical emptiness, an absence of matter; vacuum.
Idleness; listlessness.

examples.text: His pretentiousness will only expose his vacuity.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 허세는 오직 그의 공허함만을 드러낼 뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English lathen, from Old English laþian (“to invite, summon, call upon, ask”), from Proto-West Germanic *laþōn, from Proto-Germanic *la...
definition_en: A machine tool for shaping wood or metal by rotating it.

senses.gloss: To invite; bid; ask.

examples.text: The lathe painted to look like iron is seen to be but a lathe.
examples.translation_ko: 철처럼 보이게 칠한 선반도 결국은 그저 선반일 뿐임이 드러난다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English innermost, innermest, in-nermast, alteration (due to Middle English inner, innere (“inner”)) of Old English innemest (“innermos...
definition_en: The innermost part of something.

senses.gloss: Farthest inside or towards the center or middle.
senses.example: She poured her innermost feelings into her journal.

examples.text: To the acute observer no one can produce the most casual work without disclosing the innermost secrets of his soul.
examples.translation_ko: 예리한 관찰자에게는 누구든 아무리 대수롭지 않은 작품이라도 만들면서 자신의 영혼 깊숙한 비밀을 드러내지 않을 수 없다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English likinge, likinde, likende, likande, licande, from Old English līciende, līciġende, from Proto-Germanic *līkāndz, present partic...
definition_en: A feeling of pleasure or enjoyment.

senses.gloss: present participle and gerund of like

examples.text: I wondered what those friends of mine would say who demanded vast studios, and vowed they could not work unless all the conditions were to their liking.
examples.translation_ko: 거대한 화실을 요구하며 모든 조건이 마음에 들지 않으면 작업할 수 없다고 맹세하던 내 친구들이 이것을 보면 뭐라고 할까 궁금했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin mūsēum (“library, study”), from Ancient Greek Μουσεῖον (Mouseîon), shrine of the Muses (Μοῦσα (Moûsa)).
definition_en: A building where objects of historical or scientific interest are exhibited.

senses.gloss: A building or institution dedicated to the acquisition, conservation, study, exhibition, and educational interpretation of objects having scientific, historical, cultural or artistic value.
senses.example: visit the history museum

examples.text: Most of them have found their way into museums, and the rest are the treasured possessions of wealthy amateurs.
examples.translation_ko: 그 그림들 대부분은 박물관으로 들어갔고, 나머지는 부유한 수집가들의 소중한 소장품이 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From treasure + -ed.
definition_en: Highly valued or cherished.

senses.gloss: Valued; especially, having a personal value.

examples.text: Most of them have found their way into museums, and the rest are the treasured possessions of wealthy amateurs.
examples.translation_ko: 그 그림들 대부분은 박물관으로 들어갔고, 나머지는 부유한 수집가들의 소중한 소장품이 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from French amateur, from Latin amātor (“lover”), from amāre (“to love”).
definition_en: A person who engages in a pursuit or activity without financial compensation.

senses.gloss: A lover of something.
senses.example: he conducted extensive correspondence on wines with European suppliers, employing a wine vocabulary familiar to any modern amateur of wines.

senses.gloss: A person attached to a particular pursuit, study, science, or art (such as music or painting), especially one who cultivates any study, interest, taste, or attachment without engaging in it professionally.
senses.example: The contest is only open to amateurs.

senses.gloss: Someone who is unqualified or insufficiently skillful.
senses.example: The entire thing was built by some amateurs with screwdrivers and plywood.

examples.text: Most of them have found their way into museums, and the rest are the treasured possessions of wealthy amateurs.
examples.translation_ko: 그 그림들 대부분은 박물관으로 들어갔고, 나머지는 부유한 수집가들의 소중한 소장품이 되었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French impressionniste.
definition_en: A painter or artist who specializes in capturing the fleeting impressions of light and color.

senses.gloss: One who adheres to the theory or method of impressionism.
A performer who does impressions; a mimic.

examples.text: At that time I had the greatest admiration for the impressionists.
examples.translation_ko: 그 당시 나는 인상파 화가들을 가장 크게 찬탄하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French charte (“card, map”), from Late Latin charta (“paper, card, map”), Latin charta (“papyrus, writing”), from Ancient Gree...
definition_en: To draw a map or graph.

senses.gloss: A map illustrating the geography of a specific phenomenon.
A navigator's map.
A tabular presentation of data; a table.

examples.text: Now that his influence has so enormously affected modern painting, now that others have charted the country which he was among the first to explore, Strickland’s pictures, seen for the first time, would find the mind more prepared for them; but it must be remembered that I had never seen anything of the sort.
examples.translation_ko: 이제 그의 영향력이 현대 회화에 엄청난 변화를 가져왔고, 이제 다른 화가들이 그가 최초로 탐험한 영역을 지도로 그려놓은 지금, 스트릭랜드의 그림들을 처음 보는 사람이라면 더 준비된 마음으로 받아들일 수 있을 것이다. 하지만 당시 나는 그런 류의 작품을 본 적이 전혀 없었다는 점을 기억해야 한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From clumsy + -ness.
definition_en: Lack of coordination or skill.

senses.gloss: A lack of coordination or elegance; the condition or quality of being clumsy.
senses.example: He dropped them not out of spite, but out of clumsiness.

examples.text: First of all I was taken aback by what seemed to me the clumsiness of his technique.
examples.translation_ko: 무엇보다 먼저 나를 당황하게 한 것은 그의 기법이 서투르다고 여겨진 점이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From draught + -s- + -man.
definition_en: A person who draws technical diagrams or plans.

senses.gloss: A person skilled at drawing engineering or architectural plans.
A book illustrator.
One who drinks drams; a tippler.
senses.example: I have used my interest in several wards of the city , that the wholesome restorative above - mentioned may be given in tavern - kitchens to all the morning's draughtsmen within

examples.text: Accustomed to the drawing of the old masters, and convinced that Ingres was the greatest draughtsman of recent times, I thought that Strickland drew very badly.
examples.translation_ko: 고전 거장들의 소묘에 익숙하고 앵그르가 근세 최고의 소묘가라고 확신하던 나는 스트릭랜드가 그림을 매우 못 그린다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English loppe (“bough”); the verb is a back-formation from the noun.
definition_en: to cut or remove something suddenly

senses.gloss: To cut off as the top or extreme part of anything, especially to prune a small limb off a shrub or tree, or sometimes to behead someone.
senses.example:
Some, for hard masters, broken under arms,
In battle lopt away, with half their limbs,
Beg bitter bread thro’ realms their valour sav’d,

senses.gloss: To hang downward; to be pendent; to lean to one side.
To allow to hang down.
senses.example: to lop the head

examples.text: I remember a still-life of oranges on a plate, and I was bothered because the plate was not round and the oranges were lop-sided.
examples.translation_ko: 접시 위에 놓인 오렌지들을 그린 정물화가 기억나는데, 접시가 둥글지 않고 오렌지들이 비뚤어져 있어서 나는 거슬렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Having one side or aspect.

senses.gloss: simple past and past participle of side

examples.text: I remember a still-life of oranges on a plate, and I was bothered because the plate was not round and the oranges were lop-sided.
examples.translation_ko: 접시 위에 놓인 오렌지들을 그린 정물화가 기억나는데, 접시가 둥글지 않고 오렌지들이 비뚤어져 있어서 나는 거슬렸다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French caricature, from Italian caricatura. Not related to character, which is instead ultimately from Ancient Greek χαρακτήρ (kharaktḗr, “typ...
definition_en: A humorous or exaggerated representation of a person or thing.

senses.gloss: A pictorial representation of someone in which distinguishing features are exaggerated for comic effect.
senses.example: Men In Black 3 lacks the novelty of the first film, and its take on the late ’60s feels an awful lot like a psychedelic dress-up party, all broad caricatures and groovy vibes.

senses.gloss: A grotesque misrepresentation.
senses.example: They were ignoring that the feckless, toothless caricature of a world parliament — the UN — needed American money in order to keep going and would do anything to get our moolah!

senses.gloss: In facial recognition systems, a face that has been modified to look less like the average face, and thus more distinctive.

examples.text: To my eyes the faces looked like caricatures.
examples.translation_ko: 내 눈에는 그 얼굴들이 캐리커처 같아 보였다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From cab + driver.
definition_en: A person who drives a taxi.

senses.gloss: One who drives a taxi for a living.
One who drives a carriage for a living.

examples.text: There were two or three pictures of the forest at Fontainebleau and several of streets in Paris: my first feeling was that they might have been painted by a drunken cabdriver.
examples.translation_ko: 퐁텐블로 숲을 그린 그림이 두세 점 있었고 파리 거리를 그린 그림이 몇 점 있었는데, 처음 든 생각은 술 취한 마차꾼이 그린 것 같다는 것이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle French incomprehensible, from Latin incomprehensibilis. Equivalent to in- + comprehensible.
definition_en: Impossible to understand.

senses.gloss: Impossible or very difficult to understand.
senses.example: Trump’s grotesque and incomprehensible fondness for Putin makes the details of any deal highly dangerous for Europe and the NATO alliance, founded to confront Russia.

senses.gloss: Which cannot be contained; boundless, infinite.

examples.text: It passed through my mind that the whole thing was a stupendous, incomprehensible farce.
examples.translation_ko: 이 모든 것이 엄청나고 이해할 수 없는 희극이라는 생각이 머릿속을 스쳐 지나갔다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Inherited from Middle English revolucion, borrowed from Old French revolucion, from Late Latin revolūtiōnem, accusative singular of revolūtiō (“the...
definition_en: A fundamental change in the way of thinking or doing things.

senses.gloss: A political upheaval in a government or state characterized by great change.
senses.example: The revolution completely transformed the monarchy into a republic.

senses.gloss: The popular removal and replacement of a government, especially by sudden violent action.
Rotation: the turning of an object around an axis, one complete turn of an object during rotation.
senses.example: Numerous cases are recorded which incontestibly prove that during pregnancy, the uterus perform a half or even a complete revolution, on itself, producing torsion of the cervix […]

examples.text: He saw from the first that here was a revolution in art, and he recognised in its beginnings the genius which now all the world allows.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 처음부터 여기에 예술의 혁명이 있다는 것을 보았고, 그 시작에서 지금 온 세상이 인정하는 천재성을 알아보았던 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + impressed.
definition_en: Showing no enthusiasm or interest.

senses.gloss: Not impressed.

examples.text: But if I was puzzled and disconcerted, I was not unimpressed.
examples.translation_ko: 하지만 당황스럽고 어리둥절했지만, 감명을 받지 않은 것은 아니었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Examine or interpret something closely

senses.gloss: British standard spelling of analyze.

examples.text: They gave me an emotion that I could not analyse.
examples.translation_ko: 그것들은 내가 분석할 수 없는 감정을 불러일으켰다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From French symbole, from Latin symbolus, symbolum (“a sign, mark, token, symbol, in Late Latin also a creed”), from Ancient Greek σύμβολον (súmbol...
definition_en: A person or thing that represents an idea or quality.

senses.gloss: A character or glyph representing an idea, concept or object.
senses.example: "$" is the symbol for dollars in the US and some other countries.

senses.gloss: A thing considered the embodiment or cardinal exemplar of a concept, theme, or other thing.
senses.example: The lion is the symbol of courage; the lamb is the symbol of meekness or patience.

senses.gloss: A type of noun whereby the form refers to the same entity independently of the context; a symbol arbitrarily denotes a referent. See also icon and index.

examples.text: I fancy that Strickland saw vaguely some spiritual meaning in material things that was so strange that he could only suggest it with halting symbols.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 물질적인 것들 속에서 너무나 기이한 어떤 정신적 의미를 막연히 보았기에, 더듬거리는 상징으로만 그것을 암시할 수 있었던 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Morphologically mistake + -n.
definition_en: Believing something to be true that is not.

senses.gloss: past participle of mistake
senses.example: I'm frequently mistaken for my brother.

examples.text: When I imagined that on seeing his pictures I should get a clue to the understanding of his strange character I was mistaken.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 그림들을 보면 그의 기이한 성격을 이해할 단서를 얻을 수 있으리라 생각했던 나는 착각이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English manuel, from Old French manuel, from Late Latin manuāle (“handbook, manual”).
definition_en: A book or document that provides instructions on how to use something.

senses.gloss: Synonym of handbook.
A booklet that instructs on the usage of a particular machine or product.
senses.example: The dishwasher isn't working; can you remember where we put the manual?

senses.gloss: A drill in the use of weapons, etc.

examples.text: We are like people living in a country whose language they know so little that, with all manner of beautiful and profound things to say, they are condemned to the banalities of the conversation manual.
examples.translation_ko: 우리는 마치 어떤 나라에 살면서도 그 나라 말을 거의 모르는 사람들과 같아서, 아름답고 심오한 말을 하고 싶어도 회화 교본의 진부한 표현들로 만족해야 하는 신세다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: The verb is derived from Middle English sethen, seeth (“to boil, seethe; to cook; etc.”) [and other forms], from Old English sēoþan (“to boil, seet...
definition_en: To be filled with intense anger or passion.

senses.gloss: Of a liquid or other substance, or a container holding it: to be boiled (vigorously); to become boiling hot.
senses.example: Deep Hell! that seethest in thy simmering pit; / Thy thousand throned horrors shall not vie, / Or ever compass it!

senses.gloss: Of a liquid, vapor, etc., or a container holding it: to foam or froth in an agitated manner, as if boiling.
senses.example: "He seetheth like a steaming cauldron," answered the servant; "and Bauldie, the lad, walketh him about the yard with a halter, lest he take cold."

senses.gloss: Of a person: to be in an agitated or angry mental state, often in a way that is not obvious to others.
senses.example: She lay and seethed in fever many weeks, / But youth was strong and overcame the test; / Revolted soul and flesh were reconciled / And fetched back to the necessary day / And daylight duties.

examples.text: Their brain is seething with ideas, and they can only tell you that the umbrella of the gardener’s aunt is in the house.
examples.translation_ko: 머릿속에는 온갖 생각들이 끓어오르는데, 정작 할 수 있는 말이라고는 정원사 아주머니의 우산이 집에 있다는 것뿐이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Extremely talented or skilled.

senses.gloss: In a positive sense: marvellous, wonderful; (specifically) extremely talented, especially at a young age.
In a negative sense: appalling, horrifying, shocking; (specifically, archaic) abnormal, freakish, monstrous, unnatural.
senses.example: Horrible things have been in this wild world, / Prodigious mixtures, and confusions strange / Of good and ill; and worse have been conceived / Than ever there was found a heart to do.

senses.gloss: Extraordinarily amazing.
senses.example: A prodigious quantity of insects of all sorts (but no mosquitoes) assailed us at our evening meal.

examples.text: The final impression I received was of a prodigious effort to express some state of the soul, and in this effort, I fancied, must be sought the explanation of what so utterly perplexed me.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 마지막으로 받은 인상은 영혼의 어떤 상태를 표현하려는 엄청난 노력이었고, 나를 그토록 완전히 당황시킨 것의 해답도 바로 이 노력에서 찾아야 한다고 생각했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From the French simplifier, equivalent to simple + -ify.
definition_en: Make something simpler or easier to understand.

senses.gloss: To make simpler, either by reducing in complexity, reducing to component parts, or making easier to understand.
senses.example: Quizzed on simplifying fares, Heaton-Harris said the Government had inherited a "mix of ticketing and unbelievable, interesting fares up and down the system, and we do want to simplify them".

senses.gloss: To become simpler.

examples.text: He did not hesitate to simplify or to distort if he could get nearer to that unknown thing he sought.
examples.translation_ko: 자신이 추구하는 미지의 것에 더 가까이 다가갈 수 있다면 단순화하거나 왜곡하는 것도 서슴지 않았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From un- + move.
definition_en: Refuse to move or be moved.

senses.gloss: To move (something) back to its original place; undo or reverse the motion of.
senses.example: You can use this shortcut to undelete a deleted (but not trashed) file or to unmove something.

senses.gloss: To move away; remove.
senses.example: […] no dissenting voice arise to beseech them to look upon their work, to assist them to unmove the scales from their eyes […]

senses.gloss: To not move; remain still or motionless; remain in place.
senses.example: Nevertheless, James picked up a hard, cold stone and threw it with all his strength at the unmoving cat. It continued to unmove.

examples.text: Though these pictures confused and puzzled me, I could not be unmoved by the emotion that was patent in them; and, I knew not why, I felt in myself a feeling that with regard to Strickland was the last I had ever expected to experience.
examples.translation_ko: 이 그림들이 나를 혼란스럽게 하고 당황시켰지만, 그 안에 드러난 감정에 무감각할 수는 없었다. 그리고 이유는 모르겠지만, 스트릭랜드에 대해서는 결코 느끼리라 예상하지 못했던 감정을 내 안에서 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English perilous, from Old French perilleus, equivalent to peril + -ous, from the noun peril, or from Latin perīculōsus. Doublet of per...
definition_en: Full of danger or risk.

senses.gloss: Dangerous, full of peril.

examples.text: I do not know what infinite yearning possesses you, so that you are driven to a perilous, lonely search for some goal where you expect to find a final release from the spirit that torments you.
examples.translation_ko: 어떤 무한한 갈망이 당신을 사로잡고 있는지 모르겠지만, 그 때문에 당신을 괴롭히는 정신으로부터 최종적인 해방을 찾을 수 있으리라 기대하는 어떤 목표를 향해 위험하고 외로운 탐색에 내몰리고 있는 것입니다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English gol (“boundary, limit”), from Old English *gāl (“obstacle, barrier, marker”), suggested by its derivatives Old English gǣlan (“...
definition_en: A target or objective to be achieved.

senses.gloss: A result that one is attempting to achieve.

definition_en: A place of worship or reverence for a particular person or thing.

etymology: From sentimental + -ist.
definition_en: A person who values emotions and personal feelings over reason.

senses.gloss: A person who is sentimental.

etymology: From Middle English arbitrarie, Latin arbitrārius (“arbitrary, uncertain”), from arbiter (“witness, on-looker, listener, judge, overseer”).
definition_en: Decided or chosen without a clear reason.

senses.gloss: Based on individual discretion or judgment; not based on any objective distinction, perhaps even made at random.
senses.example: Benjamin Franklin's designation of "positive" and "negative" to different charges was arbitrary.

senses.gloss: Determined by impulse rather than reason; often connoting heavy-handedness.
senses.example: The bromide conforms to everything sanctioned by the majority, and may be depended upon to be trite, banal, and arbitrary.

senses.gloss: Any, out of all that are possible.
senses.example: The equation is true for an arbitrary value of x.

examples.text: The strangest, Strickland’s determination to become a painter, seems to be arbitrary; and though it must have had causes in the circumstances of his life, I am ignorant of them.

etymology: From Middle English vocacioun, from Old French vocation, from Latin vocātiō.
definition_en: A strong feeling of being called to a particular career or profession.

senses.gloss: To take part in (a wrestling bout or match).

examples.translation_ko: 아마 그녀는 자신의 지성으로 알고 있었을 것이다. 자신이 만드는 사슬이 오히려 그의 파괴 본능만 자극할 뿐이라는 것을, 마치 판유리창이 사람으로 하여금 벽돌 반 조각을 집어 던지고 싶은 충동을 불러일으키는 것처럼 말이다. 하지만 이성을 잃은 그녀의 마음은 치명적이라는 것을 알면서도 그 길을 계속 걷게 만들었다.

etymology: Borrowed from Middle French incapable, in- + capable.
definition_en: Lacking the ability or power to do something.

senses.gloss: Not capable (of doing something); unable.
senses.example: A pint glass is incapable of holding more than a pint of liquid.

senses.gloss: Not in a state to receive; not receptive; not susceptible; not able to admit.
senses.example: incapable of pain, or pleasure; incapable of stain or injury

definition_en: Causing or resulting in death.

senses.gloss: Proceeding from, or appointed by, fate or destiny.
Foreboding death or great disaster.
Causing death or destruction.
senses.example: a fatal wound; a fatal disease; that fatal day; a fatal mistake

etymology: From Middle English ficcioun, from Old French ficcion (“dissimulation, ruse, invention”), from Latin fictiō (“a making, fashioning, a feigning, a r...
definition_en: A work of imagination or a false statement.

senses.gloss: Literary type using invented or imaginative writing, instead of real facts, usually written as prose.
senses.example: I am a great reader of fiction.

senses.gloss: A verbal or written account that is not based on actual events (often intended to mislead).
senses.example: The company’s accounts contained a number of blatant fictions.

senses.gloss: A legal fiction.

examples.text: Here lies the unreality of fiction.
examples.translation_ko: 여기에 소설의 비현실성이 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology:
PIE word
 *h₂éd
From Anglo-Norman paramont, paramount (“paramount, pre-eminent; above”), from Old French par, per (“by”) + amont, amunt (“upward”)....
definition_en: Most important or of highest priority.

senses.gloss: Highest, supreme; also, chief, leading, pre-eminent.
senses.example: Hitherto she had chiefly dwelt on her unkindness and neglect; but absence, like charity, covers a multitude of sins; and the thought now paramount was, that she should see her no more.

senses.gloss: Of the highest importance.
senses.example: Getting those credit cards paid off is paramount.

senses.gloss: Of a law, right, etc.: having precedence over or superior to another.

examples.text: There are few men to whom it is the most important thing in the world, and they are not very interesting ones; even women, with whom the subject is of paramount interest, have a contempt for them.
examples.translation_ko: 이것이 세상에서 가장 중요한 일인 남자들은 거의 없으며, 그런 남자들은 별로 흥미롭지도 않다. 심지어 이 문제가 가장 중요한 관심사인 여자들조차 그런 남자들을 경멸한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: First attested 1564, from Middle French compartiment, from Italian compartimento, from Late Latin compartiri (“to divide with, to share with”), fro...
definition_en: A separate section or area within a larger space.

senses.gloss: A room, or section, or chamber, typically within a vehicle.
senses.example: Two men were seated in a well-lit compartment of a third-class railway carriage.

senses.gloss: One of the parts into which an area is subdivided.
The part of a protein that serves a specific function.

examples.text: For the most part, they keep their various activities in various compartments, and they can pursue one to the temporary exclusion of the other.
examples.translation_ko: 대부분의 경우 그들은 다양한 활동들을 각각 다른 구획에 넣어두고, 한 가지를 추구할 때는 일시적으로 다른 것들을 배제할 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Borrowed from Latin temporarius, from tempus (“time”).
definition_en: Lasting for a limited time.

senses.gloss: Not permanent; existing only for a period or periods of time.
senses.example: Sally was put in temporary charge of the department while they searched for a full-time replacement.

senses.gloss: Existing only for a short time or short times; transient, ephemeral.

examples.text: For the most part, they keep their various activities in various compartments, and they can pursue one to the temporary exclusion of the other.
examples.translation_ko: 대부분의 경우 그들은 다양한 활동들을 각각 다른 구획에 넣어두고, 한 가지를 추구할 때는 일시적으로 다른 것들을 배제할 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From else + whither (“to which place, to what place”).
definition_en: A place or region other than the one being referred to.

senses.gloss: To some other place; in some other direction.
senses.example: With Strickland the sexual appetite took a very small place. It was unimportant. It was irksome. His soul aimed elsewhither.

examples.text: His soul aimed elsewhither.
examples.translation_ko: 그의 영혼은 다른 곳을 향하고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Originally in plural from French orgies, from Latin orgia, from Ancient Greek ὄργια (órgia, “secret rites, mysteries”).
definition_en: A wild and uncontrolled party or gathering.

senses.gloss: Secret rites or ceremonies, typically involving riotous and dissolute behavior, including dancing, drunkenness and indiscriminate sexual activity, undertaken in honor of various pagan gods or goddesses (such as Attis, Bacchus, Ceres, Dionysus, Osiris, etc).
senses.example: Human sacrifices of a definitely black magical order took place at the tomb of Osiris, while similar orgies with human victims were performed at Heliopolis.

senses.gloss: A gathering of people to engage in group sex.
An instance or period of excessive indulgence in a specified activity.
senses.example: It's an orgy of perfectly choreographed cartoon uber violence and is the game the Devil May Cry series always promised but never delivered.

examples.text: He had violent passions, and on occasion desire seized his body so that he was driven to an orgy of lust, but he hated the instincts that robbed him of his self-possession.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 격렬한 정념을 품고 있었고, 때로는 욕망이 그의 몸을 사로잡아 광란의 육욕에 빠져들게 했지만, 자제력을 앗아가는 그런 본능들을 증오했다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From debauch + -ery, 1640s.
definition_en: Excessive or indulgent behavior, especially of a sexual nature.

senses.gloss: Excessive indulgence in sensual pleasures; scandalous/immoral activities; involving sex, alcohol, or drugs without inhibition.
Seduction from duty

examples.text: I think, even, he hated the inevitable partner in his debauchery.
examples.translation_ko: 심지어 그는 자신의 방탕한 행위에 불가피하게 동반되는 상대방까지도 미워했던 것 같다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English commanden, commaunden, comaunden, comanden, from Old French comander, from Late Latin commandāre, from Latin commendāre. Ultima...
definition_en: An order given to someone to do something.

senses.gloss: An order to do something.
senses.example: I was given a command to cease shooting.

senses.gloss: The right or authority to order, control or dispose of; the right to be obeyed or to compel obedience.
senses.example: It wasn't a decisive operation, and Carthage still had command of Spain.

senses.gloss: power of control, direction or disposal; mastery.
senses.example: a good command of language

examples.text: When he had regained command over himself, he shuddered at the sight of the woman he had enjoyed.
examples.translation_ko: 자제력을 되찾고 나면, 그는 자신이 즐겼던 여자를 보는 것조차 몸서리쳤다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From serene + -ly.
definition_en: In a calm and peaceful manner.

senses.gloss: In a serene manner.
senses.example: I’ve flown in flimsy microlights, soaring serenely above rich farmland. I’ve ridden tactical combat helicopters missions, skimming the desert floor and banking hard around sand dunes.

examples.text: His thoughts floated then serenely in the empyrean, and he felt towards her the horror that perhaps the painted butterfly, hovering about the flowers, feels to the filthy chrysalis from which it has triumphantly emerged.
examples.translation_ko: 그때 그의 사상은 천상계에서 고요히 떠돌았고, 꽃들 주위를 맴도는 아름다운 나비가 자신이 승리를 거두며 빠져나온 더러운 번데기에 대해 느끼는 것과 같은 혐오감을 그녀에게 느꼈다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin empȳreus, from Ancient Greek ἐμπύριος (empúrios), from ἐν (en, “in”) + πῦρ (pûr, “fire”) (whence English pyre).
definition_en: The highest heaven or realm of God.

senses.gloss: The highest heaven, supposed by the ancients to be a region of pure light and fire or else composed of ether, and sometimes seen as the dwelling-place of God or other divine beings; the highest celestial sphere according to ancient and medieval astronomy.
senses.example: Milton, a name to resound for ages; / Whose titan angels, Gabriel, Abdiel, / Starr'd from Jehovah's gorgeous armouries, / Tower, the deep-domed empyrëan / Rings to the roar of an angel onset— […]

examples.text: His thoughts floated then serenely in the empyrean, and he felt towards her the horror that perhaps the painted butterfly, hovering about the flowers, feels to the filthy chrysalis from which it has triumphantly emerged.

definition_en: A colorful flying insect with distinctive wing patterns.

senses.gloss: A flying insect of the order Lepidoptera, distinguished from moths by their diurnal activity and generally brighter colouring.
senses.example: It is true. I am like a butterfly, and I shall only live a little while.

senses.gloss: A use of surgical tape, cut into thin strips and placed across an open wound to hold it closed.
senses.example: butterfly tape; butterfly bandage; butterfly strips

senses.gloss: The butterfly stroke.

etymology: From French idéaliste, from Late Latin idealis (“ideal”), from Latin idea (“idea”), equivalent to ideal + -ist.
definition_en: A person who believes that the best way to achieve a goal is through idealistic or impractical means.

senses.gloss: One who adheres to idealism.
Someone whose conduct stems from idealism rather than from practicality.
An unrealistic or impractical visionary.

examples.text: It seems strange even to myself, when I have described a man who was cruel, selfish, brutal and sensual, to say that he was a great idealist.
examples.translation_ko: 잔인하고 이기적이며 야만적이고 관능적인 한 남자를 묘사해놓고서 그가 위대한 이상주의자였다고 말하는 것은, 나 자신에게도 이상하게 느껴진다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English poorly, pouerly, poreliche, poureliche, pouerliche, equivalent to poor + -ly.
definition_en: Not well or healthy.

senses.gloss: In a poor manner or condition; without plenty, or sufficiency, or suitable provision for comfort.
senses.example: to live poorly

senses.gloss: With little or no success; indifferently; with little profit or advantage.
senses.example: to do poorly in business

senses.gloss: Meanly; without spirit.
senses.example: Nor is their courage or their wealth so low, / That from his wars they poorly would retire.

examples.text: He lived more poorly than an artisan.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 직공보다도 더 가난하게 살았다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English odious, from Old French odieus, from Latin odiōsus, from odium (“hate”).
definition_en: Extremely unpleasant or hateful.

senses.gloss: Arousing or meriting strong dislike, aversion, or intense displeasure.
senses.example: Scrubbing the toilets in the bar at the end of a Saturday night is an odious task.

examples.text: Strickland was an odious man, but I still think he was a great one.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 혐오스러운 남자였지만, 나는 여전히 그가 위대한 인물이었다고 생각한다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A person appointed to assist a diplomat or other official.

senses.gloss: Alternative form of attaché.

examples.text: A certain importance attaches to the views on art of painters, and this is the natural place for me to set down what I know of Strickland’s opinions of the great artists of the past.
examples.translation_ko: 화가들의 예술관에는 어느 정도 중요성이 따르기 마련이고, 따라서 이곳이 과거의 위대한 예술가들에 대한 스트릭랜드의 견해를 내가 아는 대로 기록해둘 자연스러운 자리이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From conversational + -ist.
definition_en: A person who engages in conversation.

senses.gloss: A person who participates in a conversation.
senses.example: If you can just ask questions about a person and nod sagely then they will leave thinking you are a brilliant conversationalist.

senses.gloss: A person skilled in general conversation.
senses.example: But Shulgin, while a nimble conversationalist, can have trouble with names — of people and places, never chemicals.

examples.text: Strickland was not a conversationalist, and he had no gift for putting what he had to say in the striking phrase that the listener remembers.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 대화에 능한 사람이 아니었고, 자신이 하고 싶은 말을 듣는 이의 기억에 남을 만한 인상적인 문구로 표현하는 재능도 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From listen + -er.
definition_en: A person who listens to something or someone.

senses.gloss: Someone who listens, especially to a speech or a broadcast.
senses.example: And then her words tumbled out in a passion of communication, as though she hurried before her listener could be taken away.

senses.gloss: A function that runs in response to an event; an event handler.
A person's ear.

examples.text: Strickland was not a conversationalist, and he had no gift for putting what he had to say in the striking phrase that the listener remembers.
examples.translation_ko: 스트릭랜드는 대화에 능한 사람이 아니었고, 자신이 하고 싶은 말을 듣는 이의 기억에 남을 만한 인상적인 문구로 표현하는 재능도 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From re- + produce.
definition_en: To produce offspring or copies of something.

senses.gloss: To produce an image or copy of.
To generate or propagate offspring or organisms sexually or asexually.
To produce again; to recreate.

examples.text: His humour, as will be seen if I have in any way succeeded in reproducing the manner of his conversation, was sardonic.
examples.translation_ko: 내가 그의 대화 방식을 어느 정도나마 재현하는 데 성공했다면 알 수 있겠지만, 그의 유머는 냉소적이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From unusual + -ness.
definition_en: The state of being unusual.

senses.gloss: The condition or state of being unusual.
senses.example: `Was it a housekeeper?' He was the rouseabout, wearing his best clothes with awful unusualness.

senses.gloss: Something unusual; an aberration.

examples.text: He made one laugh sometimes by speaking the truth, but this is a form of humour which gains its force only by its unusualness; it would cease to amuse if it were commonly practised.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 때로 진실을 말함으로써 사람들을 웃게 만들었지만, 이런 형태의 유머는 그 드문 성격으로만 힘을 얻는 것이어서, 만약 흔히 행해진다면 재미를 잃을 것이다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin analogia, from Ancient Greek ἀναλογίᾱ (analogíā), from ἀνα- (ana-) + λόγος (lógos, “speech, reckoning”).
definition_en: A comparison between two unlike things to illustrate a similarity.

senses.gloss: A relationship of resemblance or equivalence between two situations, people, or objects, especially when used as a basis for explanation or extrapolation.
senses.example: A kid living on the street is a bit like — and please pardon the analogy here — a weed.

senses.gloss: The proportion or the equality of ratios.

The correspondence of a word or phrase with the genius of a language, as learned from the manner in which its words and phrases are ordinarily formed; similarity of derivative or inflectional processes.

examples.text: I never heard him speak of those whose work had a certain analogy with his own—of Cezanne, for instance, or of Van Gogh; and I doubt very much if he had ever seen their pictures.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그가 자신의 작품과 어느 정도 유사성을 지닌 화가들—예를 들어 세잔이나 반 고흐—에 대해 이야기하는 것을 들어본 적이 없었다. 그리고 그가 그들의 그림을 본 적이 있는지도 매우 의심스러웠다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English gretly, gretely, gretliche, greteliche, equivalent to great + -ly.
definition_en: Used to indicate a large or significant degree.

senses.gloss: To a great extent or degree.
senses.example: Expenses greatly exceeded revenues this year, much to nobody's surprise.

senses.gloss: Nobly; magnanimously.

examples.text: He was not greatly interested in the Impressionists.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 인상파 화가들에게 그다지 관심이 없었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Middle English predecessour, from Old French predecesseor (“forebear”), from Late Latin praedēcessor, from Latin prae- (“pre-”) + Latin dēcess...
definition_en: A person or thing that existed before another.

senses.gloss: One who precedes; one who has preceded another in any state, position, office, etc.; one whom another follows or comes after, in any office or position.
senses.example: I thought about my predecessor, who had died of drink and smoke; and I could have wished he had been so good as to live, and not bother me with his decease.

senses.gloss: A model or type of machinery or device which precedes the current (or later) one. Usually used to describe an earlier, outdated model.
senses.example: The steam engine was the predecessor of diesel and electric locomotives.

senses.gloss: A vertex having a directed path to another vertex

examples.text: I feel the need to ascribe to him fantastic theories about his predecessors, and it is with a certain sense of disillusion that I confess he thought about them pretty much as does everybody else.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 선배 화가들에 대한 기상천외한 이론들을 부여하고 싶은 욕구를 느끼는데, 그가 그들에 대해 다른 사람들과 거의 똑같이 생각했다고 고백하는 것은 어느 정도 환멸감을 준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From dis- + illusion: literally, the removal or undoing of illusion.
definition_en: A feeling of disappointment or disillusionment with something that was previously believed to be true.

senses.gloss: To free or deprive of illusion; to disenchant.
senses.example: To disillusion a man is not to break him, but to open his eyes to the machinery behind the curtain.

examples.text: I feel the need to ascribe to him fantastic theories about his predecessors, and it is with a certain sense of disillusion that I confess he thought about them pretty much as does everybody else.

definition_en: The act of realizing something or becoming aware of a fact.

senses.gloss: Alternative spelling of realization.

examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: To pay back something owed or given.

senses.gloss: Synonym of pay back in all senses.
senses.example: I finally repaid my student loans, just before sending my kids to college.

senses.gloss: To make worthwhile; to yield a result worth the effort; to pay off.
senses.example: The possible importance of excessive androgen secretion and the ingestion of agents such as the fluorenamines may repay further investigation.

senses.gloss: To give in return; requite.

examples.text: The society of beach-combers always repays the small pains you need be at to enjoy it.
examples.translation_ko: 해변의 부랑자들과 어울리는 사회는 그들을 즐기기 위해 들이는 작은 수고를 언제나 보상해준다.

definition_en: Requiring a lot of hard work.

senses.gloss: Requiring much physical effort; toilsome.
senses.example: The coal is then transferred to broad-gauge wagons for transport to Dublin. The transhipment is a rather laborious business, the coal being shovelled by hand from one wagon to another.

senses.gloss: Mentally difficult; painstaking.
Industrious.
senses.example: All, with united Force, combine to drive / The lazy Drones from the laborious Hive.

examples.text: You need no laborious steps to enter upon familiarity with them, and you can earn not only their confidence, but their gratitude, by turning an attentive ear to their discourse.
examples.translation_ko: 그들과 친해지기 위해 번거로운 단계를 거칠 필요가 없으며, 그들의 이야기에 귀 기울여주기만 해도 신뢰는 물론 감사까지 얻을 수 있다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: A prolonged talk or written piece on a particular subject.

senses.gloss: Verbal exchange, conversation.
senses.example:
UUho when he ſhal embrace you in his arms
UUil tell how many thouſand men he ſlew.
And when you looke for amorous diſcourſe,
Will rattle foorth his facts of war and blood: […]

senses.gloss: Expression in words, either speech or writing.
A conversation.

definition_en: The quality of being fertile or capable of producing offspring.

senses.example: Muckspreading increases the fertility of the soil.

senses.gloss: The birthrate of a population; the number of live births per 1000 people per year.
The average number of births per woman within a population.

examples.text: The extent of their experience is pleasantly balanced by the fertility of their imagination.
examples.translation_ko: 그들의 경험의 폭은 상상력의 풍부함과 기분 좋게 균형을 이룬다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From poke + -er.
definition_en: A card game played with a standard deck.

senses.gloss: A metal rod, generally of wrought iron, for adjusting the burning logs or coals in a fire; a firestick.
A tool like a soldering iron for making poker drawings.
One who pokes.
senses.example: The guy next to him poked him in the ribs and said, “Check out the bazongas on this one!” Lee pivoted toward the rib poker and found himself looking straight into the face of Romeo Bouchard.

examples.text: It is hazardous to play poker with them, but their ingenuity adds a peculiar excitement to the best game in the world.
examples.translation_ko: 그들과 포커를 치는 것은 위험하지만, 그들의 기발함은 세상에서 가장 훌륭한 게임에 독특한 흥미를 더해준다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: From Latin aequivalentem, accusative singular of aequivalēns, present active participle of aequivaleō (“I am equivalent, have equal power”). By sur...
definition_en: Having the same value or effect as something else.

senses.gloss: Similar or identical in value, meaning or effect; virtually equal.
senses.example: To burn calories, a thirty-minute jog is equivalent to a couple of hamburgers.

senses.gloss: Of two sets, having a one-to-one correspondence.
senses.example: The equivalence theorem: If both M is equivalent to a subset N₁ of N and N is equivalent to a subset M₁ of M, then the sets M and N are equivalent to each other.

senses.gloss: Relating to the corresponding elements of an equivalence relation.

examples.text: I do not consider that the cigars and whisky he consumed at my expense (he always refused cocktails, since he was practically a teetotaller), and the few dollars, borrowed with a civil air of conferring a favour upon me, that passed from my pocket to his, were in any way equivalent to the entertainment he afforded me.

definition_en: A person who owes money.

senses.gloss: A person or firm that owes money; one in debt; one who owes a debt.

One who owes another anything, or is under obligation, arising from express agreement, implication of law, or principles of natural justice, to pay money or to fulfill some other obligation; in bankruptcy or similar proceedings, the person who is the subject of the proceeding.

examples.text: I remained his debtor.
examples.translation_ko: 나는 그에게 빚을 지고 있었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

etymology: Latin reticēns, present participle of reticeō (“to keep silence”).
definition_en: Unwilling to talk or express opinions.

senses.gloss: Unwilling to communicate; keeping one's thoughts and opinions to oneself; reserved or restrained.
senses.example: But they were not reticent enough to prevent the circulation of certain uneasy rumours and extravagant stories of discreditable adventures.

senses.gloss: Hesitant or not wanting to take some action; reluctant (usually followed by a verb in the infinitive).
senses.example: The police may be reticent to charge the alleged offender, prosecutors reticent to continue with the prosecution, and juries reticent to convict.

examples.text: It was a matter upon which he was reticent, and with persons of his kind a direct question is never very discreet.
examples.translation_ko: 그는 이 문제에 대해 말을 아꼈고, 그런 부류의 사람들에게 직접적인 질문은 결코 신중하지 못한 일이었다.
examples.author: W. Somerset Maugham

definition_en: Not earned or deserved.

senses.gloss: Not deserved, earned or merited; unjustifiable or unfair.

etymology: From Middle English fraude (recorded since 1345), from Old French fraude, a borrowing from Latin fraus (“deceit, injury, offence”).

examples.text: My fancy played with the various forms of fraud and violence, and I agreed with him sympathetically when he remarked that the authorities in the old country were so damned technical.
examples.translation_ko: 내 상상력은 온갖 형태의 사기와 폭력을 떠올렸고, 그가 본국의 당국자들이 너무 빌어먹을 정도로 까다롭다고 말할 때 나는 동정심을 담아 동의했다.

senses.gloss: In some team sports, especially soccer, a practice game which does not count on a team's record.

senses.gloss: Alternative form of luster (shine, etc.)

definition_en: A rapid or irregular heartbeat.

senses.gloss: An abnormal beating of the heart that may be perceived by the patient, a result of excitement, exertion, or illness.

definition_en: A dark reddish-purple color.

senses.gloss: A colour between red and blue; violet, though often closer to magenta.
senses.example: Arraying with reflected Purple and Gold / The Clouds that on his Weſtern Throne attend.

senses.gloss: Any non-spectral colour on the line of purples on a colour chromaticity diagram or a colour wheel between violet and red.
